commentary_english:
Having spoken thus about conceiving based on formations with material form as the starting point, now, because ordinary people conceive even regarding living beings that are discerned by reference to formations, therefore, pointing out those beings, [the text] states, "He perceives beings as beings," etc.

Therein, the word "bhūta" ("being") is found in the senses of the five aggregates (pañcakkhandha), non-humans (amanussa), elements (dhātu), existing (vijjamāna), cankerless saints (khīṇāsava), living beings (satta), trees (rukkha), etc.

In passages such as, "Do you see, monks, that this has come into being (bhūtamidaṃ)," it is found referring to the five aggregates.

In "Whatever beings (bhūtāni) have assembled here," it refers to non-humans.

In "The four great elements (mahābhūtā), monks, are the cause," it refers to the elements.

In "[Offense] concerning what exists (bhūtasmiṃ)," it means existing.

In "The being (bhūto) who swallows time," it means a cankerless saint.

In "All beings (bhūtā) will lay down the body in the world," it refers to living beings.

In "The destruction of plant life (bhūtagāmapātabyatā)," it means trees, etc.

Here, however, it applies to living beings, but not without distinction. Here, "beings" signifies living beings below the heaven of the Four Great Kings (cātumahārājikānaṃ).

There, "He perceives beings as beings," etc., [is] just as said.

However, in "He conceives beings," etc., the three conceivings should also be applied. How? Here, in the way it was said, "He sees a householder or a householder's son supplied and furnished with the five strands of sense pleasure," he takes hold of the notion that "beings are beautiful" or "beings are happy" and becomes attached. Having seen them, having heard, smelled, tasted, touched, cognized them, he becomes attached.

Thus, he conceives beings through the conceiving of craving (taṇhāmaññanā).

With "[Oh,] that I might be reborn into companionship with wealthy nobles," etc.
Or, resolving his mind on the acquisition of what he has not obtained, he thinks: “O that I may be reborn in the company of great wealthy *Khattiyas*,” etc. Thus too he conceives beings through the conceiving of craving.

When, depending on his excellence or deficiency in relation to other beings, he ranks himself as superior to others.

When any being is inferior or the self is inferior, or when any being is superior.

Or as equal, he conceives beings through the conceiving of conceit.

As it is said: “Herein, someone on account of birth …or a certain ground previously ranked himself as equal to others;

At a later time he ranks himself as superior.

He ranks others as inferior; whatever such conceit.

…This is called conceit and excessive conceit” (*vibha* 876-880).

Thus he conceives in beings through the conceiving of conceit.

He conceives beings.

When he conceives beings thus: “Beings are permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change,” or “All living beings, all creatures, all beings, all souls are without power, without strength, without energy, evolving in the grip of fate, chance, or nature, experiencing pleasure and pain in the six classes” (*dī*. *ni*. 1. 168) - this is the conceiving of views (*diṭṭhimaññanā*).

In this way he conceives beings through the three conceivings.

How does he conceive in beings? He desires rebirth or pleasant rebirth in those beings.

Thus he conceives in beings through the conceiving of craving (*taṇhāmaññanā*).

Or when he gives a gift (*dāna*), undertakes precepts (*śīla*), or observes the *uposatha*, wishing for rebirth among those beings,

In this way too he conceives in beings through the conceiving of craving (*taṇhāmaññanā*).

When, having apprehended beings in terms of an aggregation, he ranks some beings as superior, some as equal, some as inferior.

Thus he conceives in beings through the conceiving of conceit (*mānamaññanā*).

So too he conceives some beings as permanent and stable.

Some as impermanent and unstable, or he conceives “I too am a certain somebody among beings”-

Thus he conceives in beings through the conceiving of views (*diṭṭhimaññanā*).

He conceives beings?

He conceives in terms of beings: Here, when he conceives the origin of himself or another, along with his equipment, from any being whatsoever, he conceives in terms of beings; this is his conceiving of views (*diṭṭhimaññanā*).

When he arouses affection and conceit for the base conceived through the conceiving of views, these are his conceivings of craving and conceit (*taṇhā-māna-maññanā*).

He conceives that "beings are mine:" Here, only one conceiving of craving (*taṇhāmaññanā*) is obtained.

This occurs when he lays claim to beings thus: “My sons, my daughters, my goats and sheep, my poultry and swine, my elephants, cattle, horses, and mares.” This proceeds from his sense of “mine.”

He rejoices in beings: this is as was said above.

Because they have not been fully understood by him: the beings are not fully understood because he has not fully understood the formations by reference to which beings are discerned.

The interpretation should be made by the method stated.

He conceives in terms of beings, he conceives that “beings are mine,” he rejoices in beings, because they have not been fully understood by him

Thus, having shown in brief the bases of conceiving by way of formations (*saṅkhāra*) and living beings (*sattva*), with the words “gods as gods” the Exalted One sets out to show the same thing in detailed classification according to the division of planes.

There, they sport with the five sense pleasures or with their own power: they are the gods (*devā*), they play and shine.
They are of three kinds: gods by convention (*sammuti-deva*), gods by rebirth (*upapatti-deva*), and gods by purification (*visuddhi-deva*).

Gods by convention are kings (*rājā*), queens (*devī*), and princes (*rājakumāra*).

Gods by rebirth include the gods of the Cātumahārājika heaven up to the heavens above them.

Gods by purification are the *arhats* who have destroyed the influxes.

Here, gods by rebirth are to be understood, but not without a distinction.

Excepting Māra and his retinue in the Paranirmita-vasavarti heaven, the remaining six desire-realm heavens are what is intended here as gods.

In that case, the entire explanation of the meaning should be understood in the manner set forth in the section on beings.

Gods, from the gods, gods; gods by convention, gods by rebirth, gods by purification.

Here, Māra should be understood as *Prajāpati*.

Some say that this is a designation for the great kings, etc., who are overlords in the various groups of gods.

But the Great Commentary rejects this as incorrect, for these are already included under the category of gods; Māra alone is intended here by the word "Prajāpati," for he is the overlord of this generation made up of living beings.

Where does he dwell? In the Paranirmita-vasavarti heaven.

There, indeed, the king of the Vasavartis exercises rule.

It is said that Māra lives in one place wielding sovereignty over his own retinue, like a rebel prince in a frontier corner of a kingdom.

The retinue of Māra should be understood as included along with Māra.

Here is the interpretation: when he arouses desire after seeing or hearing that Prajāpati is beautiful, of long life and abundant happiness, then he conceives him through the conceiving of craving (*taṇhā-maññanā*).

When he resolves his mind on the acquisition of what he has not obtained, thinking: "Oh, that I may be reborn in the company of Prajāpati," in this way too he conceives Prajāpati through the conceiving of craving.

When, after attaining the state of Prajāpati, he gives rise to the conceit: "I am the ruler of creatures, the overlord," he conceives Prajāpati through the conceiving of conceit.

Thinking "Prajāpati is permanent and stable," or "Prajāpati will be annihilated and destroyed," or "Prajāpati is without power, without strength, without energy, evolving in the grip of fate, chance, or nature, experiencing pleasure and pain in the six classes," he conceives Prajāpati through the conceiving of views (*diṭṭhi-maññanā*).

Prajāpati; in the Great Commentary; the king of the Vasavartis; Māra.

Here, only one conceiving of views is relevant.

Its occurrence should be understood thus:

Here someone conceives: "Whatever qualities are found in Prajāpati, all those are permanent, stable, eternal, and of unchanging nature."

Or else he conceives: "There is no evil in Prajāpati, nor are any evil deeds found in him."

In Prajāpati.

From Prajāpati: here the three conceivings are relevant.

How? Here someone conceives himself or another together with their accessories to originate or emanate from Prajāpati; this is his conceiving of views.

When he arouses affection and conceit for the base conceived through the conceiving of views, these are also to be understood as his conceivings of craving and conceit.

In the thought "Prajāpati is mine," only one conceiving of craving is relevant.

This occurs when he lays claim to Prajāpati thus: "Prajāpati is my master, he is my lord."

The rest is as already stated.

From Prajāpati; Prajāpati is mine.

Brahma, from Brahma: here, because he is enhanced by those various special qualities, [he is called] Brahmā.

Moreover, "Brahma" is also called Mahābrahmā, the Tathāgata, Brahmins, mother and father, and what is supreme.

In the passages: "Brahma of one thousand, Brahma of two thousand," it is Mahābrahmā that is called Brahmā.
3. 165-166) Indeed, Mahābrahmā is called Brahmā.

“'Brahmā', monks, this is a designation for the Tathāgata” - here it is the Tathāgata.

The Brahman, from Brahman, [is] Brahmā.

“The Awakened One dispels darkness, has an eye all around, has gone to the end of the world, has transcended all existence, is without outflows, has abandoned all suffering, is truthful, Brahmā is served by me.”

(Cūḷani. 104) – Here [is] a *brāhmaṇa*.

“'Brahmā' are called mother and father, teachers of old.” (Itivu. 106; Jā. 2. 20. 181) – Here [are] mother and father.

“He sets in motion the *brahmacakka*” (Ma. Ni. 1. 148; A. Ni. 5. 11) here [is] the best.

Here, however, it is the Brahmā who is first to be born and whose life-span lasts for the aeon that is intended.

The ministers of Brahmā and the assembly of Brahmā should also be included, for all these must be known.

The explanation of the meaning should be understood by the method stated in the section on Pajapati.

In the Ābhassara section, like light from the flame of a torch, radiance streams forth, streams out, from their bodies, thus they are called the gods of Streaming Radiance (*ābhassarā*).

By mentioning these, all beings occupying the plane of the second *jhāna*—the gods of Limited Radiance (*parittābhā*), of Immeasurable Radiance (*appamāṇābhā*), as well as of Streaming Radiance (*ābhassarā*)—should be included, for all these occupy a single level.

Streaming Radiance (*ābhassarā*).

In the *Subhakiṇha* section, they are covered and filled with glory, with the color of bodily radiance, a single mass, like those who have the essence of a golden statue placed in a golden casket; thus, they are the gods of Refulgent Glory (*subhakiṇhā*).

By mentioning these, all beings occupying the plane of the third *jhāna* should be included.

the gods of Limited Glory (*parittasubhā*), of Immeasurable Glory (*appamāṇasubhā*), as well as of Refulgent Glory (*subhakiṇhā*)—should be included, for all these occupy a single level.

Refulgent Glory (*subhakiṇhā*).

In the *Vehapphala* section, abundant [is their] fruit, thus [they are called] the gods of Great Fruit (*vehapphalā*).

These are the *brahmās* on the plane of the fourth *jhāna*.

The interpretation of the meaning for these three sections is the same as the method in the section on beings, so it should be understood.

Great Fruit (*vehapphalā*).
Because *abhibhū* is to overcome, therefore, *abhibhū*.

What is overcome? The four immaterial aggregates ( *arūpino khandhe* ).

This is a designation for the realm of non-percipient beings (*asaññabhava*).

The non-percipient gods (*asaññasattā devā*) reside in one section of the same plane as the gods of Abundant Fruit (*vehapphala*), where they remain in the same posture in which they are reborn throughout their lives, all with similar material form (*cittakammarūpasadisā*) resulting from the similarity of their productive karma consciousness.

All of those here are included by the expression "overcoming".

Some describe the overlord Brahmās (*adhipatibrahmānaṃ*), saying "the name *abhibhū* is a thousand Brahmās," and so forth.

However, it should be understood that this is incorrect, since those are already included in the Brahma section (*brahmaggahaṇa*).

Furthermore, understanding that the overcoming ones (*abhibhū*) are beautiful (*vaṇṇavā*) and long-lived (*dīghāyuko*), one generates desire and lust (*chandarāgaṃ uppādento*) and conceives the *abhibhū* through the conceiving of craving (*taṇhāmaññanāya maññati*).

When he resolves his mind on the acquisition of what he has not obtained, thinking: "O, that I may be reborn in the company of the overcoming ones (*abhibhuno sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya*)," in this way too he conceives the *abhibhū* through the conceiving of craving (*taṇhāmaññanāya maññati*).

Ranking himself as inferior (*hīnato*) and the overcoming ones (*abhibhū*) as superior (*seyyato*), he conceives them through the conceiving of conceit (*mānamaññanāya maññati*).

Misapprehending the overcoming ones (*abhibhū*) as permanent (*nicco*) and stable (*dhruvo*), he conceives them through the conceiving of views (*diṭṭhimaññanāya maññati*). This should be understood.

The rest follows the method stated in the section on Pajāpati (*pajāpativāra*).

*Abhibhū*.

*Abhibhū*. The description of the sections on existence, etc., is completed.

Description of the sections on the sphere of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), etc.

mula_pali:
4. ‘‘Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanato sañjānāti; ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanato saññatvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanasmiṃ maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanato maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ meti maññati, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanato sañjānāti; viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanato saññatvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanasmiṃ maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanato maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ meti maññati, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanato sañjānāti; ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanato saññatvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanasmiṃ maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanato maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ meti maññati, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanato sañjānāti; nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanato saññatvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasmiṃ maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanato maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ meti maññati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.
mula_english:
4. “He perceives the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*) as the base of infinite space. Having perceived the base of infinite space as the base of infinite space, he conceives himself as the base of infinite space, he conceives himself in the base of infinite space, he conceives himself apart from the base of infinite space, he conceives the base of infinite space to be ‘mine,’ he delights in the base of infinite space.

What is the reason? ‘Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.’

“He perceives the base of infinite consciousness (*vijñāṇāñcāyatana*) as the base of infinite consciousness. Having perceived the base of infinite consciousness as the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives himself as the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives himself in the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives himself apart from the base of infinite consciousness, he conceives the base of infinite consciousness to be ‘mine,’ he delights in the base of infinite consciousness.

What is the reason? ‘Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.’

“He perceives the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) as the base of nothingness. Having perceived the base of nothingness as the base of nothingness, he conceives himself as the base of nothingness, he conceives himself in the base of nothingness, he conceives himself apart from the base of nothingness, he conceives the base of nothingness to be ‘mine,’ he delights in the base of nothingness.

What is the reason? ‘Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.’

“He perceives the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Having perceived the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he conceives himself as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he conceives himself in the base of neither-perception-nor-nonperception, he conceives himself apart from the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he conceives the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception to be ‘mine,’ he delights in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

What is the reason? ‘Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.’
commentary_pali:
4. Evaṃ bhagavā paṭipāṭiyā devaloke dassentopi abhibhūvacanena asaññabhavaṃ dassetvā idāni yasmā ayaṃ vaṭṭakathā, suddhāvāsā ca vivaṭṭapakkhe ṭhitā, anāgāmikhīṇāsavā eva hi te devā. Yasmā vā katipayakappasahassāyukā te devā, buddhuppādakāleyeva honti. Buddhā pana asaṅkheyepi kappe na uppajjanti, tadā suññāpi sā bhūmi hoti. Rañño khandhāvāraṭṭhānaṃ viya hi buddhānaṃ suddhāvāsabhavo. Te teneva ca kāraṇena viññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsavasenapi na gahitā, sabbakālikā pana imā maññanā. Tasmā tāsaṃ sadāvijjamānabhūmiṃ dassento suddhāvāse atikkamitvā, ākāsānañcāyatanantiādimāha. Tattha ākāsānañcāyatananti tabbhūmikā cattāro kusalavipākakiriyā khandhā. Te ca tatrūpapannāyeva daṭṭhabbā bhavaparicchedakathā ayanti katvā. Esa nayo viññāṇañcāyatanādīsu. Atthayojanā pana catūsupi etesu vāresu abhibhūvāre vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Mānamaññanā cettha pajāpativāre vuttanayenāpi yujjati.

Ākāsānañcāyatanavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Diṭṭhasutavārādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
4. Thus, the Blessed One, showing the heavenly worlds in succession, having shown the non-percipient realm by way of the "overcoming" expression, now, since this is a discussion of the round of existence (*vaṭṭakathā*), and the Pure Abodes (*śuddhāvāsa*) stand on the side of the cessation of the round, since those gods are exclusively non-returners (*anāgāmi*) and those who have destroyed the corruptions (*khīṇāsava*).

Or the reason is that the lifespan of those gods is only a few thousands of aeons, and they only exist during the time when a Buddha has appeared in the world.

But Buddhas sometimes do not appear for an incalculable number of aeons (*asaṅkheyakappa*), and during this time the plane is empty.

For the realm of the Pure Abodes (*śuddhāvāsa-bhava*) belongs to the Buddhas like a campground to a king.

For this reason, they are not included in the stations of consciousness (*viññāṇaṭṭhiti*) or the abodes of beings (*sattāvāsa*). But these conceivings (*maññanā*) occur at all times.

Therefore, showing the plane where they always exist, having passed over the Pure Abodes (*śuddhāvāsa*), he said beginning with "the sphere of infinite space" (*ākāsānañcāyatana*).

There, the four aggregates (*khandha*) are wholesome result-of-action actions belonging to that plane of "the sphere of infinite space" (*ākāsānañcāyatana*).

And only the aggregates of those reborn there are to be seen, thinking, "This is a discussion delimiting the planes of existence (*bhavaparicchedakathā*)."

This is the method regarding the sphere of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*) and so forth.

The interpretation of the meaning in these four sections follows the method given in the section on the Vanquishers (*abhibhūvāre*).

But here the conceiving of conceit (*mānamaññanā*) should be interpreted according to the method of the section on Pajapati (*pajāpativāre*).

The explanation of the section on the sphere of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*) and so forth is finished.

Explanation of the section on what is seen and heard (*diṭṭhasutavārādivaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
5. ‘‘Diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhato sañjānāti; diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhato saññatvā diṭṭhaṃ maññati, diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati, diṭṭhato maññati, diṭṭhaṃ meti maññati, diṭṭhaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Sutaṃ sutato sañjānāti; sutaṃ sutato saññatvā sutaṃ maññati, sutasmiṃ maññati, sutato maññati, sutaṃ meti maññati, sutaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Mutaṃ mutato sañjānāti; mutaṃ mutato saññatvā mutaṃ maññati, mutasmiṃ maññati, mutato maññati, mutaṃ meti maññati, mutaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Viññātaṃ viññātato sañjānāti; viññātaṃ viññātato saññatvā viññātaṃ maññati, viññātasmiṃ maññati, viññātato maññati, viññātaṃ meti maññati, viññātaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.
mula_english:
5. “He perceives the seen as the seen. Having perceived the seen as the seen, he conceives himself as the seen, he conceives himself in the seen, he conceives himself apart from the seen, he conceives the seen to be ‘mine’, he delights in the seen.
What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.

“He perceives the heard as the heard. Having perceived the heard as the heard, he conceives himself as the heard, he conceives himself in the heard, he conceives himself apart from the heard, he conceives the heard to be ‘mine’, he delights in the heard.
What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.

“He perceives the sensed as the sensed. Having perceived the sensed as the sensed, he conceives himself as the sensed, he conceives himself in the sensed, he conceives himself apart from the sensed, he conceives the sensed to be ‘mine,’ he delights in the sensed.
What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.

“He perceives the cognized as the cognized. Having perceived the cognized as the cognized, he conceives himself as the cognized, he conceives himself in the cognized, he conceives himself apart from the cognized, he conceives the cognized to be ‘mine’, he delights in the cognized.
What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.
commentary_pali:
5. Evaṃ bhūmivisesādinā bhedena vitthāratopi maññanāvatthuṃ dassetvā idāni sabbamaññanāvatthubhūtaṃ sakkāyapariyāpannaṃ tebhūmakadhammabhedaṃ diṭṭhādīhi catūhi saṅgaṇhitvā dassento, diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhatotiādimāha.

Tattha diṭṭhanti maṃsacakkhunāpi diṭṭhaṃ, dibbacakkhunāpi diṭṭhaṃ. Rūpāyatanassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tattha diṭṭhaṃ maññatīti diṭṭhaṃ tīhi maññanāhi maññati. Kathaṃ? Rūpāyatanaṃ subhasaññāya sukhasaññāya ca passanto tattha chandarāgaṃ janeti, taṃ assādeti abhinandati. Vuttampi hetaṃ bhagavatā ‘‘itthirūpe, bhikkhave, sattā rattā giddhā gadhitā mucchitā ajjhosannā, te dīgharattaṃ socanti itthirūpavasānugā’’ti (a. ni. 5.55). Evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. ‘‘Iti me rūpaṃ siyā anāgatamaddhānanti vā panettha nandiṃ samannāneti, rūpasampadaṃ vā pana ākaṅkhamāno dānaṃ detī’’ti vitthāro. Evampi diṭṭhaṃ taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. Attano pana parassa ca rūpasampattiṃ vipattiṃ nissāya mānaṃ janeti. ‘‘Imināhaṃ seyyosmī’’ti vā ‘‘sadisosmī’’ti vā ‘‘hīnosmī’’ti vāti evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ mānamaññanāya maññati. Rūpāyatanaṃ pana niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassatanti maññati, attānaṃ attaniyanti maññati, maṅgalaṃ amaṅgalanti maññati, evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhimaññanāya maññati. Evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ tīhi maññanāhi maññati. Kathaṃ diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati? Rūpasmiṃ attānaṃ samanupassananayena maññanto diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati. Yathā vā dhane dhaññe. Evaṃ rūpasmiṃ rāgādayoti maññantopi diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati. Ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiññeva panassa diṭṭhimaññanāya maññite vatthusmiṃ sinehaṃ mānañca uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. Evaṃ diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati. Sesaṃ pathavīvāre vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

diṭṭha diṭṭhaṃ maññatī

Sutanti maṃsasotenapi sutaṃ, dibbasotenapi sutaṃ, saddāyatanassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

Suta

Mutanti mutvā munitvā ca gahitaṃ, āhacca upagantvāti attho, indriyānaṃ ārammaṇānañca aññamaññasaṃsilese viññātanti vuttaṃ hoti, gandharasaphoṭṭhabbāyatanānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

Muta

Viññātanti manasā viññātaṃ, sesānaṃ sattannaṃ āyatanānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ dhammārammaṇassa vā. Idha pana sakkāyapariyāpannameva labbhati. Vitthāro panettha diṭṭhavāre vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

Viññāta

Diṭṭhasuttavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Ekattavārādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
5. Having shown the object of conceiving in detail through distinctions based on the specific qualities of the elements, etc., now, showing the threefold division of phenomena pertaining to the three realms that are included in personality—which is the basis for all conceiving—by gathering [those phenomena] with the four: the seen, etc., [the text] states, " *The seen, he conceives in the seen,* " etc.

There, " *The seen* " means what is seen with the fleshy eye, and also what is seen with the divine eye. This is a designation for the visible form base (rūpāyatana). There, " *He conceives the seen* " means he conceives the seen with the three conceivings. How so? Seeing the visible form base in terms of the perception of beauty and the perception of pleasure, he arouses desire and lust for it, relishes it, and delights in it. For this has been said by the Exalted One: “Beings become lustful, *bhikkhus*, over the form of a woman, entranced, infatuated, intoxicated, and fettered. Coming under the sway of the form of a woman, they sorrow for a long time” (A.Ni. 5.55). Thus he conceives the seen with the conceiving of craving. Or he thinks: “May my body be thus in the future,” and brings delight to bear upon it; or he gives alms yearning for the attainment of physical beauty, and so on in detail. In these ways too he conceives the seen with the conceiving of craving. He arouses conceit on account of the excellence or deficiency of his own form in relation to another’s, thinking: “I am superior to him,” or “I am equal,” or “I am inferior.” Thus he conceives the seen with the conceiving of conceit. He conceives the visible form base as permanent, stable, and eternal, or as a self or the property of a self, or as auspicious or inauspicious. Thus he conceives the seen with the conceiving of views. In this way he conceives the seen with the three conceivings. How does he conceive himself “in the seen”? He conceives in the seen when he regards the self to be in visible form. Or “just as [one sees the self] in wealth or grain.” “Lust, etc. are in visible form.” - he conceives in the seen when he thinks. This is his conceiving of views. When he arouses affection and conceit for the base conceived through the conceiving of views, these are his conceivings of craving and conceit. Thus he conceives “in the seen.” The remainder should be understood by the method stated in the section on earth.

*The seen.* *He conceives the seen.*

*The heard* means what is heard with the fleshy ear, and also what is heard with the divine ear. This is a designation for the sound base (saddāyatana).

*The heard*

*The sensed* : that which is apprehended by sensing, i.e. by approach and contact. What is meant is that it is cognized through the mutual adherence of the sense faculty and objects. This is a designation for the bases of odour, flavour, and touch.

*The sensed*

*The cognized* means what is cognized by the mind; this is a designation for the remaining seven bases or for the object of the Dharma. But here only that which is included in personality is applicable. In detail these sections should be understood by the method used in the section on the seen.

*The cognized*

The explanation of the sections on the seen, heard, etc., is finished.

Explanation of the section on oneness, etc.

mula_pali:
6. ‘‘Ekattaṃ ekattato sañjānāti; ekattaṃ ekattato saññatvā ekattaṃ maññati, ekattasmiṃ maññati, ekattato maññati, ekattaṃ meti maññati, ekattaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Nānattaṃ nānattato sañjānāti; nānattaṃ nānattato saññatvā nānattaṃ maññati, nānattasmiṃ maññati, nānattato maññati, nānattaṃ meti maññati, nānattaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Sabbaṃ sabbato sañjānāti; sabbaṃ sabbato saññatvā sabbaṃ maññati, sabbasmiṃ maññati, sabbato maññati, sabbaṃ meti maññati, sabbaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Nibbānaṃ nibbānato sañjānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato saññatvā nibbānaṃ maññati, nibbānasmiṃ maññati , nibbānato maññati, nibbānaṃ meti maññati, nibbānaṃ abhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Apariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

Puthujjanavasena paṭhamanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.
mula_english:
6. “He perceives unity (*ekattaṃ*) as unity. Having perceived unity as unity, he conceives himself as unity, he conceives himself in unity, he conceives himself apart from unity, he conceives unity to be ‘mine’, he delights in unity. What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.

“He perceives diversity (*nānattaṃ*) as diversity. Having perceived diversity as diversity, he conceives himself as diversity, he conceives himself in diversity, he conceives himself apart from diversity, he conceives diversity to be ‘mine’, he delights in diversity. What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.

“He perceives all (*sabbaṃ*) as all. Having perceived all as all, he conceives himself as all, he conceives himself in all, he conceives himself apart from all, he conceives all to be ‘mine,’ he delights in all. What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.

“He perceives *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*) as *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*). Having perceived *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*) as *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*), he conceives himself as *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*), he conceives himself in *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*), he conceives himself apart from *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*), he conceives *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*) to be ‘mine,’ he delights in *Nibbana* (*nirvāṇaṃ*). What is the reason? Because it has not been fully understood by him, I declare.

The first section on the level of the ordinary person is completed.
commentary_pali:
6. Evaṃ sabbaṃ sakkāyabhedaṃ diṭṭhādīhi catūhi dassetvā idāni tameva samāpannakavārena ca asamāpannakavārena ca dvidhā dassento ekattaṃ nānattantiādimāha.

Ekattanti iminā hi samāpannakavāraṃ dasseti. Nānattanti iminā asamāpannakavāraṃ. Tesaṃ ayaṃ vacanattho ekabhāvo ekattaṃ. Nānābhāvo nānattanti. Yojanā panettha samāpannakavāraṃ catūhi khandhehi, asamāpannakavārañca pañcahi khandhehi bhinditvā ‘‘rūpaṃ attato samanupassatī’’tiādinā sāsananayena pathavīvārādīsu vuttena ca aṭṭhakathānayena yathānurūpaṃ vīmaṃsitvā veditabbā. Keci pana ekattanti ekattanayaṃ vadanti nānattanti nānattanayaṃ. Apare ‘‘ekattasaññī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā, nānattasaññī attā hotī’’ti evaṃ diṭṭhābhinivesaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ idha nādhippetattā ayuttameva hoti.

Ekatta Nānatta ekattaṃ. nānatta

Evaṃ sabbaṃ sakkāyaṃ dvidhā dassetvā idāni tameva ekadhā sampiṇḍetvā dassento sabbaṃ sabbatotiādimāha. Yojanānayo panettha sabbaṃ assādento sabbaṃ taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. ‘‘Mayā ete sattā nimmitā’’tiādinā nayena attanā nimmitaṃ maññanto sabbaṃ mānamaññanāya maññati. ‘‘Sabbaṃ pubbekatakammahetu, sabbaṃ issaranimmānahetu, sabbaṃ ahetuapaccayā, sabbaṃ atthi, sabbaṃ natthī’’tiādinā nayena maññanto sabbaṃ diṭṭhimaññanāya maññatīti veditabbo. Kathaṃ sabbasmiṃ maññati? Idhekacco evaṃdiṭṭhiko hoti ‘‘mahā me attā’’ti. So sabbalokasannivāsaṃ tassokāsabhāvena parikappetvā so kho pana me ayaṃ attā sabbasminti maññati, ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiṃyeva panassa attani sinehaṃ tabbatthukañca mānaṃ uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. Sesaṃ pathavīvāre vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

sabbaṃ sabbato

Evaṃ sabbaṃ sakkāyaṃ ekadhā dassetvā idāni aparenapi nayena taṃ ekadhā dassento nibbānaṃ nibbānatoti āha. Tattha nibbānanti ‘‘yato kho, bho, ayaṃ attā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgibhūto paricāreti. Ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ patto hotī’’tiādinā nayena pañcadhā āgataṃ paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tattha nibbānaṃ assādento taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. Tena nibbānena ‘‘ahamasmi nibbānaṃ patto’’ti mānaṃ janento mānamaññanāya maññati. Anibbānaṃyeva samānaṃ taṃ nibbānato niccādito ca gaṇhanto diṭṭhimaññanāya maññatīti veditabbo.

nibbānaṃ nibbānato nibbāna

Nibbānato pana aññaṃ attānaṃ gahetvā so kho pana me ayaṃ attā imasmiṃ nibbāneti maññanto nibbānasmiṃ maññati, ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiṃyeva panassa attani sinehaṃ tabbatthukañca mānaṃ uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. Esa nayo nibbānato maññanāyapi. Tatrapi hi nibbānato aññaṃ attānaṃ gahetvā ‘‘idaṃ nibbānaṃ, ayaṃ attā, so kho pana me ayaṃ attā ito nibbānato añño’’ti maññanto nibbānato maññati, ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiṃyeva panassa attani sinehaṃ tabbatthukañca mānaṃ uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. ‘‘Aho sukhaṃ mama nibbāna’’nti maññanto pana nibbānaṃ meti maññatīti veditabbo. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Ayaṃ panettha anugīti –

Yādiso esa sakkāyo, tathā naṃ avijānato;

Puthujjanassa sakkāye, jāyanti sabbamaññanā.

Jeguccho bhiduro cāyaṃ, dukkho apariṇāyako;

Taṃ paccanīkato bālo, gaṇhaṃ gaṇhāti maññanaṃ.

Subhato sukhato ceva, sakkāyaṃ anupassato;

Salabhasseva aggimhi, hoti taṇhāya maññanā.

Niccasaññaṃ adhiṭṭhāya, sampattiṃ tassa passato;

Gūthādī viya gūthasmiṃ, hoti mānena maññanā.

Attā attaniyo meti, passato naṃ abuddhino;

Ādāse viya bondhissa, diṭṭhiyā hoti maññanā.

Maññanāti ca nāmetaṃ, sukhumaṃ mārabandhanaṃ;

Sithilaṃ duppamuñcañca, yena baddho puthujjano.

Bahuṃ vipphandamānopi, sakkāyaṃ nātivattati;

Samussitaṃ daḷhatthambhaṃ, sāva gaddulabandhano.

Sa’so sakkāyamalīno, jātiyā ca jarāya ca;

Rogādīhi ca dukkhehi, niccaṃ haññati bāḷhaso.

Taṃ vo vadāmi bhaddante, sakkāyaṃ anupassatha;

Asātato asubhato, bhedato ca anattato.

Eso sabhāvo hetassa, passaṃ evamimaṃ budho;

Pahāya maññanā sabbā, sabbadukkhā pamuccatīti.

Ekattavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Puthujjanavasena catuvīsatipabbā paṭhamanayakathā niṭṭhitā.

Sekkhavāradutiyanayavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
6. Thus, having shown all the break-up of self-identity view (*sakkāya*) with the four, views etc., now, showing that same thing in two ways, by way of the attainer and by way of the non-attainer, he says, beginning with "*ekattaṃ nānattaṃ*."

*Ekattaṃ* indicates the case of the attainer. *Nānattaṃ* indicates the case of the non-attainer. The word meaning of these is: *ekattaṃ* = oneness; *nānattaṃ* = diversity. Here, the interpretation is to be understood by differentiating the case of the attainer by the four aggregates, and the case of the non-attainer by the five aggregates. [This is to be done] by the method of the Dispensation (*sāsana*), beginning with "He regards material form as the self (*rūpaṃ attato samanupassatī*)," and by the commentarial method given in the section on earth etc., having determined by investigation which is appropriate.

But some say that *ekattaṃ* indicates the method of unity (*ekattanayaṃ*) and *nānattaṃ* the method of diversity (*nānattanayaṃ*). Others say that the adherence to the views “the self is immutable (*attā*) after death and percipient of unity / percipient of diversity” is meant. Neither of these is correct for they aren’t intended here.

*ekattaṃ nānattaṃ ekattaṃ nānattaṃ*

Thus, having shown all self-identity in two ways, now, showing that same thing by combining it into one, he says, beginning with "*sabbaṃ sabbato*."

Here, the method of interpretation is: - Relishing all, he conceives all through the conceiving of craving (*taṇhā*). Conceiving all as created by himself, thus: “These beings have been created by me,” he conceives all with the conceiving of conceit (*māna*). “All is caused by past *kamma*, ” “All is created by God,” “All is without cause, without condition, ” “All exists, ” “All does not exist,” etc. -in these ways he conceives all through the conceiving of views (*diṭṭhi*).

How does he conceive in all? Here someone is of such a view “my self (*attā*) is great.” Imagining all the world to be the container for the self, he conceives: “This self of mine is in all”. This is his conceiving of views (*diṭṭhi*). The affection he arouses for this self and the conceit based on it are his conceivings of craving and of conceit, respectively. The remainder should be understood by the method stated in the section on earth.

*sabbaṃ sabbato*

Thus, having shown all self-identity in one way, now, showing that one again by another method, he says "*nibbānaṃ nibbānato*."

There, *nibbānaṃ* should be understood as the five kinds of "supreme *dṛṣṭadharma-nirvāṇa* " which have come down in the passage beginning with “From the time, indeed, venerable sir, that this self, endowed with and possessed of the five strands of sensual pleasure, moves about; then it has attained to supreme *dṛṣṭadharma-nirvāṇa* here and now.” There, relishing this *nirvāṇa*, he conceives it with the conceiving of craving. The conceit he arouses because of this *nirvāṇa* when he thinks “I have attained *nirvāṇa*"-this is the way he conceives *nirvāṇa*, through the conceiving of conceit. Holding that which is in reality not *nirvāṇa* to be *nirvāṇa* and to be permanent, etc., he conceives *nirvāṇa* through the conceiving of views.

*nibbānaṃ nibbānato nibbāna*

Taking his self to be other than *nirvāṇa*, conceiving “This is *nirvāṇa*, this the self. This self of mine is in *nirvāṇa* “-he conceives himself “in *nirvāṇa*”. This is his conceiving of views. The affection he arouses for this self and the conceit based on it are his conceivings of craving and of conceit, respectively. This is the method he conceives himself apart "from *nirvāṇa*": taking his self to be other than *nirvāṇa*: conceiving “This is *nirvāṇa*, this the self. This self of mine comes from *nirvāṇa*, it is other than *nirvāṇa* “-he conceives himself apart “from *nirvāṇa*.” This is his conceiving of views. His conceivings of craving and conceit are the affection he arouses for this self and the conceit based upon it, respectively. He conceives “*nirvāṇa* is mine” thus: “O, how blissful is my *nirvāṇa*!” The rest is as already stated.
This is the song herein:

For one who does not understand it thus, this *sakkāya*;

For the *puthujjana* in *sakkāya*, all conceits arise.

Repulsive, fragile, painful, bringing no satisfaction;

The fool opposed to that, grasps at conceit.

Seeing attractiveness and pleasure in *sakkāya*;

Conceit arises from craving, like a moth in the fire.

Fixing on the perception of permanence, seeing the attainment of that;

Conceit arises from pride, like in filth and the like.

"I am, mine am I," thus seeing, for one without wisdom;

Conceit arises from views, like an image in a mirror.

"Conceit": this is a name for a subtle bond of Māra;

Loose, hard to release, by which the *puthujjana* is bound.

Though struggling greatly, he does not overcome *sakkāya*;

Loosened is the strong pillar, bound by a *gaddula*.

He is attached to *sakkāya*, by birth and by old age;

By diseases and sufferings, he is constantly struck severely.

That I tell you, good sirs: contemplate *sakkāya*;

As unsatisfying, as unattractive, as breakable, and as not-self.

This is the nature of its cause, the wise one seeing thus;

Abandoning all conceits, he is freed from all suffering.

The description beginning with the section on unity is finished.

The first method-talk in the twenty-fourth section, based on *puthujjana*, is finished.

Description of the second method in the section on the learner.

mula_pali:
7. ‘‘Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekkho sekho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) appattamānaso anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamāno viharati, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya abhiññatvā (ka.) pathaviṃ mā maññi vā maññati, pathaviyā mā maññi, pathavito mā maññi, pathaviṃ meti mā maññi, pathaviṃ mābhinandi vā abhinandati (sī.) ṭīkā oloketabbā. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññeyyaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ mā maññi, nibbānasmiṃ mā maññi, nibbānato mā maññi, nibbānaṃ meti mā maññi, nibbānaṃ mābhinandi. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññeyyaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

Sekkhavasena satthāravasena (sī.), satthuvasena (syā. ka.) dutiyanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.

satthāravasena (sī.), satthuvasena (syā. ka.)
mula_english:
7. “Therefore, O monks, a trainee (śaikṣa), whose mind has not attained the ultimate security from bondage, also directly knows earth as earth; having directly known earth as earth, he should not conceive himself as earth, he should not conceive himself in earth, he should not conceive himself apart from earth, he should not conceive earth to be ‘mine’, he should not delight in earth. Why is that? I say, ‘Because it is to be fully understood.’

“He directly knows water as water… fire… air… beings… gods (deva)… Prajāpati… Brahmā… Ābhāsvara… Śubhakṛtsna… Bṛhatphala… Abhibhū… the dimension of infinite space (ākāśānantyāyatana)… the dimension of infinite consciousness (vijñānānantyāyatana)… the dimension of nothingness (ākiṃcanyāyatana)… the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception (naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana)… the seen… the heard… the sensed… the cognized… unity… diversity… all… Nibbāna as Nibbāna. Having directly known Nibbāna as Nibbāna, he should not conceive himself as Nibbāna, he should not conceive himself in Nibbāna, he should not conceive himself apart from Nibbāna, he should not conceive Nibbāna to be ‘mine’, he should not delight in Nibbāna. Why is that? I say, ‘Because it is to be fully understood.’

The Second Section, [Describing] the Level [of Practice] in Terms of a Trainee, is Concluded.
commentary_pali:
7. Evaṃ bhagavā pathavīādīsu vatthūsu sabbasakkāyadhammamūlabhūtaṃ puthujjanassa pavattiṃ dassetvā idāni tesveva vatthūsu sekkhassa pavattiṃ dassento yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekkhotiādimāha. Tattha yoti uddesavacanaṃ. Soti niddesavacanaṃ. Pikāro sampiṇḍanattho ayampi dhammo aniyatotiādīsu viya. Tena ca ārammaṇasabhāgena puggalaṃ sampiṇḍeti, no puggalasabhāgena, heṭṭhato hi puggalā diṭṭhivipannā, idha diṭṭhisampannā, na tesaṃ sabhāgatā atthi. Ārammaṇaṃ pana heṭṭhā puggalānampi tadeva, imesampi tadevāti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘ārammaṇasabhāgena puggalaṃ sampiṇḍeti no puggalasabhāgenā’’ti. Yopi soti iminā pana sakalena vacanena idāni vattabbaṃ sekkhaṃ dassetīti veditabbo. Bhikkhave, bhikkhūti idaṃ vuttanayameva.

Sekkhoti kenaṭṭhena sekkho? Sekkhadhammappaṭilābhato sekkho. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sekkho hotīti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekkhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti…pe… sekkhena sammāsamādhinā samannāgato hoti. Ettāvatā kho bhikkhu, sekkho hotī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.13). Apica sikkhatītipi sekkho. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘sikkhatīti kho bhikkhu tasmā sekkhoti vuccati. Kiñca sikkhati? Adhisīlampi sikkhati, adhicittampi sikkhati, adhipaññampi sikkhati, sikkhatīti kho bhikkhu tasmā sekkhoti vuccatī’’ti (a. ni. 3.86).

Sekkho sekkho.

Yopi kalyāṇaputhujjano anulomapaṭipadāya paripūrakārī sīlasampanno indriyesu guttadvāro bhojane mattaññū jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto pubbarattāpararattaṃ bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto viharati – ‘‘ajja vā sve vā aññataraṃ sāmaññaphalaṃ adhigamissāmī’’ti, sopi vuccati sikkhatīti sekkhoti. Imasmiṃ panatthe paṭivedhappattova sekkho adhippeto, no puthujjano.

Appattaṃ mānasaṃ etenāti appattamānaso. Mānasanti rāgopi cittampi arahattampi. ‘‘Antalikkhacaro pāso, yvāyaṃ carati mānaso’’ti (mahāva. 33; saṃ. ni. 1.151) ettha hi rāgo mānasaṃ. ‘‘Cittaṃ mano mānasa’’nti (dha. sa. 65) ettha cittaṃ. ‘‘Appattamānaso sekkho, kālaṃ kayirā janesutā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.159) ettha arahattaṃ. Idhāpi arahattameva adhippetaṃ. Tena appattārahattoti vuttaṃ hoti.

appattamānaso. Mānasa

Anuttaranti seṭṭhaṃ, asadisanti attho. Catūhi yogehi khemaṃ ananuyuttanti yogakkhemaṃ, arahattameva adhippetaṃ. Patthayamānoti dve patthanā taṇhāpatthanā ca, chandapatthanā ca. ‘‘Patthayamānassa hi pajappitāni, pavedhitaṃ vāpi pakappitesū’’ti (su. ni. 908) ettha taṇhāpatthanā.

Anuttara yogakkhemaṃ, Patthayamāno

‘‘Chinnaṃ pāpimato sotaṃ, viddhastaṃ vinaḷīkataṃ;

Pāmojjabahulā hotha, khemaṃ pattattha bhikkhavo’’ti. (ma. ni. 1.352) –

Ettha kattukamyatā kusalacchandapatthanā. Ayameva idhādhippetā. Tena patthayamānoti taṃ yogakkhemaṃ pattukāmo adhigantukāmo tanninno tappoṇo tappabbhāroti veditabbo. Viharatīti aññaṃ iriyāpathadukkhaṃ aññena iriyāpathena vicchinditvā aparipatantaṃ kāyaṃ harati. Atha vā ‘‘sabbe saṅkhārā aniccāti adhimuccanto saddhāya viharatī’’tiādināpi niddesanayenettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānātīti pathaviṃ pathavībhāvena abhijānāti, na puthujjano viya sabbākāraviparītāya saññāya sañjānāti. Apica kho abhivisiṭṭhena ñāṇena jānāti, evaṃ pathavīti etaṃ pathavībhāvaṃ adhimuccanto eva naṃ aniccātipi dukkhātipi anattātipi evaṃ abhijānātīti vuttaṃ hoti. Evañca naṃ abhiññatvā pathaviṃ mā maññīti vuttaṃ hoti. Maññatīti maññi. Ayaṃ pana maññī ca na maññī ca na vattabboti. Etasmiñhi atthe idaṃ padaṃ nipātetvā vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Ko panettha adhippāyoti. Vuccate, puthujjano tāva sabbamaññanānaṃ appahīnattā maññatīti vutto. Khīṇāsavo pahīnattā na maññatīti. Sekkhassa pana diṭṭhimaññanā pahīnā, itarā pana tanubhāvaṃ gatā, tena so maññatītipi na vattabbo puthujjano viya, na maññatītipi na vattabbo khīṇāsavo viyāti.

patthayamāno Viharatī Pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānātī maññi.

Pariññeyyaṃ tassāti tassa sekkhassa taṃ maññanāvatthu okkantaniyāmattā sambodhiparāyaṇattā ca tīhi pariññāhi pariññeyyaṃ, apariññeyyañca apariññātañca na hoti puthujjanassa viya, nopi pariññātaṃ khīṇāsavassa viya. Sesaṃ sabbattha vuttanayameva.

Pariññeyyaṃ tassā

Sekkhavasena dutiyanayakathā niṭṭhitā.

Khīṇāsavavāratatiyādinayavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
7. Thus, the Blessed One, having shown the cognitive process of the worldling ( *pṛthagjana*) in regard to the bases such as earth (*pṛthavī*), etc., which process becomes the root of all the *dharmas* included in personality, now, with the words “A *bhikkhu* who is a learner ( *śaikṣa*),” he undertakes to show the cognitive process of the learner 1 as it occurs in regard to these same bases.

There, "*yo*" is a word of designation.

"*So*" is a word of specification.

The particle "*pi*" is in the sense of combination, as in "*ayam pi dharmo aniyatotiādi*" [this *dharma* is also unfixed, and so on].

And through that aspect of the object, it combines the person, not through the aspect of the person; for below, the persons are deprived of (correct) view (*dṛṣṭi*), here they are endowed with (correct) view, there is no shared state of those.

But the object is the same for the persons below as it is for these.

Therefore it was said, “It combines the person through the aspect of the object, not through the aspect of the person.”

But by this entire statement "*yopi so*," it should be understood that it now shows the learner (*śaikṣa*) who is to be spoken of.

"*Bhikkhave, bhikkhū*" is in the same manner as stated before.

learner (*śaikṣa*) - In what sense is he a learner (*śaikṣa*)? Because of obtaining the qualities of a learner (*śaikṣa-dharma*), he is a learner (*śaikṣa*). For it was said, “To what extent, venerable sir, is one a learner (*śaikṣa*)? Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is endowed with learner correct view (*śaikṣāya samyagdṛṣṭyā*) …pe… is endowed with learner correct concentration (*śaikṣeṇa samyak samādhinā*). To this extent, *bhikkhus*, one is a learner (*śaikṣa*)” (Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.13). Moreover, “he learns, therefore he is a learner (*śaikṣa*)”. For it was said: “He learns, *bhikkhu*, thus he is called a learner (*śaikṣa*). And what does he learn? He learns higher virtue (*adhiśīla*), he learns higher consciousness (*adhicitta*), and he learns higher wisdom (*adhiprajña*). He learns, *bhikkhu*, thus he is called a learner (*śaikṣa*)” (Anguttara Nikāya 3.86).

learner (*śaikṣa*).

learner (*śaikṣa*).

The noble-minded worldling ( *kalyāṇa-pṛthagjana*) who fulfils the practice in conformity, who is endowed with virtue (*śīla*), restrained over the doors of the senses (*indriya*), moderate in eating, who applies himself to wakefulness and is devoted to the development of the constituents of enlightenment (*bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dharmānaṃ*) in the first and last watches of the night, thinking: “Today or tomorrow I will achieve one of the fruits of recluseship (*sāmaññaphalaṃ*)” - he too is called a learner (*śaikṣa*) because he learns.

But in this place only the learner (*śaikṣa*) who has attained to penetration is meant, not even the noble-minded worldling (*pṛthagjana*).

Because the mind is not reached by this, (it is called) *appattamānaso*. *Mānasa* means lust (*rāga*), mind (*citta*), and *arhatship* (*arahatva*). “The noose wanders in the sky, this *mānasa* wanders” (Mahāvagga 33; Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.151). Here *rāga* is *mānasa*. “*Cittaṃ mano mānasaṃ*" (Dhammasaṅgaṇī 65) here *cittaṃ*.
“A learner who has not attained his heart’s ideal, when he dies, O people, hear!”-here, arahatship.

In the present case arahatship is intended.

Thus the meaning is “who has not attained arahatship.”

One who has not attained his heart’s ideal.

Unsurpassed means excellent, asadisa means meaning.

Freedom from attachment to the four yokes is called *yogakkhema*; here, arahatship is intended.

*Patthayamāno* means two kinds of yearning: craving-yearning (*taṇhāpatthanā*) and aspiration-yearning (*chandapatthanā*).

"For one who is yearning there are inclinations, or he may be agitated in his imaginings"-here, craving-yearning is meant.

Unsurpassed, *yogakkhema*, *patthayamāno*

“Cut off is the stream of evil, it is scattered, made reedless;

abounding in joy, be happy, you have attained safety, monks!”

Here, yearning as desire to do the wholesome (*kusalacchandapatthanā*) is meant.

Here is intended.

Therefore, *patthayamāno* means that he should be understood as one who wants to obtain that *yogakkhema*, who wants to reach it, who is devoted to it, inclined towards it, and leaning on it.

*Viharatī* means that he removes one kind of suffering inherent in deportment by means of another kind of deportment, and maintains the body without collapsing.

Or alternatively, the meaning here should be understood in accordance with the method of exposition beginning " because he resolves upon all conditioned phenomena as impermanent, he dwells in faith."

*Pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti* means he knows the earth in accordance with its real nature; he does not perceive it with a perception that is the opposite of all its characteristics, as a worldling does.

Further, he knows it with distinguished knowledge . What is meant is that, resolving upon the earth in accordance with its real nature, he knows it as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.

And thus, having directly known it, he does not conceive the earth as ‘mine’.

*Maññati* means conceiving.

He cannot be described either as one who conceives or as one who does not conceive.

In this connection, it should be understood that this term is put down by way of exception.

What is the purport?

Because he has not abandoned any of the conceivings, the worldling is described as one who conceives.

The *arahat*, who has abandoned them all, is described as one who does not conceive.

The learner has abandoned the conceiving of views, and has diminished the others. Therefore he cannot be described as one who conceives, like the worldling, nor can he be described as one who does not conceive, like the *arahat*.

*Patthayamāno*, *viharatī*, *pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti*, conceiving.

That which is to be fully understood *tassā* means that object of conceiving on the part of that learner is to be fully understood by means of three kinds of full understanding, since it has entered the fixed order [of things] and is destined for perfect enlightenment; and [it is] not to be fully understood, and not fully understood.
It is not like that of an ordinary person, nor is it fully known like that of one whose defilements are destroyed. The rest is as already stated everywhere.

The second method of exposition according to the *sekha* is finished.

Explanation of the third and subsequent methods, beginning with the one about the destruction of defilements.

mula_pali:
8. ‘‘Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ… diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Pariññātaṃ tassā’ti vadāmi.

Khīṇāsavavasena tatiyanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, a *bhikkhu* who is an *arhat*, one whose taints are destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done (*katakaraṇīya*), laid down the burden, reached the true goal (*anuppattasadattha*), destroyed the fetters of being (*parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojana*), and is completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammadaññā vimutto*), directly knows earth (*pathavī*) as earth (*pathavī*). Having directly known earth (*pathavī*) as earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive himself as earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive himself in earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive himself apart from earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive earth (*pathavī*) to be ‘mine’, he does not delight in earth (*pathavī*).

Why is this? I say, ‘Because he has fully understood it (*pariññātaṃ*)’."

“He directly knows water (*āpa*), fire (*teja*), air (*vāya*), beings (*bhūte*), gods (*deve*),  Prajāpati (*pajāpatiṃ*), Brahma (*brahmaṃ*), Ābhassara (*ābhassare*), Subhakiṇha (*subhakiṇhe*), Vehapphala (*vehapphale*), Abhibhu (*abhibhuṃ*), the base of boundless space (*ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ*), the base of boundless consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ*), the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ*), the base of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ*), the seen (*diṭṭhaṃ*), the heard (*sutaṃ*), the sensed (*mutaṃ*), the cognized (*viññātaṃ*), oneness (*ekattaṃ*), diversity (*nānattaṃ*), all (*sabbaṃ*), and *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*) as *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*). Having directly known *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*) as *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*), he does not conceive himself as *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*), he does not conceive himself in *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*), he does not conceive himself apart from *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*), he does not conceive *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*) to be ‘mine’, he does not delight in *nirvana* (*nibbānaṃ*).

Why is this? I say, ‘Because he has fully understood it (*pariññātaṃ*)’."

The analysis of the third way of proceeding, through the destruction of the taints (*khīṇāsavavasena*), is complete.
commentary_pali:
8. Evaṃ pathavīādīsu vatthūsu sekkhassa pavattiṃ dassetvā idāni khīṇāsavassa pavattiṃ dassento yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahantiādimāha. Tattha yopīti pi-saddo sampiṇḍanattho. Tena idha ubhayasabhāgatāpi labbhatīti dasseti. Sekkho hi khīṇāsavena ariyapuggalattā sabhāgo, tena puggalasabhāgatā labbhati, ārammaṇasabhāgatā pana vuttanayā eva. Arahanti ārakakileso, dūrakileso pahīnakilesoti attho. Vuttañcetaṃ bhagavatā ‘‘kathañca , bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ hoti? Ārakāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ hotī’’ti. (Ma. ni. 1.434) khīṇāsavoti cattāro āsavā kāmāsavo…pe… avijjāsavo, ime cattāro āsavā arahato khīṇā pahīnā samucchinnā paṭippassaddhā, abhabbuppattikā ñāṇagginā daḍḍhā, tena vuccati khīṇāsavoti.

Vusitavāti garusaṃvāsepi ariyamaggasaṃvāsepi dasasu ariyavāsesupi vasi parivasi vuttho parivuttho, so vutthavāso ciṇṇacaraṇoti vusitavā katakaraṇīyoti puthujjanakalyāṇakaṃ upādāya satta sekkhā catūhi maggehi karaṇīyaṃ karonti nāma, khīṇāsavassa sabbakaraṇīyāni katāni pariyositāni, natthi tassa uttari karaṇīyaṃ dukkhakkhayādhigamāyāti katakaraṇīyo. Vuttampi hetaṃ –

Vusitavā vusitavā katakaraṇīyo

‘‘Tassa sammā vimuttassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno;

Katassa paṭicayo natthi, karaṇīyaṃ na vijjatī’’ti. (theragā. 642);

Ohitabhāroti tayo bhārā khandhabhāro kilesabhāro abhisaṅkhārabhāroti, tassime tayo bhārā ohitā oropitā nikkhittā pātitā, tena vuccati ohitabhāroti. Anuppattasadatthoti anuppatto sadatthaṃ, sakatthanti vuttaṃ hoti. Kakārassāyaṃ dakāro kato, sadatthoti ca arahattaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tañhi attupanibandhanaṭṭhena attānaṃ avijahanaṭṭhena attano paramatthaṭṭhena ca attano attho sakatthoti vuccati.

Ohitabhāro ohitabhāro Anuppattasadattho

Parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanoti bhavasaṃyojanānīti dasa saṃyojanāni kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ paṭighamānadiṭṭhivicikicchāsīlabbataparāmāsabhavarāgaissāmacchariyasaṃyojanaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ. Imāni hi satte bhavesu saṃyojenti upanibandhanti, bhavaṃ vā bhavena saṃyojenti, tasmā ‘‘bhavasaṃyojanānī’’ti vuccanti. Imāni bhavasaṃyojanāni arahato parikkhīṇāni pahīnāni ñāṇagginā daḍḍhāni, tena vuccati ‘‘parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano’’ti. Sammadaññā vimuttoti ettha sammadaññāti sammā aññāya. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti – khandhānaṃ khandhaṭṭhaṃ, āyatanānaṃ āyatanaṭṭhaṃ, dhātūnaṃ dhātuṭṭhaṃ, dukkhassa pīḷanaṭṭhaṃ, samudayassa pabhavaṭṭhaṃ, nirodhassa santaṭṭhaṃ, maggassa dassanaṭṭhaṃ, sabbe saṅkhārā aniccāti evamādiṃ vā bhedaṃ sammā yathābhūtaṃ aññāya jānitvā tīrayitvā tulayitvā vibhāvetvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti.

Parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano bhavasaṃyojanānī Sammadaññā vimutto sammadaññā

Vimuttoti dve vimuttiyo cittassa ca vimutti nibbānañca. Arahā sabbakilesehi vimuttacittattā cittavimuttiyāpi vimutto. Nibbānaṃ adhimuttattā nibbānepi vimutto. Tena vuccati ‘‘sammadaññā vimutto’’ti. Pariññātaṃ tassāti tassa arahato taṃ maññanāvatthu tīhi pariññāhi pariññātaṃ. Tasmā so taṃ vatthuṃ na maññati, taṃ vā maññanaṃ na maññatīti vuttaṃ hoti, sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

Vimutto Pariññātaṃ tassā

Nibbānavāre pana khayā rāgassātiādayo tayo vārā vuttā. Te pathavīvārādīsupi vitthāretabbā. Ayañca pariññātavāro nibbānavārepi vitthāretabbo. Vitthārentena ca pariññātaṃ tassāti sabbapadehi yojetvā puna khayā rāgassa vītarāgattāti yojetabbaṃ. Esa nayo itaresu. Desanā pana ekattha vuttaṃ sabbattha vuttameva hotīti saṃkhittā.

khayā rāgassā

Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattāti ettha ca yasmā bāhirako kāmesu vītarāgo, na khayā rāgassa vītarāgo. Arahā pana khayā yeva, tasmā vuttaṃ ‘‘khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā’’ti. Esa nayo dosamohesupi. Yathā ca ‘‘pariññātaṃ tassāti vadāmī’’ti vuttepi pariññātattā so taṃ vatthuṃ taṃ vā maññanaṃ na maññatīti attho hoti, evamidhāpi vītarāgattā so taṃ vatthuṃ taṃ vā maññanaṃ na maññatīti daṭṭhabbo.

Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā

Ettha ca pariññātaṃ tassāti ayaṃ vāro maggabhāvanāpāripūridassanatthaṃ vutto. Itare pana phalasacchikiriyāpāripūridassanatthanti veditabbā. Dvīhi vā kāraṇehi arahā na maññati vatthussa ca pariññātattā akusalamūlānañca samucchinnattā. Tenassa pariññātavārena vatthuno vatthupariññaṃ dīpeti, itarehi akusalamūlasamucchedanti. Tattha pacchimesu tīsu vāresu ayaṃ viseso veditabbo, tīsu hi vāresu rāge ādīnavaṃ disvā dukkhānupassī viharanto appaṇihitavimokkhena vimutto khayā rāgassa vītarāgo hoti. Dose ādīnavaṃ disvā aniccānupassī viharanto animittavimokkhena vimutto khayā dosassa vītadoso hoti. Mohe ādīnavaṃ disvā anattānupassī viharanto suññatavimokkhena vimutto khayā mohassa vītamoho hotīti.

Evaṃ sante na eko tīhi vimokkhehi vimuccatīti dve vārā na vattabbā siyunti ce, taṃ na. Kasmā? Aniyamitattā. Aniyamena hi vuttaṃ ‘‘yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araha’’nti. Na pana vuttaṃ appaṇihitavimokkhena vā vimutto, itarena vāti, tasmā yaṃ arahato yujjati, taṃ sabbaṃ vattabbamevāti.

Avisesena vā yo koci arahā samānepi rāgādikkhaye vipariṇāmadukkhassa pariññātattā khayā rāgassa vītarāgoti vuccati, dukkhadukkhassa pariññātattā khayā dosassa vītadosoti. Saṅkhāradukkhassa pariññātattā khayā mohassa vītamohoti. Iṭṭhārammaṇassa vā pariññātattā khayā rāgassa vītarāgo. Aniṭṭhārammaṇassa pariññātattā khayā dosassa vītadoso. Majjhattārammaṇassa pariññātattā khayā mohassa vītamoho. Sukhāya vā vedanāya rāgānusayassa samucchinnattā khayā rāgassa vītarāgo, itarāsu paṭighamohānusayānaṃ samucchinnattā vītadoso vītamoho cāti. Tasmā taṃ visesaṃ dassento āha ‘‘khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā…pe… vītamohattā’’ti.

Khīṇāsavavasena tatiyacatutthapañcamachaṭṭhanayakathā niṭṭhitā.

Tathāgatavārasattamanayavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
8. Thus, having shown the cognitive process of the *sekha* (one under training) in regard to the bases such as earth, etc., with the words “That *bhikkhu*, *arahat*, O *bhikkhus*,” he now undertakes to show the cognitive process of the *khīṇāsava* (one with extinguished cankers). Here, *yopi*—the *pi*-word is in the sense of combination. Thus, he shows that here both shared states are obtained. For the *sekha* shares the state [of purity] with the *khīṇāsava* because of [their both being] noble individuals (*ariyapuggala*); therefore, the shared state of individuals is obtained, but the shared state of objects is just as stated. *Araha*nt—the meaning is: one who is far from defilements, whose defilements are distant, whose defilements are abandoned. And this was said by the Blessed One: “And how, O *bhikkhus*, is a *bhikkhu* an *araha*nt? Evil, unwholesome things that cause defilement, lead to renewed existence, bring distress, and ripen in suffering in the future, bringing birth, aging and death, are far from him. That is how, O *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is an *araha*nt.” (M. N. 1.434) *Khīṇāsava*—the four *āsavas* (cankers) are: the canker of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*)…pe… the canker of ignorance (*avijjāsava*). These four cankers of the *arahat* are extinguished, abandoned, eradicated, silenced, incapable of arising again, burned by the fire of knowledge; therefore, he is called a *khīṇāsava*. *Vusitavā*—he has dwelt, lived around, stayed, completely stayed in the heavy dwelling, in the dwelling of the noble path, and in the ten noble dwellings; therefore, he is one who has dwelt, whose conduct is complete. *Vusitavā katakaraṇīyo*—beginning with the auspicious deeds of ordinary people, the seven *sekhas* do what needs to be done by means of the four paths; for the *khīṇāsava* all that needs to be done has been done, completed; there is nothing further for him to do in order to attain the cessation of suffering; therefore, he has done what needs to be done (*katakaraṇīyo*). And this was said: *Vusitavā vusitavā katakaraṇīyo* “For that *bhikkhu* who is rightly liberated and whose mind is peaceful, there is no accumulation of what has been done, nor does anything remain that he must do.” (Theragā. 642); *Ohitabhāro*—the three burdens are: the burden of the aggregates (*khandhabhāro*), the burden of defilements (*kilesabhāro*), and the burden of volitional activities (*abhisaṅkhārabhāro*). These three burdens of his are laid down, dropped, cast off, let fall; therefore, he is called *ohitabhāro*. *Anuppattasadattho*—he has attained his own goal (*sadatthaṃ*), it is said. This *dakāra* has been made for the *kakāra*. And *sadattho* should be understood as *arahattaṃ* (the state of being an *arhat*). For that is called one’s own goal (*sakattho*), one’s personal goal, in the sense that it is connected with oneself, that it can never be abandoned by oneself, and that it is one’s supreme goal. *Ohitabhāro ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho* *Parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano*—*bhavasaṃyojanānī*—the ten fetters (*saṃyojanāni*) are: the fetter of sensual desire (*kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ*), the fetter of aversion (*paṭighamānasaṃyojanaṃ*), the fetter of views (*diṭṭhi*), the fetter of doubt (*vicikicchā*), the fetter of clinging to rules and rituals (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*), the fetter of desire for existence (*bhava*), the fetter of envy (*issā*), the fetter of avarice (*macchariya*), and the fetter of ignorance (*avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ*). These fetter, connect, beings to the states of existence, or they fetter one existence to the next; therefore, they are called *bhavasaṃyojanānī*. These fetters of existence are eliminated by the *arahat*, abandoned, consumed by the fire of knowledge; therefore he is called one who has *parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano* (eliminated the fetters of existence). *Sammadaññā vimutto*—here, *sammadaññā* means by perfect knowledge. What is meant? Knowing, scrutinizing, investigating, clarifying, and illuminating with knowledge perfectly, as it really is, the aggregates’ meaning of aggregates, the bases’ meaning of bases, the elements’ meaning of elements, suffering’s meaning of oppressing, the origin’s meaning of source, cessation’s meaning of peace, the path’s meaning of seeing, or the division beginning thus: “All formations are impermanent,” etc. *Parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano bhavasaṃyojanānī sammadaññā vimutto sammadaññā* *Vimutto*—there are two liberations (*vimuttiyo*): the liberation of mind (*cittassa vimutti*) and *nibbāna*. Since his mind is emancipated from all defilements, the *arahat* is also emancipated by the emancipation of mind. And since he is resolved upon *nibbāna* he is also emancipated in *nibbāna*. Therefore he is called “emancipated by final knowledge.” *Pariññātaṃ tassā*—that object of conceiving of that *arahat* is fully known by three kinds of full knowledge (*pariññāhi*). Therefore he neither conceives the base nor does he conceive the conceiving. The remainder by the method stated. *Vimutto pariññātaṃ tassā* However, in the section on *nibbāna*, the three sections beginning with *khayā rāgassā* (the destruction of passion) have been stated. Each should be applied to each of the sections dealing with the bases, beginning with earth. And this section on full understanding should also be elaborated upon in the section on *nirvāṇa*. Just as the statement on full understanding should be applied to all terms, so also should the phrase "devoid of lust through the destruction of lust" be applied. So with the rest. Only one condensed statement is given since the meaning is the same in all cases. **Destruction of Lust**

BECAUSE HE IS DEVOID OF LUST THROUGH THE DESTRUCTION OF LUST Those outside who are devoid of lust for sensual pleasures are not “ devoid of lust through the destruction of lust.” But the *arhat* is devoid [of lust] only through destruction; therefore it was said “devoid of lust through the destruction of lust.” This method should also be applied to the cases of hate and delusion. Just as, when it is said “ because it has been fully understood by him,” the meaning is that because it has been fully understood he conceives neither the base nor the conceiving, so here too because he is devoid of lust he conceives neither the base nor the conceiving.

**Destruction of Lust**

In this context, the section on full understanding was stated for the purpose of showing the fulfillment of the path and of cultivation. The others, however, should be understood as being for the purpose of showing the fulfillment of the realization of the fruit. Or else, the *arhat* does not conceive for two reasons: because he has fully understood the base and because he has eradicated the unwholesome roots. Therefore the section on full understanding shows his full understanding of the base, the others his eradication of the unwholesome roots. In the three latter sections, the following distinction should be understood: Having seen the danger in lust, he dwelt in the contemplation of suffering, became emancipated through the deliverance of the wishless , and is devoid of lust through the destruction of lust. Having seen the danger in hate, he dwelt in the contemplation of impermanence, became emancipated through the deliverance of the signless , and is devoid of hate through the destruction of hate. Having seen the danger in delusion, he dwelt in the contemplation of non-self, he became emancipated through the deliverance of emptiness , and is devoid of delusion through the destruction of delusion.

If such is the case, since no one becomes emancipated through three deliverances, shouldn’t two sections be omitted? No. Why is that? Because there is no specification. For it was said “a *bhikkhu* who is an *arhat*” without specification. It was not said that he is emencipated by the wishless deliverance or by either of the other two; therefore all that is appropriate for the *arhat* should be mentioned.

Or else, without distinction, whoever is an *arhat*, by fully understanding the suffering in change (*vipariṇāmadukkha*), becomes devoid of lust through the destruction of lust: by fully understanding the suffering in painful feeling (*duḥkhaduḥkha*), becomes devoid of hate through the destruction of hate; and by fully understanding the suffering in formations (*saṃskāradukkha*), becomes devoid of delusion through the destruction of delusion. Or by fully understanding a desirable object (*iṣṭhārammaṇa*), he becomes devoid of lust through the destruction of lust; by fully understanding an undesirable object (*aniṣṭhārammaṇa*), he becomes devoid of hate through the destruction of hate; and by fully understanding a neutral object (*madhyattārammaṇa*), he becomes devoid of delusion through the destruction of delusion. Or by eradicating the latent tendency to lust (*rāgānusaya*) for a pleasant feeling, he becomes devoid of lust through the destruction of lust; and by eradicating the latent tendencies to aversion (*pratighānusaya*) and delusion (*mohānusaya*) for painful and neutral feelings, respectively, he becomes devoid of hate and devoid of delusion. Therefore, showing these distinctions, the Exalted One says “ devoid of lust, devoid of hate, devoid of delusion”

The discussion of the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth approaches in terms of the destruction of the outflows (*khīṇāsava*) is finished.

Explanation of the Seventh Approach Concerning the Tathāgata

mula_pali:
9. ‘‘Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, sopi pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānāti; pathaviṃ pathavito abhiññāya pathaviṃ na maññati, pathaviyā na maññati, pathavito na maññati, pathaviṃ meti na maññati, pathaviṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā rāgassa, vītarāgattā.

‘‘Āpaṃ…pe… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ… ābhassare… subhakiṇhe… vehapphale… abhibhuṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ … nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ … diṭṭhaṃ… sutaṃ… mutaṃ… viññātaṃ… ekattaṃ… nānattaṃ… sabbaṃ… nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhijānāti; nibbānaṃ nibbānato abhiññāya nibbānaṃ na maññati, nibbānasmiṃ na maññati, nibbānato na maññati, nibbānaṃ meti na maññati, nibbānaṃ nābhinandati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Khayā rāgassa, vītarāgattā.

Khīṇāsavavasena catutthanayabhūmiparicchedo niṭṭhito.
mula_english:
9. “Bhikkhus, a *bhikkhu* who is an *arahant* with taints destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done (*katakaraṇīya*), laid down the burden (*ohitabhāra*), reached the true goal (*anuppattasadattha*), destroyed the fetters of being (*parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojana*), and is completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammadaññā vimutto*), directly knows earth (*pathavī*) as earth (*pathavī*). Having directly known earth (*pathavī*) as earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive himself as earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive himself in earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive himself apart from earth (*pathavī*), he does not conceive earth (*pathavī*) to be ‘mine’, he does not delight in earth (*pathavī*).

Why is that? Because of the destruction of lust (*rāga*), being without lust (*vītarāga*).

“He directly knows water (*āpa*) as water… fire (*teja*)… wind (*vāyu*)… beings (*bhūta*)… gods (*deva*)… Prajāpati… Brahmā… Ābhassara… Subhakiṇha… Vehapphala… Abhibhū… the base of the infinity of space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*)… the base of the infinity of consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*)… the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*)… the base of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*)… what is seen (*diṭṭha* )… what is heard (*sutaṃ*)… what is sensed (*mutaṃ*)… what is cognized (*viññātaṃ*)… oneness (*ekattaṃ*)… diverse (*nānattaṃ*)… everything (*sabbaṃ*)… *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*) as *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*). Having directly known *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*) as *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive himself as *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive himself in *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive himself apart from *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*) to be ‘mine’, he does not delight in *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*).

Why is that? Because of the destruction of lust (*rāga*), being without lust (*vītarāga*).

The fourth section on the ground of the method, by way of the destruction of taints (*khīṇāsava*), is finished.

mula_pali:

mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, a *bhikkhu* who is an *arahant*, one whose taints are destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached the true goal, destroyed the fetters of being, and is completely liberated through final knowledge, directly knows earth as earth. “He directly knows water as water…fire…wind…beings…gods…Prajāpati…Brahmā…Ābhassara…Subhakiṇha…Vehapphala…Abhibhū…the dimension of the infinity of space (*ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ*)…the dimension of the infinity of consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ*)…the dimension of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ*)…the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ*)…the seen…the heard…the sensed…the cognized…oneness…diversity…everything…Nirvana (*nibbāna*) as Nirvana (*nibbāna*)… Having directly known Nirvana (*nibbāna*) as Nirvana (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive himself as Nirvana (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive himself in Nirvana (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive himself apart from Nirvana (*nibbāna*), he does not conceive Nirvana (*nibbāna*) to be ‘mine’, he does not delight in Nirvana (*nibbāna*).

The fifth section on the level of the way due to destruction of taints (*khīṇāsava*) is finished.
