Tatthāyaṃ saṅkhāsaddo ñāṇakoṭṭhāsapaññattigaṇanāsu dissati. ‘‘Saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevatī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.168) hi ñāṇe dissati. ‘‘Papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācarantī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.201) koṭṭhāse. ‘‘Tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ saṅkhā samaññā’’tiādīsu (dha. sa. 1313) paññattiyaṃ. ‘‘Na sukaraṃ saṅkhātu’’ntiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 2.128) gaṇanāyaṃ. Idha pana ñāṇe daṭṭhabbo.

idhā Paṭisaṅkhā

Paṭisaṅkhā yonisoti hi upāyena pathena paṭisaṅkhāya ñatvā paccavekkhitvāti attho. Ettha ca asaṃvare ādīnavapaṭisaṅkhā yoniso paṭisaṅkhāti veditabbā. Sā cāyaṃ ‘‘varaṃ, bhikkhave, tattāya ayosalākāya ādittāya sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya cakkhundriyaṃ sampalimaṭṭhaṃ, na tveva cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu anubyañjanaso nimittaggāho’’tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 4.235) ādittapariyāyanayena veditabbā. Cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharatīti ettha cakkhumeva indriyaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ, saṃvaraṇato saṃvaro, pidahanato thakanatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Satiyā etaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Cakkhundriye saṃvaro cakkhundriyasaṃvaro. Titthakāko āvāṭakacchapo vanamahiṃsotiādayo viya.

Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso Cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharatī

Tattha kiñcāpi cakkhundriye saṃvaro vā asaṃvaro vā natthi. Na hi cakkhupasādaṃ nissāya sati vā muṭṭhasaccaṃ vā uppajjati. Apica yadā rūpārammaṇaṃ cakkhussa āpāthaṃ āgacchati, tadā bhavaṅge dvikkhattuṃ uppajjitvā niruddhe kiriyamanodhātu āvajjanakiccaṃ sādhayamānā uppajjitvā nirujjhati, tato cakkhuviññāṇaṃ dassanakiccaṃ, tato vipākamanodhātu sampaṭicchanakiccaṃ, tato vipākāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu santīraṇakiccaṃ, tato kiriyāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu voṭṭhabbanakiccaṃ sādhayamānā uppajjitvā nirujjhati. Tadanantaraṃ javanaṃ javati.

Tatthapi neva bhavaṅgasamaye, na āvajjanādīnaṃ aññatarasamaye saṃvaro vā asaṃvaro vā atthi. Javanakkhaṇe pana sace dussīlyaṃ vā muṭṭhasaccaṃ vā aññāṇaṃ vā akkhanti vā kosajjaṃ vā uppajjati, ayaṃ asaṃvaro hoti. Evaṃ hontopi so cakkhundriye asaṃvaroti vuccati. Kasmā? Tasmiñhi sati dvārampi aguttaṃ hoti, bhavaṅgampi āvajjanādīni vīthicittānipi. Yathā kiṃ , yathā nagare catūsu dvāresu asaṃvutesu kiñcāpi anto gharakoṭṭhakagabbhādayo susaṃvutā, tathāpi antonagare sabbaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ arakkhitaṃ agopitameva hoti. Nagaradvārena hi pavisitvā corā yadicchanti, taṃ kareyyuṃ, evameva javane dussīlyādīsu uppannesu, tasmiṃ asaṃvare sati dvārampi aguttaṃ hoti, bhavaṅgampi āvajjanādīni vīthicittānipīti.

Tasmiṃ pana sīlādīsu uppannesu dvārampi guttaṃ hoti, bhavaṅgampi āvajjanādīni vīthicittānipi. Yathā kiṃ? Yathā nagaradvāresu susaṃvutesu kiñcāpi anto gharādayo asaṃvutā, tathāpi antonagare sabbaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ surakkhitaṃ sugopitameva hoti. Nagaradvāresu hi pihitesu corānaṃ paveso natthi, evameva javane sīlādīsu uppannesu dvārampi suguttaṃ hoti, bhavaṅgampi āvajjanādīni vīthicittānipi. Tasmā javanakkhaṇe uppajjamānopi cakkhundriye saṃvaroti vutto. Idha cāyaṃ satisaṃvaro adhippetoti veditabbo. Cakkhundriyasaṃvarena saṃvuto cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto, upetoti vuttaṃ hoti. Tathā hi, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvutoti imassa vibhaṅge ‘‘iminā pātimokkhasaṃvarena upeto hoti…pe… samannāgato’’ti (vibha. 511) vuttaṃ. Taṃ ekajjhaṃ katvā cakkhundriyasaṃvarena saṃvutoti evamattho veditabbo.

cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto,

Atha vā saṃvarīti saṃvuto, thakesi pidahīti vuttaṃ hoti. Cakkhundriye saṃvarasaṃvuto cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto, cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaññitaṃ satikavāṭaṃ cakkhudvāre, gharadvāre kavāṭaṃ viya saṃvari thakesi pidahīti vuttaṃ hoti. Ayameva cettha attho sundarataro. Tathā hi ‘‘cakkhundriyasaṃvaraṃ asaṃvutassa viharato saṃvutassa viharato’’ti etesu padesu ayameva attho dissati.

Viharatīti evaṃ cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto yena kenaci iriyāpathavihārena viharati. Yañhissātiādimhi yaṃ cakkhundriyasaṃvaraṃ assa bhikkhuno asaṃvutassa athaketvā apidahitvā viharantassāti evamattho veditabbo. Atha vā, ye-kārassa yanti ādeso. Hikāro ca padapūraṇo, ye assāti attho.

Viharatī Yañhissā ya Hi

Cakkhudvāre hi iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ āpāthagataṃ kāmassādavasena assādayato abhinandato kāmāsavo uppajjati, īdisaṃ aññasmimpi sugatibhave labhissāmīti bhavapatthanāya assādayato bhavāsavo uppajjati, sattoti vā sattassāti vā gaṇhantassa diṭṭhāsavo uppajjati, sabbeheva sahajātaṃ aññāṇaṃ avijjāsavoti cattāro āsavā uppajjanti. commentary_english:
22. Having shown the āsavas (influxes, defilements) that are to be abandoned by seeing, now, in order to show those to be abandoned by restraint which were mentioned immediately after that, he says, "What, monks, are the āsavas to be abandoned by restraint?" Thus, the connection should be understood everywhere. Hereafter, indeed, we will describe only the meaning.

But indeed, with these two—by seeing and by cultivation—there is no āsava that is not to be abandoned. Then why does he separately show those to be abandoned by restraint, etc.? Āsavas, checked in the preliminary stage by restraint, etc., go to destruction by the four paths. Therefore, showing the abandonment by checking in the preliminary stage of those paths by these five ways, he says thus. Therefore, this first path that was spoken of is just the path of seeing, and now the three paths will be spoken of by the name of cultivation; this is to be understood as the preliminary practice for all of them.

There, *idha* (here) means in this Dispensation. *Paṭisaṅkhā* means by reflection. Here, this word *saṅkhā* is seen in knowledge, division, designation and counting. For it is seen in knowledge in "[he] partakes of one after considering," etc. (MN 2.168); in division in "[proliferating perceptions and] categories surge forth," etc. (MN 1.201); in designation in "[the] category, designation of those things," etc. (Dhs. 1313); in counting in "it is not easy to count," etc. (SN 2.128). But here it should be seen in knowledge.

*Idha paṭisaṅkhā paṭisaṅkhā yoniso*: here, *paṭisaṅkhā yoniso* means knowing by reflection, by way, by path, reflecting, that is the meaning. And here, considering the danger in non-restraint is to be understood as reflection by way of origin. And that should be understood by way of the Fire Discourse, which begins thus, "Better, monks, for the eye faculty to be lacerated by a red-hot iron pin burning, blazing, and glowing, than for one to grasp the sign through the features in a form cognizable by the eye" (SN 4.235). *Cakkhundriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati*: here, the eye itself is the faculty, *cakkhundriyaṃ*, restraint is *saṃvaro* because of restraining, it is said to be obstructing, blocking. This is a designation for mindfulness.
Restraint in the eye faculty, restrained by the restraint in the eye faculty, like the crow at a ford, the tortoise in a watering place, the wild buffalo in the forest, and so on.

He dwells restrained with restraint in the eye faculty with wisdom.

Herein, there is neither restraint nor non-restraint in the actual eye faculty.

since neither mindfulness nor forgetfulness arises in dependence on eye-sensitivity.

Moreover, when a form-object comes into the range of the eye, then, when two occurrences of the life-continuum have arisen and ceased, the functional mind-element, accomplishing the function of adverting, arises and ceases; then visual consciousness [accomplishes] the function of seeing, then the resultant mind-element [accomplishes] the function of receiving, then the resultant rootless mind-consciousness element [accomplishes] the function of investigating, then the functional-root mind-consciousness element, accomplishing the function of determining, arises and ceases.

Immediately after that, impulsion occurs.

Herein, there is neither restraint nor non-restraint on the occasion of the life-continuum, or on any of the occasions beginning with adverting.

But there is non-restraint if unvirtuousness or forgetfulness or unknowing or impatience or idleness arises at the moment of impulsion.

When this happens, it is called “non-restraint in the eye faculty.”

Why? Because when this is present, the door too is unguarded, and so also are the life-continuum and the consciousnesses of the cognitive series beginning with adverting.

Like what, for example? Just as, when a city’s four gates are not secured, although inside the city house doors, storehouses, rooms, etc., are secured, yet all property inside the city is unguarded and unprotected.

since robbers coming in by the city gates can do as they please, so too, when unvirtuousness, etc., arise in impulsion in which there is no restraint, then the door too is unguarded, and so also are the life-continuum and the consciousnesses of the cognitive series beginning with adverting.

But when virtue, etc., has arisen in it, then the door too is guarded and so also are the life-continuum and the consciousnesses of the cognitive series beginning with adverting.

Like what? Just as, when the city gates are well secured, although inside the city the houses, etc., are not secured, yet all property inside the city is well guarded, well protected,

since when the city gates are shut there is no ingress for robbers, so too, when virtue, etc., have arisen in impulsion, the door too is guarded and so also are the life-continuum and the consciousnesses of the cognitive series beginning with adverting.

Thus although it actually arises at the moment of impulsion, it is nevertheless called “restraint in the eye faculty.”

Herein, it should be understood, this mindfulness-restraint is intended.

“Restrained with restraint in the eye faculty” means: he is endowed with restraint in the eye faculty.

For example, in the analysis of “restrained with restraint in the *prātimokṣa*,” it is said “he is endowed with this restraint in the *prātimokṣa*. . . and possesses it” (Vin. 511).

Having put that together, it should be understood that the meaning is thus: restrained with restraint in the eye faculty.

Restrained by restraint in the eye faculty,

Or alternatively, *saṃvarīti* [means] *saṃvuto*: he shuts off, he closes, it is said.

*Cakkhundriye saṃvarasaṃvuto* [means] restrained by restraint in the eye faculty: he shuts off, he closes, the mindfulness-door-keeper, known as restraint in the eye faculty, at the eye-door, just as a door-keeper [shuts off, closes] at a house-door, it is said.

This meaning here is more excellent.

For this very meaning appears in such passages as “restraint in the eye faculty for one dwelling unrestrained, dwelling restrained”.

He dwells: thus, restrained with restraint in the eye faculty, he dwells in whatever deportment-dwelling.

In “whatsoever will be his,” etc., it should be understood that the meaning is: whatsoever restraint in the eye faculty there will be for that bhikkhu dwelling unrestrained, not shutting off, not closing.

Or alternatively, the *ye-* is a substitute for *yaṃ*.

And the *hi-* is merely a particle, the meaning is: whatever there will be for him.

May arise.
...*nibbatteyyuṃ*.

**Āsavā vighātapariḷāhā** means the four *āsavas* and other destructive defilements and afflictions that cause suffering as a result.

When a desirable object comes into the range of sight at the eye-door, craving-āsava arises in one who savors and rejoices in it with the taste of sensual pleasure, craving-for-existence *bhavāsava* arises in one who savors it with the desire that "I will obtain such again in another happy existence," view-āsava *diṭṭhāsava* arises in one who grasps "I am" or "This belongs to me," ignorance-āsava *avijjāsavoti* the four *āsavas* arise together with innate ignorance.

Other defilements connected with these are destructive afflictions, or their results in the future.

These too are said to arise in one who lives unrestrained.

**uppajjeyyu**

**Āsavā vighātapariḷāhā** **evaṃsa te** means thus it is for you.

It has been said that it is thus by this means that they do not exist, not otherwise.

This is the method in *paṭisaṅkhā yoniso sotindriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto*, etc.

**evaṃsa te** **paṭisaṅkhā yoniso sotindriyasaṃvarasaṃvuto** **ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā** means these twenty-four *āsavas*, making four each at the six doors, are said to be abandoned by restraint.

Here, everywhere, mindfulness-restraint should be understood as restraint itself.

**ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā**

The description of *āsavas* to be abandoned by restraint is finished.

The description of *āsavas* to be abandoned by use.

mula_pali:
23. ‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cīvaraṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapa- siriṃsapa (sī. syā. pī.) samphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva hirikopīnappaṭicchādanatthaṃ’.

‘‘Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso piṇḍapātaṃ paṭisevati – ‘neva davāya, na madāya, na maṇḍanāya, na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya, vihiṃsūparatiyā, brahmacariyānuggahāya, iti purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro ca’ cāti (sī.).

cāti (sī.)

‘‘Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso senāsanaṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapasamphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva utuparissayavinodanapaṭisallānārāmatthaṃ’.

‘‘Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva uppannānaṃ veyyābādhikānaṃ vedanānaṃ paṭighātāya, abyābajjhaparamatāya’ abyāpajjhaparamatāya (sī. syā. pī.), abyāpajjaparamatāya (ka.).

abyāpajjhaparamatāya (sī. syā. pī.), abyāpajjaparamatāya (ka.)

‘‘Yañhissa, bhikkhave, appaṭisevato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, paṭisevato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā.

Adhivāsanā pahātabbāsavā
mula_english:
"23. "And what, monks, are the effluents to be abandoned by using? Here, monks, a monk, reflecting appropriately, uses robes simply to counteract cold, to counteract heat, to counteract the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; simply for the purpose of covering the private parts."

"Reflecting appropriately, he uses alms food, not playfully, nor for intoxication, nor for putting on bulk, nor for beautification; but simply for the survival & continuance of this body, for ending its afflictions, for the support of the holy life, thinking, 'Thus will I destroy old feelings and not create new feelings. I will maintain myself, be blameless, & live in comfort.'"

"Reflecting appropriately, he uses lodging simply to counteract cold, to counteract heat, to counteract the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, & reptiles; simply for protection from the inclemencies of weather and for the enjoyment of seclusion."

"Reflecting appropriately, he uses medicine and provisions for the sick simply to counteract painful feelings that have arisen, for the sake of utmost freedom from disease."

"The effluents, vexation, or fever that would arise if he were not to use these things do not arise for him when he uses them. These are called the *āsavas* (influxes, cankers, taints, effluents) to be abandoned by using."

Effluents to be Abandoned by Endurance
commentary_pali:
23.Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cīvarantiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ visuddhimagge sīlakathāyaṃ vuttameva. Yañhissāti yaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātādīsu vā aññataraṃ assa. Appaṭisevatoti evaṃ yoniso appaṭisevantassa. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Kevalaṃ panidha aladdhaṃ cīvarādiṃ patthayato laddhaṃ vā assādayato kāmāsavassa uppatti veditabbā. Īdisaṃ aññasmimpi sampattibhave sugatibhave labhissāmīti bhavapatthanāya assādayato bhavāsavassa, ahaṃ labhāmi na labhāmīti vā mayhaṃ vā idanti attasaññaṃ adhiṭṭhahato diṭṭhāsavassa uppatti veditabbā. Sabbeheva pana sahajāto avijjāsavoti evaṃ catunnaṃ āsavānaṃ uppatti vipākapariḷāhā ca navavedanuppādanatopi veditabbā.

Imevuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbāti ime ekamekasmiṃ paccaye cattāro cattāro katvā soḷasa āsavā iminā ñāṇasaṃvarasaṅkhātena paccavekkhaṇapaṭisevanena pahātabbāti vuccanti.

Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā

Paṭisevanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Adhivāsanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
23. In regard to what should be stated in "*paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cīvara*ntiādīsu," all of that has already been stated in the chapter on morality in the *Visuddhimagga*.

"yañhissā" means whatever among robes, alms food, etc., might belong to him.

"*appaṭisevato*ti" means thus, for one who does not wisely make use of.

The rest is as already stated.

However, in this context, it should be understood that the arising of the *kāmāsava* (the influx of sensuality) comes from a person who desires a robe, etc., which he has not obtained, or who savors one that he has obtained.

"I will obtain such good fortune and a good rebirth in another existence" – for one who savors with this desire for becoming, the *bhavāsava* (the influx of becoming); "I obtain, I do not obtain," or "this is mine" – it should be understood that the arising of the *diṭṭhāsava* (the influx of views) comes from one who establishes self-perception.

Moreover, it should be understood that the arising, the ripening, and the burning up of all four *āsavas*, together with the production of new feelings, are all born together with *avijjāsava* (the influx of ignorance).

These, monks, are called *āsavas* that are to be abandoned by using. That is, in each condition, making four by four, these sixteen *āsavas* are to be abandoned by using reviewing, which is designated as restraint by knowledge.

These, monks, are called *āsavas* that are to be abandoned by using.

The explanation of the *āsavas* to be abandoned by using is finished.

The explanation of the *āsavas* to be abandoned by enduring.

mula_pali:
24. ‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa, jighacchāya pipāsāya. Ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapasamphassānaṃ, duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ, uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ tippānaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.

‘‘Yañhissa, bhikkhave, anadhivāsayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, adhivāsayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā.

Parivajjanā pahātabbāsavā
mula_english:
“And which, monks, are the effluents to be abandoned by tolerating? Here, monks, a bhikkhu, reflecting wisely, is tolerant of cold and heat, hunger and thirst, the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; of unwelcome, ill-spoken words; and of arisen bodily feelings that are painful, racking, sharp, piercing, disagreeable, displeasing, and menacing to life.

The corruptions, vexation, and fever that would arise if he were not to tolerate these things do not arise for him when he tolerates them. These are called the corruptions to be abandoned by tolerating.”

Effluents to be abandoned by avoiding.
commentary_pali:
24.Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso khamo hoti sītassāti upāyena pathena paccavekkhitvā khamo hoti sītassa sītaṃ khamati sahati, na avīrapuriso viya appamattakenapi sītena calati kampati kammaṭṭhānaṃ vijahati. Apica kho lomasanāgatthero viya anappakenāpi sītena phuṭṭho na calati na kampati, kammaṭṭhānameva manasi karoti. Thero kira cetiyapabbate piyaṅguguhāyaṃ padhānaghare viharanto antaraṭṭhake himapātasamaye lokantarikaniraye paccavekkhitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ avijahantova abbhokāse vītināmesi. Evaṃ uṇhādīsupi atthayojanā veditabbā.

Kevalañhi yo bhikkhu adhimattampi uṇhaṃ sahati sveva thero viya, ayaṃ ‘‘khamo uṇhassā’’ti veditabbo. Thero kira gimhasamaye pacchābhattaṃ bahicaṅkame nisīdi. Kammaṭṭhānaṃ manasikaronto sedāpissa kacchehi muccanti. Atha naṃ antevāsiko āha ‘‘idha, bhante, nisīdatha, sītalo okāso’’ti. Thero ‘‘uṇhabhayenevamhi āvuso idha nisinno’’ti avīcimahānirayaṃ paccavekkhitvā nisīdiyeva. Uṇhanti cettha aggisantāpova veditabbo. Sūriyasantāpavasena panetaṃ vatthu vuttaṃ.

Uṇha

Yo ca dve tayo vāre bhattaṃ vā pānīyaṃ vā alabhamānopi anamatagge saṃsāre attano pettivisayūpapattiṃ paccavekkhitvā avedhento kammaṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatiyeva. Adhimattehi ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasamphassehi phuṭṭho cāpi tiracchānūpapattiṃ paccavekkhitvā avedhento kammaṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatiyeva. Sarīsapasamphassena phuṭṭho cāpi anamatagge saṃsāre sīhabyagghādimukhesu anekavāraṃ parivattitapubbabhāvaṃ paccavekkhitvā avedhento kammaṭṭhānaṃ na vijahatiyeva padhāniyatthero viya. Ayaṃ ‘‘khamo jighacchāya…pe… sarīsapasamphassāna’’nti veditabbo.

Theraṃ kira khaṇḍacelavihāre kaṇikārapadhāniyaghare ariyavaṃsaṃ suṇantaṃ ghoraviso sappo ḍaṃsi. Thero jānitvāpi pasannacitto nisinno dhammaṃyeva suṇāti. Visavego thaddho ahosi. Thero upasampadamaṇḍalaṃ ādiṃ katvā sīlaṃ paccavekkhitvā parisuddhasīlohamasmīti pītiṃ uppādesi. Saha pītuppādā visaṃ nivattitvā pathaviṃ pāvisi. Thero tattheva cittekaggataṃ labhitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

Yo pana akkosavasena durutte duruttattāyeva ca durāgate api antimavatthusaññite vacanapathe sutvā khantiguṇaṃyeva paccavekkhitvā na vedhati dīghabhāṇakaabhayatthero viya. Ayaṃ ‘‘khamo duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathāna’’nti veditabbo.

Thero kira paccayasantosabhāvanārāmatāya mahāariyavaṃsappaṭipadaṃ kathesi, sabbo mahāgāmo āgacchati. Therassa mahāsakkāro uppajjati. Taṃ aññataro mahāthero adhivāsetuṃ asakkonto dīghabhāṇako ariyavaṃsaṃ kathemīti sabbarattiṃ kolāhalaṃ karosītiādīhi akkosi. Ubhopi ca attano attano vihāraṃ gacchantā gāvutamattaṃ ekapathena agamaṃsu. Sakalagāvutampi so taṃ akkosiyeva. Tato yattha dvinnaṃ vihārānaṃ maggo bhijjati, tattha ṭhatvā dīghabhāṇakatthero taṃ vanditvā ‘‘esa, bhante, tumhākaṃ maggo’’ti āha. So asuṇanto viya agamāsi. Theropi vihāraṃ gantvā pāde pakkhāletvā nisīdi. Tamenaṃ antevāsiko ‘‘kiṃ, bhante, sakalagāvutaṃ paribhāsantaṃ na kiñci avocutthā’’ti āha. Thero ‘‘khantiyeva, āvuso, mayhaṃ bhāro, na akkhanti. Ekapaduddhārepi kammaṭṭhānaviyogaṃ na passāmī’’ti āha. Ettha ca vacanameva vacanapathoti veditabbo.

vacanapatho

Yo pana uppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhamanaṭṭhena dukkhā, bahalaṭṭhena tibbā, pharusaṭṭhena kharā, tikhiṇaṭṭhena kaṭukā, assādavirahato asātā, manaṃ avaḍḍhanato amanāpā, pāṇaharaṇasamatthatāya pāṇaharā adhivāsetiyeva, na vedhati. Evaṃ sabhāvo hoti cittalapabbate padhāniyatthero viya. Ayaṃ ‘‘uppannānaṃ…pe… adhivāsanajātiko’’ti veditabbo.

dukkhā, tibbā, kharā, kaṭukā, asātā, amanāpā, pāṇaharā

Therassa kira rattiṃ padhānena vītināmetvā ṭhitassa udaravāto uppajji. So taṃ adhivāsetuṃ asakkonto āvattati parivattati. Tamenaṃ caṅkamapasse ṭhito piṇḍapātiyatthero āha ‘‘āvuso, pabbajito nāma adhivāsanasīlo hotī’’ti. So ‘‘sādhu, bhante’’ti adhivāsetvā niccalo sayi. Vāto nābhito yāva hadayaṃ phāleti. Thero vedanaṃ vikkhambhetvā vipassanto muhuttena anāgāmī hutvā parinibbāyīti.

Yañhissāti sītādīsu yaṃkiñci ekadhammampi assa. Anadhivāsayatoti anadhivāsentassa akkhamantassa. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Āsavuppatti panettha evaṃ veditabbā. Sītena phuṭṭhassa uṇhaṃ patthayantassa kāmāsavo uppajjati, evaṃ sabbattha. Natthi no sampattibhave sugatibhave sītaṃ vā uṇhaṃ vāti bhavaṃ patthayantassa bhavāsavo. Mayhaṃ sītaṃ uṇhanti gāho diṭṭhāsavo. Sabbeheva sampayutto avijjāsavoti.

Yañhissā Anadhivāsayato

‘‘Ime vuccanti…pe… adhivāsanā pahātabbā’’ti ime sītādīsu ekamekassa vasena cattāro cattāro katvā aneke āsavā imāya khantisaṃvarasaṅkhātāya adhivāsanāya pahātabbāti vuccantīti attho. Ettha ca yasmā ayaṃ khanti sītādidhamme adhivāseti, attano upari āropetvā vāsetiyeva. Na asahamānā hutvā nirassati, tasmā ‘‘adhivāsanā’’ti vuccatīti veditabbā.

‘‘Ime vuccanti…pe… adhivāsanā pahātabbā’’

Adhivāsanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Parivajjanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
24. "Having the ability to endure cold through wise reflection" means reflecting with skillful means and wisdom, one is capable of enduring the cold. The cold is bearable and endurable. Unlike an unmanly person, one is not moved or shaken even by a little cold, and does not abandon their meditation subject ( *kammaṭṭhāna*). Moreover, just as the Elder Lomasanāga, though touched by even a slight cold, did not move or tremble, but kept the meditation subject in mind. It is said that the Elder, while dwelling in the practice chamber in the cave of Piyaṅgu on Cetiyapabbata, having reflected on the hell of Lokantarika during a time of snowfall in the intermediate region, spent his time in the open air without abandoning his meditation subject. Likewise, the application of the meaning should be understood in relation to heat and other factors also. Just as a *bhikkhu* who endures even intense heat is to be regarded as "capable of enduring heat." It is said that the Elder sat down in the outer cloister after his meal during the hot season. While focusing on his meditation subject, sweat flowed from his armpits. Then his disciple said to him, "Venerable sir, sit here; this is a cool spot." The Elder, reflecting on the Avīci Great Hell, thought, "It is out of fear of heat that I am sitting here, friend," and remained seated. Here, *uṇha* (heat) should be understood as the burning torment of fire. This topic is spoken in terms of torment from the sun. One, who not obtaining alms food or drink at two or three times on the cycle of existence without beginning (*anamatagge saṃsāre*), reflects on the state of existence in their own ancestral sphere, without wavering, does not abandon the meditation subject. One, touched by excessive contact with gnats, mosquitoes, wind, sun, or insects, and reflecting on the possibility of rebirth in the animal realm, without wavering, does not abandon the meditation subject. One, touched by contact with snakes, reflecting on the previous states of existence transmigrated many times in the cycle of existence without beginning (*anamatagge saṃsāre*) in the mouths of lions, tigers, and other animals, without wavering, does not abandon the meditation subject, like the Elder Padhāniya. This one is to be understood as “capable of hunger…pe… capable of contact with snakes.” It is said that in the Khaṇḍacela monastery, while listening to the Ariyavaṃsa in the Kaṇikāra meditation house, a deadly poisonous snake bit the Elder. The Elder, even knowing this, with a serene mind, remained seated, listening to the Dhamma. The force of the poison was stopped. The Elder, beginning with the *upasampadāmaṇḍala*, reflecting on morality, generated joy, thinking, “I am of purified morality.” Together with the arising of joy, the poison subsided, having entered the earth. The Elder, right there, having attained one-pointedness of mind, developing insight (*vipassanā*), attained *arhatship*. One who, because of abuse, hearing unpleasant, harsh, and disagreeable words related to the final object, reflecting only on the quality of patience, does not waver, like the Elder Dīghabhāṇaka Abhaya. This one is to be understood as "capable of unpleasant and disagreeable words." It is said that the Elder preached the great Ariyavaṃsa teaching, delighting in contentment and cultivation, and the entire great village came. Great honor arose for the Elder. Unable to bear that, another great Elder abused him, saying, "Because he teaches the Ariyavaṃsa, he makes noise all night long," and so forth. Both, while going to their own monasteries, went a *gāvuta*'s distance on the same path. Even for the entire *gāvuta*, he abused him. Then, where the path for the two monasteries diverged, standing there, the Elder Dīghabhāṇaka, having venerated him, said, "Venerable sir, this is your path." He departed as if not hearing. The Elder too, having gone to the monastery, washed his feet and sat down. Then a disciple said to him, "Venerable sir, why did you not say anything to him, who was speaking offensively for the entire *gāvuta*?” The Elder said, “Patience alone, friend, is my burden, not impatience. He said, "Even in extracting a single word, I do not see a separation from the practice" ( *kammaṭṭhāna*). Here, it should be understood that *vacana* itself is the "path of speech" (*vacanapatho*).

The "path of speech" (*vacanapatho*),

that which, when arisen, bodily sensation is *dukkha* [suffering] because of its characteristic of bringing unhappiness; *tibba* [intense] because of its characteristic of being thick; *khara* [harsh] because of its characteristic of being rough; *kaṭuka* [bitter] because of its characteristic of being sharp; *asātā* [unsatisfactory] because of its characteristic of being without taste; *amanāpā* [unpleasant] because of its characteristic of not pleasing the mind; *pāṇaharā* [life-destroying] because of its capacity to take life, he should endure. He should not tremble. The elder ( *thero*) at Cittalapabbata was of such a nature, like the striving Elder. This should be understood as "of the nature of endurance (*adhivāsana*) of arisen [sensations]..."

*Dukkha* [suffering], *tibba* [intense], *khara* [harsh], *kaṭuka* [bitter], *asātā* [unsatisfactory], *amanāpā* [unpleasant], *pāṇaharā* [life-destroying].

It seems that the Elder ( *therassa*), having spent the night in striving (*padhānena*), experienced flatulence (*udaravāto*) when he was standing. He, being unable to endure that, turned back and forth. The Elder, standing on the walking path (*caṅkamapasse*) for alms (*piṇḍapātiyatthero*), said to him, "Friend (*āvuso*), a renunciate (*pabbajito*) is said to be of the nature of endurance (*adhivāsanasīlo*)." He, replying "Good (*sādhu*), Venerable One (*bhante*)!" endured and lay still. The wind splits the heart from the navel. The Elder, having suppressed the sensation (*vedanaṃ vikkhambhetvā*), contemplating (*vipassanto*), in a moment, became a Non-Returner (*anāgāmī*) and attained *parinirvāṇa*.

“When there is endurance (*yañhissā*)”: whatever single element (*ekadhammampi*) there may be in cold and so on. "Because of not enduring (*anadhivāsayato*)": because of not enduring, because of not being patient (*akkhamantassa*). The rest is as already stated (*vuttanayameva*). Here, the arising of defilements (*āsavuppatti*) should be understood thus. When a person touched by cold desires heat, the defilement of sensuality (*kāmāsavo*) arises; thus everywhere. There is no defilement of existence (*bhavāsavo*) for one who desires existence, saying, "May there be cold or heat in fortunate states (*sugatibhave*) or in states of attainment (*sampattibhave*)." The grasping, "Mine is cold, [mine] is heat" is the defilement of views (*diṭṭhāsavo*). Unassociated with all, it is the defilement of ignorance (*avijjāsavoti*).

“When there is endurance (*yañhissā*), because of not enduring (*anadhivāsayato*)”:

“These are called…endurance should be abandoned (*adhivāsanā pahātabbā*)": thus, the many defilements (*aneke āsavā*) are abandoned by this endurance (*adhivāsanāya*) known as restraint through patience (*khantisaṃvarasaṅkhātāya*), making four and four for each of these, cold and so on. This is the meaning. Here, since this patience (*khanti*) causes [one] to endure (*adhivāseti*) in states such as cold and so on, placing and dwelling (*āropetvā vāsetiyeva*) on top of oneself. Not being impatient (*asahamānā hutvā*), one does not reject (*nirassati*); therefore, it should be understood that it is called "endurance (*adhivāsanā*)."

"These are called...endurance should be abandoned (*adhivāsanā pahātabbā*)."

The description of the defilements to be abandoned by endurance (*adhivāsanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā*) is finished.

Description of the defilements to be abandoned by avoidance (*parivajjanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā*)

mula_pali:
25. ‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso caṇḍaṃ hatthiṃ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṃ assaṃ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṃ goṇaṃ parivajjeti, caṇḍaṃ kukkuraṃ parivajjeti, ahiṃ khāṇuṃ kaṇṭakaṭṭhānaṃ sobbhaṃ papātaṃ candanikaṃ oḷigallaṃ. Yathārūpe anāsane nisinnaṃ yathārūpe agocare carantaṃ yathārūpe pāpake mitte bhajantaṃ viññū sabrahmacārī pāpakesu ṭhānesu okappeyyuṃ, so tañca anāsanaṃ tañca agocaraṃ te ca pāpake mitte paṭisaṅkhā yoniso parivajjeti.

‘‘Yañhissa, bhikkhave, aparivajjayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, parivajjayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā.

Vinodanā pahātabbāsavā
mula_english:
What are the effluents to be abandoned by avoiding? Here, a monk, reflecting appropriately, avoids a wild elephant (caṇḍaṃ hatthiṃ), a wild horse (caṇḍaṃ assaṃ), a wild bull (caṇḍaṃ goṇaṃ), a wild dog (caṇḍaṃ kukkuraṃ), a snake (ahiṃ), a stump (khāṇuṃ), a bramble patch (kaṇṭakaṭṭhānaṃ), a chasm (sobbhaṃ), a cliff (papātaṃ), a cesspool (candanikaṃ), an open sewer (oḷigallaṃ).

While sitting in an unsuitable seat (yathārūpe anāsane), living in an unsuitable pasture (yathārūpe agocare), associating with unsuitable bad friends (yathārūpe pāpake mitte), discerning spiritual companions would be suspicious of him in connection with evil situations (pāpakesu ṭhānesu okappeyyuṃ). He avoids that unsuitable seat (tañca anāsanaṃ), that unsuitable pasture (tañca agocaraṃ), and those unsuitable bad friends (te ca pāpake mitte), reflecting appropriately.

The āsravas, vexation, or fever (āsavā vighātapariḷāhā) that would arise if he were not to avoid these things do not arise for him when he avoids them. These are called the effluents to be abandoned by avoiding (āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā).

Effluents to be abandoned by removing.
commentary_pali:
25.Paṭisaṅkhāyoniso caṇḍaṃ hatthiṃ parivajjetīti ahaṃ samaṇoti caṇḍassa hatthissa āsanne na ṭhātabbaṃ. Tatonidānañhi maraṇampi siyā maraṇamattampi dukkhanti evaṃ upāyena pathena paccayena paccavekkhitvā caṇḍaṃ hatthiṃ parivajjeti paṭikkamati. Esa nayo sabbattha. Caṇḍanti ca duṭṭhaṃ, vāḷanti vuttaṃ hoti. Khāṇunti khadirakhāṇuādiṃ. Kaṇṭakaṭṭhānanti kaṇṭakānaṃ ṭhānaṃ, yattha kaṇṭakā vijjanti, taṃ okāsanti vuttaṃ hoti. Sobbhanti sabbato paricchinnataṭaṃ. Papātanti ekato chinnataṭaṃ. Candanikanti ucchiṭṭhodakagabbhamalādīnaṃ chaḍḍanaṭṭhānaṃ. Oḷigallanti tesaṃyeva sakaddamādīnaṃ sandanokāsaṃ. Taṃ jaṇṇumattampi asucibharitaṃ hoti, dvepi cetāni ṭhānāni amanussaduṭṭhāni honti. Tasmā tāni vajjetabbāni. Anāsaneti ettha pana ayuttaṃ āsanaṃ anāsanaṃ, taṃ atthato aniyatavatthukaṃ rahopaṭicchannāsananti veditabbaṃ. Agocareti etthapi ca ayutto gocaro agocaro, so vesiyādibhedato pañcavidho. Pāpake mitteti lāmake dussīle mittapatirūpake, amitte vā. Bhajantanti sevamānaṃ. Viññū sabrahmacārīti paṇḍitā buddhisampannā sabrahmacārayo, bhikkhūnametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Te hi ekakammaṃ ekuddeso samasikkhatāti imaṃ brahmaṃ samānaṃ caranti, tasmā sabrahmacārīti vuccanti. Pāpakesu ṭhānesūti lāmakesu ṭhānesu. Okappeyyunti saddaheyyuṃ, adhimucceyyuṃ ‘‘addhā ayamāyasmā akāsi vā karissati vā’’ti.

Yañhissāti hatthiādīsu yaṃkiñci ekampi assa. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Āsavuppatti panettha evaṃ veditabbā. Hatthiādinidānena dukkhena phuṭṭhassa sukhaṃ patthayato kāmāsavo uppajjati. Natthi no sampattibhave sugatibhave īdisaṃ dukkhanti bhavaṃ patthentassa bhavāsavo. Maṃ hatthī maddati, maṃ assoti gāho diṭṭhāsavo. Sabbeheva sampayutto avijjāsavoti.

Yañhissā

Ime vuccanti…pe… parivajjanā pahātabbāti ime hatthiādīsu ekekassa vasena cattāro cattāro katvā aneke āsavā iminā sīlasaṃvarasaṅkhātena parivajjanena pahātabbāti vuccantīti veditabbā.

Ime vuccanti…pe… parivajjanā pahātabbā

Parivajjanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Vinodanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
25. 'Having reflected, he avoids a wild elephant' means: Thinking, "I am a renunciate," one should not stand near a wild elephant. For from that cause, death might occur, or even a death-like suffering. Thus, having investigated with skill, means, reason, and cause, he avoids and retreats from a wild elephant. This method applies to all the other cases.

'Wild' (*caṇḍa*) means fierce, or as it has been said, 'violent' (*vāḷa*).

'Stump' (*khāṇu*) means a *khadira* stump and so on.

'Thorn-thicket' (*kaṇṭakaṭṭhāna*) means a place of thorns, a location where thorns are found.

'Pit' (*sobbha*) means a depression with an even rim all around.

'Precipice' (*papāta*) means a cliff with a broken edge on one side.

'Cesspool' (*candanika*) means a place for discarding leftover water, refuse, and so on.

'Puddle' (*oḷigalla*) means a place where mud and other such things collect. It might be filled knee-deep with filth. Both of these places are haunted by non-human beings. Therefore, they should be avoided.

Here, 'in an unsuitable seat' (*anāsane*) means an improper seat (*anāsana*), which is to be understood as an isolated, concealed seat consisting of unstable materials.

Similarly, 'in an improper resort' (*agocare*) means an improper resort (*agocara*), which is fivefold in terms of prostitutes and so on.

'Evil friends' (*pāpake mitte*) means base, immoral individuals who are only imitations of friends, or even enemies.

'Consorting with' (*bhajanta*) means associating with.

'Wise spiritual companions' (*viññū sabrahmacārī*) means learned, intelligent spiritual companions. This is a designation for monks, for they live the same spiritual life, with a single purpose, a single instruction, and equal training. Therefore, they are called 'spiritual companions' (*sabrahmacārī*).

'In evil places' (*pāpakesu ṭhānesu*) means in base places.

'Would impute' (*okappeyyu*) means they would believe and be convinced, "Indeed, this venerable one has done it or will do it."

'Whatever of it' (*yañhissā*) means any one of the elephants and so on.

The rest is as already stated.

Here, the arising of defilements (*āsava*) should be understood in this way:

Lust (*kāmāsava*) arises in one who has been afflicted by suffering due to elephants and so on, and who longs for pleasure. Craving for existence (*bhavāsava*) arises in one who desires continued existence, thinking, "May there not be such suffering for us in a fortunate future existence!" Grasping at the idea that "an elephant crushes me, a horse crushes me" is the defilement of views (*diṭṭhāsava*). The defilement of ignorance (*avijjāsava*) is associated with all of these.

'Whatever of it…these are called…to be avoided' means that these many defilements, based on each of the elephants and so on, four at a time, are said to be abandoned by this avoidance, which is known as moral restraint.

The explanation of defilements to be abandoned by avoidance is completed.

Explanation of Defilements to be Abandoned by Removal

mula_pali:
26. ‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṃ gameti, uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ…pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṃ gameti.

‘‘Yañhissa, bhikkhave, avinodayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, vinodayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā.

Bhāvanā pahātabbāsavā
mula_english:
"26.
"And what, monks, are the effluents to be abandoned by destroying? Here, monks, a monk, reflecting appropriately, does not tolerate an arisen thought of sensual desire (kāmavitakka). He abandons it, destroys it, dispels it, and wipes it out of existence. He does not tolerate an arisen thought of ill will... He does not tolerate an arisen thought of harmfulness... He does not tolerate arisen evil, unskillful qualities. He abandons them, destroys them, dispels them, and wipes them out of existence.

"The effluents, vexation, and fever that would arise if he were not to destroy these things do not arise for him when he destroys them. These are called the effluents to be abandoned by destroying."

Effluents to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā pahātabbāsavā).
commentary_pali:
26.Paṭisaṅkhāyoniso uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāsetīti ‘‘iti pāyaṃ vitakko akusalo, itipi sāvajjo, itipi dukkhavipāko, so ca kho attabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’’tiādinā nayena yoniso kāmavitakke ādīnavaṃ paccavekkhitvā tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ārammaṇe uppannaṃ jātamabhinibbattaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, cittaṃ āropetvā na vāseti, abbhantare vā na vāsetītipi attho.

Anadhivāsento kiṃ karotīti? Pajahati chaḍḍeti.

Pajahati

Kiṃ kacavaraṃ viya piṭakenāti? Na hi, apica kho naṃ vinodeti tudati vijjhati nīharati.

vinodeti

Kiṃ balibaddaṃ viya patodenāti? Na hi, atha kho naṃ byantīkaroti vigatantaṃ karoti. Yathāssa antopi nāvasissati antamaso bhaṅgamattampi, tathā naṃ karoti.

byantīkaroti

Kathaṃ pana naṃ tathā karotīti? Anabhāvaṃ gametīti anu anu abhāvaṃ gameti, vikkhambhanappahānena yathā suvikkhambhito hoti, tathā karotīti vuttaṃ hoti. Esa nayo byāpādavihiṃsāvitakkesu.

Anabhāvaṃ gametī byāpādavihiṃsāvitakkesu

Ettha ca kāmavitakkoti ‘‘yo kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo’’ti vibhaṅge (vibha. 910) vutto. Esa nayo itaresu. Uppannuppanneti uppanne uppanne, uppannamatteyevāti vuttaṃ hoti. Sakiṃ vā uppanne vinodetvā dutiyavāre ajjhupekkhitā na hoti, satakkhattumpi uppanne uppanne vinodetiyeva. Pāpake akusaleti lāmakaṭṭhena pāpake, akosallatāya akusale. Dhammeti teyeva kāmavitakkādayo sabbepi vā nava mahāvitakke. Tattha tayo vuttā eva. Avasesā ‘‘ñātivitakko janapadavitakko amaravitakko parānuddayatāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko lābhasakkārasilokapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko anavaññattipaṭisaṃyutto vitakko’’ti (mahāni. 207) ime cha.

kāmavitakko Uppannuppanne Pāpake akusale Dhamme

Yañhissāti etesu vitakkesu yaṃkiñci assa, sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Kāmavitakko panettha kāmāsavo eva. Tabbiseso bhavāsavo. Taṃsampayutto diṭṭhāsavo. Sabbavitakkesu avijjāsavoti evaṃ āsavuppattipi veditabbā.

Yañhissā

Ime vuccanti…pe… vinodanā pahātabbāti ime kāmavitakkādivasena vuttappakārā āsavā iminā tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vitakke ādīnavapaccavekkhaṇasahitena vīriyasaṃvarasaṅkhātena vinodanena pahātabbāti vuccantīti veditabbā.

Ime vuccanti…pe… vinodanā pahātabbā

Vinodanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Bhāvanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
26. "Having wisely abandoned sensual thought that has arisen" means, according to the method beginning with, "This thought is bad, blameworthy, and results in suffering, and it leads to self-affliction," having wisely considered the drawbacks of sensual thoughts, he does not allow the sensual thought that has arisen, originated, and come into being in that object to remain; he does not allow the mind to ascend and dwell [on it], meaning he does not allow it to dwell within.

What does he do when he does not allow it to remain? He abandons and discards it.

He abandons: Is it like rubbish with a basket? No, but he drives it away, pricks, pierces, and removes it.

He drives away: Is it like an ox with a goad? No, but he eradicates it, makes it cease. He does it in such a way that not even a bit of its end remains, not even a fraction of its destruction.

He eradicates: But how does he do it that way? "He causes it to become non-existent" means he gradually causes it to become non-existent. It is said that he acts in such a way that it is thoroughly obstructed by the abandonment of obstruction. This is the method for thoughts of ill-will and harm.

He causes it to become non-existent; thoughts of ill-will and harm.

Here, *sensual thought* (*kāmavitakko*) is that which is "connected with sensual passion, thinking, thought, wrong intention," as stated in the *Vibhaṅga* (Vibha. 910). This is the method for the others. *Whenever it arises* means whenever it arises, as soon as it arises. It is not that having driven it away once, he is indifferent the second time it arises, but he drives it away whenever it arises, even a hundred times. *Bad, unwholesome states* means bad in the sense of being inferior, unwholesome in the sense of unskillful. *States* means those very sensual thoughts, etc., or all nine great thoughts. Three of them have already been mentioned. The remaining six are: "thoughts about relatives, thoughts about the country, thoughts about immortality, thoughts connected with compassion for others, thoughts connected with gain, honor, and fame, thoughts connected with non-contempt" (Mahāni. 207).

Sensual thought; whenever it arises; bad, unwholesome states.

*Whatever he has* means whatever he has of these thoughts; the rest is as previously stated. Sensual thought here is simply the *āsava* of sensuality (*kāmāsava*). The *āsava* of becoming (*bhavāsava*) is a particular kind of it. The *āsava* of views (*diṭṭhāsava*) is associated with it. In all thoughts, the *āsava* of ignorance (*avijjāsava*) should be understood as the origin of the *āsavas* in this way.

Whatever he has.

*These are called...to be abandoned by driving away* means these *āsavas*, which have been described in terms of sensual thoughts, etc., are said to be abandoned by this driving away, which is synonymous with the restraint of energy (*vīriyasaṃvara*) together with contemplating the drawbacks in each thought, and this should be understood.

These are called...to be abandoned by driving away.

The explanation of the *āsavas* to be abandoned by driving away is finished.

Explanation of the *āsavas* to be abandoned by cultivation

mula_pali:
27. ‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ; paṭisaṅkhā yoniso dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.

‘‘Yañhissa, bhikkhave , abhāvayato uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, bhāvayato evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā.
mula_english:
"27. "And which, monks, are the effluents to be abandoned by developing? Here, monks, a monk, reflecting appropriately, cultivates mindfulness as an enlightenment factor (*satisambojjhaṅgaṃ*), which is based on seclusion (*vivekanissitaṃ*), dispassion (*virāganissitaṃ*), and cessation (*nirodhanissitaṃ*), and results in relinquishment (*vossaggapariṇāmiṃ*); reflecting appropriately, he cultivates investigation of qualities as an enlightenment factor (*dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ*)…persistence as an enlightenment factor (*vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ*)…rapture as an enlightenment factor (*pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ*)…<pb ed="v" n="1.0016"/>tranquillity as an enlightenment factor (*passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ*)…concentration as an enlightenment factor (*samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ*)…equanimity as an enlightenment factor (*upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ*), which is based on seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, and results in relinquishment.

"For if, monks,<pb ed="t" n="1.0020"/> the effluents, vexation, or fever that would arise if he were not to develop these qualities do not arise for him when he develops them. These, monks, are called the effluents to be abandoned by developing."
commentary_pali:
27.Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetīti abhāvanāya ādīnavaṃ, bhāvanāya ca ānisaṃsaṃ upāyena pathena paccavekkhitvā satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti, esa nayo sabbattha. Ettha ca kiñcāpi ime uparimaggattayasamayasambhūtā lokuttarabojjhaṅgā eva adhippetā, tathāpi ādikammikānaṃ bojjhaṅgesu asammohatthaṃ lokiyalokuttaramissakena nesaṃ nayena atthavaṇṇanaṃ karissāmi. Idha pana lokiyanayaṃ pahāya lokuttaranayo eva gahetabbo. Tattha satisambojjhaṅgantiādinā nayena vuttānaṃ sattannaṃ ādipadānaṃyeva tāva –

Atthato lakkhaṇādīhi, kamato ca vinicchayo;

Anūnādhikato ceva, viññātabbo vibhāvinā.

Tattha satisambojjhaṅge tāva saraṇaṭṭhena sati. Sā panesā upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇā, apilāpanalakkhaṇā vā. Vuttampi hetaṃ ‘‘yathā, mahārāja, rañño bhaṇḍāgāriko rañño sāpateyyaṃ apilāpeti, ettakaṃ, mahārāja, hiraññaṃ, ettakaṃ suvaṇṇaṃ, ettakaṃ sāpateyyanti, evameva kho, mahārāja , sati uppajjamānā kusalākusalasāvajjānavajjahīnapaṇītakaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāge dhamme apilāpeti. Ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’’ti (mi. pa. 2.1.13) vitthāro. Apilāpanarasā. Kiccavaseneva hissa etaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ therena vuttaṃ. Asammosarasā vā. Gocarābhimukhabhāvapaccupaṭṭhānā. Sati eva sambojjhaṅgo satisambojjhaṅgo. Tattha bodhiyā bodhissa vā aṅgoti bojjhaṅgo.

sati satisambojjhaṅgo

Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Yā hi ayaṃ dhammasāmaggī, yāya lokiyalokuttaramaggakkhaṇe uppajjamānāya līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhana-kāmasukhattakilamathānuyoga-ucchedasassatābhinivesādīnaṃ anekesaṃ upaddavānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtāya satidhammavicayavīriyapītipassaddhisamādhiupekkhāsaṅkhātāya dhammasāmaggiyā ariyasāvako bujjhatīti katvā ‘‘bodhī’’ti vuccati. Bujjhatīti kilesasantānaniddāya uṭṭhahati, cattāri vā ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhati, nibbānameva vā sacchikarotīti vuttaṃ hoti. Yathāha ‘‘satta bojjhaṅge bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’’ti. Tassā dhammasāmaggisaṅkhātāya bodhiyā aṅgotipi bojjhaṅgo, jhānaṅgamaggaṅgādayo viya.

Bujjhatī

Yopesa yathāvuttappakārāya etāya dhammasāmaggiyā bujjhatīti katvā ariyasāvako ‘‘bodhī’’ti vuccati, tassa bodhissa aṅgotipi bojjhaṅgo, senaṅgarathaṅgādayo viya. Tenāhu aṭṭhakathācariyā ‘‘bujjhanakassa puggalassa aṅgāti vā bojjhaṅgā’’ti. Apica ‘‘bojjhaṅgāti kenaṭṭhena bojjhaṅgā? Bodhāya saṃvattantīti bojjhaṅgā, bujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā, anubujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā, paṭibujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā, sambujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā’’tiādinā (paṭi. ma. 3.17) paṭisambhidānayenāpi attho veditabbo. Pasattho sundaro vā bojjhaṅgoti sambojjhaṅgo. Evaṃ sati eva sambojjhaṅgo satisambojjhaṅgo. Taṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ. Evaṃ tāva ekassa ādipadassa atthato lakkhaṇādīhi ca vinicchayo viññātabbo.

satisambojjhaṅgaṃ

Dutiyādīsu pana catusaccadhamme vicinātīti dhammavicayo. So pana vicayalakkhaṇo, obhāsanaraso, asammohapaccupaṭṭhāno. Vīrabhāvato vidhinā īrayitabbato ca vīriyaṃ. Taṃ paggahalakkhaṇaṃ , upatthambhanarasaṃ, anosīdanapaccupaṭṭhānaṃ . Pīṇayatīti pīti. Sā pharaṇalakkhaṇā, tuṭṭhilakkhaṇā vā, kāyacittānaṃ pīṇanarasā, tesaṃyeva odagyapaccupaṭṭhānā. Kāyacittadarathapassambhanato passaddhi. Sā upasamalakkhaṇā, kāyacittadarathanimmaddanarasā, āyacittānaṃ aparipphandanabhūtasītibhāvapaccupaṭṭhānā. Samādhānato samādhi. So avikkhepalakkhaṇo, avisāralakkhaṇo vā, cittacetasikānaṃ sampiṇḍanaraso, cittaṭṭhitipaccupaṭṭhāno. Ajjhupekkhanato upekkhā. Sā paṭisaṅkhānalakkhaṇā, samavāhitalakkhaṇā vā, ūnādhikatānivāraṇarasā, pakkhapātupacchedarasā vā, majjhattabhāvapaccupaṭṭhānā. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Evaṃ sesapadānampi atthato lakkhaṇādīhi ca vinicchayo viññātabbo.

dhammavicayo vīriyaṃ pīti passaddhi samādhi upekkhā

Kamatoti ettha ca ‘‘satiñca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṃ vadāmī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.234) vacanato sabbesaṃ sesabojjhaṅgānaṃ upakārakattā satisambojjhaṅgova paṭhamaṃ vutto. Tato paraṃ ‘‘so tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinatī’’tiādinā (vibha. 469) nayena sesabojjhaṅgānaṃ pubbāpariyavacane payojanaṃ sutteyeva vuttaṃ. Evamettha kamatopi vinicchayo viññātabbo.

Kamato

Anūnādhikatoti kasmā pana bhagavatā satteva bojjhaṅgā vuttā anūnā anadhikāti. Līnuddhaccapaṭipakkhato sabbatthikato ca. Ettha hi tayo bojjhaṅgā līnassa paṭipakkhā. Yathāha – ‘‘yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, kālo tasmiṃ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāyā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.234). Tayo uddhaccassa paṭipakkhā. Yathāha – ‘‘yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ hoti, kālo tasmiṃ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāyā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.234). Eko panettha sabbatthiko. Yathāha – ‘‘satiñca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṃ vadāmī’’ti. ‘‘Sabbatthaka’’ntipi pāṭho, dvinnampi sabbattha icchitabbanti attho. Evaṃ līnuddhaccapaṭipakkhato sabbatthikato ca satteva bojjhaṅgā vuttā anūnā anadhikāti, evamettha anūnādhikatopi vinicchayo viññātabbo.

Anūnādhikato

Evaṃ tāva ‘‘satisambojjhaṅga’’ntiādinā nayena vuttānaṃ sattannaṃ ādipadānaṃyeva atthavaṇṇanaṃ ñatvā idāni bhāveti vivekanissitantiādīsu evaṃ ñātabbā. Bhāvetīti vaḍḍheti, attano cittasantāne punappunaṃ janeti abhinibbattetīti attho. Vivekanissitanti viveke nissitaṃ. Vivekoti vivittatā. Svāyaṃ tadaṅgaviveko vikkhambhanasamucchedapaṭippassaddhi nissaraṇavivekoti pañcavidho. Tassa nānattaṃ ‘‘ariyadhamme avinīto’’ti ettha vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ayameva hi tattha vinayoti vutto. Evaṃ etasmiṃ pañcavidhe viveke.

bhāveti vivekanissita Bhāvetī Vivekanissita Viveko

Vivekanissitanti tadaṅgavivekanissitaṃ samucchedavivekanissitaṃ nissaraṇavivekanissitañca satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetīti ayamattho veditabbo. Tathā hi ayaṃ bojjhaṅgabhāvanānuyutto yogī vipassanākkhaṇe kiccato tadaṅgavivekanissitaṃ, ajjhāsayato nissaraṇavivekanissitaṃ, maggakāle pana kiccato samucchedavivekanissitaṃ, ārammaṇato nissaraṇavivekanissitaṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti. Pañcavidhavivekanissitantipi eke, te hi na kevalaṃ balavavipassanāmaggaphalakkhaṇesu eva bojjhaṅge uddharanti, vipassanāpādakakasiṇajjhānaānāpānāsubhabrahmavihārajjhānesupi uddharanti. Na ca paṭisiddhā aṭṭhakathācariyehi. Tasmā tesaṃ matena etesaṃ jhānānaṃ pavattikkhaṇe kiccato eva vikkhambhanavivekanissitaṃ. Yathā ca ‘‘vipassanākkhaṇe ajjhāsayato nissaraṇavivekanissita’’nti vuttaṃ, evaṃ paṭippassaddhivivekanissitampi bhāvetīti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Esa nayo virāganissitādīsu. Vivekaṭṭhā eva hi virāgādayo.

Vivekanissita virāganissitā

Kevalañhettha vossaggo duvidho pariccāgavossaggo ca pakkhandanavossaggo cāti. Tattha pariccāgavossaggoti vipassanākkhaṇe ca tadaṅgavasena, maggakkhaṇe ca samucchedavasena kilesappahānaṃ. Pakkhandanavossaggoti vipassanākkhaṇe tanninnabhāvena, maggakkhaṇe pana ārammaṇakaraṇena nibbānapakkhandanaṃ. Tadubhayampi imasmiṃ lokiyalokuttaramissake atthavaṇṇanānaye vaṭṭati. Tathā hi ayaṃ satisambojjhaṅgo yathāvuttena pakārena kilese pariccajati, nibbānañca pakkhandati. Vossaggapariṇāminti iminā pana sakalena vacanena vossaggattaṃ pariṇamantaṃ pariṇatañca paripaccantaṃ paripakkañcāti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘ayañhi bojjhaṅgabhāvanānuyutto bhikkhu yathā satisambojjhaṅgo kilesapariccāgavossaggattaṃ nibbānapakkhandanavossaggattañca paripaccati, yathā ca paripakko hoti, tathā naṃ bhāvetī’’ti. Esa nayo sesabojjhaṅgesu.

vossaggo pariccāgavossaggo Pakkhandanavossaggo Vossaggapariṇāmi

Idha pana nibbānaṃyeva sabbasaṅkhatehi vivittattā viveko, sabbesaṃ virāgabhāvato virāgo, nirodhabhāvato nirodhoti vuttaṃ. Maggo eva ca vossaggapariṇāmī, tasmā satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā pavattiyā vivekanissitaṃ. Tathā virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ. Tañca kho ariyamaggakkhaṇuppattiyā kilesānaṃ samucchedato pariccāgabhāvena ca nibbānapakkhandanabhāvena ca pariṇataṃ paripakkanti ayameva attho daṭṭhabbo. Esa nayo sesabojjhaṅgesu.

viveko, virāgo, nirodho virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ

Yañhissāti etesu bojjhaṅgesu yaṃkiñci assa. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Āsavuppattiyaṃ panettha imesaṃ uparimaggattayasampayuttānaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ abhāvitattā ye uppajjeyyuṃ kāmāsavo bhavāsavo avijjāsavoti tayo āsavā, bhāvayato evaṃsa te āsavā na hontīti ayaṃ nayo veditabbo.

Yañhissā

Ime vuccanti…pe… bhāvanā pahātabbāti ime tayo āsavā imāya maggattayasampayuttāya bojjhaṅgabhāvanāya pahātabbāti vuccantīti veditabbā.

Ime vuccanti…pe… bhāvanā pahātabbā
commentary_english:
" *paṭisaṅkhā yoniso satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetī*ti": by wisely considering, he cultivates the mindfulness enlightenment factor. That is, reflecting with skillful means and the right path on the disadvantage of non-cultivation and the advantage of cultivation, he cultivates the mindfulness enlightenment factor. This method applies in each instance.

Here, although these enlightenment factors are intended to be supramundane, having arisen at the time of the three higher paths, nevertheless, in order to prevent confusion for the beginning practitioner regarding the enlightenment factors, I will make an explanation of the meaning according to their method, with a mixture of mundane and supramundane [elements].

However, in this case, the supramundane method should be adopted, abandoning the mundane method.

First of all, regarding just the initial terms of the seven [enlightenment factors] that were mentioned in the way beginning with " *satisambojjhaṅganti*":

A discerning person should understand the ascertainment by way of the meaning, characteristics, etc., and by way of the sequence, and by way of being neither deficient nor excessive.

Therein, first, *sati* (mindfulness) in *satisambojjhaṅga* (mindfulness enlightenment factor) [means] *sati* due to the meaning of remembering.

And this *sati*, indeed, has the characteristic of attending [to something], or the characteristic of not wobbling.

For it was said, "Just as, great king, a treasurer of the king does not lose the king's property, [saying,] 'So much, great king, is silver; so much is gold; so much is property,' just so, great king, *sati* (mindfulness), when arising, does not wobble regarding phenomena that are skillful, unskillful, blameworthy, blameless, inferior, superior, dark, bright, or similar. These are the four foundations of mindfulness" (Majjhima Nikāya, Paṇṇāsa 2.1.13) in detail. It has the function of not wobbling. For the Elder spoke of this characteristic only in terms of its function. Or, it has the essence of non-confusion. It is manifested as the state of confronting an objective field. *Sati* (mindfulness) itself is *satisambojjhaṅga* (mindfulness enlightenment factor). There, *bojjhaṅga* (enlightenment factor) [means] an *aṅga* (factor) of *bodhi* (enlightenment) or for enlightenment.

What is meant by *sati satisambojjhaṅgo* (mindfulness is the mindfulness-enlightenment-factor)? The community of qualities through which the noble disciple awakens at the moment of the arising of a mundane or supramundane path is called "enlightenment" (*bodhi*), because it is the opponent of many disturbances such as a foundation for being torpid or agitated, application, addiction to pleasure, exhaustion, eternalism or annihilationism, and because of the community of qualities consisting of mindfulness, investigation of phenomena, effort, joy, tranquility, concentration, and equanimity.

"*Bujjhatī* (awakens)" means he arises from the sleep of the continuum of defilements, or he penetrates the four noble truths, or it is said that he realizes nirvāṇa itself. As it was said, "Having cultivated the seven enlightenment factors, he has awakened to unsurpassed complete enlightenment." The *bojjhaṅga* (enlightenment factor) is a factor of that *bodhi* (enlightenment) consisting of a community of qualities, just like the factors of jhāna, the factors of the path, and so forth.

Because the noble disciple awakens through this community of qualities of the type that was mentioned, he is called "*bodhi*" (enlightenment), and the *bojjhaṅga* (enlightenment factor) is a factor of that enlightenment, just like the parts of an army, the parts of a chariot, and so forth. Therefore, the teachers of the commentaries said, "*Bojjhaṅga* (enlightenment factor) is a factor of a person who awakens." Moreover, the meaning should also be understood according to the method of discrimination (Paṭisambhidāmagga 3.17) [in the following way]: "In what sense is it a *bojjhaṅga* (enlightenment factor)? Because they lead to enlightenment, they are *bojjhaṅga*s; because they awaken, they are *bojjhaṅga*s; because they awaken accordingly, they are *bojjhaṅga*s; because they awaken completely, they are *bojjhaṅga*s," and so forth. Because the *bojjhaṅga* (enlightenment factor) is excellent or beautiful, it is *sambojjhaṅga* (perfect enlightenment factor). Thus, *sati* (mindfulness) itself is *satisambojjhaṅga* (mindfulness-enlightenment-factor). That is *satisambojjhaṅgaṃ* (mindfulness-enlightenment-factor). In this way, first, the ascertainment of just one initial term by way of the meaning, the characteristics, and so forth, should be understood.
*Satisambojjhaṅgaṃ*: Furthermore, in the case of the four noble truths, *dhammavicayo* is discriminating the truths.

Moreover, it has the characteristic of investigation, the taste of illumination, and the manifestation of non-confusion.

*Vīriyaṃ*: Because of the nature of heroism, and because it should be exerted methodically.

That has the characteristic of striving, the taste of support, and the manifestation of non-collapse.

*Pīti*: It pleases.

It has the characteristic of pervading, or the characteristic of satisfaction, the taste of pleasing body and mind, and the manifestation of the elation of those same [body and mind].

*Passaddhi*: Because of the calming of the agitation of body and mind.

It has the characteristic of tranquility, the taste of suppressing the agitation of body and mind, and the manifestation of the coolness that is the state of non-trembling of the mind.

*Samādhi*: Because of concentration.

It has the characteristic of non-distraction, or the characteristic of non-dispersion, the taste of unification of consciousness and mental factors, and the manifestation of the stability of mind.

*Upekkhā*: Because of equanimity.

It has the characteristic of reflection, or the characteristic of even-handedness, the taste of preventing deficiency and excess, or the taste of cutting off partiality, and the manifestation of the state of equilibrium.

The rest is as already stated.

In this way, the exposition of the remaining terms should be known in terms of their meaning, characteristics, and so on.

*Dhammavicayo*, *vīriyaṃ*, *pīti*, *passaddhi*, *samādhi*, *upekkhā*. Moreover, concerning the order (*kamato*), it is said, "Mindfulness, monks, I declare is always useful" (*satiñca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṃ vadāmīti*). Because mindfulness (*satisambojjhaṅga*) is helpful to all the remaining awakening factors, it is mentioned first.

After that, in accordance with the principle of "Thus, while living mindfully, he investigates that Dhamma with wisdom" (*so tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinatītiādinā*), the purpose of the order of the remaining awakening factors has already been stated in the Sutta.

In this way, the explanation should also be understood in terms of its order.

Why, when the Blessed One stated the seven awakening factors, [did he say they were] neither deficient nor excessive (*anūnādhikato ti kasmā pana bhagavatā satteva bojjhaṅgā vuttā anūnā anadhikāti*)?

Because of being opposed to lethargy and agitation, and because of being universally applicable.

Here, three awakening factors are opposed to lethargy.

As it is said: "On an occasion, monks, when the mind becomes sluggish (*yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti*), it is the right time to develop the awakening factor of discrimination of states, the awakening factor of energy, and the awakening factor of joy (*dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāyā*)."

Three are opposed to agitation.

As it is said: "On an occasion, monks, when the mind becomes agitated (*yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ hoti*), it is the right time to develop the awakening factor of tranquility, the awakening factor of concentration, and the awakening factor of equanimity (*passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāyā*)."

But one here is universally applicable.

As it is said: "Mindfulness, monks, I declare is always useful" (*satiñca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṃ vadāmīti*).
"‘‘Sabbatthaka’’ntipi pāṭho," is also a reading, meaning that in both cases, "sabbattha" is intended.

Thus, because of being opposed to dullness and distraction, and because of being "sabbatthika" (applicable in all cases), only seven factors of enlightenment are mentioned, not less and not more. In this regard, the distinction between "anūnādhikato" (not less and not more) should be understood.

Having thus understood the meaning of only the first words of the seven factors mentioned in the method beginning with "‘‘satisambojjhaṅga’," now in "bhāveti vivekanissita," etc., it should be understood thus:

"Bhāveti" means develops, increases, repeatedly generates, brings into being in one's own mind-stream. This is the meaning.

"Vivekanissita" means dependent on detachment.

"Viveko" means separateness, distinction.

Now, this is fivefold: momentary detachment, detachment by suppression, detachment by eradication, detachment by tranquility, and detachment by escape.

Its variety should be understood by the method mentioned in "ariyadhamme avinīto."

This itself is what is stated there as discipline (vinaya).

Thus, in this fivefold detachment,

"Vivekanissita" means that the mindfulness enlightenment factor is developed dependent on momentary detachment, dependent on detachment by eradication, and dependent on detachment by escape. This meaning should be understood.

Thus, this yogi, engaged in developing the enlightenment factors, at the moment of insight, develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor dependent on momentary detachment in terms of function, dependent on detachment by escape in terms of intention, at the time of the path, dependent on detachment by eradication in terms of function, and dependent on detachment by escape in terms of object.

Some say "dependent on fivefold detachment." They highlight the enlightenment factors not only at the moment of powerful insight, path, and fruition, but also in the kasina jhānas that are the basis of insight, in mindfulness of breathing, in the unattractive, and in the brahma-vihāra jhānas.

And it is not refuted by the Aṭṭhakathā teachers.

Therefore, in their opinion, at the moment of the arising of these jhānas, it is dependent on detachment by suppression in terms of function.

And just as it is said "at the moment of insight, dependent on detachment by escape in terms of intention," so it is fitting to say that it also develops dependent on detachment by tranquility.

This method also applies to "virāganissitā" (dependent on detachment), and so on.

For detachment, etc., are in the sense of detachment.

Here, however, "vossaggo" (relinquishment) is twofold: relinquishment by abandonment (pariccāgavossaggo) and relinquishment by inclination (pakkhandanavossaggo).

There, "pariccāgavossaggo" means the abandoning of defilements at the moment of insight in terms of momentariness, and at the moment of the path in terms of eradication.

"Pakkhandanavossaggo" means inclining towards it at the moment of insight, and inclining towards *nirvāṇa* by making it the object at the moment of the path.

Both of these are suitable in this method of explaining the meaning mixed with the mundane and supramundane.

Thus, this mindfulness enlightenment factor, in the manner stated, abandons defilements and inclines towards *nirvāṇa*.

"Vossaggapariṇāmi" (maturing in relinquishment): by this entire statement, it means transforming into relinquishment, transformed, ripening, and ripened.

This is what is said: "Indeed, this bhikkhu, engaged in developing the enlightenment factors, just as the mindfulness enlightenment factor ripens into relinquishment by abandoning defilements and into relinquishment by inclining towards *nirvāṇa*, and just as it is ripened, so he develops it."

This method applies to the remaining enlightenment factors.

Here, however, only *nirvāṇa* is called "viveko" (detachment) because it is separate from all conditioned things, "virāgo" (dispassion) because of the state of dispassion of all, and "nirodho" (cessation) because of the state of cessation.

And only the path matures in relinquishment; therefore, the mindfulness enlightenment factor, having made detachment the object, is "vivekanissita" (dependent on detachment) because of its arising.

Similarly, "virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ" (dependent on dispassion, dependent on cessation).
And that, with the arising of the moment of the noble path, due to the destruction of the defilements, and by way of relinquishment, and by way of inclining towards *nirvāṇa*, is transformed and matures; this meaning should be seen.

And so with the rest of the enlightenment factors (*bojjhaṅga*).

Discernment (*viveko*), dispassion (*virāgo*), cessation (*nirodho*), dependent on dispassion (*virāganissitaṃ*), dependent on cessation (*nirodhanissitaṃ*), whatever of these factors of enlightenment (*bojjhaṅga*) there may be.

The rest is as already stated.

Here, however, with the arising of the pollutants (*āsava*), because these enlightenment factors (*bojjhaṅga*) connected with the three higher paths have not been developed, whatever pollutants (*āsava*) might arise—the pollutant of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*), the pollutant of existence (*bhavāsava*), and the pollutant of ignorance (*avijjāsava*)—these three pollutants (*āsava*) do not exist for one who cultivates [the path] in this way; this method should be understood.

These are called... cultivating is to be abandoned (*bhāvanā pahātabbā*)—these three pollutants (*āsava*) are to be abandoned by this cultivation of the enlightenment factors (*bojjhaṅga*) connected with the three paths; thus it is said and should be understood.

These are called... cultivating is to be abandoned (*bhāvanā pahātabbā*).

mula_pali:
28. ‘‘Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ye āsavā dassanā pahātabbā te dassanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā te saṃvarā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā te paṭisevanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā te adhivāsanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā te parivajjanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā te vinodanā pahīnā honti, ye āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā te bhāvanā pahīnā honti; ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave – ‘bhikkhu sabbāsavasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati, acchecchi acchejji (ka.) taṇhaṃ, vivattayi vāvattayi (sī. pī.) saṃyojanaṃ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā’’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Sabbāsavasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
“Now when, monks, a monk's *āsavas* (effluents, taints, corruptions) that should be abandoned by seeing have been abandoned by seeing, his *āsavas* that should be abandoned by restraining (*saṃvara*) have been abandoned by restraining, his *āsavas* that should be abandoned by using (*paṭisevanā*) have been abandoned by using, his *āsavas* that should be abandoned by tolerating (*adhivāsanā*) have been abandoned by tolerating, his *āsavas* that should be abandoned by avoiding (*parivajjanā*) have been abandoned by avoiding, his *āsavas* that should be abandoned by destroying (*vinodanā*) have been abandoned by destroying, his *āsavas* that should be abandoned by developing (*bhāvanā*) have been abandoned by developing; it is said of him, monks: ‘This monk dwells restrained with all *āsava*-restraint (*sabbāsavasaṃvarasaṃvuto*); he has cut off craving (*taṇhaṃ*), severed the fetter (*saṃyojanaṃ*), and through the right penetration of conceit (*sammā mānābhisamayā*) has made an end of suffering (*dukkhassa*).’”

This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those monks delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Sabbāsavasuttaṃ, the second, is finished.
commentary_pali:
28. Idāni imehi sattahākārehi pahīnāsavaṃ bhikkhuṃ thomento āsavappahāne cassa ānisaṃsaṃ dassento eteheva ca kāraṇehi āsavappahāne sattānaṃ ussukkaṃ janento yato kho, bhikkhave…pe… antamakāsi dukkhassāti āha. Tattha yato khoti sāmivacane tokāro, yassa khoti vuttaṃ hoti. Porāṇā pana yasmiṃ kāleti vaṇṇayanti. Ye āsavā dassanā pahātabbāti ye āsavā dassanena pahātabbā, te dassaneneva pahīnā honti, na appahīnesuyeva pahīnasaññī hoti. Evaṃ sabbattha vitthāro.

Sabbāsavasaṃvarasaṃvutoti sabbehi āsavapidhānehi pihito, sabbesaṃ vā āsavānaṃ pidhānehi pihito. Acchecchitaṇhanti sabbampi taṇhaṃ chindi, saṃchindi samucchindi. Vivattayi saṃyojananti dasavidhampi saṃyojanaṃ parivattayi nimmalamakāsi. Sammāti hetunā kāraṇena. Mānābhisamayāti mānassa dassanābhisamayā pahānābhisamayā ca. Arahattamaggo hi kiccavasena mānaṃ passati, ayamassa dassanābhisamayo. Tena diṭṭho pana so tāvadeva pahīyati diṭṭhavisena diṭṭhasattānaṃ jīvitaṃ viya. Ayamassa pahānābhisamayo.

Sabbāsavasaṃvarasaṃvuto Acchecchi taṇha saṃyojana Sammā Mānābhisamayā

Antamakāsi dukkhassāti evaṃ arahattamaggena sammā mānassa diṭṭhattā pahīnattā ca ye ime ‘‘kāyabandhanassa anto jīrati (cūḷava. 278). Haritantaṃ vā’’ti (ma. ni. 1.304) evaṃ vuttaantimamariyādanto ca, ‘‘antamidaṃ, bhikkhave, jīvikāna’’nti (itivu. 91; saṃ. ni. 3.80) evaṃ vuttalāmakanto ca, ‘‘sakkāyo eko anto’’ti (a. ni. 6.61) evaṃ vuttakoṭṭhāsanto ca, ‘‘esevanto dukkhassa sabbapaccayasaṅkhayā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 2.51) evaṃ vuttakoṭanto cāti evaṃ cattāro antā, tesu sabbasseva vaṭṭadukkhassa antaṃ catutthakoṭisaṅkhātaṃ antimakoṭisaṅkhātaṃ antamakāsi paricchedaṃ parivaṭumaṃ akāsi. Antimasamussayamattāvasesaṃ dukkhaṃ akāsīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Antamakāsi dukkhassā

Attamanā te bhikkhūti sakamanā tuṭṭhamanā, pītisomanassehi vā sampayuttamanā hutvā. Bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti idaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyāpariyosānaṃ bhagavato bhāsitaṃ sukathitaṃ sulapitaṃ, evametaṃ bhagavā evametaṃ sugatāti matthakena sampaṭicchantā abbhanumodiṃsūti.

Attamanā te bhikkhū Bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandu

Sesamettha yaṃ na vuttaṃ, taṃ pubbe vuttattā ca suviññeyyattā ca na vuttaṃ. Tasmā sabbaṃ vuttānusārena anupadaso paccavekkhitabbaṃ.

Bhāvanāpahātabbaāsavavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Sabbāsavasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
28. Now, praising the *bhikkhu* who has eliminated the āsavas with these seven characteristics, showing the benefits of eliminating the āsavas, and arousing enthusiasm in beings for eliminating the āsavas with these very reasons, he said, "When, *bhikkhus*...pe...made an end to suffering."

There, *yato kho* is the *tokāra* in the sense of emphasis, meaning *yassa kho*. However, the ancients describe it as *yasmiṃ kāle*.

*ye āsavā dassanā pahātabbā* means those āsavas that should be eliminated by seeing; they are eliminated by seeing alone; he is not under the impression that they are eliminated when they are not eliminated. Thus, the expansion [of the meaning] is everywhere.

*sabbāsavasaṃvarasaṃvuto* means covered by all the restraints on the outflows, or covered by the restraints on all the outflows.

*acchecchi taṇhaṃ* means he cut off all craving, he completely cut off, he thoroughly cut off.

*vivattayi saṃyojanaṃ* means he turned away from the ten kinds of fetters and made them spotless.

*sammā* means by reason, by cause.

*mānābhisamayā* means by seeing and eliminating conceit.

Indeed, the path of an *arhat* sees conceit as a function; this is his seeing. But by that which is seen, it is immediately eliminated, like the life of beings seen by poison. This is his elimination.

*sabbāsavasaṃvarasaṃvuto acchecchi taṇhaṃ saṃyojana sammā mānābhisamayā*

*antamakāsi dukkhassā* means thus, by the path of *arhatship*, because of the correct seeing and eliminating of conceit, these are the limits which were spoken: "The end of the body decays" (Cuḷava. 278). "Or green stalk" (ma. ni. 1. 304) Thus, the end of the ultimate limit, and "This is the end, *bhikkhus*, of livelihoods" (itivu. 91; saṃ. ni. 3. 80) Thus, the end of gain that was spoken, and "The aggregate is one end" (a. ni. 6. 61) Thus, the end of the divisions that were spoken, and "This is the end of suffering by the destruction of all conditions" (saṃ. ni. 2. 51) Thus, the spoken final end, thus, there are four ends, among those, the end of all cyclical suffering, the fourth category, the final category, made an end, a limit, a boundary. It is said that he made the remaining suffering only the measure of the final accumulation.

*antamakāsi dukkhassā*

*attamanā te bhikkhū* means with their own minds, delighted minds, or having minds conjoined with joy and happiness.

*bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandu* means this consummation of the ending of suffering, the speech of the Blessed One is well spoken, well uttered, accepting with the top of their heads, they rejoiced.

*attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandu*
Whatever remains unsaid here, was not said because it was already said earlier and because it is easily understood. Therefore, everything should be examined step by step according to what has been said.

The explanation of the cankers to be abandoned by cultivation is finished.

The explanation of the Sabbāsava Sutta is finished in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the Majjhimanikāya.

mula_pali:
29. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā. Atthi me tumhesu anukampā – ‘kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’ti. Tumhe ca me, bhikkhave, āmisadāyādā bhaveyyātha no dhammadāyādā, tumhepi tena ādiyā ādissā (sī. syā. pī.) bhaveyyātha – ‘āmisadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no dhammadāyādā’ti; ahampi tena ādiyo bhaveyyaṃ – ‘āmisadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no dhammadāyādā’ti. Tumhe ca me, bhikkhave, dhammadāyādā bhaveyyātha, no āmisadāyādā, tumhepi tena na ādiyā bhaveyyātha – ‘dhammadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no āmisadāyādā’ti; ahampi tena na ādiyo bhaveyyaṃ – ‘dhammadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no āmisadāyādā’ti. Tasmātiha me, bhikkhave, dhammadāyādā bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā. Atthi me tumhesu anukampā – ‘kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’ti.

ādissā (sī. syā. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Savatthi in the Jetavana at Anathapindika’s monastery.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: "Bhikkhus."

"Venerable sir," those bhikkhus replied to the Fortunate One.

The Blessed One said this:

“Be my heirs in the Dhamma, bhikkhus, not my heirs in material things ( *āmiṣadāyādā* ). Out of compassion for you I have thought: ‘How shall my disciples be my heirs in the Dhamma, not my heirs in material things?’

If you are my heirs in material things, bhikkhus, not my heirs in the Dhamma, you will be reproached thus: ‘The Teacher’s disciples live as his heirs in material things, not as heirs in the Dhamma’; and I will be reproached thus: ‘The Teacher’s disciples live as his heirs in material things, not as his heirs in the Dhamma.’

If you are my heirs in the Dhamma, bhikkhus, not my heirs in material things, you will not be reproached as it will be said: ‘The Teacher’s disciples live as his heirs in the Dhamma, not as his heirs in material things’; and I will not be reproached as it will be said: ‘The Teacher’s disciples live as his heirs in the Dhamma, not as his heirs in material things.’

Therefore, bhikkhus, be my heirs in the *dharma*, not my heirs in material things. Out of compassion for you I have thought: ‘How shall my disciples be my heirs in the Dhamma, not my heirs in material things?’
commentary_pali:
29.Evaṃme sutanti dhammadāyādasuttaṃ. Yasmā panassa aṭṭhuppattiko nikkhepo, tasmā taṃ dassetvā vassa apubbapadavaṇṇanaṃ karissāma. Katarāya ca panidaṃ aṭṭhuppattiyā nikkhittanti. Lābhasakkāre. Bhagavato kira mahālābhasakkāro uppajji. Yathā taṃ cattāro asaṅkhyeyye pūritadānapāramīsañcayassa. Sabbadisāsu yamakamahāmegho vuṭṭhahitvā mahoghaṃ viya sabbapāramiyo ekasmiṃ attabhāve vipākaṃ dassāmāti sampiṇḍitā viya lābhasakkāramahoghaṃ nibbattayiṃsu. Tato tato annapānayānavatthamālāgandhavilepanādihatthā khattiyabrāhmaṇādayo āgantvā – ‘‘kahaṃ buddho, kahaṃ bhagavā, kahaṃ devadevo, narāsabho, purisasīho’’ti bhagavantaṃ pariyesanti. Sakaṭasatehipi paccaye āharitvā okāsaṃ alabhamānā samantā gāvutappamāṇampi sakaṭadhurena sakaṭadhuramāhaccatiṭṭhanti ceva anubandhanti ca. Andhakavindabrāhmaṇādayo viya. Sabbaṃ khandhake tesu tesu suttesu ca āgatanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Yathā ca bhagavato, evaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassāpi.

Vuttampi cetaṃ – ‘‘tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ, bhikkhusaṅghopi kho sakkato hoti…pe… parikkhārāna’’nti (udā. 14). Tathā – ‘‘yāvatā kho, cunda, etarahi saṅgho vā gaṇo vā loke uppanno, nāhaṃ, cunda, aññaṃ ekasaṅghampi samanupassāmi, evaṃ lābhaggayasaggapattaṃ, yathariva, cunda, bhikkhusaṅgho’’ti (dī. ni. 3.176).

Svāyaṃ bhagavato ca bhikkhusaṅghassa ca uppanno lābhasakkāro ekato hutvā dvinnaṃ mahānadīnaṃ udakamiva appameyyo ahosi. Kamena bhikkhū paccayagarukā paccayabāhulikā ahesuṃ.
