Pacchābhattampi telamadhuphāṇitādīsu āhaṭesu gaṇḍiṃyeva paharitvā ‘‘amhākaṃ ācariyassa detha, upajjhāyassa dethā’’ti uccāsaddamahāsaddaṃ karonti. Sā ca nesaṃ pavatti bhagavatopi pākaṭā ahosi. Tato bhagavā ananucchavikanti dhammasaṃvegaṃ uppādetvā cintesi –

‘‘Paccayā akappiyāti na sakkā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapetuṃ. Paccayapaṭibaddhā hi kulaputtānaṃ samaṇadhammavutti. Handāhaṃ dhammadāyādapaṭipadaṃ desemi. Sā sikkhākāmānaṃ kulaputtānaṃ sikkhāpadapaññatti viya bhavissati nagaradvāre ṭhapitasabbakāyikaādāso viya ca, yathā hi nagaradvāre ṭhapite sabbakāyike ādāse cattāro vaṇṇā attano chāyaṃ disvā vajjaṃ pahāya niddosā honti, evameva sikkhākāmā kulaputtā payogamaṇḍanena attānaṃ maṇḍetukāmā imaṃ sabbakāyikādāsūpamaṃ desanaṃ āvajjitvā āmisadāyādapaṭipadaṃ vajjetvā dhammadāyādapaṭipadaṃ pūrentā khippameva jātijarāmaraṇassa antaṃ karissantī’’ti. Imissā aṭṭhuppattiyā idaṃ suttaṃ abhāsi.

Tattha dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādāti dhammassa me dāyādā, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisassa. Yo mayhaṃ dhammo, tassa paṭiggāhakā bhavatha, yañca kho mayhaṃ āmisaṃ, tassa mā paṭiggāhakā bhavathāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha dhammopi duvidho – nippariyāyadhammo, pariyāyadhammoti. Āmisampi duvidhaṃ – nippariyāyāmisaṃ, pariyāyāmisanti. Kathaṃ? Maggaphalanibbānabhedo hi navavidhopi lokuttaradhammo nippariyāyadhammo nibbattitadhammo, na yena kenaci pariyāyena kāraṇena vā lesena vā dhammo. Yaṃ panidaṃ vivaṭṭūpanissitaṃ kusalaṃ, seyyathidaṃ, idhekacco vivaṭṭaṃ patthento dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti, gandhamālādīhi vatthupūjaṃ karoti, dhammaṃ suṇāti deseti jhānasamāpattiyo nibbatteti, evaṃ karonto anupubbena nippariyāyadhammaṃ amataṃ nibbānaṃ paṭilabhati, ayaṃ pariyāyadhammo. Tathā cīvarādayo cattāro paccayā nippariyāyāmisameva, na aññena pariyāyena kāraṇena vā lesena vā āmisaṃ. Yaṃ panidaṃ vaṭṭagāmikusalaṃ, seyyathidaṃ, idhekacco vaṭṭaṃ patthento sampattibhavaṃ icchamāno dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiyo nibbatteti, evaṃ karonto anupubbena devamanussasampattiṃ paṭilabhati, idaṃ pariyāyāmisaṃ nāma.

dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā nippariyāyadhammo pariyāyadhammo nippariyāyāmisameva, pariyāyāmisaṃ

Tattha nippariyāyadhammopi bhagavatoyeva santako. Bhagavatā hi kathitattā bhikkhū maggaphalanibbānāni adhigacchanti. Vuttampi cetaṃ ‘‘so hi brāhmaṇa bhagavā anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā, asañjātassa maggassa sañjanetā, anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā, maggaññū maggavidū maggakovido. Maggānugā ca pana etarahi sāvakā viharanti pacchā samannāgatā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.79) ca – ‘‘so hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato’’ti (ma. ni. 1.203) ca. Pariyāyadhammopi bhagavatoyeva santako. Bhagavatā hi kathitattā evaṃ jānanti ‘‘vivaṭṭaṃ patthetvā dānaṃ dento…pe… samāpattiyo nibbattento anukkamena amataṃ nibbānaṃ paṭilabhatī’’ti. Nippariyāyāmisampi ca bhagavatoyeva santakaṃ. Bhagavatā hi anuññātattāyeva bhikkhūhi jīvakavatthuṃ ādiṃ katvā paṇītacīvaraṃ laddhaṃ. Yathāha ‘‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gahapaticīvaraṃ. Yo icchati, paṃsukūliko hotu, yo icchati, gahapaticīvaraṃ sādiyatu. Itarītarenapāhaṃ, bhikkhave, santuṭṭhiṃyeva vaṇṇemī’’ti (mahāva. 337).

Pubbe ca bhikkhū paṇītapiṇḍapātaṃ nālatthuṃ. Sapadānapiṇḍiyālopabhojanā evāhesuṃ. Tehi rājagahe viharantena bhagavatā – ‘‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghabhattaṃ uddesabhattaṃ nimantanaṃ salākabhattaṃ pakkhikaṃ uposathikaṃ pāṭipadika’’nti (cūḷava. 325) evaṃ anuññātattāyeva paṇītabhojanaṃ laddhaṃ. Tathā senāsanaṃ. Pubbe hi akatapabbhārarukkhamūlādisenāsanāyeva bhikkhū ahesuṃ. Te ‘‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca leṇānī’’ti (cūḷava. 294) evaṃ bhagavatā anuññātattāyeva vihāro aḍḍhayogo pāsādo hammiyaṃ guhāti imāni senāsanāni labhiṃsu. Pubbe ca muttaharītakeneva bhesajjaṃ akaṃsu. Te bhagavatāyeva – ‘‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca bhesajjāni, seyyathidaṃ, sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇita’’nti (mahāva. 260) evamādinā nayena anuññātattā nānābhesajjāni labhiṃsu.

Pariyāyāmisampi bhagavatoyeva santakaṃ. Bhagavatā hi kathitattā yeva jānanti – ‘‘sampattibhavaṃ patthento dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ…pe… samāpattiyo nibbattetvā anukkamena pariyāyāmisaṃ dibbasampattiṃ manussasampattiṃ paṭilabhatī’’ti. Tadeva, yasmā nippariyāyadhammopi pariyāyadhammopi nippariyāyāmisampi pariyāyāmisampi bhagavatoyeva santakaṃ, tasmā tattha attano sāmibhāvaṃ dassento āha – ‘‘dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha mā āmisadāyādā’’ti.

Yo mayhaṃ santako duvidhopi dhammo, tassa dāyādā bhavatha. Yañca kho etaṃ mayhameva santakaṃ āmisaṃ, tassa dāyādā mā bhavatha. Dhammakoṭṭhāsasseva sāmino bhavatha, mā āmisakoṭṭhāsassa. Yo hi jinasāsane pabbajitvā paccayaparamo viharati catūsu taṇhuppādesu sandissamāno nikkhittadhuro dhammānudhammappaṭipattiyaṃ, ayaṃ āmisadāyādo nāma. Tādisā mā bhavatha. Yo pana anuññātapaccayesu appicchatādīni nissāya paṭisaṅkhā sevamāno paṭipattiparamo viharati catūsu ariyavaṃsesu sandissamāno, ayaṃ dhammadāyādo nāma. Tādisā bhavathāti vuttaṃ hoti.

āmisadāyādo dhammadāyādo

Idāni yesaṃ tattha etadahosi, bhavissati vā anāgatamaddhānaṃ ‘‘kiṃ nu kho bhagavā sāvakānaṃ alābhatthiko evamāhā’’ti, tesaṃ atipaṇītalābhatthiko ahaṃ evaṃ vadāmīti dassetumāha atthi me tumhesu…pe… no āmisadāyādāti.

atthi me tumhesu…pe… no āmisadāyādā

Tassāyamattho – atthi me tumhesu anukampā anuddayā hitesitā, kena nu kho kāraṇena kena upāyena sāvakā dhammadāyādā assu dhammakoṭṭhāsasāmino, no āmisadāyādāti. Ayaṃ pana adhippāyo, passati kira bhagavā āmisagarukānaṃ āmise upakkhalitānaṃ atītakāle tāva kapilassa bhikkhuno, ‘‘saṅghāṭipi ādittā hotī’’tiādinā (pārā. 230; saṃ. ni. 2.218) nayena āgatapāpabhikkhubhikkhunīsikkhamānādīnañca anekasatānaṃ apāyaparipūraṇattaṃ attano sāsane pabbajitānañca devadattādīnaṃ. Dhammagarukānaṃ pana sāriputtamoggallānamahākassapādīnaṃ abhiññāpaṭisambhidādiguṇappaṭilābhaṃ. Tasmā tesaṃ apāyā parimuttiṃ sabbaguṇasampattiñca icchanto āha – ‘‘atthi me tumhesu anukampā kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’’ti. Paccayagaruko ca catuparisantare kūṭakahāpaṇo viya nibbutaṅgāro viya ca nittejo nippabho hoti. Tato vivattitacitto dhammagaruko tejavā sīhova abhibhuyyacārī, tasmāpi evamāha – ‘‘atthi me…pe… no āmisadāyādā’’ti.

Evaṃ ‘‘dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā’’ti idaṃ anukampāya paṇītataraṃ lābhaṃ icchantena vuttaṃ, no alābhatthikenāti sāvetvā idāni imassa ovādassa akaraṇe ādīnavaṃ dassento āha ‘‘tumhe ca me, bhikkhave…pe… no dhammadāyādā’’ti. Tattha tumhepi tena ādiyā bhaveyyāthāti tumhepi tena āmisadāyādabhāvena no dhammadāyādabhāvena ādiyā bhaveyyātha. Apadisitabbā visuṃ kātabbā vavatthapetabbā, viññūhi gārayhā bhaveyyāthāti vuttaṃ hoti. Kinti? Āmisadāyādā satthusāvakā viharanti, no dhammadāyādāti.

tumhepi tena ādiyā bhaveyyāthā

Ahampi tena ādiyo bhaveyyanti ahampi tena tumhākaṃ āmisadāyādabhāvena no dhammadāyādabhāvena gārayho bhaveyyaṃ. Kinti? Āmisa…pe… dāyādāti. Idaṃ bhagavā tesaṃ atīva mudukaraṇatthamāha. Ayañhi ettha adhippāyo – sace, bhikkhave, tumhe āmisalolā carissatha, tattha viññū maṃ garahissanti ‘‘kathañhi nāma sabbaññū samāno attano sāvake dhammadāyāde no āmisadāyāde kātuṃ na sakkotī’’ti. Seyyathāpi nāma anākappasampanne bhikkhū disvā ācariyupajjhāye garahanti ‘‘kassime saddhivihārikā, kassantevāsikā’’ti; seyyathā vā pana kulakumārake vā kulakumārikāyo vā dussīle pāpadhamme disvā mātāpitaro garahanti ‘‘kassime puttā, kassa dhītaro’’ti; evameva maṃ viññū garahissanti ‘‘kathañhi nāma sabbaññū samāno attano sāvake dhammadāyāde no āmisadāyāde kātuṃ na sakkotī’’ti.

Ahampi tena ādiyo bhaveyya

Evaṃ imassa ovādassa akaraṇe ādīnavaṃ dassetvā karaṇe ānisaṃsaṃ dassento tumhe ca metiādimāha. Tattha ahampi tena na ādiyo bhaveyyanti seyyathāpi nāma vattaparipūrake daharabhikkhū uddesaparipucchāsampanne vassasatikatthere viya ākappasampanne disvā, kassa saddhivihārikā, kassantevāsikāti, asukassāti, ‘‘patirūpaṃ therassa, paṭibalo vata ovadituṃ anusāsitu’’nti ācariyupajjhāyā na ādiyā na gārayhā bhavanti, evameva ahampi tena tumhākaṃ dhammadāyādabhāvena no āmisadāyādabhāvena kassa sāvakā nālakapaṭipadaṃ tuvaṭṭakapaṭipadaṃ candūpamapaṭipadaṃ rathavinītapaṭipadaṃ mahāgosiṅgasālapaṭipadaṃ mahāsuññatapaṭipadaṃ paṭipannā catupaccayasantosabhāvanārāmaariyavaṃsesu sakkhibhūtā paccayagedhato vivattamānasā abbhā muttacandasamā viharantīti; ‘‘samaṇassa gotamassā’’ti vutte ‘‘sabbaññū vata bhagavā, asakkhi vata sāvake āmisadāyādapaṭipadaṃ chaḍḍāpetvā dhammadāyādapaṭipattipūrake kātu’’nti viññūnaṃ na ādiyo na gārayho bhaveyyanti. Evamimasmiṃ pade adhippāyaṃ ñatvā sesaṃ kaṇhapakkhe vuttanayapaccanīkena veditabbaṃ. Evaṃ imassa ovādassa karaṇe ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā idāni taṃ ovādaṃ niyyātento āha – ‘‘tasmā tiha me, bhikkhave…pe… no āmisadāyādā’’ti.

tumhe ca me ahampi tena na ādiyo bhaveyya
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard: the *dhammadāyādasuttaṃ*.

Because in this case there is an occasion for [telling] the story of the origin [of this *sutta*], therefore, having shown that, we will make a [systematic] explanation of the series of words.

In which case did this origin occur?

In [connection with] gains and honors.

It seems that the Blessed One had a great accumulation of gains and honors.

Just as those four incalculable ones [accumulated merit] by fulfilling the perfection of giving.

Having risen up in all directions, like a great and paired cloud, and thinking "We will give a result in one lifetime to all perfections," and as if they were massed together, they produced a great flood of gains and honors.

Then, from here and there, nobles, Brahmins, and others, with their hands full of food, drink, vehicles, clothing, garlands, perfumes, ointments, etc., came and searched for the Blessed One, [saying] – “Where is the Buddha? Where is the Blessed One? Where is the god of gods, the best of men, the lion among men?”

Having brought hundreds of cartloads of requisites, and not getting space, they stood all around, even for the distance of a *gāvuta*, jostling cart-pole against cart-pole, and kept following along.

Like the Andhakavinda Brahmins and others.

Everything should be understood according to the method that has come down in the *khandhakas* and in those *suttas*.

Just as [it was] for the Blessed One, so also for the Saṅgha of monks.

Furthermore, this was said: "At that time, the Blessed One was respected, honored, esteemed, venerated, and revered; he obtained robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine as the requisites for the sick. The Saṅgha of monks was also respected…pe…requisites" (Udā. 14).

Similarly – "To the extent that now, Cunda, a Saṅgha or group has arisen in the world, I do not see any other Saṅgha, Cunda, that has attained such a peak of gains, status, and fame as this Saṅgha of monks" (Dī. Ni. 3.176).

This accumulation of gains and honors that arose for the Blessed One and for the Saṅgha of monks, having become one, was immeasurable, like the water of two great rivers.

Gradually, the monks became attached to requisites and indulged in them.

Even after the meal, when oil, honey, molasses, etc., were brought, they would strike the gong and shout, "Give [it] to our teacher! Give [it] to our preceptor!"

And that behavior of theirs was evident even to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, having aroused spiritual agitation [by saying] "This is not fitting," thought –

"It is not possible to establish a training rule [saying] that requisites are impermissible.

For the monastic life of those of good family is bound up with requisites.

Come now, let me teach the practice of being heirs to the Dharma.

That will be like the establishment of a training rule for those of good family who desire training, and like a mirror for viewing the whole body placed at the city gate. Just as, when a mirror for viewing the whole body is placed at the city gate, people of the four castes see their reflection, abandon faults, and become blameless, just so, those of good family who desire training, wishing to adorn themselves with the adornment of effort, having turned their attention to this teaching that is like a mirror for viewing the whole body, having avoided the practice of being heirs to material things, and fulfilling the practice of being heirs to the Dharma, will quickly make an end to birth, aging, and death."

This *sutta* was spoken on this occasion.

Therefore, “Be heirs to my Dharma, O monks; do not be heirs to material things”: Be heirs to my Dharma, O monks; do not be [heirs] to material things.

Whoever is an acceptor of my Dharma, be that; and whatever, indeed, is my material [support], do not be acceptors of that.

Therein, the Dharma is of two kinds – Dharma that is not circuitous, and Dharma that is circuitous.

Material things are also of two kinds – material things that are not circuitous, and material things that are circuitous.
How so? Indeed, although the supramundane *dharma*, distinguished by the path, the fruit, and nirvāṇa, is ninefold, it is a *nippariyāyadhamma*, a *dharma* that is brought about, not a *dharma* [arrived at] by any means, reason, or pretext.

But whatever merit is dependent on turning away [from the cycle of rebirth], for example, here someone, desiring to turn away, gives alms, undertakes precepts, performs the uposatha practice, makes offerings of objects with garlands of incense, etc., listens to and teaches the *dharma*, brings about meditative attainments; doing so, gradually he obtains the *nippariyāyadhamma*, the deathless, nirvāṇa: this is *pariyāyadhamma*.

Likewise, the four requisites, such as robes, are truly only *nippariyāyāmisa*, not material [goods] by any other means, reason, or pretext.

But whatever merit involves the round-trip, for example, here someone, desiring the round, wishing for fortunate existence, gives alms…brings about meditative attainments; doing so, gradually he obtains the good fortune of gods and humans: this is called *pariyāyāmisa*.

"Be my heirs in the *dharma*, monks, not heirs in material things!"

There, the *nippariyāyadhamma* also belongs to the Blessed One alone. For, having been spoken by the Blessed One, monks attain the path, the fruit, and nirvāṇa. And it has been said, "For the Blessed One, brahmin, is the producer of the unarisen path, the engenderer of the ungenerated path, the declarer of the undeclared path; he is the knower of the path, the finder of the path, the one skilled in the path. And now his disciples abide following the path and afterwards become endowed with it" (M.iii.79), and – "For knowing, friend, the Blessed One knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision, he is knowledge, he is the *dharma*, he is the holy one; he is the speaker, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the giver of the deathless, the lord of the *dharma*, the Tathāgata" (M.i.203).

The *pariyāyadhamma* also belongs to the Blessed One alone. For, having been spoken by the Blessed One, they know thus: "Giving alms desiring turning away…bringing about meditative attainments, one gradually obtains the deathless, nirvāṇa."

And the *nippariyāyāmisa* also belongs to the Blessed One alone. For, it is only because it has been permitted by the Blessed One that monks, starting with the things for life, have obtained excellent robes. As he said, "I allow you, monks, to use robe-cloth given by householders. Whoever wishes, let him be a rag-robe wearer; whoever wishes, let him accept robe-cloth from a householder. In both of these ways, monks, I praise contentment" (Mahāva.337).

Previously, monks did not obtain excellent almsfood. They were those who ate only morsels of food collected on alms round. Because the Blessed One, dwelling in Rajagaha, had permitted – "I allow you, monks, communal meals, designated meals, invitational meals, ticket meals, fortnightly meals, uposatha meals, and first-day meals" (Cūḷava.325) – they obtained excellent food.

Likewise, dwellings. Previously, monks were those who had only dwellings at the foot of trees, in unmade caves, etc. Because the Blessed One had permitted – "I allow you, monks, five kinds of lodgings" (Cūḷava.294) – they obtained these dwellings: a *vihāra*, an *aḍḍhayoga*, a *pāsāda*, a *hammiya*, and a cave.

Previously, they used only stale vegetables as medicine. Because the Blessed One himself had permitted – "I allow you, monks, five kinds of medicines, namely, ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses" (Mahāva.260) – in this way, they obtained various medicines.
Moreover, the Blessed One owns even the circumstantial material things.
For they know precisely because it was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘One desiring prosperity in future lives, having given a gift, [kept] morality,… having developed attainments, gradually obtains circumstantial material things, divine prosperity, [and] human prosperity’.
Therefore, since both the non-circumstantial Dharma and the circumstantial Dharma, and the non-circumstantial material things and the circumstantial material things belong to the Blessed One alone, therefore, showing his ownership there, he said: “Become my heirs in the Dharma, monks, not heirs in material things.”

Become heirs of that Dharma of both kinds which belongs to me.
Do not become heirs of that material thing which belongs only to me.
Become owners of the Dharma portion, not of the material portion.
For someone who, having gone forth in the Dispensation of the Conqueror, lives intent on requisites, appearing in the four instances of craving, having laid down the burden in the practice conforming to the Dharma, that one is called an heir in material things.
Do not be like that.
But someone who, relying on fewness of wishes and so on in the case of permitted requisites, making use of reflection, lives intent on practice, appearing in the four noble lineages, that one is called an heir in the Dharma.
It is said: Be like that.

Heir in material things, heir in the Dharma:
Now, to show those for whom that occurred there, or will occur in the future, ‘Why does the Blessed One say this as one desiring non-gain for his disciples?’, [that] I speak thus as one desiring very excellent gain, he said: “There is in me for you… not heirs in material things.”

There is in me for you… not heirs in material things:
The meaning of that is this: There is in me compassion, sympathy, a desire for welfare for you. By what cause, by what means should the disciples be heirs in the Dharma, owners of the Dharma portion, not heirs in material things?
But this is the intention: The Blessed One sees that in the past, even in the case of the monk Kapila who was attached to material things, slipped up in material things, ‘Even the outer robe is ablaze’ etc. (Pārā. 230; Saṃ. Ni. 2.218), and the filling up of the states of misery for many hundreds of wicked monks, nuns, female trainees and so on who had come by that way, and Devadatta and others who had gone forth in his Dispensation, but the obtaining of the qualities such as direct knowledges and analytical insights for Sāriputta, Moggallāna, Mahākassapa and others who were intent on the Dharma.
Therefore, wishing their release from the states of misery and the accomplishment of all qualities, he said: “There is in me compassion for you. How should my disciples be heirs in the Dharma, not heirs in material things?”
And one intent on requisites is without energy and without splendor in the midst of the four assemblies, like a counterfeit coin and like an ember without flame.
Then, one whose mind has turned away [from that], intent on the Dharma, is energetic, a lion, an overcomer in his conduct. Therefore, he said thus: “There is in me… not heirs in material things.”

Thus, having made it known that this statement “Become my heirs in the Dharma, monks, not heirs in material things” was spoken out of compassion by one desiring a more excellent gain, not by one desiring non-gain, now, showing the danger in not doing this advice, he said: “If you are my… not heirs in the Dharma.”
There, *if you are liable*: if you are liable, because of being heirs in material things, not because of being heirs in the Dharma.
It is said: You would be liable to be censured by wise people, to be pointed out, to be separated, to be distinguished.
How? The Teacher’s disciples live as heirs in material things, not as heirs in the Dharma.

*I also would be liable*: I also would be liable, because of your being heirs in material things, not because of being heirs in the Dharma.
How? Material things… heirs.
The Blessed One said this for the purpose of making them exceedingly gentle.
For this is the intention here: If, monks, you should wander about greedy for material things, then the wise will censure me, ‘How is it that, although he is omniscient, he does not exhort his own disciples"They are not able to make [their] heirs [only] in the Dharma, and not in material things."

Just as, upon seeing monks lacking proper conduct, preceptors and teachers criticize, saying, "Whose disciples are these? Whose students are these?" Or just as, when seeing young men or women of good families who are immoral and have bad habits, their parents criticize, saying, "Whose children are these, whose daughters are these?" Just so, the wise will criticize me, saying, "How could one who is said to be all-knowing, being like that, not be able to make his disciples heirs in the Dharma, and not in material things?"

"I, too, might be receptive because of that."

Thus, after showing the disadvantage of not doing this instruction, while showing the benefit of doing it, he said, "You and I," and so forth.

There, "I, too, might not be receptive because of that," just as, when seeing young monks who are complete in practice, who are accomplished in recitation and questioning, who are like elders of a hundred years standing, accomplished in conduct, one might ask, "Whose fellow practitioners are these? Whose students are these?" And they might say, "Belonging to so-and-so," [and think,] "They are a fitting image of the elders, truly capable of instructing and advising." Teachers and preceptors are neither receptive nor critical. Just so, I too, because of your being heirs in the Dharma, and not heirs in material things, [might be asked] whose disciples are these who have undertaken the path of the *tuvaṭṭaka*, the path resembling the moon (*candūpama*), the path of chariot-training (*rathavinīta*), the path of the Great Gosiṅga Sāla forest (*mahāgosiṅgasāla*), the path of great emptiness (*mahāśūnyata*), who are witnesses among the noble lineages, delighting in contentment with the four requisites, whose minds turn away from craving for conditions, dwelling like clouds, like the pure moon? Saying "Of the ascetic Gotama," the wise would [then] neither be receptive nor critical, [thinking,] "Truly, the Blessed One is all-knowing, capable of causing his disciples to abandon the path of heirs in material things and to complete the path of heirs in the Dharma!"

Having understood the meaning in this passage in this way, the remainder should be understood through the opposite method that was stated in the portion on the dark side.

Thus, having shown the benefit in doing this instruction, now, while concluding that instruction, he said: "Therefore, mendicants, because of that, I [have disciples who are] not heirs in material things."

"You and I" "I, too, might not be receptive because of that."

mula_pali:
30. ‘‘Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bhuttāvī assaṃ pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito suhito yāvadattho; siyā ca me piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo chaḍḍiyadhammo (sī. syā. pī.). Atha dve bhikkhū āgaccheyyuṃ jighacchādubbalya- jighacchādubballa (sī. pī.) paretā . Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadeyyaṃ – ‘ahaṃ khomhi, bhikkhave, bhuttāvī pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito suhito yāvadattho; atthi ca me ayaṃ piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo. Sace ākaṅkhatha, bhuñjatha, no ce tumhe bhuñjissatha sace tumhe na bhuñjissatha (sī. syā. pī.), idānāhaṃ appaharite vā chaḍḍessāmi, appāṇake vā udake opilāpessāmī’ti. Tatrekassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘bhagavā kho bhuttāvī pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito suhito yāvadattho; atthi cāyaṃ bhagavato piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo. Sace mayaṃ na bhuñjissāma, idāni bhagavā appaharite vā chaḍḍessati, appāṇake vā udake opilāpessati’ . Vuttaṃ kho panetaṃ bhagavatā – ‘dhammadāyādā me, bhikkhave, bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā’ti. Āmisaññataraṃ kho panetaṃ, yadidaṃ piṇḍapāto. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ abhuñjitvā imināva jighacchādubbalyena evaṃ imaṃ rattindivaṃ rattidivaṃ (ka.) vītināmeyya’’nti. So taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ abhuñjitvā teneva jighacchādubbalyena evaṃ taṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya. Atha dutiyassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘bhagavā kho bhuttāvī pavārito paripuṇṇo pariyosito suhito yāvadattho; atthi cāyaṃ bhagavato piṇḍapāto atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīyadhammo. Sace mayaṃ na bhuñjissāma, idāni bhagavā appaharite vā chaḍḍessati, appāṇake vā udake opilāpessati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā jighacchādubbalyaṃ paṭivinodetvā paṭivinetvā (sī. syā. pī.) evaṃ imaṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya’nti. So taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā jighacchādubbalyaṃ paṭivinodetvā evaṃ taṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya. Kiñcāpi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā jighacchādubbalyaṃ paṭivinodetvā evaṃ taṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya, atha kho asuyeva me purimo bhikkhu pujjataro ca pāsaṃsataro ca. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tañhi tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dīgharattaṃ appicchatāya santuṭṭhiyā sallekhāya subharatāya vīriyārambhāya saṃvattissati. Tasmātiha me, bhikkhave, dhammadāyādā bhavatha, mā āmisadāyādā. Atthi me tumhesu anukampā – ‘kinti me sāvakā dhammadāyādā bhaveyyuṃ, no āmisadāyādā’’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna vatvā (sī. pī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

vatvā (sī. pī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu
mula_english:
"30. “Here, *bhikkhus*, I might have eaten, finished my meal, be full, satisfied, and had what I needed; and there might be some almsfood left over, of a kind to be thrown away. Then two *bhikkhus* might come along, overcome by hunger and weakness. Then I might say this to them: ‘I, *bhikkhus*, have eaten, finished my meal, am full, satisfied, and have had what I needed; and there is this almsfood of mine left over, of a kind to be thrown away. If you wish, eat it; if you do not eat it, I shall throw it away where there is no greenery, or drop it into water where there is no life.’

"Then one *bhikkhu* might think: ‘The Blessed One has eaten, finished his meal, is full, satisfied, and has had what he needed; and there is this almsfood of the Blessed One left over, of a kind to be thrown away. If we do not eat it, the Blessed One will now throw it away where there is no greenery, or drop it into water where there is no life.’ But this has been said by the Blessed One: ‘*Bhikkhus*, be my heirs in the Dhamma, not my heirs in material things (āmiṣa).’ Now this almsfood (piṇḍapāta) is one of the material things. Suppose that instead of eating this almsfood I pass the night and day hungry and weak.’ And instead of eating that almsfood he passed that night and day hungry and weak.

“Then the second *bhikkhu* might think: ‘The Blessed One has eaten, finished his meal, is full, satisfied, and has had what he needed; and there is this almsfood of the Blessed One left over, of a kind to be thrown away. If we do not eat it, the Blessed One will now throw it away where there is no greenery, or drop it into water where there is no life. Suppose that I eat this almsfood and pass the night and day neither hungry nor weak.’ And after eating that almsfood he passed the night and day neither hungry nor weak.

“Now although that *bhikkhu* by eating that almsfood passed the night and day neither hungry nor weak, yet the first *bhikkhu* is more to be respected and commended by me. Why is that? Because that will for long conduce to his fewness of wishes (appicchatā), contentment (saṃtuṭṭhiyā), effacement (sallekhāya), easy support (subharatāya), and arousal of energy (vīriyārambhāya). Therefore, *bhikkhus*, be my heirs in Dhamma (dhammadāyādā), not my heirs in material things (āmisadāyādā). Out of compassion for you I have thought: ‘How shall my disciples be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things?’”

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Fortunate One got up from his seat and entered the monastery.
Having said (sī., pī.) in such places.
commentary_pali:
30. Evamimaṃ ovādaṃ niyyātetvā idāni tassā dhammadāyādapaṭipattiyā paripūrakāriṃ thometuṃ idhāhaṃ, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Bhagavato hi thomanaṃ sutvāpi hontiyeva tadatthāya paṭipajjitāro.

Tattha idhāti nipātapadametaṃ. Bhuttāvīti bhuttavā, katabhattakiccoti vuttaṃ hoti. Pavāritoti yāvadatthapavāraṇāya pavārito, yāvadatthaṃ bhuñjitvā paṭikkhittabhojano tittovāti vuttaṃ hoti. Catubbidhā hi pavāraṇā vassaṃvuṭṭhapavāraṇā paccayapavāraṇā anatirittapavāraṇā yāvadatthapavāraṇāti. Tattha, ‘‘anujānāmi bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tīhi ṭhānehi pavāretu’’nti (mahāva. 209) ayaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhapavāraṇā. ‘‘Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ catumāsaṃ bhesajjena pavāretu’’nti (pāci. 303) ca ‘‘aññatra punapavāraṇāya aññatra niccapavāraṇāyā’’ti (pāci. 307) ca ayaṃ paccayapavāraṇā. ‘‘Pavārito nāma asanaṃ paññāyati, bhojanaṃ paññāyati, hatthapāse ṭhito abhiharati, paṭikkhepo paññāyati, eso pavārito nāmā’’ti (pāci. 239) ayaṃ anatirittapavāraṇā. ‘‘Paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresī’’ti (dī. ni. 1.297, 358) ayaṃ yāvadatthapavāraṇā. Ayamidha adhippetā. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘pavāritoti yāvadatthapavāraṇāya pavārito’’ti.

idhā Bhuttāvī Pavārito vassaṃvuṭṭhapavāraṇā paccayapavāraṇā anatirittapavāraṇā yāvadatthapavāraṇā

Paripuṇṇoti bhojanena paripuṇṇo. Pariyositoti pariyositabhojano, uttarapadalopo daṭṭhabbo . Yāvatakaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ, tāvatakaṃ bhuttaṃ hoti, avasitā me bhojanakiriyāti attho. Suhitoti dhāto, jighacchādukkhābhāvena vā sukhitoti vuttaṃ hoti. Yāvadatthoti yāvatako me bhojanena attho, so sabbo pattoti. Ettha ca purimānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pacchimāni sādhakāni. Yo hi pariyosito, so bhuttāvī hoti. Yo ca suhito, so yāvadatthapavāraṇāya pavārito. Yo yāvadattho, so paripuṇṇoti. Purimāni vā pacchimānaṃ. Yasmā hi bhuttāvī, tasmā pariyosito. Yasmā pavārito, tasmā suhito. Yasmā paripuṇṇo, tasmā yāvadatthoti. Sabbañcetaṃ parikappetvā vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

Paripuṇṇo Pariyosito Suhito Yāvadattho

Siyāti ekaṃse ca vikappane ca. ‘‘Pathavīdhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.349) ekaṃse. ‘‘Siyā aññatarassa bhikkhuno āpatti vītikkamo’’ti (ma. ni. 3.39) vikappane. Idha ubhayampi vaṭṭati. Atirekova atirekadhammo. Tathā chaḍḍanīya dhammo. Adhiko ca chaḍḍetabbo ca, na aññaṃ kiñci kātabboti attho. Athāti tamhi kāle. Jighacchādubbalyaparetāti jighacchāya ca dubbalyena ca paretā phuṭṭhā anugatā ca aṭṭhapi dasapi divasāni. Tattha keci jighacchitāpi na dubbalā honti, sakkonti jighacchaṃ sahituṃ. Ime pana na tādisāti dassetuṃ ubhayamāha. Tyāhanti te ahaṃ. Sace ākaṅkhathāti yadi icchatha.

Siyā atirekadhammo chaḍḍanīya dhammo Athā Jighacchādubbalyaparetā Tyāha Sace ākaṅkhathā

Appahariteti apparuḷhaharite, yasmiṃ ṭhāne piṇḍapātajjhottharaṇena vinassanadhammāni tiṇāni natthi, tasminti attho. Tena nittiṇañca mahātiṇagahanaṃ ca, yattha sakaṭenapi chaḍḍite piṇḍapāte tiṇāni na vinassanti, tañca ṭhānaṃ pariggahitaṃ hoti. Bhūtagāmasikkhāpadassa hi avikopanatthametaṃ vuttaṃ.

Appaharite

Appāṇaketi nippāṇake piṇḍapātajjhottharaṇena maritabbapāṇakarahite vā mahāudakakkhandhe. Parittodake eva hi bhattapakkhepena āḷulite sukhumapāṇakā maranti, na mahātaḷākādīsūti. Pāṇakānurakkhaṇatthañhi etaṃ vuttaṃ. Opilāpessāmīti nimujjāpessāmi.

Appāṇake Opilāpessāmī

Tatrekassāti tesu dvīsu ekassa. Yo imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ suṭṭhu sutavā punappunaṃ āvajjeti ca , taṃ sandhāyāha vuttaṃ kho panetanti. Ayaṃ vutta-saddo kesohāraṇepi dissati ‘‘kāpaṭiko māṇavo daharo vuttasiro’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.426). Ropitepi ‘‘yathā sāradikaṃ bījaṃ, khette vuttaṃ virūhatī’’tiādīsu (jā. 1.3.31). Kathitepi ‘‘vuttamidaṃ bhagavatā, vuttamidaṃ arahatā’’tiādīsu. Idha pana kathite daṭṭhabbo. Kathitaṃ kho panetanti ayañhissa attho. Āmisaññataranti catunnaṃ paccayāmisānaṃ aññataraṃ, ekanti attho. Yadidanti nipāto, sabbaliṅgavibhattivacanesu tādisova tattha tattha atthato pariṇāmetabbo. Idha panāssa yo esoti attho. Yo eso piṇḍapāto nāma. Idaṃ āmisaññataranti vuttaṃ hoti. Yaṃnūnāhanti sādhu vatāhaṃ. Evanti yathā idāni imaṃ khaṇaṃ vītināmemi, evameva rattindivaṃ. Vītināmeyyanti khepeyyaṃ ativattāpeyyaṃ.

Tatrekassā vuttaṃ kho paneta vutta Āmisaññatara Yadida Yaṃnūnāha Eva Vītināmeyya

So taṃ piṇḍapātanti so taṃ sadevakena lokena sirasā sampaṭicchitabbarūpaṃ sugatātirittampi piṇḍapātaṃ abhuñjitvā dhammadāyādabhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamāno ādittasīsūpamaṃ paccavekkhitvā teneva jighacchādubbalyena evaṃ taṃ rattindivaṃ vītināmeyya.

So taṃ piṇḍapāta

Atha dutiyassāti imasmiṃ pana vāre esa saṅkhepo, sace so bhikkhu, yaṃnūnāhaṃ…pe… vītināmeyyanti cintento evampi cinteyya, pabbajitena kho vāḷamigākule araññe bhesajjaṃ viya pañcakāmaguṇavāḷākule gāme piṇḍapātopi dukkhaṃ pariyesituṃ. Ayaṃ pana piṇḍapāto iti pariyesanādīnavavimutto ca sugatātiritto cāti ubhato sujātakhattiyakumāro viya hoti, yehi ca pañcahi kāraṇehi piṇḍapāto na paribhuñjitabbo hoti. Seyyathidaṃ, puggalaṃ garahitvā na paribhuñjitabbo hoti ‘‘alajjipuggalassa santako’’ti. Aparisuddhauppattitāya na paribhuñjitabbo hoti ‘‘bhikkhuniparipācanaasantasambhāvanuppanno’’ti. Sāmikānukampāya na paribhuñjitabbo hoti ‘‘piṇḍapātasāmiko bhikkhu jighacchito’’ti. So dhāto tasseva antevāsikādīsu anukampāya na paribhuñjitabbo hoti ‘‘antevāsikā aññe vā tappaṭibaddhā jighacchitā’’ti, tepi dhātā suhitā, apica kho assaddhatāya na paribhuñjitabbo hoti ‘‘piṇḍapātasāmiko bhikkhu assaddho’’ti. Tehi ca kāraṇehi ayaṃ vimutto. Bhagavā hi lajjīnaṃ aggo, parisuddhuppattiko piṇḍapāto, bhagavā ca dhāto suhito, paccāsīsakopi añño puggalo natthi, ye loke saddhā, bhagavā tesaṃ aggoti evaṃ cintetvā ca so taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā…pe… vītināmeyya. Ettāvatā yopi abhuñjitvā samaṇadhammaṃ karoti, sopi bhuñjitabbakameva piṇḍapātaṃ na bhutto hoti. Yopi bhuñjitvā samaṇadhammaṃ karoti, sopi bhuñjitabbakameva bhutto hoti. Natthi piṇḍapāte viseso. Puggale pana atthi viseso. Tasmā taṃ dassento kiñcāpi sotiādimāha.

Atha dutiyassā kiñcāpi so

Tattha kiñcāpīti anujānanappasaṃsanatthe nipāto. Kiṃ anujānāti? Tassa bhikkhuno taṃ anavajjaparibhogaṃ. Kiṃ pasaṃsati? Bhutvā samaṇadhammakaraṇaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti yadipi so bhikkhu evaṃ bhuñjitabbameva bhuñjitvā kātabbameva kareyya. Atha kho asuyeva me purimo bhikkhūti yo purimo bhikkhu tampi piṇḍapātaṃ paṭikkhipitvā samaṇadhammaṃ karoti, soyeva mama dvīsu sūresu sūrataro viya dvīsu paṇḍitesu paṇḍitataro viya ca pujjataro ca pāsaṃsataro ca, dutiyabhikkhuto atirekena pūjanīyo ca pasaṃsanīyo cāti vuttaṃ hoti.

kiñcāpī Atha kho asuyeva me purimo bhikkhū

Idāni tamatthaṃ kāraṇena sādhento taṃ kissa hetūtiādimāha. Tassattho, tattha siyā tumhākaṃ, kasmā so bhikkhu bhagavato pujjataro ca pāsaṃsataro cāti? Tañhi tassāti yasmā taṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkhipanaṃ tassa bhikkhuno dīgharattaṃ appicchatāya…pe… vīriyārambhāya saṃvattissati. Kathaṃ? Tassa hi sace aparena samayena paccayesu atricchatā vā pāpicchatā vā mahicchatā vā uppajjissati. Tato naṃ iminā piṇḍapātapaṭikkhepaṅkusena nivāressati ‘‘are tvaṃ sugatātirittampi piṇḍapātaṃ paṭikkhipitvā īdisaṃ icchaṃ uppādesī’’ti evaṃ paccavekkhamāno. Esa nayo asantuṭṭhiyā asaṃlekhassa cuppannassa nivāraṇe. Evaṃ tāvassa appicchatāya santuṭṭhiyā saṃlekhāya saṃvattissati.

taṃ kissa hetū Tañhi tassā

Subharatāyāti ettha ayaṃ saṃvaṇṇanā – idhekacco attanopi upaṭṭhākānampi dubbharo hoti dupposo. Ekacco attanopi upaṭṭhākānampi subharo hoti suposo. Kathaṃ? Yo hi ambilādīni laddhā anambilādīni pariyesati, aññassa ghare laddhaṃ aññassa ghare chaḍḍento sabbaṃ gāmaṃ vicaritvā rittapattova vihāraṃ pavisitvā nipajjati, ayaṃ attano dubbharo. Yo pana sālimaṃsodanādīnaṃ patte pūretvā dinnepi dummukhabhāvaṃ anattamanabhāvameva ca dasseti, tesaṃ vā sammukhāva taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ ‘‘kiṃ tumhehi dinna’’nti apasādento sāmaṇeragahaṭṭhādīnampi deti , ayaṃ upaṭṭhākānaṃ dubbharo. Etaṃ disvā manussā dūrato parivajjanti dubbharo bhikkhu na sakkā positunti. Yo pana yaṃkiñci lūkhaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā laddhā tuṭṭhacittova bhuñjitvā vihāraṃ gantvā attano kammaṃ karoti, ayaṃ attano subharo. Yo ca paresampi appaṃ vā bahuṃ vā lūkhaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā dānaṃ ahīḷetvā attamano vippasannamukho hutvā tesaṃ sammukhāva paribhuñjitvā yāti, ayaṃ upaṭṭhākānaṃ subharo. Etaṃ disvā manussā ativiya vissatthā honti – ‘‘amhākaṃ bhadanto subharo thokenapi tussati, mayameva naṃ posissāmā’’ti paṭiññaṃ katvā posenti.

Subharatāyā

Tattha sace aparena samayena assa attano vā upaṭṭhākānaṃ vā dubbharatānayena cittaṃ uppajjissati. Tato naṃ iminā piṇḍapātapaṭikkhepaṅkusena nivāressati – ‘‘are tvaṃ sugatātirittampi piṇḍapātaṃ paṭikkhipitvā īdisaṃ cittaṃ uppādesī’’ti evaṃ paccavekkhamāno, evamassa subharatāya saṃvattissati. Sace panassa kosajjaṃ uppajjissati, tampi etenevaṅkusena nivāressati – ‘‘are tvaṃ nāma tadā sugatātirittampi piṇḍapātaṃ paṭikkhipitvā tathā jighacchādubbalyaparetopi samaṇadhammaṃ katvā ajja kosajjamanuyuñjasī’’ti evaṃ paccavekkhamāno, evamassa vīriyārambhāya saṃvattissati. Evamassa idaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkhipanaṃ dīgharattaṃ appicchatāya…pe… vīriyārambhāya saṃvattissati. Evamassime pañca guṇā paripūrā dasa kathāvatthūni paripūressanti.

Kathaṃ? Atra hi pāḷiyaṃyeva appicchatāsantuṭṭhitāvīriyārambhavasena tīṇi āgatāni, sesāni sallekhena saṅgahitāni. Idañhi sabbakathāvatthūnaṃ nāmameva, yadidaṃ sallekho. Yathāha – ‘‘yā ca kho ayaṃ, ānanda, kathā abhisallekhikā cetovinīvaraṇasappāyā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Seyyathidaṃ, appicchakathā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.189, 192) vitthāro. Evaṃ ime pañca guṇā paripūrā dasa kathāvatthūni paripūressanti. Dasa kathāvatthūni paripūrāni tisso sikkhā paripūressanti.

Kathaṃ? Etesu hi appicchakathā santosakathā asaṃsaggakathā sīlakathāti imā catasso kathā adhisīlasikkhāsaṅgahitāyeva . Pavivekakathā vīriyārambhakathā samādhikathāti imā tisso adhicittasikkhasaṅgahitā . Paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathāti imā tisso adhipaññāsikkhāsaṅgahitāti. Evaṃ dasa kathāvatthūni paripūrāni tisso sikkhā paripūressanti. Tisso sikkhā paripūrā pañca asekkhadhammakkhandhe paripūressanti.

Kathaṃ? Paripūrā hi adhisīlasikkhā asekkho sīlakkhandhoyeva hoti, adhicittasikkhā asekkho samādhikkhandho, adhipaññāsikkhā asekkhā paññā-vimutti-vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhā evāti evaṃ tisso sikkhā paripūrā pañca asekkhadhammakkhandhe paripūressanti. Pañca dhammakkhandhā paripūrā amataṃ nibbānaṃ paripūressanti. Seyyathāpi uparipabbate pāvussako mahāmegho abhivuṭṭho pabbatakandarasarasākhā paripūreti. Tā paripūrā kusobbhe, kusobbhā mahāsobbhe, mahāsobbhā kunnadiyo, kunnadiyo mahānadiyo, mahānadiyo mahāsamuddasāgaraṃ paripūrenti; evameva tassa bhikkhuno ime pañca guṇā paripūrā dasa kathāvatthuni ādiṃ katvā yāva amataṃ nibbānaṃ paripūressanti. Evamayaṃ bhikkhu dhammadāyādapaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno paramadhammadāyādaṃ labhatīti etamatthaṃ sampassamāno bhagavā ‘‘taṃ kissa hetu tañhi tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno’’tiādimāha.

Evaṃ tassa bhikkhuno pujjatarapāsaṃsatarabhāvaṃ kāraṇena sādhetvā idāni te bhikkhū tathattāya sanniyojento tasmā tiha me bhikkhavetiādimāha. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti, yasmā yo taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā samaṇadhammaṃ kareyya, so imehi pañcahi mūlaguṇehi paribāhiro. Yo pana abhuñjitvā kareyya, so imesaṃ bhāgī hoti – ‘‘tasmā tiha me, bhikkhave…pe… no āmisadāyādā’’ti.

tasmā tiha me bhikkhave

Idamavoca bhagavāti idaṃ nidānapariyosānato pabhuti yāva no āmisadāyādāti suttappadesaṃ bhagavā avoca. Idaṃ vatvāna sugatoti idañca suttappadesaṃ vatvāva sobhanāya paṭipadāya gatattā sugatoti saṅkhaṃ pattoyeva bhagavā. Uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisī paññattavarabuddhāsanato uṭṭhahitvā vihāraṃ attano mahāgandhakuṭiṃ pāvisi asambhinnāya eva parisāya. Kasmā dhammathomanatthaṃ.

Idamavoca bhagavā Idaṃ vatvāna sugato sugato Uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisī

Buddhā kira apariniṭṭhitāya desanāya vihāraṃ pavisantā dvīhi kāraṇehi pavisanti puggalathomanatthaṃ vā dhammathomanatthaṃ vā. Puggalathomanatthaṃ pavisanto evaṃ cintesi – ‘‘imaṃ mayā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddiṭṭhaṃ, vitthārena avibhattaṃ, dhammapaṭiggāhakā bhikkhū uggahetvā ānandaṃ vā kaccānaṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā pucchissanti, te mayhaṃ ñāṇena saṃsandetvā kathessanti, tato dhammapaṭiggāhakā puna maṃ pucchissanti, tesaṃ ahaṃ sukathitaṃ, bhikkhave, ānandena sukathitaṃ kaccānena, maṃ cepi tumhe etamatthaṃ puccheyyātha, ahampi naṃ evameva byākareyyanti evaṃ te puggale thomessāmi, tato tesu gāravaṃ janetvā bhikkhū upasaṅkamissanti, tepi bhikkhū atthe ca dhamme ca niyojessanti, te tehi niyojitā tisso sikkhā paripūrentā dukkhassantaṃ karissantī’’ti.

Dhammathomanatthaṃ pavisanto evaṃ cintesi, yathā idheva cintesi – ‘‘mayi vihāraṃ paviṭṭhe tameva āmisadāyādaṃ garahanto dhammadāyādañca thomento imissaṃyeva parisati nisinno sāriputto dhammaṃ desessati, evaṃ dvinnampi amhākaṃ ekajjhāsayāya matiyā desitā ayaṃ desanā aggā ca garukā ca bhavissati pāsāṇacchattasadisā. Caturoghanittharaṇaṭṭhena titthe ṭhapitā nāvā viya maggagamanaṭṭhena catuyuttaājaññaratho viya ca bhavissati. Yathā ca ‘evaṃ karontassa ayaṃ daṇḍo’ti parisati āṇaṃ ṭhapetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pāsādaṃ āruḷhe rājini tattheva nisinno senāpati taṃ raññā ṭhapitaṃ āṇaṃ pavatteti; evampi mayā ṭhapitaṃ desanaṃ imissaṃyeva parisati nisinno sāriputto thometvā desessati, evaṃ dvinnampi amhākaṃ matiyā desitā ayaṃ desanā balavatarā majjhanhikasūriyo viya pajjalissatī’’ti. Evamidha dhammathomanatthaṃ uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

Īdisesu ca ṭhānesu bhagavā nisinnāsaneyeva antarahito cittagatiyā vihāraṃ pavisatīti veditabbo. Yadi hi kāyagatiyā gaccheyya, sabbā parisā bhagavantaṃ parivāretvā gaccheyya, sā ekavāraṃ bhinnā puna dussannipātā bhaveyyāti bhagavā cittagatiyā eva pāvisi.
commentary_english:
Having thus conveyed this instruction, he (the Buddha) now, in order to praise the one who perfectly fulfills the practice of the Dharma-inheritance, said "Here, monks (bhikkhaves)," etc. For even upon hearing the Buddha's praise, there are those who undertake the practice for that purpose.

There, *idha* (here) is a particle. *Bhuttāvī* means having eaten, having finished the meal duties, it is said. *Pavārito* means having been invited by the *yāvadattha-pavāraṇā*, having eaten as much as needed, having refused food, being satisfied, it is said.

Indeed, there are four kinds of *pavāraṇā*: the *vassaṃvuṭṭha-pavāraṇā* (invitation at the end of the rains), the *paccaya-pavāraṇā* (invitation regarding requisites), the *an-atirikta-pavāraṇā* (invitation without excess), and the *yāvadattha-pavāraṇā* (invitation as much as needed).

There, "I allow, monks, that monks who have spent the rains invite with respect to three things" (Mahāva. 209), this is the *vassaṃvuṭṭha-pavāraṇā*.

"Venerable Sir, I wish to invite the Saṅgha to ask for tonics for four months" (Pāci. 303) and "except for another invitation, except for a constant invitation" (Pāci. 307), this is the *paccaya-pavāraṇā*.

"Being *pavārita* means eating is seen, cooked food is seen, it is brought forward within arm's reach, a refusal is seen, this is called being *pavārita*" (Pāci. 239), this is the *an-atirikta-pavāraṇā*.

"She served the Buddha and his monks with choice hard and soft food till they were satisfied" (Dī. Ni. 1.297, 358), this is the *yāvadattha-pavāraṇā*. This is what is intended here. Therefore, it was said, " *Pavārito* means having been invited by the *yāvadattha-pavāraṇā*."

*Paripuṇṇo* means full with food. *Pariyosito* means having finished eating, the elision of the later word should be noted. As much as should be eaten, that much has been eaten, the meaning is, "my eating activity is finished." *Suhito* means satisfied, it is said that he is happy due to the absence of the suffering of hunger. *Yāvadattho* means as much as I need with food, all of that has been obtained.

And here, the later three are proof of the former three. For whoever is *pariyosito* has eaten (*bhuttāvī*). And whoever is *suhito* is *pavārito* by the *yāvadattha-pavāraṇā*. Whoever is *yāvadattho* is *paripuṇṇo*.

Or the former are [proof] of the later. Since he has eaten (*bhuttāvī*), therefore he is *pariyosito*. Since he is *pavārito*, therefore he is *suhito*. Since he is *paripuṇṇo*, therefore he is *yāvadattho*. All of this should be understood as having been said conceptually.
*Siyā* means "may be" in the sense of one possibility, but also in the sense of an alternative. For example, "The earth element *siyā* (*syāt*) may be internal or external" (*pathavīdhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā*). And, "*siyā* (*syāt*) some *bhikkhu* might commit an offense or a transgression" (*siyā aññatarassa bhikkhuno āpatti vītikkamo*). Here, both apply.

*Atirekadhammo* is simply an additional quality. Likewise, *chaḍḍanīya dhammo* is a quality that should be rejected. That is, something additional should be discarded and nothing else done.

*Athā* means "at that time."

*Jighacchādubbalyaparetā* means overcome by hunger and weakness, touched and followed by hunger and weakness for eight or ten days. There, some, though hungry, are not weak; they are able to endure hunger. But to show that these are not like that, it says both.

*Tyāha* means "I say".

*Sace ākaṅkhathā* means "if you wish."

*Appaharite* means "where greenery is not overgrown," meaning in a place where there are no grasses that are liable to be destroyed by scattering alms food. Therefore, it means a place that is both devoid of grass and has thick grass, where the grasses will not be destroyed even if alms food is scattered by a cart. This is said for the sake of not disturbing beings.

*Appāṇake* means "without living beings," or in a great mass of water devoid of living beings liable to be killed by scattering alms food. For small creatures die when disturbed by scattering food in a small amount of water, but not in large lakes, etc. This is said for the sake of protecting living beings.

*Opilāpessāmī* means "I will cause to sink."

*Tatrekassā* means "of those two, to one."

"*Vuttaṃ kho paneta* ("but this was said") refers to one who has heard this teaching well and repeatedly reflects on it. The word *vutta* ("said") is also seen in the sense of hair removal, such as in "*kāpaṭiko māṇavo daharo vuttasiro*" ("a deceitful young man with a shaved head"). It is also seen in the sense of planting, such as in "*yathā sāradikaṃ bījaṃ, khette vuttaṃ virūhatī*" ("just as a seed sown in a field in autumn sprouts").
Even in statements like, “This was said by the Blessed One, this was said by the Worthy One,” the “said” (kathite) is to be understood here. However, “kathitaṃ kho panetaṃ” means “it was indeed said.”

*Āmisaññatara* means one of the four material requisites, that is, one. *Yadidaṃ* is an indeclinable particle that should be changed according to the meaning in each case, in all genders, cases, and numbers. But here, it means “yo eso” (that which). That is, what is called alms food. “Idaṃ āmisaññataraṃ” means this. *Yaṃnūnāhaṃ* means "sādhu vatāhaṃ" (it would be good if I...). *Evaṃ* means, just as I spend this moment now, so too the day and night. *Vītināmeyya* means “should spend, should pass."

*So taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ* means, not having eaten that alms food, which should be received with respect on the head by the world with its gods, and which is even more than the Sugata, desiring to be an heir to the Dharma, having reflected on the simile of the burning head, he should spend that day and night in this way with weakness from hunger.

*Atha dutiyassā* means, in this second instance, this is the summary: if that monk, thinking "it would be good if I…pe…should spend it," should think thus: for one gone forth, it is difficult to seek alms food in a village crowded with the five strands of sensual desire, like medicine in a forest crowded with wild animals. But this alms food is free from the dangers of seeking and is even more than the Sugata, like a well-born kṣatriya prince from both sides. And by these five reasons, alms food should not be consumed: that is, it should not be consumed criticizing the person, saying "it belongs to a shameless person." It should not be consumed because of impure origin, saying "it arose from the non-existent expectation of a nun cooking." It should not be consumed out of compassion for the owner, saying "the monk who owns the alms food is hungry." That donor should not be consumed out of compassion for his pupils, etc., saying, "the pupils or others related to him are hungry." Even those donors are content. Moreover, it should not be consumed out of lack of faith, saying "the monk who owns the alms food is faithless." And by these reasons, this is free. The Blessed One is the foremost of the modest, the alms food is of pure origin, the Blessed One and the donor are content, there is no other person who is hopeful, the Blessed One is the foremost of those in the world who have faith, thinking thus, he should eat that alms food…pe…he should spend it.

To this extent, even one who practices the ascetic life without eating, has not eaten alms food that should be eaten. Even one who practices the ascetic life after eating, has eaten what should be eaten. There is no difference in alms food. But there is a difference in persons. Therefore, showing that, he says, *kiñcāpi so* etc.

There, *kiñcāpi* is an indeclinable particle in the sense of permission and praise. What does he permit? That faultless use of that monk. What does he praise? Doing the ascetic life after eating. This is said: even if that monk, having eaten what should be eaten in this way, should do what should be done.

*Atha kho asuyeva me purimo bhikkhū* means: that former monk, even rejecting that alms food, practices the ascetic life, he alone is more heroic than the heroes in the two heroes, like a more wise person among the two wise people, more worthy of offerings and more praiseworthy, more worthy of honor and praise than the second monk, it is said.
Now, explaining that meaning with a reason, he says, beginning with, "What is the reason for that?"

The meaning of that is: How might it be for you there that this *bhikkhu* is more worthy of respect and praise than the Blessed One? Because that rejection of almsfood by that *bhikkhu* will lead to wanting little, and so forth, for a long time...to arousing energy.

How so? For if, at another time, excessive wanting, evil wanting, or great wanting should arise in him regarding the requisites, then, reflecting thus, he will ward it off with this goad of rejecting almsfood: "Hey, you! Having rejected even an abundance of almsfood from the Well-gone One, did you produce such a desire?"

This is the method for preventing discontent and lack of austerity that has arisen. In this way, it will lead to his wanting little, contentment, and austerity.

What is the reason for that? Because of its being easy to support. Here is the explanation: A certain person is difficult to support and hard to nourish, both for himself and for his attendants.

A certain person is easy to support and easy to nourish, both for himself and for his attendants.

How so? For one who, having received sour things and so forth, seeks non-sour things, discarding what was received in one house in another house, and wandering through the whole village, enters the monastery with an empty bowl and lies down—this one is difficult to support for himself.

But one who, even when his bowl is filled with choice rice, meat, and so forth, shows a face of gloomy sullenness and displeasure, and disparagingly gives that almsfood, saying in their presence, "What is this that you have given?", to novices or lay householders—this one is difficult to support for his attendants.

Seeing this, people keep far away, thinking, "A *bhikkhu* who is hard to support cannot be sustained."

But one who, having received any kind of almsfood, coarse or fine, eats it with a gladdened mind, goes to the monastery, and does his own work—this one is easy to support for himself.

And one who, even for others, having given a gift, small or large, coarse or fine, without disdain, being pleased in mind, with a serene face, eats it in their presence and then departs—this one is easy to support for his attendants.

Seeing this, people become exceedingly trusting, [thinking,] "Our venerable one is easy to support; he is content even with a little. We ourselves will sustain him," and having made a promise, they sustain him.

There, if at another time, a mind with a tendency toward being difficult to support should arise in him, either for himself or for his attendants, then, reflecting thus, he will ward it off with this goad of rejecting almsfood: "Hey, you! Having rejected even an abundance of almsfood from the Well-gone One, did you produce such a mind?" In this way, it will lead to his being easy to support.

If, moreover, laziness should arise in him, he will ward off even that with this goad: "Hey, you! Having at that time rejected even an abundance of almsfood from the Well-gone One, and having practiced the *śrāmaṇa* dharma even while overcome with hunger and weakness, are you today engaging in laziness?" Thus reflecting, it will lead to his arousing energy.

In this way, that rejection of almsfood by him will lead for a long time to wanting little...to arousing energy.

In this way, these five qualities of his being complete, they will completely fulfill the ten grounds for talk.

How so? Here, in the *Pāli* [canon] itself, three have come by way of wanting little, contentment, and arousing energy; the remaining ones are included by austerity.

For this is just the name of all the grounds for talk, namely, austerity.

As it was said: "And such talk, *Ānanda*, as deals with effacement, as favors the mind's release, and which leads to complete disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, and *Nirvāṇa*, that is, talk on wanting little," and so forth (*Majjhima Nikāya* 3.189, 192)—[this is] the detailed explanation.

In this way, these five qualities being complete, they will completely fulfill the ten grounds for talk.

The ten grounds for talk being complete, the three trainings will completely fulfill [them].

How so? Here, these four talks—talk on wanting little, talk on contentment, talk on aloofness from society, [and] talk on virtue—are included within the training in higher virtue.

These three talks—talk on seclusion, talk on arousing energy, [and] talk on meditative concentration—are included within the training in higher mind.

These three talks—talk on wisdom, talk on deliverance, [and] talk on the knowledge and vision of deliverance—are included within the training in higher wisdom.

In this way, the ten grounds for talk being complete, the three trainings will completely fulfill [them].
The three trainings, being complete, will completely fulfill the five aggregates of one beyond training ( *asekṣa-dharmāskandha*).

How so? Because the complete higher training in morality (*adhiśīla-śikṣā*) is the aggregate of morality of one beyond training; the higher training in mind (*adhicitta-śikṣā*) is the aggregate of meditation of one beyond training; the higher training in wisdom (*adhiprajñā-śikṣā*) is the aggregate of wisdom, liberation, the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Thus, the three trainings, being complete, will completely fulfill the five aggregates of one beyond training.

The five aggregates of the Dharma, being complete, will completely fulfill the deathless *nirvāṇa*.

Just as on the top of a mountain, a rain cloud, having rained, completely fills the mountain caves, ponds, streams, and branches;

Those being complete, [fill] small pools, the small pools fill large pools, the large pools fill small rivers, the small rivers fill large rivers, the large rivers fill the great ocean; just so, the five qualities of that *bhikṣu*, being complete, from the ten topics of discussion onward, up to the deathless *nirvāṇa*, will completely fulfill [them].

This *bhikṣu*, being one who has undertaken the practice that is the inheritance of the Dharma (*dhammadāyāda-paṭipadā*), obtains the supreme inheritance of the Dharma (*paramadhammadāyāda*). Seeing this meaning, the Blessed One said, "What is the cause? Because, *bhikṣus*, that is his," and so on.

Thus, having established the state of being worthy of offerings and praise of that *bhikṣu* by means of a cause, now, joining those *bhikṣus* to that very state, [he] said, "Therefore, *bhikṣus*..." and so on.

What was said? Because whoever, having eaten that alms food (*piṇḍapāta*), would do the practice of a *śramaṇa*, that one is excluded from these five root qualities (*mūlaguṇa*).

But whoever, without eating, would do [it], that one is a partaker of these. "Therefore, this to me, *bhikṣus*...not inheritors of material things (*āmiṣadāyāda*)."

"Therefore, this to me, *bhikṣus*"—the Blessed One said this passage of the *sūtra*, from the beginning to the end, up to "not inheritors of material things," the Blessed One said.

"*Idaṃ vatvāna sugato* [Having said this, the *Sugata*]," because having said this passage of the *sūtra*, having gone to the beautiful practice, the Blessed One attained the designation "*Sugata*."

"*Uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisī* [Having risen from the seat, he entered the *vihāra*]," having risen from the seat of the Buddha that had been prepared, he entered the *vihāra*, his own great fragrance chamber (*mahāgandhakuṭi*), without a divided assembly (*parisā*).

Why? For the sake of Dharma-praise.

"*Idam avoca bhagavā* [Thus spoke the Blessed One]," "*Idaṃ vatvāna sugato* [Having said this, the *Sugata*]," "*Sugato* [The *Sugata*]," "*Uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisī* [Having risen from the seat, he entered the *vihāra*]."

It seems that those who enter the *vihāra* after an unfinished teaching (*deśanā*) enter for two reasons: either for the sake of praising the person (*pudgala*) or for the sake of praising the Dharma.

Entering for the sake of praising the *pudgala*, he thought thus: "This outline (*uddeśa*) has been shown by me in brief, not divided in detail. The *bhikṣus* who receive the Dharma, having grasped [it], will approach Ānanda or Kātyāyana and ask. Having compared [it] with my knowledge (*jñāna*), they will speak. Then the *bhikṣus* who receive the Dharma will again ask me. To them I will say, 'Well spoken by Ānanda, *bhikṣus*, well spoken by Kātyāyana! Even if you were to ask me this meaning, I too would explain it just so.' Thus I will praise those *pudgalas*. Then, having generated respect in them, the *bhikṣus* will approach. Those *bhikṣus* too will apply [themselves] to meaning and Dharma, and those trained by them, fulfilling the three trainings, will make an end of suffering."

Entering for the sake of Dharma-praise, he thought thus, just as he thought here: "When I have entered the *vihāra*, Sāriputta, seated in this very assembly (*parisad*), while disparaging that very inheritor of material things (*āmiṣadāyāda*) and praising the inheritor of Dharma (*dhammadāyāda*), will teach the Dharma. Thus, this teaching (*deśanā*) spoken by the intention (*mati*) of both of us, being united in one place (*ekajjhāsayāya*), will be chief and weighty, like a stone umbrella.

Like a boat placed at a *tīrtha* for the sake of crossing over the four floods (*caturogha*), it will be like a chariot yoked with four well-trained horses for the sake of going on the path (*mārga*).

And just as when the king, having placed a command (*āṇa*) in the assembly, saying, 'For one doing thus, this is the punishment (*daṇḍa*)', and having risen from the seat, has ascended to the palace (*pāsāda*), the general (*senāpati*), seated right there, puts into effect that command placed by the king; just so, Sāriputta, seated in this very assembly, having praised the teaching placed by me, will teach. Thus, this teaching spoken by the intention (*mati*) of both of us will be stronger and will blaze like the midday sun."

Thus, here, for the sake of Dharma-praise, having risen from the seat, he entered the *vihāra*.

And in such places, the Blessed One, while seated, disappears from the seat itself and enters the *vihāra* by means of mental velocity (*cittagati*), it should be understood.

For if he were to go by means of bodily velocity (*kāyagati*), the entire assembly, having surrounded the Blessed One, would go, and that, having been divided once, would again be a bad gathering (*dussannipāta*). Therefore, the Blessed One entered by means of mental velocity.

mula_pali:
31. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto acirapakkantassa bhagavato bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘āvuso bhikkhave’’ti. ‘‘Āvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

‘‘Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti, kittāvatā ca pana satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekamanusikkhantī’’ti? ‘‘Dūratopi kho mayaṃ, āvuso, āgacchāma āyasmato sāriputtassa santike etassa bhāsitassa atthamaññātuṃ. Sādhu vatāyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho; āyasmato sāriputtassa sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

‘‘Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti? Idhāvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti, yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha, te ca dhamme nappajahanti, bāhulikā bāhullikā (syā.) ca honti, sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā. Tatrāvuso, therā bhikkhū tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī’ti – iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha te ca dhamme nappajahantī’ti – iminā dutiyena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Bāhulikā ca, sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā’ti – iminā tatiyena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. Therā, āvuso, bhikkhū imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. Tatrāvuso, majjhimā bhikkhū…pe… navā bhikkhū tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī’ti – iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Yesañca dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha te ca dhamme nappajahantī’ti – iminā dutiyena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. ‘Bāhulikā ca honti, sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā’ti – iminā tatiyena ṭhānena navā bhikkhū gārayhā bhavanti. Navā, āvuso, bhikkhū imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayhā bhavanti. Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhanti.

bāhullikā (syā.)
mula_english:
Soon after he had left, the venerable Sāriputta addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: “Friends, *bhikkhus*.”

—“Friend,” those *bhikkhus* replied to venerable Sāriputta. Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“In how far, friend, do disciples of the Teacher (*satthu*) who lives secluded not train in seclusion, and in how far do disciples of the Teacher who lives secluded train in seclusion?”

“Indeed, friend, we would come from far away to learn from the venerable Sāriputta the meaning of this statement. It would be good if the venerable Sariputta would explain the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from him, the *bhikkhus* will remember it.”

“Then listen, friends, and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, friend,” the *bhikkhus* replied to venerable Sāriputta. Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“In how far, friend, do disciples of the Teacher who lives secluded not train in seclusion? Here, friend, disciples of the Teacher who lives secluded do not train in seclusion; they do not abandon what the Teacher tells them to abandon; they are luxurious and careless, leaders in backsliding, neglectful of seclusion. In this the elder *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for three reasons. ‘As disciples of the Teacher who lives secluded, they do not train in seclusion’: the elder *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for this first reason. ‘They do not abandon what the Teacher tells them to abandon’: the elder *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for this second reason. ‘They are luxurious and careless, leaders in backsliding, neglectful of seclusion’: the elder *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for this third reason. The elder *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for these three reasons. In this the middle *bhikkhus*…pe… the new *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for three reasons. ‘As disciples of the Teacher who lives secluded, they do not train in seclusion’: the new *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for this first reason. ‘They do not abandon what the Teacher tells them to abandon’: the new *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for this second reason. ‘They are luxurious and careless, leaders in backsliding, neglectful of seclusion’: the new *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for this third reason. The new *bhikkhus* are to be blamed for these three reasons. It is in this way that disciples of the Teacher who lives secluded do not train in seclusion.
commentary_pali:
31. Evaṃ paviṭṭhe pana bhagavati bhagavato adhippāyānurūpaṃ taṃ dhammaṃ thometukāmo tatra khoāyasmā sāriputto…pe…etadavoca. Tattha āyasmāti piyavacanametaṃ. Sāriputtoti tassa therassa nāmaṃ, tañca kho mātito, na pitito. Rūpasāriyā hi brāhmaṇiyā so putto, tasmā sāriputtoti vuccati. Acirapakkantassāti pakkantassa sato nacirena. Āvuso, bhikkhaveti ettha pana buddhā bhagavanto sāvake ālapantā bhikkhaveti ālapanti. Sāvakā pana buddhehi sadisā mā homāti āvusoti paṭhamaṃ vatvā pacchā bhikkhaveti bhaṇanti. Buddhehi ca ālapito bhikkhusaṅgho bhadanteti paṭivacanaṃ deti, sāvakehi āvusoti.

Kittāvatānu kho, āvusoti ettha kittāvatāti paricchedavacanaṃ, kittakenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Nukāro pucchāyaṃ. Khokāro nipātamattaṃ. Satthu pavivittassa viharatoti, tīhi vivekehi kāyacittaupadhivivekehi satthuno viharantassa. Vivekaṃ nānusikkhantīti tiṇṇaṃ vivekānaṃ aññatarampi nānusikkhanti, āmisadāyādāva hontīti imamatthaṃ āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū pucchi. Esa nayo sukkapakkhepi.

Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso kittāvatā Nu Kho Satthu pavivittassa viharato Vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī

Evaṃ vutte tamatthaṃ sotukāmā bhikkhū dūratopi khotiādimāhaṃsu. Tattha dūratopīti tiroraṭṭhatopi tirojanapadatopi anekayojanagaṇanatopīti vuttaṃ hoti. Santiketi samīpe. Aññātunti jānituṃ bujjhituṃ. Āyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātūti āyasmatoyeva sāriputtassa bhāgo hotu, āyasmā pana sāriputto attano bhāgaṃ katvā vibhajatūti vuttaṃ hoti. Āyasmato hi bhāgo yadidaṃ atthakkhānaṃ, amhākaṃ pana savanaṃ bhāgoti ayamettha adhippāyo, evaṃ saddalakkhaṇena sameti. Keci pana bhaṇanti ‘‘paṭibhātūti dissatū’’ti. Apare ‘‘upaṭṭhātū’’ti. Dhāressantīti uggahessanti pariyāpuṇissanti. Tato nesaṃ kathetukāmo thero tena hītiādimāha. Tattha tenāti kāraṇavacanaṃ. Hikāro nipāto. Yasmā sotukāmāttha, yasmā ca mayhaṃ bhāraṃ āropayittha, tasmā suṇāthāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tepi bhikkhū therassa vacanaṃ sampaṭicchiṃsu, tenāha ‘‘evamāvusoti…pe…paccassosu’’nti.

dūratopi kho dūratopī Santike Aññātu Āyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātū Dhāressantī tena hī tenā Hi

Atha nesaṃ, āmisadāyādaṃ garahantena bhagavatā ‘‘tumhepi tena ādiyā bhaveyyāthā’’ti ekenevākārena vuttamatthaṃ tīhi ākārehi dassento āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – ‘‘idhāvuso , satthu pavivittassa viharato…pe… ettāvatā kho, āvuso, satthu pavivittassa viharato sāvakā vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī’’ti.

Ettāvatā yañca bhagavā āmisadāyādapaṭipadaṃ garahanto ‘‘tumhepi tena ādiyā bhaveyyāthā’’ti āha, yañca attanā pucchaṃ pucchi ‘‘kittāvatā nu kho…pe… nānusikkhantī’’ti, tassa vitthārato attho suvibhatto hoti. So ca kho bhagavato ādiyabhāvaṃ anāmasitvāva. Bhagavatoyeva hi yuttaṃ sāvake anuggaṇhantassa ‘‘ahampi tena ādiyo bhavissāmī’’ti vattuṃ, na sāvakānaṃ. Esa nayo sukkapakkhepi, ayaṃ tāvettha anusandhikkamayojanā.

Ayaṃ panatthavaṇṇanā idhāti imasmiṃ sāsane, satthu pavivittassāti satthuno tīhi vivekehi accantapavivittassa. Vivekaṃ nānusikkhantīti kāyavivekaṃ nānusikkhanti, na paripūrentīti vuttaṃ hoti. Yadi pana tividhaṃ vivekaṃ sandhāya vadeyya, pucchāya aviseso siyā. Byākaraṇapakkho hi ayaṃ. Tasmā iminā padena kāyavivekaṃ, ‘‘yesañca dhammāna’’ntiādinā cittavivekaṃ, ‘‘bāhulikā’’tiādinā upadhivivekañca dassetīti evamettha saṅkhepato attho veditabbo.

idhā satthu pavivittassā Vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī

Yesañca dhammānanti lobhādayo sandhāyāha, ye parato ‘‘tatrāvuso lobho ca pāpako’’tiādinā nayena vakkhati. Nappajahantīti na pariccajanti, cittavivekaṃ na paripūrentīti vuttaṃ hoti. Bāhulikāti cīvarādibāhullāya paṭipannā. Sāsanaṃ sithilaṃ gaṇhantīti sāthalikā. Okkamane pubbaṅgamāti ettha okkamanaṃ vuccanti avagamanaṭṭhena pañca nīvaraṇāni, tena pañcanīvaraṇapubbaṅgamāti vuttaṃ hoti. Paviveketi upadhiviveke nibbāne. Nikkhittadhurāti oropitadhurā, tadadhigamāya ārambhampi akurumānāti, ettāvatā upadhivivekaṃ na paripūrentīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Yesañca dhammāna Nappajahantī Bāhulikā sāthalikā. Okkamane pubbaṅgamā okkamanaṃ Paviveke Nikkhittadhurā

Ettāvatā aniyameneva vatvā idāni desanaṃ niyamento ‘‘tatrāvuso’’tiādimāha. Kasmā? Sāvakā ‘‘tīhi ṭhānehī’’ti evañhi aniyametvāva vuccamāne ‘‘kampi maññe bhaṇati , na amhe’’ti udāsināpi honti. ‘‘Therā navā majjhimā’’ti evaṃ pana niyametvā vuccamāne amhe bhaṇatīti ādaraṃ karonti . Yathā raññā ‘‘amaccehi nagaravīthiyo sodhetabbā’’ti vuttepi ‘‘kena nu kho sodhetabbā’’ti maññamānā na sodhenti, attano attano gharadvāraṃ sodhetabbanti pana bheriyā nikkhantāya sabbe muhuttena sodhenti ca alaṅkaronti ca, evaṃsampadamidaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Tattha tatrāti tesu sāvakesu. Therāti dasavasse upādāya vuccanti. Tīhi ṭhānehīti tīhi kāraṇehi. Ayañhi ṭhānasaddo issariyaṭṭhitikhaṇakāraṇesu dissati. ‘‘Kiṃ panāyasmā devānamindo kammaṃ katvā imaṃ ṭhānaṃ patto’’tiādīsu hi issariye dissati. ‘‘Ṭhānakusalo hoti akkhaṇavedhī’’tiādīsu ṭhitiyaṃ. ‘‘Ṭhānasovetaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhātī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.87) khaṇe. ‘‘Ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato’’tiādīsu (vibha. 809; ma. ni. 1.148) kāraṇe. Idha pana kāraṇeyeva. Kāraṇañhi yasmā tattha phalaṃ tiṭṭhati tadāyattavuttibhāvena, tasmā ṭhānanti vuccati.

tatrā Therā Tīhi ṭhānehī

Iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhāti ettha gārayhāti garahitabbā. Therā nāma samānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni na upenti, gāmantasenāsanaṃ na muñcanti, saṅgaṇikārāmataṃ vaḍḍhentā viharanti, kāyavivekampi na paripūrenti, navamajjhimakāle kīdisā ahesunti evaṃ ninditabbā honti, imaṃ nindaṃ āvuso labhantīti dasseti. Dutiyena ṭhānenāti etthāpi ime nāma āvuso therāpi samānā yesaṃ dhammānaṃ satthā pahānamāha, te lobhādidhamme na jahanti, accharāsaṅghātamattampi ekamantaṃ nisīditvā cittekaggataṃ na labhanti, navamajjhimakāle kīdisā ahesunti evaṃ ninditabbā honti, imaṃ nindaṃ āvuso labhantīti dassetīti evaṃ yojanā kātabbā. Tatiyena ṭhānenāti etthāpi ime nāmāvuso, therāpi samānā itarītarena na yāpenti, cīvarapattasenāsanapūtikāyamaṇḍanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti upadhivivekaṃ apūrayamānā, navamajjhimakāle kīdisā ahesunti evaṃ ninditabbā honti, imaṃ nindaṃ, āvuso, labhantīti dassetīti evaṃ yojanā veditabbā. Esa nayo majjhimanavavāresu.

Iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena therā bhikkhū gārayhā gārayhā Therā Dutiyena ṭhānenā Tatiyena ṭhānenā

Ayaṃ pana viseso. Majjhimāti pañcavasse upādāya yāva nava vassā vuccanti. Navāti ūnapañcavassā vuccanti. Yathā ca tattha navamajjhimakāle kīdisā ahesunti vuttaṃ, evamidha navakāle kīdisā ahesuṃ, therakāle kīdisā bhavissanti, majjhimatherakāle kīdisā bhavissantīti vatvā yojetabbaṃ.

Majjhimā Navā
commentary_english:
31. Thus, when the Blessed One had entered, wishing to praise that Dharma that was in accordance with the Blessed One's intention, the Venerable Sāriputta said...pe...this.

There, *Āyasmā* is a term of endearment.

*Sāriputto* is the name of that elder, and that too from his mother, not from his father.

He was the son of a Brāhmaṇī named Rūpasārī, therefore he is called Sāriputta.

*Acirapakkantassā* means not long after departing while mindful.

*Āvuso, bhikkhave*ti Here, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, address the disciples, calling them "bhikkhus."

Disciples, however, do not become similar to the Buddhas, so they first say "Āvuso" and afterwards say "bhikkhave."

When the Saṅgha of monks is addressed by the Buddhas, they give the reply "bhadante," and by the disciples, "āvuso."

How much, friend? Here, *kittāvatā* is a word of delimitation, it means "how much?".

*Nu* is a particle of questioning.

*Kho* is merely a particle.

*Satthu pavivittassa viharato* means of the Teacher who dwells in solitude, with three kinds of solitude: solitude of body, mind, and basis [of existence].

*Vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī* means they do not train in even one of the three solitudes; they are like heirs to material things. The Venerable Sāriputta asked the monks this meaning.

This is the method also in the bright fortnight.

How much? Now, friend, how much? Now how much does the disciple not train in solitude of the Teacher who dwells in solitude? When this was said, the monks, wishing to hear that meaning, said, "Even from afar, indeed..." etc.

There, *dūratopī* means even from a distant country, even from a distant territory, even from a distance calculated in many yojanas.

*Santike* means near.

*Aññātu* means to know, to understand.

*Āyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātū* means may the Venerable Sāriputta alone be the one to whom it occurs; may the Venerable Sāriputta make a portion for himself and distribute it.

The Venerable One's share is this exposition of the meaning; our share, however, is the hearing. This is the intention here; thus it accords with the characteristic of sound.

Some, however, say "paṭibhātūti" means "may it appear."

Others, "may it attend."

*Dhāressantī* means they will learn, they will master.

Then, wishing to explain to them, the Elder said, "tena hī" etc.

There, *tenā* is a word of reason.

*Hi* is a particle.

Because you wish to hear, and because you have placed a burden on me, therefore, listen.

Those monks accepted the Elder's word, therefore he said, "evam āvusoti...pe...paccassosu"nti.

Even from afar, indeed, even from afar, near, to know, may it occur to the Venerable Sāriputta alone, they will learn, tena hī, tenā, hi.

Then, the Blessed One, censuring those who were heirs to material things, showing the meaning that had been spoken in one way with three modes, said, "You too might be attached to that." The Venerable Sāriputta said this: "Here, friend, of the Teacher who dwells in solitude...pe...to this extent, friend, the disciples of the Teacher who dwells in solitude do not train in solitude."

To this extent, the Blessed One, censuring the practice of being heirs to material things, said, "You too might be attached to that," and the question that he himself asked, "How much, now, friend...pe...do they not train in solitude?" its meaning is well divided in detail.

And that, indeed, without appropriating the state of being attached of the Blessed One.
Indeed, it is proper for the Blessed One to favor a disciple, saying, "I too will be first in that," but not for the disciples.

This is the method also on the bright side. This much, for the present, is the connectional arrangement here.

Now, the meaning of this is explained: *idhā* means in this dispensation; *satthu pavivittassā* means of the Teacher who is utterly secluded by the three kinds of seclusion.

*vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī* means they do not train themselves in bodily seclusion; that is, they do not perfect it.

But if he should speak with reference to the threefold seclusion, there would be no distinction in the question.

This is, in fact, the grammatical approach.

Therefore, by this word, he shows bodily seclusion; by "yesañca dhammāna," mental seclusion; and by "bāhulikā," seclusion from defilements. Thus, the meaning should be understood here in brief.

*idhā* *satthu pavivittassā* *vivekaṃ nānusikkhantī*

*yesañca dhammāna* means having in mind such things as greed, which he will speak of later according to the method, "There, friend, greed is evil," and so forth.

*nappajahantī* means they do not abandon them; that is, they do not perfect mental seclusion.

*bāhulikā* means those who have undertaken abundance of robes, etc.

*sāthalikā* means they take the dispensation loosely.

*okkamane pubbaṅgamā* here, *okkamanaṃ* is said to be the five hindrances in the sense of understanding. Therefore, it is said that they are foremost in the five hindrances.

*paviveke* means in seclusion from defilements, in nirvāṇa.

*nikkhittadhurā* means those who have laid down the burden, those who do not even make an effort to attain it. To this extent, it is said that they do not perfect seclusion from defilements.

*yesañca dhammāna* *nappajahantī* *bāhulikā* *sāthalikā. okkamane pubbaṅgamā* *okkamanaṃ* *paviveke* *nikkhittadhurā*

Up to this point, having spoken indefinitely, he now makes the teaching definite, saying, "There, friend," and so forth.

Why? Because if the disciples were to be addressed indefinitely, saying, "By three things," they might be indifferent, thinking, "He is speaking about someone else, I suppose, not about us."

But when they are addressed definitely, saying, "Elders, novices, middle ones," they pay attention, thinking, "He is speaking about us."

Just as when the king says, "The city streets should be cleaned by the ministers," they do not clean them, thinking, "By whom should they be cleaned?" But when the order goes forth by drumbeat that each one should clean his own house door, they all clean and decorate them in a moment. This analogy should be understood.

There, *tatrā* means among those disciples.

*therā* means those who are reckoned as ten years [ordained] and upwards.

*tīhi ṭhānehī* means by three reasons.

For this word *ṭhāna* is seen in the senses of lordship, stability, moment, and reason.

For it is seen in the sense of lordship in such passages as "Having done what deed, venerable sir, did Devānaminda attain this *sthāna*?"

It is seen in the sense of stability in such passages as "He is skilled in *sthāna*, piercing the non-moment."

It appears to the Tathāgata as *sthāna*-sovetam (MN. 2.87) in [the sense of] moment.

It is found in the sense of cause in such passages as "*Sthāna* as *sthāna* and non-*sthāna* as non-*sthāna*" (Vibha. 809; MN. 1. 
148) *kāraṇe*.
Here, however, [it is] in the sense of cause.
For because the result (*phala*) abides there in the cause (*kāraṇa*), by way of having its activity dependent on it, therefore it is called a "basis" (*ṭhāna*).

There, the elders (*therā*), by these three bases (*ṭhānehi*)
Here, in this first basis (*ṭhānena*), the elders (*therā*) are blameworthy (*gārayhā*); here, blameworthy (*gārayhā*) means to be blamed (*garahitabbā*).
The elders (*therā*), though being the same, do not resort to forests (*araññavanapatthāni*) [or] remote lodgings (*senāsanāni*), they do not give up village lodgings (*gāmantasenāsanaṃ*), they live cultivating attachment to company (*saṅgaṇikārāmataṃ*), and they do not fulfill bodily seclusion (*kāyavivekampi*). "What were they like in the period of the new and middle [monks]?" In this way, they are to be criticized. This shows that they receive this criticism, friend.
Here also, in the second basis (*ṭhānenā*), "These elders (*therā*) also, friend, though being the same, do not abandon those things that the Teacher (*satthā*) spoke of as abandonment, the qualities of greed etc. (*lobhādidhamme*). Even for the duration of a syllable-combination (*accharāsaṅghātamattampi*), they do not attain one-pointedness of mind (*cittekaggataṃ*) having sat down in seclusion (*ekamantaṃ nisīditvā*). What were they like in the period of the new and middle [monks]?" In this way, they are to be criticized. This shows that they receive this criticism, friend. Thus, the connection (*yojanā*) should be made.
Here also, in the third basis (*ṭhānenā*), "These elders (*therā*) also, friend, though being the same, do not maintain themselves with whatever comes along, they live devoted to the pursuit of robes, alms bowls, lodgings, and adorning the foul body (*cīvarapattasenāsanapūtikāyamaṇḍanānuyogamanuyuttā*), not fulfilling the seclusion of the foundations [of mindfulness] (*upadhivivekaṃ apūrayamānā*).
