commentary_pali: 39.Thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitāti cittagelaññabhūtena thinena sesanāmakāyagelaññabhūtena middhena ca pariyuṭṭhitā, abhibhūtā gahitāti vuttaṃ hoti. Te niddābahulā honti.
commentary_english:
"Thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā" means being overcome and seized by *thina* (sloth) which is a sickness of the mind (*cittagelañña-bhūtena*), and by *middha* (torpor), which is a sickness of the remaining body (*sesanāmakāyagelañña-bhūtena*). Thus it is said.

They are full of sleep (*niddābahulā honti*).

mula_pali: 40. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā uddhatā avūpasantacittā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, uddhataavūpasantacittasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ uddhato avūpasantacitto araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; vūpasantacittohamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā vūpasantacittā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, vūpasantacittataṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english: “I considered thus, brahmin: ‘Whenever recluses or brahmins, agitated and with unpacified minds, resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest, then owing to the defect of their agitated and unpacified minds, these good recluses and brahmins evoke unwholesome fear and dread. But I do not resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest agitated and with unpacified mind; I am with pacified mind. I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones with pacified minds.’ Seeing in myself this pacified mind, I found great solace in dwelling in the forest.
commentary_pali: 40.Uddhatāti uddhaccapakatikā vipphandamānacittā, uddhaccena hi ekārammaṇe cittaṃ vipphandati dhajayaṭṭhiyaṃ vātena paṭākā viya. Avūpasantacittāti anibbutacittā, idha kukkuccaṃ gahetuṃ vaṭṭati.
commentary_english:
"Uddhatā" means one whose nature is restlessness, whose mind is agitated. For, through restlessness, the mind is agitated in a single object, like a flag fluttering in the wind on a flagpole.

"Avūpasantacittā" means one whose mind is not calmed. Here, it is fitting to take it as scruple (kukkucca).

mula_pali: 41. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kaṅkhī vicikicchī araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, kaṅkhivicikicchisandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ kaṅkhī vicikicchī araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; tiṇṇavicikicchohamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā tiṇṇavicikicchā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, tiṇṇavicikicchataṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english: “Then it occurred to me, brahmin: ‘Whenever recluses or brahmins, being subject to doubt and uncertainty, resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest, these good recluses and brahmins evoke unwholesome fear and dread owing to the defect of their being subject to doubt and uncertainty. But I do not resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest subject to doubt and uncertainty; I have gone beyond doubt (tiṇṇavicikicchohamasmi). I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones who have gone beyond doubt.’ Then, brahmin, seeing in myself this state of having gone beyond doubt, I attained even greater growth in dwelling in the forest.
commentary_pali: 41.Kaṅkhī vicikicchīti ettha ekamevidaṃ pañcamaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ. Kiṃ nu kho idanti ārammaṇaṃ kaṅkhanato kaṅkhā, idamevidanti nicchetuṃ asamatthabhāvato vicikicchāti vuccati, tena samannāgatā samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘‘kaṅkhī vicikicchī’’ti vuttā.
commentary_english:
"Doubt, skepticism" is the fifth hindrance here.

"What is this?" Doubt arises from being doubtful about the object. Skepticism is the state of being incapable of deciding "This is it." Because of that, ascetics and Brahmins endowed with that are said to be "doubtful, skeptical."

mula_pali: 42. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā attukkaṃsakā paravambhī araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, attukkaṃsanaparavambhanasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti . Na kho panāhaṃ attukkaṃsako paravambhī araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi ; anattukkaṃsako aparavambhīhamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā anattukkaṃsakā aparavambhī araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, anattukkaṃsakataṃ aparavambhitaṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english: “Then, Brahmin, it occurred to me: ‘Those recluses or Brahmins who are given to self-praise (attukkaṃsakā) and disparagement of others (paravambhī), and resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest (araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti), those good recluses and Brahmins evoke unwholesome fear and dread owing to the defect of their self-praise and disparagement of others (attukkaṃsanaparavambhanasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti). I am not given to self-praise and disparagement of others; I am without self-praise and without disparagement of others. I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones who are without self-praise and without disparagement of others.’ Seeing this freedom from self-praise and disparagement in myself, Brahmin, I found even greater inspiration for dwelling in the forest.”
commentary_pali: 42.Attukkaṃsanakā paravambhīti ye attānaṃ ukkaṃsenti ukkhipanti, ucce ṭhāne ṭhapenti, parañca vambhenti garahanti nindanti, nīce ṭhāne ṭhapenti, tesametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Te kathaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti? Te parehi ‘‘asuko ca kira asuko ca attānaṃ ukkaṃsenti, amhe garahanti, dāse viya karonti, gaṇhatha ne’’ti anubaddhā palāyitvā araññaṃ pavisitvā gacchantare vā gumbantare vāti kāyakammantasadisaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
42. *Attukkaṃsanakā paravambhī*: Those who praise themselves and disparage others—they elevate themselves, place themselves in a high position, and disparage, criticize, and blame others, placing them in a low position—this is their designation.

How do they bring about fear and terror? They are pursued by others, saying, "So-and-so praises himself and blames us, treats us like slaves, seize him!" Having fled and entered the forest, they expand on the actions of the body, whether among trees or among bushes.

mula_pali: 43. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā chambhī bhīrukajātikā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, chambhibhīrukajātikasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ chambhī bhīrukajātiko araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; vigatalomahaṃsohamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā vigatalomahaṃsā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, vigatalomahaṃsataṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english:
“Then, brahmin, I considered thus: ‘Whenever recluses or brahmins who are fearful and of a timid nature resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest, then owing to the defect of their fearful and timid nature, these good recluses and brahmins evoke unwholesome fear and dread.

But I am not fearful and of a timid nature, and I do resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest; I am without hair-raising fear.

I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones without hair-raising fear.’

Seeing in myself this absence of hair-raising fear, I found great solace in dwelling in the forest.
commentary_pali: 43.Chambhīti kāyathambhanalomahaṃsanakarena thambhena samannāgatā. Bhīrukajātikāti bhīrukapakatikā, gāmadārakā viya bhayabahulā asūrā kātarāti vuttaṃ hoti.
commentary_english:
"chambhīti": Possessing steadiness (*thambha*) through the act of steadiness of the body (*kāya-thambhana*), making the hair stand on end (*loma-haṃsana*).

"bhīrukajātikā": Cowardly (*bhīrukapakatikā*), like village boys (*gāma-dārakā*), full of fear (*bhaya-bahulā*), without courage (*asūrā*), fearful (*kātarā*), so it is said (*vuttaṃ hoti*).

mula_pali: 44. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ nikāmayamānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, lābhasakkārasilokanikāmana nikāmayamāna (sī. syā.) sandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ lābhasakkārasilokaṃ nikāmayamāno araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; appicchohamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā appicchā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, appicchataṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english: “Then, brahmin, it occurred to me: ‘Whenever recluses or brahmins, desiring gain, honor, and renown, resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest, because of their satisfaction with desiring gain, honor, and renown, those good recluses and brahmins evoke unwholesome fear and dread. But I do not, desiring gain, honor, and renown, resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest; I have few wishes. Indeed, I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones with few wishes.’ Seeing in myself this having few wishes (alpēcchata), I found great solace in dwelling in the forest."
commentary_pali:
44.Lābhasakkārasilokanti ettha labbhatīti lābho, catunnaṃ paccayānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Sakkāroti sundarakāro, paccayā eva hi paṇītapaṇītā sundarasundarā ca abhisaṅkharitvā katā sakkārāti vuccanti. Yā ca parehi attano gāravakiriyā pupphādīhi vā pūjā. Silokoti vaṇṇabhaṇanaṃ etaṃ , lābhañca sakkārañca silokañca lābhasakkārasilokaṃ. Nikāmayamānāti patthayamānā. Bhayabheravāvhāyanaṃ abhijjhāluvārasadisameva. Tadatthadīpakaṃ panettha piyagāmikavatthuṃ kathenti –

Eko kira piyagāmiko nāma bhikkhu samādinnadhutaṅgānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ lābhaṃ disvā ‘‘ahampi dhutaṅgaṃ samādiyitvā lābhaṃ uppādemī’’ti cintetvā sosānikaṅgaṃ samādāya susāne vasati. Athekadivasaṃ eko kammamutto jaraggavo divā gocare caritvā rattiṃ tasmiṃ susāne pupphagumbe sīsaṃ katvā romanthayamāno aṭṭhāsi. Piyagāmiko rattiṃ caṅkamanā nikkhanto tassa hanusaddaṃ sutvā cintesi ‘‘addhā maṃ lābhagiddho esa susāne vasatīti ñatvā devarājā viheṭhetuṃ āgato’’ti, so jaraggavassa purato añjaliṃ paggahetvā ‘‘sappurisa devarāja ajja me ekarattiṃ khama, sve paṭṭhāya na evaṃ karissāmī’’ti namassamāno sabbarattiṃ yācanto aṭṭhāsi. Tato sūriye uṭṭhite taṃ disvā kattarayaṭṭhiyā paharitvā palāpesi ‘‘sabbarattiṃ maṃ bhiṃsāpesī’’ti.
commentary_english:
44. *lābhasakkārasiloka*nti (regarding gain, honor, and fame): Here, *lābho* (gain) means that which is obtained; this is a designation for the four requisites.

*sakkāro*ti (honor) means beautiful actions; the requisites themselves, when carefully and beautifully prepared, are called honor. And also the honoring action towards oneself by others, worship with flowers, etc., is *pūjā* (worship).

*siloko*ti (fame) is the narration of virtues. *lābhañca sakkārañca silokañca* (gain, honor, and fame) is *lābhasakkārasilokaṃ* (gain, honor, and fame).

*nikāmayamānā*ti (desiring) means *patthayamānā* (longing for).

[It is] just like the frightening and terrifying invitation and the fence of covetousness.

Regarding this, they narrate the story of Piyagāmika, which illuminates the meaning:

It seems that a certain monk named Piyagāmika, seeing the gain of monks who had undertaken the dhutaṅga practices, thinking, "I, too, will undertake the dhutaṅga practices and generate gain," undertook the sosānikaṅga (dwelling in a charnel ground) and lived in a charnel ground.

Then one day, an old ox, released from work, having wandered in the pasture during the day, spent the night in that charnel ground near a bush of flowers, chewing its cud.

Piyagāmika, having gone out for walking meditation at night, hearing the sound of its jaw, thought, "Surely, the Devarāja (divine king), knowing that I am greedy for gain and living in this charnel ground, has come to torment me." So, placing his palms together in reverence before the old ox, he pleaded, "O noble Devarāja, forgive me for this one night; from tomorrow on, I will not do this again," spending the entire night begging.

Then, when the sun rose, seeing it, he struck it with a bamboo stick and chased it away, [saying], "It frightened me the whole night!"

mula_pali: 45. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kusītā hīnavīriyā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti , kusītahīnavīriyasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ kusīto hīnavīriyo araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; āraddhavīriyohamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā āraddhavīriyā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, āraddhavīriyataṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english: “I considered thus, brahmin: ‘Whenever recluses or brahmins who are lazy and lacking in energy resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest, due to the defect of laziness and lack of energy, those good recluses and brahmins evoke unwholesome fear and dread.’ But I am not lazy and lacking in energy when I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest; I am one who has aroused energy (āraddhavīriyo). I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones who have aroused energy.’ Seeing in myself this state of having aroused energy, I found great solace in dwelling in the forest."
commentary_pali: 45.Kusītāti kosajjānugatā. Hīnavīriyāti hīnā vīriyena virahitā viyuttā, nibbīriyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha kusītā kāyikavīriyārambhavirahitā honti, hīnavīriyā cetasikavīriyārambhavirahitā. Te ārammaṇavavatthānamattampi kātuṃ na sakkonti. Tesaṃ avavatthitārammaṇānanti sabbaṃ pubbasadisameva.
commentary_english:
45. *Kusītā* means associated with laziness (*kosajja*).

*Hīnavīriyā* means deficient, bereft of, and separated from effort (*vīrya*); it is said to be without effort (*nibbīriya*).

Therein, the lazy (*kusītā*) are without the initiation of physical effort (*kāyikavīryārambha*), and those with deficient effort (*hīnavīriyā*) are without the initiation of mental effort (*cetasikavīryārambha*).

They are not able to even make a determination regarding an object (*ārammaṇa*).

For them, everything is just like before regarding objects that are not determined (*avavatthitārammaṇa*).

mula_pali: 46. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā muṭṭhassatī asampajānā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, muṭṭhassatiasampajānasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ muṭṭhassati asampajāno araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; upaṭṭhitassatihamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā upaṭṭhitassatī araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, upaṭṭhitassatitaṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english: "Then, brahmin, this occurred to me: 'Whenever some ascetics or *brāhmaṇas* resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest, being unmindful and lacking awareness, those good ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* evoke unwholesome fear and dread because of their unmindfulness and lack of awareness. But I do not resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest unmindful and lacking awareness; I am established in mindfulness (*upaṭṭhitassatī*). I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones established in mindfulness.' Seeing in myself this establishment in mindfulness (*upaṭṭhitassatitaṃ*), I found great solace in dwelling in the forest."
commentary_pali: 46.Muṭṭhassatīti naṭṭhassatī. Asampajānāti paññārahitā, imassa ca paṭipakkhe ‘‘upaṭṭhitassatīhamasmī’’ti vacanato satibhājaniyamevetaṃ. Paññā panettha satidubbalyadīpanatthaṃ vuttā. Duvidhā hi sati paññāsampayuttā paññāvippayuttā ca. Tattha paññāsampayuttā balavatī, vippayuttā dubbalā, tasmā yadāpi tesaṃ sati hoti, tadāpi asampajānantā muṭṭhassatīyeva te, dubbalāya satiyā satikiccābhāvatoti etamatthaṃ dīpetuṃ ‘‘asampajānā’’ti vuttaṃ. Te evaṃ muṭṭhassatī asampajānā ārammaṇavavatthānamattampi kātuṃ na sakkontīti sabbaṃ pubbasadisameva.
commentary_english:
"Muttassatī" means with ruined mindfulness.
"Asampajānā" means devoid of wisdom; on the contrary, "upaṭṭhitassatīhamasmī" is fit for mindfulness.
Here, wisdom is said to illuminate the weakness of mindfulness.
For mindfulness is twofold: associated with wisdom and dissociated from wisdom.
There, mindfulness associated with wisdom is strong, [while] dissociated [mindfulness] is weak; therefore, even when they have mindfulness, they are without clear comprehension, they are truly with ruined mindfulness, because of the weakness of mindfulness, due to the absence of the function of mindfulness, "asampajānā" is said to illuminate this meaning.
Thus, they, being with ruined mindfulness and without clear comprehension, are not able to even perform the mere determination of the object; everything is just like before.

mula_pali: 47. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, asamāhitavibbhantacittasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ asamāhito vibbhantacitto araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; samādhisampannohamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā samādhisampannā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, samādhisampadaṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.
mula_english:
“I considered thus, *brāhmaṇa*: ‘Whenever recluses (*śramaṇa*) or *brāhmaṇas* are unconcentrated (*asamāhita*) and with straying minds (*vibbhantacitta*) resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places (*araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni*), then owing to the defect of their unconcentrated and straying minds, these good recluses and *brāhmaṇas* evoke unwholesome fear and dread (*akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti*).

But I do not resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest unconcentrated and with straying mind; I am possessed of concentration (*samādhisampanna*).

I resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest as one of the noble ones (*ārya*) possessed of concentration (*samādhisampanna*).’

Seeing in myself this possession of concentration (*samādhisampadaṃ*), *brāhmaṇa*, I found great solace in dwelling in the forest (*araññe vihārāya*).
commentary_pali: 47.Asamāhitāti upacārappanāsamādhivirahitā. Vibbhantacittāti ubbhantacittā. Samādhivirahena laddhokāsena uddhaccena tesaṃ samādhivirahānaṃ cittaṃ nānārammaṇesu paribbhamati, vanamakkaṭo viya vanasākhāsu uddhaccena ekārammaṇe vipphandati. Pubbe vuttanayenena te evaṃ asamāhitā vibbhantacittā ārammaṇavavatthānamattampi kātuṃ na sakkontīti sabbaṃ pubbasadisameva.
commentary_english:
"Asamāhitā" means devoid of approximate or applied *samādhi*.

"Vibbhantacittā" means *ubbhatacittā*.

Due to the absence of *samādhi*, their minds, having obtained an opportunity, wander in various objects because of distraction, like a forest monkey jumping among the branches of a forest due to distraction, [and] flutter in a single object.

As previously stated, thus, being without *samādhi* and with agitated minds, they are not even able to make an object the basis [of their meditation]. Everything is just as before.

mula_pali:
48. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā duppaññā eḷamūgā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti, duppaññaeḷamūgasandosahetu have te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti. Na kho panāhaṃ duppañño eḷamūgo araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevāmi; paññāsampannohamasmi. Ye hi vo ariyā paññāsampannā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti tesamahaṃ aññataro’ti. Etamahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, paññāsampadaṃ attani sampassamāno bhiyyo pallomamāpādiṃ araññe vihārāya.

Soḷasapariyāyaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.
mula_english:
"48. “I considered thus, Brahmin: ‘Whenever some ascetics or Brahmins who are unwise ( *duppañña*) and dull (*eḷamūga*) resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places (*araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti*), due to the fault of being unwise and dull, these good ascetics and Brahmins evoke unwholesome fear and dread (*akusalaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti*).

But I do not resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest unwise and dull; I am possessed of wisdom (*paññāsampanno ham asmi*). I am one of those noble ones who are possessed of wisdom and resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places.’

Seeing in myself this possession of wisdom (*paññāsampadaṃ*), I found great solace (*bhiyyo pallomam āpādiṃ*) in dwelling in the forest.

The Sixteen Modes are finished."
commentary_pali:
48.Duppaññāti nippaññānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Paññā pana duṭṭhā nāma natthi. Eḷamūgāti elamukhā, kha-kārassa ga-kāro kato. Lālamukhāti vuttaṃ hoti. Duppaññānañhi kathentānaṃ lālā mukhato galati, lālā ca elāti vuccati. Yathāha ‘‘passelamūgaṃ uragaṃ dujjivha’’nti. Tasmā te ‘‘eḷamūgā’’ti vuccanti. ‘‘Elamukhā’’tipi pāṭho. ‘‘Elamugā’’ti keci paṭhanti, apare ‘‘elamukā’’tipi, sabbattha ‘‘elamukhā’’ti attho. Te kathaṃ bhayabheravaṃ avhāyanti? Te duppaññā eḷamūgā ārammaṇavavatthānamattampi kātuṃ na sakkonti. Tesaṃ avavatthitārammaṇānaṃ araññe viharantānaṃ divā diṭṭhaṃ rattiṃ bhayabheravaṃ hutvā upaṭṭhāti ‘‘te ākulacittā appamattakenapi tasanti vittasanti, rajjuṃ vā lataṃ vā disvā sappasaññino honti, khāṇuṃ disvā yakkhasaññino, thalaṃ vā pabbataṃ vā disvā hatthisaññino sappādīhi anayavyasanaṃ āpāditā viya hontī’’ti. Evaṃ taṃ bhayabheravaṃ attani samāropanaṭṭhena avhāyanti pakkosanti. Paññāsampannohamasmīti ettha paññāsampannoti paññāya sampanno samannāgato, no ca kho vipassanāpaññāya, na maggapaññāya, apica kho pana imesu soḷasasu ṭhānesu ārammaṇavavatthānapaññāyāti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha vuttanayamevāti.

Vacīkammantavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Soḷasaṭṭhānārammaṇapariggaho niṭṭhito.

Bhayabheravasenāsanādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
48. *Duppaññā* means a designation for those lacking wisdom. But there is nothing called corrupt wisdom. *Eḷamūgā* means *elamukhā*; the *kha*-sound has been made into a *ga*-sound. That is to say, *lālamukhā*. For when those lacking wisdom speak, saliva drips from their mouths, and saliva is called *elā*. As it was said, "See the snake, dribbling and dumb." Therefore, they are called "dribbling and dumb." There is also the reading "*elamukhā*." Some read "*elamugā*," and others "*elamukā*," but everywhere the meaning is "*elamukhā*." How do they invite fear and dread? Those lacking wisdom, dribbling and dumb, are not even able to properly ascertain an object. For those with unfixed objects, living in the forest, what is seen during the day arises at night as fear and dread. "Disturbed in mind, they tremble and are terrified even by a small thing, seeing a rope or creeper, they think it is a snake; seeing a stump, they think it is a *yakkha*; seeing a plain or a mountain, they think it is an elephant, as if they were afflicted with misfortune and ruin by snakes, etc." Thus, by the fact of attributing that fear and dread to themselves, they invite and summon it.

Here, *paññāsampanno* in *paññāsampannohamasmī* means endowed with wisdom, possessed of wisdom, but not with the wisdom of insight (*vipassanāpaññā*), not with the wisdom of the path (*maggapaññā*), but rather with the wisdom of ascertaining an object (*ārammaṇavavatthānapaññā*) in these sixteen instances.

The rest is as already stated everywhere.

The description of the divisions of verbal action is finished.

The treatise on the sixteen bases for determining objects is finished.

Description of fearful and terrifying lodgings, etc.

mula_pali: 49. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ yā tā rattiyo abhiññātā abhilakkhitā – cātuddasī pañcadasī aṭṭhamī ca pakkhassa – tathārūpāsu rattīsu yāni tāni ārāmacetiyāni vanacetiyāni rukkhacetiyāni bhiṃsanakāni salomahaṃsāni tathārūpesu senāsanesu vihareyyaṃ appeva nāmāhaṃ bhayabheravaṃ passeyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, aparena samayena yā tā rattiyo abhiññātā abhilakkhitā – cātuddasī pañcadasī aṭṭhamī ca pakkhassa – tathārūpāsu rattīsu yāni tāni ārāmacetiyāni vanacetiyāni rukkhacetiyāni bhiṃsanakāni salomahaṃsāni tathārūpesu senāsanesu viharāmi. Tattha ca me, brāhmaṇa, viharato mago vā āgacchati, moro vā kaṭṭhaṃ pāteti, vāto vā paṇṇakasaṭaṃ paṇṇasaṭaṃ (sī. pī.) ereti; tassa mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa etadahosi tassa mayhaṃ evaṃ hoti (sī. syā.) – ‘etaṃ nūna taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchatī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, etadahosi – ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ aññadatthu bhayapaṭikaṅkhī bhayapāṭikaṅkhī (sī.) viharāmi? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ yathābhūtassa yathābhūtassa yathābhūtassa (sī. syā.) me taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchati, tathābhūtaṃ tathābhūtova yathābhūto yathābhūtova (sī. syā.) taṃ bhayabheravaṃ paṭivineyya’nti. Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, caṅkamantassa taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchati. So kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, neva tāva tiṭṭhāmi na nisīdāmi na nipajjāmi, yāva caṅkamantova taṃ bhayabheravaṃ paṭivinemi. Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ṭhitassa taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchati. So kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, neva tāva caṅkamāmi na nisīdāmi na nipajjāmi. Yāva ṭhitova taṃ bhayabheravaṃ paṭivinemi. Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, nisinnassa taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchati. So kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, neva tāva nipajjāmi na tiṭṭhāmi na caṅkamāmi, yāva nisinnova taṃ bhayabheravaṃ paṭivinemi. Tassa mayhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, nipannassa taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchati. So kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, neva tāva nisīdāmi na tiṭṭhāmi na caṅkamāmi, yāva nipannova taṃ bhayabheravaṃ paṭivinemi.
mula_english:
“I considered thus: ‘There are the specially auspicious nights of the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth of the fortnight. Now what if, on such nights as these, I were to dwell in such awe-inspiring, horrifying abodes as orchard shrines (*ārāmacetiya*), woodland shrines (*vanacetiya*), and tree shrines (*rukkha cetiya*)? Perhaps I might encounter that fear and dread (*bhayabherava*).'

And later, on such specially auspicious nights as the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth of the fortnight, I dwelt in such awe-inspiring, horrifying abodes as orchard shrines, woodland shrines, and tree shrines.

And while I was dwelling there, a wild animal would approach, or a peacock would drop a stick, or the wind would rustle the leaves. Then I would think: ‘Surely that is the fear and dread approaching.’

I thought: ‘Why do I dwell always expecting fear and dread? What if I subdue that fear and dread while keeping the same posture that I am in when it comes upon me?’

While I walked (*caṅkamantassa*), the fear and dread came upon me; I neither stood nor sat nor lay down till, while walking, I had subdued that fear and dread.

While I stood, the fear and dread came upon me; I neither walked nor sat nor lay down till, while standing, I had subdued that fear and dread.

While I sat (*nisinnassa*), the fear and dread came upon me; I neither lay down nor stood nor walked till, while sitting, I had subdued that fear and dread.

While I lay down (*nipannassa*), the fear and dread came upon me; I neither sat nor stood nor walked till, while lying down, I had subdued that fear and dread.
commentary_pali:
49.Tassamayhanti ko anusandhi? Bodhisatto kira imāni soḷasārammaṇāni pariggaṇhanto ca bhayabheravaṃ adisvā bhayabheravaṃ nāma evarūpāsu rattīsu evarūpe senāsane ca paññāyati, handa naṃ tatthāpi gavesissāmīti bhayabheravagavesanamakāsi, etamatthaṃ bhagavā idāni brāhmaṇassa dassento tassa mayhantiādimāha.

Tattha yā tāti ubhayametaṃ rattīnaṃyeva uddesaniddesavacanaṃ. Abhiññātāti ettha abhīti lakkhaṇatthe upasaggo. Tasmā abhiññātāti candapāripūriyā candaparikkhayenāti evamādīhi lakkhaṇehi ñātāti veditabbā. Abhilakkhitāti ettha upasaggamattameva, tasmā abhilakkhitāti lakkhaṇīyā icceva attho, uposathasamādānadhammassavanapūjāsakkārādikaraṇatthaṃ lakkhetabbā sallakkhetabbā upalakkhetabbāti vuttaṃ hoti.

yā tā Abhiññātā abhī Abhilakkhitā

Cātuddasīti pakkhassa paṭhamadivasato pabhuti catuddasannaṃ pūraṇī ekā ratti. Evaṃ pañcadasī aṭṭhamī ca. Pakkhassāti sukkapakkhassa kaṇhapakkhassa ca. Etā tisso tisso katvā cha rattiyo, tasmā sabbattha pakkhavacanaṃ yojetabbaṃ ‘‘pakkhassa cātuddasī pakkhassa pañcadasī pakkhassa aṭṭhamī’’ti. Atha pañcamī kasmā na gahitāti? Asabbakālikattā. Buddhe kira bhagavati anuppannepi uppajjitvā aparinibbutepi pañcamī anabhilakkhitāyeva, parinibbute pana dhammasaṅgāhakattherā cintesuṃ ‘‘dhammassavanaṃ cirena hotī’’ti. Tato sammannitvā pañcamīti dhammassavanadivasaṃ ṭhapesuṃ, tato pabhuti sā abhilakkhitā jātā, evaṃ asabbakālikattā ettha na gahitāti.

Cātuddasī pañcadasī aṭṭhamī Pakkhassā

Tathārūpāsūti tathāvidhāsu. Ārāmacetiyānīti pupphārāmaphalārāmādayo ārāmā eva ārāmacetiyāni. Cittīkataṭṭhena hi cetiyānīti vuccanti, pūjanīyaṭṭhenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Vanacetiyānīti baliharaṇavanasaṇḍasubhagavanadevasālavanādīni vanāniyeva vanacetiyāni. Rukkhacetiyānīti gāmanigamādidvāresu pūjanīyarukkhāyeva rukkhacetiyāni. Lokiyā hi dibbādhivatthāti vā maññamānā tesuyeva vā dibbasaññino hutvā ārāmavanarukkhe cittīkaronti , pūjenti, tena te sabbepi cetiyānīti vuccanti. Bhiṃsanakānīti bhayajanakāni, passatopi suṇatopi bhayaṃ janenti. Salomahaṃsānīti saheva lomahaṃsena vattanti, pavisamānasseva lomahaṃsajananato. Appeva nāma passeyyanti api nāma taṃ bhayabheravaṃ passeyyameva. Aparena samayenāti, ‘‘etadahosi yaṃnūnāha’’nti evaṃ cintitakālato paṭṭhāya aññena kālena.

Tathārūpāsū Ārāmacetiyānī cetiyānī Vanacetiyānī Rukkhacetiyānī cetiyānī Bhiṃsanakānī Salomahaṃsānī Appeva nāma passeyya Aparena samayenā

Tattha ca me brāhmaṇa viharatoti tathārūpesu senāsanesu yaṃ yaṃ manussānaṃ āyācanaupahārakaraṇārahaṃ yakkhaṭṭhānaṃ pupphadhūpamaṃsaruhiravasāmedapihakapapphāsasurāmerayādīhi okiṇṇakilinnadharaṇitalaṃ ekanipātaṃ viya yakkharakkhasapisācānaṃ, yaṃ divāpi passantānaṃ hadayaṃ maññe phalati, taṃ ṭhānaṃ sandhāyāha ‘‘tattha ca me, brāhmaṇa, viharato’’ti. Mago vā āgacchatīti siṅgāni vā khurāni vā koṭṭento gokaṇṇakhaggadīpivarāhādibhedo mago vā āgacchati, sabbacatuppadānañhi idha magoti nāmaṃ. Katthaci pana kāḷasiṅgālopi vuccati. Yathāha –

Tattha ca me brāhmaṇa viharato Mago vā āgacchatī mago

‘‘Usabhasseva te khandho, sīhasseva vijambhitaṃ;

Magarāja namo tyatthu, api kiñci labhāmase’’ti. (jā. 1.3.133);

Moro vā kaṭṭhaṃ pātetīti moro vā sukkhakaṭṭhaṃ rukkhato cāletvā pāteti. Moraggahaṇena ca idha sabbapakkhiggahaṇaṃ adhippetaṃ, tena yo koci pakkhīti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha vā moro vāti vā saddena añño vā koci pakkhīti. Esa nayo purime magaggahaṇepi. Vāto vā paṇṇakasaṭaṃ eretīti vāto vā paṇṇakacavaraṃ ghaṭṭeti. Etaṃ nūna taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchatīti yametaṃ āgacchati, taṃ bhayabheravaṃ nūnāti. Ito pabhuti ca ārammaṇameva bhayabheravanti veditabbaṃ. Parittassa ca adhimattassa ca bhayassa ārammaṇattā sukhārammaṇaṃ rūpaṃ sukhamiva. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ aññadatthu bhayapaṭikaṅkhī viharāmīti ahaṃ kho kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ekaṃseneva bhayaṃ ākaṅkhamāno icchamāno hutvā viharāmi.

Moro vā kaṭṭhaṃ pātetī Vāto vā paṇṇakasaṭaṃ eretī Etaṃ nūna taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchatī Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ aññadatthu bhayapaṭikaṅkhī viharāmī

Yathābhūtaṃ yathābhūtassāti yena yena iriyāpathena bhūtassa bhavitassa sato vattamānassa samaṅgībhūtassa vā. Meti mama santike. Tathābhūtaṃ tathābhūto vāti tena teneva iriyāpathena bhūto bhavito santo vattamāno samaṅgībhūto vāti attho. So kho ahaṃ…pe… paṭivinemīti bodhisattassa kira caṅkamantassa tasmiṃ magasiṅgakhurasaddādibhede bhayabheravārammaṇe āgate neva mahāsatto tiṭṭhati, na nisīdati na sayati, atha kho caṅkamantova parivīmaṃsanto parivicinanto bhayabheravaṃ na passati, magasiṅgakhurasaddādimattameva cetaṃ hoti, so taṃ ñatvā idaṃ nāmetaṃ, na bhayabheravanti tato tiṭṭhati vā nisīdati vā sayati vā. Etamatthaṃ dassento ‘‘so kho aha’’ntiādimāha. Esa nayo sabbapeyyālesu. Ito parañca iriyāpathapaṭipāṭiyā avatvā āsannapaṭipāṭiyā iriyāpathā vuttāti veditabbā, caṅkamantassa hi bhayabherave āgate na ṭhito na nisinno na nipanno ṭhitassāpi āgate na caṅkamīti evaṃ tassa āsannapaṭipāṭiyā vuttāti.

Yathābhūtaṃ yathābhūtassā Me Tathābhūtaṃ tathābhūto vā So kho ahaṃ…pe… paṭivinemī

Bhayabheravasenāsanādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Asammohavihāravaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
49. *tassa mayha*nti: What is the connection? It is said that while the Bodhisattva was taking up these sixteen objects, fear and dread appeared in such nights and in such lodgings. "Come, I will investigate it even there," he made an investigation into fear and dread. The Blessed One, showing this matter to the Brahmin now, spoke beginning with *tassa mayha*nti.

There, *yā tā*ti: This is a word of designation and indication of both nights.

*abhiññātā*ti: Here, *abhi* is a prefix in the sense of characteristic. Therefore, *abhiññātā*ti should be understood as known by characteristics beginning with the moon's fullness and the moon's waning.

*abhilakkhitā*ti: Here, there is only a prefix. Therefore, *abhilakkhitā*ti means "to be marked," this is the meaning. It means that one should be marked, well-marked, and especially marked for the purpose of undertaking the *uposatha*, taking up the Dhamma, hearing the Dhamma, and making offerings and reverence.

*yā tā abhiññātā abhī abhilakkhitā cātuddasī*ti: The fourteenth day from the first day of the fortnight is one night.

Likewise, the fifteenth and eighth days also.

*pakkhassā*ti: Of the waxing and waning fortnight.

Having made these three three, six nights, therefore, the word "fortnight" should be connected everywhere: "the fourteenth of the fortnight, the fifteenth of the fortnight, the eighth of the fortnight."

Then why is the fifth day not taken? Because it is not always timely.

It is said that even when the Buddha, the Blessed One, had not arisen, having arisen, and even when he had not passed away, the fifth day was not marked. But after he had passed away, the elders who compiled the Dhamma thought, "The hearing of the Dhamma will be slow."

Then, having agreed, they established the fifth day as the day for hearing the Dhamma. From then on, it became marked. Thus, because it is not always timely, it is not taken here.

*cātuddasī pañcadasī aṭṭhamī pakkhassā tathārūpāsū*ti: In such forms.

*ārāmacetiyānī*ti: Gardens such as flower gardens and fruit gardens are themselves garden shrines (ārāmacetiyas).

Indeed, *cetiyānī*ti are called because of the state of being built up, it is said that it is in the state of being worthy of worship.

*vanacetiyānī*ti: Forests such as forests where offerings are made, groves, beautiful forests, forests of gods, and *sāla* forests are themselves forest shrines (vanacetiyas).

*rukkhacetiyānī*ti: Trees at the gates of villages, towns, etc., that are worthy of worship are themselves tree shrines (rukkhacetiyas).

Indeed, worldly people, thinking "the gods dwell in them," or being divine-minded in those very ones, build up, worship the garden, forest, and trees. Therefore, all those are called *cetiyānī*.

*bhiṃsanakānī*ti: They are fear-producing, they generate fear even in those who see and hear.

*salomahaṃsānī*ti: They exist together with goosebumps, from the very generation of goosebumps as one enters.

*appeva nāma passeyya*nti: Perhaps one might see that very fear and dread.

*aparena samayenā*ti: "It was so that I would..." from the time of such thinking, by another time.

*tathārūpāsū ārāmacetiyānī cetiyānī vanacetiyānī rukkhacetiyānī cetiyānī bhiṃsanakānī salomahaṃsānī appeva nāma passeyya aparena samayenā tattha ca me brāhmaṇa viharato*ti: In such lodgings, whatever place of *yakkhas* worthy of making requests and offerings by humans, a ground covered and soiled by flowers, incense, meat, blood, fat, marrow, *pihaka*, *papphāsa*, liquor, and intoxicants, as if a single fall of *yakkhas*, *rakkhasas*, and *pisācas*, whatever heart of those seeing even by day I think bursts, having regard for that place, he said, "There, Brahmin, I was dwelling."

*mago vā āgacchatī*ti: Either a *maga* comes, one whose differences are cow-eared, sword-toothed, *dīpi*, boar, etc., scraping either horns or hooves. Indeed, here the name *maga* is for all quadrupeds.

But in some places, even a black jackal is called.

As he said -

*tattha ca me brāhmaṇa viharato mago vā āgacchatī mago usabhasseva* te *khandho, sīhasseva vijambhitaṃ; magarāja namo tyatthu, api kiñci labhāmase*’ti.
3.133)

*moro vā kaṭṭhaṃ pātetī*: *moro vā* means having dislodged a dry branch from a tree, it drops it. By the taking up of "peacock", all birds are intended here; therefore, it is said, "any bird." Or alternatively, *moro vāti vā* means "or any other bird" by the word "or." This is the same method as in the previous taking up of the path. *vāto vā paṇṇakasaṭaṃ eretī*: *vāto vā* means "or the wind strikes the heap of leaves." *etaṃ nūna taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchatī*: *yametaṃ āgacchati*, "that which is coming, that is certainly the cause of fear and dread." And from here onward, it should be understood that the object itself is the cause of fear and dread, since it is the object of a small or great fear. Form is a pleasant object like pleasure. *kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ aññadatthu bhayapaṭikaṅkhī viharāmī*: *ahaṃ kho kiṃ kāraṇaṃ* means "for what reason do I live desiring and wishing for fear alone?"

*moro vā kaṭṭhaṃ pātetī vāto vā paṇṇakasaṭaṃ eretī etaṃ nūna taṃ bhayabheravaṃ āgacchatī kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ aññadatthu bhayapaṭikaṅkhī viharāmī*

*yathābhūtaṃ yathābhūtassā*: *yena yena iriyāpathena bhūtassa bhavitassa sato vattamānassa samaṅgībhūtassa vā*, means "according to how it actually is," according to whatever posture, whether past, future, present, or integrated. *me* means "in my presence." *tathābhūtaṃ tathābhūto vā* means "in that very posture, whether past, future, present, or integrated." *so kho ahaṃ…pe… paṭivinemī*: it seems that for the Bodhisatta, while walking, when an object causing fear and dread comes in the form of the sound of deer horns or hooves, the great being neither stands, nor sits, nor lies down. But while walking, considering and investigating, he does not see the cause of fear and dread; it is merely the sound of deer horns or hooves. Having known that, "this is its name, it is not the cause of fear and dread," then he stands, sits, or lies down. Showing this meaning, he said, "*so kho ahaṃ*," etc. This is the same method in all the expansions. And furthermore, it should be understood that the postures are stated according to the order of proximity, not according to the order of succession of postures. For when fear and dread come to one who is walking, he does not stand, sit, or lie down; and when it comes to one who is standing, he does not walk. Thus, it is stated according to the order of proximity.

*yathābhūtaṃ yathābhūtassā me tathābhūtaṃ tathābhūto vā so kho ahaṃ…pe… paṭivinemī*

The description of fear, dread, dwelling places, etc., is finished.

Description of living without bewilderment

mula_pali: 50. ‘‘Santi kho pana, brāhmaṇa, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā rattiṃyeva samānaṃ divāti sañjānanti, divāyeva samānaṃ rattīti sañjānanti. Idamahaṃ tesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ sammohavihārasmiṃ vadāmi. Ahaṃ kho pana, brāhmaṇa, rattiṃyeva samānaṃ rattīti sañjānāmi, divāyeva samānaṃ divāti sañjānāmi. Yaṃ kho taṃ, brāhmaṇa, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘asammohadhammo satto loke uppanno bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti, mameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘asammohadhammo satto loke uppanno bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti.
mula_english:
“Now, brahmin, there are some ascetics and brahmins who perceive day when it is night and night when it is day.

I say that on their part this is an abiding in delusion (sammohavihāra).

But I, brahmin, perceive night when it is night and day when it is day.

Rightly speaking, were it to be said of anyone: ‘A being not subject to delusion (asammohadhamma) has appeared in the world for the welfare and happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans,’ it is of me indeed that rightly speaking this should be said.
commentary_pali:
50. Evaṃ bhiṃsanakesupi ṭhānesu attano bhayabheravābhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni jhāyīnaṃ sammohaṭṭhānesu attano asammohavihāraṃ dassetuṃ santi kho pana, brāhmaṇātiādimāha.

Tattha santīti atthi saṃvijjanti upalabbhanti. Rattiṃyeva samānanti rattiṃyeva santaṃ, divāti sañjānantīti ‘‘divaso aya’’nti sañjānanti. Divāyeva samānanti divasaṃyeva santaṃ. Rattīti sañjānantīti ‘‘ratti aya’’nti sañjānanti. Kasmā panete evaṃsaññino hontīti. Vuṭṭhānakosallābhāvato vā sakuṇarutato vā. Kathaṃ? Idhekacco odātakasiṇalābhī divā parikammaṃ katvā divā samāpanno divāyeva vuṭṭhahāmīti manasikāraṃ uppādeti, no ca kho addhānaparicchede kusalo hoti. So divasaṃ atikkamitvā rattibhāge vuṭṭhāti. Odātakasiṇapharaṇavasena cassa visadaṃ hoti vibhūtaṃ suvibhūtaṃ. So, divā vuṭṭhahāmīti uppāditamanasikāratāya odātakasiṇapharaṇavisadavibhūtatāya ca rattiṃyeva samānaṃ divāti sañjānāti. Idha panekacco nīlakasiṇalābhī rattiṃ parikammaṃ katvā rattiṃ samāpanno rattiṃyeva vuṭṭhahāmīti manasikāraṃ uppādeti, no ca kho addhānaparicchede kusalo hoti. So rattiṃ atikkamitvā divasabhāge vuṭṭhāti. Nīlakasiṇapharaṇavasena cassa avisadaṃ hoti avibhūtaṃ. So rattiṃ vuṭṭhahāmīti uppāditamanasikāratāya nīlakasiṇapharaṇāvisadāvibhūtatāya ca divāyeva samānaṃ rattīti sañjānāti. Evaṃ tāva vuṭṭhānakosallābhāvato evaṃsaññino honti.

santī Rattiṃyeva samāna divāti sañjānantī Divāyeva samāna Rattīti sañjānantī

Sakuṇarutato pana idhekacco antosenāsane nisinno hoti. Atha divā ravanakasakuṇā kākādayo candālokena divāti maññamānā rattiṃ ravanti, aññehi vā kāraṇehi. So tesaṃ saddaṃ sutvā rattiṃyeva samānaṃ divāti sañjānāti. Idha panekacco pabbatantare gambhīrāya ghanavanappaṭicchannāya giriguhāya sattāhavaddalikāya vattamānāya antarahitasūriyāloke kāle nisinno hoti. Atha rattiṃ ravanakasakuṇā ulūkādayo majjhanhikasamayepi tattha tattha samandhakāre nilīnā rattisaññāya vā aññehi vā kāraṇehi ravanti. So tesaṃ saddaṃ sutvā divāyeva samānaṃ rattīti sañjānāti. Evaṃ sakuṇarutato evaṃsaññino hontīti. Idamahanti idaṃ ahaṃ evaṃ sañjānanaṃ . Sammohavihārasmiṃ vadāmīti sammohavihārapariyāpannaṃ antogadhaṃ, sammohavihārānaṃ aññataraṃ vadāmīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Idamaha Sammohavihārasmiṃ vadāmī

Ahaṃ kho pana brāhmaṇa…pe… sañjānāmīti pākaṭo bodhisattassa rattindivaparicchedo sattāhavaddalepi candimasūriyesu adissamānesupi jānātiyeva ‘‘ettakaṃ purebhattakālo gato, ettakaṃ pacchābhattakālo, ettakaṃ paṭhamayāmo, ettakaṃ majjhimayāmo, ettakaṃ pacchimayāmo’’ti, tasmā evamāha. Anacchariyañcetaṃ yaṃ pūritapāramī bodhisatto evaṃ jānāti. Padesañāṇe ṭhitānaṃ sāvakānampi hi rattindivaparicchedo pākaṭo hoti.

Ahaṃ kho pana brāhmaṇa…pe… sañjānāmī

Kalyāṇiyamahāvihāre kira godattatthero dvaṅgulakāle bhattaṃ gahetvā aṅgulakāle bhuñjati. Sūriye adissamānepi pātoyeva senāsanaṃ pavisitvā tāya velāya nikkhamati. Ekadivasaṃ ārāmikā ‘‘sve therassa nikkhamanakāle passāmā’’ti bhattaṃ sampādetvā kālatthambhamūle nisīdiṃsu. Thero dvaṅgulakāleyeva nikkhamati. Tato pabhuti kira sūriye adissamānepi therassa nikkhamanasaññāya eva bheriṃ ākoṭenti.

Ajagaravihārepi kāḷadevatthero antovasse yāmagaṇḍikaṃ paharati, āciṇṇametaṃ therassa. Na ca yāmayantanāḷikaṃ payojeti, aññe bhikkhū payojenti. Atha nikkhante paṭhame yāme there muggaraṃ gahetvā ṭhitamatteyeva ekaṃ dve vāre paharanteyeva vā yāmayantaṃ patati, evaṃ tīsu yāmesu samaṇadhammaṃ katvā thero pātoyeva gāmaṃ pavisitvā piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya vihāraṃ āgantvā bhojanavelāya pattaṃ gahetvā divā vihāraṭṭhānaṃ gantvā samaṇadhammaṃ karoti. Bhikkhū kālatthambhaṃ disvā therassa adisvā āgamanatthāya pesenti. So bhikkhu theraṃ divā vihāraṭṭhānā nikkhamantameva vā antarāmagge vā passati. Evaṃ padesañāṇe ṭhitānaṃ sāvakānampi rattindivaparicchedo pākaṭo hoti, kimaṅgaṃ pana bodhisattānanti.

Yaṃ kho taṃ brāhmaṇa…pe… vadeyyāti ettha pana ‘‘yaṃ kho taṃ, brāhmaṇa, asammohadhammo satto loke uppanno…pe… sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti vacanaṃ vadamāno koci sammā vadeyya, sammā vadamāno siyā, na vitathavādī assa. Mameva taṃ vacanaṃ vadamāno sammā vadeyya, sammā vadamāno siyā, na vitathavādī assāti evaṃ padasambandho veditabbo.

Yaṃ kho taṃ brāhmaṇa…pe… vadeyyā

Tattha asammohadhammoti asammohasabhāvo. Loketi manussaloke. Bahujanahitāyāti bahujanassa hitatthāya, paññāsampattiyā diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikahitūpadesakoti. Bahujanasukhāyāti bahujanassa sukhatthāya, cāgasampattiyā upakaraṇasukhassa dāyakoti. Lokānukampāyāti lokassa anukampatthāya, mettākaruṇāsampattiyā mātāpitaro viya lokassa rakkhitā gopayitāti. Atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānanti idha devamanussaggahaṇena ca bhabbapuggalaveneyyasatteyeva gahetvā tesaṃ nibbānamaggaphalādhigamāya attano uppattiṃ dassetīti veditabbo. Atthāyāti hi vutte paramatthatthāya nibbānāyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Hitāyāti vutte taṃ sampāpakamaggatthāyāti vuttaṃ hoti, nibbānasampāpakamaggato hi uttari hitaṃ nāma natthi. Sukhāyāti vutte phalasamāpattisukhatthāyāti vuttaṃ hoti, tato uttari sukhābhāvato. Vuttañcetaṃ ‘‘ayaṃ samādhi paccuppannasukho ceva āyatiñca sukhavipāko’’ti (dī. ni. 3.355; a. ni. 5.27; vibha. 804).

asammohadhammo Loke Bahujanahitāyā Bahujanasukhāyā Lokānukampāyā Atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna Atthāyā Hitāyā Sukhāyā

Asammohavihāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Pubbabhāgapaṭipadādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
50. Thus, having shown his absence of fear and terror even in frightening places, now, in order to show his un-deluded conduct in places of delusion for meditators, he said beginning with, "But indeed, brāhmaṇas, there are."

There, *santi* means there are, they exist, they are found. *rattiṃyeva samāna*nti means existing only at night, *divāti sañjānantī*ti means "they recognize [it] as 'this is day.'" *divāyeva samāna*nti means existing only during the day. *rattīti sañjānantī*ti means "they recognize [it] as 'this is night.'" Why are these people thus minded? Either from a lack of skill in rising [from meditation], or from the sound of birds. How? Here, someone having gained a white *kasiṇa*, having done preliminary work during the day, having attained [absorption] during the day, produces the thought, "I will rise during the day," but he is not skilled in determining the duration [of time]. He rises having passed the day, in the night portion. And for him it is clear, distinct, very distinct due to the touch of the white *kasiṇa*. He, due to the thought produced "I will rise during the day," and due to the clear distinctness of the touch of the white *kasiṇa*, recognizes what is only night as day. Here, someone having gained a blue *kasiṇa*, having done preliminary work at night, having attained [absorption] at night, produces the thought, "I will rise during the night," but he is not skilled in determining the duration [of time]. He rises having passed the night, in the day portion. And for him it is unclear, indistinct due to the touch of the blue *kasiṇa*. He, due to the thought produced "I will rise during the night," and due to the unclear indistinctness of the touch of the blue *kasiṇa*, recognizes what is only day as night. Thus, firstly, from a lack of skill in rising [from meditation], they are thus minded.

*santi rattiṃyeva samāna divāti sañjānantī divāyeva samāna rattīti sañjānantī*

Moreover, from the sound of birds, here someone is sitting in an isolated dwelling. Then, during the day, birds that make noise, crows and so on, thinking [it is] day due to moonlight, caw at night, or due to other reasons. He, having heard their sound, recognizes what is only night as day. Here, someone is sitting in a mountain cave in the interior of a mountain, covered by a dense forest, where it is always the seventh day of the dark half-month, at a time when the sunlight is obscured. Then, at night, birds that make noise, owls and so on, even at midday, hidden in the surrounding darkness, caw with the perception of night, or due to other reasons. He, having heard their sound, recognizes what is only day as night. Thus, from the sound of birds, they are thus minded.

*idamaha*nti means, this, I, such recognition. *sammohavihārasmiṃ vadāmī*ti means included in conduct that is deluded, contained within, I speak of one of the deluded conducts, is what was said.

*idamaha sammohavihārasmiṃ vadāmī*

*ahaṃ kho pana brāhmaṇa…pe… sañjānāmī*ti [it is] evident that the Bodhisattva's distinction between night and day, even on the seventh day of the dark half-month, even when the moon and sun are not visible, he knows "this much is the time before the meal, this much is the time after the meal, this much is the first watch, this much is the middle watch, this much is the last watch," therefore he said thus. And it is not a wonder that a Bodhisattva who has fulfilled the perfections knows thus. For even disciples established in partial knowledge, the distinction between night and day is evident.

*ahaṃ kho pana brāhmaṇa…pe… sañjānāmī*

It is said that in the Kalyāṇī great monastery, the elder Godatta takes his meal when [the shadow] is two *aṅgula*s [long], and eats when [the shadow] is one *aṅgula* [long]. Even when the sun is not visible, he enters his dwelling early in the morning and leaves at that time. One day, the monastery attendants, having prepared the meal, sat at the base of the time pillar, [thinking] "tomorrow we will see the time the elder leaves." The elder leaves when [the shadow] is two *aṅgula*s [long].
Thereafter, it is said that even when the sun was not visible, they would strike the drum at the time that the elder usually leaves.

At Ajagara Monastery, the elder Kāḷadeva would strike the time-gong during the rains, it was his habit.

He did not use a time-keeping water clock himself, other monks used it.

Then, when the first watch of the night had passed, the elder, having taken a hammer, as soon as he had stood [there], either striking it once or twice, the time-keeper would fall, thus in the three watches of the night, having performed the duties of a recluse, the elder, early in the morning, having entered the village and having taken alms-food, would come to the monastery and at mealtime, having taken his bowl, in the daytime, having gone to the monastery grounds, would perform the duties of a recluse.

Monks, having seen the time-pillar, would send [word] to the elder for the purpose of his coming without seeing it.

That monk would see the elder either leaving the monastery grounds in the daytime or on the road.

Thus, even for disciples established in knowledge of the region, the demarcation of day and night is evident, what to say of bodhisattvas?

That which, O Brahmin...pe... one should say," here, however, the statement, "That which, O Brahmin, is a being of undistracted nature, arisen in the world...pe... for the happiness of gods and humans,"

If someone speaking should speak correctly, he would be speaking correctly, he would not be a speaker of falsehood.

Speaking that statement of mine, one should speak correctly, he would be speaking correctly, he would not be a speaker of falsehood," thus the connection of the words should be understood.

There, *asammohadhammo* means "nature of non-delusion."

*Loke* means "in the human world."

*Bahujanahitāyā* means "for the welfare of many people," that is, "with the accomplishment of wisdom, he is a teacher of benefits in this life and the next."

*Bahujanasukhāyā* means "for the happiness of many people," that is, "with the accomplishment of generosity, he is a giver of the happiness of possessions."

*Lokānukampāyā* means "out of compassion for the world," that is, "with the accomplishment of loving-kindness and compassion, he is a protector and guardian of the world like a mother and father."

*Atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna* means "here, by the mention of gods and humans, having taken only beings who are capable individuals and who can be guided, he shows his arising for the attainment of the path, fruit, and liberation for them," this should be understood.

*Atthāyā* when said, "it is said for the sake of the ultimate goal, for liberation."

*Hitāyā* when said, "it is said for the sake of the path that leads to that," for there is no benefit higher than the path that leads to liberation.

*Sukhāyā* when said, "it is said for the sake of the happiness of the fruition of attainment," for there is no higher happiness than that.

And it was said, "This *samādhi* is both present happiness and has happiness as its result in the future" (Dī.

mula_pali: 51. ‘‘Āraddhaṃ kho pana me, brāhmaṇa, vīriyaṃ ahosi asallīnaṃ, upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā appammuṭṭhā (syā.), passaddho kāyo asāraddho, samāhitaṃ cittaṃ ekaggaṃ. So kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca vihāsiṃ, sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedesiṃ; yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ.
mula_english:
51. “Tireless energy was aroused in me, O Brahmin, and unremitting mindfulness was established, my body was tranquil and untroubled, my mind concentrated and unified.

Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I entered upon and abided in the first *jhāna* (first meditative absorption), which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.

With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, I entered upon and abided in the second *jhāna* (second meditative absorption), which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration.

With the fading away as well of rapture, I abided in equanimity, and mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, I entered upon and abided in the third *jhāna* (third meditative absorption), on account of which noble ones announce: ‘He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.’

With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, I entered upon and abided in the fourth *jhāna* (fourth meditative absorption), which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
commentary_pali:
51. Evaṃ bhagavā buddhaguṇapaṭilābhāvasānaṃ attano asammohavihāraṃ brāhmaṇassa dassetvā idāni yāya paṭipadāya taṃ koṭippattaṃ asammohavihāraṃ adhigato, taṃ pubbabhāgato pabhuti dassetuṃ āraddhaṃ kho pana me brāhmaṇātiādimāha.

Keci panāhu ‘‘imaṃ asammohavihāraṃ sutvā brāhmaṇassa cittamevaṃ uppannaṃ ‘kāya nu kho paṭipadāya imaṃ patto’ti, tassa cittamaññāya imāyāhaṃ paṭipadāya imaṃ uttamaṃ asammohavihāraṃ pattoti dassento evamāhā’’ti.

Tattha āraddhaṃ kho pana me, brāhmaṇa, vīriyaṃ ahosīti, brāhmaṇa, na mayā ayaṃ uttamo asammohavihāro kusītena muṭṭhassatinā sāraddhakāyena vikkhittacittena vā adhigato, apica kho tadadhigamāya āraddhaṃ kho pana me vīriyaṃ ahosi, bodhimaṇḍe nisinnena mayā caturaṅgavīriyaṃ āraddhaṃ ahosi, paggahitaṃ asithilappavattitanti vuttaṃ hoti. Āraddhattāyeva ca metaṃ asallīnaṃ ahosi.

āraddhaṃ kho pana me, brāhmaṇa, vīriyaṃ ahosī asallīnaṃ

Upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhāti na kevalañca vīriyameva, satipi me ārammaṇābhimukhībhāvena upaṭṭhitā ahosi. Upaṭṭhitattāyeva ca asammuṭṭhā. Passaddho kāyoti kāyacittappassaddhisambhavena kāyopi me passaddho ahosi. Tattha yasmā nāmakāye passaddhe rūpakāyopi passaddhoyeva hoti, tasmā nāmakāyo rūpakāyoti avisesetvāva passaddho kāyoti vuttaṃ. Asāraddhoti so ca kho passaddhattāyeva asāraddho, vigatadarathoti vuttaṃ hoti. Samāhitaṃ cittaṃ ekagganti cittampi me sammā āhitaṃ suṭṭhu ṭhapitaṃ appitaṃ viya ahosi. Samāhitattā eva ca ekaggaṃ acalaṃ nipphandananti, ettāvatā jhānassa pubbabhāgapaṭipadā kathitā hoti.

Upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā Passaddho kāyo Asāraddho Samāhitaṃ cittaṃ ekagga

Idāni imāya paṭipadāya adhigataṃ paṭhamajjhānaṃ ādiṃ katvā vijjāttayapariyosānaṃ visesaṃ dassento so kho ahantiādimāha. Tattha vivicceva kāmehi…pe… catutthajjhānaṃ upasampajjavihāsinti ettha tāva yaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, taṃ sabbaṃ visuddhimagge pathavīkasiṇakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Kevalañhi tattha ‘‘upasampajja viharatī’’ti āgataṃ, idha ‘‘vihāsi’’nti, ayameva viseso. Kiṃ katvā pana bhagavā imāni jhānāni upasampajja vihāsīti, kammaṭṭhānaṃ bhāvetvā. Kataraṃ? Ānāpānassatikammaṭṭhānaṃ.

Imāni ca pana cattāri jhānāni kesañci cittekaggatatthāni honti, kesañci vipassanāpādakāni, kesañci abhiññāpādakāni, kesañci nirodhapādakāni, kesañci bhavokkamanatthāni. Tattha khīṇāsavānaṃ cittekaggatatthāni honti. Te hi samāpajjitvā ekaggacittā sukhaṃ divasaṃ viharissāmāti iccevaṃ kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā aṭṭha samāpattiyo nibbattenti. Sekkhaputhujjanānaṃ samāpattito vuṭṭhāya samāhitena cittena vipassissāmāti nibbattentānaṃ vipassanāpādakāni honti. Ye pana aṭṭha samāpattiyo nibbattetvā abhiññāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā samāpattito vuṭṭhāya ‘‘ekopi hutvā bahudhā hotī’’ti (dī. ni. 1.238; paṭi. ma. 1.102) vuttanayā abhiññāyo patthentā nibbattenti, tesaṃ abhiññāpādakāni honti. Ye pana aṭṭha samāpattiyo nibbattetvā nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā sattāhaṃ acittā hutvā diṭṭheva dhamme nirodhaṃ nibbānaṃ patvā sukhaṃ viharissāmāti nibbattenti, tesaṃ nirodhapādakāni honti. Ye pana aṭṭha samāpattiyo nibbattetvā aparihīnajjhānā brahmaloke uppajjissāmāti nibbattenti, tesaṃ bhavokkamanatthāni honti.

Bhagavatā panidaṃ catutthajjhānaṃ bodhirukkhamūle nibbattitaṃ, taṃ tassa vipassanāpādakañceva ahosi abhiññāpādakañca sabbakiccasādhakañca, sabbalokiyalokuttaraguṇadāyakanti veditabbaṃ.

Pubbenivāsakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
51. Thus, the Blessed One, after showing the brahmin his own state of non-delusion, which is the culmination of the Buddha's virtues, now, in order to show, from the beginning, the practice by which he attained that state of non-delusion that reached its peak, said, "Indeed, brahmin, my energy was aroused," and so on. Some, however, say, "After hearing of this state of non-delusion, such a thought arose in the brahmin's mind: 'By what practice did he attain this?' Knowing his thought, and showing that 'I attained this supreme state of non-delusion by this practice,' he said thus." There, "Indeed, brahmin, my energy was aroused," means, brahmin, this supreme state of non-delusion was not attained by me through laziness, forgetfulness, a body given to indulgence, or a distracted mind; but rather, for the attainment of that, indeed, my energy was aroused. Seated at the *bodhi* tree, fourfold energy was aroused by me; it was exerted, continuously and unremittingly. And precisely because it was aroused, it was unflagging. Indeed, brahmin, my energy was aroused, unflagging. "Mindfulness was present, unforgetful," means not only energy, but also mindfulness was present in me, through directing itself towards the object. And precisely because it was present, it was unforgetful. "The body was tranquil" means, through the arising of tranquility of body and mind, my body too was tranquil. There, since when the mind-body is tranquil, the form-body is also tranquil, therefore, without distinguishing between mind-body and form-body, it is said "the body was tranquil." "Unperturbed" means, and precisely because of that tranquility, it was unperturbed, free from agitation, it is said. "The mind was concentrated, one-pointed" means, my mind was well-composed, well-established, as if fixed. And precisely because it was concentrated, it was one-pointed, unwavering, unmoving. Thus far, the preliminary practice of *jhāna* has been described. Mindfulness was present, unforgetful, the body was tranquil, unperturbed, the mind was concentrated, one-pointed. Now, showing the distinction of the first *jhāna* and so on, attained by this practice, up to the culmination of the three knowledges, he said, "So, indeed, I," and so on. There, "Quite secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... attained and remained in the fourth *jhāna*" Here, whatever should be said, all that has been said in the *Visuddhimagga* in the section on the earth *kasina*. The only difference is that there it appears as "attains and remains," here it is "remained." But after doing what did the Blessed One attain and remain in these *jhānas*? After developing a meditation subject. Which one? The meditation subject of mindfulness of breathing. So, indeed, I, quite secluded from sensual pleasures...pe... attained and remained in the fourth *jhāna*. And these four *jhānas* are for some for the purpose of one-pointedness of mind, for some they are the basis for insight, for some they are the basis for supernormal knowledges, for some they are the basis for cessation, and for some they are for the sake of ascending to the world of existence. There, for those whose defilements are destroyed, they are for the purpose of one-pointedness of mind. For, having attained them, thinking, "Being of one-pointed mind, we will abide in happiness during the day," they develop the eight attainments after doing the preliminary work on the *kasina*. For trainees and ordinary people, when they develop them thinking, "Having arisen from the attainment, we will contemplate with a concentrated mind," they are the basis for insight. But when they develop the eight attainments, and having attained the *jhāna* that is the basis for supernormal knowledges, and having arisen from the attainment, desiring supernormal knowledges of the kind that are stated as "Having been one, he becomes many" (D.N. 1.238; Pat.M. 1.102), they are the basis for supernormal knowledges for them. But when they develop the eight attainments, and having attained the attainment of cessation, and having been without consciousness for seven days, thinking, "Having attained cessation, *nirvana*, here and now, we will abide in happiness," they are the basis for cessation for them. But when they develop the eight attainments, and not having declined from *jhāna*, they develop them thinking, "We will be reborn in the Brahma world," they are for the sake of ascending to the world of existence for them. 0125"/>

Furthermore, this fourth *dhyāna* was brought about by the Blessed One at the foot of the *bodhi* tree. It should be understood that it was the foundation for insight (*vipaśyanā*) and also the foundation for higher knowledge (*abhijñā*), the accomplisher of all tasks, and the giver of all mundane and supramundane qualities.

The description of preliminary practices etc., is complete.

Description of the discourse on previous existences

mula_pali: 52. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi. Ayaṃ kho me, brāhmaṇa, rattiyā paṭhame yāme paṭhamā vijjā adhigatā, avijjā vihatā vijjā uppannā, tamo vihato āloko uppanno, yathā taṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato.
mula_english:
“When my mind was thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, I directed it to the knowledge that consists of recollecting past lives.

I recollected my manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births; many eons of world dissolution, many eons of world evolution, and many eons of both dissolution and evolution: ‘There I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term; and passing away from there I was reborn elsewhere; and there too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term; and passing away from there I was reborn here.’

Thus with their aspects and particulars I recollected my manifold past lives.

“This was the first true knowledge attained by me in the first watch of the night. Ignorance was banished and true knowledge arose, darkness was banished and light arose, as happens in one who abides diligent, ardent, and resolute.
commentary_pali:
52. Yesañca guṇānaṃ dāyakaṃ ahosi, tesaṃ ekadesaṃ dassento so evaṃ samāhite cittetiādimāha. Tattha dvinnaṃ vijjānaṃ anupadavaṇṇanā ceva bhāvanānayo ca visuddhimagge vitthārito. Kevalañhi tattha ‘‘so evaṃ samāhite citte…pe… abhininnāmetī’’ti vuttaṃ, idha ‘‘abhininnāmesi’’nti. Ayaṃ kho me brāhmaṇāti ayañca appanāvāro tattha anāgatoti ayameva viseso. Tattha soti so ahaṃ. Abhininnāmesinti abhinīhariṃ. Abhininnāmesinti ca vacanato soti ettha so ahanti evamattho veditabbo.

Yasmā cidaṃ bhagavato vasena pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ āgataṃ, tasmā ‘‘so tato cuto idhūpapanno’’ti ettha evaṃ yojanā veditabbā. Ettha hi so tato cutoti paṭinivattantassa paccavekkhaṇaṃ. Tasmā idhūpapannoti imissā idhūpapattiyā anantaraṃ. Amutra udapādinti tusitabhavanaṃ sandhāyāhāti veditabbo. Tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmoti tatrāpi tusitabhavane setaketu nāma devaputto ahosiṃ. Evaṃgottoti tāhi devatāhi saddhiṃ ekagotto. Evaṃvaṇṇoti suvaṇṇavaṇṇo. Evamāhāroti dibbasudhāhāro. Evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedīti evaṃ dibbasukhapaṭisaṃvedī. Dukkhaṃ pana saṅkhāradukkhamattameva . Evamāyupariyantoti evaṃ sattapaññāsavassakoṭisaṭṭhivassasatasahassāyupariyanto. Sotato cutoti so ahaṃ tato tusitabhavanato cuto. Idhūpapannoti idha mahāmāyāya deviyā kucchimhi nibbatto.

Ayaṃ kho me brāhmaṇātiādīsu meti mayā. Vijjāti viditakaraṇaṭṭhena vijjā. Kiṃ viditaṃ karoti? Pubbenivāsaṃ. Avijjāti tasseva pubbenivāsassa aviditakaraṇaṭṭhena tappaṭicchādako moho vuccati. Tamoti sveva moho paṭicchādakaṭṭhena ‘‘tamo’’ti vuccati. Ālokoti sāyeva vijjā obhāsakaraṇaṭṭhena ‘‘āloko’’ti vuccati. Ettha ca vijjā adhigatāti ayaṃ attho, sesaṃ pasaṃsāvacanaṃ. commentary_english:
52. Moreover, he recounted the qualities' giver, showing a part of them, saying, "Thus, with the mind composed" and so on.

There, the detailed description of the two kinds of knowledge, the successive account and the method of cultivation, has been extensively explained in the Path of Purification (Visuddhimagga).

However, only there it was said, "Thus, with the mind composed...pe...he directs it," here it is "I direct it."

"This, indeed, O Brahmins, is mine"—this is the distinction, that this way of application is not in the future there; this itself is the distinction.

There, "so" means "so I."

"Abhininnāmesi" means "abhinīhariṃ."

And because of the statement "abhininnāmesinti," "so" here means "so ahaṃ," this meaning should be understood.

Because this recollection-knowledge of former abodes came about through the power of the Blessed One, therefore, in "so tato cuto idhūpapanno," thus the connection should be understood.

Here, indeed, "so tato cuto" is the reflection of one who is turning back.

Therefore, "idhūpapanno" is immediately after this coming-into-being here.

"Amutra udapādi" should be understood as referring to the Tusita heaven.

"Tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo" means "There also, in the Tusita heaven, I was a deva-son named Setaketu."

"Evaṃgotto" means "having the same clan as those devatās."

"Evaṃvaṇṇo" means "having a golden color (suvarṇavaṇṇo)."

"Evamāhāro" means "having divine nectar as food (dibbasudhāhāro)."

"Evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī" means "thus, experiencing divine pleasure."

Suffering, however, is merely the suffering of conditioned phenomena.

"Evamāyupariyanto" means "thus, having an आयु of seventy-five crore sixty-six hundred thousand years."

"So tato cuto" means "so I, having passed away from that Tusita heaven."

"Idhūpapanno" means "here, born in the womb of the divine Mahāmāyā."

So tato cuto idhūpapanno amutra udapādi tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto so tato cuto idhūpapanno

ayaṃ kho me brāhmaṇā and so on, "me" means "by me."

"Vijjā" means knowledge (vijjā) because of making known.

What does it make known? Former abodes (pubbenivāsaṃ).

"Avijjā" means that same ignorance (moho) is said to be the concealer of that making-not-known of former abodes.

"Tamo" means that same delusion (moho) is said to be "tamo" because of the characteristic of concealing.

"Āloko" means that same knowledge (vijjā) is said to be "āloko" because of the characteristic of making light.

And here, "vijjā adhigatā" is the meaning, the rest is words of praise.

The connection here is: "This knowledge is attained by me, for that one of whom knowledge is attained, ignorance is destroyed, ruined," this is the meaning.

Why? Because knowledge arose.

This is the method in the other two terms as well.

me vijjā avijjā tamo āloko

yathā ta nti ettha yathāti opamme.

ta nti nipāto.

satiyā avippavāsena appamattassa.
Due to zealous effort. This means, not regarding the body and life, for one who is resolute (*pahitattassa*), for one who is energetic.

This is what was said: "Just as for one who dwells diligent (*appamattassa*), ardent (*ātāpino*), and resolute (*pahitattassa*), ignorance (*avijjā*) would be destroyed, knowledge (*vijjā*) would arise.

Darkness would be destroyed, light (*āloka*) would arise.

Just so, my ignorance (*avijjā*) was destroyed, knowledge (*vijjā*) arose.

Darkness was destroyed, light (*āloka*) arose.

Corresponding to this devoted effort of mine, indeed, the fruit (*phala*) has been obtained."

The explanation of the story of former abodes is finished.

Explanation of the story of divine eye knowledge.

mula_pali: 53. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā; te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā; te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi. Ayaṃ kho me, brāhmaṇa, rattiyā majjhime yāme dutiyā vijjā adhigatā, avijjā vihatā vijjā uppannā, tamo vihato āloko uppanno, yathā taṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato.
mula_english:
53. When my mind was thus concentrated (samāhite citte), purified (parisuddhe), bright (pariyodāte), unblemished (anaṅgaṇe), rid of imperfection (vigatūpakkilese), malleable (mudubhūte), wieldy (kammaniye), steady (ṭhite), and attained to imperturbability (āneñjappatte), I directed it to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings (sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ).

With the divine eye (dibbena cakkhunā), which is purified (visuddhena) and surpasses the human (atikkantamānusakena), I saw beings (satte) passing away (cavamāne) and reappearing (upapajjamāne), inferior (hīne) and superior (paṇīte), fair (suvaṇṇe) and ugly (dubbaṇṇe), fortunate (sugate) and unfortunate (duggate), and I understood how beings pass on according to their *karma* (yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi): ‘These worthy beings (ime vata bhonto sattā) who were ill-conducted in body (kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā), speech (vacīduccaritena samannāgatā), and mind (manoduccaritena samannāgatā), revilers of the noble ones (*ariyānaṃ*) [p.1.0029] (upavādakā), holding wrong views (*micchādiṭṭhikā*), and undertaking actions governed by wrong views (*micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā*), at the breaking up of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), have reappeared in a state of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), in an unhappy destination (*duggatiṃ*), in perdition (*vinipātaṃ*), even in hell (*nirayaṃ upapannā*).

Or these worthy beings (ime vā pana bhonto sattā) who were well-conducted in body (kāyasucaritena samannāgatā), [p.1.0023] speech (vacīsucaritena samannāgatā), and mind (manosucaritena samannāgatā), not revilers of the noble ones (*ariyānaṃ anupavādakā*), holding right views (*sammādiṭṭhikā*), [p.1.0040] and undertaking actions governed by right views (*sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā*), at the breaking up of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), have reappeared in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), in a heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti*).’

Thus with the divine eye (dibbena cakkhunā), which is purified (visuddhena) and surpasses the human (atikkantamānusakena), I saw beings (satte) passing away (passāmi cavamāne) and reappearing (upapajjamāne), inferior (hīne) and superior (paṇīte), fair (suvaṇṇe) and ugly (dubbaṇṇe), fortunate (sugate) and unfortunate (duggate), and I understood how beings pass on according to their *karma* (yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi).

This was the second true knowledge (*dutiyā vijjā adhigatā*) attained by me, O *Brāhmaṇa*, in the middle watch of the night (*rattiyā majjhime yāme*). Ignorance (*avijjā*) was banished (*vihatā*) and true knowledge (*vijjā*) arose (*uppannā*), darkness (*tamo*) was banished (*vihato*) and light (*āloko*) arose (*uppanno*), as happens in one who abides diligent (*appamattassa*), ardent (*ātāpino*), and resolute (*pahitattassa viharato*).
commentary_pali:
53. Cutūpapātakathāyaṃ yasmā idha bhagavato vasena pāḷi āgatā, tasmā ‘‘passāmi pajānāmī’’ti vuttaṃ, ayaṃ viseso. Sesaṃ visuddhimagge vuttasadisameva.

Ettha pana vijjāti dibbacakkhuñāṇavijjā. Avijjāti sattānaṃ cutipaṭisandhipaṭicchādikā avijjā. Sesaṃ vuttanayamevāti. Yasmā ca pūritapāramīnaṃ mahāsattānaṃ parikammakiccaṃ nāma natthi. Te hi citte abhininnāmitamatteyeva anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti, dibbena cakkhunā satte passanti. Tasmā yo tattha parikammaṃ ādiṃ katvā bhāvanānayo vutto, na tena idha atthoti.

vijjā Avijjā

Dibbacakkhuñāṇakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Āsavakkhayañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
53. In the discourse on passing away and rebirth, since the Pali comes here by way of the Blessed One, therefore it is said, "I see, I understand," this is the distinction. The remainder is just as stated in the *Visuddhimagga*.

Here, *vijjā* is the knowledge-wisdom of the divine eye (divyacakṣuñāṇavijjā). *Avijjā* is the ignorance that obscures the passing away and rebirth of beings. The rest is as already stated.

And since for great beings who have fulfilled the perfections, there is no such thing as preliminary work to be done; for as soon as they direct their minds, they recollect their former abodes in various ways and see beings with the divine eye; therefore, the method of cultivation which was stated there, beginning with preliminary work, is not relevant here.

*Vijjā*, *Avijjā*

The explanation of the discourse on the wisdom of the divine eye is finished.

Explanation of the discourse on the knowledge of the destruction of defilements (*āsavakkhayañāṇa*).

mula_pali: 54. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ. ‘Ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ. Tassa me evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ ahosi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsiṃ. Ayaṃ kho me, brāhmaṇa, rattiyā pacchime yāme tatiyā vijjā adhigatā, avijjā vihatā vijjā uppannā, tamo vihato āloko uppanno, yathā taṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato.
mula_english:
54. Then, with my mind thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, I directed it to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints (āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya).

I directly knew as it actually is: “This is suffering (dukkha)”;…“This is the origin of suffering (dukkhasamudayo)”;…“This is the cessation of suffering (dukkhanirodho)”;…“This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering (dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā).”

I directly knew as it actually is: “These are the taints (āsavā) “…“This is the origin of the taints (āsavasamudayo)”… “This is the cessation of the taints (āsavanirodho)”…“This is the way leading to the cessation of the taints (āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā).”

When I knew and saw this, my mind was freed from the corruption of sensual desire (kāmāsavā), from the corruption of desire to exist (bhavāsavā), from the corruption of ignorance (avijjāsavā).

When it was freed, I knew it was freed (vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ ahosi).

’ I directly knew: ‘Birth is destroyed (khīṇā jāti), the holy life has been lived (vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ), what had to be done has been done (kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ), there is no more coming to any state of being (nāparaṃ itthattāyā).’

This was the third true knowledge (tatiyā vijjā) attained by me in the third watch of the night. Ignorance (avijjā) was banished and true knowledge (vijjā) arose, darkness (tamo) was banished and light (āloko) arose, as happens in one who abides diligent, ardent, and resolute (appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato), O Brahmin (brāhmaṇa).
commentary_pali:
54. Tatiyavijjāya so evaṃ samāhite citteti vipassanāpādakaṃ catutthajjhānacittaṃ veditabbaṃ. Āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāyāti arahattamaggañāṇatthāya. Arahattamaggo hi āsavavināsanato āsavānaṃ khayoti vuccati, tatra cetaṃ ñāṇaṃ, tappariyāpannattāti. Cittaṃ abhininnāmesinti vipassanācittaṃ abhinīhariṃ. So idaṃ dukkhanti evamādīsu ‘‘ettakaṃ dukkhaṃ, na ito bhiyyo’’ti sabbampi dukkhasaccaṃ sarasalakkhaṇapaṭivedhena yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ jāniṃ paṭivijjhiṃ. Tassa ca dukkhassa nibbattikaṃ taṇhaṃ ayaṃ dukkhasamudayoti. Tadubhayampi yaṃ ṭhānaṃ patvā nirujjhati, taṃ tesaṃ appavattiṃ nibbānaṃ ayaṃ dukkhanirodhoti. Tassa sampāpakaṃ ariyamaggaṃ ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti sarasalakkhaṇapaṭivedhena yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ jāniṃ paṭivijjhinti evamattho veditabbo.

Evaṃ sarūpato saccāni dassetvā idāni kilesavasena pariyāyato dassento ime āsavātiādimāha. Tassa me evaṃ jānato evaṃ passatoti tassa mayhaṃ evaṃ jānantassa evaṃ passantassa.
