Moreover, this is the taste-related benefit of morality, namely, these four requisites.

Thus, wise people, having taken out what is placed in storehouses and other places, even without giving it to their sons and others, or even without using it themselves, give it to the virtuous; therefore, this was said for the purpose of showing the benefit of morality with its pleasant taste.

In the third saying, "Whom I" means whom I. "Their deeds" means those acts of giving requisites done to me by those gods or humans. For even gods give requisites to those endowed with morality and other virtues, not only humans, like Sakka to the venerable Mahākassapa.

"Of great fruit, of great benefit" – both of these are the same in meaning, only the expressions are different. "Of great fruit" means producing great worldly happiness. "Of great benefit" means being a condition for great transcendental happiness. For even a spoonful of alms given to one endowed with morality and other virtues, or a leaf hut built and given on land the size of five jewels, protects from falling into bad destinies for many thousands of eons, and in the end, it is a condition for the deathless element of *nirvāṇa*.

Here, the stories beginning with "I gave milk-rice" (Vv. 413) and the entire *Petavatthu* and *Vimānavatthu* are evidence.
Therefore, it is shown that even someone who desires great fruit from actions done by givers of requisites should be endowed with virtue and other good qualities.

Those acts of worship are of great fruit and great benefit.

Great benefit. *Petavatthu* and *Vimānavatthu*. In the fourth instance, *ñātī* means those related to the mother-in-law and father-in-law.

*Sālohitā* means those connected by one blood, such as grandfathers and great-grandfathers.

*Petā* means those who have gone to the state of the departed.

*Kālaṅkatā* means those who are dead.

*Tesaṃ ta*nti means their pleased state of mind towards me, or remembrance with a pleased mind.

If a *bhikkhu*'s father or mother has died, and thinking, "Our relative is an elder, virtuous, and has good qualities," becomes pleased and remembers that *bhikkhu*, then that mental serenity and even that mere remembrance are of great fruit and great benefit. For hundreds of thousands of *kappa*s, it is capable of preventing from a bad destination and bringing to the deathless.

This was said by the Blessed One: "Those *bhikkhus*, who are accomplished in virtue, accomplished in concentration, accomplished in wisdom, liberation, accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation, even the sight of those *bhikkhus* is of great help, I say.

Hearing, recollection, going forth, approaching, attending on them are also of great help, I say" (Itivu. 104).

Therefore, it is shown that even someone who desires great fruit from serenity of mind and recollection in oneself towards relatives and blood relatives should be endowed with virtue and other good qualities.

Relatives and blood relatives.

Departed and dead.

mula_pali:
66. ‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘aratiratisaho assaṃ, na ca maṃ arati saheyya, uppannaṃ aratiṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘bhayabheravasaho assaṃ, na ca maṃ bhayabheravaṃ saheyya, uppannaṃ bhayabheravaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī assaṃ akicchalābhī akasiralābhī’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā, te kāyena phusitvā vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.
mula_english:
“If a *bhikṣu* should wish: ‘May I become a conqueror of discontent (*arati*) and delight (*rati*), and may discontent and delight not conquer me; may I abide transcending discontent and delight whenever they arise,’ let him fulfil the precepts… and let him cultivate empty dwellings.

“If a *bhikṣu* should wish: ‘May I become a conqueror of fear (*bhaya*) and dread (*bherava*), and may fear and dread not conquer me; may I abide transcending fear and dread whenever they arise,’ let him fulfil the precepts… and let him cultivate empty dwellings.

“If a *bhikṣu* should wish: ‘May I become one to obtain at will, without trouble (*akiccha*) or difficulty (*akasira*), the four *jhānas* that constitute the higher mind (*ābhicetasika*) and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ*),’ let him fulfil the precepts… and let him cultivate empty dwellings.

“If a *bhikṣu* should wish: ‘May I contact with the body (*kāyena*) and abide in those liberations (*vimokkhā*) that are peaceful (*santā*) and immaterial (*āruppā*), transcending forms (*rūpe*),’ let him fulfil the precepts… and let him cultivate empty dwellings.
commentary_pali:
66. Pañcamavāre aratiratisaho assanti aratiyā ratiyā ca saho abhibhavitā ajjhottharitā bhaveyyaṃ. Ettha ca aratīti adhikusalesu dhammesu pantasenāsanesu ca ukkaṇṭhā. Ratīti pañcakāmaguṇarati. Na ca maṃ arati saheyyāti mañca arati na abhibhaveyya na maddeyya na ajjhotthareyya. Uppannanti jātaṃ nibbattaṃ. Sīlādiguṇayutto hi aratiñca ratiñca sahati ajjhottharati madditvā tiṭṭhati. Tasmā īdisaṃ attānaṃ icchantenāpi sīlādiguṇayutteneva bhavitabbanti dasseti.

Chaṭṭhavāre bhayaṃ cittutrāsopi ārammaṇampi. Bheravaṃ ārammaṇameva. Sesaṃ pañcamavāre vuttanayameva. Sīlādiguṇayutto hi bhayabheravaṃ sahati ajjhottharati madditvā tiṭṭhati ariyakoṭiyavāsīmahādattatthero viya.

bhayaṃ Bheravaṃ

Thero kira maggaṃ paṭipanno aññataraṃ pāsādikaṃ araññaṃ disvā ‘‘idhevajja samaṇadhammaṃ katvā gamissāmī’’ti maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā nisīdi. Rukkhadevatāya dārakā therassa sīlatejena sakabhāvena saṇṭhātuṃ asakkontā vissaramakaṃsu. Devatāpi rukkhaṃ cālesi. Thero acalova nisīdi. Sā devatā dhūmāyi, pajjali, neva sakkhi theraṃ cāletuṃ, tato upāsakavaṇṇenāgantvā vanditvā aṭṭhāsi. ‘‘Ko eso’’ti vuttā ‘‘ahaṃ, bhante, etasmiṃ rukkhe adhivatthā devatā’’ti avoca. Tvaṃ ete vikāre akāsīti. Āma bhanteti. Kasmāti ca vuttā āha – ‘‘tumhākaṃ, bhante , sīlatejena dārakā sakabhāvena saṇṭhātuṃ asakkontā vissaramakaṃsu, sāhaṃ tumhe palāpetuṃ evamakāsi’’nti. Thero āha – ‘‘atha kasmā idha, bhante, mā vasatha, mayhaṃ aphāsūti paṭikacceva nāvacāsi. Idāni pana mā kiñci avaca, ariyakoṭiyamahādatto amanussabhayena gatoti vacanato lajjāmi, tenāhaṃ idheva vasissaṃ, tvaṃ pana ajjekadivasaṃ yattha katthaci vasāhī’’ti. Evaṃ sīlādiguṇayutto bhayabheravasaho hoti. Tasmā īdisamattānaṃ icchantenāpi sīlādiguṇayutteneva bhavitabbanti dasseti.

Sattamavāre ābhicetasikānanti abhicetoti abhikkantaṃ visuddhacittaṃ vuccati, adhicittaṃ vā, abhicetasi jātāni ābhicetasikāni, abhiceto sannissitānīti vā ābhicetasikāni. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānanti diṭṭhadhamme sukhavihārānaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammoti paccakkho attabhāvo vuccati, tattha sukhavihārabhūtānanti attho, rūpāvacarajjhānānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tāni hi appetvā nisinnā jhāyino imasmiṃyeva attabhāve asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ nekkhammasukhaṃ vindanti, tasmā ‘‘diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānī’’ti vuccanti. Nikāmalābhīti nikāmena lābhī attano icchāvasena lābhī, icchiticchitakkhaṇe samāpajjituṃ samatthoti vuttaṃ hoti. Akicchalābhīti sukheneva paccanīkadhamme vikkhambhetvā samāpajjituṃ samatthoti vuttaṃ hoti. Akasiralābhīti akasirānaṃ vipulānaṃ lābhī, yathāparicchedeyeva vuṭṭhātuṃ samatthoti vuttaṃ hoti. Ekacco hi lābhīyeva hoti, na pana sakkoti icchiticchitakkhaṇe samāpajjituṃ. Ekacco sakkoti tathā samāpajjituṃ, pāribandhike pana kicchena vikkhambheti. Ekacco tathā samāpajjati, pāribandhike ca akiccheneva vikkhambheti, na sakkoti nāḷikāyantaṃ viya yathāparicchedeyeva ca vuṭṭhātuṃ. Yo pana imaṃ tividhampi sampadaṃ icchati, sopi sīlesvevassa paripūrakārīti.

ābhicetasikāna abhiceto Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāna Diṭṭhadhammo Nikāmalābhī Akicchalābhī Akasiralābhī

Evaṃ abhiññāpādake jhāne vutte kiñcāpi abhiññānaṃ vāro āgato, atha kho naṃ bhagavā aggahetvāva yasmā na kevalaṃ abhiññāpādakajjhānāni ca abhiññāyoyeva ca sīlānaṃ ānisaṃso, apica kho cattāri āruppajhānānipi tayo ca heṭṭhimā ariyamaggā, tasmā taṃ sabbaṃ pariyādiyitvā dassetuṃ ākaṅkheyya ce…pe… ye te santāti evamādimāha.

ākaṅkheyya ce…pe… ye te santā

Tattha santāti aṅgasantatāya ceva ārammaṇasantatāya ca. Vimokkhāti paccanīkadhammehi vimuttattā ārammaṇe ca adhimuttattā. Atikkamma rūpeti rūpāvacarajjhāne atikkamitvā, ye te vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe santāti padasambandho, itarathā hi atikkamma rūpe kiṃ karotīti na paññāyeyyuṃ. Āruppāti ārammaṇato ca vipākato ca rūpavirahitā. Kāyena phusitvāti nāmakāyena phusitvā pāpuṇitvā, adhigantvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Sesaṃ vuttānameva. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘yopi bhikkhu ime vimokkhe phusitvā viharitukāmo, sopi sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī’’ti.

santā Vimokkhā Atikkamma rūpe Āruppā Kāyena phusitvā
commentary_english:
66. In the fifth instance, "one would be able to endure and overcome *arati* and *rati*," means one would be the overcomer and subduer of both *arati* and *rati*.

Here, *arati* means disgust regarding superior wholesome qualities and secluded dwelling places.

*Rati* means delight in the five strands of sense pleasure (*pañcakāmaguṇa*).

"And *arati* would not be able to overcome me," means *arati* would not be able to overpower, subdue, or overwhelm me.

"*Uppanna*" means born, originated.

Indeed, someone endowed with virtuous qualities beginning with morality endures and overcomes both *arati* and *rati*, subduing [them] and remaining [steadfast].

Therefore, [the text] shows that even someone desiring such a self should only be one who is endowed with virtuous qualities beginning with morality.

In the sixth instance, "*bhayaṃ*" fear, is both mental trembling and an object [of fear].

"*Bheravaṃ*" terrifying, is only an object [of fear].

The rest is as already stated in the fifth instance.

Indeed, someone endowed with virtuous qualities beginning with morality endures and overcomes fear and terror, subduing [them] and remaining [steadfast], like the Elder Mahādatta, a resident of Ariyakoṭi.

The Elder, it is said, having set out on the path, saw a certain pleasing forest and thought, "Here today, having practiced the ascetic life, I will leave," and descending from the path, at the foot of a certain tree, having spread out his double robe, sat down cross-legged.

The children of the tree deity, being unable to bear the Elder's moral power in their own form, made a great noise.

The deity also shook the tree.

The Elder sat unmoving.

That deity smoked, blazed, and was not able to make the Elder move; then, having come in the guise of a lay follower, [the deity] paid homage and stood to one side.

Being asked, "Who is this?", [the deity] said, "Venerable, I am the deity dwelling in this tree."

"Did you cause these disturbances?"

"Yes, Venerable."

And being asked why, [the deity] said – "Venerable, the children, unable to bear your moral power in their own form, made a great noise; I did this in order to drive you away."

The Elder said – "Then why, Venerable, did you not immediately say, 'Do not dwell here, Venerable, [it is] uncomfortable for me?'

But now, do not say anything, I am ashamed because it is said, 'Mahādatta of Ariyakoṭi left due to fear of non-humans'; therefore, I will dwell here, but you, for today only, reside wherever [you like]."

Thus, someone endowed with virtuous qualities beginning with morality is an endurer of fear and terror.

Therefore, [the text] shows that even someone desiring such a self should only be one who is endowed with virtuous qualities beginning with morality.

In the seventh instance, "*ābhicetasikāna*" means *abhiceto*, which is said to be surpassing, purified mind, or superior mind; *ābhicetasikāni* are those born in the *abhiceto*, or *ābhicetasikāni* are those dependent on the *abhiceto*.

"*Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāna*" means *sukhavihārānaṃ* in the *diṭṭhadhamma*.

*Diṭṭhadhammo* is said to be the directly perceived existence; there, it means those whose nature is dwelling in happiness; this is a designation for the form-sphere (*rūpāvacara*) *jhānas*.

For indeed, meditators, having desired those [form-sphere jhānas], sit and experience unsullied happiness of renunciation in this very existence; therefore, they are called "dwellings in happiness in the directly perceived [existence]."

"*Nikāmalābhī*" means *nikāmena lābhī*, one who obtains according to one's wish, one who obtains at will, it is said that [one is] able to attain [them] at the very moment of wishing.

"*Akicchalābhī*" means it is said that [one is] able to attain [them] by easily suppressing opposing qualities.

"*Akasiralābhī*" means one who obtains vast [qualities] without difficulty; it is said that [one is] able to arise just as one has determined.

Indeed, someone is only a gainer, but is not able to attain [the *jhānas*] at the very moment of wishing.
Someone is able to attain thus, but in adverse circumstances, he obstructs with difficulty.

Someone attains thus, and in adverse circumstances, he obstructs easily; he is not able to rise up as if at the end of a water clock, just as he had determined.

Moreover, whoever desires this threefold success, he too is a fulfiller in morality.

Concerning those who have minds that are possessed of joy and happiness in the present moment, who have attained desire in the present moment,

Easy to obtain, without difficulty to obtain: Thus, when the jhāna [meditative absorption] that leads to higher knowledge is spoken of, although the opportunity for higher knowledge has come, but the Blessed One does not take it up. Because not only are the jhānas that lead to higher knowledge and the benefits of morality...

Moreover, the four immaterial jhānas...

And the three lower noble paths, therefore, having completely mastered all that, in order to show it, one should desire... these are the peaceful ones," thus he spoke, beginning in this way.

There, "peaceful" means by the continuity of the limbs and by the continuity of the object.

"Liberations" means because of being liberated from opposing things and because of being intent on the object.

"Having transcended forms" means having transcended the jhāna of the realm of form. "Those liberations, having transcended forms, are peaceful," is the connection of the words. Otherwise, if having transcended forms, what does he do? would not be understood.

"Immaterial" means devoid of form, both from the object and from the result.

"Having touched with the body" means having touched and attained with the name-body, having realized, so it is said.

The rest is just as stated.

This is what is said: "Also, whatever bhikkhu [monk] desires to abide having touched these liberations, he too is a fulfiller in morality."

Peaceful, liberations, having transcended forms, immaterial, having touched with the body.

mula_pali:
67. ‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno assaṃ avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī assaṃ sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ kareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko assaṃ tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.
mula_english:
“67. If a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I, with the destruction of three fetters (*saṃyojana*), become a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*), no longer subject to perdition, bound for deliverance, headed for enlightenment (*sambodhiparāyaṇo*)’ let him fulfil the precepts… and develop solitary dwellings.

If a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I, with the destruction of three fetters (*saṃyojana*) and with the attenuation of lust (*rāga*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*), become a once-returner (*sakadāgāmī*), returning once to this world to make an end of suffering (*dukkha*)’ let him fulfil the precepts… and develop solitary dwellings.

If a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I, with the destruction of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiya saṃyojana*), become one who arises spontaneously (*opapātiko*), there attain final *Nirvana* (*parinibbāyī*), not liable to return (*anāvattidhammo*) from that world’ let him fulfil the precepts… and develop solitary dwellings."
commentary_pali:
67. Navamavāre tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānanti sakkāyadiṭṭhivicikicchāsīlabbataparāmāsasaṅkhātānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ bandhanānaṃ. Tāni hi saṃyojenti khandhagatibhavādīhi khandhagatibhavādayo, kammaṃ vā phalena, tasmā saṃyojanānīti vuccanti, bandhanānīti attho. Parikkhayāti parikkhayena. Sotāpannoti sotaṃ āpanno. Sototi ca maggassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Sotāpannoti taṃsamaṅgipuggalassa. Yathāha ‘‘soto sototi hidaṃ, sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, sāriputta, sototi? Ayameva hi, bhante, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Seyyathidaṃ, sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhīti. Sotāpanno sotāpannoti hidaṃ, sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, sāriputta, sotāpannoti? Yo hi, bhante, iminā aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena samannāgato, ayaṃ vuccati sotāpanno, yoyaṃ āyasmā evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto’’ti. Idha pana maggena phalassa nāmaṃ dinnaṃ, tasmā phalaṭṭho ‘‘sotāpanno’’ti veditabbo. Avinipātadhammoti vinipātetīti vinipāto, nāssa vinipāto dhammoti avinipātadhammo, na attānaṃ apāye vinipātasabhāvoti vuttaṃ hoti. Kasmā? Ye dhammā apāyagamaniyā, tesaṃ pahīnattā. Sambodhi paraṃ ayanaṃ gati assāti sambodhiparāyaṇo, uparimaggattayaṃ avassaṃ sampāpakoti attho. Kasmā? Paṭiladdhapaṭhamamaggattā. Sīlesvevāti īdiso hotukāmopi sīlesvevassa paripūraṇārīti.

Dasamavāre paṭhamamaggena parikkhīṇānipi tīṇi saṃyojanāni sakadāgāmimaggassa vaṇṇabhaṇanatthaṃ vuttāni. Rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttāti etesaṃ tanubhāvena, tanuttakaraṇenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha dvīhi kāraṇehi tanuttaṃ veditabbaṃ adhiccuppattiyā ca pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya ca. Sakadāgāmissa hi vaṭṭānusārimahājanasseva kilesā abhiṇhaṃ na uppajjanti, kadāci karahaci uppajjanti viraḷākārā hutvā, viraḷavāpite khette aṅkurā viya. Uppajjamānāpi ca vaṭṭānusārimahājanasseva maddantā pharantā chādentā andhakāraṃ karontā na uppajjanti, mandamandā uppajjanti tanukākārā hutvā, abbhapaṭalamiva makkhikāpattamiva ca.

Rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā

Tattha keci therā bhaṇanti ‘‘sakadāgāmissa kilesā kiñcāpi cirena uppajjanti, bahalāva uppajjanti, tathā hissa puttā ca dhītaro ca dissantī’’ti, etaṃ pana appamāṇaṃ. Puttadhītaro hi aṅgapaccaṅgaparāmasanamattenapi hontīti. Dvīhiyeva kāraṇehissa kilesānaṃ tanuttaṃ veditabbaṃ adhiccuppattiyā ca pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya cāti.

Sakadāgāmīti sakiṃ āgamanadhammo. Sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvāti ekavāraṃyeva imaṃ manussalokaṃ paṭisandhivasena āgantvā. Yopi hi idha sakadāgāmimaggaṃ bhāvetvā idheva parinibbāti, sopi idha na gahito. Yopi idha maggaṃ bhāvetvā devesu upapajjitvā tattheva parinibbāti. Yopi devaloke maggaṃ bhāvetvā tattheva parinibbāti. Yopi devaloke maggaṃ bhāvetvā idheva manussaloke nibbattitvā parinibbāti. Yo pana idha maggaṃ bhāvetvā devaloke nibbatto, tattha yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā puna idheva upapajjitvā parinibbāti, ayamidha gahitoti veditabbo. Dukkhassantaṃ kareyyanti vaṭṭadukkhassa paricchedaṃ kareyyaṃ. Sīlesvevāti īdiso hotukāmopi sīlesvevassa paripūrakārīti.

Sakadāgāmī Sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā Dukkhassantaṃ kareyya

Ekādasamavāre pañcannanti gaṇanaparicchedo. Orambhāgiyānanti oraṃ vuccati heṭṭhā, heṭṭhābhāgiyānanti attho, kāmāvacaraloke uppattipaccayānanti adhippāyo. Saṃyojanānanti bandhanānaṃ, tāni kāmarāgabyāpādasaṃyojanehi saddhiṃ pubbe vuttasaṃyojanāneva veditabbāni. Yassa hi etāni appahīnāni, so kiñcāpi bhavagge uppanno hoti, atha kho āyuparikkhayā kāmāvacare nibbattatiyeva, gilitabalisamacchūpamo svāyaṃ puggalo dīghasuttakena pāde baddhavihaṅgūpamo cāti veditabbo. Pubbe vuttānampi cettha vacanaṃ vaṇṇabhaṇanatthamevāti veditabbaṃ. Opapātikoti sesayonipaṭikkhepavacanametaṃ. Tatthaparinibbāyīti tattheva brahmaloke parinibbāyī. Anāvattidhammo tasmā lokāti tato brahmalokā paṭisandhivasena puna anāvattisabhāvo. Sīlesvevāti īdiso hotukāmopi sīlesvevassa paripūrakārīti.

pañcanna Orambhāgiyāna Saṃyojanāna Opapātiko Tatthaparinibbāyī Anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā
commentary_english:
67. In the ninth instance, *tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanāna* means the three fetters, namely, the aggregates of personality view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*), doubt (vicikicchā), and clinging to rules and rituals (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*), which are designated as the three bonds (*bandhanānaṃ*).

They bind (*saṃyojenti*) by means of the aggregates (*khandha*), destination (*gati*), existence (*bhava*) and so on. The aggregates, destination, existence, and so on, [bind] action (*kammaṃ*) or its fruit (*phalena*). Therefore, *saṃyojanānī* means they are called fetters (*vuccanti*), bonds (*bandhanāni*), this is the meaning (*attho*).

*parikkhayā* means by destruction (*parikkhayena*).

*sotāpanno* means one who has attained (*āpanno*) the stream (*sotaṃ*).

*sototi* is a designation (*adhivacanaṃ*) of the path (*maggassa*).

*sotāpanno* means one who possesses those qualities (*taṃsamaṅgipuggalassa*).

As he said, "The stream, the stream (*soto sototi hidaṃ*), Sāriputta, is said (*vuccati*)."

"Which stream (*sototi*) is that, Sāriputta?" "It is just this Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*), venerable sir (*bhante*).

That is to say (*seyyathidaṃ*), right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*)…pe… right concentration (*sammāsamādhīti*)."

*sotāpanno sotāpannoti hidaṃ*, Sāriputta, *vuccati*.

"Which *sotāpanno* is that, Sāriputta?" "He who is endowed (*samannāgato*) with this eightfold path (*aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena*), venerable sir (*bhante*), he is called *sotāpanno*, he is venerable (*āyasmā*) so-and-so by name (*evaṃnāmo*) and of such-and-such a clan (*evaṃgotto*)."

Here, the name of the fruit (*phalassa nāmaṃ*) is given by the path (*maggena*), therefore the one who stands in the fruit (*phalaṭṭho*) is to be understood as "stream-enterer" (*sotāpanno*).

*avinipātadhammo* means *vinipātetīti vinipāto*, not his (*nāssa*) downfall (*vinipāto*) is the quality (*dhammo*) therefore *avinipātadhammo*, it is said (*vuttaṃ hoti*) that he is not of the nature (*sabhāvoti*) of falling (*vinipāta*) into the states of loss (*apāye*).

Why (*kasmā*)? Because of the abandonment (*pahīnattā*) of those qualities (*dhammā*) that lead to the states of loss (*apāyagamaniyā*).

*sambodhi paraṃ ayanaṃ gati assāti sambodhiparāyaṇo*, one for whom perfect enlightenment (*sambodhi*) is the supreme (*paraṃ*) course (*ayanaṃ*) and destination (*gati assāti*), meaning (*attho*) he will definitely attain (*avassaṃ sampāpako*) the three higher paths (*uparimaggattayaṃ*).

Why (*kasmā*)? Because he has obtained the first path (*paṭiladdhapaṭhamamaggattā*).

*sīlesvevā* means even if he wishes to become such (*īdiso hotukāmopi*), he is the one who perfects morality (*sīlesvevassa paripūraṇārīti*).

In the tenth instance, the three fetters that are destroyed (*parikkhīṇānipi*) by the first path (*paṭhamamaggena*) are stated (*vuttāni*) for the purpose of describing the path of the once-returner (*sakadāgāmimaggassa vaṇṇabhaṇanatthaṃ*).

*rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā* means by the attenuation (*tanubhāvena*) of those, it is said (*vuttaṃ hoti*) by the act of making them thin (*tanuttakaraṇenāti*).

There, attenuation (*tanuttaṃ*) is to be understood (*veditabbaṃ*) by two causes (*dvīhi kāraṇehi*), namely, by occasional occurrence (*adhiccuppattiyā ca*) and by the weakness of the upsurge (*pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya ca*).

For the once-returner (*sakadāgāmissa hi*), just as for a great crowd following a beaten path (*vaṭṭānusārimahājanasseva*), defilements (*kilesā*) do not arise frequently (*abhiṇhaṃ na uppajjanti*), [but] they arise (*uppajjanti*) occasionally (*kadāci karahaci*) having a sparse form (*viraḷākārā hutvā*), like sprouts (*aṅkurā viya*) in a field that has been sparsely sown (*viraḷavāpite khette*).

And even when arising (*uppajjamānāpi ca*), just as for a great crowd following a beaten path (*vaṭṭānusārimahājanasseva*) they do not arise (*na uppajjanti*) crushing (*maddantā*), pervading (*pharantā*), covering (*chādentā*), making darkness (*andhakāraṃ karontā*), [but] they arise (*uppajjanti*) slowly slowly (*mandamandā*) having a thin form (*tanukākārā hutvā*), like a layer of clouds (*abbhapaṭalamiva*) and like a drop of honey (*makkhikāpattamiva ca*).

*rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā*

There (*tattha*), some elders (*keci therā*) say (*bhaṇanti*) "For the once-returner (*sakadāgāmissa*), although defilements (*kilesā*) arise after a long time (*cirena uppajjanti*), they arise very strongly (*bahalāva uppajjanti*), thus his sons (*puttā*) and daughters (*dhītaro*) are seen (*dissantī*)," but that (*etaṃ pana*) is incorrect (*appamāṇaṃ*).

For sons and daughters (*puttadhītaro hi*) come about even by merely touching limbs (*aṅgapaccaṅgaparāmasanamattenapi hontīti*).

Attenuation (*tanuttaṃ*) of defilements (*kilesānaṃ*) is to be understood (*veditabbaṃ*) by just two causes (*dvīhiyeva kāraṇehi*), namely, by occasional occurrence (*adhiccuppattiyā ca*) and by the weakness of the upsurge (*pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya ca*).

*sakadāgāmī* means one who has the nature (*dhamma*) of returning once (*sakiṃ āgamanadhammo*).

*sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā* means having come (*āgantvā*) to this world (*imaṃ lokaṃ*) just one time (*ekavāraṃyeva*) having come (*āgantvā*) to this human world (*imaṃ manussalokaṃ*) by way of rebirth (*paṭisandhivasena*).

He who, having developed (*bhāvetvā*) the path of the once-returner (*sakadāgāmimaggaṃ*) here (*idha*), attains final nirvāṇa (*parinibbāti*) right here (*idheva*), he too (*sopi*) is not included (*na gahito*) here (*idha*).

He who, having developed (*bhāvetvā*) the path (*maggaṃ*) here (*idha*), is reborn (*upapajjitvā*) among the gods (*devesu*) and attains final nirvāṇa (*parinibbāti*) right there (*tattheva*).

He who, having developed (*bhāvetvā*) the path (*maggaṃ*) in the world of the gods (*devaloke*), attains final nirvāṇa (*parinibbāti*) right there (*tattheva*).

He who, having developed (*bhāvetvā*) the path (*maggaṃ*) in the world of the gods (*devaloke*), having been reborn (*nibbattitvā*) right here (*idheva*) in the human world (*manussaloke*), attains final nirvāṇa (*parinibbāti*).

But he who, having developed (*bhāvetvā*) the path (*maggaṃ*) here (*idha*), is reborn (*nibbatto*) in the world of the gods (*devaloke*), having stayed (*ṭhatvā*) there (*tattha*) as long as his life lasts (*yāvatāyukaṃ*), having been reborn (*upapajjitvā*) right here (*idheva*) again (*puna*), attains final nirvāṇa (*parinibbāti*), he (*ayaṃ*) is to be understood (*veditabbo*) as being included (*gahitoti*) here (*idha*).

*dukkhassantaṃ kareyya* means I would make (*kareyyaṃ*) an end (*paricchedaṃ*) of the round of suffering (*vaṭṭadukkhassa*).

*sīlesvevā* means even if he wishes to become such (*īdiso hotukāmopi*), he is the one who perfects morality (*sīlesvevassa paripūrakārīti*).
*Sakadāgāmī*: A once-returner.

*Sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ kareyya*: Having come to this world once, he will make an end to suffering.

In the eleventh instance, *pañcanna* means a delimitation of enumeration.

*Orambhāgiyāna* means *oraṃ* is said to be *heṭṭhā*, meaning lower, the intention being causes for rebirth in the desire realm.

*Saṃyojanāna* means bonds; these should be understood as the bonds previously mentioned, together with the bonds of desire-attachment and ill-will.

For someone whose bonds are not abandoned, even though they are born in the peak of existence (*bhavāgra*), at the exhaustion of their life-span, they will definitely be reborn in the desire realm. That person should be understood as like a fish that has swallowed a baited hook, or like a bird tied by a long string to its feet.

It should be understood that mentioning what was said earlier is just for the sake of praising its qualities.

*Opapātiko* means this is a statement rejecting other modes of birth.

*Tatthaparinibbāyī* means one who attains final Nirvāṇa right there in the Brahmā world.

*Anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā* means having the nature of not returning again from that Brahmā world in the manner of rebirth.

*Sīlesvevā* means even someone who desires to be like this is a perfecter of discipline (*śīla*).

*pañcanna orambhāgiyāna saṃyojanāna*

*opapātiko tatthaparinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā*

mula_pali:
68. ‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhaveyyaṃ – ekopi hutvā bahudhā assaṃ, bahudhāpi hutvā eko assaṃ; āvibhāvaṃ tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ kareyyaṃ, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kameyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parāmaseyyaṃ parimajjeyyaṃ; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇeyyaṃ – dibbe ca mānuse ca ye dūre santike cā’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajāneyyaṃ – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ vītadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samohaṃ vā cittaṃ samohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ vītamohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ vikkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ mahaggataṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ amahaggataṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ sauttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ anuttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ samāhitaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ asamāhitaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ avimuttaṃ cittanti pajāneyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jāti satasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapannoti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyyaṃ – ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannāti, iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.
mula_english:
68. “If, monks, a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I experience the various kinds of supernormal powers: having been one, may I become many; having been many, may I become one; may I appear and vanish; may I go unhindered through a wall, through an enclosure, through a mountain as though through space; may I dive in and out of the earth as though it were water; may I walk on water without sinking as though it were earth; seated cross-legged, may I travel in space like a bird; with my hand may I touch and stroke the moon and sun, so powerful and mighty; may I exert influence with my body even as far as the *Brahma* world’—let him be one who perfectly fulfills the precepts…and let him develop secluded dwellings.

“If, monks, a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I, with the divine ear element (*dibbāya sotadhātuyā*), which is purified and surpasses the human, hear both kinds of sounds, the divine and the human, those that are far as well as near’—let him be one who perfectly fulfills the precepts…and let him develop secluded dwellings.

“If, monks, a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I understand the minds of other beings, of other persons, having encompassed them with my own mind. May I understand a mind affected by lust (*sarāgaṃ cittaṃ*) as affected by lust and a mind unaffected by lust (*vītarāgaṃ cittaṃ*) as unaffected by lust; may I understand a mind affected by hate (*sadosaṃ cittaṃ*) as affected by hate and a mind unaffected by hate (*vītadosaṃ cittaṃ*) as unaffected by hate; may I understand a mind affected by delusion (*samohaṃ cittaṃ*) as affected by delusion and a mind unaffected by delusion (*vītamohaṃ cittaṃ*) as unaffected by delusion; may I understand a contracted mind (*saṃkhittaṃ cittaṃ*) as contracted and a distracted mind (*vikkhittaṃ cittaṃ*) as distracted; may I understand an exalted mind (*mahaggataṃ cittaṃ*) as exalted and an unexalted mind (*amahaggataṃ cittaṃ*) as unexalted; may I understand a surpassable mind (*sauttaraṃ cittaṃ*) as surpassable and an unsurpassed mind (*anuttaraṃ cittaṃ*) as unsurpassed; may I understand a concentrated mind (*samāhitaṃ cittaṃ*) as concentrated and an unconcentrated mind (*asamāhitaṃ cittaṃ*) as unconcentrated; may I understand a liberated mind (*vimuttaṃ cittaṃ*) as liberated and an unliberated mind (*avimuttaṃ cittaṃ*) as unliberated’—let him be one who perfectly fulfills the precepts…and let him develop secluded dwellings.

“If, monks, a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I recollect my manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ*), that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of world-contraction, many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of world-contraction and expansion: There I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term. Passing away from there, I was reborn in such-and-such other circumstances. There too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term. Passing away from there, I was reborn here.’ Thus with their aspects and their particulars may I recollect my manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ*)’—let him be one who perfectly fulfills the precepts…and let him develop secluded dwellings.

“If, monks, a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I, with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), which is purified and surpasses the human, see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate; may I understand how beings pass on according to their actions thus: “These worthy beings who were ill-conducted in body, speech, and mind, revilers of noble ones, wrong in their views, giving effect to wrong view in their actions, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination, in the abyss, in hell; but these worthy beings who were well-conducted in body, speech, and mind, not revilers of noble ones, right in their views, giving effect to right view in their actions, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a good destination, in a heavenly world”’—thus may I, with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), which is purified and surpasses the human, see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate; may I understand how beings pass on according to their actions’—let him be one who perfectly fulfills the precepts, devoted to internal serenity of mind, not rejecting meditative absorption, possessed of insight, and let him develop secluded dwellings.
commentary_pali:
68. Evaṃ anāgāmimagge vutte kiñcāpi catutthamaggassa vāro āgato, atha kho naṃ bhagavā aggahetvāva yasmā na kevalā āsavakkhayābhiññā eva sīlānaṃ ānisaṃso, apica kho lokiyapañcābhiññāyopi, tasmā tāpi dassetuṃ, yasmā ca āsavakkhaye kathite desanā niṭṭhitā hoti, evañca sati imesaṃ guṇānaṃ akathitattā ayaṃ kathā muṇḍābhiññākathā nāma bhaveyya, tasmā ca abhiññāpāripūriṃ katvā dassetumpi, yasmā ca anāgāmimagge ṭhitassa sukhena iddhivikuppanā ijjhati, samādhiparibandhānaṃ kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ samūhatattā, anāgāmī hi sīlesu ca samādhimhi ca paripūrakārī, tasmā yuttaṭṭhāneyeva lokiyābhiññāyo dassetumpi ‘‘ākaṅkheyya ce…pe… anekavihita’’nti evamādimāhāti ayamanusandhi.

Tattha ‘‘anekavihitaṃ iddhividha’’ntiādinā nayena āgatānaṃ pañcannampi lokiyābhiññānaṃ pāḷivaṇṇanā saddhiṃ bhāvanānayena visuddhimagge vuttā.

visuddhimagge
commentary_english:
Thus, it has been said regarding the path of the non-returner (*anāgāmin*). Although the turn of the fourth path has come, the Blessed One did not take it up. Because it is not only the benefit of morality that is the knowledge of the destruction of the influxes (*āsavakkhaya-abhiññā*), but also the worldly five knowledges (*lokiyapañcābhiññā*), therefore, in order to show these as well, since the teaching is completed when the destruction of the influxes is spoken of, and thus the story would be called a "truncated knowledge story" because these qualities are not spoken of, and therefore, in order to show the completion of the knowledges, and because the supernormal transformations (*iddhi-vikuppanā*) of one established in the path of the non-returner easily succeed, since the obstructions to concentration, desire, passion, and ill-will are eradicated, the non-returner is a fulfiller in morality and in concentration. Therefore, it is fitting and appropriate to show the worldly knowledges. "If he should desire...pe...manifold," thus, and so on, he says. This is the connection.

There, the *Pāḷi* commentary on the five worldly knowledges that have come in the manner beginning with "manifold supernormal power" (*anekavihitaṃ iddhividha*) is spoken of in the *Visuddhimagga* together with the method of cultivation.

*Visuddhimagga*

mula_pali:
69. ‘‘Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu – ‘āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭhevadhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

‘‘Sampannasīlā, bhikkhave, viharatha sampannapātimokkhā; pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvutā viharatha ācāragocarasampannā aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvino; samādāya sikkhatha sikkhāpadesū’’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vutta’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Ākaṅkheyyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
“If a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I, by realizing for myself with direct knowledge, here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the destruction of the *āsavas* (influxes, taints),’ let him fulfill the precepts, be devoted to internal serenity of mind (*cetosamatha*), not neglect meditation (*jhāna*), be possessed of insight (*vipassanā*), and dwell in empty huts.

“Bhikkhus, dwell possessed of virtue (*sīla*), possessed of the *Pātimokkha*, restrained with the restraint of the *Pātimokkha*, perfect in conduct (*ācāra*) and resort (*gocara*), and seeing fear in the slightest fault (*vajja*), train by undertaking the training precepts (*sikkhāpada*).’ So it was with reference to this that it was said."

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*bhagavā*). Gratified, the monks (*bhikkhu*) delighted in the Blessed One’s words (*bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti*).

The sixth *Ākaṅkheyya Sutta* is finished.
commentary_pali:
69. Chaṭṭhābhiññāya āsavānaṃ khayāti arahattamaggena sabbakilesānaṃ khayā. Anāsavanti āsavavirahitaṃ. Cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttinti ettha cetovacanena arahattaphalasampayuttova samādhi, paññāvacanena taṃsampayuttā paññāva vuttā. Tattha ca samādhi rāgato vimuttattā cetovimutti, paññā avijjāya vimuttattā paññāvimuttīti veditabbā. Vuttañcetaṃ bhagavatā ‘‘yo hissa, bhikkhave, samādhi, tadassa samādhindriyaṃ. Yā hissa, bhikkhave, paññā, tadassa paññindriyaṃ. Iti kho, bhikkhave , rāgavirāgā cetovimutti, avijjāvirāgā paññāvimuttī’’ti, apicettha samathaphalaṃ cetovimutti, vipassanāphalaṃ paññāvimuttīti veditabbā.

Diṭṭheva dhammeti imasmiṃyeva attabhāve. Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvāti attanoyeva paññāya paccakkhaṃ katvā, aparapaccayena ñatvāti attho. Upasampajja vihareyyanti pāpuṇitvā sampādetvā vihareyyaṃ. Sīlesvevāti evaṃ sabbāsave niddhunitvā cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ adhigantukāmopi sīlesvevassa paripūrakārīti.

Diṭṭheva dhamme Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā Upasampajja vihareyya Sīlesvevā

Evaṃ bhagavā sīlānisaṃsakathaṃ yāva arahattā kathetvā idāni sabbampi taṃ sīlānisaṃsaṃ sampiṇḍetvā dassento nigamanaṃ āha ‘‘sampannasīlā, bhikkhave…pe… idametaṃ paṭicca vutta’’nti. Tassāyaṃ saṅkhepattho, ‘‘sampannasīlā, bhikkhave, viharatha…pe… samādāya sikkhatha sikkhāpadesū’’ti iti yaṃ taṃ mayā pubbe evaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ sabbampi sampannasīlo bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṃ piyo hoti manāpo, garu bhāvanīyo paccayānaṃ lābhī, paccayadāyakānaṃ mahapphalakaro, pubbañātīnaṃ anussaraṇacetanāya phalamahattakaro, aratiratisaho, bhayabheravasaho, rūpāvacarajjhānānaṃ arūpāvacarajjhānānañca lābhī, heṭṭhimāni tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni pañca lokiyābhiññā āsavakkhayañāṇanti ca ime ca guṇe sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikattā hoti, etaṃ paṭicca idaṃ sandhāya vuttanti. Idamavoca bhagavā, attamanā te bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Ākaṅkheyyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
69. *āsavānaṃ khayā* ("the destruction of the āsavas") means the destruction of all defilements by the path of Arhatship. *anāsava* ("taintless") means devoid of āsavas. *cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimutti* ("liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom"): here, *ceto* ("mind") refers to the samādhi associated with the fruition of Arhatship, and *paññā* ("wisdom") refers to the wisdom associated with that. And there, it should be understood that *samādhi* is *cetovimutti* ("liberation of mind") because of being liberated from passion, and *paññā* is *paññāvimutti* ("liberation by wisdom") because of being liberated from ignorance. This was said by the Blessed One: "That which is his, monks, is samādhi, that is his faculty of samādhi. That which is his, monks, is wisdom, that is his faculty of wisdom. Thus, monks, , liberation of mind comes from the absence of passion, liberation by wisdom comes from the absence of ignorance," also, it should be understood that the fruit of serenity is *cetovimutti* ("liberation of mind"), and the fruit of insight (*vipassanā*) is *paññāvimutti* ("liberation by wisdom"). *diṭṭheva dhamme* ("in the visible here and now") means in this very existence. *sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā* ("having realized it oneself through super-knowledge") means having directly made it, having known it through one's own wisdom, not through another's agency; that is the meaning. *upasampajja vihareyya* ("having attained, he dwells") means having reached and accomplished, he dwells. *sīlesvevā* ("only in virtue") means that even desiring to attain liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, after having completely driven away all the taints in this way, he is a perfecter only in virtue. diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya sīlesvevā Thus, the Blessed One, having spoken of the benefits of virtue up to Arhatship, now summing up all those benefits of virtue, and showing [them], speaks the conclusion: "Accomplished in virtue, monks…pe… this was said dependent on this." This is the condensed meaning: "Accomplished in virtue, monks, dwell…pe… undertake the training in the trainings," thus, that which was previously said by me in this way, all of this: the monk accomplished in virtue is dear and pleasing to his fellow ব্রহ্মচারীs, he is respected and worthy of reverence, he obtains requisites, he is of great fruit to those who give requisites, he is of great fruit through the thought of remembrance to former relatives, he is able to endure both discontent and content, he is able to endure fear and terror, and he gains the rūpāvacara-jhānas and the arūpāvacara-jhānas, the three lower fruits of asceticism, the five mundane super-knowledges, and the knowledge of the destruction of the āsavas, and he himself is the direct experiencer of these qualities through super-knowledge , this was said dependent on this, intending this. This is what the Blessed One said, the monks were delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

Papañcasūdanī, Commentary on the Middle Length Discourses (Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā) The Aspiration Sutta Explanation is Concluded.

mula_pali:
70. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vatthaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ malaggahitaṃ; tamenaṃ rajako yasmiṃ yasmiṃ raṅgajāte upasaṃhareyya – yadi nīlakāya yadi pītakāya yadi lohitakāya yadi mañjiṭṭhakāya mañjeṭṭhakāya (sī. pī.), mañjeṭṭhikāya (syā.) durattavaṇṇamevassa aparisuddhavaṇṇamevassa. Taṃ kissa hetu? Aparisuddhattā, bhikkhave, vatthassa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, citte saṃkiliṭṭhe, duggati pāṭikaṅkhā. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vatthaṃ parisuddhaṃ pariyodātaṃ; tamenaṃ rajako yasmiṃ yasmiṃ raṅgajāte upasaṃhareyya – yadi nīlakāya yadi pītakāya yadi lohitakāya yadi mañjiṭṭhakāya – surattavaṇṇamevassa parisuddhavaṇṇamevassa. Taṃ kissa hetu? Parisuddhattā, bhikkhave, vatthassa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, citte asaṃkiliṭṭhe, sugati pāṭikaṅkhā.

mañjeṭṭhakāya (sī. pī.), mañjeṭṭhikāya (syā.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: "Monks."

"Venerable sir," those monks replied.

The Blessed One said this:

"Bhikkhus, suppose a cloth were soiled and stained; whatever color a dyer might dip it in—whether blue, or yellow, or red, or madder dye (mañjiṭṭhakāya)—it would look badly dyed and impure in color. Why is that? Because of the impurity of the cloth, bhikkhus. So too, bhikkhus, when the mind is defiled (**citte saṃkiliṭṭhe**), an unhappy destination may be expected (**duggati pāṭikaṅkhā**).

Bhikkhus, suppose a cloth were pure and bright; whatever color a dyer might dip it in—whether blue, or yellow, or red, or madder dye—it would look well-dyed and pure in color. Why is that? Because of the purity of the cloth, bhikkhus. So too, bhikkhus, when the mind is undefiled (**citte asaṃkiliṭṭhe**), a happy destination may be expected (**sugati pāṭikaṅkhā**)."
commentary_pali:
70.Evaṃme sutanti vatthasuttaṃ. Tattha seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vatthanti upamāvacanamevetaṃ. Upamaṃ karonto ca bhagavā katthaci paṭhamaṃyeva upamaṃ dassetvā pacchā atthaṃ dasseti, katthaci paṭhamamatthaṃ dassetvā pacchā upamaṃ, katthaci upamāya atthaṃ parivāretvā dasseti, katthaci atthena upamaṃ.

Tathā hesa – ‘‘seyyathāpissu, bhikkhave, dve agārā sadvārā, tattha cakkhumā puriso majjhe ṭhito passeyyā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.261) sakalampi devadūtasuttaṃ upamaṃ paṭhamaṃ dassetvā pacchā atthaṃ dassento āha. ‘‘Tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gacchati, seyyathāpi ākāse’’tiādinā (dī. ni. 1.238; paṭi. ma. 1.102) pana nayena sakalampi iddhividhamatthaṃ paṭhamaṃ dassetvā pacchā upamaṃ dassento āha. ‘‘Seyyathāpi brāhmaṇapuriso sāratthiko sāragavesī’’tiādināva (ma. ni. 1.318) nayena sakalampi cūḷasāropamasuttaṃ upamāya atthaṃ parivāretvā dassento āha. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacce kulaputtā dhammaṃ pariyāpuṇanti suttaṃ…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso alagaddatthiko’’tiādinā (ma. ni. 1.238) nayena sakalampi alagaddasuttaṃ mahāsāropamasuttanti evamādīni suttāni atthena upamaṃ parivāretvā dassento āha.

Svāyaṃ idha paṭhamaṃ upamaṃ dassetvā pacchā atthaṃ dasseti. Kasmā panevaṃ bhagavā dassetīti? Puggalajjhāsayena vā desanāvilāsena vā. Ye hi puggalā paṭhamaṃ upamaṃ dassetvā vuccamānamatthaṃ sukhena paṭivijjhanti, tesaṃ paṭhamaṃ upamaṃ dasseti. Esa nayo sabbattha. Yassā ca dhammadhātuyā suppaṭividdhattā desanāvilāsaṃ patto hoti, tassā suppaṭividdhā. Tasmā esa desanāvilāsampatto dhammissaro dhammarājā, so yathā yathā icchati, tathā tathā dhammaṃ desetīti evaṃ iminā puggalajjhāsayena vā desanāvilāsena vā evaṃ dassetīti veditabbo.

Tattha vatthanti pakatiparisuddhaṃ vatthaṃ. Saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ malaggahitanti āgantukena paṃsurajādinā saṃkilesena saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ, sedajallikādinā malena gahitattā malaggahitaṃ. Raṅgajāteti ettha raṅgameva raṅgajātaṃ. Upasaṃhareyyāti upanāmeyya. Yadi nīlakāyāti nīlakāya vā, nīlakatthāya vāti vuttaṃ hoti. Evaṃ sabbattha. Rajako hi nīlakatthāya upasaṃharanto kaṃsanīlapalāsanīlādike nīlaraṅge upasaṃharati. Pītakatthāya upasaṃharanto kaṇikārapupphasadise pītakaraṅge. Lohitakatthāya upasaṃharanto bandhujīvakapupphasadise lohitakaraṅge. Mañjiṭṭhakatthāya upasaṃharanto kaṇavīrapupphasadise mandarattaraṅge. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘yadi nīlakāya…pe… yadi mañjiṭṭhakāyā’’ti.

vattha Saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ malaggahita Raṅgajāte Upasaṃhareyyā Yadi nīlakāyā

Durattavaṇṇamevassāti duṭṭhu rañjitavaṇṇameva assa. Aparisuddhavaṇṇamevassāti nīlavaṇṇopissa parisuddho na bhaveyya, sesavaṇṇopi. Tādisañhi vatthaṃ nīlakumbhiyā pakkhittampi sunīlaṃ na hoti, sesakumbhīsu pakkhittampi pītakādivaṇṇaṃ na hoti, milātanīla kuraṇḍa-kaṇikāra-bandhujīvaka-kaṇavīrapupphavaṇṇameva hoti. Taṃ kissa hetūti taṃ vatthaṃ kissa hetu kiṃ kāraṇā īdisaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ vā vatthe raṅgajātaṃ kissa hetu īdisaṃ durattavaṇṇaṃ aparisuddhavaṇṇaṃ hotīti? Yasmā panassa vatthassa saṃkiliṭṭhabhāvoyevettha kāraṇaṃ, na aññaṃ kiñci, tasmā ‘‘aparisuddhattā, bhikkhave, vatthassā’’ti āha.

Durattavaṇṇamevassā Aparisuddhavaṇṇamevassā Taṃ kissa hetū

Evameva khoti upamāsampaṭipādanaṃ. Citte saṃkiliṭṭheti cittamhi saṃkiliṭṭhamhi. Kasmā pana bhagavā saṃkiliṭṭhavatthena opammaṃ akāsīti ce, vāyāmamahapphaladassanatthaṃ. Yathā hi āgantukehi malehi saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ vatthaṃ pakatiyā paṇḍarattā puna dhovīyamānaṃ paṇḍaraṃ hoti, na tattha jātikāḷake viya eḷakalome vāyāmo nipphalo hoti, evaṃ cittampi āgantukehi kilesehi saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ. Pakatiyā pana taṃ sakalepi paṭisandhibhavaṅgavāre paṇḍarameva. Yathāha – ‘‘pabhassaramidaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ, tañca kho āgantukehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭha’’nti (a. ni. 1.51). Taṃ visodhīyamānaṃ sakkā pabhassarataraṃ kātuṃ, na tattha vāyāmo nipphaloti evaṃ vāyāmamahapphaladassanatthaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhavatthena opammaṃ akāsīti veditabbo.

Evameva kho Citte saṃkiliṭṭhe

Duggati pāṭikaṅkhāti īdise citte duggati pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, duggatiṃ eva esa pāpuṇissati , nāññanti evaṃ duggati icchitabbā, avassaṃ bhāvīti vuttaṃ hoti. Sā cāyaṃ duggati nāma paṭipattiduggati, gatiduggatīti duvidhā hoti. Paṭipattiduggatipi agāriyapaṭipattiduggati, anagāriyapaṭipattiduggatīti duvidhā hoti.

Duggati pāṭikaṅkhā

Agāriyo hi saṃkiliṭṭhacitto pāṇampi hanati, adinnampi ādiyati, sakalepi dasa akusalakammapathe pūreti, ayamassa agāriyapaṭipattiduggati. So tattha ṭhito kāyassa bhedā nirayampi gacchati, tiracchānayonimpi, pettivisayampi gacchati, ayamassa gatiduggati.

agāriyapaṭipattiduggati gatiduggati

Anagāriyopi imasmiṃ sāsane pabbajito saṃkiliṭṭhacitto dūteyyapahiṇagamanaṃ gacchati, vejjakammaṃ karoti, saṅghabhedāya cetiyabhedāya parakkamati, veḷudānādīhi jīvikaṃ kappeti, sakalampi anācāraṃ agocarañca paripūreti, ayamassa anagāriyapaṭipattiduggati.So tattha ṭhito kāyassa bhedā nirayampi gacchati, tiracchānayonimpi, pettivisayampi gacchati samaṇayakkho nāma hoti samaṇapeto, ādittehi saṅghāṭiādīhi sampajjalitakāyo aṭṭassaraṃ karonto vicarati, ayamassa gatiduggati.

anagāriyapaṭipattiduggati. gatiduggati

Seyyathāpīti sukkapakkhaṃ dassetumāraddho, tassattho kaṇhapakkhe vuttapaccanīkeneva veditabbo. Etthāpi ca sugati nāma paṭipattisugati gatisugatīti duvidhā hoti. Paṭipattisugatipi agāriyapaṭipattisugati anagāriyapaṭipattisugatīti duvidhā hoti. Agāriyo hi parisuddhacitto pāṇātipātāpi viramati, adinnādānāpi, sakalepi dasa kusalakammapathe paripūreti, ayamassa agāriyapaṭipattisugati. So tattha ṭhito kāyassa bhedā manussamahantatampi devamahantatampi upapajjati, ayamassa gatisugati.

Seyyathāpī agāriyapaṭipattisugati gatisugati

Anagāriyopi imasmiṃ sāsane pabbajitvā parisuddhacitto catupārisuddhisīlaṃ sodheti, terasa dhutaṅgāni samādiyati, aṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇesu attano anukūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā pantasenāsane paṭisevamāno kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā jhānasamāpattiyo nibbatteti, sotāpattimaggaṃ bhāveti…pe… anāgāmimaggaṃ bhāveti, ayamassa anagāriyapaṭipattisugati. So tattha ṭhito kāyassa bhedā manussaloke vā tīsu mahākulesu, chasu vā kāmāvacaradevesu, dasasu vā brahmabhavanesu , pañcasu vā suddhāvāsesu, catūsu vā āruppesu upapajjati, ayamassa gatisugatīti.

anagāriyapaṭipattisugati gatisugatī
commentary_english:
70. *Evaṃ me sutaṃ* means the *vatthasutta*. There, *seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vattha* is simply a word of comparison. While making a comparison, the Blessed One sometimes shows the comparison first and afterwards shows the meaning. Sometimes he shows the meaning first and afterwards the comparison. Sometimes he surrounds the meaning with the comparison, and sometimes [surrounds] the comparison with the meaning. Thus, indeed, in the entire Devadūtasutta, he speaks, showing the comparison first and afterwards showing the meaning, “Just as, monks, there are two houses with doors, and a man with sight standing in the middle might see…” (M. ni. 3. 261). But by the method beginning with "He goes unimpeded through walls, ramparts, and mountains as if through space" (Dī. ni. 1. 238; Paṭi. ma. 1. 102), he speaks, showing the entire meaning of psychic power first and afterwards showing the comparison. By the method beginning with "Just as a brahmin man, seeking essence, searching for essence" (M. ni. 1. 318), he speaks, showing the entire Cūḷasāropamasutta surrounding the meaning with the comparison. He speaks, showing the suttas beginning with "Here, monks, some clansmen learn the Dhamma, a sutta…pe… Just as, monks, a man in need of a snake" (M. ni. 1. 238), the entire Alagaddasutta, Mahāsāropamasutta and so forth, surrounding the comparison with the meaning. Here, he shows the comparison first and afterwards shows the meaning. Why does the Blessed One show it in this way? Either by way of people’s inclinations or by skillful teaching. For to those people who easily understand the meaning being spoken after showing the comparison first, he shows the comparison first. This method applies to everything. And because of the perfect penetration of the element of the Dhamma, he has attained skill in teaching; for her it is perfectly penetrated. Therefore, this lord of the Dhamma, the king of the Dhamma, having attained skill in teaching, teaches the Dhamma as he wishes. Thus, it should be understood that he shows it in this way by way of people’s inclinations or by skill in teaching. There, *vattha* means a cloth pure in its nature. *Saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ malaggahitaṃ* means soiled by the adventitious defilement of dust and so on, and seized by the impurity of sweat, grime and so on, hence seized by impurity. In *raṅgajāte*, *raṅga* itself is *raṅgajāta*. *Upasaṃhareyya* means he might present it. *Yadi nīlakāyā* means whether *nīlakāya* or *nīlakatthāya* is said. So in each instance. Indeed, when a washerman applies blue dye, he applies blue dye to things like metal, sapphire, *palāsa*, or indigo. When he applies yellow dye, he applies yellow dye to things resembling *kaṇikāra* flowers. When he applies red dye, he applies red dye to things resembling *bandhujīvaka* flowers. When he applies madder dye, he applies madder dye to things resembling *kaṇavīra* flowers, [things] with a reddish shimmer. Therefore, it was said, “Whether [it is] a blue body…pe…whether [it is] a madder body.”

Cloth is soiled, seized by dirt in the quality of dye he would apply if [it were] a blue body

It would be of poor color”, it would be of badly dyed color. It would be of impure color”, even a blue color of it would not be pure, nor [would] another color. Indeed, such cloth, even when placed in a blue vat, does not become very blue; even when placed in other vats, it does not become of yellow color, etc.; it only becomes of a wilted blue, *kuraṇḍa*, *kaṇikāra*, *bandhujīvaka*, *kaṇavīra* flower color. What is the cause of that?” What is the cause, what is the reason that such cloth is like this? Or, what is the cause that the quality of dye in that cloth is of such poor color, impure color? Because, indeed, the cause here is simply the soiled nature of that cloth; there is no other [cause]. Therefore, he said, “Because of impurity, monks, of the cloth.”

It would be of poor color It would be of impure color What is the cause of that?

Just so” is the setting forth of an analogy. When the mind is soiled” [means] when the mind is soiled. Why did the Blessed One make the comparison with soiled cloth? For the purpose of showing the great fruit of effort. Just as cloth, soiled by incidental dirt, being naturally white, again becoming purified by being washed, becomes white; there, effort is not fruitless, like a *jāti* black mark, or a goat hair. Just so, the mind, too, is soiled by incidental defilements. But by nature, it is only bright in every rebirth linking (*paṭisandhi*) moment of existence (*bhavaṅga*). As he said – “This mind, monks, is radiant, but it is soiled by incidental defilements” (a. ni. 1. 51). Being purified, it is possible to make it even more radiant; there, effort is not fruitless. Thus, for the purpose of showing the great fruit of effort, it should be understood that he made the comparison with soiled cloth.

Just so when the mind is soiled

Bad destination is to be expected”, in such a mind a bad destination is to be expected; that one will simply reach a bad destination , not another. Thus, a bad destination is to be desired; it was said that it is necessarily becoming. And that bad destination, namely, is twofold: bad conduct (*paṭipatti-duggati*), bad rebirth (*gati-duggati*). And bad conduct (*paṭipatti-duggati*), too, is twofold: bad conduct of a householder (*agāriya-paṭipatti-duggati*), bad conduct of a homeless one (*anagāriya-paṭipatti-duggati*).

Bad destination is to be expected

For a householder, indeed, with a soiled mind kills living beings, takes what is not given, completely fills every one of the ten unwholesome courses of action. This is his bad conduct of a householder. He, abiding there, at the breaking up of the body, goes to hell, goes to the animal realm, goes to the realm of ghosts. This is his bad rebirth.

Bad conduct of a householder Bad rebirth

A homeless one, too, gone forth in this Teaching, with a soiled mind, engages in going as a messenger or errand-goer, practices medicine, strives for schism in the *Saṅgha*, for schism in a *cetiya*, makes a living by bamboo work, etc., completely fills every improper and out-of-bounds thing. This is his bad conduct of a homeless one. He, abiding there, at the breaking up of the body, goes to hell, goes to the animal realm, goes to the realm of ghosts. He is called a *samaṇa*-demon, a *samaṇa*-departed one; with robes, etc. ablaze, with body completely ablaze, he wanders about making a harsh sound. This is his bad rebirth.

Bad conduct of a homeless one. Bad rebirth

Just as” he has begun to show the bright side (*sukka-pakkha*); its meaning should be understood simply in the way opposite to what was said on the dark side (*kaṇha-pakkha*). And here, too, a good destination (*sugati*), namely, is twofold: good conduct (*paṭipatti-sugati*), good rebirth (*gati-sugati*). Good conduct (*paṭipatti-sugati*), too, is twofold: good conduct of a householder (*agāriya-paṭipatti-sugati*), good conduct of a homeless one (*anagāriya-paṭipatti-sugati*). For a householder, indeed, with a purified mind, abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given, completely fills every one of the ten wholesome courses of action. This is his good conduct of a householder. So, staying there, at the dissolution of the body, he is reborn in a state of great human existence or great divine existence; this is his *gatisugati* (good destination). Just as a good destination due to practicing the life of a householder, [is a] *gatisugati* (good destination). Even a homeless one, having gone forth in this dispensation, with a perfectly pure mind, purifies the fourfold purification of virtue, undertakes the thirteen ascetic practices, having taken a meditation subject suitable to himself from among the thirty-eight objects, frequenting a secluded dwelling, having performed the preliminary work on the *kasiṇa*, develops the attainments of *jhāna*, cultivates the path of stream-entry…pe… cultivates the path of non-returning; this is his *anagāriyapaṭipattisugati* (good destination due to practicing the homeless life). So, staying there, at the dissolution of the body, he is reborn in the human world, or in three great families, or in the six *kāmāvacara* heavens, or in the ten Brahma abodes, or in the five *śuddhāvāsa* heavens, or in the four *ārūppa* realms; this is his *gatisugatī* (good destinations).

mula_pali: 71. ‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, cittassa upakkilesā? Abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso, byāpādo cittassa upakkileso, kodho cittassa upakkileso, upanāho cittassa upakkileso, makkho cittassa upakkileso, paḷāso cittassa upakkileso, issā cittassa upakkileso, macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso, māyā cittassa upakkileso, sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso, thambho cittassa upakkileso, sārambho cittassa upakkileso, māno cittassa upakkileso, atimāno cittassa upakkileso, mado cittassa upakkileso, pamādo cittassa upakkileso.
mula_english: "71. And what, monks, are the imperfections that defile the mind (cittassa upakkilesā)? Covetousness and unrighteous greed (abhijjhāvisamalobho) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Ill will (byāpādo) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Anger (kodho) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Revenge (upanāho) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Contempt (makkho) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. A domineering attitude (paḷāso) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Envy (issā) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Avarice (macchariyaṃ) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Deceit (māyā) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Fraud (sāṭheyyaṃ) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Obstinacy (thambho) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Presumption (sārambho) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Conceit (māno) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Arrogance (atimāno) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Vanity (mado) is an imperfection that defiles the mind. Negligence (pamādo) is an imperfection that defiles the mind."
commentary_pali:
71. Evaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhe citte duggati pāṭikaṅkhā, asaṃkiliṭṭhe ca sugatīti vatvā idāni yehi upakkilesehi cittaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ hoti, te dassento katame ca, bhikkhave, cittassa upakkilesā? Abhijjhā visamalobhotiādimāha.

Tattha sakabhaṇḍe chandarāgo abhijjhā, parabhaṇḍe visamalobho. Atha vā sakabhaṇḍe vā parabhaṇḍe vā hotu, yuttapattaṭṭhāne chandarāgo abhijjhā, ayuttāpattaṭṭhāne visamalobho. Thero panāha ‘‘kissa vinibbhogaṃ karotha, yutte vā ayutte vā hotu, ‘rāgo visamaṃ doso visamaṃ moho visama’nti (vibha. 924) vacanato na koci lobho avisamo nāma, tasmā lobhoyeva abhijjhāyanaṭṭhena abhijjhā, visamaṭṭhena visamaṃ, ekatthametaṃ byañjanameva nāna’’nti. So panesa abhijjhāvisamalobho uppajjitvā cittaṃ dūseti, obhāsituṃ na deti. Tasmā ‘‘cittassa upakkileso’’ti vuccati.

abhijjhā, visamalobho

Yathā cesa, evaṃ navavidhaāghātavatthusambhavo byāpādo. Dasavidhaāghātavatthusambhavo kodho. Punappunaṃ cittapariyonandhano upanāho. Agāriyassa vā anagāriyassa vā sukatakaraṇavināsano makkho. Agāriyopi hi kenaci anukampakena daliddo samāno ucce ṭhāne ṭhapito, aparena samayena ‘‘kiṃ tayā mayhaṃ kata’’nti tassa sukatakaraṇaṃ vināseti. Anagāriyopi sāmaṇerakālato pabhuti ācariyena vā upajjhāyena vā catūhi paccayehi uddesaparipucchāhi ca anuggahetvā dhammakathānayapakaraṇakosallādīni sikkhāpito, aparena samayena rājarājamahāmattādīhi sakkato garukato ācariyupajjhāyesu acittīkato caramāno ‘‘ayaṃ amhehi daharakāle evaṃ anuggahito saṃvaḍḍhito ca, atha panidāni nissineho jāto’’ti vuccamāno ‘‘kiṃ mayhaṃ tumhehi kata’’nti tesaṃ sukatakaraṇaṃ vināseti, tassa so sukatakaraṇavināsano makkho uppajjitvā cittaṃ dūseti, obhāsituṃ na deti. Tasmā ‘‘cittassa upakkileso’’ti vuccati.

byāpādo kodho upanāho makkho

Yathā cāyaṃ, evaṃ bahussutepi puggale ajjhottharitvā ‘‘īdisassa ceva bahussutassa aniyatā gati, tava vā mama vā ko viseso’’tiādinā nayena uppajjamāno yugaggāhagāhī paḷāso. Paresaṃ sakkārādīni khīyanā issā. Attano sampattiyā parehi sādhāraṇabhāvaṃ asahamānaṃ macchariyaṃ. Vañcanikacariyabhūtā māyā. Kerāṭikabhāvena uppajjamānaṃ sāṭheyyaṃ. Kerāṭiko hi āyatanamaccho viya hoti. Āyatanamaccho nāma kira macchānaṃ naṅguṭṭhaṃ dasseti sappānaṃ sīsaṃ , ‘‘tumhehi sadiso aha’’nti jānāpetuṃ. Evameva kerāṭiko puggalo yaṃ yaṃ suttantikaṃ vā ābhidhammikaṃ vā upasaṅkamati, taṃ taṃ evaṃ vadati ‘‘ahaṃ tumhākaṃ baddhacaro, tumhe mayhaṃ anukampakā, nāhaṃ tumhe muñcāmī’’ti ‘‘evamete ‘sagāravo ayaṃ amhesu sappatisso’ti maññissantī’’ti. Tassetaṃ kerāṭikabhāvena uppajjamānaṃ sāṭheyyaṃ uppajjitvā cittaṃ dūseti, obhāsituṃ na deti. Tasmā ‘‘cittassa upakkileso’’ti vuccati.

paḷāso issā macchariyaṃ māyā sāṭheyyaṃ Āyatanamaccho

Yathā cetaṃ, evaṃ vātabharitabhastasadisathaddhabhāvapaggahitasiraanivātavuttikārakaraṇo thambho. Taduttarikaraṇo sārambho. So duvidhena labbhati akusalavasena ceva kusalavasena ca. Tattha agāriyassa parena kataṃ alaṅkārādiṃ disvā taddiguṇakaraṇena uppajjamāno, anagāriyassa ca yattakaṃ yattakaṃ paro pariyāpuṇāti vā katheti vā, mānavasena taddiguṇataddiguṇakaraṇena uppajjamāno akusalo. Agāriyassa pana paraṃ ekaṃ salākabhattaṃ dentaṃ disvā attanā dve vā tīṇi vā dātukāmatāya uppajjamāno, anagāriyassa ca parena ekanikāye gahite mānaṃ anissāya kevalaṃ taṃ disvā attanā ālasiyaṃ abhibhuyya dve nikāye gahetukāmatāya uppajjamāno kusalo. Idha pana akusalo adhippeto. Ayañhi uppajjitvā cittaṃ dūseti, obhāsituṃ na deti. Tasmā ‘‘cittassa upakkileso’’ti vuccati.

thambho sārambho

Yathā cāyaṃ, evaṃ jātiādīni nissāya cittassa uṇṇativasena pavattamāno māno, accuṇṇativasena atimāno, madaggahaṇākāro mado, kāmaguṇesu cittavossaggavasena uppajjamāno pamādo uppajjitvā cittaṃ dūseti, obhāsituṃ na deti. Tasmā ‘‘cittassa upakkileso’’ti vuccati.

māno, atimāno, mado, pamādo

Kasmā pana bhagavā upakkilesaṃ dassento lobhamādiṃ katvā dassetīti? Tassa paṭhamuppattito. Sabbasattānañhi yattha katthaci upapannānaṃ antamaso suddhāvāsabhūmiyampi sabbapaṭhamaṃ bhavanikantivasena lobho uppajjati, tato attano attano anurūpapaccayaṃ paṭicca yathāsambhavaṃ itare, na ca ete soḷaseva cittassa upakkilesā, etena pana nayena sabbepi kilesā gahitāyeva hontīti veditabbā.
commentary_english:
Thus, when thought is defiled, a bad rebirth [duggati] is hoped for, and when undefiled, a good rebirth [sugati] is hoped for. Having said this, now, to show by which defilements [upakkilesa] thought [citta] becomes defiled, [he] says: “Which are the defilements of thought, *bhikkhus*? Namely, covetousness ( *abhijjhā*) and excessive greed (*visamalobha*),” and so forth.

Therein, *abhijjhā* is desire and passion (chandarāga) for one's own possessions (sakabhaṇḍa), and *visamalobha* is desire and passion for the possessions of others (parabhaṇḍa). Or rather, whether it be one's own possessions or the possessions of others, *abhijjhā* is desire and passion in a fitting situation (yuttapattaṭṭhāna), and *visamalobha* is desire and passion in an unfitting situation (ayuttāpattaṭṭhāna).

But the *thera* said: “Why do you make a distinction? Whether it be fitting or unfitting, lust (*rāga*) is uneven [visama], hatred (*dosa*) is uneven, delusion (*moha*) is uneven.” According to the *vacana* ( Vibha. 924), there is no greed (*lobha*) that is not uneven. Therefore, greed is *abhijjhā* by way of being fixated [abhijjhāyanaṭṭhena], and it is *visama* by way of being uneven [visamaṭṭhena]; this is the same meaning, only the expression is different [byañjanameva nāna].

But this *abhijjhāvisamalobha*, having arisen, corrupts the mind [cittaṃ dūseti], and does not allow it to shine [obhāsituṃ na deti]. Therefore, it is called “a defilement of thought [cittassa upakkileso].”

*Abhijjhā*, *visamalobha*. Just as that is, so also, ill-will (*byāpāda*) arises from nine kinds of grounds for hatred [navavidhaāghātavatthusambhava]. Anger (*kodha*) arises from ten kinds of grounds for hatred [dasavidhaāghātavatthusambhava]. Enmity (*upanāha*) is the repeated binding of the mind [punappunaṃ cittapariyonandhana]. Spite (*makkha*) is the destruction of good actions done by either a householder [agāriyassa] or a homeless one [anagāriyassa].

For example, even a householder, if he is poor, having been placed in a high position by someone compassionate, after some time destroys the good actions done for him, [saying,] “What have you done for me?”

Even a homeless one, from the time of being a novice [sāmaṇerakālato pabhuti], having been favored by his teacher (*ācariya*) or preceptor (*upajjhāya*) with the four requisites [catūhi paccayehi] and with lessons [uddesaparipucchāhi], and having been taught the skill of delivering Dharma talks and expositions of doctrine [dhammakathānayapakaraṇakosallādīni sikkhāpito], after some time, being honored and respected by kings, royal ministers and so on, and behaving disrespectfully towards his teachers and preceptors, when people say, “He was favored and raised by us when he was young, but now he has become ungrateful,” he destroys their good actions [saying,] “What have you done for me?” That spite [makkha], destructive of good actions, having arisen, corrupts the mind [cittaṃ dūseti], and does not allow it to shine [obhāsituṃ na deti]. Therefore, it is called “a defilement of thought [cittassa upakkileso].”

*Byāpāda*, *kodha*, *upanāha*, *makkha*. Just as that is, so also, disparagement (*paḷāso*) is being generated in one who is very learned, having overwhelmed that person [bahussutepi puggale ajjhottharitvā] with the thought, "What difference is there between you or me, since even such a learned person has an uncertain destiny?" [īdTherefore, it is called "a defilement of the mind" (cittassa upakkileso).

*Thambho*, *sārambho*.

Just as this [pride, *māna*] arises depending on birth etc., in the manner of inflation of the mind; *atimāna* [excessive pride] in the manner of non-inflation; *mada* [intoxication] having the nature of grasping at intoxication; *pamāda* [negligence] arising in the manner of casting off the mind from sense qualities, having arisen, defiles the mind, and does not allow it to shine.

Therefore, it is called "a defilement of the mind" (cittassa upakkileso).

*Māna*, *atimāna*, *mada*, *pamāda*. Why does the Blessed One, while indicating defilements (upakkilesaṃ), indicate greed (lobha) etc., having made it the beginning? Because of its first arising.

Indeed, for all beings (sabbasattānaṃ) who are born anywhere (yattha katthaci), even in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsabhūmi), greed (lobho) arises as the very first thing in the manner of delight in existence (bhavanikantivasena). Then, depending on a suitable condition (anurūpapaccayaṃ), each for themselves (attano attano), the others arise according to possibility (yathāsambhavaṃ). And these are not only sixteen defilements (soḷaseva cittassa upakkilesā) of the mind; but by this method, all the defilements (kilesā) are indeed included; it should be understood (veditabbā).

mula_pali: 72. ‘‘Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā byāpādaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati ; ‘kodho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā kodhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘upanāho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā upanāhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘makkho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā makkhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘paḷāso cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā paḷāsaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘issā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā issaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘māyā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā māyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘thambho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā thambhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘sārambho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā sārambhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘māno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā mānaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘atimāno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atimānaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘mado cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā madaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati; ‘pamādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā pamādaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahati.
mula_english: 72. “Knowing that covetousness and unrighteous greed (*abhijjhāvisamalobha*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind (*cittassa upakkileso*), a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that ill will (*byāpādo*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that anger (*kodho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that resentment (*upanāho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that hypocrisy (*makkho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that insolence (*paḷāso*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that envy (*issā*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that stinginess (*macchariyaṃ*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that deceit (*māyā*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that craftiness (*sāṭheyyaṃ*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that obstinacy (*thambho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that contentiousness (*sārambho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that conceit (*māno*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that arrogance (*atimāno*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that vanity (*mado*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it. Knowing that negligence (*pamādo*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind, a *bhikkhu* abandons it.
commentary_pali:
72. Ettāvatā saṃkilesaṃ dassetvā idāni vodānaṃ dassento sa kho so, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha iti viditvāti evaṃ jānitvā. Pajahatīti samucchedappahānavasena ariyamaggena pajahati. Tattha kilesapaṭipāṭiyā maggapaṭipāṭiyāti dvidhā pahānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Kilesapaṭipāṭiyā tāva abhijjhāvisamalobho thambho sārambho māno atimāno madoti ime cha kilesā arahattamaggena pahīyanti. Byāpādo kodho upanāho pamādoti ime cattāro kilesā anāgāmimaggena pahīyanti. Makkho paḷāso issā macchariyaṃ māyā sāṭheyyanti ime cha sotāpattimaggena pahīyantīti. Maggapaṭipāṭiyā pana, sotāpattimaggena makkho paḷāso issā macchariyaṃ māyā sāṭheyyanti ime cha pahīyanti. Anāgāmimaggena byāpādo kodho upanāho pamādoti ime cattāro. Arahattamaggena abhijjhāvisamalobho thambho sārambho māno atimāno madoti ime cha pahīyantīti.

Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne ime kilesā sotāpattimaggavajjhā vā hontu, sesamaggavajjhā vā, atha kho anāgāmimaggeneva pahānaṃ sandhāya ‘‘abhijjhāvisamalobhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahatī’’tiādimāhāti veditabbā. Ayamettha paveṇimaggāgato sambhavo, so ca upari catutthamaggasseva niddiṭṭhattā yujjati, tatiyamaggena pahīnāvasesānañhi visamalobhādīnaṃ tena pahānaṃ hoti, sesānaṃ imināva. Yepi hi sotāpattimaggena pahīyanti, tepi taṃsamuṭṭhāpakacittānaṃ appahīnattā anāgāmimaggeneva suppahīnā hontīti. Keci pana paṭhamamaggena cettha pahānaṃ vaṇṇayanti, taṃ pubbāparena na sandhiyati. Keci vikkhambhanappahānampi, taṃ tesaṃ icchāmattameva.
commentary_english:
72. Having thus shown defilement, now, showing purification, he said, "But so, monks," etc.

There, *iti viditvā* means having known thus.

*Pajahati* means he abandons by means of the noble path in terms of abandonment by eradication.

There, abandonment should be understood as twofold: in terms of the order of defilements and in terms of the order of the paths.

First, in terms of the order of defilements, these six defilements—covetousness, unequal greed (*abhijjhāvisamalobha*), obstinacy (*thambho*), contentiousness (*sārambho*), conceit (*māno*), arrogance (*atimāno*), and intoxication (*mada*)—are abandoned by the path of Arhatship.

These four defilements—ill will (*byāpādo*), anger (*kodho*), hostility (*upanāho*), and negligence (*pamādo*)—are abandoned by the path of non-returning.

These six—hypocrisy (*makkho*), insolence (*paḷāso*), envy (*issā*), stinginess (*macchariyaṃ*), deceit (*māyā*), and craftiness (*sāṭheyyanti*)—are abandoned by the path of stream-entry.

Moreover, in terms of the order of the paths, these six—hypocrisy (*makkho*), insolence (*paḷāso*), envy (*issā*), stinginess (*macchariyaṃ*), deceit (*māyā*), and craftiness (*sāṭheyyanti*)—are abandoned by the path of stream-entry.

These four—ill will (*byāpādo*), anger (*kodho*), hostility (*upanāho*), and negligence (*pamādo*)—[are abandoned] by the path of non-returning.

These six—covetousness, unequal greed (*abhijjhāvisamalobha*), obstinacy (*thambho*), contentiousness (*sārambho*), conceit (*māno*), arrogance (*atimāno*), and intoxication (*mada*)—are abandoned by the path of Arhatship.

In this case, however, it should be understood that these defilements, whether subject to the path of stream-entry or subject to the remaining paths, are spoken of with reference to abandonment by the path of non-returning only, [saying] “He abandons covetousness, unequal greed (*abhijjhāvisamalobha*), a defilement of the mind,” etc.

Here, this is the traditional explanation, and it is fitting because only the fourth path is specified above; for the abandonment of unequal greed (*visamalobha*) etc., which remain after being abandoned by the third path, occurs by that [fourth path], and of the remaining [defilements] by this very [path of non-returning].

Indeed, even those [defilements] that are abandoned by the path of stream-entry are very well abandoned by the path of non-returning, since the minds that give rise to them are not abandoned [by the path of stream-entry].

Some, however, explain the abandonment here by the first path, but that does not connect with what precedes and follows.

Some [explain it] also as abandonment by suppression, but that is merely their wish.
