mula_pali: 73. ‘‘Yato kho yato ca kho (sī. syā.), bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti, ‘byāpādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā byāpādo cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘kodho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā kodho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘upanāho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā upanāho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘makkho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā makkho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘paḷāso cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā paḷāso cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘issā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā issā cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā macchariyaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘māyā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā māyā cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā sāṭheyyaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘thambho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā thambho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘sārambho cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā sārambho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘māno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā māno cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘atimāno cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atimāno cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘mado cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā mado cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti; ‘pamādo cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā pamādo cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti.
mula_english: “When a *bhikkhu* has known that covetousness and unrighteous greed (*abhijjhāvisamalobho*) is an imperfection (*upakkileso*) that defiles the mind (*cittassa*) and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that ill will (*byāpādo*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that anger (*kodho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that resentment (*upanāho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that spite (*makkho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that insolence (*paḷāso*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that envy (*issā*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that selfishness (*macchariyaṃ*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that deceit (*māyā*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that craftiness (*sāṭheyyaṃ*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that obstinacy (*thambho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that impetuosity (*sārambho*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that conceit (*māno*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that arrogance (*atimāno*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that vanity (*mado*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it; when a *bhikkhu* has known that negligence (*pamādo*) is an imperfection that defiles the mind and has abandoned it.
commentary_pali: 73.Yatokho, bhikkhaveti ettha yatoti yamhi kāle. Pahīno hotīti anāgāmimaggakkhaṇe pahānaṃ sandhāyevāha.
commentary_english: 73. yatokho, bhikkhave: Here, *yato* means at the time when. pahīno hotī: He speaks with reference to abandonment at the moment of the path of the *anāgāmin*.

mula_pali: 74. ‘‘So buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti; dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti; saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni, aṭṭha purisapuggalā. Esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo , anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti.
mula_english:
He possesses unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arhat, a perfectly enlightened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct (*vidyācaraṇasampanna*), a *Sugata*, a knower of the world (*lokavidū*), an unsurpassed guide for training people (*anuttaro purisa-dammasārathi*), teacher of gods and humans (*satthā devamanussānam*), the Buddha, the Blessed One.’

He possesses unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, visible here and now (*sandiṭṭhiko*), immediately effective (*akāliko*), inviting inspection (*ehipassiko*), onward leading (*opaneyyiko*), to be experienced by the wise for themselves (*paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi*).’

He possesses unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The Sangha of the Blessed One's disciples is practicing the good way (*suppaṭipanno*), practicing the straight way (*ujuppaṭipanno*), practicing the true way (*ñāyappaṭipanno*), practicing the proper way (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*); that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals—this Sangha of the Blessed One's disciples is worthy of gifts (*āhuneyyo*), worthy of hospitality (*pāhuneyyo*), worthy of offerings (*dakkhiṇeyyo*), worthy of reverential salutation (*añjalikaraṇīyo*), the unsurpassed field of merit for the world (*anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa*).’
commentary_pali:
74.So buddhe aveccappasādenāti etaṃ ‘‘yato kho, bhikkhave, abhijjhāvisamalobho pahīno hoti, so buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hotī’’ti evaṃ ekamekena padena yojetabbaṃ. Imassa hi bhikkhuno anāgāmimaggena lokuttarappasādo āgato, athassa aparena samayena buddhaguṇe dhammaguṇe saṅghaguṇe ca anussarato lokiyo uppajjati, tamassa sabbampi lokiyalokuttaramissakaṃ pasādaṃ dassento bhagavā ‘‘buddhe aveccappasādenā’’tiādimāha.

Tattha aveccappasādenāti buddhadhammasaṅghaguṇānaṃ yāthāvato ñātattā acalena accutena pasādena. Idāni yathā tassa bhikkhuno anussarato so aveccappasādo uppanno, taṃ vidhiṃ dassento ‘‘itipi so bhagavā’’tiādinā nayena tīṇi anussatiṭṭhānāni vitthāresi. Tesaṃ atthavaṇṇanā sabbākārena visuddhimagge anussatikathāyaṃ vuttā.

aveccappasādenā visuddhimagge
commentary_english:
So *buddhe aveccappasādenā* means that "when, monks, covetousness and greed are abandoned, one is endowed with unwavering faith in the Buddha," thus it should be connected with each word.

For this monk, supramundane faith has arisen through the path of non-returning. Then at a later time, as he recollects the qualities of the Buddha, the qualities of the Dharma, and the qualities of the Saṅgha, mundane faith arises for him. Showing that all of that faith of his is a mixture of mundane and supramundane, the Blessed One said, "with unwavering faith in the Buddha," and so on.

There, *aveccappasādenā* means with unwavering, unshakeable faith because of truly knowing the qualities of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.

Now, showing the manner in which that unwavering faith arose in that monk as he recollected, he elaborated on the three objects of recollection with the words "Indeed, the Blessed One," and so on.

The explanation of their meaning has been stated in every way in the *Visuddhimagga*, in the discourse on recollection.

*Aveccappasādenā* *Visuddhimagge*

mula_pali: 75. ‘‘Yathodhi yatodhi (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pāṭhantaraṃ) kho panassa cattaṃ hoti vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, so ‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī’ti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedeti, sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati; ‘dhamme…pe… saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī’ti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ; pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedeti, sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. ‘Yathodhi kho pana me cattaṃ vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭha’nti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ; pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedeti, sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati.
mula_english:
75. “When, indeed, his mind has been given up (cattaṃ), relinquished (vantaṃ), released (muttaṃ), abandoned (pahīnaṃ), and relinquished (paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ), he gains inspiration in the meaning (attha-vedaṃ), gains inspiration in the Dharma (dhamma-vedaṃ), gains gladness connected with the Dharma (dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ), thinking, ‘I am possessed of perfect confidence in the Buddha (buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī).’
When he is joyful (pamuditassa), rapture (pīti) arises (jāyati). For one with a rapturous mind (pītimanassa), the body (kāyo) becomes tranquil (passambhati). One tranquil in body (passaddhakāyo) feels pleasure (sukhaṃ vedeti). For one feeling pleasure (sukhino), the mind (cittaṃ) becomes concentrated (samādhiyati). ‘In the Dharma (dhamme)… etc… In the *saṃgha* (saṅghe) ... I am possessed of perfect confidence (aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī),' he gains inspiration in the meaning (attha-vedaṃ), gains inspiration in the Dharma (dhamma-vedaṃ), gains gladness connected with the Dharma (dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ). When he is joyful (pamuditassa), rapture (pīti) arises (jāyati). For one with a rapturous mind (pītimanassa), the body (kāyo) becomes tranquil (passambhati). One tranquil in body (passaddhakāyo) feels pleasure (sukhaṃ vedeti). For one feeling pleasure (sukhino), the mind (cittaṃ) becomes concentrated (samādhiyati).
'When, indeed, my mind (me) has been given up (cattaṃ), relinquished (vantaṃ), released (muttaṃ), abandoned (pahīnaṃ), and relinquished (paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ),' he gains inspiration in the meaning (attha-vedaṃ), gains inspiration in the Dharma (dhamma-vedaṃ), gains gladness connected with the Dharma (dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ). When he is joyful (pamuditassa), rapture (pīti) arises (jāyati). For one with a rapturous mind (pītimanassa), the body (kāyo) becomes tranquil (passambhati). One tranquil in body (passaddhakāyo) feels pleasure (sukhaṃ vedeti). For one feeling pleasure (sukhino), the mind (cittaṃ) becomes concentrated (samādhiyati).
commentary_pali:
75. Evamassa lokiyalokuttaramissakaṃ pasādaṃ dassetvā idāni kilesappahānaṃ aveccappasādasamannāgatañca paccavekkhato uppajjamānaṃ somanassādiānisaṃsaṃ dassento yathodhi kho panassātiādimāha. Anāgāmissa hi paccante vuṭṭhitaṃ corupaddavaṃ vūpasametvā taṃ paccavekkhato mahānagare vasantassa rañño viya ime cime ca mama kilesā pahīnāti attano kilesappahānaṃ paccavekkhato balavasomanassaṃ uppajjati. Taṃ dassento bhagavā ‘‘yathodhi kho panassā’’tiādimāha.

Tassattho – yvāyaṃ anāgāmī bhikkhu evaṃ ‘‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti…pe… dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’’ti, tassa yathodhi kho cattaṃ hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, sakasakaodhivasena cattameva hoti, taṃ taṃ kilesajātaṃ vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ. Sakasakaodhivasenāti dve odhī kilesodhi ca maggodhi ca. Tattha kilesodhivasenāpi ye kilesā yaṃ maggavajjhā, te aññamaggavajjhehi amissā hutvā sakeneva odhinā pahīnā. Maggodhivasenāpi ye kilesā yena maggena pahātabbā, tena teyeva pahīnā honti. Evaṃ sakasakaodhivasena taṃ taṃ kilesajātaṃ cattameva hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, taṃ paccavekkhitvā ca laddhasomanasso tatuttaripi so ‘‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī’’ti labhati atthavedanti sambandho.

Sakasakaodhivasenā

Yatodhi khotipi pāṭho. Tassa vasena ayamattho, assa bhikkhuno yatodhi kho pana cattaṃ hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ. Tattha yatoti kāraṇavacanaṃ, yasmāti vuttaṃ hoti. Odhīti heṭṭhā tayo maggā vuccanti. Kasmā? Te hi odhiṃ katvā koṭṭhāsaṃ katvā uparimaggena pahātabbakilese ṭhapetvā pajahanti, tasmā odhīti vuccanti. Arahattamaggo pana kiñci kilesaṃ anavasesetvā pajahati, tasmā anodhīti vuccati. Imassa ca bhikkhuno heṭṭhāmaggattayena cattaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘yatodhi kho panassa cattaṃ hotī’’ti. Tattha kho panāti nipātamattaṃ. Ayaṃ pana piṇḍattho. Yasmā assa odhi cattaṃ hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, tasmā taṃ paccavekkhitvā ca laddhasomanasso tatuttaripi so ‘‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī’’ti labhati atthavedanti yathāpāḷi netabbaṃ.

khoti yato Odhī odhī anodhī kho panā

Tattha cattanti idaṃ sakabhāvapariccajanavasena vuttaṃ. Vantanti idaṃ pana anādiyanabhāvadassanavasena. Muttanti idaṃ santatito vinimocanavasena. Pahīnanti idaṃ muttassapi kvaci anavaṭṭhānadassanavasena. Paṭinissaṭṭhanti idaṃ pubbe ādinnapubbassa paṭinissaggadassanavasena paṭimukhaṃ vā nissaṭṭhabhāvadassanavasena bhāvanābalena abhibhuyya nissaṭṭhabhāvadassanavasenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Labhati atthavedaṃ labhati dhammavedanti ettha buddhādīsu aveccappasādoyeva araṇīyato attho, upagantabbatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Dhāraṇato dhammo, vinipatituṃ appadānatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Vedoti ganthopi ñāṇampi somanassampi. ‘‘Tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū’’tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.256) hi gantho ‘‘vedo’’ti vuccati. ‘‘Yaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vedagumābhijaññā, akiñcanaṃ kāmabhāve asatta’’ntiādīsu (su. ni. 1065) ñāṇaṃ. ‘‘Ye vedajātā vicaranti loke’’tiādīsu somanassaṃ. Idha pana somanassañca somanassasampayuttañāṇañca adhippetaṃ, tasmā ‘‘labhati atthavedaṃ labhati dhammavedanti aveccappasādārammaṇasomanassañca somanassamayañāṇañca labhatī’’ti evamettha attho veditabbo.

catta Vanta Mutta Pahīna Paṭinissaṭṭha Labhati atthavedaṃ labhati dhammaveda attho, dhammo, Vedo

Atha vā atthavedanti aveccappasādaṃ paccavekkhato uppannaṃ vuttappakārameva vedaṃ. Dhammavedanti aveccappasādassa hetuṃ odhiso kilesappahānaṃ paccavekkhato uppannaṃ vuttappakārameva vedanti evampi ettha attho veditabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘hetumhi ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, hetuphale ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā’’ti (vibha. 718-719). Dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjanti tameva atthañca dhammañca atthadhammānisaṃsabhūtaṃ vedañca paccavekkhato uppannaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Tañhi anavajjalakkhaṇena paccavekkhaṇākārappavattena dhammena upasañhitanti vuccati. Pamuditassa pīti jāyatīti iminā pāmojjena pamuditassa nirāmisā pīti jāyati. Pītimanassāti tāya pītiyā pīṇitamanassa. Kāyo passambhatīti kāyopi passaddho hoti vūpasantadaratho. Passaddhakāyo sukhanti evaṃ vūpasantakāyadaratho cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Cittaṃ samādhiyatīti cittaṃ sammā ādhiyati appitaṃ viya acalaṃ tiṭṭhati.

atthaveda Dhammaveda Dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojja upasañhita Pamuditassa pīti jāyatī Pītimanassā Kāyo passambhatī Passaddhakāyo sukha Cittaṃ samādhiyatī
commentary_english:
75. Thus, having shown the serenity consisting of both mundane and supramundane mixed together, and now, showing the benefit of joy and so on, arising for one who reflects on the abandonment of defilements and who is endowed with serene confidence, he (the Blessed One) said, beginning with "yathodhi kho panassāti." For an Anāgāmi, just as for a king living in a great city who, after having quelled a bandit disturbance that arose in the border area, reflects on that, thinking, "These and these defilements of mine are abandoned," strong joy arises when he reflects on the abandonment of his defilements. Showing that, the Blessed One said, beginning with "yathodhi kho panassā." Its meaning is: Whatever Anāgāmi bhikkhu is thus "endowed with serene confidence in the Buddha…pe… in the Dhamma…pe… in the Saṅgha…pe… [and recognizes the Saṅgha as] the unsurpassed field of merit for the world," for him, whatever has been relinquished, abandoned, is relinquished in accordance with its own division. That particular type of defilement is vomited, released, abandoned, relinquished. "sakasakaodhivasenāti": there are two divisions: the division of defilements and the division of the path. There, even in the division of defilements, those defilements that are vulnerable to a particular path are abandoned by their own division, not mixed with those vulnerable to another path. Even in the division of the path, those defilements that should be abandoned by a particular path, are abandoned by that very path. Thus, in accordance with its own division, whatever type of defilement is relinquished, abandoned, and having reflected on that and gained joy, he further gains this: "I am endowed with serene confidence in the Buddha," this is the connection. sakasakaodhivasenā yatodhi khotipi is also a reading. According to that, this is the meaning: for that bhikkhu, whatever is relinquished, abandoned. There, yatoti is a word of reason, it is said in the sense of "because." Odhīti: the three lower paths are called "divisions." Why? Because they make a division, make a section, set aside the defilements to be abandoned by the higher path, and abandon [the rest]. Therefore, they are called odhīti. But the path of Arahatship abandons every defilement without remainder; therefore, it is called anodhīti. And for this bhikkhu, [defilements are] abandoned by the three lower paths. Therefore, it was said, "yatodhi kho panassa cattaṃ hoti." There, kho panāti is merely a particle. This, however, is the condensed meaning. Since a division is relinquished, abandoned for him, therefore, having reflected on that and gained joy, he further gains this: "I am endowed with serene confidence in the Buddha," the rest should be construed as in the Pāḷi. khoti yato odhī odhī anodhī kho panā There, cattanti is said in the sense of abandoning one's own nature. vantanti, however, [is said] in the sense of showing the state of non-attachment. muttanti is in the sense of liberation from continuity. pahīnanti is in the sense of showing that even what is released is sometimes not permanent. paṭinissaṭṭhanti is said in the sense of relinquishing what was previously taken, or in the sense of showing the state of being cast off face to face, or in the sense of showing the state of being cast off after overpowering by the power of meditation. labhati atthavedaṃ labhati dhammavedanti, here, with regard to the Buddha and so on, serene confidence itself is attho, because it is worthy of refuge, it is said in the sense of what should be approached. dhammo, because of upholding, it is said in the sense of not giving way to falling away. vedoti: is both the text, knowledge, and joy. In passages such as "gone to the beyond of the three Vedas" (dī. ni. 1.256), the text is called "vedo." In passages such as "that brahmin is known by the Vedas, without possessions, unattached to sensual pleasures" (su. ni. 1065) *Jñāna* (knowledge). "Those who are born of the Vedas wander in the world," etc., are instances of joy (*somanassa*). Here, however, both joy (*somanassa*) and knowledge associated with joy are intended; therefore, "he obtains the knowledge of meaning (*arthaveda*), he obtains the knowledge of the Dharma (*dhammaveda*)," thus, in this context, the meaning should be understood as: he obtains joy with the object of serene confidence (*aveccappasāda*) as well as knowledge consisting of joy.

Abandoned, relinquished, freed, eliminated, utterly rejected He obtains knowledge of meaning, he obtains knowledge of the Dharma; meaning, Dharma, knowledge atha Or, knowledge of meaning, meaning knowledge arisen from the inspection of serene confidence, in the manner stated above. Knowledge of the Dharma The cause of serene confidence is the inspection of the abandonment of defilements (*kilesa-ppahāna*) by way of discrimination; meaning knowledge arisen in the manner stated above, thus, in this context, the meaning should also be understood. It has been said, "Knowledge in the cause is analytical knowledge of the Dharma (*dhamma-paṭisambhidā*), knowledge in the cause and result is analytical knowledge of the meaning (*attha-paṭisambhidā*)" (Vibha. 718-719). Joy accompanied by the Dharma, meaning joy arisen from inspecting that very meaning and the Dharma, and knowledge consisting of the benefits of meaning and the Dharma. For it is called accompanied by the Dharma, which proceeds in the mode of inspecting the characteristic of faultlessness. Joy arises for the delighted one, meaning, through this joy, non-carnal joy arises for the delighted one. Having a joyful mind, meaning, one whose mind is nourished by that joy. The body is calmed, meaning the body is calmed, and the fear is pacified. Pleasant is the calmed body, meaning, thus, with the fear of the body pacified, he experiences mental pleasure. The mind is concentrated, meaning the mind is well-placed, as if fixed, it stands unmoving.

Knowledge of meaning, knowledge of the Dharma Joy accompanied by the Dharma, accompanied, joy arises for the delighted one, having a joyful mind, the body is calmed, pleasant is the calmed body, the mind is concentrated

mula_pali: 76. ‘‘Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃsīlo evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño sālīnaṃ cepi piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati vicitakāḷakaṃ anekasūpaṃ anekabyañjanaṃ, nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vatthaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ malaggahitaṃ acchodakaṃ āgamma parisuddhaṃ hoti pariyodātaṃ , ukkāmukhaṃ vā panāgamma jātarūpaṃ parisuddhaṃ hoti pariyodātaṃ, evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃsīlo evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño sālīnaṃ cepi piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjati vicitakāḷakaṃ anekasūpaṃ anekabyañjanaṃ , nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāya.
mula_english:
76. "Monks, if a *bhikṣu* of such virtue (*śīla*), such a state of concentration (*dharma*), and such wisdom (*prajñā*) eats almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*) consisting of choice hill rice (*sālīnaṃ*) along with various (*aneka*) sauces (*sūpa*) and curries (*byañjana*), even that will be no obstacle (*antarāya*) for him.

Just as a cloth that is defiled (*saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ*) and stained (*malaggahitaṃ*) becomes pure (*parisuddhaṃ*) and bright (*pariyodātaṃ*) with the help of clear water (*acchodakaṃ*) , or just as gold (*jātarūpaṃ*) becomes pure (*parisuddhaṃ*) and bright (*pariyodātaṃ*) with the help of a furnace (*ukkāmukhaṃ*), so too, if a *bhikṣu* of such virtue...eats almsfood...that will be no obstacle for him.
commentary_pali:
76. Evamassa kilesappahānaṃ aveccappasādasamannāgataṃ paccavekkhato uppajjamānaṃ somanassādiānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā idāni ‘‘yathodhi kho pana me’’ti vārena tassa paccavekkhaṇāya pavattākāraṃ pakāsetvā tasseva anāgāmimaggānubhāvasūcakaṃ phalaṃ dassento sa kho so, bhikkhavetiādimāha.

Tattha evaṃsīloti tassa anāgāmimaggasampayuttaṃ sīlakkhandhaṃ dasseti. Evaṃdhammo evaṃpaññoti taṃsampayuttameva samādhikkhandhaṃ paññākkhandhañca dasseti. Sālīnanti lohitasāligandhasāliādīnaṃ anekarūpānaṃ. Piṇḍapātanti odanaṃ. Vicitakāḷakanti apanītakāḷakaṃ. Nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāyāti tassa evaṃvidhassa bhikkhuno taṃ vuttappakārapiṇḍapātabhojanaṃ maggassa vā phalassa vā neva antarāyāya hoti, paṭiladdhaguṇassa hi taṃ kimantarāyaṃ karissati? Yopissa appaṭiladdho catutthamaggo ca phalaṃ ca tappaṭilābhāya vipassanaṃ ārabhatopi nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāya, antarāyaṃ kātuṃ asamatthameva hoti. Kasmā? Vuttappakārasīladhammapaññāsaṅgahena maggena visuddhacittattā.

evaṃsīlo Evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño Sālīna Piṇḍapāta Vicitakāḷaka Nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāyā

Yasmā cettha etadeva kāraṇaṃ, tasmā tadanurūpaṃ upamaṃ dassento seyyathāpītiādimāha.

seyyathāpī

Tattha acchanti vippasannaṃ. Parisuddhaṃ malavigamena. Pariyodātaṃ pabhassaratāya. Ukkāmukhanti suvaṇṇakārānaṃ mūsāmukhaṃ. Suvaṇṇakārānaṃ mūsā hi idha ukkā, aññattha pana dīpikādayopi vuccanti. ‘‘Ukkāsu dhārīyamānāsū’’ti (dī. ni. 1.159) hi āgataṭṭhāne dīpikā ‘‘ukkā’’ti vuccati. ‘‘Ukkaṃ bandheyya, ukkaṃ bandhitvā ukkāmukhaṃ ālimpeyyā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.360) āgataṭṭhāne aṅgārakapallaṃ. ‘‘Kammārānaṃ yathā ukkā, anto jhāyati no bahī’’ti (jā. 2.22.649) āgataṭṭhāne kammāruddhanaṃ. ‘‘Evaṃvipāko ukkāpāto bhavissatī’’ti (dī. ni. 1.24) āgataṭṭhāne vātavego ‘‘ukkā’’ti vuccati. Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne aññesu ca evarūpesu ‘‘saṇḍāsena jātarūpaṃ gahetvā ukkāmukhe pakkhipatī’’ti āgataṭṭhānesu suvaṇṇakārānaṃ mūsā ‘‘ukkā’’ti veditabbā.

accha Parisuddhaṃ Pariyodātaṃ Ukkāmukha ukkā,

Tatrāyaṃ upamāsaṃsandanā – saṃkiliṭṭhavatthaṃ viya hi saṃkiliṭṭhajātarūpaṃ viya ca imassa bhikkhuno puthujjanakāle kāmarāgādimalānugataṃ cittaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Acchodakaṃ viya ukkāmukhaṃ viya ca anāgāmimaggo. Taṃ udakaṃ ukkāmukhañca āgamma vatthasuvaṇṇānaṃ parisuddhatā viya tassa bhikkhuno vuttappakārasīladhammapaññāsaṅgahaṃ anāgāmimaggaṃ āgamma visuddhacittatāti.
commentary_english:
76. Thus, after showing the benefits of joy and so forth that arise for one who frequently reflects, endowed with unwavering faith in the abandonment of defilements, now, by way of "Just as indeed for me," having revealed the manner in which that reflection proceeds, [and] while showing the fruit that indicates the power of the path of the non-returner, [he] says, "Sa kho so, bhikkhave" and so forth.

There, *evaṃsīlo* means he shows the aggregate of moral discipline connected with the path of the non-returner. *evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño* means he shows the aggregate of concentration and the aggregate of wisdom that are connected with that. *sālīna*nti [means] of various kinds, such as red rice, fragrant rice, and so forth. *piṇḍapāta*nti [means] boiled rice. *vicitakāḷaka*nti [means] that from which the husks have been removed. *nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāyā*ti [means] that meal of alms food of the kind described does not become an obstacle to the path or the fruit for that bhikkhu of such a kind; for what obstacle will that make for one who has obtained qualities? Even if he, without having obtained the fourth path and fruit, should undertake insight meditation for the sake of obtaining that, that does not become an obstacle for him; it is simply incapable of creating an obstacle. Why? Because of purified mind due to the path that consists of the collection of moral discipline, dhamma, and wisdom of the kind described.

*evaṃsīlo evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño sālīna piṇḍapāta vicitakāḷaka nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāyā* Because here this alone is the cause, therefore, while showing a simile in accordance with that, he says, *seyyathāpī* and so forth.

*seyyathāpī* There, *accha*nti [means] clear. *parisuddhaṃ* [means] by the removal of dirt. *pariyodātaṃ* [means] because of luminosity. *ukkāmukha*nti [means] the mouth of the crucible of goldsmiths. For here, the crucible of goldsmiths is called *ukkā,* but elsewhere it is also called a lamp and so forth. In the passage, "While torches are being carried," (D. N. 1.159) the lamp is called "torches" in the place where it has come. "He should bind the torch, and having bound the torch, he should smear the mouth of the torch," (M. N. 3.360) in the place where it has come, [it means] a heap of coals. "Just as the torch of smiths glows inside but not outside," (Jā. 2.22.649) in the place where it has come, [it means] the bellows of smiths. "The result of that will be a fall of torches," (D. N. 1.24) in the place where it has come, [it means] a gust of wind is called "torches".

But in this place, and in other instances of this sort, in the passages where it has come, "Having taken the gold with tongs, he throws it into the mouth of the torch," the crucible of goldsmiths should be understood to be "the torch."

*accha parisuddhaṃ pariyodātaṃ ukkāmukha ukkā,* There, this is the connection of the simile: The mind of this bhikkhu in the time of an ordinary person, accompanied by defilements such as sensual desire, should be seen as like a soiled cloth and like soiled gold. The path of the non-returner is like clear water and like the mouth of a torch. That water and the mouth of the torch
Like the purity of gold in cloth, so too, the purity of mind of that *bhikṣu* (monk) comes about through the collection of the virtues (śīla), *dharma*, and wisdom (prajñā) mentioned, having attained the path of the *anāgāmin* (non-returner), thus it is said, is of purified mind.

mula_pali: 77. ‘‘So mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ catutthiṃ (sī. pī.). Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati; karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
mula_english:
“He abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (*maitrī-sahagatena cetasā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth.

Thus above, below, across, everywhere, in its entirety, he dwells pervading the entire world with his heart endued with loving- kindness (*maitrī-sahagatena cetasā*), abundant, exalted, measureless, free from enmity, and free from affliction. He abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion (*karuṇā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with a mind imbued with appreciative joy (*muditā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekṣā-sahagatena cetasā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth.

Thus above, below, across, everywhere, in its entirety, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekṣā-sahagatena cetasā*), abundant, exalted, measureless, free from enmity, and free from affliction.
commentary_pali: 77.So mettāsahagatena cetasāti yathānusandhivasena desanā āgatā. Tayo hi anusandhī pucchānusandhi ajjhāsayānusandhi yathānusandhīti. Tattha ‘‘evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca ‘siyā nu kho, bhante, bahiddhā asati paritassanā’ti? ‘Siyā bhikkhū’ti bhagavā avocā’’ti (ma. ni. 1.242). Evaṃ pucchantānaṃ vissajjitasuttavasena pucchānusandhi veditabbo. ‘‘Siyā kho pana te brāhmaṇa evamassa, ajjāpi nūna samaṇo gotamo avītarāgo’’ti (ma. ni. 1.55) evaṃ paresaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā vuttassa suttassa vasena ajjhāsayānusandhi veditabbo. Yena pana dhammena ādimhi desanā uṭṭhitā, tassa dhammassa anurūpadhammavasena vā paṭipakkhavasena vā yesu suttesu upari desanā āgacchati, tesaṃ vasena yathānusandhi veditabbo . Seyyathidaṃ, ākaṅkheyyasutte heṭṭhā sīlena desanā uṭṭhitā, upari cha abhiññā āgatā. Kakacūpame heṭṭhā akkhantiyā uṭṭhitā, upari kakacūpamovādo āgato. Alagadde heṭṭhā diṭṭhiparidīpanena uṭṭhitā, upari tiparivaṭṭasuññatāpakāsanā āgatā, cūḷaassapure heṭṭhā kilesaparidīpanena uṭṭhitā, upari brahmavihārā āgatā. Kosambiyasutte heṭṭhā bhaṇḍanena uṭṭhitā, upari sāraṇīyadhammā āgatā. Imasmimpi vatthasutte heṭṭhā kilesaparidīpanena uṭṭhitā, upari brahmavihārā āgatā. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘yathānusandhivasena desanā āgatā’’ti. Brahmavihāresu pana anupadavaṇṇanā ca bhāvanānayo ca sabbo sabbākārena visuddhimagge vutto.
commentary_english:
77. "So *mettāsahagatena cetasā*" means that the teaching has come down by way of a natural sequence of meaning.

For suttas have three kinds of sequence of meaning: a sequence of meaning based on a question; a sequence of meaning dictated by inclination; and a sequence of meaning dictated by the natural structure of the teaching.

Herein, the *pucchānusandhi* should be understood as in the case of suttas answering questions, such as "When this was said, a certain monk said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, could there be anguish apart from what is external?’ ‘There could be, monk,’ the Blessed One said" (Majjhima Nikāya 1.242).

The *ajjhāsayānusandhi* should be understood as in the case of suttas spoken after understanding the inclination of others, such as "'Now, brahmin, it might be that you think: "Perhaps the recluse Gotama is not free from lust..."'" (Majjhima Nikāya 1.55).

The *yathānusandhi* should be understood in the case of suttas in which the teaching arises at the beginning due to a certain principle, and in which the subsequent teaching comes in accordance with that principle, or by way of its opposite. For example, in the Ākaṅkheyya Sutta, the teaching is set up at the beginning by way of virtue (*śīla*) and culminates in the six kinds of direct knowledge (*abhiññā*). In the Simile of the Saw (*kakacūpama*), the teaching is set up by way of impatience (*akkhanti*) and culminates in the simile of the saw. In the Alagadda Sutta, the teaching is set up by way of the exposition of views (*diṭṭhiparidīpana*) and culminates in the declaration of emptiness in three cycles (*tiparivaṭṭasuññatāpakāsanā*). In the Cūḷaassapura Sutta, the teaching is set up at the beginning by way of the exposition of defilements (*kilesaparidīpana*) and culminates in the divine abodes (*brahmavihārā*). In the Kosambiya Sutta, the teaching is set up by way of schism (*bhaṇḍana*) and culminates in the principles of fraternal harmony (*sāraṇīyadhammā*). In this Vattha Sutta too, the teaching is set up at the beginning by way of the exposition of defilements (*kilesaparidīpana*) and culminates in the divine abodes (*brahmavihārā*).

Thus it is said: “This teaching has come down by way of a sequence of meaning dictated by the natural structure of the teaching.”

Moreover, in the Visuddhimagga, a full description of the absence of danger and the method of meditation in the divine abodes is given in every way.

mula_pali: 78. ‘‘So ‘atthi idaṃ, atthi hīnaṃ, atthi paṇītaṃ, atthi imassa saññāgatassa uttariṃ nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti . Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave – ‘bhikkhu sināto antarena sinānenā’’’ti.
mula_english:
“He understands thus: ‘There is this (*idaṃ*), there is the inferior (*hīnaṃ*), there is the superior (*paṇītaṃ*), and beyond there is an escape (*nissaraṇaṃ*) from this whole field of perception (*saññāgatassa*).’

When he knows and sees thus, his mind (*cittaṃ*) is liberated (*vimuccati*) from the taint (*āsava*) of sensual desire (*kāmā*), from the taint (*āsava*) of existence (*bhava*), and from the taint (*āsava*) of ignorance (*avijjā*).

When it is liberated (*vimuttasmiṃ*), there comes the knowledge (*ñāṇaṃ*): ‘It’s liberated (*vimuttamiti*)’

He understands: ‘Birth (*jāti*) is destroyed (*khīṇā*), the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) has been lived (*vusitaṃ*), what had to be done (*karaṇīyaṃ*) has been done (*kataṃ*), there is no more coming (*na aparaṃ*) to any state of being (*itthattāya*)’

Bhikkhus, this bhikkhu is called one bathed (*sināto*) with the inner (*antarena*) bathing (*sinānena*).”
commentary_pali:
78. Evaṃ bhagavā abhijjhādīnaṃ upakkilesānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtaṃ sabbaso ca kāmarāgabyāpādappahānena vihatapaccatthikattā laddhapadaṭṭhānaṃ tassa anāgāmino brahmavihārabhāvanaṃ dassetvā idānissa arahattāya vipassanaṃ dassetvā arahattappattiṃ dassetuṃ so atthi idantiādimāha.

Tassattho – so anāgāmī evaṃ bhāvitabrahmavihāro etesaṃ brahmavihārānaṃ yato kutoci vuṭṭhāya te eva brahmavihāradhamme nāmavasena tesaṃ nissayaṃ hadayavatthuṃ vatthunissayāni bhūtānīti iminā nayena bhūtupādāyadhamme rūpavasena ca vavatthapetvā atthi idanti pajānāti, ettāvatānena dukkhasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tato tassa dukkhassa samudayaṃ paṭivijjhanto atthi hīnanti pajānāti, ettāvatānena samudayasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tato tassa pahānupāyaṃ vicinanto atthi paṇītanti pajānāti, ettāvatānena maggasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tato tena maggena adhigantabbaṭṭhānaṃ vicinanto atthi uttari imassa saññāgatassa nissaraṇanti pajānāti, imassa mayā adhigatassa brahmavihārasaññāgatassa uttari nissaraṇaṃ nibbānaṃ atthīti evaṃ pajānātīti adhippāyo, ettāvatānena nirodhasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passatoti tassa vipassanāpaññāya evaṃ catūhi ākārehi cattāri saccāni jānato, maggapaññāya evaṃ passato, bhayabherave vuttanayeneva kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati…pe… itthattāyāti pajānātīti.

atthi ida atthi hīna atthi paṇīta atthi uttari imassa saññāgatassa nissaraṇa Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato

Evaṃ yāva arahattā desanaṃ pāpetvā idāni yasmā tassaṃ parisati nhānasuddhiko brāhmaṇo nisinno, so evaṃ nhānasuddhiyā vaṇṇaṃ vuccamānaṃ sutvā pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissatīti bhagavatā vidito, tasmā tassa codanatthāya ‘‘ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sināto antarena sinānenā’’ti imaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ anusandhimāha. Tattha antarena sinānenāti abbhantarena kilesavuṭṭhānasinānena.

antarena sinānenā
commentary_english:
Thus, the Blessed One, having shown the cultivation of the *brahmavihāra* dwelling, which is the opponent of the defilements beginning with covetousness (*abhijjhā*), which has gained a foothold by means of the complete abandonment of craving for sensual pleasures (*kāmarāga*) and ill-will (*byāpāda*), whose adversaries are destroyed, and now, in order to show the insight (*vipassanā*) for Arhatship and to show the attainment of Arhatship, [the Bhagavān] declares "so *atthi ida*," etc.

The meaning of that is: that non-returner (*anāgāmī*), having thus cultivated the *brahmavihāra* dwelling, having arisen from whichever of these *brahmavihāras* it may be, distinguishes by way of name those very *brahmavihāra* qualities (*brahmavihāradhamme*) – relying on them, the heart-basis (*hadayavatthu*), the material phenomena which are the support of the basis – in this way, and also having discriminated the material phenomena (*bhūtupādāyadhamme*) by way of form (*rūpavasena*), knows "*atthi ida*," and by just that much, the establishment of the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) has been done.

Then, penetrating the origin (*samudaya*) of that suffering (*dukkha*), [he] knows "*atthi hīna*," and by just that much, the establishment of the truth of the origin (*samudayasacca*) has been done.

Then, investigating the means of abandoning that, [he] knows "*atthi paṇīta*," and by just that much, the establishment of the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) has been done.

Then, investigating the state to be attained by that path, [he] knows "*atthi uttari imassa saññāgatassa nissaraṇa*," the intention is that he knows thus: "There is a further escape (*nissaraṇa*) from this *brahmavihāra* dwelling-aggregate (*saññāgatassa*) I have attained, namely, *nirvāṇa*," and by just that much, the establishment of the truth of cessation (*nirodhasacca*) has been done.

"*tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato*," by thus knowing and thus seeing, to that [person's] wisdom of insight (*vipassanāpaññā*), thus, by the four aspects (*ākārehi*), knowing the four truths (*saccāni*), and by thus seeing with the wisdom of the path (*maggapaññāya*), even craving for sensual pleasures (*kāmāsavāpi*) releases the mind from fear and dread (*bhayabherave*)…pe… [he] knows "for the sake of such-and-suchness (*itthattāyāti*)."

"*atthi ida* *atthi hīna* *atthi paṇīta* *atthi uttari imassa saññāgatassa nissaraṇa* *tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato*"

Thus, having brought the teaching up to Arhatship, now, because in that assembly a *brāhmaṇa* purified by bathing (*nhānasuddhiko*) is seated, and he, having heard the praise of purity by bathing (*nhānasuddhiyā vaṇṇaṃ vuccamānaṃ*) thus being spoken, having gone forth (*pabbajitvā*) will attain Arhatship—this was known by the Blessed One, therefore, for the sake of urging him on (*codanatthāya*), [he] says, "This is called, monks, a monk who has bathed (*sināto*) with inner bathing (*antarena sinānenā*)," this he said, referring to a distinct connection (*pāṭiyekkaṃ anusandhimāha*).

There, "*antarena sinānenā*," by inner bathing (*abbhantarena sinānenā*) with the washing away of the defilements (*kilesavuṭṭhāna*).

"*antarena sinānenā*"

mula_pali:
79. Tena kho pana samayena sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti. Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘gacchati pana bhavaṃ gotamo bāhukaṃ nadiṃ sināyitu’’nti? ‘‘Kiṃ, brāhmaṇa, bāhukāya nadiyā? Kiṃ bāhukā nadī karissatī’’ti? ‘‘Lokkhasammatā lokhyasammatā (sī.), mokkhasammatā (pī.) hi, bho gotama, bāhukā nadī bahujanassa, puññasammatā hi, bho gotama, bāhukā nadī bahujanassa, bāhukāya pana nadiyā bahujano pāpakammaṃ kataṃ pavāhetī’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā sundarikabhāradvājaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Bāhukaṃ adhikakkañca, gayaṃ sundarikaṃ mapi sundarikāmapi (sī. syā. pī.), sundarikaṃ mahiṃ (itipi);

sundarikāmapi (sī. syā. pī.), sundarikaṃ mahiṃ (itipi)

Sarassatiṃ payāgañca, atho bāhumatiṃ nadiṃ;

Niccampi bālo pakkhando pakkhanno (sī. syā. pī.), kaṇhakammo na sujjhati.

pakkhanno (sī. syā. pī.)

‘‘Kiṃ sundarikā karissati, kiṃ payāgā payāgo (sī. syā. pī.) kiṃ bāhukā nadī;

payāgo (sī. syā. pī.)

Veriṃ katakibbisaṃ naraṃ, na hi naṃ sodhaye pāpakamminaṃ.

‘‘Suddhassa ve sadā phaggu, suddhassuposatho sadā;

Suddhassa sucikammassa, sadā sampajjate vataṃ;

Idheva sināhi brāhmaṇa, sabbabhūtesu karohi khemataṃ.

‘‘Sace musā na bhaṇasi, sace pāṇaṃ na hiṃsasi;

Sace adinnaṃ nādiyasi, saddahāno amaccharī;

Kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā, udapānopi te gayā’’ti.
mula_english:
Now on that occasion the brahmin Sundarika Bharadvaja was sitting not far from the Blessed One.

Then Sundarika Bharadvaja said to the Blessed One, "Master Gotama, do you go to the Bahuka River to bathe?". "What, brahmin, is the Bahuka River? What can the Bahuka River do?". "Master Gotama, the Bahuka River is considered by many to give liberation (*lokkhasammatā*), the Bahuka River is considered by many to give merit (*puññasammatā*), and in the Bahuka River many wash away the evil deed that has been done".

Then the Blessed One addressed Sundarika Bharadvaja with these verses:

"The Bahuka, Adhikakka, Gaya, and also the Sundarika, the Sarasvati, Payaga, and also the Bahumati River—

Even if one is always wicked, with deeds that are dark, one is not purified.

What will the Sundarika do? What Payaga? What the Bahuka River?

They cannot purify an evil-doer, a man who has done cruel and brutal deeds.

One pure in heart (*śuddha*) has evermore the Feast of Spring (*phaggu*), the Holy Day (*uposatha*);

For one who is pure, whose deeds are immaculate, always is his observance fulfilled.

Bathe right here, brahmin, show goodwill to all beings.

If you do not speak falsely, if you do not kill living beings,

if you do not take what is not given, trusting, un-avaricious,

what will you do by going to Gaya? Your well is Gaya."
commentary_pali:
79.Sundarikabhāradvājoti bhāradvājo nāma so brāhmaṇo attano gottavasena, sundarikāya pana nadiyā sinātassa pāpappahānaṃ hotīti ayamassa diṭṭhi, tasmā ‘‘sundarikabhāradvājo’’ti vuccati. So taṃ bhagavato vacanaṃ sutvā cintesi ‘‘mayaṃ sinānasuddhiṃ vaṇṇema, samaṇopi gotamo tatheva vaṇṇeti, samānacchando dāni esa amhehī’’ti. Atha bhagavantaṃ bāhukaṃ nadiṃ gantvā taṃ tattha pāpaṃ pavāhetvā āgataṃ viya maññamāno āha ‘‘gacchati pana bhavaṃ gotamo bāhukaṃ nadiṃ sināyitu’’nti? Bhagavā tassa gacchāmīti vā na gacchāmīti vā avatvāyeva brāhmaṇassa diṭṭhisamugghātaṃ kattukāmo ‘‘kiṃ brāhmaṇa bāhukāya nadiyā , kiṃ bāhukā nadī karissatī’’ti āha. Tassattho kiṃ payojanaṃ bāhukāya, kiṃ sā karissati? Asamatthā sā kassaci atthāya, kiṃ tattha gamissāmīti?

Atha brāhmaṇo taṃ pasaṃsanto lokkhasammatātiādimāha. Tattha lokkhasammatāti lūkhabhāvasammatā, lūkhabhāvanti cokkhabhāvaṃ, visuddhibhāvaṃ detīti evaṃ sammatāti vuttaṃ hoti. Lokyasammatātipi pāṭho. Tassattho, seṭṭhaṃ lokaṃ gamayatīti evaṃ sammatāti. Puññasammatāti puññanti sammatā. Pavāhetīti gamayati visodheti. Gāthāhi ajjhabhāsīti gāthāhi abhāsi. Gāthā ca vuccamānā tadatthadīpanatthameva vā gāthārucikānaṃ vuccati, visesatthadīpanatthaṃ vā. Idha panetā ubhayatthadīpanatthaṃ vuttāti veditabbā.

lokkhasammatā lokkhasammatā lūkhabhāva Lokyasammatā Puññasammatā Pavāhetī Gāthāhi ajjhabhāsī

Bāhukanti idameva hi ettha vacanaṃ tadatthadīpakaṃ, sesāni visesatthadīpakāni. Yatheva hi bāhukaṃ, evaṃ adhikakkādīnipi loko gacchati nhānena pāpaṃ pavāhetuṃ. Tattha ye tesaṃ ṭhānānaṃ āsannā honti, te divasassa tikkhattuṃ nhāyanti. Ye dūrā, te yathākkamaṃ dvikkhattuṃ sakiṃ ekadivasantaraṃ, evaṃ yāva saṃvaccharantaraṃ nhāyanti. Ye pana sabbathāpi gantuṃ na sakkonti, te ghaṭehipi tato udakaṃ āharāpetvā nhāyanti. Sabbañcetaṃ niratthakaṃ, tasmā imaṃ visesatthaṃ dīpetuṃ adhikakkādīnipīti āha.

Bāhuka adhikakkādīnipī

Tattha adhikakkanti nhānasambhāravasena laddhavohāraṃ ekaṃ titthaṃ vuccati. Gayātipi maṇḍalavāpisaṇṭhānaṃ titthameva vuccati. Payāgāti etampi gaṅgāya ekaṃ titthameva mahāpanādassa rañño gaṅgāyaṃ nimuggapāsādassa sopānasammukhaṭṭhānaṃ, bāhukā sundarikā sarassatī bāhumatīti imā pana catasso nadiyo. Bāloti duppañño. Pakkhandoti pavisanto. Na sujjhatīti kilesasuddhiṃ na pāpuṇāti, kevalaṃ rajojallameva pavāheti.

adhikakka Gayā Payāgā Bālo Pakkhando Na sujjhatī

Kiṃ sundarikā karissatīti sundarikā kilesavisodhane kiṃ karissati? Na kiñci kātuṃ samatthāti adhippāyo. Esa nayo payāgabāhukāsu. Imehi ca tīhi padehi vuttehi itarānipi cattāri lakkhaṇāhāranayena vuttāneva honti, tasmā yatheva sundarikā payāgā bāhukā na kiñci karonti, tathā adhikakkādayopīti veditabbā.

Kiṃ sundarikā karissatī payāgabāhukā

Verinti pāṇātipātādipañcaverasamannāgataṃ. Katakibbisanti kataluddakammaṃ. Na hi naṃ sodhayeti sundarikā vā payāgā vā bāhukā vā na sodhaye, na sodhetīti vuttaṃ hoti. Pāpakamminanti pāpakehi verakibbisakammehi yuttaṃ, lāmakakamme yuttaṃ vā verakibbisabhāvaṃ appattehi khuddakehipi pāpehi yuttanti vuttaṃ hoti.

Veri Katakibbisa Na hi naṃ sodhaye Pāpakammina

Suddhassāti nikkilesassa. Sadā phaggūti niccampi phaggunīnakkhattameva. Phaggunamāse kira ‘‘uttaraphaggunadivase yo nhāyati, so saṃvaccharaṃ katapāpaṃ sodhetī’’ti evaṃ diṭṭhiko so brāhmaṇo, tenassa bhagavā taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭihananto āha ‘‘suddhassa ve sadā phaggū’’ti. Nikkilesassa niccaṃ phaggunīnakkhattaṃ, itaro kiṃ sujjhatīti? Uposatho sadāti suddhassa ca cātuddasapannarasādīsu uposathaṅgāni asamādiyatopi niccameva uposatho. Suddhassa sucikammassāti nikkilesatāya suddhassa sucīhi ca kāyakammādīhi samannāgatassa. Sadā sampajjate vatanti īdisassa ca kusalūpasañhitaṃ vatasamādānampi niccaṃ sampannameva hotīti. Idheva sināhīti imasmiṃyeva mama sāsane sināhi. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? ‘‘Sace ajjhattikakilesamalappavāhanaṃ icchasi, idheva mama sāsane aṭṭhaṅgikamaggasalilena sināhi, aññatra hi idaṃ natthī’’ti.

Suddhassā Sadā phaggū Uposatho sadā Suddhassa sucikammassā Sadā sampajjate vata Idheva sināhī

Idānissa sappāyadesanāvasena tīsupi dvāresu suddhiṃ dassento sabbabhūtesu karohi khematantiādimāha. Tattha khematanti abhayaṃ hitabhāvaṃ, mettanti vuttaṃ hoti. Etenassa manodvārasuddhi dassitā hoti.

sabbabhūtesu karohi khemata khemata

Sace musā na bhaṇasīti etenassa vacīdvārasuddhi. Sace pāṇaṃ na hiṃsasi sace adinnaṃ nādiyasīti etehi kāyadvārasuddhi. Saddahāno amaccharīti etehi pana naṃ evaṃ parisuddhadvāraṃ saddhāsampadāya cāgasampadāya ca niyojesi. Kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā, udapānopi te gayāti ayaṃ pana upaḍḍhagāthā, sace sabbabhūtesu khemataṃ karissasi, musā na bhaṇissasi, pāṇaṃ na hanissasi, adinnaṃ nādiyissasi, saddhahāno amaccharī bhavissasi, kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā udapānopi te gayā , gayāyapi hi te nhāyantassa udapānepi imāya eva paṭipattiyā kilesasuddhi, sarīramalasuddhi pana ubhayattha samāti evaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Yasmā ca loke gayā sammatatarā, tasmā tassa bhagavā ‘‘gacchati pana bhavaṃ gotamo bāhuka’’nti puṭṭhopi ‘‘kiṃ kāhasi bāhukaṃ gantvā’’ti avatvā ‘‘kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā’’ti āhāti veditabbo.

Sace musā na bhaṇasī Sace pāṇaṃ na hiṃsasi sace adinnaṃ nādiyasī Saddahāno amaccharī Kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā, udapānopi te gayā
commentary_english:
79. *Sundarikabhāradvājo*: *Bhāradvājo* was the name of that Brahmin, due to his lineage (*gottavasena*). The view of he who bathes in the Sundarika river is that it results in the abandonment of evil (*pāpappahānaṃ hoti*), therefore he is called "Sundarikabhāradvājo." Having heard that statement of the Blessed One, he thought, "We describe the purity of bathing (*sinānasuddhiṃ vaṇṇema*), the renunciate Gotama describes it similarly. Now, this one shares the same inclination as us." Then, having gone to the Bāhuka river, thinking he was going to wash away evil, he said, "Does the esteemed Gotama go to the Bāhuka river to bathe?" The Blessed One, not saying "I go" or "I do not go," but wishing to uproot the Brahmin's view, said, "What can the Bāhuka river do, Brahmin? 0182 What can the Bāhuka river do?" Its meaning: what is the use of the Bāhuka? What will it do? It is incapable of any benefit. Why would I go there? Then, the Brahmin, praising him, spoke, beginning with "*lokkhasammatā*." There, *lokkhasammatā* means esteemed as rough in nature (*lūkhabhāvasammatā*). *lūkhabhāva* means it gives a state of purity, a state of purification (*visuddhibhāvaṃ detīti*). Thus it is said to be esteemed (*sammatāti vuttaṃ hoti*). *lokyasammatā* is also a reading. Its meaning: it leads to the best world (*seṭṭhaṃ lokaṃ gamayatīti*), thus it is esteemed (*evaṃ sammatāti*). *puññasammatā* means esteemed as merit (*puññanti sammatā*). *pavāhetī* means it causes to go, it purifies (*gamayati visodheti*). *gāthāhi ajjhabhāsī* means he spoke with verses (*gāthāhi abhāsi*). The verse being spoken is said to be for the purpose of illuminating its meaning (*tadatthadīpanatthameva vā*), or for those who delight in verses (*gāthārucikānaṃ vuccati*), or for the purpose of illuminating a specific meaning (*visesatthadīpanatthaṃ vā*). Here, however, it should be understood that it is spoken for the purpose of illuminating both meanings (*ubhayatthadīpanatthaṃ vuttāti*). 0178 *lokkhasammatā lokkhasammatā lūkhabhāva lokyasammatā puññasammatā pavāhetī gāthāhi ajjhabhāsī* 0178 *bāhuka* means this very statement here is an illuminator of its meaning (*tadatthadīpakaṃ*), the remaining ones are illuminators of specific meanings (*visesatthadīpakāni*). Just as with the Bāhuka, likewise, people go to the Adhikakkā etc. to wash away evil with bathing (*nhānena pāpaṃ pavāhetuṃ*). There, those who are near those places bathe three times a day (*divasassa tikkhattuṃ nhāyanti*). Those who are far, in due order, bathe twice, once, every other day (*ekadivasantaraṃ*), thus even once a year (*yāva saṃvaccharantaraṃ nhāyanti*). But those who are altogether unable to go, having had water brought from there in pots, they bathe (*ghaṭehipi tato udakaṃ āharāpetvā nhāyanti*). All of this is pointless (*niratthakaṃ*), therefore, to illuminate this specific meaning, he said *adhikakkādīnipī*. *bāhuka adhikakkādīnipī* 0187 *adhikakka* means a bathing place (*titthaṃ*) that has gained common usage (*laddhavohāraṃ*) by means of the requisites for bathing (*nhānasambhāravasena*) is called *ekaṃ*. *gayā* also refers to a bathing place, its arrangement being circular ponds (*maṇḍalavāpisaṇṭhānaṃ titthameva vuccati*). *payāgā* also refers to a bathing place on the Ganges, a place facing the stairs of the submerged palace of King Mahāpanāda (*mahāpanādassa rañño gaṅgāyaṃ nimuggapāsādassa sopānasammukhaṭṭhānaṃ*). Bāhukā, Sundarikā, Sarassatī, and Bāhumatī are four rivers. *bālo* means lacking wisdom (*duppañño*). *pakkhando* means entering (*pavisanto*). *na sujjhatī* means one does not attain purity from defilements (*kilesasuddhiṃ na pāpuṇāti*), one only washes away dirt and grime (*kevalaṃ rajojallameva pavāheti*). 0187 *adhikakka gayā payāga bālo pakkhando na sujjhatī* *kiṃ sundarikā karissatī* means what will the Sundarika do in purifying defilements (*kilesavisodhane kiṃ karissati*)? The meaning is that it is incapable of doing anything (*na kiñci kātuṃ samatthāti adhippāyo*). This is the method regarding *payāgabāhukā*. And with these three terms having been spoken, the other four are also spoken in the manner of essential characteristics, therefore, just as the Sundarika, Payāga, 0183 Bāhukā do nothing, so too, it should be understood, do the Adhikakkā etc. (*adhikakkādayopīti veditabbā*). *kiṃ sundarikā karissatī payāgabāhukā* 0183 *veri* means associated with the five kinds of enmity, beginning with killing living beings (*pāṇātipātādipañcaverasamannāgataṃ*). *katakibbisa* means having done cruel deeds (*kataluddakammaṃ*). *na hi naṃ sodhaye* means the Sundarika or the Payāga or the Bāhuka does not purify, it is said, it does not purify (*na sodhetīti vuttaṃ hoti*). *pāpakammina* means associated with evil deeds of enmity and cruelty (*pāpakehi verakibbisakammehi yuttaṃ*), or associated with low deeds (*lāmakakamme yuttaṃ vā*), it is said, associated with minor evils even when not having attained the state of enmity and cruelty (*verakibbisabhāvaṃ appattehi khuddakehipi pāpehi yuttanti vuttaṃ hoti*). *veri katakibbisa na hi naṃ sodhaye pāpakammina* *suddhassā* 0179"/> *nikkilesassa.* **sadā phaggū**ti niccampi phaggunīnakkhattameva. phaggunamāse kira ‘‘uttaraphaggunadivase yo nhāyati, so saṃvaccharaṃ katapāpaṃ sodhetī’’ti evaṃ diṭṭhiko so brāhmaṇo, tenassa bhagavā taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭihananto āha ‘‘suddhassa ve sadā phaggū’’ti. nikkilesassa niccaṃ phaggunīnakkhattaṃ, itaro kiṃ sujjhatīti? **uposatho sadā**ti suddhassa ca cātuddasapannarasādīsu uposathaṅgāni asamādiyatopi niccameva uposatho. **suddhassa sucikammassā**ti nikkilesatāya suddhassa sucīhi ca kāyakammādīhi samannāgatassa. **sadā sampajjate vata**nti īdisassa ca kusalūpasañhitaṃ vatasamādānampi niccaṃ sampannameva hotīti. **idheva sināhī**ti imasmiṃyeva mama sāsane sināhi. kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? ‘‘sace ajjhattikakilesamalappavāhanaṃ icchasi, idheva mama sāsane aṭṭhaṅgikamaggasalilena sināhi, aññatra hi idaṃ natthī’’ti.

**suddhassā** **sadā phaggū** **uposatho sadā** **suddhassa sucikammassā** **sadā sampajjate vata** **idheva sināhī** idānissa sappāyadesanāvasena tīsupi dvāresu suddhiṃ dassento **sabbabhūtesu karohi khemata**ntiādimāha. tattha **khemata**nti abhayaṃ hitabhāvaṃ, mettanti vuttaṃ hoti. etenassa manodvārasuddhi dassitā hoti.

**sabbabhūtesu karohi khemata** **khemata** **sace musā na bhaṇasī**ti etenassa vacīdvārasuddhi. **sace pāṇaṃ na hiṃsasi sace adinnaṃ nādiyasī**ti etehi kāyadvārasuddhi. **saddahāno amaccharī**ti etehi pana naṃ evaṃ parisuddhadvāraṃ saddhāsampadāya cāgasampadāya ca niyojesi. **kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā, udapānopi te gayā**ti ayaṃ pana upaḍḍhagāthā, sace sabbabhūtesu khemataṃ karissasi, musā na bhaṇissasi, pāṇaṃ na hanissasi, adinnaṃ nādiyissasi, saddhahāno amaccharī bhavissasi, kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā udapānopi te gayā , gayāyapi hi te nhāyantassa udapānepi imāya eva paṭipattiyā kilesasuddhi, sarīramalasuddhi pana ubhayattha samāti evaṃ yojetabbaṃ. yasmā ca loke gayā sammatatarā, tasmā tassa bhagavā ‘‘gacchati pana bhavaṃ gotamo bāhuka’’nti puṭṭhopi ‘‘kiṃ kāhasi bāhukaṃ gantvā’’ti avatvā ‘‘kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā’’ti āhāti veditabbo.
