mula_pali:
80. Evaṃ vutte, sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada’’nti. Alattha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā bhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭhevadhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosīti.

Vatthasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
80. When this was said, the Brahmin Sundarika Bharadvaja said this to the Blessed One: "Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! Master Gotama has made the Dhamma (Law) clear in many ways, as though he were turning upright what had been overthrown, revealing what was hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, or holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyesight to see forms. I go to Master Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, and to the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* (community of monks). May I receive the going forth (*pravrajya*) in the presence of venerable Gotama, may I obtain the full admission (*upasampadā*)".

And the Brahmin Sundarika Bharadvaja received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, and he received the full admission.

Then the venerable Bharadvaja, not long after his full admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, realized for himself with direct knowledge, here and now entered upon and abided in that unsurpassed goal of the holy life (*brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ*) for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.

He directly knew: "Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being."

And the venerable Bharadvaja became another one of the *arhats* (worthy ones).

The Vattha Sutta, the seventh, is complete.
commentary_pali:
80.Evaṃ vutteti evamādi bhayabherave vuttattā pākaṭameva. Eko vūpakaṭṭhotiādīsu pana eko kāyavivekena . Vūpakaṭṭho cittavivekena. Appamatto kammaṭṭhāne sati avijahanena. Ātāpī kāyikacetasikavīriyasaṅkhātena ātāpena. Pahitatto kāye ca jīvite ca anapekkhatāya. Viharanto aññatarairiyāpathavihārena. Nacirassevāti pabbajjaṃ upādāya vuccati. Kulaputtāti duvidhā kulaputtā jātikulaputtā ca ācārakulaputtā ca, ayaṃ pana ubhayathāpi kulaputto. Agārasmāti gharā. Agārassa hitaṃ agāriyaṃ, kasigorakkhādikuṭumbaposanakammaṃ vuccati, natthi ettha agāriyanti anagāriyaṃ, pabbajjāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Pabbajantīti upagacchanti upasaṅkamanti. Tadanuttaranti taṃ anuttaraṃ. Brahmacariyapariyosānanti maggabrahmacariyassa pariyosānaṃ, arahattaphalanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tassa hi atthāya kulaputtā pabbajanti. Diṭṭheva dhammeti tasmiṃyeva attabhāve. Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvāti attanāyeva paññāya paccakkhaṃ katvā, aparappaccayaṃ katvāti attho. Upasampajja vihāsīti pāpuṇitvā sampādetvā vihāsīti, evaṃ viharanto ca khīṇā jāti…pe… abbhaññāsi. Etenassa paccavekkhaṇabhūmiṃ dasseti.

Katamā panassa jāti khīṇā? Kathañca naṃ abbhaññāsīti? Vuccate, kāmañcetaṃ bhayabheravepi vuttaṃ, tathāpi naṃ idha paṭhamapurisavasena yojanānayassa dassanatthaṃ puna saṅkhepato bhaṇāma. Na tāvassa atītā jāti khīṇā, pubbeva khīṇattā. Na anāgatā, tattha vāyāmābhāvato. Na paccuppannā, vijjamānattā. Maggassa pana abhāvitattā yā uppajjeyya ekacatupañcavokārabhavesu ekacatupañcakkhandhappabhedā jāti, sā maggassa bhāvitattā anuppādadhammataṃ āpajjanena khīṇā, taṃ so maggabhāvanāya pahīnakilese paccavekkhitvā kilesābhāve vijjamānampi kammaṃ āyatiṃ appaṭisandhikaṃ hotīti jānanto jānāti.

Vusitanti vutthaṃ parivutthaṃ, kataṃ caritaṃ niṭṭhāpitanti attho. Brahmacariyanti maggabrahmacariyaṃ. Kataṃ karaṇīyanti catūsu saccesu catūhi maggehi pariññāpahānasacchikiriyabhāvanāvasena soḷasavidhampi kiccaṃ niṭṭhāpitanti attho. Nāparaṃ itthattāyāti idāni punaitthabhāvāya evaṃsoḷasakiccabhāvāya, kilesakkhayāya vā maggabhāvanā natthīti. Atha vā, itthattāyāti itthabhāvato imasmā evaṃpakārā idāni vattamānakkhandhasantānā aparaṃ khandhasantānaṃ natthi. Ime pana pañcakkhandhā pariññātā tiṭṭhanti, chinnamūlako rukkho viyāti abbhaññāsi. Aññataroti eko. Arahatanti arahantānaṃ, bhagavato sāvakānaṃ arahataṃ abbhantaro ahosīti.

Vusita Brahmacariya Kataṃ karaṇīya Nāparaṃ itthattāyā itthattāyā Aññataro Arahata

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Vatthasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
80. “*Evaṃ vutte*,” this is manifestly stated due to the mentioning of such fearsome terrors. “*Eko vūpakaṭṭho*” in these [phrases], “*eko*” [means] by physical seclusion. "*Vūpakaṭṭho*" [means] by mental seclusion. "*Appamatto*" [means] through non-abandonment of mindfulness in meditation subject. "*Ātāpī*" [means] through the heat of zeal consisting of bodily and mental effort. "*Pahitatto*" [means] through non-dependence on the body and on life. "*Viharanto*" [means] through dwelling in some mode of conduct. "*Nacirassevā*" is said taking ordination as the starting point. "*Kulaputtā*" means two kinds of *kulaputtā*: *jātikulaputtā* and *ācārakulaputtā*; but this one is a *kulaputto* in both ways. "*Agārasmā*" [means] from the house. "*Agāriyaṃ*," [is] benefit to the house, is said to be activity such as agriculture, cattle-rearing, and supporting the family. "*Natthi ettha agāriyanti anagāriyaṃ,*" where there is no benefit to the house, that is *anagāriyaṃ*, this is a designation for ordination. "*Pabbajantī*" means they approach, they come near. "*Tadanuttara*" means that unsurpassed. "*Brahmacariyapariyosāna*" means the culmination of the path of the holy life, it is said to be the fruit of arhatship. For that benefit, young men of good families become monks. "*Diṭṭheva dhamme*" means in that very existence. "*Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā*" means having directly realized through one's own wisdom, having done [it] without reliance on another, this is the meaning. "*Upasampajja vihāsī*" means having attained, having accomplished, he dwelt, thus dwelling, and "destroyed birth…pe… fully comprehended." By this, he shows the ground of his reflection. What then is his exhausted birth? And how did he fully comprehend it? It is said: Granted, this was also said in [the section on] fearsome terrors, nevertheless, in order to show the method of the connection in terms of the first person, we will again speak concisely. It is not a past birth that is destroyed, for that was already destroyed previously. It is not a future one, for there is no effort in regard to the future. And it is not the present one, because that presently exists. But because of the uncultivated nature of the path, that birth that would arise in the one, four, five-aggregate existences, the class of one, four, five-aggregate differentiations, that, because of the cultivated nature of the path, is exhausted by entering the state of non-arising. He knows, knowing that having reflected on those abandoned afflictions through that path-cultivation, even existing action in the absence of afflictions, becomes without future rebirth. "*Vusita*," is lived, completely lived, done, practiced, completed, this is the meaning. "*Brahmacariya*" is the holy life of the path. "*Kataṃ karaṇīya*" is having completed the task in sixteen ways through the paths of full knowledge, abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation in the four truths, this is the meaning. "*Nāparaṃ itthattāyā*" means now, there is no further cultivation of the path for this existence, for this condition of sixteen things to be done, or for the destruction of defilements. Or else, "*itthattāyā*" means from this present aggregate continuum of this present condition, there is no further aggregate continuum. However, these five aggregates are known, they stand, like a tree with its roots cut off, he fully comprehended. "*Aññataro*" means one. "*Arahata*" means among the *arhats*, he was among the inner circle of the Blessed One's disciples, the *arhats*. 0181"/> itthattāyā aññataro arahata

Papañcasūdani of the commentary to the Majjhimanikāya

The explanation of the Vatthasutta is finished.

mula_pali: 81. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā mahācundo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā mahācundo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yā imā, bhante, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti – attavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā lokavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā – ādimeva nu kho, bhante, bhikkhuno manasikaroto evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ paṭinissaggo hotī’’ti?
mula_english:
81. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Savatthi in the Jeta Grove, Anathapindika’s Park.

Then, when it was evening, the venerable Mahācunda rose from meditation and went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to the Blessed One he sat down at one side.

Sitting at one side, the venerable Mahācunda said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, various views arise in the world associated either with doctrines of a self (ātma-vāda) or with doctrines about the world (loka-vāda). Now does the abandoning and relinquishing of those views come about in a bhikkhu who is attending only to the beginning of his meditative training?"
commentary_pali:
81.Evaṃme sutanti sallekhasuttaṃ. Tattha mahācundoti tassa therassa nāmaṃ. Sāyanhasamayanti sāyanhakāle. Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitoti ettha paṭisallānanti tehi tehi sattasaṅkhārehi paṭinivattitvā sallānaṃ nilīyanaṃ, ekībhāvo pavivekoti vuttaṃ hoti. Yo tato vuṭṭhito, so paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito nāma hoti. Ayaṃ pana yasmā paṭisallānānaṃ uttamato phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhāsi, tasmā ‘‘paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito’’ti vutto. Bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvāti samadasanakhujjalavibhūsitena sirasā bhagavantaṃ sakkaccaṃ vanditvā, abhivādāpetvā vā ‘‘sukhī bhava, cundā’’ti evaṃ vacībhedaṃ kārāpetvā, bhagavā pana kira vandito samāno suvaṇṇadundubhisadisaṃ gīvaṃ paggayha kaṇṇasukhaṃ pemaniyaṃ amatābhisekasadisaṃ brahmaghosaṃ nicchārento ‘‘sukhī hohī’’ti tassa tassa nāmaṃ gahetvā vadati, etaṃ āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatānaṃ. Tatridaṃ sādhakasuttaṃ, ‘‘sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatīti, sukhī hotu pañcasikha sakko devānamindo sāmacco saparijano, sukhakāmā hi devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā, ye caññe santi puthukāyā’’ti. Evañca pana tathāgatā evarūpe mahesakkhe yakkhe abhivadantīti.

Yā imāti idāni vattabbābhimukhaṃ karonto viya āha. Anekavihitāti nānappakārā. Diṭṭhiyoti micchādiṭṭhiyo . Loke uppajjantīti sattesu pātubhavanti. Attavādappaṭisaṃyuttāti ‘‘rūpaṃ attato samanupassatī’’tiādinayappavattena attavādena paṭisaṃyuttā, tā vīsati bhavanti. Lokavādappaṭisaṃyuttāti ‘‘sassato attā ca loko cā’’tiādinayappavattena lokavādena paṭisaṃyuttā, tā aṭṭha honti sassato, asassato, sassato ca asassato ca, neva sassato nāsassato, antavā, anantavā, antavā ca anantavā ca, nevantavā nānantavā attā ca loko cāti evaṃ pavattattā.

Yā imā Anekavihitā Diṭṭhiyo Loke uppajjantī Attavādappaṭisaṃyuttā Lokavādappaṭisaṃyuttā

Ādimevātiādīsu ayamattho kiṃ nu kho bhante ādimeva manasikarontassa appatvāpi sotāpattimaggaṃ vipassanāmissakapaṭhamamanasikārameva manasikarontassa bhikkhuno evametāsaṃ ettakeneva upāyena etāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānañca paṭinissaggo ca hotīti. Idañca thero attanā anadhimānikopi samāno adhimānikānaṃ adhimānappahānatthaṃ adhimāniko viya hutvā pucchatīti veditabbo. Apare panāhu ‘‘therassa antevāsikā ādimanasikāreneva diṭṭhīnaṃ samucchedappahānaṃ hotīti evaṃsaññinopi, samāpattivihārā sallekhavihārāti evaṃsaññinopi atthi. So tesaṃ atthāya bhagavantaṃ pucchatī’’ti.

Ādimevā
commentary_english:
81. Thus have I heard, the *Sallekha Sutta*.

There, *mahācundo* means the name of that elder.

*sāyanhasamaya* means at evening time.

*paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito* means here, *paṭisallāna* means having turned back from those various clinging to existence (sattasaṅkhārehi), seclusion (sallānaṃ), retreat (nilīyanaṃ), unification, it is said to be solitude (pavivekoti vuttaṃ hoti).

He who has arisen from that, is said to have arisen from seclusion.

Moreover, since he arose from the highest attainment of fruition of the instances of seclusion, therefore he is called "arisen from seclusion."

*bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā* means having respectfully venerated the Blessed One with a head adorned with a joyful smile, and also having caused [someone] to salute, or having caused [him] to make a distinction of speech thus: "May you be happy, Cunda," the Blessed One, it is said, being venerated, raising his neck resembling a golden kettledrum, emanating a Brahmā-like voice that is pleasing to the ear, lovely, and like an anointment of immortality, taking the name of each of them, says, "May you be happy." This is the custom of the *Tathāgatas*.

There is this establishing sutra, "Sakka, Venerable Sir, *devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatīti*, may Sakka, king of the gods, his ministers and followers be happy, *devas, humans, asuras, nāgas, gandhabbas*, whatever other groups of beings there are, are happy."

And that is how the *Tathāgatas* greet such mighty *yakṣas*.

*yā imā* means now, as if making [someone] face what is to be said, he said.

*anekavihitā* means various kinds.

*diṭṭhiyo* means wrong views.

*loke uppajjantī* means they appear in beings.

*attavādappaṭisaṃyuttā* means "form, he perceives as self," connected with the doctrine of self that arises from the way beginning with this, they are twenty.

*lokavādappaṭisaṃyuttā* means "the self and the world are eternal," connected with the doctrine of the world that arises from the way beginning with this, they are eight: eternal (sassato), non-eternal (asassato), both eternal and non-eternal (sassato ca asassato ca), neither eternal nor non-eternal (neva sassato nāsassato), having an end (antavā), not having an end (anantavā), both having an end and not having an end (antavā ca anantavā ca), neither having an end nor not having an end (nevantavā nānantavā), the self and the world, are of such a nature.

*yā imā anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjantī attavādappaṭisaṃyuttā lokavādappaṭisaṃyuttā*

*ādimevā* etc., in these, what is the meaning? Venerable Sir, even if one does not attain the path of stream-entry (sotāpattimaggaṃ), through initially directing the mind (ādimeva manasikarontassa), the renunciation (pahānañca) and relinquishment (paṭinissaggo ca) of these views (diṭṭhīnaṃ) occur for a *bhikkhu* who initially directs the mind (manasikarontassa bhikkhuno), by this mere means (ettakeneva upāyena), in this way (evametāsaṃ) (through the initial mental application mixed with insight (vipassanāmissakapaṭhamamanasikārameva)).

And this elder, though not conceited himself, should be known as asking as if he were conceited, for the sake of abandoning the conceit of the conceited.

Others, however, say, "For the residents of the elder, the destruction and abandonment of views occur only through the initial direction of the mind (ādimanasikāreneva). Even for those who are so-minded, there are abodes of attainment and abodes of relinquishment."

He asks the Blessed One for their benefit.

*ādimevā*

mula_pali:
82. ‘‘Yā imā, cunda, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti – attavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā lokavādapaṭisaṃyuttā vā – yattha cetā diṭṭhiyo uppajjanti yattha ca anusenti yattha ca samudācaranti taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na me so attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññā passato evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ paṭinissaggo hoti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca vihareyya, sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeyya, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasuṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā, paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā, nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā, ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti. Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihareyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘sallekhena viharāmī’ti . Na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti. Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti.
mula_english:
82. Cunda, as to those various views that arise in the world associated either with doctrines of a self or with doctrines about the world: if the object in relation to which those views arise, which they underlie, and which they are exercised upon is seen as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self,’ then the abandoning and relinquishing of those views comes about.

It is possible here that with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, some *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*: rapture & pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought & evaluation.

He might think thus: ‘I am abiding in effacement ( *sallekha* ).’

But these attainments are not called ‘effacement’ in the Noble One’s Discipline: these are called ‘pleasant abidings here and now’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.

It is possible here that with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, some *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration.

He might think thus: ‘I am abiding in effacement ( *sallekha* ).’

But these attainments are not called ‘effacement’ in the Noble One’s Discipline: these are called ‘pleasant abidings here and now’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.

It is possible here that with the fading away as well of rapture, some *bhikkhu* abides in equanimity, and mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, he enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*, on account of which noble ones announce: ‘He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.’

He might think thus: ‘I am abiding in effacement ( *sallekha* ).’

But these attainments are not called ‘effacement’ in the Noble One’s Discipline: these are called ‘pleasant abidings here and now’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.

It is possible here that with the abandoning of pleasure & pain—as with the earlier disappearance of elation & distress—some *bhikkhu* enters & remains in the fourth *jhāna*: purity of equanimity & mindfulness, neither pleasure nor pain.

He might think thus: ‘I am abiding in effacement ( *sallekha* ).’

But these attainments are not called ‘effacement’ in the Noble One’s Discipline: these are called ‘pleasant abidings here and now’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.

It is possible here that with the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ some *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ).

He might think thus: ‘I am abiding in effacement ( *sallekha* ).’

But these attainments are not called ‘effacement’ in the Noble One’s Discipline: these are called ‘peaceful abidings’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.

It is possible here that by completely surmounting the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ some *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ).

He might think thus: ‘I am abiding in effacement ( *sallekha* ).’

But these attainments are not called ‘effacement’ in the Noble One’s Discipline: these are called ‘peaceful abidings’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.

It is possible here that by completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ some *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ).

He might think thus: ‘I am abiding in effacement ( *sallekha* ).’

But these attainments are not called ‘effacement’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.
These are called ‘peaceful abidings’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.

“It is possible here, Cunda, that by completely surmounting the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ), some *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ).
It might occur to him, ‘I am abiding in detachment (sallekhena viharāmī).’

But these, Cunda, are not called detachment (*sallekhā*) in the Noble One’s Discipline (*ariyassa vinaye*).
These are called ‘peaceful abidings’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.
commentary_pali:
82. Athassa bhagavā tāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānūpāyaṃ dassento yā imātiādimāha. Tattha yattha cetā diṭṭhiyo uppajjantītiādi pañcakkhandhe sandhāya vuttaṃ. Etesu hi etā diṭṭhiyo uppajjanti. Yathāha ‘‘rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati, so attā so loko so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo’’ti (saṃ. ni. 3.152) vitthāro. Ārammaṇavasena pana ekavacanaṃ katvā yattha cāti āha, yasmiṃ ārammaṇe uppajjantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Ettha ca uppajjanti anusenti samudācarantīti imesaṃ evaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Jātivasena hi ajātā jāyamānā uppajjantīti vuccanti. Punappunaṃ āsevitā thāmagatā appaṭivinītā anusentīti. Kāyavacīdvāraṃ sampattā samudācarantīti, idametesaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ. Taṃ netaṃ mamātiādīsu taṃ pañcakkhandhappabhedaṃ ārammaṇametaṃ mayhaṃ na hoti, ahampi eso na asmi, eso me attāpi na hotīti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passatoti evaṃ tāva padattho veditabbo.

Yasmā pana ettha etaṃ mamāti taṇhāgāho, tañca gaṇhanto aṭṭhasatataṇhāvicaritappabhedaṃ taṇhāpapañcaṃ gaṇhāti. Esohamasmīti mānagāho, tañca gaṇhanto navappabhedaṃ mānapapañcaṃ gaṇhāti. Eso me attāti diṭṭhigāho, tañca gaṇhanto dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhigatappabhedaṃ diṭṭhipapañcaṃ gaṇhāti. Tasmā netaṃ mamāti vadanto bhagavā yathāvuttappabhedaṃ taṇhāpapañcaṃ paṭikkhipati. Nesohamasmīti mānapapañcaṃ. Na meso attāti diṭṭhipapañcaṃ. Diṭṭhekaṭṭhāyeva cettha taṇhāmānā veditabbā. Evametanti evaṃ ‘‘netaṃ mamā’’tiādinā ākārena etaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ. Yathābhūtanti yathā sabhāvaṃ, yathā atthīti vuttaṃ hoti. Khandhapañcakañhi eteneva ākārena atthi. Mamantiādinā pana gayhamānampi tenākārena nevatthīti adhippāyo. Sammappaññāya passatoti sotāpattimaggapaññāpariyosānāya vipassanāpaññāya suṭṭhu passantassa. Evametāsanti etena upāyena etāsaṃ. Pahānaṃ paṭinissaggoti ubhayampetaṃ samucchedappahānassevādhivacanaṃ.

netaṃ mamā Nesohamasmī Na meso attā Evameta Yathābhūta Sammappaññāya passato Evametāsa Pahānaṃ paṭinissaggo

Evaṃ bhagavā ādimanasikāreneva diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti nu kho noti āyasmatā mahācundena adhimānikānaṃ vasena pañhaṃ puṭṭho sotāpattimaggena diṭṭhippahānaṃ dassetvā idāni sayameva adhimānikānaṃ jhānaṃ vibhajanto ṭhānaṃ kho panetantiādimāha. Tattha adhimānikā nāma yesaṃ appatte pattasaññāya adhimāno uppajjati, svāyaṃ uppajjamāno neva lokavaṭṭānusārīnaṃ bālaputhujjanānaṃ uppajjati, na ariyasāvakānaṃ. Na hi sotāpannassa ‘‘sakadāgāmī aha’’nti adhimāno uppajjati, na sakadāgāmissa ‘‘anāgāmī aha’’nti, na anāgāmino ‘‘arahā aha’’nti, kārakasseva pana samathavasena vā vipassanāvasena vā vikkhambhitakilesassa niccaṃ yuttapayuttassa āraddhavipassakassa uppajjati. Tassa hi samathavikkhambhitānaṃ vā vipassanāvikkhambhitānaṃ vā kilesānaṃ samudācāraṃ apassato ‘‘sotāpanno ahanti vā, sakadāgāmī, anāgāmī , arahā aha’’nti vā adhimāno uppajjati, talaṅgaratissapabbatavāsidhammadinnattherena ovādiyamānattherānaṃ viya.

ṭhānaṃ kho paneta adhimānikā

Therassa kira acirūpasampannasseva ovāde ṭhatvā bahū bhikkhū visesaṃ adhigacchiṃsu. Taṃ pavattiṃ sutvā tissamahāvihāravāsī bhikkhusaṅgho ‘‘na aṭṭhānaniyojako theroti theraṃ ānethā’’ti sambahule bhikkhū pāhesi. Te gantvā, ‘‘āvuso, dhammadinna bhikkhusaṅgho taṃ pakkosāpetī’’ti āhaṃsu. So āha ‘‘kiṃ pana tumhe, bhante, attānaṃ gavesatha para’’nti? Attānaṃ sappurisāti, so tesaṃ kammaṭṭhānamadāsi, sabbeva arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Bhikkhusaṅgho puna aññe bhikkhū pāhesi, evaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ pahitā sabbepi tattheva arahattaṃ patvā vihariṃsu.

Tato saṅgho gatagatā nāgacchantīti aññataraṃ vuḍḍhapabbajitaṃ pāhesi. So gantvā ca, ‘‘bhante, dhammadinna tikkhattuṃ tissamahāvihāravāsī bhikkhusaṅgho tuyhaṃ santike pesesi, tvaṃ nāma saṅghassa āṇaṃ garuṃ na karosi, nāgacchasī’’ti āha. Thero kimetanti paṇṇasālaṃ appavisitvāva pattacīvaraṃ gāhāpetvā tāvadeva nikkhami, so antarāmagge haṅkanavihāraṃ pāvisi. Tattha ceko mahāthero saṭṭhivassātīto adhimānena arahattaṃ paṭijānāti. Thero taṃ upasaṅkamitvā vanditvā paṭisanthāraṃ katvā adhigamaṃ pucchi. Thero āha ‘‘āma dhammadinna, yaṃ pabbajitena kātabbaṃ, cirakataṃ taṃ mayā, atītasaṭṭhivassomhi etarahī’’ti. Kiṃ, bhante, iddhimpi vaḷañjethāti. Āma dhammadinnāti. Sādhu vata, bhante, hatthiṃ tumhākaṃ paṭimukhaṃ āgacchantaṃ māpethāti. Sādhāvusoti thero sabbasetaṃ sattappatiṭṭhaṃ tidhāpabhinnaṃ naṅguṭṭhaṃ bījayamānaṃ soṇḍaṃ mukhe pakkhipitvā dvīhi dantehi vijjhitukāmaṃ viya paṭimukhaṃ āgacchantaṃ mahāhatthiṃ māpesi. So taṃ attanāyeva māpitaṃ hatthiṃ disvā bhīto palāyituṃ ārabhi. Tadāva attānaṃ ‘‘nāhaṃ arahā’’ti ñatvā dhammadinnassa pādamūle ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā ‘‘patiṭṭhā me hohi, āvuso’’ti āha. Dhammadinno ‘‘mā, bhante, soci, mā anattamano ahosi, kārakānaṃyeva adhimāno uppajjatī’’ti theraṃ samassāsetvā kammaṭṭhānamadāsi. Thero tassovāde ṭhatvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

Cittalapabbatepi tādisova thero vasati. Dhammadinno tampi upasaṅkamitvā tatheva pucchi. Sopi tatheva byākāsi. Tato naṃ dhammadinno kiṃ, bhante, iddhimpi vaḷañjethāti āha. Āmāvusoti. Sādhu vata, bhante, ekaṃ pokkharaṇiṃ māpethāti. Thero māpesi. Ettha, bhante, padumagumbaṃ māpethāti. Tampi māpesi. Padumagumbe mahāpadumaṃ māpethāti. Tampi māpesi. Etasmiṃ padumagumbe ṭhatvā madhurassarena gāyantaṃ naccantañca ekaṃ itthiviggahaṃ māpethāti. Tampi māpesi. So etaṃ, bhante, punappunaṃ upanijjhāyathāti vatvā sayaṃ pāsādaṃ pāvisi. Therassa taṃ upanijjhāyato saṭṭhivassāni vikkhambhitakilesā caliṃsu, so tadā attānaṃ ñatvā purimatthero viya dhammadinnattherassa santike kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

Dhammadinnopi anupubbena tissamahāvihāraṃ agamāsi. Tasmiñca samaye therā cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ sammajjitvā buddhārammaṇaṃ pītiṃ uppādetvā nisinnā honti, etaṃ kira tesaṃ vattaṃ. Tena nesaṃ ekopi ‘‘idha pattacīvaraṃ ṭhapehī’’ti dhammadinnaṃ vattā pucchitāpi nāhosi. Dhammadinno eso bhaveyyāti ñatvā pana pañhaṃ pucchiṃsu. So pucchitapañhe tiṇhena asinā kumudanāḷakalāpaṃ viya chinditvā pādaṅguliyā mahāpathaviṃ pahari. Bhante ayaṃ acetanā mahāpathavīpi dhammadinnassa guṇaṃ jānāti. Tumhe pana na jānitthāti ca vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –

‘‘Acetanāyaṃ pathavī, vijānāti guṇāguṇaṃ;

Sacetanātha kho bhante, na jānātha guṇāguṇa’’nti.

Tāvadeva ca ākāse abbhuggantvā talaṅgaratissapabbatameva agamāsi. Evaṃ kārakasseva adhimāno uppajjati. Tasmā bhagavā tādisānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasena jhānaṃ vibhajanto ṭhānaṃ kho panetantiādimāha.

ṭhānaṃ kho paneta

Tassattho, atthetaṃ kāraṇaṃ, no natthi. Yena idhekacco bhikkhu bāhiraparibbājakehi sādhāraṇaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya, yaṃ pana tassa evamassa sallekhena viharāmīti, yaṃ paṭipattividhānaṃ kilese saṃlikhati, tenāhaṃ viharāmīti, taṃ na yujjati, na hi adhimānikassa bhikkhuno jhānaṃ sallekho vā sallekhapaṭipadā vā hoti. Kasmā? Avipassanāpādakattā. Na hi so jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā tato vuṭṭhāya saṅkhāre sammasati, jhānaṃ panassa cittekaggamattaṃ karoti, diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro hoti. Tasmā tamatthaṃ dassento bhagavā ‘‘na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti, diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccantī’’ti āha.

tassa evamassa sallekhena viharāmī

Tattha eteti jhānadhammavasena bahuvacanaṃ veditabbaṃ, ete paṭhamajjhānadhammāti vuttaṃ hoti. Samāpattivasena vā, ekampi hi paṭhamajjhānaṃ punappunaṃ samāpattivasena pavattattā bahuttaṃ gacchati. Ārammaṇavasena vā, ekampi hi paṭhamajjhānaṃ pathavīkasiṇādīsu pavattivasena bahuttaṃ gacchatīti. Esa nayo dutiyatatiyacatutthajjhānesu. Āruppajhānesu pana ārammaṇabhedābhāvato purimakāraṇadvayavaseneva bahuvacanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

ete

Yasmā cetesaṃ aṅgānipi santāni ārammaṇānipi, nibbutāni ceva sukhumāni cāti vuttaṃ hoti, tasmā tāni santā ete vihārāti evaṃ vuttānīti veditabbāni. Ayaṃ tāva tesaṃ catunnampi sādhāraṇā vaṇṇanā. Visesavaṇṇanā pana ‘‘sabbaso rūpasaññāna’’ntiādipadānusārato vattabbā siyā. Sā visuddhimagge sabbākārena vuttāyeva.

santā ete vihārā visuddhimagge
commentary_english:
82. Then, in order to show the way to abandon those views, the Blessed One said, "These which..." etc.

There, "where these views arise" etc. was said referring to the five aggregates (pañcakkhandha). For in these, these views arise. As he said, "When there is form (rūpa), monks, by clinging to form, this view arises: 'This is the self, this is the world, after death I will be permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change'" (Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.152) in detail.

However, having made it singular in terms of object (ārammaṇa), he said "and where," meaning, in which object they arise. And here, it should be understood that "arise, lie latent, manifest" have different meanings in this way. For, in terms of genus (jāti), those that are not yet arisen, but are arising, are called "arise (uppajjanti)." Those that are repeatedly cultivated, have become strong, unabandoned are called "lie latent (anusenti)." Those that have reached the body and speech doors are called "manifest (samudācaranti)," this is the difference between them.

In "This is not mine" etc., that which is the object (ārammaṇa), the variety of the five aggregates, this is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self either, thus one should understand the meaning of the words first, seeing this as it actually is with proper wisdom (sammappaññā).

But since here "This is mine" is grasping of craving (taṇhā), and while grasping that, one grasps the manifold proliferation of craving (taṇhāpapañca), with its eight-hundred variations. "I am this" is grasping of conceit (māna), and while grasping that, one grasps the ninefold proliferation of conceit (mānapapañca). "This is my self" is grasping of views (diṭṭhi), and while grasping that, one grasps the proliferation of views (diṭṭhipapañca) with its sixty-two varieties. Therefore, the Blessed One, saying "This is not mine," rejects the proliferation of craving (taṇhāpapañca) in its aforementioned variety. "I am not this" [rejects] the proliferation of conceit (mānapapañca). "This is not my self" [rejects] the proliferation of views (diṭṭhipapañca). Here, craving (taṇhā) and conceit (māna) should be understood as having the same basis as views (diṭṭhi).

"Thus" (evam) means, in this way, with "This is not mine" etc., this five aggregates (khandhapañcaka). "As it actually is" (yathābhūta) means as its own nature (sabhāva), as it is. For the five aggregates exist in just this way. But even when grasped as "mine" etc., the meaning is that it does not exist in that way. "Seeing with proper wisdom" (sammappaññāya passato) means for one who sees well with the wisdom of insight (vipassanāpaññā), ending in the wisdom of the path of stream-entry (sotāpattimagga). "In this way" (evametāsaṃ) means by this means, of these. "Abandoning (pahānaṃ), relinquishing (paṭinissaggo)" both of these are terms for abandoning by cutting off (samucchedappahāna).

This is not mine. I am not this. This is not my self. Thus. As it actually is. Seeing with proper wisdom. In this way. Abandoning. Relinquishing.

Thus, the Blessed One, having shown the abandonment of views (diṭṭhippahāna) by the path of stream-entry (sotāpattimagga), having been asked a question by venerable Mahācunda in terms of those with excessive conceit (adhimānikānaṃ), [asking] whether the abandonment of views occurs only with initial attention (ādimanasikārena), now dividing the jhāna of those with excessive conceit himself, says, "This is a case of..." etc.

There, "those with excessive conceit" (adhimānikā) are those in whom excessive conceit arises with the perception of having attained what is not yet attained. Now, this arising does not arise in foolish ordinary people (bālaputhujjanānaṃ) who follow the ways of the world (lokavaṭṭānusārīnaṃ), nor in noble disciples (ariyasāvakānaṃ). For excessive conceit does not arise in a stream-enterer (sotāpanna) [thinking] "I am a once-returner (sakadāgāmī)," nor in a once-returner [thinking] "I am a non-returner (anāgāmī)," nor in a non-returner [thinking] "I am an arahant." But it arises only in one who is doing [practice], whose defilements (kilesa) are suppressed (vikkambhitakilesa) by means of tranquility (samatha) or insight (vipassanā), who is constantly engaged and striving, who has started insight (āraddhavipassaka). For him, not seeing the manifestation (samudācāraṃ) of defilements that are suppressed by tranquility or suppressed by insight, excessive conceit arises: "I am a stream-enterer," or "a once-returner, a non-returner, an arahant," like the elders being instructed by the elder Dhammadinna, who lived on Talangaratissa mountain.

This is a case of. Those with excessive conceit.
It is said that many *bhikkhus* attained distinction by dwelling in the instruction of that Elder (therassa), who had recently attained the higher ordination.

Having heard that account, the *bhikkhu-saṅgha*, dwelling at Tissamahāvihāra, sent numerous *bhikkhus*, saying, "The Elder is not one who applies himself to what is inappropriate; bring the Elder here."

Having gone, they said, "Friend (āvuso), the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* of Dhammadinna summons you."

He said, "Why, *bhante*, do you search for self (attānaṃ) in another (para)?" He then gave them a subject of meditation (kammaṭṭhāna), and all attained *arahatta*.

The *bhikkhu-saṅgha* again sent other *bhikkhus*; in this way, those sent even up to the third time, all attained *arahatta* right there, and lived (vihariṃsu).

Then the *saṅgha*, [thinking], "Those who have gone do not return," sent another elder monk (vuḍḍhapabbajitaṃ).

Having gone, he said, "*Bhante*, Dhammadinna, the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* dwelling at Tissamahāvihāra, has sent [messengers] to you three times. You, it seems, do not hold the command (āṇaṃ) of the *saṅgha* in high regard; you do not come."

The Elder, [thinking], "What is this?", without even entering the leaf hut (paṇṇasālaṃ), had his bowl and robe (pattacīvaraṃ) taken, and immediately departed. He entered the Haṅkana-vihāra on the way.

There, a certain great Elder (mahāthero), sixty years past [his ordination], arrogantly claimed to have attained *arahatta*.

The Elder approached him, and after saluting (vanditvā), exchanging friendly greetings (paṭisanthāraṃ katvā), asked about his attainment (adhigamaṃ).

The Elder said, "Yes, Dhammadinna, what should be done by one gone forth (pabbajitena kātabbaṃ), that has been done by me for a long time; I am now over sixty years [since ordination] (atīta-saṭṭhi-vasso-mhi)."

"[Can you], *bhante*, wield psychic power (iddhi)?"

"Yes, friend (dhammadinna)."

"Good, *bhante*, then conjure up an elephant coming towards you!"

"Very well, friend (sādhāvusoti)," said the Elder, and he conjured up a great elephant, completely white (sabbasetaṃ), standing firmly on seven supports (sattappatiṭṭhaṃ), with its tail split in three (tidhāpabhinnaṃ), fanning [with] its trunk (naṅguṭṭhaṃ bījayamānaṃ), putting its trunk in its mouth (soṇḍaṃ mukhe pakkhipitvā), as if desiring to pierce [him] with its two tusks (dvīhi dantehi vijjhitukāmaṃ), coming towards [him].

Having seen that elephant conjured up by himself, he, frightened, began to flee (palāyituṃ ārabhi).

Then and there (tadāva), having realized that he [was] not an *araha*, squatting down (ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā) at the foot of Dhammadinna, he said, "Be a refuge (patiṭṭhā) for me, friend (āvuso)!"

Dhammadinna, consoling (samassāsetvā) the Elder, [said], "Do not, *bhante*, grieve (soci); do not be disheartened (anattamano ahosi); conceit (adhimāno) arises only for those who are doing [something](kārakānaṃyeva)," and gave [him] a subject of meditation (kammaṭṭhānamadāsi).

The Elder, dwelling in his instruction (tassovāde ṭhatvā), attained *arahatta*.

At Cittalapabbata too, there lives an Elder just like that (tādisova thero vasati).

Dhammadinna approached that one too, and asked in the same way (tatheva pucchi).

That one too declared (byākāsi) in the same way (tatheva).

Then Dhammadinna said to him, "*Bhante*, can you wield psychic power (iddhi)?"

"Yes, friend (āmāvusoti)."

"Good, *bhante*, then conjure up a pond (pokkharaṇiṃ)!"

The Elder conjured [one].

"Here, *bhante*, conjure up a lotus thicket (padumagumbaṃ)!"

He conjured that too.

"In that lotus thicket, conjure up a great lotus (mahāpadumaṃ)!"

He conjured that too.

"In this lotus thicket, conjure up the figure of a woman (itthiviggahaṃ) standing (ṭhatvā), singing (gāyantaṃ), and dancing (naccantaṃ) in a sweet voice (madhurassarena)!"

He conjured that too.

"You should contemplate (upanijjhāyatha) this again and again, *bhante*," having said [this], he himself entered the mansion (pāsādaṃ pāvisi).

While the Elder was contemplating that, the defilements (kilesā) suppressed for sixty years (saṭṭhivassāni vikkhambhitakilesā) were shaken (caliṃsu), then, having recognized himself (attānaṃ ñatvā), like the former Elder (purimatthero viya), having taken a subject of meditation (kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā) near (santike) Dhammadinna, the Elder, he attained *arahatta*.
Dhammadinna also gradually went to Tissa Great Monastery.
At that time, the elders, having swept the Cetiya courtyard and having generated joy by taking the Buddha as their object [of meditation], were sitting there; this, it seems, was their custom.
Therefore, not even one of them asked Dhammadinna, "Keep your bowl and robe here."
However, having recognized that this was Dhammadinna, they asked a question.
He, having answered the question, having cut a cluster of kumuda stalks with a sharp sword, struck the great earth with his toe.
"Venerable, even this unconscious great earth knows the virtues of Dhammadinna.
But you did not know," and having said that, he spoke this verse:

"This unconscious earth knows virtue and vice;
but you, the conscious ones, venerable, do not know virtue and vice."

Immediately, rising up into the sky, he went to Talangaratissa Mountain itself.
Adhimāna (false pride), arises just like that of a doer.
Therefore, the Blessed One, while distinguishing jhāna (meditation) based on such monks, said, "This is a basis," and so on.

This is a basis:

Its meaning is, it is a cause, it is not without.
Because here, some monk, having completely secluded himself from sensual pleasures common to outside wanderers... attains and dwells in the first jhāna, but that which is, "Thus, I dwell with detachment," that mode of practice that scratches away defilements, "I dwell with that," that is not fitting, because for a monk with false pride, there is neither jhāna nor the practice of detachment.
Why? Because it does not lead to insight.
He, having attained jhāna, does not then rise up from it and contemplate conditioned things, but jhāna only makes his mind one-pointed, it is dwelling in happiness in this very life.
Therefore, showing that meaning, the Blessed One said, "These, Cunda, are not called detachment in the Noble One's discipline, these are called dwelling in happiness in this very life in the Noble One's discipline."

Thus, I dwell with detachment:

There, "these" should be understood as plural in the sense of jhāna-dharmas, it is said, "these are the first jhāna-dharmas."
Or in the sense of attainment, because even one first jhāna, due to recurring in the sense of attainment, goes to plurality.
Or in the sense of object, because even one first jhāna, due to occurring in earth kasina and so on, goes to plurality.
This is the method for the second, third, and fourth jhāna.
But in the immaterial jhāna, due to the absence of difference in object, plurality should be understood only in the sense of the former two reasons.

These:

Because it is said that their constituents and their objects are peaceful and subtle, therefore, it should be understood that they are called "peaceful are these dwellings."
This, for now, is the general description for all four of them.
But the specific description should be stated according to the words "with the complete transcending of perceptions of form," and so on.
That has been completely stated in the *Visuddhimagga*.

Peaceful are these dwellings. *Visuddhimagga*.

83. ‘‘Idha kho pana vo, cunda, sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pāṇātipātī bhavissanti, mayamettha pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare adinnādāyī bhavissanti, mayamettha adinnādānā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare abrahmacārī bhavissanti, mayamettha brahmacārī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare musāvādī bhavissanti, mayamettha musāvādā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pisuṇavācā pisuṇā vācā (sī. pī.) bhavissanti, mayamettha pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare pharusavācā pharusā vācā (sī. pī.) bhavissanti, mayamettha pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare samphappalāpī bhavissanti, mayamettha samphappalāpā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare abhijjhālū bhavissanti, mayamettha anabhijjhālū bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare byāpannacittā bhavissanti, mayamettha abyāpannacittā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchādiṭṭhī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammādiṭṭhī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāsaṅkappā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāsaṅkappā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāvācā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāvācā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchākammantā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammākammantā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāājīvā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāājīvā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāvāyāmā bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāvāyāmā bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāsatī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāsatī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāsamādhi bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāsamādhī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāñāṇī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāñāṇī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo. ‘Pare micchāvimuttī bhavissanti, mayamettha sammāvimuttī bhavissāmā’ti sallekho karaṇīyo.

83. Now, Cunda, here effacement (*sallekho karaṇīyo*) should be practised.

‘Others will be cruel (*vihiṃsakā bhavissanti*); we shall not be cruel (*avihiṃsakā bhavissāma*) here’: effacement (*sallekho karaṇīyo*) should be practised thus.

‘Others will kill living beings (*pāṇātipātī bhavissanti*); we shall abstain from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā*) here’: effacement (*sallekho karaṇīyo*) should be practised thus.

‘Others will be uncelibate (*abrahmacārī bhavissanti*); we shall be celibate (*brahmacārī bhavissāmā*) here’: effacement (*sallekho karaṇīyo*) should be practised thus.

‘Others will be of wrong speech (*micchāvācā bhavissanti*); we shall be of right speech (*sammāvācā bhavissāmā*) here’: effacement (*sallekho karaṇīyo*) should be practised thus.
