83. Evaṃ yasmā adhimānikassa bhikkhuno jhānavihāro avipassanāpādakattā sallekhavihāro na hoti, na hi so jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā tato vuṭṭhāya saṅkhāre sammasati, cittekaggakaro diṭṭhadhamme sukhavihāro panassa hoti, tasmā tamatthaṃ dassento rūpajjhānāni ca arūpajjhānāni ca vibhajitvā idāni ca yattha sallekho kātabbo catucattālīsāya ākārehi, tañca vatthuṃ tañca sallekhaṃ dassento idha kho pana votiādimāha.

Kasmā pana ‘‘aṭṭhahi samāpattīhi avihiṃsādayo sallekhā’’ti vuttā? Lokuttarapādakattā. Bāhirakānañhi aṭṭha samāpattiyo vaṭṭapādakāyeva. Sāsane saraṇagamanampi lokuttarapādakaṃ, pageva avihiṃsādayo. Imināyeva ca suttena veditabbaṃ ‘‘yathā bāhirakassa aṭṭhasamāpattilābhino pañcābhiññassāpi dinnadānato sāsane tisaraṇagatassa dinnadānaṃ mahapphalataraṃ hotī’’ti. Idañhi sandhāya dakkhiṇāvisuddhisutte ‘‘bāhirake kāmesu vītarāge dānaṃ datvā koṭisatasahassaguṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dānaṃ datvā asaṅkheyyā appameyyā dakkhiṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, ko pana vādo sotāpanne’’ti vuttaṃ (ma. ni. 3.379). Saraṇagamanato paṭṭhāya hi tattha sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno adhippetoti, ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷiyojanā.

Anupadavaṇṇanāyaṃ pana idhāti vihiṃsādivatthudīpanametaṃ. Kho panāti nipātamattaṃ. Voti karaṇatthe sāmivacanaṃ, ayaṃ pana saṅkhepattho, yadetaṃ ‘‘pare vihiṃsakā bhavissantī’’tiādinā nayena vihiṃsādivatthuṃ vadāma. Idha, cunda, tumhehi sallekho kātabboti.

idhā Kho panā Vo

Evaṃ saṅkhepato vatvā idāni vitthārento ‘‘pare vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmāti sallekho karaṇīyo’’tiādimāha.

Tattha pareti ye keci imaṃ sallekhamananuyuttā. Vihiṃsakā bhavissantīti pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vātiādīhi sattānaṃ vihesakā bhavissanti. Mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmāti mayaṃ pana yattheva vatthusmiṃ pare evaṃ vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, ettheva avihiṃsakā bhavissāma, avihiṃsaṃ uppādetvā viharissāma. Iti sallekho karaṇīyoti evaṃ tumhehi sallekho kātabbo . Sallekhoti ca idha avihiṃsāva veditabbā. Avihiṃsā hi vihiṃsaṃ sallekhati, taṃ chindati, tasmā sallekhoti vuccati. Esa nayo sabbattha. Ayaṃ pana viseso. Pare micchādiṭṭhīti ettha kammapathānaṃ antamicchādiṭṭhiñca micchattānaṃ ādimicchādiṭṭhiñca missetvā diṭṭhi vuttāti veditabbā. Tathā mayamettha sammādiṭṭhīti vuttaṭṭhāne sammādiṭṭhi. Ettha ca kammapathakathā vitthārato sammādiṭṭhisutte āvi bhavissati. Micchattesu micchādiṭṭhiādayo dvedhāvitakke.

pare Vihiṃsakā bhavissantī Mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmā Iti sallekho karaṇīyo Sallekho sallekho Pare micchādiṭṭhī mayamettha sammādiṭṭhī

Ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepo, pāṇaṃ atipātentīti pāṇātipātī pāṇaghātakāti attho. Adinnaṃ ādiyantīti adinnādāyī, parassa hārinoti attho. Abrahmaṃ hīnaṃ lāmakadhammaṃ carantīti abrahmacārī, methunadhammappaṭisevakāti attho. Brahmaṃ seṭṭhaṃ paṭipadaṃ carantīti brahmacārī, methunā paṭiviratāti attho. Ettha ca brahmacariyaṃ sallekhoti veditabbaṃ. Brahmacariyañhi abrahmacariyaṃ sallekhati. Musā vadantīti musāvādī, paresaṃ atthabhañjanakaṃ tucchaṃ alikaṃ vācaṃ bhāsitāroti attho. Pisuṇā vācā etesanti pisuṇavācā. Paresaṃ mammacchedikā pharusā vācā etesanti pharusavācā. Samphaṃ niratthakavacanaṃ palapantīti samphappalāpī. Abhijjhāyantīti abhijjhālū, parabhaṇḍalubbhanasīlāti attho. Byāpannaṃ pūtibhūtaṃ cittametesanti byāpannacittā. Micchā pāpikā viññugarahitā etesaṃ diṭṭhīti micchādiṭṭhī, kammapathapariyāpannāya natthi dinnantiādivatthukāya, micchattapariyāpannāya aniyyānikadiṭṭhiyā ca samannāgatāti attho. Sammā sobhanā viññuppasatthā etesaṃ diṭṭhīti sammādiṭṭhī, kammapathapariyāpannāya atthi dinnantiādikāya kammassakatādiṭṭhiyā, sammattapariyāpannāya maggadiṭṭhiyā ca samannāgatāti attho.

pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī, abrahmacārī, brahmacārī, musāvādī, pisuṇavācā pharusavācā samphappalāpī abhijjhālū, byāpannacittā micchādiṭṭhī, sammādiṭṭhī,

Micchāsaṅkappāti ayāthāvaaniyyānikaakusalasaṅkappā. Esa nayo micchāvācātiādīsu. Ayaṃ pana viseso, micchāsaṅkappādayo viya hi micchāsati nāma pāṭiekko koci dhammo natthi, atītaṃ pana cintayato pavattānaṃ catunnampi akusalakkhandhānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Yampi vuttaṃ bhagavatā – ‘‘atthesā, bhikkhave, anussati, nesā natthīti vadāmi, puttalābhaṃ vā, bhikkhave, anussarato, dhanalābhaṃ vā, bhikkhave, anussarato, yasalābhaṃ vā, bhikkhave, anussarato’’ti, tampi taṃ taṃ cintentassa satipatirūpakena uppattiṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ . Micchāñāṇīti ettha ca micchāñāṇanti pāpakiriyāsu upāyacintāvasena pāpaṃ katvā ‘‘sukataṃ mayā’’ti paccavekkhaṇākārena ca uppanno moho veditabbo, tena samannāgatā puggalā micchāñāṇī. Sammāñāṇīti ettha pana ekūnavīsatibhedaṃ paccavekkhaṇāñāṇaṃ ‘‘sammāñāṇa’’nti vuccati, tena samannāgatā puggalā sammāñāṇī. Micchāvimuttīti avimuttāyeva samānā ‘‘vimuttā maya’’nti evaṃsaññino, avimuttiyaṃ vā vimuttisaññino. Tatrāyaṃ vacanattho, micchā pāpikā viparītā vimutti etesaṃ atthīti micchāvimuttī. Micchāvimuttīti ca yathāvuttenākārena pavattānaṃ akusalakkhandhānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Phalasampayuttāni pana sammādiṭṭhiādīni aṭṭhaṅgāni ṭhapetvā sesadhammā sammāvimuttīti veditabbā. Sā ca micchāvimuttiṃ sallikhitvā ṭhitattā sallekhoti veditabbā. Tattha niyojento āha ‘‘mayamettha sammāvimuttī bhavissāmāti sallekho karaṇīyo’’ti.

Micchāsaṅkappā micchāvācā micchāsati Micchāñāṇī micchāñāṇa micchāñāṇī. Sammāñāṇī sammāñāṇī. Micchāvimuttī micchāvimuttī sammāvimuttī sallekho

Ito parāni tīṇi nīvaraṇavasena vuttāni. Abhijjhālū byāpannacittāti evaṃ kammapathesu vuttattā panettha paṭhamāni dve nīvaraṇāni na vuttānīti veditabbāni. Tattha thinamiddhena pariyuṭṭhitā abhibhūtāti thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā. Uddhaccena samannāgatāti uddhatā. Vicinantā kicchanti na sakkonti sanniṭṭhānaṃ kātunti vicikicchī. Kodhanātiādīni dasa cittassa upakkilesavasena vuttāni. Tattha kodhādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, taṃ sabbaṃ dhammadāyādavatthasuttesu vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha vacanattho – kodhanāti kujjhanasīlā. Upanāhīti upanāhanasīlā, upanāho vā etesaṃ atthīti upanāhī. Tathā makkhī palāsī ca. Issantīti issukī. Maccharāyantīti maccharī, maccheraṃ vā etesaṃ atthīti maccharī. Saṭhayantīti saṭhā, na sammā bhāsantīti vuttaṃ hoti, kerāṭikayuttānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Māyā etesaṃ atthīti māyāvī. Thambhasamaṅgitāya thaddhā. Atimānayogena atimānī. Vuttapaccanīkanayena sukkapakkho veditabbo.

Abhijjhālū byāpannacittā thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā uddhatā vicikicchī. Kodhanā kodhanā Upanāhī upanāhī makkhī palāsī issukī maccharī, saṭhā, māyāvī thaddhā atimānī

Dubbacāti vattuṃ dukkhā kiñci vuccamānā na sahanti. Tabbiparītā suvacā. Devadattādisadisā pāpakā mittā etesanti pāpamittā. Buddhā vā sāriputtādisadisā vā kalyāṇā mittā etesanti kalyāṇamittā. Kāyaduccaritādīsu cittavossaggavasena pamattā. Viparītā appamattāti veditabbā. Imāni tīṇi pakiṇṇakavasena vuttāni. Assaddhātiādīni satta asaddhammavasena. Tattha tīsu vatthūsu saddhā etesaṃ natthīti assaddhā. Sukkapakkhe saddahantīti saddhā, saddhā vā etesaṃ atthītipi saddhā. Natthi etesaṃ hirīti ahirikā, akusalasamāpattiyā ajigucchamānānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Hirī etesaṃ mane, hiriyā vā yuttamanāti hirimanā. Na ottappantīti anottappī, akusalasamāpattiyā na bhāyantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tabbiparītā ottappī. Appaṃ sutametesanti appassutā, appanti ca thokanti na gahetabbaṃ, natthīti gahetabbaṃ. ‘‘Appassutā’’ti hi nissutā sutavirahitā vuccanti. Bahu sutametesanti bahussutā, tathāgatabhāsitaṃ ekampi gāthaṃ yāthāvato ñatvā anurūpapaṭipannānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Kucchitā sīdantīti kusītā, hīnavīriyānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Āraddhaṃ vīriyametesanti āraddhavīriyā, sammappadhānayuttānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ, muṭṭhā sati etesanti muṭṭhassatī, naṭṭhassatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Upaṭṭhitā sati etesanti upaṭṭhitassatī, niccaṃ ārammaṇābhimukhappavattasatīnametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Duṭṭhā paññā etesanti duppaññā, naṭṭhapaññāti vuttaṃ hoti. Paññāya sampannāti paññāsampannā, paññāti ca idha vipassanāpaññā veditabbā. Vipassanāsambhāro hi paripūro imasmiṃ ṭhāne āgato, tasmā vipassanāpaññāva ayanti porāṇānaṃ āṇā.

Dubbacā suvacā pāpamittā kalyāṇamittā pamattā appamattā Assaddhā assaddhā saddhā, ahirikā, hirimanā anottappī, ottappī appassutā, appa bahussutā, kusītā, āraddhavīriyā, muṭṭhassatī, upaṭṭhitassatī, duppaññā, paññāsampannā, paññā

Idāni ekameva lokuttaraguṇānaṃ antarāyakaraṃ aniyyānikadiṭṭhiṃ tīhākārehi dassento sandiṭṭhiparāmāsītiādimāha. Tattha sandiṭṭhiṃ parāmasantīti sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī. Ādhānaṃ gaṇhantīti ādhānaggāhī, ādhānanti daḷhaṃ vuccati, daḷhaggāhīti attho. Yuttakāraṇaṃ disvāva laddhiṃ paṭinissajjantīti paṭinissaggī, dukkhena kicchena kasirena bahumpi kāraṇaṃ dassetvā na sakkā paṭinissaggaṃ kātunti duppaṭinissaggī, ye attano uppannaṃ diṭṭhiṃ idameva saccanti daḷhaṃ gaṇhitvā api buddhādīhi kāraṇaṃ dassetvā vuccamānā na paṭinissajjanti, tesametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tādisā hi puggalā yaṃ yadeva dhammaṃ vā adhammaṃ vā gaṇhanti, taṃ sabbaṃ ‘‘evaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyehi kathitaṃ, evaṃ amhehi suta’’nti kummova aṅgāni sake kapāle antoyeva samodahanti, kumbhīlaggāhaṃ gaṇhanti na vissajjanti. Vuttavipariyāyena sukkapakkho veditabbo.

sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī, ādhāna paṭinissaggī, duppaṭinissaggī,
commentary_english:
83. Thus, because for a monk who is overly conceited, dwelling in *jhāna* is not conducive to insight (*vipaśyanā*), dwelling in effacement (*sallekha*) is not [possible]. For he, having attained *jhāna*, does not reflect on conditioned things (*saṅkhāra*) after arising from that. But for him there is a dwelling of happiness (*sukhavihāra*) in the visible dharma, making the mind one-pointed. Therefore, showing that meaning, and distinguishing the rūpa *jhānas* and arūpa *jhānas*, and now, where effacement should be practiced with forty-four aspects, and showing that thing and that effacement, [he] says, "<hi rend="bold">Here, Cunda, effacement should be practiced by you</hi>," and so on.

Why is it said that "effacements (*sallekha*) are non-harming (*avihiṃsā*) and so on, with eight attainments (*samāpatti*)?" Because [they] are conducive to the supramundane (*lokuttara*). For those outside [the Buddhist teaching], the eight attainments are merely conducive to continued existence (*vaṭṭa*). In the teaching (*sāsana*), going for refuge (*saraṇagamana*) is also conducive to the supramundane, what to say of non-harming and so on. And by this very *sutta* it should be understood that "giving a gift (*dinnadāna*) by one who has attained the eight attainments and has the five superknowledges (*pañcābhiñña*), even for one gone for three refuges (*tisaraṇagata*) in the teaching (*sāsana*), is more greatly fruitful (*mahapphalataraṃ*)." For, referring to this, in the Dakkhiṇāvisuddhi Sutta, "having given a gift to one free from lust (*vītarāga*) for sense pleasures (*kāmesu*), a hundred thousand times a crore (*koṭisatasahassaguṇā*) may be expected. Having given a gift to one who has undertaken the realization (*sacchikiriyāya*) of the fruit (*phala*) of stream-entry (*sotāpatti*), immeasurable and incalculable merit (*dakkhiṇā*) may be expected, what to say of a stream-enterer (*sotāpanne*)," is said (Majjhima Nikāya 3.379). From going for refuge onwards, one who has undertaken the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is intended there, this is the explanation of the *pāḷi* here.

In the subsequent commentary, "<hi rend="bold">Here</hi>" indicates the object (*vatthu*) of non-harming and so on. "<hi rend="bold">Kho panā</hi>" is merely a particle (*nipātamattaṃ*). "<hi rend="bold">Vo</hi>" is a possessive expression in the sense of instrumentality; this is, however, an abbreviated meaning: "We speak of the object of non-harming and so on by the method of 'others will be harmful (*vihiṃsakā*),' and so on." Here, Cunda, effacement should be practiced by you.

<hi rend="bold">Here</hi> <hi rend="bold">kho panā</hi> <hi rend="bold">vo</hi> Having thus spoken in brief, and now elaborating, [he] says, "Others will be harmful (*vihiṃsakā bhavissanti*), we shall be non-harmful (*avihiṃsakā bhavissāmāti*) here': effacement (*sallekho*) should be practiced thus," and so on.

There, "<hi rend="bold">others</hi>" are whoever is not engaged in this effacement (*sallekha*). "<hi rend="bold">Will be harmful</hi>" means will be injurers (*vihesakā*) of beings (*sattānaṃ*) by hand or stick or sword, and so on. "<hi rend="bold">We shall be non-harmful here</hi>" means we, however, in whatever object others will be thus harmful, just there we shall be non-harmful, having produced non-harming, we shall dwell. "<hi rend="bold">Thus, effacement should be practiced</hi>" means thus effacement should be done by you.

And "<hi rend="bold">effacement</hi>" here should be understood as just non-harming. For non-harming effaces harming, it cuts it off, therefore it is called "<hi rend="bold">effacement</hi>." This method [applies] everywhere. This, however, is the distinction. "<hi rend="bold">Others [are of] wrong view</hi>": here, having mixed wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*) which is the extreme of the paths of action (*kammapathānaṃ*), and wrongness (*micchattānaṃ*), which is the beginning of wrong view, view is said thus it should be understood. Similarly, "<hi rend="bold">we [are of] right view here</hi>" is right view in the place where it is said. And here, the story of the paths of action will become manifest in detail in the Right View Sutta. In wrongnesses, wrong view and so on [are] twofold thoughts.

<hi rend="bold">Others</hi> <hi rend="bold">will be harmful</hi> <hi rend="bold">we shall be non-harmful here</hi> <hi rend="bold">thus, effacement should be practiced</hi> <hi rend="bold">effacement</hi> <hi rend="bold">effacement</hi> <hi rend="bold">others [are of] wrong view</hi> <hi rend="bold">we [are of] right view here</hi> This is the summary here: One who destroys life (*pāṇa*) is a killer of life (*pāṇātipātī*), the meaning is a destroyer of life (*pāṇaghātaka*). One who takes what is not given (*adinnaṃ*) is a taker of what is not given (*adinnādāyī*), the meaning is a carrier of what belongs to another (*parassa hārino*). One who practices what is not *brahma*, inferior, and a low dharma is a non-*brahmacārī*, a follower of the *methuna* dharma.
It is reached, is the meaning. One who engages in the best practice, the supreme conduct, is called a *brahmacārī*, one who abstains from sexual activity, is the meaning. And here, monastic life (*brahmacariya*) should be understood as austerity (*sallekha*). For monastic life refines non-monastic life. One who speaks falsehoods is a liar (*musāvādī*), one who speaks words that ruin the benefit of others, that are empty and untrue, is the meaning. These are words that cause dissension, therefore, [they are called] divisive speech (*pisuṇavācā*). Harsh speech (*pharusavācā*) is speech that wounds others' hearts. One who babbles nonsensical talk is a prattler (*samphappalāpī*). One who is always coveting is covetous (*abhijjhālū*), one who has a nature of being greedy for the possessions of others, is the meaning. Those whose minds are corrupted and putrid are with corrupted minds (*byāpannacittā*). False and evil views that are devoid of knowledge are called wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhī*), which is connected to things such as "there is no gift," etc., which are included in the path of action, and wrong views that lead to no escape, which are included in wrongness, is the meaning. Good and beautiful views that are praised by the wise are called right view (*sammādiṭṭhī*), which is connected to things such as "there is a gift," etc., which are included in the path of action, and the view that actions are one's own, and the path view which is included in correctness, is the meaning.

One who kills living beings (*pāṇātipātī*). One who takes what is not given (*adinnādāyī*), one who does not live a monastic life (*abrahmacārī*). *Brahmacārī*, liar (*musāvādī*), divisive speech (*pisuṇavācā*), harsh speech (*pharusavācā*), prattler (*samphappalāpī*), covetous (*abhijjhālū*), with corrupted minds (*byāpannacittā*), wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhī*), right view (*sammādiṭṭhī*). Wrong thought (*micchāsaṅkappā*) are thoughts that are not true, that lead to no escape, and that are unwholesome.

This is the method for wrong speech (*micchāvācā*) and so forth. Now, this is the distinction: just as wrong thought and so forth, indeed, there is no isolated phenomenon called wrong mindfulness (*micchāsati*); rather, this is an epithet for all four unwholesome aggregates that arise when one thinks about the past.

Also, what was said by the Blessed One: "O monks, there is mindfulness, I say that there is no lack of it. O monks, when one is mindful of gaining a son, or, O monks, when one is mindful of gaining wealth, or, O monks, when one is mindful of gaining fame," that, too, should be understood as referring to the arising, in dependence on mindfulness-like things, for one who is thinking of this and that.

Wrong knowledge (*micchāñāṇī*): here, wrong knowledge (*micchāñāṇa*) is delusion (*moha*) that has arisen due to thinking of means in evil actions and doing evil, thinking "I have done well" by way of reflection. Persons endowed with that are with wrong knowledge (*micchāñāṇī*). Right knowledge (*sammāñāṇī*): here, reviewing knowledge (*paccavekkhaṇāñāṇa*), which has nineteen kinds, is called right knowledge (*sammāñāṇa*). Persons endowed with that are with right knowledge (*sammāñāṇī*).

Wrong liberation (*micchāvimuttī*): although they are not liberated, they are those who think, "We are liberated," thus, or those who have the perception of liberation in non-liberation. There, this is the meaning of the words: wrong, evil, and reversed liberation exists for them, therefore [they are called] wrong liberation (*micchāvimuttī*). Also, wrong liberation (*micchāvimuttī*) is an epithet for the unwholesome aggregates that arise in accordance with what was said. But after setting aside the eight limbs beginning with right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*) that are connected with the result, the remaining phenomena should be understood as right liberation (*sammāvimuttī*). And because that austerity (*sallekha*) is established after refining wrong liberation (*micchāvimutti*), it should be understood as austerity (*sallekho*). There, enjoining, he said, "Austerity (*sallekho*) should be done so that we will have right liberation (*sammāvimuttī*) here."

Wrong thought (*micchāsaṅkappā*), wrong speech (*micchāvācā*), wrong mindfulness (*micchāsati*). Wrong knowledge (*micchāñāṇī*), wrong knowledge (*micchāñāṇa*), wrong knowledge (*micchāñāṇī*). Right knowledge (*sammāñāṇī*). Right knowledge (*sammāñāṇī*). Wrong liberation (*micchāvimuttī*), wrong liberation (*micchāvimuttī*), right liberation (*sammāvimuttī*), austerity (*sallekho*).

From here on, the three that follow are spoken of in terms of hindrances. Because "covetous (*abhijjhālū*) and with corrupted minds (*byāpannacittā*)" were spoken of in the paths of action in this way, therefore, it should be understood that the first two hindrances were not spoken of here. There, those who are completely surrounded and overcome by sloth and torpor are with sloth and torpor (*thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā*). Those who are endowed with excitement are excited (*uddhatā*). Those who are searching, are afflicted, and are not able to make a determination are with doubt (*vicikicchī*). Anger (*kodhanā*) and so forth, these ten are spoken of in terms of the defilements of the mind.
Everything that needs to be said concerning anger and the rest has been said in the Dhammadāyādavatthasutta.

Here is the word-meaning: *kodhana* means habitually angry.

*upanāhī* means habitually bearing grudges, or they have grudges, thus *upanāhī*.

Likewise *makkhī* and *palāsī*.

*issantīti issukī*: being envious, thus *issukī*.

*maccharāyantīti maccharī*: being stingy, thus *maccharī*, or they have stinginess, thus *maccharī*.

*saṭhayantīti saṭhā*: being deceitful, it is said that they do not speak correctly; this is a designation for those who are associated with trickery.

*māyā etesaṃ atthīti māyāvī*: they have deceit, thus *māyāvī* (deceitful).

*thambhasamaṅgitāya thaddhā*: being rigid through rigidity.

*atimānayogena atimānī*: being arrogant through excessive pride.

The bright side should be understood in the opposite way from what has been stated.

*abhijjhālū byāpannacittā thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā uddhatā vicikicchī.*

*kodhanā upanāhī makkhī palāsī issukī maccharī, saṭhā, māyāvī thaddhā atimānī*

*dubbacā* means difficult to speak to; they do not tolerate anything being said to them.

The opposite of that is *suvacā* (easy to speak to).

*pāpamittā*: they have evil friends like Devadatta and others.

*kalyāṇamittā*: they have good friends like the Buddha or Sāriputta and others.

*pamattā*: being negligent due to mental distraction regarding bad conduct of body and so on.

The opposite of that is *appamattā* (non-negligent) – this should be understood.

These three have been stated as miscellaneous.

*assaddhā* and so on are seven in terms of lack of good qualities.

There, because they do not have faith in the three objects, thus *assaddhā* (faithless).

On the bright side, *saddahantīti saddhā*: they have faith, thus *saddhā*, or they have faith, thus also *saddhā* (faithful).

*natthi etesaṃ hirīti ahirikā*: they have no shame; this is a designation for those who do not feel disgust for attaining unwholesome states.

*hirī etesaṃ mane, hiriyā vā yuttamanāti hirimanā*: they have shame in mind, or their minds are associated with shame, thus *hirimanā* (shameful).

*na ottappantīti anottappī*: they do not feel fear; it is said that they are not afraid of attaining unwholesome states.

The opposite of that is *ottappī* (conscientious).

*appaṃ sutametesanti appassutā*: they have heard little; here *appaṃ* should not be taken as "a little", but as "none."

For "appassutā" (unlearned) means those who are without learning, devoid of hearing.

*bahu sutametesanti bahussutā*: they have heard much; this is a designation for those who, having understood a single verse spoken by the Tathāgata as it really is, practice accordingly.

*kucchitā sīdantīti kusītā*: they are lazy, thus *kusītā*; this is a designation for those who are deficient in energy.

*āraddhaṃ vīriyametesanti āraddhavīriyā*: they have aroused energy; this is a designation for those who are associated with right effort. *muṭṭhā sati etesanti muṭṭhassatī*: they are forgetful; it is said that they have lost mindfulness.

*upaṭṭhitā sati etesanti upaṭṭhitassatī*: mindfulness is present to them; this is a designation for those whose mindfulness constantly turns towards its object.

*duṭṭhā paññā etesanti duppaññā*: their wisdom is bad; it is said that they have lost wisdom.

*paññāya sampannāti paññāsampannā*: they are endowed with wisdom; here *paññā* should be understood as insight wisdom (vipassanāpaññā).

For the accumulation of insight has come to this place fully complete; therefore, it is insight wisdom itself, according to the teaching of the elders.

*dubbacā suvacā pāpamittā kalyāṇamittā pamattā appamattā*

*assaddhā assaddhā*
clinging to views, not having faith (*śraddhā*), shameless (*āhrikā*), without moral dread (*anottappī*), conscientious (*ottappī*), unlearned (*appassutā*), very learned (*bahussutā*), lazy (*kusītā*), with aroused vigor (*āraddhavīriyā*), with a distracted mindfulness (*muṭṭhassatī*), with established mindfulness (*upaṭṭhitassatī*), unwise (*duppaññā*), endowed with wisdom (*paññāsampannā*).

Now, showing with three aspects the single obstruction to the supramundane qualities, the view that does not lead out, he says, "clinging to views" (*sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī*), etc.

There, *sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī* means those who grasp views.

*ādhānaggāhī* means those who grasp appropriation. *ādhāna* means firmness, the meaning is grasping firmly.

*paṭinissaggī* means those who relinquish a belief upon seeing a valid reason. *duppaṭinissaggī* means it is not possible to relinquish [a belief] even after showing many reasons with difficulty, trouble, and hardship. This is a designation for those who, having firmly grasped the view that what has arisen in themselves is the truth, do not relinquish it even when told with reasons given by the Buddha and others.

For such individuals, whatever dharma or non-dharma they grasp, they all gather it inward like a tortoise gathering its limbs into its own shell, thinking, "Thus it was spoken by our teachers, thus it was heard by us," they grasp the alligator-grip and do not let go.

The bright side should be understood in the opposite way.

mula_pali: 84. ‘‘Cittuppādampi kho ahaṃ, cunda, kusalesu dhammesu bahukāraṃ bahūpakāraṃ (ka.) vadāmi, ko pana vādo kāyena vācāya anuvidhīyanāsu! Tasmātiha, cunda, ‘pare vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmā’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ. ‘Pare pāṇātipātī bhavissanti, mayamettha pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā bhavissāmā’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ…‘pare sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī bhavissanti, mayamettha asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī bhavissāmā’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.
mula_english:
84. Furthermore, I say, Cunda, that the arising of thought (*cittuppāda*) is very helpful with regard to wholesome qualities (*kusalesu dhammesu*), what then to say of conduct in body and speech! Therefore, Cunda, mind should be developed thus: ‘Others will be harmful (*vihiṃsakā bhavissanti*), but here we will be harmless (*avihiṃsakā bhavissāma*.’

‘Others will kill living beings (*pāṇātipātī bhavissanti*), but here we will abstain from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā bhavissāma*)’… ‘Others will adhere to their own views (*sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī*), hold on to them tenaciously (*ādhānaggāhī*), and relinquish them with difficulty (*duppaṭinissaggī bhavissanti*); we shall not adhere to our own views (*asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī*) or hold on to them tenaciously (*anādhānaggāhī*), but shall relinquish them easily (*suppaṭinissaggī bhavissāmā*)’: mind should be developed thus.
commentary_pali:
84. Evaṃ catucattālīsāya ākārehi sallekhaṃ dassetvā idāni tasmiṃ sallekhe cittuppādassāpi bahūpakārataṃ dassetuṃ cittuppādampi kho ahantiādimāha.

Tassattho , ahaṃ, cunda, kusalesu dhammesu cittuppādampi bahūpakāraṃ vadāmi, yā panetā kāyena ca vācāya ca anuvidhiyanā, yathā paṭhamaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ, tatheva tesaṃ dhammānaṃ kāyena karaṇaṃ, vācāya ca ‘‘karothā’’ti āṇāpanaṃ vā, uggahaparipucchādīni vā, tattha vādoyeva ko, ekantabahūpakārāyeva hi tā anuvidhiyanāti dasseti. Kasmā panettha cittuppādopi bahūpakāroti? Ekantahitasukhāvahattā anuvidhiyanānaṃ hetuttā ca.

‘‘Dānaṃ dassāmī’’ti hi cittuppādo sayampi ekantahitasukhāvaho anuvidhiyanānampi hetu, evañhi uppannacittattāyeva dutiyadivase mahāvīthiṃ pidahitvā mahāmaṇḍapaṃ katvā bhikkhusatassa vā bhikkhusahassassa vā dānaṃ deti, ‘‘bhikkhusaṅghaṃ nimantetha pūjetha parivisathā’’ti parijane āṇāpeti. Evaṃ ‘‘saṅghassa cīvaraṃ senāsanaṃ bhesajjaṃ dassāmī’’ti cittuppādo sayampi ekantahitasukhāvaho anuvidhiyanānampi hetu, evaṃ uppannacittattāyeva hi cīvarādīni abhisaṅkharoti deti dāpeti ca. Esa nayo saraṇagamanādīsu.

‘‘Saraṇaṃ gacchāmī’’ti hi cittaṃ uppādetvāva pacchā kāyena vā vācāya vā saraṇaṃ gaṇhāti. Tathā ‘‘pañcaṅgaṃ aṭṭhaṅgaṃ dasaṅgaṃ vā sīlaṃ samādiyissāmī’’ti cittaṃ uppādetvā kāyena vā vācāya vā samādiyati, ‘‘pabbajitvā catūsu sīlesu patiṭṭhahissāmī’’ti ca cittaṃ uppādetvā kāyena vācāya ca pūretabbaṃ sīlaṃ pūreti. ‘‘Buddhavacanaṃ uggahessāmī’’ti cittaṃ uppādetvāva ekaṃ vā nikāyaṃ dve vā tayo vā cattāro vā pañca vā nikāye vācāya uggaṇhāti. Evaṃ dhutaṅgasamādāna-kammaṭṭhānuggaha-kasiṇaparikamma-jhānasamāpattivipassanāmaggaphala- paccekabodhi-sammāsambodhivasena netabbaṃ.

‘‘Buddho bhavissāmī’’ti hi cittuppādo sayampi ekantahitasukhāvaho anuvidhiyanānampi hetu, evañhi uppannacittattāyeva aparena samayena kappasatasahassādhikāni cattāri asaṅkheyyāni kāyena vācāya ca pāramiyo pūretvā sadevakaṃ lokaṃ tārento vicarati. Evaṃ sabbattha cittuppādopi bahūpakāro. Kāyavācāhi pana anuvidhiyanā atibahūpakārāyevāti veditabbā.

Evaṃ kusalesu dhammesu cittuppādassāpi bahūpakārataṃ dassetvā idāni tattha niyojento ‘‘tasmā tiha cundā’’tiādimāha. Taṃ atthato pākaṭameva.
commentary_english:
Thus, having shown clearly with forty-four aspects the *sallekha* [practice of mental cultivation], now, in order to show the great usefulness of even the arising of thought in that *sallekha*, [the text] says, "Even the arising of thought, indeed…" and so on.

The meaning of this is: I, Cunda, declare that even the arising of thought is of great use in wholesome *dharmas*. That which is conforming conduct by body and speech, just as the first thought arises, so also is the act done by the body with regard to those *dharmas*, and the command "Do thus!" by speech, or study, questioning, and so on. What need to mention it there? Indeed, it shows that those conforming behaviors are solely of great use.

Why is the arising of thought here of great use? Because it is exclusively the bringer of benefit and happiness, and because it is the cause of conforming conduct.

"I will give a gift (dānaṁ dassāmī)," thus indeed, the arising of thought itself is exclusively the bringer of benefit and happiness, and is also the cause of conforming conduct. Thus indeed, because of the arising of thought, on the second day having closed off the great street, having made a great pavilion, he gives a gift to a hundred or a thousand monks, he commands his attendants, "Invite the monastic Saṃgha, honor them, serve them."

Thus, "I will give robes, lodging, medicine to the Saṃgha (saṅghassa cīvaraṃ senāsanaṃ bhesajjaṃ dassāmī)," thus the arising of thought itself is exclusively the bringer of benefit and happiness, and is also the cause of conforming conduct. Thus indeed, because of the arising of such thought, he prepares robes and so on, he gives, and causes [others] to give.

This is the method with regard to going for refuge and so on.

"I go for refuge (saraṇaṃ gacchāmī)," thus indeed, having produced the thought, afterwards by body or by speech, he takes refuge.

Thus, "I will undertake the precepts, five-membered, eight-membered, or ten-membered (pañcaṅgaṃ aṭṭhaṅgaṃ dasaṅgaṃ vā sīlaṃ samādiyissāmī)," thus having produced the thought, by body or by speech he undertakes it; "Having gone forth, I will be established in the four moralities (catūsu sīlesu patiṭṭhahissāmī)," and thus having produced the thought, he fulfills the morality which should be fulfilled by body and speech.

"I will learn the word of the Buddha (buddhavacanaṃ uggahessāmī)," thus having produced the thought, either one Nikāya, two, three, four, or five Nikāyas he learns by speech.

Thus, it should be led according to ascetic practices (dhutaṅga), undertaking (*samādāna*), the basis of action (*kammaṭṭhāna*), support (*anuggaha*), preliminary work on the *kasiṇa*, absorption in *jhāna*, attainment (*samāpatti*), insight (*vipassanā*), path (*magga*) and fruit (*phala*), solitary awakening (*paccekabodhi*), and perfect complete enlightenment (*sammāsambodhi*).

"I will become a Buddha (buddho bhavissāmī)," thus indeed, the arising of thought itself is exclusively the bringer of benefit and happiness, and is also the cause of conforming conduct. Thus indeed, because of the arising of such thought, after another time, for four incalculable [periods], exceeding a hundred thousand aeons, having perfected the perfections (pāramiyo) by body and speech, he wanders, saving the world together with the *devas*.

Thus, everywhere even the arising of thought is of great use.

But conforming conduct by body and speech, it should be understood, is exceedingly useful.

Thus, having shown the great usefulness of even the arising of thought in the wholesome *dharmas*, now, enjoining there, [the text] says, "Therefore, here, Cunda…" and so on.

That is clear in meaning.

mula_pali:
85. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, cunda, visamo maggo assa, tassa maggo tassāssa (sī. syā. pī.) añño samo maggo parikkamanāya; seyyathā vā pana, cunda, visamaṃ titthaṃ assa, tassa aññaṃ samaṃ titthaṃ parikkamanāya; evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa avihiṃsā hoti parikkamanāya, pāṇātipātissa purisapuggalassa pāṇātipātā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, adinnādāyissa purisapuggalassa adinnādānā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, abrahmacārissa purisapuggalassa abrahmacariyā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya , musāvādissa purisapuggalassa musāvādā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, pisuṇavācassa purisapuggalassa pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, pharusavācassa purisapuggalassa pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, samphappalāpissa purisapuggalassa samphappalāpā veramaṇī hoti parikkamanāya, abhijjhālussa purisapuggalassa anabhijjhā hoti parikkamanāya, byāpannacittassa purisapuggalassa abyāpādo hoti parikkamanāya, micchādiṭṭhissa purisapuggalassa sammādiṭṭhi hoti parikkamanāya, micchāsaṅkappassa purisapuggalassa sammāsaṅkappo hoti parikkamanāya, micchāvācassa purisapuggalassa sammāvācā hoti parikkamanāya, micchākammantassa purisapuggalassa sammākammanto hoti parikkamanāya, micchāājīvassa purisapuggalassa sammāājīvo hoti parikkamanāya, micchāvāyāmassa purisapuggalassa sammāvāyāmo hoti parikkamanāya, micchāsatissa purisapuggalassa sammāsati hoti parikkamanāya, micchāsamādhissa purisapuggalassa sammāsamādhi hoti parikkamanāya, micchāñāṇissa purisapuggalassa sammāñāṇaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, micchāvimuttissa purisapuggalassa sammāvimutti hoti parikkamanāya.

‘‘Thīnamiddhapariyuṭṭhitassa purisapuggalassa vigatathinamiddhatā hoti parikkamanāya, uddhatassa purisapuggalassa anuddhaccaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, vicikicchissa purisapuggalassa tiṇṇavicikicchatā hoti parikkamanāya, kodhanassa purisapuggalassa akkodho hoti parikkamanāya, upanāhissa purisapuggalassa anupanāho hoti parikkamanāya, makkhissa purisapuggalassa amakkho hoti parikkamanāya, paḷāsissa purisapuggalassa apaḷāso hoti parikkamanāya , issukissa purisapuggalassa anissukitā hoti parikkamanāya, maccharissa purisapuggalassa amacchariyaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, saṭhassa purisapuggalassa asāṭheyyaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, māyāvissa purisapuggalassa amāyā amāyāvitā (ka.) hoti parikkamanāya, thaddhassa purisapuggalassa atthaddhiyaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, atimānissa purisapuggalassa anatimāno hoti parikkamanāya, dubbacassa purisapuggalassa sovacassatā hoti parikkamanāya, pāpamittassa purisapuggalassa kalyāṇamittatā hoti parikkamanāya, pamattassa purisapuggalassa appamādo hoti parikkamanāya, assaddhassa purisapuggalassa saddhā hoti parikkamanāya, ahirikassa purisapuggalassa hirī hoti parikkamanāya, anottāpissa purisapuggalassa ottappaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, appassutassa purisapuggalassa bāhusaccaṃ hoti parikkamanāya, kusītassa purisapuggalassa vīriyārambho hoti parikkamanāya, muṭṭhassatissa purisapuggalassa upaṭṭhitassatitā hoti parikkamanāya, duppaññassa purisapuggalassa paññāsampadā hoti parikkamanāya , sandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-ādhānaggāhi-duppaṭinissaggissa purisapuggalassa asandiṭṭhiparāmāsianādhānaggāhi-suppaṭinissaggitā hoti parikkamanāya.

amāyāvitā (ka.)
mula_english:
85. “Cunda, suppose there were an uneven path and another even path by which to avoid it; and suppose there were an uneven ford and another even ford by which to avoid it. So too: A person given to cruelty has non-cruelty by which to avoid it. One given to killing living beings has abstention from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā veramaṇī) by which to avoid it. One given to taking what is not given has abstention from taking what is not given (adinnādānā veramaṇī) by which to avoid it. One given to be uncelibate has celibacy (abrahmacariyā veramaṇī) by which to avoid it, One given to lying has abstention from lying (musāvādā veramaṇī) by which to avoid it, One given to malicious speech has abstention from malicious speech (pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī) by which to avoid it, One given to harsh speech has abstention from harsh speech (pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī) by which to avoid it, One given to idle chatter has abstention from idle chatter (samphappalāpā veramaṇī) by which to avoid it, One given to covetousness has non-covetousness (anabhijjhā) by which to avoid it, One with a malicious mind has non-malice (abyāpādo) by which to avoid it, One with wrong view has right view (sammādiṭṭhi) by which to avoid it, One with wrong resolve has right resolve (sammāsaṅkappo) by which to avoid it, One with wrong speech has right speech (sammāvācā) by which to avoid it, One with wrong action has right action (sammākammanto) by which to avoid it, One with wrong livelihood has right livelihood (sammāājīvo) by which to avoid it, One with wrong effort has right effort (sammāvāyāmo) by which to avoid it, One with wrong mindfulness has right mindfulness (sammāsati) by which to avoid it, One with wrong concentration has right concentration (sammāsamādhi) by which to avoid it, One with wrong knowledge has right knowledge (sammāñāṇaṃ) by which to avoid it, One with wrong liberation has right liberation (sammāvimutti) by which to avoid it.

One given to sloth and torpor has freedom from sloth and torpor (vigatathinamiddhatā) by which to avoid it. One given to restlessness has non-restlessness (anuddhaccaṃ) by which to avoid it. One given to doubt has the state beyond doubt (tiṇṇavicikicchatā) by which to avoid it. One given to anger has non-anger (akkodho) by which to avoid it. One given to revenge has non-revenge (anupanāho) by which to avoid it. One given to contempt has non-contempt (amakkho) by which to avoid it. One given to a domineering attitude has a non-domineering attitude (apaḷāso) by which to avoid it, One given to envy has non-envy (anissukitā) by which to avoid it, One given to stinginess has non-stinginess (amacchariyaṃ) by which to avoid it, One given to deceit has non-deceit (asāṭheyyaṃ) by which to avoid it, One given to craftiness has non-craftiness (amāyā) by which to avoid it, One given to stubbornness has non-stubbornness (atthaddhiyaṃ) by which to avoid it, One given to conceit has non-conceit (anatimāno) by which to avoid it, One given to disobedience has obedience (sovacassatā) by which to avoid it, One given to bad friends has good friends (kalyāṇamittatā) by which to avoid it, One given to negligence has diligence (appamādo) by which to avoid it, One given to faithlessness has faith (saddhā) by which to avoid it, One given to shamelessness has shame (hirī) by which to avoid it, One given to recklessness has scruple (ottappaṃ) by which to avoid it, One with little learning has great learning (bāhusaccaṃ) by which to avoid it, One given to laziness has arousal of energy (vīriyārambho) by which to avoid it, One with confused mindfulness has established mindfulness (upaṭṭhitassatitā) by which to avoid it, One with lack of wisdom has accomplishment of wisdom (paññāsampadā) by which to avoid it, One given to adhere to his own views, who holds on to them tenaciously and relinquishes them with difficulty, has non-adherence to his own views, not holding on to them tenaciously and relinquishing them easily (asandiṭṭhiparāmāsianādhānaggāhi-suppaṭinissaggitā) by which to extinguish it.
commentary_pali:
85. Evaṃ catucattālīsāya ākārehi dassite sallekhe cittuppādassāpi bahūpakārataṃ dassetvā idāni tasseva sallekhassa hitādhigamāya maggabhāvaṃ dassento seyyathāpītiādimāha.

Tassattho , yathā nāma, cunda, khāṇukaṇṭakapāsāṇādīhi visamo maggo bhaveyya, tassa parikkamanāya parivajjanatthāya añño suparikammakato viya bhūmibhāgo samo maggo bhaveyya, yathā ca rukkhamūlapāsāṇapapātakumbhīlamakarādi paribyākulaṃ visamaṃ titthamassa, tassa parikkamanāya parivajjanatthāya aññaṃ avisamaṃ anupubbagambhīraṃ sopānaphalakasadisaṃ titthaṃ bhaveyya, yaṃ paṭipanno sukheneva taṃ nadiṃ vā taḷākaṃ vā ajjhogāhetvā nhāyeyya vā uttareyya vā, evameva kho, cunda, visamamaggavisamatitthasadisāya vihiṃsāya samannāgatassa vihiṃsakapuggalassa samamaggasamatitthasadisā avihiṃsā hoti parikkamanāya. Yatheva hi visamamaggatitthaparivajjanatthāya samo maggo ca titthañca paṭiyattaṃ, evaṃ vihiṃsāparivajjanatthāya avihiṃsā paṭiyattā, yaṃ paṭipanno sukheneva manussagatiṃ vā devagatiṃ vā ajjhogāhetvā sampattiṃ vā anubhaveyya uttareyya vā lokā. Eteneva upāyena sabbapadāni yojetabbāni.
commentary_english:
85. Thus, having shown in forty-four ways the sallekha’s great assistance to the arising of the mind, now, showing the path-nature of that same sallekha for the attainment of benefit, he says, “*seyyathāpī*tiādi.”

Its meaning [is as follows]: Just as, Cunda, there might be a rough path with stumps, thorns, stones, and so on; for going around that, for avoiding it, there might be another level ground, a smooth path, as it were, well-prepared. And just as a landing place might be rough, confused with tree roots, stones, precipices, crocodiles, makaras, and so on; for going around that, for avoiding it, there might be another even landing place, gradually deep, like a step-stone, where one who has undertaken it, easily entering that river or that pond, might bathe or cross over. Just so, Cunda, non-violence, like a smooth path and a smooth landing place, is for the violent person who is endowed with violence like a rough path and a rough landing place, for going around. Just as a smooth path and a landing place are prepared for avoiding a rough path and landing place, so non-violence is prepared for avoiding violence, where one who has undertaken it, easily entering human existence or divine existence, might experience prosperity or cross over the world. In this way, all the words should be connected.

mula_pali: 86. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, cunda, ye keci akusalā dhammā sabbe te adhobhāgaṅgamanīyā adhobhāvaṅgamanīyā (sī. syā. pī.), ye keci kusalā dhammā sabbe te uparibhāgaṅgamanīyā uparibhāvaṅgamanīyā (sī. syā. pī.), evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa avihiṃsā hoti uparibhāgāya uparibhāvāya (sī. syā. ka.), pāṇātipātissa purisapuggalassa pāṇātipātā veramaṇī hoti uparibhāgāya…pe… sandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-ādhānaggāhi-duppaṭinissaggissa purisapuggalassa asandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-anādhānaggāhi-suppaṭinissaggitā hoti uparibhāgāya.
mula_english: 86. Just as, Cunda, all unwholesome *dharmas* lead downwards (adhobhāgaṅgamanīyā), all wholesome *dharmas* lead upwards (uparibhāgaṅgamanīyā), so too, Cunda, for a person given to violence, non-violence (*avihiṃsā*) leads upwards; for a person given to taking life, abstaining from taking life (*pāṇātipātā veramaṇī*) leads upwards... for a person who adheres to his own views (*sandiṭṭhiparāmāsi*), holds on to them tenaciously (*ādhānaggāhi*), and relinquishes them with difficulty (*duppaṭinissaggi*), non-adherence to his own views (*asandiṭṭhiparāmāsi*), not holding on to them tenaciously (*anādhānaggāhi*), and relinquishing them easily (*suppaṭinissaggitā*) leads upwards.
commentary_pali:
86. Evaṃ tasseva hitādhigamāya maggabhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni uparibhāgaṅgamanīyataṃ dassento, seyyathāpītiādimāha.

Tassattho, yathā nāma, cunda, ye keci akusalā dhammā paṭisandhiyā janakā vā ajanakā vā, dinnāyapi paṭisandhiyā vipākajanakā vā ajanakā vā, sabbe te jātivasena adhobhāgaṅgamanīyāti evaṃnāmāva honti, vipākakāle aniṭṭhākantavipākattā. Yathā ca ye keci kusalā dhammā paṭisandhiyā janakā vā ajanakā vā dinnāyapi paṭisandhiyā vipākajanakā vā ajanakā vā, sabbe te jātivasena uparibhāgaṅgamanīyāti evaṃnāmāva honti, vipākakāle iṭṭhakantavipākattā, evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa…pe… uparibhāgāyāti. Tatrāyaṃ opammasaṃsandanā – yathā sabbe akusalā adhobhāgaṅgamanīyā, evaṃ vihiṃsakassa ekā vihiṃsāpi. Yathā ca sabbe kusalā uparibhāgaṅgamanīyā, evaṃ avihiṃsakassa ekā avihiṃsāpi. Eteneva upāyena akusalaṃ akusalena kusalañca kusalena upametabbaṃ, ayaṃ kirettha adhippāyoti.
commentary_english:
86. Thus, having shown the path for attaining that same benefit, now, showing the quality of leading to the upper realms, he says, beginning with, "Just as."

Its meaning is: Just as, Cunda, whatever unwholesome dharmas, whether generative or non-generative of rebirth, whether generative or non-generative of result after rebirth has been given, all of them, by their very nature, are called "leading to the lower realms," because their result is undesirable and unpleasant at the time of fruition.

And just as whatever wholesome dharmas, whether generative or non-generative of rebirth, whether generative or non-generative of result after rebirth has been given, all of them, by their very nature, are called "leading to the upper realms," because their result is desirable and pleasant at the time of fruition, just so, Cunda, for the violent…pe… to the upper realms.

Here is the connection to the simile: Just as all unwholesome [things] lead to the lower realms, so too does even a single act of violence of a violent person. And just as all wholesome [things] lead to the upper realms, so too does even a single act of non-violence of a non-violent person. In this way, the unwholesome should be compared with the unwholesome, and the wholesome with the wholesome; this, it seems, is the intention here.

mula_pali:
87. ‘‘So vata, cunda, attanā palipapalipanno paraṃ palipapalipannaṃ uddharissatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vata, cunda, attanā apalipapalipanno paraṃ palipapalipannaṃ uddharissatīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. So vata, cunda, attanā adanto avinīto aparinibbuto paraṃ damessati vinessati parinibbāpessatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vata , cunda, attanā danto vinīto parinibbuto paraṃ damessati vinessati parinibbāpessatīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa avihiṃsā hoti parinibbānāya, pāṇātipātissa purisapuggalassa pāṇātipātā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Adinnādāyissa purisapuggalassa adinnādānā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Abrahmacārissa purisapuggalassa abrahmacariyā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Musāvādissa purisapuggalassa musāvādā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Pisuṇavācassa purisapuggalassa pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Pharusavācassa purisapuggalassa pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Samphappalāpissa purisapuggalassa samphappalāpā veramaṇī hoti parinibbānāya. Abhijjhālussa purisapuggalassa anabhijjhā hoti parinibbānāya. Byāpannacittassa purisapuggalassa abyāpādo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchādiṭṭhissa purisapuggalassa sammādiṭṭhi hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāsaṅkappassa purisapuggalassa sammāsaṅkappo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāvācassa purisapuggalassa sammāvācā hoti parinibbānāya. Micchākammantassa purisapuggalassa sammākammanto hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāājīvassa purisapuggalassa sammāājīvo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāvāyāmassa purisapuggalassa sammāvāyāmo hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāsatissa purisapuggalassa sammāsati hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāsamādhissa purisapuggalassa sammāsamādhi hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāñāṇissa purisapuggalassa sammāñāṇaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Micchāvimuttissa purisapuggalassa sammāvimutti hoti parinibbānāya.

‘‘Thīnamiddhapariyuṭṭhitassa purisapuggalassa vigatathinamiddhatā hoti parinibbānāya. Uddhatassa purisapuggalassa anuddhaccaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Vicikicchissa purisapuggalassa tiṇṇavicikicchatā hoti parinibbānāya. Kodhanassa purisapuggalassa akkodho hoti parinibbānāya. Upanāhissa purisapuggalassa anupanāho hoti parinibbānāya. Makkhissa purisapuggalassa amakkho hoti parinibbānāya. Paḷāsissa purisapuggalassa apaḷāso hoti parinibbānāya. Issukissa purisapuggalassa anissukitā hoti parinibbānāya. Maccharissa purisapuggalassa amacchariyaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Saṭhassa purisapuggalassa asāṭheyyaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Māyāvissa purisapuggalassa amāyā hoti parinibbānāya. Thaddhassa purisapuggalassa atthaddhiyaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Atimānissa purisapuggalassa anatimāno hoti parinibbānāya. Dubbacassa purisapuggalassa sovacassatā hoti parinibbānāya. Pāpamittassa purisapuggalassa kalyāṇamittatā hoti parinibbānāya. Pamattassa purisapuggalassa appamādo hoti parinibbānāya. Assaddhassa purisapuggalassa saddhā hoti parinibbānāya. Ahirikassa purisapuggalassa hirī hoti parinibbānāya. Anottāpissa purisapuggalassa ottappaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Appassutassa purisapuggalassa bāhusaccaṃ hoti parinibbānāya. Kusītassa purisapuggalassa vīriyārambho hoti parinibbānāya. Muṭṭhassatissa purisapuggalassa upaṭṭhitassatitā hoti parinibbānāya. Duppaññassa purisapuggalassa paññāsampadā hoti parinibbānāya. Sandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-ādhānaggāhi-duppaṭinissaggissa purisapuggalassa asandiṭṭhiparāmāsi-anādhānaggāhi-suppaṭinissaggitā hoti parinibbānāya.
mula_english:
87. “Cunda, that one who is himself sinking in the mud should pull out another who is sinking in the mud is impossible; but that one who is himself not sinking in the mud should pull out another who is sinking in the mud is possible.

Cunda, that one who is himself untamed, undisciplined, with defilements unextinguished, should tame another, discipline him, and help extinguish his defilements is impossible; but that one who is himself tamed, disciplined, with defilements extinguished, should tame another, discipline him, and help extinguish his defilements is possible.

So too: A person given to cruelty (*vihiṃsaka*) has non-cruelty (*avihiṃsā*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One given to killing living beings (*pāṇātipātin*) has abstention from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā veramaṇī*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One given to taking what is not given (*adinnādāyin*) has abstention from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā veramaṇī*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One given to be unchaste (*abrahmacārin*) has celibacy (*abrahmacariyā veramaṇī*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One given to lying (*musāvādin*) has abstention from lying (*musāvādā veramaṇī*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One given to divisive speech (*pisuṇavāca*) has abstention from divisive speech (*pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One given to harsh speech (*pharusavāca*) has abstention from harsh speech (*pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One given to idle chatter (*samphappalāpin*) has abstention from idle chatter (*samphappalāpā veramaṇī*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One who is covetous (*abhijjhālu*) has non-covetousness (*anabhijjhā*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with a mind full of ill-will (*byāpannacitta*) has non-ill-will (*abyāpādo*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*) has right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong intention (*micchāsaṅkappa*) has right intention (*sammāsaṅkappo*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong speech (*micchāvāca*) has right speech (*sammāvācā*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong action (*micchākammanta*) has right action (*sammākammanto*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong livelihood (*micchāājīva*) has right livelihood (*sammāājīvo*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong effort (*micchāvāyāma*) has right effort (*sammāvāyāmo*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong mindfulness (*micchāsati*) has right mindfulness (*sammāsati*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong concentration (*micchāsamādhi*) has right concentration (*sammāsamādhi*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong knowledge (*micchāñāṇa*) has right knowledge (*sammāñāṇaṃ*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). One with wrong liberation (*micchāvimutti*) has right liberation (*sammāvimutti*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*).

A person overcome by sloth and torpor (*thīnamiddhapariyuṭṭhita*) has the dispelling of sloth and torpor (*vigatathinamiddhatā*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is restless (*uddhatassa*) has non-restlessness (*anuddhaccaṃ*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is doubtful (*vicikicchissa*) has overcoming doubt (*tiṇṇavicikicchatā*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is angry (*kodhana*) has non-anger (*akkodho*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is bearing grudges (*upanāhin*) has non-grudge-bearing (*anupanāho*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is disparaging (*makkhin*) has non-disparagement (*amakkho*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is insolent (*paḷāsin*) has non-insolence (*apaḷāso*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is jealous (*issukin*) has non-jealousy (*anissukitā*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is stingy (*maccharin*) has non-stinginess (*amacchariyaṃ*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is deceitful (*saṭha*) has non-deceitfulness (*asāṭheyyaṃ*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*). A person who is scheming (*māyāvin*) has non-scheming (*amāyā*) by which to extinguish it (for *parinirvāṇa*).
For a stubborn person, there is non-stubbornness by which to extinguish it.
For an arrogant person, there is non-arrogance by which to extinguish it.
For an obstinate person, there is obedience by which to extinguish it.
For a person with bad friends, there is good friendship by which to extinguish it.
For a negligent person, there is diligence by which to extinguish it.
For a faithless person, there is faith (*śraddhā*) by which to extinguish it.
For a shameless person, there is shame (*hrī*) by which to extinguish it.
For an unscrupulous person, there is scruple (*otappaṃ*) by which to extinguish it.
For an unlearned person, there is great learning (*bāhusaccaṃ*) by which to extinguish it.
For a lazy person, there is energetic effort (*vīriyārambho*) by which to extinguish it.
For a person with confused mindfulness, there is established mindfulness (*upaṭṭhitassatitā*) by which to extinguish it.
For an unwise person, there is accomplishment in wisdom (*paññāsampadā*) by which to extinguish it.
For a person given to adhering to his own views, who holds on to them tenaciously and relinquishes them with difficulty, there is non-adherence to his own views, not holding on to them tenaciously and relinquishing them easily, by which to extinguish it.
commentary_pali:
87. Evaṃ tasseva sallekhassa uparibhāgaṅgamanīyataṃ dassetvā idāni parinibbāpane samatthabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ so vata cundātiādimāha. Tattha soti vuttappakārapuggalaniddeso. Tassa yoti imaṃ uddesavacanaṃ āharitvā yo attanā palipapalipanno, so vata, cunda, paraṃ palipapalipannaṃ uddharissatīti evaṃ sabbapadesu sambandho veditabbo. Palipapalipannoti gambhīrakaddame nimuggo vuccati, no ca kho ariyassa vinaye. Ariyassa pana vinaye palipanti pañca kāmaguṇā vuccanti. Palipannoti tattha nimuggo bālaputhujjano, tasmā evamettha atthayojanā veditabbā. Yathā, cunda, koci puriso yāva nāsikaggā gambhīre kaddame nimuggo aparaṃ tattheva nimuggaṃ hatthe vā sīse vā gahetvā uddharissatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati, na hi taṃ kāraṇamatthi, yena so taṃ uddharitvā thale patiṭṭhapeyya, evameva yo attanā pañcakāmaguṇapalipe palipanno, so vata paraṃ tatheva palipapalipannaṃ uddharissatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

Tattha siyā ayuttametaṃ, puthujjanānampi bhikkhubhikkhunīupāsakaupāsikānaṃ dhammadesanaṃ sutvā hontiyeva dhammaṃ abhisametāro, tasmā palipapalipanno uddharatīti, taṃ na tathā daṭṭhabbaṃ. Bhagavāyeva hi tattha uddharati, pasaṃsāmattameva pana dhammakathikā labhanti raññā pahitalekhavācako viya. Yathā hi rañño paccantajanapade pahitaṃ lekhaṃ tattha manussā lekhaṃ vācetuṃ ajānantā yo vācetuṃ jānāti, tena vācāpetvā tamatthaṃ sutvā ‘‘rañño āṇā’’ti ādarena sampādenti, na ca nesaṃ hoti ‘‘lekhavācakassa ayaṃ āṇā’’ti. Lekhavācako pana ‘‘vissaṭṭhāya vācāya vācesi anelagaḷāyā’’ti pasaṃsāmattameva labhati, evameva kiñcāpi sāriputtapabhutayo dhammakathikā dhammaṃ desenti, atha kho likhitapaṇṇavācako viya te honti. Bhagavatoyeva pana sā dhammadesanā rañño āṇā viya. Ye ca taṃ sutvā dhammaṃ abhisamenti, te bhagavāyeva uddharatīti veditabbā. Dhammakathikā pana ‘‘vissaṭṭhāya vācāya dhammaṃ desenti anelagaḷāyā’’ti pasaṃsāmattameva labhantīti. Tasmā yuttamevetanti. Vuttavipariyāyena sukkapakkho veditabbo.

Adantoavinīto aparinibbutoti ettha pana anibbisatāya adanto. Asikkhitavinayatāya avinīto. Anibbutakilesatāya aparinibbutoti veditabbo. So tādiso paraṃ damessati, nibbisaṃ karissati , vinessati vā tisso sikkhā sikkhāpessati, parinibbāpessati vā tassa kilese nibbāpessatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Vuttavipariyāyena sukkapakkho veditabbo.

Adanto avinīto aparinibbuto adanto avinīto aparinibbuto

Evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa…pe… parinibbānāyāti ettha pana evamattho veditabbo – yathā hi attanā apalipapalipanno paraṃ palipapalipannaṃ uddharissati, danto damessati, vinīto vinessati, parinibbuto parinibbāpessatīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjatīti. Kiṃ pana tanti? Apalipapalipannattaṃ, dantattaṃ vinītattaṃ parinibbutattañca, evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa avihiṃsā hoti parinibbānāya. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Yo attanā avihiṃsako, tassa yā avihiṃsā, ayaṃ yā esā vihiṃsakassa parassa vihiṃsā, tassā parinibbānāya hoti, attanā hi avihiṃsako parassa vihiṃsācetanaṃ nibbāpessatīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Kiṃ pana tanti? Avihiṃsakattameva. Yañhi yena attanā adhigataṃ hoti, so paraṃ tadatthāya samādapetuṃ sakkotīti.

Evameva kho, cunda, vihiṃsakassa…pe… parinibbānāyā

Atha vā yathā attanā apalipanno danto vinīto parinibbuto paraṃ palipapalipannaṃ adantaṃ avinītaṃ aparinibbutañca uddharissati damessati vinessati parinibbāpessatīti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati, evameva vihiṃsakassa purisapuggalassa vihiṃsāpahānāya maggaṃ bhāvayato uppannā avihiṃsā hoti parinibbānāya. Parinibbuto viya hi aparinibbutaṃ avihiṃsācetanāva vihiṃsācetanaṃ parinibbāpetuṃ samatthā. Etamatthaṃ dassento ‘‘evameva kho, cundā’’tiādimāhāti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Yathā cettha, evaṃ sabbapadesu. Ativitthārabhayena pana anupadayojanā na katāti.
commentary_english:
87. Thus, having shown the attainability of the superior state of that *sallekha*, now, in order to show the capability of complete *nirvāṇa*, [he] says, "<*So vata cundā*>," and so forth.

There, "*so*" indicates the designation of a person of the aforementioned kind.

Having brought forth this statement of purpose, "*yo*," whoever is himself mired in the mire, "*so vata*, Cunda, will lift up another who is mired in the mire," thus, the connection should be understood in all the wordings.

"*Palipapalipanno*" means sunk in deep mud, it is said, but not in the discipline of the noble ones (*ārya*).

But in the discipline of the noble ones, "*palipa*" means the five sensual qualities, it is said.

"*Palipanno*" means a fool, an ordinary person, sunk there; therefore, thus the interpretation of the meaning here should be understood.

Just as, Cunda, a certain man sunk in deep mud up to the tip of his nose would lift up another sunk in that same mud by grasping his hand or head, that is not possible, there is no such possibility. For how could he lift him up and establish him on dry land? Just so, whoever is himself mired in the mire of the five sensual qualities, that one will lift up another who is likewise sunk in the mire, this is not possible.

There, it might be objected, "This is inappropriate. Even ordinary people, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, having heard the teaching of the Dharma, are indeed able to comprehend the Dharma. Therefore, [it is said that] one mired in the mire lifts up [another]," but that is not how it should be viewed.

For the Blessed One (*bhagavān*) himself lifts [them] up there; however, the teachers of the Dharma only obtain mere praise, like a letter-reader sent by the king.

Just as, indeed, a letter sent by the king to a border district, the people there, not knowing how to read the letter, have it read by someone who knows how to read it, and having heard its meaning, they respectfully carry out the "*āṇā*" (command) of the king, but for them there is no "*ayaṃ āṇā*" (this is the command) of the letter-reader.

The letter-reader, however, obtains only mere praise, "*vissaṭṭhāya vācāya vācesi anelagaḷāyā*," (he caused [it] to be read with a clear voice, without stammering). Just so, although Sāriputta and other teachers of the Dharma teach the Dharma, they are like letter-readers.

But that teaching of the Dharma is like the command of the king.

And those who, having heard that, comprehend the Dharma, it should be understood that the Blessed One (*bhagavān*) himself lifts [them] up.

The teachers of the Dharma, however, obtain only mere praise, "*vissaṭṭhāya vācāya dhammaṃ desenti anelagaḷāyā*," (they teach the Dharma with a clear voice, without stammering).

Therefore, it is indeed appropriate.

The bright side should be understood in the opposite way.

*Adanto avinīto aparinibbuto* (untamed, undisciplined, unreleased). Here, *adanto* (untamed) [is said] because of not being tamed.

*Avinīto* (undisciplined) because of lack of training in discipline.

*Aparinibbuto* (unreleased) should be understood as because of not extinguishing the defilements (*kleśa*).

Such a one will tame another, will make [him] calm, will discipline, will train [him in] the three trainings (*śikṣā*), or will completely release [him], will extinguish his defilements—this is not possible.

The bright side should be understood in the opposite way.

*Adanto avinīto aparinibbuto adanto avinīto aparinibbuto* (untamed, undisciplined, unreleased; untamed, undisciplined, unreleased).

"*Evameva kho, Cunda, vihiṃsakassa…pe… parinibbānāyā*" (Just so, Cunda, for the violent…pe… for final *nirvāṇa*). Here, however, this meaning should be understood: Just as one who is himself un-mired will lift up another who is mired, one who is tamed will tame, one who is disciplined will discipline, one who is released will completely release—this is possible.

What, then, is the reason? It is the state of being un-mired, the state of being tamed, the state of being disciplined, and the state of being released. Just so, Cunda, for the violent person, there is non-violence for final *nirvāṇa*.

What is said? For the one who is himself non-violent, that non-violence, this that is violence towards another for the violent person, is for final *nirvāṇa*. For one who is himself non-violent will extinguish the intention of violence towards another—this is possible.

What, then, is the reason? It is simply the state of being non-violent.

For whatever one has attained by oneself, that one is able to encourage another for that purpose.

"*Evameva kho, Cunda, vihiṃsakassa…pe… parinibbānāyā*" (Just so, Cunda, for the violent…pe… for final *nirvāṇa*).

Or, just as one who is himself un-mired, tamed, disciplined, released will lift up another who is mired, untamed, undisciplined, unreleased; will tame, will discipline, will completely release—this is possible. Just so, for the violent person, cultivating the path for the abandonment of violence, the non-violence that arises is for final *nirvāṇa*.

For, like one who is completely released, the intention of non-violence is able to completely release the intention of violence.

Showing this meaning, [he] says, ""*Evameva kho, Cunda*,"" and so forth. Thus, the meaning here should be understood.

As here, so in all the wordings.

However, for fear of excessive elaboration, the analysis has not been done step by step.

mula_pali:
88. ‘‘Iti kho, cunda, desito mayā sallekhapariyāyo, desito cittuppādapariyāyo, desito parikkamanapariyāyo, desito uparibhāgapariyāyo, desito parinibbānapariyāyo. Yaṃ kho, cunda, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā. ‘Etāni, cunda, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni, jhāyatha, cunda, mā pamādattha, mā pacchāvippaṭisārino ahuvattha’ – ayaṃ kho amhākaṃ anusāsanī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā mahācundo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Catuttālīsapadā vuttā, sandhayo pañca desitā;

Sallekho nāma suttanto, gambhīro sāgarūpamoti.

Sallekhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
88. “Thus, Cunda, the discourse on effacement (*sallekhapariyāya*) has been taught by me, the discourse on the arising of the mind (*cittuppādapariyāya*) has been taught by me, the discourse on avoidance (*parikkamanapariyāya*) has been taught by me, the discourse on the higher portion (*uparibhāgapariyāya*) has been taught by me, and the discourse on complete extinguishing (*parinibbānapariyāya*) has been taught by me.

Whatever should be done by a teacher, seeking the welfare of his disciples, out of compassion, that I have done for you, Cunda.

‘These are the roots of trees, these are empty huts. Meditate, Cunda, do not delay, or you will regret it later.’ This is our instruction to you.”

Thus spoke the Blessed One.

The venerable Mahācunda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

Forty-four verses were spoken, and five joining verses were taught;

The *sūtra* named "Effacement" is profound, like the ocean.

The eighth *sūtra*, "Effacement," is concluded.
commentary_pali:
88. Evaṃ tassa parinibbāpane samatthabhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni taṃ desanaṃ nigametvā dhammapaṭipattiyaṃ niyojetuṃ iti kho, cundātiādimāha. Tattha sallekhapariyāyoti sallekhakāraṇaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha ettha avihiṃsādayo eva vihiṃsādīnaṃ sallekhanato sallekhakāraṇaṃ . Tesaṃ vasena cittassa uppādetabbato cittupādakāraṇaṃ, vihiṃsādi, parikkamanassa hetuto parikkamanakāraṇaṃ, uparibhāganipphādanato uparibhāgakāraṇaṃ , vihiṃsādīnaṃ parinibbāpanato parinibbānakāraṇanti veditabbā. Hitesināti hitaṃ esantena. Anukampakenāti anukampamānena. Anukampaṃ upādāyāti anukampaṃ cittena pariggahetvā, pariccātipi vuttaṃ hoti. Kataṃ vo taṃ mayāti taṃ mayā ime pañca pariyāye dassentena tumhākaṃ kataṃ. Ettakameva hi anukampakassa satthu kiccaṃ, yadidaṃ aviparītadhammadesanā. Ito paraṃ pana paṭipatti nāma sāvakānaṃ kiccaṃ. Tenāha etāni, cunda, rukkhamūlāni…pe… amhākaṃ anusāsanīti.

Tattha ca rukkhamūlānīti iminā rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ dasseti. Suññāgārānīti iminā janavivittaṭṭhānaṃ. Ubhayenāpi ca yogānurūpasenāsanamācikkhati, dāyajjaṃ niyyāteti. Jhāyathāti ārammaṇūpanijjhānena aṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇāni, lakkhaṇūpanijjhānena ca aniccādito khandhāyatanādīni upanijjhāyatha, samathañca vipassanañca vaḍḍhethāti vuttaṃ hoti. Mā pamādatthāti mā pamajjittha. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvatthāti ye hi pubbe daharakāle, ārogyakāle, sattasappāyādisampattikāle, satthu sammukhībhāvakāle ca yonisomanasikāravirahitā rattindivaṃ maṅgulabhattā hutvā seyyasukhaṃ middhasukhamanubhontā pamajjanti, te pacchā jarākāle, rogakāle, maraṇakāle, vipattikāle, satthu parinibbutakāle ca taṃ pubbe pamādavihāraṃ anussarantā, sappaṭisandhikālakiriyañca bhāriyaṃ sampassamānā vippaṭisārino honti, tumhe pana tādisā mā ahuvatthāti etamatthaṃ dassento āha ‘‘mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvatthā’’ti. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanīti ayaṃ amhākaṃ santikā ‘‘jhāyatha mā pamādatthā’’ti tumhākaṃ anusāsanī, ovādoti vuttaṃ hoti.

rukkhamūlānī Suññāgārānī Jhāyathā Mā pamādatthā Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvatthā Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Sallekhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
88. Thus, having shown the capacity for his complete emancipation, now, in order to apply that teaching to the practice of Dharma, he said, "Thus, Cunda," and so on.

There, *sallekhapariyāyo* means the cause of refinement (*sallekhakāraṇaṃ*).

This is the method everywhere here: non-injury and so forth are indeed the cause of refinement because of the refinement of injury and so forth.

Because of the origination of the mind depending on them, it is the cause of the arising of the mind (*cittupādakāraṇaṃ*), [namely] injury and so forth; because of the reason for exertion, it is the cause of exertion (*parikkamanakāraṇaṃ*); because of the production of an upper portion, it is the cause of an upper portion (*uparibhāgakāraṇaṃ*), because of the complete emancipation of injury and so forth, it should be understood as the cause of complete emancipation (*parinibbānakāraṇaṃ*).

*hitesinā* means seeking benefit (*hitaṃ esantena*).

*anukampakenā* means being compassionate (*anukampamānena*).

*anukampaṃ upādāyā* means having taken up compassion with the mind (*anukampaṃ cittena pariggahetvā*), it is said to be also giving up (*pariccātipi vuttaṃ hoti*).

*kataṃ vo taṃ mayā* means that which was done by me, done by me showing these five methods (*taṃ mayā ime pañca pariyāye dassentena tumhākaṃ kataṃ*).

Indeed, the task of the compassionate teacher is only this: the teaching of the Dharma that is not reversed (*aviparītadhammadesanā*).

But from here on, practice (*paṭipatti*) is the task of the disciples (*sāvakānaṃ kiccaṃ*).

Therefore, he said, "These, Cunda, are the roots of trees...pe...our instruction (*amhākaṃ anusāsanī*)."

And there, *rukkhamūlānī* means he shows a dwelling at the root of a tree (*rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ dasseti*).

*suññāgārānī* means a place secluded from people (*janavivittaṭṭhānaṃ*).

And by both, he indicates a dwelling suitable for yoga (*yogānurūpasenāsanamācikkhati*), he bestows an inheritance (*dāyajjaṃ niyyāteti*).

*jhāyathā* means meditate (*ārammaṇūpanijjhānena aṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇāni*), and by contemplating the characteristics (*lakkhaṇūpanijjhānena*), contemplate impermanence and so forth, the aggregates, the sense bases and so forth (*aniccādito khandhāyatanādīni upanijjhāyatha*), it is said that one develops serenity and insight (*samathañca vipassanañca vaḍḍhethāti vuttaṃ hoti*).

*mā pamādatthā* means do not be negligent (*mā pamajjittha*).

*mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvatthā* means those who were previously negligent in their youth (*ye hi pubbe daharakāle*), in health (*ārogyakāle*), at the time of possessing suitable circumstances and so forth (*sattasappāyādisampattikāle*), at the time of facing the Teacher (*satthu sammukhībhāvakāle ca*), being without proper attention (*yonisomanasikāravirahitā*), having become gluttons day and night (*rattindivaṃ maṅgulabhattā hutvā*), enjoying the pleasure of lying down and the pleasure of sleep (*seyyasukhaṃ middhasukhamanubhontā pamajjanti*), they later, in old age (*jarākāle*), in sickness (*rogakāle*), at the time of death (*maraṇakāle*), at the time of misfortune (*vipattikāle*), and at the time of the Teacher's complete *nirvāṇa* (*satthu parinibbutakāle ca*) recalling that former conduct of negligence (*taṃ pubbe pamādavihāraṃ anussarantā*), and seeing the heavy burden of rebirth-linking activity (*sappaṭisandhikālakiriyañca bhāriyaṃ sampassamānā*), they are remorseful (*vippaṭisārino honti*), but do not be like that (*tumhe pana tādisā mā ahuvatthāti*), showing this meaning, he said, "Do not be remorseful later (*mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvatthā*)."

*ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī* means this is our instruction to you from us (*ayaṃ amhākaṃ santikā*), "Meditate, do not be negligent (*jhāyatha mā pamādatthā*)," this is your instruction, it is said to be advice (*ovādoti vuttaṃ hoti*).

The roots of trees, empty dwellings, meditate, do not be negligent, do not be remorseful later, this is our instruction to you.

The commentary on the *Sallekha Sutta* is finished.

mula_pali:
89. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘āvuso bhikkhave’’ti. ‘‘Āvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

‘‘‘Sammādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhī (sī. syā.) sammādiṭṭhī’ti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ujugatāssa diṭṭhi, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato, āgato imaṃ saddhamma’’nti?

sammādiṭṭhī (sī. syā.)

‘‘Dūratopi kho mayaṃ, āvuso, āgaccheyyāma āyasmato sāriputtassa santike etassa bhāsitassa atthamaññātuṃ. Sādhu vatāyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Āyasmato sāriputtassa sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, āvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

‘‘Yato kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako akusalañca pajānāti, akusalamūlañca pajānāti, kusalañca pajānāti, kusalamūlañca pajānāti – ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ujugatāssa diṭṭhi, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato, āgato imaṃ saddhammaṃ. Katamaṃ panāvuso, akusalaṃ, katamaṃ akusalamūlaṃ, katamaṃ kusalaṃ, katamaṃ kusalamūlaṃ? Pāṇātipāto kho, āvuso, akusalaṃ, adinnādānaṃ akusalaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro akusalaṃ, musāvādo akusalaṃ, pisuṇā vācā pisuṇavācā (ka.) akusalaṃ, pharusā vācā pharusavācā (ka.) akusalaṃ, samphappalāpo akusalaṃ, abhijjhā akusalaṃ, byāpādo akusalaṃ, micchādiṭṭhi akusalaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso akusalaṃ. Katamañcāvuso, akusalamūlaṃ? Lobho akusalamūlaṃ, doso akusalamūlaṃ, moho akusalamūlaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso, akusalamūlaṃ.

pisuṇavācā (ka.) pharusavācā (ka.)

‘‘Katamañcāvuso , kusalaṃ? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ, samphappalāpā veramaṇī kusalaṃ, anabhijjhā kusalaṃ, abyāpādo kusalaṃ, sammādiṭṭhi kusalaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso, kusalaṃ. Katamañcāvuso, kusalamūlaṃ? Alobho kusalamūlaṃ, adoso kusalamūlaṃ, amoho kusalamūlaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso, kusalamūlaṃ.

‘‘Yato kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako evaṃ akusalaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ akusalamūlaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ kusalaṃ pajānāti, evaṃ kusalamūlaṃ pajānāti, so sabbaso rāgānusayaṃ pahāya, paṭighānusayaṃ paṭivinodetvā, ‘asmī’ti diṭṭhimānānusayaṃ samūhanitvā, avijjaṃ pahāya vijjaṃ uppādetvā, diṭṭhevadhamme dukkhassantakaro hoti – ettāvatāpi kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ujugatāssa diṭṭhi, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato, āgato imaṃ saddhamma’’nti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Savatthi in the Jetavana in Anathapindika’s park.

There the venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Friends, bhikkhus.”

“Yes, friend,” the monks responded to venerable Sāriputta.

The venerable Sāriputta said this:

“‘Right view, right view’ is said, friends. In what way, friend, is a noble disciple one of right view, whose view is straight, who has perfect confidence in the Dhamma, and has arrived at this true Dhamma?”

“Indeed, friend, we would come from far away to learn from the Venerable Sariputta the meaning of this statement. It would be good if the venerable Sariputta would explain the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from him the bhikkhus will remember it.”

“Then, friends, listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, friend,” the bhikkhus replied to the venerable Sāriputta.

The venerable Sāriputta said this:

“When, friends, a noble disciple understands the unwholesome (*akuśala*), the root of the unwholesome (*akuśalamūla*), the wholesome (*kuśala*), and the root of the wholesome (*kuśalamūla*)—in that way he is one of right view, whose view is straight, who has perfect confidence in the Dhamma, and has arrived at this true Dhamma.

“And what, friend, is the unwholesome? What is the root of the unwholesome? What is the wholesome? What is the root of the wholesome? Killing living beings is unwholesome, taking what is not given is unwholesome, misconduct in sensual pleasures is unwholesome, false speech is unwholesome, malicious speech is unwholesome, harsh speech is unwholesome, gossip is unwholesome, covetousness (*abhijjhā*) is unwholesome, ill will (*byāpādo*) is unwholesome, wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*) is unwholesome. This is called the unwholesome.

“And what, friend, is the root of the unwholesome? Greed (*lobho*) is a root of the unwholesome, hate (*doso*) is a root of the unwholesome, delusion (*moho*) is a root of the unwholesome. This is called the root of the unwholesome.

“And what, friend, is the wholesome? Abstention from killing living beings is wholesome, abstention from taking what is not given is wholesome, abstention from misconduct in sensual pleasures is wholesome, abstention from false speech is wholesome, abstention from malicious speech is wholesome, abstention from harsh speech is wholesome, abstention from gossip is wholesome, non-covetousness (*anabhijjhā*) is wholesome, non-ill will (*abyāpādo*) is wholesome, right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*) is wholesome. This is called the wholesome.

“And what, friend, is the root of the wholesome? Non-greed (*alobho*) is a root of the wholesome, non-hate (*adoso*) is a root of the wholesome, non-delusion (*amoho*) is a root of the wholesome. This is called the root of the wholesome.

“When a noble disciple has thus understood the unwholesome, the root of the unwholesome, the wholesome, and the root of the wholesome, he entirely abandons the underlying tendency to lust, he abolishes the underlying tendency to aversion, he extirpates the underlying tendency to the view and conceit ‘I am,’ and by abandoning ignorance and arousing true knowledge he here and now makes an end of suffering. In that way too a noble disciple is one of right view, whose view is straight, who has perfect confidence in the Dhamma, and has arrived at this true Dhamma.”
commentary_pali:
89.Evaṃme sutanti sammādiṭṭhisuttaṃ. Tattha ‘‘sammādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhīti, āvuso, vuccati, kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso’’ti vā ‘‘katamaṃ panāvuso , akusala’’nti vā evaṃ yattakā therena pucchā vuttā, sabbā kathetukamyatā pucchā eva.

Tattha yasmā jānantāpi sammādiṭṭhīti vadanti ajānantāpi bāhirakāpi sāsanikāpi anussavādivasenāpi attapaccakkhenāpi, tasmā taṃ bahūnaṃ vacanaṃ upādāya dvikkhattuṃ āmasanto ‘‘sammādiṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhīti, āvuso, vuccatī’’ti āha. Ayañhi ettha adhippāyo, aparehipi sammādiṭṭhīti vuccati, athāparehipi sammādiṭṭhīti vuccati, svāyaṃ evaṃ vuccamāno atthañca lakkhaṇañca upādāya kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hotīti. Tattha sammādiṭṭhīti sobhanāya pasatthāya ca diṭṭhiyā samannāgato. Yadā pana dhammeyeva ayaṃ sammādiṭṭhisaddo vattati, tadāssa sobhanā pasatthā ca diṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhīti evamattho veditabbo.

sammādiṭṭhī sammādiṭṭhī

Sā cāyaṃ sammādiṭṭhi duvidhā hoti lokiyā lokuttarāti. Tattha kammassakatāñāṇaṃ saccānulomikañāṇañca lokiyā sammādiṭṭhi, saṅkhepato vā sabbāpi sāsavā paññā. Ariyamaggaphalasampayuttā paññā lokuttarā sammādiṭṭhi. Puggalo pana tividho hoti puthujjano sekkho asekkho ca. Tattha puthujjano duvidho hoti bāhirako sāsaniko ca. Tattha bāhirako kammavādī kammassakatādiṭṭhiyā sammādiṭṭhi hoti, no saccānulomikāya attadiṭṭhiparāmāsakattā. Sāsaniko dvīhipi. Sekkho niyatāya sammādiṭṭhiyā sammādiṭṭhi. Asekkho asekkhāya. Idha pana niyatāya niyyānikāya lokuttarakusalasammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato ‘‘sammādiṭṭhī’’ti adhippeto. Tenevāha ‘‘ujugatāssa diṭṭhi dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato āgato imaṃ saddhamma’’nti, lokuttarakusalasammādiṭṭhiyeva hi antadvayamanupagamma ujubhāvena gatattā , kāyavaṅkādīni ca sabbavaṅkāni samucchinditvā gatattā ujugatā hoti, tāyeva ca diṭṭhiyā samannāgato navappakārepi lokuttaradhamme aveccappasādena acalappasādena samannāgato hoti, sabbadiṭṭhigahanāni ca vinibbeṭhento sabbakilese pajahanto jātisaṃsārā nikkhamanto paṭipattiṃ pariniṭṭhapento ariyena maggena āgato imaṃ sambuddhappaveditaṃ amatogadhaṃ nibbānasaṅkhātaṃ saddhammanti vuccati.

saddhamma

Yato khoti kālaparicchedavacanametaṃ, yasmiṃ kāleti vuttaṃ hoti. Akusalañca pajānātīti dasākusalakammapathasaṅkhātaṃ akusalañca pajānāti, nirodhārammaṇāya pajānanāya kiccavasena ‘‘idaṃ dukkha’’nti paṭivijjhanto akusalaṃ pajānāti. Akusalamūlañca pajānātīti tassa mūlapaccayabhūtaṃ akusalamūlañca pajānāti, teneva pakārena ‘‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’’ti paṭivijjhanto. Esa nayo kusalañca kusalamūlañcāti etthāpi. Yathā cettha, evaṃ ito paresu sabbavāresu kiccavaseneva vatthupajānanā veditabbā. Ettāvatāpīti ettakena iminā akusalādippajānanenāpi. Sammādiṭṭhi hotīti vuttappakārāya lokuttarasammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti. Ujugatāssa…pe… imaṃ saddhammanti ettāvatā saṃkhittadesanā niṭṭhitā hoti. Desanāyeva cesā saṃkhittā, tesaṃ pana bhikkhūnaṃ vitthāravaseneva sammāmanasikārappaṭivedho veditabbo.

Yato kho Akusalañca pajānātī Akusalamūlañca pajānātī kusalañca kusalamūlañcā Ettāvatāpī Sammādiṭṭhi hotī Ujugatāssa…pe… imaṃ saddhamma

Dutiyavāre pana desanāpi vitthārena manasikārappaṭivedhopi vitthāreneva vuttoti veditabbo. Tattha ‘‘saṃkhittadesanāya dve heṭṭhimamaggā, vitthāradesanāya dve uparimamaggā kathitā’’ti bhikkhū āhaṃsu vitthāradesanāvasāne ‘‘sabbaso rāgānusayaṃ pahāyā’’tiādivacanaṃ sampassamānā.
