mula_pali:
139. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Idheva, bhikkhave, samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo; suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehīti samaṇehi aññeti (sī. pī. ka.) ettha aññehīti sakāya paṭiññāya saccābhiññehīti attho veditabbo. Evametaṃ evameva (syā. ka.), bhikkhave, sammā sīhanādaṃ nadatha.

samaṇehi aññeti (sī. pī. ka.) ettha aññehīti sakāya paṭiññāya saccābhiññehīti attho veditabbo evameva (syā. ka.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapindika's Park. There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: "Monks." "Venerable sir," those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

"Here, monks, is a *śramana*; here a second *śramana*; here a third *śramana*; here a fourth *śramana*. Other teachings are empty of *śramanas*."

"In this way, monks, roar the lion's roar rightly."
commentary_pali:
139.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷasīhanādasuttaṃ. Yasmā panassa atthuppattiko nikkhepo, tasmā taṃ dassetvā cassa anupubbapadavaṇṇanaṃ karissāma. Katarāya panidaṃ atthuppattiyā nikkhittanti? Lābhasakkārapaccayā titthiyaparidevite. Bhagavato kira dhammadāyādasutte vuttanayena mahālābhasakkāro uppajji. Catuppamāṇiko hi ayaṃ lokasannivāso, rūpappamāṇo rūpappasanno, ghosappamāṇo ghosappasanno, lūkhappamāṇo lūkhappasanno, dhammappamāṇo dhammappasannoti imesaṃ puggalānaṃ vasena catudhā ṭhito.

Tesaṃ idaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ – katamo ca puggalo rūpappamāṇo rūpappasanno? Idhekacco puggalo ārohaṃ vā passitvā pariṇāhaṃ vā passitvā saṇṭhānaṃ vā passitvā pāripūriṃ vā passitvā tattha pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasādaṃ janeti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo rūpappamāṇo rūpappasanno.

Katamo ca puggalo ghosappamāṇo ghosappasanno? Idhekacco puggalo paravaṇṇanāya parathomanāya parapasaṃsanāya paravaṇṇahārikāya, tattha pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasādaṃ janeti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo ghosappamāṇo ghosappasanno.

Katamo ca puggalo lūkhappamāṇo lūkhappasanno? Idhekacco puggalo cīvaralūkhaṃ vā passitvā pattalūkhaṃ vā passitvā, senāsanalūkhaṃ vā passitvā vividhaṃ vā dukkarakārikaṃ passitvā tattha pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasādaṃ janeti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo lūkhappamāṇo lūkhappasanno.

Katamo ca puggalo dhammappamāṇo dhammappasanno? Idhekacco puggalo sīlaṃ vā passitvā samādhiṃ vā passitvā paññaṃ vā passitvā tattha pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasādaṃ janeti, ayaṃ vuccati puggalo dhammappamāṇo dhammappasannoti.

Imesu catūsu puggalesu rūpappamāṇopi bhagavato ārohapariṇāhasaṇṭhānapāripūrivaṇṇapokkharataṃ, asītianubyañjanappaṭimaṇḍitattā nānāratanavicittamiva suvaṇṇamahāpaṭaṃ, dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇasamākiṇṇatāya tārāgaṇasamujjalaṃ viya gaganatalaṃ sabbaphāliphullaṃ viya ca yojanasatubbedhaṃ pāricchattakaṃ aṭṭhārasaratanubbedhaṃ byāmappabhāparikkhepaṃ sassirikaṃ anopamasarīraṃ disvā sammāsambuddheyeva pasīdati.

Ghosappamāṇopi, bhagavatā kappasatasahassādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni dasa pāramiyo dasa upapāramiyo dasa paramatthapāramiyo pūritā aṅgapariccāgo puttadārapariccāgo, rajjapariccāgo attapariccāgo nayanapariccāgo ca katotiādinā nayena pavattaṃ ghosaṃ sutvā sammāsambuddheyeva pasīdati.

Lūkhappamāṇopi bhagavato cīvaralūkhaṃ disvā ‘‘sace bhagavā agāraṃ ajjhāvasissa, kāsikavatthameva adhārayissa. Pabbajitvā panānena sāṇapaṃsukūlacīvarena santussamānena bhāriyaṃ kata’’nti sammāsambuddheyeva pasīdati. Pattalūkhampi disvā – ‘‘iminā agāraṃ ajjhāvasantena rattavarasuvaṇṇabhājanesu cakkavattibhojanārahaṃ sugandhasālibhojanaṃ paribhuttaṃ, pabbajitvā pana pāsāṇamayaṃ pattaṃ ādāya uccanīcakuladvāresu sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā laddhapiṇḍiyālopena santussamāno bhāriyaṃ karotī’’ti sammāsambuddheyeva pasīdati. Senāsanalūkhaṃ disvāpi – ‘‘ayaṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasanto tiṇṇaṃ utūnaṃ anucchavikesu tīsu pāsādesu tividhanāṭakaparivāro dibbasampattiṃ viya rajjasiriṃ anubhavitvā idāni pabbajjūpagato rukkhamūlasenāsanādīsu dāruphalakasilāpaṭṭapīṭhamañcakādīhi santussamāno bhāriyaṃ karotī’’ti sammāsambuddheyeva pasīdati. Dukkarakārikamassa disvāpi – ‘‘chabbassāni nāma muggayūsakulatthayūsahareṇuyūsādīnaṃ pasaṭamattena yāpessati, appāṇakaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyissati, sarīre ca jīvite ca anapekkho viharissati, aho dukkarakārako bhagavā’’ti sammāsambuddheyeva pasīdati.

Dhammappamāṇopi bhagavato sīlaguṇaṃ samādhiguṇaṃ paññāguṇaṃ jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattisampadaṃ abhiññāpāripūriṃ yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ devorohaṇaṃ pāthikaputtadamanādīni ca anekāni acchariyāni disvā sammāsambuddheyeva pasīdati, te evaṃ pasannā bhagavato mahantaṃ lābhasakkāraṃ abhiharanti. Titthiyānaṃ pana bāverujātake kākassa viya lābhasakkāro parihāyittha. Yathāha –

bāverujātake

‘‘Adassanena morassa, sikhino mañjubhāṇino;

Kākaṃ tattha apūjesuṃ, maṃsena ca phalena ca.

Yadā ca sarasampanno, moro bāverumāgamā;

Atha lābho ca sakkāro, vāyasassa ahāyatha.

Yāva nuppajjati buddho, dhammarājā pabhaṅkaro;

Tāva aññe apūjesuṃ, puthū samaṇabrāhmaṇe.

Yadā ca sarasampanno, buddho dhammamadesayi;

Atha lābho ca sakkāro, titthiyānaṃ ahāyathā’’ti. (jā. 1.4.153-156);

Te evaṃ pahīnalābhasakkārā rattiṃ ekadvaṅgulamattaṃ obhāsetvāpi sūriyuggamane khajjopanakā viya hatappabhā ahesuṃ.

Yathā hi khajjopanakā, kāḷapakkhamhi rattiyā;

Nidassayanti obhāsaṃ, etesaṃ visayo hi so.

Yadā ca rasmisampanno, abbhudeti pabhaṅkaro;

Atha khajjupasaṅghānaṃ, pabhā antaradhāyati.

Evaṃ khajjupasadisā, titthiyāpi puthū idha;

Kāḷapakkhūpame loke, dīpayanti sakaṃ guṇaṃ.

Yadā ca buddho lokasmiṃ, udeti amitappabho;

Nippabhā titthiyā honti, sūriye khajjupakā yathāti.

Te evaṃ nippabhā hutvā kacchupiḷakādīhi kiṇṇasarīrā paramapārijuññapattā yena buddho yena dhammo yena saṅgho yena ca mahājanassa sannipāto, tena tena gantvā antaravīthiyampi siṅghāṭakepi catukkepi sabhāyampi ṭhatvā paridevanti –

‘‘Kiṃ bho samaṇoyeva gotamo samaṇo, mayaṃ assamaṇā; samaṇasseva gotamassa sāvakā samaṇā, amhākaṃ sāvakā assamaṇā? Samaṇasseva gotamassa sāvakānañcassa dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, na amhākaṃ, sāvakānañca no dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ? Nanu samaṇopi gotamo samaṇo, mayampi samaṇā. Samaṇassapi gotamassa sāvakā samaṇā, amhākampi sāvakā samaṇā. Samaṇassapi gotamassa sāvakānañcassa dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, amhākampi sāvakānañca no dinnaṃ mahapphalañceva? Samaṇassapi gotamassa sāvakānañcassa detha karotha, amhākampi sāvakānañca no detha sakkarotha? Nanu samaṇo gotamo purimāni divasāni uppanno, mayaṃ pana loke uppajjamāneyeva uppannā’’ti.

Evaṃ nānappakāraṃ viravanti. Atha bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyoti catasso parisā tesaṃ saddaṃ sutvā bhagavato ārocesuṃ ‘‘titthiyā bhante idañcidañca kathentī’’ti . Taṃ sutvā bhagavā – ‘‘mā tumhe, bhikkhave, titthiyānaṃ vacanena ‘aññatra samaṇo atthī’ti saññino ahuvatthā’’ti vatvā aññatitthiyesu samaṇabhāvaṃ paṭisedhento idheva ca anujānanto imissā atthuppattiyā idheva, bhikkhave, samaṇoti idaṃ suttaṃ abhāsi.

idheva, bhikkhave, samaṇo

Tattha idhevāti imasmiṃyeva sāsane. Ayaṃ pana niyamo sesapadesupi veditabbo. Dutiyādayopi hi samaṇā idheva, na aññattha. Samaṇoti sotāpanno. Tenevāha – ‘‘katamo ca, bhikkhave, paṭhamo samaṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo, ayaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo samaṇo’’ti (a. ni. 4.241).

idhevā Samaṇo

Dutiyoti sakadāgāmī. Tenevāha – ‘‘katamo ca? Bhikkhave, dutiyo samaṇo. Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyo samaṇo’’ti.

Dutiyo

Tatiyoti anāgāmī. Tenevāha – ‘‘katamo ca, bhikkhave, tatiyo samaṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyo samaṇo’’ti.

Tatiyo

Catutthoti arahā. Tenevāha – ‘‘katamo ca, bhikkhave, catuttho samaṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, catuttho samaṇo’’ti (a. ni. 4.241). Iti imasmiṃ ṭhāne cattāro phalaṭṭhakasamaṇāva adhippetā.

Catuttho

Suññāti rittā tucchā. Parappavādāti cattāro sassatavādā, cattāro ekaccasassatikā, cattāro antānantikā, cattāro amarāvikkhepikā, dve adhiccasamuppannikā, soḷasa saññīvādā, aṭṭha asaññīvādā, aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā, satta ucchedavādā, pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādāti ime sabbepi brahmajāle āgatā dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhiyo. Ito bāhirānaṃ paresaṃ vādā parappavādā nāma. Te sabbepi imehi catūhi phalaṭṭhakasamaṇehi suññā, na hi te ettha santi. Na kevalañca eteheva suññā, catūhi pana maggaṭṭhakasamaṇehipi catunnaṃ maggānaṃ atthāya āraddhavipassakehipīti dvādasahipi samaṇehi suññā eva. Imameva atthaṃ sandhāya bhagavatā mahāparinibbāne vuttaṃ –

Suññā Parappavādā brahmajāle parappavādā mahāparinibbāne

‘‘Ekūnatiṃso vayasā subhadda,

Yaṃ pabbajiṃ kiṃ kusalānuesī;

Vassāni paññāsa samādhikāni,

Yato ahaṃ pabbajito subhadda;

Ñāyassa dhammassa padesavattī,

Ito bahiddhā samaṇopi natthi.

‘‘Dutiyopi samaṇo natthi, tatiyopi samaṇo natthi, catutthopi samaṇo natthi. Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehī’’ti (dī. ni. 2.214).

Ettha hi padesavattīti āraddhavipassako adhippeto. Tasmā sotāpattimaggassa āraddhavipassakaṃ maggaṭṭhaṃ phalaṭṭhanti tayopi ekato katvā samaṇopi natthīti āha. Sakadāgāmimaggassa āraddhavipassakaṃ maggaṭṭhaṃ phalaṭṭhanti tayopi ekato katvā dutiyopi samaṇo natthīti āha. Itaresupi dvīsu eseva nayo.

Kasmā panete aññattha natthīti? Akhettatāya. Yathā hi na āragge sāsapo tiṭṭhati, na udakapiṭṭhe aggi jalati, na piṭṭhipāsāṇe bījāni ruhanti, evameva bāhiresu titthāyatanesu na ime samaṇā uppajjanti, imasmiṃyeva pana sāsane uppajjanti. Kasmā? Khettatāya. Tesaṃ akhettatā ca khettatā ca ariyamaggassa abhāvato ca bhāvato ca veditabbā. Tenāha bhagavā –

‘‘Yasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo na upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhati, dutiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati, tatiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati, catutthopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Yasmiñca kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha upalabbhati, dutiyopi tattha…pe…. Catutthopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati. Imasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, idheva, subhadda, samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo, suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehī’’ti (dī. ni. 2.214).

Evaṃ yasmā titthāyatanaṃ akhettaṃ, sāsanaṃ khettaṃ, tasmā yathā surattahatthapādo sūrakesarako sīho migarājā na susāne vā saṅkārakūṭe vā paṭivasati, tiyojanasahassavitthataṃ pana himavantaṃ ajjhogāhetvā maṇiguhāyaṃyeva paṭivasati. Yathā ca chaddanto nāgarājā na gocariyahatthikulādīsu navasu nāgakulesu uppajjati, chaddantakuleyeva uppajjati. Yathā ca valāhako assarājā na gadrabhakule vā ghoṭakakule vā uppajjati, sindhuyā tīre pana sindhavakuleyeva uppajjati. Yathā ca sabbakāmadadaṃ manoharaṃ maṇiratanaṃ na saṅkārakūṭe vā paṃsupabbatādīsu vā uppajjati, vepullapabbatabbhantareyeva uppajjati. Yathā ca timirapiṅgalo maccharājā na khuddakapokkharaṇīsu uppajjati, caturāsītiyojanasahassagambhīre mahāsamuddeyeva uppajjati. Yathā ca diyaḍḍhayojanasatiko supaṇṇarājā na gāmadvāre eraṇḍavanādīsu paṭivasati, mahāsamuddaṃ pana ajjhogāhetvā simbalidahavaneyeva paṭivasati. Yathā ca dhataraṭṭho suvaṇṇahaṃso na gāmadvāre āvāṭakādīsu paṭivasati, navutihaṃsasahassaparivāro hutvā cittakūṭapabbateyeva paṭivasati. Yathā ca catuddīpissaro cakkavattirājā na nīcakule uppajjati, asambhinnajātikhattiyakuleyeva pana uppajjati. Evameva imesu samaṇesu ekasamaṇopi na aññatitthāyatane uppajjati, ariyamaggaparikkhitte pana buddhasāsaneyeva uppajjati. Tenāha bhagavā ‘‘idheva, bhikkhave, samaṇo…pe… suññā parappavādā samaṇehi samaṇebhi aññehī’’ti.

Sammā sīhanādaṃ nadathāti ettha sammāti hetunā nayena kāraṇena. Sīhanādanti seṭṭhanādaṃ abhītanādaṃ appaṭinādaṃ. Imesañhi catunnaṃ samaṇānaṃ idheva atthitāya ayaṃ nādo seṭṭhanādo nāma hoti uttamanādo. ‘‘Ime samaṇā idheva atthī’’ti vadantassa aññato bhayaṃ vā āsaṅkā vā natthīti abhītanādo nāma hoti. ‘‘Amhākampi sāsane ime samaṇā atthī’’ti pūraṇādīsu ekassāpi uṭṭhahitvā vattuṃ asamatthatāya ayaṃ nādo appaṭinādo nāma hoti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘sīhanādanti seṭṭhanādaṃ abhītanādaṃ appaṭināda’’nti.

Sammā sīhanādaṃ nadathā sammā Sīhanāda
commentary_english:
139. Thus have I heard: the Cūḷasīhanāda Sutta.

Since there is a presentation of its contextual origin, we will explain that and then give a word-by-word commentary in the proper order.

How is this placed in terms of its contextual origin? Because of the gains and honors [received by the Buddha], the Tīrthikas lamented.

It seems that a great gain and honor arose for the Blessed One, according to the method stated in the Dhammadāyāda Sutta.

This world-system is based on four standards, namely, those who are pleased by form, those who are pleased by sound, those who are pleased by austerity, and those who are pleased by the Dhamma.

Among them, what sort of person is pleased by form? Here, a certain person, having seen stature, or having seen circumference, or having seen shape, or having seen completeness, taking that as a standard, generates faith. This is called a person who is pleased by form.

What sort of person is pleased by sound? Here, a certain person, by another's praise, another's eulogy, another's commendation, another's eloquence, taking that as a standard, generates faith. This is called a person who is pleased by sound.

What sort of person is pleased by austerity? Here, a certain person, having seen the coarseness of robes, or having seen the coarseness of a bowl, or having seen the coarseness of lodgings, or having seen various difficult practices, taking that as a standard, generates faith. This is called a person who is pleased by austerity.

What sort of person is pleased by the Dhamma? Here, a certain person, having seen virtue, or having seen concentration, or having seen wisdom, taking that as a standard, generates faith. This is called a person who is pleased by the Dhamma.

Among these four types of individuals, even one who is pleased by form, seeing the Blessed One's perfection of stature, circumference, shape, completeness, beauty, adorned with eighty minor marks, like a great cloth of gold variegated with various jewels, crowded with thirty-two marks of a great man, like the surface of the sky radiant with a multitude of stars, like a Pāricchatta tree a hundred leagues high completely covered with blossoms, surrounded by a fathom-long aura eighteen times the size of a jewel, with a beautiful and incomparable body, is pleased only with the Sammāsambuddha.

Even one who is pleased by sound, hearing the Blessed One's voice, which arose because the ten perfections, the ten secondary perfections, and the ten highest perfections were fulfilled for four incalculable aeons plus one hundred thousand aeons, [and because] the sacrifice of limbs, the sacrifice of children and spouses, the sacrifice of kingdoms, the sacrifice of self, and the sacrifice of eyes, etc., were made, is pleased only with the Sammāsambuddha.

Even one who is pleased by austerity, seeing the Blessed One's coarse robes, [thinks,] "If the Blessed One were to live at home, he would wear only Kāsika cloth. Having gone forth, however, he is content with a robe made of hemp or discarded rags, and he does something extraordinary," and is pleased only with the Sammāsambuddha.

Also, having seen the coarseness of the bowl, [he thinks,] "This man, while living at home, partook of fragrant Sāli rice worthy of a universal monarch in golden dishes adorned with red gems. Having gone forth, however, taking a bowl made of stone, wandering for alms from house to house in villages high and low, he is content with a mouthful of food obtained by alms, and he does something extraordinary," and is pleased only with the Sammāsambuddha.

Also, having seen the coarseness of the lodgings, [he thinks,] "This man, while living at home, having enjoyed the prosperity of kingship like divine wealth in three palaces suitable for the three seasons, surrounded by a variety of dancers, now, having gone forth, is content with lodgings at the root of a tree, etc., with wooden planks, stone slabs, benches, and beds, and he does something extraordinary," and is pleased only with the Sammāsambuddha.

Also, having seen his difficult practices, [he thinks,] "For six years, he will sustain himself with only a handful of mung bean soup, horsebean soup, vetch soup, and wild grain soup, he will meditate on mindless meditation, and he will live without concern for his body or his life. How difficult is the Blessed One's practice!" and is pleased only with the Sammāsambuddha.

Even one who is pleased by the Dhamma, seeing the Blessed One's virtues of morality, virtues of concentration, virtues of wisdom, the accomplishment of the attainment of jhāna, liberation, concentration, and samāpatti, the perfection of the higher knowledges, the twin miracle, the descent from the divine realm, the taming of Pāthikaputta, etc., and many other wonders, is pleased only with the Sammāsambuddha. Being thus pleased, they bring great gain and honor to the Blessed One.

However, the gains and honors of the Tīrthikas declined, like the crow in the *Bāveru Jātaka*.

As it was said:

In the *Bāveru Jātaka*:

"When the peacock, with its crest and sweet voice, was not seen,
There they worshiped the crow with meat and fruit.

But when the peacock, full of charm, came to Bāveru,
Then the gain and honor of the crow vanished.

As long as the Buddha, the Dhamma-king, the radiant one, had not arisen,
So long did others worship various ascetics and brahmins.

But when the Buddha, full of charm, taught the Dhamma,
Then the gain and honor of the Tīrthikas vanished."
(Jā. 1.
4.153-156);

Having thus lost their gains and honor, they, even though shining a finger or two's breadth during the night, became devoid of luster like fireflies at sunrise.

As fireflies, indeed, on a dark night, show a light; that is their domain.

And when the radiant, light-making sun rises, then the light of the firefly assembly disappears.

Even so, the sectarians, though diverse here, display their qualities in a world comparable to a dark night.

And when the Buddha, of limitless radiance, arises in the world, the sectarians become lusterless, like fireflies at sunrise.

Having thus become lusterless, their bodies covered with boils and the like, having reached utter despondency, they went to where the Buddha was, to where the Dhamma was, to where the Saṅgha was, and to where a great crowd had gathered; and standing in the inner streets, at the crossroads, at the squares, and in the assembly hall, they lamented:

“What? Is only the ascetic Gotama an ascetic, and are we non-ascetics? Are only the disciples of the ascetic Gotama ascetics, and are our disciples non-ascetics? Is only what is given to the ascetic Gotama and his disciples of great fruit, and not to us and our disciples of great fruit? Surely the ascetic Gotama is an ascetic, and we too are ascetics. The disciples of the ascetic Gotama are ascetics, and our disciples too are ascetics. What is given to the ascetic Gotama and his disciples is of great fruit, and what is given to us and our disciples is also of great fruit? Give and do [good] to the ascetic Gotama and his disciples, and give and honor [us] and our disciples? Surely the ascetic Gotama arose in recent days, but we have arisen as soon as the world arose!”

Thus, they wailed in various ways. Then the four assemblies, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, having heard their sound, reported to the Blessed One, “Venerable sir, the sectarians are saying this and that.” Having heard that, the Blessed One, rejecting the state of being an ascetic in other sects while approving it here, uttered this sutta, saying, "Do not, monks, by the words of the sectarians, become convinced that 'there is an ascetic elsewhere'," for this reason:

"Here, monks, is the ascetic."

There, "here" means in this very dispensation. But this rule should be understood in the remaining words as well. For the second and so on are ascetics here, not elsewhere.

"Ascetic" means a stream-enterer ( *sotāpanna*). Therefore, he said, "And what, monks, is the first ascetic? Here, monks, a monk, by the destruction of the three fetters, is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling, fixed, destined for enlightenment. This, monks, is the first ascetic" (A. Ni. 4.241).

"Here is the ascetic."

"The second" means a once-returner (*sakadāgāmī*). Therefore, he said, "And what, monks, is the second ascetic? Here, monks, a monk, by the destruction of the three fetters and by the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, is a once-returner, who, after coming back to this world only one more time, will make an end to suffering. This, monks, is the second ascetic."

"The second."

"The third" means a non-returner (*anāgāmī*). Therefore, he said, "And what, monks, is the third ascetic? Here, monks, a monk, by the destruction of the five lower fetters, is spontaneously born [in the Pure Abodes], there to attain final *nirvāṇa*, not subject to returning from that world. This, monks, is the third ascetic."

"The third."

"The fourth" means an *arhat*.
Therefore, he said: "And which, monks, is the fourth *samaṇa* (ascetic)? Here, monks, a monk, by the destruction of the *āsavas* (influxes or taints), having realized here and now with his own super-knowledge and attained the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, abides in it. This, monks, is the fourth *samaṇa*."

Thus, in this context, only the four *samaṇas* who have attained the fruits (of the path) are intended.

*Catuttho*... *Suññā* means empty, void.

*Parappavādā* means the sixty-two views that appear in the *Brahmajāla* (Brahma's Net): the four eternalist doctrines (*sassatavādā*), the four semi-eternalists (*ekaccasassatikā*), the four believers in the finitude or infinity of the world (*antānantikā*), the four evasive wrigglers (*amarāvikkhepikā*), the two holding that things arise without cause (*adhiccasamuppannikā*), the sixteen who maintain that mind and body are coextensive and blissful (*saññīvādā*), the eight annihilationists (*ucchedavādā*), and the five who hold that *nirvāṇa* is possible in this very life (*diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā*).

The doctrines of others external to this (teaching) are called *parappavādā*. All of them are empty of these four *samaṇas* who have attained the fruits, for they are not present in them. Not only are they empty of these, but they are also empty of the four *samaṇas* who are on the path and those who have begun insight practice for the sake of the four paths, that is, empty even of the twelve *samaṇas*. With this meaning in mind, the Buddha said in the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta*—

*Suññā Parappavādā*… *Brahmajāle*… *Parappavādā*… *Mahāparinibbāne*…

“Subhadda, when I was twenty-nine years old, I went forth seeking what is skillful. Subhadda, since I went forth, fifty years and more have passed. Outside of this Dispensation, which is the domain of just Dhamma, no *samaṇa* is to be found."

"There is no second *samaṇa*, no third *samaṇa*, no fourth *samaṇa*. Other teachings are empty of ascetics."

Here, *padesavattī* is intended to mean one who has started insight practice. Therefore, having combined into one the one who has started insight practice on the path of stream-entry (*sotāpatti*), the one who is on the path, and the one who has attained the fruit, he said, "There is no *samaṇa*." Having combined into one the one who has started insight practice on the path of once-returning (*sakadāgāmi*), the one who is on the path, and the one who has attained the fruit, he said, "There is no second *samaṇa*." The same method applies to the other two.

But why are these not found elsewhere? Because of the unsuitability of the ground. Just as mustard seed does not grow on a cart, fire does not burn on the surface of water, and seeds do not sprout on a rocky surface, so these *samaṇas* do not arise in external heretical abodes, but arise only in this Dispensation. Why? Because of the suitability of the ground. Their unsuitability and suitability should be understood as due to the absence and presence of the Noble Eightfold Path. Therefore, the Blessed One said:

“Subhadda, in whatsoever Dhamma and Discipline the Noble Eightfold Path is not found, there is not found a *samaṇa*, there is not found a second *samaṇa*, there is not found a third *samaṇa*, there is not found a fourth *samaṇa*. But in whatsoever Dhamma and Discipline the Noble Eightfold Path is found, there is found a *samaṇa*, there is found a second…pe… there is found a fourth *samaṇa*. Subhadda, in this Dhamma and Discipline the Noble Eightfold Path is found, and here, Subhadda, is a *samaṇa*, here a second *samaṇa*, here a third *samaṇa*, here a fourth *samaṇa*. Other teachings are empty of ascetics."
Therefore, just as a lion, the king of beasts, with blood-red hands and feet and a brave mane, does not dwell in a cemetery or on a heap of rubbish, but enters the Himavant mountain, which is three thousand yojanas in extent, and dwells only in a jeweled cave;

Just as the Nāga king Chaddanta is not born in the nine Nāga families beginning with the elephant-tamer family, but is born only in the Chaddanta family;

Just as the horse king Valāhaka is not born in a donkey family or a horse family, but is born only on the bank of the Sindh River, in the Sindh family;

Just as a wish-fulfilling, delightful jewel is not born on a heap of rubbish or on a sandy mountain, but is born only inside Mount Vepulla;

Just as the fish king Timirapingala is not born in small ponds, but is born only in the great ocean, which is eighty-four thousand yojanas deep;

Just as the Supaṇṇa king, who is one and a half hundred yojanas [in size], does not dwell at a village gate or in an eraṇḍa forest, but enters the great ocean and dwells only in the Simbalidaha forest;

Just as the golden swan Dhataraṭṭha does not dwell at a village gate or in a ditch, but dwells only on Mount Cittakūṭa, surrounded by ninety thousand swans;

Just as a universal monarch, lord of the four continents, is not born in a low family, but is born only in an unmixed Khattiya family;

Even so, not even one ascetic among these ascetics is born in another hereticalOrder, but is born only in the Buddha's dispensation, which is surrounded by the Noble Path.

Therefore, the Blessed One said, "Here, monks, is an ascetic... empty are the doctrines of others from other ascetics."

sammā sīhanādaṃ nadathāti ettha sammāti hetunā nayena kāraṇena.

sīhanādanti seṭṭhanādaṃ abhītanādaṃ appaṭinādaṃ.

imesañhi catunnaṃ samaṇānaṃ idheva atthitāya ayaṃ nādo seṭṭhanādo nāma hoti uttamanādo.

‘‘ime samaṇā idheva atthī’’ti vadantassa aññato bhayaṃ vā āsaṅkā vā natthīti abhītanādo nāma hoti.

‘‘amhākampi sāsane ime samaṇā atthī’’ti pūraṇādīsu ekassāpi uṭṭhahitvā vattuṃ asamatthatāya ayaṃ nādo appaṭinādo nāma hoti.

tena vuttaṃ ‘‘sīhanādanti seṭṭhanādaṃ abhītanādaṃ appaṭināda’’nti.

sammā sīhanādaṃ nadathā sammā sīhanāda

"Rightly roar the lion's roar," here, sammā means with reason, method, cause.

sīhanādaṃ means the best roar, the fearless roar, the unanswerable roar.

Indeed, since these four ascetics exist here, this roar is called the best roar, the highest roar.

For one who says, "These ascetics exist here," there is no fear or apprehension from elsewhere, therefore it is called the fearless roar.

Since none of the Pūraṇas and others are able to rise up and say, "These ascetics exist in our dispensation too," this roar is called the unanswerable roar.

Therefore it was said, "sīhanādaṃ means the best roar, the fearless roar, the unanswerable roar."

Rightly roar the lion's roar, rightly, lion's roar.

mula_pali: 140. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ko panāyasmantānaṃ assāso, kiṃ balaṃ, yena tumhe āyasmanto evaṃ vadetha – idheva samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo; suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehī’ti? Evaṃvādino, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘atthi kho no, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro dhammā akkhātā ye mayaṃ attani sampassamānā evaṃ vadema – idheva samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo; suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehīti. Katame cattāro? Atthi kho no, āvuso, satthari pasādo, atthi dhamme pasādo, atthi sīlesu paripūrakāritā; sahadhammikā kho pana piyā manāpā – gahaṭṭhā ceva pabbajitā ca. Ime kho no, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro dhammā akkhātā ye mayaṃ attani sampassamānā evaṃ vadema – idheva samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo; suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehī’ti.
mula_english:
Bhikkhus, it is possible that wanderers of other sects might say thus: ‘Friends, what is the assurance, what is the strength, by which you venerable ones say thus: “Only here is there a recluse, only here a second recluse, only here a third recluse, only here a fourth recluse. The doctrines of others are devoid of recluses”?’

Wanderers of other sects who ask thus, bhikkhus, may be answered in this way: ‘Friends, four things have been declared to us by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened; on seeing these in ourselves we say thus: “Only here is there a recluse, only here a second recluse, only here a third recluse, only here a fourth recluse. The doctrines of others are devoid of recluses.”’

What are the four? We have confidence in the Teacher ( *satthari prasāda*), we have confidence in the Dhamma (*dhamme prasāda*), we have fulfilled the precepts (*sīlesu paripūrakāritā*), and our companions in the Dhamma (*sahadhammikā*) are dear and agreeable to us whether they are laymen (*gahaṭṭhā*) or those gone forth (*pabbajitā*).

These are the four things, friends, declared to us by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened, on seeing which in ourselves we say as we do.
commentary_pali:
140.Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjatīti idaṃ kho pana kāraṇaṃ vijjati. Yaṃ aññatitthiyāti yena kāraṇena aññatitthiyā. Ettha ca titthaṃ jānitabbaṃ, titthakaro jānitabbo titthiyā jānitabbā, titthiyasāvakā jānitabbā. Titthaṃnāma dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhiyo. Ettha hi sattā taranti uppalavanti ummujjanimujjaṃ karonti, tasmā titthanti vuccanti. Tāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ uppādetā titthakaro nāma. Tassa laddhiṃ gahetvā pabbajitā titthiyā nāma. Tesaṃ paccayadāyakā titthiyasāvakāti veditabbā. Paribbājakāti gihibandhanaṃ pahāya pabbajjūpagatā. Assāsoti avassayo patiṭṭhā upatthambho. Balanti thāmo. Yena tumheti yena assāsena vā balena vā evaṃ vadetha.

Atthikho no, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhenāti ettha ayaṃ saṅkhepattho – yo so bhagavā samatiṃsa pāramiyo pūretvā sabbakilese bhañjitvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho, tena bhagavatā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ āsayānusayaṃ jānatā, hatthatale ṭhapitaṃ āmalakaṃ viya sabbaṃ ñeyyadhammaṃ passatā. Apica pubbenivāsādīhi jānatā, dibbena cakkhunā passatā. Tīhi vijjāhi chahi vā pana abhiññāhi jānatā, sabbattha appaṭihatena samantacakkhunā passatā. Sabbadhammajānanasamatthāya paññāya jānatā, sabbasattānaṃ cakkhuvisayātītāni tirokuṭṭādigatāni vāpi rūpāni ativisuddhena maṃsacakkhunā passatā. Attahitasādhikāya samādhipadaṭṭhānāya paṭivedhapaññāya jānatā, parahitasādhikāya karuṇāpadaṭṭhānāya desanāpaññāya passatā. Arīnaṃ hatattā paccayādīnaṃ arahattā ca arahatā, sammā sāmañca saccānaṃ buddhattā sammāsambuddhena. Antarāyikadhamme vā jānatā, niyyānikadhamme passatā. Kilesārīnaṃ hatattā arahatā, sammā sāmaṃ sabbadhammānaṃ buddhattā sammāsambuddhenāti, evaṃ catuvesārajjavasena catūhi ākārehi thomitena cattāro dhammā akkhātā, ye mayaṃ attani sampassamānā evaṃ vadema, na rājarājamahāmattādīnaṃ upatthambhaṃ kāyabalanti.

Atthi kho no, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhenā jānatā, passatā arahatā, sammāsambuddhena

Sattharipasādoti ‘‘itipi so bhagavā’’tiādinā nayena buddhaguṇe anussarantānaṃ uppannappasādo. Dhamme pasādoti ‘‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo’’tiādinā nayena dhammaguṇe anussarantānaṃ uppannappasādo. Sīlesu paripūrakāritāti ariyakantesu sīlesu paripūrakāritā. Ariyakantasīlāni nāma pañcasīlāni. Tāni hi bhavantaragatopi ariyasāvako attano ariyasāvakabhāvaṃ ajānantopi na vītikkamati. Sacepi hi naṃ koci vadeyya – ‘‘imaṃ sakalaṃ cakkavattirajjaṃ sampaṭicchitvā khuddakamakkhikaṃ jīvitā voropehī’’ti, aṭṭhānametaṃ, yaṃ so tassa vacanaṃ kareyya. Evaṃ ariyānaṃ sīlāni kantāni piyāni manāpāni. Tāni sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘sīlesu paripūrakāritā’’ti.

Satthari pasādo Dhamme pasādo Sīlesu paripūrakāritā pañcasīlāni

Sahadhammikā kho panāti bhikkhu bhikkhunī sikkhamānā sāmaṇero sāmaṇerī upāsako upāsikāti ete satta sahadhammacārino. Etesu hi bhikkhu bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ sahadhammaṃ carati samānasikkhatāya. Tathā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi…pe… upāsikā upāsikāhi, sotāpanno sotāpannehi, sakadāgāmī…pe… anāgāmīhi sahadhammaṃ carati. Tasmā sabbepete sahadhammikāti vuccanti. Apicettha ariyasāvakāyeva adhippetā. Tesañhi bhavantarepi maggadassanamhi vivādo natthi, tasmā te accantaṃ ekadhammacāritāya sahadhammikā. Iminā, ‘‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’’tiādinā nayena saṅghaṃ anussarantānaṃ uppannappasādo kathito. Ettāvatā cattāri sotāpannassa aṅgāni kathitāni honti.

Sahadhammikā kho panā sahadhammacārino. sahadhammikā

Ime kho no, āvuso
commentary_english:
140. ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjatī: This is the reason that exists.

yaṃ aññatitthiyā: For this reason, they are other sectarians.

Here, *titthaṃ* should be understood, *titthakaro* should be understood, *titthiyā* should be understood, and *titthiyasāvakā* should be understood.

*titthaṃ* means sixty-two views.

Here, beings cross over, float, and perform diving and submerging, therefore they are called *titthanti*.

*titthakaro* is the originator of those views.

*titthiyā* means those who have gone forth, having adopted his doctrine.

*titthiyasāvakā* should be understood as those who give support to them.

*paribbājakā* means those who have abandoned the bonds of household life and have undertaken the ascetic life.

*assāso* means dependence, support, and upholding.

*bala* means strength.

yena tumhe: By whatever dependence or strength you might say this.

atthi kho no, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhenā: Here is the concise meaning: That Blessed One who, having fulfilled the thirty perfections (pāramī), having broken all defilements (kilesa), and having awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (sammāsambodhi), that Blessed One, knowing the inclinations and tendencies of those beings, *jānatā*, seeing all knowable things as if an *āmalaka* fruit placed on the palm of the hand, *passatā*.

Moreover, knowing through the knowledge of past lives, etc., seeing through the divine eye.

Knowing through the three wisdoms (*tīhi vijjāhi*) or the six higher knowledges (*abhiññā*), seeing with the unobstructed all-around eye (*samantacakkhunā*) everywhere.

Knowing through the wisdom capable of knowing all things (dhammas), seeing with the extremely pure fleshly eye (*maṃsacakkhunā*) even forms beyond the range of vision of all beings, such as those behind walls, etc.

Knowing through the wisdom of penetration (*paṭivedhapaññā*) that secures one's own welfare and has concentration as its proximate cause, seeing through the wisdom of teaching (*desanāpaññā*) that secures the welfare of others and has compassion as its proximate cause.

*arahatā* because of destroying the enemies [defilements] and being worthy of offerings, etc., *sammāsambuddhena* because of being rightly self-awakened to the truth.

Or, knowing the obstructive things, seeing the liberating things.

*arahatā* because of destroying the defilements, *sammāsambuddhena* because of being rightly self-awakened to all things, thus, the four qualities have been declared in four ways, praised by way of the four confidences (*catuvesārajja*), which we, experiencing in ourselves, might say thus, not the support of kings, royal ministers, etc., or physical strength.

atthi kho no, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhenā jānatā, passatā arahatā, sammāsambuddhena

satthari pasādo: *pasādo* in the Teacher, is the arisen faith of those recollecting the qualities of the Buddha in the manner beginning with "itipi so bhagavā."

dhamme pasādo: *pasādo* in the Dharma, is the arisen faith of those recollecting the qualities of the Dharma in the manner beginning with "svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo."

sīlesu paripūrakāritā: Perfecting the virtues which are pleasing to the noble ones.

*ariyakantasīlāni* nāma *pañcasīlāni*: The virtues pleasing to the noble ones are the five precepts (*pañcasīlāni*).

Indeed, even when reborn, a noble disciple, even without knowing his state as a noble disciple, does not transgress them.

Even if someone should say to him, "Having accepted this entire universal rulership, take the life of a small fly," it is impossible that he would do his bidding.

Thus, the virtues of the noble ones are pleasing, dear, and agreeable.

Referring to those, it was said "sīlesu paripūrakāritā."

sahadhammikā kho panā: *sahadhammacārino* are these seven: monk (bhikkhu), nun (bhikkhunī), female trainee (*sikkhamānā*), novice (sāmaṇero), female novice (sāmaṇerī), lay follower (upāsako), female lay follower (upāsikā).

Among these, a monk lives the same Dharma with monks because of having the same training.

Similarly, a nun with nuns... a female lay follower with female lay followers, a stream-enterer with stream-enterers, a once-returner… an non-returner lives the same Dharma.

Therefore, all of these are called *sahadhammikā*.
Moreover, here, it is precisely the noble disciples who are intended.
For them, even in a future existence, there is no dispute regarding the vision of the path. Therefore, they are entirely in harmony, practicing the same dharma.
By this, it is said that joy arises in those who recollect the *saṃgha* (community), in the manner beginning with "the community of the Blessed One's disciples is practicing the good way."
Thus far, the four qualities of a stream-enterer have been spoken of.
The *sahadharmikas* (those who share the Dharma) are indeed *sahadharmacārins* (those who practice the Dharma together).
"These, indeed, O *āvuso* (friend)," O *āvuso*, these four *dharmas* (teachings) have been declared by that Blessed One as our comfort and strength, which we, perceiving in ourselves, would thus speak.
"These, indeed, O *āvuso*."

mula_pali:
141. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘amhākampi kho, āvuso, atthi satthari pasādo yo amhākaṃ satthā, amhākampi atthi dhamme pasādo yo amhākaṃ dhammo, mayampi sīlesu paripūrakārino yāni amhākaṃ sīlāni, amhākampi sahadhammikā piyā manāpā – gahaṭṭhā ceva pabbajitā ca. Idha no, āvuso, ko viseso ko adhippayāso adhippāyo (ka. sī. syā. pī.), adhippayogo (ka.) kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ yadidaṃ tumhākañceva amhākañcā’ti?

‘‘Evaṃvādino, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘kiṃ panāvuso, ekā niṭṭhā, udāhu puthu niṭṭhā’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘ekāvuso, niṭṭhā, na puthu niṭṭhā’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā sarāgassa udāhu vītarāgassā’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘vītarāgassāvuso, sā niṭṭhā, na sā niṭṭhā sarāgassā’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā sadosassa udāhu vītadosassā’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘vītadosassāvuso, sā niṭṭhā, na sā niṭṭhā sadosassā’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā samohassa udāhu vītamohassā’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘vītamohassāvuso, sā niṭṭhā, na sā niṭṭhā samohassā’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā sataṇhassa udāhu vītataṇhassā’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘vītataṇhassāvuso, sā niṭṭhā, na sā niṭṭhā sataṇhassā’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā saupādānassa udāhu anupādānassā’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave , aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘anupādānassāvuso, sā niṭṭhā, na sā niṭṭhā saupādānassā’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā viddasuno udāhu aviddasuno’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘viddasuno, āvuso, sā niṭṭhā, na sā niṭṭhā aviddasuno’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā anuruddhappaṭiviruddhassa udāhu ananuruddhaappaṭiviruddhassā’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘ananuruddhaappaṭiviruddhassāvuso, sā niṭṭhā, na sā niṭṭhā anuruddhappaṭiviruddhassā’ti.

‘‘‘Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā papañcārāmassa papañcaratino udāhu nippapañcārāmassa nippapañcaratino’ti? Sammā byākaramānā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ byākareyyuṃ – ‘nippapañcārāmassāvuso, sā niṭṭhā nippapañcaratino, na sā niṭṭhā papañcārāmassa papañcaratino’ti.
mula_english:
141. "It is possible, *bhikkhus*, that wanderers of other sects might say thus: 'Friends, we too have confidence in the Teacher, that is, in our Teacher; we too have confidence in the *Dhamma*, that is, in our *Dhamma*; we too have fulfilled the precepts (*śīla*), that is, our precepts (*śīla*); and our companions in the *Dhamma* are dear and agreeable to us too whether they are laymen or those gone forth. What is the distinction here, friends, what is the variance, what is the difference between you and us?'

"Speaking thus, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects should be addressed thus: 'But friends, is there one goal (*niṭṭhā*), or are there diverse goals (*niṭṭhā*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'There is one goal (*niṭṭhā*), friend, not diverse goals (*niṭṭhā*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by lust (*sarāga*) or for one free from lust (*vītarāga*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one free from lust (*vītarāga*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by lust (*sarāga*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by hate (*sadosa*) or for one free from hate (*vītadosa*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one free from hate (*vītadosa*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by hate (*sadosa*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by delusion (*samoha*) or for one free from delusion (*vītamoha*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one free from delusion (*vītamoha*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by delusion (*samoha*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by craving (*satṇha*) or for one free from craving (*vītataṇha*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one free from craving (*vītataṇha*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by craving (*satṇha*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by clinging (*saupādāna*) or for one free from clinging (*anupādāna*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one free from clinging (*anupādāna*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one affected by clinging (*saupādāna*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one with vision (*viddasu*) or for one without vision (*aviddasu*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one with vision (*viddasu*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one without vision (*aviddasu*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one who favours and opposes (*anuruddhaappaṭiviruddha*) or for one who does not favour and oppose (*ananuruddhaappaṭiviruddha*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one who does not favour and oppose (*ananuruddhaappaṭiviruddha*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one who favours and opposes (*anuruddhaappaṭiviruddha*).'

"'But friend, is that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one delighting and indulging in proliferation (*papañcārāma* *papañcarati*) or for one not delighting and indulging in proliferation (*nippapañcārāma* *nippapañcarati*)?' Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus: 'That goal (*niṭṭhā*) is for one not delighting and indulging in proliferation (*nippapañcārāma* *nippapañcarati*), not that goal (*niṭṭhā*) for one delighting and indulging in proliferation (*papañcārāma* *papañcarati*).'
commentary_pali:
141.Yo amhākaṃ satthāti iminā pūraṇakassapādike cha satthāro apadissanti. Yathā pana idāni sāsane ācariyupajjhāyādīsu ‘‘amhākaṃ ācariyo, amhākaṃ upajjhāyo’’ti gehasitapemaṃ hoti. Evarūpaṃ pemaṃ sandhāya ‘‘satthari pasādo’’ti vadanti. Thero panāha – ‘‘yasmā satthā nāma na ekassa, na dvinnaṃ hoti, sadevakassa lokassa ekova satthā, tasmā titthiyā ‘amhākaṃ satthā’ ti ekapadeneva satthāraṃ visuṃ katvā imināva padena viruddhā parājitā’’ti. Dhamme pasādoti idaṃ pana yathā idāni sāsane ‘‘amhākaṃ dīghanikāyo amhākaṃ majjhimanikāyo’’ti mamāyanti, evaṃ attano attano pariyattidhamme gehasitapemaṃ sandhāya vadanti. Sīlesūti ajasīlagosīlameṇḍakasīlakukkurasīlādīsu. Idha no āvusoti ettha idhāti pasādaṃ sandhāya vadanti. Ko adhippayāsoti ko adhikappayogo. Yadidanti yamidaṃ tumhākañceva amhākañca nānākaraṇaṃ vadeyyātha. Taṃ kiṃ nāma? Tumhākampi hi catūsu ṭhānesu pasādo, amhākampi. Nanu etasmiṃ pasāde tumhe ca amhe ca dvedhā bhinnasuvaṇṇaṃ viya ekasadisāti vācāya samadhurā hutvā aṭṭhaṃsu.

Atha nesaṃ taṃ samadhurataṃ bhindanto bhagavā evaṃ vādinotiādimāha. Tattha ekā niṭṭhāti yā tassa pasādassa pariyosānabhūtā niṭṭhā, kiṃ sā ekā, udāhu puthūti evaṃ pucchathāti vadati. Yasmā pana tasmiṃ tasmiṃ samaye niṭṭhaṃ apaññapento nāma natthi, brāhmaṇānañhi brahmaloko niṭṭhā, mahātāpasānaṃ ābhassarā, paribbājakānaṃ subhakiṇhā, ājīvakānaṃ ‘‘anantamānaso’’ti evaṃ parikappito asaññībhavo . Imasmiṃ sāsane pana arahattaṃ niṭṭhā. Sabbeva cete arahattameva niṭṭhāti vadanti. Diṭṭhivasena pana brahmalokādīni paññapenti. Tasmā attano attano laddhivasena ekameva niṭṭhaṃ paññapenti, taṃ dassetuṃ bhagavā sammā byākaramānātiādimāha.

evaṃ vādino ekā niṭṭhā sammā byākaramānā

Idāni bhikkhūnampi ekā niṭṭhā, titthiyānampi ekā niṭṭhāti dvīsu aṭṭakārakesu viya ṭhitesu bhagavā anuyogavattaṃ dassento sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā sarāgassa, udāhu vītarāgassātiādimāha. Tattha yasmā rāgarattādīnaṃ niṭṭhā nāma natthi. Yadi siyā, soṇasiṅgālādīnampi siyāti imaṃ dosaṃ passantānaṃ titthiyānaṃ ‘‘vītarāgassa āvuso sā niṭṭhā’’tiādinā nayena byākaraṇaṃ dassitaṃ.

sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā sarāgassa, udāhu vītarāgassā

Tattha viddasunoti paṇḍitassa. Anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassāti rāgena anuruddhassa kodhena paṭiviruddhassa. Papañcārāmassa papañcaratinoti ettha āramanti etthāti ārāmo. Papañco ārāmo assāti papañcārāmo. Papañce rati assāti papañcarati. Papañcoti ca mattapamattākārabhāvena pavattānaṃ taṇhādiṭṭhimānānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Idha pana taṇhādiṭṭhiyova adhippetā. Sarāgassātiādīsu pañcasu ṭhānesu ekova kileso āgato. Tassa ākārato nānattaṃ veditabbaṃ. Sarāgassāti hi vuttaṭṭhāne pañcakāmaguṇikarāgavasena gahito. Sataṇhassāti bhavataṇhāvasena. Saupādānassāti gahaṇavasena. Anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassāti yugaḷavasena. Papañcārāmassāti papañcuppattidassanavasena. Sarāgassāti vā ettha akusalamūlavasena gahito. Sataṇhassāti ettha taṇhāpaccayā upādānadassanavasena. Sesaṃ purimasadisameva. Thero panāha ‘‘kasmā evaṃ viddhaṃsetha? Ekoyeva hi ayaṃ lobho rajjanavasena rāgoti vutto. Taṇhākaraṇavasena taṇhā. Gahaṇaṭṭhena upādānaṃ. Yugaḷavasena anurodhapaṭivirodho. Papañcuppattidassanaṭṭhena papañco’’ti.

viddasuno Anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassā Papañcārāmassa papañcaratino papañcārāmo papañcarati. Papañco Sarāgassā Sarāgassā Sataṇhassā Saupādānassā Anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassā Papañcārāmassā Sarāgassā Sataṇhassā rāgo taṇhā upādānaṃ anurodhapaṭivirodho papañco’’
commentary_english:
141. "Yo amhākaṃ satthā"ti: By this, the six teachers such as Pūraṇa Kassapa are indicated. Just as now in the Dispensation there is affection rooted in household life towards teachers, preceptors, etc., [with the thought,] "Our teacher, our preceptor," they speak of "confidence in the teacher" with reference to such affection. But the Elder said: "Since a teacher is not for one person, nor for two, but the teacher is one for the world with the devas, therefore the adherents of other views, having separated the teacher by the single expression 'our teacher', by this very expression are opposed and defeated." "Dhamme pasādo": But this is as now in the Dispensation [they say], "Our *Dīgha Nikāya*, our *Majjhima Nikāya*," and so they are possessive, and speak with reference to affection rooted in household life for their own textual Dharma. "Sīlesū": In dog-conduct, etc., such as goat-conduct, ram-conduct, and dog-conduct. "Idha no āvuso": Here, "idhā" they say with reference to confidence. "Ko adhippayāso": What is the additional application? "Yadida"nti: What you might say is a differentiating of both you and us. What is that? Confidence in the four bases is both yours and ours. Surely in this confidence, you and we, like gold split in two, stood having harmonious voices as if of one likeness.

Then, breaking up that harmoniousness of theirs, the Blessed One spoke beginning with "Evaṃ vādino." There, "ekā niṭṭhā" means what is the niṭṭhā that is the culmination of that confidence? Is that one, or many? Thus he speaks asking. Since there is no one who does not designate a *niṭṭhā* at that time, for Brahmins the Brahma-world is the *niṭṭhā*, for the great ascetics the Ābhassara world, for the wandering ascetics the Subhakiṇha world, for the Ājīvakas an unconscious existence conceived as "endless-consciousness." But in this Dispensation, arahantship is the *niṭṭhā*. And all these say that arahantship is the *niṭṭhā*. But they designate the Brahma-world etc. from the point of view of views. Therefore they designate one *niṭṭhā* each according to their own attainment. To show that, the Blessed One spoke beginning with "Sammā byākaramānā."

Evaṃ vādino ekā niṭṭhā Sammā byākaramānā

Now, when it was established as if in two debaters, that there is one *niṭṭhā* for the monks, and one *niṭṭhā* for the adherents of other views, the Blessed One, showing the proper course of questioning, spoke beginning with "Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā sarāgassa, udāhu vītarāgassā." There, since there is no *niṭṭhā* for those stained with passion, etc., if there were, there would be for jackals and dogs etc., and seeing this fault, the adherents of other views were shown a statement in the manner beginning with "vītarāgassa āvuso sā niṭṭhā."

Sā panāvuso, niṭṭhā sarāgassa, udāhu vītarāgassā

There, "viddasuno" means of the wise. "Anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassā" means attached to by passion, opposed to by anger. "Papañcārāmassa papañcaratino": Here, it is delighted in here, therefore it is a delight (*ārāma*). Proliferation is his delight, therefore "papañcārāmo." He has delight in proliferation, therefore "papañcarati." And "papañco" is a designation for craving, views, and conceit which occur in a state of intoxication and heedlessness. But here craving and views are intended. In the five places beginning with "sarāgassā" only one defilement comes. Its diversity is to be understood from its mode. For in the place where "sarāgassā" is stated, it is taken as passion connected with the five strands of sense desire. "Sataṇhassā" is in the mode of craving for existence. "Saupādānassā" is in the mode of grasping.
*Anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassā* means according to the pair.

*Papañcārāmassā* means according to the display of the origination of *papañca*.

*Sarāgassā* here is taken in terms of the unwholesome root.

*Sataṇhassā* here is according to the display of grasping (*upādāna*) because of craving (*taṇhā*).

The rest is the same as before.

The elder said, "Why do you analyze it like this? This one greed (*lobha*) is called *rāga* because of clinging.

It is *taṇhā* because of causing craving.

It is *upādānaṃ* in the sense of grasping.

It is *anurodhapaṭivirodho* according to the pair.

It is *papañco* in the sense of displaying the origination of *papañca*."

*Viddasuno anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassā papañcārāmassa papañcaratino papañcārāmo papañcarati*.
*Papañco sarāgassā*.
*Sarāgassā sataṇhassā saupādānassā anuruddhapaṭiviruddhassā papañcārāmassā sarāgassā sataṇhassā rāgo taṇhā upādānaṃ anurodhapaṭivirodho papañco*

mula_pali: 142. ‘‘Dvemā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyo – bhavadiṭṭhi ca vibhavadiṭṭhi ca. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhavadiṭṭhiṃ allīnā bhavadiṭṭhiṃ upagatā bhavadiṭṭhiṃ ajjhositā, vibhavadiṭṭhiyā te paṭiviruddhā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā vibhavadiṭṭhiṃ allīnā vibhavadiṭṭhiṃ upagatā vibhavadiṭṭhiṃ ajjhositā, bhavadiṭṭhiyā te paṭiviruddhā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imāsaṃ dvinnaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, ‘te sarāgā te sadosā te samohā te sataṇhā te saupādānā te aviddasuno te anuruddhappaṭiviruddhā te papañcārāmā papañcaratino; te na parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi; na parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi. Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imāsaṃ dvinnaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānanti, ‘te vītarāgā te vītadosā te vītamohā te vītataṇhā te anupādānā te viddasuno te ananuruddhaappaṭiviruddhā te nippapañcārāmā nippapañcaratino; te parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi; parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
mula_english:
142. Bhikkhus, there are these two views: the view of being (bhavaditthi) and the view of non-being (vibhavaditthi).

Any recluses or Brahmins who rely on the view of being (bhavaditthi), adopt the view of being (bhavaditthi), accept the view of being (bhavaditthi), are opposed to the view of non-being (vibhavaditthi).

Any recluses or Brahmins who rely on the view of non-being (vibhavaditthi), adopt the view of non-being (vibhavaditthi), accept the view of non-being (vibhavaditthi), are opposed to the view of being (bhavaditthi).

Any recluses or Brahmins who do not understand as they actually are the origin (samudaya), the disappearance (atthaṅgama), the gratification (assāda), the danger (ādīnava), and the escape (nissaraṇa) in the case of these two views are affected by lust (sarāgā), affected by hate (sadosā), affected by delusion (samohā), affected by craving (sataṇhā), affected by clinging (saupādānā), without vision (aviddasuno), given to favouring and opposing (anuruddhappaṭiviruddhā), and they delight in and enjoy proliferation (papañcārāmā papañcaratino). They are not freed from birth (jātiyā), aging (jarāya), and death (maraṇena); from sorrow (sokehi), lamentation (paridevehi), pain (dukkhehi), grief (domanassehi), and despair (upāyāsehi); they are not freed from suffering (dukkhasmā), I say.

Any recluses or Brahmins who understand as they actually are the origin (samudaya), the disappearance (atthaṅgama), the gratification (assāda), the danger (ādīnava), and the escape (nissaraṇa) in the case of these two views are without lust (vītarāgā), without hate (vītadosā), without delusion (vītamohā), without craving (vītataṇhā), without clinging (anupādānā), with vision (viddasuno), not given to favouring and opposing (ananuruddhaappaṭiviruddhā), and they do not delight in and enjoy proliferation (nippapañcārāmā nippapañcaratino). They are freed from birth (jātiyā), aging (jarāya), and death (maraṇena); from sorrow (sokehi), lamentation (paridevehi), pain (dukkhehi), grief (domanassehi), and despair (upāyāsehi); they are freed from suffering (dukkhasmā), I say.
commentary_pali:
142. Idāni imesaṃ kilesānaṃ mūlabhūtaṃ diṭṭhivādaṃ dassento dvemā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyotiādimāha.

Tattha bhavadiṭṭhīti sassatadiṭṭhi. Vibhavadiṭṭhīti ucchedadiṭṭhi. Bhavadiṭṭhiṃ allīnāti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena sassatadiṭṭhiṃ allīnā. Upagatāti taṇhādiṭṭhivaseneva upagatā. Ajjhositāti taṇhādiṭṭhivaseneva anupaviṭṭhā. Vibhavadiṭṭhiyā te paṭiviruddhāti te sabbe ucchedavādīhi saddhiṃ – ‘‘tumhe andhabālā na jānātha, sassato ayaṃ loko, nāyaṃ loko ucchijjatī’’ti paṭiviruddhā niccaṃ kalahabhaṇḍanapasutā viharanti. Dutiyavārepi eseva nayo.

bhavadiṭṭhī Vibhavadiṭṭhī Bhavadiṭṭhiṃ allīnā Upagatā Ajjhositā Vibhavadiṭṭhiyā te paṭiviruddhā

Samudayañcātiādīsu dve diṭṭhīnaṃ samudayā khaṇikasamudayo paccayasamudayo ca. Khaṇikasamudayo diṭṭhīnaṃ nibbatti. Paccayasamudayo aṭṭha ṭhānāni. Seyyathidaṃ, khandhāpi diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ, avijjāpi, phassopi, saññāpi, vitakkopi, ayonisomanasikāropi, pāpamittopi, paratoghosopi diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ. ‘‘Khandhā hetu khandhā paccayo diṭṭhīnaṃ upādāya samuṭṭhānaṭṭhena. Evaṃ khandhāpi diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ. Avijjā… phasso… saññā… vitakko… ayonisomanasikāro… pāpamitto… paratoghoso hetu, paratoghoso paccayo diṭṭhīnaṃ upādāya samuṭṭhānaṭṭhena. Evaṃ paratoghosopi diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ’’ (paṭi. ma. 1.124). Atthaṅgamāpi dveyeva khaṇikatthaṅgamo paccayatthaṅgamo ca. Khaṇikatthaṅgamo nāma khayo vayo bhedo paribhedo aniccatā antaradhānaṃ. Paccayatthaṅgamo nāma sotāpattimaggo. Sotāpattimaggo hi diṭṭhiṭṭhānasamugghātoti vutto.

Samudayañcā Khaṇikasamudayo Paccayasamudayo Khaṇikatthaṅgamo Paccayatthaṅgamo

Assādanti diṭṭhimūlakaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘yaṃdiṭṭhiko satthā hoti, taṃdiṭṭhikā sāvakā honti. Yaṃdiṭṭhikā satthāraṃ sāvakā sakkaronti, garuṃ karonti, mānenti, pūjenti, labhanti tatonidānaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhadhammiko ānisaṃso’’ti. Ādīnavanti diṭṭhiggahaṇamūlakaṃ upaddavaṃ. So vaggulivataṃ ukkuṭikappadhānaṃ kaṇṭakāpassayatā pañcātapatappanaṃ sānupapātapatanaṃ kesamassuluñcanaṃ appoṇakaṃ jhānantiādīnaṃ vasenaṃ veditabbo. Nissaraṇanti diṭṭhīnaṃ nissaraṇaṃ nāma nibbānaṃ. Yathābhūtaṃnappajānantīti ye etaṃ sabbaṃ yathāsabhāvaṃ na jānanti. Na parimuccanti dukkhasmāti sakalavaṭṭadukkhato na parimuccanti. Iminā etesaṃ niṭṭhā nāma natthīti dasseti. Parimuccanti dukkhasmāti sakalavaṭṭadukkhato parimuccanti. Iminā etesaṃ niṭṭhā nāma atthīti dvinnaṃ aṭṭakārakānaṃ aṭṭaṃ chindanto viya sāsanasmiṃyeva niṭṭhāya atthitaṃ patiṭṭhapeti.

Assāda Ādīnava Nissaraṇa Yathābhūtaṃ nappajānantī Na parimuccanti dukkhasmā Parimuccanti dukkhasmā
commentary_english:
142. Now, showing the root of these afflictions, which is the doctrine of views, he said, "There are these two views, monks," and so on.

Therein, *bhavadiṭṭhi* means the eternalist view (śāśvatadṛṣṭi). *vibhavadiṭṭhi* means the annihilationist view (ucchedadṛṣṭi). *bhavadiṭṭhiṃ allīnā* means clinging to the eternalist view through craving and views. *upagatā* means approaching [it] through craving and views. *ajjhositā* means entering [it] through craving and views. *vibhavadiṭṭhiyā te paṭiviruddhā* means that all those [who hold the eternalist view] are opposed to the annihilationists, [saying,] "You are blind fools, you do not know that this world is eternal, this world is not annihilated," and they constantly live engaged in quarrels and disputes. The same method [of explanation] applies in the second instance as well.

*bhavadiṭṭhī vibhavadiṭṭhi bhavadiṭṭhiṃ allīnā upagatā ajjhositā vibhavadiṭṭhiyā te paṭiviruddhā*

In *samudayañcā* etc., there are two kinds of arising of views: momentary arising (kṣaṇikasamudaya) and causal arising (pratyayasamudaya). *khaṇikasamudayo* means the origination of views. *paccayasamudayo* [refers to] eight bases, namely, the aggregates are a basis for views (dṛṣṭi-sthāna), ignorance (*avidyā*) is a basis, contact (*sparśa*) is a basis, perception (*saṃjñā*) is a basis, thought (*vitarka*) is a basis, unwise attention (*ayoniśomanasikāra*) is a basis, evil friends (*pāpamitra*) are a basis, and the voice of another (*parato-ghoṣa*) is a basis for views. "The aggregates are a cause, the aggregates are a condition for views, in the sense of being the basis for their arising. Thus, the aggregates are a basis for views. Ignorance… contact… perception… thought… unwise attention… evil friends… the voice of another is a cause, the voice of another is a condition for views, in the sense of being the basis for their arising. Thus, the voice of another is a basis for views" (Paṭisambhidāmagga 1.124). There are likewise two kinds of cessation (*athaṅgama*): momentary cessation (kṣaṇikatthaṅgama) and causal cessation (pratyayatthaṅgama). *khaṇikatthaṅgamo* means decay (khayo), aging (vayo), breaking (bhedo), complete breaking (paribhedo), impermanence (aniccatā), and disappearance (antaradhānaṃ). *paccayatthaṅgamo* means the path of stream-entry (sotāpattimaggo). For the path of stream-entry is said to be the uprooting of the bases for views.

*samudayañcā khaṇikasamudayo paccayasamudayo khaṇikatthaṅgamo paccayatthaṅgamo*

*assāda* means the advantage rooted in views. With this in mind, it was said, "Whatever view the teacher holds, the disciples hold the same view. Holding the same view as the teacher, the disciples honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the teacher, and on that account, they obtain robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites. This, monks, is the immediate benefit of views." *ādīnava* means the danger rooted in seizing views. This should be understood in terms of such practices as the bat-asceticism, the squatting posture, reliance on thorns, scorching with the five fires, falling with a crash, plucking out hair and beard, and the meditation of the unclad ascetics. *nissaraṇa* means the escape from views, namely, *nirvāṇa*. *yathābhūtaṃ nappajānantī* means those who do not know all this as it really is. *na parimuccanti dukkhasmā* means they are not freed from the entirety of the round of suffering. By this, he shows that there is no end for them.
"<hi rend="bold">parimuccanti dukkhasmā</hi> means they are completely liberated from all suffering of the cycle [of rebirth].
By this, he establishes the existence of completion in the dispensation itself, as if cutting off the eight causes of the two eights, [saying] 'these have a completion'.

<hi rend="bold">assāda</hi> <hi rend="bold">ādīnava</hi> <hi rend="bold">nissaraṇa</hi> <hi rend="bold">yathābhūtaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">nappajānantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">na parimuccanti dukkhasmā</hi> <hi rend="bold">parimuccanti dukkhasmā</hi>"

mula_pali:
143. ‘‘Cattārimāni , bhikkhave, upādānāni. Katamāni cattāri? Kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ. Santi, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā. Te na sammā sabbupādānapariññaṃ paññapenti – kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imāni hi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā tīṇi ṭhānāni yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti. Tasmā te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā; te na sammā sabbupādānapariññaṃ paññapenti – kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti.

‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā. Te na sammā sabbupādānapariññaṃ paññapenti – kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imāni hi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā dve ṭhānāni yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti. Tasmā te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā; te na sammā paṭijānamānā na sammā (?) sabbupādānapariññaṃ paññapenti – kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti.

paṭijānamānā na sammā (?)

‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā. Te na sammā sabbupādānapariññaṃ paññapenti – kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imañhi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekaṃ ṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti. Tasmā te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā; te na sammā paṭijānamānā na sammā (?) sabbupādānapariññaṃ paññapenti – kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti, na attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti.

paṭijānamānā na sammā (?)

‘‘Evarūpe kho, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo satthari pasādo so na sammaggato akkhāyati; yo dhamme pasādo so na sammaggato akkhāyati; yā sīlesu paripūrakāritā sā na sammaggatā akkhāyati; yā sahadhammikesu piyamanāpatā sā na sammaggatā akkhāyati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite.
mula_english:
143. “There are, monastics, these four attachments ( *upādāna*). What are the four? Clinging to sensual pleasures (*kāmuppādānaṃ*), clinging to views (*diṭṭhuppādānaṃ*), clinging to rules and observances (*sīlabbatupādānaṃ*), and clinging to a doctrine of self (*attavāduppādānaṃ*).

“There are some ascetics and brahmins, monastics, who claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging ( *sabbupādānapariññāvādā*). They do not completely describe the full understanding of all kinds of clinging. They describe the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures (*kāmuppādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti*) without describing the full understanding of clinging to views (*diṭṭhuppādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti*), clinging to rules and observances (*sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti*), and clinging to a doctrine of self (*attavāduppādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti*). Why is that? Those good ascetics and brahmins do not understand these three instances as they actually are. Therefore, though they claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging, they describe only the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures without describing the full understanding of clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.

“There are some ascetics and brahmins, monastics, who claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging. They describe the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, without describing the full understanding of clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self. Why is that? Those good ascetics and brahmins do not understand two instances as they actually are. Therefore, though they claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging, they describe only the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, without describing the full understanding of clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self.

“There are some ascetics and brahmins, monastics, who claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging. They describe the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, and clinging to rules and observances without describing the full understanding of clinging to a doctrine of self. Why is that? Those good ascetics and brahmins do not understand one instance as it actually is. Therefore, though they claim to propound the full understanding of all kinds of clinging, they describe only the full understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, and clinging to rules and observances without describing the full understanding of clinging to a doctrine of self.

“Monastics, in such a *Dhamma-vinaya*, confidence in the Teacher is not rightly directed, confidence in the *Dhamma* is not rightly directed, fulfillment of the precepts is not rightly directed, and affection among companions in the *Dhamma* is not rightly directed. Why is that? Because that is how it is when the *Dhamma-vinaya* is badly proclaimed and badly expounded, unemancipating, unconducive to calming, and expounded by one who is not fully enlightened.
commentary_pali:
143. Idāni diṭṭhicchedanaṃ dassento cattārimāni, bhikkhave, upādānānītiādimāha. Tesaṃ vitthārakathā visuddhimagge vuttāyeva.

Sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānāti mayaṃ sabbesaṃ upādānānaṃ pariññaṃ samatikkamaṃ vadāmāti evaṃ paṭijānamānā. Na sammā sabbupādānapariññanti sabbesaṃ upādānānaṃ samatikkamaṃ sammā na paññapenti. Keci kāmupādānamattassa pariññaṃ paññapenti. Keci diṭṭhupādānamattassa paññapenti, keci sīlabbatupādānassāpi. Attavādupādānassa pana pariññaṃ paññapento nāma natthi. Tesaṃ pana bhedaṃ dassento kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapentītiādimāha. Tattha sabbepi kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapentiyeva, channavuti pāsaṇḍāpi hi ‘‘kāmā kho pabbajitena na sevitabbā’’ti vatthupaṭisevanaṃ kāmaṃ kappatīti na paññapenti, akappiyameva katvā paññapenti. Ye pana sevanti, te theyyena sevanti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapentī’’ti.

Sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā Na sammā sabbupādānapariñña kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapentī

Yasmā ‘‘natthi dinna’’ntiādīni gahetvā caranti. ‘‘Sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi, bhāvanāya suddhī’’ti gaṇhanti, attupaladdhiṃ na pajahanti, tasmā na diṭṭhupādānassa, na sīlabbatupādānassa , na attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti. Taṃ kissa hetūti taṃ apaññāpanaṃ etesaṃ kissa hetu, kiṃ kāraṇā? Imāni hi te bhontoti yasmā te bhonto imāni tīṇi kāraṇāni yathāsabhāvato na jānantīti attho. Ye panettha dvinnaṃ pariññānaṃ paññāpanakāraṇaṃ diṭṭhiñceva sīlabbatañca ‘‘etaṃ pahātabba’’nti yathāsabhāvato jānanti. Te sandhāya parato dve vārā vuttā. Tattha ye ‘‘atthi dinna’’ntiādīni gaṇhanti, te diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti. Ye pana ‘‘na sīlena suddhi, na vatena suddhi, na bhāvanāya suddhī’’ti gaṇhanti, te sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapenti. Attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ pana ekopi paññapetuṃ na sakkoti. Aṭṭhasamāpattilābhinopi hi candimasūriye pāṇinā parimajjitvā caramānāpi ca titthiyā tisso pariññā paññapenti. Attavādaṃ muñcituṃ na sakkonti. Tasmā punappunaṃ vaṭṭasmiṃyeva patanti. Pathavijigucchanasasako viya hi ete.

Taṃ kissa hetū Imāni hi te bhonto

Tatthāyaṃ atthasallāpikā upamā – pathavī kira sasakaṃ āha – ‘‘bho sasakā’’ti. Sasako āha – ‘‘ko eso’’ti. ‘‘Kasmā mameva upari sabbairiyāpathe kappento uccārapassāvaṃ karonto maṃ na jānāsī’’ti. ‘‘Suṭṭhu tayā ahaṃ diṭṭho, mayā akkantaṭṭhānampi aṅgulaggehi phuṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ viya hoti, vissaṭṭhaudakaṃ appamattakaṃ, karīsaṃ katakaphalamattaṃ. Hatthiassādīhi pana akkantaṭṭhānampi mahantaṃ, passāvopi nesaṃ ghaṭamatto hoti, uccāropi pacchimatto hoti, alaṃ mayhaṃ tayā’’ti uppatitvā aññasmiṃ ṭhāne patito. Tato naṃ pathavī āha – ‘‘are dūraṃ gatopi nanu mayhaṃ upariyeva patitosī’’ti. So puna taṃ jigucchanto uppatitvā aññattha patito, evaṃ vassasahassampi uppatitvā patamāno sasako pathaviṃ muñcituṃ na sakkoti. Evamevaṃ titthiyā sabbūpādānapariññaṃ paññapentopi kāmupādānādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃyeva samatikkamaṃ paññapenti. Attavādaṃ pana muñcituṃ na sakkonti, asakkontā punappunaṃ vaṭṭasmiṃyeva patantīti.

Evaṃ yaṃ titthiyā samatikkamituṃ na sakkonti, tassa vasena diṭṭhicchedavādaṃ vatvā idāni pasādapacchedavādaṃ dassento evarūpe kho, bhikkhave, dhammavinayetiādimāha. Tattha dhammavinayeti dhamme ceva vinaye ca, ubhayenapi aniyyānikasāsanaṃ dasseti. ‘‘Yo satthari pasādo so na sammaggato’’ti aniyyānikasāsanamhi hi satthā kālaṃ katvā sīhopi hoti, byagghopi hoti, dīpipi acchopi taracchopi. Sāvakā panassa migāpi sūkarāpi pasadāpi honti, so ‘‘ime mayhaṃ pubbe upaṭṭhākā paccayadāyakā’’ti khantiṃ vā mettaṃ vā anuddayaṃ vā akatvā tesaṃ upari patitvā lohitaṃ pivati, thūlathūlamaṃsānipi khādati. Satthā vā pana biḷāro hoti, sāvakā kukkuṭā vā mūsikā vā. Atha ne vuttanayeneva anukampaṃ akatvā khādati. Atha vā satthā nirayapālo hoti, sāvakā nerayikasattā. So ‘‘ime mayhaṃ pubbe upaṭṭhākā paccayadāyakā’’ti anukampaṃ akatvā vividhā kammakāraṇā karoti, ādittepi rathe yojeti, aṅgārapabbatampi āropeti, lohakumbhiyampi khipati , anekehipi dukkhadhammehi sampayojeti. Sāvakā vā pana kālaṃ katvā sīhādayo honti, satthā migādīsu aññataro. Te ‘‘imaṃ mayaṃ pubbe catūhi paccayehi upaṭṭhahimhā, satthā no aya’’nti tasmiṃ khantiṃ vā mettaṃ vā anuddayaṃ vā akatvā vuttanayeneva anayabyasanaṃ pāpenti. Evaṃ aniyyānikasāsane yo satthari pasādo, so na sammaggato hoti, kañci kālaṃ gantvāpi pacchā vinassatiyeva.

evarūpe kho, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye dhammavinaye

Yo dhamme pasādoti aniyyānikasāsanasmiñhi dhamme pasādo nāma, uggahitapariyāpuṭa – dhāritavācittamattake tantidhamme pasādo hoti, vaṭṭamokkho panettha natthi. Tasmā yo ettha pasādo, so punappunaṃ vaṭṭameva gambhīraṃ karotīti sāsanasmiṃ asammaggato asabhāvato akkhāyati.

Yo dhamme pasādo

Yā sīlesu paripūrakāritāti yāpi ca aniyyānikasāsane ajasīlādīnaṃ vasena paripūrakāritā, sāpi yasmā vaṭṭamokkhaṃ bhavanissaraṇaṃ na sampāpeti, sampajjamānā pana tiracchānayoniṃ āvahati, vipaccamānā nirayaṃ, tasmā sā na sammaggatā akkhāyati. Yā sahadhammikesūti aniyyānikasāsanasmiñhi ye sahadhammikā, tesu yasmā ekacce kālaṃ katvā sīhādayopi honti, ekacce migādayo, tattha sīhādibhūtā ‘‘ime amhākaṃ sahadhammikā ahesu’’nti migādibhūtesu khantiādīni akatvā pubbe vuttanayeneva nesaṃ mahādukkhaṃ uppādenti. Tasmā ettha sahadhammikesu piyamanāpatāpi asammaggatā akkhāyati.

Yā sīlesu paripūrakāritā Yā sahadhammikesū

Idaṃ pana sabbampi kāraṇabhedaṃ ekato katvā dassento bhagavā taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hotītiādimāha. Tatrāyaṃ saṃkhepattho – evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti, yaṃ mayā vuttaṃ ‘‘yo satthari pasādo so na sammaggato akkhāyatī’’tiādi, taṃ evameva hoti. Kasmā? Yasmā te pasādādayo durakkhāte dhammavinaye …pe… asammāsambuddhappavediteti, ettha hi yathā tanti kāraṇatthe nipāto. Tattha durakkhāteti dukkathite, dukkhathitattāyeva duppavedite. So panesa yasmā maggaphalatthāya na niyyāti, tasmā aniyyāniko. Rāgādīnaṃ upasamāya asaṃvattanato anupasamasaṃvattaniko. Na sammāsambuddhena sabbaññunā paveditoti asammāsambuddhappavedito. Tasmiṃ aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite. Ettāvatā bhagavā titthiyesu pasādo surāpītasiṅgāle pasādo viya niratthakoti dasseti.

taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ bhikkhave, hotī yathā ta durakkhāte duppavedite aniyyāniko anupasamasaṃvattaniko asammāsambuddhappavedito aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite

Eko kira kāḷasiṅgālo rattiṃ nagaraṃ paviṭṭho surājallikaṃ khāditvā punnāgavane nipajjitvā niddāyanto sūriyuggamane pabujjhitvā cintesi ‘‘imasmiṃ kāle na sakkā gantuṃ, bahū amhākaṃ verino, ekaṃ vañcetuṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti. So ekaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gacchantaṃ disvā imaṃ vañcessāmīti ‘‘ayya brāhmaṇā’’ti āha. Ko eso brāhmaṇaṃ pakkosatīti. ‘‘Ahaṃ, sāmī, ito tāva ehīti. Kiṃ bhoti? Maṃ bahigāmaṃ nehi, ahaṃ te dve kahāpaṇasatāni dassāmīti. Sopi nayissāmīti taṃ pādesu gaṇhi. Are bāla brāhmaṇa, na mayhaṃ kahāpaṇā chaḍḍitakā atthi, dullabhā kahāpaṇā, sādhukaṃ maṃ gaṇhāhīti. Kathaṃ bho gaṇhāmīti? Uttarāsaṅgena gaṇṭhikaṃ katvā aṃse laggetvā gaṇhāhīti. Brāhmaṇo taṃ tathā gahetvā dakkhiṇadvārasamīpaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā ettha otāremīti pucchi. Kataraṭṭhānaṃ nāma etanti? Mahādvāraṃ etanti. Are bāla, brāhmaṇa, kiṃ tava ñātakā antaradvāre kahāpaṇaṃ ṭhapenti, parato maṃ harā’’ti. So punappunaṃ thokaṃ thokaṃ gantvā ‘‘ettha otāremi ettha otāremī’’ti pucchitvā tena tajjito khemaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā tattha otārehīti vutto otāretvā sāṭakaṃ gaṇhi. Kāḷasiṅgālo āha ‘‘ahaṃ te dve kahāpaṇasatāni dassāmīti avocaṃ. Mayhaṃ pana kahāpaṇā bahū, na dve kahāpaṇasatāneva, yāva ahaṃ kahāpaṇe āharāmi, tāva tvaṃ sūriyaṃ olokento tiṭṭhā’’ti vatvā thokaṃ gantvā nivattetvā puna brāhmaṇaṃ āha ‘‘ayya brāhmaṇa mā ito olokehi, sūriyameva olokento tiṭṭhā’’ti. Evañca pana vatvā ketakavanaṃ pavisitvā yathāruciṃ pakkanto. Brāhmaṇassapi sūriyaṃ olokentasseva nalāṭato ceva kacchehi ca sedā mucciṃsu. Atha naṃ rukkhadevatā āha –

‘‘Saddahāsi siṅgālassa, surāpītassa brāhmaṇa;

Sippikānaṃ sataṃ natthi, kuto kaṃsasatā duve’’ti. (jā. 1.1.113);

Evaṃ yathā kāḷasiṅgāle pasādo niratthako, evaṃ titthiyesupīti.
commentary_english:
143. Now, showing the cutting off of views, he says, "These four, monks, are grasping ( *cattārimāni, bhikkhave, upādānāni*)," and so on.
Their detailed discussion is indeed stated in the *Visuddhimagga*.

"Those who profess the doctrine of the complete knowledge of all grasping (*sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā*)" means those who profess, "We declare the transcendence of the knowledge of all grasping," thus professing.
"There is no correct complete knowledge of all grasping (*na sammā sabbupādānapariñña*)" means they do not correctly teach the transcendence of the knowledge of all grasping.
Some teach the knowledge of only grasping at sensual pleasure (*kāmupādānamattassa pariññaṃ paññapenti*).
Some teach the knowledge of only grasping at views, and some [teach] even grasping at ethical practices and vows.
But there is no one who teaches the knowledge of grasping at the doctrine of self.
Now, showing the distinction among them, he says, "Those who teach the knowledge of grasping at sensual pleasure (*kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapentī*)," and so on.
There, all of them indeed teach the knowledge of grasping at sensual pleasure. For even the ninety-six heretics do not teach that the proper practice is the rejection of the basis, saying, "Sensual pleasures should not be cultivated by one who has gone forth," but they teach that it is indeed improper.
But those who cultivate them, cultivate them by stealth.
Therefore, it was said, "Those who teach the knowledge of grasping at sensual pleasure (*kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapentī*)."

Those who profess the doctrine of the complete knowledge of all grasping (*sabbupādānapariññāvādā paṭijānamānā*), [there is] no correct complete knowledge of all grasping (*na sammā sabbupādānapariñña*), those who teach the knowledge of grasping at sensual pleasure (*kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapentī*), because they conduct themselves by taking up, "There is no giving," and so on.
They grasp, "Purification is by ethical conduct, purification is by vows, purification is by meditation," they do not abandon the attainment of self, therefore, they do not teach the knowledge of grasping at views, nor grasping at ethical practices and vows, nor the knowledge of grasping at the doctrine of self.
"What is the reason for that? (*taṃ kissa hetū*)" means what is the reason, what is the cause, for that non-teaching of these? "These, monks (*imāni hi te bhonto*)," means because those monks do not know these three causes as they really are, is the meaning.
Those who here know as they really are the cause of the teaching of the two kinds of knowledge, both views and ethical practices and vows, [saying], "This should be abandoned."
With reference to them, two further statements have been made.
There, those who grasp, "There is giving," and so on, teach the knowledge of grasping at views.
But those who grasp, "There is no purification by ethical conduct, no purification by vows, no purification by meditation," teach the knowledge of grasping at ethical practices and vows.
But not even one is able to teach the knowledge of grasping at the doctrine of self.
Even those who have gained the eight attainments, the heretics who go about caressing the moon and sun with their hands, also teach three kinds of knowledge.
They are not able to relinquish the doctrine of self.
Therefore, again and again, they fall into the cycle itself.
For these are like a rabbit that is disgusted with the earth.

What is the reason for that? (*taṃ kissa hetū*) These, monks (*imāni hi te bhonto*)

There, this is an illustrative simile that accords with the meaning: the earth, it seems, said to a rabbit, "Hey, rabbit."
The rabbit said, "Who is that?"
"[It is] because you, making all bodily activities on top of me, making excrement and urine, do not know me."
