"I have been seen well by you. The place trampled by me is like a place touched by the tips of the fingers, with scattered water, very little, with dung the size of a *kataka* fruit.
But even the place trampled by elephants and horses is great, and their urine is a potful, and even the excrement is a cartload. Enough of you for me!" Having flown up, he fell in another place.
Then the earth said to him, "Hey, even having gone far away, you have indeed fallen on top of me!"
That one, again, disgusted with it, having flown up, fell elsewhere. In this way, even for a thousand years, the rabbit, flying up and falling, is not able to relinquish the earth.
Just so, even though the heretics teach the knowledge of all grasping, they teach the transcendence of only three, beginning with grasping at sensual pleasure.
But they are not able to relinquish the doctrine of self. Not being able, they fall again and again into the cycle itself.

Thus, having spoken of the doctrine of the cutting off of views, in dependence on which the heretics are not able to transcend, now, showing the doctrine of the cutting off of confidence, he says, "In such a doctrine and discipline as this, monks (*evarūpe kho, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye*)," and so on.
There, **"dhammavinaye"** means in the Dharma and in the Vinaya, [the passage] shows that the teaching does not lead out [of saṃsāra] by both of these.

"“The faith in the teacher is not well-gone”" indeed, in the teaching that does not lead out, the teacher, having made time, is sometimes a lion, sometimes a tiger, sometimes a leopard, sometimes a bear, sometimes a hyena. But his disciples are sometimes deer, sometimes pigs, sometimes birds, so he, “These were formerly my attendants, providers of requisites,” without doing patience, loving-kindness, or compassion, falling upon them, drinks [their] blood, and eats thick, thick flesh.

Or the teacher is a cat, and the disciples are chickens or mice. Then he eats them without compassion in just the way that has been said. Or the teacher is a guard of hell, and the disciples are beings in hell. He, “These were formerly my attendants, providers of requisites,” without doing compassion, does various karmic actions, he yokes [them] even to a burning chariot, he makes [them] climb even a mountain of embers, he throws [them] even into a copper pot, he connects [them] with many painful things.

Or the disciples, having made time, are lions, etc., and the teacher is one of the deer, etc. They, “We formerly attended to this one with the four requisites, this is our teacher,” without doing patience, loving-kindness, or compassion towards him, cause unhappiness and ruin in just the way that has been said. Thus, in the teaching that does not lead out, the faith in the teacher is not well-gone, having gone for some time, it afterwards completely perishes.

**"In such a Dharma and Vinaya, O monks,"**

**"The faith in the Dharma"** indeed, in the teaching that does not lead out, the faith in the Dharma, by name, is the faith in the Dharma of the texts, merely [in] the texts that have been learned, recited, and kept in mind, there is no escape from the round [of rebirths] here. Therefore, the faith that is here, again and again only makes the round deep, thus it is said to be not well-gone and not substantial in the teaching.

**"The perfection in virtue"** indeed, that which is the perfection in virtue in the teaching that does not lead out by way of goat-virtue etc., since that does not bring about escape from the round [of rebirths] and release from existence, but bringing about rebirth in the animal womb, ripening in hell, therefore it is said to be not well-gone.

**"Towards fellow practitioners"** indeed, in the teaching that does not lead out, those who are fellow practitioners, since some of them, having made time, are lions, etc., and some are deer, etc., there, those who have become lions, etc., “These were our fellow practitioners,” without doing patience, etc. towards those who have become deer, etc., cause great suffering for them in just the way that has been said before. Therefore, here, even pleasantness and agreeability towards fellow practitioners is said to be not well-gone.

Now the Blessed One, showing all this division of causes, having made [it] into one, **"Why is that? It is thus, O monks,"** etc. In that, this is the meaning in brief: It is thus, O monks, as that which was said by me, “The faith in the teacher is said to be not well-gone,” etc., it is just thus. Why? Since those faiths, etc., [are] in a Dharma and Vinaya that is badly explained…pe… not proclaimed by a Fully Awakened One, here, indeed, **"as that"** is a particle in the sense of cause. There, **"badly explained"** means badly spoken, just because it is badly spoken, [it is] **"badly proclaimed."** But since it does not lead out for the sake of the path and fruit, therefore [it is] **"not leading out."** Because it does not conduce to the calming of lust, etc., [it is] **"not conducive to calming."** [It is] **"not proclaimed by a Fully Awakened One,"** [that is,] not proclaimed by the All-Knowing Fully Awakened One. In that [teaching] that is **"not leading out, not conducive to calming, not proclaimed by a Fully Awakened One."**

To this extent, the Blessed One shows that faith in the sectarians is meaningless, like faith in a jackal that has drunk liquor.

Indeed, once a black jackal, having entered a city at night, having eaten the refuse of liquor, lying down in a punnaga-grove, falling asleep, waking up at sunrise, thought, “It is not possible to go at this time, many are our enemies, it is fitting to deceive one.” Seeing a brahmin going, [he thought,] “I will deceive this one,” [and] said, “Good brahmin!” “Who is this calling a brahmin?” “I am, lord, come here for a moment.”
What is it, lady? Take me to Bahigama, and I will give you two hundred *kahāpaṇa* coins.

Thinking, "I will take him," he seized his feet.

"Hey, foolish *brāhmaṇa*, I don't have abandoned *kahāpaṇa* coins. *Kahāpaṇa* coins are hard to find. Hold me carefully."

"How should I hold you, sir?" "Make a bundle with your upper garment, place it on your shoulder, and hold [me]."

The *brāhmaṇa*, having taken him in that way, went to a place near the southern gate and asked, "Should I set you down here?"

"What is this place called?" "This is the great gate."

"Hey, foolish *brāhmaṇa*, why do your relatives leave the *kahāpaṇa* coin at the inner gate? Take me further!"

He, again and again, going a little, a little, and asking, "Should I set you down here? Should I set you down here?", and being rebuked by him, went to a safe place and, being told, "Set [me] down there!", set [him] down and took the garment.

Kāḷasiṅgāla said, "I said, 'I will give you two hundred *kahāpaṇa* coins.'"

"But I have many *kahāpaṇa* coins, not just two hundred *kahāpaṇa* coins. Until I bring the *kahāpaṇa* coins, you stand looking at the sun," he said, and going a little, returning, again said to the *brāhmaṇa*, "Sir *brāhmaṇa*, don't look here, stand looking only at the sun."

And so saying, having entered the ketaka forest, he departed as he pleased.

Even as the *brāhmaṇa* was looking at the sun, sweat dripped from his forehead and armpits.

Then the tree deity said to him –

"Do you trust Siṅgāla, a *brāhmaṇa* who drinks liquor?

A hundred *sippika* coins do not exist; where are two hundred *kaṃsa* coins?"

(Jā. 1.1.113);

Thus, just as trust in Kāḷasiṅgāla was useless, so it is with the Tīrthikas.

mula_pali: 144. ‘‘Tathāgato ca kho, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho sabbupādānapariññāvādo paṭijānamāno sammā sabbupādānapariññaṃ paññapeti – kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapeti, diṭṭhupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapeti, sīlabbatupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapeti, attavādupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapeti. Evarūpe kho, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo satthari pasādo so sammaggato akkhāyati; yo dhamme pasādo so sammaggato akkhāyati; yā sīlesu paripūrakāritā sā sammaggatā akkhāyati; yā sahadhammikesu piyamanāpatā sā sammaggatā akkhāyati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye suppavedite niyyānike upasamasaṃvattanike sammāsambuddhappavedite.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, when a *Tathāgata*, worthy (*arahaṃ*) and perfectly enlightened (*sammāsambuddho*), claiming to teach the complete understanding of all clinging (*sabbupādānapariññāvādo*), truly elucidates the complete understanding of all clinging, he elucidates the understanding of clinging to sensual pleasures (*kāmupādānassa pariññā*), the understanding of clinging to views (*diṭṭhupādānassa pariññā*), the understanding of clinging to rules and observances (*sīlabbatupādānassa pariññā*), and the understanding of clinging to a doctrine of self (*attavādupādānassa pariññā*).

"Bhikkhus, in such a *Dhamma* and *Vinaya*, confidence in the Teacher is said to be rightly directed; confidence in the *Dhamma* is said to be rightly directed; complete fulfillment in virtuous conduct is said to be rightly directed; and affection among companions in the *Dhamma* is said to be rightly directed.

"Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, that is how it is when the *Dhamma* and *Vinaya* are well-proclaimed (*svākkhāte*) and well-expounded (*suppavedite*), leading to liberation (*niyyānike*), conducive to peace (*upasamasaṃvattanike*), and proclaimed by a perfectly enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddhappavedite*)."
commentary_pali:
144. Aniyyānikasāsane pasādassa niratthakabhāvaṃ dassetvā niyyānikasāsane tassa sātthakataṃ dassetuṃ tathāgato ca kho, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapetīti arahattamaggena kāmupādānassa pahānapariññaṃ samatikkamaṃ paññapeti, itaresaṃ tiṇṇaṃ upādānānaṃ sotāpattimaggena pariññaṃ paññapeti. Evarūpe kho, bhikkhave, dhammavinayeti, bhikkhave, evarūpe dhamme ca vinaye ca. Ubhayenapi niyyānikasāsanaṃ dasseti. Satthari pasādoti evarūpe sāsane yo satthari pasādo, so sammaggato akkhāyati, bhavadukkhanissaraṇāya saṃvattati.

Tatrimāni vatthūni – bhagavā kira vediyakapabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ paṭivasati. Atheko ulūkasakuṇo bhagavati gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisante upaḍḍhamaggaṃ anugacchati, nikkhamante upaḍḍhamaggaṃ paccuggamanaṃ karoti. So ekadivasaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ sāyanhasamaye bhikkhusaṅghaparivutaṃ nisinnaṃ pabbatā oruyha vanditvā pakkhe paṇāmetvā añjaliṃ paggayha sīsaṃ heṭṭhā katvā dasabalaṃ namassamāno aṭṭhāsi. Bhagavā taṃ oloketvā sitaṃ pātvākāsi. Ānandatthero ‘‘ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo sitassa pātukammāyā’’ti pucchi. ‘‘Passānanda, imaṃ ulūkasakuṇaṃ, ayaṃ mayi ca bhikkhusaṅghe ca cittaṃ pasādetvā satasahassakappe devesu ca manussesu ca saṃsaritvā somanasso nāma paccekabuddho bhavissatī’’ti āha –

Ulūkamaṇḍalakkhika, vediyake ciradīghavāsika;

Sukhitosi tvaṃ ayya kosiya, kāluṭṭhitaṃ passasi buddhavaraṃ.

Mayi cittaṃ pasādetvā, bhikkhusaṅghe anuttare;

Kappānaṃ satasahassāni, duggateso na gacchati.

Devalokā cavitvāna, kusalamūlena codito;

Bhavissati anantañāṇo, somanassoti vissutoti.

Aññānipi cettha rājagahanagare sumanamālākāravatthu mahābherivādakavatthu morajikavatthu vīṇāvādakavatthu saṅkhadhamakavatthūti evamādīni vatthūni vitthāretabbāni. Evaṃ niyyānikasāsane satthari pasādo sammaggato hoti.

Dhamme pasādoti niyyānikasāsanamhi dhamme pasādo sammaggato hoti. Saramatte nimittaṃ gahetvā suṇantānaṃ tiracchānagatānampi sampattidāyako hoti, paramatthe kiṃ pana vattabbaṃ. Ayamattho maṇḍūkadevaputtādīnaṃ vatthuvasena veditabbo.

Dhamme pasādo

Sīlesu paripūrakāritāti niyyānikasāsanamhi sīlesu paripūrakāritāpi sammaggatā hoti, saggamokkhasampattiṃ āvahati. Tattha chattamāṇavakavatthusāmaṇeravatthuādīni dīpetabbāni.

Sīlesu paripūrakāritā

Sahadhammikesūti niyyānikasāsane sahadhammikesu piyamanāpatāpi sammaggatā hoti, mahāsampattiṃ āvahati. Ayamattho vimānapetavatthūhi dīpetabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ –

Sahadhammikesū vimānapetavatthūhi

‘‘Khīrodanamahamadāsiṃ, bhikkhuno piṇḍāya carantassa…pe…

Phāṇitaṃ…pe… ucchukhaṇḍikaṃ… timbarusakaṃ… kakkārikaṃ…

Eḷālukaṃ… vallipakkaṃ… phārusakaṃ… hatthapatākaṃ…

Sākamuṭṭhiṃ … pupphakamuṭṭhiṃ… mūlakaṃ… nimbamuṭṭhiṃ…

Ambikañjikaṃ… doṇinimmajjaniṃ… kāyabandhanaṃ…

Aṃsabaddhakaṃ… āyogapaṭṭaṃ… vidhūpanaṃ… tālavaṇṭaṃ…

Morahatthaṃ… chattaṃ… upāhanaṃ… pūvaṃ modakaṃ…

Sakkhalikaṃ ahamadāsiṃ, bhikkhuno piṇḍāya carantassa…pe…

Tassā me passa vimānaṃ, accharā kāmavaṇṇinīhamasmī’’ti (vi. va. 406).

Taṃ kissa hetūtiādi vuttanayānusāreneva yojetvā veditabbaṃ.

Taṃ kissa hetū
commentary_english:
144. Showing that the reverence [in the form] that does not lead out [of *saṃsāra*] in the *Aniyyānika Sāsana* is without benefit and in order to show that the reverence in the *Niyyānika Sāsana* has benefit, [the text] says "*tathāgato ca kho, bhikkhave*," etc.

There, "*kāmupādānassa pariññaṃ paññapetī*": By means of the path of the state of an *arhat*, he makes known the complete understanding and overcoming of the grasping at sensual pleasures and, by means of the path of stream-entry, he makes known the complete understanding of the remaining three kinds of grasping.

"*evarūpe kho, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye*": O monks, in such a *dharma* and *vinaya*. By means of both, he shows the teaching that leads outwards.

"*satthari pasādo*": In such a teaching, that reverence towards the Teacher is said to be in accordance with the *dharma*, and it leads to liberation from the suffering of existence.

Here are the facts: It seems the Blessed One dwells on Mount Vediyaka, in the Indasāla Cave. Then, a certain owl, as the Blessed One enters the village for alms, follows him halfway, and as he leaves, it goes to greet him halfway.

One day, the owl, having descended from the mountain and worshiped the Sammāsambuddha, who was sitting surrounded by a community of monks in the evening, and after circumambulating him, folded its hands in reverence and bowed its head, stood worshiping the Ten-Powered One.

The Blessed One, having looked at it, manifested a smile. The Venerable Ānanda asked, "What, venerable sir, is the cause and the reason for the appearance of a smile?"

"Ānanda, look at this owl; having pleased its mind towards me and towards the community of monks, and having transmigrated through hundreds of thousands of aeons among gods and humans, it will become a *paccekabuddha* named Somanassa," he said:

"Owl, marked by a circle, long-dweller in Vediyaka; you are happy, O noble Kosiya, you see the excellent Buddha at the right time.

Having pleased [its] mind towards me, in the unsurpassed community of monks;

For hundreds of thousands of aeons, it shall not go to a bad state.

Having departed from the world of gods, impelled by skillful roots;

He will become one with endless knowledge, known as Somanassa."

Other facts here in the city of Rājagaha, such as the story of Sumana the garland-maker, the story of the great kettle-drum player, the story of Morajika, the story of the lute player, the story of the conch-blower, and so forth, should be elaborated. Thus, in the teaching that leads outwards, the reverence towards the Teacher is in accordance with the *dharma*.

*dhamme pasādo*: In the teaching that leads outwards, the reverence towards the *dharma* is in accordance with the *dharma*. Merely taking a sign in sound is even the giver of success to beings gone to the animal realm, what then should be said in the highest sense? This meaning should be understood in terms of the story of Maṇḍūka, the son of a god, and so forth.

*dhamme pasādo sīlesu paripūrakāritā*: In the teaching that leads outwards, even the perfect fulfillment of morality is in accordance with the *dharma*, and it brings about the attainment of heaven and liberation. There, the story of Chatta the youth, the story of the novice, and so forth, should be illuminated.

*sīlesu paripūrakāritā sahadhammikesū*: In the teaching that leads outwards, even affection towards those sharing the *dharma* is in accordance with the *dharma*, and it brings about great wealth. This meaning should be illuminated by the stories of the *vimānapeta*.

It was said:

*sahadhammikesū vimānapetavatthūhi*

"I gave milk-rice, to a monk wandering for alms...

...molasses...sugar cane pieces... *timbarusakaṃ*... *kakkārikaṃ*...

*eḷālukaṃ*... *vallipakkaṃ*... *phārusakaṃ*... *hatthapatākaṃ*...

A handful of greens...a handful of flowers...a radish...a handful of *nimba*...

*ambikañjikaṃ*... a ladle for washing a bowl... a waistband...

A shoulder strap... a belt... a fan... a palm leaf fan...

A peacock feather fan... an umbrella... a shoe... a cake... a sweet...

*sakkhalikaṃ* I gave, to a monk wandering for alms..."

"Behold my celestial mansion, I am a nymph of sensuous beauty" (Vi. va. 406).

*taṃ kissa hetū*, etc., should be connected and understood in accordance with the manner previously stated.

*taṃ kissa hetū*

mula_pali:
145. ‘‘Ime ca, bhikkhave, cattāro upādānā. Kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Ime cattāro upādānā taṇhānidānā taṇhāsamudayā taṇhājātikā taṇhāpabhavā. Taṇhā cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Taṇhā vedanānidānā vedanāsamudayā vedanājātikā vedanāpabhavā. Vedanā cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Vedanā phassanidānā phassasamudayā phassajātikā phassapabhavā. Phasso cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidāno kiṃsamudayo kiṃjātiko kiṃpabhavo? Phasso saḷāyatananidāno saḷāyatanasamudayo saḷāyatanajātiko saḷāyatanapabhavo. Saḷāyatanañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānaṃ kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ? Saḷāyatanaṃ nāmarūpanidānaṃ nāmarūpasamudayaṃ nāmarūpajātikaṃ nāmarūpapabhavaṃ. Nāmarūpañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānaṃ kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ? Nāmarūpaṃ viññāṇanidānaṃ viññāṇasamudayaṃ viññāṇajātikaṃ viññāṇapabhavaṃ. Viññāṇañcidaṃ, bhikkhave , kiṃnidānaṃ kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ? Viññāṇaṃ saṅkhāranidānaṃ saṅkhārasamudayaṃ saṅkhārajātikaṃ saṅkhārapabhavaṃ. Saṅkhārā cime, bhikkhave, kiṃnidānā kiṃsamudayā kiṃjātikā kiṃpabhavā? Saṅkhārā avijjānidānā avijjāsamudayā avijjājātikā avijjāpabhavā.

‘‘Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno avijjā pahīnā hoti vijjā uppannā, so avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā neva kāmupādānaṃ upādiyati, na diṭṭhupādānaṃ upādiyati, na sīlabbatupādānaṃ upādiyati, na attavādupādānaṃ upādiyati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassati, aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Cūḷasīhanādasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
145. “Now these four kinds of clinging, *bhikkhus*, what is their source (nidāna), what is their origin (samudaya), what is their nature (jātika), what is their condition (pabhava)? These four kinds of clinging have craving (taṇhā) as their source, craving as their origin, craving as their nature, and craving as their condition.

"And this craving, *bhikkhus*, what is its source, what is its origin, what is its nature, what is its condition? Craving has feeling (vedanā) as its source, feeling as its origin, feeling as its nature, and feeling as its condition.

"And this feeling, *bhikkhus*, what is its source, what is its origin, what is its nature, what is its condition? Feeling has contact (phassa) as its source, contact as its origin, contact as its nature, and contact as its condition.

"And this contact, *bhikkhus*, what is its source, what is its origin, what is its nature, what is its condition? Contact has the six sense bases (saḷāyatana) as its source, the six sense bases as its origin, the six sense bases as its nature, and the six sense bases as its condition.

"And these six sense bases, *bhikkhus*, what is their source, what is their origin, what is their nature, what is their condition? The six sense bases have name and form (nāmarūpa) as their source, name and form as their origin, name and form as their nature, and name and form as their condition.

"And this name and form, *bhikkhus*, what is its source, what is its origin, what is its nature, what is its condition? Name and form have consciousness (viññāṇa) as their source, consciousness as their origin, consciousness as their nature, and consciousness as their condition.

"And this consciousness, *bhikkhus*, what is its source, what is its origin, what is its nature, what is its condition? Consciousness has volitional formations (saṅkhāra) as its source, volitional formations as its origin, volitional formations as its nature, and volitional formations as its condition.

"And these volitional formations, *bhikkhus*, what is their source, what is their origin, what is their nature, what is their condition? Volitional formations have ignorance (avijjā) as their source, ignorance as their origin, ignorance as their nature, and ignorance as their condition."

“Bhikkhus, when ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge (vidyā) has arisen in a bhikkhu, then with the fading away of ignorance and the arising of true knowledge he no longer clings to sensual pleasures (*kāmupādāna*), no longer clings to views (*diṭṭhupādāna*), no longer clings to rules and observances (*sīlabbatupādāna*), no longer clings to a doctrine of self (*attavādupādāna*).

When he does not cling, he is not agitated. When he is not agitated, he personally attains *Nibbana* (parinibbāyati).

‘Destroyed is birth (jāti), the holy life (brahmacariya) has been lived, what had to be done (karaṇīyaṃ) has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being’ (*na paraṃ itthattāyā*)’ he understands.”

This is what the Blessed One (bhagavā) said. Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement (*bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti*).

The Cūḷasīhanāda Suttaṃ is finished, the first.
commentary_pali:
145. Idāni yesaṃ upādānānaṃ titthiyā na sammā pariññaṃ paññapenti, tathāgato paññapeti, tesaṃ paccayaṃ dassetuṃ ime ca, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha kiṃnidānātiādīsu nidānādīni sabbāneva kāraṇavevacanāni. Kāraṇañhi yasmā phalaṃ nideti handa, naṃ gaṇhathāti appeti viya, tasmā nidānanti vuccati. Yasmā taṃ tato jāyati samudeti pabhavati, tasmā samudayo, jāti, pabhavoti vuccati. Ayaṃ panettha padattho – kiṃ nidānaṃ etesanti kiṃnidānā. Ko samudayo etesanti kiṃsamudayā. Kā jāti etesanti kiṃjātikā. Ko pabhavo etesanti kiṃpabhavā. Yasmā pana tesaṃ taṇhā yathāvuttena atthena nidānañceva samudayo ca jāti ca pabhavo ca, tasmā ‘‘taṇhānidānā’’tiādimāha. Evaṃ sabbapadesu attho veditabbo. Yasmā pana bhagavā na kevalaṃ upādānasseva paccayaṃ jānāti, upādānassa paccayabhūtāya taṇhāyapi, taṇhādipaccayānaṃ vedanādīnampi paccayaṃ jānātiyeva, tasmā taṇhā cāyaṃ, bhikkhavetiādimāha.

Yatoca khoti yasmiṃ kāle. Avijjā pahīnā hotīti vaṭṭamūlikā avijjā anuppādanirodhena pahīnā hoti. Vijjā uppannāti arahattamaggavijjā uppannā. So avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādāti. So bhikkhu avijjāya ca pahīnattā vijjāya ca uppannattā. Neva kāmupādānaṃ upādiyatīti neva kāmupādānaṃ gaṇhāti na upeti, na sesāni upādānāni. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassatīti evaṃ kiñci upādānaṃ aggaṇhanto taṇhāparitassanāya na paritassati. Aparitassanti aparitassanto taṇhaṃ anuppādento. Paccattaṃyeva parinibbāyatīti sayameva kilesaparinibbānena parinibbāyati. Evamassa āsavakkhayaṃ dassetvā idāni khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno paccavekkhaṇaṃ dassento khīṇā jātītiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthamevāti.

Yato ca kho Avijjā pahīnā hotī Vijjā uppannā So avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā Neva kāmupādānaṃ upādiyatī Anupādiyaṃ na paritassatī Aparitassa Paccattaṃyeva parinibbāyatī khīṇā jātī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷasīhanādasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
145. Now, to show the condition of those graspings about which the sectarians do not explain the correct understanding, but the Tathāgata explains, he said, "These, monks," etc.

There, in "What is the cause?" etc., all the words beginning with cause are synonyms for *kāraṇa*.

For, because a *kāraṇa* gives a fruit, as if saying, "Here, take it," it is called *nidāna* (cause).

Because that is born, arises, and originates from that, it is called *samudaya* (arising), *jāti* (birth), and *pabhava* (origin).

Here, the meaning of the words is this: "What is the cause of these?" is *kiṃnidānā*.

"What is the arising of these?" is *kiṃsamudayā*.

"What is the birth of these?" is *kiṃjātikā*.

"What is the origin of these?" is *kiṃpabhavā*.

But because for them, craving is the cause, the arising, the birth, and the origin, in the sense previously stated, therefore he said, "craving is the cause," etc.

In this way, the meaning should be understood in all the words.

But because the Blessed One knows not only the condition of grasping, but also the condition of craving, which is the condition for grasping, and he knows the condition of feeling, etc., which are the conditions for craving, etc., therefore he said, "This craving, monks," etc.

"When," that is, at what time.

"Ignorance is abandoned," that is, ignorance, the root of the round [of rebirth], is abandoned by the cessation of non-arising.

"Knowledge arises," that is, knowledge of the path of *arhattva* arises.

"He, through the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge."

That monk, because of the abandoning of ignorance and because of the arising of knowledge.

"He does not grasp sensual grasping," that is, he does not grasp sensual grasping, he does not approach it, nor the remaining graspings.

"Not grasping, he is not agitated," thus, not grasping any grasping, he is not agitated by the agitation of craving.

"Not agitated," not agitating, not producing craving.

"He attains *parinirvāṇa* for himself," that is, he himself attains *parinirvāṇa* by the *parinirvāṇa* of defilements.

Having thus shown the destruction of the influxes for him, now, showing the reviewing of a monk whose influxes are destroyed, he said, "Destroyed is birth," etc.

That is just what has been said.

When ignorance is abandoned, knowledge arises, he, through the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge, does not grasp sensual grasping, not grasping, he is not agitated, not agitated, he attains *parinirvāṇa* for himself, destroyed is birth.

*Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*

The commentary on the *Cūḷasīhanādasutta* is finished.

mula_pali:
146. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati bahinagare aparapure vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena sunakkhatto licchaviputto acirapakkanto hoti imasmā dhammavinayā. So vesāliyaṃ parisati parisatiṃ (sī. pī.) evaṃ etaṃ (pī. ka.) vācaṃ bhāsati – ‘‘natthi samaṇassa gotamassa uttari uttariṃ (pī.) manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso. Takkapariyāhataṃ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ. Yassa ca khvāssa atthāya dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’’ti.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Assosi kho āyasmā sāriputto sunakkhattassa licchaviputtassa vesāliyaṃ parisati evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsamānassa – ‘‘natthi samaṇassa gotamassa uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso. Takkapariyāhataṃ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ. Yassa ca khvāssa atthāya dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’’ti.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sunakkhatto, bhante, licchaviputto acirapakkanto imasmā dhammavinayā. So vesāliyaṃ parisati evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsati – ‘natthi samaṇassa gotamassa uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso. Takkapariyāhataṃ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ. Yassa ca khvāssa atthāya dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Vesālī in the grove outside the city to the west.

Now on that occasion Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, had recently left this Dhamma and Discipline.

He was making this statement before the Vesālī assembly: “The recluse Gotama does not have any superhuman states, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. The recluse Gotama teaches a Dhamma merely hammered out by reasoning, following his own line of inquiry as it occurs to him, and when he teaches the Dhamma to anyone, it leads him when he practises it to the complete destruction of suffering.”

Then, when it was morning, the venerable Sāriputta dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Vesālī for alms.

Then he heard Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, making this statement before the Vesālī assembly: “The recluse Gotama does not have any superhuman states, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. The recluse Gotama teaches a Dhamma merely hammered out by reasoning, following his own line of inquiry as it occurs to him, and when he teaches the Dhamma to anyone, it leads him when he practises it to the complete destruction of suffering.”

Then, having wandered for alms in Vesālī and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, the venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, has recently left this Dhamma and Discipline. He is making this statement before the Vesālī assembly: ‘The recluse Gotama does not have any superhuman states, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. The recluse Gotama teaches a Dhamma merely hammered out by reasoning, following his own line of inquiry as it occurs to him, and when he teaches the Dhamma to anyone, it leads him when he practises it to the complete destruction of suffering.’”
commentary_pali:
146.Evaṃme sutanti mahāsīhanādasuttaṃ. Tattha vesāliyanti evaṃnāmake nagare. Taṃ kira aparāparaṃ visālībhūtatāya ‘‘vesālī’’ti saṅkhaṃ gataṃ. Tatrāyaṃ anupubbakathā – bārāṇasirañño kira aggamahesiyā kucchimhi gabbho saṇṭhāsi. Sā ñatvā rañño nivedesi. Rājā gabbhaparihāraṃ adāsi. Sā sammā pariharīyamānā gabbhaparipākakāle vijāyanagharaṃ pāvisi. Puññavantīnaṃ paccūsasamaye gabbhavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, sā ca tāsaṃ aññatarā, tena paccūsasamaye alattakapaṭalabandhujīvakapupphasadisaṃ maṃsapesiṃ vijāyi. Tato ‘‘aññā deviyo suvaṇṇabimbasadise putte vijāyanti, aggamahesī maṃsapesinti rañño purato mama avaṇṇo uppajjeyyā’’ti cintetvā tena avaṇṇabhayena taṃ maṃsapesiṃ ekasmiṃ bhājane pakkhipitvā paṭikujjitvā rājamuddikāya lañchetvā gaṅgāya sote pakkhipāpesi. Manussehi chaḍḍitamatte devatā ārakkhaṃ saṃvidahiṃsu. Suvaṇṇapaṭṭakañcettha jātihiṅgulakena ‘‘bārāṇasirañño aggamahesiyā pajā’’ti likhitvā bandhiṃsu. Tato taṃ bhājanaṃ ūmibhayādīhi anupaddutaṃ gaṅgāsotena pāyāsi.

Tena ca samayena aññataro tāpaso gopālakakulaṃ nissāya gaṅgātīre viharati. So pātova gaṅgaṃ otiṇṇo taṃ bhājanaṃ āgacchantaṃ disvā paṃsukūlasaññāya aggahesi. Athettha taṃ akkharapaṭṭikaṃ rājamuddikālañchanaṃ ca disvā muñcitvā taṃ maṃsapesiṃ addasa, disvānassa etadahosi ‘‘siyā gabbho, tathā hissa duggandhapūtikabhāvo natthī’’ti. Assamaṃ netvā suddhe okāse ṭhapesi. Atha aḍḍhamāsaccayena dve maṃsapesiyo ahesuṃ. Tāpaso disvā sādhutaraṃ ṭhapesi. Tato puna aḍḍhamāsaccayena ekamekissā maṃsapesiyā hatthapādasīsānamatthāya pañca pañca piḷakā uṭṭhahiṃsu. Atha tato aḍḍhamāsaccayena ekā maṃsapesi suvaṇṇabimbasadiso dārako, ekā dārikā ahosi.

Tesu tāpasassa puttasineho uppajji, aṅguṭṭhakato cassa khīraṃ nibbatti. Tato pabhuti ca khīrabhattaṃ alabhittha, so bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā khīraṃ dārakānaṃ mukhe āsiñcati. Tesaṃ udaraṃ yaṃ yaṃ pavisati, taṃ taṃ sabbaṃ maṇibhājanagataṃ viya dissati, evaṃ nicchavī ahesuṃ. Apare āhu ‘‘sibbetvā ṭhapitā viya nesaṃ aññamaññaṃ līnā chavi ahosī’’ti. Evaṃ te nicchavitāya vā līnacchavitāya vā licchavīti paññāyiṃsu.

licchavī

Tāpaso dārake posento ussūre gāmaṃ sikkhāya pavisati, atidivā paṭikkamati. Tassa taṃ byāpāraṃ ñatvā gopālakā āhaṃsu – ‘‘bhante, pabbajitānaṃ dārakaposanaṃ palibodho, amhākaṃ dārake detha, mayaṃ posessāma, tumhe attano kammaṃ karothā’’ti. Tāpaso sādhūti paṭissuṇi. Gopālakā dutiyadivase maggaṃ samaṃ katvā pupphehi okiritvā dhajapaṭākā ussāpetvā tūriyehi vajjamānehi assamaṃ āgatā. Tāpaso – ‘‘mahāpuññā dārakā appamādena vaḍḍhetha, vaḍḍhetvā ca aññamaññaṃ āvāhavivāhaṃ karotha, pañcagorasena rājānaṃ tosetvā bhūmibhāgaṃ gahetvā nagaraṃ māpetha, tattha kumāraṃ abhisiñcathā’’ti vatvā dārake adāsi. Te sādhūti paṭissuṇitvā dārake netvā posesuṃ.

Dārakā vuddhimanvāya kīḷantā vivādaṭṭhānesu aññe gopālakadārake hatthenapi pādenapi paharanti. Te rodanti. ‘‘Kissa rodathā’’ti ca mātāpitūhi vuttā ‘‘ime nimmātāpitikā tāpasapositā amhe atipaharantī’’ti vadanti. Tato tesaṃ mātāpitaro ‘‘ime dārakā aññe dārake vināsenti dukkhāpenti, na ime saṅgahetabbā, vajjetabbā ime’’ti āhaṃsu. Tato pabhuti kira so padeso vajjīti vuccati yojanasatiko parimāṇena. Atha taṃ padesaṃ gopālakā rājānaṃ tosetvā aggahesuṃ. Tattha ca nagaraṃ māpetvā soḷasavassuddesikaṃ kumāraṃ abhisiñcitvā rājānaṃ akaṃsu. Tāya cassa dārikāya saddhiṃ vivāhaṃ katvā katikaṃ akaṃsu ‘‘bāhirakadārikā na ānetabbā, ito dārikā na kassaci dātabbā’’ti. Tesaṃ paṭhamasaṃvāsena dve dārakā jātā dhītā ca putto ca. Evaṃ soḷasakkhattuṃ dve dve jātā. Tato tesaṃ dārakānaṃ yathākkamaṃ vaḍḍhantānaṃ ārāmuyyānanivāsaṭṭhānaparivārasampattiṃ gahetuṃ appahontā nagaraṃ tikkhattuṃ gāvutantarena gāvutantarena parikkhipiṃsu . Tassa punappunaṃ visālīkatattā vesālītveva nāmaṃ jātaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘vesāliyanti evaṃ nāmake nagare’’ti.

vajjī
commentary_english:
146. Thus have I heard: the Mahāsīhanāda Sutta.

There, *vesāli* means in a city of such a name. It is said that because it was constantly expanding, it came to be called "Vesālī."

Here is the sequential story: It seems that a child was conceived in the womb of the chief queen of a king of Benares (Bārāṇasī). Knowing this, she informed the king. The king gave her the "child-protection" ceremony (gabbhaparihāraṃ). As she was being well cared for, at the time of the child's maturity, she entered the maternity home. For virtuous women, the rising from the womb occurs at dawn, and she was one of those. Therefore, at dawn, she gave birth to a piece of flesh resembling a lump of lac or hibiscus flowers (*alattakapaṭalabandhujīvakapupphasadisaṃ maṃsapesiṃ*). Then, thinking, "Other goddesses give birth to sons like golden statues (*suvaṇṇabimbasadise putte vijāyanti*), but the chief queen gives birth to a piece of flesh—there might be criticism of me in front of the king," out of fear of that criticism, she put that piece of flesh in a vessel, covered it, sealed it with the royal seal, and cast it into the current of the Ganges River (Gaṅgā). As soon as it was discarded by humans, deities arranged for its protection. They inscribed on a gold plate in vermilion (*jātihiṅgulakena*) the words "Offspring of the chief queen of the King of Benares (Bārāṇasī)" and attached it to the vessel. Then that vessel floated along the Ganges River current, undisturbed by fear of waves and other dangers.

At that time, a certain ascetic (tāpaso), relying on a cowherd village, was living on the bank of the Ganges. That morning, having gone down to the Ganges, he saw that vessel coming and picked it up, regarding it as discarded rags (*paṃsukūlasaññāya*). Then, seeing the inscribed plate and the royal seal, he unwrapped it and saw that piece of flesh. Having seen it, he thought, "It could be a fetus, as it does not have a foul, putrid odor." He took it to his hermitage and placed it in a clean place. Then, after half a month, there were two pieces of flesh. The ascetic, seeing this, placed them in an even better place. Then, after another half-month, on each piece of flesh, five swellings appeared for the hands, feet, and head. Then, after another half-month, one piece of flesh became a boy like a golden statue (*suvaṇṇabimbasadiso dārako*), and the other became a girl.

Affection for the children arose in that ascetic. Milk arose from his thumb. From then on, he did not obtain milk-rice. So, after eating his meal, he poured milk into the mouths of the children. Whatever entered their stomachs was visible as if it were inside a crystal vessel. Thus, they were without skin (*nicchavī*). Others said, "Their skin adhered to each other as if stitched together." Thus, they were known as Licchavi (Licchavī) because of their lack of skin or because their skins adhered together.

The ascetic, while raising the children, would enter a village named Ussūra for alms and return late in the day. Knowing of his activity, the cowherds said, "Venerable sir, raising children is an impediment for those who have gone forth. Give us the children; we will raise them. You do your own work." The ascetic agreed. The cowherds, on the second day, leveled the road, scattered it with flowers, raised flags and banners, and came to the hermitage playing musical instruments. The ascetic said, "These children are of great merit. Raise them with diligence. And when they are grown, arrange a marriage between them. After pleasing the king with the five products of the cow, obtain a portion of land, have a city built there, and anoint the boy as king." Having said this, he gave them the children.
They agreed, and so they brought the children away and looked after them.

As the children grew up, they played with the cowherds’ children, and in the course of quarrels they cuffed and kicked them.

They cried.

and when asked by their parents ‘ What are you crying for? ‘, they said ‘These orphans the ascetic used to nurse are hitting us too much ‘.

Then their parents said ‘ These children are bullying and hurting the other children, they must not be kept company with, they must be kept away from ’.

From that time on, that region was called *Vajjī*, with a measurement of one hundred *yojana*s.

Then the cowherds made a present to the king and took over that place.

after which they had a town built there. The boy, who was now sixteen years old, they anointed king.

and they married him to the girl. Then they made an agreement that no girls were to be brought in from outside and that no girls were to be given out from there.

From their first cohabitation two children were born, a daughter (dhītā) and a son (putto).

Sixteen times there were two born in this way.

Then, as those children gradually grew, being unable to secure the prosperity of parks, gardens, dwelling places, sites and retinue, they encircled the city three times at intervals of one *gāvuta*.

Because it was repeatedly made wide (visālīkata), the name Vesālī (vesālī) arose.

Therefore it was said, "In a city named Vesālī (vesālī)."

*Vajjī*

mula_pali:
147. ‘‘Kodhano heso, sāriputta, sunakkhatto moghapuriso. Kodhā ca panassa esā vācā bhāsitā. ‘Avaṇṇaṃ bhāsissāmī’ti kho, sāriputta, sunakkhatto moghapuriso vaṇṇaṃyeva tathāgatassa bhāsati . Vaṇṇo heso, sāriputta, tathāgatassa yo evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yassa ca khvāssa atthāya dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti.

‘‘Ayampi hi nāma, sāriputta, sunakkhattassa moghapurisassa mayi dhammanvayo na bhavissati – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi, satthā devamanussānaṃ, buddho bhagavā’ti.

‘‘Ayampi hi nāma, sāriputta, sunakkhattassa moghapurisassa mayi dhammanvayo na bhavissati – ‘itipi so bhagavā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gacchati, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ karoti, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāno gacchati, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamati, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasati parimajjati; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattetī’ti.

‘‘Ayampi hi nāma, sāriputta, sunakkhattassa moghapurisassa mayi dhammanvayo na bhavissati – ‘itipi so bhagavā dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇāti – dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike cā’ti.

‘‘Ayampi hi nāma, sāriputta, sunakkhattassa moghapurisassa mayi dhammanvayo na bhavissati – ‘itipi so bhagavā parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittanti pajānāti, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittanti pajānāti; sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittanti pajānāti, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ vītadosaṃ cittanti pajānāti; samohaṃ vā cittaṃ samohaṃ cittanti pajānāti, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ vītamohaṃ cittanti pajānāti; saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃkhittaṃ cittanti pajānāti , vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ vikkhittaṃ cittanti pajānāti; mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ mahaggataṃ cittanti pajānāti, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ amahaggataṃ cittanti pajānāti; sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ sauttaraṃ cittanti pajānāti, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ anuttaraṃ cittanti pajānāti; samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ samāhitaṃ cittanti pajānāti, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ asamāhitaṃ cittanti pajānāti; vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ cittanti pajānāti, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ avimuttaṃ cittanti pajānātī’ti.
mula_english:
147. The Blessed One said: “Sariputta, the misguided man Sunakkhatta is angry, and his words are spoken out of anger. Sariputta, the misguided man Sunakkhatta, intending to speak dispraise, speaks only praise of the *Tathāgata*. For it is praise of the *Tathāgata* to say of him: ‘When he teaches the *Dhamma* to anyone, it leads him when he practises it to the complete destruction of suffering.’

“Sariputta, this misguided man Sunakkhatta will never infer of me according to *Dhamma*: ‘That Blessed One is an *arhat*, a *sammāsambuddha* (fully enlightened), perfect in true knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇa-sampanno*), a *sugata* (sublime), a knower of worlds (*lokavidū*), an *anuttara* (incomparable) leader of persons to be tamed (*purisadammasārathi*), a teacher of gods and humans (*satthā devamanussānam*), a *Buddha* (enlightened), a *Bhagavā* (blessed).’

“And he will never infer of me according to *Dhamma*: ‘That Blessed One enjoys the various kinds of supernormal power (*anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti*): having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one; he appears and vanishes; he goes unhindered through a wall, through an enclosure, through a mountain as though through space; he dives in and out of the earth as though it were water; he walks on water without sinking as though it were earth; seated cross-legged, he travels in space like a bird; with his hand he touches and strokes the moon and sun so powerful and mighty; he wields power with his body even as far as the *Brahma* world.’

“And he will never infer of me according to *Dhamma*: ‘With the divine ear element (*dibbāya sotadhātuyā*), which is purified and surpasses the human, that Blessed One hears both kinds of sounds, the heavenly and the human, those that are far as well as near.’

“And he will never infer of me according to *Dhamma*: ‘That Blessed One encompasses with his own mind (*cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti*) the minds of other beings, other persons. He understands a mind affected by lust (*sarāgaṃ*) as affected by lust (*sarāgaṃ cittaṃ*), and a mind unaffected by lust (*vītarāgaṃ*) as unaffected by lust (*vītarāgaṃ cittaṃ*); he understands a mind affected by hate (*sadosaṃ*) as affected by hate (*sadosaṃ cittaṃ*), and a mind unaffected by hate (*vītadosaṃ*) as unaffected by hate (*vītadosaṃ cittaṃ*); he understands a mind affected by delusion (*samohaṃ*) as affected by delusion (*samohaṃ cittaṃ*), and a mind unaffected by delusion (*vītamohaṃ*) as unaffected by delusion (*vītamohaṃ cittaṃ*); he understands a contracted mind (*saṃkhittaṃ*) as contracted (*saṃkhittaṃ cittaṃ*), and a distracted mind (*vikkhittaṃ*) as distracted (*vikkhittaṃ cittaṃ*); he understands an exalted mind (*mahaggataṃ*) as exalted (*mahaggataṃ cittaṃ*), and an unexalted mind (*amahaggataṃ*) as unexalted (*amahaggataṃ cittaṃ*); he understands a surpassable mind (*sauttaraṃ*) as surpassable (*sauttaraṃ cittaṃ*), and an unsurpassed mind (*anuttaraṃ*) as unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ cittaṃ*); he understands a concentrated mind (*samāhitaṃ*) as concentrated (*samāhitaṃ cittaṃ*), and an unconcentrated mind (*asamāhitaṃ*) as unconcentrated (*asamāhitaṃ cittaṃ*); he understands a liberated mind (*vimuttaṃ*) as liberated (*vimuttaṃ cittaṃ*), and an unliberated mind (*avimuttaṃ*) as unliberated (*avimuttaṃ cittaṃ*).’”
commentary_pali:
147.Kodhanoti caṇḍo pharuso. Moghapurisoti tucchapuriso. Yassa hi tasmiṃ attabhāve maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo natthi, taṃ buddhā ‘‘moghapuriso’’ti vadanti. Upanissaye satipi tasmiṃ khaṇe magge vā phale vā asati ‘‘moghapuriso’’ti vadantiyeva. Imassa pana tasmiṃ attabhāve maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo samucchinnoyeva, tena taṃ ‘‘moghapuriso’’ti āha. Kodhā ca panassa esā vācā bhāsitāti esā ca panassa vācā kodhena bhāsitā.

Kasmā panesa bhagavato kuddhoti? Ayañhi pubbe bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā dibbacakkhuparikammaṃ pucchi. Athassa bhagavā kathesi. So dibbacakkhuṃ nibbattetvā ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā devaloke olokento nandanavanacittalatāvanaphārusakavanamissakavanesu dibbasampattiṃ anubhavamāne devaputte ca devadhītaro ca disvā etesaṃ evarūpāya attabhāvasampattiyā ṭhitānaṃ kīvamadhuro nu kho saddo bhavissatīti saddaṃ sotukāmo hutvā dasabalaṃ upasaṅkamitvā dibbasotadhātuparikammaṃ pucchi. Bhagavā panassa dibbasotadhātuyā upanissayo natthīti ñatvā parikammaṃ na kathesi. Na hi buddhā upanissayavirahita tassa parikammaṃ kathenti. So bhagavati āghātaṃ bandhitvā cintesi ‘‘ahaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ paṭhamaṃ dibbacakkhuparikammaṃ pucchiṃ, so ‘mayhaṃ taṃ sampajjatu vā mā vā sampajjatū’ti kathesi. Ahaṃ pana paccattapurisakārena taṃ nibbattetvā dibbasotadhātuparikammaṃ pucchiṃ, taṃ me na kathesi. Addhāssa evaṃ hoti ‘ayaṃ rājapabbajito dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ nibbattetvā dibbasotadhātuñāṇaṃ nibbattetvā cetopariyañāṇaṃ nibbattetvā āsavānaṃ khayañāṇaṃ nibbattetvā mayā samasamo bhavissatī’ti issāmacchariyavasena mayhaṃ na kathetī’’ti. Bhiyyoso āghātaṃ bandhitvā kāsāyāni chaḍḍetvā gihibhāvaṃ patvāpi na tuṇhībhūto vicarati. Dasabalaṃ pana asatā tucchena abbhācikkhanto vicarati. Tenāha bhagavā ‘‘kodhā ca panassa esā vācā bhāsitā’’ti.

Vaṇṇo heso, sāriputtāti, sāriputta, tathāgatena satasahassakappādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni pāramiyo pūrentena etadatthameva vāyāmo kato ‘‘desanādhammo me niyyāniko bhavissatī’’ti. Tasmā yo evaṃ vadeyya, so vaṇṇaṃyeva tathāgatassa bhāsati. Vaṇṇo heso, sāriputta, tathāgatassa guṇo eso tathāgatassa, na aguṇoti dasseti.

Vaṇṇo heso, sāriputtā

Ayampihi nāma sāriputtātiādinā kiṃ dasseti? Sunakkhattena paṭisiddhassa uttarimanussadhammassa attani atthitaṃ dasseti. Bhagavā kira ayaṃ, sāriputta, sunakkhatto moghapuriso natthi tathāgatassa uttarimanussadhammoti vadati. Mayhañca sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ nāma atthi, iddhividhañāṇaṃ nāma atthi, dibbasotadhātuñāṇaṃ nāma atthi, cetopariyañāṇaṃ nāma atthi, dasabalañāṇaṃ nāma atthi, catuvesārajjañāṇaṃ nāma atthi, aṭṭhasu parisāsu akampanañāṇaṃ nāma atthi, catuyoniparicchedakañāṇaṃ nāma atthi, pañcagatiparicchedakañāṇaṃ nāma atthi, sabbepi cete uttarimanussadhammāyeva. Evarūpesu uttarimanussadhammesu ekassāpi vijānanasamatthaṃ dhammanvayamattampi nāma etassa moghapurisassa na bhavissatīti etamatthaṃ dassetuṃ ayampi hi nāma sāriputtātiādinā nayena imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha anvetīti anvayo, jānāti , anubujjhatīti attho. Dhammassa anvayo dhammanvayo, taṃ taṃ sabbaññutaññāṇādidhammaṃ jānanapaññāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. ‘‘Itipi so bhagavā’’tiādīhi evarūpampi nāma mayhaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇasaṅkhātaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ vijjamānameva atthīti jānituṃ tassa moghapurisassa dhammanvayopi na bhavissatīti dasseti. Iddhividhañāṇādīsupi evaṃ yojanā veditabbā.

Ayampi hi nāma sāriputtā ayampi hi nāma sāriputtā anvayo, dhammanvayo,

Uttarimanussadhammādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

commentary_english:
147. "Kodhana" means irritable and harsh. "Moghapurisa" means empty person. For, if in that existence, there is no supporting condition for the path and its fruit, the Buddhas call him "moghapurisa". Even if there is a supporting condition, if at that moment there is no path or fruit, they still call him "moghapurisa". But for this person, in that existence, the supporting condition for the path and its fruit is completely cut off, therefore he called him "moghapurisa". "Kodhā ca panassa esā vācā bhāsitā" means this speech of his was spoken in anger. Why was he angry with the Blessed One? Because previously he approached the Blessed One and asked about the preliminary practice for the divine eye. Then the Blessed One told him. Having developed the divine eye, increasing the light, looking at the deva-world, seeing the deva-sons and deva-daughters experiencing divine fortune in the Nandanavana, Cittalatavana, Pharusakavana, and Missakavana, he, desiring to hear what kind of sound would be very sweet to those abiding in such an attainment of existence, approached the Ten-Powered One and asked about the preliminary practice for the divine ear-element. The Blessed One, knowing that there was no supporting condition for the divine ear-element in him, did not tell him the preliminary practice. For the Buddhas do not tell the preliminary practice to one devoid of a supporting condition. He, harboring resentment towards the Blessed One, thought, "I first asked the ascetic Gotama about the preliminary practice for the divine eye, and he told me, 'May that succeed for me or may it not succeed.' But I, having developed that through my own personal effort, asked about the preliminary practice for the divine ear-element, and he did not tell me that. Certainly, it is like this for him: 'This royal renunciate, having developed the knowledge of the divine eye, having developed the knowledge of the divine ear-element, having developed the knowledge of reading minds, having developed the knowledge of the destruction of the defilements, will become equal to me,' out of envy and stinginess, he does not tell me." Harboring even more resentment, discarding the robes, even having attained the state of a householder, he does not wander silently. But he wanders, falsely accusing the Ten-Powered One with emptiness and worthlessness. Therefore, the Blessed One said, "Kodhā ca panassa esā vācā bhāsitā". "Vaṇṇo heso, sāriputtā", Sāriputta, the Tathāgata, having fulfilled the perfections for four incalculable periods, each exceeding one hundred thousand eons, made effort for this very purpose, "May the teaching of the Dhamma be a means of escape for me." Therefore, whoever would say so, speaks only the praise of the Tathāgata. "Vaṇṇo heso, sāriputta", this is the quality of the Tathāgata, this is the quality of the Tathāgata, not a non-quality, he shows. "Vaṇṇo heso, sāriputtā" "Ayampi hi nāma sāriputtā," with what does he show beginning with this? He shows the existence in himself of the superhuman Dhamma that was rejected by Sunakkhatta. It seems that this Blessed One, Sāriputta, the empty person Sunakkhatta says, "There is no superhuman Dhamma in the Tathāgata." And I have the knowledge of omniscience, I have the knowledge of the various kinds of magical power, I have the knowledge of the divine ear-element, I have the knowledge of reading minds, I have the knowledge of the ten powers, I have the knowledge of the four confidences, I have the knowledge of unwaveringness in the eight assemblies, I have the knowledge of distinguishing the four births, I have the knowledge of distinguishing the five destinies, all these are indeed superhuman Dhammas. To show this meaning that even a trace of the understanding of the Dhamma capable of understanding even one of these superhuman Dhammas will not exist for this empty person, he began this teaching in this way, beginning with "ayampi hi nāma sāriputtā". There, "anveti" means "anvayo", he knows, it means he comprehends. "Dhammassa anvayo" is "dhammanvayo", this is a designation for the wisdom that knows that particular Dhamma, the Dhamma of omniscience, etc. By "itipi so bhagavā," he shows that even such a superhuman Dhamma of mine, reckoned as the knowledge of omniscience, exists, but the empty person will not even have an understanding of the Dhamma to know this. In the case of the knowledge of the various kinds of magical power, etc., the connection should be understood in this way. 0338"/> dhammanvayo,

The description of superior human states and the Dharma is complete.

mula_pali:
148. ‘‘Dasa kho panimāni, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Katamāni dasa?

‘‘Idha, sāriputta, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi , sāriputta, tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Yampi, sāriputta, tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

‘‘Imāni kho, sāriputta, dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

148. “Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* has these ten *Tathāgata's* powers (*tathāgatabalāni*), possessing which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

Which ten?

“Here, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* understands as it actually is the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible.

And that is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

“Again, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* understands as it actually is the results of actions undertaken, past, future, and present, with possibilities and with causes.

That too is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

“Again, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* understands as it actually is the ways leading to all destinations.

That too, Sāriputta, is a power of the *Tathāgata*, by which the *Tathāgata*, claiming the place of a leader, roars the lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the Wheel of Brahma.

“Again, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* understands as it actually is the world with its many and different elements (*anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ*).

That too is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

Again, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* understands as it actually is how beings have different inclinations (*nānādhimuttikataṃ*).

That too is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

“Again, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* understands as it actually is the disposition of the faculties of other beings, other persons.

That too is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

“Again, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* understands as it actually is the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in regard to the *jhānas*, liberations, concentrations, and attainments.

That too is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

Again, Sāriputta, the *Tathāgata* recollects his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many eons of world-contraction, many eons of world-expansion, many eons of world-contraction and expansion: ‘There I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term. Passing away from that [existence], I arose there; there too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term. Passing away from that [existence], I arose here.’

Thus he recollects his numerous past lives in their modes and their details.

That too is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.

Again, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, the *Tathāgata* sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands how beings fare in accordance with their *kamma*: ‘These beings who were ill-conducted in body, speech, and mind, revilers of noble ones, wrong in their views, giving effect to wrong view in their actions, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination, a lower realm, in hell.

But these beings, on account of good conduct of body, speech or thought, of praising the Noble Ones, have right view and will reap the *kammic* reward of right view. At the breaking-up of the body after death they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

Thus with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands how beings fare in accordance with their *kamma*.

That too is a *Tathāgata’s* power that the *Tathāgata* has, by virtue of which he claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma.
Thus, with the divine eye ( *dibba-cakkhu*), purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away (*cavamāne*) and arising (*upapajjamāne*), inferior (*hīne*) and superior (*paṇīte*), beautiful (*suvaṇṇe*) and ugly (*dubbaṇṇe*), fortunate (*sugate*) and unfortunate (*duggate*), and understands beings passing on according to their actions (*yathākammūpage satte pajānāti*).

Furthermore, Sāriputta, the Tathāgata's power is such that, relying on it, the Tathāgata claims the leader's place (*āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti*), roars his lion's roar (*sīhanādaṃ nadati*) in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma (*brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti*).

Again, Sāriputta, the Tathāgata, through the destruction of the taints (*āsavānaṃ khayā*), having realized and directly experienced for himself the taintless deliverance of mind (*anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ*) and deliverance through wisdom (*paññāvimuttiṃ*) in this very life, abides in it.

And again, Sāriputta, the Tathāgata, through the destruction of the taints (*āsavānaṃ khayā*), having realized and directly experienced for himself the taintless deliverance of mind (*anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ*) and deliverance through wisdom (*paññāvimuttiṃ*) in this very life, abides in it; this too, Sāriputta, is a power of the Tathāgata (*tathāgatabalaṃ*) by which the Tathāgata, claiming the leader's place (*āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti*), roars his lion's roar (*sīhanādaṃ nadati*) in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma (*brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti*).

These, Sāriputta, are the ten powers of a Tathāgata (*dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni*) possessing which the Tathāgata claims the leader's place (*āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti*), roars his lion's roar (*sīhanādaṃ nadati*) in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Wheel of Brahma (*brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti*).
commentary_pali:
148. Ettha ca kiñcāpi cetopariyañāṇānantaraṃ tisso vijjā vattabbā siyuṃ, yasmā pana tāsu vuttāsu upari dasabalañāṇaṃ na paripūrati, tasmā tā avatvā tathāgatassa dasabalañāṇaṃ paripūraṃ katvā dassento dasa kho panimāni sāriputtātiādimāha. Tattha tathāgatabalānīti aññehi asādhāraṇāni tathāgatasseva balāni. Yathā vā pubbabuddhānaṃ balāni puññussayasampattiyā āgatāni, tathā āgatabalānītipi attho. Tattha duvidhaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ kāyabalañca ñāṇabalañca. Tesu kāyabalaṃ hatthikulānusārena veditabbaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ porāṇehi –

‘‘Kālāvakañca gaṅgeyyaṃ, paṇḍaraṃ tambapiṅgalaṃ;

Gandhamaṅgalahemañca, uposathachaddantime dasā’’ti.

Imāni hi dasa hatthikulāni. Tattha kālāvakanti pakatihatthikulaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yaṃ dasannaṃ purisānaṃ kāyabalaṃ, taṃ ekassa kālāvakahatthino. Yaṃ dasannaṃ kālāvakānaṃ balaṃ, taṃ ekassa gaṅgeyyassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ gaṅgeyyānaṃ, taṃ ekassa paṇḍarassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ paṇḍarānaṃ, taṃ ekassa tambassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ tambānaṃ, taṃ ekassa piṅgalassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ piṅgalānaṃ, taṃ ekassa gandhahatthino. Yaṃ dasannaṃ gandhahatthīnaṃ, taṃ ekassa maṅgalassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ maṅgalānaṃ, taṃ ekassa hemavatassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ hemavatānaṃ, taṃ ekassa uposathassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ uposathānaṃ, taṃ ekassa chaddantassa. Yaṃ dasannaṃ chaddantānaṃ taṃ ekassa tathāgatassa. Nārāyanasaṅghātabalantipi idameva vuccati . Tadetaṃ pakatihatthigaṇanāya hatthīnaṃ koṭisahassānaṃ purisagaṇanāya dasannaṃ purisakoṭisahassānaṃ balaṃ hoti. Idaṃ tāva tathāgatassa kāyabalaṃ.

kāyabalaṃ

Ñāṇabalaṃ pana pāḷiyaṃ tāva āgatameva. Dasabalañāṇaṃ, catuvesārajjañāṇaṃ, aṭṭhasu parisāsu akampanañāṇaṃ, catuyoniparicchedakañāṇaṃ, pañcagatiparicchedakañāṇaṃ. Saṃyuttake (saṃ. ni. 2.34) āgatāni tesattati ñāṇāni sattasattati ñāṇānīti evaṃ aññānipi anekāni ñāṇasahassāni, etaṃ ñāṇabalaṃ nāma. Idhāpi ñāṇabalameva adhippetaṃ. Ñāṇañhi akampiyaṭṭhena upatthambhanaṭṭhena ca balanti vuttaṃ.

ñāṇabalaṃ bala

Yehi balehi samannāgatoti yehi dasahi ñāṇabalehi upeto samupeto. Āsabhaṃ ṭhānanti seṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ uttamaṭṭhānaṃ. Āsabhā vā pubbabuddhā, tesaṃ ṭhānanti attho. Apica gavasatajeṭṭhako usabho, gavasahassajeṭṭhako vasabho. Vajasatajeṭṭhako vā usabho, vajasahassajeṭṭhako vasabho. Sabbagavaseṭṭho sabbaparissayasaho seto pāsādiko mahābhāravaho asanisatasaddehipi akampaniyo nisabho, so idha usabhoti adhippeto. Idampi hi tassa pariyāyavacanaṃ. Usabhassa idanti āsabhaṃ. Ṭhānanti catūhi pādehi pathaviṃ uppīḷetvā acalaṭṭhānaṃ. Idaṃ pana āsabhaṃ viyāti āsabhaṃ. Yatheva hi nisabhasaṅkhāto usabho usabhabalena samannāgato catūhi pādehi pathaviṃ uppīḷetvā acalaṭṭhānena tiṭṭhati, evaṃ tathāgatopi dasahi tathāgatabalehi samannāgato catūhi vesārajjapādehi aṭṭhaparisapathaviṃ uppīḷetvā sadevake loke kenaci paccatthikena paccāmittena akampiyo acalaṭṭhānena tiṭṭhati. Evaṃ tiṭṭhamānova taṃ āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, upagacchati na paccakkhāti attani āropeti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānātī’’ti.

Yehi balehi samannāgato Āsabhaṃ ṭhāna āsabhaṃ. Ṭhāna

Parisāsūti aṭṭhasu parisāsu. Sīhanādaṃ nadatīti seṭṭhanādaṃ abhītanādaṃ nadati, sīhanādasadisaṃ vā nādaṃ nadati. Ayamattho sīhanādasuttena dīpetabbo. Yathā vā sīho sahanato hananato ca sīhoti vuccati, evaṃ tathāgato lokadhammānaṃ sahanato parappavādānañca hananato sīhoti vuccati. Evaṃ vuttassa sīhassa nādaṃ sīhanādaṃ. Tattha yathā sīho sīhabalena samannāgato sabbattha visārado vigatalomahaṃso sīhanādaṃ nadati, evaṃ tathāgatasīhopi tathāgatabalehi samannāgato aṭṭhasu parisāsu visārado vigatalomahaṃso iti rūpantiādinā nayena nānāvidhadesanāvilāsasampannaṃ sīhanādaṃ nadati. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadatī’’ti. Brahmacakkaṃ pavattetīti ettha brahmanti seṭṭhaṃ uttamaṃ visiṭṭhaṃ. Cakka-saddo panāyaṃ –

Parisāsū Sīhanādaṃ nadatī Brahmacakkaṃ pavattetī brahma

Sampattiyaṃ lakkhaṇe ca, rathaṅge iriyāpathe;

Dāne ratanadhammūra-cakkādīsu ca dissati;

Dhammacakke idha mato, tañca dvedhā vibhāvaye.

‘‘Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, cakkāni, yehi samannāgatānaṃ devamanussāna’’ntiādīsu (a. ni. 4.31) hi ayaṃ sampattiyaṃ dissati. ‘‘Pādatalesu cakkāni jātānī’’ti (dī. ni. 2.35) ettha lakkhaṇe. ‘‘Cakkaṃva vahato pada’’nti (dha. pa. 1) ettha rathaṅge. ‘‘Catucakkaṃ navadvāra’’nti (saṃ. ni. 1.29) ettha iriyāpathe. ‘‘Dadaṃ bhuñja mā ca pamādo, cakkaṃ pavattaya sabbapāṇina’’nti (jā. 1.7.149) ettha dāne. ‘‘Dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pāturahosī’’ti (dī. ni. 2.243) ettha ratanacakke. ‘‘Mayā pavattitaṃ cakka’’nti (su. ni. 562) ettha dhammacakke. ‘‘Icchāhatassa posassa, cakkaṃ bhamati matthake’’ti (jā. 1.1.104; 1.5.103) ettha uracakke. ‘‘Khurapariyantena cepi cakkenā’’ti (dī. ni. 1.166) ettha paharaṇacakke. ‘‘Asanivicakka’’nti (dī. ni. 3.61; saṃ. ni. 2.162) ettha asanimaṇḍale. Idha panāyaṃ dhammacakke adhippeto.

Taṃ pana dhammacakkaṃ duvidhaṃ hoti paṭivedhañāṇañceva desanāñāṇañca. Tattha paññāpabhāvitaṃ attano ariyabalāvahaṃ paṭivedhañāṇaṃ. Karuṇāpabhāvitaṃ sāvakānaṃ ariyabalāvahaṃ desanāñāṇaṃ. Tattha paṭivedhañāṇaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppannanti duvidhaṃ. Tañhi abhinikkhamanato yāva arahattamaggā uppajjamānaṃ, phalakkhaṇe uppannaṃ nāma. Tusitabhavanato vā yāva mahābodhipallaṅke arahattamaggā uppajjamānaṃ, phalakkhaṇe uppannaṃ nāma. Dīpaṅkaradasabalato paṭṭhāya vā yāva arahattamaggā uppajjamānaṃ, phalakkhaṇe uppannaṃ nāma. Desanāñāṇampi pavattamānaṃ pavattanti duvidhaṃ. Tañhi yāva aññātakoṇḍaññassa sotāpattimaggā pavattamānaṃ, phalakkhaṇe pavattaṃ nāma. Tesu paṭivedhañāṇaṃ lokuttaraṃ, desanāñāṇaṃ lokiyaṃ. Ubhayampi panetaṃ aññehi asādhāraṇaṃ, buddhānaṃyeva orasañāṇaṃ.

Idāni yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, yāni āditova ‘‘dasa kho panimāni, sāriputta, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalānī’’ti nikkhittāni, tāni vitthārato dassetuṃ katamāni dasa? Idha, sāriputta, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānatotiādimāha. Tattha ṭhānañca ṭhānatoti kāraṇañca kāraṇato. Kāraṇañhi yasmā tattha phalaṃ tiṭṭhati tadāyattavuttiyāya uppajjati ceva pavattati ca, tasmā ṭhānanti vuccati. Taṃ bhagavā ‘‘ye ye dhammā yesaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ hetū paccayā uppādāya, taṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ. Ye ye dhammā yesaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ na hetū na paccayā uppādāya, taṃ taṃ aṭṭhāna’’nti pajānanto ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Abhidhamme panetaṃ, ‘‘tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇa’’ntiādinā (vibha. 809) nayena vitthāritameva. Yampīti yena ñāṇena. Idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassāti idampi ṭhānāṭṭhānañāṇaṃ tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ nāma hotīti attho. Evaṃ sabbapadesu yojanā veditabbā.

katamāni dasa? Idha, sāriputta, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato ṭhānañca ṭhānato Yampī Idampi, sāriputta, tathāgatassā

Kammasamādānānanti samādiyitvā katānaṃ kusalākusalakammānaṃ, kammameva vā kammasamādānaṃ. Ṭhānaso hetusoti paccayato ceva hetuto ca. Tattha gatiupadhikālapayogā vipākassa ṭhānaṃ. Kammaṃ hetu. Imassa pana ñāṇassa vitthārakathā ‘‘atthekaccāni pāpakāni kammasamādānāni gatisampattipaṭibāḷhāni na vipaccantī’’tiādinā (vibha. 810) nayena abhidhamme āgatāyeva.

Kammasamādānāna Ṭhānaso hetuso abhidhamme

Sabbatthagāmininti sabbagatigāminiṃ agatigāminiñca. Paṭipadanti maggaṃ. Yathābhūtaṃ pajānātīti bahūsupi manussesu ekameva pāṇaṃ ghātentesu imassa cetanā nirayagāminī bhavissati, imassa cetanā tiracchānayonigāminīti iminā nayena ekavatthusmimpi kusalākusalacetanāsaṅkhātānaṃ paṭipattīnaṃ aviparītato sabhāvaṃ jānāti. Imassa ca ñāṇassa vitthārakathā ‘‘tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ? Idha tathāgato ayaṃ maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā nirayagāmīti pajānātī’’tiādinā (vibha. 811) nayena abhidhamme āgatāyeva.

Sabbatthagāmini Paṭipada Yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī abhidhamme

Anekadhātunti cakkhudhātuādīhi kāmadhātuādīhi vā dhātūhi bahudhātuṃ. Nānādhātunti tāsaṃyeva dhātūnaṃ vilakkhaṇatāya nānappakāradhātuṃ. Lokanti khandhāyatanadhātulokaṃ. Yathābhūtaṃ pajānātīti tāsaṃ tāsaṃ dhātūnaṃ aviparītato sabhāvaṃ paṭivijjhati. Idampi ñāṇaṃ ‘‘tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ, idha tathāgato khandhanānattaṃ pajānātī’’tiādinā nayena abhidhamme vitthāritameva.

Anekadhātu Nānādhātu Loka Yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī abhidhamme

Nānādhimuttikatanti hīnādīhi adhimuttīhi nānādhimuttikabhāvaṃ. Idampi ñāṇaṃ, ‘‘tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ, idha tathāgato pajānāti santi sattā hīnādhimuttikā’’ti ādinā nayena abhidhamme vitthāritameva.

Nānādhimuttikata abhidhamme

Parasattānanti padhānasattānaṃ. Parapuggalānanti tato paresaṃ hīnasattānaṃ. Ekatthameva vā etaṃ padadvayaṃ. Veneyyavasena pana dvedhā vuttaṃ. Indriyaparopariyattanti saddhādīnaṃ indriyānaṃ parabhāvaṃ aparabhāvañca, vuddhiñca hāniñcāti attho. Imassapi ñāṇassa vitthārakathā – ‘‘tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ, idha tathāgato sattānaṃ āsayaṃ pajānāti anusayaṃ pajānātī’’tiādinā (vibha. 814) nayena abhidhamme āgatāyeva.

Parasattāna Parapuggalāna Indriyaparopariyatta abhidhamme

Jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnanti paṭhamādīnaṃ catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ rūpī rūpāni passatītiādīnaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ vimokkhānaṃ savitakkasavicārādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ samādhīnaṃ paṭhamajjhānasamāpattiādīnañca navannaṃ anupubbasamāpattīnaṃ. Saṃkilesanti hānabhāgiyadhammaṃ. Vodānanti visesabhāgiyadhammaṃ. Vuṭṭhānanti ‘‘vodānampi vuṭṭhānaṃ. Tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhānampi vuṭṭhāna’’nti (vibha. 828) evaṃ vuttapaguṇajjhānañceva bhavaṅgaphalasamāpattiyo ca. Heṭṭhimaṃ heṭṭhimañhi paguṇajjhānaṃ uparimassa uparimassa padaṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Tasmā ‘‘vodānampi vuṭṭhāna’’nti vuttaṃ. Bhavaṅgena pana sabbajjhānehi vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Phalasamāpattiyā nirodhasamāpattito vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Taṃ sandhāya ‘‘tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhānampi vuṭṭhāna’’nti vuttaṃ. Idampi ñāṇaṃ ‘‘tattha katamaṃ tathāgatassa jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ, jhāyīti cattāro jhāyī, atthekacco jhāyī sampattiṃyeva samānaṃ vipattīti paccetī’’tiādinā (vibha. 828) nayena abhidhamme vitthāritaṃ. Sattannaṃ ñāṇānaṃ vitthārakathāvinicchayo sammohavinodaniyaṃ vibhaṅgaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vutto. Pubbenivāsānussatidibbacakkhuñāṇakathā visuddhimagge vitthāritā. Āsavakkhayakathā bhayabherave.

Jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīna Saṃkilesa Vodāna Vuṭṭhāna abhidhamme vibhaṅgaṭṭhakathāyaṃ visuddhimagge
commentary_english:
148. Here, although the three knowledges should be stated immediately after the knowledge of awareness of the minds of others, since the ten powers of knowledge are not completed when those are stated above, therefore, not stating those, but showing the completion of the *tathāgata's* ten powers of knowledge, he said, "These ten, Sāriputta," and so forth. There, *tathāgatabalāni* means the powers of the *tathāgata* alone, which are not common to others. Or, just as the powers of previous Buddhas are obtained through the perfection of the accumulation of merit, so too, it is the meaning of attained powers. There, the power of the *tathāgata* is twofold: body-power (*kāyabala*) and knowledge-power (*jñānabala*). Among these, body-power is to be understood according to the lineage of elephants. This was said by the ancients: “Kālāva and Gaṅgeyya, Paṇḍara and Tambapiṅgala; Gandhamaṅgalahema and Uposatha Chaddantime are the ten.” These are the ten elephant lineages. There, *kālāvaka* is to be seen as the natural elephant lineage. The body-power of ten men is [equal to] that of one *kālāvaka* elephant. The power of ten *kālāvaka* elephants is [equal to] that of one *gaṅgeyya*. The power of ten *gaṅgeyya* elephants is [equal to] that of one *paṇḍara*. The power of ten *paṇḍara* elephants is [equal to] that of one *tamba*. The power of ten *tamba* elephants is [equal to] that of one *piṅgala*. The power of ten *piṅgala* elephants is [equal to] that of one rutting elephant (gandhahastin). The power of ten rutting elephants (gandhahastin) is [equal to] that of one *maṅgala*. The power of ten *maṅgala* elephants is [equal to] that of one *hemavata*. The power of ten *hemavata* elephants is [equal to] that of one *uposatha*. The power of ten *uposatha* elephants is [equal to] that of one *chaddanta*. The power of ten *chaddanta* elephants is [equal to] that of one *tathāgata*. It is also said that the power of the *nārāyanasaṅghāta* is this very thing. Therefore, this is the power of millions of *koṭis* of elephants according to the calculation of natural elephants, and according to the calculation of men, the power of ten million *koṭis* of men. This, then, is the *tathāgata's* body-power (*kāyabala*). The knowledge-power (*jñānabala*), however, has already come in the Pāli [canon]. The ten powers of knowledge (*daśabala-jñāna*), the four confidences of knowledge (*catu-vaiśārajya-jñāna*), the knowledge of being unshaken in the eight assemblies (*aṣṭha-pariṣāsu-akampana-jñāna*), the knowledge of discerning the four types of birth (*catu-yoni-paricchedaka-jñāna*), the knowledge of discerning the five destinies (*pañca-gati-paricchedaka-jñāna*). In the Saṃyutta (Saṃ. Ni. 2. 34) it has come [that there are] seventy-three knowledges (*jñānāni*), seventy-seven knowledges (*jñānāni*), and thus other various thousands of knowledges (*jñāna-sahasrāṇi*); this is called knowledge-power (*jñānabala*). Here too, knowledge-power (*jñānabala*) is intended. For knowledge (*jñāna*) is called power (*bala*) because of its unshakable nature and its supportive nature. Knowledge-power (*jñānabala*) [is] power (*bala*). "Endowed with which powers (*yehi balehi samannāgato*)": [this means] endowed and fully endowed with which ten knowledge powers (*daśahi jñānabalehi upeto samupeto*). "*Āsabham ṭhāna*": [this means] the best place (*seṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ*), the highest place (*uttamaṭṭhānaṃ*). "*Āsabhā* are previous Buddhas (*pubbabuddhā*), *ṭhāna* is their place," is the meaning. Moreover, an *uṣabha* is foremost among a hundred cows, and a *vṛṣabha* is foremost among a thousand cows. Or, an *uṣabha* is foremost among a hundred *vāja* offerings, and a *vṛṣabha* is foremost among a thousand *vāja* offerings. The bull that is the best of all cattle, that endures all hardships, white, pleasing, carrying a great burden, unshakeable even by the sound of a hundred thunderbolts, that is *niṣabha*, that here is considered an *uṣabha*. This too is a synonym for him. That which belongs to the *uṣabha* is called *āṣabha*. "*Sthāna*" means the immovable state of pressing down on the earth with four feet. This *āṣabha* certainly surpasses the *āṣabha*. Just as the *uṣabha* called *niṣabha*, endowed with the strength of an *uṣabha*, stands having pressed down on the earth with four feet in an immovable position, so too, the *tathāgata*, endowed with the ten powers of a *tathāgata*, having pressed down on the *aṣṭapariṣatpathavī* with four *vaiśārajjapāda*s, unshakeable and in an immovable position in the world with the *sadevaka*s by any adversary or enemy, stands. Thus, remaining in that very *āṣabha sthāna*, he acknowledges, approaches, and does not reject it, [but] places it within himself. Therefore it was said, "He acknowledges the *āṣabha sthāna*."

Endowed with which powers, the *āṣabha sthāna* is *āṣabha*. *Sthāna*
