Again, a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he prevaricates, leads the talk aside, and shows anger, hate, and bitterness. This is a quality that makes him difficult to admonish.

Again, a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he is not pleased with giving explanations. This is a quality that makes him difficult to admonish.

Again, a *bhikkhu* is contemptuous and domineering. This is a quality that makes him difficult to admonish.

Again, a *bhikkhu* is envious and avaricious. This is a quality that makes him difficult to admonish.

Again, a *bhikkhu* is fraudulent and deceitful. This is a quality that makes him difficult to admonish.

Again, a *bhikkhu* is obstinate and arrogant. This is a quality that makes him difficult to admonish.

Again, a *bhikkhu* adheres to his own views, tenaciously clinging to them and relinquishing them with difficulty. This is a quality that makes him difficult to admonish. These, friends, are called the qualities that make him difficult to admonish (*dovacassakaraṇā dhammā*).
commentary_pali:
181.Evaṃme sutanti anumānasuttaṃ. Tattha bhaggesūti evaṃnāmake janapade, vacanattho panettha vuttānusāreneva veditabbo. Susumāragireti evaṃnāmake nagare. Tassa kira nagarassa vatthupariggahadivase avidūre udakarahade suṃsumāro saddamakāsi, giraṃ nicchāresi. Atha nagare niṭṭhite suṃsumāragiraṃ tvevassa nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Bhesakaḷāvaneti bhesakaḷānāmake vane. ‘‘Bhesagaḷāvane’’tipi pāṭho. Migadāyeti taṃ vanaṃ migapakkhīnaṃ abhayadinnaṭṭhāne jātaṃ, tasmā migadāyoti vuccati.

Pavāretīti icchāpeti. Vadantūti ovādānusāsanivasena vadantu, anusāsantūti attho. Vacanīyomhīti ahaṃ tumhehi vattabbo, anusāsitabbo ovaditabboti attho. So ca hoti dubbacoti so ca dukkhena vattabbo hoti, vutto na sahati. Dovacassakaraṇehīti dubbacabhāvakārakehi upari āgatehi soḷasahi dhammehi. Appadakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaninti yo hi vuccamāno tumhe maṃ kasmā vadatha, ahaṃ attano kappiyākappiyaṃ sāvajjānavajjaṃ atthānatthaṃ jānāmīti vadati. Ayaṃ anusāsaniṃ padakkhiṇato na gaṇhāti, vāmato gaṇhāti, tasmā appadakkhiṇaggāhīti vuccati.

Pavāretī Vadantū Vacanīyomhī So ca hoti dubbaco Dovacassakaraṇehī Appadakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsani appadakkhiṇaggāhī

Pāpikānaṃ icchānanti lāmakānaṃ asantasambhavanapatthanānaṃ. Paṭippharatīti paṭiviruddho, paccanīko hutvā tiṭṭhati, apasādetīti kiṃ nu kho tuyhaṃ bālassa abyattassa bhaṇitena, tvampi nāma bhaṇitabbaṃ maññissasīti evaṃ ghaṭṭeti. Paccāropetīti, tvampi khosi itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, taṃ tāva paṭikarohīti evaṃ paṭiāropeti.

Pāpikānaṃ icchāna Paṭippharatī apasādetī Paccāropetī

Aññenaññaṃ paṭicaratīti aññena kāraṇena vacanena vā aññaṃ kāraṇaṃ vacanaṃ vā paṭicchādeti. ‘‘Āpattiṃ āpannosī’’ti vutte ‘‘ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathā’’ti vā vadati. ‘‘Evarūpaṃ kiñci tayā diṭṭha’’nti vutte ‘‘na suṇāmī’’ti sotaṃ vā upaneti. Bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmetīti ‘‘itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpannosī’’ti puṭṭho ‘‘pāṭaliputtaṃ gatomhī’’ti vatvā puna ‘‘na tava pāṭaliputtagamanaṃ pucchāma, āpattiṃ pucchāmā’’ti vutte ‘‘tato rājagehaṃ gatomhī’’ti, rājagehaṃ vā yāhi brāhmaṇagehaṃ vā, āpattiṃ āpannosīti. Tattha me sūkaramaṃsaṃ laddhantiādīni vadanto kathaṃ bahiddhā vikkhipati.

Aññenaññaṃ paṭicaratī Bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmetī

Apadāneti attano cariyāya. Na sampāyatīti, āvuso, tvaṃ kuhiṃ vasasi, kaṃ nissāya vasasīti vā, yaṃ tvaṃ vadesi ‘‘mayā esa āpattiṃ āpajjanno diṭṭho’’ti. Tvaṃ tasmiṃ samaye kiṃ karosi, ayaṃ kiṃ karoti, kattha vā tvaṃ acchasi kattha vā ayantiādinā nayena cariyaṃ puṭṭho sampādetvā kathetuṃ na sakkoti.

Apadāne Na sampāyatī
commentary_english:
181.
evaṃ me suta nti anumānasuttaṃ.
There, bhaggesū means in a country called evaṃnāmaka, the meaning of the word here should be understood according to what has been said.
susumāragire means in a city called evaṃnāmaka.
It is said that on the day of the laying of the foundation of that city, not far away in a water lake, the crocodile made a sound, uttering a cry.
Then when the city was finished, they gave it the name suṃsumāragiraṃ.
bhesakaḷāvane means in a forest called bhesakaḷānāmaka.
‘‘bhesagaḷāvane’’tipi pāṭho.
migadāye means that forest was born in a place where fearlessness was given to birds and deer, therefore it is called migadāyo.

pavāretī means he desires.
vadantū means let them speak by way of instruction and guidance, that is the meaning.
vacanīyomhī means I should be spoken to by you, I should be instructed and advised, that is the meaning.
so ca hoti dubbaco means and he is difficult to speak to, he is difficult to address, he does not endure when spoken to.
dovacassakaraṇehī means by the sixteen qualities that have come upon one who is a maker of the state of being difficult to speak to.
appadakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsani nti yo hi vuccamāno tumhe maṃ kasmā vadatha, ahaṃ attano kappiyākappiyaṃ sāvajjānavajjaṃ atthānatthaṃ jānāmīti vadati.
This one does not take the teaching with respect, he takes it from the left, therefore he is called appadakkhiṇaggāhī.

pavāretī
vadantū
vacanīyomhī
so ca hoti dubbaco
dovacassakaraṇehī
appadakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsani
appadakkhiṇaggāhī
pāpikānaṃ icchāna means of base desires, of aspirations for non-existent becoming.
paṭippharatī means being opposed, having become an enemy, he stands, apasādetī means what is the use of your speech, foolish and unskillful child, even you will think you should speak, thus he strikes.
paccāropetī, even you have fallen into such an offense, first correct that, thus he brings about a counter-charge.

pāpikānaṃ icchāna
paṭippharatī
apasādetī
paccāropetī
aññenaññaṃ paṭicaratī means with one reason or word, he covers up another reason or word.
‘‘āpattiṃ āpannosī’’ti vutte ‘‘ko āpanno, kiṃ āpanno, kismiṃ āpanno, kaṃ bhaṇatha, kiṃ bhaṇathā’’ti vā vadati.
‘‘evarūpaṃ kiñci tayā diṭṭha’’nti vutte ‘‘na suṇāmī’’ti sotaṃ vā upaneti.
bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmetī means when asked ‘‘you have fallen into such an offense’’, saying ‘‘I have gone to Pāṭaliputta’’ and again ‘‘we are not asking about your going to Pāṭaliputta, we are asking about the offense’’, saying ‘‘then I have gone to the royal house’’, whether you go to the royal house or the Brahman house, you have fallen into an offense.
There, saying things like I have obtained pig's meat etc., how does he scatter outwards?

aññenaññaṃ paṭicaratī
bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmetī
apadāne means by his own conduct.
na sampāyatī, friend, where do you live, relying on whom do you live, or, what you say ‘‘I have seen that one falling into an offense’’.
What were you doing at that time, what was he doing, where were you staying or where was he-in this way, asked about his conduct in this manner, he is not able to accomplish and tell.

mula_pali:
182. ‘‘No cepi, āvuso, bhikkhu pavāreti – ‘vadantu maṃ āyasmanto, vacanīyomhi āyasmantehī’ti, so ca hoti suvaco, sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato, khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ, atha kho naṃ sabrahmacārī vattabbañceva maññanti, anusāsitabbañca maññanti, tasmiñca puggale vissāsaṃ āpajjitabbaṃ maññanti.

‘‘Katame cāvuso, sovacassakaraṇā dhammā? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu na pāpiccho hoti, na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na pāpiccho hoti na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu anattukkaṃsako hoti aparavambhī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu anattukkaṃsako hoti aparavambhī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhābhibhūto. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhābhibhūto – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu upanāhī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu upanāhī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu abhisaṅgī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhahetu abhisaṅgī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā. Yampāvuso , bhikkhu na kodhano hoti na kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharati. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharati – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo .

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ na apasādeti. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakaṃ na apasādeti – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakassa na paccāropeti. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena codakassa na paccāropeti – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena apadāne sampāyati. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu codito codakena apadāne sampāyati – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu anissukī hoti amaccharī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu anissukī hoti amaccharī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti amāyāvī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti amāyāvī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu atthaddho hoti anatimānī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu atthaddho hoti anatimānī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī. Yampāvuso, bhikkhu asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti, anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī – ayampi dhammo sovacassakaraṇo. Ime vuccantāvuso, sovacassakaraṇā dhammā.
mula_english:
“Friends, though a bhikkhu does not ask thus: ‘Let the venerable ones admonish me; I need to be admonished by the venerable ones,’ yet if he is easy to admonish (suvaco), possesses qualities that make him easy to admonish (sovacassakaraṇā dhammā), if he is patient and takes instruction rightly,’ then his companions in the holy life think that he should be admonished and instructed, and they think of him as a person to be trusted.

“And what, friends, are the qualities that make one easy to admonish? Here, a *bhikkhu* has no evil wishes (na pāpiccho hoti), and is not dominated by evil wishes. The fact that a *bhikkhu* has no evil wishes and is not dominated by evil wishes – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* does not laud himself (anattukkaṃsako hoti), nor disparage others (aparavambhī). The fact that a *bhikkhu* does not laud himself, nor disparage others – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is not angry (na kodhano hoti), nor allows anger to overcome him (na kodhābhibhūto). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is not angry, nor allows anger to overcome him – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is not angry, or revengeful because of anger (na kodhahetu upanāhī). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is not angry, or revengeful because of anger – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is not angry, or stubborn because of anger (na kodhahetu abhisaṅgī). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is not angry, or stubborn because of anger – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is not angry, and he does not utter words bordering on anger (na kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is not angry, and he does not utter words bordering on anger – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not resist the reprover (codakaṃ nappaṭippharati). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not resist the reprover– this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not denigrate the reprover (codakaṃ na apasādeti). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not denigrate the reprover – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not counter-reprove the reprover (codakassa na paccāropeti). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not counter-reprove the reprover – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not prevaricate, lead the talk aside, and show anger, hate, and bitterness (na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he does not prevaricate, lead the talk aside, and show anger, hate, and bitterness – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he accounts for his conduct (apadāne sampāyati). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is reproved, and he accounts for his conduct – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is not contemptuous and domineering (amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī). The fact that a *bhikkhu* is not contemptuous and domineering – this is a quality that makes him easy to admonish.

“Again, a *bhikkhu* is without envy and is unselfish (anissukī hoti amaccharī).
Again, friends, a *bhikṣu* is not fraudulent or deceitful. This is a quality, friends, that makes a *bhikṣu* easy to admonish.

Again, friends, a *bhikṣu* is not obstinate or arrogant. This is a quality, friends, that makes a *bhikṣu* easy to admonish.

Again, friends, a *bhikṣu* does not adhere to his own views or hold on to them tenaciously, and he relinquishes them easily; this is a quality, friends, that makes him easy to admonish.

These, friends, are called the qualities that make him easy to admonish.

mula_pali:
183. ‘‘Tatrāvuso , bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ anuminitabbaṃ anumānitabbaṃ (sī.) – ‘yo khvāyaṃ puggalo pāpiccho, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ pāpiccho pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na pāpiccho bhavissāmi, na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo attukkaṃsako paravambhī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ attukkaṃsako paravambhī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘anattukkaṃsako bhavissāmi aparavambhī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhābhibhūto, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo. Ahañceva kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhābhibhūto, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhābhibhūto’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhahetu upanāhī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘na kodhano bhavissāmi na kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāressāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena codakaṃ paṭippharati, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena codakaṃ paṭipphareyyaṃ , ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharissāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena codakaṃ apasādeti, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena codakaṃ apasādeyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena codakaṃ na apasādessāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena codakassa paccāropeti, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena codakassa paccāropeyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena codakassa na paccāropessāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicareyyaṃ, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeyyaṃ , kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukareyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarissāmi, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmessāmi, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukarissāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo codito codakena apadāne na sampāyati, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho pana codito codakena apadāne na sampāyeyyaṃ, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘codito codakena apadāne sampāyissāmī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo makkhī paḷāsī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ makkhī paḷāsī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘amakkhī bhavissāmi apaḷāsī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo issukī maccharī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ issukī maccharī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘anissukī bhavissāmi amaccharī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo saṭho māyāvī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ saṭho māyāvī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘asaṭho bhavissāmi amāyāvī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo thaddho atimānī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ thaddho atimānī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘atthaddho bhavissāmi anatimānī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.

‘‘‘Yo khvāyaṃ puggalo sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī, ayaṃ me puggalo appiyo amanāpo; ahañceva kho panassaṃ sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī, ahaṃpāssaṃ paresaṃ appiyo amanāpo’ti. Evaṃ jānantenāvuso, bhikkhunā ‘asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī bhavissāmi anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī’ti cittaṃ uppādetabbaṃ.
mula_english:
"183. Now, friends, a *bhikkhu* ought to infer about himself in the following way: ‘A person with evil wishes and dominated by evil wishes is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to have evil wishes and be dominated by evil wishes, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘I shall not have evil wishes and be dominated by evil wishes.’

‘A person who lauds himself and disparages others is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to laud myself and disparage others, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘I shall not laud myself and disparage others.’

‘A person who is angry and overcome by anger is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to be angry and overcome by anger, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘I shall not be angry and overcome by anger.’

‘A person who is angry and harbors resentment because of anger is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to be angry and harbor resentment because of anger, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘I shall not be angry and harbor resentment because of anger.’

‘A person who is angry and is hardened because of anger is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to be angry and hardened because of anger, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘I shall not be angry and hardened because of anger.’

‘A person who is angry and utters speech influenced by anger is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to be angry and utter speech influenced by anger, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘I shall not be angry and utter speech influenced by anger.’

‘A person who, when censured, retaliates against the one who censures him is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to retaliate against the one who censures me, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘When censured, I shall not retaliate against the one who censures me.’

‘A person who, when censured, disparages the one who censures him is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to disparage the one who censures me, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘When censured, I shall not disparage the one who censures me.’

‘A person who, when censured, accuses the one who censures him in return is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to accuse the one who censures me in return, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘When censured, I shall not accuse the one who censures me in return.’

‘A person who, when censured, equivocates, deflects the discussion elsewhere, and manifests anger, hatred, and discontent is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to equivocate, deflect the discussion elsewhere, and manifest anger, hatred, and discontent, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘When censured, I shall not equivocate, deflect the discussion elsewhere, and manifest anger, hatred, and discontent.’

‘A person who, when censured, does not agree with the grounds for censure is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to not agree with the grounds for censure, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’ A *bhikkhu* who knows this should arouse his mind thus: ‘When censured, I shall agree with the grounds for censure.’"
‘‘‘Indeed, that person is a hypocrite and spiteful. That person is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were a hypocrite and spiteful, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’
Knowing this, a *bhikkhu*, friend, should develop his mind thus: ‘I shall not be a hypocrite and spiteful.’

‘‘‘Indeed, that person is jealous and stingy. That person is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were jealous and stingy, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’
Knowing this, a *bhikkhu*, friend, should develop his mind thus: ‘I shall not be jealous and stingy.’

‘‘‘Indeed, that person is deceitful and a trickster. That person is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were deceitful and a trickster, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’
Knowing this, a *bhikkhu*, friend, should develop his mind thus: ‘I shall not be deceitful and a trickster.’

‘‘‘Indeed, that person is stubborn and arrogant. That person is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were stubborn and arrogant, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’
Knowing this, a *bhikkhu*, friend, should develop his mind thus: ‘I shall not be stubborn and arrogant.’

‘‘‘Indeed, that person adheres to their own views, holds on to them tenaciously, and relinquishes them with difficulty. That person is displeasing and disagreeable to me. If I were to adhere to my own views, hold on to them tenaciously, and relinquish them with difficulty, I would be displeasing and disagreeable to others.’
Knowing this, a *bhikkhu*, friend, should develop his mind thus: ‘I shall not adhere to my own views, I shall not hold on to them tenaciously, and I shall relinquish them easily.’
commentary_pali: 183.Tatrāvusoti , āvuso, tesu soḷasasu dhammesu. Attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ anuminitabbanti evaṃ attanāva attā anumetabbo tuletabbo tīretabbo.
commentary_english: There, *āvuṣo*—*āvuṣo*, among those sixteen *dharmas*. Thus, one should infer oneself by oneself (*attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ anuminitabba*). Thus, oneself should be inferred, weighed, and judged by oneself.

mula_pali:
184. ‘‘Tatrāvuso , bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi pāpiccho, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti? Sace, āvuso , bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘pāpiccho khomhi, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi pāpiccho, na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi attukkaṃsako paravambhī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘attukkaṃsako khomhi paravambhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anattukkaṃsako khomhi aparavambhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhābhibhūto’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kodhano khomhi kodhābhibhūto’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhābhibhūto’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘kodhano khomhi kodhahetu upanāhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhahetu upanāhī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kodhano khomhi kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhahetu abhisaṅgī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kodhano khomhi kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na khomhi kodhano kodhasāmantā vācaṃ nicchāretā’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena codakaṃ paṭippharāmī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ paṭippharāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ nappaṭippharāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena codakaṃ apasādemī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ apasādemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakaṃ na apasādemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena codakassa paccāropemī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakassa paccāropemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena codakassa na paccāropemī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicarāmi, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmemi, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaromī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena aññenaññaṃ paṭicarāmi, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmemi, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaromī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena na aññenaññaṃ paṭicarāmi, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmemi, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaromī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi codito codakena apadāne na sampāyāmī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena apadāne na sampāyāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘codito khomhi codakena apadāne sampāyāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ , āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi makkhī paḷāsī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘makkhī khomhi paḷāsī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘amakkhī khomhi apaḷāsī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi issukī maccharī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘issukī khomhi maccharī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anissukī khomhi amaccharī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi saṭho māyāvī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘saṭho khomhi māyāvī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘asaṭho khomhi amāyāvī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi thaddho atimānī’ti? Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘thaddho khomhi atimānī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘atthaddho khomhi anatimānī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhunā attanāva attānaṃ evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu khomhi sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī’ti? Sace, āvuso , bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī khomhi ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī khomhi anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Sace , āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ, ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, āvuso, itthī vā puriso vā, daharo yuvā maṇḍanajātiko, ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte, acche vā udakapatte, sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno, sace tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati; no ce tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, teneva attamano hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, parisuddhaṃ vata me’ti. Evameva kho, āvuso, sace bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ, ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesū’’ti.

Idamavocāyasmā mahāmoggallāno. Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Anumānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
184. "Furthermore, a monk should review himself thus: 'Am I one with evil wishes, dominated by evil wishes?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am one with evil wishes, dominated by evil wishes,' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I have no evil wishes, I am not dominated by evil wishes,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'Am I one who praises myself and disparages others?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am one who praises myself and disparages others,' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I do not praise myself, nor do I disparage others,' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'Am I irascible and overcome by anger ( *krodha* )?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am irascible and overcome by anger ( *krodha* ),' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am not irascible and not overcome by anger ( *krodha* ),' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'Am I irascible and, due to anger ( *krodha* ), do I harbor resentment ( *upanāhī* )?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am irascible and, due to anger ( *krodha* ), I harbor resentment ( *upanāhī* ),' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am not irascible and, due to anger ( *krodha* ), I do not harbor resentment ( *upanāhī* ),' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'Am I irascible and, due to anger ( *krodha* ), do I bear a grudge ( *abhisaṅgī* )?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am irascible and, due to anger ( *krodha* ), I bear a grudge ( *abhisaṅgī* ),' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am not irascible and, due to anger ( *krodha* ), I do not bear a grudge ( *abhisaṅgī* ),' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'Am I irascible and, under the influence of anger ( *krodha* ), do I let fly with speech?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am irascible and, under the influence of anger ( *krodha* ), I let fly with speech,' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'I am not irascible and, under the influence of anger ( *krodha* ), I do not let fly with speech,' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'When criticized by a critic, do I strike back at the critic ( *codakaṃ paṭippharāmī* )?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I strike back at the critic ( *codakaṃ paṭippharāmī* ),' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I do not strike back at the critic ( *codakaṃ paṭippharāmī* ),' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'When criticized by a critic, do I disparage the critic ( *codakaṃ apasādemī* )?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I disparage the critic ( *codakaṃ apasādemī* ),' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I do not disparage the critic ( *codakaṃ apasādemī* ),' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'When criticized by a critic, do I retort against the critic ( *codakassa paccāropemī* )?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I retort against the critic ( *codakassa paccāropemī* ),' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I do not retort against the critic ( *codakassa paccāropemī* ),' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

"Again, a monk should review himself thus: 'When criticized by a critic, do I evade the issue by turning the discussion to something else, deflecting the conversation outward, and manifesting anger, aversion, and discontent?' If, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I evade the issue by turning the discussion to something else, deflecting the conversation outward, and manifesting anger, aversion, and discontent,' then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states. But if, when he reviews himself, he knows: 'When criticized by a critic, I do not evade the issue by turning the discussion to something else, do not deflect the conversation outward, and do not manifest anger, aversion, and discontent,' then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.
"Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should review himself thus: 'When rebuked by a critic, do I fail to make amends?' If, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'When rebuked by a critic, I fail to make amends,' then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'When rebuked by a critic, I do make amends,' then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.

"Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should review himself thus: 'Am I angry and resentful?' If, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am angry and resentful,' then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am not angry and resentful,' then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.

"Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should review himself thus: 'Am I envious and stingy?' If, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am envious and stingy,' then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am not envious and stingy,' then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.

"Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should review himself thus: 'Am I deceitful and scheming?' If, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am deceitful and scheming,' then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am not deceitful and scheming,' then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.

"Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should review himself thus: 'Am I stubborn and arrogant?' If, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am stubborn and arrogant,' then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I am not stubborn and arrogant,' then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.

"Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu should review himself thus: 'Do I adhere to my own views, holding on tightly, and relinquishing them with difficulty?' If, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I adhere to my own views, holding on tightly, and relinquishing them with difficulty,' then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon those evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu knows: 'I do not adhere to my own views, I do not hold on tightly, and I relinquish them easily,' then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.

"If, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu sees that all these evil, unwholesome qualities are not abandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon all of these evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu sees that all these evil, unwholesome qualities are abandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.

"Just as, friends, a woman or a man, young, youthful, fond of ornaments, on viewing the image of her own face in a clear bright mirror or in a basin of clear water, sees a smudge or a blemish on it, she makes an effort to remove that smudge or blemish, but if she sees no smudge or blemish on it, she becomes glad thus: 'It is a gain for me that it is clean';

Even so, friends, if a bhikkhu, when reviewing himself, sees that all these evil, unwholesome qualities are not abandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu should strive to abandon all of these evil, unwholesome qualities.

But if, friends, when reviewing himself, a bhikkhu sees that all these evil, unwholesome qualities are abandoned in himself, then, friends, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities."

This is what the venerable Mahā-Moggallāna said. The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the venerable Mahā-Moggallāna's words.

The Anumānasutta (Inference Discourse) is finished, the fifth.
commentary_pali:
184.Paccavekkhitabbanti paccavekkhitabbo. Ahorattānusikkhināti divāpi rattimpi sikkhantena, ratiñca divā ca kusalesu dhammesu sikkhantena pītipāmojjameva uppādetabbanti attho.

Acche vā udakapatteti pasanne vā udakabhājane. Mukhanimittanti mukhapaṭibimbaṃ. Rajanti āgantukarajaṃ. Aṅgaṇanti tattha jātakaṃ tilakaṃ vā piḷakaṃ vā. Sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīneti iminā sabbappahānaṃ kathesi. Kathaṃ? Ettakā akusalā dhammā pabbajitassa nānucchavikāti paṭisaṅkhānaṃ uppādayato hi paṭisaṅkhānappahānaṃkathitaṃ hoti. Sīlaṃ padaṭṭhānaṃ katvā kasiṇaparikammaṃ ārabhitvā aṭṭha samāpattiyo nibbattentassa vikkhambhanappahānaṃ kathitaṃ. Samāpattiṃ padaṭṭhānaṃ katvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhentassa tadaṅgappahānaṃ kathitaṃ. Vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā maggaṃ bhāventassa samucchedappahānaṃ kathitaṃ. Phale āgate paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ, nibbāne āgate nissaraṇappahānanti evaṃ imasmiṃ sutte sabbappahānaṃ kathitaṃva hoti.

Acche vā udakapatte Mukhanimitta Raja Aṅgaṇa Sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne paṭisaṅkhānappahānaṃ vikkhambhanappahānaṃ tadaṅgappahānaṃ samucchedappahānaṃ paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ, nissaraṇappahāna

Idañhi suttaṃ bhikkhupātimokkhaṃ nāmāti porāṇā vadanti. Idaṃ divasassa tikkhattuṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ. Pāto eva vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisitvā nisinnena ‘‘ime ettakā kilesā atthi nu kho mayhaṃ natthī’’ti paccavekkhitabbā. Sace atthīti passati, tesaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. No ce passati, supabbajitosmīti attamanena bhavitabbaṃ. Bhattakiccaṃ katvā rattiṭṭhāne vā divāṭṭhāne vā nisīditvāpi paccavekkhitabbaṃ. Sāyaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne nisīditvāpi paccavekkhitabbaṃ. Tikkhattuṃ asakkontena dve vāre paccavekkhitabbaṃ. Dve vāre asakkontena pana avassaṃ ekavāraṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ, appaccavekkhituṃ na vaṭṭatīti vadanti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

bhikkhupātimokkhaṃ

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Anumānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
184. *Paccavekkhitabba* means that which should be reviewed. *Ahorattānusikkhinā* means one who trains day and night, one who trains in wholesome qualities both night and day, meaning that one should only generate joy and gladness.

*Acche vā udakapatte* means in a clear water bowl. *Mukhanimitta* means the reflection of the face. *Raja* means adventitious dust. *Aṅgaṇa* means a birthmark, a mole, or a pimple there. *Sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne* means by this he described the abandonment of all. How? Because for one generating reflection, thinking, "These unwholesome qualities are not suitable for one gone forth," *paṭisaṅkhānappahānaṃ* (abandonment by reflection) is described. For one making moral discipline the foundation, beginning the preliminary work on the kasiṇa, and generating the eight attainments, *vikkhambhanappahānaṃ* (abandonment by suppression) is described. For one making attainment the foundation and developing insight, *tadaṅgappahānaṃ* (momentary abandonment) is described. For one developing insight and cultivating the path, *samucchedappahānaṃ* (abandonment by cutting off) is described. When the fruition comes, *paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ* (abandonment by tranquility) [is described], when *nirvāṇa* comes, *nissaraṇappahāna* (abandonment by escape) [is described]. Thus, in this *sūtra*, the abandonment of all is described.

*Acche vā udakapatte, mukhanimitta, raja, aṅgaṇa, sabbepime pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne, paṭisaṅkhānappahānaṃ, vikkhambhanappahānaṃ, tadaṅgappahānaṃ, samucchedappahānaṃ, paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ, nissaraṇappahāna.*

This *sūtra* is called the *bhikkhupātimokkhaṃ*, so the elders say. This should be reviewed three times a day. In the morning, having entered one's dwelling and sat down, one should review, "Are these many defilements present in me, or are they not?" If one sees that they are present, one should strive for their abandonment. If one does not see them, one should be glad, thinking, "I have gone forth well." Having done the meal duty, having sat down in one's night dwelling or day dwelling, one should review. In the evening, having sat down in one's dwelling, one should review. If one is unable to [do it] three times, one should review [it] two times. If one is unable to [do it] two times, one should necessarily review [it] one time; it is not proper not to review, so they say.

The rest is clear throughout.

*bhikkhupātimokkhaṃ*

The Anumānasuttavaṇṇanā is finished.

mula_pali:
185. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañca cetokhilā appahīnā, pañca cetasovinibandhā cetasovinibaddhā (sī.), cetovinibaddhā (sāratthadīpanīṭīkā) asamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

cetasovinibaddhā (sī.), cetovinibaddhā (sāratthadīpanīṭīkā)

‘‘Katamāssa pañca cetokhilā appahīnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ dutiyo cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghe kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ tatiyo cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhāya kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetokhilo appahīno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetokhilā appahīnā honti.
mula_english:
185. Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Bhikkhus”.

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“Bhikkhus, it is impossible that any bhikkhu in this Dhamma-Vinaya will achieve growth, increase, or abundance if they have not abandoned five mental blockages (*cetokhilā*) and have not severed five mental shackles (*cetasovinibandhā*).

“What are the five mental blockages that they have not abandoned? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, indecisive, and unconfident about the Teacher ( *satthari*). When a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, indecisive, and unconfident about the Teacher, his mind does not incline to ardour (*ātappāya*), devotion (*anuyogāya*), perseverance (*sātaccāya*), and exertion (*padhānāya*). When one’s mind does not incline to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and exertion, that is the first mental blockage that he has not abandoned.

“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, indecisive, and unconfident about the Dhamma…As his mind does not incline to ardour…that is the second mental blockage that he has not abandoned.

“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, indecisive, and unconfident about the Sangha…As his mind does not incline to ardour…that is the third mental blockage that he has not abandoned.

“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, indecisive, and unconfident about the training (*sikkhāya*). When a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, indecisive, and unconfident about the training, his mind does not incline to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and exertion. When one’s mind does not incline to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and exertion, that is the fourth mental blockage that he has not abandoned.

“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is angry and displeased with his companions in the holy life (*sabrahmacārīsu*), resentful and callous (*āhatacitto khilajāto*) towards them. When a bhikkhu is angry and displeased with his companions in the holy life, resentful and callous towards them, his mind does not incline to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and exertion. When one’s mind does not incline to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and exertion, that is the fifth mental blockage that he has not abandoned. These are the five mental blockages that he has not abandoned.
commentary_pali: 185.Evaṃme sutanti cetokhilasuttaṃ. Tattha cetokhilāti cittassa thaddhabhāvā kacavarabhāvā khāṇukabhāvā. Cetaso vinibandhāti cittaṃ bandhitvā muṭṭhiyaṃ katvā viya gaṇhantīti cetaso vinibandhā. Vuddhintiādīsu sīlena vuddhiṃ, maggena viruḷhiṃ, nibbānena vepullaṃ. Sīlasamādhīhi vā vuddhiṃ, vipassanāmaggehi viruḷhiṃ, phalanibbānehi vepullaṃ. Satthari kaṅkhatīti satthu sarīre vā guṇe vā kaṅkhati. Sarīre kaṅkhamāno dvattiṃsavaralakkhaṇappaṭimaṇḍitaṃ nāma sarīraṃ atthi nu kho natthīti kaṅkhati, guṇe kaṅkhamāno atītānāgatapaccuppannajānanasamatthaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ atthi nu kho natthīti kaṅkhati. Vicikicchatīti vicinanto kicchati, dukkhaṃ āpajjati, vinicchetuṃ na sakkoti. Nādhimuccatīti evametanti adhimokkhaṃ na paṭilabhati. Na sampasīdatīti guṇesu otaritvā nibbicikicchabhāvena pasīdituṃ, anāvilo bhavituṃ na sakkoti. Ātappāyāti kilesasantāpakavīriyakaraṇatthāya. Anuyogāyāti punappunaṃ yogāya. Sātaccāyāti satatakiriyāya padhānāyāti padahanatthāya. Ayaṃ paṭhamo cetokhiloti ayaṃ satthari vicikicchāsaṅkhāto paṭhamo cittassa thaddhabhāvo, evametassa bhikkhuno appahīno hoti. Dhammeti pariyattidhamme ca paṭivedhadhamme ca. Pariyattidhamme kaṅkhamāno, tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassānīti vadanti, atthi nu kho etaṃ natthīti kaṅkhati. Paṭivedhadhamme kaṅkhamāno vipassanānissando maggo nāma, magganissando phalaṃ nāma, sabbasaṅkhārapaṭinissaggo nibbānaṃ nāmāti vadanti. Taṃ atthi nu kho natthīti kaṅkhati. Saṅghe kaṅkhatīti suppaṭipannotiādīnaṃ padānaṃ vasena evarūpaṃ paṭipadaṃ paṭipannā cattāro maggaṭṭhā cattāro phalaṭṭhāti aṭṭhannaṃ puggalānaṃ samūhabhūto saṅgho nāma, so atthi nu kho natthīti kaṅkhati. Sikkhāya kaṅkhamāno adhisīlasikkhā nāma adhicittasikkhā nāma adhipaññāsikkhā nāmāti vadanti. Sā atthi nu kho natthīti kaṅkhati. Ayaṃ pañcamoti ayaṃ sabrahmacārīsu kopasaṅkhāto pañcamo cittassa thaddhabhāvo kacavarabhāvo khāṇukabhāvo.
commentary_english:
185. Thus have I heard the Cetokhila Sutta.

There, *cetokhilā* means rigidity of mind, the state of being like rubbish, the state of being like a stake. *Cetaso vinibandhā* means what seizes the mind, as if making a fist, therefore *cetaso vinibandhā*.

In *vuddhi* etc., *vuddhiṃ* through morality, *virūḷhiṃ* through the path, *vepullaṃ* through *nirvāṇa*. Or, *vuddhiṃ* through morality and concentration, *virūḷhiṃ* through the path of insight, *vepullaṃ* through the fruit of *nirvāṇa*.

*Satthari kaṅkhatī* means he doubts the teacher's body or qualities. Doubting the body, he doubts, "Is there indeed a body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, or is there not?" Doubting the qualities, he doubts, "Is there indeed the knowledge of omniscience capable of knowing the past, future, and present, or is there not?"

*Vicikicchatī* means he is troubled while investigating, he encounters suffering, he is unable to decide. *Nādhimuccatī* means he does not attain conviction that "This is so." *Na sampasīdatī* means he is unable to be confident, to become untroubled, by entering into the qualities with a non-wavering attitude.

*Ātappāya* means for the purpose of making an effort that inflames the defilements. *Anuyogāya* means for repeated practice. *Sātaccāya* means for continuous action. *Padhānāya* means for striving.

*Ayaṃ paṭhamo cetokhilo* means this first rigidity of the mind, reckoned as doubt in the teacher, is unabandoned in this monk.

*Dhamme* means in the Dharma of learning and the Dharma of realization. Doubting the Dharma of learning, he doubts, "They say that the Tipiṭaka is the word of the Buddha, eighty-four thousand aggregates of teachings; is this indeed so, or is it not?" Doubting the Dharma of realization, he doubts, "They say that there is a path that is the outflow of insight, a fruit that is the outflow of the path, *nirvāṇa* that is the relinquishing of all formations; is that indeed so, or is it not?"

*Saṅghe kaṅkhatī* means he doubts, "Is there indeed a *saṅgha*, a group of eight individuals, those who have entered the path and those who abide in the fruit, who are practicing such conduct in accordance with the words *suppaṭipanno* etc., or is there not?"

*Sikkhāya kaṅkhamāno* means he doubts, "They say that there is the training in higher morality, the training in higher mind, the training in higher wisdom; is that indeed so, or is it not?"

*Ayaṃ pañcamo* means this fifth rigidity of the mind, the state of being like rubbish, the state of being like a stake, is reckoned as anger towards one's fellow *brahmacārīs*.

mula_pali:
186. ‘‘Katamāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme avītarāgo avigatarāgo (katthaci) hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye avītarāgo hoti…pe… evamassāyaṃ dutiyo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpe avītarāgo hoti…pe… evamassāyaṃ tatiyo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya . Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā honti.

‘‘Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ime pañca cetokhilā appahīnā, ime pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.
mula_english:
186. “And what are the five mental bonds ( *cetaso-vinibandha*) that he has not severed? Here, monks, a monk is not free of passion (*avītarāga*), not free of desire (*avigata-chanda*), not free of affection (*avigata-pema*), not free of thirst (*avigata-pipāsa*), not free of fever (*avigata-pariḷāha*), not free of craving (*avigata-taṇhā*) for sensual pleasures (*kāma*).

When a monk is not free of passion, desire, affection, thirst, fever, or craving for sensual pleasures, then his mind doesn’t tend toward ardency (*ātappa*), commitment (*anuyoga*), perseverance (*sātacca*), or exertion (*padhāna*). As his mind does not incline to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and striving, this is the first mental bond (*cetaso-vinibandha*) that he has not severed.

“Again, monks, a monk is not free from lust for the body (*kāya*)… As his mind does not incline to ardour…that is the second mental bond (*cetaso-vinibandha*) that he has not severed.

“Again, monks, a monk is not free from lust for form (*rūpa*)… As his mind does not incline to ardour…that is the third mental bond (*cetaso-vinibandha*) that he has not severed.

“Again, monks, a monk eats as much as he likes until his belly is full (*yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā*) and indulges in the pleasures of sleeping (*seyyasukha*), lolling (*passasukha*), and drowsing (*middhasukha*). When a monk eats as much as he likes until his belly is full and indulges in the pleasures of sleeping, lolling, and drowsing, then his mind doesn’t tend toward ardency, commitment, perseverance, or exertion. As his mind does not incline to ardour…that is the fourth mental bond (*cetaso-vinibandha*) that he has not severed.

“Again, monks, a monk practices the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ carati*) aspiring to some order of gods (*aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya*) thus: ‘By this virtue (*sīla*) or observance (*vata*) or asceticism (*tapa*) or holy life (*brahmacariya*), I shall become a god (*deva*) or some lesser god (*devaññataro vā*)’. When a monk practices the holy life intent on being born in one or another of the deva hosts, ‘By this virtue or practice or abstinence or holy life I will be a deva of one sort or another,’ then his mind doesn’t tend toward ardency, commitment, perseverance, or exertion. As his mind does not incline to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and striving, this is the fifth mental bond (*cetaso-vinibandha*) that he has not severed. These are the five mental bonds (*cetaso-vinibandha*) that he has not severed.

“Bhikkhus, that any bhikkhu who has not abandoned these five mental hindrances (*ceto-khila*) and severed these five mental bonds (*cetaso-vinibandha*), should come to growth, increase, and fulfilment in this Dhamma and Discipline - that is impossible.
commentary_pali:
186. Vinibandhesu kāmeti vatthukāmepi kilesakāmepi. Kāyeti attano kāye. Rūpeti bahiddhā rūpe. Yāvadatthanti yattakaṃ icchati, tattakaṃ. Udarāvadehakanti udarapūraṃ. Tañhi udaraṃ avadehanato udarāvadehakanti vuccati. Seyyasukhanti mañcapīṭhasukhaṃ, utusukhaṃ vā. Passasukhanti yathā samparivattakaṃ sayantassa dakkhiṇapassavāmapassānaṃ sukhaṃ hoti, evaṃ uppannasukhaṃ. Middhasukhanti niddāsukhaṃ. Anuyuttoti yuttapayutto viharati.

Paṇidhāyāti patthayitvā. Sīlenātiādīsu sīlanti catupārisuddhisīlaṃ. Vatanti vatasamādānaṃ. Tapoti tapacaraṇaṃ. Brahmacariyanti methunavirati. Devo vā bhavissāmīti mahesakkhadevo vā bhavissāmi. Devaññataro vāpi appesakkhadevesu vā aññataro.

Paṇidhāyā Sīlenā sīla Vata Tapo Brahmacariya Devo vā bhavissāmī Devaññataro vā
commentary_english:
186. In bonds, *kāme* means both the object of desire (vatthukāma) and the defilement of desire (kilesakāma). *Kāye* means in one's own body. *Rūpe* means in external form. *Yāvadattha* means as much as one wants, that much. *Udarāvadehaka* means filling the belly. For that belly is called udarāvadehaka because of filling the belly. *Seyyasukha* means the pleasure of couch and chair, or the pleasure of the seasons. *Passasukha* means the pleasure that arises when lying down, such as the pleasure of the right side or left side while lying with changing sides. *Middhasukha* means the pleasure of sleep. *Anuyutto* means lives engaged and devoted.

*Paṇidhāyā* means desiring. In *sīlenā*, etc., *sīla* means the fourfold purity of morality (catupārisuddhisīlaṃ). *Vata* means undertaking a vow (vatasamādānaṃ). *Tapo* means practicing asceticism (tapacaraṇaṃ). *Brahmacariya* means abstinence from sexual intercourse (methunavirati). *Devo vā bhavissāmī* means I will become a god of great power (mahesakkhadevo). *Devaññataro vā* means or one of the gods of little power (appesakkhadevesu).

*Paṇidhāyā, sīlenā, sīla, vata, tapo, brahmacariya, devo vā bhavissāmī, devaññataro vā*

mula_pali:
187. ‘‘Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañca cetokhilā pahīnā, pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

‘‘Katamāssa pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ dutiyo cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghe na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ tatiyo cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhāya na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati…pe… evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu na kupito hoti na anattamano attamano (sī. pī.) anāhatacitto akhilajāto. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu na kupito hoti na anattamano anāhatacitto akhilajāto, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetokhilo pahīno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti.

attamano (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
187.  “Bhikkhus, that any *bhikkhu* who has abandoned five wildernesses of the heart ( *pañca cetokhilā pahīnā*), and severed five mental bonds (*pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā*) should come to growth (*vuddhiṃ*), increase (*virūḷhiṃ*), and fulfilment (*vepullaṃ āpajjissati*) in this *Dhamma* and Discipline (*dhammavinaye*) - that is possible (*ṭhānametaṃ vijjati*).

“What are the five wildernesses of the heart that he has abandoned (*katamāssa pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti*)? Here (*idha*), *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is not doubtful (*na kaṅkhati*) , uncertain (*na vicikicchati*),  decided (*adhimuccati*), and confident (*sampasīdati*) about the Teacher (*satthari*).
When a *bhikkhu* is not doubtful (*na kaṅkhati*) , uncertain (*na vicikicchati*), decided (*adhimuccati*), and confident (*sampasīdati*) about the Teacher (*satthari*), his mind (*cittaṃ*) inclines (*namati*) to ardour (*ātappāya*), devotion (*anuyogāya*), perseverance (*sātaccāya*), and striving (*padhānāya*).
As his mind inclines to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and striving, the first wilderness of the heart (*paṭhamo cetokhilo*) has been abandoned (*pahīno hoti*) by him.

“Again (*puna caparaṃ*), *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is not doubtful (*na kaṅkhati*), uncertain (*na vicikicchati*), decided (*adhimuccati*), and confident (*sampasīdati*) about the Dhamma (*dhamme*)… As his mind inclines to ardour…the second wilderness of the heart (*dutiyo cetokhilo*) has been abandoned (*pahīno hoti*) by him.

“Again (*puna caparaṃ*), *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is not doubtful (*na kaṅkhati*), uncertain (*na vicikicchati*), decided (*adhimuccati*), and confident (*sampasīdati*) about the Sangha (*saṅghe*)… As his mind inclines to ardour…the third wilderness of the heart (*tatiyo cetokhilo*) has been abandoned (*pahīno hoti*) by him.

“Again (*puna caparaṃ*), *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is not doubtful (*na kaṅkhati*), uncertain (*na vicikicchati*), decided (*adhimuccati*), and confident (*sampasīdati*) about the training (*sikkhāya*)… As his mind inclines to ardour…the fourth wilderness of the heart (*catuttho cetokhilo*) has been abandoned (*pahīno hoti*) by him.

“Again (*puna caparaṃ*), *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is not angry (*na kupito hoti*) and displeased (*na anattamano*) with his companions in the holy life (*sabrahmacārīsu*), nor resentful (*anāhatacitto*) and callous (*akhilajāto*) towards them.
When a *bhikkhu* is not angry and displeased with his companions in the holy life, nor resentful and callous towards them, his mind (*cittaṃ*) inclines (*namati*) to ardour (*ātappāya*), devotion (*anuyogāya*), perseverance (*sātaccāya*), and striving (*padhānāya*).
As his mind inclines to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and striving, the fifth wilderness in the heart (*pañcamo cetokhilo*) has been abandoned (*pahīno hoti*) by him.
These are the five wildernesses in the heart that he has abandoned (*imāssa pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti*).

mula_pali:
188. ‘‘Katamāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāme vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye vītarāgo hoti…pe… rūpe vītarāgo hoti…pe… na yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ catuttho cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti. Imāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā honti.

‘‘Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ime pañca cetokhilā pahīnā, ime pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā, so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.
mula_english:
188. "What, bhikkhus, are the five shackles in the heart that he has severed? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, and craving for sensual pleasures (kāme vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho). When a monk is free of passion, desire, love, thirst, fever, or craving for sensual pleasures, then his mind tends toward ardency, commitment, perseverance, or exertion (tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya). As his mind inclines to ardour, devotion, perseverance, and striving, the first shackle in the heart has been severed by him (evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti).

“Again, a bhikkhu is free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, and craving for the body… free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, and craving for form… does not eat as much as he likes until his belly is full and indulges in the pleasures of sleeping, lolling, and drowsing (na yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati). Again, a bhikkhu does not eat as much as he likes until his belly is full and does not indulge in the pleasures of sleeping, lolling, and drowsing, then his mind tends toward ardency, commitment, perseverance, or exertion. As his mind inclines to ardour…the fourth shackle in the heart has been severed by him.

“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not practice the holy life intent on being born in one or another of the deva hosts, ‘By this virtue or practice or abstinence or holy life, may I become a deva of one sort or another.’ (na aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti). When a monk does not practice the holy life intent on being born in one or another of the deva hosts…then his mind tends toward ardency, commitment, perseverance, or exertion. As his mind inclines to ardour…the fifth shackle in the heart has been severed by him. These are the five shackles in the heart that he has severed (imāssa pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā honti).

“Bhikkhus, that any bhikkhu who has abandoned these five wildernesses in the heart and severed these five shackles in the heart should come to growth, increase, and fulfilment in this Dhamma and Discipline - that is possible (so vatimasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati).

mula_pali:
189. ‘‘So chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, ussoḷhīyeva pañcamī. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, evaṃ ussoḷhīpannarasaṅgasamannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo abhinibbidāya, bhabbo sambodhāya, bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā. Tānassu kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitāni sammā pariseditāni sammā paribhāvitāni. Kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyā na evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vatime kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjeyyu’nti. Atha kho bhabbāva te kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, evaṃ ussoḷhipannarasaṅgasamannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo abhinibbidāya, bhabbo sambodhāya, bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Cetokhilasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
“He cultivates the basis for spiritual power consisting of concentration due to zeal with determined striving (*chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti*); he cultivates the basis for spiritual power consisting of concentration due to energy with determined striving (*vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti*); he cultivates the basis for spiritual power consisting of concentration due to purity of mind with determined striving; he cultivates the basis for spiritual power consisting of concentration due to investigation with determined striving (*vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti*). And enthusiasm is the fifth.

"So too, a *bhikkhu* who possesses the fifteen factors including enthusiasm is capable of breaking out, capable of enlightenment, capable of attaining the supreme security from bondage."

“Suppose there were a hen with eight, ten, or twelve eggs. which she had properly covered, warmed, and incubated. Even though she did not wish: ‘Oh, that my chicks might pierce their shells with the points of their claws and beaks and hatch out safely! ‘ yet the chicks are capable of piercing their shells with the points of their claws and beaks and hatching out safely.

“So too, a *bhikkhu* who thus possesses the fifteen factors including enthusiasm is capable of breaking out, capable of enlightenment, capable of attaining the supreme safety from bondage.”

The Buddha spoke thus.

Gratified, the monks delighted at his words.

The Cetokhila Sutta, the sixth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
189. Iddhipādesu chandaṃ nissāya pavatto samādhi chandasamādhi. Padhānabhūtā saṅkhārā padhānasaṅkhārā. Samannāgatanti tehi dhammehi upetaṃ. Iddhiyā pādaṃ, iddhibhūtaṃ vā pādanti iddhipādaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo, ayamettha saṅkhepo. Vitthāro pana iddhipādavibhaṅge āgato yeva. Visuddhimaggepissa attho dīpito. Iti imehi catūhi iddhipādehi vikkhambhanappahānaṃ kathitaṃ. Ussoḷhīyeva pañcamīti ettha ussoḷhīti sabbattha kattabbavīriyaṃ dasseti. Ussoḷhīpannarasaṅgasamannāgatoti pañca cetokhilappahānāni pañca vinibandhappahānāni cattāro iddhipādā ussoḷhīti evaṃ ussoḷhiyā saddhiṃ pannarasahi aṅgehi samannāgato. Bhabboti anurūpo, anucchaviko. Abhinibbhidāyāti ñāṇena kilesabhedāya. Sambodhāyāti catumaggasambodhāya. Anuttarassāti seṭṭhassa. Yogakkhemassāti catūhi yogehi khemassa arahattassa. Adhigamāyāti paṭilābhāya. Seyyathāti opammatthe nipāto. Pīti sambhāvanatthe. Ubhayenapi seyyathāpi nāma, bhikkhaveti dasseti .

Kukkuṭiyāaṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vāti ettha pana kiñcāpi kukkuṭiyā vuttappakārato ūnādhikānipi aṇḍāni honti, vacanasiliṭṭhatāya pana evaṃ vuttaṃ. Evañhi loke siliṭṭhaṃ vacanaṃ hoti. Tānassūti tāni assu, bhaveyyunti attho. Kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitānīti tāya janettiyā kukkuṭiyā pakkhe pasāretvā tesaṃ upari sayantiyā sammā adhisayitāni. Sammā pariseditānīti kālena kālaṃ utuṃ gāhāpentiyā suṭṭhu samantato seditāni usmīkatāni. Sammā paribhāvitānīti kālena kālaṃ suṭṭhu samantato bhāvitāni, kukkuṭagandhaṃ gāhāpitānīti attho. Kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyāti tassā kukkuṭiyā imaṃ tividhakiriyākaraṇena appamādaṃ katvā kiñcāpi na evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya. Atha kho bhabbāva teti atha kho te kukkuṭapotakā vuttanayena sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṃ bhabbāva. Te hi yasmā tāya kukkuṭiyā evaṃ tīhākārehi tāni aṇḍāni paripālīyamānāni na pūtīni honti. Yopi nesaṃ allasineho, sopi pariyādānaṃ gacchati, kapālaṃ tanukaṃ hoti, pādanakhasikhā ca mukhatuṇḍakañca kharaṃ hoti, sayaṃ paripākaṃ gacchati, kapālassa tanuttā bahi āloko anto paññāyati, tasmā ‘‘ciraṃ vata mayaṃ saṅkuṭitahatthapādā sambādhe sayimhā, ayañca bahi āloko dissati, ettha dāni no sukhavihāro bhavissatī’’ti nikkhamitukāmā hutvā kapālaṃ pādena paharanti, gīvaṃ pasārenti, tato taṃ kapālaṃ dvedhā bhijjati. Atha te pakkhe vidhunantā taṅkhaṇānurūpaṃ viravantā nikkhamantiyeva, nikkhamitvā ca gāmakkhettaṃ upasobhayamānā vicaranti.

Kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā Tānassū Kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitānī Sammā pariseditānī Sammā paribhāvitānī Kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyā Atha kho bhabbāva te

Evameva khoti idaṃ opammasampaṭipādanaṃ. Taṃ evaṃ atthena saṃsandetvā veditabbaṃ – tassā kukkuṭiyā aṇḍesu tividhakiriyākaraṇaṃ viya hi imassa bhikkhuno ussoḷhīpannarasehi aṅgehi samannāgatabhāvo. Kukkuṭiyā tividhakiriyāsampādanena aṇḍānaṃ apūtibhāvo viya pannarasaṅgasamannāgatassa bhikkhuno tividhānupassanāsampādanena vipassanāñāṇassa aparihāni. Tassā tividhakiriyākaraṇena aṇḍānaṃ allasinehapariyādānaṃ viya tassa bhikkhuno tividhānupassanāsampādanena bhavattayānugatanikantisinehapariyādānaṃ . Aṇḍakalāpānaṃ tanubhāvo viya bhikkhuno avijjaṇḍakosassa tanubhāvo. Kukkuṭapotakānaṃ pādanakhamutuṇḍakānaṃ thaddhakharabhāvo viya bhikkhuno vipassanāñāṇassa tikkhakharavippasannasūrabhāvo. Kukkuṭapotakānaṃ pariṇāmakālo viya bhikkhuno vipassanāñāṇassa pariṇāmakālo vaḍḍhitakālo gabbhaggahaṇakālo. Kukkuṭapotakānaṃ pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā pakkhe papphoṭetvā sotthinā abhinikkhamanakālo viya tassa bhikkhuno vipassanāñāṇagabbhaṃ gaṇhāpetvā vicarantassa tajjātikaṃ utusappāyaṃ vā bhojanasappāyaṃ vā puggalasappāyaṃ vā dhammassavanasappāyaṃ vā labhitvā ekāsane nisinnasseva vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhentassa anupubbādhigatena arahattamaggena avijjaṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā abhiññāpakkhe papphoṭetvā sotthinā arahattappattakālo veditabbo. Yathā pana kukkuṭapotakānaṃ pariṇatabhāvaṃ ñatvā mātāpi aṇḍakosaṃ bhindati, evaṃ tathārūpassa bhikkhuno ñāṇaparipākaṃ ñatvā satthāpi –

Evameva kho

‘‘Ucchinda sinehamattano, kumudaṃ sāradikaṃva pāṇinā;

Santimaggameva brūhaya, nibbānaṃ sugatena desita’’nti. (dha. pa. 285) –

Ādinā nayena obhāsaṃ pharitvā gāthāya avijjaṇḍakosaṃ paharati, so gāthāpariyosāne avijjāṇḍakosaṃ bhinditvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti. Tato paṭṭhāya yathā te kukkuṭapotakā gāmakkhettaṃ upasobhayamānā tattha tattha vicaranti, evaṃ ayampi mahākhīṇāsavo nibbānarammaṇaṃ phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā saṅghārāmaṃ upasobhayamāno vicarati.

Iti imasmiṃ sutte cattāri pahānāni kathitāni. Kathaṃ? Cetokhilānañhi cetovinibandhānaṃ pahānena paṭisaṅkhānappapahānaṃ kathitaṃ, iddhipādehi vikkhambhanappahānaṃ kathita, magge āgate samucchedappahānaṃ kathitaṃ, phale āgate paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ kathitaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

paṭisaṅkhānappapahānaṃ vikkhambhanappahānaṃ samucchedappahānaṃ paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cetokhilasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
189. Concentration (samādhi) that arises dependent on desire (chanda) in the bases of supernormal power (iddhipāda) is desire-concentration (chandasamādhi).

Formative factors that are dominant are dominant formative factors (padhānasaṅkhārā).

"Endowed" means possessed of these qualities.

The foot (pāda) of supernormal power (iddhi), or what is the basis of supernormal power (iddhi), is supernormal power-foot (iddhipāda).

This is the method in the remainder too; this is the summary here.
