But the detailed explanation is in the Vibhaṅga (Division) of the Bases of Supernormal Power (iddhipāda).

Its meaning is explained in the *Visuddhimagga* (Path of Purification).

Thus, the suppression-abandonment (vikkhambhanappahāna) through these four bases of supernormal power (iddhipāda) has been spoken of.

"Zeal alone is fifth (ussoḷhīyeva pañcamī)"—here, zeal (ussoḷhī) shows energy that should be done everywhere.

"Endowed with zeal and fifteen factors (ussoḷhīpannarasaṅgasamannāgato)" means endowed with five abandonings of mental barrenness (cetokhilappahānāni), five abandonings of bonds (vinibandhappahānāni), four bases of supernormal power (iddhipādā), and zeal (ussoḷhī); thus, endowed with zeal and fifteen factors (aṅga).

"Capable (bhabbo)" means suitable, conforming.

"For penetration (abhinibbhidāyā)" means for the breaking of defilements (kilesa) through knowledge (ñāṇa).

"For full awakening (sambodhāyā)" means for the full awakening to the four paths (catumagga).

"Of the unsurpassed (anuttarassā)" means of the best (seṭṭhassa).

"Of the safety from yokes (yogakkhemassā)" means of the safety from the four yokes (yoga), of the Arahantship (arahatta).

"For attainment (adhigamāyā)" means for gain (paṭilābhāya).

"Just as (seyyathā)" is a particle (nipāta) in the sense of comparison (opamma).

"Indeed (pī)" is in the sense of possibility (sambhāvana).

He shows (dasseti) through both, just as, monks (bhikkhave), by name.

Eggs, eight or ten or twelve: Here, although there are eggs fewer or more than the stated kind of hen, thus it is spoken due to skillfulness of speech.

For in the world, speech is skillful thus.

"May they be (tānassū)" means may those (tāni) be (assu), may they come to be (bhaveyyunti), [this is the] meaning (attho).

"Well incubated by the hen (kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitānī)" means well incubated by that mother hen (janettiyā kukkuṭiyā), spreading the wings (pakkha) and lying on top of them (tesaṃ upari sayantiyā).

"Well heated (sammā pariseditānī)" means well heated from all around (samantato seditāni) by causing heat (utuṃ gāhāpentiyā) at the right time (kālena kālaṃ), warmed (usmīkatāni).

"Well fostered (sammā paribhāvitānī)" means well fostered from all around (samantato bhāvitāni) at the right time (kālena kālaṃ), caused to take up the hen-smell (kukkuṭagandhaṃ gāhāpitānīti), [this is the] meaning (attho).

"Although of that hen (kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyā)" means although such a desire (icchā) would not arise even if, making non-negligence (appamādaṃ katvā), by that hen (tassā kukkuṭiyā) the action of doing this threefold activity (imaṃ tividhakiriyākaraṇena).

"But they are capable (atha kho bhabbāva te)" means but those chicks (kukkuṭapotakā) are indeed capable of breaking forth safely (sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṃ bhabbāva) by the stated method (vuttanayena).

Since those eggs (tāni aṇḍāni), being protected (paripālīyamānāni) by that hen (tāya kukkuṭiyā) in such a threefold way (evaṃ tīhākārehi), are not putrid (na pūtīni honti).

Also, that tenderness in them (nesaṃ allasineho) goes to wearing away (pariyādānaṃ gacchati), the shell (kapālaṃ) is thin (tanukaṃ hoti), and the toenail-tips (pādanakhasikhā ca) and the beak-tips (mukhatuṇḍakañca) are hard (kharaṃ hoti), it itself goes to ripening (paripākaṃ gacchati), because of the thinness of the shell (kapālassa tanuttā) the light (āloko) outside (bahi) appears (paññāyati) inside (anto), therefore, "For a long time (ciraṃ vata) we (mayaṃ) have been lying (sayimhā) cramped (saṅkuṭitahatthapādā) in confinement (sambādhe), and this light (āloko) outside (bahi) is seen (dissati), now (dāni) here (ettha) there will be ease (sukhavihāro bhavissatī)", becoming desirous of going out (nikkhamitukāmā hutvā), they strike the shell (kapālaṃ paharanti) with the foot (pādena), they stretch out (pasārenti) the neck (gīvaṃ), then (tato) that (taṃ) shell (kapālaṃ) is split in two (dvedhā bhijjati).

Then (atha) they (te), flapping the wings (pakkhe vidhunantā), sounding the appropriate note (taṅkhaṇānurūpaṃ viravantā), come forth (nikkhamanti); and having come forth (nikkhamitvā ca), beautifying (upasobhayamānā) the village-field (gāmakkhettaṃ), they wander (vicaranti).

Hen: Eggs, eight or ten or twelve, may they be well incubated by the hen, well heated, well fostered, although of that hen, but they are capable. Thus indeed: This is the presentation of the simile.

That should be understood by connecting it to the meaning thus: Just as the activity of the threefold doing by that hen in the eggs, so is the state of having become endowed with the fifteen factors by this monk.

Just as, by the accomplishment of the threefold activity by the hen, there is non-putridity of the eggs, so, by the accomplishment of the threefold contemplation by the monk endowed with the fifteen factors, there is non-decline of the insight-knowledge.

Just as, by that hen's activity of the threefold doing, there is a wearing away of the oily tenderness (allasineha) of the eggs, so, by this monk's accomplishment of the threefold contemplation, there is a wearing away of the desire-tenderness associated with the triple existence.
As the thinness of eggshells, so [is] the thinness of the ignorant bhikkhu's shell of ignorance.

As the firm, hard nature of the feet, nails, and beaks of chicks, so [is] the sharp, hard, clear, and valorous nature of the bhikkhu's insight knowledge.

As the time for the development of chicks, so [is] the time for the development, growth, and grasping of the embryo of the bhikkhu's insight knowledge.

As the time when chicks break open the eggshell with the tip of their feet or the beak of their mouths, and flapping their wings, safely emerge; so should it be understood as the time when that bhikkhu, causing the embryo of insight knowledge to be grasped and wandering about, and having obtained suitable weather, suitable food, a suitable person, or the hearing of suitable Dharma, and sitting in a solitary place, developing insight, by the successively attained path of Arahantship, breaks open the eggshell of ignorance, flaps his wings of direct knowledge, and safely attains Arahantship.

Moreover, just as the mother, knowing the ripened state of the chicks, also breaks the eggshell, so too, the Teacher, knowing the ripened state of the bhikkhu, [speaks thus:]

"Cut off your affection for yourself, as one would a water lily in autumn with one's hand; cultivate only the path to peace: Nibbāna, as taught by the Sugata" (Dhp. 285).

In this way, pervading [him] with light, with the verse, he strikes at the eggshell of ignorance; at the end of the verse, he breaks the eggshell of ignorance and attains Arahantship.

From then on, just as those chicks, adorning the village fields, wander here and there, so too, this great Khīṇāsava, having attained the bliss of fruition, the object of which is Nibbāna, wanders about adorning the Saṅghārāma.

Thus, in this sutta, four kinds of abandoning have been spoken of. How? By the abandoning of the mind's barrenness, for indeed, with the abandoning of the mind's fetters, *paṭisaṅkhānappahānaṃ* [abandoning by reflective knowledge] is spoken of; with the bases of psychic power, *vikkhambhanappahānaṃ* [abandoning by suppression] is spoken of; with the path having arisen, *samucchedappahānaṃ* [abandoning by eradication] is spoken of; with the fruition having arisen, *paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ* [abandoning by tranquillization] is spoken of. The rest is clear throughout.

*Paṭisaṅkhānappahānaṃ*, *vikkhambhanappahānaṃ*, *samucchedappahānaṃ*, *paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ*.

The Cetokhilasuttavaṇṇanā in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the Majjhimanikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 190. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘vanapatthapariyāyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park (jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: "Monks (bhikkhavo)".

"Venerable sir (bhadante)," those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this: “Monks, I will teach you the discourse on jungle thickets (vanapatthapariyāyaṃ). Listen to that, pay close attention, I will speak.”

"As you say, lord (evaṃ, bhante)," those monks responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said:
commentary_pali: 190.Evaṃme sutanti vanapatthapariyāyaṃ. Tattha vanapatthapariyāyanti vanapatthakāraṇaṃ, vanapatthadesanaṃ vā.
commentary_english: 190. *evaṃ me suta* means the *vanapatthapariyāya*. There, *vanapatthapariyāya* means the reason for *vanapattha*, or the teaching on *vanapattha*.

mula_pali: 191. ‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi, tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchantī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā rattibhāgaṃ vā divasabhāgaṃ vā tamhā vanapatthā pakkamitabbaṃ, na vatthabbaṃ.
mula_english:
“Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* lives in dependence upon a certain jungle thicket (*vanapattha*).

While he is living there in dependence upon that jungle thicket (*vanapattha*), his unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind (*citta*) does not become concentrated, his undestroyed taints (*āsava*) do not come to destruction, he does not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (*anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*).

And also the requisites of life (*jīvitaparikkhārā*) that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā*) – are hard to come by.

The *bhikkhu* should consider thus: ‘I am living in dependence upon this jungle thicket (*vanapattha*). While I am living here in dependence upon this jungle thicket (*vanapattha*) my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind (*citta*) does not become concentrated, my undestroyed taints (*āsava*) do not come to destruction, I do not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (*anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*).

And also the requisites of life (*jīvitaparikkhārā*) that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā*) – are hard to come by.’

That *bhikkhu* should depart from that jungle thicket (*vanapattha*) that very night or that very day; he should not continue living there.
commentary_pali: 191.Vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharatīti manussūpacārātikkantaṃ vanasaṇḍasenāsanaṃ nissāya samaṇadhammaṃ karonto viharati. Anupaṭṭhitātiādīsu pubbe anupaṭṭhitā sati taṃ upanissāya viharatopi na upaṭṭhāti, pubbe asamāhitaṃ cittaṃ na samādhiyati, pubbe aparikkhīṇā āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, pubbe ananuppattaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemasaṅkhātaṃ arahattañca na pāpuṇātīti attho. Jīvitaparikkhārāti jīvitasambhārā. Samudānetabbāti samāharitabbā. Kasirena samudāgacchantīti dukkhena uppajjanti. Rattibhāgaṃ vā divasabhāgaṃ vāti rattikoṭṭhāse vā divasakoṭṭhāse vā. Ettha ca rattibhāge paṭisañcikkhamānena ñatvā rattiṃyeva pakkamitabbaṃ, rattiṃ caṇḍavāḷādīnaṃ paribandhe sati aruṇuggamanaṃ āgametabbaṃ. Divasabhāge ñatvā divāva pakkamitabbaṃ, divā paribandhe sati sūriyatthaṅgamanaṃ āgametabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
191. "Living in dependence on a forest thicket (vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharatī)" means living while practicing the ascetic's life, relying on a forest-thicket dwelling-place that transcends human habitation.

In "unestablished (anupaṭṭhitā)" etc., even if mindfulness was previously unestablished and one lives relying on that, it is not established; the mind, previously uncollected, is not concentrated; the defilements (āsava), previously unextinguished, do not go to exhaustion; and one does not attain the unsurpassed Arahantship, described as security from bondage (yogakkhemasaṅkhātaṃ arahattañca), which was previously unattained—this is the meaning.

"Requisites of life (jīvitaparikkhārā)" means provisions for life (jīvitasambhārā).

"Should be acquired (samudānetabbā)" means should be collected (samāharitabbā).

"Arise with difficulty (kasirena samudāgacchantī)" means they arise with suffering (dukkhena uppajjanti).

"Night portion or day portion (rattibhāgaṃ vā divasabhāgaṃ vā)" means either in a portion of the night or in a portion of the day.

Here, one reflecting in the night portion, having known, should depart during the night itself; if there is a hindrance from fierce beasts, etc., during the night, the dawn should be awaited.

Having known in the day portion, one should depart during the day itself; if there is a hindrance during the day, the sunset should be awaited.

mula_pali: 192. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena , bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Atha ca pana me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅkhāpi tamhā vanapatthā pakkamitabbaṃ, na vatthabbaṃ.
mula_english:
192. “Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* lives in dependence upon a certain jungle thicket (*vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati*).

While he is living there in dependence upon that jungle thicket, his unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his undestroyed taints (*āsavā*) do not come to destruction, he does not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (*anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*);

and also the requisites of life (*jīvitaparikkhārā*) that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajja*)- are easy to come by.

Therefore, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* should consider thus: ‘I am living in dependence upon this jungle thicket.

While I am living here in dependence upon this jungle thicket, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my undestroyed taints (*āsavā*) do not come to destruction, I do not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (*anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*);

and also the requisites of life (*jīvitaparikkhārā*) that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajja*) – are easy to come by.

However, I did not go forth from the home life into homelessness for the sake of robes (*cīvarahetu*), nor for the sake of almsfood (*piṇḍapātahetu*)…pe… nor for the sake of a resting place (*senāsanahetu*)…pe… nor for the sake of medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu*).

Moreover, while I am living here in dependence upon this jungle thicket, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my undestroyed taints (*āsavā*) do not come to destruction, I do not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (*anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*).’

Therefore, *bhikkhus*, having reflected thus, that *bhikkhu* should depart from that jungle thicket (*vanapatthā pakkamitabbaṃ*); he should not continue living there (*na vatthabbaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 192.Saṅkhāpīti evaṃ samaṇadhammassa anipphajjanabhāvaṃ jānitvā. Anantaravāre pana saṅkhāpīti evaṃ samaṇadhammassa nipphajjanabhāvaṃ jānitvā.
commentary_english: Paragraph 192. Knowing that in this way, the state of non-accomplishment of the ascetic's Dharma is Saṅkhāpī, and knowing that in the next turn, the state of accomplishment of the ascetic's Dharma is Saṅkhāpī.

mula_pali: 193. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā, te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito . Atha ca pana me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅkhāpi tasmiṃ vanapatthe vatthabbaṃ, na pakkamitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
“Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* lives dependent upon a certain jungle thicket. While he is living dependent on that jungle thicket, his unestablished mindfulness becomes established, his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, his undestroyed taints come to destruction, and he attains the unattained supreme security from bondage ( *anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*). And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā*) – are hard to come by.

“The *bhikkhu* should consider thus: ‘I am living dependent upon this jungle thicket. While I am living dependent on this jungle thicket, my unestablished mindfulness becomes established, my unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, my undestroyed taints come to destruction, and I attain the unattained supreme security from bondage. And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes, almsfood, resting place, and medicinal requisites – are hard to come by. However, I did not go forth from the home life into homelessness for the sake of robes, not for the sake of almsfood... not for the sake of a resting place... not for the sake of medicinal requisites. Moreover, while I am living dependent upon this jungle thicket, my unestablished mindfulness becomes established, my unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, my undestroyed taints come to destruction, and I attain the unattained supreme security from bondage.’

“Having reflected thus, that *bhikkhu* should continue living in that jungle thicket; he should not depart.

mula_pali: 194. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ vanapatthaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchantī’ti . Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā yāvajīvampi tasmiṃ vanapatthe vatthabbaṃ, na pakkamitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
“Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* lives in dependence upon a certain jungle thicket. While he is living in dependence upon that jungle thicket, his unestablished mindfulness becomes established, his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, his undestroyed taints (*āsavā*) come to destruction, and he attains the unattained supreme security from bondage (*anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*). And also the requisites of life (*jīvitaparikkhārā*) that should be obtained by one gone forth (*pabbajitena*) - robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā*) - are easy to come by.

Therefore, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* should consider thus: ‘I am living in dependence upon this jungle thicket.’ While I am living here in dependence upon this jungle thicket, my unestablished mindfulness has become established, my unconcentrated mind has become concentrated, my undestroyed taints (*āsavā*) have come to destruction, and I have attained the unattained supreme security from bondage (*anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ*). And also the requisites of life (*jīvitaparikkhārā*) that should be obtained by one gone forth (*pabbajitena*) - robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā*) - are easy to come by.’

Therefore, *bhikkhus*, that *bhikkhu* should continue living in that jungle thicket as long as life lasts; he should not depart.
commentary_pali: 194.Yāvajīvanti yāva jīvitaṃ pavattati, tāva vatthabbameva.
commentary_english: 194. yāvajīvanti (as long as life lasts) yāva jīvitaṃ pavattati, tāva vatthabbameva (so long as life continues, so long should one speak thus).

mula_pali: 195. ‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ gāmaṃ upanissāya viharati …pe… aññataraṃ nigamaṃ upanissāya viharati…pe… aññataraṃ nagaraṃ upanissāya viharati…pe… aññataraṃ janapadaṃ upanissāya viharati…pe… aññataraṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchantī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā rattibhāgaṃ vā divasabhāgaṃ vā so puggalo anāpucchā pakkamitabbaṃ, nānubandhitabbo.
mula_english:
"195.

Here, mendicants, a mendicant lives in dependence upon a certain village... a certain town... a certain city... a certain country... a certain person.

While he is living in dependence upon that person, his unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his undestroyed taints (āsava) do not come to destruction, and he does not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ).

And also the requisites of life (jīvitaparikkhārā) that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (cīvara), almsfood (piṇḍapāta), resting place (senāsana), and medicinal requisites (gilānappaccayabhesajja) – are hard to come by.

The mendicant should consider thus: ‘I am living in dependence upon this person.’

While I am living in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my undestroyed taints (āsava) do not come to destruction, and I do not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ).

And also the requisites of life (jīvitaparikkhārā) that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (cīvara), almsfood (piṇḍapāta), resting place (senāsana), and medicinal requisites (gilānappaccayabhesajja) – are hard to come by.’

Therefore, mendicants, that mendicant should depart from that person without taking leave, neither during the night nor during the day; he should not continue following him.
commentary_pali: 195.So puggaloti padassa nānubandhitabboti iminā sambandho. Anāpucchāti idha pana taṃ puggalaṃ anāpucchā pakkamitabbanti attho.
commentary_english:
"So *puggala*," the connection is with the statement that this word should not be pursued.

"Without asking": Here, however, it means that one should leave without asking that person.

Tassa taṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati na upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ na samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā na parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nānupāpuṇāti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. mula_english: “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu lives in dependence upon a certain person. While he is living in dependence upon that person, his unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his undestroyed taints do not come to destruction, he does not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage. And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes ( *cīvara*), almsfood ( *piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā*) – are easy to come by. The bhikkhu should consider thus: ‘I am living in dependence upon this person. While I am living in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my undestroyed taints do not come to destruction, I do not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage. And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes, almsfood, resting place, and medicinal requisites – are easy to come by. However, I did not go forth from the home life into homelessness for the sake of robes, almsfood, resting place, and medicinal requisites. Moreover, while I am living in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, my undestroyed taints do not come to destruction, I do not attain the unattained supreme security from bondage.’ Having reflected thus, that bhikkhu should depart from that person after taking leave; he should not continue following him.

mula_pali: 197. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharāmi. Tassa me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te kasirena samudāgacchanti. Na kho panāhaṃ cīvarahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, na piṇḍapātahetu…pe… na senāsanahetu…pe… na gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Atha ca pana me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅkhāpi so puggalo anubandhitabbo, na pakkamitabbaṃ.
mula_english: “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu lives in dependence upon a certain person. While he is living in dependence upon that person, his unestablished mindfulness becomes established, his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, his undestroyed taints come to destruction, he attains the unattained supreme security from bondage (anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ). And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (cīvara), almsfood (piṇḍapāta), resting place (senāsana), and medicinal requisites (gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā) – are hard to come by. The bhikkhu should consider thus: ‘I am living in dependence upon this person. While I am living in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness becomes established, my unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, my undestroyed taints come to destruction, I attain the unattained supreme security from bondage (anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ). And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (cīvara), almsfood (piṇḍapāta), resting place (senāsana), and medicinal requisites (gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā) – are hard to come by. However, I did not go forth from the home life (agārasmā) into homelessness (anagāriyaṃ) for the sake of robes (cīvarahetu), nor for the sake of almsfood… nor for the sake of a resting place… nor for the sake of medicinal requisites (gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu) from the home (agārasmā) to homelessness (anagāriyaṃ). Moreover, while I am living in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness becomes established, my unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, my undestroyed taints come to destruction, I have attained the unattained supreme security from bondage (anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ.’ Having reflected thus, that bhikkhu should continue following that person; he should not depart from him.
commentary_pali: 197.Saṅkhāpīti evaṃ samaṇadhammassa anipphajjanabhāvaṃ ñatvā so puggalo nānubandhitabbo, taṃ āpucchā pakkamitabbaṃ.
commentary_english: Saṅkhāpī: Having understood thus that the monastic practice does not arise, that person should not be followed persistently, but having taken leave, one should depart.

mula_pali:
198. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharati. Tassa taṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti , ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchanti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharāmi . Tassa me imaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya viharato anupaṭṭhitā ceva sati upaṭṭhāti, asamāhitañca cittaṃ samādhiyati, aparikkhīṇā ca āsavā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, ananuppattañca anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāmi. Ye ca kho ime pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā – cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā – te appakasirena samudāgacchantī’ti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā yāvajīvampi so puggalo anubandhitabbo, na pakkamitabbaṃ, api panujjamānenapī’’ti api paṇujjamānenāti (?).

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Vanapatthasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* lives in dependence upon a certain person. While he is living in dependence upon that person, his unestablished mindfulness becomes established, his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, his undestroyed taints come to destruction, he attains the unattained supreme security from bondage ( *anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ anupāpuṇāti*). And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting place (*senāsana*), and medicinal requisites (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā*) – are easy to come by. That *bhikkhu* should consider thus: ‘I am living in dependence upon this person.’ While I am living in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness has become established, my unconcentrated mind has become concentrated, my undestroyed taints come to destruction, I have attained the unattained supreme security from bondage. And also the requisites of life that should be obtained by one gone forth – robes, almsfood, resting place, and medicinal requisites – are easy to come by.’ That *bhikkhu* should continue following that person as long as life lasts; he should not depart from him even if told to go away.”

The Blessed One spoke thus. Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Seventh, the Vanapattha Sutta, is finished.
commentary_pali:
198.Apipanujjamānenāpīti api nikkaḍḍhīyamānenāpi. Evarūpo hi puggalo sacepi dārukalāpasataṃ vā udakaghaṭasataṃ vā vālikambaṇasataṃ vā daṇḍaṃ āharāpeti, mā idha vasīti nikkaḍḍhāpeti vā, taṃ taṃ khamāpetvā yāvajīvaṃ vatthabbamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Vanapatthapariyāyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
198.

And also, "while being driven out," means also while being expelled.

Indeed, if a person of such character were to bring a hundred bundles of firewood, or a hundred water jars, or a hundred blankets, or a staff, or if he were to drive [someone] out saying, "Do not live here!", having asked forgiveness for that, one should live there for as long as life lasts.

The Commentary on the Majjhimanikāya, the Papañcasūdanī.

The commentary on the Vanapatthapariyāyasutta is complete.

mula_pali:
199. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kapilavatthuṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Kapilavatthusmiṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena mahāvanaṃ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā beluvalaṭṭhikāya mūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Daṇḍapāṇipi kho sakko jaṅghāvihāraṃ jaṅghavihāraṃ (ka.) anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena mahāvanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā yena beluvalaṭṭhikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā daṇḍamolubbha ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho daṇḍapāṇi sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kiṃvādī samaṇo kimakkhāyī’’ti? ‘‘Yathāvādī kho, āvuso, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya na kenaci loke viggayha tiṭṭhati, yathā ca pana kāmehi visaṃyuttaṃ viharantaṃ taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ akathaṃkathiṃ chinnakukkuccaṃ bhavābhave vītataṇhaṃ saññā nānusenti – evaṃvādī kho ahaṃ, āvuso, evamakkhāyī’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte daṇḍapāṇi sakko sīsaṃ okampetvā , jivhaṃ nillāḷetvā, tivisākhaṃ nalāṭikaṃ nalāṭe vuṭṭhāpetvā daṇḍamolubbha pakkāmi.
mula_english:
Thus I have heard.

On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in Nigrodha’s Park. Then, when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Kapilavatthu for alms. When he had wandered for alms in Kapilavatthu and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he went to the Great Wood for the day’s abiding. And entering the Great Wood, sat down at the root of a *beluva* sapling for the day’s abiding.

Dandapani the Sakyan, while walking and wandering for exercise (*jaṅghāvihāraṃ*), also went to the Great Wood. and when he had entered the Great Wood, he went to the *beluva* sapling where the Blessed One was and exchanged greetings with him. When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he stood at one side leaning on his stick (*daṇḍamolubbha ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi*).

Standing to one side, Dandapani the Sakyan said to the Blessed One: “What doctrine does this *śramaṇa* profess? What does he proclaim?”

“Friend, I assert and proclaim such a teaching that one does not quarrel with anyone in the world with its gods (*sadevake loke*), its Maras (*samārake*), and its Brahmas (*sabrahmake*), in this generation with its recluses and *brāhmaṇas* (*sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya*), its princes and its people; such a teaching that perceptions no more underlie that *brāhmaṇa* who abides detached from sensual pleasures (*kāmehi visaṃyuttaṃ*), without perplexity (*akathaṃkathiṃ*), shorn of worry (*chinnakukkuccaṃ*), free from craving for any kind of being (*bhavābhave vītataṇhaṃ*).”

When this was said, Dandapani the Sakyan shook his head, wagged his tongue, and raised his eyebrows until his forehead was puckered in three lines. Then he departed, leaning on his stick.
commentary_pali: 199. Evaṃ me sutanti madhupiṇḍikasuttaṃ. Tattha mahāvananti himavantena saddhiṃ ekābaddhaṃ aropimaṃ jātivanaṃ, na yathā vesāliyaṃ ropitāropitamissakaṃ. Divāvihārāyāti divā paṭisallānatthāya. Beluvalaṭṭhikāyāti taruṇabeluvarukkhassa. Daṇḍapāṇīti na jarādubbalatāya daṇḍahattho. Ayañhi taruṇo paṭhamavaye ṭhito, daṇḍacittatāya pana suvaṇṇadaṇḍaṃ gahetvā vicarati, tasmā daṇḍapāṇīti vutto. Jaṅghāvihāranti jaṅghākilamathavinodanatthaṃ jaṅghācāraṃ. Anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramānoti ārāmadassana-vanadassana-pabbatadassanādīnaṃ atthāya ito cito ca vicaramāno. Adhiccanikkhamano kiresa kadāci deva nikkhamitvā evaṃ vicarati. Daṇḍamolubbhāti daṇḍaṃ olumbhitvā gopālakadārako viya daṇḍaṃ purato ṭhapetvā daṇḍamatthake dve hatthe patiṭṭhāpetvā piṭṭhipāṇiṃ hanukena uppīḷetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi.
commentary_english:
199.
Thus, "me suta " means the *madhupiṇḍikasutta*.

There, "mahāvana" means a *jātivana* that is connected to the Himalayas, not like the *vesāliyaṃ ropitāropitamissakaṃ*.

"divāvihārāyā" means for the sake of rest by day.

"beluvalaṭṭhikāyā" means of a young *beluvarukkha*.

"daṇḍapāṇī" means not one who has a stick in [his] hand due to the weakness of old age.

Indeed, this youth, standing at an early age, wanders around holding a golden staff because of [his] interest in sticks, therefore, he is called "daṇḍapāṇī."

"jaṅghāvihāra" means *jaṅghācāraṃ* for the sake of dispelling the weariness of the shanks.

"anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno" means wandering here and there for the sake of seeing gardens, seeing forests, seeing mountains, and so on.

It seems that this deity sometimes leaves by chance and wanders in this way.

"daṇḍamolubbhā" means having leaned on a stick, like a cowherd boy, having placed the stick in front, having established two hands on the top of the stick, having pressed the back of the hand with the chin, he stood on one side.

mula_pali:
200. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena nigrodhārāmo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kapilavatthuṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Kapilavatthusmiṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena mahāvanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃ divāvihārāya. Mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā beluvalaṭṭhikāya mūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdiṃ. Daṇḍapāṇipi kho, bhikkhave, sakko jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena mahāvanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā yena beluvalaṭṭhikā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mayā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā daṇḍamolubbha ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, daṇḍapāṇi sakko maṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃvādī samaṇo kimakkhāyī’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhikkhave, daṇḍapāṇiṃ sakkaṃ etadavocaṃ – yathāvādī kho, āvuso, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya na kenaci loke viggayha tiṭṭhati, yathā ca pana kāmehi visaṃyuttaṃ viharantaṃ taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ akathaṃkathiṃ chinnakukkuccaṃ bhavābhave vītataṇhaṃ saññā nānusenti – evaṃvādī kho ahaṃ, āvuso, evamakkhāyī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte bhikkhave, daṇḍapāṇi sakko sīsaṃ okampetvā, jivhaṃ nillāḷetvā, tivisākhaṃ nalāṭikaṃ nalāṭe vuṭṭhāpetvā daṇḍamolubbha pakkāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, when it was evening, the Blessed One arose from seclusion and went to Nigrodha's Park; having arrived, he sat down on a seat that was prepared.

Seated, the Blessed One addressed the monks, "Here, monks, in the morning, having dressed, taking my bowl and robe, I entered Kapilavatthu for alms. Having wandered for alms in Kapilavatthu, and having returned from the alms round, after my meal, I went to the Great Wood for the day's abiding. Having plunged into the Great Wood, I sat down at the root of a *beluva* sapling for the day's abiding.

"Then, monks, Daṇḍapāṇi the Śākya, while walking and wandering for exercise, also went to the Great Wood. Having entered the Great Wood, he went to the *beluva* sapling where I was; having arrived, he exchanged greetings with me. After an exchange of friendly greetings and courteous talk, he stood to one side, leaning on his stick.

Standing to one side, monks, Daṇḍapāṇi the Śākya said to me, 'What doctrine does the *śramaṇa* profess? What does he proclaim?'"

"When this was said, monks, I said to Daṇḍapāṇi the Śākya, 'That speaker, friend, who in the world with its deities, with Māra, with Brahmā, in this generation with its *śramaṇas* and Brahmins, with its deities and humans, does not stand contending with anyone in the world; and that Brahmin who lives detached from sensual pleasures, free from perplexity, who has cut off hesitation, whose thirst for existence and non-existence is extinguished, whom concepts do not pursue—that is the doctrine I profess, friend, that is what I proclaim.'"

"When this was said, monks, Daṇḍapāṇi the Śākya shook his head, wagged his tongue, raised his triple-lined brow on his forehead, and departed, leaning on his stick."
commentary_pali:
200.Kiṃvādīti kiṃdiṭṭhiko. Kimakkhāyīti kiṃ katheti. Ayaṃ rājā bhagavantaṃ avanditvā paṭisanthāramattakameva katvā pañhaṃ pucchati. Tampi na aññātukāmatāya, acittīkārena pucchati. Kasmā? Devadattassa pakkhiko kiresa. Devadatto attano santikaṃ āgacchamāne tathāgate bhindati. So kira evaṃ vadeti ‘‘samaṇo gotamo amhākaṃ kulena saddhiṃ verī, na no kulassa vuddhiṃ icchati. Bhaginīpi me cakkavattiparibhogā, taṃ pahāya ‘nassatesā’ti nikkhamitvā pabbaji. Bhāgineyyopi me cakkavattibījanti ñatvā amhākaṃ kulassa vaḍḍhiyā atussanto ‘nassateta’nti tampi daharakāleyeva pabbājesi. Ahaṃ pana tena vinā vattituṃ asakkonto anupabbajito. Evaṃ pabbajitampi maṃ pabbajitadivasato paṭṭhāya na ujukehi akkhīhi oloketi. Parisamajjhe bhāsantopi mahāpharasunā paharanto viya āpāyiko devadattotiādīni bhāsatī’’ti. Evaṃ ayampi rājā devadattena bhinno, tasmā evamakāsi.

Atha bhagavā yathā ayaṃ rājā mayā pañhe pucchite na kathetīti vattuṃ na labhati, yathā ca bhāsitassa atthaṃ na jānāti, evamassa kathessāmīti tassānucchavikaṃ kathento yathāvādī khotiādimāha.

yathāvādī kho

Tattha na kenaci loke viggayha tiṭṭhatīti loke kenaci saddhiṃ viggāhikakathaṃ na karoti na vivadati. Tathāgato hi lokena saddhiṃ na vivadati; loko pana tathāgatena saddhiṃ aniccanti vutte niccanti vadamāno, dukkhaṃ, anattā, asubhanti vutte subhanti vadamāno vivadati. Tenevāha ‘‘nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, lokena vivadāmi, lokova kho, bhikkhave, mayā vivadati, tathā na, bhikkhave, dhammavādī kenaci lokasmiṃ vivadati, adhammavādīva kho, bhikkhave, vivadatī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 3.94). Yathāti yena kāraṇena. Kāmehīti vatthukāmehipi kilesakāmehipi. Taṃ brāhmaṇanti taṃ khīṇāsavaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ. Akathaṃkathinti nibbicikicchaṃ. Chinnakukkuccanti vippaṭisārakukkuccassa ceva hatthapādakukkuccassa ca chinnattā chinnakukkuccaṃ. Bhavābhaveti punappunabbhave, hīnapaṇīte vā bhave, paṇīto hi bhavo vuddhippatto abhavoti vuccati. Saññāti kilesasaññā. Kilesāyeva vā idha saññānāmena vuttā, tasmā yena kāraṇena kāmehi visaṃyuttaṃ viharantaṃ taṃ loke ninnāvādiṃ khīṇāsavabrāhmaṇaṃ kilesasaññā nānusenti, tañca kāraṇaṃ ahaṃ vadāmīti ayamettha attho. Iti bhagavā attano khīṇāsavabhāvaṃ dīpeti. Nillāḷetvāti nīharitvā kīḷāpetvā. Tivisākhanti tisākhaṃ. Nalāṭikanti valibhaṅgaṃ nalāṭe tisso rājiyo dassento valibhaṅgaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvāti attho. Daṇḍamolubbhāti daṇḍaṃ uppīḷetvā. ‘‘Daṇḍamālubbhā’’tipi pāṭho, gahetvā pakkāmīti attho.

na kenaci loke viggayha tiṭṭhatī Yathā Kāmehī Taṃ brāhmaṇa Akathaṃkathi Chinnakukkucca Bhavābhave Saññā Nillāḷetvā Tivisākha Nalāṭika Daṇḍamolubbhā
commentary_english:
200. "What is he saying?" means, "What is his view?"

"What does he declare?" means, "What does he say?"

This king, without venerating the Blessed One, only makes a slight greeting and asks a question.

And he does not ask out of a desire to know, but he asks disrespectfully.

Why? Because he is a partisan of Devadatta, it is said.

Devadatta breaks with the *Tathāgata* when he comes into his presence.

He says thus: "The *samaṇa* Gotama is an enemy to our family, he does not desire the growth of our family.

My sister was enjoying the wealth of a wheel-turning monarch, but having abandoned that, she left home, saying, 'I will be destroyed,' and became a renunciate.

My nephew, knowing [he was] the seed of a wheel-turning monarch, being displeased with the prosperity of our family, made him renounce, saying, 'He will be destroyed,' even in his early youth.

But I, unable to live without him, followed him into homelessness.

Even though I have gone forth, from the day I went forth, he does not look at me with upright eyes.

Even while speaking in the midst of an assembly, he speaks saying, 'Devadatta is destined for the lower realms, striking with a great axe', and so forth."

Thus, this king, too, is split off by Devadatta; therefore, he acted thus.

Then, the Blessed One [knew that] just as this king is not able to speak when asked a question by me, and just as he does not understand the meaning of what is spoken, [so] I will speak about him appropriately, saying, "He is one who speaks the truth," and so on.

He is one who speaks the truth: There, "He does not stand disputing with anyone in the world" means he does not engage in quarrelsome talk or dispute with anyone in the world.

For the *Tathāgata* does not dispute with the world; but the world disputes with the *Tathāgata*. When it is said, "Impermanent," he speaks, saying, "Permanent." Suffering, not-self, impure, when it is said, he speaks, saying, "Pure," he disputes.

Therefore, he said, "Monks, I do not dispute with the world, but the world disputes with me. Thus, monks, one who speaks the Dharma does not dispute with anyone in the world, but it is the one who speaks non-Dharma who disputes" (Saṃ. Ni. 3.94).

"As" means by whatever reason.

"Desiring sense pleasures" means desiring both the objects of sense pleasure and the defilements of sense pleasure. (*vatthukāmehipi kilesakāmehipi*)

"That *brāhmaṇa*" means that *brāhmaṇa* whose *āsavas* are destroyed ( *khīṇāsava*).

"*Akathaṃkathi*" means without doubt ( *nibbicikicchaṃ*).

"*Chinnakukkucca*" means because remorseful worry and worry about hands and feet are cut off, [he is one] whose worry is cut off (*vippaṭisārakukkuccassa ceva hatthapādakukkuccassa ca chinnattā chinnakukkuccaṃ*).

"*Bhavābhave*" means again and again in existence, or in inferior or superior existence, for a superior existence that has attained growth is called non-existence.

"*Saññā*" means defiled perception (*kilesasaññā*).

Or, here, it is said by the name of defilements themselves. Therefore, for whatever reason the defilements of perception do not follow that one who dwells detached from sense pleasures, who is a *khīṇāsavabrāhmaṇa* who refrains from leading others astray in the world, that reason I will speak, this is the meaning here.

Thus, the Blessed One reveals his state of being one whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsava*).

"*Nillāḷetvā*" means having brought out, having played with (*nīharitvā kīḷāpetvā*).

"*Tivisākha*" means three-branched (*tisākhaṃ*).

"*Nalāṭika*" means showing three lines on the forehead in the form of broken wrinkles, the meaning is having established the broken wrinkles.

"*Daṇḍamolubbhā*" means having oppressed the stick (*daṇḍaṃ uppīḷetvā*).
The reading is also "daṇḍamālubbhā," meaning having taken [it], he departed.

He does not stand quarreling with anyone in the world. Just as with desires, that *brāhmaṇa*, who is without questions, who has cut off worry, in being and non-being, having discarded perception, three-pronged, with a forehead plate, *daṇḍamolubbhā*.

mula_pali: 201. Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kiṃvādī pana, bhante, bhagavā sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya na kenaci loke viggayha tiṭṭhati? Kathañca pana, bhante, bhagavantaṃ kāmehi visaṃyuttaṃ viharantaṃ taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ akathaṃkathiṃ chinnakukkuccaṃ bhavābhave vītataṇhaṃ saññā nānusentī’’ti? ‘‘Yatonidānaṃ, bhikkhu, purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti. Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṃ abhivaditabbaṃ ajjhositabbaṃ. Esevanto rāgānusayānaṃ, esevanto paṭighānusayānaṃ, esevanto diṭṭhānusayānaṃ , esevanto vicikicchānusayānaṃ, esevanto mānānusayānaṃ, esevanto bhavarāgānusayānaṃ, esevanto avijjānusayānaṃ, esevanto daṇḍādāna-satthādāna-kalaha-viggaha-vivāda-tuvaṃtuvaṃ-pesuñña-musāvādānaṃ. Etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.
mula_english:
Thus it was said, a certain *bhikkhu* said this to the Blessed One: “But, venerable sir, what is the Blessed One’s doctrine that he abides in the world together with the *devas*, with *Māra*, with *Brahmā*, with the generation together with ascetics and *brāhmaṇas*, with *devas* and humans, without contending with anyone in the world? And how do perceptions not underlie that *brāhmaṇa* who abides detached from sensual pleasures, is without doubt, has cut off worry, and is without craving for existence and non-existence?”

“*Bhikkhu*, expansive perceptions and notions harass a person because of whatever cause.

If nothing is found there to delight in, welcome, and hold to, this is the end of the underlying tendency to craving (*rāgānusaya*), this is the end of the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*), this is the end of the underlying tendency to views (*dīṭṭhānusaya*), this is the end of the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*), this is the end of the underlying tendency to conceit (*mānānusaya*), this is the end of the underlying tendency to craving for existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*), this is the end of the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*); this is the end of resorting to rods and weapons, of quarrels (*kalaha*), brawls (*viggaha*), disputes (*vivāda*), recrimination, malice (*pesuñña*), and false speech (*musāvāda*).

Here these evil unwholesome states (*akusala dharma*) cease without remainder.”

That is what the Blessed One said.

Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling (*vihāra*).
commentary_pali:
201.Aññataroti nāmena apākaṭo eko bhikkhu. So kira anusandhikusalo, bhagavatā yathā daṇḍapāṇī na jānāti, tathā mayā kathitanti vutte kinti nu kho bhagavatā aviññeyyaṃ katvā pañho kathitoti anusandhiṃ gahetvā dasabalaṃ yācitvā imaṃ pañhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa pākaṭaṃ karissāmīti uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dasanakhasamujjalaṃ añjaliṃ paggayha kiṃvādī pana, bhante bhagavātiādimāha.

Yatonidānanti bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ etaṃ, yena kāraṇena yasmiṃ kāraṇe satīti attho. Papañcasaññāsaṅkhāti ettha saṅkhāti koṭṭhāso. Papañcasaññāti taṇhāmānadiṭṭhipapañcasampayuttā saññā , saññānāmena vā papañcāyeva vuttā. Tasmā papañcakoṭṭhāsāti ayamettha attho. Samudācarantīti pavattanti. Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbanti yasmiṃ dvādasāyatanasaṅkhāte kāraṇe sati papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti, ettha ekāyatanampi ce abhinanditabbaṃ abhivaditabbaṃ ajjhositabbaṃ natthīti attho. Tattha abhininditabbanti ahaṃ mamanti abhinanditabbaṃ. Abhivaditabbanti ahaṃ mamāti vattabbaṃ. Ajjhositabbanti ajjhositvā gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā gahetabbayuttaṃ. Etenettha taṇhādīnaṃyeva appavattiṃ katheti. Esevantoti ayaṃ abhinandanādīnaṃ natthibhāvova rāgānusayādīnaṃ anto. Eseva nayo sabbattha.

Yatonidāna Papañcasaññāsaṅkhā saṅkhā Papañcasaññā Samudācarantī Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabba abhininditabba Abhivaditabba Ajjhositabba Esevanto

Daṇḍādānādīsu pana yāya cetanāya daṇḍaṃ ādiyati, sā daṇḍādānaṃ. Yāya satthaṃ ādiyati parāmasati, sā satthādānaṃ. Matthakappattaṃ kalahaṃ. Nānāgāhamattaṃ viggahaṃ. Nānāvādamattaṃ vivādaṃ. Tuvaṃ tuvanti evaṃ pavattaṃ tuvaṃ tuvaṃ. Piyasuññakaraṇaṃ pesuññaṃ. Ayathāsabhāvaṃ musāvādaṃ karoti, sā musāvādoti veditabbā. Ettheteti ettha dvādasasu āyatanesu ete kilesā. Kilesā hi uppajjamānāpi dvādasāyatanāni nissāya uppajjanti, nirujjhamānāpi dvādasasu āyatanesuyeva nirujjhanti. Evaṃ yatthuppannā, tattheva niruddhā honti. Svāyamattho samudayasaccapañhena dīpetabbo –

Daṇḍādānā daṇḍādānaṃ satthādānaṃ kalahaṃ viggahaṃ vivādaṃ. Tuvaṃ tuva pesuññaṃ musāvādo Etthete

‘‘Sā kho panesā taṇhā kattha uppajjamānā uppajjati, kattha nivisamānā nivisatī’’ti vatvā – ‘‘yaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ, etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati. Kiñca loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ? Cakkhu loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpa’’ntiādinā (vibha. 203) nayena dvādasasuyeva āyatanesu tassā uppatti ca nirodho ca vutto. Yatheva ca taṇhā dvādasasu āyatanesu uppajjitvā nibbānaṃ āgamma niruddhāpi āyatanesu puna samudācārassa abhāvato āyatanesuyeva niruddhāti vuttā, evamimepi pāpakā akusalā dhammā āyatanesu nirujjhantīti veditabbā. Atha vā yvāyaṃ abhinandanādīnaṃ abhāvova rāgānusayādīnaṃ antoti vutto. Etthete rāgānusayādīnaṃ antoti laddhavohāre nibbāne pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti. Yañhi yattha natthi, taṃ tattha niruddhaṃ nāma hoti, svāyamattho nirodhapañhena dīpetabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhārā paṭippassaddhā hontī’’tiādi (paṭi. ma. 1.83).
commentary_english:
201. *A certain one* means a certain monk, not well-known by name. It seems he was skilled in investigation. Having heard it said, "The Blessed One does not know in the way that Daṇḍapāṇī does, [but] I have spoken in that way," taking up the investigation [thinking], "In what way did the Blessed One ask a question, having made it unknowable?" and requesting the Ten Powers, [thinking,] "I will make this question known to the Sangha of monks," rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, raising his añjali, with its ten fingernails gleaming, he said, "But what does the Blessed One advocate, venerable sir?" and so forth.

*Yatonidāna* is a neuter instrumental compound, meaning: by which cause, when this cause exists. *Papañcasaññāsaṅkhā*: here, *saṅkhā* means section. *Papañcasaññā* means perception associated with craving, conceit, and views, or indeed, *papañca* is referred to by way of perception. Therefore, *papañca* section is the meaning here. *Samudācarantī* means they occur, or arise. *Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabba*: When this cause, known as the twelve sense-fields exists, the *papañcasaññāsaṅkhā* arise; if there is not even one sense-field here that should be rejoiced over, praised, or clung to, is the meaning. *Abhininditabba* means should be rejoiced over as "I" or "mine." *Abhivaditabba* means should be spoken of as "I" or "mine." *Ajjhositabba* means fit to be clung to, swallowed, completely finished, and taken. By this, he speaks of the non-occurrence of craving, etc. here. *Esevanto* means this very non-existence of rejoicing, etc. is the end of latent passion, etc. The same method [applies] everywhere.

*Daṇḍādānā*, etc.: However, the intention by which one takes up a stick, that is *daṇḍādānaṃ* (stick-taking). The intention by which one takes up or touches a weapon, that is *satthādānaṃ* (weapon-taking). *Kalahaṃ* [means] a quarrel that has reached a head. *Viggahaṃ* [means] grasping at various things. *Vivādaṃ* [means] speaking various things. *Tuvaṃ tuvaṃ* [means] "You, you!" occurring in this way. *Pesuññaṃ* [means] making what is dear empty. *Musāvādo* should be understood as making a false statement contrary to the true state of affairs. *Etthete*: here, in these twelve sense-fields, are these defilements. For even when arising, defilements arise dependent on the twelve sense-fields; even when ceasing, they cease in the twelve sense-fields themselves. Thus, having arisen where they did, they are stopped right there. This meaning should be illuminated by the question about the truth of origination:

"But where does this craving arise when arising? Where does it dwell when dwelling?" Having said that, "That which is likeable and pleasing in the world, that is where this craving arises when arising; that is where it dwells when dwelling. And what is likeable and pleasing in the world? The eye is likeable and pleasing in the world," and so on, according to this method (Vibha. 203), its origination and cessation are spoken of only in the twelve sense-fields. And just as craving, having arisen in the twelve sense-fields, having come to nirvāṇa, even though it has ceased, it is said to have ceased only in the sense-fields because of the non-occurrence of arising again in the sense-fields; in the same way, these evil, unwholesome states should be understood to cease in the sense-fields. Or rather, this very absence of rejoicing, etc., is said to be the end of latent passion, etc. In nirvāṇa, where it is customary to say, "Here is the end of latent passion, etc.," evil, unwholesome states cease completely.
Indeed, whatever is not there, that is called cessation there. This meaning should be explained by the question of cessation. And it was said, "For one who has attained the second *jhāna* (*dhyāna*), initial and sustained thought, and verbal formations are calmed" etc. (Paṭi. Ma. 1.83).

mula_pali:
202. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā, vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā, uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘yatonidānaṃ, bhikkhu, purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti. Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṃ abhivaditabbaṃ ajjhositabbaṃ. Esevanto rāgānusayānaṃ…pe… etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’ti . Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’’ti? Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’’ti.

Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘yatonidānaṃ, bhikkhu, purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti. Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṃ abhivaditabbaṃ ajjhositabbaṃ. Esevanto rāgānusayānaṃ…pe… etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’ti. Tesaṃ no, āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘‘yatonidānaṃ, bhikkhu, purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti. Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṃ abhivaditabbaṃ ajjhositabbaṃ. Esevanto rāgānusayānaṃ…pe… etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’’ti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyāti? Tesaṃ no, āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ, pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti. Vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, soon after the Blessed One had left, the bhikkhus considered: “Now, friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, saying: ‘It is from that condition that proliferation-perception-and-ideas harass a man.’ If nothing is found there to delight in, welcome and hold to, this is the end of the underlying tendency to lust…here these evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.” Who now could expound the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning?" Then the bhikkhus considered: “The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning. Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.”

Then the bhikkhus went to the venerable Mahā Kaccāna and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, they sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the bhikkhus said to the venerable Mahā Kaccāna: “Friend Kaccāna, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, saying: ‘It is from that condition that proliferation-perception-and-ideas harass a man. If nothing is found there to delight in, welcome and hold to, this is the end of the underlying tendency to lust…here these evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.’ Then, friend Kaccāna, soon after the Blessed One had left, we considered: ‘The Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, saying: ‘It is from that condition that proliferation-perception-and-ideas harass a man. If nothing is found there to delight in, welcome and hold to, this is the end of the underlying tendency to lust…here these evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.’ Who now could expound the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning?" Then, friend Kaccāna, we considered: ‘The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning. Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.’ Let the venerable Mahā Kaccāna expound it.”
commentary_pali: 202.Satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇitoti satthārā ca pasaṃsito. Viññūnanti idampi karaṇatthe sāmivacanaṃ, paṇḍitehi sabrahmacārīhi ca sambhāvitoti attho. Pahotīti sakkoti.
commentary_english: 202. satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito means praised by the teacher (satthārā) and commended. viññūna means this word "sāmi" in the sense of instrumentality (karaṇatthe), [namely] esteemed by the wise (paṇḍitehi) and fellow religious practitioners (sabrahmacārīhi). pahotī means is able (sakkoti).

mula_pali: 203. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva mūlaṃ, atikkamma khandhaṃ, sākhāpalāse sāraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ maññeyya; evaṃsampadamidaṃ āyasmantānaṃ satthari sammukhībhūte, taṃ bhagavantaṃ atisitvā , amhe etamatthaṃ paṭipucchitabbaṃ maññatha. So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto, vattā pavattā, atthassa ninnetā, amatassa dātā, dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi, yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha. Yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā’’ti. ‘‘Addhāvuso kaccāna, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto, vattā pavattā, atthassa ninnetā, amatassa dātā, dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi, yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma. Yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāma. Api cāyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ, pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno agaruṃ katvā’’ti agarukatvā (sī.), agarukaritvā (syā. pī.). ‘‘Tena hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahākaccāno etadavoca –
mula_english:
203. It is as if, friends, a man needing heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, thought that heartwood should be sought for among the branches and leaves of a great tree standing possessed of heartwood, after he had passed over the root and the trunk. So it is with you, venerable sirs, that you think that I should be asked about the meaning of this, after you passed the Blessed One (Bhagavān) by when you were face to face with the Teacher.

For knowing, the Blessed One (Bhagavān) knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision, he is knowledge (jñāṇa), he is the Dhamma, he is the holy one (brahmabhūto); he is the sayer, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning (attha), the giver of the Deathless (amata), the lord of the Dhamma, the *Tathāgata*.

That was the time when you should have asked the Blessed One (Bhagavān) the meaning. As he told you, so you should have remembered it.

“Surely, friend Kaccāna, knowing, the Blessed One (Bhagavān) knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision, he is knowledge (jñāṇa), he is the Dhamma, he is the holy one (brahmabhūto); he is the sayer, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning (attha), the giver of the Deathless (amata), the lord of the Dhamma, the *Tathāgata*.

That was the time when we should have asked the Blessed One (Bhagavān) the meaning. As he told us, so we should have remembered it.

Yet the venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One (Bhagavān) without expounding the detailed meaning.

Let the venerable Mahākaccāna expound it without finding it troublesome."

“Then listen, friends, and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, friend,” the monks replied to the venerable Mahākaccāna.

The venerable Mahākaccāna said this:
commentary_pali: 203.Atikkammeva mūlaṃ atikkamma khandhanti sāro nāma mūle vā khandhe vā bhaveyya, tampi atikkamitvāti attho. Evaṃsampadanti evaṃsampattikaṃ, īdisanti attho. Atisitvāti atikkamitvā. Jānaṃ jānātīti jānitabbameva jānāti. Passaṃ passatīti passitabbameva passati. Yathā vā ekacco viparītaṃ gaṇhanto jānantopi na jānāti, passantopi na passati, na evaṃ bhagavā. Bhagavā pana jānanto jānātiyeva, passanto passatiyeva. Svāyaṃ dassanapariṇāyakaṭṭhena cakkhubhūto. Viditakaraṇaṭṭhena ñāṇabhūto. Aviparītasabhāvaṭṭhena pariyattidhammappavattanato vā hadayena cintetvā vācāya nicchāritadhammamayoti dhammabhūto. Seṭṭhaṭṭhena brahmabhūto. Atha vā cakkhu viya bhūtoti cakkhubhūtoti evametesu padesu attho veditabbo. Svāyaṃ dhammassa vattanato vattā. Pavattāpanato pavattā. Atthaṃ nīharitvā dassanasamatthatāya atthassa ninnetā. Amatādhigamāya paṭipattiṃ dadātīti amatassa dātā. Agaruṃ katvāti punappunaṃ āyācāpentopi hi garuṃ karoti nāma, attano sāvakapāramīñāṇe ṭhatvā sinerūpādato vālukaṃ uddharamāno viya dubbiññeyyaṃ katvā kathentopi garuṃ karotiyeva nāma. Evaṃ akatvā amhe punappunaṃ ayācāpetvā suviññeyyampi no katvā kathehīti vuttaṃ hoti.
commentary_english:
203. *Atikkammeva mūlaṃ atikkamma khandha* means if the essence were in the root or the trunk, it would have surpassed even that.

*Evaṃsampada* means having such accomplishment, meaning "of this sort."

*Atisitvā* means having surpassed.

*Jānaṃ jānātī* means he knows what should be known.

*Passaṃ passatī* means he sees what should be seen.

Just as some, taking things perversely, do not know even when knowing, and do not see even when seeing, the Blessed One is not like that.

The Blessed One, however, knows when knowing, and sees when seeing.

He is *cakkhubhūto* (eye-like) because of having the characteristic of guiding vision (dassanapariṇāyakaṭṭhena).

[He is] *ñāṇabhūto* (knowledge-like) because of having the characteristic of making known (viditakaraṇaṭṭhena).

[He is] *dhammabhūto* (dharma-like) because of having the characteristic of non-perversion (aviparītasabhāvaṭṭhena), or because of the turning of the transmitted teaching (pariyattidhammappavattanato), or because of being made of the *dharma* discharged by speech after thinking in the heart (hadayena cintetvā vācāya nicchāritadhammamayoti).

[He is] *brahmabhūto* (brahma-like) because of having the characteristic of excellence (seṭṭhaṭṭhena).

Or alternatively, *cakkhubhūto* means like an eye, it should be understood that the meaning in these passages [is such].

He is *vattā* (speaker) because of the turning of the *dharma* (dhammassa vattanato).

[He is] *pavattā* (one who causes to speak) because of causing to speak (pavattāpanato).

[He is] *atthassa ninnetā* (leader of meaning) because of the ability to show, after leading out the meaning (atthaṃ nīharitvā dassanasamatthatāya).

[He is] *amatassa dātā* (giver of the deathless) because he gives the practice for the attainment of the deathless (amatādhigamāya paṭipattiṃ dadātīti).

*Agaruṃ katvā* means even when repeatedly requesting, one makes it heavy indeed, standing in the knowledge of the perfection of the disciple, as if drawing sand from the foot of Mount Meru, even when speaking after making it difficult to know, one makes it heavy indeed.

Without doing so, it is said "after causing us to request again and again, speak, without making it easy for us to know."

mula_pali:
204. ‘‘Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘yatonidānaṃ, bhikkhu, purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti . Ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṃ abhivaditabbaṃ ajjhositabbaṃ, esevanto rāgānusayānaṃ…pe… etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’ti, imassa kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi –

‘‘Cakkhuñcāvuso, paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, yaṃ vedeti taṃ sañjānāti , yaṃ sañjānāti taṃ vitakketi, yaṃ vitakketi taṃ papañceti, yaṃ papañceti tatonidānaṃ purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti atītānāgatapaccuppannesu cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu. Sotañcāvuso, paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇaṃ…pe… ghānañcāvuso, paṭicca gandhe ca uppajjati ghānaviññāṇaṃ…pe… jivhañcāvuso, paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyañcāvuso, paṭicca phoṭṭhabbe ca uppajjati kāyaviññāṇaṃ…pe… manañcāvuso, paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, yaṃ vedeti taṃ sañjānāti, yaṃ sañjānāti taṃ vitakketi, yaṃ vitakketi taṃ papañceti, yaṃ papañceti tatonidānaṃ purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti atītānāgatapaccuppannesu manoviññeyyesu dhammesu.

‘‘So vatāvuso, cakkhusmiṃ sati rūpe sati cakkhuviññāṇe sati phassapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Phassapaññattiyā sati vedanāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Vedanāpaññattiyā sati saññāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Saññāpaññattiyā sati vitakkapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Vitakkapaññattiyā sati papañcasaññāsaṅkhāsamudācaraṇapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. So vatāvuso, sotasmiṃ sati sadde sati…pe… ghānasmiṃ sati gandhe sati…pe… jivhāya sati rase sati…pe… kāyasmiṃ sati phoṭṭhabbe sati…pe… manasmiṃ sati dhamme sati manoviññāṇe sati phassapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Phassapaññattiyā sati vedanāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Vedanāpaññattiyā sati saññāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Saññāpaññattiyā sati vitakkapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Vitakkapaññattiyā sati papañcasaññāsaṅkhāsamudācaraṇapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

‘‘So vatāvuso, cakkhusmiṃ asati rūpe asati cakkhuviññāṇe asati phassapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Phassapaññattiyā asati vedanāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Vedanāpaññattiyā asati saññāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Saññāpaññattiyā asati vitakkapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Vitakkapaññattiyā asati papañcasaññāsaṅkhāsamudācaraṇapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vatāvuso, sotasmiṃ asati sadde asati…pe… ghānasmiṃ asati gandhe asati…pe… jivhāya asati rase asati…pe… kāyasmiṃ asati phoṭṭhabbe asati…pe… manasmiṃ asati dhamme asati manoviññāṇe asati phassapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Phassapaññattiyā asati vedanāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Vedanāpaññattiyā asati saññāpaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Saññāpaññattiyā asati vitakkapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Vitakkapaññattiyā asati papañcasaññāsaṅkhāsamudācaraṇapaññattiṃ paññāpessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

‘‘Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘yatonidānaṃ, bhikkhu, purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti ettha ce natthi abhinanditabbaṃ abhivaditabbaṃ ajjhositabbaṃ esevanto rāgānusayānaṃ…pe… etthete pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhantī’ti, imassa kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe āyasmanto bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha. Yathā no bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā’’ti.
mula_english:
204. “Friends, when the Blessed One rose from his seat and went into his dwelling after giving a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, that is: ‘Bhikkhus, as to the source through which perceptions and notions tinged by mental proliferation (*papañcasaññāsaṅkhā*) beset a man: if nothing is found there to delight in, welcome, and hold to, this is the end of the underlying tendency to lust…and there these evil unwholesome states cease without remainder’—this is how I understand in detail the meaning of that summary in brief spoken by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning:

“Dependent on the eye (*cakkhu*) and forms (*rūpa*), eye-consciousness (*cakkhuviññāṇa*) arises. The meeting of the three is contact (*phassa*). With contact as condition there is feeling (*vedanā*). What one feels, that one perceives (*sañjānāti*). What one perceives, that one thinks about (*vitakketi*). What one thinks about, that one mentally proliferates (*papañceti*). With what one has mentally proliferated as the source, perceptions and notions tinged by mental proliferation beset a man with respect to past, future, and present forms cognizable through the eye.

“Dependent on the ear (*sota*) and sounds (*sadda*)…Dependent on the nose (*ghāna*) and odours (*gandha*)…Dependent on the tongue (*jivhā*) and flavours (*rasa*)…Dependent on the body (*kāya*) and tangibles (*phoṭṭhabba*)…Dependent on the mind (*mana*) and mind-objects (*dhamma*), mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇa*) arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition there is feeling. What one feels, that one perceives. What one perceives, that one thinks about. What one thinks about, that one mentally proliferates. With what one has mentally proliferated as the source, perceptions and notions tinged by mental proliferation beset a man with respect to past, future, and present mind-objects cognizable through the mind.

“When there is the eye, a form, and eye-consciousness, it is possible to point out the manifestation of contact (*phassapaññatti*). When there is the manifestation of contact, it is possible to point out the manifestation of feeling (*vedanāpaññatti*). When there is the manifestation of feeling, it is possible to point out the manifestation of perception (*saññāpaññatti*). When there is the manifestation of perception, it is possible to point out the manifestation of thinking (*vitakkapaññatti*). When there is the manifestation of thinking, it is possible to point out the manifestation of being beset by perceptions and notions tinged by mental proliferation (*papañcasaññāsaṅkhāsamudācaraṇapaññatti*).

“When there is the ear, a sound…When there is the nose, an odour…When there is the tongue, a flavour…When there is the body, a tangible…When there is the mind, a mind-object, and mind-consciousness, it is possible to point out the manifestation of contact. When there is the manifestation of contact, it is possible to point out the manifestation of feeling. When there is the manifestation of feeling, it is possible to point out the manifestation of perception. When there is the manifestation of perception, it is possible to point out the manifestation of thinking. When there is the manifestation of thinking, it is possible to point out the manifestation of being beset by perceptions and notions tinged by mental proliferation.

“When there is no eye, no form, and no eye-consciousness, it is impossible to point out the manifestation of contact. When there is no manifestation of contact, it is impossible to point out the manifestation of feeling. When there is no manifestation of feeling, it is impossible to point out the manifestation of perception. When there is no manifestation of perception, it is impossible to point out the manifestation of thinking. When there is no manifestation of thinking, it is impossible to point out the manifestation of being beset by perceptions and notions tinged by mental proliferation.

“When there is no ear, no sound…When there is no nose, no odour…When there is no tongue, no flavour…When there is no body, no tangible…When there is no mind, no mind-object, and no mind-consciousness, it is impossible to point out the manifestation of contact.
