iti kho, *bhikkhave*, mayā *imesaṃ sattānaṃ hitacaraṇena sammāsambodhiṃ patvā ahaṃ buddhosmīti tuṇhībhūtena anisīditvā dhammacakkappavattanato paṭṭhāya dhammaṃ desentena vivaṭo khemo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, pihito kummaggo*, O monks, thus, by me, having attained perfect awakening through beneficial conduct for these beings, I am the Buddha, the secure, noble eightfold path is opened by me who, being silent, did not sit down, but from the turning of the wheel of the Dharma onwards, taught the Dharma; the wrong path is closed off.

*aññātakoṇḍaññādīnaṃ bhabbapuggalānaṃ ūhato okacaro nandīrāgo dvedhā chetvā pātito, nāsitā okacārikā avijjā sabbena sabbaṃ samugghātitāti attano hitūpacāraṃ dassesi.* The delight and passion that roam in the house, inferred from the suitable individuals such as Ājñāta-Kauṇḍinya, has been cut in two and cast down, ignorance that wanders in the house is destroyed, all is completely uprooted: thus he showed his beneficial service to himself.

*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.* The rest is clear throughout.

*iti kho, bhikkhave, vivaṭo mayā khemo maggo* O monks, thus, the secure path is opened by me.

*papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya* The Papañcasūdanī commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya.

*dvedhāvitakkasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.* The commentary on the Dvedhāvitakka Sutta is finished.

mula_pali:
216. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Adhicittamanuyuttena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā pañca nimittāni kālena kālaṃ manasi kātabbāni. Katamāni pañca? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno yaṃ nimittaṃ āgamma yaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tamhā nimittā aññaṃ nimittaṃ manasi kātabbaṃ kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ. Tassa tamhā nimittā aññaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti ekodibhoti (syā. ka.) samādhiyati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dakkho palagaṇḍo vā palagaṇḍantevāsī vā sukhumāya āṇiyā oḷārikaṃ āṇiṃ abhinihaneyya abhinīhareyya abhinivatteyya abhinivajjeyya (sī. pī.); evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno yaṃ nimittaṃ āgamma yaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tamhā nimittā aññaṃ nimittaṃ manasi kātabbaṃ kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ. Tassa tamhā nimittā aññaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati.

ekodibhoti (syā. ka.) abhinivajjeyya (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One was staying at Sāavatthī in the Jetavana, Anāthapindika’s monastery.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks!”

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Monks, a monk intent on heightened mind should attend to five themes from time to time. What are the five? Here, monks, if evil, unskillful thoughts, imbued with desire ( *chandūpasaṃhitā* ), aversion ( *dosūpasaṃhitā* ), or delusion ( *mohūpasaṃhitā* ), arise in a monk while he is referring to and attending to a particular theme ( *nimittaṃ* ), he should attend to another theme, apart from that one, connected with what is skillful ( *kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ* ). When he is attending to this other theme, apart from that one, connected with what is skillful, then those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated ( *samādhiyati* ).

Just as a skilled carpenter or his apprentice would use a small peg to knock out, drive out, and pull out a large one; in the same way, if evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion, or delusion — arise in a monk while he is referring to and attending to a particular theme, he should attend to another theme, apart from that one, connected with what is skillful. When he is attending to this other theme, apart from that one, connected with what is skillful, then those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
commentary_pali:
216.Evaṃme sutanti vitakkasaṇṭhānasuttaṃ. Tattha adhicittamanuyuttenāti dasakusalakammapathavasena uppannaṃ cittaṃ cittameva, vipassanāpādakaaṭṭhasamāpatticittaṃ tato cittato adhikaṃ cittanti adhicittaṃ. Anuyuttenāti taṃ adhicittaṃ anuyuttena, tattha yuttappayuttenāti attho.

Tatrāyaṃ bhikkhu purebhattaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto nisīdanaṃ ādāya asukasmiṃ rukkhamūle vā vanasaṇḍe vā pabbatapāde vā pabbhāre vā samaṇadhammaṃ karissāmīti nikkhamantopi, tattha gantvā hatthehi vā pādehi vā nisajjaṭṭhānato tiṇapaṇṇāni apanentopi adhicittaṃ anuyuttoyeva. Nisīditvā pana hatthapāde dhovitvā pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā viharantopi adhicittaṃ anuyuttoyeva.

Nimittānīti kāraṇāni. Kālena kālanti samaye samaye. Na nu ca kammaṭṭhānaṃ nāma muhuttampi achaḍḍetvā nirantaraṃ manasikātabbaṃ, kasmā bhagavā ‘‘kālena kāla’’nti āhāti. Pāḷiyañhi aṭṭhatiṃsa kammaṭṭhānāni vibhattāni, tesu bhikkhunā attano cittarucitaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā nisinnena yāva kocideva upakkileso nuppajjati, tāva imesaṃ nimittānaṃ manasikārakiccaṃ natthi. Yadā pana uppajjati, tadā imāni gahetvā citte uppannaṃ abbudaṃ nīharitabbanti dassento evamāha.

Nimittānī Kālena kāla

Chandūpasaṃhitāti chandasahagatā rāgasampayuttā. Imesaṃ pana tiṇṇaṃ vitakkānaṃ khettañca ārammaṇañca jānitabbaṃ. Tattha chandūpasañhitānaṃ aṭṭha lobhasahagatacittāni khettaṃ, dosūpasañhitānaṃ dve domanassasahagatāni, mohūpasañhitānaṃ dvādasapi akusalacittāni. Vicikicchāuddhaccasampayuttacittāni pana dve etesaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ khettaṃ. Sabbesampi sattā ceva saṅkhārā ca ārammaṇaṃ, iṭṭhāniṭṭhaasamapekkhitesu hi sattesu ca saṅkhāresu ca te uppajjanti . Aññampi nimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ kusalūpasaṃhitanti tato nimittato aññaṃ kusalanissitaṃ nimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ. Tattha aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma chandūpasañhite vitakke sattesu uppanne asubhabhāvanā aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma. Saṅkhāresu uppanne aniccamanasikāro aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma. Dosūpasañhite sattesu uppanne mettābhāvanā aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma. Saṅkhāresu uppanne dhātumanasikāro aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma. Mohūpasañhite yattha katthaci uppanne pañcadhammūpanissayo aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma.

Chandūpasaṃhitā Aññampi nimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ kusalūpasaṃhita aññaṃ nimittaṃ

Imassa hatthā vā sobhanā pādā vātiādinā nayena hi sattesu lobhe uppanne asubhato upasaṃharitabbaṃ. Kimhi sārattosi? Kesesu sārattosi. Lomesu…pe… muttesu sārattosi. Ayaṃ attabhāvo nāma tīhi aṭṭhisatehi ussāpito, navahi nhārusatehi ābaddho, navahi maṃsapesisatehi anulitto, allacammena pariyonaddho, chavirāgena paṭicchanno, navahi vaṇamukhehi navanavutilomakūpasahassehi ca asuci paggharati, kuṇapapūrito, duggandho, jeguccho, paṭikūlo, dvattiṃsakuṇapasañcayo, natthettha sāraṃ vā varaṃ vāti evaṃ asubhato upasaṃharantassa sattesu uppanno lobho pahīyati, tenassa asubhato upasaṃharaṇaṃ aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma hoti.

Pattacīvarādīsu saṅkhāresu lobhe uppanne dvīhākārehi saṅkhāramajjhattataṃ samuṭṭhāpetīti satipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayena assāmikatāvakālikabhāvavasena manasikaroto so pahīyati. Tenassa aniccato manasikāro aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma hoti. Sattesu dose uppanne pana āghātavinayakakacopamovādādīnaṃ vasena mettā bhāvetabbā, taṃ bhāvayato doso pahīyati, tenassa mettābhāvanā aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma hoti. Khāṇukaṇṭakatiṇapaṇṇādīsu pana dose uppanne tvaṃ kassa kuppasi, kiṃ pathavīdhātuyā, udāhu āpodhātuyā, ko vā panāyaṃ kuppati nāma, kiṃ pathavīdhātu udāhu āpodhātūtiādinā nayena dhātumanasikāraṃ karontassa doso pahīyati. Tenassa dhātumanasikāro aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma hoti.

Mohe pana yattha katthaci uppanne –

‘‘Garūsaṃvāso uddeso, uddiṭṭhaparipucchanaṃ;

Kālena dhammassavanaṃ, ṭhānāṭṭhānavinicchayo;

Pañca dhammūpanissāya, mohadhātu pahīyatī’’ti. –

Ime pañca dhammā upanissitabbā. Garuṃ upanissāya viharanto hi bhikkhu – ‘‘ācariyo gāmappavesanaṃ anāpucchantassa pattakāle vattaṃ akarontassa ghaṭasataudakāharaṇādidaṇḍakammaṃ karotī’’ti yattappaṭiyatto hoti, athassa moho pahīyati. Uddesaṃ gaṇhantopi – ‘‘ācariyo uddesakāle uddesaṃ aggaṇhantassa asādhukaṃ sajjhāyantassa ca daṇḍakammaṃ karotī’’ti yattappaṭiyatto hoti, evampissa moho pahīyati. Garubhāvanīye bhikkhū upasaṃkamitvā ‘‘idaṃ bhante kathaṃ imassa ko attho’’ti paripucchanto kaṃkhaṃ vinodeti, evampissa moho pahīyati. Kālena dhammasavanaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā sakkaccaṃ dhammaṃ suṇantassāpi tesu tesu ṭhānesu attho pākaṭo hoti. Evampissa moho pahīyati. Idamassa kāraṇaṃ, idaṃ na kāraṇanti ṭhānāṭṭhānavinicchaye cheko hoti, evampissa moho pahīyati. Tenassa pañcadhammūpanissayo aññaṃ nimittaṃ nāma hoti.

Apica aṭṭhatiṃsāya ārammaṇesu yaṃkiñci bhāventassāpi ime vitakkā pahīyanti eva. Imāni pana nimittāni ujuvipaccanīkāni paṭipakkhabhūtāni. Imehi pahīnā rāgādayo suppahīnā honti. Yathā hi aggiṃ allakaṭṭhehipi paṃsūhipi sākhādīhipi pothetvā nibbāpentiyeva, udakaṃ pana aggissa ujuvipaccanīkaṃ, tena nibbuto sunibbuto hoti, evamimehi nimittehi pahīnā rāgādayo suppahīnā honti. Tasmā etāni kathitānīti veditabbāni.

Kusalūpasaṃhitanti kusalanissitaṃ kusalassa paccayabhūtaṃ. Ajjhattamevāti gocarajjhattaṃyeva. Palagaṇḍoti vaḍḍhakī. Sukhumāya āṇiyāti yaṃ āṇiṃ nīharitukāmo hoti, tato sukhumatarāya sāradāruāṇiyā. Oḷārikaṃ āṇinti candaphalake vā sāraphalake vā ākoṭitaṃ visamāṇiṃ. Abhinihaneyyāti muggarena ākoṭento haneyya. Abhinīhareyyāti evaṃ abhinihananto phalakato nīhareyya. Abhinivaseyyāti idāni bahu nikkhantāti ñatvā hatthena cāletvā nikkaḍḍheyya . Tattha phalakaṃ viya cittaṃ, phalake visamāṇī viya akusalavitakkā, sukhumāṇī viya aññaṃ asubhabhāvanādikusalanimittaṃ, sukhumāṇiyā oḷārikāṇinīharaṇaṃ viya asubhabhāvanādīhi kusalanimittehi tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ nīharaṇaṃ.

Kusalūpasaṃhita Ajjhattamevā Palagaṇḍo Sukhumāya āṇiyā Oḷārikaṃ āṇi Abhinihaneyyā Abhinīhareyyā Abhinivaseyyā
commentary_english:
216. Thus have I heard: The *vitakka-saṇṭhāna-sutta*.

Therein, "*adhicittamanuyuttenā*" means the mind (*citta*) that has arisen through the ten wholesome courses of action (*dasakusalakammapatha*), [is] just mind. The mind of the eight attainments that are the basis of insight (*vipassanāpādakaaṭṭhasamāpatti*), that mind is more than mind, thus "*adhicitta*." "*anuyuttenā*" means that *adhicitta* by means of being engaged (*anuyuttena*), there the meaning is "by means of being yoked and applied" (*yuttappayuttenāti attho*).

Therein, this *bhikkhu*, having wandered for alms before the meal (*purebhattaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā*), having returned from the alms-round after the meal (*pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto*), taking his sitting cloth (*nisīdanaṃ ādāya*), even as he goes forth saying, "At such-and-such a tree-root (*asukasmiṃ rukkhamūle vā*), or in a forest thicket (*vanasaṇḍe vā*), or at the foot of a mountain (*pabbatapāde vā*), or in a mountain cave (*pabbhāre vā*) I will do the ascetic's duty (*samaṇadhammaṃ karissāmīti nikkhamantopi*)", even as he goes there and removes grass and leaves from the sitting place with his hands or feet (*hatthehi vā pādehi vā nisajjaṭṭhānato tiṇapaṇṇāni apanentopi*) is engaged in the higher mind (*adhicittaṃ anuyuttoyeva*).

Moreover, having sat down, having washed his hands and feet, having crossed his legs in the lotus position, having taken a root meditation subject (*mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā*), even as he dwells (*viharantopi*) is engaged in the higher mind (*adhicittaṃ anuyuttoyeva*).

"*nimittānī*": causes (*kāraṇāni*).

"*kālena kāla*": at the right time (*samaye samaye*).

But surely, a meditation subject (*kammaṭṭhānaṃ*) by name should be attended to uninterruptedly, without abandoning it even for a moment (*muhuttampi achaḍḍetvā nirantaraṃ manasikātabbaṃ*), why did the Blessed One say "*kālena kāla*"?

In the Pali, thirty-eight meditation subjects (*aṭṭhatiṃsa kammaṭṭhānāni*) are distinguished (*vibhattāni*), of those, by the *bhikkhu* who has taken a meditation subject agreeable to his own mind (*attano cittarucitaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā*) and is sitting (*nisinnena*) as long as any defilement (*upakkileso*) does not arise (*nuppajjati*), there is no task of attending to these causes (*imesaṃ nimittānaṃ manasikārakiccaṃ natthi*).

But when it arises (*yadā pana uppajjati*), then showing that "having taken these, the boil that has arisen in the mind (*citte uppannaṃ abbudaṃ*) should be extracted (*nīharitabbanti dassento*)", thus he said (*evamāha*).

*Nimittāni, Kālena kāla*.

"*chandūpasaṃhitā*": accompanied by desire (*chandasahagatā*), connected with passion (*rāgasampayuttā*).

Moreover, the field (*khettaṃ*) and object (*ārammaṇañca*) of these three thoughts (*tiṇṇaṃ vitakkānaṃ*) should be known (*jānitabbaṃ*).

Therein, the eight minds accompanied by greed (*lobhasahagatacittāni*) are the field (*khettaṃ*) of those connected with desire (*chandūpasañhitānaṃ*), the two minds accompanied by sadness (*domanassasahagatāni*) of those connected with aversion (*dosūpasañhitānaṃ*), the twelve unwholesome minds (*akusalacittāni*) as well of those connected with delusion (*mohūpasañhitānaṃ*).

But the two minds connected with doubt and agitation (*vicikicchāuddhaccasampayuttacittāni*) are the individual field (*pāṭipuggalikaṃ khettaṃ*) of these (*etesaṃ*).

All beings and formations (*sabbesampi sattā ceva saṅkhārā ca*) are the object (*ārammaṇaṃ*), for they arise in beings and formations that are indifferent to what is desired and not desired (*iṭṭhāniṭṭhaasamapekkhitesu hi sattesu ca saṅkhāresu ca te uppajjanti*).

"*aññampi nimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ kusalūpasaṃhita*": moreover, another cause (*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*) that is connected with the wholesome (*kusalūpasaṃhita*) should be attended to (*manasikātabbaṃ*), that is, another cause (*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*) that is dependent on the wholesome (*kusalanissitaṃ*) should be attended to (*manasikātabbaṃ*).

Therein, "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name is, when thoughts connected with desire (*chandūpasañhite vitakke*) arise in beings (*sattesu uppanne*), the contemplation of the unattractive (*asubhabhāvanā*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name.

When formations (*saṅkhāresu*) have arisen, the attention to impermanence (*anicca-manasikāro*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name.

When aversion (*dose*) has arisen in beings (*sattesu uppanne*), the cultivation of loving-kindness (*mettābhāvanā*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name.

When formations (*saṅkhāresu*) have arisen, attention to the elements (*dhātumanasikāro*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name.

When delusion (*moha*) has arisen anywhere (*yattha katthaci uppanne*), the support of the five factors (*pañcadhammūpanissayo*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name.

*chandūpasaṃhitā,* *aññampi nimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ kusalūpasaṃhita,* *aññaṃ nimittaṃ*

"These hands or feet are beautiful (*imassa hatthā vā sobhanā pādā vātiādinā nayena*)": for in this way, when greed has arisen in beings (*sattesu lobhe uppanne*), one should connect it to the unattractive (*asubhato upasaṃharitabbaṃ*).

"In what are you passionate (*kimhi sārattosi*)? In the hair are you passionate (*kesesu sārattosi*)."

"In the body hairs...pe...in the urine are you passionate (*lomesu…pe… muttesu sārattosi*)."

This self (*ayaṃ attabhāvo*) by name is propped up by three hundred bones (*tīhi aṭṭhisatehi ussāpito*), bound by nine hundred tendons (*navahi nhārusatehi ābaddho*), smeared with nine hundred masses of flesh (*navahi maṃsapesisatehi anulitto*), covered with moist skin (*allacammena pariyonaddho*), concealed by the color of the skin (*chavirāgena paṭicchanno*), from nine wounds (*navahi vaṇamukhehi*) and ninety-nine thousand pores (*navanavutilomakūpasahassehi ca*) impurity flows (*asuci paggharati*), filled with a corpse (*kuṇapapūrito*), foul-smelling (*duggandho*), disgusting (*jeguccho*), repulsive (*paṭikūlo*), a collection of thirty-two corpses (*dvattiṃsakuṇapasañcayo*), there is no essence or excellence in it (*natthettha sāraṃ vā varaṃ vāti*)": thus, for one who connects to the unattractive (*evaṃ asubhato upasaṃharantassa*) the greed that has arisen in beings (*sattesu uppanno lobho*) is abandoned (*pahīyati*), therefore for him this connecting to the unattractive (*tenassa asubhato upasaṃharaṇaṃ*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name (*nāma hoti*).

When greed has arisen in formations (*saṅkhāresu*) such as robes and bowls (*pattacīvarādīsu*), by establishing the middleness of formations through two aspects (*dvīhākārehi saṅkhāramajjhattataṃ samuṭṭhāpetīti*), according to the method spoken of in the commentary on the Foundations of Mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayena*), through the power of thinking according to the nature of being ownerless and temporary (*assāmikatāvakālikabhāvavasena manasikaroto*) that (*so*) is abandoned (*pahīyati*).

Therefore for him, attention to impermanence (*tenassa aniccato manasikāro*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name (*nāma hoti*).

But when aversion (*dose*) has arisen in beings (*sattesu dose uppanne*), loving-kindness (*mettā*) should be cultivated (*bhāvetabbā*) through the power of the removal of hatred and the advice of the saw simile (*āghātavinayakakacopamovādādīnaṃ vasena*), as one cultivates that (*taṃ bhāvayato*) aversion (*doso*) is abandoned (*pahīyati*), therefore for him the cultivation of loving-kindness (*tenassa mettābhāvanā*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name (*nāma hoti*).

When aversion (*dose*) has arisen in stumps, thorns, grass, leaves, etc. (*khāṇukaṇṭakatiṇapaṇṇādīsu*), "to whom do you get angry (*tvaṃ kassa kuppasi*)? To the earth element (*kiṃ pathavīdhātuyā*), or to the water element (*udāhu āpodhātuyā*)? Who is it that gets angry (*ko vā panāyaṃ kuppati nāma*)? Is it the earth element (*kiṃ pathavīdhātu*) or the water element (*udāhu āpodhātūtiādinā nayena*)": thus, for one who attends to the elements (*dhātumanasikāraṃ karontassa*) aversion (*doso*) is abandoned (*pahīyati*).

Therefore for him, attention to the elements (*tenassa dhātumanasikāro*) is "*aññaṃ nimittaṃ*" by name (*nāma hoti*).

mula_pali: 217. ‘‘Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno tamhā nimittā aññaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ ādīnavo upaparikkhitabbo – ‘itipime vitakkā akusalā, itipime vitakkā sāvajjā, itipime vitakkā dukkhavipākā’ti. Tassa tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ ādīnavaṃ upaparikkhato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ahikuṇapena vā kukkurakuṇapena vā manussakuṇapena vā kaṇṭhe āsattena aṭṭiyeyya harāyeyya jiguccheyya; evameva kho, bhikkhave, tassa ce bhikkhuno tamhāpi nimittā aññaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ ādīnavo upaparikkhitabbo – ‘itipime vitakkā akusalā, itipime vitakkā sāvajjā, itipime vitakkā dukkhavipākā’ti. Tassa tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ ādīnavaṃ upaparikkhato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati.
commentary_pali:
217.Ahikuṇapenātiādi atijegucchapaṭikūlakuṇapadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Kaṇṭhe āsattenāti kenacideva paccatthikena ānetvā kaṇṭhe baddhena paṭimukkena. Aṭṭiyeyyāti aṭṭo dukkhito bhaveyya. Harāyeyyāti lajjeyya. Jiguccheyyāti sañjātajiguccho bhaveyya.

Pahīyantīti evaṃ imināpi kāraṇena ete akusalā dhammā sāvajjā dukkhavipākāti attano paññābalena upaparikkhato ahikuṇapādīni viya jigucchantassa pahīyanti. Yo pana attano paññābalena upaparikkhituṃ na sakkoti, tena ācariyaṃ vā upajjhāyaṃ vā aññataraṃ vā garuṭṭhāniyaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ saṅghattheraṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā ghaṇḍiṃ paharitvā bhikkhusaṅghameva vā sannipātetvā ārocetabbaṃ, bahunañhi sannipāte bhavissateva eko paṇḍitamanusso, svāyaṃ evaṃ etesu ādīnavo daṭṭhabboti kathessati, kāyavicchindanīyakathādīhi vā pana te vitakke niggaṇhissatīti.

Pahīyantī
commentary_english:
217. "Because of a snake-corpse" etc., it is said to show a very disgusting, repulsive corpse.

"With [something] fastened to the neck," this means that a rival brings [something], fastens it to the neck with a counter-release.

"He would be troubled," means he would be afflicted and unhappy.

"He would be disgusted," means he would feel ashamed.

"He would be repelled," means he would become repelled.

"They are abandoned," means in this way, through this cause, these unwholesome *dharmas* that are blameworthy and result in suffering, are abandoned by one who, through the power of their own wisdom, investigates and feels disgusted, like with snake-corpses, etc.

But, one who is not able to investigate through the power of their own wisdom, should approach a teacher (*ācārya*) or preceptor (*upādhyāya*), or any other respected fellow monastic (*sabrahmacārin*), or an elder of the *saṃgha*, strike the bell, convene the *bhikṣu-saṃgha*, and make it known, because in a large gathering there will certainly be a wise person, who will say, "This is how danger should be seen in these things," and he will ward off those thoughts with talk about cutting off the body, etc.

They are abandoned.

mula_pali: 218. ‘‘Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno tesampi vitakkānaṃ ādīnavaṃ upaparikkhato uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ asatiamanasikāro āpajjitabbo. Tassa tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ asatiamanasikāraṃ āpajjato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, cakkhumā puriso āpāthagatānaṃ rūpānaṃ adassanakāmo assa; so nimīleyya vā aññena vā apalokeyya. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, tassa ce bhikkhuno tesampi vitakkānaṃ ādīnavaṃ upaparikkhato uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati.
mula_english: “If evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, *chanda*, aversion or delusion — still arise in the monk, *bhikkhu*, while he is scrutinizing the drawbacks, *ādīnava*, of those thoughts, he should pay no mind, *asatiamanasikāra*, and pay no attention to those thoughts. As he is paying no mind and paying no attention to them, those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, *ajjhatta*, settles it, unifies it, *ekodi*, and concentrates it, *samādhiyati*. Just as a man with good eyes, not wanting to see forms that had come into range, would close his eyes or look away; in the same way, if evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion or delusion — still arise in the monk while he is scrutinizing the drawbacks of those thoughts, those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it.
commentary_pali:
218.Asatiamanasikāro āpajjitabboti neva so vitakko saritabbo na manasikātabbo, aññavihitakena bhavitabbaṃ. Yathā hi rūpaṃ apassitukāmo puriso akkhīni nimīleyya, evameva mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā nisinnena bhikkhunā cittamhi vitakke uppanne aññavihitakena bhavitabbaṃ. Evamassa so vitakko pahīyati, tasmiṃ pahīne puna kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā nisīditabbaṃ.

Sace na pahīyati, uggahito dhammakathāpabandho hoti, so mahāsaddena sajjhāyitabbo. Evampi ce aññavihitakassa sato so na pahīyati. Thavikāya muṭṭhipotthako hoti, yattha ca buddhavaṇṇāpi dhammavaṇṇāpi likhitā honti, taṃ nīharitvā vācentena aññavihitakena bhavitabbaṃ. Evampi ce na pahīyati, thavikato araṇisahitāni nīharitvā ‘‘ayaṃ uttarāraṇī ayaṃ adharāraṇī’’ti āvajjentena aññavihitakena bhavitabbaṃ. Evampi ce na pahīyati, sipāṭikaṃ nīharitvā ‘‘idaṃ ārakaṇṭakaṃ nāma, ayaṃ pipphalako nāma, idaṃ nakhacchedanaṃ nāma, ayaṃ sūci nāmā’’ti parikkhāraṃ samannānentena aññavihitakena bhavitabbaṃ. Evampi ce na pahīyati, sūciṃ gahetvā cīvare jiṇṇaṭṭhānaṃ sibbantena aññavihitakena bhavitabbaṃ. Evaṃ yāva na pahīyati, tāva taṃ taṃ kusalakammaṃ karontena aññavihitakena bhavitabbaṃ. Pahīne puna mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā nisīditabbaṃ, navakammaṃ pana na paṭṭhapetabbaṃ. Kasmā? Vitakke pacchinne kammaṭṭhānamanasikārassa okāso na hoti.

Porāṇakapaṇḍitā pana navakammaṃ katvāpi vitakkaṃ pacchindiṃsu. Tatridaṃ vatthu – tissasāmaṇerassa kira upajjhāyo tissamahāvihāre vasati. Tissasāmaṇero ‘‘bhante ukkaṇṭhitomhī’’ti āha. Atha naṃ thero ‘‘imasmiṃ vihāre nhānaudakaṃ dullabhaṃ, maṃ gahetvā cittalapabbataṃ gacchāhī’’ti āha. So tathā akāsi. Tattha naṃ thero āha ‘‘ayaṃ vihāro accantasaṅghiko, ekaṃ puggalikaṭṭhānaṃ karohī’’ti. So sādhu bhanteti ādito paṭṭhāya saṃyuttanikāyaṃ pabbhārasodhanaṃ tejodhātukasiṇaparikammanti tīṇīpi ekato ārabhitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ appanaṃ pāpesi, saṃyuttanikāyaṃ pariyosāpesi, leṇakammaṃ niṭṭhāpesi, sabbaṃ katvā upajjhāyassa saññaṃ adāsi. Upajjhāyo ‘‘dukkhena te sāmaṇera kataṃ, ajja tāva tvaṃyeva vasāhī’’ti āha. So taṃ rattiṃ leṇe vasanto utusappāyaṃ labhitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ patvā tattheva parinibbāyi. Tassa dhātuyo gahetvā cetiyaṃ akaṃsu. Ajjāpi tissattheracetiyanti paññāyati. Idaṃ pabbaṃ asatipabbaṃ nāma.

saṃyuttanikāyaṃ tissattheracetiya
commentary_english:
218. “*Asatiamanasikāro āpajjitabbo*”:ti that thought should neither be remembered nor reflected upon; one should engage in something else.

Just as a man who does not want to see a form might close his eyes, so too, when a thought arises in the mind of a monk who is sitting having taken up the basic meditation subject, he should engage in something else.

In this way that thought of his is abandoned. When it is abandoned, he should again sit down having taken up the meditation subject.

If it is not abandoned, there is a related chain of Dhamma talk that has been grasped, that should be recited with a loud voice.

Even so, if that mindfulness of something else is not abandoned, there is a book of texts in a bag, in which both Buddha qualities and Dhamma qualities are written, having taken that out, while reciting it, one should engage in something else.

Even so, if it is not abandoned, having taken out from the bag pieces of kindling wood, thinking, "This is the upper fire-stick, this is the lower fire-stick,” one should engage in something else.

Even so, if it is not abandoned, having taken out the case, thinking, “This is called ārakaṇṭaka, this is called pipphalako, this is called nail-cutter, this is called needle,” while considering the requisites, one should engage in something else.

Even so, if it is not abandoned, having taken a needle, while sewing a worn-out place in the robe, one should engage in something else.

In this way, for as long as it is not abandoned, while doing this and that skillful action, one should engage in something else.

When it is abandoned, one should again sit down having taken up the basic meditation subject; but a new work should not be begun.

Why? When the thought is removed, there is no opportunity for lack of attention to the meditation subject.

However, ancient learned men removed the thought even after doing new work.

In that regard, this is a story: It seems that the preceptor of Tissa the novice was living in Tissa Great Monastery.

Tissa the novice said, "Venerable sir, I am bored."

Then the elder said to him, "In this monastery, bathing water is hard to get, taking me, you should go to Cittala Mountain."

He did so.

There the elder said to him, "This monastery is entirely for the Saṅgha; you should make a private place."

He said, "Good, venerable sir," having begun with the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* from the beginning, clearing a cave, and the preliminary work for the fire element kasiṇa, having started all three together, he brought the meditation subject to absorption, finished the *Saṃyutta Nikāya*, completed the cave work, having done everything, he gave a sign to the preceptor.

The preceptor said, "Novice, it was done with difficulty by you; just you should stay here today."

While living in the cave that night, having obtained a suitable season, having increased insight, having attained arahantship, he passed away there itself.

Having taken his relics, they made a shrine.

Even today, it is known as Tissa Elder's Shrine.

This section is called the Section on Lack of Mindfulness.

mula_pali: 219. ‘‘Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno tesampi vitakkānaṃ asatiamanasikāraṃ āpajjato uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikātabbaṃ. Tassa tesaṃ vitakkānaṃ vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikaroto ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso sīghaṃ gaccheyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ sīghaṃ gacchāmi? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṇikaṃ gaccheyya’nti. So saṇikaṃ gaccheyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ saṇikaṃ gacchāmi? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ tiṭṭheyya’nti. So tiṭṭheyya . Tassa evamassa – ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ ṭhito? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ nisīdeyya’nti. So nisīdeyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ nisinno? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ nipajjeyya’nti. So nipajjeyya. Evañhi so, bhikkhave, puriso oḷārikaṃ oḷārikaṃ iriyāpathaṃ abhinivajjetvā abhinissajjetvā (syā.) sukhumaṃ sukhumaṃ iriyāpathaṃ kappeyya. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, tassa ce bhikkhuno tesampi vitakkānaṃ asatiamanasikāraṃ āpajjato uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati.
mula_english: 219. “If evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion or delusion — still arise in the monk while he is paying no mind and paying no attention to those thoughts, he should attend to the relaxing of thought-fabrication with regard to those thoughts. As he is attending to the relaxing of thought-fabrication with regard to those thoughts, those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it. Just as the thought would occur to a man walking quickly, ‘Why am I walking quickly? I should walk slowly.’ So he walks slowly. The thought occurs to him, ‘Why am I walking slowly? I should stand.’ So he stands. The thought occurs to him, ‘Why am I standing? I should sit down.’ So he sits down. The thought occurs to him, ‘Why am I sitting? I should lie down.’ So he lies down. In this way, giving up the grosser posture, he takes up the more refined one. In the same way, if evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion or delusion — still arise in the monk while he is paying no mind and paying no attention to those thoughts, those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it.
commentary_pali:
219. Imasmiṃ ṭhatvā vitakke niggaṇhituṃ asakkonto idha ṭhatvā niggaṇhissatīti vitakkamūlabhedaṃ pabbaṃ dassento puna tassa ce bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikātabbanti saṅkharotīti saṅkhāro, paccayo, kāraṇaṃ mūlanti attho. Santiṭṭhati etthāti saṇṭhānaṃ, vitakkasaṅkhārassa saṇṭhānaṃ vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ, taṃ manasikātabbanti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, ayaṃ vitakko kiṃ hetu kiṃ paccayā kiṃ kāraṇā uppannoti vitakkānaṃ mūlañca mūlamūlañca manasikātabbanti. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ sīghaṃgacchāmīti kena nu kho kāraṇena ahaṃ sīghaṃ gacchāmi? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṇikaṃ gaccheyyanti kiṃ me iminā sīghagamanena, saṇikaṃ gacchissāmīti cintesi. So saṇikaṃ gaccheyyāti so evaṃ cintetvā saṇikaṃ gaccheyya. Esa nayo sabbattha.

Tattha tassa purisassa sīghagamanakālo viya imassa bhikkhuno vitakkasamāruḷhakālo. Tassa saṇikagamanakālo viya imassa vitakkacārapacchedanakālo. Tassa ṭhitakālo viya imassa vitakkacāre pacchinne mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ cittotaraṇakālo. Tassa nisinnakālo viya imassa vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattappattakālo. Tassa nipannakālo viya imassa nibbānārammaṇāya phalasamāpattiyā divasaṃ vītivattanakālo. Tattha ime vitakkā kiṃ hetukā kiṃ paccayāti vitakkānaṃ mūlamūlaṃ gacchantassa vitakkacāro sithilo hoti. Tasmiṃ sithilībhūte matthakaṃ gacchante vitakkā sabbaso nirujjhanti. Ayamattho duddubhajātakenapi dīpetabbo –

Sasakassa kira beluvarukkhamūle niddāyantassa beluvapakkaṃ vaṇṭato chijjitvā kaṇṇamūle patitaṃ. So tassa saddena ‘‘pathavī bhijjatī’’ti saññāya uṭṭhahitvā vegena palāyi. Taṃ disvā purato aññepi catuppadā palāyiṃsu. Tadā bodhisatto sīho hoti. So cintesi – ‘‘ayaṃ pathavī nāma kappavināse bhijjati, antarā pathavībhedo nāma natthi, yaṃnūnāhaṃ mūlamūlaṃ gantvā anuvijjeyya’’nti. So hatthināgato paṭṭhāya yāva sasakaṃ pucchi ‘‘tayā, tāta, pathavī bhijjamānā diṭṭhā’’ti. Saso ‘‘āma devā’’ti āha. Sīho ‘‘ehi, bho, dassehī’’ti. Saso ‘‘na sakkomi sāmī’’ti. ‘‘Ehi, re, mā bhāyī’’ti saṇhamudukena gahetvā gato saso rukkhassa avidūre ṭhatvā –

‘‘Duddubhāyati bhaddante, yasmiṃ dese vasāmahaṃ;

Ahampetaṃ na jānāmi, kimetaṃ duddubhāyatī’’ti. (jā. 1.4.85) –

Gāthamāha. Bodhisatto ‘‘tvaṃ ettheva tiṭṭhā’’ti rukkhamūlaṃ gantvā sasakassa nipannaṭṭhānaṃ addasa, beluvapakkaṃ addasa, uddhaṃ oleketvā vaṇṭaṃ addasa, disvā ‘‘ayaṃ saso ettha nipanno, niddāyamāno imassa kaṇṇamūle patitassa saddena ‘pathavī bhijjatī’ti evaṃsaññī hutvā palāyī’’ti ñatvā taṃ kāraṇaṃ sasaṃ pucchi. Saso ‘‘āma, devā’’ti āha. Bodhisatto imaṃ gāthamāha –

‘‘Beluva patitaṃ sutvā, duddubhanti saso javi;

Sasassa vacanaṃ sutvā, santattā migavāhinī’’ti. (jā. 1.4.86);

Tato bodhisatto ‘‘mā bhāyathā’’ti migagaṇe assāsesi. Evaṃ vitakkānaṃ mūlamūlaṃ gacchantassa vitakkā pahīyanti.
commentary_english:
219. Being unable to restrain thoughts while staying in this [place], showing the section on the division of the root of thought, thinking, "Staying here, he will restrain them," he says again, "Tassa ce bhikkhave," and so forth.

There, “*vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikātabba*” means *saṅkhāro* because it conditions; [it is] a cause, a reason, a root—this is the meaning.

"*saṇṭhānaṃ*" means that in which [something] stands together; *vitakkasaṅkhārassa saṇṭhānaṃ* [is] the standing together of the conditioning of thought; *vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ*, that should be contemplated.

This is what is said: "What is the cause, what is the condition, what is the reason by which this thought arose?" The root and the root of the root of thoughts should be contemplated.

“*kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ sīghaṃ gacchāmī*” – by what cause, now, do I go quickly? “*yaṃnūnāhaṃ saṇikaṃ gaccheyya*” – what is the point of this quick going of mine? I will go slowly, he thought.

"*so saṇikaṃ gaccheyyā*" — thinking thus, he would go slowly.

This method [applies] everywhere.

There, the time of that man’s quick going is like this monk’s time of being mounted by thoughts.

The time of his slow going is like this one’s time of cutting off the wandering of thoughts.

The time of his standing still is like this one's time, when the wandering of thoughts is cut off, of turning the mind to the fundamental object of meditation.

The time of his sitting down is like this one’s time of developing *vipaśyanā* and attaining *arhat*-ship.

The time of his lying down is like this one’s time of spending the day in the fruition attainment that has *nirvāṇa* as its object.

There, when these thoughts [arise], what is their cause, what is their condition? For one who goes to the root of the root of thoughts, the wandering of thoughts becomes loose.

When that has become loose, as they go to the summit, the thoughts are completely stopped.

This meaning should also be shown through the Duddubha Jātaka—

It seems that for a rabbit sleeping at the foot of a *beluva* tree, a ripe *beluva* fruit, having broken off from its stem, fell at the root of its ear.

That one, with the sound of that, with the perception "the earth is breaking," having risen up, fled with speed.

Having seen that, other quadrupeds in front also fled.

At that time, the *bodhisattva* was a lion.

He thought, "This earth is said to break at the destruction of an eon; in between, there is no such thing as an earthquake. What if I were to go to the root of the root and investigate?"

That one, having come as a lion, starting from there, asked as far as the rabbit, "By you, sir, has an earth been seen breaking?"

The rabbit said, "Yes, deva."

The lion: "Come, friend, show [me]."

The rabbit: "I am not able, lord."

"Come, hey, do not fear!" Taking [him], who was gentle and soft, and having gone, the rabbit, standing not far from the tree—

“Duddubhāyati bhaddante, yasmiṃ dese vasāmahaṃ;

ahampetaṃ na jānāmi, kimetaṃ duddubhāyatīti."

(Jā. 1.4.85) –

He spoke a verse.

The *bodhisattva*: "You stay right here!" Having gone to the foot of the tree, he saw the place where the rabbit had lain down, he saw the ripe *beluva* fruit, having looked upwards, he saw the stem, having seen [these], "This rabbit, having lain down here, with the sound of [something] having fallen at the root of this one's ear, with the perception 'the earth is breaking,' having become thusly aware, fled," having known that reason, he asked the rabbit.

The rabbit said, "Yes, deva."

The *bodhisattva* spoke this verse—

"Beluva patitaṃ sutvā, duddubhanti saso javi;

sasassa vacanaṃ sutvā, santattā migavāhinīti."
(Jā.)
1.
4.
86);

Then the *bodhisattva* reassured the herd of deer, saying, "Do not fear!"
Thus, as thoughts go to their very root, the thoughts are abandoned.

mula_pali: 220. ‘‘Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno tesampi vitakkānaṃ vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikaroto uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā dantebhidantamādhāya dante + abhidantaṃ + ādhāyāti ṭīkāyaṃ padacchedo, dantebhīti panettha karaṇattho yutto viya dissati jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhitabbaṃ abhinippīḷetabbaṃ abhisantāpetabbaṃ . Tassa dantebhidantamādhāya jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhato abhinippīḷayato abhisantāpayato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, balavā puriso dubbalataraṃ purisaṃ sīse vā gale vā khandhe vā gahetvā abhiniggaṇheyya abhinippīḷeyya abhisantāpeyya; evameva kho, bhikkhave, tassa ce bhikkhuno tesampi vitakkānaṃ vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikaroto uppajjanteva pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā dantebhidantamādhāya jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhitabbaṃ abhinippīḷetabbaṃ abhisantāpetabbaṃ. Tassa dantebhidantamādhāya jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhato abhinippīḷayato abhisantāpayato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati.
mula_english:
220.
“If evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire (chandūpasaṃhitā), aversion (dosūpasaṃhitā) or delusion (mohūpasaṃhitā) — still arise in the monk (bhikkhu) while he is attending to the relaxing of thought-fabrication (vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhāna) with regard to those thoughts,
then — with his teeth clenched (dantebhi dantaṃ ādhāya) and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth (jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca)— he should beat down, constrain, and crush his mind (cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhitabbaṃ abhinippīḷetabbaṃ abhisantāpetabbaṃ) with his awareness.

As — with his teeth clenched (dantebhi dantaṃ ādhāya) and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth (jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca)— he is beating down, constraining, and crushing his mind (cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhato abhinippīḷayato abhisantāpayato) with his awareness, those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside.
With their abandoning (tesaṃ pahānā), he steadies his mind right within (ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati), settles it (sannisīdati), unifies it (ekodi hoti), and concentrates it (samādhiyati).
Just as a strong man, seizing a weaker man by the head or the throat or the shoulders, would beat him down, constrain, and crush him; in the same way, if evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion, or delusion — still arise in the monk while he is attending to the relaxing of thought-fabrication with regard to those thoughts,
then — with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth — he should beat down, constrain, and crush his mind with his awareness.
As — with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth — he is beating down, constraining, and crushing his mind with his awareness, those evil, unskillful thoughts are abandoned and subside.
With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it.
commentary_pali:
220. Imasmiṃ vitakkamūlabhedapabbe ṭhatvā vitakke niggaṇhituṃ asakkontena pana evaṃ niggaṇhitabbāti aparampi kāraṇaṃ dassento puna tassa ce, bhikkhavetiādimāha.

Dantebhidantamādhāyāti heṭṭhādante uparidantaṃ ṭhapetvā. Cetasā cittanti kusalacittena akusalacittaṃ abhiniggaṇhitabbaṃ. Balavā purisoti yathā thāmasampanno mahābalo puriso dubbalaṃ purisaṃ sīse vā gale vā khandhe vā gahetvā abhiniggaṇheyya abhinippīḷeyya abhisantāpeyya santattaṃ kilantaṃ mucchāparetaṃ viya kareyya, evameva bhikkhunā vitakkehi saddhiṃ paṭimallena hutvā ‘‘ke ca tumhe ko cāha’’nti abhibhavitvā – ‘‘kāmaṃ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu sarīre upasussatu maṃsalohita’’nti (a. ni. 2.5) evaṃ mahāvīriyaṃ paggayha vitakkā niggaṇhitabbāti dassento ima atthadīpikaṃ upamaṃ āhari.

Dantebhidantamādhāyā Cetasā citta Balavā puriso
commentary_english:
220. Furthermore, in this section on the root divisions of thought, when one is unable to restrain thoughts, he should restrain them in this way, again showing another reason, he says, "For him, oh monks," and so forth.

"Placing the teeth on the teeth" means placing the upper teeth on the lower teeth.

"Mind with mind" means unwholesome mind should be restrained by wholesome mind.

"A strong man" means just as a very powerful man, full of strength, seizing a weak man by the head, throat, or shoulders, would beat him down, constrain him, and crush him, making him as if he were troubled, exhausted, and overcome by delusion, just so, the monk, having become a wrestler together with his thoughts, having overcome them, thinking, "Who are you, and who am I?"—"Let only skin, sinew, and bone remain, let flesh and blood dry up in the body" (A.N. 2.5)—thus showing that thoughts should be restrained by exerting great vigor, he brings forth this simile illuminating the meaning.

Placing the teeth on the teeth. Mind with mind. A strong man.

mula_pali:
221. ‘‘Yato kho yato ca kho (syā. ka.), bhikkhave, bhikkhuno yaṃ nimittaṃ āgamma yaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi, tassa tamhā nimittā aññaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Tesampi vitakkānaṃ ādīnavaṃ upaparikkhato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Tesampi vitakkānaṃ asatiamanasikāraṃ āpajjato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Tesampi vitakkānaṃ vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikaroto ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Dantebhidantamādhāya jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca cetasā cittaṃ abhiniggaṇhato abhinippīḷayato abhisantāpayato ye pāpakā akusalā vitakkā chandūpasaṃhitāpi dosūpasaṃhitāpi mohūpasaṃhitāpi te pahīyanti te abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Tesaṃ pahānā ajjhattameva cittaṃ santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vasī vitakkapariyāyapathesu. Yaṃ vitakkaṃ ākaṅkhissati taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkessati, yaṃ vitakkaṃ nākaṅkhissati na taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkessati. Acchecchi taṇhaṃ, vivattayi vāvattayi (sī. pī.) saṃyojanaṃ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Vitakkasaṇṭhānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Sīhanādavaggo niṭṭhito dutiyo.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Cūḷasīhanādalomahaṃsavaro, mahācūḷadukkhakkhandhaanumānikasuttaṃ;

Khilapatthamadhupiṇḍikadvidhāvitakka, pañcanimittakathā puna vaggo.
mula_english:
221. “There is the case where, monks, evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire (chandūpasaṃhitāpi), aversion (dosūpasaṃhitāpi), or delusion (mohūpasaṃhitāpi) — arise in a monk while he is referring to and attending to a particular theme (nimittaṃ āgamma yaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto).

He should attend to another theme (aññaṃ nimittaṃ), apart from that one, connected with what is skillful (kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ). When he is attending to this other theme, apart from that one, connected with what is skillful, then those evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion, or delusion — are abandoned (pahīyanti) and subside (abbatthaṃ gacchanti). With their abandoning (tesaṃ pahānā), he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it (eko-di), and concentrates it (samādhiyati).

As he is scrutinizing the drawbacks (ādīnavaṃ upaparikkhato) of those thoughts (tesampi vitakkānaṃ), those evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion, or delusion — are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it.

As he is paying no mind and paying no attention (asatiamanasikāraṃ āpajjato) to those thoughts, those evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion, or delusion — are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it.

As he is attending to the relaxing of thought-fabrication (vitakkasaṅkhārasaṇṭhānaṃ manasikaroto) with regard to those thoughts, those evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion, or delusion — are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it.

As — with his teeth clenched (dantebhi dantaṃ ādhāya) and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth (jivhāya tāluṃ āhacca) — he is beating down (abhiniggaṇhato), constraining (abhinippīḷayato), and crushing (abhisantāpayato) his mind with his awareness (cetasā cittaṃ), those evil, unskillful thoughts — imbued with desire, aversion, or delusion — are abandoned and subside. With their abandoning, he steadies his mind right within, settles it, unifies it, and concentrates it.

He is then called a monk with mastery (vasī) over the ways of thought sequences (vitakkapariyāyapathesu). He thinks whatever thought he wants to (yaṃ vitakkaṃ ākaṅkhissati taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkessati), and doesn’t think whatever thought he doesn’t want to (yaṃ vitakkaṃ nākaṅkhissati na taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkessati). He has severed craving (taṇhaṃ), thrown off the fetters (saṃyojanaṃ), and — through the right penetration of conceit (sammā mānābhisamayā) — has made an end to suffering and stress (dukkhassā’’ti)."

That is what the Blessed One (bhagavā) said. Gratified (attamanā), the monks delighted at the Blessed One’s words (bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti).

The Tenth Discourse on the Subduing of Thought is Concluded.

The Second Chapter called Sīhanāda is concluded.

This is the summary:

Cūḷasīhanāda, Lomahaṃsaka, Mahācūḷa, Dukkhakkhandha, Anumānika;

Kila, Pattha, Madhupiṇḍika, Dvidhāvitakka, Pañcanimittakathā, again the chapter.
commentary_pali:
221.Yato kho, bhikkhaveti idaṃ pariyādānabhājaniyaṃ nāma, taṃ uttānatthameva. Yathā pana satthācariyo tiroraṭṭhā āgataṃ rājaputtaṃ pañcāvudhasippaṃ uggaṇhāpetvā ‘‘gaccha, attano raṭṭhe rajjaṃ gaṇha. Sace te antarāmagge corā uṭṭhahanti, dhanunā kammaṃ katvā gaccha. Sace te dhanu nassati vā bhijjati vā sattiyā asinā’’ti evaṃ pañcahipi āvudhehi kattabbaṃ dassetvā uyyojeti. So tathā katvā sakaraṭṭhaṃ gantvā rajjaṃ gahetvā rajjasiriṃ anubhoti. Evamevaṃ bhagavā adhicittamanuyuttaṃ bhikkhuṃ arahattagahaṇatthāya uyyojento – ‘‘sacassa antarā akusalavitakkā uppajjanti, aññanimittapabbe ṭhatvā te niggaṇhitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissati. Tattha asakkonto ādīnavapabbe ṭhatvā, tatrāpi asakkonto asatipabbe ṭhatvā, tatrāpi asakkonto vitakkamūlabhedapabbe ṭhatvā, tatrāpi asakkonto abhiniggaṇhanapabbe ṭhatvā vitakke niggaṇhitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissatī’’ti imāni pañca pabbāni desesi.

Vasī vitakkapariyāyapathesūti vitakkacārapathesu ciṇṇavasī paguṇavasīti vuccati. Yaṃ vitakkaṃ ākaṅkhissatīti idaṃ assa vasībhāvākāradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Ayañhi pubbe yaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakketukāmo hoti, taṃ na vitakketi. Yaṃ na vitakketukāmo hoti, taṃ vitakketi. Idāni pana vasībhūtattā yaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakketukāmo hoti, taṃyeva vitakketi. Yaṃ na vitakketukāmo, na taṃ vitakketi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘yaṃ vitakkaṃ ākaṅkhissati, taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkessati. Yaṃ vitakkaṃ nākaṅkhissati, na taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkhessatī’’ti. Acchecchi taṇhantiādi sabbāsavasutte vuttamevāti.

Vasī vitakkapariyāyapathesū Yaṃ vitakkaṃ ākaṅkhissatī Acchecchi taṇha sabbāsavasutte

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Vitakkasaṇṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Mūlapaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathāya paṭhamo bhāgo niṭṭhito.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Majjhimanikāye

Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā

(Dutiyo bhāgo)
commentary_english:
221. "Because, monks," this is called analysis of the complete exhaustion [of defilements], and its meaning is clear.

Just as a teacher of skills, having taught the five weapons skills to a prince who came from a foreign country, sends him forth, saying, "Go, take the kingdom in your own country. If thieves arise against you on the way, go making use of the bow. If your bow is destroyed or broken, [use] the spear or the sword," thus, having shown what is to be done with each of the five weapons, he sends him off. Having done so, he goes to his own country, takes the kingdom, and experiences the glory of kingship.

In the same way, the Blessed One, sending forth a monk devoted to higher consciousness for the sake of attaining arahantship, [says:] "If unwholesome thoughts arise in him, by staying in the attention-to-another-object section, having warded them off, and having developed insight, he will attain arahantship. Not being able to [do that] there, by staying in the danger section; not being able to [do that] even there, by staying in the inattention section; not being able to [do that] even there, by staying in the thought-root-severance section; not being able to [do that] even there, by staying in the forceful-warding-off section, having warded off thoughts, and having developed insight, he will attain arahantship," thus he taught these five sections.

"Mastered in the avenues of thought analysis" means he is called one who is practiced in mastery, skilled in mastery, in the avenues of thought-wandering.

"He will think whatever thought he wants" - this was said to show the mode of his being mastered. For formerly, whatever thought he wanted to think, that he did not think; whatever he did not want to think, that he thought. But now, because he is mastered, whatever thought he wants to think, that very thought he thinks; whatever he does not want to think, that he does not think. Therefore, it was said, "He will think whatever thought he wants, that thought he will think; whatever thought he does not want, that thought he will not think."

"He has cut off craving," etc., was already said in the *Sabbāsava Sutta.*

Mastered in the avenues of thought analysis. He will think whatever thought he wants. He has cut off craving. In the *Sabbāsava Sutta.*

The Vitakkasaṇṭhāna Sutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, the commentary to the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished.

The commentary on the Second Section is finished.

The first part of the Mūlapaṇṇāsa Commentary is finished.

Homage to that Blessed One, Worthy One, Perfectly Enlightened One.

Majjhima Nikāya

Mūlapaṇṇāsa-Aṭṭhakathā

(Second Part)

mula_pali: 222. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ ativelaṃ saṃsaṭṭho viharati. Evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ viharati – sace koci bhikkhu āyasmato moḷiyaphaggunassa sammukhā tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, tenāyasmā moḷiyaphagguno kupito anattamano adhikaraṇampi karoti. Sace pana koci bhikkhu tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ sammukhā āyasmato moḷiyaphaggunassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, tena tā bhikkhuniyo kupitā anattamanā adhikaraṇampi karonti. Evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ viharati. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘āyasmā, bhante, moḷiyaphagguno bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ ativelaṃ saṃsaṭṭho viharati. Evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho, bhante, āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ viharati – sace koci bhikkhu āyasmato moḷiyaphaggunassa sammukhā tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, tenāyasmā moḷiyaphagguno kupito anattamano adhikaraṇampi karoti. Sace pana koci bhikkhu tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ sammukhā āyasmato moḷiyaphaggunassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, tena tā bhikkhuniyo kupitā anattamanā adhikaraṇampi karonti. Evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho, bhante, āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ viharatī’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

Now at that time the venerable Moliya Phagguna was associating excessively with nuns (bhikkhunīs).

The venerable Moliya Phagguna was associating with nuns in such a way that if any monk spoke disparagingly of those nuns in the presence of the venerable Moliya Phagguna, the venerable Moliya Phagguna would become angry and displeased and would even make an issue of it (adhikaraṇaṃ karoti).

But if any monk spoke disparagingly of the venerable Moliya Phagguna in the presence of those nuns, then those nuns would become angry and displeased and would even make an issue of it.

The venerable Moliya Phagguna was associating with nuns in this way.

Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, Moliya Phagguna is associating excessively with nuns.

Venerable sir, the venerable Moliya Phagguna is associating with nuns in such a way that if any monk speaks disparagingly of those nuns in the presence of the venerable Moliya Phagguna, the venerable Moliya Phagguna becomes angry and displeased and even makes an issue of it (adhikaraṇaṃ karoti).

But if any monk speaks disparagingly of the venerable Moliya Phagguna in the presence of those nuns, then those nuns become angry and displeased and even make an issue of it.

Venerable sir, the venerable Moliya Phagguna is associating with nuns in this way."
commentary_pali:
222.Evaṃme sutanti kakacūpamasuttaṃ. Tattha moḷiyaphaggunoti moḷīti cūḷā vuccati. Yathāha –

‘‘Chetvāna moḷiṃ varagandhavāsitaṃ,

Vehāyasaṃ ukkhipi sakyapuṅgavo;

Ratanacaṅkoṭavarena vāsavo,

Sahassanetto sirasā paṭiggahī’’ti.

Sā tassa gihikāle mahatī ahosi, tenassa moḷiyaphaggunoti saṅkhā udapādi. Pabbajitampi naṃ teneva nāmena sañjānanti. Ativelanti velaṃ atikkamitvā. Tattha kālavelā, sīmavelā, sīlavelāti tividhā velā. ‘‘Tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesī’’ti (dhammapade vaggānamuddānaṃ, gāthānamuddānaṃ; mahāva. 1-3) ayaṃ kālavelā nāma. ‘‘Ṭhitadhammo velaṃ nātivattatī’’ti (cūḷava. 384; udā. 45; a. ni. 8.19) ayaṃ sīmavelā nāma. ‘‘Velāanatikkamo setughāto’’ti (dha. sa. 299-301) ca, ‘‘velā cesā avītikkamanaṭṭhenā’’ti ca, ayaṃ sīlavelā nāma. Taṃ tividhampi so atikkamiyeva. Bhikkhuniyo hi ovadituṃ kālo nāma atthi, so atthaṅgatepi sūriye ovadanto taṃ kālavelampi atikkami. Bhikkhunīnaṃ ovāde pamāṇaṃ nāma atthi sīmā mariyādā. So uttarichappañcavācāhi ovadanto taṃ sīmavelampi atikkami. Kathento pana davasahagataṃ katvā duṭṭhullāpattipahonakaṃ katheti, evaṃ sīlavelampi atikkami.

Ativela

Saṃsaṭṭhoti missībhūto samānasukhadukkho hutvā. Sammukhāti purato. Avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti tā pana pacanakoṭṭanādīni karontiyo disvā natthi imāsaṃ anāpatti nāma, imā bhikkhuniyo anācārā dubbacā pagabbhāti aguṇaṃ katheti. Adhikaraṇampi karotīti imesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ imā bhikkhuniyo diṭṭhakālato paṭṭhāya akkhīni dayhanti, imasmiṃ vihāre pupphapūjā vā āsanadhovanaparibhaṇḍakaraṇādīni vā imāsaṃ vasena vattanti. Kuladhītaro etā lajjiniyo , tumhe imā idañcidañca vadatha, ayaṃ nāma tumhākaṃ āpatti hoti, vinayadharānaṃ santikaṃ āgantvā vinicchayaṃ me dethāti adhikaraṇaṃ ākaḍḍhati.

Saṃsaṭṭho Sammukhā Avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī Adhikaraṇampi karotī

Moḷiyaphaggunassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti natthi imassa bhikkhuno anāpatti nāma. Niccakālaṃ imassa pariveṇadvāraṃ asuññaṃ bhikkhunīhīti aguṇaṃ katheti. Adhikaraṇampi karontīti imesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ moḷiyaphaggunattherassa diṭṭhakālato paṭṭhāya akkhīni dayhanti. Imasmiṃ vihāre aññesaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ oloketumpi na sakkā. Vihāraṃ āgatabhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ vā paṭisanthāraṃ vā uddesapadaṃ vā therameva nissāya labhanti, kulaputtako lajjī kukkuccako, evarūpaṃ nāma tumhe idañcidañca vadatha, etha vinayadharānaṃ santike vinicchayaṃ dethāti adhikaraṇaṃ ākaḍḍhanti.

Moḷiyaphaggunassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī Adhikaraṇampi karontī

Sobhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavocāti neva piyakamyatāya na bhedādhippāyena, atthakāmatāya avoca. Ekaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘imassa bhikkhussa evaṃ saṃsaṭṭhassa viharato ayaso uppajjissati. So sāsanassāpi avaṇṇoyeva. Aññena pana kathito ayaṃ na oramissati, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desetvā ovadito oramissatī’’ti tassa atthakāmatāya bhagavantaṃ etaṃ, ‘‘āyasmā, bhante’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca.

So bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavocā
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard: the Kakacūpamasutta.

There, *moḷiyaphagguno* means *moḷī* is called a crest. As it was said:

"Having cut the crest, scented with excellent perfumes,
The Sakyan bull threw it into the sky;
Vāsava, with a jewel diadem,
With a thousand eyes, received it on his head."

That was very great in his householder days, therefore the designation *moḷiyaphagguno* arose for him. Even when he had gone forth, they recognized him by that same name. *Ativela* means having transgressed the time (vela). There, there are three kinds of time: time of day (kālavelā), boundary time (sīmavelā), and morality time (sīlavelā). “At that time, he uttered this utterance” (Dhammapada, summary of the chapters, summary of the verses; Mahāva. 1-3) this is called time of day. “One established in the Dhamma does not transgress the time” (Cūḷava. 384; Udāna 45; A. Ni. 8.19) this is called boundary time. And “non-transgression of time is a dam” (Dha. Sa. 299-301), and “this is time by way of non-transgression” this is called morality time. He transgressed all three of those. For there is a time for admonishing nuns, even when the sun had set, he was admonishing, thus he transgressed that time of day too. For the admonishment of nuns, there is a measure, a boundary, a limit. Admonishing with more than five or six utterances, he transgressed that boundary time too. But when speaking, having made it accompanied by burning, he speaks what is suitable for an offense of wrong speech; thus he transgressed the morality time too.

*Ativela saṃsaṭṭho* means having become mixed, having become one who shares the same happiness and suffering. *Sammukhā* means in front of. *Avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī* means seeing those nuns doing cooking, pounding, and so on, he says, "There is no non-offense for these, these nuns are of bad conduct, difficult to speak to, impudent," he speaks what is not good. *Adhikaraṇampi karotī* means, "From the time they are seen, these nuns burn the eyes of these monks; in this monastery, flower offerings or washing seats or preparing paraphernalia or whatever, proceed according to these nuns. These daughters of good families are ashamed, you say this and that to these nuns; this is an offense for you," having come to the presence of the Vinaya-holders, he drags up a case, saying, "Give me a judgment."

*Moḷiyaphaggunassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī* means, "There is no non-offense for this monk." He speaks what is not good, saying, "The door of this monk's enclosure is never empty of nuns."
Because they also create disputes (*adhikaraṇampi karontī*), these monks' eyes burn from the time they saw the Elder Moḷiyaphagguna. In this monastery, it is not possible to even look at other dwelling places. Nuns who come to the monastery receive instruction, friendly conversation, or a recitation-section only by relying on the Elder. The clansmen are ashamed and scrupulous, saying, "You say such and such things; come, let's give a judgement in the presence of the Vinaya-holders," and they stir up disputes.

They speak disparagingly of Moḷiyaphagguna, and they also create disputes (*adhikaraṇampi karontī*).

That monk (*so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavocā*) spoke to the Blessed One not out of a desire to be liked, nor with the intention to cause dissension, but out of a desire for what was beneficial. For he had this one thought: "If this monk lives in such close association, dishonor will arise for him. That is also a cause for disparagement of the teaching itself. But if someone else says this, he will not desist; if the Blessed One teaches the Dharma and gives instruction, he will desist." Because he desired what was beneficial for him, he spoke these words to the Blessed One, beginning with, "Venerable sir."

That monk (*so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavocā*)

mula_pali:
223. Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ , bhikkhu, mama vacanena moḷiyaphaggunaṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantehi – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso phagguna, āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā moḷiyaphagguno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ moḷiyaphaggunaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘satthā taṃ, āvuso phagguna, āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ moḷiyaphaggunaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, phagguna, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ ativelaṃ saṃsaṭṭho viharasi? Evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho kira tvaṃ, phagguna, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ viharasi – sace koci bhikkhu tuyhaṃ sammukhā tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, tena tvaṃ kupito anattamano adhikaraṇampi karosi. Sace pana koci bhikkhu tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ sammukhā tuyhaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, tena tā bhikkhuniyo kupitā anattamanā adhikaraṇampi karonti. Evaṃ saṃsaṭṭho kira tvaṃ, phagguna, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ viharasī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti. ‘‘Nanu tvaṃ, phagguna, kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed a certain *bhikkhu* (monk) thus: “Come, *bhikkhu*, tell the *bhikkhu* Moliya Phagguna in my name that the Teacher calls you, friend Phagguna.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” that *bhikkhu* replied to the Blessed One, and he went to the venerable Moliya Phagguna, and having gone there, he said to the venerable Moliya Phagguna: “The Teacher calls you, friend Phagguna.”

“Very good, friend,” the venerable Moliya Phagguna replied to that *bhikkhu*, and he went to the Blessed One, and having gone there, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side.

As the venerable Moliya Phagguna was sitting at one side, the Blessed One said to him:

“Phagguna, is it true that you are living in overly close association with *bhikkhunīs* (nuns)? Is it true that you are living in such close association with *bhikkhunīs* that if any *bhikkhu* speaks ill of those *bhikkhunīs* in your presence, you become angry and displeased and even bring a case? And that if any *bhikkhu* speaks ill of you in the presence of those *bhikkhunīs*, then they become angry and displeased and even bring a case? Is it true that you are living in such close association with *bhikkhunīs*?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Phagguna, aren't you a son of good family who went forth from the house life into homelessness out of faith (*śraddhā*)?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”
commentary_pali: 223.Āmantehīti jānāpehi. Āmantetīti pakkosati.
commentary_english:
223.
"Call to me," let [him] make [it] known.
"[He/She] calls to [someone]," thus [he/she] summons.

mula_pali:
224. ‘‘Na kho te etaṃ, phagguna, patirūpaṃ kulaputtassa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitassa, yaṃ tvaṃ bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ ativelaṃ saṃsaṭṭho vihareyyāsi. Tasmātiha, phagguna, tava cepi koci sammukhā tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāseyya, tatrāpi tvaṃ, phagguna, ye gehasitā gehassitā (?) chandā ye gehasitā vitakkā te pajaheyyāsi. Tatrāpi te, phagguna, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na ceva me cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāmi, hitānukampī ca viharissāmi mettacitto, na dosantaro’ti. Evañhi te, phagguna, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha, phagguna, tava cepi koci sammukhā tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pāṇinā pahāraṃ dadeyya, leḍḍunā pahāraṃ dadeyya, daṇḍena pahāraṃ dadeyya, satthena pahāraṃ dadeyya. Tatrāpi tvaṃ, phagguna, ye gehasitā chandā ye gehasitā vitakkā te pajaheyyāsi. Tatrāpi te, phagguna, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ ‘na ceva me cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāmi, hitānukampī ca viharissāmi mettacitto, na dosantaro’ti. Evañhi te, phagguna, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha, phagguna, tava cepi koci sammukhā avaṇṇaṃ bhāseyya, tatrāpi tvaṃ, phagguna , ye gehasitā chandā ye gehasitā vitakkā te pajaheyyāsi. Tatrāpi te, phagguna, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ ‘na ceva me cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāmi, hitānukampī ca viharissāmi mettacitto, na dosantaro’ti. Evañhi te, phagguna, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha, phagguna, tava cepi koci pāṇinā pahāraṃ dadeyya, leḍḍunā pahāraṃ dadeyya, daṇḍena pahāraṃ dadeyya, satthena pahāraṃ dadeyya, tatrāpi tvaṃ, phagguna, ye gehasitā chandā ye gehasitā vitakkā te pajaheyyāsi. Tatrāpi te, phagguna, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ ‘na ceva me cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāmi, hitānukampī ca viharissāmi mettacitto, na dosantaro’ti. Evañhi te, phagguna, sikkhitabba’’nti.
mula_english:
224. “Phagguna, it is not proper for you, a clansman gone forth out of faith from the house life into homelessness, to associate overmuch with *bhikkhunls*.

Therefore, Phagguna, if anyone speaks dispraise of those *bhikkhunls* in your presence, you should abandon any desires and any thoughts based on the household life.

And herein you should train thus: ‘My mind will be unaffected, and I shall utter no evil words; I shall abide compassionate for his welfare, with a mind of loving-kindness, without inner hate.’

That is how you should train, Phagguna.

“Therefore, Phagguna, if anyone gives those *bhikkhunls* a blow with his hand, with a clod, with a stick, or with a knife in your presence,

you should abandon any desires and any thoughts based on the household life.

And herein you should train thus: ‘My mind will be unaffected, and I shall utter no evil words; I shall abide compassionate for his welfare, with a mind of loving-kindness, without inner hate.’

That is how you should train, Phagguna.

And herein you should train thus: ‘My mind will be unaffected, and I shall utter no evil words; I shall abide compassionate for his welfare, with a mind of loving-kindness, without inner hate.’

That is how you should train, Phagguna.”
commentary_pali: 224.Saddhāti saddhāya. Tasmāti yasmā tvaṃ kulaputto ceva saddhāpabbajito ca, yasmā vā te etāhi saddhiṃ saṃsaṭṭhassa viharato ye tā akkosissanti vā, paharissanti vā, tesu domanassaṃ uppajjissati, saṃsagge pahīne nuppajjissati, tasmā. Tatrāti tasmiṃ avaṇṇabhāsane. Gehasitāti pañcakāmaguṇanissitā. Chandāti taṇhāchandāpi paṭighachandāpi. Vipariṇatanti rattampi cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ. Duṭṭhampi, mūḷhampi cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ. mula_pali:
225. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘ārādhayiṃsu vata me, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ekaṃ samayaṃ cittaṃ. Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū āmantesiṃ – ahaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ekāsanabhojanaṃ bhuñjāmi. Ekāsanabhojanaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhuñjamāno appābādhatañca sañjānāmi appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Etha tumhepi, bhikkhave, ekāsanabhojanaṃ bhuñjatha. Ekāsanabhojanaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tumhepi bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcāti. Na me, bhikkhave, tesu bhikkhūsu anusāsanī karaṇīyā ahosi; satuppādakaraṇīyameva me, bhikkhave, tesu bhikkhūsu ahosi.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, subhūmiyaṃ catumahāpathe ājaññaratho yutto assa ṭhito odhastapatodo. Tamenaṃ dakkho yoggācariyo assadammasārathi abhiruhitvā, vāmena hatthena rasmiyo gahetvā, dakkhiṇena hatthena patodaṃ gahetvā, yenicchakaṃ yadicchakaṃ sāreyyapi paccāsāreyyapi. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, na me tesu bhikkhūsu anusāsanī karaṇīyā ahosi, satuppādakaraṇīyameva me, bhikkhave, tesu bhikkhūsu ahosi. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhepi akusalaṃ pajahatha, kusalesu dhammesu āyogaṃ karotha. Evañhi tumhepi imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatha.

‘‘Seyyathāpi , bhikkhave, gāmassa vā nigamassa vā avidūre mahantaṃ sālavanaṃ. Tañcassa eḷaṇḍehi sañchannaṃ. Tassa kocideva puriso uppajjeyya atthakāmo hitakāmo yogakkhemakāmo. So yā tā sālalaṭṭhiyo kuṭilā ojāpaharaṇiyo ojaharaṇiyo (ka.) tā chetvā tacchetvā (sī. syā. pī.) bahiddhā nīhareyya, antovanaṃ suvisodhitaṃ visodheyya. Yā pana tā sālalaṭṭhiyo ujukā sujātā tā sammā parihareyya. Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, sālavanaṃ aparena samayena vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyya. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, tumhepi akusalaṃ pajahatha, kusalesu dhammesu āyogaṃ karotha. Evañhi tumhepi imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatha.

ojaharaṇiyo (ka.) tacchetvā (sī. syā. pī.)
mula_english:
Then, the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: “*Bhikkhus*, there was an occasion when the *bhikkhus* satisfied my mind.

Here I addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: '*Bhikkhus*, I eat at a single session (*ekāsanabhojanaṃ*).

By so doing, I, *bhikkhus*, am aware of being free from illness (*appābādhatañca*) and affliction (*appātaṅkatañca*), and I enjoy health, strength, and a comfortable abiding (*phāsuvihārañca*).

Come, *bhikkhus*, eat at a single session (*ekāsanabhojanaṃ*).

By so doing, you too, *bhikkhus*, will be free from illness (*appābādhatañca*) and affliction (*appātaṅkatañca*), and you will enjoy health, strength, and a comfortable abiding (*phāsuvihārañca*.”

And I had no need to keep on instructing those *bhikkhus*; I had only to arouse mindfulness in them.

Suppose, *bhikkhus*, there were a suitable ground, at the junction of four great highways, and a thoroughbred chariot was yoked and standing there, with the goad fitted.

Then a skilled trainer, a charioteer of horses to be tamed, might mount it, and taking the reins in his left hand and the goad in his right hand, might drive out and back by any road whenever he likes.

So too, *bhikkhus*, I had no need to keep on instructing those *bhikkhus*; I had only to arouse mindfulness in them.

Therefore, *bhikkhus*, abandon what is unwholesome (*akusalaṃ*) and devote yourselves to wholesome states (*kusalesu dhammesu āyogaṃ*),

for that is how you will come to growth (*vuddhiṃ*), increase (*virūḷhiṃ*), and fulfillment (*vepullaṃ*) in this *Dhamma* and Discipline.

Suppose, *bhikkhus*, near a village or town, there were a big *sāla*-tree grove.

And it was choked with castor-oil weeds.

Then suppose some man were to appear desiring its good, welfare, and protection (*yogakkhemakāmo*).

He would cut down and throw out the crooked *sālalaṭṭhiyo* that robbed the sap, and he would clean up the interior of the grove and tend the straight well-formed *sālalaṭṭhiyo*.

so that the *sāla*-tree grove later on would come to growth (*vuddhiṃ*), increase (*virūḷhiṃ*), and fulfillment (*vepullaṃ*).

So too, *bhikkhus*, abandon what is unwholesome (*akusalaṃ*) and devote yourselves to wholesome states (*kusalesu dhammesu āyogaṃ*),

for that is how you too will come to growth (*vuddhiṃ*), increase (*virūḷhiṃ*), and fulfillment (*vepullaṃ*) in this *Dhamma* and Discipline.
commentary_pali:
225.Atha kho bhagavāti kasmā ārabhi? Phaggunassa kira ettakaṃ ovādaṃ sutvāpi, ‘‘bhikkhunisaṃsaggato oramissāmi viramissāmī’’ti cittampi na uppannaṃ, bhagavatā pana saddhiṃ paṭāṇī viya paṭiviruddho aṭṭhāsi, athassa bhagavato yathā nāma jighacchitassa bhojane, pipāsitassa pānīye, sītena phuṭṭhassa uṇhe dukkhitassa sukhe patthanā uppajjati. Evameva imaṃ dubbacaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā paṭhamabodhiyaṃ subbacā bhikkhū āpāthaṃ āgamiṃsu. Atha tesaṃ vaṇṇaṃ kathetukāmo hutvā imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Tattha ārādhayiṃsūti gaṇhiṃsu pūrayiṃsu. Ekaṃ samayanti ekasmiṃ samaye. Ekāsanabhojananti ekaṃ purebhattabhojanaṃ. Sūriyuggamanato hi yāva majjhanhikā sattakkhattuṃ bhuttabhojanampi idha ekāsanabhojananteva adhippetaṃ. Appābādhatanti nirābādhataṃ. Appātaṅkatanti niddukkhataṃ. Lahuṭṭhānanti sarīrassa sallahukaṃ uṭṭhānaṃ. Balanti kāyabalaṃ. Phāsuvihāranti kāyassa sukhavihāraṃ. Iminā kiṃ kathitaṃ? Divā vikālabhojanaṃ pajahāpitakālo kathito. Bhaddālisutte pana rattiṃ vikālabhojanaṃ pajahāpitakālo kathito. Imāni hi dve bhojanāni bhagavā na ekappahārena pajahāpesi. Kasmā? Imāneva hi dve bhojanāni vaṭṭe sattānaṃ āciṇṇāni. Santi kulaputtā sukhumālā, te ekato dvepi bhojanāni pajahantā kilamanti. Tasmā ekato apajahāpetvā ekasmiṃ kāle divā vikālabhojanaṃ, ekasmiṃ rattiṃ vikālabhojananti visuṃ pajahāpesi. Tesu idha divā vikālabhojanaṃ pajahāpitakālo kathito. Tattha yasmā buddhā na bhayaṃ dassetvā tajjetvā pajahāpenti, ānisaṃsaṃ pana dassetvā pajahāpenti, evañhi sattā sukhena pajahanti. Tasmā ānisaṃsaṃ dassento ime pañca guṇe dassesi. Anusāsanī karaṇīyāti punappunaṃ sāsane kattabbaṃ nāhosi. ‘‘Idaṃ karotha, idaṃ mā karothā’’ti satuppādakaraṇīyamattameva ahosi. Tāvattakeneva te kattabbaṃ akaṃsu, pahātabbaṃ pajahiṃsu, paṭhamabodhiyaṃ, bhikkhave, subbacā bhikkhū ahesuṃ assavā ovādapaṭikarāti.

ārādhayiṃsū Ekaṃ samaya Ekāsanabhojana Appābādhata Appātaṅkata Lahuṭṭhāna Bala Phāsuvihāra Anusāsanī karaṇīyā

Idāni nesaṃ subbacabhāvadīpikaṃ upamaṃ āharanto seyyathāpītiādimāha. Tattha subhūmiyanti samabhūmiyaṃ. ‘‘Subhūmyaṃ sukhette vihatakhāṇuke bījāni patiṭṭhapeyyā’’ti (dī. ni. 2.438) ettha pana maṇḍabhūmi subhūmīti āgatā. Catumahāpatheti dvinnaṃ mahāmaggānaṃ vinivijjhitvā gataṭṭhāne. Ājaññarathoti vinītaassaratho. Odhastapatodoti yathā rathaṃ abhiruhitvā ṭhitena sakkā hoti gaṇhituṃ, evaṃ ālambanaṃ nissāya tiriyato ṭhapitapatodo. Yoggācariyoti assācariyo. Sveva assadamme sāretīti assadammasārathi. Yenicchakanti yena yena maggena icchati. Yadicchakanti yaṃ yaṃ gatiṃ icchati. Sāreyyāti ujukaṃ purato peseyya. Paccāsāreyyāti paṭinivatteyya.

seyyathāpī subhūmiya Catumahāpathe Ājaññaratho Odhastapatodo Yoggācariyo assadammasārathi. Yenicchaka Yadicchaka Sāreyyā Paccāsāreyyā

Evameva khoti yathā hi so yoggācariyo yena yena maggena gamanaṃ icchati, taṃ taṃ assā āruḷhāva honti. Yāya yāya ca gatiyā icchati, sā sā gati gahitāva hoti. Rathaṃ pesetvā assā neva vāretabbā na vijjhitabbā honti. Kevalaṃ tesaṃ same bhūmibhāge khuresu nimittaṃ ṭhapetvā gamanameva passitabbaṃ hoti. Evaṃ mayhampi tesu bhikkhūsu punappunaṃ vattabbaṃ nāhosi. Idaṃ karotha idaṃ mā karothāti satuppādanamattameva kattabbaṃ hoti. Tehipi tāvadeva kattabbaṃ katameva hoti, akattabbaṃ jahitameva. Tasmāti yasmā subbacā yuttayānapaṭibhāgā hutvā satuppādanamatteneva pajahiṃsu, tasmā tumhepi pajahathāti attho. Elaṇḍehīti elaṇḍā kira sāladūsanā honti, tasmā evamāha. Visodheyyāti elaṇḍe ceva aññā ca valliyo chinditvā bahi nīharaṇena sodheyya. Sujātāti susaṇṭhitā. Sammā parihareyyāti mariyādaṃ bandhitvā udakāsiñcanenapi kālenakālaṃ mūlamūle khaṇanenapi valligumbādicchedanenapi kipillapūṭakaharaṇenapi makkaṭakajālasukkhadaṇḍakaharaṇenapi sammā vaḍḍhetvā poseyya. Vuddhiādīni vuttatthāneva.

Evameva kho Tasmā Elaṇḍehī Visodheyyā Sujātā Sammā parihareyyā Vuddhi
commentary_english:
225. Then, why did the Blessed One begin by saying, "Now, monks"? Even after hearing so much advice from Phagguna, the thought, "I will abstain from association with nuns; I will cease," did not arise in his mind. But he stood stubbornly opposed to the Blessed One, like someone at odds with a teacher. Then, to the Blessed One, just as to one who is hungry there arises a desire for food, to one who is thirsty, for drink, to one who is chilled, for warmth, to one who is suffering, for happiness, so it happens.

Just so, having seen this difficult-to-instruct *bhikṣu*, the easy-to-instruct *bhikṣus* came within range of the first enlightenment. Then, desiring to describe their virtues, he began this discourse.

There, *ārādhayiṃsū* means they grasped and fulfilled. *Ekaṃ samaya* means at one time. *Ekāsanabhojana* means one meal before noon. Since sunrise until noon, having eaten a meal seven times, that too is regarded as one sitting meal. *Appābādhata* means without oppression. *Appātaṅkata* means without suffering. *Lahuṭṭhāna* means a light rising of the body. *Bala* means physical strength. *Phāsuvihāra* means a comfortable dwelling of the body, a pleasant dwelling.

What was said by this? [Namely,] the time for abandoning eating at the wrong time of day was spoken of. But in the Bhaddāli Sutta, the time for abandoning eating at the wrong time of night was spoken of. The Blessed One did not cause these two meals to be abandoned with one blow. Why? Because these two meals are habitually practiced by beings in the round. There are sons of good families who are very delicate. If they were to abandon even two meals at once, they would become exhausted. Therefore, having caused [one] to be abandoned at one time, at one time eating at the wrong time of day, and at another time eating at the wrong time of night, he caused [them] to be abandoned separately. Among these, here the time for abandoning eating at the wrong time of day was spoken of.

There, since Buddhas do not cause [beings] to abandon [wrongdoing] by showing fear and threatening, but by showing the benefits, in this way beings easily abandon [wrongdoing]. Therefore, showing the benefits, he showed these five qualities. *Anusāsanī karaṇīyā* means there was no need for repeated instruction. "Do this, do not do that" -- there was only the bare minimum of what needed to be done to produce mindfulness.

Just with that much, they did what needed to be done, they abandoned what needed to be abandoned. At the first enlightenment, *bhikṣus*, the easy-to-instruct *bhikṣus* were those who did not have outflows and who heeded instruction.

Now, bringing forth an analogy that illuminates their state of being easy to instruct, he said, "*Seyyathāpi*," and so forth.

There, *subhūmiya* means on level ground. "On level ground, in a good field, free from stumps, seeds should be established" (Dī. Ni. 2.438).
