Here, however, *maṇḍabhūmi* and *subhūmi* have come [to mean the same thing]. *Catumahāpathe* means in a place gone beyond, having pierced through two great roads. *Ājaññaratho* means a chariot with well-trained horses. *Odhastapatodo* means just as when one has climbed up into a chariot, it is possible for one standing [there] to grasp [the goad], so the goad is placed sideways, relying on a support.
*yoggācariyo*ti: horse trainer.
sveva assadamme sāretīti *assadammasārathi*: one who trains his own horses.
*yenicchaka*nti: whichever way one desires.
*yadicchaka*nti: whichever destination one desires.
*sāreyyā*ti: he should send straight ahead.
*paccāsāreyyā*ti: he should turn back.

*seyyathāpī subhūmiya catumahāpathe ājaññaratho odhastapatodo yoggācariyo assadammasārathi.
yenicchaka yadicchaka sāreyyā paccāsāreyyā*

*evameva kho*ti: Just as that horse trainer, whichever way he wishes to go, the horses are already trained to go that way.
And to whichever destination he wishes, that destination is already known.
Having sent the chariot, the horses should neither be stopped nor spurred.
Merely, on the level ground, having placed a mark at the hooves, only the going should be observed.
Likewise, I did not have to tell those monks again and again,
"Do this, don't do that." Only the arising of mindfulness had to be done.
By them, only what should be done was done, and what should not be done was abandoned.
*tasmā*ti: Because they were easy to train, skilled in yoked vehicles, having abandoned [defilements] by the mere arising of mindfulness, therefore you also abandon [them], this is the meaning.
*elaṇḍehī*ti: It is said that elaṇḍa plants are harmful to sāla trees, therefore he said thus.
*visodheyyā*ti: He should purify [the area] by cutting off elaṇḍa plants and other creepers and taking them outside.
*sujātā*ti: Well-made means well-composed.
*sammā parihareyyā*ti: Having made a boundary, by sprinkling water, from time to time at the roots, by digging, by cutting creepers and bushes, by removing ant hills, by removing spider webs and dry branches, he should properly nurture and nourish [the tree].
*vuddhi*ādīni: "Growth" and so on [have] the same meaning as stated before.

*evameva kho tasmā elaṇḍehī visodheyyā sujātā sammā parihareyyā vuddhi*

mula_pali:
226. ‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, imissāyeva sāvatthiyā vedehikā nāma gahapatānī ahosi. Vedehikāya, bhikkhave, gahapatāniyā evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘soratā vedehikā gahapatānī, nivātā vedehikā gahapatānī, upasantā vedehikā gahapatānī’ti. Vedehikāya kho pana, bhikkhave, gahapatāniyā kāḷī nāma dāsī ahosi dakkhā analasā susaṃvihitakammantā.

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, kāḷiyā dāsiyā etadahosi – ‘mayhaṃ kho ayyāya evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘‘soratā vedehikā gahapatānī, nivātā vedehikā gahapatānī, upasantā vedehikā gahapatānī’’ti. Kiṃ nu kho me ayyā santaṃyeva nu kho ajjhattaṃ kopaṃ na pātukaroti udāhu asantaṃ udāhu mayhamevete mayhevete (sī. pī.) kammantā susaṃvihitā yena me ayyā santaṃyeva ajjhattaṃ kopaṃ na pātukaroti, no asantaṃ? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ ayyaṃ vīmaṃseyya’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, kāḷī dāsī divā uṭṭhāsi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vedehikā gahapatānī kāḷiṃ dāsiṃ etadavoca – ‘he je kāḷī’ti. ‘Kiṃ, ayye’ti? ‘Kiṃ, je, divā uṭṭhāsī’ti? ‘Na khvayye na kho ayye (sī. pī.), kiñcī’ti. ‘No vata re kiñci, pāpi dāsi pāpadāsi (syā. ka.), divā uṭṭhāsī’ti kupitā anattamanā bhākuṭiṃ bhūkuṭiṃ (sī. pī.), bhakuṭīṃ (syā.) akāsi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, kāḷiyā dāsiyā etadahosi – ‘santaṃyeva kho me ayyā ajjhattaṃ kopaṃ na pātukaroti, no asantaṃ; mayhamevete kammantā susaṃvihitā, yena me ayyā santaṃyeva ajjhattaṃ kopaṃ na pātukaroti, no asantaṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhiyyosomattāya ayyaṃ vīmaṃseyya’’’nti.

mayhevete (sī. pī.) na kho ayye (sī. pī.) pāpadāsi (syā. ka.) bhūkuṭiṃ (sī. pī.), bhakuṭīṃ (syā.)

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, kāḷī dāsī divātaraṃyeva uṭṭhāsi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vedehikā gahapatānī kāḷiṃ dāsiṃ etadavoca – ‘he je, kāḷī’ti. ‘Kiṃ, ayye’ti? ‘Kiṃ, je, divātaraṃ uṭṭhāsī’ti? ‘Na khvayye, kiñcī’ti. ‘No vata re kiñci, pāpi dāsi, divātaraṃ uṭṭhāsī’ti kupitā anattamanā anattamanavācaṃ nicchāresi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, kāḷiyā dāsiyā etadahosi – ‘santaṃyeva kho me ayyā ajjhattaṃ kopaṃ na pātukaroti, no asantaṃ. Mayhamevete kammantā susaṃvihitā, yena me ayyā santaṃyeva ajjhattaṃ kopaṃ na pātukaroti, no asantaṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhiyyosomattāya ayyaṃ vīmaṃseyya’nti.

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, kāḷī dāsī divātaraṃyeva uṭṭhāsi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vedehikā gahapatānī kāḷiṃ dāsiṃ etadavoca – ‘he je, kāḷī’ti. ‘Kiṃ, ayye’ti? ‘Kiṃ, je, divā uṭṭhāsī’ti? ‘Na khvayye, kiñcī’ti. ‘No vata re kiñci, pāpi dāsi, divā uṭṭhāsī’ti kupitā anattamanā aggaḷasūciṃ gahetvā sīse pahāraṃ adāsi, sīsaṃ vobhindi vi + ava + bhindi = vobhindi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, kāḷī dāsī bhinnena sīsena lohitena galantena paṭivissakānaṃ ujjhāpesi – ‘passathayye, soratāya kammaṃ; passathayye, nivātāya kammaṃ, passathayye, upasantāya kammaṃ! Kathañhi nāma ekadāsikāya divā uṭṭhāsīti kupitā anattamanā aggaḷasūciṃ gahetvā sīse pahāraṃ dassati, sīsaṃ vobhindissatī’ti.

vi + ava + bhindi = vobhindi

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, vedehikāya gahapatāniyā aparena samayena evaṃ pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchi – ‘caṇḍī vedehikā gahapatānī, anivātā vedehikā gahapatānī, anupasantā vedehikā gahapatānī’ti.

‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu tāvadeva soratasorato hoti nivātanivāto hoti upasantūpasanto hoti yāva na amanāpā vacanapathā phusanti. Yato ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ amanāpā vacanapathā phusanti, atha bhikkhu ‘sorato’ti veditabbo, ‘nivāto’ti veditabbo, ‘upasanto’ti veditabbo. Nāhaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ ‘suvaco’ti vadāmi yo cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu suvaco hoti, sovacassataṃ āpajjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tañhi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ alabhamāno na suvaco hoti, na sovacassataṃ āpajjati. Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṃyeva sakkaronto, dhammaṃ garuṃ karonto, dhammaṃ mānento, dhammaṃ pūjento, dhammaṃ apacāyamāno dhammaṃ yeva sakkaronto dhammaṃ garukaronto dhammaṃ apacāyamāno (sī. syā. pī.) suvaco hoti, sovacassataṃ āpajjati, tamahaṃ ‘suvaco’ti vadāmi. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘dhammaṃyeva sakkarontā, dhammaṃ garuṃ karontā, dhammaṃ mānentā, dhammaṃ pūjentā, dhammaṃ apacāyamānā suvacā bhavissāma, sovacassataṃ āpajjissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.

dhammaṃ yeva sakkaronto dhammaṃ garukaronto dhammaṃ apacāyamāno (sī. syā. pī.)
mula_english:
226. Formerly, monks, in this very Śrāvastī (Sāvatthī), there lived a housewife named Vedehikā.

Monks, about Vedehikā, the housewife, a good reputation had spread thus: ‘Vedehikā, the housewife, is gentle, Vedehikā, the housewife, is meek, Vedehikā, the housewife, is peaceful.’

Furthermore, monks, Vedehikā, the housewife, had a maid named Kālī, who was skillful, not lazy, and a good manager of her tasks.

Then, monks, it occurred to Kālī, the maid: ‘Such a good reputation has spread about my mistress: “Vedehikā, the housewife, is gentle, Vedehikā, the housewife, is meek, Vedehikā, the housewife, is peaceful.”

Now, how is it? Does my mistress not show anger, even though anger is present within her, or is it absent? Or is it just because my tasks are well-managed that my mistress does not show anger, even though it is present within her, and not absent? Suppose I were to test my mistress.’

Then, monks, Kālī, the maid, got up late in the day.

Then, monks, Vedehikā, the housewife, said to Kālī, the maid: ‘Hey, Kālī!’

‘What is it, mistress?’ ‘Why, girl, did you get up late?’ ‘Nothing is the matter, mistress.’

‘Nothing is the matter, you wicked maid, [yet] you get up late!’ Angry and displeased, she scowled.

Then, monks, it occurred to Kālī, the maid: ‘Indeed, my mistress does not show anger, even though anger is present within her, not absent. It is just because my tasks are well-managed that my mistress does not show anger, even though it is present within her, not absent. Suppose I were to test my mistress even more.’

Then, monks, Kālī, the maid, got up very late in the day.

Then, monks, Vedehikā, the housewife, said to Kālī, the maid: ‘Hey, Kālī!’

‘What is it, mistress?’ ‘Why, girl, did you get up so late?’ ‘Nothing is the matter, mistress.’

‘Nothing is the matter, you wicked maid, [yet] you get up so late!’ Angry and displeased, she uttered words of displeasure.

Then, monks, it occurred to Kālī, the maid: ‘Indeed, my mistress does not show anger, even though anger is present within her, not absent.
It must just be that my work is very well done, since my lady does not show anger though it is actually present within her, and not because it is absent.
Suppose I test my lady a little more."

"Then, monks, the maid Kāḷī got up late in the day.
Then, monks, the housewife from Videha said this to the maid Kāḷī— ‘Hey Kāḷī!’
‘What is it, lady?’ ‘Hey, why did you get up so late in the day?’ ‘Nothing, lady.’
‘Nothing is the matter, wicked girl, and yet you get up so late in the day!’ Angry and displeased, she took a rolling pin, struck her on the head, and cut her head open.
Then, monks, Kāḷī, her head broken and blood flowing, complained to the neighbors: ‘Look, everyone, at the kindness! Look, everyone, at the gentleness! Look, everyone, at the peacefulness! How can it be that, just because I got up late in the day, angry and displeased, she would take a rolling pin, strike me on the head, and cut my head open?’"

"Then, monks, after a while, this bad report spread about the housewife from Videha: ‘The housewife from Videha is fierce, the housewife from Videha is not gentle, the housewife from Videha is not peaceful.’"

"In the same way, monks, some monk is extremely kind, extremely gentle, extremely peaceful, as long as disagreeable courses of speech do not touch him.
But it is when disagreeable courses of speech touch a monk that it can be understood whether that monk is really kind, gentle, and peaceful.
I do not call a monk easy to admonish who is easy to admonish only for the sake of robes, alms-food, a resting place, and medicinal requisites.
Why is that? Because that monk is not easy to admonish when he gets no robes, alms-food, resting place, and medicinal requisites.
But when a monk is easy to admonish because he honors, respects, and reveres the Dharma, him I call easy to admonish.
Therefore, monks, you should train thus: ‘We shall be easy to admonish because we honor, respect, and revere the Dharma.’
That is how you should train, monks.
commentary_pali:
226. Idāni akkhantiyā dosaṃ dassento bhūtapubbantiādimāha. Tattha vedehikāti videharaṭṭhavāsikassa dhītā. Atha vā vedoti paññā vuccati, vedena īhati iriyatīti vedehikā, paṇḍitāti attho. Gahapatānīti gharasāminī. Kittisaddoti kittighoso. Soratāti soraccena samannāgatā. Nivātāti nivātavutti. Upasantāti nibbutā. Dakkhāti bhattapacanasayanattharaṇadīpujjalanādikammesu chekā. Analasāti uṭṭhāhikā, susaṃvihitakammantāti suṭṭhu saṃvihitakammantā. Ekā analasā hoti, yaṃ yaṃ pana bhājanaṃ gaṇhāti, taṃ taṃ bhindati vā chiddaṃ vā karoti, ayaṃ na tādisāti dasseti.

Divā uṭṭhāsīti pātova kattabbāni dhenuduhanādikammāni akatvā ussūre uṭṭhitā. He je kāḷīti are kāḷi. Kiṃ je divā uṭṭhāsīti kiṃ te kiñci aphāsukaṃ atthi, kiṃ divā uṭṭhāsīti? No vata re kiñcīti are yadi te na kiñci aphāsukaṃ atthi, neva sīsaṃ rujjhati, na piṭṭhi, atha kasmā pāpi dāsi divā uṭṭhāsīti kupitā anattamanā bhākuṭimakāsi. Divātaraṃ uṭṭhāsīti punadivase ussūrataraṃ uṭṭhāsi. Anattamanavācanti are pāpi dāsi attano pamāṇaṃ na jānāsi; kiṃ aggiṃ sītoti maññasi, idāni taṃ sikkhāpessāmītiādīni vadamānā kupitavacanaṃ nicchāresi.

Divā uṭṭhāsī He je kāḷī Kiṃ je divā uṭṭhāsī No vata re kiñcī Divātaraṃ uṭṭhāsī Anattamanavāca

Paṭivisakānanti sāmantagehavāsīnaṃ. Ujjhāpesīti avajānāpesi. Caṇḍīti asoratā kibbisā. Iti yattakā guṇā, tato diguṇā dosā uppajjiṃsu. Guṇā nāma saṇikaṃ saṇikaṃ āgacchanti; dosā ekadivaseneva patthaṭā honti. Soratasoratoti ativiya sorato, sotāpanno nu kho, sakadāgāmī anāgāmī arahā nu khoti vattabbataṃ āpajjati. Phusantīti phusantā ghaṭṭentā āpāthaṃ āgacchanti.

Paṭivisakāna Ujjhāpesī Caṇḍī Soratasorato Phusantī

Athabhikkhu soratoti veditabboti atha adhivāsanakkhantiyaṃ ṭhito bhikkhu soratoti veditabbo. Yo cīvara…pe… parikkhārahetūti yo etāni cīvarādīni paṇītapaṇītāni labhanto pādaparikammapiṭṭhiparikammādīni ekavacaneneva karoti. Alabhamānoti yathā pubbe labhati, evaṃ alabhanto. Dhammaññeva sakkarontoti dhammaṃyeva sakkāraṃ sukatakāraṃ karonto. Garuṃ karontoti garubhāriyaṃ karonto. Mānentoti manena piyaṃ karonto. Pūjentoti paccayapūjāya pūjento. Apacāyamānoti dhammaṃyeva apacāyamāno apacitiṃ nīcavuttiṃ dassento.

Atha bhikkhu soratoti veditabbo Yo cīvara…pe… parikkhārahetū Alabhamāno Dhammaññeva sakkaronto Garuṃ karonto Mānento Pūjento Apacāyamāno
commentary_english:
226. Now, showing the fault of impatience, [he] says "bhūtapubba" etc.

There, "vedehikā" means the daughter of an inhabitant of the Videha country.

Or, "veda" means wisdom (paññā), because she strives and moves with wisdom, therefore "vedehikā," meaning wise (paṇḍitā).

"Gahapatānī" means the lady of the house (gharasāminī).

"Kittisaddo" means the sound of fame (kittighoso).

"Soratā" means endowed with gentleness (soraccena samannāgatā).

"Nivātā" means humble conduct (nivātavutti).

"Upasantā" means extinguished (nibbutā).

"Dakkhā" at page 2.0099 means skilled (chekā) in tasks such as cooking food, making beds, spreading mats, lighting lamps, and so on.

"Analasā" means energetic (uṭṭhāhikā), "susaṃvihitakammantā" means well-arranged in her undertakings (suṭṭhu saṃvihitakammantā).

One is not energetic (analasā) if, whatever vessel (bhājanaṃ) she takes, she breaks it or makes a hole in it; [the text] shows that she is not like that.

"Divā uṭṭhāsī" means having arisen early, without having done the tasks to be done in the morning, such as milking the cows (dhenuduhanādikammāni akatvā ussūre uṭṭhitā).

"He je kāḷī" means O black one! (are kāḷi).

"Kiṃ je divā uṭṭhāsī" means, "Why did you get up in the daytime?" (kiṃ te kiñci aphāsukaṃ atthi, kiṃ divā uṭṭhāsīti?). "No vata re kiñcī" means, "If there is nothing wrong with you, neither your head nor your back hurts, then why, you wicked slave girl (dāsi), did you get up in the daytime?" Thus, being angry and displeased, she frowned (kupitā anattamanā bhākuṭimakāsi).

"Divātaraṃ uṭṭhāsī" means she arose even earlier on the following day (punadivase ussūrataraṃ uṭṭhāsi).

"Anattamanavāca" means, "O wicked slave girl, you do not know your measure! Do you think fire is cold? Now I will teach you!" Thus, speaking such words, she uttered angry speech (kupitavacanaṃ nicchāresi).

Divā uṭṭhāsī He je kāḷī Kiṃ je divā uṭṭhāsī No vata re kiñcī Divātaraṃ uṭṭhāsī Anattamanavāca

"Paṭivisakāna" means those living in neighboring houses (sāmantagehavāsīnaṃ).

"Ujjhāpesī" means she caused to despise (avajānāpesi).

"Caṇḍī" means lacking gentleness, wicked (asoratā kibbisā).

Thus, as many as were the qualities (guṇā), twice as many faults (dosā) arose (uppajjiṃsu).

Qualities (guṇā) come slowly, slowly (saṇikaṃ saṇikaṃ āgacchanti); faults (dosā) are spread abroad in a single day (ekadivaseneva patthaṭā honti).

"Soratasorato" means exceedingly gentle, a stream-enterer (sotāpanno) who attains the state of being worthy of being asked, "Is he a once-returner (sakadāgāmī), a non-returner (anāgāmī), an Arhat (arahā)?"

"Phusantī" means touching, striking, they come into view (phusantā ghaṭṭentā āpāthaṃ āgacchanti).

Paṭivisakāna Ujjhāpesī Caṇḍī Soratasorato Phusantī

"Atha bhikkhu soratoti veditabbo" means then, a monk established in forbearance (adhivāsanakkhantiyaṃ ṭhito) should be known as gentle (bhikkhu soratoti veditabbo).

"Yo cīvara…pe… parikkhārahetū" means whoever, obtaining these robes (cīvara) etc., excellent (paṇīta) things, does things such as foot massage and back massage with single-minded devotion (ekavacaneneva karoti).

"Alabhamāno" means not obtaining in the way he formerly obtained (yathā pubbe labhati, evaṃ alabhanto).

"Dhammaññeva sakkaronto" means honoring (sakkāraṃ) the Dhamma (dhammaṃ) itself, doing good deeds (sukatakāraṃ karonto).

"Garuṃ karonto" means making it heavy (garubhāriyaṃ karonto).

"Mānento" means making it dear with his mind (manena piyaṃ karonto).

"Pūjento" means honoring it with the offering of requisites (paccayapūjāya pūjento).

"Apacāyamāno" means showing reverence for the Dhamma itself, showing humility and lowliness (dhammaṃyeva apacāyamāno apacitiṃ nīcavuttiṃ dassento).

Atha Bhikkhu soratoti veditabbo Yo cīvara…pe… parikkhārahetū Alabhamāno Dhammaññeva sakkaronto Garuṃ karonto Mānento Pūjento Apacāyamāno

mula_pali: 227. ‘‘Pañcime, bhikkhave, vacanapathā yehi vo pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ – kālena vā akālena vā; bhūtena vā abhūtena vā; saṇhena vā pharusena vā; atthasaṃhitena vā anatthasaṃhitena vā; mettacittā vā dosantarā vā. Kālena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ akālena vā; bhūtena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ abhūtena vā; saṇhena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ pharusena vā; atthasaṃhitena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ anatthasaṃhitena vā ; mettacittā vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ dosantarā vā. Tatrāpi vo, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na ceva no cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāma, hitānukampī ca viharissāma mettacittā, na dosantarā. Tañca puggalaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā pharitvā viharissāma, tadārammaṇañca sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cittena vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena abyāpajjhena (sī. syā. pī.), abyāpajjena (ka.) aṅguttaratikanipātaṭīkā oloketabbā pharitvā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, there are these five courses of speech that others may use when they address you: their speech may be timely or untimely; true or untrue; gentle or harsh; connected with good or with harm; spoken with a mind of loving-kindness (mettacittā) or with inner hate.

When others address you, bhikkhus, their speech may be timely or untimely; when others address you, bhikkhus, their speech may be true or untrue; when others address you, bhikkhus, their speech may be gentle or harsh; when others address you, bhikkhus, their speech may be connected with good or with harm; when others address you, bhikkhus, their speech may be spoken with a mind of loving-kindness (mettacittā) or with inner hate.

Herein, bhikkhus, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will remain unaffected, and we shall utter no evil words; we shall abide compassionate for their welfare, with a mind of lovingkindness (mettacittā), without inner hate.

We shall abide pervading that person with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (mettāsahagatena cetasā), and starting with him, we shall abide pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (mettāsahagatena cittena), abundant, exalted (mahaggatena), immeasurable (appamāṇena), without hostility (averena) and without ill will (abyābajjhena).’

That is how you should train, bhikkhus. (evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.)
commentary_pali: 227. Evaṃ akkhantiyā dosaṃ dassetvā idāni ye adhivāsenti, te evaṃ adhivāsentīti pañca vacanapathe dassento pañcime, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha kālenāti yuttapattakālena. Bhūtenāti satā vijjamānena. Saṇhenāti sammaṭṭhena . Atthasañhitenāti atthanissitena kāraṇanissitena. Akālenātiādīni tesaṃyeva paṭipakkhavasena veditabbāni. Mettacittāti uppannamettacittā hutvā. Dosantarāti duṭṭhacittā, abbhantare uppannadosā hutvā. Tatrāti tesu vacanapathesu. Pharitvāti adhimuccitvā. Tadārammaṇañcāti kathaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karoti? Pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgataṃ puggalaṃ mettacittassa ārammaṇaṃ katvā puna tasseva mettacittassa avasesasatte ārammaṇaṃ karonto sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ karoti nāma. Tatrāyaṃ vacanattho. Tadārammaṇañcāti tasseva mettacittassa ārammaṇaṃ katvā. Sabbāvantanti sabbasattavantaṃ. Lokanti sattalokaṃ. Vipulenāti anekasattārammaṇena. Mahaggatenāti mahaggatabhūmikena. Appamāṇenāti subhāvitena. Averenāti niddosena. Abyābajjhenāti niddukkhena. Pharitvā viharissāmāti evarūpena mettāsahagatena cetasā tañca puggalaṃ sabbañca lokaṃ tassa cittassa ārammaṇaṃ katvā adhimuccitvā viharissāma.
commentary_english:
227.

Thus, having shown the fault in not enduring, now, those who endure, showing the five paths of speech, saying, "These five, *bhikkhus*," etc.

There, *kālena* means at the proper time for a suitable alms bowl.

*Bhūtena* means with what exists, with what is present.

*Saṇhena* means with what is polished.

*Atthasañhitena* means with what is based on meaning, with what is based on reason.

*Akālena*, etc., should be understood as the opposite of those.

*Mettacittā* means having a mind of loving-kindness that has arisen.

*Dosantarā* means having a corrupt mind, having a fault that has arisen internally.

*Tatrā* means in those paths of speech.

*Pharitvā* means having been intent.

*Tadārammaṇañcā* means how does [one] make the entire world its object? Having taken a person who has come into the five paths of speech, having made [that person] the object of a mind of loving-kindness, again, making the remaining beings the object of that very mind of loving-kindness, [one] makes the entire world its object.

Here, the meaning of the word is this.

*Tadārammaṇañcā* means having made the object of that very mind of loving-kindness.

*Sabbāvanta* means having all beings.

*Loka* means the world of beings.

*Vipulenā* means with an object of many beings.

*Mahaggatenā* means with what pertains to the level of the great.

*Appamāṇenā* means with what is well developed.

*Averenā* means with what is faultless.

*Abyābajjhenā* means with what is without suffering.

*Pharitvā viharissāmā* means with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness of this form, having made that person and the entire world the object of that mind, having been intent, we will dwell.

mula_pali: 228. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso āgaccheyya kudālapiṭakaṃ kuddālapiṭakaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) ādāya. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ apathaviṃ karissāmī’ti . So tatra tatra vikhaṇeyya khaṇeyya (sī. syā. pī.), tatra tatra vikireyya, tatra tatra oṭṭhubheyya, tatra tatra omutteyya – ‘apathavī bhavasi, apathavī bhavasī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu so puriso imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ apathaviṃ kareyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Ayañhi, bhante, mahāpathavī gambhīrā appameyyā. Sā na sukarā apathavī kātuṃ; yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañcime vacanapathā yehi vo pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ – kālena vā akālena vā; bhūtena vā abhūtena vā; saṇhena vā pharusena vā; atthasaṃhitena vā anatthasaṃhitena vā; mettacittā vā dosantarā vā. Kālena vā , bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ akālena vā; bhūtena vā bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ abhūtena vā; saṇhena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ pharusena vā; atthasaṃhitena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ anatthasaṃhitena vā; mettacittā vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ dosantarā vā. Tatrāpi vo, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na ceva no cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāma, hitānukampī ca viharissāma mettacittā na dosantarā. Tañca puggalaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā pharitvā viharissāma, tadārammaṇañca sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ pathavisamena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
228. “Just as, monks, a man might come carrying a hoe and a basket, and he might say this: ‘I will make this great earth to be without earth.’ He would dig here and there, scatter [the soil] here and there, spit here and there, and urinate here and there, [saying,] ‘Be without earth! Be without earth!’ What do you think, monks? Could that man make this great earth to be without earth?”

“No, venerable sir.”

“What is the reason for that?”

“Because, venerable sir, this great earth is deep and immeasurable. It is not easy to make it without earth. The man would only get his share of weariness and frustration.”

“In the same way, monks, there are these five courses of speech with which others might address you: they might speak at the right time or at the wrong time; truthfully or untruthfully; gently or harshly; in connection with benefit or in connection with harm; with a mind of loving-kindness or with inner hatred.

Whether, monks, others address you at the right time or the wrong time; whether, monks, others address you truthfully or untruthfully; whether, monks, others address you gently or harshly; whether, monks, others address you in connection with benefit or in connection with harm; whether, monks, others address you with a mind of loving-kindness or with inner hatred, even then you should train yourselves thus: ‘Our minds will remain unaffected. We will utter no evil words. We will abide compassionate for their welfare, with a mind of loving-kindness, without inner hatred.’ We will dwell having pervaded that person with a mind imbued with loving-kindness. Starting with him, we will dwell having pervaded the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, vast, exalted, measureless, without hostility, and without ill will.’ That is how you should train, monks.
commentary_pali: 228. Idāni tadatthadīpikaṃ upamaṃ āharanto seyyathāpītiādimāha. Tattha apathavinti nippathaviṃ karissāmīti attho. Tatra tatrāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Vikireyyāti pacchiyā paṃsuṃ uddharitvā bījāni viya vikireyya. Oṭṭhubheyyāti kheḷaṃ pāteyya. Apathaviṃ kareyyāti evaṃ kāyena ca vācāya ca payogaṃ katvāpi sakkuṇeyya apathaviṃ kātunti? Gambhīrāti bahalattena dviyojanasatasahassāni cattāri ca nahutāni gambhīrā. Appameyyāti tiriyaṃ pana aparicchinnā. Evameva khoti ettha idaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ – pathavī viya hi mettacittaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kudālapiṭakaṃ gahetvā āgatapuriso viya pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo. Yathā so kudālapiṭakena mahāpathaviṃ apathaviṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, evaṃ vo pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo mettacittassa aññathattaṃ kātuṃ na sakkhissatīti.
commentary_english:
228. Now, introducing an illustration that illuminates its meaning, he says, "Just as..." etc.

There, *apathavi* means "I will make it without earth," this is the meaning.

*Tatra tatra* means in each and every place, in each and every location (tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne).

*Vikireyyā* means having lifted up the dust with a winnowing basket, one would scatter it like seeds.

*Oṭṭhubheyyā* means one should spit out phlegm.

*Apathaviṃ kareyyā* means could one, having made an effort with body and speech, be able to make it without earth? *Gambhīrā* means deep, due to its thickness it is deep for two hundred thousand *yojana*s, and four *nahuta*s.

*Appameyyā* means in breadth it is unlimited.

*Evameva kho* means here, this is a connection with the illustration— the mind of loving-kindness (maitrī-citta) should be regarded as like the earth (pathavī).

Like a person who has come carrying a hoe and a basket, [so is] a person who has come grasping five courses of speech.

Just as that person is not able to make the great earth without earth with a hoe and a basket, so also, the person who has come grasping five courses of speech will not be able to make the otherness of the mind of loving-kindness.

mula_pali: 229. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso āgaccheyya lākhaṃ vā haliddiṃ vā nīlaṃ vā mañjiṭṭhaṃ vā ādāya. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ imasmiṃ ākāse rūpaṃ likhissāmi, rūpapātubhāvaṃ karissāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu so puriso imasmiṃ ākāse rūpaṃ likheyya, rūpapātubhāvaṃ kareyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Ayañhi, bhante, ākāso arūpī anidassano. Tattha na sukaraṃ rūpaṃ likhituṃ, rūpapātubhāvaṃ kātuṃ; yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañcime vacanapathā yehi vo pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ kālena vā akālena vā …pe… ‘na ceva… tadārammaṇañca sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ ākāsasamena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, suppose a man came with *lākhaṃ* (crimson), *haliddiṃ* (turmeric), *nīlaṃ* (indigo), or *mañjiṭṭhaṃ* (carmine), and said: ‘I shall draw pictures (*rūpaṃ likhissāmi*) and make pictures appear (*rūpapātubhāvaṃ karissāmī*) on empty space (*ākāse*).’ What do you think, bhikkhus? Could that man draw pictures (*rūpaṃ likheyya*) and make pictures appear (*rūpapātubhāvaṃ kareyyā*) on empty space (*ākāse*)?”

“No, *bhante*.”

“What is the reason (*kissa hetu*)?”

“Because, *bhante*, empty space (*ākāso*) is without form (*arūpī*) and invisible (*anidassano*). It is not easy to draw a picture (*rūpaṃ likhituṃ*) or make a picture appear (*rūpapātubhāvaṃ kātuṃ*) there. Eventually the man would reap only weariness and disappointment (*kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā*).”

“So too, bhikkhus, there are these five courses of speech that others may use when they address you: their speech may be timely (*kālena*) or untimely (*akālena*)…

‘Our minds will remain unaffected…and starting with him, we shall abide pervading the all-encompassing world (*sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ*) with a mind similar to empty space (*ākāsasamena cetasā*), abundant (*vipulena*), exalted (*mahaggatena*), immeasurable (*appamāṇena*), without hostility (*averena*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhena*).’

That is how you should train, bhikkhus (*evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 229. Dutiyaupamāyaṃ haliddinti yaṃkiñci pītakavaṇṇaṃ. Nīlanti kaṃsanīlaṃ vā palāsanīlaṃ vā. Arūpīti arūpo . Nanu ca, dvinnaṃ kaṭṭhānaṃ vā dvinnaṃ rukkhānaṃ vā dvinnaṃ seyyānaṃ vā dvinnaṃ selānaṃ vā antaraṃ paricchinnākāsarūpanti āgataṃ, kasmā idha arūpīti vuttoti? Sanidassanabhāvapaṭikkhepato. Tenevāha ‘‘anidassano’’ti. Tasmiñhi rūpaṃ likhituṃ, rūpapātubhāvaṃ dassetuṃ na sakkā, tasmā ‘‘arūpī’’ti vutto. Anidassanoti dassanassa cakkhuviññāṇassa anāpātho. Upamāsaṃsandane panettha ākāso viya mettacittaṃ. Tulikapañcamā cattāro raṅgajātā viya pañca vacanapathā, tulikapañcame raṅge gahetvā āgatapuriso viya pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo. Yathā so tulikapañcamehi raṅgehi ākāse rūpapātubhāvaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, evaṃ vo pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo mettacittassa aññathattaṃ katvā dosuppattiṃ dassetuṃ na sakkhissatīti.
commentary_english:
229.
In the second simile, *haliddi* means anything yellow in color.

*Nīla* means *kaṃsanīlaṃ* or *palāsanīlaṃ*.

*Arūpī* means without form.

But indeed, it is stated that the space between two pieces of wood, two trees, two beds, or two rocks is defined as space-form (*paricchinnākāsarūpa*), so why is it said here that it is formless (*arūpī*)? It is because of the rejection of having an appearance (*sanidassanabhāvapaṭikkhepato*).

That is why [he] said, "Without appearance (*anidassano*)".

Since it is not possible to draw a form or show the manifestation of form in it, therefore it is said to be "formless" (*arūpī*).

"Without appearance" (*anidassano*) means not being in the range of vision, of visual consciousness (cakṣurvijñāna).

Here, in the connection with the simile, the loving-kindness (*maitrī*) mind is like space (*ākāśa*).

Just as four kinds of colors are like five ways of speech with the fifth [color] as brush, so a person who has come taking the five ways of speaking is like a person who has come taking the color with the fifth brush.

Just as he cannot bring about the manifestation of form in space (*ākāśa*) with those five colors [using] a brush, so also a person who has come grasping the five paths of speech, by changing the loving-kindness (*maitrī*) mind, will not be able to show the arising of faults.

mula_pali: 230. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso āgaccheyya ādittaṃ tiṇukkaṃ ādāya. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ imāya ādittāya tiṇukkāya gaṅgaṃ nadiṃ santāpessāmi saṃparitāpessāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu so puriso ādittāya tiṇukkāya gaṅgaṃ nadiṃ santāpeyya saṃparitāpeyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Gaṅgā hi, bhante, nadī gambhīrā appameyyā. Sā na sukarā ādittāya tiṇukkāya santāpetuṃ saṃparitāpetuṃ; yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañcime vacanapathā yehi vo pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ kālena vā akālena vā…pe… ‘na ceva… tadārammaṇañca sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ gaṅgāsamena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharissāmā’’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english: “Bhikkhus, suppose a man came with a blazing grass torch and said: ‘I shall heat up and burn away the river Ganges (gaṅgā nadī) with this blazing grass torch.’ What do you think, bhikkhus? Could that man heat up and burn away the river Ganges (gaṅgā nadī) with that blazing grass torch?” “No, venerable sir.” “What is the reason for that?” “Because the river Ganges (gaṅgā), venerable sir, is deep and immense; it cannot possibly be heated up and burned away with a blazing grass torch; that man would only get his fill of weariness and vexation.” “So too, bhikkhus, there are these five courses of speech that others may use when they address you: their speech may be timely or untimely… ‘Our minds will remain unaffected…and starting with him, we shall abide pervading the all-encompassing world (lokaṃ) with a mind similar to the river Ganges (gaṅgāsamena cetasā), abundant (vipulena), exalted (mahaggatena), immeasurable (appamāṇena), without hostility (averena) and without ill will (abyābajjhena).’ That is how you should train, bhikkhus (evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ).
commentary_pali: 230. Tatiyaupamāyaṃ ādittanti pajjalitaṃ. Gambhīrā appameyyāti imissā gaṅgāya gambhīraṭṭhānaṃ gāvutampi atthi, aḍḍhayojanampi, yojanampi. Puthulaṃ panassā evarūpaṃyeva, dīghato pana pañcayojanasatāni. Sā kathaṃ gambhīrā appameyyāti? Etena payogena parivattetvā uddhane udakaṃ viya tāpetuṃ asakkuṇeyyato. Ṭhitodakaṃ pana kenaci upāyena aṅgulamattaṃ vā aḍḍhaṅgulamattaṃ vā evaṃ tāpetuṃ sakkā bhaveyya, ayaṃ pana na sakkā, tasmā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Upamāsaṃsandane panettha gaṅgā viya mettacittaṃ, tiṇukkaṃ ādāya āgatapuriso viya pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo. Yathā so ādittāya tiṇukkāya gaṅgaṃ tāpetuṃ na sakkoti, evaṃ vo pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo mettacittassa aññathattaṃ kātuṃ na sakkhissatīti.
commentary_english:
230.
"Āditta" in the third simile means blazing.

"Gambhīrā appameyyā": This Gaṅgā has deep places a *gāvuta* in depth, or half a *yojana*, or a *yojana*.

Its width is just like that, but in length it is five hundred *yojana*s.

How is it deep and immeasurable? Because it cannot be heated by turning it around with this effort, like water in a pot.

Still water, however, could be heated to the extent of a finger's breadth or half a finger's breadth by some means; but this is not possible, therefore it was said thus.

Here in the connection of similes, *mettacitta* is like the Gaṅgā; a person who has come taking a grass torch is like a person who has come taking hold of the five paths of speech.

Just as he cannot heat the Gaṅgā with a blazing grass torch, so a person who has come taking hold of the five paths of speech will not be able to change the *mettacitta*.

mula_pali: 231. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, biḷārabhastā madditā sumadditā suparimadditā, mudukā tūlinī chinnasassarā chinnabhabbharā. Atha puriso āgaccheyya kaṭṭhaṃ vā kathalaṃ kaṭhalaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) vā ādāya. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahaṃ imaṃ biḷārabhastaṃ madditaṃ sumadditaṃ suparimadditaṃ, mudukaṃ tūliniṃ, chinnasassaraṃ chinnabhabbharaṃ kaṭṭhena vā kathalena vā sarasaraṃ karissāmi bharabharaṃ karissāmī’ti . Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu so puriso amuṃ biḷārabhastaṃ madditaṃ sumadditaṃ suparimadditaṃ, mudukaṃ tūliniṃ, chinnasassaraṃ chinnabhabbharaṃ kaṭṭhena vā kathalena vā sarasaraṃ kareyya, bharabharaṃ kareyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Amu hi, bhante, biḷārabhastā madditā sumadditā suparimadditā, mudukā tūlinī, chinnasassarā chinnabhabbharā. Sā na sukarā kaṭṭhena vā kathalena vā sarasaraṃ kātuṃ bharabharaṃ kātuṃ; yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañcime vacanapathā yehi vo pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ kālena vā akālena vā; bhūtena vā abhūtena vā; saṇhena vā pharusena vā; atthasaṃhitena vā anatthasaṃhitena vā; mettacittā vā dosantarā vā. Kālena vā bhikkhave pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ akālena vā; bhūtena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ abhūtena vā; saṇhena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ pharusena vā; atthasaṃhitena vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ anatthasaṃhitena vā; mettacittā vā, bhikkhave, pare vadamānā vadeyyuṃ dosantarā vā. Tatrāpi vo, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na ceva no cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāma hitānukampī ca viharissāma mettacittā na dosantarā. Tañca puggalaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā pharitvā viharissāma, tadārammaṇañca sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ biḷārabhastāsamena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
231. Bhikkhus, suppose there were a catskin bag ( *biḷārabhastā*) that was rubbed, well-rubbed, thoroughly well-rubbed, soft, silky (*tūlinī*), rid of rustling, rid of crackling.

Then a man came with a stick (*kaṭṭhaṃ*) or a potsherd (*kathalaṃ*)— or a *kaṭhalaṃ* as some say— and took it up.

He would say thus: ‘I shall make this catskin bag ( *biḷārabhastaṃ*) that is rubbed, well-rubbed, thoroughly well-rubbed, soft, silky, rid of rustling, rid of crackling, rustle (*sarasaraṃ*) and crackle (*bharabharaṃ*) with the stick or the potsherd.’

What do you think, bhikkhus? Could that man make that catskin bag ( *biḷārabhastaṃ*) that is rubbed, well-rubbed, thoroughly well-rubbed, soft, silky, rid of rustling, rid of crackling, rustle (*sarasaraṃ*) and crackle (*bharabharaṃ*) with the stick or the potsherd?” “No, venerable sir.”

“What is the reason for that?” “Because that catskin bag ( *biḷārabhastā*) being rubbed, well-rubbed, thoroughly well-rubbed, soft, silky (*tūlinī*), rid of rustling, rid of crackling, cannot possibly be made to rustle (*sarasaraṃ*) or crackle (*bharabharaṃ*) with the stick or the potsherd. Eventually the man would reap only weariness and disappointment.”

“So too, bhikkhus, there are these five courses of speech that others may use when they address you: their speech may be timely or untimely; true or untrue; gentle or harsh; connected with good or with harm; spoken with a mind of loving-kindness ( *mettacittā*) or with inner hate (*dosantarā*).

When others address you, their speech may be timely or untimely; when others address you, their speech may be true or untrue; when others address you, their speech may be gentle or harsh; when others address you, their speech may be connected with good or with harm; when others address you, their speech may be spoken with a mind of loving-kindness ( *mettacittā*) or with inner hate (*dosantarā*).

Herein, bhikkhus, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will remain unaffected, and we shall utter no evil words; we shall abide compassionate for their welfare, with a mind of loving-kindness ( *mettacittā*), without inner hate (*dosantarā*).

We shall abide pervading that person with a mind imbued with loving-kindness ( *mettāsahagatena cetasā*); and starting with him, we shall abide pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind similar to a catskin bag ( *biḷārabhastāsamena cetasā*), abundant, exalted, immeasurable (*appamāṇena*), without hostility (*averena*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhena*).’

That is how you should train, bhikkhus.
commentary_pali: 231. Catutthaupamāyaṃ biḷārabhastāti biḷāracammapasibbakā. Sumadditāti suṭṭhu madditā. Suparimadditāti anto ca bahi ca samantato suparimadditā. Tūlinīti simbalitūlalatātūlasamānā. Chinnasassarāti chinnasassarasaddā. Chinnabhabbharāti chinnabhabbharasaddā. Upamāsaṃsandane panettha biḷārabhastā viya mettacittaṃ, kaṭṭhakaṭhalaṃ ādāya āgatapuriso viya pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo. Yathā so kaṭṭhena vā kaṭhalena vā biḷārabhastaṃ sarasaraṃ bharabharaṃ saddaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, evaṃ vo pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo mettacittassa aññathattaṃ katvā dosānugatabhāvaṃ kātuṃ na sakkhissatīti.
commentary_english:
231. In the fourth simile, "biḷārabhastā" means a cat-skin bag.

"sumadditā" means well-rubbed.

"suparimadditā" means well-rubbed inside and outside, everywhere.

"tūlinī" means similar to *simbali* cotton, *latā* cotton, and *tūla* cotton.

"chinnasassarā" means a cut, hissing sound.

"chinnabhabbharā" means a cut *bhabbhara* sound.

Here, in the connection of similes, *biḷārabhastā viya mettacittaṃ* (the mind of loving-kindness is like a cat-skin bag), *kaṭṭhakaṭhalaṃ ādāya āgatapuriso viya pañca vacanapathe gahetvā āgatapuggalo* (a person who has come taking a wooden dish is like a person who has come grasping the five paths of speech).

Just as he is not able to make the sound *sarassaraṃ bharabharaṃ* with a wooden or clay *biḷārabhastaṃ*, so too, that person who has come grasping the five paths of speech, having made the otherness of the mind of loving-kindness, will not be able to make a state following aversion, thus (iti).

mula_pali: 232. ‘‘Ubhatodaṇḍakena cepi, bhikkhave, kakacena corā ocarakā aṅgamaṅgāni okanteyyuṃ, tatrāpi yo mano padūseyya, na me so tena sāsanakaro. Tatrāpi vo, bhikkhave , evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na ceva no cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ bhavissati, na ca pāpikaṃ vācaṃ nicchāressāma, hitānukampī ca viharissāma mettacittā na dosantarā. Tañca puggalaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā pharitvā viharissāma tadārammaṇañca sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
232. Bhikkhus, even if bandits were to sever you savagely limb by limb with a two-handled saw (ubhatodaṇḍakena kakacena), he who gave rise to a mind of hate (mano padūseyya) towards them would not be carrying out my teaching (sāsanakaro).

Herein, bhikkhus, you should train thus (evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ): ‘Our minds will remain unaffected (cittaṃ vipariṇataṃ na bhavissati), and we shall utter no evil words (pāpikaṃ vācaṃ na nicchāressāma); we shall abide compassionate for their welfare (hitānukampī viharissāma), with a mind of loving-kindness (mettacittā), without inner hate (na dosantarā).

We shall abide pervading them with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (mettāsahagatena cetasā pharitvā viharissāma); and starting with them, we shall abide pervading the all-encompassing world (sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ) with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (mettāsahagatena cetasā), abundant (vipulena), exalted (mahaggatena), immeasurable (appamāṇena), without hostility (averena) and without ill will (abyābajjhena).’

That is how you should train, bhikkhus (evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ).
commentary_pali: 232.Ocarakāti avacarakā heṭṭhācarakā, nīcakammakārakāti attho. Yo mano padūseyyāti yo bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā mano padūseyya, taṃ kakacena okantanaṃ nādhivāseyya. Na me so tena sāsanakaroti so tena anadhivāsanena mayhaṃ ovādakaro na hoti. Āpatti panettha natthi.
commentary_english:
Ocarakā: avacarakā means heṭṭhācarakā, meaning nīcakammakārakā.

Yo mano padūseyyā: Yo, whether a *bhikkhu* or *bhikkhunī*, if one corrupts the mind ( *mano padūseyya*), one should not tolerate being cut with a saw ( *kakacena okantanaṃ nādhivāseyya*).

Na me so tena sāsanakaro: so tena anadhivāsanena means he is not my advisor ( *ovādakaro*).

There is no offense (*āpatti*) here (*ettha natthi*).

mula_pali:
233. ‘‘Imañca imañce (?) tumhe, bhikkhave, kakacūpamaṃ ovādaṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ manasi kareyyātha. Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, taṃ vacanapathaṃ, aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vā, yaṃ tumhe nādhivāseyyāthā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, imaṃ kakacūpamaṃ ovādaṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ manasikarotha. Taṃ vo bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Kakacūpamasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
233.

“And therefore, *bhikkhus*, you should keep this advice on the simile of the saw (kakacūpamaṃ ovādaṃ) constantly in mind (abhikkhaṇaṃ manasi kareyyātha).

Do you see any course of speech, trivial (*aṇuṃ*) or gross (*thūlaṃ*), that you could not endure?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Therefore, *bhikkhus*, you should keep this advice on the simile of the saw (kakacūpamaṃ ovādaṃ) constantly in mind (abhikkhaṇaṃ manasikarotha).

That will lead to your welfare (*hitāya*) and happiness (*sukhāya*) for a long time (dīgharattaṃ).”

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*bhagavā*).

Elated (*attamanā*), those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement (*bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti*).

The Kakacūpamasuttaṃ, the first, is finished.
commentary_pali:
233.Aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vāti appasāvajjaṃ vā mahāsāvajjaṃ vā. Yaṃ tumhe nādhivāseyyāthāti yo tumhehi adhivāsetabbo na bhaveyyāti attho. No hetaṃ, bhanteti, bhante, anadhivāsetabbaṃ nāma vacanapathaṃ na passāmāti adhippāyo. Dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyāti iti bhagavā arahattena kūṭaṃ gaṇhanto yathānusandhinā desanaṃ niṭṭhapesīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Kakacūpamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
233. "Aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vā" means whether it is a small offense (appasāvajjaṃ) or a great offense (mahāsāvajjaṃ).

"Yaṃ tumhe nādhivāseyyāthā" means the meaning (attho) is that which should not be tolerated (adhivāsetabbo) by you (tumhehi), should not happen (na bhaveyya).

"No hetaṃ, bhante" means, O venerable one (bhante), the meaning (adhippāyo) is that we do not see (na passāmāti) a way of speaking (vacanapathaṃ) called (nāma) intolerable (anadhivāsetabbaṃ).

"Dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā" thus, the Blessed One (bhagavā), grasping (gaṇhanto) the peak (kūṭaṃ) through Arahantship (arahattena), completed (niṭṭhapesīti) the teaching (desanaṃ) in accordance with the connection (yathānusandhinā).

This is the end of the Commentary to the Kakacūpamasutta of the Majjhimanikāya in the Papañcasūdanī.

mula_pali:
234. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena ariṭṭhassa nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa gandhabādhipubbassa (ka.) evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – ‘‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’’ti. Assosuṃ kho sambahulā bhikkhū – ‘‘ariṭṭhassa kira nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’’’ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘saccaṃ kira te, āvuso ariṭṭha, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃbyākho evaṃ kho (?) bhagavato sammukhāyevassa ‘‘evaṃbyākho’’ti ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’’ti.

Atha kho tepi bhikkhū ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetukāmā samanuyuñjanti samanugāhanti samanuggāhanti (syā.) samanubhāsanti – ‘‘mā hevaṃ, āvuso ariṭṭha, avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi; na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ abbhācikkhanaṃ (ka.), na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyenāvuso ariṭṭha, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā,ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā…pe… maṃsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo’’ti. Evampi kho ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tehi bhikkhūhi samanuyuñjiyamāno samanugāhiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno (syā. vinayepi) samanubhāsiyamāno tadeva tatheva taṃ (vinaye) pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharati – ‘‘evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’’ti.

samanuggāhanti (syā.) abbhācikkhanaṃ (ka.) samanuggāhiyamāno (syā. vinayepi) tatheva taṃ (vinaye)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī) in the Jetavana (Jeta Grove) at Anāthapiṇḍika’s (Anathapindika’s) monastery.

At that time, a pernicious view had arisen in a monk named Ariṭṭha (Arishta), formerly of the vulture killers (gaddhabādhipubba), thus: “As I understand the Dharma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructions (*antarāyikā dharmā*) by the Blessed One are not able to obstruct one who engages in them.”

Several monks, having heard about this, [said:] “The monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, has such a pernicious view: ‘As I understand the Dharma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to obstruct one who engages in them.’”

Then these monks went to the monk Ariṭṭha; having gone there, they said to Ariṭṭha: “Is it true, friend Ariṭṭha, that such a pernicious view has arisen in you: ‘As I understand the Dharma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to obstruct one who engages in them’?”

“As I understand it, friend, the Dharma was taught by the Blessed One thus: ‘Those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to obstruct one who engages in them.’”

Then those monks, desiring to detach Ariṭṭha from that pernicious view, questioned and cross-questioned and remonstrated with him: “Do not say so, friend Ariṭṭha. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One; it is not right to misrepresent the Blessed One, and the Blessed One would not speak thus. In many discourses, friend Ariṭṭha, the Blessed One has stated that obstructive things are truly obstructive, and that they are able to obstruct one who engages in them. The Blessed One has stated that sensual pleasures provide little gratification, much suffering, and much despair, and that the danger in them is more. The Blessed One has stated that sensual pleasures are like a skeleton… like a piece of meat… like a grass torch… like a pit of coals… like a dream… like borrowed goods… like a tree laden with fruit… like a slaughterhouse… like a sword stake… similar to a snake’s head; they are much suffering and much trouble, and the danger in them is greater.”

Even so, the monk Ariṭṭha, being questioned and cross-questioned and remonstrated with by those monks, tenaciously clung to that same pernicious view, insisted upon it, and said: “As I understand it, friend, the Dharma was taught by the Blessed One thus: ‘Those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to obstruct one who engages in them.’”
commentary_pali:
234.Evaṃme sutanti alagaddūpamasuttaṃ. Tattha gaddhe bādhayiṃsūti gaddhabādhino, gaddhabādhino pubbapurisā assāti gaddhabādhipubbo, tassa gaddhabādhipubbassa, gijjhaghātakakulappasutassāti attho. Saggamokkhānaṃ antarāyaṃ karontīti antarāyikā. Te kammakilesavipākaupavādaāṇāvītikkamavasena pañcavidhā. Tattha pañcānantariyadhammā kammantarāyikā nāma. Tathā bhikkhunīdūsakakammaṃ, taṃ pana mokkhasseva antarāyaṃ karoti, na saggassa. Niyatamicchādiṭṭhidhammā kilesantarāyikā nāma. Paṇḍakatiracchānagataubhatobyañjanakānaṃ paṭisandhidhammā vipākantarāyikā nāma. Ariyūpavādadhammā upavādantarāyikā nāma, te pana yāva ariye na khamāpenti, tāvadeva, na tato paraṃ. Sañcicca vītikkantā satta āpattikkhandhā āṇāvītikkamantarāyikā nāma. Tepi yāva bhikkhubhāvaṃ vā paṭijānāti, na vuṭṭhāti vā, na deseti vā, tāvadeva, na tato paraṃ.

Tatrāyaṃ bhikkhu bahussuto dhammakathiko sesantarāyike jānāti, vinaye pana akovidattā paṇṇattivītikkamantarāyike na jānāti, tasmā rahogato evaṃ cintesi – ime āgārikā pañca kāmaguṇe paribhuñjantā sotāpannāpi sakadāgāminopi anāgāminopi honti. Bhikkhūpi manāpikāni cakkhuviññeyyāni rūpāni passanti…pe… kāyaviññeyye phoṭṭhabbe phusanti, mudukāni attharaṇapāvuraṇādīni paribhuñjanti, etaṃ sabbaṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā itthīnaṃyeva rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbā na vaṭṭanti? Etepi vaṭṭantīti. Evaṃ rasena rasaṃ saṃsandetvā sacchandarāgaparibhogañca nicchandarāgaparibhogañca ekaṃ katvā thūlavākehi saddhiṃ atisukhumasuttaṃ upanento viya, sāsapena saddhiṃ sineruṃ upasaṃharanto viya, pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppādetvā, ‘‘kiṃ bhagavatā mahāsamuddaṃ bandhantena viya mahatā ussāhena paṭhamapārājikaṃ paññattaṃ, natthi ettha doso’’ti sabbaññutaññāṇena saddhiṃ paṭivirujjhanto vesārajjañāṇaṃ paṭibāhanto ariyamagge khāṇukaṇṭakādīni pakkhipanto methunadhamme doso natthīti jinassa āṇācakke pahāraṃ adāsi. Tenāha – ‘‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmī’’tiādi.

Evaṃbyā khoti evaṃ viya kho. Samanuyuñjantītiādīsu kiṃ laddhiko tvaṃ, laddhiṃ vadehīti pucchamānā samanuyuñjanti nāma. Diṭṭhiṃ patiṭṭhāpentā samanuggāhanti nāma. Kena kāraṇena evaṃ vadasīti kāraṇaṃ pucchantā samanubhāsanti nāma. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamātiādīsu (ma. ni. 2.42-48) aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā appassādaṭṭhena. Maṃsapesūpamā bahusādhāraṇaṭṭhena. Tiṇukkūpamā anudahanaṭṭhena. Aṅgārakāsūpamā mahābhitāpanaṭṭhena. Supinakūpamā ittarapaccupaṭṭhānaṭṭhena. Yācitakūpamā tāvakālikaṭṭhena. Rukkhaphalūpamā sabbaṅgapaccaṅgapalibhañjanaṭṭhena. Asisūnūpamā adhikuṭṭanaṭṭhena. Sattisūlūpamā vinivijjhanaṭṭhena. Sappasirūpamā sāsaṅkasappaṭibhayaṭṭhena. Thāmasāti diṭṭhithāmena. Parāmāsāti diṭṭhiparāmāsena. Abhinivissa voharatīti adhiṭṭhahitvā voharati dīpeti vā.

byā kho Samanuyuñjantī Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā Maṃsapesūpamā Tiṇukkūpamā Aṅgārakāsūpamā Supinakūpamā Yācitakūpamā Rukkhaphalūpamā Asisūnūpamā Sattisūlūpamā Sappasirūpamā Thāmasā Parāmāsā Abhinivissa voharatī
commentary_english:
234. It is like this: "Thus I have heard," namely, the Alagaddūpama-sutta.

There, "those who oppress desires" are called *gaddhabādhino*; *gaddhabādhipubbo* [means] the ancestors of the *gaddhabādhino*; this means "born in a family of vulture-killers."

"Those that make intervention in heaven and liberation" are called *antarāyikā* (obstructive things).

These are fivefold by way of action, defilement, result, disparagement, command, and transgression.

There, the five deeds bringing immediate retribution are called action-obstructive things (*kammantarāyikā*).

Likewise, the act of defiling a *bhikkhunī* (nun) only causes obstruction to liberation (*mokkha*), not to heaven (*sagga*).

Determined wrong views are called defilement-obstructive things (*kilesantarāyikā*).

The rebirth-dharmas of hermaphrodites, animals, and the ambisexual are called result-obstructive things (*vipākantarāyikā*).

The dharmas of disparaging noble ones (*ariyūpavādadhammā*) are called disparagement-obstructive things (*upavādantarāyikā*); however, they [are obstructive] only until they ask forgiveness from the noble ones; not beyond that.

The seven intentional transgressions of the aggregates of offenses (*āpattikkhandhā*) are called command-transgression-obstructive things (*āṇāvītikkamantarāyikā*).

Likewise, they [are obstructive] only until he acknowledges the state of being a *bhikkhu*, or until he departs [from the order], or until he confesses; not beyond that.

There, this *bhikkhu*, being very learned and a speaker of the Dharma, knows the remaining obstructive things; however, because of his lack of skill in the *Vinaya*, he does not know the obstructive things related to the transgression of the precepts. Therefore, being alone, he thought thus: "These householders, while enjoying the five sense qualities, are stream-enterers (*sotāpanna*), once-returners (*sakadāgāmin*), and non-returners (*anāgāmin*)."

"Even *bhikkhus* see forms cognizable by the eye that are pleasing…pe… they touch tangible objects cognizable by the body, they enjoy soft things, such as spreads and blankets, etc.; all this is permissible."

"Why are forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tactile objects not permissible only for women? These too are permissible," thus [he thinks].

Thus, mixing taste with taste, making enjoyment with desire and passion and enjoyment without desire and passion one, as if bringing a very fine thread together with coarse ropes, as if comparing Mount Sineru with a mustard seed, having produced a wicked view, and opposing the all-knowing wisdom, saying, "Why did the Blessed One prescribe the first expulsion offense (*paṭhamapārājikaṃ*) with great effort, as if binding the great ocean; there is no fault in this," rejecting the wisdom of self-confidence, throwing sticks and thorns, etc., on the noble path, he gave a blow to the wheel of the command of the Conqueror [by saying] "there is no fault in sexual intercourse."

Therefore, he said: "As I understand the Dharma taught by the Blessed One," etc.

"Just as," namely, like that.

"Questioning," etc., [means] asking, "What is your view, declare your view," those who question are called those who interrogate (*samanuyuñjantī*).

Those who establish a view are called those who support (*samanuggāhanti*).

Those who ask for a reason, [saying] "For what reason do you say this?" are called those who explain (*samanubhāsanti*).

"Like a skeleton," etc. (M. Ni. 2.42-48) "like a skeleton" [is to be understood] in the sense of little satisfaction.

"Like a lump of flesh" [is to be understood] in the sense of being much shared.

"Like a grass torch" [is to be understood] in the sense of not being burned.

"Like a pit of embers" [is to be understood] in the sense of great torment.

"Like a dream" [is to be understood] in the sense of momentary presence.

"Like something borrowed" [is to be understood] in the sense of being temporary.

"Like the fruit of a tree" [is to be understood] in the sense of causing the destruction of all limbs, great and small.

"Like a butcher's knife" [is to be understood] in the sense of excessive cutting.

"Like a spear or trident" [is to be understood] in the sense of piercing through.

"Like the head of a snake" [is to be understood] in the sense of a dangerous and frightening snake.
*thāmasā* means with tenacity of views (*dṛṣṭi-thāmena*).

*parāmāsā* means with adherence to views (*dṛṣṭi-parāmāsena*).

*abhinivissa voharatī* means he speaks having determined, or it means he reveals.

"By which, while cross-examining, [they are like] a skeleton (*aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā*), a lump of flesh (*maṃsapesūpamā*), a torch of grass (*tiṇukkūpamā*), a pit of embers (*aṅgārakāsūpamā*), a dream (*supinakūpamā*), a loan (*yācitakūpamā*), tree fruits (*rukkhaphalūpamā*), a sword and ploughshare (*asisūnūpamā*), a stake (*sattisūlūpamā*), the head of a snake (*sappasirūpamā*), with tenacity of views (*thāmasā*), with adherence to views (*parāmāsā*), he speaks having determined."

mula_pali:
235. Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṃ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ariṭṭhassa nāma, bhante, bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti. Assumha kho mayaṃ, bhante – ‘ariṭṭhassa kira nāma bhikkhuno gaddhabādhipubbassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yena ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etadavocumha – ‘saccaṃ kira te, āvuso ariṭṭha, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, bhante, ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo amhe etadavoca – ‘evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetukāmā samanuyuñjimha samanugāhimha samanubhāsimha – ‘mā hevaṃ, āvuso ariṭṭha, avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi; na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ , na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyenāvuso ariṭṭha, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā…pe… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo’ti. Evampi kho, bhante, ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo amhehi samanuyuñjiyamāno samanugāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno tadeva pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharati – ‘evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’ti. Yato kho mayaṃ, bhante, nāsakkhimha ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṃ, atha mayaṃ etamatthaṃ bhagavato ārocemā’’ti.
mula_english:
235. Since the *bhikkhus* were unable to detach the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubba*), from that pernicious view (*pāpakā diṭṭhigatā*), they went to the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), and after paying homage to him (*bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā*), they sat down at one side (*ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu*).

Seated to one side, the *bhikkhus* told the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ*): “Venerable sir (*bhante*), such a pernicious view (*pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ*) has arisen in the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbassa*): ‘As I understand the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā desitaṃ*), those things called obstructions (*antarāyikā dhammā*) by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) are not able to obstruct one who engages in them (*te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā*)’."

We have heard, venerable sir (*bhante*): “Such a pernicious view (*pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ*) has arisen in the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbassa*): ‘As I understand the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā desitaṃ*), those things called obstructions (*antarāyikā dhammā*) by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) are not able to obstruct one who engages in them (*te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā*)’."

Then, venerable sir (*bhante*), we went to the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbo*), and said to the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbaṃ*): “Is it true, friend Ariṭṭha (*āvuso ariṭṭha*), that such a pernicious view (*pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ*) has arisen in you: ‘As I understand the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā desitaṃ*), those things called obstructions (*antarāyikā dhammā*) by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) are not able to obstruct one who engages in them (*te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā*)’?”

When this was said, venerable sir (*bhante*), the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbo*), said to us: “As I understand the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā desitaṃ*), those things called obstructions (*antarāyikā dhammā*) by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) are not able to obstruct one who engages in them (*te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā*).”

Then, venerable sir (*bhante*), wishing to detach the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbaṃ*), from this pernicious view (*pāpakā diṭṭhigatā*), we questioned him, pressed him, and reasoned with him: “Don’t say that, friend Ariṭṭha (*āvuso ariṭṭha*), don’t misrepresent the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi*); for it’s not right to misrepresent the Blessed One (*bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ*), and the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) would never say such a thing (*evaṃ vadeyya*). In many ways, friend Ariṭṭha (*anekapariyāyenāvuso ariṭṭha*), the obstructive things (*antarāyikā dhammā*) have been described as obstructive (*antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā*) by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*), and they are indeed able to obstruct one who engages in them (*alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya*). The Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) has said that sensual pleasures (*kāmā*) provide little gratification (*appassādā*), much suffering (*bahudukkhā*), and much despair (*bahupāyāsā*), and how great is the danger (*ādīnavo*) in them (*ettha bhiyyo*). The Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) has said that sensual pleasures (*kāmā*) are like a skeleton (*aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā*)…like a snake’s head (*sappasirūpamā*), providing much suffering (*bahudukkhā*) and much despair (*bahupāyāsā*), and how great is the danger (*ādīnavo*) in them (*ettha bhiyyo*)’ti.”

Even when we questioned, pressed, and reasoned with him in this way, venerable sir (*bhante*), the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbo*), continued to insist, holding firmly to that same pernicious view (*pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ*): “As I understand the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā desitaṃ*), those things called obstructions (*antarāyikā dhammā*) by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) are not able to obstruct one who engages in them (*te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā*).”

Since we were unable, venerable sir (*bhante*), to detach the *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers (*gaddhabādhipubbaṃ*), from this pernicious view (*pāpakā diṭṭhigatā*), we have reported this matter to the Blessed One (*bhagavato ārocemā’’ti*).”
commentary_pali: 235.Yato kho te bhikkhūti yadā te bhikkhū. Evaṃbyā kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatāti idaṃ esa attano ajjhāsayena natthīti vattukāmopi bhagavato ānubhāvena sampaṭicchati, buddhānaṃ kira sammukhā dve kathā kathetuṃ samattho nāma natthi.
commentary_english:
235.
"Because those *bhikkhus*," means when those *bhikkhus*.
"Thus, I, O *bhante*, by the Blessed One," this, even though wishing to say it is not according to his own intention, he accepts it through the power of the Blessed One; indeed, there is no one who is capable of uttering two words in the presence of the Buddhas.

mula_pali:
236. Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ āmantehi – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso ariṭṭha, āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā, yena ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘satthā taṃ, āvuso ariṭṭha, āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘saccaṃ kira te, ariṭṭha, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃbyākho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi – ‘yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā te paṭisevato nālaṃ antarāyāyā’’’ti. ‘‘Kassa kho nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi? Nanu mayā, moghapurisa, anekapariyāyena antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā? Alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā mayā, bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… maṃsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā, bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Atha ca pana tvaṃ, moghapurisa, attanā duggahitena amhe ceva abbhācikkhasi, attānañca khanasi, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavasi. Tañhi te, moghapurisa, bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’’ti.

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nāyaṃ ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo usmīkatopi imasmiṃ dhammavinaye’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi kiṃti (ka.) siyā, bhante; no hetaṃ, bhante’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno nisīdi. Atha kho bhagavā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ maṅkubhūtaṃ pattakkhandhaṃ adhomukhaṃ pajjhāyantaṃ appaṭibhānaṃ viditvā ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘paññāyissasi kho tvaṃ, moghapurisa, etena sakena pāpakena diṭṭhigatena. Idhāhaṃ bhikkhū paṭipucchissāmī’’ti.

kiṃti (ka.)
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk, saying: "Come, monk, tell the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, in my name that the Teacher calls him."

"Good, venerable sir," that monk replied to the Blessed One, and he went to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers; after going, he said to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers: "The Teacher calls you, friend Ariṭṭha."

"Very good, friend," replied the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, to that monk, and he went to the Blessed One; after going to the Blessed One, he bowed and sat down at one side.

The Blessed One then said to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, who was sitting at one side: "Ariṭṭha, is it true that such a pernicious view has arisen in you: 'As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to obstruct one who engages in them'?"

"That is how I understand the Dhamma as it has been taught by the Blessed One, venerable sir: 'As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to obstruct one who engages in them.'"

"From whom, misguided man, do you understand the Dhamma to have been taught thus by me? Have I not, misguided man, in many ways stated that obstructing things are obstructing? And indeed, they are sufficient to obstruct one who engages in them.

I have stated that sensual pleasures offer little gratification, much suffering, and much trouble, and that the danger in them is greater.

I have stated that sensual pleasures are like a skeleton… like a lump of flesh… like a grass torch… like a pit of coals… like a dream… like borrowed goods… like a tree laden with fruit… like a slaughterhouse… like a sword stake… like a snake’s head, [offering] much suffering, much trouble, and the danger in them is greater.

And yet, misguided man, by your own wrong grasp, you misrepresent me, injure yourself, and accumulate much demerit.

Indeed, misguided man, that will lead to your long-lasting harm and suffering."

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: "What do you think, monks, has this monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, kindled even a spark of wisdom in this Dhamma and Discipline?" "How could he, venerable sir; no, venerable sir."

When this was said, the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, sat silent, dismayed, with shoulders drooping and head down, glum, and without response.

Then, knowing that the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, was silent, dismayed, with shoulders drooping and head down, glum, and without response, the Blessed One said to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers: "Misguided man, you will be known by this, your own pernicious view.

Here I shall question the monks about this."
commentary_pali:
236.Kassa kho nāma tvaṃ moghapurisāti tvaṃ moghapurisa kassa khattiyassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā vessassa vā suddassa vā gahaṭṭhassa vā pabbajitassa vā devassa vā manussassa vā mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesīti ayaṃ pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Ariṭṭho kira cintesi – ‘‘bhagavā maṃ moghapurisoti vadati, na kho pana moghapurisāti vuttamattakena maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo na hoti. Upasenampi hi vaṅgantaputtaṃ, ‘atilahuṃ kho tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bāhullāya āvatto’ti (mahāva. 75) bhagavā moghapurisavādena ovadi. Thero aparabhāge ghaṭento vāyamanto cha abhiññā sacchākāsi. Ahampi tathārūpaṃ vīriyaṃ paggaṇhitvā maggaphalāni nibbattessāmī’’ti. Athassa bhagavā bandhanā pavuttassa paṇḍupalāsassa viya aviruḷhibhāvaṃ dassento imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Usmīkatopīti , bhikkhave, tumhe kinti maññatha, ayaṃ ariṭṭho evaṃladdhiko sabbaññutaññāṇena paṭivirujjhitvā vesārajjañāṇaṃ paṭibāhitvā tathāgatassa āṇācakke pahāraṃ dadamāno api nu imasmiṃ dhammavinaye usmīkatopi? Yathā nibbutepi mahante aggikkhandhe khajjupanakamattāpi aggipapaṭikā hotiyeva, yaṃ nissāya puna mahāaggikkhandho bhaveyya. Kiṃ nu kho evaṃ imassa appamattikāpi ñāṇusmā atthi, yaṃ nissāya vāyamanto maggaphalāni nibbatteyyāti? No hetaṃ, bhanteti, bhante, evaṃladdhikassa kuto evarūpā ñāṇusmāti? Maggaphalānaṃ paccayasamatthāya ñāṇusmāya usmīkatabhāvaṃ paṭikkhipantā vadanti. Maṅkubhūtoti nittejabhūto. Pattakkhandhoti patitakkhandho. Appaṭibhānoti kiñci paṭibhānaṃ apassanto bhinnapaṭibhāno evarūpampi nāma niyyānikasāsanaṃ labhitvā aviruḷhidhammo kiramhi samugghātitapaccayo jātoti attano abhabbataṃ paccavekkhanto pādaṅguṭṭhakena bhūmiṃ khaṇamāno nisīdi.

Usmīkatopī No hetaṃ, bhante Maṅkubhūto Pattakkhandho Appaṭibhāno

Paññāyissasikhoti ayampi pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Ariṭṭho kira cintesi – ‘‘bhagavā mayhaṃ maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo pacchinnoti vadati, na kho pana buddhā saupanissayānaṃyeva dhammaṃ desenti, anupanissayānampi desenti, ahaṃ satthu santikā sugatovādaṃ labhitvā attano sampattūpagaṃ kusalaṃ karissāmī’’ti. Athassa bhagavā ovādaṃ paṭipassambhento ‘‘paññāyissasī’’tiādimāha. Tassattho, tvaṃyeva, moghapurisa, iminā pāpakena diṭṭhigatena nirayādīsu paññāyissasi, mama santikā tuyhaṃ sugatovādo nāma natthi, na me tayā attho, idhāhaṃ bhikkhū paṭipucchissāmīti.

Paññāyissasi kho
commentary_english:
236. "To whom, you foolish man?" means, you foolish man, to whom—whether a kṣatriya, a brāhmaṇa, a vaiśya, a śūdra, a householder, a renunciant, a deva, or a human—do you understand that I have taught the Dharma in this way?

"Then the Bhagavān addressed the bhiksus" means this is a distinct connection.

Ariṣṭha apparently thought: "The Bhagavān calls me a foolish man, but just by being called a foolish man, the support for the paths and fruits is not eliminated. The Bhagavān also advised Upasena Vaṅgantaputta, 'You are too quick, foolish man, to be swayed by abundance' (Mahāva. 75) with the words 'foolish man.' The Elder, striving and exerting himself in the latter part [of his life], realized the six superknowledges. I too, having roused such energy, will produce the paths and fruits."

Then, showing him the state of non-growth, like a dry leaf fallen from its bond, the Bhagavān began this teaching.

"Would he still be smoldering?" O monks, what do you think? Would this Ariṣṭha, having acquired such a view, opposing the knowledge of omniscience, rejecting the knowledge of confidence, striking the wheel of the Tathāgata's command, still be smoldering in this Dharma-vinaya? Just as even in a great extinguished fire, there is still a spark the size of a sesame cake, which could cause a great fire to arise again. Does he have even this small spark of knowledge, that he could produce the paths and fruits by striving? "No, venerable sir," they say, rejecting the state of smoldering of knowledge capable of supporting the paths and fruits, [saying] "where could such a spark of knowledge be in one who has acquired such a view?"

"Having become crestfallen" means having become devoid of energy.

"A heap of fallen leaves" means a heap of fallen leaves.

"Without inspiration" means not seeing any inspiration, having broken inspiration. Having obtained such a teaching that leads out [of suffering], he sat down, digging the ground with his toe, reflecting on his own inability, [thinking] "I am one whose Dhamma does not grow, because I have become one whose support has been uprooted."

"Would he still be smoldering?" "No, venerable sir." "Having become crestfallen," "a heap of fallen leaves," "without inspiration."

"You will be known" is also a distinct connection.

Ariṣṭha apparently thought: "The Bhagavān says that the support for my paths and fruits is cut off, but the Buddhas teach the Dharma to those with and without support. Having received the Sugata's advice from the Teacher, I will do skillful deeds that lead to my attainment."

Then, the Bhagavān, thwarting his advice, said, "You will be known," etc.

Its meaning is: You yourself, foolish man, will be known in hells and other places because of this evil wrong view. There is no Sugata's advice for you from me. I have no use for you. Here I will question the monks.

mula_pali: 237. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘tumhepi me, bhikkhave , evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha yathāyaṃ ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo attanā duggahitena amhe ceva abbhācikkhati, attānañca khanati, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavatī’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante. Anekapariyāyena hi no, bhante, antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā; alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā…pe… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā , ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave, sādhu, kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha. Anekapariyāyena hi kho, bhikkhave, antarāyikā dhammā vuttā mayā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāya. Appassādā kāmā vuttā mayā , bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā…pe… sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā mayā, bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Atha ca panāyaṃ ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo attanā duggahitena amhe ceva abbhācikkhati, attānañca khanati, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavati. Tañhi tassa moghapurisassa bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. So vata, bhikkhave, aññatreva kāmehi aññatra kāmasaññāya aññatra kāmavitakkehi kāme paṭisevissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’’.
mula_english:
237. Then the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: “*Bhikkhus*, do you understand the *Dhamma* taught by me as this *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, does when he misrepresents us by his wrong grasp and injures himself and stores up much demerit?”

“No, venerable sir.”

For in many discourses, venerable sir, the Blessed One has stated how obstructive things (*antarāyika dharmā*) are obstructions, and how they are able to obstruct one who engages in them. The Blessed One has stated how sensual pleasures (*kāmā*) provide little gratification (*appassādā*), much suffering (*bahudukkhā*), and much despair (*bahupāyāsā*), and how great is the danger (*ādīnava*) in them. With the simile of the skeleton (*aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā*)… with the simile of the snake’s head (*sappasirūpamā*), the Blessed One has stated… how great is the danger in them.

“Good, good, *bhikkhus*! It is good that you understand the *Dhamma* taught by me in such a way. For in many discourses, *bhikkhus*, I have stated how obstructive things are obstructions, and how they are able to obstruct one who engages in them. I have said that there is little enjoyment in worldly pleasures (*kāmā*), but much suffering (*bahudukkhā*) and much trouble (*bahupāyāsā*), and that the danger (*ādīnava*) in them is greater. With the simile of the skeleton (*aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā*)… with the simile of the snake’s head (*sappasirūpamā*), I have stated how sensual pleasures provide little gratification, much suffering, and much despair, and how great is the danger in them. But this *bhikkhu* Ariṭṭha, formerly of the vulture killers, misrepresents us by his wrong grasp and injures himself and stores up much demerit; for this will lead to this misguided man’s harm and suffering for a long time.
