Katthaci pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅganti. Katthaci paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhīti . Katthaci tammayatāpariyādānanti. Katthaci tīhi nāmehi. Katthaci dvīhīti.

Tattha poṭṭhapādasutte tāva ‘‘saññā kho, poṭṭhapāda, paṭhamaṃ uppajjati, pacchā ñāṇa’’nti (dī. ni. 1.416) evaṃ saññagganti vuttā. Susimasutte ‘‘pubbe kho, susima, dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ , pacchā nibbāne ñāṇa’’nti (saṃ. ni. 2.70) evaṃ dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇanti vuttā. Dasuttarasutte ‘‘paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhipadhāniyaṅga’’nti (dī. ni. 3.359) evaṃ pārisuddhipadāniyaṅganti vuttā. Rathavinīte ‘‘kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.257) evaṃ paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhīti vuttā. Saḷāyatanavibhaṅge ‘‘atammayataṃ, bhikkhave, nissāya atammayataṃ āgamma yāyaṃ upekkhā nānattā nānattasitā, taṃ abhinivajjetvā yāyaṃ upekkhā ekattā ekattasitā, taṃ nissāya taṃ āgamma evametissā pahānaṃ hoti, evametissā samatikkamo hotī’’ti (dī. ni. 3.310) evaṃ tammayatāpariyādānanti vuttā. Paṭisambhidāmagge ‘‘yā ca muñcitukamyatā, yā ca paṭisaṅkhānupassanā, yā ca saṅkhārupekkhā, ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nāna’’nti (paṭi. ma. 1.54) evaṃ tīhi nāmehi vuttā. Paṭṭhāne ‘‘anulomaṃ gotrabhussa anantarapaccayena paccayo, anulomaṃ vodānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo’’ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.417) evaṃ dvīhi nāmehi vuttā. Imasmiṃ pana alagaddasutte nibbindatīti nibbidānāmena āgatā.

poṭṭhapādasutte saññagga Susimasutte dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇa Dasuttarasutte pārisuddhipadāniyaṅga Rathavinīte paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhī Saḷāyatanavibhaṅge tammayatāpariyādāna Paṭisambhidāmagge Paṭṭhāne

Nibbidā virajjatīti ettha virāgoti maggo virāgā vimuccatīti ettha virāgena maggena vimuccatīti phalaṃ kathitaṃ. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hotīti idha paccavekkhaṇā kathitā.

Nibbidā virajjatī virāgo virāgā vimuccatī Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hotī

Evaṃ vimuttacittaṃ mahākhīṇāsavaṃ dassetvā idāni tassa yathābhūtehi pañcahi kāraṇehi nāmaṃ gaṇhanto ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Avijjāti vaṭṭamūlikā avijjā. Ayañhi durukkhipanaṭṭhena palighoti vuccati. Tenesa tassa ukkhittattā ukkhittapalighoti vutto. Tālāvatthukatāti sīsacchinnatālo viya katā, samūlaṃ vā tālaṃ uddharitvā tālassa vatthu viya katā, yathā tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ puna so tālo na paññāyati, evaṃ puna apaññattibhāvaṃ nītāti attho. Ponobbhavikoti punabbhavadāyako. Jātisaṃsārotiādīsu jāyanavasena ceva saṃsaraṇavasena ca evaṃ laddhanāmānaṃ punabbhavakhandhānaṃ paccayo kammābhisaṅkhāro. So hi punappunaṃ uppattikaraṇavasena parikkhipitvā ṭhitattā parikkhāti vuccati, tenesa tassā saṃkiṇṇattā vikiṇṇattā saṃkiṇṇaparikkhoti vutto. Taṇhāti vaṭṭamūlikā taṇhā. Ayañhi gambhīrānugataṭṭhena esikāti vuccati. Tenesa tassā abbūḷhattā luñcitvā chaḍḍitattā abbūḷhesikoti vutto. Orambhāgiyānīti oraṃ bhajanakāni kāmabhave upapattipaccayāni. Etāni hi kavāṭaṃ viya nagaradvāraṃ cittaṃ pidahitvā ṭhitattā aggaḷāti vuccanti. Tenesa tesaṃ nirākatattā bhinnattā niraggaḷoti vutto. Ariyoti nikkileso parisuddho. Pannaddhajoti patitamānaddhajo. Pannabhāroti khandhabhārakilesabhāraabhisaṅkhārabhārapañcakāmaguṇabhārā pannā orohitā assāti pannabhāro. Apica idha mānabhārasseva oropitattā pannabhāroti adhippeto. Visaṃyuttoti catūhi yogehi sabbakilesehi ca visaṃyutto. Idha pana mānasaṃyogeneva visaṃyuttattā visaṃyuttoti adhippeto. Asmimānoti rūpe asmīti māno, vedanāya… saññāya… saṅkhāresu… viññāṇe asmīti māno.

ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave Avijjā paligho ukkhittapaligho Tālāvatthukatā Ponobbhaviko Jātisaṃsāro parikkhā saṃkiṇṇaparikkho Taṇhā esikā abbūḷhesiko Orambhāgiyānī aggaḷā niraggaḷo Ariyo Pannaddhajo Pannabhāro pannabhāro Visaṃyutto Asmimāno

Ettāvatā bhagavatā maggena kilese khepetvā nirodhasayanavaragatassa nibbānārammaṇaṃ phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā viharato khīṇāsavassa kālo dassito. Yathā hi dve nagarāni ekaṃ coranagaraṃ, ekaṃ khemanagaraṃ. Atha ekassa mahāyodhassa evaṃ bhaveyya – ‘‘yāvimaṃ coranagaraṃ tiṭṭhati, tāva khemanagaraṃ bhayato na muccati, coranagaraṃ anagaraṃ karissāmī’’ti sannāhaṃ katvā khaggaṃ gahetvā coranagaraṃ upasaṅkamitvā nagaradvāre ussāpite esikatthambhe khaggena chinditvā sadvārabāhakaṃ kavāṭaṃ chinditvā palighaṃ ukkhipitvā pākāraṃ bhindanto parikkhaṃ saṃkiritvā nagarasobhanatthāya ussite dhaje pātetvā nagaraṃ agginā jhāpetvā khemanagaraṃ pavisitvā pāsādaṃ abhiruyha ñātigaṇaparivuto surasabhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya, evaṃ coranagaraṃ viya sakkāyo, khemanagaraṃ viya nibbānaṃ, mahāyodho viya yogāvacaro. Tassevaṃ hoti, ‘‘yāva sakkāyavaṭṭaṃ vattati, tāva dvattiṃsakammakāraṇaaṭṭhanavutirogapañcavīsatimahābhayehi parimuccanaṃ natthī’’ti. So mahāyodho viya sannāhaṃ sīlasannāhaṃ katvā, paññākhaggaṃ gahetvā khaggena esikatthambhe viya arahattamaggena taṇhesikaṃ luñcitvā, so yodho sadvārabāhakaṃ nagarakavāṭaṃ viya pañcorambhāgiyasaṃyojanaggaḷaṃ ugghāṭetvā, so yodho palighaṃ viya, avijjāpalighaṃ ukkhipitvā , so yodho pākāraṃ bhindanto parikkhaṃ viya kammābhisaṅkhāraṃ bhindanto jātisaṃsāraparikkhaṃ saṃkiritvā, so yodho nagarasobhanatthāya ussāpite dhaje viya mānaddhaje pātetvā sakkāyanagaraṃ jhāpetvā, so yodho khemanagare uparipāsāde surasabhojanaṃ viya kilesanibbānaṃ nagaraṃ pavisitvā amatanirodhārammaṇaṃ phalasamāpattisukhaṃ anubhavamāno kālaṃ vītināmeti.
commentary_english:
"One is disgusted" means one feels revulsion. Here, *nibbidā* is understood as the discernment leading to detachment. For discernment leading to detachment has many names. Sometimes it is called the cessation of perception (*saññagganti*). Sometimes it is called the knowledge of the stability of the law (*dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇanti*). Sometimes it is called a factor conducive to perfect purity (*pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅganti*). Sometimes it is called the purity of knowledge and vision regarding the path (*paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhīti*). Sometimes it is called the relinquishment of identification (*tammayatāpariyādānanti*). Sometimes it is called by three names. Sometimes by two. There, in the *Poṭṭhapāda Sutta*, it is stated thus, "Perception, Poṭṭhapāda, arises first, and knowledge later" (*saññagga*). In the *Susima Sutta*, it is stated thus, "First, Susima, comes the knowledge of the stability of the law, and later knowledge of nirvāṇa" (*dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇa*). In the *Dasuttara Sutta*, it is stated thus, "A factor conducive to the purity of knowledge and vision regarding the path" (*pārisuddhipadāniyaṅga*). In the *Rathavinīta*, it is stated thus, "Is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of the purity of knowledge and vision regarding the path?" (*paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhī*). In the *Saḷāyatanavibhaṅga*, it is stated thus, "Having relied on non-identification, having come to non-identification, whatever equanimity there is, based on diversity, supported by diversity, having abandoned that, whatever equanimity there is, based on unity, supported by unity, thus there is abandonment of this, thus there is overcoming of this" (*tammayatāpariyādāna*). In the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, it is stated thus, "And the desire for deliverance, and contemplation of reflection, and equanimity about formations: these things are one in meaning and only the letter is different" (*tīhi nāmehi*). In the *Paṭṭhāna*, "Proximity-condition by means of the immediately following condition to the fruition of change of lineage, proximity-condition by means of the immediately following condition to the fruition of emergence" (*anulomaṃ gotrabhussa anantarapaccayena paccayo, anulomaṃ vodānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo*). 1. 417. Thus it is said by two names. In this *Alagadda Sutta*, it comes with the name *nibbidā* because it causes disgust. Poṭṭhapādasutte Saññagga Susimasutte Dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇa Dasuttarasutte Pārisuddhipadāniyaṅga Rathavinīte Paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhī Saḷāyatanavibhaṅge Tammayatāpariyādāna Paṭisambhidāmagge Paṭṭhāne

“Disgust fades away,” here, *virāga* is the path. “From fading away, one is liberated,” here, the fruit is spoken of as being liberated through the path of fading away. The knowledge that "in liberation, there is liberation" is called retrospection here.

Nibbidā Virajjati Virāgo Virāgā Vimuccati Vimuttasmiṃ Vimuttamiti Ñāṇaṃ Hotī

Having shown the liberated mind to be a great one who has destroyed the āsavas, now, while taking the name with five reasons that are in accordance with reality, he says, “This is called, oh monastics.” *Avijjā* means ignorance is the root of the cycle [of rebirths]. This is called a bar ( *paligha*) because of the meaning of difficult removal. Because of its being raised, it is said to be a raised bar (*ukkhittapaligho*). *Tālāvatthukatā* means made like a palmyra tree with its head cut off, or having uprooted the palmyra tree with its root, it is made like the base of the palmyra tree. Just as that palmyra tree is not known again in that base, likewise, the meaning is that it is led to a state of non-manifestation again. *Ponobbhaviko* means giving rise to renewed existence (*punarbhava*). *Jātisaṃsāro* etc., the karmic formations are the cause/condition for the aggregates of renewed existence (*punabbhavakhandha*), which have thus obtained their names due to the characteristic of birth (*jāyana*) and due to the characteristic of transmigration (*saṃsaraṇa*). Because it repeatedly surrounds and remains by way of being the cause of arising, it is called *parikkhā*. Because of its being mixed and scattered, it is called *saṃkiṇṇaparikkho*. *Taṇhā* means craving is the root of the cycle [of rebirths]. This is called a pillar (*esikā*) because of the meaning of being profoundly ingrained. Because of its eradicated nature, having plucked and discarded, it is said to be *abbūḷhesiko*. *Orambhāgiyānī* means things that partake of what is lower, are causes/conditions for rebirth in the realm of desire (*kāmabhava*). These are called bolts (*aggaḷā*) because, like the leaf of a door, they block the mind, which is like the city gate, and remain. Because of their being warded off and broken, it is said to be free from bolts (*niraggaḷo*). *Ariyo* means without defilements (*nikkileso*), completely pure (*parisuddho*). *Pannaddhajo* means one whose flag of pride is fallen (*patitamānaddhajo*). *Pannabhāro* means one who has laid down the burdens: the burden of the aggregates ( *khandhabhāra*), the burden of the defilements (*kilesabhāra*), the burden of karmic formations (*abhisaṅkhārabhāra*), and the burden of the five strands of sense desire (*pañcakāmaguṇabhāra*) are laid down, relinquished by him; therefore, he is *pannabhāro*. Moreover, here, *pannabhāro* is intended to mean that it is precisely the burden of conceit (*mānabhārasseva*) that is relinquished. *Visaṃyutto* means one who is detached from the four yokes and from all the defilements. Here, however, *visaṃyutto* is intended to mean one who is detached precisely from the yoke of conceit (*mānasaṃyogeneva*). *Asmimāno* means, "I am" in the form (*rūpe*) is conceit; "I am" in feeling (*vedanāya*)… in perception (*saññāya*)… in formations (*saṅkhāresu*)… "I am" in consciousness (*viññāṇe*) is conceit. This is called, oh monastics: ignorance (*avijjā*), a bar (*paligho*), a raised bar (*ukkhittapaligho*), having a base like a palmyra tree (*tālāvatthukatā*), giving rise to renewed existence (*ponobbhaviko*), the cycle of existence (*jātisaṃsāro*), surrounding (*parikkhā*), completely mixed up in surrounding (*saṃkiṇṇaparikkho*), craving (*taṇhā*), a pillar (*esikā*), thoroughly eradicated (*abbūḷhesiko*), partaking of what is lower (*orambhāgiyānī*), bolts (*aggaḷā*), free from bolts (*niraggaḷo*), noble (*ariyo*), one whose flag is lowered (*pannaddhajo*), one who has laid down the burden (*pannabhāro*), detached (*visaṃyutto*), and the conceit "I am" (*asmimāno*). In this much, the time of the one with destroyed āsavas, who, with the Bhagavat having destroyed the defilements with the path and having gone to the best bed of cessation, dwells having passed beyond the attainment of fruition, with the object of nibbāna, is shown. Just as there are two cities: one is a city of thieves (*coranagaraṃ*), and one is a safe city (*khemanagaraṃ*). Then it might occur to a great warrior, "As long as this city of thieves exists, the safe city is not freed from fear. I will make the city of thieves a non-city." Having made an armament, having taken his sword, having approached the city of thieves, having split the door post (*esikatthambhe*) erected at the city gate with his sword, having split the door panel (*kavāṭaṃ*) along with its jambs (*dvārabāhakaṃ*), having raised the bar (*palighaṃ*) and broken the wall (*pākāraṃ*), having scattered the surrounding moat (*parikkhaṃ saṃkiritvā*), having caused the raised flags to fall so as to beautify the city (*nagarasobhanatthāya*), having burnt the city with fire, having entered the safe city and ascended the palace, surrounded by his kinsmen, he might enjoy delicious meals. Likewise, the city of thieves is like the existing body (*sakkāyo*), the safe city is like *nibbāna*, the great warrior is like the practitioner (*yogāvacaro*). It occurs to him thus: "As long as the cycle of the existing body revolves, there is no release from the thirty-two parts [of the body], the ninety-eight diseases, and the twenty-five great fears." That great warrior, having made an armament, just as the armament of morality, having taken the sword of wisdom (*paññākhaggaṃ*), having plucked out the pillar of craving (*taṇhesikaṃ*) with the path of arhatship, like pillar at the city gate (*esikatthambhe*), that warrior, having unbolted the bolts of the five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyasaṃyojanaggaḷaṃ*), like the door panel of the city gate along with its jambs (*sadvārabāhakaṃ nagarakavāṭaṃ*), that warrior, having lifted the bar of ignorance (*avijjāpalighaṃ*), like the bar (*palighaṃ*). That warrior, breaking through the wall, like breaking through the moat of karmic formations, breaking through the moat of the cycle of rebirths, that warrior, like lowering the flag of pride, which was raised for the beauty of the city, burning down the city of self-identity (satkāyanagara), that warrior, entering the city of the extinguishing of defilements (kilesanibbāna), like delicious food in an upper palace in the city of safety (khemanagare), experiencing the happiness of fruition attainment (phalasamāpattisukha), which has the cessation of deathlessness (amṛtanirodhārammaṇa) as its object, spends his time.

mula_pali:
246. ‘‘Evaṃ vimuttacittaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ saindā devā sabrahmakā sapajāpatikā anvesaṃ nādhigacchanti – ‘idaṃ nissitaṃ tathāgatassa viññāṇa’nti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Diṭṭhevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, dhamme tathāgataṃ ananuvijjoti vadāmi. Evaṃvādiṃ kho maṃ, bhikkhave, evamakkhāyiṃ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhanti – ‘venayiko samaṇo gotamo, sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññāpetī’ti. Yathā cāhaṃ na, bhikkhave bhikkhave na (sī. syā. pī.), yathā cāhaṃ na vadāmi, tathā maṃ te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhanti – ‘venayiko samaṇo gotamo, sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññāpetī’ti. Pubbe cāhaṃ bhikkhave, etarahi ca dukkhañceva paññāpemi, dukkhassa ca nirodhaṃ. Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṃ akkosanti paribhāsanti rosenti vihesenti, tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa na hoti āghāto na appaccayo na cetaso anabhiraddhi.

‘‘Tatra ce, bhikkhave, pare tathāgataṃ sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa na hoti ānando na somanassaṃ na cetaso uppilāvitattaṃ. Tatra ce, bhikkhave , pare vā tathāgataṃ sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññātaṃ tattha me evarūpā kārā sakkārā (ka.) karīyantī’ti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhe cepi pare akkoseyyuṃ paribhāseyyuṃ roseyyuṃ viheseyyuṃ, tatra tumhe hi na āghāto na appaccayo na cetaso anabhiraddhi karaṇīyā. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhe cepi pare sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyuṃ, tatra tumhehi na ānando na somanassaṃ na cetaso uppilāvitattaṃ karaṇīyaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhe cepi pare sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyuṃ, tatra tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññātaṃ, tattha me tattha no (ka.) tattha + imeti padacchedo evarūpā kārā karīyantī’ti.

sakkārā (ka.) tattha no (ka.) tattha + imeti padacchedo
mula_english:
246.
“Bhikkhus, when the gods with Indra (saindā), with Brahmā (sabrahmakā) and with Pajāpati (sapajāpatikā) seek a bhikkhu (bhikkhuṃ) who is thus liberated in mind (vimuttacittaṃ), they do not find anything of which they could say: “The consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) of one thus gone (tathāgatassa) is supported by this (idaṃ nissitaṃ).”

Why (taṃ kissa hetu)? One thus gone (tathāgataṃ), I say (vadāmi), is untraceable (ananuvijjoti) here and now (diṭṭheva ahaṃ, bhikkhave, dhamme)."

“So saying (evaṃvādiṃ kho maṃ), bhikkhus (bhikkhave), so proclaiming (evamakkhāyiṃ), I have been baselessly (asatā), vainly (tucchā), falsely (musā), and wrongly misrepresented (abhūtena abbhācikkhanti) by some recluses and Brahmins (eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā) thus: ‘The recluse Gotama (samaṇo gotamo) is one who leads astray (venayiko); he teaches the annihilation (ucchedaṃ), the destruction (vināsaṃ), the extermination (vibhavaṃ) of an existing being (sato sattassa).’”

"As I am not (yathā cāhaṃ na), bhikkhus, as I do not proclaim (yathā cāhaṃ na vadāmi), so have I been baselessly (asatā), vainly (tucchā), falsely (musā), and wrongly misrepresented (abhūtena abbhācikkhanti) by some recluses and Brahmins (samaṇabrāhmaṇā) thus: ‘The recluse Gotama (samaṇo gotamo) is one who leads astray (venayiko); he teaches the annihilation (ucchedaṃ), the destruction (vināsaṃ), the extermination (vibhavaṃ) of an existing being (sato sattassa).’"

"Bhikkhus, both formerly (pubbe cāhaṃ) and now (etarahi ca) what I teach (paññāpemi) is suffering (dukkhañceva) and the cessation (nirodhaṃ) of suffering (dukkhassa)."

"If others (pare), bhikkhus, abuse (akkosanti), revile (paribhāsanti), scold (rosenti), and harass (vihesenti) the Thus Gone One (tathāgataṃ), on that account (tatra), bhikkhus, the Thus Gone One (tathāgatassa) feels no annoyance (na hoti āghāto), bitterness (na appaccayo), or dejection (na cetaso anabhiraddhi)."

“And if others (pare), bhikkhus, honour (sakkaronti), respect (garuṃ karonti), revere (mānenti), and venerate (pūjenti) the Thus Gone One (tathāgataṃ), the Thus Gone One (tathāgatassa) on that account (tatra), bhikkhus, feels no delight (na hoti ānando), joy (na somanassaṃ), or elation (na cetaso uppilāvitattaṃ) of the heart."

"If others (pare), bhikkhus, honour (sakkaronti), respect (garuṃ karonti), revere (mānenti), and venerate (pūjenti) the Thus Gone One (tathāgataṃ), the Thus Gone One (tathāgatassa) on that account (tatra), bhikkhus, thinks thus (evaṃ hoti): ‘They perform such services (evarūpā kārā karīyantī) as these for the sake of what had earlier come to be fully understood (yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññātaṃ tattha me)."

“Therefore (tasmātiha), bhikkhus (bhikkhave), if others (pare) abuse (akkoseyyuṃ), revile (paribhāseyyuṃ), scold (roseyyuṃ), and harass (viheseyyuṃ) you (tumhe), on that account (tatra) you (tumhe) should not entertain any annoyance (na āghāto), bitterness (na appaccayo), or dejection (na cetaso anabhiraddhi) of the heart (karaṇīyā)."

"And if others (pare), bhikkhus, honour (sakkareyyuṃ), respect (garuṃ kareyyuṃ), revere (māneyyuṃ), and venerate (pūjeyyuṃ) you (tumhe), on that account (tatra) you (tumhehi) should not entertain any delight (na ānando), joy (na somanassaṃ), or elation (na cetaso uppilāvitattaṃ) of the heart (karaṇīyaṃ)."

“If others (pare), bhikkhus, honour (sakkareyyuṃ), respect (garuṃ kareyyuṃ), revere (māneyyuṃ), and venerate (pūjeyyuṃ) you (tumhe), on that account (tatra) you (tumhākaṃ) should think thus (evamassa): ‘They perform such services (evarūpā kārā karīyantī) as these for the sake of what had earlier come to be fully understood (yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññātaṃ, tattha me)."
commentary_pali:
246. Idāni evaṃ vimuttacittassa khīṇāsavassa parehi anadhigamanīyaviññāṇataṃ dassento evaṃ vimuttacittaṃ khotiādimāha. Tattha anvesanti anvesantā gavesantā. Idaṃ nissitanti idaṃ nāma nissitaṃ. Tathāgatassāti ettha sattopi tathāgatoti adhippeto, uttamapuggalo khīṇāsavopi. Ananuvijjoti asaṃvijjamāno vā avindeyyo vā. Tathāgatoti hi satte gahite asaṃvijjamānoti attho vaṭṭati, khīṇāsave gahite avindeyyoti attho vaṭṭati.

Tattha purimanaye ayamadhippāyo – bhikkhave, ahaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme dharamānakaṃyeva khīṇāsavaṃ tathāgato satto puggaloti na paññapemi. Appaṭisandhikaṃ pana parinibbutaṃ khīṇāsavaṃ sattoti vā puggaloti vā kiṃ paññapessāmi? Ananuvijjo tathāgato. Na hi paramatthato satto nāma koci atthi, tassa avijjamānassa idaṃ nissitaṃ viññāṇanti anvesantāpi kiṃ adhigacchissanti? Kathaṃ paṭilabhissantīti attho. Dutiyanaye ayamadhippāyo – bhikkhave, ahaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme dharamānakaṃyeva khīṇāsavaṃ viññāṇavasena indādīhi avindiyaṃ vadāmi. Na hi saindā devā sabrahmakā sapajāpatikā anvesantāpi khīṇāsavassa vipassanācittaṃ vā maggacittaṃ vā phalacittaṃ vā, idaṃ nāma ārammaṇaṃ nissāya vattatīti jānituṃ sakkonti. Te appaṭisandhikassa parinibbutassa kiṃ jānissantīti?

Asatāti asantena. Tucchāti tucchakena. Musāti musāvādena. Abhūtenāti yaṃ natthi, tena. Abbhācikkhantīti abhiācikkhanti, abhibhavitvā vadanti. Venayikoti vinayati vināsetīti vinayo, so eva venayiko, sattavināsakoti adhippāyo. Yathā cāhaṃ na, bhikkhaveti, bhikkhave, yena vākārena ahaṃ na sattavināsako. Yathā cāhaṃ na vadāmīti yena vā kāraṇena ahaṃ sattavināsaṃ na paññapemi . Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yathāhaṃ na sattavināsako, yathā ca na sattavināsaṃ paññapemi, tathā maṃ te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘‘venayiko samaṇo gotamo’’ti vadantā sattavināsako samaṇo gotamoti ca, ‘‘sato sattassa ucchedaṃ vināsaṃ vibhavaṃ paññapetī’’ti vadantā sattavināsaṃ paññapetīti ca asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhantīti.

Asatā Tucchā Musā Abhūtenā Abbhācikkhantī Venayiko vinayo, venayiko, Yathā cāhaṃ na, bhikkhave Yathā cāhaṃ na vadāmī

Pubbe cāti pubbe mahābodhimaṇḍamhiyeva ca. Etarahi cāti etarahi dhammadesanāyañca. Dukkhañceva paññapemi, dukkhassa ca nirodhanti dhammacakkaṃ appavattetvā bodhimaṇḍe viharantopi dhammacakkappavattanato paṭṭhāya dhammaṃ desentopi catusaccameva paññapemīti attho. Ettha hi dukkhaggahaṇena tassa mūlabhūto samudayo, nirodhaggahaṇena taṃsampāpako maggo gahitova hotīti veditabbo. Tatra ceti tasmiṃ catusaccappakāsane. Pareti saccāni ājānituṃ paṭivijjhituṃ asamatthapuggalā. Akkosantīti dasahi akkosavatthūhi akkosanti. Paribhāsantīti vācāya paribhāsanti. Rosenti vihesentīti rosessāma vihesessāmāti adhippāyena ghaṭṭenti dukkhāpenti. Tatrāti tesu akkosādīsu, tesu vā parapuggalesu. Āghātoti kopo. Appaccayoti domanassaṃ. Anabhiraddhīti atuṭṭhi.

Pubbe cā Etarahi cā Dukkhañceva paññapemi, dukkhassa ca nirodha Tatra ce Pare Akkosantī Paribhāsantī Rosenti vihesentī Tatrā Āghāto Appaccayo Anabhiraddhī

Tatra ceti catusaccappakāsaneyeva. Pareti catusaccappakāsanaṃ ājānituṃ paṭivijjhituṃ samatthapuggalā. Ānandoti ānandapīti. Uppilāvitattanti uppilāpanapīti. Tatra ceti catusaccappakāsanamhiyeva. Tatrāti sakkārādīsu. Yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññātanti idaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ pubbe bodhimaṇḍe tīhi pariññāhi pariññātaṃ. Tatthameti tasmiṃ khandhapañcake ime. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Tatrāpi tathāgatassa ime sakkārā mayi karīyantīti vā ahaṃ ete anubhavāmīti vā na hoti. Pubbe pariññātakkhandhapañcakaṃyeva ete sakkāre anubhotīti ettakameva hotīti. Tasmāti yasmā saccāni paṭivijjhituṃ asamatthā tathāgatampi akkosanti, tasmā. Sesaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

Tatra ce Pare Ānando Uppilāvitatta Tatra ce Tatrā Yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññāta Tatthame Tasmā
commentary_english:
246. Now, showing that the consciousness of the liberated-minded, taintless one is unattainable by others, [he] says, “*Evaṃ vimuttacittaṃ kho*” etc.

There, *anvesa* means searching and seeking.

*Idaṃ nissita* means relying on this name.

*Tathāgatassā* means that here, *tathāgata* is intended as the supreme individual, the taintless one.

*Ananuvijjo* means either non-existent or unattainable.

Because *tathāgata* means that when beings are seized, the meaning is non-existent; when the taintless one is seized, the meaning is unattainable.

There, in the previous way, this is the purport: Monks, I do not declare that the taintless *tathāgata* is a being or a person while still in this very life.

But what shall I declare of the taintless one who has attained *parinirvāṇa* without rebirth, as either a being or a person? The *tathāgata* is unknowable.

For in ultimate truth, there is no being by the name of a *sattva*. Since he is non-existent, what will those who search for the consciousness relying on this attain? How will they regain it? This is the meaning.

In the second way, this is the purport: Monks, I say that the taintless one is unattainable even by Indra and others due to [their] consciousness while still in this very life.

For even the gods with Indra, with Brahmā, and with Prajāpati, even searching, are not able to know the mind of insight (*vipassanācitta*) or the path-mind (*maggacitta*) or the fruition-mind (*phalacitta*) of the taintless one, [namely] that it exists relying on this object (*ārammaṇa*).

What will they know of one who has attained *parinirvāṇa* without rebirth?

*Asatā* means by the non-existent.

*Tucchā* means by the empty.

*Musā* means by false speech.

*Abhūtenā* means by that which is not.

*Abbhācikkhantī* means they accuse, overpowering [him], they speak.

*Venayiko* means "he trains, he destroys," thus *vinaya*; that very one is *venayiko*, meaning one who destroys beings.

*Yathā cāhaṃ na, bhikkhave*, monks, by whatever manner I am not a destroyer of beings.

*Yathā cāhaṃ na vadāmī*, by whatever cause I do not declare the destruction of beings.

This is what is said: Just as I am not a destroyer of beings, and just as I do not declare the destruction of beings, so those venerable *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s, saying "the *śramaṇa* Gotama is a guide," and also "the *śramaṇa* Gotama is a destroyer of beings," and also saying, "he declares the annihilation, destruction, and dissolution of an existing being," thus they falsely, emptily, untruthfully, and with what is not, accuse [me].

*Asatā*, *tucchā*, *musā*, *abhūtenā*, *abbhācikkhantī*, *venayiko*, *vinayo*, *venayiko*,

*Yathā cāhaṃ na, bhikkhave*, *yathā cāhaṃ na vadāmī*

*Pubbe cā*, formerly, and also just at the great *bodhimaṇḍa*.

*Etarahi cā*, at present, and also during the teaching of the Dharma.

*Dukkhañceva paññapemi, dukkhassa ca nirodha*, I declare only suffering and the cessation of suffering. Even dwelling at the *bodhimaṇḍa* without setting the wheel of the Dharma in motion, and also teaching the Dharma from the time of setting the wheel of the Dharma in motion, I declare only the four noble truths. This is the meaning.

Here, it should be understood that by the seizing of suffering, its root cause, arising (*samudaya*), is seized; by the seizing of cessation (*nirodha*), the path (*magga*) that leads to it is seized.

*Tatra ce*, there, in that exposition of the four noble truths.

*Pare*, those persons incapable of knowing and penetrating the truths.

*Akkosantī*, they abuse with the ten grounds for abuse (*akkosavatthū*).

*Paribhāsantī*, they revile with speech (*vācāya*).

*Rosenti vihesentī*, intending "we will provoke and harass," they agitate and torment.

*Tatrā*, there, among those abuses etc., or among those other persons.

*Āghāto*, anger.

*Appaccayo*, sadness.

*Anabhiraddhī*, displeasure.
Formerly and now, I proclaim only suffering and the cessation of suffering.
"When others are angry, reviling, and harassing, there is resentment, dissatisfaction, and displeasure."
"Tatra ce" means in the very declaration of the Four Noble Truths.
"Pare" means persons capable of understanding and penetrating the declaration of the Four Noble Truths.
"Ānando" means the joy of bliss.
"Uppilāvitatta" means the bliss of elation.
"Tatra ce" means in the very declaration of the Four Noble Truths.
"Tatrā" means in offerings and so on.
"Yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññāta" means this aggregate of five aggregates was previously understood in the bodhimaṇḍa by three kinds of understanding.
"Tatthame" means these are in that aggregate of five aggregates.
What is said? There is no thought that these offerings are being made to me by the *tathāgata*, or that I am experiencing these.
Only the previously understood aggregate of five aggregates experiences these offerings; that is all there is.
"Tasmā" because those who are unable to penetrate the truths revile even the *tathāgata*, therefore.
The rest should be understood in the way already described.

"Tatra ce," "pare," "ānando," "uppilāvitatta," "tatra ce," "tatrā," "yaṃ kho idaṃ pubbe pariññāta," "tatthame," "tasmā"

mula_pali: 247. ‘‘Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ na tumhākaṃ taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Kiñca, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Vedanā, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; sā vo pahīnā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Saññā, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; sā vo pahīnā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Saṅkhārā, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, te pajahatha; te vo pahīnā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissanti. Viññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, yaṃ imasmiṃ jetavane tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ, taṃ jano hareyya vā daheyya vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā kareyya. Api nu tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘amhe jano harati vā dahati vā yathāpaccayaṃ vā karotī’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Na hi no etaṃ, bhante, attā vā attaniyaṃ vā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ na tumhākaṃ taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Kiñca, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ? Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati. Vedanā, bhikkhave…pe… saññā, bhikkhave… saṅkhārā, bhikkhave…pe… viññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.
mula_english:
247. “Therefore, *bhikkhus*, whatever is not yours, abandon it; when you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, what is not yours? Material form (*rūpa*), *bhikkhus*, is not yours. Abandon it. When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Feeling (*vedanā*), *bhikkhus*, is not yours. Abandon it. When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Perception (*saññā*), *bhikkhus*, is not yours. Abandon it. When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Formations (*saṅkhārā*), *bhikkhus*, are not yours. Abandon them. When you have abandoned them, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Consciousness (*viññāṇaṃ*), *bhikkhus*, is not yours. Abandon it. When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

What do you think, *bhikkhus*? If people carried off the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves in this Jeta Grove, or burned them, or did what they liked with them, would you think:

‘People are carrying us off or burning us or doing what they like with us’? “No, venerable sir.”

“What is the reason for that?” “Because that is not our self (*attā*) or what belongs to a self (*attaniyaṃ*), venerable sir.”

“So too, *bhikkhus*, whatever is not yours, abandon it; when you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, what is not yours? Material form (*rūpa*), *bhikkhus*, is not yours. Abandon it. When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Feeling (*vedanā*), *bhikkhus*… Perception (*saññā*), *bhikkhus*… Formations (*saṅkhārā*), *bhikkhus*… Consciousness (*viññāṇaṃ*), *bhikkhus*, is not yours. Abandon it. When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.
commentary_pali: 247.Tasmā tiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ na tumhākanti yasmā attaniyepi chandarāgappahānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya saṃvattati, tasmā yaṃ na tumhākaṃ, taṃ pajahathāti attho. Yathāpaccayaṃ vākareyyāti yathā yathā iccheyya tathā tathā kareyya. Na hi no etaṃ, bhante, attā vāti, bhante, etaṃ tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ amhākaṃ neva attā na amhākaṃ rūpaṃ na viññāṇanti vadanti. Attaniyaṃ vāti amhākaṃ cīvarādiparikkhāropi na hotīti attho. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ na tumhākaṃ taṃ pajahathāti bhagavā, khandhapañcakaṃyeva na tumhākanti dassetvā pajahāpeti, tañca kho na uppāṭetvā, luñcitvā vā. Chandarāgavinayena panetaṃ pajahāpeti.
commentary_english:
247. Therefore, here, O *bhikkhus*, “whatever is not yours”: because the abandonment of desire and passion even in oneself conduces to welfare and happiness for a long time, therefore, whatever is not yours, abandon that—is the meaning.

Or according to one's resources, one may do as one chooses.

“No, indeed, is this, *bhante*, a self”: *bhante*, this grass, wood, branches, and leaves are not our self, nor our form (*rūpa*), nor our consciousness (*vijñāna*)—so they say.

“Or belonging to oneself”: meaning that even our robes and equipment do not exist.

“Even so, *bhikkhus*, abandon whatever is not yours”: the Blessed One, having shown that only the five aggregates (*skandhapañcaka*) are not yours, causes [them] to be abandoned, but not by uprooting or plucking.

By the discipline of desire and passion, he causes this to be abandoned.

mula_pali:
248. ‘‘Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike ye te bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāya. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, sabbe te opapātikā, tattha parinibbāyino, anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, rāgadosamohā tanubhūtā, sabbe te sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, sabbe te sotāpannā, avinipātadhammā , niyatā sambodhiparāyanā. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike ye te bhikkhū dhammānusārino saddhānusārino sabbe te sambodhiparāyanā. Evaṃ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko. Evaṃ svākkhāte, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike yesaṃ mayi saddhāmattaṃ pemamattaṃ sabbe te saggaparāyanā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Alagaddūpamasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
248. “Bhikkhus, the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork. In the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus, which is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork, there is no future round for manifestation in the case of those *bhikkhus* who are *arahants* with taints destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), who have lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached the true goal, destroyed the fetters of being (*bhava-saṃyojana*), and are completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammad-aññā vimuttā*).

“Bhikkhus, the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork. In the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus, which is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork, those *bhikkhus* who have abandoned the five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*) are all due to reappear spontaneously (*opapātikā*) in the Pure Abodes and there attain final *Nibbāna* (*parinibbāyino*), without ever returning from that world (*anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā*).

“Bhikkhus, the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork. In the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus, which is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork, those *bhikkhus* who have abandoned the three fetters (*tīṇi saṃyojanāni*) and attenuated lust (*rāga*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*) are all once-returners (*sakadāgāmino*), returning once to this world to make an end of suffering (*dukkha*).

“Bhikkhus, the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork. In the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus, which is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork, those *bhikkhus* who have abandoned three fetters (*tīṇi saṃyojanāni*) are all stream-enterers (*sotāpannā*), no longer subject to perdition (*avinipātadhammā*), bound for deliverance and headed for enlightenment (*niyatā sambodhi-parāyanā*).

“Bhikkhus, the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork. In the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus, which is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork, those *bhikkhus* who are Dhamma-followers (*dhammānusārino*) or faith-followers (*saddhānusārino*) are all headed for enlightenment (*sambodhi-parāyanā*).

“Bhikkhus, the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork. In the Dhamma well proclaimed by me thus, which is clear, open, evident, and free of patchwork, those *bhikkhus* who have sufficient faith (*saddhāmattaṃ*) in me, sufficient love (*pemamattaṃ*) for me, are all headed for heaven (*saggaparāyanā*.”

Thus spoke the Blessed One. Gratified, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Shorter Discourse on the Simile of the Water-Snake, the Second [Discourse], is concluded.
commentary_pali:
248.Evaṃ svākkhātoti ettha tiparivaṭṭato paṭṭhāya yāva imaṃ ṭhānaṃ āharitumpi vaṭṭati, paṭilomena pemamattakena saggaparāyaṇato paṭṭhāya yāva imaṃ ṭhānaṃ āharitumpi vaṭṭati. Svākkhātoti sukathito. Sukathitattā eva uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito. Chinnapilotikoti pilotikā vuccati chinnaṃ bhinnaṃ tattha tattha sibbitaṃ gaṇṭhikataṃ jiṇṇaṃ vatthaṃ, taṃ yassa natthi, aṭṭhahatthaṃ vā navahatthaṃ vā ahatasāṭakaṃ nivattho, so chinnapilotiko nāma. Ayampi dhammo tādiso, na hettha kohaññādivasena chinnabhinnasibbitagaṇṭhikatabhāvo atthi. Apica kacavaro pilotikoti vuccati. Imasmiñca sāsane samaṇakacavaraṃ nāma patiṭṭhātuṃ na labhati. Tenevāha –

‘‘Kāraṇḍavaṃ niddhamatha, kasambuñcāpakassatha;

Tato palāpe vāhetha, assamaṇe samaṇamānine.

Niddhamitvāna pāpicche, pāpaācāragocare;

Suddhā suddhehi saṃvāsaṃ, kappayavho patissatā;

Tato samaggā nipakā, dukkhassantaṃ karissathā’’ti. (su. ni. 283-285);

Iti samaṇakacavarassa chinnattāpi ayaṃ dhammo chinnapilotiko nāma hoti. Vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ natthi paññāpanāyāti tesaṃ vaṭṭaṃ apaññattibhāvaṃ gataṃ nippaññattikaṃ jātaṃ. Evarūpo mahākhīṇāsavo evaṃ svākkhāte sāsaneyeva uppajjati. Yathā ca khīṇāsavo, evaṃ anāgāmiādayopi.

chinnapilotiko nāma Vaṭṭaṃ tesa natthi paññāpanāyā

Tattha dhammānusārino saddhānusārinoti ime dve sotāpattimaggaṭṭhā honti. Yathāha – ‘‘katamo ca puggalo dhammānusārī? Yassa puggalassa sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa paññindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti, paññāvāhiṃ paññāpubbaṅgamaṃ ariyamaggaṃ bhāveti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo dhammānusārī. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo dhammānusārī, phale ṭhito diṭṭhippatto. Katamo ca puggalo saddhānusārī? Yassa puggalassa sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa saddhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti, saddhāvāhiṃ saddhāpubbaṅgamaṃ ariyamaggaṃ bhāveti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo saddhānusārī. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo saddhānusārī, phale ṭhito saddhāvimutto’’ti (pu. pa. 30). Yesaṃ mayi saddhāmattaṃ pemamattanti iminā yesaṃ añño ariyadhammo natthi, tathāgate pana saddhāmattaṃ pemamattameva hoti. Te vipassakapuggalā adhippetā. Vipassakabhikkhūnañhi evaṃ vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā nisinnānaṃ dasabale ekā saddhā ekaṃ pemaṃ uppajjati. Tāya saddhāya tena pemena hatthe gahetvā sagge ṭhapitā viya honti, niyatagatikā kira ete. Porāṇakattherā pana evarūpaṃ bhikkhuṃ cūḷasotāpannoti vadanti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

dhammānusārino saddhānusārino Yesaṃ mayi saddhāmattaṃ pemamatta

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Alagaddūpamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
248. "Thus, well-proclaimed (evaṃ svākkhāto)" means that beginning from the threefold revolution (tiparivaṭṭato), it is suitable to bring it up to this point; by reversal, it is suitable to bring it up to this point with love and affection (pemamattakena) from heaven as the final goal (saggaparāyaṇato).

"Well-proclaimed (svākkhāto)" means well-spoken (sukathito). Because it is well-spoken (sukathitattā), it is indeed explained, elucidated, and clarified (uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito).

"Tattered rag-wearer (chinnapilotiko)" means a rag (pilotikā) is said to be a torn (chinnaṃ), broken (bhinnaṃ), stitched (sibbitaṃ) here and there, knotted (gaṇṭhikataṃ), old (jiṇṇaṃ) cloth (vatthaṃ), that which he does not have; he is clothed in an eight- or nine-cubit, unwashed (ahata), new cloth (sāṭakaṃ), he is called a *chinnapilotiko*.

This *dharma* too is such; here, there is no state of being torn, broken, stitched, and knotted by way of deceitfulness and so on.

Moreover, trash (*kacavaro*) is said to be a rag (*pilotikoti*).

In this Dispensation (*sāsane*), one cannot establish the name "ascetic trash (*samaṇakacavaraṃ nāma*)."

Therefore, he said:

"Drive out the kāraṇḍava bird, cast away the kasambu; then drive away the chaff, those who consider themselves ascetics when they are not."

"Having driven out those who desire evil, who are in the range of evil conduct; the pure ones, associate with the pure; be capable of mindfulness; then, being harmonious and wise, you will make an end to suffering." (Su. Ni. 283-285);

Thus, even though there is the state of being torn for the ascetic trash (*samaṇakacavarassa chinnattāpi*), this *dharma* is called "tattered rag-wearer (*chinnapilotiko nāma*)."

"*Vaṭṭaṃ*...there is no proclamation for them (natthi paññāpanāyā)": their circle (*vaṭṭaṃ*) has gone to the state of non-proclamation (apaññattibhāvaṃ), it has become un-proclaimable (nippaññattikaṃ jātaṃ).

Such a great *khīṇāsava* arises only in a Dispensation that is thus well-proclaimed (*evaṃ svākkhāte sāsaneyeva uppajjati*). And as with the *khīṇāsava*, so also with the *anāgāmi* and others.

"*Chinnapilotiko nāma vaṭṭaṃ*...there is no proclamation for them (natthi paññāpanāyā)". There, the *dhammānusārino* and *saddhānusārino* are the two who are standing on the path of stream-entry (*sotāpattimaggaṭṭhā honti*).

As he said: "And what kind of person is a follower of the Dharma (*dhammānusārī*)? For whichever person who has undertaken the realization of the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa*) has an abundance of the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti*), cultivates the Noble Path (*ariyamaggaṃ bhāveti*) that carries wisdom (*paññāvāhiṃ*), that has wisdom as its forerunner (*paññāpubbaṅgamaṃ*). This person is called a follower of the Dharma (*dhammānusārī*). A person who has undertaken the realization of the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalaḥ*) is a follower of the Dharma (*dhammānusārī*), one who is standing in the fruit (*phale ṭhito*), who has attained the right view (*diṭṭhippatto*).

And what kind of person is a follower of faith (*saddhānusārī*)? For whichever person who has undertaken the realization of the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa*) has an abundance of the faculty of faith (*saddhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti*), cultivates the Noble Path (*ariyamaggaṃ bhāveti*) that carries faith (*saddhāvāhiṃ*), that has faith as its forerunner (*saddhāpubbaṅgamaṃ*). This person is called a follower of faith (*saddhānusārī*). A person who has undertaken the realization of the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalaḥ*) is a follower of faith (*saddhānusārī*), one who is standing in the fruit (*phale ṭhito*), who is liberated by faith (*saddhāvimutto*)." (Pu. Pa. 30).

"For whom there is only faith and affection in me (*yesaṃ mayi saddhāmattaṃ pemamatta*)" means that for whom there is no other Noble *Dharma*, but in the *Tathāgata* there is only faith and affection (*saddhāmattaṃ pemamattameva hoti*).

Those are the *vipassanā* individuals who are intended (*vipassakapuggalā adhippetā*).

For when *vipassanā* monks, having established *vipassanā* thus, are sitting, a single faith and a single affection arises in the ten powers (dasabale).

By that faith, by that affection, having taken them by the hand, they are as if established in heaven (*sagge ṭhapitā viya honti*), these are indeed of fixed destiny (*niyatagatikā kira ete*).

The ancient elders (*porāṇakattherā*) say that a monk of such a kind is a "lesser stream-enterer (*cūḷasotāpannoti vadanti*)."

The rest is clear in meaning throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti*).

*Dhammānusārino saddhānusārino yesaṃ mayi saddhāmattaṃ pemamatta*

The *Alagaddūpamasutta* commentary of the *Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā* in the *Papañcasūdanī* is finished (*niṭṭhitā*).

mula_pali:
249. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā kumārakassapo andhavane viharati. Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ andhavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāyasmā kumārakassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā āyasmantaṃ kumārakassapaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Bhikkhu bhikkhu, ayaṃ vammiko vammīko (katthaci) sakkatānurūpaṃ rattiṃ dhūmāyati, divā pajjalati. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa laṅgiṃ ‘laṅgī, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa laṅgiṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa uddhumāyikaṃ. ‘Uddhumāyikā, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa uddhumāyikaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa dvidhāpathaṃ. ‘Dvidhāpatho, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa dvidhāpathaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa caṅgavāraṃ paṅkavāraṃ (syā.), caṅkavāraṃ (ka.). ‘Caṅgavāro, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa caṅgavāraṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa kummaṃ. ‘Kummo , bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa kummaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa asisūnaṃ. ‘Asisūnā, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa asisūnaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa maṃsapesiṃ. ‘Maṃsapesi, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘ukkhipa maṃsapesiṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya addasa nāgaṃ. ‘Nāgo, bhadante’ti. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘tiṭṭhatu nāgo, mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesi; namo karohi nāgassā’’’ti.

vammīko (katthaci) sakkatānurūpaṃ paṅkavāraṃ (syā.), caṅkavāraṃ (ka.)

‘‘Ime kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, pañhe bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyāsi, yathā ca te bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāsi. Nāhaṃ taṃ, bhikkhu, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo imesaṃ pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyya aññatra tathāgatena vā, tathāgatasāvakena vā, ito vā pana sutvā’’ti – idamavoca sā devatā. Idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Anāthapindika’s monastery, in the Jeta Grove, near Sāvatthi. Now on that occasion the venerable Kumārakassapa was living in the Blind Men’s Grove (andhavana). Then, when the night was well advanced, a certain deity (devatā) of beautiful appearance who illuminated the whole of the Blind Men’s Grove approached the venerable Kumārakassapa and stood at one side. Standing at one side, that deity said this to the venerable Kumārakassapa: “Monk, this anthill (vammiko), [namely:] the anthill (vammīko) is in some way corresponding to Sanskrit, smokes by night, and blazes by day. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Dig, wise Sumedha (sumedha), taking the knife (sattham)’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw a bar (laṅgiṃ): ‘A bar (laṅgī), venerable sir (bhadante)’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Remove the bar (laṅgiṃ); dig, wise Sumedha, taking the knife’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw a toad (uddhumāyikaṃ). ‘A toad (uddhumāyikā), venerable sir’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Remove the toad (uddhumāyikaṃ); dig, wise Sumedha, taking the knife’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw a fork (dvidhāpathaṃ). ‘A fork (dvidhāpatho), venerable sir’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Remove the fork (dvidhāpathaṃ); dig, wise Sumedha, taking the knife’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw a sieve (caṅgavāraṃ). ‘A sieve (caṅgavāro), venerable sir’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Remove the sieve (caṅgavāraṃ); dig, wise Sumedha, taking the knife’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw a tortoise (kummaṃ). ‘A tortoise (kummo), venerable sir’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Remove the tortoise (kummaṃ); dig, wise Sumedha, taking the knife’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw an axe and block (asisūnaṃ). ‘An axe and block (asisūnā), venerable sir’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Remove the axe and block (asisūnaṃ); dig, wise Sumedha, taking the knife’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw a piece of meat (maṃsapesiṃ). ‘A piece of meat (maṃsapesi), venerable sir’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Remove the piece of meat (maṃsapesiṃ); dig, wise Sumedha, taking the knife’. Digging, wise Sumedha, taking the knife, saw a *Nāga* serpent (nāgaṃ). ‘A *Nāga* serpent (nāgo), venerable sir’. The *brāhmana* said thus: ‘Let the *Nāga* serpent stay; do not harm the *Nāga* serpent; honor the *Nāga* serpent’." 0143"/>

‘‘These Indeed, you, *bhikṣu*, should approach the Fortunate One with these questions, and as the Fortunate One explains, so you should remember it. ( *kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, pañhe bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyāsi, yathā ca te bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāsi.*) I do not see anyone, *bhikṣu*, in this world with its gods ( *sadevake*), with its *Māras* ( *samārake*), and with its *Brahmās* ( *sabrahmake*), in this generation with its ascetics ( *śramaṇa*) and *brāhmaṇas* ( *brāhmaṇī*), with its gods and humans ( *sadevamanuṣyāya*), who, other than a *Tathāgata* or a disciple of a *Tathāgata* or one who has heard it from them, could satisfy the mind ( *cittaṃ ārādheyya*) with an explanation of these questions. ( *nāhaṃ taṃ, bhikkhu, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanuṣyāya, yo imesaṃ pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyya aññatra tathāgatena vā, tathāgatasāvakena vā, ito vā pana sutvā’'ti.*) That is what the deity ( *sā devatā*) said. ( *idamavoca sā devatā.*) Having said this, she vanished at once. ( *idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi.*)
commentary_pali:
249.Evaṃme sutanti vammikasuttaṃ. Tattha āyasmāti piyavacanametaṃ. Kumārakassapoti tassa nāmaṃ. Kumārakāle pabbajitattā pana bhagavatā, ‘‘kassapaṃ pakkosatha, idaṃ phalaṃ vā khādanīyaṃ vā kassapassa dethā’’ti vutte, katarassa kassapassāti kumārakassapassāti evaṃ gahitanāmattā tato paṭṭhāya vuḍḍhakālepi ‘‘kumārakassapo’’ tveva vuccati. Apica raññā posāvanikaputtattāpi taṃ ‘‘kumārakassapo’’ti sañjāniṃsu. Ayaṃ panassa pubbayogato paṭṭhāya āvibhāvakathā –

Thero kira padumuttarassa bhagavato kāle seṭṭhiputto ahosi. Athekadivasaṃ bhagavantaṃ citrakathiṃ ekaṃ attano sāvakaṃ ṭhānantare ṭhapentaṃ disvā bhagavato sattāhaṃ dānaṃ datvā, ‘‘ahampi bhagavā anāgate ekassa buddhassa ayaṃ thero viya citrakathī sāvako bhaveyya’’nti patthanaṃ katvā puññāni karonto kassapassa bhagavato sāsane pabbajitvā visesaṃ nibbattetuṃ nāsakkhi.

Tadā kira parinibbutassa bhagavato sāsane osakkante pañca bhikkhū nisseṇiṃ bandhitvā pabbataṃ abhiruyha samaṇadhammaṃ akaṃsu. Saṅghatthero tatiyadivase arahattaṃ patto. Anuthero catutthadivase anāgāmī ahosi. Itare tayo visesaṃ nibbattetuṃ asakkontā devaloke nibbattiṃsu. Tesaṃ ekaṃ buddhantaraṃ devesu ca manussesu ca sampattiṃ anubhontānaṃ eko takkasilāyaṃ rājakule nibbattitvā pukkusāti nāma rājā hutvā bhagavantaṃ uddissa pabbajitvā rājagahaṃ gacchanto kumbhakārasālāyaṃ bhagavato dhammadesanaṃ sutvā anāgāmiphalaṃ patto. Eko ekasmiṃ samuddapaṭṭane kulaghare nibbattitvā nāvaṃ āruyha bhinnanāvo dārucīrāni nivāsetvā lābhasampattiṃ patto, ‘‘ahaṃ arahā’’ti cittaṃ uppādetvā, ‘‘na tvaṃ arahā, gaccha satthāraṃ pañhaṃ pucchā’’ti atthakāmāya devatāya codito tathā katvā arahattaphalaṃ patto.

Eko rājagahe ekissā kuladārikāya kucchimhi uppanno. Sā ca paṭhamaṃ mātāpitaro yācitvā pabbajjaṃ alabhamānā kulagharaṃ gatā gabbhasaṇṭhitampi ajānantī sāmikaṃ ārādhetvā tena anuññātā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā. Tassā gabbhininimittaṃ disvā bhikkhuniyo devadattaṃ pucchiṃsu, so ‘‘assamaṇī’’ti āha. Dasabalaṃ pucchiṃsu, satthā upālittheraṃ paṭicchāpesi. Thero sāvatthinagaravāsīni kulāni visākhañca upāsikaṃ pakkosāpetvā sodhento, – ‘‘pure laddho gabbho, pabbajjā arogā’’ti āha. Satthā ‘‘suvinicchitaṃ adhikaraṇa’’nti therassa sādhukāraṃ adāsi. Sā bhikkhunī suvaṇṇabimbasadisaṃ puttaṃ vijāyi, taṃ gahetvā rājā pasenadi kosalo posāpesi. ‘‘Kassapo’’ti cassa nāmaṃ katvā aparabhāge alaṅkaritvā satthu santikaṃ netvā pabbājesi. Iti rañño posāvanikaputtattāpi taṃ ‘‘kumārakassapo’’ti sañjāniṃsūti.

Andhavaneti evaṃnāmake vane. Taṃ kira vanaṃ dvinnaṃ buddhānaṃ kāle avijahitanāmaṃ andhavanaṃtveva paññāyati. Tatrāyaṃ paññattivibhāvanā – appāyukabuddhānañhi sarīradhātu na ekagghanā hoti. Adhiṭṭhānānubhāvena vippakiriyati. Teneva amhākampi bhagavā, – ‘‘ahaṃ na ciraṭṭhitiko, appakehi sattehi ahaṃ diṭṭho, yehi na diṭṭho, teva bahutarā, te me dhātuyo ādāya tattha tattha pūjentā saggaparāyaṇā bhavissantī’’ti parinibbānakāle, ‘‘attano sarīraṃ vippakiriyatū’’ti adhiṭṭhāsi. Dīghāyukabuddhānaṃ pana suvaṇṇakkhandho viya ekagghanaṃ dhātusarīraṃ tiṭṭhati.

Andhavane

Kassapassāpi bhagavato tatheva aṭṭhāsi. Tato mahājanā sannipatitvā, ‘‘dhātuyo ekagghanā na sakkā viyojetuṃ, kiṃ karissāmā’’ti sammantayitvā ekagghanameva cetiyaṃ karissāma, kittakaṃ pana hotu tanti āhaṃsu. Eke sattayojaniyanti āhaṃsu. Etaṃ atimahantaṃ, anāgate jaggituṃ na sakkā, chayojanaṃ hotu, pañcayojanaṃ… catuyojanaṃ… tiyojanaṃ… dviyojanaṃ… ekayojanaṃ hotūti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā iṭṭhakā kīdisā hontūti bāhirante iṭṭhakā rattasuvaṇṇamayā ekagghanā satasahassagghanikā hontu, abbhantarimante paññāsasahassagghanikā. Haritālamanosilāhi mattikākiccaṃ kayiratu, telena udakakiccanti niṭṭhaṃ gantvā cattāri mukhāni catudhā vibhajiṃsu. Rājā ekaṃ mukhaṃ gaṇhi, rājaputto pathavindarakumāro ekaṃ, amaccānaṃ jeṭṭhako hutvā senāpati ekaṃ, janapadānaṃ jeṭṭhako hutvā seṭṭhi ekaṃ.

Tattha dhanasampannatāya rājāpi suvaṇṇaṃ nīharāpetvā attanā gahitamukhe kammaṃ ārabhi, uparājāpi, senāpatipi. Seṭṭhinā gahitamukhe pana kammaṃ olīyati. Tato yasorato nāma eko upāsako tepiṭako bhāṇako anāgāmī ariyasāvako, so kammaṃ olīyatīti ñatvā pañca sakaṭasatāni yojāpetvā janapadaṃ gantvā ‘‘kassapasammāsambuddho vīsativassasahassāni ṭhatvā parinibbuto. Tassa yojanikaṃ ratanacetiyaṃ kayirati, yo yaṃ dātuṃ ussahati suvaṇṇaṃ vā hiraññaṃ vā sattaratanaṃ vā haritālaṃ vā manosilaṃ vā, so taṃ detū’’ti samādapesi. Manussā attano attano thāmena hiraññasuvaṇṇādīni adaṃsu. Asakkontā telataṇḍulādīni dentiyeva. Upāsako telataṇḍulādīni kammakārānaṃ bhattavetanatthaṃ pahiṇāti, avasesehi suvaṇṇaṃ cetāpetvā pahiṇāti, evaṃ sakalajambudīpaṃ acari.

Cetiye kammaṃ niṭṭhitanti cetiyaṭṭhānato paṇṇaṃ pahiṇiṃsu – ‘‘niṭṭhitaṃ kammaṃ ācariyo āgantvā cetiyaṃ vandatū’’ti. Sopi paṇṇaṃ pahiṇi – ‘‘mayā sakalajambudīpo samādapito, yaṃ atthi, taṃ gahetvā kammaṃ niṭṭhāpentū’’ti. Dvepi paṇṇāni antarāmagge samāgamiṃsu. Ācariyassa paṇṇato pana cetiyaṭṭhānato paṇṇaṃ paṭhamataraṃ ācariyassa hatthaṃ agamāsi. So paṇṇaṃ vācetvā cetiyaṃ vandissāmīti ekakova nikkhami. Antarāmagge aṭaviyaṃ pañca corasatāni uṭṭhahiṃsu. Tatrekacce taṃ disvā iminā sakalajambudīpato hiraññasuvaṇṇaṃ sampiṇḍitaṃ, nidhikumbhī no pavaṭṭamānā āgatāti avasesānaṃ ārocetvā taṃ aggahesuṃ. Kasmā tātā, maṃ gaṇhathāti? Tayā sakalajambudīpato sabbaṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇaṃ sampiṇḍitaṃ, amhākampi thokaṃ thokaṃ dehīti. Kiṃ tumhe na jānātha, kassapo bhagavā parinibbuto, tassa yojanikaṃ ratanacetiyaṃ kayirati, tadatthāya mayā samādapitaṃ, no attano atthāya. Taṃ taṃ laddhaladdhaṭṭhānato tattheva pesitaṃ, mayhaṃ pana nivatthasāṭakamattaṃ ṭhapetvā aññaṃ vittaṃ kākaṇikampi natthīti.

Eke, ‘‘evametaṃ vissajetha ācariya’’nti āhaṃsu. Eke, ‘‘ayaṃ rājapūjito amaccapūjito , amhesu kañcideva nagaravīthiyaṃ disvā rājarājamahāmattādīnaṃ ārocetvā anayavyasanaṃ pāpuṇāpeyyā’’ti āhaṃsu. Upāsako, ‘‘tātā, nāhaṃ evaṃ karissāmī’’ti āha. Tañca kho tesu kāruññena, na attano jīvitanikantiyā. Atha tesu gahetabbo vissajjetabboti vivadantesu gahetabboti laddhikā eva bahutarā hutvā jīvitā voropayiṃsu.

Tesaṃ balavaguṇe ariyasāvake aparādhena nibbutadīpasikhā viya akkhīni antaradhāyiṃsu. Te, ‘‘kahaṃ bho cakkhu, kahaṃ bho cakkhū’’ti vippalapantā ekacce ñātakehi gehaṃ nītā. Ekacce noñātakā anāthāti tattheva aṭaviyaṃ rukkhamūle paṇṇasālāyaṃ vasiṃsu. Aṭaviṃ āgatamanussā kāruññena tesaṃ taṇḍulaṃ vā puṭabhattaṃ vā paribbayaṃ vā denti. Dārupaṇṇādīnaṃ atthāya gantvā āgatā manussā kuhiṃ gatatthāti vutte andhavanaṃ gatamhāti vadanti. Evaṃ dvinnampi buddhānaṃ kāle taṃ vanaṃ andhavanaṃtveva paññāyati. Kassapabuddhakāle panetaṃ chaḍḍitajanapade aṭavi ahosi. Amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle sāvatthiyā avidūre jetavanassa piṭṭhibhāge pavivekakāmānaṃ kulaputtānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ padhānagharaṃ ahosi, tattha āyasmā kumārakassapo tena samayena sekhapaṭipadaṃ pūrayamāno viharati. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘andhavane viharatī’’ti.

Aññatarā devatāti nāmagottavasena apākaṭā ekā devatāti attho. ‘‘Abhijānāti no, bhante, bhagavā ahuñātaññatarassa mahesakkhassa saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṃ bhāsitā’’ti (ma. ni. 1.365) ettha pana abhiññāto sakkopi devarājā aññataroti vutto. Devatāti ca idaṃ devānampi devadhītānampi sādhāraṇavacanaṃ. Imasmiṃ panatthe devo adhippeto. Abhikkantāya rattiyāti ettha abhikkantasaddo khayasundarābhirūpaabbhanumodanādīsu dissati. Tattha – ‘‘abhikkantā, bhante, ratti, nikkhanto paṭhamo yāmo, ciranisinno bhikkhusaṅgho, uddisatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkha’’nti evamādīsu (a. ni. 8.20) khaye dissati. ‘‘Ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’’ti (a. ni. 4.100) evamādīsu sundare.

Aññatarā devatā Devatā Abhikkantāya rattiyā

‘‘Ko me vandati pādāni, iddhiyā yasasā jalaṃ;

Abhikkantena vaṇṇena, sabbā obhāsayaṃ disā’’ti. (vi. va. 857) –

Evamādīsu abhirūpe. ‘‘Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotamā’’ti evamādīsu (pārā. 15) abbhanumodane. Idha pana khaye. Tena abhikkantāya rattiyāti parikkhīṇāya rattiyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tatthāyaṃ devaputto majjhimayāmasamanantare āgatoti veditabbo. Abhikkantavaṇṇāti idha abhikkantasaddo abhirūpe. Vaṇṇasaddo pana chavi-thuti-kulavaggakāraṇa-saṇṭhānapamāṇarūpāyatanādīsu dissati. Tattha, ‘‘suvaṇṇavaṇṇosi bhagavā’’ti evamādīsu chaviyā. ‘‘Kadā saññūḷhā pana te gahapati samaṇassa gotamassa vaṇṇā’’ti (ma. ni. 2.77) evamādīsu thutiyaṃ. ‘‘Cattārome, bho gotama, vaṇṇā’’ti evamādīsu (dī. ni. 3.115) kulavagge. ‘‘Atha kena nu vaṇṇena, gandhathenoti vuccatī’’ti evamādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.234) kāraṇe. ‘‘Mahantaṃ hatthirājavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā’’ti evamādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.138) saṇṭhāne. ‘‘Tayo pattassa vaṇṇā’’ti evamādīsu (pārā. 602) pamāṇe. ‘‘Vaṇṇo gandho raso ojā’’ti evamādīsu rūpāyatane. So idha chaviyaṃ daṭṭhabbo. Tena abhikkantavaṇṇāti abhirūpachaviiṭṭhavaṇṇā, manāpavaṇṇāti vuttaṃ hoti. Devatā hi manussalokaṃ āgacchamānā pakativaṇṇaṃ pakatiiddhiṃ pajahitvā oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ katvā atirekavaṇṇaṃ atirekaiddhiṃ māpetvā naṭasamajjādīni gacchantā manussā viya abhisaṅkhatena kāyena āgacchanti. Ayampi devaputto tatheva āgato. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘abhikkantavaṇṇā’’ti.

abhikkantāya rattiyā Abhikkantavaṇṇā abhikkantavaṇṇā

Kevalakappanti ettha kevalasaddo anavasesa-yebhūyya-abyāmissānatirekadaḷhattha-visaṃyogādianekattho. Tathā hissa, ‘‘kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariya’’nti (pārā. 1) evamādīsu anavasesattamattho. ‘‘Kevalakappā ca aṅgamagadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya upasaṅkamissantī’’ti evamādīsu yebhuyyatā. ‘‘Kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī’’ti (vibha. 225) evamādīsu abyāmissatā. ‘‘Kevalaṃ saddhāmattakaṃ nūna ayamāyasmā’’ti (mahāva. 244) evamādīsu anatirekatā. ‘‘Āyasmato anuruddhassa bāhiyo nāma saddhivihāriko kevalakappaṃ saṅghabhedāya ṭhito’’ti (a. ni. 4.243) evamādīsu daḷhatthatā . ‘‘Kevalī vusitavā uttamapurisoti vuccatī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 3.57) evamādīsu visaṃyogo. Idha panassa anavasesattamatthoti adhippeto.

Kevalakappa

Kappasaddo panāyaṃ abhisaddahana-vohāra-kāla-paññatti- chedana-vikappa-lesa-samantabhāvādi-anekattho. Tathā hissa, ‘‘okappaniyametaṃ bhoto gotamassa, yathā taṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’’ti (ma. ni. 1.387) evamādīsu abhisaddahanamattho. ‘‘Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṃ paribhuñjitu’’nti (cūḷava. 250) evamādīsu vohāro. ‘‘Yena sudaṃ niccakappaṃ viharāmī’’ti evamādīsu (ma. ni. 1.387) kālo. ‘‘Iccāyasmā kappo’’ti (saṃ. ni. 3.124) evamādīsu paññatti. ‘‘Alaṅkatā kappitakesamassū’’ti (saṃ. ni. 4.365) evamādīsu chedanaṃ. ‘‘Kappati dvaṅgulakappo’’ti (cūḷava. 446) evamādīsu vikappo. ‘‘Atthi kappo nipajjitu’’nti (a. ni. 8.80) evamādīsu leso. ‘‘Kevalakappaṃ veḷuvanaṃ obhāsetvā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.94) evamādīsu samantabhāvo. Idha panassa samantabhāvo attho adhippeto. Tasmā kevalakappaṃ andhavananti ettha anavasesaṃ samantato andhavananti evamattho daṭṭhabbo.

kevalakappaṃ andhavana

Obhāsetvāti vatthālaṅkārasarīrasamuṭṭhitāya ābhāya pharitvā, candimā viya ca sūriyo viya ca ekobhāsaṃ ekapajjotaṃ karitvāti attho. Ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsīti ekasmiṃ ante, ekasmiṃ okāse aṭṭhāsi. Etadavocāti etaṃ ‘‘bhikkhu bhikkhū’’tiādivacanamavoca. Kasmā panāyaṃ avanditvā samaṇavohāreneva kathetīti? Samaṇasaññāsamudācāreneva. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ antarā kāmāvacare vasi. Ahaṃ pana asmi tato kālato paṭṭhāya brahmacārī’’ti samaṇasaññāvassa samudācarati, tasmā avanditvā samaṇavohāreneva katheti. Pubbasahāyo kireso devaputto therassa. Kuto paṭṭhāyāti? Kassapasammāsambuddhakālato paṭṭhāya. Yo hi pubbayoge āgatesu pañcasu sahāyesu anuthero catutthadivase anāgāmī ahosīti vutto, ayaṃ so. Tadā kira tesu saṅghattherassa arahatteneva saddhiṃ abhiññā āgamiṃsu. So, ‘‘mayhaṃ kiccaṃ matthakaṃ patta’’nti vehāsaṃ uppatitvā anotattadahe mukhaṃ dhovitvā uttarakuruto piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya āgantvā, ‘‘imaṃ, āvuso, piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā appamattā samaṇadhammaṃ karothā’’ti āha. Itare āhaṃsu – ‘‘na, āvuso, amhākaṃ evaṃ katikā atthi – ‘yo paṭhamaṃ visesaṃ nibbattetvā piṇḍapātaṃ āharati, tenābhataṃ bhuñjitvā sesehi samaṇadhammo kātabbo’ti. Tumhe attano upanissayena kiccaṃ matthakaṃ pāpayittha. Mayampi sace no upanissayo bhavissati, kiccaṃ matthakaṃ pāpessāma. Papañco esa amhākaṃ, gacchatha tumhe’’ti. So yathāphāsukaṃ gantvā āyupariyosāne parinibbāyi.

Obhāsetvā Ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsī Etadavocā

Punadivase anuthero anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchakāsi, tassa abhiññāyo āgamiṃsu. Sopi tatheva piṇḍapātaṃ āharitvā tehi paṭikkhitto yathāphāsukaṃ gantvā āyupariyosāne suddhāvāse nibbatti. So suddhāvāse ṭhatvā te sahāye olokento, eko tadāva parinibbuto, eko adhunā bhagavato santike ariyabhūmiṃ patto, eko lābhasakkāraṃ nissāya, ‘‘ahaṃ arahā’’ti cittaṃ uppādetvā suppārakapaṭṭane vasatīti disvā taṃ upasaṅkamitvā, ‘‘na tvaṃ arahā, na arahattamaggaṃ paṭipanno, gaccha bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā dhammaṃ suṇāhī’’ti uyyojesi. Sopi antaraghare bhagavantaṃ ovādaṃ yācitvā, ‘‘tasmā tiha te bāhiya evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ diṭṭhe diṭṭhamattaṃ hotū’’ti (udā. 10) bhagavatā saṃkhittena ovadito ariyabhūmiṃ sampāpuṇi.

Tato añño eko atthi, so kuhinti olokento andhavane sekkhapaṭipadaṃ pūrayamāno viharatīti disvā cintesi – ‘‘sahāyakassa santike gamissāmīti, gacchantena pana tucchahatthena agantvā kiñci paṇṇākāraṃ gahetvā gantuṃ vaṭṭati, sahāyo kho pana me nirāmiso pabbatamatthake vasanto mayā ākāse ṭhatvā dinnaṃ piṇḍapātampi aparibhuñjitvā samaṇadhammaṃ akāsi, idāni āmisapaṇṇākāraṃ kiṃ gaṇhissati? Dhammapaṇṇākāraṃ gahetvā gamissāmī’’ti brahmaloke ṭhitova ratanāvaḷiṃ ganthento viya pannarasa pañhe vibhajitvā taṃ dhammapaṇṇākāraṃ ādāya āgantvā sahāyassa avidūre ṭhatvā attano samaṇasaññāsamudācāravasena taṃ anabhivādetvāva, ‘‘bhikkhu bhikkhū’’ti ālapitvā ayaṃ vammikotiādimāha. Tattha turitālapanavasena bhikkhu bhikkhūti āmeḍitaṃ veditabbaṃ. Yathā vā ekaneva tilakena nalāṭaṃ na sobhati, taṃ parivāretvā aññesupi dinnesu phullitamaṇḍitaṃ viya sobhati, evaṃ ekeneva padena vacanaṃ na sobhati , parivārikapadena saddhiṃ phullitamaṇḍitaṃ viya sobhatīti taṃ parivārikapadavasena vacanaṃ phullitamaṇḍitaṃ viya karontopi evamāha.

ayaṃ vammiko

Ayaṃvammikoti purato ṭhito vammiko nāma natthi, desanāvasena pana purato ṭhitaṃ dassento viya ayanti āha. Laṅginti satthaṃ ādāya khaṇanto palighaṃ addasa. Ukkhipa laṅgiṃ abhikkhaṇa sumedhāti tāta, paṇḍita, laṅgī nāma rattiṃ dhūmāyati divā pajjalati. Ukkhipeta paraṃ parato khaṇāti. Evaṃ sabbapadesu attho daṭṭhabbo. Uddhumāyikanti maṇḍūkaṃ. Caṅkavāranti khāraparissāvanaṃ. Kummanti kacchapaṃ. Asisūnanti maṃsacchedakaṃ asiñceva adhikuṭṭanañca. Maṃsapesinti nisadapotappamāṇaṃ allamaṃsapiṇḍaṃ. Nāganti sumanapupphakalāpasadisaṃ mahāphaṇaṃ tividhasovatthikaparikkhittaṃ ahināgaṃ addasa. Mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesīti daṇḍakakoṭiyā vā vallikoṭiyā vā paṃsucuṇṇaṃ vā pana khipamāno mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭayi. Namo karohi nāgassāti uparivātato apagamma suddhavatthaṃ nivāsetvā nāgassa namakkāraṃ karohi. Nāgena adhisayitaṃ dhanaṃ nāma yāva sattamā kulaparivaṭṭā khādato na khīyati, nāgo te adhisayitaṃ dhanaṃ dassati, tasmā namo karohi nāgassāti. Ito vā pana sutvāti yathā dukkhakkhandhe itoti sāsane nissakaṃ, na tathā idha. Idha pana devaputte nissakkaṃ, tasmā ito vā panāti mama vā pana santikā sutvāti ayamettha attho.

Ayaṃ vammiko aya Laṅgi Ukkhipa laṅgiṃ abhikkhaṇa sumedhā Uddhumāyika Caṅkavāra Kumma Asisūna Maṃsapesi Nāga Mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesī Namo karohi nāgassā Ito vā pana sutvā ito vā panā
commentary_english:
249. Thus have I heard (me suta) from the Vammikasutta. There, the venerable (āyasmā) is a term of affection. “Kumārakassapa” was his name. Because he went forth in his youth (kumārakāle pabbajitattā), the Blessed One (bhagavatā) said, "Call Kassapa, give this fruit or food to Kassapa," and because his name was taken up as "Kumārakassapa," therefore even in old age, he was called "Kumārakassapa." This is what is meant. Moreover, they recognized him as "Kumārakassapa" also because the king raised him as his adopted son (posāvanikaputtattāpi). This is the story of his manifestation from his prior practice:

The elder (thero) was a wealthy man's son (seṭṭhiputto) in the time of the Blessed One Padumuttara. Then, one day, having seen the Blessed One placing one of his disciples, Citrakathi, in a certain position, and having given alms (dānaṃ) to the Blessed One for a week (sattāhaṃ), he made the aspiration (patthanaṃ), "May I also, in the future, be a disciple of a Buddha, a Citrakathi, like this elder (thero viya citrakathī sāvako bhaveyya)," and while performing meritorious deeds (puññāni karonto), he was unable to attain distinction (visesaṃ nibbattetuṃ nāsakkhi) after going forth (pabbajitvā) in the dispensation (sāsane) of the Blessed One Kassapa.

Then, when the dispensation of the Blessed One, who had attained final nirvāṇa (parinibbutassa bhagavato), declined (osakkante), five monks (bhikkhū) built a ladder (nisseṇiṃ bandhitvā), climbed a mountain (pabbataṃ abhiruyha), and practiced the monastic life (samaṇadhammaṃ akaṃsu). The Sangha elder (saṅghatthero) attained arahantship (arahattaṃ patto) on the third day (tatiyadivase). The sub-elder (anuthero) became a non-returner (anāgāmī ahosi) on the fourth day (catutthadivase). The other three, unable to achieve distinction (visesaṃ nibbattetuṃ asakkontā), were reborn in the heaven world (devaloke nibbattiṃsu). Of those (tesaṃ), one (eko), experiencing prosperity (sampattiṃ anubhontānaṃ) among gods (devesu ca) and humans (manussesu ca) for an aeon (buddhantaraṃ), was reborn in a royal family (rājakule nibbattitvā) in Takkasilā, became a king named Pukkusāti (pukkusāti nāma rājā hutvā), went forth (pabbajitvā) having renounced the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ uddissa), and while going to Rājagaha (rājagahaṃ gacchanto), having heard the Blessed One's (bhagavato) teaching of the Dharma (dhammadesanaṃ sutvā) in a potter's shed (kumbhakārasālāyaṃ), attained the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphalaṃ patto). One (eko), having been reborn (nibbattitvā) in a family (kulaghare) in a certain seaport town (samuddapaṭṭane), having boarded a ship (nāvaṃ āruyha), having settled the timber dues of the broken ships (bhinnanāvo dārucīrāni nivāsetvā), attained wealth and prosperity (lābhasampattiṃ patto), and having generated the thought, "I am an arahant (arahā)," was urged by a deity (devatāya codito) who desired his welfare (atthakāmāya), "You are not an arahant, go ask the teacher (satthāraṃ pañhaṃ pucchā)," having done so (tathā katvā), he attained the fruit of arahantship (arahattaphalaṃ patto).

One (eko) was born (uppanno) in Rājagaha in the womb (kucchimhi) of a certain maiden (kuladārikāya). She (sā ca), first (paṭhamaṃ) having asked her parents (mātāpitaro yācitvā) and not obtaining ordination (pabbajjaṃ alabhamānā), having gone to a family home (kulagharaṃ gatā), not even knowing that she was pregnant (gabbhasaṇṭhitampi ajānantī), having pleased her husband (sāmikaṃ ārādhetvā) and being permitted by him (tena anuññātā), went forth among the nuns (bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā). The nuns (bhikkhuniyo), having seen the signs of her pregnancy (gabbhininimittaṃ disvā), asked Devadatta (devadattaṃ pucchiṃsu), and he (so) said, "She is not a samaṇa (assamaṇī)." They asked the One with Ten Powers (dasabalaṃ pucchiṃsu), and the Teacher (satthā) had Upāli, the elder (upālittheraṃ), examine her (paṭicchāpesi). The elder (thero), having had families (kulāni) living in Sāvatthi (sāvatthinagaravāsīni) and Visākha, the female lay follower (upāsikaṃ pakkosāpetvā), summoned and purified her (sodhento), said, "The pregnancy was conceived before (pure laddho gabbho), the going forth is healthy (pabbajjā arogā)." The Teacher (satthā) gave his approval (sādhukāraṃ adāsi) to the elder (therassa), "The case (adhikaraṇa) is well decided (suvinicchitaṃ)." That nun (sā bhikkhunī) gave birth (vijāyi) to a son (puttaṃ) like a golden image (suvaṇṇabimbasadisaṃ), and having taken him (taṃ gahetvā), King (rājā) Pasenadi Kosala raised him (posāpesi). Having named him Kassapa (kassapo’’ti nāmaṃ katvā) and decorating him (alaṅkaritvā) at a later time (aparabhāge), he led him (netvā) to the Teacher's (satthu) presence (santikaṃ) and had him ordained (pabbājesi). Thus (iti), they recognized him as "Kumārakassapa" also because the king raised him as his adopted son (rañño posāvanikaputtattāpi taṃ ‘‘kumārakassapo’’ti sañjāniṃsūti).

Andhavana (andhavane) means in such and such a forest (evaṃnāmake vane). That forest (taṃ kira vanaṃ), in the time of two Buddhas (dvinnaṃ buddhānaṃ kāle), is known as Andhavana (andhavanaṃtveva paññāyati), having not lost its name (avijahitanāmaṃ). There (tatra), this is the exposition of the designation (paññattivibhāvanā) - indeed, the bodily relics (sarīradhātu) of Buddhas with short lifespans (appāyukabuddhānañhi) are not of one mass (na ekagghanā hoti). By the power of their resolution (adhiṭṭhānānubhāvena), they are scattered (vippakiriyati). Just so (teneva), our Blessed One (amhākampi bhagavā) – “I am not long-lasting (na ciraṭṭhitiko), I am seen by few beings (appakehi sattehi ahaṃ diṭṭho), those by whom I am not seen (yehi na diṭṭho), they are more numerous (teva bahutarā), taking my relics (dhātuyo ādāya), worshiping them here and there (tattha tattha pūjentā), they will be destined for heaven (saggaparāyaṇā bhavissantī)” – at the time of final Nirvāṇa (parinibbānakāle), resolved (adhiṭṭhāsi), “May my body (attano sarīraṃ) be scattered (vippakiriyatū)!” However (pana), the bodily relics (dhātusarīraṃ) of Buddhas with long lifespans (dīghāyukabuddhānaṃ) remain (tiṭṭhati) as one mass (ekagghanaṃ), like a golden trunk (suvaṇṇakkhandho viya).

In Andhavana (andhavane), it was the same (tatheva aṭṭhāsi) for the Blessed One Kassapa (kassapassāpi bhagavato).
Then, the great multitude gathered together and, having conferred, [said:] "The relics are solid and cannot be separated; what shall we do?" Having agreed, they [said:] "We will build a solid *cetiya*. How large should it be?"

Some said, "Seven *yojanas*."

"That is too large, it will be impossible to maintain in the future. Let it be six *yojanas*, five *yojanas*... four *yojanas*... three *yojanas*... two *yojanas*... one *yojana*," having made this decision, [they asked:] "What should the bricks be like?" The bricks on the outside should be of red-gold, solid, and worth one hundred thousand, and the bricks on the inside worth fifty thousand.

"Let the work on the clay be done with *haritāla* and *manosila*, and the work on the water with oil," having come to a conclusion, they divided the four faces into four parts.

The king took one face, the king's son Pathavindarakumāra took one, the eldest of the ministers, having become a general, took one, and the eldest of the regions, having become a merchant, took one.

There, because of the abundance of wealth, the king also, having had gold extracted, began the work with his own hand at the face he had taken; the sub-king also, and the general also.

But the work at the face taken by the merchant was delayed.

Then a lay follower named Yasorato, a master of the three baskets (*tepiṭaka*), a reciter (*bhāṇaka*), a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), a noble disciple (*ariyasāvako*), knowing that the work was delayed, having harnessed five hundred carts, went to the district and [announced:] "Kassapasammāsambuddho, having lived for twenty thousand years, attained *parinirvāṇa*.

A *ratanacetiya* measuring one *yojana* should be made for him. Whoever can afford to give gold, or silver, or the seven jewels (*sattaratana*), or *haritāla*, or *manosila*, let him give it," thus he exhorted them.

People gave gold, silver, and so on, according to their own ability.

Those who could not afford it gave oil, rice, and so on.

The lay follower sends oil, rice, and so on for the food and wages of the workers, and having had gold bought with the remainder, he sends it. Thus, he traveled throughout all of *Jambudvīpa*.

Having finished the work on the *cetiya*, they sent a letter from the site of the *cetiya*: "The work is finished, let the teacher come and worship the *cetiya*."

He also sent a letter: "I have exhorted all of *Jambudvīpa*, whatever there is, having taken that, let them finish the work."

Both letters met on the way.

The letter from the site of the *cetiya*, however, reached the teacher's hand earlier than the letter from the teacher.

Having had the letter read, he left alone, thinking, "I will worship the *cetiya*."

On the way, in the forest, five hundred thieves arose.

There, some, seeing him, [said:] "This man has gathered gold and silver from all of *Jambudvīpa*, a treasure pot that does not continue [to be depleted] has come," and having announced it to the others, they seized him.

"Why, fathers, do you seize me?" [he asked.] "You have gathered all the gold and silver from all of *Jambudvīpa*, give us a little bit too."

"Do you not know that Kassapa, the Blessed One, has attained *parinirvāṇa*, and a *ratanacetiya* measuring one *yojana* is being made for him? For that purpose, I have exhorted [people], not for my own purpose.

That, that was sent from each place where it was obtained, but for me, having left only a wearing cloth, there is not even a *kākaṇika* of other wealth."

Some [said:] "In this way, release this teacher."

Some [said:] "This man, honored by the king and honored by the ministers, if some of us see him in the city street, they will announce it to the king, the great ministers, and so on, and we will incur misfortune."

The lay follower [said,] "Fathers, I will not do that."

And that [was done] out of compassion for them, not out of a desire to save his own life.

Then, while they were disputing whether he should be seized or released, the robbers, having become more numerous, took his life.

Due to the offense against that noble disciple who possessed great virtue, their eyes vanished like the flame of an extinguished lamp.

Those, exclaiming, "Where, sirs, [are our] eyes? Where, sirs, [are our] eyes?" some were taken home by relatives.

Some, being unknown and helpless, lived there in the forest at the foot of a tree in a leaf hut.
People who come to the forest (aṭaviṃ) give rice grains (taṇḍulaṃ), packed meals (puṭabhattaṃ), or necessary provisions (paribbayaṃ) to them out of compassion (kāruññena). People who have gone and returned for the sake of wood, leaves, etc. (dārupaṇṇādīnaṃ atthāya), when asked, "Where did you go?", say, "We went to the Dark Forest (andhavanaṃ)." Thus, even in the time of two Buddhas (dvinnampi buddhānaṃ), that forest was known as the Dark Forest (andhavanaṃtveva paññāyati). However, in the time of Kassapa Buddha (kassapabuddhakāle), this (etaṃ) was a forest (aṭavi) in an abandoned district (chaḍḍitajanapade). In the time of our Blessed One (amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle), near Sāvatthī (sāvatthiyā avidūre), behind Jetavana (jetavanassa piṭṭhibhāge), it was a dwelling place (vasanaṭṭhānaṃ) and a principal house (padhānagharaṃ) for noble men (kulaputtānaṃ) who desired solitude (pavivekakāmānaṃ). There, at that time (tena samayena), the venerable Kumārakassapa (āyasmā kumārakassapo) lived (viharati), fulfilling the training of a learner (sekhapaṭipadaṃ pūrayamāno). Therefore (tena), it was said (vuttaṃ), "He dwells (viharati) in the Dark Forest (andhavane)."

Furthermore (aññatarā devatā), "a certain (aññatarā) deity (devatā)" means (attho) one deity (ekā devatāti), not manifest (apākaṭā) by name and clan (nāmagottavasena). But in (ettha pana) "Does the Blessed One remember (abhijānāti no, bhante, bhagavā) stating in brief (saṃkhittena) - to a certain one (ahuñātaññatarassa) of the renowned (mahesakkhassa) spirits - deliverance (vimuttiṃ) through the destruction of craving (taṇhāsaṅkhaya)?" (ma. ni. 1.365), even Sakka (sakkopi), king of the gods (devarājā), who is well-known (abhiññāto), is called (vutto) "a certain one (aññataro)." And this word (idaṃ) "deity (devatā)" is a general term (sādhāraṇavacanaṃ) common to (deities) gods (devānampi) and goddesses (devadhītānampi). But in this context (imasmiṃ panatthe), "god (devo)" is intended (adhippeto).

In this connection (ettha), "in the night's last extreme (abhikkantāya rattiyā)," the word (saddo) "abhikkanta" is seen (dissati) in the senses of exhaustion (khaya), beautiful (sundara), pleasing (abhirūpa), agreement (abbhanumodanā), and so on (ādīsu). There (tattha), in such passages as (evamādīsu) "Venerable sir (bhante), the night is nearing its last extreme (abhikkantā, bhante, ratti), the first watch (paṭhamo yāmo) is ending (nikkhanto), the Community of bhikkhus (bhikkhusaṅgho) has been sitting long (cirasinno), venerable sir (bhante), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) recite (uddisatu) the Rule (pātimokkha) to the bhikkhus (bhikkhūnaṃ)" (a. ni. 8.20), it is seen (dissati) in the sense of exhaustion (khaye). In such passages as (evamādīsu) "This (ayaṃ) is the most outstanding (abhikkantataro) and superior (ca paṇītataro) of those four (imesaṃ catunnaṃ) persons (puggalānaṃ)" (a. ni. 4.100), it is in the sense of beautiful (sundare).
