"Whose (ko) feet (pādāni) do I worship (vandati), shining (jalaṃ) with power (iddhiyā) and glory (yasasā); illuminating (obhāsayaṃ) all (sabbā) directions (disā) with pleasing (abhikkantena) complexion (vaṇṇena)?" (vi. va. 857), in such passages (evamādīsu) it is in the sense of pleasing (abhirūpe). In such passages as (evamādīsu) "Magnificent (abhikkantaṃ), good Gotama (bho gotamā)!" (pārā. 15), it is in the sense of agreement (abbhanumodane). Here (idha pana), however, it is in the sense of exhaustion (khaye). Therefore (tena), "in the night's last extreme (abhikkantāya rattiyā)" means (vuttaṃ hoti) "when the night was becoming exhausted (parikkhīṇāya rattiyā)." Here (tattha), this (ayaṃ) young god (devaputto) came (āgato) immediately after the middle watch of the night (majjhimayāmasamanantare) - this should be understood (veditabbo). "Of pleasing complexion (abhikkantavaṇṇā)" here (idha), the word (saddo) "abhikkanta" is in the sense of pleasing (abhirūpe). The word (saddo) "complexion (vaṇṇa)" is seen (dissati) in the senses of skin (chavi), praise (thuti), clan (kula), class (vagga), cause (kāraṇa), shape (saṇṭhāna), measure (pamāṇa), form as a sense object (rūpāyatana), and so on (ādīsu). There (tattha), in such passages as (evamādīsu), "Blessed One (bhagavā), thou art gold-complexioned (suvaṇṇavaṇṇosi)" it is in the sense of skin (chaviyā).
"When did you concoct that hymn of praise to the recluse Gotama, householder?" In such passages, it is eulogy.

"There are these four castes, Master Gotama." In such passages, it is a group of clans.

"Then by what token can one tell a man to be a thief of scents?" In such passages, it is a reason.

"Having created the appearance of a huge royal elephant." In such passages, it is shape.

"The three sizes for a bowl." In such passages, it is measure.

"Colour, odour, flavour, nutritive-essence." In such passages, it is the visible-form base (rūpāyatana).

Here it should be understood as skin (chavi).

Therefore, "of surpassing colour" means of handsome skin, of pleasing colour, it is said.

Gods, when coming to the human world, having abandoned their natural colour (pakativaṇṇa) and natural power (pakatiiddhi), and having created a coarse physical form (oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ), having fashioned an exceeding colour (atirekavaṇṇaṃ) and exceeding power (atirekaiddhiṃ), when going to theatrical performances and so on, they come with a body fashioned like humans.

This young deva (devaputto) also came just like that.

Therefore it was said, "Of surpassing colour (abhikkantavaṇṇā)."

Of surpassing night.

Of surpassing colour. Of surpassing colour.

In this connection, the word *kevala* ("entire, whole") has various meanings such as: remainderlessness (anavasesa), the most part (yebhuyya), unmixedness (abyāmissa), nothing extra (anatireka), firmness (daḷhattha), dissociation (visaṃyoga), and so on.

For in such passages as, "A Divine Life as utterly perfect and pure (*kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariya*)," the meaning is remainderlessness (*anavasesattamattho*).

"The whole of Aṅga and Magadha will come bringing quantities of food" In such passages, it is the most part (*yebhuyyatā*).

"Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering (*kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti*)." In such passages, it is unmixedness (*abyāmissatā*).

"Surely it is only by mere faith that this venerable one (*kevalaṃ saddhāmattakaṃ nūna ayamāyasmā*)." In such passages, it is with nothing extra (*anatirekatā*).

"This co-resident of the venerable Anuruddha's named Bāhika has taken his stand entirely for the schism in the Community (*āyasmato anuruddhassa bāhiyo nāma saddhivihāriko kevalakappaṃ saṅghabhedāya ṭhito*)." In such passages, it is firmness (*daḷhatthatā*).

"One who has reached the absolute (kevalī), lived out the life, is called the Supreme Man (*uttamapuriso*)."

4.  57) In such passages, *visaṃyoga* (separation) [is meant].
Here, however, the meaning intended is remainderlessness (*anavasesatta*).

kevalakappa

The word *kappa*, however, has many meanings, such as: adherence, convention, time, designation, cutting, option, a little, all-aroundness, and so on.

Thus, in passages such as, "This is acceptable to the venerable Gotama, as [it is] for the *Arhat*, the Perfectly Enlightened One" (*okappaniyametaṃ bhoto gotamassa, yathā taṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā*), the meaning is adherence.

In passages such as, "I allow you, monks, to partake of fruit that is allowable for monastics for any of five reasons" (*anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṃ paribhuñjituṃ*), it is convention.

In passages such as, "In which I constantly abide" (*yena sudaṃ niccakappaṃ viharāmi*), it is time.

In passages such as, "Thus venerable Kappa" (*iccāyasmā kappo*), it is designation.

In passages such as, "Adorned, with hair and beard trimmed" (*alaṅkatā kappitakesamassū*), it is cutting.

In passages such as, "A two-finger length is allowable" (*kappati dvaṅgulakappo*), it is option.

In passages such as, "There is a place to lie down" (*atthi kappo nipajjituṃ*), it is a little.

In passages such as, "Having illuminated the entire bamboo grove" (*kevalakappaṃ veḷuvanaṃ obhāsetvā*), it is all-aroundness.

Here, however, the meaning intended is all-aroundness (*samantabhāva*).

Therefore, in *kevalakappaṃ andhavanaṃ* (entire Andhavana), the meaning should be understood as: *anavasesaṃ samantato andhavananti*, the entire Andhavana all around.
0032"/> *Kevalakappaṃ andhavana*: *Obhāsetvā* means pervading with radiance by the light arising from the cloth, ornaments, and body; the meaning is ‘having made all into one glow, all into one illumination.’
*Ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsī*: He stood at one side, in one place, he stood.
*Etadavocā*: This means he spoke the words beginning "monk, monks."
Why does he speak in the way of a *śramaṇa* without venerating? [It is] only by the behavior of a *śramaṇa*-perception.
Thus, it occurred to him, "This one dwells amidst desires.
But I am a *brahmacārī* from that time onward," he behaves with the perception of a *śramaṇa*, therefore he speaks in the way of a *śramaṇa* without venerating.
He was a former friend, a *devaputra* of the *thera*.
From where onward? From the time of the *kassapasammāsambuddha*.
Indeed, among the five friends who came in the former yoga, the *anuthera* became a *anāgāmī* on the fourth day, that one is he.
Then, it seems, the *abhiññā* came to the *saṅghatthera* together with the *arhatship*.
He, "My task is accomplished," rising up into the sky, washing his face in Lake Anotatta, taking alms from Uttarakuru, coming, said, "Having eaten this alms food, be diligent, do the *śramaṇa*-dharma."
The others said, "No, friend, we do not have such an agreement: 'Whoever first
0032"/> brings alms having created a distinction, having eaten what is brought by him, the *śramaṇa*-dharma should be done with the remainder.'"
You have brought the task to completion by means of your
0033"/> support.
If we also have a support, we will bring the task to completion.
This is a proliferation for us, you go."
He, having gone as was comfortable, at the end of his life, attained *parinirvāṇa*.

*Obhāsetvā, ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsī, etadavocā*

0127"/>
0033"/> On the next day, the *anuthera* realized the fruit of *anāgāmī*, the *abhiññā* came to him.
He also, having brought alms in the same way, being rejected by them, having gone as was comfortable, at the end of his life, was born in *śuddhāvāsa*.
He, staying in *śuddhāvāsa*, looking at those friends, one had attained *parinirvāṇa* at that time, one had now attained the noble ground near the *bhagavat*, one, relying on gain and honor, generating the thought, "I am an *arhat*," dwelling in Suppāraka, seeing him, approaching him, exhorted, "You are not an *arhat*, you have not entered the path of *arhatship*, go, approaching the *bhagavat*, hear the dharma."
He also, in the inner chamber, requesting instruction from the *bhagavat*, "Therefore, here, for you, Bāhiya, thus should be trained: in the seen, let there be only the seen" (udā.
10), being instructed by the *bhagavat* in brief, attained the noble ground.

Then, there is another one, he, looking around, "Where is he?" seeing him dwelling in Andhavana, fulfilling the *śaikṣa*-practice, thought, "I will go to the friend," but going with empty hands without bringing any gift, it is fitting to go, but my friend, being desireless, dwelling on the summit of the mountain, even not consuming the alms given by me standing in the sky, did the *śramaṇa*-dharma, now what will he take as a gift of desire? Taking a gift of *dharma* I will go," in the Brahma world, as if stringing a garland of jewels, dividing the fifteen questions, taking that gift of *dharma*, coming, standing not far from the friend, by means of his own behavior of a *śramaṇa*-perception, without venerating him, addressing him, "Monk, monks," said the words beginning *ayaṃ vammiko*.
There, by means of hurried address, *bhikkhu bhikkhūti* should be understood as reiterated.
Just as, indeed, the forehead does not shine by only one mark, surrounding it, when others are given, it shines like something flowered and ornamented, so, indeed, speech does not shine by only one word,

0128"/> with a surrounding word,
0034"/> as if making the speech flowered and ornamented, he said thus.

*Ayaṃ vammiko*
0128"/>
0034"/> *Ayaṃ vammiko*: There is no *vammika* named standing in front, but by way of teaching, as if showing what is standing in front, he said *ayaṃ*.
*Laṅgi*: Taking a knife, digging, he saw a beam.
*Ukkhipa laṅgiṃ abhikkhaṇa sumedhā*: Father, wise one, a *laṅgi* smokes at night, blazes by day.
Having lifted up, he digs beyond what is far.
Thus, the meaning should be seen in all the words.
*Uddhumāyika* means frog.
*Caṅkavāra* means a strainer for alkaline liquid.
*Kumma* means tortoise.
*Asisūna* means a meat cleaver, both a knife and an additional chopper.
*Maṃsapesi* means a lump of raw meat the size of a *nisadapotappa*.
*Nāga* means he saw a snake (*ahi-nāga*) with a great hood resembling a collection of *sumana* flowers, adorned with three kinds of auspicious signs (*tividhasovatthika*).
"*Mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesī*" means do not strike the *nāga* while scattering dust with the tip of a stick or the tip of a creeper.
"*Namo karohi nāgassā*" means after moving away from the updraft, dress in clean clothes and pay homage to the *nāga*.
The wealth deposited by the *nāga* does not diminish as long as seven generations of families eat it. The *nāga* will give you the deposited wealth, therefore, pay homage to the *nāga*.
"*Ito vā pana sutvā*" means just as in the teaching, it is certain that the aggregate of suffering is from here, but not so here.
Here, however, there is certainty regarding the sons of the gods, therefore, "*ito vā panā*" means having heard from me or from my presence, this is the meaning here.

*Ayaṃ*

*Vammiko*, *ayaṃ*, *laṅgi*, *ukkhipa laṅgiṃ abhikkhaṇa sumedhā*, *uddhumāyika*, *caṅkavāra*, *kumma*, *asisūna*, *maṃsapesi*, *nāga*, *mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesī*, *namo karohi nāgassā*, *ito vā pana sutvā*, *ito vā panā*

mula_pali: 250. Atha kho āyasmā kumārakassapo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā kumārakassapo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘imaṃ, bhante, rattiṃ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ andhavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho, bhante, sā devatā maṃ etadavoca – ‘bhikkhu bhikkhu, ayaṃ vammiko rattiṃ dhūmāyati, divā pajjalati’. Brāhmaṇo evamāha – ‘abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyā’ti. Abhikkhaṇanto sumedho satthaṃ ādāya…pe… ito vā pana sutvāti. Idamavoca, bhante, sā devatā. Idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi. ‘Ko nu kho, bhante, vammiko, kā rattiṃ dhūmāyanā, kā divā pajjalanā, ko brāhmaṇo, ko sumedho, kiṃ satthaṃ, kiṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ, kā laṅgī, kā uddhumāyikā, ko dvidhāpatho, kiṃ caṅgavāraṃ, ko kummo, kā asisūnā , kā maṃsapesi, ko nāgo’’’ti?
mula_english:
Then, the venerable Kumārakassapa, when the night had passed, went to where the Blessed One was; having approached, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the venerable Kumārakassapa said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, a certain *devatā*, of surpassing radiance, having illuminated the entire Andhavana forest, approached me during the night, and having approached, stood to one side. Standing to one side, venerable sir, that *devatā* said this to me: 'O *bhikkhu*, O *bhikkhu*, this anthill smokes by night and blazes by day.'

A *brāhmaṇa* spoke thus: 'Dig, O wise one, taking the knife.' The wise one digs, taking the knife... after having heard it from here.

That *devatā* said this, venerable sir. Having said this, it vanished immediately.

'What, venerable sir, is the anthill (*vammiko*)? What is the night's smoking (*rattiṃ dhūmāyanā*)? What is the day's blazing (*divā pajjalanā*)? What is the *brāhmaṇa*? What is the wise one (*sumedha*)? What is the knife (*satthaṃ*)? What is the digging (*abhikkhaṇaṃ*)? What is the ploughshare (*laṅgī*)? What is the smoking ashes (*uddhumāyikā*)? What is the forked path (*dvidhāpatho*)? What is the sieve (*caṅgavāraṃ*)? What is the tortoise (*kummo*)? What is the cleaver (*asisūnā*)? What is the lump of meat (*maṃsapesi*)? What is the *nāga* (serpent or excellent one)?'"

mula_pali:
251. ‘‘‘Vammiko’ti kho, bhikkhu, imassetaṃ cātumahābhūtikassa cātummahābhūtikassa (sī. syā. pī.) kāyassa adhivacanaṃ, mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādana-parimaddanabhedana-viddhaṃsana-dhammassa.

‘‘Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, divā kammante kammantaṃ (ka.) ārabbha rattiṃ anuvitakketi anuvicāreti – ayaṃ rattiṃ dhūmāyanā. Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, rattiṃ anuvitakketvā anuvicāretvā divā kammante payojeti kāyena vācāya ‘manasā’ ( ) natthi (sī. syā.) – ayaṃ divā pajjalanā.

kammantaṃ (ka.) ( ) natthi (sī. syā.)

‘‘‘Brāhmaṇo’ti kho, bhikkhu, tathāgatassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. ‘Sumedho’ti kho bhikkhu sekkhassetaṃ bhikkhuno adhivacanaṃ.

‘‘‘Sattha’nti kho, bhikkhu, ariyāyetaṃ paññāya adhivacanaṃ. ‘Abhikkhaṇa’nti kho, bhikkhu, vīriyārambhassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

‘‘‘Laṅgī’ti kho, bhikkhu, avijjāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa laṅgiṃ, pajaha avijjaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

‘‘‘Uddhumāyikā’ti kho, bhikkhu, kodhūpāyāsassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa uddhumāyikaṃ, pajaha kodhūpāyāsaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

‘‘‘Dvidhāpatho’ti kho, bhikkhu, vicikicchāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa dvidhāpathaṃ, pajaha vicikicchaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

‘‘‘Caṅgavāra’nti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kāmacchandanīvaraṇassa, byāpādanīvaraṇassa, thīnamiddhanīvaraṇassa, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇassa, vicikicchānīvaraṇassa. Ukkhipa caṅgavāraṃ, pajaha pañca nīvaraṇe ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

‘‘‘Kummo’ti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ adhivacanaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandhassa, vedanupādānakkhandhassa, saññupādānakkhandhassa, saṅkhārupādānakkhandhassa, viññāṇupādānakkhandhassa. Ukkhipa kummaṃ, pajaha pañcupādānakkhandhe; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

‘‘‘Asisūnā’ti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ – cakkhuviññeyyānaṃ rūpānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ piyarūpānaṃ kāmūpasaṃhitānaṃ rajanīyānaṃ, sotaviññeyyānaṃ saddānaṃ…pe… ghānaviññeyyānaṃ gandhānaṃ…pe… jivhāviññeyyānaṃ rasānaṃ…pe… kāyaviññeyyānaṃ phoṭṭhabbānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ piyarūpānaṃ kāmūpasaṃhitānaṃ rajanīyānaṃ. Ukkhipa asisūnaṃ, pajaha pañca kāmaguṇe; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

‘‘‘Maṃsapesī’ti kho, bhikkhu, nandīrāgassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Ukkhipa maṃsapesiṃ, pajaha nandīrāgaṃ; abhikkhaṇa, sumedha, satthaṃ ādāyāti ayametassa attho.

‘‘‘Nāgo’ti kho, bhikkhu, khīṇāsavassetaṃ bhikkhuno adhivacanaṃ. Tiṭṭhatu nāgo, mā nāgaṃ ghaṭṭesi; namo karohi nāgassāti ayametassa attho’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā kumārakassapo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Vammikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
251. “Bhikkhu, the ant-hill is a symbol for this body (kāya), made of material form (cātumahābhūtika), consisting of the four great elements (mahābhūta), procreated by a mother and father (mātāpettikasambhava), built up out of boiled rice and porridge (odanakummāsūpacaya), and subject to impermanence (anicca), to being worn and rubbed away (ucchādana-parimaddana), to dissolution and disintegration (bhedana-viddhaṃsana-dhamma).

“What one thinks and ponders by night based upon one’s actions during the day is the ‘fuming by night.’

“The actions one undertakes during the day by body, speech, and mind after thinking and pondering by night is the ‘flaming by day.’

“The *brāhmaṇa* (brāhmaṇa) is a symbol for the *Tathāgata*, accomplished and fully enlightened (*arahato sammāsambuddhassa*). The wise one (*sumedha*) is a symbol for a *bhikkhu* in higher training (*sekkhassa bhikkhuno*).

“The knife (*sattha*) is a symbol for noble wisdom (*ariyāya paññāya*). The delving (*abhikkhaṇa*) is a symbol for the arousing of energy (*vīriyārambhassa*).

“The bar (*laṅgī*) is a symbol for ignorance (*avijjāya*). Throw out the bar: abandon ignorance (*avijjaṃ*). Delve with the knife, thou wise one (*sumedha*).’ This is the meaning.

“The toad (*uddhumāyikā*) is a symbol for the despair due to anger (*kodhūpāyāsassa*). Throw out the toad: abandon despair due to anger (*kodhūpāyāsaṃ*). Delve with the knife, thou wise one (*sumedha*).’ This is the meaning.

“The forked path (*dvidhāpatho*) is a symbol for doubt (*vicikicchāya*). Throw out the forked path: abandon doubt (*vicikicchaṃ*). Delve with the knife, thou wise one (*sumedha*).’ This is the meaning.

“The sieve (*caṅgavāra*) is a symbol for the five hindrances (*pañcannetaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ*), namely: the hindrance of sensual desire (*kāmacchandanīvaraṇassa*), the hindrance of ill-will (*byāpādanīvaraṇassa*), the hindrance of sloth and torpor (*thīnamiddhanīvaraṇassa*), the hindrance of restlessness and remorse (*uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇassa*), the hindrance of doubt (*vicikicchānīvaraṇassa*). Throw out the sieve: abandon the five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇe*). Delve with the knife, thou wise one (*sumedha*).’ This is the meaning.

“The tortoise (*kummo*) is a symbol for the five aggregates affected by clinging (*pañcannetaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ*), namely: the aggregate of form affected by clinging (*rūpupādānakkhandhassa*), the aggregate of feeling affected by clinging (*vedanupādānakkhandhassa*), the aggregate of perception affected by clinging (*saññupādānakkhandhassa*), the aggregate of mental formations affected by clinging (*saṅkhārupādānakkhandhassa*), and the aggregate of consciousness affected by clinging (*viññāṇupādānakkhandhassa*). Throw out the tortoise: abandon the five aggregates affected by clinging (*pañcupādānakkhandhe*). Delve with the knife, thou wise one (*sumedha*).’ This is the meaning.

“The axe and block (*asisūnā*) is a symbol for the five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ*) – forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for (*iṭṭhānaṃ*), desired (*kantānaṃ*), agreeable (*manāpānaṃ*), pleasing (*piyarūpānaṃ*), connected with sensual pleasure (*kāmūpasaṃhitānaṃ*), and enticing (*rajanīyānaṃ*); sounds cognizable by the ear…pe… scents cognizable by the nose…pe… tastes cognizable by the tongue…pe… tactile objects cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual pleasure, and enticing. Throw out the axe and block: abandon the five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañca kāmaguṇe*). Delve with the knife, thou wise one (*sumedha*).’ This is the meaning.
"‘A piece of meat’ ( *maṃsapesī*), O monk, is a designation for delight and lust ( *nandīrāga*).
Throw out the piece of meat ( *maṃsapesī*): abandon delight and lust ( *nandīrāga*). Delve with the knife, thou wise one.’ This is the meaning.

‘*Nāga*,’ O monk, is a designation for the monk whose outflows are ended (*khīṇāsava*).
Leave the *Nāga*; do not harm the *Nāga*; honour the *Nāga*.’ This is the meaning.”

The Blessed One said this.
The venerable Kumāra Kassapa was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Vammika Sutta, the third, is finished.
commentary_pali:
251.Cātummahābhūtikassāti catumahābhūtamayassa. Kāyassetaṃ adhivacananti sarīrassa nāmaṃ. Yatheva hi bāhirako vammiko, vamatīti vantakoti vantussayoti vantasinehasambandhoti catūhi kāraṇehi vammikoti vuccati. So hi ahimaṅgusaundūragharagoḷikādayo nānappakāre pāṇake vamatīti vammiko. Upacikāhi vantakoti vammiko. Upacikāhi vamitvā mukhatuṇḍakena ukkhittapaṃsucuṇṇena kaṭippamāṇenapi porisappamāṇenapi ussitoti vammiko. Upacikāhi vantakheḷasinehena ābaddhatāya sattasattāhaṃ deve vassantepi na vippakiriyati, nidāghepi tato paṃsumuṭṭhiṃ gahetvā tasmiṃ muṭṭhinā pīḷiyamāne sineho nikkhamati, evaṃ vantasinehena sambaddhoti vammiko. Evamayaṃ kāyopi, ‘‘akkhimhā akkhigūthako’’tiādinā nayena nānappakārakaṃ asucikalimalaṃ vamatīti vammiko. Buddhapaccekabuddhakhīṇāsavā imasmiṃ attabhāve nikantipariyādānena attabhāvaṃ chaḍḍetvā gatāti ariyehi vantakotipi vammiko. Yehi cāyaṃ tīhi aṭṭhisatehi ussito nhārusambaddho maṃsāvalepano allacammapariyonaddho chavirañjito satte vañceti, taṃ sabbaṃ ariyehi vantamevāti vantussayotipi vammiko. ‘‘Taṇhā janeti purisaṃ, cittamassa vidhāvatī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.55) evaṃ taṇhāya janitattā ariyehi vanteneva taṇhāsinehena sambaddho ayanti vantasinehena sambaddhotipi vammiko. Yathā ca vammikassa anto nānappakārā pāṇakā tattheva jāyanti, uccārapassāvaṃ karonti, gilānā sayanti, matā patanti. Iti so tesaṃ sūtigharaṃ vaccakuṭi gilānasālā susānañca hoti. Evaṃ khattiyamahāsālādīnampi kāyo ayaṃ gopitarakkhito maṇḍitappasādhito mahānubhāvānaṃ kāyoti acintetvā chavinissitā pāṇā cammanissitā pāṇā maṃsanissitā pāṇā nhārunissitā pāṇā aṭṭhinissitā pāṇā aṭṭhimiñjanissitā pāṇāti evaṃ kulagaṇanāya asītimattāni kimikulasahassāni antokāyasmiṃyeva jāyanti, uccārapassāvaṃ karonti, gelaññena āturitāni sayanti, matāni patanti, iti ayampi tesaṃ pāṇānaṃ sūtigharaṃ vaccakuṭi gilānasālā susānañca hotīti ‘‘vammiko’’ tveva saṅkhaṃ gato. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘vammikoti kho, bhikkhu, imassa cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassetaṃ adhivacana’’nti.

Mātāpettikasambhavassāti mātito ca pitito ca nibbattena mātāpettikena sukkasoṇitena sambhūtassa. Odanakummāsūpacayassāti odanena ceva kummāsena ca upacitassa vaḍḍhitassa. Aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammassāti ettha ayaṃ kāyo hutvā abhāvaṭṭhena aniccadhammo. Duggandhavighātatthāya tanuvilepanena ucchādanadhammo. Aṅgapaccaṅgābādhavinodanatthāya khuddakasambāhanena parimaddanadhammo. Daharakāle vā ūrūsu sayāpetvā gabbhavāsena dussaṇṭhitānaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ aṅgānaṃ saṇṭhānasampādanatthaṃ añchanapīḷanādivasena parimaddanadhammo. Evaṃ pariharatopi ca bhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo bhijjati ceva vikirati ca, evaṃ sabhāvoti attho. Tattha mātāpettikasambhavaodanakummāsūpacayaucchādanaparimaddanapadehi samudayo kathito, aniccabhedaviddhaṃsanapadehi atthaṅgamo. Evaṃ sattahipi padehi cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa uccāvacabhāvo vaḍḍhiparihāni samudayatthaṅgamo kathitoti veditabbo.

Mātāpettikasambhavassā Odanakummāsūpacayassā Aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammassā aniccadhammo ucchādanadhammo parimaddanadhammo

Divā kammanteti divā kattabbakammante. Dhūmāyanāti ettha ayaṃ dhūmasaddo kodhe taṇhāya vitakke pañcasu kāmaguṇesu dhammadesanāya pakatidhūmeti imesu atthesu vattati. ‘‘Kodho dhūmo bhasmanimosavajja’’nti (saṃ. ni. 1.165) ettha hi kodhe vattati. ‘‘Icchādhūmāyitā sattā’’ti ettha taṇhāya. ‘‘Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bhagavato avidūre dhūmāyanto nisinno hotī’’ti ettha vitakke.

Divā kammante Dhūmāyanā

‘‘Paṅko ca kāmā palipo ca kāmā,

Bhayañca metaṃ timūlaṃ pavuttaṃ;

Rajo ca dhūmo ca mayā pakāsitā;

Hitvā tuvaṃ pabbaja brahmadattā’’ti. (jā. 1.6.14) –

Ettha pañcakāmaguṇesu. ‘‘Dhūmaṃ kattā hotī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.349) ettha dhammadesanāya. ‘‘Dhajo rathassa paññāṇaṃ, dhūmo paññāṇamaggino’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.72) ettha pakatidhūme. Idha panāyaṃ vitakke adhippeto. Tenāha ‘‘ayaṃ rattiṃ dhūmāyanā’’ti.

Tathāgatassetaṃ adhivacananti tathāgato hi sattannaṃ dhammānaṃ bāhitattā brāhmaṇo nāma. Yathāha – ‘‘sattannaṃ kho, bhikkhu, dhammānaṃ bāhitattā brāhmaṇo. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Rāgo bāhito hoti, doso… moho… māno… sakkāyadiṭṭhi… vicikicchā… sīlabbataparāmāso bāhito hoti. Imesaṃ bhikkhu sattannaṃ dhammānaṃ bāhitattā brāhmaṇo’’ti (cūḷani. mettagūmāṇavapucchāniddesa 28). Sumedhoti sundarapañño. Sekkhassāti ettha sikkhatīti sekkho. Yathāha – ‘‘sikkhatīti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā sekkhoti vuccati. Kiñca sikkhati? Adhisīlampi sikkhati, adhicittampi sikkhati, adhipaññampi sikkhatī’’ti (a. ni. 3.86).

Tathāgatassetaṃ adhivacana brāhmaṇo Sumedho Sekkhassā

Paññāyaadhivacananti lokiyalokuttarāya paññāya etaṃ adhivacanaṃ, na āvudhasatthassa. Vīriyārambhassāti kāyikacetasikavīriyassa. Taṃ paññāgatikameva hoti. Lokiyāya paññāya lokiyaṃ, lokuttarāya paññāya lokuttaraṃ. Ettha panāyaṃ atthadīpanā –

Paññāya adhivacana Vīriyārambhassā

Eko kira jānapado brāhmaṇo pātova māṇavakehi saddhiṃ gāmato nikkhamma divasaṃ araññe mante vācetvā sāyaṃ gāmaṃ āgacchati. Antarāmagge ca eko vammiko atthi. So rattiṃ dhūmāyati, divā pajjalati. Brāhmaṇo antevāsiṃ sumedhaṃ māṇavaṃ āha – ‘‘tāta, ayaṃ vammiko rattiṃ dhūmāyati, divā pajjalati, vikāramassa passissāma, bhinditvā naṃ cattāro koṭṭhāse katvā khipāhī’’ti. So sādhūti kudālaṃ gahetvā samehi pādehi pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya tathā akāsi. Tatra ācariyabrāhmaṇo viya bhagavā. Sumedhamāṇavako viya sekkho bhikkhu. Vammiko viya kāyo. ‘‘Tāta, ayaṃ vammiko rattiṃ dhūmāyati, divā pajjalati, vikāramassa passissāma, bhinditvā naṃ cattāro koṭṭhāse katvā khipāhī’’ti brāhmaṇena vuttakālo viya, ‘‘bhikkhu cātumahābhūtikaṃ kāyaṃ cattāro koṭṭhāse katvā pariggaṇhāhī’’ti bhagavatā vuttakālo. Tassa sādhūti kudālaṃ gahetvā tathākaraṇaṃ viya sekkhassa bhikkhuno, ‘‘yo vīsatiyā koṭṭhāsesu thaddhabhāvo, ayaṃ pathavīdhātu. Yo dvādasasu koṭṭhāsesu ābandhanabhāvo, ayaṃ āpodhātu. Yo catūsu koṭṭhāsesu paripācanabhāvo, ayaṃ tejodhātu. Yo chasu koṭṭhāsesu vitthambhanabhāvo, ayaṃ vāyodhātū’’ti evaṃ catudhātuvavatthānavasena kāyapariggaho veditabbo.

Laṅgīti kho, bhikkhūti kasmā bhagavā avijjaṃ laṅgīti katvā dassesīti? Yathā hi nagarassa dvāraṃ pidhāya palighe yojite mahājanassa gamanaṃ pacchijjati, ye nagarassa anto, te antoyeva honti. Ye bahi, te bahiyeva. Evameva yassa ñāṇamukhe avijjālaṅgī patati, tassa nibbānasampāpakaṃ ñāṇagamanaṃ pacchijjati, tasmā avijjaṃ laṅgīti katvā dassesi. Pajaha avijjanti ettha kammaṭṭhānauggahaparipucchāvasena avijjāpahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Laṅgīti kho, bhikkhū Pajaha avijja

Uddhumāyikātikho, bhikkhūti ettha uddhumāyikamaṇḍūko nāma no mahanto, nakhapiṭṭhippamāṇo hoti, purāṇapaṇṇantare vā gacchantare vā valliantare vā vasati. So daṇḍakoṭiyā vā vallikoṭiyā vā paṃsucuṇṇakena vā ghaṭṭito āyamitvā mahanto parimaṇḍalo beluvapakkappamāṇo hutvā cattāro pāde ākāsagate katvā pacchinnagamano hutvā amittavasaṃ yāti, kākakulalādibhattameva hoti. Evameva ayaṃ kodho paṭhamaṃ uppajjanto cittāvilamattakova hoti. Tasmiṃ khaṇe aniggahito vaḍḍhitvā mukhavikulanaṃ pāpeti. Tadā aniggahito hanusañcopanaṃ pāpeti. Tadā aniggahito pharusavācānicchāraṇaṃ pāpeti. Tadā aniggahito disāvilokanaṃ pāpeti. Tadā aniggahito ākaḍḍhanaparikaḍḍhanaṃ pāpeti. Tadā aniggahito pāṇinā leḍḍudaṇḍasatthaparāmasanaṃ pāpeti. Tadā aniggahito daṇḍasatthābhinipātaṃ pāpeti . Tadā aniggahito paraghātanampi attaghātanampi pāpeti. Vuttampi hetaṃ – ‘‘yato ayaṃ kodho paraṃ ghātetvā attānaṃ ghāteti, ettāvatāyaṃ kodho paramussadagato hoti paramavepullappatto’’ti. Tattha yathā uddhumāyikāya catūsu pādesu ākāsagatesu gamanaṃ pacchijjati, uddhumāyikā amittavasaṃ gantvā kākādibhattaṃ hoti, evameva kodhasamaṅgīpuggalo kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti, amittavasaṃ yāti, sabbesaṃ mārānaṃ yathākāmakaraṇīyo hoti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘uddhumāyikāti kho, bhikkhu, kodhūpāyāsassetaṃ adhivacana’’nti. Tattha balavappatto kodhova kodhūpāyāso. Pajaha kodhūpāyāsanti ettha paṭisaṅkhānappahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Uddhumāyikāti kho, bhikkhū uddhumāyikamaṇḍūko Pajaha kodhūpāyāsa

Dvidhāpathoti ettha, yathā puriso sadhano sabhogo kantāraddhānamaggappaṭipanno dvedhāpathaṃ patvā, ‘‘iminā nu kho gantabbaṃ, iminā gantabba’’nti nicchetuṃ asakkonto tattheva tiṭṭhati, atha naṃ corā uṭṭhahitvā anayabyasanaṃ pāpenti, evameva kho mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā nisinno bhikkhu buddhādīsu kaṅkhāya uppannāya kammaṭṭhānaṃ vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti, atha naṃ kilesamārādayo sabbe mārā anayabyasanaṃ pāpenti, iti vicikicchā dvedhāpathasamā hoti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘dvidhāpathoti kho, bhikkhu, vicikicchāyetaṃ adhivacana’’nti. Pajaha vicikicchanti ettha kammaṭṭhānauggahaparipucchāvasena vicikicchāpahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Dvidhāpatho Pajaha vicikiccha

Caṅgavāranti ettha, yathā rajakehi khāraparissāvanamhi udake pakkhitte eko udakaghaṭo dvepi dasapi vīsatipi ghaṭasatampi paggharatiyeva, pasaṭamattampi udakaṃ na tiṭṭhati, evameva nīvaraṇasamaṅgino puggalassa abbhantare kusaladhammo na tiṭṭhati. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘caṅgavāranti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ adhivacana’’nti. Pajaha pañcanīvaraṇeti ettha vikkhambhanatadaṅgavasena nīvaraṇappahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Caṅgavāra Pajaha pañcanīvaraṇe

Kummoti ettha, yathā kacchapassa cattāro pādā sīsanti pañceva aṅgāni honti, evameva sabbepi saṅkhatā dhammā gayhamānā pañceva khandhā bhavanti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘kummoti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ adhivacana’’nti. Pajaha pañcupādānakkhandheti ettha pañcasu khandhesu chandarāgappahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Kummo Pajaha pañcupādānakkhandhe

Asisūnāti ettha, yathā sūnāya upari maṃsaṃ ṭhapetvā asinā koṭṭenti, evamime sattā vatthukāmatthāya kilesakāmehi ghātayamānā vatthukāmānaṃ upari katvā kilesakāmehi kantitā koṭṭitā ca honti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘asisūnāti kho, bhikkhu, pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacana’’nti. Pajaha pañca kāmaguṇeti ettha pañcasu kāmaguṇesu chandarāgappahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Asisūnā Pajaha pañca kāmaguṇe

Maṃsapesīti kho, bhikkhūti ettha ayaṃ maṃsapesi nāma bahujanapatthitā khattiyādayo manussāpi naṃ patthenti kākādayo tiracchānāpi. Ime hi sattā avijjāya sammattā nandirāgaṃ upagamma vaṭṭaṃ vaḍḍhenti. Yathā vā maṃsapesi ṭhapitaṭhapitaṭṭhāne laggati, evamime sattā nandirāgabaddhā vaṭṭe lagganti, dukkhaṃ patvāpi na ukkaṇṭhanti , iti nandirāgo maṃsapesisadiso hoti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘maṃsapesīti kho, bhikkhu, nandirāgassetaṃ adhivacana’’nti. Pajaha nandīrāganti ettha catutthamaggena nandīrāgappahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Maṃsapesīti kho, bhikkhū maṃsapesi Pajaha nandīrāga

Nāgoti kho, bhikkhu, khīṇāsavassetaṃ bhikkhuno adhivacananti ettha yenatthena khīṇāsavo nāgoti vuccati, so anaṅgaṇasutte (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.63) pakāsito eva. Namo karohi nāgassāti khīṇāsavassa buddhanāgassa, ‘‘buddho so bhagavā bodhāya dhammaṃ deseti, danto so bhagavā damathāya dhammaṃ deseti, santo so bhagavā samathāya dhammaṃ deseti, tiṇṇo so bhagavā taraṇāya dhammaṃ deseti, parinibbuto so bhagavā parinibbānāya dhammaṃ desetī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.361) evaṃ namakkāraṃ karohīti ayamettha attho. Iti idaṃ suttaṃ therassa kammaṭṭhānaṃ ahosi. Theropi idameva suttaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ katvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ patto. Ayametassa atthoti ayaṃ etassa pañhassa attho. Iti bhagavā ratanarāsimhi maṇikūṭaṃ gaṇhanto viya yathānusandhināva desanaṃ niṭṭhapesīti.

Nāgoti kho, bhikkhu, khīṇāsavassetaṃ bhikkhuno adhivacana Namo karohi nāgassā Ayametassa attho

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Vammikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
251. *Cātummahābhūtikassā* means consisting of the four great elements ( *catumahābhūtamayassa*). *Kāyassetaṃ adhivacana* means a name for the body ( *sarīrassa nāmaṃ*). Just as there is an external anthill ( *vammiko*), it is called *vammiko* because it vomits (*vamati*), it is a vomiter ( *vantako*), it is a refuge for vomit ( *vantussayo*), and it is connected with the stickiness of vomit (*vantasinehasambandho*). [It is called *vammiko*] for these four reasons. It is *vammiko* because it vomits various kinds of living beings such as snakes, ahimaṅgus, saundūras, house-geckos, and goḷikās. *Vantakoti vammiko* means *vammiko* because it vomits sores (*upacikāhi*). *Upacikāhi vamitvā mukhatuṇḍakena ukkhittapaṃsucuṇṇena kaṭippamāṇenapi porisappamāṇenapi ussitoti vammiko* means it is called *vammiko* because, having vomited sores, it is raised with the powder of dust thrown up by the mouth like the size of the hip or the size of a person. *Upacikāhi* [page 2.0129] *vantakheḷasinehena ābaddhatāya sattasattāhaṃ deve vassantepi na vippakiriyati, nidāghepi tato paṃsumuṭṭhiṃ gahetvā tasmiṃ muṭṭhinā pīḷiyamāne sineho nikkhamati, evaṃ vantasinehena sambaddhoti vammiko* means because it is bound by the stickiness of vomit and saliva, even if the god rains for seven weeks, it is not scattered. Even in the hot season, if a handful of dust is taken from it and the stickiness comes out when it is pressed with that fist, it is *vammiko* because it is connected with the stickiness of vomit in this way. This body is also like that. "From the eye [page 2.0035] is eye-excrement," and in this way, it is *vammiko* because it vomits various kinds of impure dirt. *Buddhapaccekabuddhakhīṇāsavā imasmiṃ attabhāve nikantipariyādānena attabhāvaṃ chaḍḍetvā gatāti ariyehi vantakotipi vammiko* means it is also *vammiko* because buddhas, *paccekabuddhas*, and *khīṇāsavas*, having abandoned existence in this existence by means of the complete abandoning of craving, have gone, [and] it is vomited by the noble ones (*ariyehi vantakotipi vammiko*). Since this [body] is raised by three hundred bones, is bound by tendons, is smeared with flesh, is covered with moist skin, is colored with skin, and deceives beings, it is *vammiko* because all that is vomited by the noble ones. Thus, it is also a refuge for vomit (*vantussayotipi vammiko*). "Craving generates a person; his mind runs about" (Saṃ. Ni. 1. 55). Thus, because it is generated by craving [page 2.0034], it is connected with the stickiness of craving (*taṇhāsinehena sambaddho*) and is vomited by the noble ones (*ariyehi vanteneva*). It comes, and thus, it is *vammiko* because it is connected with the stickiness of vomit (*vantasinehena sambaddhotipi vammiko*). Just as various kinds of living beings are born inside an anthill ( *vammikassa anto*), they are born right there, they excrete urine and feces, the sick lie down, and the dead fall down. Thus, it is their delivery room, toilet, sickroom, and cemetery. Similarly, even for khattiyas, mahāsālas, and others, this body, [which is] guarded and protected, adorned and ornamented, [and] the body of those of great power, without thinking, "Living beings are dependent on skin, living beings are dependent on flesh, living beings are dependent on tendons, living beings are dependent on bones, living beings are dependent on bone marrow," in this way, eighty kinds of thousands of worm-families are born inside the body itself, they excrete urine and feces, those afflicted with disease lie down, [and] the dead fall down. Thus, this too is their delivery room, toilet, sickroom, and cemetery for those living beings. Thus, it has gone to the designation "anthill" (*vammiko*). Therefore, the Blessed One said, "O *bhikkhu*, the term *vammiko* is a designation for this body consisting of the four great elements (*cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassaetaṃ adhivacana*)." *Mātāpettikasambhavassā* means born from the sperm and blood of the mother and father ( *mātito ca pitito ca nibbattena mātāpettikena sukkasoṇitena sambhūtassa*). *Odanakummāsūpacayassā* means nourished and grown by rice and gruel (*odanena ceva kummāsena ca upacitassa vaḍḍhitassa*). *Aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammassā* means, here, this body, having become, by the meaning of non-existence, impermanent (*aniccadhammo*). *Duggandhavighātatthāya tanuvilepanena ucchādanadhammo* means it is subject to rubbing (*ucchādanadhammo*) because it is anointed with perfume, etc. in order to remove its bad smell ( *duggandhavighātatthāya tanuvilepanena*). *Aṅgapaccaṅgābādhavinodanatthāya khuddakasambāhanena parimaddanadhammo* means it is subject to being massaged (*parimaddanadhammo*) because it [dim. of the preceding] massage in order to get rid of pain in the limbs and members (*aṅgapaccaṅgābādhavinodanatthāya khuddakasambāhanena*). *Daharakāle* [page 2.0130] *vā ūrūsu sayāpetvā gabbhavāsena dussaṇṭhitānaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ aṅgānaṃ saṇṭhānasampādanatthaṃ añchanapīḷanādivasena parimaddanadhammo* means also, when children have limbs that have been misshapen during their stay in the womb, during infancy they are made to lie between the thighs and are pulled and pushed in order that their limbs may acquire the proper shape. *Evaṃ pariharatopi ca bhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo bhijjati ceva vikirati ca, evaṃ sabhāvoti attho* means it is “subject to dissolution and dispersion” because, though maintained in such ways, it is its very nature to break up and be scattered. There [page 2.0036], the arising (*samudayo*) is stated by the terms *mātāpettikasambhava, odanakummāsūpacaya, ucchādana*, and *parimaddana*, and the ceasing (*atthaṅgamo*) is stated by the terms *anicca, bheda,* and *viddhaṃsana*. Thus, by these seven terms, the high and low nature of the body consisting of the four great elements, its growth and decay, its arising and ceasing have been stated. Thus, it should be understood. *Mātāpettikasambhavassā* *odanakummāsūpacayassā* *aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammassā* *aniccadhammo* *ucchādanadhammo* *parimaddanadhammo* [page 2.0130] [page 2.0036] *Divā kammante* means in the daytime the work that should be done (*divā kattabbakammante*). *Dhūmāyanā* means here the word *dhūma* applies to these meanings: in anger, in craving, in thought, in the five sense qualities, in the teaching of the Dharma, and in natural smoke (*kodhe taṇhāya vitakke pañcasu kāmaguṇesu dhammadesanāya pakatidhūmeti imesu atthesu vattati*). "Anger is smoke, always blameworthy, bereft of ashes" (*kodho dhūmo bhasmanimosavajja*) (Saṃ. Ni. 1. Here, indeed, anger prevails. "Beings are smoking with desire," here [it refers to] craving (*taṇhā*). "And on that occasion, a certain monk was sitting not far from the Blessed One, enveloped in smoke," here [it refers to] thought (*vitakka*). During the day, in the course of work, smoking. "Mud and desires, deceit and desires, Fear, too—these three roots are proclaimed; Dust and smoke are declared by me; Having abandoned [them], you should renounce, Brahmdatta." (Jā. 1.6.14) Here [it refers to] the five strands of sense desire (*pañcakāmaguṇesu*). "One who makes smoke," here [it refers to] the teaching of the Dharma (*dhammadesanāya*). "A flag is the sign of a chariot, and smoke is the sign of fire (*aggin*)," here [it refers to] natural smoke. Here, however, this refers to thought (*vitakka*) [as being] intended. Therefore, he said, "This is smoking at night." "This is an appellation of the Thus-Gone One" (*tathāgatassetaṃ adhivacana*), for the Thus-Gone One is called a *brāhmaṇa* because of having eliminated seven qualities. As he said, "A *brāhmaṇa*, monk, is so called because of the elimination of seven qualities. What are the seven? Lust is eliminated, hatred… delusion… pride… belief in a permanent self (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*)… doubt (*vicikicchā*)… clinging to rules and vows (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*) is eliminated. It is because of the elimination of these seven qualities, monk, that [one is called] a *brāhmaṇa*." (Cūḷani. Mettagūmāṇavapucchāniddesa 28). "Wise" (*sumedho*) means beautiful wisdom (*sundarapañño*). "*Sekkhassā*," here, because he is training, [he is called] a trainee (*sekkho*). As he said, "Because he trains, monk, therefore he is called a trainee (*sekkho*). And what does he train in? He trains in higher virtue (*adhisīla*), he trains in higher mind (*adhicitta*), and he trains in higher wisdom (*adhipañña*)." (A. Ni. 3.86). This is an appellation of the Thus-Gone One, a *brāhmaṇa*, wise (*sumedho*), a trainee (*sekkhassa*). "Appellation of wisdom" (*paññāya adhivacana*) means this is an appellation of mundane and supramundane wisdom, not of a weapon or sword. "Of energetic effort" (*vīriyārambhassa*) [means] of bodily and mental energy (*vīriya*). That is just the course of wisdom (*paññāgatikameva*). Mundane wisdom is mundane, supramundane wisdom is supramundane. Here, however, this is an explanation of the meaning: of wisdom (*paññāya*). The designation *vīriyārambhassā*: Once upon a time, a learned *brāhmaṇa* from the countryside, leaving his village early in the morning with his students, would spend the day in the forest reciting *mantras*, returning to the village in the evening. On the road between, there was a termite mound. At night it smoked, and during the day it blazed. The *brāhmaṇa* said to his pupil, the wise youth Sumedha, "Dear Sumedha, this termite mound smokes at night and blazes during the day. We will observe its changes. Split it into four parts and throw them away." "As you wish," said Sumedha, and taking a spade, standing firmly on the ground with even feet, he did as he was told. There, the Blessed One was like the *ācārya brāhmaṇa*. The *śaikṣa bhikṣu* was like the wise youth Sumedha. The body is like the termite mound. "Dear Sumedha, this termite mound smokes at night and blazes during the day. We will observe its changes. Split it into four parts and throw them away." Just as this was the time the *brāhmaṇa* spoke, so the Blessed One spoke, "Monk, divide this body, composed of the four great elements, into four parts and examine it." Just as the wise youth Sumedha took a spade, saying "As you wish," and acted accordingly, so the *śaikṣa bhikṣu*: "That which is solidity in the twenty parts is the earth element (*pṛthivī-dhātu*). That which is cohesion in the twelve parts is the water element (*āpo-dhātu*). That which is maturing in the four parts is the fire element (*tejo-dhātu*). That which is support in the six parts is the air element (*vāyo-dhātu*)." Thus, the consideration of the body in terms of the four elements should be understood.

laṅgīti kho, bhikkhūti why did the Blessed One show ignorance to be a cripple? Just as, when the gate of a city is shut and the bar is applied, the going forth of the people is obstructed, and those who are inside the city remain inside. Those who are outside remain outside. Just so, when the cripple of ignorance falls on the face of wisdom, the going forth of wisdom that leads to *nirvāṇa* is obstructed. Therefore, ignorance is shown to be a cripple. pajaha avijjanti Here, the abandonment of ignorance is discussed in terms of taking up and questioning the object of meditation (*karmaṭṭhāna*). laṅgīti kho, bhikkhū pajaha avijja uddhumāyikāti kho, bhikkhūti Here, *uddhumāyikamaṇḍūko* is the name of a frog that is not large, but the size of a fingernail, and lives inside old leaves, trees, or vines. When it is struck with the tip of a stick, the tip of a vine, or with powdered dust, it swells up and becomes large and round, the size of a *beluva* fruit. Then, making its four feet point towards the sky, it ceases to move, and goes into the power of its enemy, becoming food for crows and the like. Just so, when this anger arises, at first it is only a slight disturbance of the mind. If it is not checked at that moment, it grows and causes distortion of the face. Then, if it is not checked, it causes trembling of the jaws. Then, if it is not checked, it causes the uttering of harsh, unwanted speech. Then, if it is not checked, it causes wild glances in all directions. Then, if it is not checked, it causes pulling and tugging. Then, if it is not checked, it causes touching a clod of dirt, a stick, or a weapon with the hand. Then, if it is not checked, it causes striking with a stick or a weapon. Then, if it is not checked, it causes harming others and harming oneself. So it was said, "Because this anger, having killed others, kills oneself, to that extent this anger has reached the highest point and attained the greatest extent." There, just as when the four feet of the *uddhumāyika* frog are in the sky, its movement ceases, and the *uddhumāyika*, going into the power of its enemy, becomes food for crows and the like, just so, a person possessed by anger cannot take up an object of meditation (*karmaṭṭhāna*) and develop it. He goes into the power of his enemy and becomes subject to the will of all the *māras*. Therefore, the Blessed One said, "*uddhumāyikāti kho, bhikkhu*, this is a designation for the affliction of anger." There, the affliction of anger is simply anger that has reached strength. pajaha kodhūpāyāsanti Here, the abandonment of affliction is discussed through reflective abandonment. “Good, *bhikkhus*! The bloated frog…” “Give up anger and vexation! Concerning ‘the two-way path’ (*dvidhāpatha*), it is like a man with resources and possessions, traveling along a difficult road through the wilderness, who comes to a fork in the road (*dvedhāpatha*). Unable to decide, ‘Should I go this way? Or should I go that way?’ he just stands there. Then thieves rise up, inflict misfortune and disaster on him. Just so, a *bhikkhu*, having taken up a basic meditation subject (*mūlakammaṭṭhāna*) and sat down, if doubt (*kaṅkhā*) arises concerning the Buddha, etc., is unable to develop that meditation subject. Then all the *māras*, beginning with the *kilesa-māra*, inflict misfortune and disaster on him. Thus, uncertainty (*vicikicchā*) is like a two-way path. Therefore, the Blessed One said: ‘*Dvidhāpatha*, *bhikkhu*, is a designation (*adhivacana*) for uncertainty (*vicikicchā*).’ ‘Give up uncertainty (*vicikicchā*)’ means that abandoning uncertainty is discussed in terms of undertaking and questioning about a meditation subject. The two-way path… Give up uncertainty! Concerning ‘the drain’ (*caṅgavāra*), it is like when a launderer pours water into a filter for lye, one water-pot, or two, or ten, or twenty, or even a hundred pots, just keeps flowing out. Not even a drop of water remains. Just so, a *puggala* endowed with the hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*) has no wholesome qualities (*kusala-dhamma*) remaining within. Therefore, the Blessed One said: ‘*Caṅgavāra*, *bhikkhu*, is a designation (*adhivacana*) for the five hindrances (*pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ*)’ ‘Give up the five hindrances (*pañcanīvaraṇe*)’ means that abandoning the hindrances is discussed in terms of overcoming them by means of strength and temporary suppression. The drain, give up the five hindrances! Concerning ‘the turtle’ (*kummo*), it is like a turtle whose four feet and head are drawn in; there are just five limbs (*aṅgāni*). Just so, all conditioned (*saṅkhata*) things, when grasped, become just five aggregates (*khandha*). Therefore, the Blessed One said: ‘The turtle, *bhikkhu*, is a designation (*adhivacana*) for the five aggregates of clinging (*pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ*)’ ‘Give up the five aggregates of clinging (*pañcupādānakkhandhe*)’ means that abandoning desire and lust (*chandarāgappahānaṃ*) for the five aggregates is discussed. The turtle, give up the five aggregates of clinging! Concerning ‘the butcher’s block’ (*asisūnā*), here, just as after putting meat on a butcher’s block (*sūnā*), they chop it with a sword (*asinā*), so these beings (*sattā*), being killed by the *kilesa*-desires (*kilesakāmehi*) for the sake of sense-objects (*vatthukāmatthāya*), having made the sense-objects supreme, are cut and chopped by the *kilesa*-desires. Therefore, the Blessed One said: ‘The butcher’s block, *bhikkhu*, is a designation (*adhivacana*) for the five strands of sensual desire (*pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ*)’ ‘Give up the five strands of sensual desire (*pañca kāmaguṇe*)’ means that abandoning desire and lust (*chandarāgappahānaṃ*) for the five strands of sensual desire is discussed. The butcher’s block… Give up the five strands of sensual desire! Concerning ‘the lump of flesh’ (*maṃsapesī*), here, this ‘lump of flesh’ (*maṃsapesī*) is something desired by many people; even *khattiyas* and other humans desire it, and crows and other animals do too. These beings, intoxicated by ignorance (*avijjāya sammattā*), approaching delight and lust (*nandirāgaṃ upagamma*), develop the round (*vaṭṭaṃ vaḍḍhenti*). Or, just as a lump of flesh sticks wherever it is put, so these beings, bound by delight and lust (*nandirāgabaddhā*), stick in the round (*vaṭṭe lagganti*); even having attained suffering (*dukkhaṃ patvāpi*) they do not shrink back. Thus, delight and lust is like a lump of flesh. Therefore, the Blessed One said: ‘The lump of flesh, *bhikkhu*, is a designation (*adhivacana*) for delight and lust (*nandirāgassa*)’ ‘Give up delight and lust (*nandīrāga*)’ means that abandoning delight and lust by means of the fourth path is discussed. The lump of flesh… Give up delight and lust! Concerning ‘the *nāga*’ (*nāgoti*), here, this is a designation (*adhivacana*) for the *bhikkhu* who is a destroyer of the *āsavas* (*khīṇāsavassetaṃ bhikkhuno*)’ is discussed, the meaning (*atthena*) by which a destroyer of the *āsavas* (*khīṇāsavo*) is called a *nāga* (*nāgoti vuccati*), that is explained in the Anaṅgaṇasutta (M. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1. 63). ‘Pay homage to the *nāga* (*namo karohi nāgassa*)’ means to the Buddha-*nāga* (*buddhanāgassa*) who is a destroyer of the *āsavas* (*khīṇāsavassa*): ‘‘That Blessed One is enlightened and teaches the *Dhamma* for enlightenment, he is tamed and teaches the *Dhamma* for taming, he is calmed and teaches the *Dhamma* for calming, he has crossed over and teaches the *Dhamma* for crossing over, he is extinguished and teaches the *Dhamma* for extinguishing” (M. Ni. 1. 361). Thus, to pay homage is the meaning here. Thus, this *sutta* was the meditation subject (*kammaṭṭhānaṃ ahosi*) of the Elder. That Elder, having made just this *sutta* his meditation subject (*kammaṭṭhānaṃ katvā*), having developed insight (*vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā*), attained to Arahatship (*arahattaṃ patto*). ‘This is its meaning (*ayametassa attho*)’ means: this is the meaning of that question (*pañhassa*). Thus, the Blessed One, like one picking up a gem from a heap of jewels, concluded the teaching according to what was connected and appropriate (*yathānusandhināva desanaṃ niṭṭhapesīti*). Monk, the word *nāga* is an epithet for a monk who has destroyed the āsavas. Pay homage to the *nāga*! This is its meaning. The commentary on the Vammika Sutta in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished.

mula_pali:
252. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho sambahulā jātibhūmakā bhikkhū jātibhūmiyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Ko nu kho, bhikkhave, jātibhūmiyaṃ jātibhūmakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ evaṃ sambhāvito – ‘attanā ca appiccho appicchakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca santuṭṭho santuṭṭhikathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca pavivitto pavivekakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho asaṃsaggakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca āraddhavīriyo vīriyārambhakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca sīlasampanno sīlasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca samādhisampanno samādhisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca paññāsampanno paññāsampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca vimuttisampanno vimuttisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, ovādako viññāpako sandassako samādapako samuttejako sampahaṃsako sabrahmacārīna’’’nti? ‘‘Puṇṇo nāma, bhante, āyasmā mantāṇiputto jātibhūmiyaṃ jātibhūmakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ evaṃ sambhāvito – ‘attanā ca appiccho appicchakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā, attanā ca santuṭṭho…pe… ovādako viññāpako sandassako samādapako samuttejako sampahaṃsako sabrahmacārīna’’’nti.
mula_english:
252. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

Then a number of bhikkhus from the Blessed One’s native land (jātibhūmakā), who had spent the Rains there, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side.

Sitting to one side, these monks said this to the Blessed One:

“Venerable sir, is there any among the monks (bhikkhu) of the native land (jātibhūmi), who are your fellow-brahmacārins, who is regarded thus: ‘He himself is of few desires (appiccho) and speaks in praise of being of few desires; he himself is content (santuṭṭho) and speaks in praise of contentment; he himself is secluded (pavivitto) and speaks in praise of seclusion; he himself is unassociated (asaṃsaṭṭho) and speaks in praise of non-association; he himself is energetic (āraddhavīriyo) and speaks in praise of the instigation of energy; he himself is accomplished in virtue (sīlasampanno) and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of virtue; he himself is accomplished in concentration (samādhisampanno) and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of concentration (samādhi); he himself is accomplished in wisdom (paññāsampanno) and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of wisdom (paññā); he himself is accomplished in liberation (vimuttisampanno) and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of liberation (vimutti); he himself is accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation (vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno) and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation, is an instructor (ovādako), an informer (viññāpako), an inspirer (sandassako), an encourager (samādapako), an exhorter (samuttejako), a rejoicer (sampahaṃsako) of his fellow-brahmacārins’?”

“Venerable sir, the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta is regarded thus among the monks of the native land who are your fellow-brahmacārins: ‘He himself is of few desires (appiccho) and speaks in praise of being of few desires; he himself is content (santuṭṭho)…pe… is an instructor (ovādako), an informer (viññāpako), an inspirer (sandassako), an encourager (samādapako), an exhorter (samuttejako), a rejoicer (sampahaṃsako) of his fellow-brahmacārins.’”
commentary_pali:
252.Evaṃme sutanti rathavinītasuttaṃ. Tattha rājagaheti evaṃnāmake nagare, tañhi mandhātumahāgovindādīhi pariggahitattā rājagahanti vuccati. Aññepettha pakāre vaṇṇayanti. Kiṃ tehi? Nāmametaṃ tassa nagarassa. Taṃ panetaṃ buddhakāle ca cakkavattikāle ca nagaraṃ hoti, sesakāle suññaṃ hoti yakkhapariggahitaṃ, tesaṃ vasantavanaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhati. Veḷuvane kalandakanivāpeti veḷuvananti tassa uyyānassa nāmaṃ, taṃ kira veḷūhi parikkhittaṃ ahosi aṭṭhārasahatthena ca pākārena, gopuraṭṭālakayuttaṃ nīlobhāsaṃ manoramaṃ, tena veḷuvananti vuccati. Kalandakānañcettha nivāpaṃ adaṃsu, tena kalandakanivāpoti vuccati.

Pubbe kira aññataro rājā tattha uyyānakīḷanatthaṃ āgato surāmadena matto divāseyyaṃ upagato supi. Parijanopissa, ‘‘sutto rājā’’ti pupphaphalādīhi palobhiyamāno ito cito ca pakkāmi, atha surāgandhena aññatarasmā susirarukkhā kaṇhasappo nikkhamitvā raññābhimukho āgacchati. Taṃ disvā rukkhadevatā, ‘‘rañño jīvitaṃ dammī’’ti kāḷakavesena āgantvā kaṇṇamūle saddamakāsi. Rājā paṭibujjhi, kaṇhasappo nivatto. So taṃ disvā, ‘‘imāya mama jīvitaṃ dinna’’nti kāḷakānaṃ tattha nivāpaṃ paṭṭhapesi, abhayaghosanañca ghosāpesi. Tasmā taṃ tato pabhuti kalandakanivāpanti saṅkhyaṃ gataṃ. Kalandakāti kāḷakānaṃ nāmaṃ.

kalandakanivāpa Kalandakā

Jātibhūmikāti jātibhūmivāsino. Tattha jātibhūmīti jātaṭṭhānaṃ. Taṃ kho panetaṃ neva kosalamahārājādīnaṃ na caṅkībrāhamaṇādīnaṃ na sakkasuyāmasantusitādīnaṃ na asītimahāsāvakādīnaṃ na aññesaṃ sattānaṃ jātaṭṭhānaṃ ‘‘jātibhūmī’’ti vuccati. Yassa pana jātadivase dasasahassilokadhātu ekaddhajamālāvippakiṇṇakusumavāsacuṇṇagandhasugandhā sabbapāliphullamiva nandanavanaṃ virocamānā paduminipaṇṇe udakabindu viya akampittha, jaccandhādīnañca rūpadassanādīni anekāni pāṭihāriyāni pavattiṃsu, tassa sabbaññubodhisattassa jātaṭṭhānasākiyajanapado kapilavatthāhāro, sā ‘‘jātibhūmī’’ti vuccati.

Jātibhūmikā jātibhūmī

Dhammagarubhāvavaṇṇanā

Vassaṃvuṭṭhāti temāsaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhā pavāritapavāraṇā hutvā. Bhagavā etadavocāti ‘‘kacci, bhikkhave, khamanīya’’ntiādīhi vacanehi āgantukapaṭisanthāraṃ katvā etaṃ, ‘‘ko nu kho, bhikkhave’’tiādivacanamavoca. Te kira bhikkhu, – ‘‘kacci, bhikkhave, khamanīyaṃ kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kaccittha appakilamathena addhānaṃ āgatā, na ca piṇḍakena kilamittha, kuto ca tumhe, bhikkhave, āgacchathā’’ti paṭisanthāravasena pucchitā – ‘‘bhagavā sākiyajanapade kapilavatthāhārato jātibhūmito āgacchāmā’’ti āhaṃsu. Atha bhagavā neva suddhodanamahārājassa, na sakkodanassa, na sukkodanassa, na dhotodanassa, na amitodanassa, na amittāya deviyā, na mahāpajāpatiyā, na sakalassa sākiyamaṇḍalassa ārogyaṃ pucchi. Atha kho attanā ca dasakathāvatthulābhiṃ parañca tattha samādapetāraṃ paṭipattisampannaṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchanto idaṃ – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhikkhave’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca.

Vassaṃvuṭṭhā Bhagavā etadavocā

Kasmā pana bhagavā suddhodanādīnaṃ ārogyaṃ apucchitvā evarūpaṃ bhikkhumeva pucchati? Piyatāya. Buddhānañhi paṭipannakā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo ca piyā honti manāpā. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Dhammagarutāya. Dhammagaruno hi tathāgatā, so ca nesaṃ dhammagarubhāvo, ‘‘dukkhaṃ kho agāravo viharati, appatisso’’ti (a. ni. 4.21) iminā ajapālanigrodhamūle uppannajjhāsayena veditabbo. Dhammagarutāyeva hi bhagavā mahākassapattherassa abhinikkhamanadivase paccuggamanaṃ karonto tigāvutaṃ maggaṃ agamāsi. Atirekatiyojanasataṃ maggaṃ gantvā gaṅgātīre dhammaṃ desetvā mahākappinaṃ saparisaṃ arahatte patiṭṭhapesi. Ekasmiṃ pacchābhatte pañcacattālīsayojanaṃ maggaṃ gantvā kumbhakārassa nivesane tiyāmarattiṃ dhammakathaṃ katvā pukkusātikulaputtaṃ anāgāmiphale patiṭṭhapesi. Vīsayojanasataṃ gantvā vanavāsisāmaṇerassa anuggahaṃ akāsi. Saṭṭhiyojanamaggaṃ gantvā khadiravaniyattherassa dhammaṃ desesi. Anuruddhatthero pācīnavaṃsadāye nisinno mahāpurisavitakkaṃ vitakketīti ñatvā tattha ākāsena gantvā therassa purato oruyha sādhukāramadāsi. Koṭikaṇṇasoṇattherassa ekagandhakuṭiyaṃ senāsanaṃ paññapāpetvā paccūsakāle dhammadesanaṃ ajjhesitvā sarabhaññapariyosāne sādhukāramadāsi. Tigāvutaṃ maggaṃ gantvā tiṇṇaṃ kulaputtānaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne gosiṅgasālavane sāmaggirasānisaṃsaṃ kathesi. Kassapopi bhagavā – ‘‘anāgāmiphale patiṭṭhito ariyasāvako aya’’nti vissāsaṃ uppādetvā ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa nivesanaṃ gantvā sahatthā āmisaṃ gahetvā paribhuñji.

Amhākaṃyeva bhagavā upakaṭṭhāya vassūpanāyikāya jetavanato bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto cārikaṃ nikkhami. Kosalamahārājaanāthapiṇḍikādayo nivattetuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Anāthapiṇḍiko gharaṃ āgantvā domanassappatto nisīdi. Atha naṃ puṇṇā nāma dāsī domanassappattosi sāmīti āha. ‘‘Āma je, satthāraṃ nivattetuṃ nāsakkhiṃ, atha me imaṃ temāsaṃ dhammaṃ vā sotuṃ, yathādhippāyaṃ vā dānaṃ dātuṃ na labhissāmī’’ti cintā uppannāti. Ahampi sāmi satthāraṃ nivattessāmīti. Sace nivattetuṃ sakkosi, bhujissāyeva tvanti. Sā gantvā dasabalassa pādamūle nipajjitvā ‘‘nivattatha bhagavā’’ti āha. Puṇṇe tvaṃ parapaṭibaddhajīvikā kiṃ me karissasīti. Bhagavā mayhaṃ deyyadhammo natthīti tumhepi jānātha, tumhākaṃ nivattanapaccayā panāhaṃ tīsu saraṇesu pañcasu sīlesu patiṭṭhahissāmīti. Bhagavā sādhu sādhu puṇṇeti sādhukāraṃ katvā nivattetvā jetavanameva paviṭṭho. Ayaṃ kathā pākaṭā ahosi. Seṭṭhi sutvā puṇṇāya kira bhagavā nivattitoti taṃ bhujissaṃ katvā dhītuṭṭhāne ṭhapesi. Sā pabbajjaṃ yācitvā pabbaji, pabbajitvā vipassanaṃ ārabhi. Athassā satthā āraddhavipassakabhāvaṃ ñatvā imaṃ obhāsagāthaṃ vissajjesi –

‘‘Puṇṇe pūresi saddhammaṃ, cando pannaraso yathā;

Paripuṇṇāya paññāya, dukkhassantaṃ karissasī’’ti. (therīgā. 3);

Gāthāpariyosāne arahattaṃ patvā abhiññātā sāvikā ahosīti. Evaṃ dhammagaruno tathāgatā.

Nandakatthere upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ dhammaṃ desentepi bhagavā anahātova gantvā tiyāmarattiṃ ṭhitakova dhammakathaṃ sutvā desanāpariyosāne sādhukāramadāsi. Thero āgantvā vanditvā, ‘‘kāya velāya, bhante, āgatatthā’’ti pucchi. Tayā suttante āraddhamatteti. Dukkaraṃ karittha, bhante, buddhasukhumālā tumheti. Sace tvaṃ, nanda, kappaṃ desetuṃ sakkuṇeyyāsi, kappamattampāhaṃ ṭhitakova suṇeyyanti bhagavā avoca. Evaṃ dhammagaruno tathāgatā. Tesaṃ dhammagarutāya paṭipannakā piyā honti, tasmā paṭipannake pucchi. Paṭipannako ca nāma attahitāya paṭipanno no parahitāya, parahitāya paṭipanno no attahitāya, no attahitāya ca paṭipanno no parahitāya ca, attahitāya ca paṭipanno parahitāya cāti catubbidho hoti.

Tattha yo sayaṃ dasannaṃ kathāvatthūnaṃ lābhī hoti, paraṃ tattha na ovadati na anusāsati āyasmā bākulo viya. Ayaṃ attahitāya paṭipanno nāma no parahitāya paṭipanno, evarūpaṃ bhikkhuṃ bhagavā na pucchati. Kasmā? Na mayhaṃ sāsanassa vaḍḍhipakkhe ṭhitoti.

Yo pana dasannaṃ kathāvatthūnaṃ alābhī, paraṃ tehi ovadati tena katavattasādiyanatthaṃ upanando sakyaputto viya, ayaṃ parahitāya paṭipanno nāma no attahitāya, evarūpampi na pucchati. Kasmā? Assa taṇhā mahāpacchi viya appahīnāti.

Yo attanāpi dasannaṃ kathāvatthūnaṃ alābhī, parampi tehi na ovadati, lāḷudāyī viya, ayaṃ neva attahitāya paṭipanno na parahitāya, evarūpampi na pucchati. Kasmā? Assa anto kilesā pharasuchejjā viya mahantāti.

Yo pana sayaṃ dasannaṃ kathāvatthūnaṃ lābhī, parampi tehi ovadati, ayaṃ attahitāya ceva parahitāya ca paṭipanno nāma sāriputtamoggallānamahākassapādayo asītimahātherā viya, evarūpaṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchati. Kasmā? Mayhaṃ sāsanassa vuḍḍhipakkhe ṭhitoti. Idhāpi evarūpameva pucchanto – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhikkhave’’tiādimāha.

Evaṃ bhagavatā puṭṭhānaṃ pana tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhagavā attano jātibhūmiyaṃ ubhayahitāya paṭipannaṃ dasakathāvatthulābhiṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchati, ko nu kho tattha evarūpoti na aññamaññaṃ cintanā vā samantanā vā ahosi. Kasmā? Āyasmā hi mantāṇiputto tasmiṃ janapade ākāsamajjhe ṭhito cando viya sūriyo viya ca pākaṭo paññāto. Tasmā te bhikkhū meghasaddaṃ sutvā ekajjhaṃ sannipatitamoraghaṭā viya ghanasajjhāyaṃ kātuṃ, āraddhabhikkhū viya ca attano ācariyaṃ puṇṇattheraṃ bhagavato ārocentā therassa ca guṇaṃ bhāsituṃ appahontehi mukhehi ekappahāreneva puṇṇo nāma, bhante, āyasmātiādimāhaṃsu. Tattha puṇṇoti tassa therassa nāmaṃ. Mantāṇiyā pana so putto, tasmā mantāṇiputtoti vuccati. Sambhāvitoti guṇasambhāvanāya sambhāvito.

puṇṇo nāma, bhante, āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto Sambhāvito

Appicchatādivaṇṇanā

Appicchoti icchāvirahito niiccho nittaṇho. Ettha hi byañjanaṃ sāvasesaṃ viya, attho pana niravaseso. Na hi tassa anto aṇumattāpi pāpikā icchā nāma atthi. Khīṇāsavo hesa sabbaso pahīnataṇho. Apicettha atricchatā pāpicchatā mahicchatā appicchatāti ayaṃ bhedo veditabbo.

Appiccho

Tattha sakalābhe atittassa paralābhe patthanā atricchatā nāma. Tāya samannāgatassa ekabhājena pakkapūvopi attano patte patito na supakko viya khuddako viya ca khāyati. Sveva parassa patte pakkhitto supakko viya mahanto viya ca khāyati. Asantaguṇasambhāvanatā pana paṭiggahaṇe ca amattaññutā pāpicchatā nāma, sā, ‘‘idhekacco assaddho samāno saddhoti maṃ jano jānātū’’tiādinā nayena abhidhamme āgatāyeva, tāya samannāgato puggalo kohaññe patiṭṭhāti. Santaguṇasambhāvanā pana paṭiggahaṇe ca amattaññutā mahicchatā nāma. Sāpi, ‘‘idhekacco saddho samāno saddhoti maṃ jano jānātūti icchati, sīlavā samāno sīlavāti maṃ jano jānātū’’ti (vibha. 851) iminā nayena āgatāyeva, tāya samannāgato puggalo dussantappayo hoti, vijātamātāpissa cittaṃ gahetuṃ na sakkoti. Tenetaṃ vuccati –

atricchatā pāpicchatā mahicchatā

‘‘Aggikkhandho samuddo ca, mahiccho cāpi puggalo;

Sakaṭena paccayaṃ detu, tayopete atappayā’’ti.

Santaguṇanigūhanatā pana paṭiggahaṇe ca mattaññutā appicchatā nāma, tāya samannāgato puggalo attani vijjamānampi guṇaṃ paṭicchādetukāmatāya, ‘‘saddho samāno saddhoti maṃ jano jānātūti na icchati. Sīlavā, pavivitto, bahussuto, āraddhavīriyo, samādhisampanno, paññavā, khīṇāsavo samāno khīṇāsavoti maṃ jano jānātū’’ti na icchati, seyyathāpi majjhantikatthero.

appicchatā

Thero kira mahākhīṇāsavo ahosi, pattacīvaraṃ panassa pādamattameva agghati, so asokassa dhammarañño vihāramahadivase saṅghatthero ahosi. Athassa atilūkhabhāvaṃ disvā manussā, ‘‘bhante, thokaṃ bahi hothā’’ti āhaṃsu. Thero, ‘‘mādise khīṇāsave rañño saṅgahaṃ akaronte añño ko karissatī’’ti pathaviyaṃ nimujjitvā saṅghattherassa ukkhittapiṇḍaṃ gaṇhantoyeva ummujji. Evaṃ khīṇāsavo samāno, ‘‘khīṇāsavoti maṃ jano jānātū’’ti na icchati. Evaṃ appiccho pana bhikkhu anuppannaṃ lābhaṃ uppādeti, uppannaṃ lābhaṃ thāvaraṃ karoti, dāyakānaṃ cittaṃ ārādheti, yathā yathā hi so attano appicchatāya appaṃ gaṇhāti, tathā tathā tassa vatte pasannā manussā bahū denti.

Aparopi catubbidho appiccho – paccayaappiccho dhutaṅgaappiccho pariyattiappiccho adhigamaappicchoti. Tattha catūsu paccayesu appiccho paccayaappiccho nāma, so dāyakassa vasaṃ jānāti, deyyadhammassa vasaṃ jānāti, attano thāmaṃ jānāti. Yadi hi deyyadhammo bahu hoti, dāyako appaṃ dātukāmo, dāyakassa vasena appaṃ gaṇhāti. Deyyadhammo appo, dāyako bahuṃ dātukāmo, deyyadhammassa vasena appaṃ gaṇhāti. Deyyadhammopi bahu, dāyakopi bahuṃ dātukāmo, attano thāmaṃ ñatvā pamāṇeneva gaṇhāti.

paccayaappiccho

Dhutaṅgasamādānassa attani atthibhāvaṃ najānāpetukāmo dhutaṅgaappiccho nāma. Tassa vibhāvanatthaṃ imāni vatthūni – sosānikamahāsumanatthero kira saṭṭhi vassāni susāne vasi, añño ekabhikkhupi na aññāsi, tenevāha –

dhutaṅgaappiccho

‘‘Susāne saṭṭhi vassāni, abbokiṇṇaṃ vasāmahaṃ;

Dutiyo maṃ na jāneyya, aho sosānikuttamo’’ti.

Cetiyapabbate dvebhātiyattherā vasiṃsu. Tesu kaniṭṭho upaṭṭhākena pesitā ucchukhaṇḍikā gahetvā jeṭṭhassa santikaṃ agamāsi. Paribhogaṃ, bhante, karothāti. Therassa ca bhattakiccaṃ katvā mukhaṃ vikkhālanakālo ahosi. So alaṃ, āvusoti āha. Kacci, bhante, ekāsanikatthāti. Āharāvuso, ucchukhaṇḍikāti paññāsa vassāni ekāsaniko samānopi dhutaṅgaṃ nigūhamāno paribhogaṃ katvā mukhaṃ vikkhāletvā puna dhutaṅgaṃ adhiṭṭhāya gato.

Yo pana sāketakatissatthero viya bahussutabhāvaṃ jānāpetuṃ na icchati, ayaṃ pariyattiappiccho nāma. Thero kira khaṇo natthīti uddesaparipucchāsu okāsaṃ akaronto maraṇakkhayaṃ, bhante, labhissathāti codito gaṇaṃ vissajjetvā kaṇikāravālikasamuddavihāraṃ gato. Tattha antovassaṃ theranavamajjhimānaṃ upakāro hutvā mahāpavāraṇāya uposathadivase dhammakathāya janataṃ khobhetvā gato.

pariyattiappiccho

Yo pana sotāpannādīsu aññataro hutvā sotāpannādibhāvaṃ jānāpetuṃ na icchati, ayaṃ adhigamaappiccho nāma, tayo kulaputtā viya ghaṭikārakumbhakāro viya ca.

adhigamaappiccho

Āyasmā pana puṇṇo atricchataṃ pāpicchataṃ mahicchatañca pahāya sabbaso icchāpaṭipakkhabhūtāya alobhasaṅkhātāya parisuddhāya appicchatāya samannāgatattā appiccho nāma ahosi. Bhikkhūnampi, ‘‘āvuso, atricchatā pāpicchatā mahicchatāti ime dhammā pahātabbā’’ti tesu ādīnavaṃ dassetvā evarūpaṃ appicchataṃ samādāya vattitabbanti appicchakathaṃ kathesi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘attanā ca appiccho appicchakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’’ti.

Dvādasavidhasantosavaṇṇanā

Idāni attanā ca santuṭṭhotiādīsu visesatthameva dīpayissāma. Yojanā pana vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Santuṭṭhoti itarītarapaccayasantosena samannāgato. So panesa santoso dvādasavidho hoti. Seyyathidaṃ, cīvare yathālābhasantoso yathābalasantoso yathasāruppasantosoti tividho, evaṃ piṇḍapātādīsu. Tassāyaṃ pabhedasaṃvaṇṇanā.

attanā ca santuṭṭho Santuṭṭho

Idha bhikkhu cīvaraṃ labhati sundaraṃ vā asundaraṃ vā. So teneva yāpeti aññaṃ na pattheti, labhantopi na gaṇhāti, ayamassa cīvare yathālābhasantoso. Atha yo pakatidubbalo vā hoti ābādhajarābhibhūto vā, garucīvaraṃ pārupanto kilamati, so sabhāgena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ taṃ parivattetvā lahukena yāpentopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa cīvare yathābalasantoso. Aparo paṇītapaccayalābhī hoti, so paṭṭacīvarādīnaṃ aññataraṃ mahagghacīvaraṃ bahūni vā pana cīvarāni labhitvā idaṃ therānaṃ cirapabbajitānaṃ idaṃ bahussutānaṃ anurūpaṃ, idaṃ gilānānaṃ idaṃ appalābhānaṃ hotūti datvā tesaṃ purāṇacīvaraṃ vā saṅkārakūṭādito vā nantakāni uccinitvā tehi saṅghāṭiṃ katvā dhārentopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa cīvare yathāsāruppasantoso.

yathālābhasantoso yathābalasantoso yathāsāruppasantoso

Idha pana bhikkhu piṇḍapātaṃ labhati lūkhaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā, so teneva yāpeti, aññaṃ na pattheti, labhantopi na gaṇhāti, ayamassa piṇḍapāte yathālābhasantoso. Yo pana attano pakativiruddhaṃ vā byādhiviruddhaṃ vā piṇḍapātaṃ labhati, yenassa paribhuttena aphāsu hoti, so sabhāgassa bhikkhuno taṃ datvā tassa hatthato sappāyabhojanaṃ bhuñjitvā samaṇadhammaṃ karontopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa piṇḍapāte yathābalasantoso. Aparo bahuṃ paṇītaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ labhati, so taṃ cīvaraṃ viya cirapabbajitabahussutaappalābhigilānānaṃ datvā tesaṃ vā sesakaṃ piṇḍāya vā caritvā missakāhāraṃ bhuñjantopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa piṇḍapāte yathāsāruppasantoso.

yathālābhasantoso yathābalasantoso yathāsāruppasantoso

Idha pana bhikkhu senāsanaṃ labhati manāpaṃ vā amanāpaṃ vā, so tena neva somanassaṃ na paṭighaṃ uppādeti, antamaso tiṇasanthārakenāpi yathāladdheneva tussati, ayamassa senāsane yathālābhasantoso. Yo pana attano pakativiruddhaṃ vā byādhiviruddhaṃ vā senāsanaṃ labhati, yatthassa vasato aphāsu hoti, so taṃ sabhāgassa bhikkhuno datvā tassa santake sappāyasenāsane vasantopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa senāsane yathābalasantoso. Aparo mahāpuñño leṇamaṇḍapakūṭāgārādīni bahūni paṇītasenāsanāni labhati, so tāni cīvarādīni viya cirapabbajitabahussutaappalābhigilānānaṃ datvā yattha katthaci vasantopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa senāsane yathāsāruppasantoso. Yopi, ‘‘uttamasenāsanaṃ nāma pamādaṭṭhānaṃ, tattha nisinnassa thinamiddhaṃ okkamati, niddābhibhūtassa puna paṭibujjhato pāpavitakkā pātubhavantī’’ti paṭisañcikkhitvā tādisaṃ senāsanaṃ pattampi na sampaṭicchati, so taṃ paṭikkhipitvā abbhokāsarukkhamūlādīsu vasantopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayampissa senāsane yathāsāruppasantoso.

yathālābhasantoso yathābalasantoso yathāsāruppasantoso yathāsāruppasantoso

Idha pana bhikkhu bhesajjaṃ labhati lūkhaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā, so yaṃ labhati, teneva santussati, aññaṃ na pattheti, labhantopi na gaṇhāti, ayamassa gilānapaccaye yathālābhasantoso. Yo pana telena atthiko phāṇitaṃ labhati, so taṃ sabhāgassa bhikkhuno datvā tassa hatthato telaṃ gahetvā aññadeva vā pariyesitvā tehi bhesajjaṃ karontopi santuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa gilānapaccaye yathābalasantoso. Aparo mahāpuñño bahuṃ telamadhuphāṇitādipaṇītabhesajjaṃ labhati, so taṃ cīvaraṃ viya cirapabbajitabahussutaappalābhigilānānaṃ datvā tesaṃ ābhatakena yena kenaci yāpentopi santuṭṭhova hoti. Yo pana ekasmiṃ bhājane muttaharītakaṃ ṭhapetvā ekasmiṃ catumadhuraṃ, ‘‘gaṇha, bhante, yadicchasī’’ti vuccamāno sacassa tesu aññatarenapi rogo vūpasammati, atha muttaharītakaṃ nāma buddhādīhi vaṇṇitanti catumadhuraṃ paṭikkhipitvā muttaharītakeneva bhesajjaṃ karonto paramasantuṭṭhova hoti, ayamassa gilānapaccaye yathāsāruppasantoso.

yathālābhasantoso yathābalasantoso yathāsāruppasantoso

Imesaṃ pana paccekaṃ paccayesu tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ santosānaṃ yathāsāruppasantosova aggo. Āyasmā puṇṇo ekekasmiṃ paccaye imehi tīhi santosehi santuṭṭho ahosi. Santuṭṭhikathañcāti bhikkhūnampi ca imaṃ santuṭṭhikathaṃ kattāva ahosi.

Santuṭṭhikathañcā

Tividhapavivekavaṇṇanā

Pavivittoti kāyapaviveko cittapaviveko upadhipavivekoti imehi tīhi pavivekehi samannāgato. Tattha eko gacchati, eko tiṭṭhati, eko nisīdati, eko seyyaṃ kappeti, eko gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisati, eko paṭikkamati, eko caṅkamamadhiṭṭhāti, eko carati, eko viharatīti ayaṃ kāyapaviveko nāma. Aṭṭha samāpattiyo pana cittapaviveko nāma. Nibbānaṃ upadhipaviveko nāma. Vuttampi hetaṃ – ‘‘kāyapaviveko ca vivekaṭṭhakāyānaṃ nekkhammābhiratānaṃ. Cittapaviveko ca parisuddhacittānaṃ paramavodānappattānaṃ. Upadhiviveko ca nirupadhīnaṃ puggalānaṃ visaṅkhāragatāna’’nti (mahāni. 57). Pavivekakathanti bhikkhūnampi ca imaṃ pavivekakathaṃ kattā.

Pavivitto kāyapaviveko cittapaviveko upadhipaviveko Pavivekakatha

Pañcavidhasaṃsaggavaṇṇanā

Asaṃsaṭṭhoti pañcavidhena saṃsaggena virahito. Savanasaṃsaggo dassanasaṃsaggo samullapanasaṃsaggo sambhogasaṃsaggo kāyasaṃsaggoti pañcavidho saṃsaggo. Tesu idha bhikkhu suṇāti, ‘‘asukasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā kumārikā vā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā’’ti. So taṃ sutvā saṃsīdati visīdati na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ, sikkhādubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā hīnāyāvattatīti evaṃ parehi vā kathīyamānaṃ rūpādisampattiṃ attanā vā hasitalapitagītasaddaṃ suṇantassa sotaviññāṇavīthivasena uppanno rāgo savanasaṃsaggo nāma. So anitthigandhapaccekabodhisattassa ca pañcaggaḷaleṇavāsītissadaharassa ca vasena veditabbo –

Asaṃsaṭṭho savanasaṃsaggo

Daharo kira ākāsena gacchanto girigāmavāsikammāradhītāya pañcahi kumārīhi saddhiṃ padumasaraṃ gantvā nhatvā padumāni ca pilandhitvā madhurassarena gāyantiyā saddaṃ sutvā kāmarāgena viddho visesā parihāyitvā anayabyasanaṃ pāpuṇi. Idha bhikkhu na heva kho suṇāti, apica kho sāmaṃ passati itthiṃ vā kumāriṃ vā abhirūpaṃ dassanīyaṃ pāsādikaṃ paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgataṃ. So taṃ disvā saṃsīdati visīdati na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ, sikkhādubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā hīnāyāvattatīti evaṃ visabhāgarūpaṃ olokentassa pana cakkhuviññāṇavīthivasena uppannarāgo dassanasaṃsaggo nāma. So evaṃ veditabbo –

dassanasaṃsaggo

Eko kira daharo kāladīghavāpidvāravihāraṃ uddesatthāya gato. Ācariyo tassa antarāyaṃ disvā okāsaṃ na karoti. So punappunnaṃ anubandhati. Ācariyo sace antogāme na carissasi. Dassāmi te uddesanti āha. So sādhūti sampaṭicchitvā uddese niṭṭhite ācariyaṃ vanditvā gacchanto ācariyo me imasmiṃ gāme carituṃ na deti, kiṃ nu kho kāraṇanti cīvaraṃ pārupitvā gāmaṃ pāvisi, ekā kuladhītā pītakavatthaṃ nivāsetvā gehe ṭhitā daharaṃ disvā sañjātarāgā uḷuṅkena yāguṃ āharitvā tassa patte pakkhipitvā nivattitvā mañcake nipajji. Atha naṃ mātāpitaro kiṃ ammāti pucchiṃsu, dvārena gataṃ daharaṃ labhamānā jīvissāmi, alabhamānā marissāmīti. Mātāpitaro vegena gantvā gāmadvāre daharaṃ patvā vanditvā, ‘‘nivattatha, bhante, bhikkhaṃ gaṇhāhī’’ti āhaṃsu. Daharo alaṃ gacchāmīti. Te, ‘‘idaṃ nāma, bhante, kāraṇa’’nti yācitvā – ‘‘amhākaṃ, bhante, gehe ettakaṃ nāma dhanaṃ atthi, ekāyeva no dhītā, tvaṃ no jeṭṭhaputtaṭṭhāne ṭhassasi, sukhena sakkā jīvitu’’nti āhaṃsu. Daharo, ‘‘na mayhaṃ iminā palibodhena attho’’ti anādiyitvāva pakkanto.

Mātāpitaro gantvā, ‘‘amma, nāsakkhimhā daharaṃ nivattetuṃ, yaṃ aññaṃ sāmikaṃ icchasi, taṃ labhissasi, uṭṭhehi khāda ca piva cā’’ti āhaṃsu. Sā anicchantī sattāhaṃ nirāhārā hutvā kālamakāsi. Mātāpitaro tassā sarīrakiccaṃ katvā taṃ pītakavatthaṃ dhuravihāre bhikkhusaṅghassa adaṃsu, bhikkhū vatthaṃ khaṇḍākhaṇḍaṃ katvā bhājayiṃsu. Eko mahallako attano koṭṭhāsaṃ gahetvā kalyāṇīvihāraṃ āgato. Sopi daharo cetiyaṃ vandissāmīti tattheva gantvā divāṭṭhāne nisīdi. Mahallako taṃ vatthakhaṇḍaṃ gahetvā, ‘‘iminā me parissāvanaṃ vicārethā’’ti daharaṃ avoca. Daharo mahāthera ‘‘kuhiṃ laddha’’nti āha. So sabbaṃ pavattiṃ kathesi. So taṃ sutvāva, ‘‘evarūpāya nāma saddhiṃ saṃvāsaṃ nālattha’’nti rāgagginā daḍḍho tattheva kālamakāsi.

Aññamaññaṃ ālāpasallāpavasena uppannarāgo pana samullapanasaṃsaggo nāma. Bhikkhuno bhikkhuniyā santakaṃ, bhikkhuniyā vā bhikkhussa santakaṃ gahetvā paribhogakaraṇavasena uppannarāgo sambhogasaṃsaggo nāma. So evaṃ veditabbo – maricavaṭṭivihāramahe kira bhikkhūnaṃ satasahassaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ navutisahassāni eva ahesuṃ. Eko sāmaṇero uṇhayāguṃ gahetvā gacchanto sakiṃ cīvarakaṇṇe ṭhapesi, sakiṃ bhūmiyaṃ. Ekā sāmaṇerī disvā ettha pattaṃ ṭhapetvā yāhīti thālakaṃ adāsi. Te aparabhāge ekasmiṃ bhaye uppanne parasamuddaṃ agamaṃsu. Tesu bhikkhunī puretaraṃ agamāsi. Sā, ‘‘eko kira sīhaḷabhikkhu āgato’’ti sutvā therassa santikaṃ gantvā paṭisanthāraṃ katvā nisinnā, – ‘‘bhante, maricavaṭṭivihāramahakāle tumhe kativassā’’ti pucchi. Tadāhaṃ sattavassikasāmaṇero. Tvaṃ pana kativassāti? Ahaṃ sattavassikasāmaṇerīyeva ekassa sāmaṇerassa uṇhayāguṃ gahetvā gacchantassa pattaṭhapanatthaṃ thālakamadāsinti. Thero, ‘‘ahaṃ so’’ti vatvā thālakaṃ nīharitvā dassesi. Te ettakeneva saṃsaggena brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ asakkontā dvepi saṭṭhivassakāle vibbhamiṃsu.

samullapanasaṃsaggo sambhogasaṃsaggo

Hatthagāhādivasena pana uppannarāgo kāyasaṃsaggo nāma. Tatridaṃ vatthu – mahācetiyaṅgaṇe kira daharabhikkhū sajjhāyaṃ gaṇhanti. Tesaṃ piṭṭhipasse daharabhikkhuniyo dhammaṃ suṇanti. Tatreko daharo hatthaṃ pasārento ekissā daharabhikkhuniyā kāyaṃ chupi. Sā taṃ hatthaṃ gahetvā attano urasmiṃ ṭhapesi, ettakena saṃsaggena dvepi vibbhamitvā gihibhāvaṃ pattā.

kāyasaṃsaggo

Gāhagāhakādivaṇṇanā

Imesu pana pañcasu saṃsaggesu bhikkhuno bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ savanadassanasamullapanasambhogakāyaparāmāsā niccampi hontiyeva, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ ṭhapetvā kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sesā kālena kālaṃ honti; tathā upāsakaupāsikāhi saddhiṃ sabbepi kālena kālaṃ honti. Tesu hi kilesuppattito cittaṃ rakkhitabbaṃ. Eko hi bhikkhu gāhagāhako hoti, eko gāhamuttako, eko muttagāhako, eko muttamuttako.

Tattha yaṃ bhikkhuṃ manussāpi āmisena upalāpetvā gahaṇavasena upasaṅkamanti, bhikkhupi pupphaphalādīhi upalāpetvā gahaṇavasena upasaṅkamati, ayaṃ gāhagāhako nāma. Yaṃ pana manussā vuttanayena upasaṅkamanti, bhikkhu dakkhiṇeyyavasena upasaṅkamati, ayaṃ gāhamuttako nāma. Yassa manussā dakkhiṇeyyavasena cattāro paccaye denti, bhikkhu pupphaphalādīhi upalāpetvā gahaṇavasena upasaṅkamati, ayaṃ muttagāhako nāma. Yassa manussāpi dakkhiṇeyyavasena cattāro paccaye denti, bhikkhupi cūḷapiṇḍapātiyatissatthero viya dakkhiṇeyyavasena paribhuñjati, ayaṃ muttamuttako nāma.

gāhagāhako gāhamuttako muttagāhako muttamuttako

Theraṃ kira ekā upāsikā dvādasa vassāni upaṭṭhahi. Ekadivasaṃ tasmiṃ gāme aggi uṭṭhahitvā gehāni jhāpesi. Aññesaṃ kulūpakabhikkhū āgantvā – ‘‘kiṃ upāsike, api kiñci bhaṇḍakaṃ arogaṃ kātuṃ asakkhitthā’’ti paṭisanthāraṃ akaṃsu. Manussā, ‘‘amhākaṃ mātu kulūpakatthero bhuñjanavelāyameva āgamissatī’’ti āhaṃsu. Theropi punadivase bhikkhācāravelaṃ sallakkhetvāva āgato. Upāsikā koṭṭhacchāyāya nisīdāpetvā bhikkhaṃ sampādetvā adāsi. There bhattakiccaṃ katvā pakkante manussā āhaṃsu – ‘‘amhākaṃ mātu kulūpakatthero bhuñjanavelāyameva āgato’’ti. Upāsikā, ‘‘tumhākaṃ kulūpakā tumhākaṃyeva anucchavikā, mayhaṃ thero mayheva anucchaviko’’ti āha. Āyasmā pana mantāṇiputto imehi pañcahi saṃsaggehi catūhipi parisāhi saddhiṃ asaṃsaṭṭho gāhamuttako ceva muttamuttako ca ahosi. Yathā ca sayaṃ asaṃsaṭṭho, evaṃ bhikkhūnampi taṃ asaṃsaggakathaṃ kattā ahosi.

Āraddhavīriyoti paggahitavīriyo, paripuṇṇakāyikacetasikavīriyoti attho. Yo hi bhikkhu gamane uppannakilesaṃ ṭhānaṃ pāpuṇituṃ na deti, ṭhāne uppannakilesaṃ nisajjaṃ, nisajjāya uppannakilesaṃ sayanaṃ pāpuṇituṃ na deti, mantena kaṇhasappaṃ uppīḷetvā gaṇhanto viya, amittaṃ gīvāya akkamanto viya ca vicarati, ayaṃ āraddhavīriyo nāma. Thero ca tādiso ahosi. Bhikkhūnampi tatheva vīriyārambhakathaṃ kattā ahosi.

Āraddhavīriyo āraddhavīriyo

Sīlasampannotiādīsu sīlanti catupārisuddhisīlaṃ. Samādhīti vipassanāpādakā aṭṭha samāpattiyo. Paññāti lokiyalokuttarañāṇaṃ. Vimuttīti ariyaphalaṃ. Vimuttiñāṇadassananti ekūnavīsatividhaṃ paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ. Thero sayampi sīlādīhi sampanno ahosi bhikkhūnampi sīlādikathaṃ kattā. Svāyaṃ dasahi kathāvatthūhi ovadatīti ovādako. Yathā pana eko ovadatiyeva, sukhumaṃ atthaṃ parivattetvā jānāpetuṃ na sakkoti. Na evaṃ thero. Thero pana tāni dasa kathāvatthūni viññāpetīti viññāpako. Eko viññāpetuṃ sakkoti, kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ na sakkoti. Thero kāraṇampi sandassetīti sandassako. Eko vijjamānaṃ kāraṇaṃ dasseti, gāhetuṃ pana na sakkoti. Thero gāhetumpi sakkotīti samādapako. Evaṃ samādapetvā pana tesu kathāvatthūsu ussāhajananavasena bhikkhū samuttejetīti samuttejako. Ussāhajāte vaṇṇaṃ vatvā sampahaṃsetīti sampahaṃsako.

Sīlasampanno sīla Samādhī Paññā Vimuttī Vimuttiñāṇadassana ovādako viññāpako sandassako samādapako samuttejako sampahaṃsako

Pañcalābhavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
252. Thus have I heard.
This is the Rathavinīta Sutta.
There, "in Rājagaha" means in a city of that name. It is called *Rājagaha* because it was completely surrounded by Mandhātu, Mahāgovinda, and others.
Others describe the circumstances differently.
What is the point of that? This is the name of that city.
At the time of the Buddhas and the *cakkavatti* kings, this city flourished. At other times it was deserted and inhabited by *yakkhas*. It remained a forest for them to dwell in.
