"*Bhagavati no, āvuso, brahmacariyaṃ vussatī*" (In the Blessed One, friend, the *brahmacariya* is lived), friend, is the *brahmacariya* lived by the venerable one near our Blessed One? This, the venerable Sāriputta, knowing that the dwelling of the *brahmacariya* was in the Blessed One, asked for the purpose of arousing conversation.

For if the former conversation is not established, the latter conversation does not arise; therefore he asked thus.

The Elder, assenting, said, "Yes, friend."

Then, wishing to hear the answer to his question, the venerable Sāriputta asked in order the seven purifications, "Is the *brahmacariya* lived in the Blessed One for the sake of purification of virtue, friend?"

The expanded account of these is stated in the *Visuddhimagga*.

The venerable Puṇṇa, however, since even for one established in the fourfold purity of virtue etc., the dwelling of the *brahmacariya* does not reach the summit, therefore, he rejected everything, saying, "No, this is not it, friend."

"*Bhagavati no, āvuso, brahmacariyaṃ vussatī*" (In the Blessed One, friend, the *brahmacariya* is lived) *Visuddhimagga*

"*Kimatthaṃ carahāvuso*" (For what, then, friend?) If the *brahmacariya* is not lived for the sake of purification of virtue etc., then for what is it lived?, he asked.

"*Anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ kho, āvuso*" (For the sake of *anupādāparinibbāna*, friend), here, *anupādāparinibbāna* means *appaccayaparinibbāna* (cessation without grasping).

There are two kinds of *upādāna* (grasping): grasping of acquisition (*gahaṇūpādāna*) and grasping of condition (*paccayūpādāna*).

"*Gahaṇūpādānaṃ*" means the fourfold grasping of sense pleasures etc., "*paccayūpādānaṃ*" means the conditioned things (saṅkhārā) because of ignorance, thus are the conditioned things spoken of.

There, the teachers who advocate grasping of acquisition (*gahaṇūpādānavādino*) say that *anupādāparinibbāna* is the fruition of *arhatship* that occurs without grasping any *dhamma* by any of the four graspings, and thus they speak of *anupādāparinibbāna*.

For indeed, it is neither associated with grasping nor does it grasp any *dhamma*, and because the defilements have ceased, it is called *parinibbāna*.

But the advocates of conditional grasping (*paccayūpādānavādino*) say that *anupādāparinibbāna* is *appaccayaparinibbāna* (cessation without conditions).
They declare that the unconditioned *asaṅkhataṃ* deathless element *amatadhātu* which has not arisen due to conditions, is indeed *anupādāparinibbāna*.

This is the end *anta*, this is the limit *koṭi*, this is the completion *niṭṭhā*.

For one who has attained unconditioned *appaccaya* passing away, the life of celibacy *brahmacariyavāsa* has reached its peak *matthakaṃ*. Therefore, the elder *thero* said, "The goal is passing away without remainder *anupādāparinibbānattha*."

Then, while questioning him further, venerable *āyasmā* Śāriputra asked again, "But what, friend *āvuso*, is purity of moral conduct *sīlavisuddhi*? Is it passing away without remainder *anupādāparinibbāna*?"

What is the purpose *kimatthaṃ*?

Wanderer, friend *carahāvuso*, the goal is passing away without remainder *anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ*, friend *āvuso*. Passing away without remainder *anupādāparinibbānaṃ*, clinging by grasping *gahaṇūpādānaṃ*, clinging by conditions *paccayūpādānaṃ*.

mula_pali:
257. ‘‘Bhagavati no, āvuso, brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ panāvuso, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ panāvuso, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhatthaṃ…pe… kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhatthaṃ…pe… maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ…pe… paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ…pe… kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ āvuso’ti vadesi. Kimatthaṃ carahāvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti? ‘‘Anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ panāvuso kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti ?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ panāvuso, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti?

‘‘No hidaṃ , āvuso’’.

‘‘Kiṃ panāvuso, aññatra imehi dhammehi anupādāparinibbāna’’nti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’’.

‘‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso, cittavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, diṭṭhivisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti…pe… kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi… maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi… paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi… ‘kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso, aññatra imehi dhammehi anupādāparinibbāna’nti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘no hidaṃ, āvuso’ti vadesi. Yathākathaṃ panāvuso, imassa bhāsitassa attho daṭṭhabbo’’ti?
mula_english:
"Is the holy life lived under the Blessed One, friend?"

"Yes, friend."

"But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of virtue?"

"No, friend."

"Then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of mind?"

"No, friend."

"But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of view?"

"No, friend."

"Then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by overcoming doubt?"

"No, friend."

"But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path?"

"No, friend."

"Then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision of the way?"

"No, friend."

"But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision?"

"No, friend."

"'Friend, when asked, "But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of virtue?" you replied, "No, friend." When asked, "Then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of mind?" you replied, "No, friend." But, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification of view…purification by overcoming doubt…purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path…purification by knowledge and vision of the way…but, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the sake of purification by knowledge and vision?" you replied, "No, friend." For what purpose, then, friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One?' "It is for the sake of final Nirvāṇa without clinging ( *anupādāparinirvāṇa*) that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One."

"But, friend, is purification of virtue final Nirvāṇa without clinging?"

"No, friend."

"Then, friend, is purification of mind final Nirvāṇa without clinging?"

"No, friend."

"But, friend, is purification of view final Nirvāṇa without clinging?"

"No, friend."

"Then, friend, is purification by overcoming doubt final Nirvāṇa without clinging?"

"No, friend."

"But, friend, is purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path final Nirvāṇa without clinging?"

"No, friend."

"Then, friend, is purification by knowledge and vision of the way final Nirvāṇa without clinging?"

"No, friend."

"But, friend, is purification by knowledge and vision final Nirvāṇa without clinging?"

"No, friend."

"Then, friend, is final Nirvāṇa without clinging to be attained without these states?"

"No, friend."

" 'Friend, when asked, "But, friend, is purification of virtue final Nirvāṇa without clinging?" you replied, "No, friend." When asked, "Then, friend, is purification of mind final Nirvāṇa without clinging?" you replied, "No, friend." But, friend, is purification of view final Nirvāṇa without clinging…purification by overcoming doubt…purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path…purification by knowledge and vision of the way…but, friend, is purification by knowledge and vision final Nirvāṇa without clinging?" you replied, "No, friend." Then, friend, is final Nirvāṇa without clinging to be attained without these states?' you replied, "No, friend." But how, friend, should the meaning of these statements be regarded?"

mula_pali: 258. ‘‘Sīlavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya paññāpessa (sī. syā.) evamaññatthapi. Cittavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Diṭṭhivisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya . Maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Ñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ ce, āvuso, bhagavā anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya, saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya. Aññatra ce, āvuso, imehi dhammehi anupādāparinibbānaṃ abhavissa, puthujjano parinibbāyeyya. Puthujjano hi, āvuso, aññatra imehi dhammehi. Tena hāvuso, upamaṃ te karissāmi; upamāyapidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti.
mula_english: 258. “Friend, if the Blessed One had described purification of virtue (*śīlavisuddhi*) as final Nirvāṇa (*anupādāparinirvāṇa*) without clinging, he would have described what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nirvāṇa without clinging. If the Blessed One had described purification of mind (*cittavisuddhi*) as final Nirvāṇa without clinging, he would have described what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nirvāṇa without clinging. If the Blessed One had described purification of view (*dṛṣṭivisuddhi*) as final Nirvāṇa without clinging, he would have described what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nirvāṇa without clinging. If the Blessed One had described purification by overcoming doubt (*kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi*) as final Nirvāṇa without clinging, he would have described what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nirvāṇa without clinging. If the Blessed One had described purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path (*maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi*) as final Nirvāṇa without clinging, he would have described what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nirvāṇa without clinging. If the Blessed One had described purification by knowledge and vision of the way (*paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi*) as final Nirvāṇa without clinging, he would have described what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nirvāṇa without clinging. If the Blessed One had described purification by knowledge and vision (*ñāṇadassanavisuddhi*) as final Nirvāṇa without clinging, he would have described what is still accompanied by clinging as final Nirvāṇa without clinging. And if final Nirvāṇa without clinging (*anupādāparinirvāṇa*) were to be attained without these states, then an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) would have attained final Nirvāṇa. For an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) is without these states. As to that, friend, I shall give you a simile, for some wise men understand the meaning of a statement by means of a simile.
commentary_pali:
258. Theropi sabbaparivattesu tatheva paṭikkhipitvā pariyosāne dosaṃ dassento sīlavisuddhiṃ ce, āvusotiādimāha. Tattha paññapeyyāti yadi paññapeyya. Saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyyāti saṅgahaṇadhammameva niggahaṇadhammaṃ sappaccayadhammameva appaccayadhammaṃ saṅkhatadhammameva asaṅkhatadhammanti paññapeyyāti attho. Ñāṇadassanavisuddhiyaṃ pana sappaccayadhammameva appaccayadhammaṃ saṅkhatadhammameva asaṅkhatadhammanti paññapeyyāti ayameva attho gahetabbo. Puthujjano hi, āvusoti ettha vaṭṭānugato lokiyabālaputhujjano daṭṭhabbo. So hi catupārisuddhisīlamattassāpi abhāvato sabbaso aññatra imehi dhammehi. Tena hīti yena kāraṇena ekacce paṇḍitā upamāya atthaṃ jānanti, tena kāraṇena upamaṃ te karissāmīti attho.

Sattarathavinītavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
The Elder, having rejected all the turnings in that same way and showing the fault at the end, said, "Purity of morality, friend," etc.

There, *paññapeyya* means if he should make known.

*Saupādānaṃyeva samānaṃ anupādāparinibbānaṃ paññapeyya* means that he should make known that the inclusive Dhamma is the exclusive Dhamma, that the conditioned Dhamma is the unconditioned Dhamma, that the conditioned Dhamma is the unconditioned Dhamma, is the meaning.

But in the purification of knowledge and vision, the meaning that should be taken is that he should make known that the conditioned Dhamma is the unconditioned Dhamma, that the conditioned Dhamma is the unconditioned Dhamma.

*Puthujjano hi, āvuso* means that the worldling fool, who is subject to the cycle [of rebirths], should be seen here.

For he is completely different from these things because of the absence of even mere morality consisting of the fourfold purity.

*Tena hī* means that because some wise people understand the meaning by means of a simile, for that reason I will make a simile for them, is the meaning.

Explanation of the Relays of the Seven Chariots

mula_pali:
259. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasantassa sākete kiñcideva accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ uppajjeyya. Tassa antarā ca sāvatthiṃ antarā ca sāketaṃ satta rathavinītāni upaṭṭhapeyyuṃ. Atha kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sāvatthiyā nikkhamitvā antepuradvārā paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya, paṭhamena rathavinītena dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Dutiyena rathavinītena tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Tatiyena rathavinītena catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Catutthena rathavinītena pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Pañcamena rathavinītena chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Chaṭṭhena rathavinītena sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇeyya, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjeyya, sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruheyya. Sattamena rathavinītena sāketaṃ anupāpuṇeyya antepuradvāraṃ. Tamenaṃ antepuradvāragataṃ samānaṃ mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘iminā tvaṃ, mahārāja, rathavinītena sāvatthiyā sāketaṃ anuppatto antepuradvāra’nti ? Kathaṃ byākaramāno nu kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sammā byākaramāno byākareyyā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ byākaramāno kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sammā byākaramāno byākareyya – ‘idha me sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasantassa sākete kiñcideva accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ uppajji uppajjati (ka.). Tassa me antarā ca sāvatthiṃ antarā ca sāketaṃ satta rathavinītāni upaṭṭhapesuṃ. Atha khvāhaṃ sāvatthiyā nikkhamitvā antepuradvārā paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Paṭhamena rathavinītena dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Dutiyena rathavinītena tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, dutiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Tatiyena rathavinītena catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, tatiyaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Catutthena rathavinītena pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, catutthaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Pañcamena rathavinītena chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, pañcamaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Chaṭṭhena rathavinītena sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ pāpuṇiṃ, chaṭṭhaṃ rathavinītaṃ vissajjiṃ, sattamaṃ rathavinītaṃ abhiruhiṃ. Sattamena rathavinītena sāketaṃ anuppatto antepuradvāra’nti. Evaṃ byākaramāno kho, āvuso, rājā pasenadi kosalo sammā byākaramāno byākareyyā’’ti.

uppajjati (ka.)

‘‘Evameva kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhi yāvadeva cittavisuddhatthā, cittavisuddhi yāvadeva diṭṭhivisuddhatthā, diṭṭhivisuddhi yāvadeva kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhatthā, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi yāvadeva maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva ñāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva anupādāparinibbānatthā. Anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’’ti.
mula_english:
259. Just as, friend, if King Pasenadi of Kosala, while residing in Śrāvastī, had some urgent business to attend to in Sāketa, seven relay chariots would be kept ready for him between Śrāvastī and Sāketa.

Then, friend, King Pasenadi of Kosala, leaving Śrāvastī through the inner palace door, would mount the first relay chariot, and by means of the first relay chariot he would arrive at the second relay chariot; he would dismiss the first relay chariot and mount the second relay chariot.

By means of the second relay chariot, he would arrive at the third relay chariot; he would dismiss the second relay chariot and mount the third relay chariot.

By means of the third relay chariot, he would arrive at the fourth relay chariot; he would dismiss the third relay chariot and mount the fourth relay chariot.

By means of the fourth relay chariot, he would arrive at the fifth relay chariot; he would dismiss the fourth relay chariot and mount the fifth relay chariot.

By means of the fifth relay chariot, he would arrive at the sixth relay chariot; he would dismiss the fifth relay chariot and mount the sixth relay chariot.

By means of the sixth relay chariot, he would arrive at the seventh relay chariot; he would dismiss the sixth relay chariot and mount the seventh relay chariot.

By means of the seventh relay chariot, he would arrive at the inner palace door in Sāketa.

Then, when he had come to the inner palace door, his friends and acquaintances, his kinsmen and relatives, would ask him: ‘Sire, did you come from Śrāvastī to the inner palace door in Sāketa by means of this relay chariot?’ How then should King Pasenadi of Kosala answer in order to answer correctly?"

"In order to answer correctly he should answer thus: 'Here, while I was residing in Śrāvastī, some urgent business arose for me to attend to in Sāketa.

Seven relay chariots were kept ready for me between Śrāvastī and Sāketa.

Then, leaving Śrāvastī through the inner palace door, I mounted the first relay chariot.

By means of the first relay chariot, I arrived at the second relay chariot; I dismissed the first relay chariot and mounted the second relay chariot.

By means of the second relay chariot, I arrived at the third relay chariot; I dismissed the second relay chariot and mounted the third relay chariot.

By means of the third relay chariot, I arrived at the fourth relay chariot; I dismissed the third relay chariot and mounted the fourth relay chariot.

By means of the fourth relay chariot, I arrived at the fifth relay chariot; I dismissed the fourth relay chariot and mounted the fifth relay chariot.

By means of the fifth relay chariot, I arrived at the sixth relay chariot; I dismissed the fifth relay chariot and mounted the sixth relay chariot.

By means of the sixth relay chariot, I arrived at the seventh relay chariot; I dismissed the sixth relay chariot and mounted the seventh relay chariot.

By means of the seventh relay chariot, I arrived at the inner palace door in Sāketa.’

In order to answer correctly, King Pasenadi of Kosala should answer thus."

Just so, friend, purification of virtue (*śīla-viśuddhi*) is for the sake of reaching purification of mind (*citta-viśuddhi*); purification of mind (*citta-viśuddhi*) is for the sake of reaching purification of view (*dṛṣṭi-viśuddhi*); purification of view (*dṛṣṭi-viśuddhi*) is for the sake of reaching purification by overcoming doubt (*kāṅkhāvitaraṇa-viśuddhi*); purification by overcoming doubt (*kāṅkhāvitaraṇa-viśuddhi*) is for the sake of reaching purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path (*maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi*); purification by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path (*maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi*) is for the sake of reaching purification by knowledge and vision of the way (*paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi*); purification by knowledge and vision of the way (*paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi*) is for the sake of reaching purification by knowledge and vision (*ñāṇadassanavisuddhi*); purification by knowledge and vision (*ñāṇadassanavisuddhi*) is for the sake of final Nirvāṇa without clinging (*anupādāparinibbānatthā*).

It is for the sake of final Nirvāṇa without clinging (*anupādāparinibbānatthā*) that the holy life (*brahmacarya*) is lived under the Blessed One (*bhagavati*)."
commentary_pali:
259.Sattarathavinītānīti vinītaassājāniyayutte satta rathe. Yāvadeva, cittavisuddhatthāti , āvuso, ayaṃ sīlavisuddhi nāma, yāvadeva, cittavisuddhatthā. Cittavisuddhatthāti nissakkavacanametaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha attho, yāvadeva, cittavisuddhisaṅkhātā atthā, tāva ayaṃ sīlavisuddhi nāma icchitabbā. Yā pana ayaṃ cittavisuddhi, esā sīlavisuddhiyā attho, ayaṃ koṭi, idaṃ pariyosānaṃ, cittavisuddhiyaṃ ṭhitassa hi sīlavisuddhikiccaṃ kataṃ nāma hotīti. Esa nayo sabbapadesu.

Idaṃ panettha opammasaṃsandanaṃ – rājā pasenadi kosalo viya hi jarāmaraṇabhīruko yogāvacaro daṭṭhabbo. Sāvatthinagaraṃ viya sakkāyanagaraṃ, sāketanagaraṃ viya nibbānanagaraṃ, rañño sākete vaḍḍhiāvahassa sīghaṃ gantvā pāpuṇitabbassa accāyikassa kiccassa uppādakālo viya yogino anabhisametānaṃ catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ abhisamayakiccassa uppādakālo. Satta rathavinītāni viya satta visuddhiyo, paṭhamaṃ rathavinītaṃ āruḷhakālo viya sīlavisuddhiyaṃ ṭhitakālo, paṭhamarathavinītādīhi dutiyādīni āruḷhakālo viya sīlavisuddhiādīhi cittavisuddhiādīsu ṭhitakālo. Sattamena rathavinītena sākete antepuradvāre oruyha uparipāsāde ñātimittagaṇaparivutassa surasabhojanaparibhogakālo viya yogino ñāṇadassanavisuddhiyā sabbakilese khepetvā dhammavarapāsādaṃ āruyha paropaṇṇāsakusaladhammaparivārassa nibbānārammaṇaṃ phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā nirodhasayane nisinnassa lokuttarasukhānubhavanakālo daṭṭhabbo.

Iti āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ dasakathāvatthulābhiṃ dhammasenāpatisāriputtatthero satta visuddhiyo pucchi. Āyasmā puṇṇo dasa kathāvatthūni vissajjesi. Evaṃ pucchanto pana dhammasenāpati kiṃ jānitvā pucchi, udāhu ajānitvā? Titthakusalo vā pana hutvā visayasmiṃ pucchi, udāhu atitthakusalo hutvā avisayasmiṃ? Puṇṇattheropi ca kiṃ jānitvā vissajjesi, udāhu ajānitvā? Titthakusalo vā pana hutvā visayasmiṃ vissajjesi, udāhu atitthakusalo hutvā avisayeti? Jānitvā titthakusalo hutvā visaye pucchīti hi vadamāno dhammasenāpatiṃyeva vadeyya. Jānitvā titthakusalo hutvā visaye vissajjesīti vadamāno puṇṇattheraṃyeva vadeyya. Yañhi visuddhīsu saṃkhittaṃ, taṃ kathāvatthūsu vitthiṇṇaṃ. Yaṃ kathāvatthūsu saṃkhittaṃ, taṃ visuddhīsu vitthiṇṇaṃ. Tadaminā nayena veditabbaṃ.

Visuddhīsu hi ekā sīlavisuddhi cattāri kathāvatthūni hutvā āgatā appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā asaṃsaggakathā, sīlakathāti. Ekā cittavisuddhi tīṇi kathāvatthūni hutvā āgatā – pavivekakathā, vīriyārambhakathā, samādhikathāti, evaṃ tāva yaṃ visuddhīsu saṃkhittaṃ, taṃ kathāvatthūsu vitthiṇṇaṃ. Kathāvatthūsu pana ekā paññākathā pañca visuddhiyo hutvā āgatā – diṭṭhivisuddhi, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi, ñāṇadassanavisuddhīti, evaṃ yaṃ kathāvatthūsu saṃkhittaṃ, taṃ visuddhīsu vitthiṇṇaṃ. Tasmā sāriputtatthero satta visuddhiyo pucchanto na aññaṃ pucchi, dasa kathāvatthūniyeva pucchi. Puṇṇattheropi satta visuddhiyo vissajjento na aññaṃ vissajjesi, dasa kathāvatthūniyeva vissajjesīti. Iti ubhopete jānitvā titthakusalā hutvā visayeva pañhaṃ pucchiṃsu ceva vissajjesuṃ cāti veditabbo.
commentary_english:
259.
*Satta rathavinītāni* means seven chariots yoked with well-trained thoroughbreds.
*Yāvadeva, cittavisuddhatthā*… Brother, this is called purity of morality, as far as purity of mind.
*Cittavisuddhatthā* means this is a statement without doubt.
Herein lies the meaning, as far as the meanings known as purity of mind, so far this is called purity of morality, [something] to be desired.
Moreover, this purity of mind, this is the meaning of purity of morality, this is the limit, this is the end, because for one established in purity of mind, the task of purity of morality is said to be done.
This same method applies to all the remaining cases.

Herein is a comparison: the king, Pasenadi Kosala, like a yogin fearful of old age and death, should be seen.
Sāvatthi City, like Sakkāya City; Sāketa City, like Nirvāṇa City; like the time of the arising of an urgent task that should be quickly undertaken by the king in Sāketa who is the bringer of increase, like the time of the arising of the task of comprehension of the four noble truths for the yogin who has not comprehended [them].
Seven trained chariots are like seven purifications; the time of mounting the first trained chariot is like the time of being established in purity of morality; the time of mounting the second, etc., with the first trained chariot, etc., is like the time of being established in purity of mind, etc., with purity of morality, etc.
By the seventh trained chariot, having descended at the inner gate in Sāketa, in the upper palace, surrounded by a retinue of relatives and friends, the time of partaking in delicious food and enjoyment is like the time for the yogin, through the purification of the knowledge and vision, having destroyed all defilements, having ascended to the excellent Dhamma palace, the time for experiencing transcendental happiness for one sitting on the couch of cessation, having abandoned the attainment of the fruit of Nirvāṇa as an object, [and surrounded by] a retinue of noble and wholesome dhammas.

Thus, the venerable Puṇṇa, the receiver of ten grounds for discussion, the general of the Dhamma, Sāriputtatthera, asked about the seven purifications.
The venerable Puṇṇa explained the ten grounds for discussion.
How was it that while asking thus, the general of the Dhamma asked knowing [something], or without knowing? Or did he ask in a domain, being skilled in the doctrines, or did he ask in a non-domain, being unskilled in the doctrines? And how was it that Puṇṇatthera explained knowing [something], or without knowing? Or did he explain in a domain, being skilled in the doctrines, or did he explain in a non-domain, being unskilled in the doctrines? Indeed, the one speaking, “Having known [something], being skilled in the doctrines, he asked in a domain,” would speak to the general of the Dhamma himself.
The one speaking, “Having known [something], being skilled in the doctrines, he explained in a domain,” would speak to Puṇṇatthera himself.
Indeed, what is condensed in the purifications, that is expanded in the grounds for discussion.
What is condensed in the grounds for discussion, that is expanded in the purifications.
That should be understood by this method.

Indeed, in the purifications, one purity of morality, having become four grounds for discussion, has come: the talk of few wishes, the talk of contentment, the talk of non-association, the talk of morality.
One purity of mind, having become three grounds for discussion, has come: the talk of seclusion, the talk of initiating effort, the talk of samādhi. Thus, so far, what is condensed in the purifications, that is expanded in the grounds for discussion.
Moreover, in the grounds for discussion, one talk of wisdom, having become five purifications, has come: purity of vision, purity of overcoming doubt, purity of knowledge and vision of the path and non-path, purity of knowledge and vision of the course of practice, purity of knowledge and vision; thus, what is condensed in the grounds for discussion, that is expanded in the purifications.
Therefore, Sāriputtatthero, while asking about the seven purifications, did not ask about something else, but asked only about the ten grounds for discussion.
Puṇṇatthera also, while explaining the seven purifications, did not explain something else, but explained only the ten grounds for discussion.
Thus, it should be understood that both of them, having known [something], being skilled in the doctrines, asked and explained the question in a domain.

mula_pali:
260. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘konāmo āyasmā, kathañca panāyasmantaṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī’’ti? ‘‘Puṇṇoti kho me, āvuso, nāmaṃ; mantāṇiputtoti ca pana maṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī’’ti. ‘‘Acchariyaṃ, āvuso, abbhutaṃ, āvuso! Yathā taṃ sutavatā sāvakena sammadeva satthusāsanaṃ ājānantena, evameva āyasmatā puṇṇena mantāṇiputtena gambhīrā gambhīrapañhā anumassa anumassa byākatā. Lābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ, ye āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ labhanti dassanāya, labhanti payirūpāsanāya. Celaṇḍukena celaṇḍakena (ka.), celaṇḍupekena (?) cepi sabrahmacārī āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ muddhanā pariharantā labheyyuṃ dassanāya, labheyyuṃ payirūpāsanāya, tesampi lābhā tesampi suladdhaṃ, amhākampi lābhā amhākampi suladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ puṇṇaṃ mantāṇiputtaṃ labhāma dassanāya, labhāma payirūpāsanāyā’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ko nāmo āyasmā, kathañca panāyasmantaṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī’’ti? ‘‘Upatissoti kho me, āvuso, nāmaṃ; sāriputtoti ca pana maṃ sabrahmacārī jānantī’’ti. ‘‘Satthukappena vata kira, bho kho (ka.), sāvakena saddhiṃ mantayamānā na jānimha – ‘āyasmā sāriputto’ti. Sace hi mayaṃ jāneyyāma ‘āyasmā sāriputto’ti, ettakampi no nappaṭibhāseyya nappaṭibheyya (?). Acchariyaṃ, āvuso, abbhutaṃ, āvuso! Yathā taṃ sutavatā sāvakena sammadeva satthusāsanaṃ ājānantena, evameva āyasmatā sāriputtena gambhīrā gambhīrapañhā anumassa anumassa pucchitā. Lābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ suladdhalābhā sabrahmacārīnaṃ, ye āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ labhanti dassanāya, labhanti payirūpāsanāya. Celaṇḍukena cepi sabrahmacārī āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ muddhanā pariharantā labheyyuṃ dassanāya, labheyyuṃ payirūpāsanāya, tesampi lābhā tesampi suladdhaṃ, amhākampi lābhā amhākampi suladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ labhāma dassanāya, labhāma payirūpāsanāyā’’ti.

kho (ka.) nappaṭibheyya (?)

Itiha te ubhopi mahānāgā aññamaññassa subhāsitaṃ samanumodiṃsūti.

Rathavinītasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
260.

Thus spoken, the venerable Śāriputra said to the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, "What is the venerable one's name? And how do your companions in the holy life know the venerable one?"

"My name, friend, is Puṇṇa, and my companions in the holy life know me as Mantāṇiputta."

"Amazing, friend, astonishing, friend! Just as a learned disciple would rightly understand the Teacher’s Dispensation, even so, venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, have profound questions been explained point by point.

It is a gain for his companions in the holy life, a great gain for his companions in the holy life, that they have the opportunity to see and honour the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta.

Even if it were by carrying the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta about on a cushion on their heads that his companions in the holy life would get the opportunity to see and honour him, it would be a gain for them, a great gain for them. And it is a gain for us, a great gain for us that we have the opportunity to see and honor the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta."

Thus spoken, the venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta said to the venerable Śāriputta, "What is the venerable one's name? And how do your companions in the holy life know the venerable one?"

"My name, friend, is Upatissa, and my companions in the holy life know me as Śāriputta."

"Indeed, friend, we did not know that we were talking with the venerable Śāriputra, the disciple who is like the Teacher himself.

If we had known that it was the venerable Śāriputra, we would not have been able to say so much. Amazing, friend, astonishing, friend! Just as a learned disciple would rightly understand the Teacher’s Dispensation, even so, venerable Śāriputra, have profound questions been asked point by point.

It is a gain for his companions in the holy life, a great gain for his companions in the holy life, that they have the opportunity to see and honour the venerable Śāriputra.

Even if it were by carrying the venerable Śāriputra about on a cushion on their heads that his companions in the holy life would get the opportunity to see and honour him, it would be a gain for them, a great gain for them. And it is a gain for us, a great gain for us that we have the opportunity to see and honor the venerable Śāriputra."

Thus it was that these two great beings rejoiced in each other’s good words.

The Rathavinīta Sutta, the fourth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
260.Ko nāmo āyasmāti na thero tassa nāmaṃ na jānāti. Jānantoyeva pana sammodituṃ labhissāmīti pucchi. Kathañca panāyasmantanti idaṃ pana thero sammodamāno āha. Mantāṇiputtoti mantāṇiyā brāhmaṇiyā putto. Yathā tanti ettha tanti nipātamattaṃ, yathā sutavatā sāvakena byākātabbā, evameva byākatāti ayamettha saṅkhepattho. Anumassa anumassāti dasa kathāvatthūni ogāhetvā anupavisitvā. Celaṇḍupakenāti ettha celaṃ vuccati vatthaṃ, aṇḍupakaṃ cumbaṭakaṃ. Vatthacumbaṭakaṃ sīse katvā āyasmantaṃ tattha nisīdāpetvā pariharantāpi sabrahmacārī dassanāya labheyyuṃ, evaṃ laddhadassanampi tesaṃ lābhāyevāti aṭṭhānaparikappena abhiṇhadassanassa upāyaṃ dassesi. Evaṃ apariharantena hi pañhaṃ vā pucchitukāmena dhammaṃ vā sotukāmena ‘‘thero kattha ṭhito kattha nisinno’’ti pariyesantena caritabbaṃ hoti. Evaṃ pariharantā pana icchiticchitakkhaṇeyeva sīsato oropetvā mahārahe āsane nisīdāpetvā sakkā honti pañhaṃ vā pucchituṃ dhammaṃ vā sotuṃ. Iti aṭṭhānaparikappena abhiṇhadassanassa upāyaṃ dassesi.

Sāriputtoti ca pana manti sāriyā brāhmaṇiyā puttoti ca pana evaṃ maṃ sabrahmacārī jānanti. Satthukappenāti satthusadisena. Iti ekapadeneva āyasmā puṇṇo sāriputtattheraṃ candamaṇḍalaṃ āhacca ṭhapento viya ukkhipi. Therassa hi imasmiṃ ṭhāne ekantadhammakathikabhāvo pākaṭo ahosi. Amaccañhi purohitaṃ mahantoti vadamāno rājasadisoti vadeyya, goṇaṃ hatthippamāṇoti, vāpiṃ samuddappamāṇoti, ālokaṃ candimasūriyālokappamāṇoti, ito paraṃ etesaṃ mahantabhāvakathā nāma natthi. Sāvakampi mahāti vadanto satthupaṭibhāgoti vadeyya, ito paraṃ tassa mahantabhāvakathā nāma natthi. Iccāyasmā puṇṇo ekapadeneva theraṃ candamaṇḍalaṃ āhacca ṭhapento viya ukkhipi.

Sāriputtoti ca pana ma Satthukappenā

Ettakampi no nappaṭibhāseyyāti paṭisambhidāpattassa appaṭibhānaṃ nāma natthi. Yā panāyaṃ upamā āhaṭā, taṃ na āhareyyāma, atthameva katheyyāma. Upamā hi ajānantānaṃ āharīyatīti ayamettha adhippāyo. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana idampi paṭikkhipitvā upamā nāma buddhānampi santike āharīyati, theraṃ panesa apacāyamāno evamāhāti.

Ettakampi no nappaṭibhāseyyā

Anumassa anumassa pucchitāti dasa kathāvatthūni ogāhetvā ogāhetvā pucchitā. Kiṃ pana pañhassa pucchanaṃ bhāriyaṃ, udāhu vissajjananti? Uggahetvā pucchanaṃ no bhāriyaṃ, vissajjanaṃ pana bhāriyaṃ. Sahetukaṃ vā sakāraṇaṃ katvā pucchanampi vissajjanampi bhāriyameva. Samanumodiṃsūti samacittā hutvā anumodiṃsu. Iti yathānusandhināva desanā niṭṭhitāti.

Anumassa anumassa pucchitā Samanumodiṃsū

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Rathavinītasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
260. "What is the name, venerable one?" The elder does not know his name.

Knowing, he asked, "Will I be able to converse?"

"And how, venerable sir?" Thus, the elder, conversing, said:

"Mantāṇiputta" means the son of Mantāṇī, a *brāhmaṇī*.

"As that": here, "that" is merely a particle, as it should be explained by a learned disciple; just so it should be explained: this is the meaning in brief here.

"Anumassa anumassā": having plunged into the ten topics of discussion, and having sat down.

"Celaṇḍupakenā": here, "celaṃ" is said to be cloth, "aṇḍupakaṃ" is a bag.

Having put the cloth-bag on [his] head, having caused the venerable one to sit down there, even those fellow- ব্রহ্মচারীs who were carrying [him] might obtain a vision; thus, having obtained a vision, even that would be for their gain: by means of an improper imagination, he showed a means of frequent vision.

Thus, by one who does not carry [him], indeed, if one desires to ask a question or desires to hear the Dharma, "Where does the elder stand? Where does he sit?" 2.0159"/> it should be practiced by one who seeks.

Thus, those who are carrying [him], however, are able, at the very moment of wishing and desiring, having taken [him] down from [their] heads, having caused [him] to sit down on a very valuable seat, either to ask a question or to hear the Dharma.

Thus, by means of an improper imagination, he showed a means of frequent vision.

mula_pali:
261. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Na , bhikkhave, nevāpiko nivāpaṃ nivapati migajātānaṃ – ‘imaṃ me nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ migajātā paribhuñjantā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ yāpentū’ti. Evañca kho, bhikkhave, nevāpiko nivāpaṃ nivapati migajātānaṃ – ‘imaṃ me nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ migajātā anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissanti, anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjissanti, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjissanti, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissanti imasmiṃ nivāpe’ti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying at Sāvatthī (sāvatthiyaṃ) in the Jeta Grove (jetavane), in Anāthapiṇḍika's (anāthapiṇḍikassa) park (ārāme).

There the Blessed One (bhagavā) addressed the monks (bhikkhū), saying: "Monks (bhikkhavo)!"

"Venerable sir (bhadante)," those monks (bhikkhū) replied to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said this:

"Monks (bhikkhave), a deer-trapper (nevāpiko) does not lay down bait (nivāpaṃ nivapati) for a deer herd (migajātānaṃ), intending thus: 'May the deer herd (migajātā) enjoy (paribhuñjantā) this bait (imaṃ me nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ) that I have laid down and so be long-lived (dīghāyukā), handsome (vaṇṇavanto) and endure (yāpentū) for a long time (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ).'

A deer-trapper (nevāpiko) lays down bait (nivāpaṃ nivapati) for a deer herd (migajātānaṃ) intending thus: 'The deer herd (migajātā) will eat (bhuñjissanti) food (bhojanāni) unwarily (anupakhajja) by going right in amongst (mucchitā) the bait (imaṃ me nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ) that I have laid down; by so doing they will become intoxicated (anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjissanti); when they are intoxicated (mattā samānā), they will fall into negligence (pamādaṃ āpajjissanti); when they are negligent (pamattā samānā), I can do with them as I like (yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissanti) on account of this bait (imasmiṃ nivāpe).' "
commentary_pali: 261.Evaṃme sutanti nivāpasuttaṃ. Tattha nevāpikoti yo migānaṃ gahaṇatthāya araññe tiṇabījāni vapati ‘‘idaṃ tiṇaṃ khādituṃ āgate mige sukhaṃ gaṇhissāmī’’ti. Nivāpanti vappaṃ. Nivuttanti vapitaṃ. Migajātāti migaghaṭā. Anupakhajjāti anupavisitvā. Mucchitāti taṇhāmucchanāya mucchitā, taṇhāya hadayaṃ pavisitvā mucchanākāraṃ pāpitāti attho. Madaṃ āpajjissantīti mānamadaṃ āpajjissanti. Pamādanti vissaṭṭhasatibhāvaṃ. Yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissantīti yathā icchissāma, tathā kātabbā bhavissanti. Imasmiṃ nivāpeti imasmiṃ nivāpaṭṭhāne. Ekaṃ kira nivāpatiṇaṃ nāma atthi nidāghabhaddakaṃ, taṃ yathā yathā nidāgho hoti, tathā tathā nīvāravanaṃ viya meghamālā viya ca ekagghanaṃ hoti, taṃ luddakā ekasmiṃ udakaphāsukaṭṭhāne kasitvā vapitvā vatiṃ katvā dvāraṃ yojetvā rakkhanti. Atha yadā mahānidāghe sabbatiṇāni sukkhāni honti, jivhātemanamattampi udakaṃ dullabhaṃ hoti, tadā migajātā sukkhatiṇāni ceva purāṇapaṇṇāni ca khādantā kampamānā viya vicarantā nivāpatiṇassa gandhaṃ ghāyitvā vadhabandhanādīni agaṇayitvā vatiṃ ajjhottharantā pavisanti. Tesañhi nivāpatiṇaṃ ativiya piyaṃ hoti manāpaṃ. Nevāpiko te disvā dve tīṇi divasāni pamatto viya hoti, dvāraṃ vivaritvā tiṭṭhati. Antonivāpaṭṭhāne tahiṃ tahiṃ udakaāvāṭakāpi honti, migā vivaṭadvārena pavisitvā khāditamattakaṃ pivitamattakameva katvā pakkamanti, punadivase kiñci na karontīti kaṇṇe cālayamānā khāditvā pivitvā ataramānā gacchanti, punadivase koci kiñci kattā natthīti yāvadatthaṃ khāditvā pivitvā maṇḍalagumbaṃ pavisitvā nipajjanti. Luddakā tesaṃ pamattabhāvaṃ jānitvā dvāraṃ pidhāya samparivāretvā koṭito paṭṭhāya koṭṭetvā gacchanti, evaṃ te tasmiṃ nivāpe nevāpikassa yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavanti.
commentary_english:
261. Thus, I have heard: the Nivāpa Sutta.

There, *nevāpika* means one who, for the purpose of catching deer, scatters grass seeds in the forest, thinking, "When deer come to eat this grass, I will easily catch them."

*Nivāpa* means sowing.

*Nivutta* means sown.

*Migajātā* means a group of deer.

*Anupakhajjā* means having approached.

*Mucchitā* means intoxicated with craving; intoxicated by the intoxication of craving, having entered the heart due to craving, it has reached the state of intoxication. This is the meaning.

*Madaṃ āpajjissantī* means they will indulge in the intoxication of pride.

*Pamāda* means a state of scattered mindfulness.

*Yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissantī* means they will be able to do as they please, as we wish, so it should be done.

*Imasmiṃ nivāpe* means in this *nivāpa*-place.

It is said that there is a certain grass called *nivāpatiṇaṃ*, which is excellent in the hot season. As the hot season progresses, it becomes a single mass like a *nīvāra* forest or a chain of clouds. Hunters, having tilled and sown it in a place with accessible water, make a fence, join a door, and guard it.

Then, when in the great heat all the grasses are dry, and even a tongue's tip of water is hard to find, then the deer, eating dry grasses and old leaves, wandering about as if trembling, smelling the scent of the *nivāpatiṇa*, not counting the dangers of death and imprisonment, enter, pushing through the fence.

For them, that *nivāpatiṇaṃ* is exceedingly dear and pleasing.

The *nevāpika*, having seen them, acts as if he is careless for two or three days, and stands having opened the door.

In the inner *nivāpa* place, here and there, there are also water-holes. The deer, having entered through the open door, having eaten and drunk only a little, depart. On the next day, thinking that no one will do anything, they go shaking their ears, eating, drinking, and not hurrying. On the next day, thinking that no one is the maker of anything, having eaten and drunk as much as they want, they enter the circular thicket and lie down.

The hunters, having known their state of carelessness, having closed the door, having surrounded them, starting from the edge, go striking and killing them. Thus, in that *nivāpa*, they become able to be treated as they please by the *nevāpika*.

mula_pali: 262. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, paṭhamā migajātā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.
mula_english: “Now, *bhikkhus*, the deer of the first herd, without caution, approached and consumed the intoxicating food in that bait laid by the deer-trapper (*nevāpika*); by approaching and consuming that intoxicating food, they became intoxicated (*mada*); being intoxicated, they fell into negligence (*pramāda*); being negligent, they became subject to the deer-trapper’s will in that bait. Thus, *bhikkhus*, the deer of the first herd did not escape the power (*iddhānubhāva*) of the deer-trapper (*nevāpika*).
commentary_pali: 262.Tatra, bhikkhaveti, bhikkhave, tesu migajātesu. Paṭhamā migajātāti, migajātā paṭhamadutiyā nāma natthi. Bhagavā pana āgatapaṭipāṭivasena kappetvā paṭhamā, dutiyā, tatiyā , catutthāti nāmaṃ āropetvā dassesi. Iddhānubhāvāti yathākāmaṃ kattabbabhāvato; vasībhāvoyeva hi ettha iddhīti ca ānubhāvoti ca adhippeto.
commentary_english:
There, *bhikkhaves*, that is, *bhikkhaves*, among those kinds of deer.

The first kind of deer, that is, there is no such thing as a second first kind of deer.

The Blessed One, however, having imagined it in the order in which it came, showed it by imposing the name first, second, third, fourth.

The power ofiddhi, that is, because of the possibility of doing as one wishes; for mastery alone is intended here as *iddhi*, and *anubhāva*.

mula_pali: 263. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihariṃsu. Tesaṃ gimhānaṃ pacchime māse, tiṇodakasaṅkhaye, adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Tesaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ pattakāyānaṃ balavīriyaṃ parihāyi. Balavīriye parihīne tameva nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa paccāgamiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.
mula_english: 263. “Here, monks, the second herd of deer thought thus: ‘Those first deer ate food unwarily by going right in amongst the bait that the deer-trapper had laid down. They ate food unwarily by going right in amongst it, and by so doing they became intoxicated; when they were intoxicated, they fell into negligence; when they were negligent, the deer-trapper did with them as he liked on account of that bait. Suppose we altogether shun that bait food; shunning that fearful enjoyment, let us go out into the forest wilds and live there.’ They altogether shunned that bait food; shunning that fearful enjoyment, they went out into the forest wilds and lived there. But in the last month of the hot season when the grass and the water were used up, their bodies were reduced to extreme emaciation; with that they lost their strength and energy; when they had lost their strength and energy, they returned to that same bait that the deer-trapper had laid down. They ate food unwarily by going right in amongst it. They ate food unwarily by going right in amongst it, and by so doing they became intoxicated; when they were intoxicated, they fell into negligence; when they were negligent, the deer-trapper did with them as he liked on account of that bait. And that is how the deer of the second herd also failed to get free from the deer-trapper’s power and control.
commentary_pali: 263.Bhayabhogāti bhayena bhogato. Balavīriyanti aparāparaṃ sañcaraṇavāyodhātu, sā parihāyīti attho.
commentary_english: 263. *bhayabhogā* means by fear, by enjoyment. *balavīriya* means the wind element that moves from one to another, that is what is meant by declining.

mula_pali:
264. ‘‘Tatra , bhikkhave, tatiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmāti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihariṃsu. Tesaṃ gimhānaṃ pacchime māse tiṇodakasaṅkhaye adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Tesaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ pattakāyānaṃ balavīriyaṃ parihāyi. Balavīriye parihīne tameva nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa paccāgamiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe. Evañhi te dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyāma. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjissāma, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissāma nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe’ti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṃ kappayiṃsu. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘saṭhāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā ketabino, iddhimantāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā parajanā; imañca nāma nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ paribhuñjanti, na ca nesaṃ jānāma āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi daṇḍavāgurāhi (syā.) samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāreyyāma – appeva nāma tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ passeyyāma, yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyu’nti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresuṃ. Addasaṃsu kho, bhikkhave, nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ, yattha te gāhaṃ agamaṃsu. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, tatiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.

daṇḍavāgurāhi (syā.)
mula_english:
264. It is said, "There, monks, the deer of the third herd thought thus: 'Those deer of the first herd, by acting as they did without precaution, failed to get free from the deer-trapper’s *nivāpa* that was laid down... and so on... and that is how those deer of the first herd failed to get free from the deer-trapper’s power and control.

And those deer of the second herd thought thus: 'Those deer of the first herd, by acting as they did without precaution, failed to get free from the deer-trapper’s *nivāpa* that was laid down... and so on... and that is how those deer of the first herd failed to get free from the deer-trapper’s power and control.

Suppose we altogether shun that *nivāpa*-food; shunning that fearful enjoyment, let us go out into the forest wilds (*araññāyatana*) and live there.'

They altogether shunned that *nivāpa*-food; shunning that fearful enjoyment, they went out into the forest wilds (*araññāyatana*) and lived there.

But in the last month of the hot season when the grass and the water were used up, their bodies were reduced to extreme emaciation;

with that they lost their strength (*bala*) and energy (*vīriya*);

when they had lost their strength (*bala*) and energy (*vīriya*), they returned to that same *nivāpa* that the deer-trapper had laid down.

They ate food unwarily by going right in amongst it;

by so doing they became intoxicated; when they were intoxicated, they fell into negligence; when they were negligent, the deer-trapper did with them as he liked on account of that *nivāpa*.

And that is how the deer of the second herd also failed to get free from the deer-trapper’s power and control.

Suppose we make our dwelling place within range of the deer-trapper’s *nivāpa* that was laid down.

Then, having done so, we shall eat food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the *nivāpa* that the deer-trapper has laid down; by doing so we shall not become intoxicated; when we are not intoxicated, we shall not fall into negligence; when we are not negligent, the deer-trapper shall not do with us as he likes on account of that *nivāpa*.’

They made their dwelling place within range of the deer-trapper’s *nivāpa* that was laid down.

Then, having done so, they ate food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the *nivāpa* that the deer-trapper has laid down; by doing so they did not become intoxicated; when they were not intoxicated, they did not fall into negligence; when they were not negligent, the deer-trapper did not do with them as he liked on account of that *nivāpa*.

It is said, "There, monks, the deer-trapper and the deer-trapper’s retinue thought thus: ‘These deer of the third herd are certainly deceitful and cunning; these deer of the third herd are certainly powerful and strange; they enjoy that *nivāpa* that is laid down, and we do not know their coming or going.

Suppose we have this *nivāpa* that is laid down completely surrounded all round over a wide area with large wicker hurdles (*daṇḍavākara*); then perhaps we might see the third deer herd’s dwelling place (*āsaya*), where they go to hide.’

They had this *nivāpa* that was laid down completely surrounded all round over a wide area with large wicker hurdles (*daṇḍavākara*).

Monks, the deer-trapper and the deer-trapper’s retinue saw the third deer herd’s dwelling place (*āsaya*), where they went to hide.

And that is how those deer of the third herd also failed to get free from the deer-trapper’s power and control.
commentary_pali: 264.Upanissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyāmāti anto nipajjitvā khādantānampi bhayameva, bāhirato āgantvā khādantānampi bhayameva, mayaṃ pana amuṃ nivāpaṭṭhānaṃ nissāya ekamante āsayaṃ kappeyyāmāti cintayiṃsu. Upanissāyaāsayaṃ kappayiṃsūti luddakā nāma na sabbakālaṃ appamattā honti. Mayaṃ tattha tattha maṇḍalagumbesu ceva vatipādesu ca nipajjitvā etesu mukhadhovanatthaṃ vā āhārakiccakaraṇatthaṃ vā pakkantesu nivāpavatthuṃ pavisitvā khāditamattaṃ katvā amhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisissāmāti nivāpavatthuṃ upanissāya gahanesu gumbavatipādādīsu āsayaṃ kappayiṃsu. Bhuñjiṃsūti vuttanayena luddakānaṃ pamādakālaṃ ñatvā sīghaṃ sīghaṃ pavisitvā bhuñjiṃsu. Ketabinoti sikkhitakerāṭikā. Iddhimantāti iddhimanto viya. Parajanāti yakkhā. Ime na migajātāti. Āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vāti iminā nāma ṭhānena āgacchanti, amutra gacchantīti idaṃ nesaṃ na jānāma. Daṇḍavākarāhīti daṇḍavākarajālehi. Samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresunti atimāyāvino ete, na dūraṃ gamissanti, santikeyeva nipannā bhavissantīti nivāpakkhettassa samantā sappadesaṃ mahantaṃ okāsaṃ anuparivāresuṃ. Addasaṃsūti evaṃ parivāretvā vākarajālaṃ samantato cāletvā olokentā addasaṃsu. Yattha teti yasmiṃ ṭhāne te gāhaṃ agamaṃsu, taṃ ṭhānaṃ addasaṃsūti attho.
commentary_english:
264. Thinking, "We will make a dwelling by relying on [this]," even those who lie down inside and eat have fear; even those who come from outside and eat have fear. We, however, relying on that *nivāpaṭṭhāna*, will make a dwelling in a secluded place," they thought.

"Having relied on [this], they made a dwelling," because hunters are not always heedful.

We, having lain down in various *maṇḍalagumbas*, *vatipādas*, when they have gone out for the purpose of washing their faces or doing their business relating to food, having entered the *nivāpavatthu*, having made [it such that] only what has been eaten [remains], we will enter our dwelling place," thus, relying on the *nivāpavatthu*, they made a dwelling in secluded places among the thickets, *gumbavatipādas*, and so forth.

"They enjoyed," in the manner stated, having known the hunters' time of negligence, having entered quickly, they enjoyed.

"*Ketabino*" means those trained in deception.

"*Iddhimantā*" means those who are like possessors of psychic power.

"*Parajanā*" means *yakṣas*.

These are not of the deer species.

"*Āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā*" means, "They come by means of this place, they go to the world beyond," we do not know this of them.

"*Daṇḍavākarāhī*" means with *daṇḍavākarajālas*.

"*Samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresuṃ*" means, "These are excessively deceitful; they will not go far; they will be lying down nearby," they completely surrounded the *nivāpakkhetta* with a large space all around.

"*Addasaṃsū*" means, "Having thus surrounded [it], having moved the *vākarajāla* all around, while looking around, they saw."

"*Yattha te*" means, "In whatever place they went to take hold of, they saw that place," is the meaning.

mula_pali:
265. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, catutthā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu…pe… evañhi te dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te tatiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te dutiyā migajātā evaṃ samacintesuṃ ‘ye kho te paṭhamā migajātā…pe… evañhi te paṭhamā migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā paṭiviramiṃsu…pe… evañhi te dutiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyāma, tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjissāma, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissāma nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe’ti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa upanissāya āsayaṃ kappayiṃsu, tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe.

‘‘Tatra nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘saṭhāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā ketabino, iddhimantāssunāmime tatiyā migajātā parajanā, imañca nāma nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ paribhuñjanti. Na ca nesaṃ jānāma āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīti daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāreyyāma, appeva nāma tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ passeyyāma, yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyu’nti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīti daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresuṃ. Addasaṃsu kho nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca tatiyānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ, yattha te gāhaṃ agamaṃsu. Evañhi te tatiyāpi migajātā na parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yattha agati nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca tatrāsayaṃ kappeyyāma, tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjissāma, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissāma nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe’ti. Te yattha agati nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca tatrāsayaṃ kappayiṃsu. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ nevāpikassa ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu, te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ nevāpikassa amusmiṃ nivāpe.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘saṭhāssunāmime catutthā migajātā ketabino, iddhimantāssunāmime catutthā migajātā parajanā. Imañca nāma nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ paribhuñjanti, na ca nesaṃ jānāma āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāreyyāma, appeva nāma catutthānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ passeyyāma yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyu’nti. Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mahatīhi daṇḍavākarāhi samantā sappadesaṃ anuparivāresuṃ. Neva kho, bhikkhave, addasaṃsu nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca catutthānaṃ migajātānaṃ āsayaṃ, yattha te gāhaṃ gaccheyyuṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca etadahosi – ‘sace kho mayaṃ catutthe migajāte ghaṭṭessāma, te ghaṭṭitā aññe ghaṭṭissanti te ghaṭṭitā aññe ghaṭṭissanti. Evaṃ imaṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ sabbaso migajātā parimuñcissanti. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ catutthe migajāte ajjhupekkheyyāmā’ti. Ajjhupekkhiṃsu kho, bhikkhave, nevāpiko ca nevāpikaparisā ca catutthe migajāte. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, catutthā migajātā parimucciṃsu nevāpikassa iddhānubhāvā.
mula_english:
265. Monks, the fourth herd of deer thought, "The first herd of deer...failed to get free from the deer-trapper's power and control. And so did the second and third herds."

"Suppose we shun that bait food altogether; shunning that fearful enjoyment, let us go out into the forest wilds and live there."

They shunned that bait food altogether...And so the second herd of deer failed to get free from the deer-trapper's power and control.

The third herd of deer thought, "The first herd of deer...failed to get free from the deer-trapper's power and control."

"Suppose we make our dwelling place within range of that bait that the deer-trapper has laid down; Then, having done so, we shall eat food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the bait that the deer-trapper has laid down. By doing so we shall not become intoxicated; when we are not intoxicated, we shall not fall into negligence; when we are not negligent, the deer-trapper shall not do with us as he likes on account of that bait."

They made their dwelling place within range of that bait that the deer-trapper had laid down. Then, having done so, they ate food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the bait that the deer-trapper had laid down. By doing so they did not become intoxicated; when they were not intoxicated, they did not fall into negligence; when they were not negligent, the deer-trapper did not do with them as he liked on account of that bait.

The deer-trapper and his following considered thus: "These third herd of deer are as cunning and crafty as wizards and sorcerers. They eat the bait that is laid down, but we do not know how they come and go.

Suppose we have the bait that is laid down completely surrounded all round over a wide area with wicker hurdles; then perhaps we might see the third deer herd's dwelling place, where they go to hide."

They had the bait that was laid down completely surrounded all round over a wide area with wicker hurdles.

The deer-trapper and his following saw the third herd of deer's dwelling place, where they went to hide.

And that is how the third herd of deer also failed to get free from the deer-trapper's power and control.

"Suppose we make our dwelling place where the deer-trapper and his following cannot go; Then, having done so, we shall eat food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the bait that the deer-trapper has laid down. By doing so we shall not become intoxicated; when we are not intoxicated, we shall not fall into negligence; when we are not negligent, the deer-trapper shall not do with us as he likes on account of that bait."

They made their dwelling place where the deer-trapper and his following could not go.

Having done so, they ate food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the bait that the deer-trapper had laid down. By doing so they did not become intoxicated; when they were not intoxicated, they did not fall into negligence; when they were not negligent, the deer-trapper did not do with them as he liked on account of that bait.

Monks, the deer-trapper and his following considered thus: "These fourth herd of deer are as cunning and crafty as wizards and sorcerers. They eat the bait that is laid down, but we do not know how they come and go.

Suppose we have the bait that is laid down completely surrounded all round over a wide area with wicker hurdles; then perhaps we might see the fourth deer herd's dwelling place, where they go to hide."

They had the bait that was laid down completely surrounded all round over a wide area with wicker hurdles.

Monks, the deer-trapper and his following did not see the fourth deer herd's dwelling place, where they went to hide.

Monks, the deer-trapper and his following considered thus: "If we scare the fourth deer herd, being scared they will alert others, and so the deer herds will all desert this bait that we have laid down.

Suppose we treat the fourth deer herd with indifference."But the deer-trapper and his company overlooked the fourth deer herd.

And that is how the deer of the fourth herd were freed from the deer-trapper’s power (*iddhānubhāva*).
commentary_pali: 265.Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yattha agatīti te kira evaṃ cintayiṃsu – ‘‘anto nipajjitvā anto khādantānampi bhayameva, bāhirato āgantvā khādantānampi santike vasitvā khādantānampi bhayameva, tepi hi vākarajālena parikkhipitvā gahitāyevā’’ti, tena tesaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘yaṃnūna mayaṃ yattha nevāpikassa ca nevāpikaparisāya ca agati avisayo, tattha tattha seyyaṃ kappeyyāmā’’ti. Aññe ghaṭṭessantīti tato tato dūrataravāsino aññe ghaṭṭessanti. Te ghaṭṭitā aññeti tepi ghaṭṭitā aññe tato dūrataravāsino ghaṭṭessanti. Evaṃ imaṃnivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ sabbaso migajātā parimuccissantīti evaṃ imaṃ amhehi nivuttaṃ nivāpaṃ sabbe migaghaṭā migasaṅghā vissajjessanti pariccajissanti. Ajjhupekkheyyāmāti tesaṃ gahaṇe abyāvaṭā bhaveyyāmāti; yathā tathā āgacchantesu hi taruṇapotako vā mahallako vā dubbalo vā yūthaparihīno vā sakkā honti laddhuṃ, anāgacchantesu kiñci natthi. Ajjhupekkhiṃsu kho, bhikkhaveti evaṃ cintetvā abyāvaṭāva ahesuṃ.
commentary_english:
265. "Where, indeed, there is no refuge for us," thus they considered: "Even remaining inside and eating inside, there is fear. Even coming from outside and eating, even dwelling nearby and eating, there is fear, since they are seized, having been surrounded by a net of words." Therefore, this occurred to them: "Where, indeed, there is no approach or domain for the barber and the barber's assembly, in that place, let us arrange our resting place."

"Others will strike," meaning others dwelling far away will strike.

"They, being struck, others," meaning those, being struck, others from there... dwelling far away will strike.

"Thus, this offering, abandoned, all the deer will be released," meaning thus, this offering abandoned by us, all the herds of deer, the assemblies of deer, will abandon and relinquish.

"We should be indifferent," meaning we would not be occupied with seizing them; for, as such, among those coming, either a young fawn, or an old one, or a weak one, or one excluded from the herd, it is possible to obtain; among those not coming, there is nothing.

"They were indifferent, monks," meaning, having thought thus, they were not occupied.

mula_pali: 266. ‘‘Upamā kho me ayaṃ, bhikkhave, katā atthassa viññāpanāya. Ayaṃ cevettha attho – nivāpoti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Nevāpikoti kho, bhikkhave, mārassetaṃ pāpimato adhivacanaṃ. Nevāpikaparisāti kho, bhikkhave, māraparisāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Migajātāti kho, bhikkhave, samaṇabrāhmaṇānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ.
mula_english:
266. “I have given this simile, *bhikkhus*, to illustrate a meaning.

This is the meaning: ‘Bait’ (*nivāpa*) is a term for the five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañcakāmaguṇāni*).

‘Deer-trapper’ (*nevāpika*) is a term for Māra the Evil One.

‘The deer-trapper’s following’ (*nevāpikaparisa*) is a term for Māra’s following.

‘Deer herd’ (*migajāta*) is a term for *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*.

mula_pali: 267. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise . Evañhi te, bhikkhave, paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Seyyathāpi te, bhikkhave, paṭhamā migajātā tathūpame ahaṃ ime paṭhame samaṇabrāhmaṇe vadāmi.
mula_english:
There, monks, those first *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s, unwarily approaching that bait which was set by Māra, and these material things of the world, ate food.

They ate food unwarily by going right in amongst it, they became intoxicated; when they were intoxicated, they fell into negligence; when they were negligent, they were at the mercy of Māra on account of that bait and those material things of the world.

And that is how those first *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s failed to get free from Māra’s power and control.

Monks, those *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s, I say, are just like the deer of the first herd.
commentary_pali: 267.Amuṃnivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisānīti ettha nivāpoti vā lokāmisānīti vā vaṭṭāmisabhūtānaṃ pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Māro na ca bījāni viya kāmaguṇe vapento āhiṇḍati, kāmaguṇagiddhānaṃ pana upari vasaṃ vatteti, tasmā kāmaguṇā mārassa nivāpā nāma honti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassā’’ti. Na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvāti mārassa vasaṃ gatā ahesuṃ, yathākāmakaraṇīyā. Ayaṃ saputtabhariyapabbajjāya āgataupamā.
commentary_english:
267. "That offering, ceased, of Māra, and these worldly baits," here, the term *nivāpa* or the term *lokāmisāni*, is an appellation for the five sense qualities which are the essence of attachment.

Māra does not wander sowing seeds in the sense qualities, but he controls those who are attached to the sense qualities. Therefore, the sense qualities are called Māra's offerings (nivāpa).

Thus it was said: "That offering, ceased, of Māra."

"They were not released from Māra's power (iddhānubhāvā)," means they came under Māra's control, acting according to his will.

This is a comparison that has come by way of renunciation with wife and children.

mula_pali:
268. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, dutiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise. Evañhi te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmāti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭiviramiṃsu, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihariṃsu. Te tattha sākabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, sāmākabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, nīvārabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, daddulabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, haṭabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, kaṇabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, ācāmabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, piññākabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, tiṇabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, gomayabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ, vanamūlaphalāhārā yāpesuṃ pavattaphalabhojī.

‘‘Tesaṃ gimhānaṃ pacchime māse, tiṇodakasaṅkhaye, adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Tesaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ pattakāyānaṃ balavīriyaṃ parihāyi. Balavīriye parihīne cetovimutti parihāyi. Cetovimuttiyā parihīnāya tameva nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa paccāgamiṃsu tāni ca lokāmisāni. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise. Evañhi te, bhikkhave, dutiyāpi samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Seyyathāpi te, bhikkhave, dutiyā migajātā tathūpame ahaṃ ime dutiye samaṇabrāhmaṇe vadāmi.
mula_english:
268. There, O monks, the second kind of *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s thought thus: ‘Those first *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s, having unwarily partaken of the bait ( *nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ* ) laid down by Māra, and those worldly allurements (*lokāmisāni*), ate food.

There, having unwarily partaken of the food, they became intoxicated (*madaṃ āpajjiṃsu*); being intoxicated, they fell into negligence (*pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu*); being negligent, Māra did with them as he pleased in that bait and those worldly allurements.

Indeed, those first *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s did not escape from the power of Māra (*mārassa iddhānubhāvā*).

Suppose we completely abstain from the bait-food (*nivāpabhojanā*) and worldly allurements (*lokāmisā*); shunning fearful enjoyments (*bhayabhogā*), let us enter the forest abodes (*araññāyatanāni*) and live there.’

They completely abstained from the bait-food and worldly allurements; shunning fearful enjoyments, [thinking] ‘Let us enter the forest abodes and live there.’

They completely abstained from the bait-food and worldly allurements; shunning fearful enjoyments, they entered the forest abodes and lived there.

There, they lived on greens (*sākabhakkhā*), or millet (*sāmākabhakkhā*), or wild rice (*nīvārabhakkhā*), or *daddula* (*daddulabhakkhā*), or *haṭa* (*haṭabhakkhā*), or rice-bran (*kaṇabhakkhā*), or the scum of boiled rice (*ācāmabhakkhā*), or oil-cake (*piññākabhakkhā*), or grass (*tiṇabhakkhā*), or cow dung (*gomayabhakkhā*); they sustained themselves on forest roots and fruits (*vanamūlaphalāhārā*), eating fallen fruits (*pavattaphalabhojī*).

In the last month of those hot seasons, when the grass and water had dwindled, their bodies became extremely emaciated (*adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti*).

Their strength and energy (*balavīriyaṃ*) diminished due to their extremely emaciated bodies.

With strength and energy diminished, their deliverance of mind (*cetovimutti*) diminished.

With the deliverance of mind diminished, they returned to that very bait laid down by Māra, and those worldly allurements.

There, having unwarily partaken of the food, they ate.

There, having unwarily partaken of the food, they became intoxicated; being intoxicated, they fell into negligence; being negligent, Māra did with them as he pleased in that bait and those worldly allurements.

Indeed, O monks, even those second kind of *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s did not escape from the power of Māra.

Just as those deer of the second herd, so too, I say, are these second *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s.
commentary_pali: 268.Cetovimutti parihāyīti ettha cetovimutti nāma araññe vasissāmāti uppannaajjhāsayo; so parihāyīti attho. Tathūpame ahaṃ ime dutiyeti ayaṃ brāhmaṇadhammikapabbajjāya upamā. Brāhmaṇā hi aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṃ caritvā vaṭṭupacchedabhayena paveṇiṃ ghaṭayissāmāti dhanaṃ pariyesitvā bhariyaṃ gahetvā agāramajjhe vasantā ekasmiṃ putte jāte ‘‘amhākaṃ putto jāto vaṭṭaṃ na ucchinnaṃ paveṇi ghaṭitā’’ti puna nikkhamitvā pabbajanti vā tameva vā sa’kalattavāsaṃ vasanti.
commentary_english: 268. Ceto-vimutti parihāyī: Here, ceto-vimutti means having the intention "I will live in the forest," which then diminishes; this is the meaning of *parihāyī*. Tathūpame ahaṃ ime dutiye: This is a comparison to the *brāhmaṇadhammikapabbajjā*. Brahmins, after practicing the *komārabrahmacariya* for eighty-eight years, thinking "We will establish the lineage" due to the fear of the cutting off of the family line (*vaṭṭupaccheda*), seek wealth, take a wife, and dwell in the midst of a house. When a son is born, thinking "Our son is born, the cycle is not broken, the lineage is established," they then leave again and take ordination (*pabbajanti*), or they continue to live the same married life (*sa’kalattavāsa*).

mula_pali:
269. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, tatiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni…pe…. Evañhi te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Yepi te dutiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃ samacintesuṃ – ‘ye kho te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni…pe…. Evañhi te paṭhamā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭivirameyyāma, bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihareyyāmā’ti. Te sabbaso nivāpabhojanā lokāmisā paṭiviramiṃsu. Bhayabhogā paṭiviratā araññāyatanāni ajjhogāhetvā vihariṃsu. Te tattha sākabhakkhāpi ahesuṃ…pe… pavattaphalabhojī. Tesaṃ gimhānaṃ pacchime māse tiṇodakasaṅkhaye adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Tesaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ pattakāyānaṃ balavīriyaṃ parihāyi, balavīriye parihīne cetovimutti parihāyi, cetovimuttiyā parihīnāya tameva nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa paccāgamiṃsu tāni ca lokāmisāni. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha anupakhajja mucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, mattā samānā pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, pamattā samānā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise. Evañhi te dutiyāpi samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni upanissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyāma, tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjissāma, ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjissāma, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjissāma, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā bhavissāma mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise’’ti.

‘‘Te amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni upanissāya āsayaṃ kappayiṃsu. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā amuṃ nivāpaṃ nivuttaṃ mārassa amūni ca lokāmisāni ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjiṃsu. Te tattha ananupakhajja amucchitā bhojanāni bhuñjamānā na madaṃ āpajjiṃsu, amattā samānā na pamādaṃ āpajjiṃsu, appamattā samānā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ mārassa amusmiṃ nivāpe amusmiñca lokāmise . Api ca kho evaṃdiṭṭhikā ahesuṃ – sassato loko itipi, asassato loko itipi; antavā loko itipi, anantavā loko itipi; taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ itipi, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ itipi; hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā itipi, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā itipi, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā itipi, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā itipi . Evañhi te, bhikkhave, tatiyāpi samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsu mārassa iddhānubhāvā. Seyyathāpi te, bhikkhave, tatiyā migajātā tathūpame ahaṃ ime tatiye samaṇabrāhmaṇe vadāmi.
mula_english:
“Now, bhikkhus, recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the third kind reckoned thus: ‘Those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the first kind, by acting as they did without precaution, regarding that bait that Māra had laid down and those material things of the world...

That is how the recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the first kind failed to get free from Māra’s power and control.
