Those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the second kind, by reckoning how the recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the first kind had failed, and then planning and acting as they did with the precaution of going to live in the forest wilds...

That is how the recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the first kind failed to get free from Māra’s power and control.

Suppose we altogether shun that bait food and those material things of the world; shunning that fearful enjoyment, let us go out into the forest wilds and live there.’

They altogether shunned that bait food and those material things of the world.

Shunning that fearful enjoyment, they went out into the forest wilds and lived there.

They were eaters even of pot-herbs there… and eaters of fallen fruit.

In the last month of the hot season, when the supply of grass and water was giving out, this body became excessively emaciated.

When the bodies of those with excessively emaciated bodies failed of strength and energy, when strength and energy had failed, concentration-release failed, and through concentration-release having failed, they went back again to that very bait that Māra had laid down and those material things of the world.

They ate food unwarily by going right in amongst it.

By so doing they became intoxicated; when they were intoxicated, they fell into negligence; when they were negligent, Mara did with them as he liked on account of that bait and those material things of the world.

and also the recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the second kind had failed,

Suppose we make our dwelling place within range of that bait that Māra has laid down and those material things of the world. Then, having done so, we shall eat food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the bait that Māra has laid down and the material things of the world. By doing so we shall not become intoxicated; when we are not intoxicated, we shall not fall into negligence; when we are not negligent, Māra shall not do with us as he likes on account of that bait and those material things of the world.’

They made their dwelling place within range of that bait that Māra had laid down and those material things of the world.

Then, having done so, they ate food not unwarily and without going right in amongst the bait that Māra had laid down and the material things of the world.

By so doing they did not become intoxicated; when they were not intoxicated, they did not fall into negligence; when they were not negligent, Māra did not do with them as he liked on account of that bait and those material things of the world.

“But then they came to hold views such as ‘the world is eternal’ and ‘the world is not eternal’ and ‘the world is finite’ and ‘the world is infinite’ and ‘the soul and the body are the same’ and ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’ and ‘after death a *Tathāgata* exists’ and ‘after death a *Tathāgata* does not exist’ and ‘after death a *Tathāgata* both exists and does not exist’ and ‘after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist.’

That is how those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of the third kind failed to get free ftorn Māra’s power and control.

Those recluses and *brāhmaṇas*, I say, are just like the deer of the third herd.
commentary_pali: 269.Evañhi te, bhikkhave, tatiyāpi samaṇabrāhmaṇā na parimucciṃsūti purimā viya tepi mārassa iddhānubhāvā na mucciṃsu; yathākāmakaraṇīyāva ahesuṃ. Kiṃ pana te akaṃsūti? Gāmanigamarājadhāniyo osaritvā tesu tesu ārāmauyyānaṭṭhānesu assamaṃ māpetvā nivasantā kuladārake hatthiassarathasippādīni nānappakārāni sippāni sikkhāpesuṃ. Iti te vākarajālena tatiyā migajātā viya mārassa pāpimato diṭṭhijālena parikkhipitvā yathākāmakaraṇīyā ahesuṃ.
commentary_english:
269. Indeed, bhikkhus, in this way, those *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s of the third kind did not escape; just like the previous ones, they also did not escape from the power and influence of Māra; they were just under his control.

But what did they do? Having moved away from villages, towns, and capital cities, and having built hermitages in various parks, gardens, and places, and dwelling there, they taught various kinds of crafts, such as elephant riding, horse riding, chariot driving, and other crafts to young boys from good families.

Thus, through the net of words, like the third kind of deer, they were surrounded by the net of views of the evil Māra and were under his control.

mula_pali:
271. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, agati mārassa ca māraparisāya ca? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu andhamakāsi māraṃ, apadaṃ vadhitvā māracakkhuṃ adassanaṃ gato pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati. Paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu andhamakāsi māraṃ, apadaṃ vadhitvā māracakkhuṃ adassanaṃ gato pāpimato tiṇṇo loke visattika’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Nivāpasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
271. “And how, monks, is there non-access for Māra and the host of Māra? Here, monks, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a *bhikkhu* enters and dwells in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra, to have become invisible to the Evil One by depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

“Again, monks, with the subsiding of thought and examination, a *bhikkhu* enters and dwells in the second *jhāna*, which has internal placidity and unification of mind and consists of rapture and pleasure born of concentration, without thought and examination. This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra...

“Again, monks, with the fading away of rapture, a *bhikkhu* dwells in equanimity, mindful and fully aware, and experiences pleasure with the body; he enters and dwells in the third *jhāna* of which the noble ones declare: ‘He is equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily.’ This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra...

“Again, monks, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a *bhikkhu* enters and dwells in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra...

“Again, monks, with the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*). This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra...

“Again, monks, by completely surmounting the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*). This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra...

“Again, monks, by completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*), aware that ‘there is nothing,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*). This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra...

“Again, monks, by completely surmounting the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*). This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra...

“Again, monks, by completely surmounting the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha*). And his taints are destroyed by his seeing with wisdom. This *bhikkhu*, monks, is said to have blindfolded Māra, to have become invisible to the Evil One by depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity, and to have crossed beyond attachment to the world.”

This is what the Blessed One said. Gratified, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Nivāpa Discourse, the fifth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
271.Andhamakāsi māranti na mārassa akkhīni bhindi. Vipassanāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpannassa pana bhikkhuno imaṃ nāma ārammaṇaṃ nissāya cittaṃ vattatīti māro passituṃ na sakkoti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘andhamakāsi māra’’nti. Apadaṃ vadhitvā māracakkhunti teneva pariyāyena yathā mārassa cakkhu apadaṃ hoti nippadaṃ, appatiṭṭhaṃ, nirārammaṇaṃ, evaṃ vadhitvāti attho. Adassanaṃ gato pāpimatoti teneva pariyāyena mārassa pāpimato adassanaṃ gato. Na hi so attano maṃsacakkhunā tassa vipassanāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpannassa bhikkhuno ñāṇasarīraṃ daṭṭhuṃ sakkoti. Paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā hontīti maggapaññāya cattāri ariyasaccāni disvā cattāro āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Tiṇṇo loke visattikanti loke sattavisattabhāvena visattikāti evaṃ saṅkhaṃ gataṃ. Atha vā ‘‘visattikāti kenaṭṭhena visattikā? Visatāti visattikā visaṭāti visattikā, vipulāti visattikā, visālāti visattikā, visamāti visattikā, visakkatīti visattikā, visaṃ haratīti visattikā, visaṃvādikāti visattikā, visamūlāti visattikā, visaphalāti visattikā, visaparibhogāti visattikā, visālā vā pana sā taṇhā rūpe sadde gandhe rase phoṭṭhabbe’’ti (mahāni. 3; cūḷani. mettagūmāṇavapucchāniddesa 22, khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa 124) visattikā. Evaṃ visattikāti saṅkhaṃ gataṃ taṇhaṃ tiṇṇo nittiṇṇo uttiṇṇo. Tena vuccati – ‘‘tiṇṇo loke visattika’’nti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Nivāpasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
271. *andhamakāsi māra* means he did not break Māra's eyes.

However, Māra is not able to see a *bhikkhu* who has attained the *jhāna* that is the basis of insight, thinking, "The mind functions relying on such and such an object."

Therefore, it was said: *andhamakāsi māra*.

*apadaṃ vadhitvā māracakkhu* means, according to that same method, just as Māra's eye becomes *apadaṃ*, *nippadaṃ* (without footing), *appatiṭṭhaṃ* (unsupported), *nirārammaṇaṃ* (without object), so he kills it. This is the meaning.

*adassanaṃ gato pāpimato* means, by that same method, he has gone out of sight of Māra, the evil one.

Indeed, he is not able to see with his fleshly eye the body of wisdom (*ñāṇasarīraṃ*) of that *bhikkhu* who has attained the *jhāna* that is the basis of insight.

*paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā hontī* means, having seen the four noble truths with the wisdom of the path (*maggapaññāya*), the four *āsavas* are destroyed.

*tiṇṇo loke visattika* means *visattikā* has gone to such a designation, due to the fact of clinging (*sattavisattabhāvena*) in the world.

Or rather, "In what sense is *visattikā visattikā*? Because it is *visata*, it is *visattikā*; because it is *visaṭa*, it is *visattikā*; because it is *vipula*, it is *visattikā*; because it is *visāla*, it is *visattikā*; because it is *visama*, it is *visattikā*; because it *visakkati*, it is *visattikā*; because it removes poison (*visaṃ harati*), it is *visattikā*; because it is deceitful (*visaṃvādikā*), it is *visattikā*; because it has poisonous roots (*visamūlā*), it is *visattikā*; because it has poisonous fruits (*visaphalā*), it is *visattikā*; because it has poisonous enjoyment (*visaparibhogā*), it is *visattikā*; or rather, that desire (*taṇhā*) is extensive (*visālā*) regarding forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tactile objects" (*mahāni.* 3; *cūḷani. mettagūmāṇavapucchāniddesa* 22, *khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* 124) *visattikā*.

Thus, *visattikā* has gone to such a designation: he has crossed over, completely crossed over, gone beyond that desire (*taṇhaṃ*).

Therefore, it is said: *tiṇṇo loke visattika*.

The Nivāpasutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary to the Majjhimanikāya, is finished.

mula_pali:
272. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘cirassutā no, āvuso ānanda, bhagavato sammukhā dhammī kathā. Sādhu mayaṃ, āvuso ānanda, labheyyāma bhagavato sammukhā dhammiṃ kathaṃ savanāyā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hāyasmanto yena rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamo tenupasaṅkamatha; appeva nāma labheyyātha bhagavato sammukhā dhammiṃ kathaṃ savanāyā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṃ.

Atha kho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena pubbārāmo migāramātupāsādo tenupasaṅkamissāma divāvihārāyā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ yena pubbārāmo migāramātupāsādo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena pubbakoṭṭhako tenupasaṅkamissāma gattāni parisiñcitu’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
mula_english:
272. Thus have I heard: At one time, the Blessed One (Bhagavān) was dwelling in Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī), in the Jeta Grove (Jetavana), in Anāthapiṇḍika’s (Anāthapiṇḍadasya) monastery (ārāma).

Then, early in the morning, the Blessed One having dressed, took his bowl and outer robe and went into Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī) for alms (piṇḍāya).

Then a number of monks (bhikkhus) approached the venerable Ānanda; having approached, they said to the venerable Ānanda: “It has been a long time, friend Ānanda, since we have heard a Dhamma talk (dharmī kathā) directly from the Blessed One (bhagavato sammukhā).

It would be good, friend Ānanda, if we might hear a Dhamma talk directly from the Blessed One (bhagavato sammukhā dhammīṃ kathaṃ savanāya)!”

“Then, venerable ones, go to the hermitage (assamo) of the brahmin (brāhmaṇassa) Rammaka; perhaps you might hear a Dhamma talk directly from the Blessed One (bhagavato sammukhā dhammīṃ kathaṃ savanāya)!”

“Yes, friend,” the monks replied to the venerable Ānanda.

Then the Blessed One, having wandered for alms in Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī), after the meal, returning from his alms round, addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to the Eastern Park (pubbārāmo), the Palace of Migāra’s Mother (Migāramātupāsādo), for the day’s abiding (divāvihārāya)!”

“So be it, venerable sir (bhante),” replied the venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with the venerable Ānanda, went to the Eastern Park (pubbārāmo), the Palace of Migāra’s Mother (Migāramātupāsādo), for the day’s abiding (divāvihārāya).

Then the Blessed One, in the evening, rising from retreat (paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito), addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to the eastern tank (pubbakoṭṭhako) to bathe our limbs (gattāni parisiñcitu)!”

“So be it, venerable sir (bhante),” replied the venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One.
commentary_pali:
272.Evaṃme sutanti pāsarāsisuttaṃ. Tattha sādhu mayaṃ, āvusoti āyācantā bhaṇanti. Ete kira pañcasatā bhikkhū janapadavāsino ‘‘dasabalaṃ passissāmā’’ti sāvatthiṃ anuppattā. Satthudassanaṃ pana etehi laddhaṃ, dhammiṃ kathaṃ na tāva suṇanti. Te satthugāravena ‘‘amhākaṃ, bhante , dhammakathaṃ kathethā’’ti vattuṃ na sakkonti. Buddhā hi garū honti, ekacāriko sīho migarājā viya, pabhinnakuñjaro viya, phaṇakataāsīviso viya, mahāaggikkhandho viya ca durāsadā vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Āsīviso yathā ghoro, migarājāva kesarī;

Nāgova kuñjaro dantī, evaṃ buddhā durāsadā’’ti.

Evaṃ durāsadaṃ satthāraṃ te bhikkhū sayaṃ yācituṃ asakkontā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ yācamānā ‘‘sādhu mayaṃ, āvuso’’ti āhaṃsu.

Appeva nāmāti api nāma labheyyātha. Kasmā pana thero te bhikkhū ‘‘rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamaṃ upasaṅkameyyāthā’’ti āha? Pākaṭakiriyatāya. Dasabalassa hi kiriyā therassa pākaṭā hoti; jānāti thero, ‘‘ajja satthā jetavane vasitvā pubbārāme divāvihāraṃ karissati; ajja pubbārāme vasitvā jetavane divāvihāraṃ karissati; ajja ekakova piṇḍāya pavisissati; ajja bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto imasmiṃ kāle janapadacārikaṃ nikkhamissatī’’ti. Kiṃ panassa evaṃ jānanatthaṃ cetopariyañāṇaṃ atthīti? Natthi. Anumānabuddhiyā pana katakiriyāya nayaggāhena jānāti. Yañhi divasaṃ bhagavā jetavane vasitvā pubbārāme divāvihāraṃ kātukāmo hoti, tadā senāsanaparikkhārabhaṇḍānaṃ paṭisāmanākāraṃ dasseti, thero sammajjanisaṅkārachaḍḍanakādīni paṭisāmeti. Pubbārāme vasitvā jetavanaṃ divāvihārāya āgamanakālepi eseva nayo.

Appeva nāmā

Yadā pana ekako piṇḍāya pavisitukāmo hoti, tadā pātova sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā gandhakuṭiṃ pavisitvā dvāraṃ pidhāya phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā nisīdati. Thero ‘‘ajja bhagavā bodhaneyyabandhavaṃ disvā nisinno’’ti tāya saññāya ñatvā ‘‘ajja, āvuso, bhagavā ekako pavisitukāmo, tumhe bhikkhācārasajjā hothā’’ti bhikkhūnaṃ saññaṃ deti. Yadā pana bhikkhusaṅghaparivāro pavisitukāmo hoti, tadā gandhakuṭidvāraṃ upaḍḍhapidahitaṃ katvā phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā nisīdati, thero tāya saññāya ñatvā pattacīvaraggahaṇatthāya bhikkhūnaṃ saññaṃ deti. Yadā janapadacārikaṃ nikkhamitukāmo hoti, tadā ekaṃ dve ālope atirekaṃ bhuñjati, sabbakālaṃ caṅkamanañcāruyha aparāparaṃ caṅkamati, thero tāya saññāya ñatvā ‘‘bhagavā, āvuso, janapadacārikaṃ caritukāmo, tumhākaṃ kattabbaṃ karothā’’ti bhikkhūnaṃ saññaṃ deti.

Bhagavā paṭhamabodhiyaṃ vīsati vassāni anibaddhavāso ahosi, pacchā pañcavīsati vassāni abbokiṇṇaṃ sāvatthiṃyeva upanissāya vasanto ekadivase dve ṭhānāni paribhuñjati. Jetavane rattiṃ vasitvā punadivase bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto dakkhiṇadvārena sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisitvā pācīnadvārena nikkhamitvā pubbārāme divāvihāraṃ karoti. Pubbārāme rattiṃ vasitvā punadivase pācīnadvārena sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisitvā dakkhiṇadvārena nikkhamitvā jetavane divāvihāraṃ karoti. Kasmā? Dvinnaṃ kulānaṃ anukampāya. Manussattabhāve ṭhitena hi anāthapiṇḍikena viya aññena kenaci, mātugāmattabhāve ṭhitāya ca visākhāya viya aññāya itthiyā tathāgataṃ uddissa dhanapariccāgo kato nāma natthi, tasmā bhagavā tesaṃ anukampāya ekadivase imāni dve ṭhānāni paribhuñjati. Tasmiṃ pana divase jetavane vasi, tasmā thero – ‘‘ajja bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā sāyanhakāle gattāni parisiñcanatthāya pubbakoṭṭhakaṃ gamissati; athāhaṃ gattāni parisiñcitvā ṭhitaṃ bhagavantaṃ yācitvā rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamaṃ gahetvā gamissāmi. Evamime bhikkhū bhagavato sammukhā labhissanti dhammakathaṃ savanāyā’’ti cintetvā te bhikkhū evamāha.

Migāramātupāsādoti visākhāya pāsādo. Sā hi migārena seṭṭhinā mātuṭṭhāne ṭhapitattā migāramātāti vuccati. Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitoti tasmiṃ kira pāsāde dvinnaṃ mahāsāvakānaṃ sirigabbhānaṃ majjhe bhagavato sirigabbho ahosi. Thero dvāraṃ vivaritvā antogabbhaṃ sammajjitvā mālākacavaraṃ nīharitvā mañcapīṭhaṃ paññapetvā satthu saññaṃ adāsi. Satthā sirigabbhaṃ pavisitvā dakkhiṇena passena sato sampajāno sīhaseyyaṃ upagamma darathaṃ paṭippassambhetvā uṭṭhāya phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā nisīditvā sāyanhasamaye tato vuṭṭhāsi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito’’ti.

Migāramātupāsādo migāramātā Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito

Parisiñcitunti yo hi cuṇṇamattikādīhi gattāni ubbaṭṭento mallakamuṭṭhādīhi vā ghaṃsanto nhāyati, so nhāyatīti vuccati. Yo tathā akatvā pakatiyāva nhāyati, so parisiñcatīti vuccati. Bhagavatopi sarīre tathā haritabbaṃ rajojallaṃ nāma na upalimpati, utuggahaṇatthaṃ pana bhagavā kevalaṃ udakaṃ otarati. Tenāha – ‘‘gattāni parisiñcitu’’nti. Pubbakoṭṭhakoti pācīnakoṭṭhako.

Parisiñcitu nhāyatī parisiñcatī Pubbakoṭṭhako

Sāvatthiyaṃ kira vihāro kadāci mahā hoti kadāci khuddako. Tathā hi so vipassissa bhagavato kāle yojaniko ahosi, sikhissa tigāvuto, vessabhussa aḍḍhayojaniko, kakusandhassa gāvutappamāṇo, koṇāgamanassa aḍḍhagāvutappamāṇo, kassapassa vīsatiusabhappamāṇo, amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle aṭṭhakarīsappamāṇo jāto. Tampi nagaraṃ tassa vihārassa kadāci pācīnato hoti, kadāci dakkhiṇato, kadāci pacchimato, kadāci uttarato. Jetavane gandhakuṭiyaṃ pana catunnaṃ mañcapādānaṃ patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ acalameva.

Cattāri hi acalacetiyaṭṭhānāni nāma mahābodhipallaṅkaṭṭhānaṃ isipatane dhammacakkappavattanaṭṭhānaṃ saṅkassanagaradvāre devorohaṇakāle sopānassa patiṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ mañcapādaṭṭhānanti. Ayaṃ pana pubbakoṭṭhako kassapadasabalassa vīsatiusabhavihārakāle pācīnadvāre koṭṭhako ahosi. So idānipi pubbakoṭṭhakotveva paññāyati. Kassapadasabalassa kāle aciravatī nagaraṃ parikkhipitvā sandamānā pubbakoṭṭhakaṃ patvā udakena bhinditvā mahantaṃ udakarahadaṃ māpesi samatitthaṃ anupubbagambhīraṃ. Tattha ekaṃ rañño nhānatitthaṃ, ekaṃ nāgarānaṃ, ekaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa, ekaṃ buddhānanti evaṃ pāṭiyekkāni nhānatitthāni honti ramaṇīyāni vippakiṇṇarajatapaṭṭasadisavālikāni. Iti bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ yena ayaṃ evarūpo pubbakoṭṭhako tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṃ . Athāyasmā ānando udakasāṭikaṃ upanesi. Bhagavā rattadupaṭṭaṃ apanetvā udakasāṭikaṃ nivāsesi. Thero dupaṭṭena saddhiṃ mahācīvaraṃ attano hatthagatamakāsi. Bhagavā udakaṃ otari. Sahotaraṇenevassa udake macchakacchapā sabbe suvaṇṇavaṇṇā ahesuṃ. Yantanālikāhi suvaṇṇarasadhārānisiñcamānakālo viya suvaṇṇapaṭapasāraṇakālo viya ca ahosi. Atha bhagavato nhānavattaṃ dassetvā nhatvā paccuttiṇṇassa thero rattadupaṭṭaṃ upanesi. Bhagavā taṃ nivāsetvā vijjulatāsadisaṃ kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā mahācīvaraṃ antantena saṃharitvā padumagabbhasadisaṃ katvā upanītaṃ dvīsu kaṇṇesu gahetvā aṭṭhāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘pubbakoṭṭhake gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsī’’ti.

acalacetiyaṭṭhānāni

Evaṃ ṭhitassa pana bhagavato sarīraṃ vikasitakamaluppalasaraṃ sabbapāliphullaṃ pāricchattakaṃ tārāmarīcivikasitaṃ ca gaganatalaṃ siriyā avahasamānaṃ viya virocittha. Byāmappabhāparikkhepavilāsinī cassa dvattiṃsavaralakkhaṇamālā ganthetvā ṭhapitā dvattiṃsacandamālā viya, dvattiṃsasūriyamālā viya, paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapitā dvattiṃsacakkavatti dvattiṃsadevarājā dvattiṃsamahābrahmāno viya ca ativiya virocittha, vaṇṇabhūmināmesā. Evarūpesu ṭhānesu buddhānaṃ sarīravaṇṇaṃ vā guṇavaṇṇaṃ vā cuṇṇiyapadehi vā gāthāhi vā atthañca upamāyo ca kāraṇāni ca āharitvā paṭibalena dhammakathikena pūretvā kathetuṃ vaṭṭatīti evarūpesu ṭhānesu dhammakathikassa thāmo veditabbo.
commentary_english:
272. Thus have I heard: the Pāsarāsi Sūtra.

There, while requesting, they speak, "Excellent, friend!"

These approximately five hundred *bhikṣus*, residents of the countryside, having arrived at Śrāvastī, [thinking,] "We will see the Ten-Powered One."

But the sight of the Teacher was obtained by them. Why then, do they not hear the Dharma?

They, out of reverence for the Teacher, are not able to say, "Venerable sir, may you speak the Dharma to us."

For Buddhas are venerable, like a solitary lion, king of beasts, like a rutting elephant, like a hooded poisonous snake, like a great mass of fire, they are difficult to approach. This was said:

"Just as a poisonous snake is dreadful, the lion is king of beasts;

Just as an elephant is tusked, so are Buddhas difficult to approach."

Thus, those *bhikṣus*, not being able to ask the Teacher, who is difficult to approach, themselves, requesting the venerable Ānanda, said, "Excellent, friend!"

Perhaps you may obtain [this].

Why then did the Elder say to those *bhikṣus*, "Go to the hermitage of the *brāhmaṇa* Rammaka"? Because of manifest action.

For the action of the Ten-Powered One is manifest to the Elder. The Elder knows, "Today the Teacher, having stayed in Jetavana, will spend the day at Pūrvārāma; today, having stayed at Pūrvārāma, he will spend the day at Jetavana; today he, alone, will enter for alms; today, surrounded by the *bhikṣu*-*saṃgha*, at this time, he will set out on a tour of the countryside."

Does he have the knowledge of others' minds in order to know thus? No.

But he knows by inference, by the method of grasping the action that has been done.

For on whichever day the Blessed One, having stayed at Jetavana, intends to spend the day at Pūrvārāma, on that day he shows the preparation for the lodging, the Elder arranges the sweeping, the dust, the throwing away [of rubbish], and so on.

The same method applies also at the time of coming to Jetavana for the day's dwelling, having stayed at Pūrvārāma.

Perhaps, when he intends to enter alone for alms, then, early in the morning, having performed the care of his body, having entered the Perfume Chamber, having closed the door, having emerged from fruition-attainment, he sits down.

The Elder, knowing with that perception, "Today the Blessed One, having seen those who are fit to be awakened, is seated," gives the *bhikṣus* a sign, "Today, friends, the Blessed One intends to enter alone, you should be prepared for the alms round."

When, however, the *bhikṣu*-*saṃgha* entourage intends to enter, then, having made the door of the Perfume Chamber half-closed, having emerged from fruition-attainment, he sits down, the Elder, knowing with that perception, gives the *bhikṣus* a sign for the purpose of taking the bowl and robes.

When he intends to set out on a tour of the countryside, then he eats one or two extra mouthfuls, having mounted the walkway at all times, he walks back and forth, the Elder, knowing with that perception, gives the *bhikṣus* a sign, "Friends, the Blessed One intends to go on a tour of the countryside, you should do what is to be done."

The Blessed One, during the first awakening, spent twenty years unattached; afterwards, for twenty-five years, dwelling dependent only on crowded Śrāvastī, on one day, he enjoys two places.

Having spent the night in Jetavana, on the following day, surrounded by the *bhikṣu*-*saṃgha*, having entered Śrāvastī for alms by the southern gate, having left by the eastern gate, he spends the day at Pūrvārāma.

Having spent the night in Pūrvārāma, on the following day, having entered Śrāvastī for alms by the eastern gate, having left by the southern gate, he spends the day at Jetavana.

Why? Out of compassion for the two families.

For, while abiding in the state of being a human being, there is no gift of wealth, having been made to the Tathāgata, offered by someone else like Anāthapiṇḍika, and by another woman like Visākhā, while abiding in the state of being a woman, therefore the Blessed One, out of compassion for them, on one day, enjoys these two places.

But on that day he stayed in Jetavana, therefore the Elder [thought]: "Today the Blessed One, having wandered for alms in Śrāvastī, in the evening, will go to the former storehouse to bathe his limbs; then, having bathed my limbs, having asked the Blessed One who is standing [there], I will take [him to] the hermitage of the *brāhmaṇa* Rammaka.

Thus these *bhikṣus* will obtain the Dharma talk in the presence of the Blessed One for the sake of hearing," thinking thus, he said this to those *bhikṣus*.

Migāramātupāsāda means Visākhā's mansion.

For she is called Migāramātā because she was placed in the position of a mother by the merchant Migāra.

"Having arisen from seclusion" means that in that mansion, in the middle of the auspicious chambers of the two great disciples, was the Blessed One's auspicious chamber.
The elder opened the door, swept the inner chamber, removed the faded garlands, set out the chair-stool, and signaled the Teacher.

The Teacher entered the auspicious chamber, mindfully and consciously lay down on his right side in the lion's posture, dispelled any discomfort, arose, emerged from fruition attainment, sat down, and then, in the late afternoon, got up.

Referring to that, it was said, "Having arisen from seclusion."

Migāramātupāsāda, Migāramātā, having arisen from seclusion.

"Parisiñcituṃ" means one who bathes by rubbing their body with powder, earth, and so on, or by scrubbing with a bowl-brush and so on, is called "nhāyati".

One who bathes without doing so, simply by nature, is called "parisiñcati".

Even in the Blessed One's body, dirt and grime to be removed do not adhere; however, for the sake of upholding tradition, the Blessed One simply goes down into the water.

Therefore, he said, "To bathe the limbs."

"Pubbakoṭṭhako" means eastern chamber.

Parisiñcituṃ, nhāyati, parisiñcati, pubbakoṭṭhako. In Sāvatthī, it is said that the monastery is sometimes large and sometimes small.

Thus, in the time of Vipassī Buddha, it was one *yojana* in extent; in the time of Sikhī, three *gāvuta*s; in the time of Vessabhū, half a *yojana*; in the time of Kakusandha, the measure of a *gāvuta*; in the time of Koṇāgamana, half a *gāvuta*; in the time of Kassapa, twenty *usabha*s; in the time of our Blessed One, it was eight *karīsa*s in extent.

That city, too, of that monastery, was sometimes to the east, sometimes to the south, sometimes to the west, sometimes to the north.

In Jetavana, however, the established place of the four legs of the Perfumed Chamber's couch was unmoving.

These four are indeed named *acalacetiyaṭṭhānāni* "unmoving shrine places": the place of the Great Bodhi Tree's Platform, the place in Isipatana where the Wheel of the Dharma was set in motion, the place at the gate of Saṅkassa City where the stairway was established at the time of the gods' descent, and the place of the couch's legs.

This eastern chamber, however, in the time of Kassapa, the One with the Ten Powers, in the era of the twenty-*usabha* monastery, was the chamber at the eastern gate.

Even now, it appears as the eastern chamber.

In the time of Kassapa, the One with the Ten Powers, Aciravatī, surrounding the city and flowing along, reaching the eastern chamber, breaking through with water, created a great water-lake that was level-banked and gradually deep.

There, one bathing place for the king, one for the townsfolk, one for the *bhikkhu* Sangha, one for the Buddhas—thus, there were separate bathing places, delightful, with sand like scattered silver plates.

Thus, the Blessed One, together with the venerable Ānanda, approached that eastern chamber in this manner to bathe his limbs.

Then the venerable Ānanda offered a water-cloth.

The Blessed One, removing the red upper robe, put on the water-cloth.

The elder, together with the upper robe, made the great robe reach his own hand.

The Blessed One went down into the water.

As soon as he entered the water, the fish and turtles were all the color of gold.

It was like a time of sprinkling with streams of golden essence from water-spouts, and like a time of spreading out golden cloths.

Then, after showing the bathing custom of the Blessed One and having bathed and come back up, the elder offered the red upper robe.

The Blessed One, having worn it, tied on a body-band like a streak of lightning, gathered up the great robe with its extremities, made it like the inside of a lotus bud, took the offered robe in his two ears, and stood there.

Therefore it was said: "Having bathed the limbs in the eastern chamber, having come back up, he stood there in a single robe."

Acalacetiyaṭṭhānāni.

Thus, the body of the Blessed One, standing, with its blossoming lotus and *uppala* lake, fully adorned on all sides, resembled the *pāricchattaka* tree, and the sky, with its expanded starlight rays, was as if mocking glory.

And his thirty-two excellent marks, woven into a garland, shone exceedingly, as if thirty-two moon garlands, as if thirty-two sun garlands, as if thirty-two *cakravartin*s arrayed in order, thirty-two *devarāja*s, thirty-two Great Brahmās. This is the ground of color.

In places like these, when speaking of the color of the Buddhas' bodies or the color of their virtues, a skilled *dhamma* speaker, bringing forward meanings, similes, and reasons from verses or from summaries, is able to fill [the audience] and speak, and in places like these, the strength of the *dhamma* speaker should be understood.
[Page break]

mula_pali:
273. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ yena pubbakoṭṭhako tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṃ. Pubbakoṭṭhake gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsi gattāni pubbāpayamāno. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ayaṃ, bhante, rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamo avidūre. Ramaṇīyo, bhante, rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamo; pāsādiko, bhante, rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamo. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamo tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.

Atha kho bhagavā yena rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamo tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assame dhammiyā kathāya sannisinnā honti. Atha kho bhagavā bahidvārakoṭṭhake aṭṭhāsi kathāpariyosānaṃ āgamayamāno. Atha kho bhagavā kathāpariyosānaṃ viditvā ukkāsitvā aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesi. Vivariṃsu kho te bhikkhū bhagavato dvāraṃ. Atha kho bhagavā rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamaṃ pavisitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘kāyanuttha, bhikkhave, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā? Kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā’’ti ? ‘‘Bhagavantameva kho no, bhante, ārabbha dhammī kathā vippakatā, atha bhagavā anuppatto’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu, bhikkhave! Etaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tumhākaṃ patirūpaṃ kulaputtānaṃ saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitānaṃ yaṃ tumhe dhammiyā kathāya sannisīdeyyātha. Sannipatitānaṃ vo, bhikkhave, dvayaṃ karaṇīyaṃ – dhammī vā kathā, ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo’’.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One went with the venerable Ānanda to the Eastern Bathing Place to bathe. When he was finished, he came up out of the water and stood in one robe drying his limbs. Then the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the *brāhmaṇa* Rammaka’s hermitage is nearby. The *brāhmaṇa* Rammaka’s hermitage is delightful, reverend Sir, The *brāhmaṇa* Rammaka’s hermitage is pleasing, reverend Sir. Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One went there out of compassion.” The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.

Then the Blessed One went to the *brāhmaṇa* Rammaka’s hermitage. Now on that occasion a number of *bhikkhus* were sitting together in the hermitage discussing the *dharma*. Then the Fortunate One stood outside the door waiting for their discussion to end. When he knew that it was over, he coughed and knocked. Those *bhikkhus* opened the door for the Fortunate One. The Blessed One entered, sat down on a seat made ready, and addressed the *bhikkhus*: “What kind of discussion were you holding just now, *bhikkhus*? What was the subject of your conversation?” “Venerable sir, our discussion on the *dharma* that was interrupted was about the Blessed One himself. Then the Blessed One arrived.” “Good, *bhikkhus*! It is fitting for you clansmen who have gone forth out of faith from the home life into homelessness to sit together to discuss the *dharma*. When you have gathered you have two duties: either *dharma*-talk or noble silence.”
commentary_pali:
273.Gattāni pubbāpayamānoti pakatibhāvaṃ gamayamāno nirudakāni kurumāno, sukkhāpayamānoti attho. Sodakena gattena cīvaraṃ pārupantassa hi cīvare kaṇṇikā uṭṭhahanti, parikkhārabhaṇḍaṃ dussati. Buddhānaṃ pana sarīre rajojallaṃ na upalimpati; padumapatte pakkhittaudakabindu viya udakaṃ vinivattetvā gacchati, evaṃ santepi sikkhāgāravatāya bhagavā, ‘‘pabbajitavattaṃ nāmeta’’nti mahācīvaraṃ ubhosu kaṇṇesu gahetvā purato kāyaṃ paṭicchādetvā aṭṭhāsi. Tasmiṃ khaṇe thero cintesi – ‘‘bhagavā mahācīvaraṃ pārupitvā migāramātupāsādaṃ ārabbha gamanābhihārato paṭṭhāya dunnivattiyo bhavissati; buddhānañhi adhippāyakopanaṃ nāma ekacārikasīhassa gahaṇatthaṃ hatthappasāraṇaṃ viya; pabhinnavaravāraṇassa soṇḍāya parāmasanaṃ viya; uggatejassa āsīvisassa gīvāya gahaṇaṃ viya ca bhāriyaṃ hoti. Idheva rammakassa brāhmaṇassa assamassa vaṇṇaṃ kathetvā tattha gamanatthāya bhagavantaṃ yācissāmī’’ti. So tathā akāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho āyasmā ānando…pe… anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti.

Tattha anukampaṃ upādāyāti bhagavato sammukhā dhammiṃ kathaṃ sossāmāti taṃ assamaṃ gatānaṃ pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ anukampaṃ paṭicca, tesu kāruññaṃ katvāti attho. Dhammiyā kathāyāti dasasu pāramitāsu aññatarāya pāramiyā ceva mahābhinikkhamanassa ca vaṇṇaṃ kathayamānā sannisinnā honti. Āgamayamānoti olokayamāno. Ahaṃ buddhoti sahasā appavisitvā yāva sā kathā niṭṭhāti, tāva aṭṭhāsīti attho. Aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesīti agganakhena kavāṭe saññaṃ adāsi. Vivariṃsūti sotaṃ odahitvāva nisinnattā taṅkhaṇaṃyeva āgantvā vivariṃsu.

anukampaṃ upādāyā Dhammiyā kathāyā Āgamayamāno Aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesī Vivariṃsū

Paññatte āsaneti buddhakāle kira yattha yattha ekopi bhikkhu viharati, sabbattha buddhāsanaṃ paññattameva hoti. Kasmā? Bhagavā kira attano santike kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā phāsukaṭṭhāne viharante manasi karoti ‘‘asuko mayhaṃ santike kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā gato, sakkhissati nu kho visesaṃ nibbattetuṃ no vā’’ti. Atha naṃ passati kammaṭṭhānaṃ vissajjetvā akusalavitakke vitakkayamānaṃ, tato ‘‘kathañhi nāma mādisassa satthu santike kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā viharantaṃ imaṃ kulaputtaṃ akusalavitakkā abhibhavitvā anamatagge vaṭṭadukkhe saṃsāressantī’’ti tassa anuggahatthaṃ tattheva attānaṃ dassetvā taṃ kulaputtaṃ ovaditvā ākāsaṃ uppatitvā puna attano vasanaṭṭhānameva gacchati. Athevaṃ ovadiyamānā te bhikkhū cintayiṃsu – ‘‘satthā amhākaṃ manaṃ jānitvā āgantvā amhākaṃ samīpe ṭhitaṃyeva attānaṃ dasseti; tasmiṃ khaṇe, ‘bhante, idha nisīdatha, idha nisīdathā’ti āsanapariyesanaṃ nāma bhāro’’ti. Te āsanaṃ paññapetvāva viharanti. Yassa pīṭhaṃ atthi, so taṃ paññapeti. Yassa natthi, so mañcaṃ vā phalakaṃ vā kaṭṭhaṃ vā pāsāṇaṃ vā vālikapuñjaṃ vā paññapeti. Taṃ alabhamānā purāṇapaṇṇānipi saṅkaḍḍhitvā tattha paṃsukūlaṃ pattharitvā ṭhapenti. Idha pana pakatipaññattameva āsanaṃ ahosi, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘paññatte āsane nisīdī’’ti.

Paññatte āsane

Kāyanutthāti katamāya nu kathāya sannisinnā bhavathāti attho. ‘‘Kāya netthā’’tipi pāḷi, tassā katamāya nu etthāti attho. ‘‘Kāya notthā’’tipi pāḷi, tassāpi purimoyeva attho. Antarā kathāti kammaṭṭhānamanasikārauddesaparipucchādīnaṃ antarā aññā ekā kathā. Vippakatāti mama āgamanapaccayā apariniṭṭhitā sikhaṃ appattā. Atha bhagavā anuppattoti atha etasmiṃ kāle bhagavā āgato. Dhammī vā kathāti dasakathāvatthunissitā vā dhammī kathā. Ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvoti ettha pana dutiyajjhānampi ariyo tuṇhībhāvo mūlakammaṭṭhānampi. Tasmā taṃ jhānaṃ appetvā nisinnopi, mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā nisinnopi bhikkhu ariyena tuṇhībhāvena nisinnoti veditabbo.

Kāya nutthā Antarā kathā Vippakatā Atha bhagavā anuppatto Dhammī vā kathā Ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo
commentary_english:
273. *Gattāni pubbāpayamāno* means making them devoid of water by making them attain their natural state, making them without water, causing them to dry out, this is the meaning.

Indeed, when one with a wet body puts on a robe, the iron filings adhere to the robe, and the sundry articles get soiled.

But for the Buddhas, dirt and grime do not stick to the body; like a drop of water placed on a lotus leaf, it slides off, in this way, even when he was present, because of maintaining proper respect for the training, the Blessed One, thinking, "Let it not be an unsuitable practice for one gone forth," having taken the large robe at both edges, stood concealing his body in front.

At that moment, the elder thought: "The Blessed One, having put on the great robe, having started from the Migāramātupāsāda, will be difficult to turn back from his going to meet [them]; for the intention of the Buddhas is like extending a hand to grasp a single wandering lion; like touching the trunk of an elephant with excellent tusks it is weighty.

"Here, indeed, having described the qualities of the hermitage of the brahmin Rammaka, I will ask the Blessed One for the purpose of going there."

He did so.

Therefore it was said: "Then, indeed, the venerable Ānanda… out of compassion having approached…”

There, *anukampaṃ upādāya* means having regarded with compassion the five hundred monks who had gone to that hermitage, thinking, "How will we hear the Dhamma in the presence of the Blessed One?", that is, having done kindness towards them, this is the meaning.

*Dhammiyā kathāyā* means by any one of the ten perfections, namely, they are seated speaking of the qualities of that perfection and of the Great Renunciation.

*Āgamayamāno* means looking around.

Without suddenly entering, until that talk was finished, so long he stood, this is the meaning.

*Aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesī* means he gave a sign on the door with his thumbnail.

*Vivariṃsū* means because they were seated having listened intently, at that very moment they came and opened it.

*Anukampaṃ upādāya Dhammiyā kathāyā Āgamayamāno Aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesī Vivariṃsū Paññatte āsane* means in the Buddha-time it is said that wherever even a single monk dwells, everywhere a Buddha-seat is always prepared.

Why? It is said that the Blessed One, having taken a meditation subject from his own presence, while dwelling in a comfortable place, reflects: "Such-and-such a one, having taken a meditation subject from my presence, has gone; will he be able to produce a distinction, or not?"

Then he sees him, having dismissed the meditation subject, reflecting on unwholesome thoughts; then thinking, "How, indeed, should unwholesome thoughts overwhelm this clansman who, having taken a meditation subject from a Teacher such as myself, is dwelling [there], and cause him to transmigrate in the round of suffering without beginning?", for the purpose of favoring him, having shown himself right there, having admonished that clansman, having risen into the sky, again he goes to his own dwelling place.

Then, being thus admonished, those monks thought: "The Teacher, having known our mind, having come, shows himself right near us; at that moment, 'Venerable Sir, sit here, sit here!'— the seeking of a seat is a burden."

They dwell having prepared a seat.

He who has a chair prepares that.

He who has none prepares a bed or a bench or a log or a stone or a heap of sand.

Not obtaining that, even gathering old leaves, having piled them up there, they spread a rag and place it.

Here, however, there was only a naturally prepared seat, referring to that it was said: “Sit on the prepared seat.”

*Paññatte āsane* *Kāya nutthā* means “with what sort of talk are you seated?” is the meaning.

“Kāya netthā” is also a reading, its meaning is: “with what sort [of talk] in this [situation]?”

“Kāya notthā” is also a reading; its meaning is just the same as before.

*Antarā kathā* means another talk in between, in between the meditation subject, mental attention, recitation, and questioning, etc.

*Vippakatā* means unfinished, not having reached the top, because of my arrival as a condition.

*Atha bhagavā anuppatto* means then, at this time, the Blessed One arrived.

*Dhammī vā kathā* means either a talk about the Dhamma, or a talk based on the ten grounds for talk.

*Ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo* means here, however, the noble silence is also the second jhāna, and also the basic meditation subject.

Therefore, it should be understood that a monk, having withdrawn from that jhāna and being seated, or having taken up the basic meditation subject and being seated, is seated with the noble silence.
kāya nutthā antarā kathā vippakatā atha bhagavā anuppatto dhammī vā kathā ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo

Having dismissed that talk, when another talk had arisen, then the Blessed One arrived; or a discourse on the Dharma, or the noble silence.

mula_pali:
274. ‘‘Dvemā, bhikkhave, pariyesanā – ariyā ca pariyesanā, anariyā ca pariyesanā.

‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, anariyā pariyesanā? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesati, attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhammaṃyeva pariyesati, attanā byādhidhammo samāno byādhidhammaṃyeva pariyesati, attanā maraṇadhammo samāno maraṇadhammaṃyeva pariyesati, attanā sokadhammo samāno sokadhammaṃyeva pariyesati, attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, jātidhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, jātidhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ jātidhammaṃ, ajeḷakaṃ jātidhammaṃ, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ jātidhammaṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ jātidhammaṃ, jātarūparajataṃ jātidhammaṃ. Jātidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo. Etthāyaṃ gathito gadhīto (syā. ka.) mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

gadhīto (syā. ka.)

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, jarādhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, jarādhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ jarādhammaṃ, ajeḷakaṃ jarādhammaṃ, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ jarādhammaṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ jarādhammaṃ , jātarūparajataṃ jarādhammaṃ. Jarādhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo. Etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, byādhidhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, byādhidhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ byādhidhammaṃ, ajeḷakaṃ byādhidhammaṃ, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ byādhidhammaṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ byādhidhammaṃ. Byādhidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo. Etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā byādhidhammo samāno byādhidhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, maraṇadhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, maraṇadhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ maraṇadhammaṃ, ajeḷakaṃ maraṇadhammaṃ, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ maraṇadhammaṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ maraṇadhammaṃ. Maraṇadhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo. Etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā maraṇadhammo samāno maraṇadhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, sokadhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, sokadhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ sokadhammaṃ, ajeḷakaṃ sokadhammaṃ, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ sokadhammaṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ sokadhammaṃ. Sokadhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo. Etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā sokadhammo samāno sokadhammaṃyeva pariyesati.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, saṃkilesadhammaṃ vadetha? Puttabhariyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃkilesadhammaṃ, dāsidāsaṃ saṃkilesadhammaṃ, ajeḷakaṃ saṃkilesadhammaṃ , kukkuṭasūkaraṃ saṃkilesadhammaṃ, hatthigavāssavaḷavaṃ saṃkilesadhammaṃ, jātarūparajataṃ saṃkilesadhammaṃ. Saṃkilesadhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo. Etthāyaṃ gathito mucchito ajjhāpanno attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhammaṃyeva pariyesati. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, anariyā pariyesanā.
mula_english:
274. “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of search: the noble search (*ariyā pariyesanā*) and the ignoble search (*anariyā pariyesanā*).

“And what, monks, is an ignoble search? Here, monks, someone being himself subject to birth (*jātidhammo*), seeks what is also subject to birth (*jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesati*); being himself subject to aging (*jarādhammo*), he seeks what is also subject to aging; being himself subject to sickness (*byādhidhammo*), he seeks what is also subject to sickness; being himself subject to death (*maraṇadhammo*), he seeks what is also subject to death; being himself subject to sorrow (*sokadhammo*), he seeks what is also subject to sorrow; being himself subject to defilement (*saṃkilesadhammo*), he seeks what is also subject to defilement.

“And what, monks, may be said to be subject to birth (*jātidhammaṃ vadetha*)? Wife and children, monks, are subject to birth, men and women slaves, goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares, gold and silver are subject to birth.
These acquisitions are subject to birth (*jātidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*).
And one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to birth (*attanā jātidhammo samāno*), seeks what is also subject to birth (*jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesati*).

“And what, monks, may be said to be subject to aging (*jarādhammaṃ vadetha*)? Wife and children, monks, are subject to aging, men and women slaves, goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares, gold and silver are subject to aging.
These acquisitions are subject to aging (*jarādhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*).
And one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to aging (*attanā jarādhammo samāno*), seeks what is also subject to aging (*jarādhammaṃyeva pariyesati*).

“And what, monks, may be said to be subject to sickness (*byādhidhammaṃ vadetha*)? Wife and children, monks, are subject to sickness, men and women slaves, goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares are subject to sickness.
These acquisitions are subject to sickness (*byādhidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*).
And one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to sickness (*attanā byādhidhammo samāno*), seeks what is also subject to sickness (*byādhidhammaṃyeva pariyesati*).

“And what, monks, may be said to be subject to death (*maraṇadhammaṃ vadetha*)? Wife and children, monks, are subject to death, men and women slaves, goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares are subject to death.
These acquisitions are subject to death (*maraṇadhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*).
And one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to death (*attanā maraṇadhammo samāno*), seeks what is also subject to death (*maraṇadhammaṃyeva pariyesati*).

“And what, monks, may be said to be subject to sorrow (*sokadhammaṃ vadetha*)? Wife and children, monks, are subject to sorrow, men and women slaves, goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares are subject to sorrow.
These acquisitions are subject to sorrow (*sokadhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*).
And one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to sorrow (*attanā sokadhammo samāno*), seeks what is also subject to sorrow (*sokadhammaṃyeva pariyesati*).

“And what, monks, may be said to be subject to defilement (*saṃkilesadhammaṃ vadetha*)? Wife and children, monks, are subject to defilement, men and women slaves, goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares, gold and silver are subject to defilement.
These acquisitions are subject to defilement (*saṃkilesadhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*).
And one who is tied to these things, infatuated with them, and utterly committed to them, being himself subject to defilement (*attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno*), seeks what is also subject to defilement (*saṃkilesadhammaṃyeva pariyesati*).
This, monks, is an ignoble search (*anariyā pariyesanā*).
commentary_pali:
274.Dvemā, bhikkhave, pariyesanāti ko anusandhi? Te bhikkhū sammukhā dhammiṃ kathaṃ sossāmāti therassa bhāraṃ akaṃsu, thero tesaṃ assamagamanamakāsi. Te tattha nisīditvā atiracchānakathikā hutvā dhammiyā kathāya nisīdiṃsu. Atha bhagavā ‘‘ayaṃ tumhākaṃ pariyesanā ariyapariyesanā nāmā’’ti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha katamā ca, bhikkhave, anariyapariyesanāti ettha yathā maggakusalo puriso paṭhamaṃ vajjetabbaṃ apāyamaggaṃ dassento ‘‘vāmaṃ muñcitvā dakkhiṇaṃ gaṇhā’’ti vadati. Evaṃ bhagavā desanākusalatāya paṭhamaṃ vajjetabbaṃ anariyapariyesanaṃ ācikkhitvā pacchā itaraṃ ācikkhissāmīti uddesānukkamaṃ bhinditvā evamāha. Jātidhammoti jāyanasabhāvo. Jarādhammoti jīraṇasabhāvo. Byādhidhammoti byādhisabhāvo. Maraṇadhammoti maraṇasabhāvo. Sokadhammoti socanakasabhāvo. Saṃkilesadhammoti saṃkilissanasabhāvo.

Puttabhariyanti puttā ca bhariyā ca. Esa nayo sabbattha. Jātarūparajatanti ettha pana jātarūpanti suvaṇṇaṃ. Rajatanti yaṃkiñci vohārūpagaṃ lohamāsakādi. Jātidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayoti ete pañcakāmaguṇūpadhayo nāma honti, te sabbepi jātidhammāti dasseti. Byādhidhammavārādīsu jātarūparajataṃ na gahitaṃ, na hetassa sīsarogādayo byādhayo nāma honti, na sattānaṃ viya cutisaṅkhātaṃ maraṇaṃ, na soko uppajjati. Ayādīhi pana saṃkilesehi saṃkilissatīti saṃkilesadhammavāre gahitaṃ. Tathā utusamuṭṭhānattā jātidhammavāre. Malaṃ gahetvā jīraṇato jarādhammavāre ca.

Puttabhariya Jātarūparajata jātarūpa Rajata Jātidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo
commentary_english:
274. “*dvemā, bhikkhave, pariyesanā*” what is the connection? Those monks placed the burden on the elder, saying, "How shall we hear the *dhammiṃ* face to face?" The elder made their going to the hermitage.

Having sat down there, having engaged in irrelevant talk, they sat down for a talk on the *dhamma*.

Then the Blessed One, in order to show that "this search of yours is called the noble search," began this teaching.

There, "*katamā ca, bhikkhave, anariyapariyesanā*" here, just as a man skilled in paths, showing the path of misfortune to be avoided first, says, "Release the left and take the right."

Thus the Blessed One, with skill in teaching, having first explained the ignoble search to be avoided, afterwards, breaking the order of exposition, said thus:

"*jātidhammo*" means having the nature of birth (jāyanasabhāvo).

"*jarādhammo*" means having the nature of aging (jīraṇasabhāvo).

"*byādhidhammo*" means having the nature of sickness (byādhisabhāvo).

"*maraṇadhammo*" means having the nature of death (maraṇasabhāvo).

"*sokadhammo*" means having the nature of sorrow (socanakasabhāvo).

"*saṃkilesadhammo*" means having the nature of defilement (saṃkilissanasabhāvo).

"*puttabhariya*” means sons and wives (*puttā ca bhariyā ca*).

This method applies everywhere.

"*jātarūparajata*" here, "*jātarūpa*" means gold (*suvaṇṇaṃ*).

"*rajata*" means whatever is fit for use, such as metal coins (*lohamāsakādi*).

"*jātidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*" these are called the five aggregates of clinging pertaining to sensual pleasure; he shows that all of these have the nature of birth.

In the sections on sickness, etc., gold and silver are not included, for head diseases, etc., are not called sicknesses of these; nor is death, reckoned as decease, like that of beings, nor does sorrow arise.

But it is taken in the section on defilements, because one is defiled by defilements beginning with desire (*ayādīhi pana saṃkilesehi saṃkilissatīti saṃkilesadhammavāre gahitaṃ*).

Likewise, because it arises from the seasons, in the section on birth (*tathā utusamuṭṭhānattā jātidhammavāre*).

And having taken dirt, because of decay, in the section on aging (*malaṃ gahetvā jīraṇato jarādhammavāre ca*).

*puttabhariya jātarūparajata jātarūpa rajata jātidhammā hete, bhikkhave, upadhayo*

mula_pali: 275. ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, ariyā pariyesanā? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajātaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati, attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajaraṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati, attanā byādhidhammo samāno byādhidhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā abyādhiṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati, attanā maraṇadhammo samāno maraṇadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā amataṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati, attanā sokadhammo samāno sokadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā asokaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati, attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesati. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyā pariyesanā.
mula_english: ‘‘And what, monks, is the noble search (ariyā pariyesanā)? Here, monks, someone being himself subject to birth (jātidhammo), having understood the danger (ādīnavaṃ) in what is subject to birth, seeks the unborn (ajātaṃ), unsurpassed (anuttaraṃ) security from bondage (yogakkhemaṃ), Nibbāna; being himself subject to aging (jarādhammo), having understood the danger in what is subject to aging, he seeks the unaging (ajaraṃ), unsurpassed security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to sickness (byādhidhammo), having understood the danger in what is subject to sickness, he seeks the unailing (abyādhiṃ), unsurpassed security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to death (maraṇadhammo), having understood the danger in what is subject to death, he seeks the deathless (amataṃ), unsurpassed security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to sorrow (sokadhammo), having understood the danger in what is subject to sorrow, he seeks the sorrowless (asokaṃ), unsurpassed security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to defilement (saṃkilesadhammo), having understood the danger in what is subject to defilement, he seeks the undefiled (asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ), unsurpassed security from bondage, Nibbāna. This, monks, is the noble search (ariyā pariyesanā).
commentary_pali: 275.Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyā pariyesanāti, bhikkhave, ayaṃ niddosatāyapi ariyehi pariyesitabbatāyapi ariyapariyesanāti veditabbā.
commentary_english: "This, monks, is the noble search." Monks, this should be understood as the noble search because it is faultless and should be sought by the noble ones.

mula_pali: 276. ‘‘Ahampi sudaṃ, bhikkhave, pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddho bodhisattova samāno attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi, attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi, attanā byādhidhammo samāno byādhidhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi, attanā maraṇadhammo samāno maraṇadhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi, attanā sokadhammo samāno sokadhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi, attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi, attanā jarādhammo samāno…pe… byādhidhammo samāno… maraṇadhammo samāno… sokadhammo samāno… attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhammaṃyeva pariyesāmi? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ attanā jātidhammo samāno jātidhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajātaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyeseyyaṃ, attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajaraṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyeseyyaṃ, attanā byādhidhammo samāno byādhidhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā abyādhiṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyeseyyaṃ, attanā maraṇadhammo samāno maraṇadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā amataṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyeseyyaṃ, attanā sokadhammo samāno sokadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā asokaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyeseyyaṃ, attanā saṃkilesadhammo samāno saṃkilesadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyeseyya’nti.
mula_english:
"Bhikkhus, before my full awakening, while I was still an unawakened Bodhisattva, I myself being subject to birth ( *jātidhamma*), sought what was likewise subject to birth; myself being subject to old age (*jarādhammo*), I sought what was likewise subject to old age; myself being subject to sickness (*byādhidhammo*), I sought what was likewise subject to sickness; myself being subject to death (*maraṇadhammo*), I sought what was likewise subject to death; myself being subject to sorrow (*sokadhammo*), I sought what was likewise subject to sorrow; myself being subject to defilement (*saṃkilesadhammo*), I sought what was likewise subject to defilement.

Then it occurred to me, bhikkhus: 'Why do I, being myself subject to birth (*jātidhammo*), seek what is likewise subject to birth? Why do I, being myself subject to old age… subject to sickness… subject to death… subject to sorrow… subject to defilement (*saṃkilesadhammo*), seek what is likewise subject to old age, sickness, death, sorrow, and defilement? Instead, why don't I, being myself subject to birth (*jātidhammo*), realize the danger in what is subject to birth and seek the unborn (*ajāta*), the unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*) security from bondage (*yogakkhemaṃ*), *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*)? Why don't I, being myself subject to old age (*jarādhammo*), realize the danger in what is subject to old age and seek the un-aging (*ajaraṃ*), the unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*) security from bondage (*yogakkhemaṃ*), *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*)? Why don't I, being myself subject to sickness (*byādhidhammo*), realize the danger in what is subject to sickness and seek the un-ailing (*abyādhiṃ*), the unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*) security from bondage (*yogakkhemaṃ*), *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*)? Why don't I, being myself subject to death (*maraṇadhammo*), realize the danger in what is subject to death and seek the deathless (*amataṃ*), the unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*) security from bondage (*yogakkhemaṃ*), *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*)? Why don't I, being myself subject to sorrow (*sokadhammo*), realize the danger in what is subject to sorrow and seek the sorrowless (*asokaṃ*), the unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*) security from bondage (*yogakkhemaṃ*), *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*)? Why don't I, being myself subject to defilement (*saṃkilesadhammo*), realize the danger in what is subject to defilement and seek the undefiled (*asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ*), the unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*) security from bondage (*yogakkhemaṃ*), *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*)?'"
commentary_pali: 276.Ahampi sudaṃ, bhikkhaveti kasmā ārabhi? Mūlato paṭṭhāya mahābhinikkhamanaṃ dassetuṃ. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘bhikkhave, ahampi pubbe anariyapariyesanaṃ pariyesiṃ. Svāhaṃ taṃ pahāya ariyapariyesanaṃ pariyesitvā sabbaññutaṃ patto. Pañcavaggiyāpi anariyapariyesanaṃ pariyesiṃsu. Te taṃ pahāya ariyapariyesanaṃ pariyesitvā khīṇāsavabhūmiṃ pattā. Tumhepi mama ceva pañcavaggiyānañca maggaṃ āruḷhā. Ariyapariyesanā tumhākaṃ pariyesanā’’ti mūlato paṭṭhāya attano mahābhinikkhamanaṃ dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.
commentary_english:
"And even I, monks"—why did he begin thus? To show the great going forth, starting from the root.

It occurred to him thus: "Monks, even I formerly sought the ignoble quest. Then, abandoning that, having sought the noble quest, I attained omniscience. The group of five also sought the ignoble quest. They, abandoning that, having sought the noble quest, attained the state of one whose āsavas are destroyed. You too have ascended the path of myself and the group of five. The noble quest is your quest." To show his own great going forth, starting from the root, he began this teaching.

mula_pali:
277. ‘‘So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, aparena samayena daharova samāno susukāḷakeso , bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato paṭhamena vayasā akāmakānaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ assumukhānaṃ rudantānaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajiṃ. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno kiṃ kusalagavesī kiṃkusalaṃgavesī (ka.) anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ pariyesamāno yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ. Upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘icchāmahaṃ, āvuso kālāma, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye brahmacariyaṃ caritu’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, āḷāro kālāmo maṃ etadavoca – ‘viharatāyasmā; tādiso ayaṃ dhammo yattha viññū puriso nacirasseva sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, nacirasseva khippameva taṃ dhammaṃ pariyāpuṇiṃ. So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, tāvatakeneva oṭṭhapahatamattena lapitalāpanamattena ñāṇavādañca vadāmi theravādañca, ‘jānāmi passāmī’ti ca paṭijānāmi ahañceva aññe ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘na kho āḷāro kālāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ kevalaṃ saddhāmattakena sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedeti; addhā āḷāro kālāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ viharatī’ti.

‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘kittāvatā no, āvuso kālāma, imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedesī’ti upasampajja pavedesīti (sī. syā. pī.)? Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, āḷāro kālāmo ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ pavedesi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi saddhā, mayhaṃpatthi saddhā; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi vīriyaṃ, mayhaṃpatthi vīriyaṃ; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi sati, mayhaṃpatthi sati; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi samādhi, mayhaṃpatthi samādhi; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi paññā, mayhaṃpatthi paññā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ āḷāro kālāmo sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedeti, tassa dhammassa sacchikiriyāya padaheyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, nacirasseva khippameva taṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsiṃ.

upasampajja pavedesīti (sī. syā. pī.)

‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavocaṃ –

‘Ettāvatā no, āvuso kālāma, imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedesī’ti?

‘Ettāvatā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedemī’ti.

‘Ahampi kho, āvuso, ettāvatā imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmī’ti.

‘Lābhā no, āvuso, suladdhaṃ no, āvuso, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ tādisaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ passāma. Iti yāhaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedemi taṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharasi. Yaṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharasi tamahaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedemi. Iti yāhaṃ dhammaṃ jānāmi taṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ jānāsi, yaṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ jānāsi tamahaṃ dhammaṃ jānāmi. Iti yādiso ahaṃ tādiso tuvaṃ, yādiso tuvaṃ tādiso ahaṃ. Ehi dāni, āvuso, ubhova santā imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharāmā’ti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, āḷāro kālāmo ācariyo me samāno (attano) ( ) natthi (sī. syā. pī.) antevāsiṃ maṃ samānaṃ attanā attano (sī. pī.) samasamaṃ ṭhapesi, uḷārāya ca maṃ pūjāya pūjesi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘nāyaṃ dhammo nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati, yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, taṃ dhammaṃ analaṅkaritvā tasmā dhammā nibbijja apakkamiṃ.

( ) natthi (sī. syā. pī.) attano (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
277. “Then, monks, at a later time, while still young, a boy with black hair, endowed with a fortunate youth, in the prime of life, against the wishes of my grieving parents weeping with tear-stained faces, having shaved off my hair and beard and donned brown robes, I went forth from the home to the homeless life. Having thus gone forth, being one who searches for what is wholesome, seeking the unsurpassed state of sublime peace, I went to Āḷāra Kālāma. Having gone to him, I said this to Āḷāra Kālāma: ‘I wish, friend Kālāma, to live the spiritual life in this Dhamma-Vinaya.’ When this was said, monks, Āḷāra Kālāma said this to me: ‘The venerable one may dwell here. Such is this Dharma that in no long time a wise man can realize his own teacher's doctrine, directly experience it through his own insight, attain it, and abide in it.’ So I, monks, in no long time quickly mastered that Dharma. So I, monks, only to that extent, with mere lip-reciting and rehearsal, I spoke of the doctrine of knowledge and the doctrine of the elders. And I claimed, ‘I know and see’—and there were others who did likewise. Then it occurred to me: ‘It is not through mere faith alone that Āḷāra Kālāma declares: “By realising for myself with direct knowledge, I enter upon and abide in this Dhamma.” Certainly Āḷāra Kālāma abides knowing and seeing this Dhamma.’ “Then I went to Āḷāra Kālāma and said to him: ‘Friend Kālāma, in what way do you declare that by realizing for yourself with direct knowledge you enter upon and abide in this Dhamma?’ When this was said, monks, Āḷāra Kālāma declared the realm of nothingness. It occurred to me: ‘Not only does Āḷāra Kālāma have faith, I too have faith; not only does Āḷāra Kālāma have energy, I too have energy; not only does Āḷāra Kālāma have mindfulness, I too have mindfulness; not only does Āḷāra Kālāma have concentration, I too have concentration; not only does Āḷāra Kālāma have wisdom, I too have wisdom. Suppose I endeavor to realize the Dharma that Āḷāra Kālāma declares he enters upon and abides in by realizing for himself with direct knowledge?’ So I, monks, in no long time quickly realized that Dharma by direct knowledge and attained it. “Then I went to Āḷāra Kālāma and said to him: ‘Is it in this way, friend Kālāma, that you declare that you enter upon and abide in this Dhamma by realizing it for yourself with direct knowledge?’ ‘It is to this extent that I, friend, enter upon and abide in this Dhamma by realizing it for myself with direct knowledge.’ ‘I, too, friend, enter upon and abide in this Dhamma to this extent, realizing it for myself with direct knowledge.’ ‘It is a gain for us, friend, a great gain for us that we have such a venerable one for our companion in the holy life. Thus, the Dharma that I declare I have realized through direct knowing and have attained, is the very Dharma that you have realized through direct knowing and abide in. The Dharma that you have realized through direct knowing and abide in, is the very Dharma that I have realized through direct knowing and attained. As I am, so are you; as you are, so am I. Come now, friend, let us both lead this community.’ Thus, monks, Āḷāra Kālāma, my teacher, placed me, his pupil, on a par with himself and honored me with the highest honor. May it be. Taunt. Placed me, the pupil (antevāsiṃ), as equal (samānaṃ), and in the very same position (samasamaṃ) as himself (attanā). He established [me] and worshipped (pūjesi) me with the highest (uḷārāya) worship (pūjāya). It occurred (ahosi) to me (mayhaṃ), monks (bhikkhave): ‘This (ayaṃ) Dharma (dhammo) does not lead (saṃvattati) to disenchantment (nibbidāya), to dispassion (virāgāya), to cessation (nirodhāya), to peace (upasamāya), to direct knowledge (abhiññāya), to enlightenment (sambodhāya), to Nibbāna (nibbānāya), but only (yāvadeva) to reappearance (upapattiyā) in the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatana).’ Not being satisfied (analaṅkaritvā) with that (taṃ) Dhamma (dhammaṃ), disappointed (nibbijja) with it (tasmā dhammā), I (ahaṃ) left (apakkamiṃ).

( ) There is not (natthi). May it be. Taunt.
commentary_pali:
277. Tattha daharova samānoti taruṇova samāno. Susukāḷakesoti suṭṭhu kāḷakeso, añjanavaṇṇakesova hutvāti attho. Bhadrenāti bhaddakena. Paṭhamena vayasāti tiṇṇaṃ vayānaṃ paṭhamavayena. Akāmakānanti anicchamānānaṃ, anādaratthe sāmivacanaṃ. Assūni mukhe etesanti assumukhā; tesaṃ assumukhānaṃ, assukilinnamukhānanti attho. Rudantānanti kanditvā rodamānānaṃ. Kiṃkusalagavesīti kiṃ kusalanti gavesamāno. Anuttaraṃ santivarapadanti uttamaṃ santisaṅkhātaṃ varapadaṃ, nibbānaṃ pariyesamānoti attho. Yena āḷāro kālāmoti ettha āḷāroti tassa nāmaṃ, dīghapiṅgalo kireso. Tenassa āḷāroti nāmaṃ ahosi. Kālāmoti gottaṃ. Viharatāyasmāti viharatu āyasmā. Yattha viññū purisoti yasmiṃ dhamme paṇḍito puriso. Sakaṃ ācariyakanti attano ācariyasamayaṃ. Upasampajja vihareyyāti paṭilabhitvā vihareyya. Ettāvatā tena okāso kato hoti. Taṃ dhammanti taṃ tesaṃ samayaṃ tantiṃ. Pariyāpuṇinti sutvāva uggaṇhiṃ.

Oṭṭhapahatamattenāti tena vuttassa paṭiggahaṇatthaṃ oṭṭhapaharaṇamattena; aparāparaṃ katvā oṭṭhasañcaraṇamattakenāti attho. Lapitalāpanamattenāti tena lapitassa paṭilāpanamattakena. Ñāṇavādanti jānāmīti vādaṃ . Theravādanti thirabhāvavādaṃ, thero ahametthāti etaṃ vacanaṃ. Ahañceva aññe cāti na kevalaṃ ahaṃ, aññepi bahū evaṃ vadanti. Kevalaṃ saddhāmattakenāti paññāya asacchikatvā suddhena saddhāmattakeneva. Bodhisatto kira vācāya dhammaṃ uggaṇhantoyeva, ‘‘na kālāmassa vācāya pariyattimattameva asmiṃ dhamme, addhā esa sattannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ lābhī’’ti aññāsi, tenassa etadahosi.

Oṭṭhapahatamattenā Lapitalāpanamattenā Ñāṇavāda Theravāda Ahañceva aññe cā Kevalaṃ saddhāmattakenā

Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ pavedesīti ākiñcaññāyatanapariyosānā satta samāpattiyo maṃ jānāpesi. Saddhāti imāsaṃ sattannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ nibbattanatthāya saddhā. Vīriyādīsupi eseva nayo. Padaheyyanti payogaṃ kareyyaṃ. Nacirasseva taṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsinti bodhisatto kira vīriyaṃ paggahetvā katipāhaññeva satta suvaṇṇanisseṇiyo pasārento viya satta samāpattiyo nibbattesi; tasmā evamāha.

Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ pavedesī Saddhā Vīriyā Padaheyya Nacirasseva taṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi

Lābhā no, āvusoti anusūyako kiresa kālāmo. Tasmā ‘‘ayaṃ adhunāgato, kinti katvā imaṃ dhammaṃ nibbattesī’’ti usūyaṃ akatvā pasanno pasādaṃ pavedento evamāha. Ubhova santā imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharāmāti ‘‘mahā ayaṃ gaṇo, dvepi janā pariharāmā’’ti vatvā gaṇassa saññaṃ adāsi, ‘‘ahampi sattannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ lābhī, mahāpurisopi sattannameva , ettakā janā mahāpurisassa santike parikammaṃ uggaṇhatha, ettakā mayha’’nti majjhe bhinditvā adāsi. Uḷārāyāti uttamāya. Pūjāyāti kālāmassa kira upaṭṭhākā itthiyopi purisāpi gandhamālādīni gahetvā āgacchanti. Kālāmo – ‘‘gacchatha, mahāpurisaṃ pūjethā’’ti vadati. Te taṃ pūjetvā yaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti, tena kālāmaṃ pūjenti. Mahagghāni mañcapīṭhāni āharanti; tānipi mahāpurisassa dāpetvā yadi avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti, attanā gaṇhāti. Gatagataṭṭhāne varasenāsanaṃ bodhisattassa jaggāpetvā sesakaṃ attanā gaṇhāti. Evaṃ uḷārāya pūjāya pūjesi. Nāyaṃ dhammo nibbidāyātiādīsu ayaṃ sattasamāpattidhammo neva vaṭṭe nibbindanatthāya, na virajjanatthāya, na rāgādinirodhatthāya, na upasamatthāya, na abhiññeyyadhammaṃ abhijānanatthāya, na catumaggasambodhāya, na nibbānasacchikiriyāya saṃvattatīti attho.

Lābhā no, āvuso Ubhova santā imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharāmā Uḷārāyā Pūjāyā Nāyaṃ dhammo nibbidāyā

Yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyāti yāva saṭṭhikappasahassāyuparimāṇe ākiñcaññāyatanabhave upapatti, tāvadeva saṃvattati, na tato uddhaṃ. Evamayaṃ punarāvattanadhammoyeva; yañca ṭhānaṃ pāpeti, taṃ jātijarāmaraṇehi aparimuttameva maccupāsaparikkhittamevāti. Tato paṭṭhāya ca pana mahāsatto yathā nāma chātajjhattapuriso manuññabhojanaṃ labhitvā sampiyāyamānopi bhuñjitvā pittavasena vā semhavasena vā makkhikāvasena vā chaḍḍetvā puna ekaṃ piṇḍampi bhuñjissāmīti manaṃ na uppādeti; evameva imā satta samāpattiyo mahantena ussāhena nibbattetvāpi, tāsu imaṃ punarāvattikādibhedaṃ ādīnavaṃ disvā, puna imaṃ dhammaṃ āvajjissāmi vā samāpajjissāmi vā adhiṭṭhahissāmi vā vuṭṭhahissāmi vā paccavekkhissāmi vāti cittameva na uppādesi. Analaṅkaritvāti alaṃ iminā, alaṃ imināti punappunaṃ alaṅkaritvā. Nibbijjāti nibbinditvā. Apakkaminti agamāsiṃ.

Yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyā Analaṅkaritvā Nibbijjā Apakkami
commentary_english:
277. In that connection, *daharova samāno* means still young, still youthful.

*Susukāḷakeso* means with very black hair, meaning with hair the color of *añjana*.

*Bhadrenā* means with what is auspicious.

*Paṭhamena vayasā* means with the first period of the three periods of life.

*Akāmakānaṃ* means of those who are unwilling, the *sāmivacana* [expressing] lack of regard.

*Assūni mukhe etesanti assumukhā*; *tesaṃ assumukhānaṃ*, means of those with tearful faces, meaning with faces wet with tears.

*Rudantānaṃ* means of those who, having cried, are weeping.

*Kiṃ kusalagavesī*ti means seeking, searching for what is good.

*Anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ* means the unsurpassed excellent state consisting of peace, meaning seeking after *Nirvāṇa*.

In this connection, *yena āḷāro kālāmo*, *āḷāro* is his name; it seems he was tall and tawny.

Therefore, his name was *Āḷāra*.

*Kālāmo* is the *gotra*.

*Viharatāyasmā* means may the venerable one dwell.

*Yattha viññū puriso* means in whatever *Dharma* the wise person [is skilled].

*Sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ* means his own teacher's tradition.

*Upasampajja vihareyyā* means may live, having obtained.

To this extent, he has made an opportunity.

*Taṃ dhammaṃ* means that, their tradition, lineage.

*Pariyāpuṇi* means having heard, he learned.

*Oṭṭhapahatamattenā* means merely with the striking of the lips for the purpose of accepting what was said by him; meaning merely by moving the lips by doing [it] again and again.

*Lapitalāpanamattenā* means merely by repeating what was spoken by him.

*Ñāṇavādaṃ* means the assertion "I know."

*Theravādaṃ* means the assertion of steadfastness, the statement "I am an elder here."

*Ahañceva aññe cā* means not only I, but many others also say this.

*Kevalaṃ saddhāmattakenā* means merely by pure faith alone, without experiencing with wisdom.

It seems that the *Bodhisattva*, while learning the *Dharma* by speech, realized, "Not only is there a statement of the teachings in this *Dharma* of *Kālāma*, truly he is an obtainer of the seven attainments," therefore this occurred to him.

*Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ pavedesī* means he made me know the seven attainments ending in the *Ākiñcaññāyatana*.

*Saddhā* means faith for the sake of producing these seven attainments.

The same method applies to *vīriyā*, and so on.

*Padaheyyaṃ* means I would make an effort.

*Nacirasseva taṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi* means it seems that the *Bodhisattva*, having generated energy, in just a few days produced the seven golden ladders, as if extending [them]; therefore he said this.

*Lābhā no, āvuso* means it seems that *Kālāma* was not envious.

Therefore, without being envious, thinking, "This person has come now; how has he produced this *Dharma*?", being pleased, while expressing pleasure, he said this.

*Ubova santā imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharāmā* means having said "This *gaṇa* is large, let us both maintain [it]," he gave the *saṃjñā* of the *gaṇa*, "I also am an obtainer of the seven attainments, and the great person is also [an obtainer] of just seven.
And he gave after dividing it in the middle, "[So many] people should learn the preparation near the great man, [and so many] are mine."

*Uḷārāyā* means to the highest.

*Pūjāyā* means Kālāma's attendants, both women and men, bring garlands, perfumes, and so on and come.

Kālāma says, "Go, honor the great man."

Having honored him, they honor Kālāma with what is left over.

They bring expensive couches and chairs; having had them given to the great man, if something is left over, he takes it himself.

At each place where he goes, having had the best lodging prepared for the *bodhisattva*, he takes the remainder himself.

Thus, he honored with the highest worship.

"*Nāyaṃ dhammo nibbidāyā*," etc., this sevenfold attainment (*sattasamāpatti*) teaching does not lead to disgust in the round, nor to dispassion, nor to the cessation of passion and so on, nor to peace, nor to the understanding of what is to be understood, nor to the perfect enlightenment of the four paths, nor does it lead to the realization of *nirvāṇa*, this is the meaning.

Oh, friends, gain for us! Both being good, let us cultivate this group.

*Uḷārāyā*, *pūjāyā*, *nāyaṃ dhammo nibbidāyā*.

"*Yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyā*," means up to the arising in the realm of the Ākiñcaññāyatana, which is measured as sixty thousand aeons, so far it leads, not beyond that.

Thus, this is just a teaching that revolves again; and the place it leads to is not freed from birth, old age, and death, it is just surrounded by the noose of death.

Thenceforth, the great being, just as a man afflicted with hunger, having obtained delicious food, although savoring it, having eaten it, whether due to bile or mucus or flies, having thrown it away, does not produce the thought, "Again I will eat even one morsel"; just so, having produced these seven attainments with great effort, having seen the danger in them, this round of rebirths and so on, he does not even produce the thought, "Again I will consider this teaching, or attain it, or resolve upon it, or arise from it, or review it."

"*Analaṅkaritvā*" means "Enough of this, enough of this," having adorned it again and again.

"*Nibbijjā*" means having become disgusted.

"*Apakkami*" means I went away.

*Yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyā*.

*Analaṅkaritvā*, *nibbijjā*, *apakkami*.

mula_pali:
