Accompanied by Channa, he mounted the back of the royal horse, left the city, showed [Channa] the site of the Kaṇṭhaka-turning-back-shrine, crossed three kingdoms, went forth on the bank of the Anomā River, wandering on step by step, he begged for alms in Rājagaha, sat on Paṇḍava Mountain, and when asked his name and clan by King Bimbisāra of Magadha, and told, "Accept this kingdom!", he said, "Enough, great king! I have no need of a kingdom. Having abandoned the kingdom, I will strive for the good of the world, and become one whose roof is removed (vivaṭacchado) in the world." He said, "Then, having become a Buddha, you should first visit my conquered territory." He took this promise, approached Āḷāra Kālāma and Udaka Rāmaputta, and not finding the essence in their teaching of the Dharma, having departed from there, even while performing difficult ascetic practices for six years at Uruvelā, not being able to penetrate the deathless, he refreshed his body by partaking of coarse food.

Then, at that time, in the village of Uruvelā, a daughter of a wealthy family named Sujātā made a vow at a certain banyan tree: "If I go to a family home of equal birth, and obtain a son in my first pregnancy, I will perform a rice-milk offering (balikammaṃ)."
This her vow took effect.
On the Visakha full-moon day, thinking, "Early in the morning I will perform a rice-milk offering," at dawn, she herself prepared rice-milk.
When that rice-milk was boiling, huge bubbles rising, turned to the right and ran round together.
Not a single drop fell outside.
The great Brahmā held over it a canopy of state.
The four guardians of the world took up guard with swords in their hands.
Śakka, bringing the burning sticks together, lit the fire.
The deities, having collected the essence in the four continents, put it there.
The Bodhisattva, awaiting the time for begging alms, early in the morning went and sat at the foot of the tree.
A female servant, who had gone to sweep at the foot of the tree, came and announced to Sujātā: "A deity is sitting at the foot of the tree!"
Sujātā, having prepared all the adornments, having loaded the rice-milk into a golden bowl worth a hundred thousand [pieces], having covered it with another golden dish, having lifted it up, went, and seeing the Great Being, having placed [the bowl], together with the dish, in his hand, having paid homage, said, "Just as my wish has been fulfilled, so may your [wish] also be fulfilled!" and departed.

The Bodhisattva, having gone to the bank of the Nerañjarā River, having placed the golden bowl on the bank, having bathed, having come back up, while making forty-nine morsels, having eaten the rice-milk, threw [the bowl] saying, "If today I become a Buddha, may the bowl go upstream!"
The bowl, having gone upstream, having stayed for a moment, having entered the abode of the Kāla-Nāga king, lifted up the bowls of the three Buddhas, and remained [there].

The Great Being, having spent the day in a grove, at eventide, having taken the eight handfuls of grass given by Sottiya, having ascended the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), stood on the southern side.
That place did not tremble, like a drop of water on a lotus leaf.
The Great Being, [thinking], "This is not able to bear my merit," went to the western side, and that too did not tremble in the same way.
He went to the northern side, and that too did not tremble in the same way.
He went to the eastern side, there a place measuring the length of a cross-legged sitting posture was as firm as a well-planted stake of Indra.
The Great Being, [thinking], "This is the place for all Buddhas to shatter and destroy defilements," shook those grasses, having taken [them] by the tips.
Those were like [a carpet] cut around with a painter’s brush.
The Bodhisattva, [thinking], "Without attaining enlightenment, I will not destroy this seat," having determined upon an unwavering effort, sat cross-legged.

At that very moment, Māra, having fashioned a thousand arms, having mounted the elephant named Girimekhala, one and a half yojanas in height, having taken an army of Māra nine yojanas [in extent], peering about with a menacing gaze, came near, covering [the earth] like a mountain.
The Great Being, [thinking], "While I was fulfilling the ten perfections, there is no other renunciate or Brahmin, god, Māra, or Brahmā as a witness. However, in my existence as Vessantara, the great earth was a witness in seven instances. Now also, this very inanimate great earth, resembling a wooden pestle, is my witness," stretched out his hand.
At that very instant, the great earth, emitting a hundred and a thousand sounds, like a bell-metal bowl struck with an iron rod, thundered, and as it whirled around, made the army of Māra flee to the rim of the universe.
The great being, just as the sun arises, having scattered the power of Māra, in the first watch [of the night] purified the knowledge of previous existences, in the middle watch, the divine eye, and in the last watch, having directed the knowledge towards dependent origination, having contemplated arising and ceasing, at dawn, having become a Buddha, [thought,] "By me for hundreds of thousands of millions of aeons, effort has been made for the sake of this seat," and sat for seven days in one seat.

Then to some deities, the doubt arose, "Are there other qualities that bring about Buddhahood?"

Then, on the eighth day, the Blessed One, rising from concentration, knowing the doubt of the deities, in order to dispel their doubt, having risen into the sky and having shown the twin miracle, having dispelled their doubt, having stood slightly to the east of the seat in the northern direction, gazing with unblinking eyes at the place of attaining the fruit of the perfections that had been fulfilled for four incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of aeons, the seat, and the Bodhi tree, spent seven days. That place became known as the *Animisa Cetiya*.

*Animisa Cetiya*. Then, between the seat and the standing place, walking back and forth on the jeweled promenade that stretched from east to west, he spent seven days. That place became known as the *Ratana Caṅkama Cetiya*.

Then in the western direction, the deities constructed a jeweled house. There, having sat on the seat, contemplating the *Abhidhamma Piṭaka*, especially the Anantanayasamantapaṭṭhāna, he spent seven days. That place became known as the *Ratanaghara Cetiya*.

Thus, having spent four weeks near the Bodhi tree, in the fifth week, from the root of the Bodhi tree, he approached the Ajapāla Banyan tree. There too, contemplating the Dharma, experiencing the bliss of liberation, he sat. Contemplating the Dharma, he reflected in this way on the path of reasoning in the Abhidhamma: first the Dhammasaṅgaṇīpakaraṇa, then the Vibhaṅgapakaraṇa, the Dhātukathāpakaraṇa, the Puggalapaññattipakaraṇa, the Kathāvatthu nāma pakaraṇaṃ, the Yamakaṃ nāma pakaraṇaṃ, then the Mahāpakaraṇaṃ, the Paṭṭhānaṃ nāmāti.

*Ratana Caṅkama Cetiya*. *Abhidhamma Piṭaka*. *Ratana Ghara Cetiya*.

There, when a subtle, pleasant Paṭṭhāna entered his mind, joy arose. When joy arose, his blood became clear. When his blood was clear, his skin became clear.

When his skin was clear, rays, the size of an upper chamber and beginning with the upper chamber, having risen from the eastern part of his body, spread into the sky like a flock of Chaddanta Nāgas, reaching countless world-systems in the eastern direction; having risen from the western part of his body, in the western direction; having risen from the right shoulder, in the southern direction; having risen from the left shoulder, having risen in the northern direction, spread into countless world-systems. Rays, the color of coral sprouts, having emerged from the soles of his feet, having pierced the great earth, having split the water in two, having blown apart the wind-element, spread into the open sky. A circle of rays, the color of sapphires, like a revolving jeweled garland, having risen from his head, having pierced the six deva-worlds, having pierced the nine Brahma-worlds, Vehapphala, the five Śuddhāvāsas, and having passed beyond the four Āruppe, spread into the open sky.

On that day, in immeasurable world-systems, immeasurable beings all became golden-colored.

And from that day, the rays that emerged from the body of the Blessed One, even to this day, continue to go to countless world-elements.

Thus, the Blessed One, having spent a week at the Ajapāla Banyan tree, then spent another week at Mucalinda, and as soon as he had sat down, a great untimely cloud arose, filling the entire womb of the universe.

It is said that such a great cloud rains only at two times: when a wheel-turning monarch arises, or when a Buddha arises.

Here it arose in the Buddha-time.

Then, when that had arisen, Mucalinda, the Nāga-king, thought, "This cloud arose just as the Teacher entered my dwelling. It is fitting for me to give him a dwelling."

Even though he was able to create a palace made of seven jewels, he thought, "If I do so, it will not be of great benefit to me. I will do service to the body of the one with ten powers," and having made his own form great, having encircled the Teacher seven times with his coils, he held his hood above.

The space inside the coils below was the size of a Lohapāsāda.

The Nāga-king's intention was that the Teacher would abide with whatever posture he desired.

Therefore, he encircled such a great space.

In the middle, a jeweled seat was arranged, and above, there was a canopy of cloth adorned with golden stars, filled with gathered garlands of fragrant flowers.

In the four corners, lamps were lit with fragrant oil, and in the four directions, sandalwood boxes were opened and placed.

Thus, the Blessed One, having spent that week there, then spent another week at Rājāyatana.

On the eighth week, Sakka, the king of the gods, offered a toothpick and a myrobalan fruit, and having chewed [the toothpick], having washed his face, having partaken of the alms-food brought by the four world-protectors in a precious, stone bowl, again having returned and sat at the Ajapāla Banyan tree, this thought, which is customary for all Buddhas, arose.

There, *Paṇḍito* means endowed with wisdom.

*Viyatto* means endowed with discernment.

*Medhāvī* means endowed with knowledge arising from the basis.
Being *apparajakkhajātika* means being of pure essence (*visuddhasattva*), of taintless nature (*nikkilesajātika*), because of having warded off [defilements] through attainment (*samāpatti*).
“He will understand” means he will consider, he will penetrate.
“And wisdom is mine” means that even to me arose the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñatājñāna*).
It is said that the Blessed One, without going to the end merely by what was said by the deity, but himself surveying with the wisdom of omniscience, saw that he, having made an end at the end of the seventh day from here, was reborn in the realm of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*).
Referring to that, he said: “And vision arose to me.”
Being *mahājāniya* means that because of being deprived of the path and its fruit which should be attained within seven days, he has great loss, therefore he is *mahājāniya*.
Because of being reborn at an inauspicious moment (*akkhaṇa*), having gone, he does not have the faculty of hearing to hear the Dharma being taught; here, there are no feet to come to the place where the Dharma is being taught; thus, he shows that he is born *mahājāniya*.
Being *abhidosakālaṅkata* means having made an end at midnight.
“And wisdom is mine” means that even to me arose the wisdom of omniscience.
Here too, it is said that the Blessed One, without making a determination by the word of the deity, but surveying with the wisdom of omniscience, saw: “Yesterday at midnight, Udaka, the son of Rāma, having made an end, was reborn in the realm of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*).”
Therefore, he spoke thus.
The rest is just like the previous method.
Being *bahukārā* means being very helpful (*bahūpakārā*).
“They attended upon him, being sent for the purpose of exertion” means that they attended upon him with sweeping the monastery (*pariveṇa*) in the dwelling place, with taking the bowl and robes (*pattacīvara*), and with continual giving of face-water, tooth sticks, etc., being in the state of being sent for the purpose of exertion (*padhānatthāya pesitattabhāvaṃ*).
Who then are those called the group of five (*pañcavaggiyā*)? These are—
The wise (*paṇḍitaḥ*), the intelligent (*viyattaḥ*), the learned (*medhāvī*), the one born without attachment (*apparajakkhajātikaḥ*), he will understand (*ājānissati*), and wisdom is mine (*ñāṇañca pana me*), the great loss (*mahājāniyo*), the great loss (*mahājāniyo*), having made an end at midnight (*abhidosakālaṅkato*), and wisdom is mine (*ñāṇañca pana me*), very helpful (*bahukārā*), they attended upon him, being sent for the purpose of exertion (*padhānapahitattaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃsū*), the group of five (*pañcavaggiyā*).
Rāma, banner, mark, luminous,
sacrifice, well-fed, well-controlled, well-given;
These then were eight Brahmins,
with six limbs, they explained the *mantra*.
At the time of the Bodhisattva's birth, there were eight *brāhmaṇas*, dream interpreters as well as sign interpreters.
Among them, three declared in two ways: “He who is endowed with these marks, if he lives in a house, will be a king, a wheel-turner (*cakravartin*), if he goes forth, he will be a Buddha.”
Five *brāhmaṇas* made a one-sided declaration: “He who is endowed with these marks does not remain in a house; he will be a Buddha.”
Among them, the former three went according to the word of the *mantra*; but these five transcended the word of the *mantra*.
They, having given away the full bowl they had obtained to their relatives, and being free from doubt, having set out for the going-forth of a mendicant (*samaṇapabbajja*) with respect to the Bodhisattva, went forth.
They also call them sons.
That is rejected by the commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*).
It is said that these, while still young, knew many *mantras*; therefore, those *brāhmaṇas* established them in the place of teachers (*ācariyaṭṭhāne*).
They, later, thinking, “It will not be possible for us to go forth, having abandoned our children, wives, and matted hair,” while still young, having gone forth, wandering about, enjoying pleasant dwellings.
From time to time, they ask: “Friend, has the great man gone forth on the great going-forth (*mahābhinikkhamana*?”
People say: “Where will you see the great man? He enjoys prosperity like a god in the middle of the three palaces, with three kinds of dancing.”
Having heard that, thinking, “The great man's wisdom has not yet reached maturity,” they lived with little effort.
Why, in this connection, did the Blessed One say, “These five in the group are very helpful (*bahukārā*)?” Does he teach the Dharma only to those who are helpful, and not teach those who are not helpful? No, he does not not teach.
Because of familiarity, he surveyed Āḷāra and Kālāma, and Udaka, the son of Rāma.
In this Buddha-field, having set aside Aññāsikoṇḍañña, there is no one who is capable of realizing the first Dharma.
Why? Because of the condition of such.
It is said that in the past, at the time of doing meritorious deeds, there were two brothers.
They made a crop together.
There, the elder brother thought, "I must give the first fruits of the crop nine times during one season."

So, at the time of sowing, having given what was called the *bījagga* (first seed), he consulted with his younger brother at the time of the embryo, "We will split the embryo at the time of the embryo and give it."

The younger brother said, "You want to destroy the young crop."

The elder brother, knowing that the younger brother was not complying, divided the field, split the embryo from his share, extracted the milk, and gave it mixed with ghee and molasses. At the time of *puthuka* (new grain), he had *puthuka* made and gave it. At the time of threshing, the first of the threshing; at the time of winnowing, the first of the winnowing; among bundles, the first bundle; the first of the chaff; the first of the goods; the first of the storehouse—in this way, he gave the first gift nine times in one season.

But the younger brother gave it after harvesting. Among them, the elder brother was born as Aññāsikoṇḍañña Thera, the younger brother as Subhadda the wanderer.

Thus, because of giving the first of the nine gifts in one season, except for the Thera, there was no one else capable of realizing the Dhamma for the first time.

"These five ascetics are very helpful," this was said only with regard to remembering their help.

At Isipatana in the Deer Park: It is said that in that place, when a Buddha had not arisen, Paccekabuddhas, after spending seven days in cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*) on Gandhamādana Mountain, would rise from cessation, chew a *nāgalatā* toothpick, wash their faces in Anotatta Lake, take their robes and bowls, and come through the sky and land there.

There, after putting on their robes, they would go to the city for alms, and after finishing their meal, they would fly up from there again when it was time to leave.

Thus, because sages land and take off here, that place went by the name "Isipatana" (the place where the sages land).

Moreover, because it was given for the safety of the deer, it is called "Migadāya" (Deer Park).

Therefore, it was said, "At Isipatana in the Deer Park."

mula_pali:
285. ‘‘Addasā kho maṃ, bhikkhave, upako ājīvako antarā ājīviko (sī. pī. ka.) ca gayaṃ antarā ca bodhiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannaṃ. Disvāna maṃ etadavoca – ‘vippasannāni kho te, āvuso, indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto! Kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī’ti ? Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, upakaṃ ājīvakaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsiṃ –

‘Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūhamasmi, sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto;

Sabbañjaho taṇhākkhaye vimutto, sayaṃ abhiññāya kamuddiseyyaṃ.

‘Na me ācariyo atthi, sadiso me na vijjati;

Sadevakasmiṃ lokasmiṃ, natthi me paṭipuggalo.

‘Ahañhi arahā loke, ahaṃ satthā anuttaro;

Ekomhi sammāsambuddho, sītibhūtosmi nibbuto.

‘Dhammacakkaṃ pavattetuṃ, gacchāmi kāsinaṃ puraṃ;

Andhībhūtasmiṃ andhabhūtasmiṃ (sī. syā. pī.) lokasmiṃ, āhañchaṃ amatadundubhi’nti.

andhabhūtasmiṃ (sī. syā. pī.)

‘Yathā kho tvaṃ, āvuso, paṭijānāsi, arahasi anantajino’ti!

‘Mādisā ve jinā honti, ye pattā āsavakkhayaṃ;

Jitā me pāpakā dhammā, tasmāhamupaka jino’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, upako ājīvako ‘hupeyyapāvuso’ti huveyyapāvuso (sī. pī.), huveyyāvuso (syā.) vatvā sīsaṃ okampetvā ummaggaṃ gahetvā pakkāmi.

huveyyapāvuso (sī. pī.), huveyyāvuso (syā.)
commentary_pali:
285.Antarā ca gayaṃ antarā ca bodhinti gayāya ca bodhissa ca vivare tigāvutantare ṭhāne. Bodhimaṇḍato hi gayā tīṇi gāvutāni. Bārāṇasī aṭṭhārasa yojanāni. Upako bodhimaṇḍassa ca gayāya ca antare bhagavantaṃ addasa. Antarāsaddena pana yuttattā upayogavacanaṃ kataṃ. Īdisesu ca ṭhānesu akkharacintakā ‘‘antarā gāmañca nadiñca yātī’’ti evaṃ ekameva antarāsaddaṃ payujjanti. So dutiyapadenapi yojetabbo hoti . Ayojiyamāne upayogavacanaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Idha pana yojetvā eva vuttoti. Addhānamaggapaṭipannanti addhānasaṅkhātaṃ maggaṃ paṭipannaṃ, dīghamaggapaṭipannanti attho. Addhānamaggagamanasamayassa hi vibhaṅge ‘‘addhayojanaṃ gacchissāmīti bhuñjitabba’’ntiādivacanato (pāci. 218) addhayojanampi addhānamaggo hoti. Bodhimaṇḍato pana gayā tigāvutaṃ.

Sabbābhibhūti sabbaṃ tebhūmakadhammaṃ abhibhavitvā ṭhito. Sabbavidūti sabbaṃ catubhūmakadhammaṃ avediṃ aññāsiṃ. Sabbesu dhammesu anupalittoti sabbesu tebhūmakadhammesu kilesalepanena anupalitto. Sabbaṃ jahoti sabbaṃ tebhūmakadhammaṃ jahitvā ṭhito. Taṇhākkhaye vimuttoti taṇhākkhaye nibbāne ārammaṇato vimutto. Sayaṃ abhiññāyāti sabbaṃ catubhūmakadhammaṃ attanāva jānitvā. Kamuddiseyyanti kaṃ aññaṃ ‘‘ayaṃ me ācariyo’’ti uddiseyyaṃ.

Sabbābhibhū Sabbavidū Sabbesu dhammesu anupalitto Sabbaṃ jaho Taṇhākkhaye vimutto Sayaṃ abhiññāyā Kamuddiseyya

Na me ācariyo atthīti lokuttaradhamme mayhaṃ ācariyo nāma natthi. Natthi me paṭipuggaloti mayhaṃ paṭibhāgapuggalo nāma natthi. Sammāsambuddhoti sahetunā nayena cattāri saccāni sayaṃ buddho. Sītibhūtoti sabbakilesagginibbāpanena sītibhūto. Kilesānaṃyeva nibbutattā nibbuto. Kāsinaṃ puranti kāsiraṭṭhe nagaraṃ. Āhañchaṃ amatadundubhinti dhammacakkapaṭilābhāya amatabheriṃ paharissāmīti gacchāmi. Arahasi anantajinoti anantajinoti bhavituṃ yutto. Hupeyya pāvusoti, āvuso, evampi nāma bhaveyya. Pakkāmīti vaṅkahārajanapadaṃ nāma agamāsi.

Na me ācariyo atthī Natthi me paṭipuggalo Sammāsambuddho Sītibhūto nibbuto. Kāsinaṃ pura Āhañchaṃ amatadundubhi Arahasi anantajino Hupeyya pāvuso Pakkāmī

Tatthekaṃ migaluddakagāmakaṃ nissāya vāsaṃ kappesi. Jeṭṭhakaluddako taṃ upaṭṭhāsi. Tasmiñca janapade caṇḍā makkhikā honti. Atha naṃ ekāya cāṭiyā vasāpesuṃ, migaluddako dūre migavaṃ gacchanto ‘‘amhākaṃ arahante mā pamajjī’’ti chāvaṃ nāma dhītaraṃ āṇāpetvā agamāsi saddhiṃ puttabhātukehi. Sā cassa dhītā dassanīyā hoti koṭṭhāsasampannā. Dutiyadivase upako gharaṃ āgato taṃ dārikaṃ sabbaṃ upacāraṃ katvā parivisituṃ upagataṃ disvā rāgena abhibhūto bhuñjitumpi asakkonto bhājanena bhattaṃ ādāya vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā bhattaṃ ekamante nikkhipitvā sace chāvaṃ labhāmi, jīvāmi, no ce, marāmīti nirāhāro sayi. Sattame divase māgaviko āgantvā dhītaraṃ upakassa pavattiṃ pucchi. Sā ‘‘ekadivasameva āgantvā puna nāgatapubbo’’ti āha. Māgaviko āgataveseneva naṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāmīti taṃkhaṇaṃyeva gantvā ‘‘kiṃ, bhante, apphāsuka’’nti pāde parāmasanto pucchi. Upako nitthunanto parivattatiyeva. So ‘‘vadatha bhante, yaṃ mayā sakkā kātuṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ karissāmī’’ti āha. Upako, ‘‘sace chāvaṃ labhāmi, jīvāmi, no ce, idheva maraṇaṃ seyyo’’ti āha. Jānāsi pana, bhante, kiñci sippanti. Na jānāmīti. Na, bhante, kiñci sippaṃ ajānantena sakkā gharāvāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātunti.

chāvaṃ upako

So āha – ‘‘nāhaṃ kiñci sippaṃ jānāmi, apica tumhākaṃ maṃsahārako bhavissāmi, maṃsañca vikkīṇissāmī’’ti. Māgaviko, ‘‘amhākampi etadeva ruccatī’’ti uttarasāṭakaṃ datvā gharaṃ ānetvā dhītaraṃ adāsi. Tesaṃ saṃvāsamanvāya putto vijāyi. Subhaddotissa nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Chāvā tassa rodanakāle ‘‘maṃsahārakassa putta, migaluddakassa putta mā rodī’’tiādīni vadamānā puttatosanagītena upakaṃ uppaṇḍesi. Bhadde tvaṃ maṃ anāthoti maññasi. Atthi me anantajino nāma sahāyo. Tassāhaṃ santike gamissāmīti āha. Chāvā evamayaṃ aṭṭīyatīti ñatvā punappunaṃ katheti. So ekadivasaṃ anārocetvāva majjhimadesābhimukho pakkāmi.

Subhaddo anantajino

Bhagavā ca tena samayena sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane mahāvihāre. Atha kho bhagavā paṭikacceva bhikkhū āṇāpesi – ‘‘yo, bhikkhave, ‘anantajino’ti pucchamāno āgacchati, tassa maṃ dasseyyāthā’’ti. Upakopi kho ‘‘kuhiṃ anantajino vasatī’’ti pucchanto anupubbena sāvatthiṃ āgantvā vihāramajjhe ṭhatvā kuhiṃ anantajinoti pucchi. Taṃ bhikkhū bhagavato santikaṃ nayiṃsu. So bhagavantaṃ disvā – ‘‘sañjānātha maṃ bhagavā’’ti āha. Āma, upaka, sañjānāmi, kuhiṃ pana tvaṃ vasitthāti. Vaṅkahārajanapade, bhanteti. Upaka, mahallakosi jāto pabbajituṃ sakkhissasīti. Pabbajissāmi, bhanteti. Bhagavā pabbājetvā tassa kammaṭṭhānaṃ adāsi. So kammaṭṭhāne kammaṃ karonto anāgāmiphale patiṭṭhāya kālaṃ katvā avihesu nibbatto. Nibbattakkhaṇeyeva arahattaṃ pāpuṇīti. Avihesu nibbattamattā hi satta janā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu, tesaṃ so aññataro.

Vuttañhetaṃ –

‘‘Avihaṃ upapannāse, vimuttā satta bhikkhavo;

Rāgadosaparikkhīṇā, tiṇṇā loke visattikaṃ.

Rāgadosa

Upako palagaṇḍo ca, pukkusāti ca te tayo;

Bhaddiyo khaṇḍadevo ca, bahuraggi ca saṅgiyo;

Te hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upajjhagu’’nti. (saṃ. ni. 1.105);
commentary_english:
285. "Between Gayā and between Bodhi" means in the space between Gayā and the Bodhi tree, in a place three *gāvutas* distant. Gayā is three *gāvutas* from the Bodhi-tree (*bodhimaṇḍa*). Bārāṇasī is eighteen *yojanas*. Upaka saw the Blessed One between the Bodhi-tree (*bodhimaṇḍa*) and Gayā. Because of being connected with the word *antarā*, the accusative case is used. In such places, those who ponder over the letters use only one word *antarā* thus: "between the village and the river he goes." That should be connected with the second word too. If it is not connected, it does not obtain the accusative case. But here it is said having connected [the words]. "Having entered upon the high road" (*addhānamaggapaṭipanna*) means having entered upon the road called *addhāna*, it means having entered upon a long road. For in the analysis of the time of going on the high road, because of the saying beginning with "one should eat having thought 'I will go half a *yojana*,'" even half a *yojana* is a high road. But from the Bodhi-tree (*bodhimaṇḍa*) to Gayā is three *gāvutas*. "All-conquering" (*sabbābhibhū*) means having conquered all the three-world phenomena, he remains. "All-knowing" (*sabbavidū*) means I knew and understood all the four-world phenomena. "Unstained in all things" (*sabbesu dhammesu anupalitto*) means unstained by the stain of defilements in all the three-world phenomena. "All-abandoning" (*sabbaṃ jaho*) means having abandoned all the three-world phenomena, he remains. "Liberated in the destruction of craving" (*taṇhākkhaye vimutto*) means liberated in nirvāṇa, in the destruction of craving, from an object. "Through direct knowledge oneself" (*sayaṃ abhiññāyā*) means having known all the four-world phenomena oneself. "Whom should I point out?" (*kamuddiseyya*) means whom else should I point out saying "this is my teacher?" "I have no teacher" (*na me ācariyo atthī*) means in the supramundane phenomena, I have no teacher. "There is no equal to me" (*natthi me paṭipuggalo*) means there is no one equal to me. "Perfectly enlightened" (*sammāsambuddho*) means having understood the four truths oneself, through a reasoned method. "Cool" (*sītibhūto*) means having become cool through the extinguishing of all the fires of defilements. "Extinguished" (*nibbuto*) because of the extinguishing of the defilements themselves. "To the city of Kāsī" (*kāsinaṃ pura*) means to a city in the kingdom of Kāsī. "I shall beat the drum of the immortal" (*āhañchaṃ amatadundubhi*) means I am going to beat the drum of the immortal for the gaining of the wheel of the law (*dharmacakra*). "You deserve to be the endless conqueror" (*arahasi anantajino*) means you are fit to be the endless conqueror. "It might be so, friend" (*hupeyya pāvuso*), friend (*āvusho*), it might be so. "He departed" (*pakkāmī*) means he went to a district named Vaṅkahāra. There he arranged his dwelling depending on a hamlet of hunters. Jeṭṭhakaluddaka attended upon him. And in that district there are fierce flies. Then they kept him safe with a pot. The hunter, going far away to hunt, having ordered his daughter named Chāvaṃ, "Do not neglect our venerable one" went away together with his sons and nephews. And that daughter of his was beautiful, possessing excellent limbs. On the second day, *Upaka* came to the house. Having shown all courtesy to the girl, when he was about to serve the food that had been brought, he was overcome by passion. Unable to even eat, he took the food in a bowl, went to the sleeping place, put the food on one side, and thought, "If I get the *chāva*, I will live; if not, I will die," and lay down without food. On the seventh day, *Māgavika* came and asked his daughter about *Upaka's* behavior. She said, "Having come only one day, he has not come again." *Māgavika*, appearing as if just arriving, approached him and asked, "What is the matter, venerable sir? Are you unwell?" touching his feet. *Upaka* kept moaning and tossing about. He said, "Tell me, venerable sir, what I am able to do; I will do everything." *Upaka* said, "If I get the *chāva*, I will live; if not, death here is better." "Do you know any craft, venerable sir?" "I do not know." "It is not possible, venerable sir, for one who does not know any craft to maintain a household."

chāvaṃ upako

He said, "I do not know any craft, but I will be a meat-eater for you, and I will sell meat." *Māgavika* said, "Even that is pleasing to us." Giving an upper garment, he brought him home and gave him his daughter. Through their cohabitation, a son was born. They named him *Subhaddatissa*. When the *chāvā* was crying, saying things like, "Son of a meat-eater, son of a hunter, do not cry," she caressed *Upaka* with songs to please the child. "My dear, do you think I am helpless? I have a friend named *Anantajina*." He said, "I will go to his presence." Knowing that the *chāvā* was being annoying, she repeatedly told him. One day, without announcing it, he left, heading towards the middle country.

subhaddo anantajino

And at that time, the Blessed One was staying in *Sāvatthi*, in the *Jetavana* monastery, in the great monastery. Then the Blessed One, early in the morning, instructed the monks, "If anyone comes asking, 'Where is *Anantajina*?', you should show him to me." *Upaka* also, asking, "Where does *Anantajina* live?", gradually came to *Sāvatthi*. Standing in the middle of the monastery, he asked, "Where is *Anantajina*?" The monks led him to the presence of the Blessed One. Having seen the Blessed One, he said, "Do you recognize me, Blessed One?" "Yes, *Upaka*, I recognize you. Where do you live?" "In the country of *Vaṅkahāra*, venerable sir." "Upaka, you have become old. Will you be able to go forth (into homelessness)?" "I will go forth, venerable sir." The Blessed One ordained him and gave him a meditation subject (kammaṭṭhāna). Practicing the *kammaṭṭhāna*, establishing himself in the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala), at the end of his life, he was reborn in *Aviha*. In the very moment of rebirth, he attained Arhatship. For, indeed, seven beings, as soon as they were born in Aviha, attained *arhattva*; he was one of them. It was said: "In Aviha, seven monks arose, liberated, their *rāga* and *dosa* destroyed, having crossed over attachment in the world. Upaka, Palagaṇḍa, and Pukkusāti, these three; Bhaddiya, Khaṇḍadeva, Bahuraggi, and Saṅgiya; having abandoned the human body, they attained divine union." (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.105)

mula_pali:
286. ‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bārāṇasī isipatanaṃ migadāyo yena pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃ. Addasaṃsu kho maṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū dūrato āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna aññamaññaṃ saṇṭhapesuṃ aññamaññaṃ katikaṃ saṇṭhapesuṃ (vinayapiṭake mahāvagge) – ‘ayaṃ kho, āvuso, samaṇo gotamo āgacchati bāhulliko bāhuliko (sī. pī.) sāratthadīpanīṭīkāya sameti padhānavibbhanto āvatto bāhullāya. So neva abhivādetabbo, na paccuṭṭhātabbo; nāssa pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Api ca kho āsanaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ, sace ākaṅkhissati nisīdissatī’ti. Yathā yathā kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, upasaṅkamiṃ tathā tathā pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu sakāya katikāya saṇṭhātuṃ. Appekacce maṃ paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesuṃ, appekacce āsanaṃ paññapesuṃ, appekacce pādodakaṃ upaṭṭhapesuṃ. Api ca kho maṃ nāmena ca āvusovādena ca samudācaranti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavocaṃ – ‘mā, bhikkhave, tathāgataṃ nāmena ca āvusovādena ca samudācaratha samudācarittha (sī. syā. pī.). Arahaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sammāsambuddho . Odahatha, bhikkhave, sotaṃ, amatamadhigataṃ, ahamanusāsāmi, ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamānā nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū maṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘tāyapi kho tvaṃ, āvuso gotama, iriyāya tāya paṭipadāya tāya dukkarakārikāya nājjhagamā uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ, kiṃ pana tvaṃ etarahi bāhulliko padhānavibbhanto āvatto bāhullāya adhigamissasi uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesa’nti? Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavocaṃ – ‘na, bhikkhave, tathāgato bāhulliko, na padhānavibbhanto, na āvatto bāhullāya . Arahaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sammāsambuddho. Odahatha, bhikkhave, sotaṃ, amatamadhigataṃ, ahamanusāsāmi, ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamānā nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti. Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū maṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘tāyapi kho tvaṃ, āvuso gotama, iriyāya tāya paṭipadāya tāya dukkarakārikāya nājjhagamā uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ, kiṃ pana tvaṃ etarahi bāhulliko padhānavibbhanto āvatto bāhullāya adhigamissasi uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesa’nti? Dutiyampi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavocaṃ – ‘na, bhikkhave, tathāgato bāhulliko…pe… upasampajja viharissathā’ti. Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū maṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘tāyapi kho tvaṃ, āvuso gotama, iriyāya tāya paṭipadāya tāya dukkarakārikāya nājjhagamā uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ, kiṃ pana tvaṃ etarahi bāhulliko padhānavibbhanto āvatto bāhullāya adhigamissasi uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesa’nti?

samudācarittha (sī. syā. pī.)

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavocaṃ – ‘abhijānātha me no tumhe, bhikkhave, ito pubbe evarūpaṃ pabhāvitameta’nti bhāsitametanti (sī. syā. vinayepi)? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Arahaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sammāsambuddho. Odahatha, bhikkhave, sotaṃ, amatamadhigataṃ, ahamanusāsāmi, ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamānā nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’ti.

bhāsitametanti (sī. syā. vinayepi)

‘‘Asakkhiṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū saññāpetuṃ. Dvepi sudaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ovadāmi, tayo bhikkhū piṇḍāya caranti. Yaṃ tayo bhikkhū piṇḍāya caritvā āharanti tena chabbaggiyā chabbaggā (sī. syā.) yāpema. Tayopi sudaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ovadāmi, dve bhikkhū piṇḍāya caranti. Yaṃ dve bhikkhū piṇḍāya caritvā āharanti tena chabbaggiyā yāpema. Atha kho, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū mayā evaṃ ovadiyamānā evaṃ anusāsiyamānā attanā jātidhammā samānā jātidhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajātaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesamānā ajātaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ ajjhagamaṃsu, attanā jarādhammā samānā jarādhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā ajaraṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesamānā ajaraṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ ajjhagamaṃsu, attanā byādhidhammā samānā…pe… attanā maraṇadhammā samānā… attanā sokadhammā samānā… attanā saṃkilesadhammā samānā saṃkilesadhamme ādīnavaṃ viditvā asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ pariyesamānā asaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ ajjhagamaṃsu. Ñāṇañca pana nesaṃ dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā no vimutti akuppā nesaṃ vimutti (ka.), ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’ti.

chabbaggā (sī. syā.) akuppā nesaṃ vimutti (ka.)
mula_english:
286. “Then, monks, wandering by stages, I eventually came to Benares, to the Deer Park at Isipatana, and I approached the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū).

The group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū) saw me coming in the distance. Having seen me, they made this agreement among themselves: ‘Friends, here comes the ascetic Gotama, who lives luxuriously, has given up striving, and has turned to a life of indulgence. We shouldn’t bow down to him, stand up for him, or receive his bowl and robe. Still, a seat should be set out; if he wants to, he can sit down.’

However, as I approached, monks, the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū) were unable to keep their agreement. Some came to meet me and took my bowl and outer robe, some prepared a seat, and some set out water for my feet. Still, they addressed me by name and as ‘friend.’

“When this was said, I said to the group of five monks (pañcavaggiye bhikkhū): ‘Monks, do not address the *Tathāgata* by name and as “friend.” Monks, the *Tathāgata* is an *Arhat*, a *Sammāsambuddha* (perfectly self-awakened one). Lend ear, monks: the Deathless has been attained. I will instruct you. I will teach you the *Dhamma*. Practicing as you are instructed, you will soon attain in this very life, realize for yourselves with direct knowledge, and abide in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness.’

When this was said, monks, the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū) said to me: ‘Friend Gotama, even by that conduct, that practice, and that performance of austerities, you did not achieve any superhuman states, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. So how will you now, living luxuriously, having given up striving, and reverting to a life of indulgence, achieve any superhuman states, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?’

When this was said, I said to the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū): ‘Monks, the *Tathāgata* does not live luxuriously, has not given up striving, and has not turned to a life of indulgence. Monks, the *Tathāgata* is an *Arhat*, a *Sammāsambuddha*. Lend ear, monks: the Deathless has been attained. I will instruct you. I will teach you the *Dhamma*. Practicing as you are instructed, you will soon attain in this very life, realize for yourselves with direct knowledge, and abide in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness.’

A second time the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū) said to me: ‘Friend Gotama, even by that conduct, that practice, and that performance of austerities, you did not achieve any superhuman states…any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?’ A second time I said to the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū): ‘Monks, the *Tathāgata* does not live luxuriously…you will abide.’

A third time the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū) said to me: ‘Friend Gotama, even by that conduct, that practice, and that performance of austerities, you did not achieve any superhuman states…any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?’

“When this was said, I said to the group of five monks (pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū): ‘Monks, do you recall me ever speaking like this before?’ ‘No, venerable sir.’ ‘Monks, the *Tathāgata* is an *Arhat*, a *Sammāsambuddha*. Lend ear, monks: the Deathless has been attained. I will instruct you. I will teach you the *Dhamma*.
Living in accordance with the instruction, before long, you will yourselves realize and attain to full understanding of the unsurpassed goal of the holy life, for which sons of good family rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness in this very life, having realized it with your own super-knowledge.

“I was able to convince the bhikkhus of the group of five. Then I sometimes instructed two *bhikkhus*, while the other three went for alms. The group of six subsisted on whatever the three *bhikkhus* brought them after walking for alms-food. Then, monks, I advised three *bhikkhus*, and two *bhikkhus* wandered for alms. The group of six subsisted on whatever the two *bhikkhus* brought back after going for alms.

“Then the *bhikkhus* of the group of five, thus taught and instructed by me, being themselves subject to birth, having understood the danger in what is subject to birth, seeking the unborn, unsurpassed security from bondage, *nirvāṇa*, attained the unborn, unsurpassed security from bondage, *nirvāṇa*; being themselves subject to aging, having understood the danger in what is subject to aging, seeking the unaging, unsurpassed security from bondage, *nirvāṇa*, attained the unaging, unsurpassed security from bondage, *nirvāṇa*; being themselves subject to sickness…pe… being themselves subject to death… being themselves subject to sorrow… being themselves subject to defilement, having understood the danger in what is subject to defilement, seeking the undefiled, unsurpassed security from bondage, *nirvāṇa*, attained the undefiled, unsurpassed security from bondage, *nirvāṇa*. Knowledge and vision arose in them: ‘Unshakable is our liberation; this is my last birth; now there is no renewal of being.’”
commentary_pali:
286.Saṇṭhapesunti katikaṃ akaṃsu. Bāhullikoti cīvarabāhullādīnaṃ atthāya paṭipanno. Padhānavibbhantoti padhānato vibbhanto bhaṭṭho parihīno. Āvatto bāhullāyāti cīvarādīnaṃ bahulabhāvatthāya āvatto. Apica kho āsanaṃ ṭhapetabbanti apica kho panassa uccakule nibbattassa āsanamattaṃ ṭhapetabbanti vadiṃsu. Nāsakkhiṃsūti buddhānubhāvena buddhatejasā abhibhūtā attano katikāya ṭhātuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Nāmena ca āvusovādena ca samudācarantīti gotamāti, āvusoti ca vadanti. Āvuso gotama, mayaṃ uruvelāyaṃ padhānakāle tuyhaṃ pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā vicarimhā, mukhodakaṃ dantakaṭṭhaṃ adamhā, vutthapariveṇaṃ sammajjimhā, pacchā ko te vattappaṭipattimakāsi, kacci amhesu pakkantesu na cintayitthāti evarūpiṃ kathaṃ kathentīti attho. Iriyāyāti dukkarairiyāya. Paṭipadāyāti dukkarapaṭipattiyā. Dukkarakārikāyāti pasatapasata-muggayūsādiāharakaraṇādinā dukkarakaraṇena. Abhijānātha me noti abhijānātha nu mama. Evarūpaṃ pabhāvitametanti etaṃ evarūpaṃ vākyabhedanti attho. Api nu ahaṃ uruvelāya padhāne tumhākaṃ saṅgaṇhanatthaṃ anukkaṇṭhanatthaṃ rattiṃ vā divā vā āgantvā, – ‘‘āvuso, mā vitakkayittha, mayhaṃ obhāso vā nimittaṃ vā paññāyatī’’ti evarūpaṃ kañci vacanabhedaṃ akāsinti adhippāyo. Te ekapadeneva satiṃ labhitvā uppannagāravā, ‘‘handa addhā esa buddho jāto’’ti saddahitvā no hetaṃ, bhanteti āhaṃsu. Asakkhiṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū saññāpetunti ahaṃ , bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū buddho ahanti jānāpetuṃ asakkhiṃ. Tadā pana bhagavā uposathadivaseyeva āgacchi. Attano buddhabhāvaṃ jānāpetvā koṇḍaññattheraṃ kāyasakkhiṃ katvā dhammacakkappavattanasuttaṃ kathesi. Suttapariyosāne thero aṭṭhārasahi brahmakoṭīhi saddhiṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāsi. Sūriye dharamāneyeva desanā niṭṭhāsi. Bhagavā tattheva vassaṃ upagacchi.

Dvepi sudaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ovadāmītiādi pāṭipadadivasato paṭṭhāya piṇḍapātatthāyapi gāmaṃ appavisanadīpanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tesañhi bhikkhūnaṃ kammaṭṭhānesu uppannamalavisodhanatthaṃ bhagavā antovihāreyeva ahosi. Uppanne uppanne kammaṭṭhānamale tepi bhikkhū bhagavato santikaṃ gantvā pucchanti. Bhagavāpi tesaṃ nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā malaṃ vinodeti. Atha nesaṃ bhagavatā evaṃ nīhaṭabhattena ovadiyamānānaṃ vappatthero pāṭipadadivase sotāpanno ahosi. Bhaddiyatthero dutiyāyaṃ, mahānāmatthero tatiyāyaṃ, assajitthero catutthiyaṃ. Pakkhassa pana pañcamiyaṃ sabbeva te ekato sannipātetvā anattalakkhaṇasuttaṃ kathesi, suttapariyosāne sabbepi arahattaphale patiṭṭhahiṃsu. Tenāha – ‘‘atha kho, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū mayā evaṃ ovadiyamānā…pe… anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ nibbānaṃ ajjhagamaṃsu…pe… natthi dāni punabbhavo’’ti. Ettakaṃ kathāmaggaṃ bhagavā yaṃ pubbe avaca – ‘‘tumhepi mamañceva pañcavaggiyānañca maggaṃ āruḷhā, ariyapariyesanā tumhākaṃ pariyesanā’’ti imaṃ ekameva anusandhiṃ dassento āhari.

Dvepi sudaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ovadāmī
commentary_english:
286. *Saṇṭhapesuṃ* means they made an agreement.

*Bāhulliko* means one who is engaged for the sake of an abundance of robes, etc.

*Padhānavibbhanto* means one who is ruined, fallen away, and declined from striving.

*Āvatto bāhullāya* means turned towards the abundance of robes, etc.

*Apica kho āsanaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ* means, moreover, they said that at least a seat should be prepared for him who was born in a high family.

*Nāsakkhiṃsū* means they were not able to stand by their agreement, being overcome by the Buddha's power and Buddha's glory.

*Nāmena ca āvusovādena ca samudācarantī* means they say "Gotama" and "Āvuso."

"Friend Gotama, we wandered in Uruvelā during the time of striving, taking your bowl and robe, we gave you water for your mouth and a toothbrush, we swept the dwelling place, afterwards who attended to your duties, didn't you think about us when we had left?" This is the meaning of how they were speaking.

*Iriyāyā* means by difficult conduct.

*Paṭipadāyā* means by difficult practice.

*Dukkarakārikāyā* means by doing difficult things, such as preparing food consisting of flour-water, bean-soup, etc.

*Abhijānātha me no* means do you recognize me?

*Evarūpaṃ pabhāvitametaṃ* means this is such a distinction of speech.

The meaning is: "Did I, coming to Uruvelā during the striving, at night or during the day, for the purpose of helping you, for the purpose of not cutting you off, say any such distinction of speech, saying, 'Friends, do not be anxious, an aura or an omen appears to me'?"

Having gained mindfulness with just one word, and with respect arisen, believing "Indeed, this is the Buddha who has arisen," they said, *No hetaṃ, bhante*.

*Asakkhiṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcavaggiye bhikkhū saññāpetuṃ* means, monks, I was able to make the group of five monks know that I am the Buddha.

Then the Blessed One came on the Uposatha day itself.

Having made known his Buddhahood, having made Koṇḍañña Thera a witness of the body, he spoke the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta.

At the end of the Sutta, the Thera was established in the fruit of stream-entry together with eighteen Brahma-koṭīs.

The teaching ended just as the sun was setting.

The Blessed One spent the rainy season right there.

*Dvepi sudaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ovadāmītiādi* was said to indicate that they did not even enter the village for alms starting from the first day of the lunar fortnight.

For the Blessed One stayed right there in the inner monastery in order to purify the impurities that had arisen in the meditation subjects of those monks.

Whenever impurities arose in their meditation subjects, those monks would go to the Blessed One and ask.

The Blessed One would also go to their sitting place and dispel the impurity.

Then, while they were being instructed by the Blessed One, who removed the impurities in this way, Vappa Thera became a stream-enterer on the first day of the lunar fortnight.

Bhaddiya Thera on the second, Mahānāma Thera on the third, Assaji Thera on the fourth.

Then, on the fifth day of the lunar fortnight, having gathered them all together, he spoke the Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta, at the end of the Sutta, they were all established in the fruit of arahantship.

Therefore he said: "Then, monks, the group of five monks, being thus instructed by me...pe...attained the unsurpassed security from bondage, Nibbāna...pe...now there is no more renewed existence."

The Blessed One brought forth this much of the path of talk which he had said previously - "You too have ascended the path of me and the group of five, the noble search is your search," showing this one connection.

*Dvepi sudaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ovadāmī*

mula_pali:
287. ‘‘Pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāmaguṇā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ime pañca kāmaguṇe gathitā mucchitā ajjhopannā anādīnavadassāvino anissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti, te evamassu veditabbā – ‘anayamāpannā byasanamāpannā yathākāmakaraṇīyā pāpimato’ pāpimato’’ti (?). ‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āraññako mago baddho pāsarāsiṃ adhisayeyya. So evamassa veditabbo – anayamāpanno byasanamāpanno yathākāmakaraṇīyo luddassa. Āgacchante ca pana ludde yena kāmaṃ na pakkamissatī’ti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ime pañca kāmaguṇe gathitā mucchitā ajjhopannā anādīnavadassāvino anissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti, te evamassu veditabbā – ‘anayamāpannā byasanamāpannā yathākāmakaraṇīyā pāpimato’. Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ime pañca kāmaguṇe agathitā amucchitā anajjhopannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti, te evamassu veditabbā – ‘na anayamāpannā na byasanamāpannā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā pāpimato’.

‘‘Seyyathāpi , bhikkhave, āraññako mago abaddho pāsarāsiṃ adhisayeyya. So evamassa veditabbo – ‘na anayamāpanno na byasanamāpanno na yathākāmakaraṇīyo luddassa. Āgacchante ca pana ludde yena kāmaṃ pakkamissatī’ti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ime pañca kāmaguṇe agathitā amucchitā anajjhopannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjanti, te evamassu veditabbā – ‘na anayamāpannā na byasanamāpannā na yathākāmakaraṇīyā pāpimato’.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āraññako mago araññe pavane caramāno vissattho gacchati, vissattho tiṭṭhati, vissattho nisīdati, vissattho seyyaṃ kappeti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anāpāthagato, bhikkhave, luddassa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu andhamakāsi māraṃ apadaṃ, vadhitvā māracakkhuṃ adassanaṃ gato pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati, sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave…pe… pāpimato.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu andhamakāsi māraṃ apadaṃ, vadhitvā māracakkhuṃ adassanaṃ gato pāpimato. Tiṇṇo loke visattikaṃ vissattho gacchati, vissattho tiṭṭhati, vissattho nisīdati, vissattho seyyaṃ kappeti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Anāpāthagato, bhikkhave, pāpimato’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Pāsarāsisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
287. “There are these five cords of sensual pleasure, monks.

Which five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual pleasure, tantalizing; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … tactile objects cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual pleasure, tantalizing.

These, monks, are the five cords of sensual pleasure.

As to those recluses and brahmins who are tied to these five cords of sensual pleasure, infatuated with them and utterly committed to them, and who use them without seeing the danger in them or understanding the escape from them, it may be understood of them: ‘They have met with calamity, met with disaster, the Evil One may do with them as he likes.’

Suppose a forest deer who was bound lay down on a heap of snares;

it might be understood of him: ‘He has met with calamity, met with disaster, the hunter can do with him as he likes.

and when the hunter comes he cannot go where he wants.’

So too, as to those recluses and brahmins who are tied to these five cords of sensual pleasure…it may be understood of them: ‘They have met with calamity, met with disaster, the Evil One may do with them as he likes.’

As to those recluses and brahmins who are not tied to these five cords of sensual pleasure, who are not infatuated with them or utterly committed to them, and who use them seeing the danger in them and understanding the escape from them, it may be understood of them: ‘They have not met with calamity, not met with disaster, the Evil One cannot do with them as he likes.

Suppose a forest deer who was unbound lay down on a heap of snares;

it might be understood of him: ‘He has not met with calamity, not met with disaster, the hunter cannot do with him as he likes,

and when the hunter comes he can depart as he desires.’

So too, as to those recluses and brahmins who are not tied to these five cords of sensual pleasure…it may be understood of them: ‘They have not met with calamity, not met with disaster, the Evil One cannot do with them as he likes.’

Suppose a forest deer is wandering in the forest wilds: he walks confidently, stands confidently, sits confidently, lies down confidently.

What is the reason? He is out of the hunter's range.

So too, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.

This *bhikkhu* is said to have blindfolded Māra, to have become invisible to the Evil One by depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.

Again, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration.

This *bhikkhu* is said to have blindfolded Mara…

Again, with the fading away as well of rapture, a *bhikkhu* abides in equanimity, and mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, he enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*, on account of which noble ones announce: ‘He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.’

This *bhikkhu* is said to have blindfolded Mara…

Again, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.

This *bhikkhu* is said to have blindfolded Mara…

Again, by completely surmounting all perception of matter, with the disappearance of perceptions of sense-reaction, and by giving no attention to diversity-perceptions, one becomes aware of, attains to, and abides in the sphere of infinite space.

This *bhikkhu* is said to have blindfolded Mara…

Again, by completely surmounting the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness.

This *bhikkhu* is said to have blindfolded Mara…
“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness, thinking, ‘there is nothing at all’ (*natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati*).
This, bhikkhus, is said to…pe…of the Evil One.

“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by completely surmounting the base of nothingness, enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati*).
This, bhikkhus, is said to…pe…of the Evil One.

“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by completely surmounting the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati*), and his taints are destroyed by seeing with wisdom (*paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti*).
This bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to have blindfolded Māra, to have become invisible to the Evil One by depriving Māra’s eye of its opportunity.
He walks confidently, stands confidently, sits confidently, lies down confidently, having crossed beyond attachment to the world (*tiṇṇo loke visattikaṃ vissattho gacchati, vissattho tiṭṭhati, vissattho nisīdati, vissattho seyyaṃ kappeti*).
Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, he is out of the Evil One’s reach.”

This is what the Blessed One said.
Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement (*attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti*).

The Pāsarāsi Sutta, the sixth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
287. Idāni yasmā na agāriyānaṃyeva pañcakāmaguṇapariyesanā hoti, anagāriyānampi cattāro paccaye appaccavekkhitvā paribhuñjantānaṃ pañcakāmaguṇavasena anariyapariyesanā hoti, tasmā taṃ dassetuṃ pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇātiādimāha. Tattha navarattesu pattacīvarādīsu cakkhuviññeyyā rūpātiādayo cattāro kāmaguṇā labbhanti. Raso panettha paribhogaraso hoti. Manuññe piṇḍapāte bhesajje ca pañcapi labbhanti. Senāsanamhi cīvare viya cattāro. Raso pana etthāpi paribhogarasova. Ye hi keci, bhikkhaveti kasmā ārabhi? Evaṃ pañca kāmaguṇe dassetvā idāni ye evaṃ vadeyyuṃ, ‘‘pabbajitakālato paṭṭhāya anariyapariyesanā nāma kuto, ariyapariyesanāva pabbajitāna’’nti, tesaṃ paṭisedhanatthāya ‘‘pabbajitānampi catūsu paccayesu appaccavekkhaṇaparibhogo anariyapariyesanā evā’’ti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha gadhitāti taṇhāgedhena gadhitā. Mucchitāti taṇhāmucchāya mucchitā . Ajjhopannāti taṇhāya ajjhogāḷhā. Anādīnavadassāvinoti ādīnavaṃ apassantā. Anissaraṇapaññāti nissaraṇaṃ vuccati paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ. Te tena virahitā.

Idāni tassatthassa sādhakaṃ upamaṃ dassento seyyathāpi, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tatrevaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ veditabbaṃ – āraññakamago viya hi samaṇabrāhmaṇā, luddakena araññe ṭhapitapāso viya cattāro paccayā, tassa luddassa pāsarāsiṃ ajjhottharitvā sayanakālo viya tesaṃ cattāro paccaye appaccavekkhitvā paribhogakālo. Luddake āgacchante magassa yena kāmaṃ agamanakālo viya samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ mārassa yathākāmakaraṇīyakālo, māravasaṃ upagatabhāvoti attho. Magassa pana abaddhassa pāsarāsiṃ adhisayitakālo viya samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ catūsu paccayesu paccavekkhaṇaparibhogo, luddake āgacchante magassa yena kāmaṃ gamanaṃ viya samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ māravasaṃ anupagamanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Vissatthoti nibbhayo nirāsaṅko. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

seyyathāpi, bhikkhave Vissattho

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Pāsarāsisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Ariyapariyesanātipi etasseva nāmaṃ.
commentary_english:
Now, because not only householders seek the five sensual pleasures (*pañcakāmaguṇa*), but also renunciates, when enjoying the four requisites without reflection, [engage in] ignoble seeking through the five sensual qualities; therefore, to show that, he said, "These are the five sensual qualities, *bhikkhus*," and so forth.

Therein, in the nine kinds of robes, bowls, and so on, four sensual qualities (*kāmaguṇa*) are obtained, namely, forms cognizable by eye-consciousness (*cakkhuviññeyyā rūpātiādayo*).

Here, taste is the taste of enjoyment (*paribhogarasa*).

In agreeable alms food (*piṇḍapāta*) and medicine, all five are obtained.

In lodging (*senāsana*), as with robes, there are four.

But here too, taste is the taste of enjoyment (*paribhogarasa*).

" *Ye hi keci, bhikkhave* (Those who, *bhikkhus*)"—why did he begin? Having shown the five sensual qualities (*pañca kāmaguṇe*), now, lest some should say, "From the time of renunciation, whence comes ignoble seeking? For renunciates, there is only noble seeking," to prevent that, he began this discourse to show that "Even for renunciates, enjoying the four requisites without reflection is ignoble seeking."

There, *gadhitā* (attached) means attached with the attachment of craving (*taṇhāgedhena gadhitā*).

*Mucchitā* (deluded) means deluded by the delusion of craving (*taṇhāmucchāya mucchitā*).

*Ajjhopannā* (bound) means overwhelmed by craving (*taṇhāya ajjhogāḷhā*).

*Anādīnavadassāvino* (not seeing the danger) means not seeing the danger (*ādīnavaṃ apassantā*).

*Anissaraṇapaññā* (lacking the wisdom of escape) means escape is called reflective knowledge (*paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ*).

They are devoid of that.

Now, showing an analogy to establish that meaning, he said, "Just as, *bhikkhus*," and so forth.

Here, the connection of the analogy should be understood thus: the wandering deer are like *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*; the four requisites are like the snare set in the forest by the hunter; enjoying the four requisites without reflection is like their time for lying down, having covered the heap of snares of that hunter.

The time when the hunter comes, and the deer cannot go anywhere it pleases, is like the time when Māra can do as he pleases with the *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*, their state of having come under the power of Māra—this is the meaning.

But the time when the un-snared deer lies down covering the heap of snares is like the *śramaṇas'* and *brāhmaṇas'* reflective enjoyment of the four requisites; the deer's going anywhere it pleases when the hunter comes is like the *śramaṇas'* and *brāhmaṇas'* not coming under the power of Māra.

*Vissattho* (trustful) means fearless (*nibbhayo*) and without apprehension (*nirāsaṅko*).

The rest is clear everywhere.

Just as, *bhikkhus*, trustful.

The commentary on the *Pāsarāsi Sutta* is finished.

Even noble seeking is its name.

mula_pali:
288. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathena vaḷabhīrathena (sī. pī.) sāvatthiyā niyyāti divādivassa. Addasā kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo pilotikaṃ paribbājakaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna pilotikaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Handa, kuto nu bhavaṃ vacchāyano āgacchati divādivassā’’ti?

‘‘Ito hi kho ahaṃ , bho, āgacchāmi samaṇassa gotamassa santikā’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññati, bhavaṃ vacchāyano, samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ?

‘‘Paṇḍito maññe’’ti.

‘‘Ko cāhaṃ, bho, ko ca samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmi! Sopi nūnassa tādisova yo samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jāneyyā’’ti.

‘‘Uḷārāya khalu bhavaṃ vacchāyano samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsāya pasaṃsatī’’ti.

‘‘Ko cāhaṃ, bho, ko ca samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsissāmi?

‘‘Pasatthapasatthova so bhavaṃ gotamo seṭṭho devamanussāna’’nti.

‘‘Kaṃ pana bhavaṃ vacchāyano atthavasaṃ sampassamāno samaṇe gotame evaṃ abhippasanno’’ti abhippasanno hotīti (syā.)?

abhippasanno hotīti (syā.)

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bho, kusalo nāgavaniko nāgavanaṃ paviseyya. So passeyya nāgavane mahantaṃ hatthipadaṃ, dīghato ca āyataṃ, tiriyañca vitthataṃ. So niṭṭhaṃ gaccheyya – ‘mahā vata, bho, nāgo’ti. Evameva kho ahaṃ, bho, yato addasaṃ samaṇe gotame cattāri padāni athāhaṃ niṭṭhamagamaṃ – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
288. Thus have I heard: On one occasion the Blessed One (Bhagavā) was living near Śrāvastī (Sāvatthiyaṃ) in Jeta's Grove (Jetavana), Anāthapindika's Park (Anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

Now on that occasion, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi was driving out of Śrāvastī in the middle of the day in an all-white chariot (sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathena).

The brahmin Jāṇussoṇi saw the wanderer Pilotika coming in the distance. Seeing the wanderer Pilotika, he said this:

“Friend Vacchāyana, from where are you coming in the middle of the day?”

“Sir (bho), I am coming from the presence of the ascetic Gotama (samaṇassa gotamassa santikā).”

“What does Master Vacchāyana think of the recluse Gotama’s lucidity of wisdom (paññāveyyattiyaṃ)?”

“I think [he is] wise (paṇḍito maññe).”

“Who am I, sir (bho), and who is [able to understand] the recluse Gotama’s lucidity of wisdom (paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmi)! That sort of person would be needed to understand the recluse Gotama’s lucidity of wisdom (paññāveyyattiyaṃ jāneyyā)!”

“Master Vacchāyana praises the ascetic Gotama with lofty praise (uḷārāya khalu bhavaṃ vacchāyano samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsāya pasaṃsatī)!”

“Who am I, sir (bho), to praise the ascetic Gotama (samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsissāmi)?"

“Indeed, the esteemed Gotama (bhavaṃ gotamo) is the best (seṭṭho) among gods and humans (devamanussāna)!”

“But, Master Vacchāyana, seeing what advantage are you so convinced about the ascetic Gotama (samaṇe gotame evaṃ abhippasanno)?”

“Just as, sir (bho), a skilled elephant tracker (kusalo nāgavaniko) might enter an elephant wood (nāgavanaṃ paviseyya), and might see in the elephant wood (nāgavane) a big elephant’s footprint (mahantaṃ hatthipadaṃ), long in extent (dīghato ca āyataṃ) and broad across (tiriyañca vitthataṃ). He would come to the conclusion: ‘Indeed (vata), this is a big bull elephant (mahā nāgo).’

“In the same way (evameva kho ahaṃ), sir (bho), when I saw four footprints (cattāri padāni) of the ascetic Gotama (samaṇe gotame), then I came to the conclusion (niṭṭhamagamaṃ): ‘The Blessed One (bhagavā) is a Fully Enlightened One (sammāsambuddho), the Dharma (dhammo) is well proclaimed by the Blessed One (svākkhāto bhagavatā), the Saṅgha (saṅgho) of the Blessed One’s disciples is practising the good way (suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho).’”
commentary_pali:
288.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷahatthipadopamasuttaṃ. Tattha sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathenāti, ‘‘setā sudaṃ assā yuttā honti setālaṅkārā. Seto ratho setālaṅkāro setaparivāro, setā rasmiyo, setā patodalaṭṭhi, setaṃ chattaṃ, setaṃ uṇhīsaṃ, setāni vatthāni, setā upāhanā, setāya sudaṃ vālabījaniyā bījiyatī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.4) evaṃ vuttena sakalasetena catūhi vaḷavāhi yuttarathena.

Ratho ca nāmeso duvidho hoti – yodharatho, alaṅkārarathoti. Tattha yodharatho caturassasaṇṭhāno hoti nātimahā, dvinnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vā janānaṃ gahaṇasamattho. Alaṅkāraratho mahā hoti, dīghato dīgho, puthulato puthulo. Tattha chattaggāhako vālabījaniggāhako tālavaṇṭaggāhakoti evaṃ aṭṭha vā dasa vā sukhena ṭhātuṃ vā nisīdituṃ vā nipajjituṃ vā sakkonti, ayampi alaṅkārarathoyeva. So sabbo sacakkapañjarakubbaro rajataparikkhitto ahosi. Vaḷavā pakatiyā setavaṇṇāva. Pasādhanampi tādisaṃ rajatamayaṃ ahosi. Rasmiyopi rajatapanāḷi suparikkhittā. Patodalaṭṭhipi rajataparikkhittā. Brāhmaṇopi setavatthaṃ nivāsetvā setaṃyeva uttarāsaṅgamakāsi, setavilepanaṃ vilimpi, setamālaṃ pilandhi, dasasu aṅgulīsu aṅgulimuddikā, kaṇṇesu kuṇḍalānīti evamādialaṅkāropissa rajatamayova ahosi. Parivārabrāhmaṇāpissa dasasahassamattā tatheva setavatthavilepanamālālaṅkārā ahesuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathenā’’ti.

Sāvatthiyā niyyātīti so kira channaṃ channaṃ māsānaṃ ekavāraṃ nagaraṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karoti. Ito ettakehi divasehi nagaraṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karissatīti puretarameva ghosanā karīyati; taṃ sutvā ye nagarato na pakkantā, te na pakkamanti. Ye pakkantā, tepi, ‘‘puññavato sirisampattiṃ passissāmā’’ti āgacchanti. Yaṃ divasaṃ brāhmaṇo nagaraṃ anuvicarati, tadā pātova nagaravīthiyo sammajjitvā vālikaṃ okiritvā lājapañcamehi pupphehi abhippakiritvā puṇṇaghaṭe ṭhapetvā kadaliyo ca dhaje ca ussāpetvā sakalanagaraṃ dhūpitavāsitaṃ karonti. Brāhmaṇo pātova sīsaṃ nhāyitvā purebhattaṃ bhuñjitvā vuttanayeneva setavatthādīhi attānaṃ alaṅkaritvā pāsādā oruyha rathaṃ abhiruhati. Atha naṃ te brāhmaṇā sabbasetavatthavilepanamālālaṅkārā setacchattāni gahetvā parivārenti; tato mahājanassa sannipātanatthaṃ paṭhamaṃyeva taruṇadārakānaṃ phalāphalāni vikiritvā tadanantaraṃ māsakarūpāni; tadanantaraṃ kahāpaṇe vikiranti; mahājanā sannipatanti. Ukkuṭṭhiyo ceva celukkhepā ca pavattanti. Atha brāhmaṇo maṅgalikasovatthikādīsu maṅgalāni ceva suvatthiyo ca karontesu mahāsampattiyā nagaraṃ anuvicarati. Puññavantā manussā ekabhūmakādipāsāde āruyha sukapattasadisāni vātapānakavāṭāni vivaritvā olokenti. Brāhmaṇopi attano yasasirisampattiyā nagaraṃ ajjhottharanto viya dakkhiṇadvārābhimukho hoti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘sāvatthiyā niyyātī’’ti.

Sāvatthiyā niyyātī

Divā divassāti divasassa divā, majjhanhakāleti attho. Pilotikaṃ paribbājakanti pilotikāti evaṃ itthiliṅgavohāravasena laddhanāmaṃ paribbājakaṃ. So kira paribbājako daharo paṭhamavaye ṭhito suvaṇṇavaṇṇo buddhupaṭṭhāko, pātova tathāgatassa ceva mahātherānañca upaṭṭhānaṃ katvā tidaṇḍakuṇḍikādiparikkhāraṃ ādāya jetavanā nikkhamitvā nagarābhimukho pāyāsi. Taṃ esa dūratova āgacchantaṃ addasa. Etadavocāti anukkamena santikaṃ āgataṃ sañjānitvā etaṃ, ‘‘handa kuto nu bhavaṃ vacchāyano āgacchatī’’ti gottaṃ kittento vacanaṃ avoca. Paṇḍito maññeti bhavaṃ vacchāyano samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ paṇḍitoti maññati, udāhu noti ayamettha attho.

Divā divassā Pilotikaṃ paribbājaka pilotikā Etadavocā Paṇḍito maññe

Ko cāhaṃ, bhoti, bho, samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānane ahaṃ ko nāma? Ko ca samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmīti kuto cāhaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmi, kena kāraṇena jānissāmīti? Evaṃ sabbathāpi attano ajānanabhāvaṃ dīpeti . Sopi nūnassa tādisovāti yo samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jāneyya, sopi nūna dasa pāramiyo pūretvā sabbaññutaṃ patto tādiso buddhoyeva bhaveyya. Sineruṃ vā himavantaṃ vā pathaviṃ vā ākāsaṃ vā pametukāmena tappamāṇova daṇḍo vā rajju vā laddhuṃ vaṭṭati. Samaṇassa gotamassa paññaṃ jānantenapi tassa ñāṇasadisameva sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Ādaravasena panettha āmeḍitaṃ kataṃ. Uḷārāyāti uttarāya seṭṭhāya. Ko cāhaṃ, bhoti, bho, ahaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa pasaṃsane ko nāma? Ko ca samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsissāmīti kena kāraṇena pasaṃsissāmi? Pasatthapasatthoti sabbaguṇānaṃ uttaritarehi sabbalokapasatthehi attano guṇeheva pasattho, na tassa aññehi pasaṃsanakiccaṃ atthi. Yathā hi campakapupphaṃ vā nīluppalaṃ vā padumaṃ vā lohitacandanaṃ vā attano vaṇṇagandhasiriyāva pāsādikañceva sugandhañca, na tassa āgantukehi vaṇṇagandhehi thomanakiccaṃ atthi. Yathā ca maṇiratanaṃ vā candamaṇḍalaṃ vā attano ālokeneva obhāsati, na tassa aññena obhāsanakiccaṃ atthi. Evaṃ samaṇo gotamo sabbalokapasatthehi attano guṇeheva pasattho thomito sabbalokassa seṭṭhataṃ pāpito, na tassa aññena pasaṃsanakiccaṃ atthi. Pasatthehi vā pasatthotipi pasatthapasattho.

Ko cāhaṃ, bho Ko ca samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmī Sopi nūnassa tādisovā Uḷārāyā Ko cāhaṃ, bho Ko ca samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsissāmī Pasatthapasattho

Ke pasatthā nāma? Rājā pasenadi kosalo kāsikosalavāsikehi pasattho, bimbisāro aṅgamagadhavāsīhi. Vesālikā licchavī vajjiraṭṭhavāsīhi pasatthā. Pāveyyakā mallā, kosinārakā mallā, aññepi te te khattiyā tehi tehi jānapadehi pasatthā. Caṅkīādayo brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇagaṇehi, anāthapiṇḍikādayo upāsakā anekasatehi upāsakagaṇehi, visākhādayo upāsikā anekasatāhi upāsikāhi, sakuludāyiādayo paribbājakā anekehi paribbājakasatehi, uppalavaṇṇātheriādikā mahāsāvikā anekehi bhikkhunisatehi, sāriputtattherādayo mahāsāvakā anekasatehi bhikkhūhi, sakkādayo devā anekasahassehi devehi, mahābrahmādayo brahmāno anekasahassehi brahmehi pasatthā. Te sabbepi dasabalaṃ thomenti vaṇṇenti, pasaṃsantīti bhagavā ‘‘pasatthapasattho’’ti vuccati.

Atthavasanti atthānisaṃsaṃ. Athassa paribbājako attano pasādakāraṇaṃ ācikkhanto seyyathāpi, bho, kusalo nāgavanikotiādimāha. Tattha nāgavanikoti nāgavanavāsiko anuggahitasippo puriso. Parato pana uggahitasippo puriso nāgavanikoti āgato. Cattāri padānīti cattāri ñāṇapadāni ñāṇavalañjāni, ñāṇena akkantaṭṭhānānīti attho.

Atthavasa seyyathāpi, bho, kusalo nāgavaniko nāgavaniko Cattāri padānī
commentary_english:
288. Thus, "me suta" is the Cūḷahatthipadopamasuttaṃ.

There, "sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathenā" means, "Indeed, white horses are yoked [to the chariot], they have white ornaments. The chariot is white, its ornaments are white, its retinue is white, the reins are white, the whip is white, the parasol is white, the turban is white, the clothes are white, the shoes are white, and indeed, it is fanned by a white fan." Thus it was said, [the chariot was] equipped with four white mares, entirely white.

The chariot is twofold: a war chariot (yodharatho) and an ornamented chariot (alaṅkārarathoti). There, the war chariot is square-shaped and not very large, capable of holding two or three people. The ornamented chariot is large, long, and wide. There, umbrella holders, fan holders, and palm-leaf fan holders, eight or ten people, can easily stand, sit, or lie down. This too is an ornamented chariot. It is all silver-plated, including the wheels, the frame, and the yoke. The mares are naturally white. The decorations are also silver. The reins are also well-covered with silver tubes. The whip is also covered with silver. The *brāhmaṇa* also dressed in white clothes, put on a white upper garment, smeared himself with white unguent, wore a white garland, finger rings on ten fingers, earrings on his ears, so his ornaments were all silver. The retinue of *brāhmaṇas*, about ten thousand, were likewise adorned with white clothes, unguents, garlands, and ornaments. Thus it was said, "sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathenā".

"sāvatthiyā niyyātī" means that he circles the city once every six months. The announcement is made well in advance that "the city will be circled in so many days"; those who have not left the city, having heard that, do not leave. Those who have left come back, thinking, "We will see the prosperity of the meritorious one." On the day the *brāhmaṇa* goes around the city, early in the morning, they sweep the city streets, scatter sand, scatter flowers with fried grains, spread [them] around, place filled water pots, raise banana trees and flags, and perfume the entire city with incense. The *brāhmaṇa*, early in the morning, takes a bath, eats a pre-noon meal, dresses himself in white clothes and so on, descends from the palace, and mounts the chariot. Then those *brāhmaṇas*, adorned with all white clothes, unguents, garlands, take white parasols and surround him; then, for the purpose of gathering the multitude, first they scatter fruits and unripe fruits for the young children, then they scatter *māsakas*; then they scatter *kahāpaṇas*; the masses gather. Shouts and waving of clothes arise. Then, the *brāhmaṇa* goes around the city with great prosperity, with auspicious [things] such as *maṅgalikas* and *sovatthikas*. The meritorious people, having ascended to palaces with one or more stories, open the windows that are like parrot wings and look. The *brāhmaṇa*, as if covering the city with his fame, glory, and prosperity, faces the southern gate. Thus it was said, "sāvatthiyā niyyātī".
"""*Divā divassā* means *divā* of *divasa*, meaning in the middle of the day."
"*Pilotikaṃ paribbājaka* means *pilotikā* as the name of a wandering ascetic [ *paribbājaka* ] acquired through usage of the feminine gender."
"That *paribbājaka*, a young man, staying in his early years, of golden complexion, a Buddhist attendant, having performed the service to the Tathāgata and also to the great elders in the morning, taking the requisites such as the triple staff and water pot, having left Jetavana, he went towards the city."
"He saw him coming from afar."
"*Etadavocā* means having understood that he had come near in succession, he said this, ""Well, from where are you coming, Master Vacchāyana?"" mentioning the clan, he spoke the word."
""*Paṇḍito maññe* means Master Vacchāyana thinks of the *śramaṇa* Gotama as wise, or not, this is the meaning here."
"*Ko cāhaṃ, bho* means, sir, who am I to know the lucidity of wisdom of the *śramaṇa* Gotama? *Ko ca samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmī* means from where will I know the lucidity of wisdom of the *śramaṇa* Gotama, by what reason will I know?"" Thus in every way he indicates his state of not knowing."

"*Sopi nūnassa tādisovā* means whoever would know the lucidity of wisdom of the *śramaṇa* Gotama, he too, having fulfilled the ten perfections, having attained omniscience, would be such a Buddha indeed."
"Just as one desiring to measure Mount Meru, or the Himalayas, or the earth, or the sky is wearied, so also [with] a staff or rope, it is fitting to obtain."
"It indicates that even one knowing the wisdom of the *śramaṇa* Gotama, it is fitting to obtain the omniscience-knowledge itself, similar to his knowledge."
"Here, it has been repeated out of respect."
""*Uḷārāyā* means to the superior, to the best."
""*Ko cāhaṃ, bho* means, sir, who am I to praise the *śramaṇa* Gotama? *Ko ca samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsissāmī* means by what reason will I praise? *Pasatthapasattho* means he is praised by his own qualities, which are more excellent than all qualities, praised by the whole world, there is no need for him to be praised by others."
"Just as the *campaka* flower, or the blue lotus, or the lotus, or the red sandalwood is lovely and fragrant by its own color, smell, and splendor, there is no need for it to be praised by adventitious colors and smells."
"And just as a jewel-gem, or the orb of the moon, shines by its own light, there is no need for it to be illuminated by another."
"Thus the *śramaṇa* Gotama, praised by his own qualities, praised by all the world, brought to the best of all the world, there is no need for him to be praised by another."
"He is praised or he is praiseworthy, therefore he is greatly praised."

"*Ko cāhaṃ, bho* *Ko ca samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmī*"
"*Sopi nūnassa tādisovā*"
"*Uḷārāyā* *Ko cāhaṃ, bho* *Ko ca samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsissāmī* *Pasatthapasattho*"
"Who are the praised ones by name? King Pasenadi Kosala is praised by the inhabitants of Kāsi-Kosala, Bimbisāra is praised by the inhabitants of Aṅga-Magadha."
"The Licchavis of Vesāli are praised by the inhabitants of Vajjiraṭṭha."
"The Mallas of Pāveyyaka, the Mallas of Kosināraka, and also those other Kṣatriyas are praised by those inhabitants of those countries."
"Caṅkī and others, the Brahmins, [are praised] by the Brahmin assemblies, Anāthapiṇḍika and others, the laymen, [are praised] by the laymen assemblies with hundreds of members, Visākhā and others, the laywomen, [are praised] by the laywomen with hundreds of members, Sakuludāyin and others, the wandering ascetics, [are praised] by the wandering ascetics with hundreds of members, Uppalavaṇṇātherī and others, the great female disciples, [are praised] by the nuns with hundreds of members, Sāriputtatthera and others, the great disciples, [are praised] by the monks with hundreds of members, Sakka and others, the gods, [are praised] by the gods with thousands of members, Mahābrahmā and others, the Brahmās, [are praised] by the Brahmās with thousands of members."
"All of them praise, extol, and commend the One with the Ten Powers, therefore the Blessed One is called ""greatly praised."""

""*Atthavasa* means advantage of meaning."
"Then the wandering ascetic, while relating the cause of his faith, said this: *Seyyathāpi, bho, kusalo nāgavaniko* and so on."
"There, *nāgavaniko* means a man living in Nāgavana who has taken up a craft."
"But afterwards, a man who has taken up a craft is said to have come to Nāgavanikoti."
""*Cattāri padānī* means four knowledge-steps, knowledge-footprints, meanings places crossed by knowledge."
"*Atthavasa* *Seyyathāpi, bho, kusalo nāgavaniko* *Nāgavaniko* *Cattāri padānī*"

mula_pali:
289. ‘‘Katamāni cattāri? Idhāhaṃ, bho, passāmi ekacce khattiyapaṇḍite nipuṇe kataparappavāde vālavedhirūpe, te bhindantā vobhindantā (sī. pī.) vi + ava + bhindantā maññe caranti paññāgatena diṭṭhigatāni. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osarissatī’ti. Te pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharonti – ‘imaṃ mayaṃ pañhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma. Evaṃ ce no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evamassa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāma. Evaṃ cepi no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evampissa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāmā’ti. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osaṭo’ti. Te yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkamanti. Te samaṇo gotamo dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te samaṇena gotamena dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā na ceva samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, kutossa kutassa (sī. syā. pī.) vādaṃ āropessanti? Aññadatthu samaṇasseva gotamassa sāvakā sampajjanti.
