326. ‘‘Kacci vo, anuruddhā, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci piṇḍakena na kilamathā’’ti ? ‘‘Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ, bhagavā; na ca mayaṃ, bhante, piṇḍakena kilamāmā’’ti. ‘‘Kacci pana vo, anuruddhā, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharathā’’ti? ‘‘Taggha mayaṃ , bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharāmā’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, anuruddhā, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharathā’’ti? ‘‘Idha mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yohaṃ evarūpehi sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṃ viharāmī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vatteyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vattāmi. Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā ekañca pana maññe citta’’nti.

Āyasmāpi kho nandiyo…pe… āyasmāpi kho kimilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mayhampi, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yohaṃ evarūpehi sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṃ viharāmī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca, mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca, mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vatteyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vattāmi. Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā ekañca pana maññe cittanti.

‘‘Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharāmā’’ti.
mula_english:
326. "Are you all keeping well, Anuruddhas? Are you comfortable? Are you not finding it difficult to get alms food?"
"We are keeping well, Blessed One. We are comfortable, Blessed One, and we are not having any trouble getting alms food."

“And how are you living, Anuruddhas? Are you living harmoniously, cordially, without dispute, blending like milk and water, looking at one another with eyes of affection?”
“Indeed, venerable sir, we are living harmoniously, cordially, without dispute, blending like milk and water, looking at one another with eyes of affection.”

“But how is it that you live in such harmony, Anuruddhas, with appreciation, without quarreling, blended like milk and water, regarding each other with loving eyes?”
“Here, venerable sir, it occurs to me: ‘It is a gain for me, a great gain for me, that I live together with such companions in the holy life.’
I maintain bodily acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-kāyakarma*) towards these venerable ones both openly and privately; I maintain verbal acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-vacīkarma*) towards them both openly and privately; I maintain mental acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-manokarma*) towards them both openly and privately.
The thought occurs to me: ‘Why don’t I, having put aside my own thoughts ( *sva-citta*), conduct myself in line with the thoughts of these venerable ones?’
And having put aside my own thoughts ( *sva-citta*), I do conduct myself in line with the thoughts of these venerable ones.
We are indeed different in body (*nānā hi kāyā*), venerable sir, but I consider us to be one in mind (*ekaṃ citta*)."

The venerable Nandiya…pe… the venerable Kimbila said this to the Blessed One: "It also occurs to me: ‘It is a gain for me, a great gain for me, that I live together with such companions in the holy life.’
I maintain bodily acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-kāyakarma*) towards these venerable ones both openly and privately; I maintain verbal acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-vacīkarma*) towards them both openly and privately; I maintain mental acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-manokarma*) towards them both openly and privately.
The thought occurs to me: ‘Why don’t I, having put aside my own thoughts ( *sva-citta*), conduct myself in line with the thoughts of these venerable ones?’
And having put aside my own thoughts ( *sva-citta*), I do conduct myself in line with the thoughts of these venerable ones.
We are indeed different in body (*nānā hi kāyā*), venerable sir, but I consider us to be one in mind (*ekaṃ citta*)."

“That is how, venerable sir, we are living harmoniously, cordially, without dispute, blending like milk and water, looking at one another with eyes of affection.”
commentary_pali:
326. Tassa saṅgahe kate sesānaṃ katova hotīti theraññeva etaṃ kacci vo anuruddhātiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tattha kaccīti pucchanatthe nipāto. Voti sāmivacanaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – kacci anuruddhā tumhākaṃ khamanīyaṃ, iriyāpatho vo khamati? Kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci vo jīvitaṃ yāpeti ghaṭiyati? Kacci piṇḍakena na kilamatha, kacci tumhākaṃ sulabhapiṇḍaṃ, sampatte vo disvā manussā uḷuṅkayāguṃ vā kaṭacchubhikkhaṃ vā dātabbaṃ maññantīti bhikkhācāravattaṃ pucchati. Kasmā? Paccayena akilamantena hi sakkā samaṇadhammo kātuṃ, vattameva vā etaṃ pabbajitānaṃ. Atha tena paṭivacane dinne, ‘‘anuruddhā, tumhe rājapabbajitā mahāpuññā, manussā tumhākaṃ araññe vasantānaṃ adatvā kassa aññassa dātabbaṃ maññissanti, tumhe pana etaṃ bhuñjitvā kiṃ nu kho migapotakā viya aññamaññaṃ saṅghaṭṭentā viharatha, udāhu sāmaggibhāvo vo atthī’’ti sāmaggirasaṃ pucchanto, kacci pana vo, anuruddhā, samaggātiādimāha.

Tattha khīrodakībhūtāti yathā khīrañca udakañca aññamaññaṃ saṃsandati, visuṃ na hoti, ekattaṃ viya upeti, kacci evaṃ sāmaggivasena ekattūpagatacittuppādā viharathāti pucchati. Piyacakkhūhīti mettacittaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā olokanacakkhūni piyacakkhūni nāma. Kacci tathārūpehi cakkhūhi aññamaññaṃ sampassantā viharathāti pucchati. Tagghāti ekaṃsatthe nipāto. Ekaṃsena mayaṃ, bhanteti vuttaṃ hoti. Yathā kathaṃ panāti ettha yathāti nipātamattaṃ. Kathanti kāraṇapucchā. Kathaṃ pana tumhe evaṃ viharatha, kena kāraṇena viharatha, taṃ me kāraṇaṃ brūthāti vuttaṃ hoti. Mettaṃ kāyakammanti mettacittavasena pavattaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Āvi ceva raho cāti sammukhā ceva parammukhā ca. Itaresupi eseva nayo.

khīrodakībhūtā Piyacakkhūhī Tagghā Yathā kathaṃ panā yathā Katha Mettaṃ kāyakamma Āvi ceva raho cā

Tattha sammukhā kāyavacīkammāni sahavāse labbhanti, itarāni vippavāse. Manokammaṃ sabbattha labbhati. Yañhi sahavasantesu ekena mañcapīṭhaṃ vā dārubhaṇḍaṃ vā mattikābhaṇḍaṃ vā bahi dunnikkhittaṃ hoti, taṃ disvā kenidaṃ vaḷañjitanti avaññaṃ akatvā attanā dunnikkhittaṃ viya gahetvā paṭisāmentassa paṭijaggitabbayuttaṃ vā pana ṭhānaṃ paṭijaggantassa sammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma hoti. Ekasmiṃ pakkante tena dunnikkhittaṃ senāsanaparikkhāraṃ tatheva nikkhipantassa paṭijaggitabbayuttaṭṭhānaṃ vā pana paṭijaggantassa parammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma hoti. Sahavasantassa pana tehi saddhiṃ madhuraṃ sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ paṭisanthārakathaṃ sāraṇīyakathaṃ dhammīkathaṃ sarabhaññaṃ sākacchaṃ pañhapucchanaṃ pañhavissajjananti evamādikaraṇe sammukhā mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma hoti. Theresu pana pakkantesu mayhaṃ piyasahāyo nandiyatthero kimilatthero evaṃ sīlasampanno, evaṃ ācārasampannotiādiguṇakathanaṃ parammukhā mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma hoti. Mayhaṃ piyamitto nandiyatthero kimilatthero avero hotu, abyāpajjo sukhī hotūti evaṃ samannāharato pana sammukhāpi parammukhāpi mettaṃ manokammaṃ hotiyeva.

Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyāti kāyañhi piṭṭhaṃ viya mattikā viya ca omadditvā ekato kātuṃ na sakkā. Ekañca pana maññe cittanti cittaṃ pana no hitaṭṭhena nirantaraṭṭhena aviggahaṭṭhena samaggaṭṭhena ekamevāti dasseti. Kathaṃ panetaṃ sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā itaresaṃ cittavasena vattiṃsūti? Ekassa patte malaṃ uṭṭhahati, ekassa cīvaraṃ kiliṭṭhaṃ hoti, ekassa paribhaṇḍakammaṃ hoti. Tattha yassa patte malaṃ uṭṭhitaṃ, tena mamāvuso, patte malaṃ uṭṭhitaṃ pacituṃ vaṭṭatīti vutte itare mayhaṃ cīvaraṃ kiliṭṭhaṃ dhovitabbaṃ, mayhaṃ paribhaṇḍaṃ kātabbanti avatvā araññaṃ pavisitvā dārūni āharitvā chinditvā pattakaṭāhe paribhaṇḍaṃ katvā tato paraṃ cīvaraṃ vā dhovanti, paribhaṇḍaṃ vā karonti. Mamāvuso, cīvaraṃ kiliṭṭhaṃ dhovituṃ vaṭṭati, mama paṇṇasālā uklāpā paribhaṇḍaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti paṭhamataraṃ ārocitepi eseva nayo.

Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā Ekañca pana maññe citta
commentary_english:
326. When that is gathered, the rest is as if it were done, thus the elder spoke this statement such as “*kacci vo anuruddhā*”.

There, *kaccī* is a particle in the sense of a question.

*vo* is a respectful expression.

This is what was said: “Are things tolerable for you, Anuruddhas? Is your conduct bearable for you? Is it manageable? Does life proceed and thrive for you? Are you not weary with alms, do people, seeing you arriving with easily obtained alms, think that watery gruel or alms from a ladle should be given?” He asks about the practice of the alms-round.

Why? For the monastic life can be lived with a cause that does not cause weariness, or indeed this is the practice of those who have gone forth.

Then, when that reply had been given, “Anuruddhas, you are royal renunciates, greatly meritorious, people, without giving to you dwelling in the forest, to whom else would they think alms should be given? But you, having enjoyed this, why do you live associating with each other like young deer, or is there harmony among you?” Asking about the taste of harmony, he said this, beginning with "*kacci pana vo, anuruddhā, samaggā*."

There, *khīrodakībhūtā* means just as milk and water mix together, there is no separation, it goes to oneness, does the arising of consciousness that has reached oneness in harmony occur thus?” he asks.

*piyacakkhūhī* means having established a mind of loving-kindness, the eyes of looking are called eyes of affection.

“Do you live seeing each other with eyes of such a kind?” he asks.

*tagghā* is a particle in the sense of certainty.

“We are certain, venerable sir,” is what was said.

"*yathā kathaṃ panā*" here, *yathā* is merely a particle.

"*kathaṃ*" is a question of cause.

“How do you live thus, by what cause do you live, tell me that cause,” is what was said.

*mettaṃ kāyakamma* means bodily action proceeding by way of a mind of loving-kindness.

*āvi ceva raho cā* means both face to face and behind the back.

The same method applies to the others as well.

*khīrodakībhūtā piyacakkhūhī tagghā yathā kathaṃ panā yathā katha mettaṃ kāyakamma āvi ceva raho cā* There, bodily and verbal actions face to face are obtained in cohabitation, the others in separation.

Mental action is obtained everywhere.

For when a couch or chair or wooden vessel or clay vessel is badly placed outside by one of those living together, having seen that, without disrespecting "By whom was this ruined?" but taking it as if it was badly placed by himself, that is called bodily action of loving-kindness face to face for one who puts it back or one who attends to a place fit to be attended to.

When one has departed, that is called bodily action of loving-kindness behind the back for one who puts back just so the requisites of a dwelling-place badly placed by him or who attends to a place fit to be attended to.

Moreover, for one cohabiting with them, sweet, pleasing talk, talk of friendliness, talk causing remembrance, talk about the Dharma, recitation, discussion, asking questions, answering questions, in such causes, that is called verbal action of loving-kindness face to face.

Moreover, when those elders have departed, saying such talk of qualities as “My dear companion, the venerable Nandiya, the venerable Kimila, is thus endowed with virtue, is thus endowed with conduct,” that is called verbal action of loving-kindness behind the back.

“May my dear friend the venerable Nandiya, the venerable Kimila, be without enmity, be without affliction, be happy,” for one bringing this to mind, both face to face and behind the back, mental action of loving-kindness certainly occurs.

*nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā* means for bodies cannot be made one by kneading like a seat or like clay.

*ekañca pana maññe citta* means but the mind shows that it is indeed one by way of benefit, by way of continuity, by way of non-separation, by way of harmony.

How is it that, having put aside their own minds, they lived according to the minds of others? For one, filth arises in the bowl, for one, the robe is soiled, for one, there is work to be done on the requisites.

There, when one whose bowl has filth arisen says, “My friend, filth has arisen in the bowl, it is fitting to wash it,” the others, without saying, “My robe is soiled, it should be washed, my requisites should be made,” enter the forest, bring back wood, chop it, make the requisites in a bowl, and then wash the robe or make the requisites.

Even when one says beforehand, “My friend, the robe is soiled, it is fitting to wash it, my leaf-hut is disarranged, it is fitting to make the requisites,” this same method applies.

*nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā ekañca pana maññe citta*

mula_pali: 327. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Kacci pana vo, anuruddhā, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharathā’’ti? ‘‘Taggha mayaṃ, bhante, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāmā’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, anuruddhā, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharathā’’ti? ‘‘Idha, bhante, amhākaṃ yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati so āsanāni paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, avakkārapātiṃ upaṭṭhāpeti. Yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, sace hoti bhuttāvaseso sace ākaṅkhati bhuñjati, no ce ākaṅkhati appaharite vā chaḍḍeti, appāṇake vā udake opilāpeti. So āsanāni paṭisāmeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmeti, avakkārapātiṃ paṭisāmeti, bhattaggaṃ sammajjati. Yo passati pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ so upaṭṭhāpeti. Sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpema, na tveva mayaṃ, bhante, tappaccayā vācaṃ bhindāma. Pañcāhikaṃ kho pana mayaṃ, bhante, sabbarattikaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sannisīdāma. Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāmā’’ti.
mula_english:
327. "Excellent, excellent, Anuruddhas! Are you, Anuruddhas, diligent, ardent, and resolute?" "Yes, venerable sir, we are diligent, ardent, and resolute."

"But how are you, Anuruddhas, diligent, ardent, and resolute?" "Here, venerable sir, whoever returns first from the village for alms, lays out the seats, sets out drinking water and water for washing, and sets out the refuse bucket.

Whoever returns afterwards from the village for alms, if there is any food left over, eats it if he wishes; and if not, he throws it away where there is no greenery, or drops it into water where there is no life. He puts away the seats, puts away the drinking water and the water for washing, puts away the refuse bucket, and sweeps the refectory.

Whoever sees a drinking water pitcher, a washing water pitcher, or a latrine pitcher that is empty, refills it.

If it is too much for him, he calls another by a hand signal and together they refill it. We do not, venerable sir, break out into speech because of that.

And every five days, venerable sir, we sit together all night discussing the *dharma*.

Thus, venerable sir, we are diligent, ardent, and resolute."
commentary_pali:
327.Sādhusādhu, anuruddhāti bhagavā heṭṭhā na ca mayaṃ, bhante, piṇḍakena kilamimhāti vutte na sādhukāramadāsi. Kasmā? Ayañhi kabaḷīkāro āhāro nāma imesaṃ sattānaṃ apāyalokepi devamanussalokepi āciṇṇasamāciṇṇova. Ayaṃ pana lokasannivāso yebhuyyena vivādapakkhando, apāyaloke devamanussalokepi ime sattā paṭiviruddhā eva, etesaṃ sāmaggikālo dullabho, kadācideva hotīti samaggavāsassa dullabhattā idha bhagavā sādhukāramadāsi. Idāni tesaṃ appamādalakkhaṇaṃ pucchanto kaccipana vo, anuruddhātiādimāha. Tattha voti nipātamattaṃ paccattavacanaṃ vā, kacci tumheti attho. Amhākanti amhesu tīsu janesu. Piṇḍāya paṭikkamatīti gāme piṇḍāya caritvā paccāgacchati. Avakkārapātinti atirekapiṇḍapātaṃ apanetvā ṭhapanatthāya ekaṃ samuggapātiṃ dhovitvā ṭhapeti.

Yo pacchāti te kira therā na ekatova bhikkhācāraṃ pavisanti, phalasamāpattiratā hete. Pātova sarīrappaṭijagganaṃ katvā vattappaṭipattiṃ pūretvā senāsanaṃ pavisitvā kālaparicchedaṃ katvā phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā nisīdanti. Tesu yo paṭhamataraṃ nisinno attano kālaparicchedavasena paṭhamataraṃ uṭṭhāti; so piṇḍāya caritvā paṭinivatto bhattakiccaṭṭhānaṃ āgantvā jānāti – ‘‘dve bhikkhū pacchā, ahaṃ paṭhamataraṃ āgato’’ti. Atha pattaṃ pidahitvā āsanapaññāpanādīni katvā yadi patte paṭivisamattameva hoti, nisīditvā bhuñjati. Yadi atirekaṃ hoti, avakkārapātiyaṃ pakkhipitvā pātiṃ pidhāya bhuñjati. Katabhattakicco pattaṃ dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā thavikāya osāpetvā pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisati. Dutiyopi āgantvāva jānāti – ‘‘eko paṭhamaṃ āgato, eko pacchato’’ti. So sace patte bhattaṃ pamāṇameva hoti, bhuñjati. Sace mandaṃ, avakkārapātito gahetvā bhuñjati. Sace atirekaṃ hoti, avakkārapātiyaṃ pakkhipitvā pamāṇameva bhuñjitvā purimatthero viya vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisati. Tatiyopi āgantvāva jānāti – ‘‘dve paṭhamaṃ āgatā, ahaṃ pacchato’’ti. Sopi dutiyatthero viya bhuñjitvā katabhattakicco pattaṃ dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā thavikāya osāpetvā āsanāni ukkhipitvā paṭisāmeti; pānīyaghaṭe vā paribhojanīyaghaṭe vā avasesaṃ udakaṃ chaḍḍetvā ghaṭe nikujjitvā avakkārapātiyaṃ sace avasesabhattaṃ hoti, taṃ vuttanayena jahitvā pātiṃ dhovitvā paṭisāmeti; bhattaggaṃ sammajjati. Tato kacavaraṃ chaḍḍetvā sammajjaniṃ ukkhipitvā upacikāhi muttaṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā pattacīvaramādāya vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisati. Idaṃ therānaṃ bahivihāre araññe bhattakiccakaraṇaṭṭhāne bhojanasālāyaṃ vattaṃ. Idaṃ sandhāya, ‘‘yo pacchā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

Yo pacchā

Yo passatītiādi pana nesaṃ antovihāre vattanti veditabbaṃ. Tattha vaccaghaṭanti ācamanakumbhiṃ. Rittanti rittakaṃ. Tucchanti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Avisayhanti ukkhipituṃ asakkuṇeyyaṃ, atibhāriyaṃ. Hatthavikārenāti hatthasaññāya. Te kira pānīyaghaṭādīsu yaṃkiñci tucchakaṃ gahetvā pokkharaṇiṃ gantvā anto ca bahi ca dhovitvā udakaṃ parissāvetvā tīre ṭhapetvā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ hatthavikārena āmantenti, odissa vā anodissa vā saddaṃ na karonti. Kasmā odissa saddaṃ na karonti? Taṃ bhikkhuṃ saddo bādheyyāti. Kasmā anodissa saddaṃ na karonti? Anodissa sadde dinne, ‘‘ahaṃ pure, ahaṃ pure’’ti dvepi nikkhameyyuṃ, tato dvīhi kattabbakamme tatiyassa kammacchedo bhaveyya. Saṃyatapadasaddo pana hutvā aparassa bhikkhuno divāṭṭhānasantikaṃ gantvā tena diṭṭhabhāvaṃ ñatvā hatthasaññaṃ karoti, tāya saññāya itaro āgacchati, tato dve janā hatthena hatthaṃ saṃsibbantā dvīsu hatthesu ṭhapetvā upaṭṭhapenti. Taṃ sandhāyāha – ‘‘hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhapemā’’ti.

Yo passatī vaccaghaṭa Ritta Tuccha Avisayha Hatthavikārenā

Pañcāhikaṃ kho panāti cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyanti idaṃ tāva pakatidhammassavanameva, taṃ akhaṇḍaṃ katvā pañcame pañcame divase dve therā nātivikāle nhāyitvā anuruddhattherassa vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gacchanti. Tattha tayopi nisīditvā tiṇṇaṃ piṭakānaṃ aññatarasmiṃ aññamaññaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti , aññamaññaṃ vissajjenti, tesaṃ evaṃ karontānaṃyeva aruṇaṃ uggacchati. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Ettāvatā therena bhagavatā appamādalakkhaṇaṃ pucchitena pamādaṭṭhānesuyeva appamādalakkhaṇaṃ vissajjitaṃ hoti. Aññesañhi bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhācāraṃ pavisanakālo, nikkhamanakālo, nivāsanaparivattanaṃ, cīvarapārupanaṃ, antogāme piṇḍāya caraṇaṃ dhammakathanaṃ, anumodanaṃ , gāmato nikkhamitvā bhattakiccakaraṇaṃ, pattadhovanaṃ, pattaosāpanaṃ, pattacīvarapaṭisāmananti papañcakaraṇaṭṭhānāni etāni. Tasmā thero amhākaṃ ettakaṃ ṭhānaṃ muñcitvā pamādakālo nāma natthīti dassento pamādaṭṭhānesuyeva appamādalakkhaṇaṃ vissajjesi.

Pañcāhikaṃ kho panā
commentary_english:
327. *Sādhu*.
*Sādhu, anuruddhā* Thus spoke the Blessed One, "Indeed, I would not give approval when I was below, O venerable one, as we are exhausted by the alms."
Why is that? This morsel food, named nutriment, is something that is habitually accumulated by beings in the realms of misery as well as in the world of gods and humans.
Now, this dwelling of the world is mostly subject to disputes. In the realm of misery and the world of gods and humans, these beings are indeed hostile. It is rare to have a time of concord for them. Because dwelling in concord is difficult, here the Blessed One gave approval.
Now, while asking about their characteristic of diligence, he spoke the saying beginning with, *kacci pana vo, anuruddhā.*
There, *vo* is a mere particle, or a term relating to oneself. The meaning is, "Is it perhaps so for you?"
*Amhāka* means among us, the three people.
*Piṇḍāya paṭikkamati* means having wandered for alms in the village, he returns.
*Avakkārapāti* means having removed the excess almsfood, he washes and sets aside one container-bowl for the purpose of setting it aside.

*Yo pacchā* means those venerable ones do not enter for alms all at once. They are devoted to the attainment of fruition.
Early in the morning, having performed the attending to the body, having fulfilled the practice of duties, having entered the lodging, having made a demarcation of time, having awaited the attainment of fruition, they sit down.
Among them, whoever sits down earlier rises earlier due to the force of his demarcation of time. Having wandered for alms, having returned, having come to the place of meal-duty, he knows, "Two monks [came] later, I came earlier."
Then, having covered the bowl, having performed the laying out of seats and so forth, if there is just the right amount in the bowl, he sits down and eats.
If there is an excess, having put [it] into the refuse-bowl, having covered the bowl, he eats.
Having completed the meal duty, having washed the bowl, having made water, having put it away in the bag, having taken his bowl and robe, he enters his dwelling place.
The second one, too, having come, knows, "One came earlier, one [came] later."
If there is just the right amount of food in the bowl, he eats.
If there is too little, having taken [some] from the refuse-bowl, he eats.
If there is an excess, having put [it] into the refuse-bowl, having eaten just the right amount, like the former venerable one, he enters his dwelling place.
The third one, too, having come, knows, "Two came earlier, I [came] later."
He, too, having eaten like the second venerable one, having completed the meal duty, having washed the bowl, having made water, having put it away in the bag, having lifted up the seats, he puts them away; having thrown away the remaining water in the drinking water jar or the water-for-use jar, having overturned the jars, if there is remaining food in the refuse-bowl, having discarded it in the manner stated, having washed the bowl, he puts it away; he sweeps the refectory.
Then, having discarded the rubbish, having lifted up the broom, having placed it in the proper place with the support, having taken his bowl and robe, he enters his dwelling place.
This is the duty of the venerable ones in the outer monastery, in the forest, in the place for performing meal duty, in the dining hall.
Referring to this, the saying beginning with "whoever [came] later" and so forth, was spoken.

*Yo pacchā*
*Yo passatī* But the saying beginning with "whoever sees" should be understood as their duty in the inner monastery.
There, *vaccaghaṭa* means a pot for rinsing the mouth.
*Ritta* means empty.
*Tuccha* means a synonym of that.
*Avisayha* means it is not possible to lift it up, it is very heavy.
*Hatthavikārena* means by a gesture of the hand.
Those [monks], it is said, having taken some empty thing from among the drinking water pots and so forth, having gone to the pond, having washed [it] inside and out, having strained the water, having placed it on the bank, they summon another monk with a gesture of the hand, they do not make a sound by addressing [him] or by not addressing [him].
Why do they not make a sound by addressing [him]? So that the sound would not disturb that monk.
Why don't they make a sound without being instructed? If a sound is made without being instructed, both would come out saying, "I [was] first, I [was] first," and then the action to be done by two would be interrupted for the third.

Having become one whose words are restrained, he goes to the vicinity of another *bhikkhu*'s daytime dwelling, and having learned that he has been seen, he makes a hand sign. By that sign, the other one comes. Then two people, sewing hand to hand, place [it] on two hands and present [it].

Referring to that, he said: “Having summoned a second [person] with a hand gesture, let us present [it] with a hand-waving.”

He who sees a water pot, empty, void, ungraspable, with a hand gesture. The *pañcāhikaṃ kho panā* is the fourteenth, fifteenth, eighth day. This is merely listening to the natural law. Having made that unfragmented, on every fifth day, two *theras* bathe, not too early, and go to Anuruddha Thera's dwelling place.

There, those three, having sat down, ask each other questions about one of the three *piṭakas*, answer each other, and while they are doing thus, the dawn rises.

This was said regarding that.

Thus, by the Thera, the characteristic of diligence (*apramāda-lakṣaṇaṃ*) having been asked by the Blessed One (Bhagavān), the characteristic of diligence (*apramāda-lakṣaṇaṃ*) was explained right in the places of negligence (*pramāda-sthānesu*).

Indeed, for other *bhikkhus*, it is the time to enter for alms-gathering, the time to leave, changing robes, covering robes, wandering for alms in the village, teaching the *dharma*, rejoicing, leaving the village, doing the meal duty, washing the bowl, drying the bowl, fixing the bowl and robe, these are the places of proliferation.

Therefore, the Thera, showing that there is no time for negligence (*pramāda-kālo*), having relinquished such a place for us, explained the characteristic of diligence (*apramāda-lakṣaṇaṃ*) right in the places of negligence (*pramāda-sthānesu*).

mula_pali:
328. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Atthi pana vo, anuruddhā, evaṃ appamattānaṃ ātāpīnaṃ pahitattānaṃ viharantānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Ayaṃ kho no, bhante, amhākaṃ appamattānaṃ ātāpīnaṃ pahitattānaṃ viharantānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti.

‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti.

‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhakā ca viharāma, satā ca sampajānā, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedema, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti.

‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti ? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti.

‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti.

‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāma…pe… sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāma…pe… sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāma. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti.
mula_english:
328. “Good, good, Anuruddha! But is there, Anuruddha, a superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, attained by those abiding diligent, ardent, and resolute in this way?”

“Why wouldn’t there be, venerable sir! Here, venerable sir, as long as we want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, we enter upon and abide in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by thought and examination, born of seclusion, filled with rapture and pleasure. This, venerable sir, is a superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which we have attained while abiding diligent, ardent, and resolute.”

“Good, good, Anuruddha! But is there, Anuruddha, another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which you have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside?”

“Why wouldn’t there be, venerable sir! Here, venerable sir, as long as we want, with the subsiding of thought and examination, gaining inner tranquility, the unification of the mind, without thought, without examination, we enter upon and abide in the second *jhāna*, which is born of concentration, filled with rapture and pleasure. This, venerable sir, is another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which we have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside.”

“Good, good, Anuruddha! But is there, Anuruddha, another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which you have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside?”

“Why wouldn’t there be, venerable sir! Here, venerable sir, as long as we want, with the fading away as well of rapture, we abide in equanimity, mindful and fully aware, and experience pleasure with the body; we enter upon and abide in the third *jhāna* of which the noble ones declare: ‘He is equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily.’ This, venerable sir, is another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which we have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside.”

“Good, good, Anuruddha! But is there, Anuruddha, another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which you have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside?”

“Why wouldn’t there be, venerable sir! Here, venerable sir, as long as we want, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, we enter upon and abide in the fourth *jhāna*, which is neither painful nor pleasant and contains purification of mindfulness through equanimity. This, venerable sir, is another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which we have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside.”

“Good, good, Anuruddha! But is there, Anuruddha, another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which you have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside?”

“Why wouldn’t there be, venerable sir! Here, venerable sir, as long as we want, by completely surmounting perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, we enter upon and abide in the base of infinite space (ākāśānantyāyatana). This, venerable sir, is another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which we have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside.”

“Good, good, Anuruddha! But is there, Anuruddha, another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which you have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside?”

“Why wouldn’t there be, venerable sir! Here, venerable sir, as long as we want, by completely surmounting the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, we enter upon and abide in the base of infinite consciousness…By completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing’, we enter upon and abide in the base of nothingness…By completely surmounting the base of nothingness, we enter upon and abide in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. This, venerable sir, is another superior human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding, which we have attained by surmounting that abiding, by making that abiding subside.”
commentary_pali: 328. Athassa bhagavā sādhukāraṃ datvā paṭhamajjhānaṃ pucchanto puna atthi pana votiādimāha. Tattha uttari manussadhammāti manussadhammato uttari. Alamariyañāṇadassanavisesoti ariyabhāvakaraṇasamattho ñāṇaviseso. Kiñhi no siyā, bhanteti kasmā, bhante, nādhigato bhavissati, adhigatoyevāti. Yāva devāti yāva eva.
commentary_english:
328. Then, the Bhagavān, having given approval and questioning about the first *jhāna*, again said, “Is there?” etc.

There, "*uttari manussadhammā*" means superior to human qualities.

"*alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso*" means a special knowledge capable of bringing about the state of an *ariya*.

"*kiñhi no siyā, bhante*" means why, *bhante*, will it not be attained? It will indeed be attained.

"*yāva devā*" means as long as.

mula_pali: 329. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etassa pana vo, anuruddhā, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā atthañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bhante! Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāma sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharāma, paññāya ca no disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā. Etassa, bhante, vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā ayamañño uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro. Imamhā ca mayaṃ, bhante, phāsuvihārā aññaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ uttaritaraṃ vā paṇītataraṃ vā na samanupassāmā’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Imamhā phāsuvihārā uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā phāsuvihāro natthī’’ti.
mula_english:
"Excellent! Excellent, Anuruddha! Have you, Anuruddha, attained to a comfortable abiding ( *phāsuvihāro* ) , a superhuman state ( *uttarimanussadhammā* ), a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones ( *alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato* ), by surmounting the preceding abiding of this dwelling (*etassa vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā* )? "

"Venerable sir (*bhante*) , what would not be possible for us? Here, venerable sir (*bhante*) , as long as we wish, having completely transcended the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma*), we attain to and abide in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharāma*), and our taints (*āsavā parikkhīṇā*) are destroyed by seeing with wisdom (*paññāya ca no disvā*)."

"Venerable sir (*bhante*) , this is another superhuman state ( *uttarimanussadhammā* ), a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones ( *alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato* ), a comfortable abiding ( *phāsuvihāro* ), which we have attained by surmounting the preceding abiding of this dwelling (*etassa vihārassa samatikkamāya etassa vihārassa paṭippassaddhiyā* )."

"And, venerable sir (*bhante*) , we do not see any other comfortable abiding ( *phāsuvihāraṃ* ) higher ( *uttaritaraṃ* ) or more sublime ( *paṇītataraṃ* ) than this one ( *imamhā ca mayaṃ* )."

"Excellent! Excellent, Anuruddha! There is no comfortable abiding ( *phāsuvihāro natthī* ) higher ( *uttaritaraṃ* ) or more sublime ( *paṇītataraṃ* ) than this comfortable abiding ( *imamhā phāsuvihārā* )."
commentary_pali: 329. Evaṃ paṭhamajjhānādhigame byākate dutiyajjhānādīni pucchanto etassa pana votiādimāha. Tattha samatikkamāyāti samatikkamatthāya. Paṭippassaddhiyāti paṭippassaddhatthāya. Sesaṃ sabbattha vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Pacchimapañhe pana lokuttarañāṇadassanavasena adhigataṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ pucchanto alamariyañāṇadassanavisesoti āha. Theropi pucchānurūpeneva byākāsi. Tattha yasmā vedayitasukhato avedayitasukhaṃ santataraṃ paṇītataraṃ hoti, tasmā aññaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ uttaritaraṃ vā paṇītataraṃ vā na samanupassāmāti āha.
commentary_english:
Thus, when the attainment of the first *jhāna* is explained, he asks about the second *jhāna*, etc., saying, "But what about this?" and so on.

There, "*samatikkamāyā* means for overcoming."

"*paṭippassaddhiyā* means for tranquillizing."

The rest should be understood by the method already described everywhere.

Furthermore, in the last question, when asking about the *nirodhasamāpatti* attained through the way of supramundane knowledge and vision, he says, "*alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso*."

The elder also explained it in accordance with the question.

There, since unfelt pleasure is more peaceful and refined than felt pleasure, therefore he says, "We do not perceive any other comfortable abiding that is higher or more refined," and so on.

mula_pali: 330. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantañca anuruddhaṃ āyasmantañca nandiyaṃ āyasmantañca kimilaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca nandiyo āyasmā ca kimilo bhagavantaṃ anusaṃyāyitvā anusaṃsāvetvā (sī.), anusāvetvā (ṭīkā) tato paṭinivattitvā āyasmā ca nandiyo āyasmā ca kimilo āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho mayaṃ āyasmato anuruddhassa evamārocimha – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ mayaṃ lābhino’ti, yaṃ no āyasmā anuruddho bhagavato sammukhā yāva āsavānaṃ khayā pakāsetī’’ti? ‘‘Na kho me āyasmanto evamārocesuṃ – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ mayaṃ lābhino’ti, api ca me āyasmantānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca vidito – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ ime āyasmanto lābhino’ti. Devatāpi me etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – ‘imāsañca imāsañca vihārasamāpattīnaṃ ime āyasmanto lābhino’ti. Tamenaṃ bhagavatā pañhābhipuṭṭhena byākata’’nti.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One, having instructed, inspired, and gladdened the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya, and the venerable Kimila with a teaching, got up from his seat and left.

Then the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya, and the venerable Kimila accompanied the Blessed One a little way and turned back again. The venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimila said to the venerable Anuruddha: “Have we ever reported to the venerable Anuruddha that we have obtained those abidings and attainments of monasteries that the venerable Anuruddha, in the Blessed One’s presence, ascribed to us up to the destruction of the āsavas (taints)?”

“No, venerable sirs, you have not reported to me thus: ‘We have obtained these abidings and attainments of monasteries.’ But rather, by my mind, mind was known to me concerning the venerable ones: ‘These venerable ones have obtained these abidings and attainments of monasteries.’

Deities also reported this matter to me: ‘These venerable ones have obtained these abidings and attainments of monasteries.’

Then I declared it when directly questioned by the Blessed One.”
commentary_pali: 330.Dhammiyā kathāyāti sāmaggirasānisaṃsappaṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya. Sabbepi te catūsu saccesu pariniṭṭhitakiccā, tena tesaṃ paṭivedhatthāya kiñci kathetabbaṃ natthi. Sāmaggirasena pana ayañca ayañca ānisaṃsoti sāmaggirasānisaṃsameva nesaṃ bhagavā kathesi. Bhagavantaṃ anusaṃyāyitvāti anugantvā. Te kira bhagavato pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā thokaṃ agamaṃsu, atha bhagavā vihārassa pariveṇapariyantaṃ gatakāle, ‘‘āharatha me pattacīvaraṃ, tumhe idheva tiṭṭhathā’’ti pakkāmi. Tato paṭinivattitvāti tato ṭhitaṭṭhānato nivattitvā. Kiṃ nu kho mayaṃ āyasmatoti bhagavantaṃ nissāya pabbajjādīni adhigantvāpi attano guṇakathāya aṭṭiyamānā adhigamappicchatāya āhaṃsu. Imāsañca imāsañcāti paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ lokiyalokuttarānaṃ. Cetasā ceto paricca viditoti ajja me āyasmanto lokiyasamāpattiyā vītināmesuṃ, ajja lokuttarāyāti evaṃ cittena cittaṃ paricchinditvā viditaṃ. Devatāpi meti, bhante anuruddha, ajja ayyo nandiyatthero, ajja ayyo kimilatthero imāya ca imāya ca samāpattiyā vītināmesīti evamārocesunti attho. Pañhābhipuṭṭhenāti tampi mayā sayaṃ viditanti vā devatāhi ārocitanti vā ettakeneva mukhaṃ me sajjanti kathaṃ samuṭṭhāpetvā apuṭṭheneva me na kathitaṃ. Bhagavatā pana pañhābhipuṭṭhena pañhaṃ abhipucchitena satā byākataṃ, tatra me kiṃ na rocathāti āha.
commentary_english:
330. *Dhammiyā kathāyā* means a *dhammiyā kathā* connected to concord, savor, and benefit.

Even though all of them have completed their task regarding the four truths ( *catūsu saccesu* ), there is nothing that should be said for their comprehension.

However, the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ) spoke to them only of concord, savor, and benefit, [saying,] "This and this is the benefit."

*Bhagavantaṃ anusaṃyāyitvā* means having followed after.

They went, having taken the bowl and robe (*pattacīvaraṃ*) of the Blessed One ( *bhagavato* ) for a short distance. Then, when the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ) had reached the entire enclosure of the monastery ( *vihārassa pariveṇapariyantaṃ* ), he departed, [saying,] "Bring me the bowl and robe (*pattacīvaraṃ*), you all stay right here."

*Tato paṭinivattitvā* means having turned back from that very place.

*Kiṃ nu kho mayaṃ āyasmato* means having relied on the Blessed One ( *bhagavantaṃ* ), even after attaining ordination etc. (*pabbajjādīni*), they spoke, being troubled by speaking of their own qualities, [desiring] little attainment.

*Imāsañca imāsañcā* means of the mundane and supramundane (*lokiyalokuttarānaṃ*) first *jhāna* and so forth (*paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ*).

*Cetasā ceto paricca vidito* means, "Today, the venerable ones have passed beyond the mundane attainment (*lokiyasamāpattiyā vītināmesuṃ*), today, the supramundane." Thus, having distinguished mind with mind, it is known.

*Devatāpi me* means, "Venerable Anuruddha ( *bhante anuruddha* ), today the venerable Nandiya ( *ayyo nandiyatthero* ), today the venerable Kimila ( *ayyo kimilatthero* ) has passed beyond this and this attainment ( *samāpattiyā vītināmesīti*)," this is the meaning of "they announced thus (*evamārocesunti attho*)."

*Pañhābhipuṭṭhenā* means, "Even that, whether I knew it myself or it was announced by the deities, my face lights up just by this much; how could I establish it and not say it even without being asked?"

However, the Blessed One ( *bhagavatā* ), when questioned with a question, with the question being interrogated, spoke. He said, "What is it there that does not please you?"

mula_pali:
331. Atha kho dīgho parajano yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho dīgho parajano yakkho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘lābhā vata, bhante, vajjīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā vajjipajāya, yattha tathāgato viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, ime ca tayo kulaputtā – āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca nandiyo, āyasmā ca kimilo’’ti. Dīghassa parajanassa yakkhassa saddaṃ sutvā bhummā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – ‘lābhā vata, bho, vajjīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā vajjipajāya, yattha tathāgato viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, ime ca tayo kulaputtā – āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca nandiyo, āyasmā ca kimilo’ti. Bhummānaṃ devānaṃ saddaṃ sutvā cātumahārājikā devā…pe… tāvatiṃsā devā…pe… yāmā devā…pe… tusitā devā…pe… nimmānaratī devā…pe… paranimmitavasavattī devā…pe… brahmakāyikā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – ‘‘lābhā vata, bho, vajjīnaṃ, suladdhalābhā vajjipajāya, yattha tathāgato viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, ime ca tayo kulaputtā – āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca nandiyo, āyasmā ca kimilo’’ti. Itiha te āyasmanto tena khaṇena (tena layena) ( ) sī. syā. pī. potthakesu natthi tena muhuttena yāvabrahmalokā viditā saṃviditā (ka.) ahesuṃ.

‘‘Evametaṃ, dīgha, evametaṃ, dīgha! Yasmāpi, dīgha, kulā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, tañcepi kulaṃ ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittaṃ anussareyya, tassapāssa kulassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, kulaparivaṭṭā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, so cepi kulaparivaṭṭo ete tayo kulaputte pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa kulaparivaṭṭassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, gāmā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, so cepi gāmo ete tayo kulaputte pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa gāmassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, nigamā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, so cepi nigamo ete tayo kulaputte pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa nigamassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, nagarā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, tañcepi nagaraṃ ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittaṃ anussareyya, tassapāssa nagarassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Yasmāpi, dīgha, janapadā ete tayo kulaputtā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, so cepi janapado ete tayo kulaputte pasannacitto anussareyya, tassapāssa janapadassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Sabbe cepi, dīgha, khattiyā ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittā anussareyyuṃ, sabbesānaṃpāssa khattiyānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Sabbe cepi, dīgha, brāhmaṇā…pe… sabbe cepi, dīgha, vessā…pe… sabbe cepi, dīgha, suddā ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittā anussareyyuṃ, sabbesānaṃpāssa suddānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Sadevako cepi, dīgha, loko samārako sabrahmako sassamaṇabrāhmaṇī pajā sadevamanussā ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittā anussareyya, sadevakassapāssa lokassa samārakassa sabrahmakassa sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Passa, dīgha, yāva ete tayo kulaputtā bahujanahitāya paṭipannā bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya, atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano dīgho parajano yakkho bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Cūḷagosiṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
331. Then the spirit Dīgha Parājana went to the Blessed One and on arrival, having bowed down to the Blessed One, stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Dīgha Parājana, the spirit, said this to the Blessed One: “It is a gain, venerable sir, for the Vajjis, a great gain for the Vajjian people, that the *Tathāgata*, accomplished and fully enlightened, dwells among them, and these three clansmen—the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya, and the venerable Kimbila!”

On hearing the words of Dīgha Parājana, the spirit, the earth gods exclaimed: “It is a gain, venerable sir, for the Vajjis, a great gain for the Vajjian people, that the *Tathāgata*, accomplished and fully enlightened, dwells among them, and these three clansmen—the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya, and the venerable Kimbila!”

On hearing the words of the earth gods, the gods of the heaven of the Four Great Kings…the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three…the Yama gods…the gods of the Tusita heaven…the gods who delight in creating…the gods who wield power over others’ creations…the gods of Brahma’s retinue exclaimed: “It is a gain, venerable sir, for the Vajjis, a great gain for the Vajjian people, that the *Tathāgata*, accomplished and fully enlightened, dwells among them, and these three clansmen—the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya, and the venerable Kimbila!”

Thus, at that instant, at that moment, those venerable ones were known as far as the Brahma-world.

“So it is, Dīgha, so it is, Dīgha! Dīgha, if the clan from which those three clansmen went forth from the house life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of that clan for a long time.

Dīgha, if the retinue of the clan from which those three clansmen went forth from the house life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of that retinue of the clan for a long time.

Dīgha, if the village from which those three clansmen went forth from the house life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of that village for a long time.

Dīgha, if the town from which those three clansmen went forth from the house life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of that town for a long time.

Dīgha, if the city from which those three clansmen went forth from the house life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of that city for a long time.

Dīgha, if the country from which those three clansmen went forth from the house life into homelessness should remember them with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of that country for a long time.

Dīgha, if all nobles should remember those three clansmen with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of the nobles for a long time.

Dīgha, if all brahmins…all merchants…all workers should remember those three clansmen with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of the workers for a long time.

Dīgha, if the world with its gods, its *Māras*, and its *Brahmās*, this generation with its recluses and *brāhmaṇas*, its princes and its people, should remember those three clansmen with confident heart, that would lead to the welfare and happiness of the world, with its gods, its *Māras*, and its *Brahmās*, this generation with its recluses and *brāhmaṇas*, its princes and its people, for a long time.

See, Dīgha, how those three clansmen are practicing for the welfare and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

The Blessed One said this. The spirit Dīgha Parājana was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Cūḷagosiṅga Sutta, the first, is finished.
commentary_pali:
331.Dīghoti ‘‘maṇi māṇivaro dīgho, atho serīsako sahā’’ti (dī. ni. 3.293) evaṃ āgato aṭṭhavīsatiyā yakkhasenāpatīnaṃ abbhantaro eko devarājā. Parajanoti tasseva yakkhassa nāmaṃ. Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamīti so kira vessavaṇena pesito etaṃ ṭhānaṃ gacchanto bhagavantaṃ sayaṃ pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā giñjakāvasathato gosiṅgasālavanassa antare disvā bhagavā attanā pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā gosiṅgasālavane tiṇṇaṃ kulaputtānaṃ santikaṃ gacchati. Ajja mahatī dhammadesanā bhavissati. Mayāpi tassā desanāya bhāginā bhavitabbanti adissamānena kāyena satthu padānupadiko gantvā avidūre ṭhatvā dhammaṃ sutvā satthari gacchantepi na gato, – ‘‘ime therā kiṃ karissantī’’ti dassanatthaṃ pana tattheva ṭhito. Atha te dve there anuruddhattheraṃ paliveṭhente disvā, – ‘‘ime therā bhagavantaṃ nissāya pabbajjādayo sabbaguṇe adhigantvāpi bhagavatova maccharāyanti, na sahanti, ativiya nilīyanti paṭicchādenti, na dāni tesaṃ paṭicchādetuṃ dassāmi, pathavito yāva brahmalokā etesaṃ guṇe pakāsessāmī’’ti cintetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.

Lābhā vata, bhanteti ye, bhante, vajjiraṭṭhavāsino bhagavantañca ime ca tayo kulaputte passituṃ labhanti, vandituṃ labhanti, deyyadhammaṃ dātuṃ labhanti, dhammaṃ sotuṃ labhanti, tesaṃ lābhā, bhante, vajjīnanti attho. Saddaṃ sutvāti so kira attano yakkhānubhāvena mahantaṃ saddaṃ katvā sakalaṃ vajjiraṭṭhaṃ ajjhottharanto taṃ vācaṃ nicchāresi. Tena cassa tesu rukkhapabbatādīsu adhivatthā bhummā devatā saddaṃ assosuṃ. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘saddaṃ sutvā’’ti. Anussāvesunti mahantaṃ saddaṃ sutvā sāvesuṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. Yāva brahmalokāti yāva akaniṭṭhabrahmalokā. Tañcepi kulanti, ‘‘amhākaṃ kulato nikkhamitvā ime kulaputtā pabbajitā evaṃ sīlavanto guṇavanto ācārasampannā kalyāṇadhammā’’ti evaṃ tañcepi kulaṃ ete tayo kulaputte pasannacittaṃ anussareyyāti evaṃ sabbattha attho daṭṭhabbo. Iti bhagavā yathānusandhināva desanaṃ niṭṭhapesīti.

Lābhā vata, bhante Saddaṃ sutvā Anussāvesu Yāva brahmalokā Tañcepi kula

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷagosiṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
331.

"dīgho" means, as in, "maṇi māṇivaro dīgho, atho serīsako sahā" (Dīgha Nikāya 2. 0143).

(Dī. Ni. 3.293) Thus, Āgata, an inner one of the twenty-eight yakṣa generals, is a deva-king.

"parajano" is the name of that very yakṣa.

"yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamī" means that he, sent by Vessavaṇa, while going to that place, having taken the bowl and robe himself, saw the Blessed One between Giñjakāvasatha and the Gosiṅga Sāla Forest, and the Blessed One, having taken the bowl and robe himself, went to the presence of three sons of good family in the Gosiṅga Sāla Forest.

Today there will be a great Dharma teaching.

"May I also be a partaker in that teaching," [thinking thus,] by an invisible body, going closely behind the Teacher, having stood not far away, having heard the Dharma, even though the Teacher was going, he did not go, – "what will these elders do?" – for the purpose of showing this, he remained right there.

Then, having seen those two elders embracing Anuruddha, [he thought,] – "these elders, relying on the Blessed One, even having attained all the qualities beginning with ordination, are jealous of the Blessed One himself; they are not able to bear it, they hide themselves exceedingly, they conceal [him]; now I will not give [them] an opportunity to conceal [him]; from the earth up to the Brahma realm I will proclaim their virtues" – having thought [this], he approached the Blessed One.

"lābhā vata, bhante" means, "O Blessed One, those inhabitants of the Vajji country who obtain the opportunity to see the Blessed One and these three sons of good family, obtain the opportunity to worship, obtain the opportunity to give offerings of Dharma, obtain the opportunity to hear the Dharma, their gain, O Blessed One, is the Vajjis," is the meaning.

"saddaṃ sutvā" means that he, by the power of his own yakṣa, having made a great sound, while overwhelming the entire Vajji country, uttered that speech.

And by that sound, the deities dwelling in those trees, mountains, and so on, heard the sound.

With reference to that, it was said – "saddaṃ sutvā".

"anussāvesu" means, having heard the great sound, they announced [it].

This method [applies] everywhere.

"yāva brahmalokā" means up to the Akaniṣṭha Brahma realm.

"tañcepi kula" means, "having gone forth from our family, these sons of good family are ordained, are virtuous, are endowed with good qualities, are accomplished in conduct, [and possess] auspicious qualities," thus, if that family should call to mind those three sons of good family with a serene mind, thus, the meaning should be regarded everywhere.

Thus, the Blessed One brought the teaching to a conclusion in accordance with the connection.

lābhā vata, bhante, saddaṃ sutvā, anussāvesu, yāva brahmalokā, tañcepi kula.

Papañcasūdanīya Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷagosiṅgasuttavaṇṇanā Niṭṭhitā.

mula_pali: 332. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā gosiṅgasālavanadāye viharati sambahulehi abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ – āyasmatā ca sāriputtena āyasmatā ca mahāmoggallānena āyasmatā ca mahākassapena āyasmatā ca anuruddhena āyasmatā ca revatena āyasmatā ca ānandena, aññehi ca abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘āyāmāvuso, kassapa, yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamissāma dhammassavanāyā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca anuruddho yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu dhammassavanāya. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantañca mahāmoggallānaṃ āyasmantañca mahākassapaṃ āyasmantañca anuruddhaṃ yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamante dhammassavanāya. Disvāna yenāyasmā revato tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavoca – ‘‘upasaṅkamantā kho amū, āvuso āyasmantāvuso (ka.) revata, sappurisā yenāyasmā sāriputto tena dhammassavanāya. Āyāmāvuso revata, yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamissāma dhammassavanāyā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā revato āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā ca revato āyasmā ca ānando yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu dhammassavanāya.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Park of the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood together with a number of very well-known elder disciples—the venerable Śāriputra, the venerable Mahā Moggallāna, the venerable Mahā Kāśyapa, the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Revata, the venerable Ānanda, and other very well known elder disciples.

Then, when it was evening, the venerable Mahā Moggallāna rose from meditation, went to the venerable Mahā Kāśyapa, and said to him: “Friend Kāśyapa, let us go to the venerable Śāriputra to listen to the *dharma* (dhamma).”

—“Yes, friend,” the venerable Mahā Kāśyapa replied to the venerable Mahā Moggallāna.

Then the venerable Mahā Moggallāna, the venerable Mahā Kāśyapa, and the venerable Anuruddha went to the venerable Śāriputra to listen to the *dharma* (dhamma).

The venerable Ānanda saw the venerable Mahā Moggallāna, the venerable Mahā Kāśyapa, and the venerable Anuruddha going to the venerable Śāriputra to listen to the *dharma* (dhamma).

Thereupon he went to the venerable Revata and said to him: “Friend Revata, those true men are going to the venerable Śāriputra to listen to the *dharma* (dhamma). Let us also go to the venerable Śāriputra to listen to the *dharma* (dhamma).”

—“Yes, friend,” the venerable Revata replied to the venerable Ānanda.

Then the venerable Revata and the venerable Ānanda went to the venerable Śāriputra to listen to the *dharma* (dhamma).
commentary_pali:
332.Evaṃme sutanti mahāgosiṅgasuttaṃ. Tattha gosiṅgasālavanadāyeti idaṃ vasanaṭṭhānadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Aññesu hi suttesu, ‘‘sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme’’ti evaṃ paṭhamaṃ gocaragāmaṃ dassetvā pacchā vasanaṭṭhānaṃ dasseti. Imasmiṃ pana mahāgosiṅgasutte bhagavato gocaragāmo anibandho, kocideva gocaragāmo bhavissati. Tasmā vasanaṭṭhānameva paridīpitaṃ. Araññanidānakaṃ nāmetaṃ suttanti. Sambahulehīti bahukehi. Abhiññātehi abhiññātehīti sabbattha vissutehi pākaṭehi. Therehi sāvakehi saddhinti pātimokkhasaṃvarādīhi thirakārakeheva dhammehi samannāgatattā therehi, savanante jātattā sāvakehi saddhiṃ ekato. Idāni te there sarūpato dassento, āyasmatā ca sāriputtenātiādimāha. Tatthāyasmā sāriputto attano sīlādīhi guṇehi buddhasāsane abhiññāto. Cakkhumantānaṃ gaganamajjhe ṭhito sūriyo viya cando viya, samuddatīre ṭhitānaṃ sāgaro viya ca pākaṭo paññāto. Na kevalañcassa imasmiṃ sutte āgataguṇavaseneva mahantatā veditabbā, ito aññesaṃ dhammadāyādasuttaṃ anaṅgaṇasuttaṃ sammādiṭṭhisuttaṃ sīhanādasuttaṃ rathavinītaṃ mahāhatthipadopamaṃ mahāvedallaṃ cātumasuttaṃ dīghanakhaṃ anupadasuttaṃ sevitabbāsevitabbasuttaṃ saccavibhaṅgasuttaṃ piṇḍapātapārisuddhi sampasādanīyaṃ saṅgītisuttaṃ dasuttarasuttaṃ pavāraṇāsuttaṃ (saṃ. ni. 1.215 ādayo) susimasuttaṃ therapañhasuttaṃ mahāniddeso paṭisambhidāmaggo therasīhanādasuttaṃ abhinikkhamanaṃ etadagganti imesampi suttānaṃ vasena therassa mahantatā veditabbā. Etadaggasmiñhi, ‘‘etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mahāpaññānaṃ yadidaṃ sāriputto’’ti (a. ni. 1.188-189) vuttaṃ.

Mahāmoggallānopi sīlādiguṇehi ceva imasmiṃ sutte āgataguṇehi ca thero viya abhiññāto pākaṭo mahā. Apicassa anumānasuttaṃ, cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasuttaṃ māratajjaniyasuttaṃ pāsādakampanaṃ sakalaṃ iddhipādasaṃyuttaṃ nandopanandadamanaṃ yamakapāṭihāriyakāle devalokagamanaṃ vimānavatthu petavatthu therassa abhinikkhamanaṃ etadagganti imesampi vasena mahantabhāvo veditabbo . Etadaggasmiñhi, ‘‘etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ iddhimantānaṃ yadidaṃ mahāmoggallāno’’ti (a. ni. 1.190) vuttaṃ.

Mahāmoggallāno

Mahākassapopi sīlādiguṇehi ceva imasmiṃ sutte āgataguṇehi ca thero viya abhiññāto pākaṭo mahā. Apicassa cīvaraparivattanasuttaṃ jiṇṇacīvarasuttaṃ (saṃ. ni. 2.154 ādayo) candopamaṃ sakalaṃ kassapasaṃyuttaṃ mahāariyavaṃsasuttaṃ therassa abhinikkhamanaṃ etadagganti imesampi vasena mahantabhāvo veditabbo. Etadaggasmiñhi, ‘‘etadaggaṃ , bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhutavādānaṃ yadidaṃ mahākassapo’’ti (a. ni. 1.191) vuttaṃ.

Mahākassapo

Anuruddhattheropi sīlādiguṇehi ceva imasmiṃ sutte āgataguṇehi ca thero viya abhiññāto pākaṭo mahā. Apicassa cūḷagosiṅgasuttaṃ naḷakapānasuttaṃ anuttariyasuttaṃ upakkilesasuttaṃ anuruddhasaṃyuttaṃ mahāpurisavitakkasuttaṃ therassa abhinikkhamanaṃ etadagganti imesampi vasena mahantabhāvo veditabbo. Etadaggasmiñhi, ‘‘etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dibbacakkhukānaṃ yadidaṃ anuruddho’’ti (a. ni. 1.192) vuttaṃ.

Anuruddhatthero

Āyasmatā ca revatenāti ettha pana dve revatā khadiravaniyarevato ca kaṅkhārevato ca. Tattha khadiravaniyarevato dhammasenāpatittherassa kaniṭṭhabhātiko, na so idha adhippeto. ‘‘Akappiyo guḷo, akappiyā muggā’’ti (mahāva. 272) evaṃ kaṅkhābahulo pana thero idha revatoti adhippeto. Sopi sīlādiguṇehi ceva imasmiṃ sutte āgataguṇehi ca thero viya abhiññāto pākaṭo mahā. Apicassa abhinikkhamanenapi etadaggenapi mahantabhāvo veditabbo. Etadaggasmiñhi, ‘‘etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ yadidaṃ kaṅkhārevato’’ti (a. ni. 1.204) vuttaṃ.

Āyasmatā ca revatenā

Ānandattheropi sīlādiguṇehi ceva imasmiṃ sutte āgataguṇehi ca thero viya abhiññāto pākaṭo mahā. Apicassa sekkhasuttaṃ bāhitikasuttaṃ āneñjasappāyaṃ gopakamoggallānaṃ bahudhātukaṃ cūḷasuññataṃ mahāsuññataṃ acchariyabbhutasuttaṃ bhaddekarattaṃ mahānidānaṃ mahāparinibbānaṃ subhasuttaṃ cūḷaniyalokadhātusuttaṃ abhinikkhamanaṃ etadagganti imesampi vasena mahantabhāvo veditabbo. Etadaggasmiñhi, ‘‘etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahussutānaṃ yadidaṃ ānando’’ti (a. ni. 1.219-223) vuttaṃ.

Ānandatthero

Aññehi ca abhiññātehi abhiññātehīti na kevalañca eteheva, aññehi ca mahāguṇatāya pākaṭehi abhiññātehi bahūhi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ bhagavā gosiṅgasālavanadāye viharatīti attho. Āyasmā hi sāriputto sayaṃ mahāpañño aññepi bahū mahāpaññe bhikkhū gahetvā tadā dasabalaṃ parivāretvā vihāsi. Āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sayaṃ iddhimā, āyasmā mahākassapo sayaṃ dhutavādo, āyasmā anuruddho sayaṃ dibbacakkhuko, āyasmā revato sayaṃ jhānābhirato, āyasmā ānando sayaṃ bahussuto aññepi bahū bahussute bhikkhū gahetvā tadā dasabalaṃ parivāretvā vihāsi, evaṃ tadā ete ca aññe ca abhiññātā mahātherā tiṃsasahassamattā bhikkhū dasabalaṃ parivāretvā vihariṃsūti veditabbā.

Aññehi ca abhiññātehi abhiññātehī

Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitoti phalasamāpattivivekato vuṭṭhito. Yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkamīti thero kira paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito pacchimalokadhātuṃ olokento vanante kīḷantassa mattakhattiyassa kaṇṇato patamānaṃ kuṇḍalaṃ viya, saṃharitvā samugge pakkhipamānaṃ rattakambalaṃ viya, maṇināgadantato patamānaṃ satasahassagghanikaṃ suvaṇṇapātiṃ viya ca atthaṃ gacchamānaṃ paripuṇṇapaṇṇāsayojanaṃ sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ addasa. Tadanantaraṃ pācīnalokadhātuṃ olokento nemiyaṃ gahetvā parivattayamānaṃ rajatacakkaṃ viya, rajatakūṭato nikkhamantaṃ khīradhārāmaṇḍaṃ viya, sapakkhe papphoṭetvā gaganatale pakkhandamānaṃ setahaṃsaṃ viya ca meghavaṇṇāya samuddakucchito uggantvā pācīnacakkavāḷapabbatamatthake sasalakkhaṇappaṭimaṇḍitaṃ ekūnapaṇṇāsayojanaṃ candamaṇḍalaṃ addasa. Tato sālavanaṃ olokesi. Tasmiñhi samaye sālarukkhā mūlato paṭṭhāya yāva aggā sabbapāliphullā dukūlapārutā viya, muttākalāpavinaddhā viya ca virociṃsu. Bhūmitalaṃ pupphasantharapūjāya paṭimaṇḍitaṃ viya, tattha tattha nipatantena pupphareṇunā lākhārasena siñcamānaṃ viya ca ahosi. Bhamaramadhukaragaṇā kusumareṇumadamattā upagāyamānā viya vanantaresu vicaranti. Tadā ca uposathadivasova hoti. Atha thero, ‘‘kāya nu kho ajja ratiyā vītināmessāmī’’ti cintesi, ariyasāvakā ca nāma piyadhammassavanā honti. Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘ajja mayhaṃ jeṭṭhabhātikassa dhammasenāpatittherassa santikaṃ gantvā dhammaratiyā vītināmessāmī’’ti. Gacchanto pana ekakova agantvā ‘‘mayhaṃ piyasahāyaṃ mahākassapattheraṃ gahetvā gamissāmī’’ti nisinnaṭṭhānato vuṭṭhāya cammakhaṇḍaṃ papphoṭetvā yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami.

Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito Yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkamī

Evamāvusotikho āyasmā mahākassapoti theropi yasmā piyadhammassavanova ariyasāvako, tasmā tassa vacanaṃ sutvā gacchāvuso, tvaṃ, mayhaṃ sīsaṃ vā rujjati piṭṭhi vāti kiñci lesāpadesaṃ akatvā tuṭṭhahadayova, ‘‘evamāvuso’’tiādimāha. Paṭissutvā ca nisinnaṭṭhānato vuṭṭhāya cammakhaṇḍaṃ papphoṭetvā mahāmoggallānaṃ anubandhi. Tasmiṃ samaye dve mahātherā paṭipāṭiyā ṭhitāni dve candamaṇḍalāni viya, dve sūriyamaṇḍalāni viya, dve chaddantanāgarājāno viya, dve sīhā viya, dve byagghā viya ca virociṃsu. Anuruddhattheropi tasmiṃ samaye divāṭṭhāne nisinno dve mahāthere sāriputtattherassa santikaṃ gacchante disvā pacchimalokadhātuṃ olokento sūriyaṃ vanantaṃ pavisantaṃ viya, pācīnalokadhātuṃ olokento candaṃ vanantato uggacchantaṃ viya, sālavanaṃ olokento sabbapāliphullameva sālavanañca disvā ajja uposathadivaso, ime ca me jeṭṭhabhātikā dhammasenāpatissa santikaṃ gacchanti, mahantena dhammassavanena bhavitabbaṃ, ahampi dhammassavanassa bhāgī bhavissāmīti nisinnaṭṭhānato vuṭṭhāya cammakhaṇḍaṃ papphoṭetvā mahātherānaṃ padānupadiko hutvā nikkhami. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca anuruddho yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsū’’ti. Upasaṅkamiṃsūti. Paṭipāṭiyā ṭhitā tayo candā viya, sūriyā viya, sīhā viya ca virocamānā upasaṅkamiṃsu.

Evamāvusoti kho āyasmā mahākassapo Upasaṅkamiṃsū
commentary_english:
332. Thus have I heard: the Mahāgosiṅga Sūtra.

There, "in the Gosiṅga Sāla-tree-grove," this is said to show the dwelling place.

In other sūtras, "He dwells at Śrāvastī, in Jetavana, in Anāthapiṇḍada's park," thus, first showing the pasture village, afterwards he shows the dwelling place.

In this Mahāgosiṅga Sūtra, however, the Blessed One's pasture village is unfixed; some pasture village or other will exist.

Therefore, the dwelling place itself is thoroughly illuminated.

"It is a forest-based" -- this is the name of the sūtra.

"With many" means with numerous ones.

"Well-known, well-known" means everywhere famous, manifest.

"With elders, with disciples" means with elders who are endowed with dharmas that are firm-making, such as the *prātimokṣa-saṃvara*, and with disciples, because they were born at the end of the *savana*, together in one place.

Now, showing the real form of those elders, he says, "with the venerable Sāriputta," and so on.

There, the venerable Sāriputta is well-known in the Buddha's Dispensation through his qualities, beginning with ethical conduct (*śīla*).

To those with eyes, the sun standing in the midst of the sky is like the moon, and to those standing on the seashore, the ocean is known as manifest.

Not only must his greatness be understood through the power of the qualities that have come in this sutra, but also, from this, the *dhammadāyāda-sūtra*, the *anaṅgaṇa-sūtra*, the *sammādiṭṭhi-sūtra*, the *sīhanāda-sūtra*, the *rathavinīta*, the *mahāhatthipadopama*, the *mahāvedalla*, the *cātuma-sūtra*, the *dīghanakha*, the *anupada-sūtra*, the *sevitabbāsevitabba-sūtra*, the *saccavibhaṅga-sūtra*, the *piṇḍapātapārisuddhi*, the *sampasādanīyaṃ*, the *saṅgīti-sūtra*, the *dasuttarasutta*, the *pavāraṇā-sūtra* (Saṃ.

Ni.
1.
215 and so on), the *susima-sūtra*, the *therapañha-sūtra*, the *mahāniddeso*, the *paṭisambhidāmaggo*, the *therasīhanāda-sūtra*, the *abhinikkhamanaṃ*, the *etadagga*—through the power of even these sūtras, the elder's greatness must be understood.

In the *etadagga*, "This is the foremost, monks, of my disciples, the *bhikkhus* of great wisdom, namely Sāriputta," is said (A.
Ni.
1.
188-189).

Mahāmoggallāna also, through qualities beginning with ethical conduct (*śīla*) and through the qualities that have come in this sutra, is known as an elder, manifest, great.

Moreover, the *anumāna-sūtra*, the *cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhaya-sūtra*, the *māratajjaniya-sūtra*, the *pāsādakampanaṃ*, the complete *iddhipādasaṃyuttaṃ*, the *nandopanandadamanaṃ*, the *yamakapāṭihāriyakāle devalokagamanaṃ*, the *vimānavatthu*, the *petavatthu*, the elder's *abhinikkhamanaṃ*, the *etadagga*—through even these, his greatness must be understood.

In the *etadagga*, "This is the foremost, monks, of my disciples, the *bhikkhus* possessing supernormal power, namely Mahāmoggallāna," is said (A.
Ni.
1.
190).

Mahāmoggallāna

Mahākassapa also, through qualities beginning with ethical conduct (*śīla*) and through the qualities that have come in this sutra, is known as an elder, manifest, great.

Moreover, the *cīvaraparivattana-sūtra*, the *jiṇṇacīvara-sūtra* (Saṃ.
Ni.
2.
154 and so on), the *candopamaṃ*, the complete *kassapasaṃyuttaṃ*, the *mahāariyavaṃsa-sūtra*, the elder's *abhinikkhamanaṃ*, the *etadagga*—through even these, his greatness must be understood.

In the *etadagga*, "This is the foremost, monks, of my disciples, the *bhikkhus* who are advocates of ascetic practices (*dhuta*), namely Mahākassapa," is said (A.
Ni.
1.  191) It is said.

**Mahākassapa:**

**The venerable Anuruddha** was also known and famous as a great elder through qualities such as morality and the qualities that come in this *sutta*. Moreover, his greatness should be understood by way of the *Cūḷagosiṅga Sutta*, the *Naḷakapāna Sutta*, the *Anuttariya Sutta*, the *Upakkilesa Sutta*, the *Anuruddha Saṃyutta*, the *Mahāpurisavitakka Sutta*, the elder's renunciation, and the foremost (*etadagga*). For in the foremost, it is said, “This, monks, is the foremost of my disciples who are monks with the divine eye, namely, Anuruddha” (A. Ni. 1.192).

**The venerable Anuruddha:**

**And by the venerable Revata:** Here, however, there are two Revatas: Khadiravaniyarevata and Kaṅkhārevata. Of these, Khadiravaniyarevata was the younger brother of the *Dhammasenāpati* elder, and he is not intended here. But the elder who is full of doubt, “*Akappa* is *guḷa*, *akappiya* is *muggā*” (Mahāva. 272), is intended here as Revata. He too was known and famous as a great elder through qualities such as morality and the qualities that come in this *sutta*. Moreover, his greatness should be understood by his renunciation and by the foremost (*etadagga*). For in the foremost, it is said, “This, monks, is the foremost of my disciples who are monks who meditate, namely, Kaṅkhārevata” (A. Ni. 1.204).

**And by the venerable Revata:**

**The venerable Ānanda** was also known and famous as a great elder through qualities such as morality and the qualities that come in this *sutta*. Moreover, his greatness should be understood by way of the *Sekkha Sutta*, the *Bāhitika Sutta*, the *Āneñjasappāya*, the *Gopakamoggallāna*, the *Bahudhātuka*, the *Cūḷasuññata*, the *Mahāsuññata*, the *Acchariyabbhuta Sutta*, the *Bhaddekaratta*, the *Mahānidāna*, the *Mahāparinibbāna*, the *Subha Sutta*, the *Cūḷaniyalokadhātusutta*, renunciation, and the foremost (*etadagga*). For in the foremost, it is said, “This, monks, is the foremost of my disciples who are monks who are much learned, namely, Ānanda” (A. Ni. 1.219-223).

**The venerable Ānanda:**

**And by others who were known and recognized:** Not only by these, but the Blessed One dwelt in the *Gosiṅgasālavanadāya* together with other great elders and disciples who were famous for their great qualities. For the venerable Sāriputta himself, being of great wisdom, took many other monks of great wisdom and then dwelt surrounding the ten-powered one. The venerable Mahāmoggallāna himself was powerful, the venerable Mahākassapa himself was an ascetic, the venerable Anuruddha himself had the divine eye, the venerable Revata himself delighted in *jhāna*, the venerable Ānanda himself was much learned, and he took many other much learned monks and then dwelt surrounding the ten-powered one. Thus, at that time, these and other known great elders, about thirty thousand monks, should be understood as dwelling surrounding the ten-powered one.

**And by others who were known and recognized:**

**Having arisen from seclusion:** Having arisen from the seclusion of the fruition attainment.

**He approached the venerable Mahākassapa:** It seems that the elder, having arisen from seclusion, looking at the western world-element, saw the sun-circle, fully fifty yojanas, setting like an earring falling from the ear of a drunkard playing in the forest, like a red blanket being gathered up and put into a box, and like a golden bowl worth a hundred thousand [coins] falling from a jewel-snake's tooth. Then, looking at the eastern world-element, he saw the moon-circle, forty-nine yojanas, decorated with a hare-mark, rising from the ocean's belly of cloud color and on the summit of the eastern *cakkavāḷa* mountain, like a silver wheel being turned around after being grasped at the rim, like a stream of milk coming out of a silver mountain, and like a white swan flapping its wings and leaping into the sky. Then he looked at the *sāla* forest.
At that time, the *sāla* trees, from their roots to their tips, were entirely covered with flowers, shining as if draped in fine cloth (*dukūla*), as if adorned with pearl necklaces.

The surface of the earth was adorned as if for a flower-scattering offering (*puṣpa-saṃthara-pūjā*), and it was as if sprinkled with lac-dye by the pollen falling there and there.

Swarms of bees and *madhukara* were intoxicated by the pollen of the flowers, wandering in the groves as if singing.

And then it was the day of the *uposatha*.

Then the elder thought, "How shall I spend this night?" For noble disciples are known to delight in hearing the Dharma.

Then it occurred to him, "Today, I will go to my elder brother, the *dharma-senāpati-tthera*, and spend the night delighting in the Dharma."

As he was going, instead of going alone, he thought, "I will go and take my dear friend, the *Mahākassapa-tthera*." Rising from his seat, he clapped his outer cloak, approached the venerable Mahākassapa.

Having arisen from seclusion, he approached the venerable Mahākassapa.

"Thus, friend," The elder Mahākassapa, because he was a noble disciple who loved to hear the Dharma, having heard his words, without making any excuse such as, "Go, friend, my head aches or my back hurts," but with a delighted heart, said, "Even so, friend," and so on.

Having agreed, and rising from his seat, clapping his outer cloak, he followed Mahāmoggallāna.

At that time, the two great elders, standing in order, shone like two moons, like two suns, like two *Chaddanta nāga* kings, like two lions, like two tigers.

The venerable Anuruddha, at that time, sitting in his daytime dwelling, seeing the two great elders going to the venerable Sāriputta, looking at the western world-realm, [it was] like the sun entering the forest; looking at the eastern world-realm, [it was] like the moon rising from the forest; looking at the *sāla* grove, and seeing that the entire *sāla* grove was covered in flowers, [he thought,] "Today is the *uposatha* day, and these elder brothers of mine are going to the *dharma-senāpati*, there must be a great discourse on the Dharma. I, too, will partake in the hearing of the Dharma." Rising from his seat, clapping his outer cloak, he followed closely behind the great elders.

Therefore it was said – "Then the venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the venerable Mahākassapa, and the venerable Anuruddha approached the venerable Sāriputta."

They approached.

Standing in order, they approached, shining like three moons, like suns, like lions.

"Thus, friend," The venerable Mahākassapa approached.

mula_pali: 333. Addasā kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantañca revataṃ āyasmantañca ānandaṃ dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etu kho āyasmā ānando! Svāgataṃ āyasmato ānandassa bhagavato upaṭṭhākassa bhagavato santikāvacarassa! Ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso ānanda, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sabbapāliphullā (sī.) sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso ānanda, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti? ‘‘Idhāvuso sāriputta , bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā; kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti, dhātā dhatā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. So catassannaṃ parisānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi anuppabandhehi appabaddhehi (sī. pī.) anusayasamugghātāya. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti.
mula_english:
333. The venerable Sāriputta saw the venerable Revata and the venerable Ānanda coming in the distance.

Having seen the venerable Ānanda, he said this: "Come, venerable Ānanda! Welcome to the venerable Ānanda, the Blessed One's attendant, the Blessed One's constant companion! Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, friend Ānanda, the night is moonlit, the *sāla* trees are all in bloom, divine scents, I think, are blowing; in what way, friend Ānanda, could a *bhikkhu* illuminate Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?"

"Here, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* has learned much, remembers what he has learned, and consolidates what he has learned.

Those teachings that are admirable in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇa*), admirable in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇa*), admirable in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇa*), with the meaning (*sāttha*) and the letter (*sabyañjana*); which proclaim the holy life (*brahmacariya*) that is entirely perfect (*kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ*), surpassingly pure (*parisuddhaṃ*): those teachings he has listened to often, retained, mastered verbally (*vacasā paricitā*), investigated with the mind (*manasānupekkhitā*), and well-penetrated in terms of his views (*diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā*).

And he teaches the *dharma* to the four assemblies with well-rounded (*parimaṇḍalehi*) and coherent statements and phrases (*padabyañjanehi anuppabandhehi*) for the eradication of the underlying tendencies (*anusayasamugghātāya*).

That kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood."
commentary_pali:
333. Evaṃ upasaṅkamante pana te mahāthere āyasmā ānando attano divāṭṭhāne nisinnoyeva disvā, ‘‘ajja mahantaṃ dhammassavanaṃ bhavissati, mayāpi tassa bhāginā bhavitabbaṃ, na kho pana ekakova gamissāmi, mayhaṃ piyasahāyampi revatattheraṃ gahetvā gamissāmī’’ti sabbaṃ mahāmoggallānassa mahākassapassa anuruddhassa upasaṅkamane vuttanayeneva vitthārato veditabbaṃ.
