Iti te dve janā paṭipāṭiyā ṭhitā dve candā viya, sūriyā viya, sīhā viya ca virocamānā upasaṅkamiṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘addasā kho āyasmā sāriputto’’tiādi . Disvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocāti dūratova disvā anukkamena kathāupacāraṃ sampattametaṃ, ‘‘etu kho āyasmā’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Ramaṇīyaṃ, āvusoti ettha duvidhaṃ rāmaṇeyyakaṃ vanarāmaṇeyyakaṃ puggalarāmaṇeyyakañca. Tattha vanaṃ nāma nāgasalaḷasālacampakādīhi sañchannaṃ hoti bahalacchāyaṃ pupphaphalūpagaṃ vividharukkhaṃ udakasampannaṃ gāmato nissaṭaṃ, idaṃ vanarāmaṇeyyakaṃ nāma. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ –

‘‘Ramaṇīyāni araññāni, yattha na ramatī jano;

Vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino’’ti. (dha. pa. 99);

Vanaṃ pana sacepi ujjaṅgale hoti nirudakaṃ viralacchāyaṃ kaṇṭakasamākiṇṇaṃ, buddhādayopettha ariyā viharanti, idaṃ puggalarāmaṇeyyakaṃ nāma. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ –

‘‘Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, ninne vā yadi vā thale;

Yattha arahanto viharanti, taṃ bhūmirāmaṇeyyaka’’nti. (dha. pa. 98);

Idha pana taṃ duvidhampi labbhati. Tadā hi gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sabbapāliphullaṃ hoti kusumagandhasugandhaṃ, sadevake cettha loke aggapuggalo sammāsambuddho tiṃsasahassamattehi abhiññātabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ viharati. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso ānanda, gosiṅgasālavana’’nti.

Dosināti dosāpagatā, abbhaṃ mahikā dhūmo rajo rāhūti imehi pañcahi upakkilesehi virahitāti vuttaṃ hoti. Sabbapāliphullāti sabbattha pāliphullā, mūlato paṭṭhāya yāva aggā apupphitaṭṭhānaṃ nāma natthi. Dibbā maññe gandhā sampavantīti dibbā mandārapupphakoviḷārapāricchattakacandanacuṇṇagandhā viya samantā pavāyanti, sakkasuyāsantusitanimmānaratiparanimmitamahābrahmānaṃ otiṇṇaṭṭhānaṃ viya vāyantīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Dosinā Sabbapāliphullā Dibbā maññe gandhā sampavantī

Kathaṃrūpena, āvuso ānandāti ānandatthero tesaṃ pañcannaṃ therānaṃ saṅghanavakova. Kasmā thero taṃyeva paṭhamaṃ pucchatīti? Mamāyitattā. Te hi dve therā aññamaññaṃ mamāyiṃsu. Sāriputtatthero, ‘‘mayā kattabbaṃ satthu upaṭṭhānaṃ karotī’’ti ānandattheraṃ mamāyi. Ānandatthero bhagavato sāvakānaṃ aggoti sāriputtattheraṃ mamāyi, kuladārake pabbājetvā sāriputtattherassa santike upajjhaṃ gaṇhāpesi. Sāriputtattheropi tatheva akāsi. Evaṃ ekamekena attano pattacīvaraṃ datvā pabbājetvā upajjhaṃ gaṇhāpitāni pañca bhikkhusatāni ahesuṃ. Āyasmā ānando paṇītāni cīvarādīnipi labhitvā therasseva deti.

Kathaṃrūpena āvuso ānandā

Eko kira brāhmaṇo cintesi – ‘‘buddharatanassa ca saṅgharatanassa ca pūjā paññāyati, kathaṃ nu kho dhammaratanaṃ pūjitaṃ nāma hotī’’ti? So bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchi. Bhagavā āha – ‘‘sacesi, brāhmaṇa, dhammaratanaṃ pūjitukāmo, ekaṃ bahussutaṃ pūjehī’’ti bahussutaṃ, bhante, ācikkhathāti bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pucchati. So bhikkhusaṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bahussutaṃ, bhante, ācikkhathāti āha. Ānandatthero brāhmaṇāti. Brāhmaṇo theraṃ sahassagghanikena cīvarena pūjesi. Thero taṃ gahetvā bhagavato santikaṃ agamāsi. Bhagavā ‘‘kuto, ānanda, laddha’’nti āha. Ekena, bhante, brāhmaṇena dinnaṃ, idaṃ panāhaṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa dātukāmoti. Dehi, ānandāti. Cārikaṃ pakkanto, bhanteti. Āgatakāle dehīti. Sikkhāpadaṃ, bhante, paññattanti. Kadā pana sāriputto āgamissatīti? Dasāhamattena, bhanteti. ‘‘Anujānāmi, ānanda, dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ nikkhipitu’’nti (pārā. 461; mahāva. 347) sikkhāpadaṃ paññapesi. Sāriputtattheropi tatheva yaṃkiñci manāpaṃ labhati, taṃ ānandattherassa deti. Evaṃ te therā aññamaññaṃ mamāyiṃsu, iti mamāyitattā paṭhamaṃ pucchi.

Apica anumatipucchā nāmesā khuddakato paṭṭhāya pucchitabbā hoti. Tasmā thero cintesi – ‘‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ ānandaṃ pucchissāmi, ānando attano paṭibhānaṃ byākarissati. Tato revataṃ, anuruddhaṃ, mahākassapaṃ, mahāmoggallānaṃ pucchissāmi. Mahāmoggallāno attano paṭibhānaṃ byākarissati. Tato pañcapi therā maṃ pucchissanti, ahampi attano paṭibhānaṃ byākarissāmī’’ti. Ettāvatāpi ayaṃ dhammadesanā sikhāppattā vepullappattā na bhavissati, atha mayaṃ sabbepi dasabalaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma, satthā sabbaññutaññāṇena byākarissati. Ettāvatā ayaṃ dhammadesanā sikhāppattā vepullappattā bhavissati. Yathā hi janapadamhi uppanno aṭṭo gāmabhojakaṃ pāpuṇāti, tasmiṃ nicchituṃ asakkonte janapadabhojakaṃ pāpuṇāti, tasmiṃ asakkonte mahāvinicchayaamaccaṃ, tasmiṃ asakkonte senāpatiṃ, tasmiṃ asakkonte uparājaṃ, tasmiṃ vinicchituṃ asakkonte rājānaṃ pāpuṇāti, raññā vinicchitakālato paṭṭhāya aṭṭo aparāparaṃ na sañcarati, rājavacaneneva chijjati. Evamevaṃ ahañhi paṭhamaṃ ānandaṃ pucchissāmi…pe… atha mayaṃ sabbepi dasabalaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma, satthā sabbaññutaññāṇena byākarissati. Ettāvatā ayaṃ dhammadesanā sikhāppattā vepullappattā bhavissati. Evaṃ anumatipucchaṃ pucchanto thero paṭhamaṃ ānandattheraṃ pucchi.

Bahussuto hotīti bahu assa sutaṃ hoti, navaṅgaṃ satthusāsanaṃ pāḷianusandhipubbāparavasena uggahitaṃ hotīti attho. Sutadharoti sutassa ādhārabhūto. Yassa hi ito gahitaṃ ito palāyati, chiddaghaṭe udakaṃ viya na tiṭṭhati, parisamajjhe ekaṃ suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā kathetuṃ vā vācetuṃ vā na sakkoti, ayaṃ na sutadharo nāma. Yassa pana uggahitaṃ buddhavacanaṃ uggahitakālasadisameva hoti, dasapi vīsatipi vassāni sajjhāyaṃ akarontassa na nassati, ayaṃ sutadharo nāma. Sutasannicayoti sutassa sannicayabhūto. Yathā hi sutaṃ hadayamañjūsāya sannicitaṃ silāyaṃ lekhā viya, suvaṇṇaghaṭe pakkhittasīhavasā viya ca ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati, ayaṃ sutasannicayo nāma. Dhātāti ṭhitā paguṇā. Ekaccassa hi uggahitaṃ buddhavacanaṃ dhātaṃ paguṇaṃ niccalitaṃ na hoti, asukasuttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā kathehīti vutte sajjhāyitvā saṃsanditvā samanuggāhitvā jānissāmīti vadati. Ekaccassa dhātaṃ paguṇaṃ bhavaṅgasotasadisaṃ hoti, asukasuttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā kathehīti vutte uddharitvā tameva katheti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘dhātā’’ti.

Bahussuto hotī Sutadharo na sutadharo sutadharo Sutasannicayo sutasannicayo Dhātā

Vacasā paricitāti suttadasaka-vaggadasaka-paṇṇāsadasakānaṃ vasena vācāya sajjhāyitā. Manasānupekkhitāti cittena anupekkhitā, yassa vācāya sajjhāyitaṃ buddhavacanaṃ manasā cintentassa tattha tattha pākaṭaṃ hoti. Mahādīpaṃ jāletvā ṭhitassa rūpagataṃ viya paññāyati. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā’’ti. Diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhāti atthato ca kāraṇato ca paññāya suppaṭividdhā. Parimaṇḍalehipadabyañjanehīti ettha padameva atthassa byañjanato padabyañjanaṃ, taṃ akkharapāripūriṃ katvā dasavidhabyañjanabuddhiyo aparihāpetvā vuttaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ nāma hoti, evarūpehi padabyañjanehīti attho. Apica yo bhikkhu parisati dhammaṃ desento suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā nikkhapitvā aññaṃ upārambhakaraṃ suttaṃ āharati, tassa upamaṃ katheti, tadatthaṃ ohāreti, evamidaṃ gahetvā ettha khipanto ekapasseneva pariharanto kālaṃ ñatvā vuṭṭhahati. Nikkhittasuttaṃ pana nikkhattamattameva hoti, tassa kathā aparimaṇḍalā nāma hoti. Yo pana suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā nikkhipitvā bahi ekapadampi agantvā pāḷiyā anusandhiñca pubbāparañca amakkhento ācariyehi dinnanaye ṭhatvā tulikāya paricchindanto viya, gambhīramātikāya udakaṃ pesento viya, padaṃ koṭṭento sindhavājānīyo viya gacchati, tassa kathā parimaṇḍalā nāma hoti. Evarūpiṃ kathaṃ sandhāya – ‘‘parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehī’’ti vuttaṃ.

Vacasā paricitā Manasānupekkhitā Diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā Parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehī

Anuppabandhehīti ettha yo bhikkhu dhammaṃ kathento suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā ārabhitvā āraddhakālato paṭṭhāya turitaturito araṇiṃ manthento viya, uṇhakhādanīyaṃ khādanto viya, pāḷiyā anusandhipubbāparesu gahitaṃ gahitameva aggahitaṃ aggahitameva ca katvā purāṇapaṇṇantaresu caramānaṃ godhaṃ uṭṭhapento viya tattha tattha paharanto osāpento ohāya gacchati. Yopi dhammaṃ kathento kālena sīghaṃ kālena dandhaṃ kālena mahāsaddaṃ kālena khuddakasaddaṃ karoti. Yathā petaggi kālena jalati, kālena nibbāyati, evameva idha petaggidhammakathiko nāma hoti, parisāya uṭṭhātukāmāya punappunaṃ ārabhati. Yopi kathento tattha tattha vitthāyati, nitthunanto kandanto viya katheti, imesaṃ sabbesampi kathā appabandhā nāma hoti. Yo pana suttaṃ ārabhitvā ācariyehi dinnanaye ṭhito acchinnadhāraṃ katvā nadīsotaṃ viya pavatteti, ākāsagaṅgato bhassamānaṃ udakaṃ viya nirantaraṃ kathaṃ pavatteti, tassa kathā anuppabandhā hoti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘anuppabandhehī’’ti. Anusayasamugghātāyāti sattannaṃ anusayānaṃ samugghātatthāya. Evarūpenāti evarūpena bahussutena bhikkhunā tathārūpeneva bhikkhusatena bhikkhusahassena vā saṅghāṭikaṇṇena vā saṅghāṭikaṇṇaṃ, pallaṅkena vā pallaṅkaṃ āhacca nisinnena gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyya. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo.

Anuppabandhehī petaggidhammakathiko Anusayasamugghātāyā Evarūpenā
commentary_english:
333. Thus, as those great elders were approaching, the venerable Ānanda, sitting in his daytime dwelling, seeing them, [thought,] "Today there will be a great Dhamma talk. I too must be a partaker in it. I will not go alone. I will take my dear friend the venerable Revata and go." All of this should be understood in detail in the same way as was said in the approach of Mahāmoggallāna, Mahākassapa, and Anuruddha.

Thus those two people, standing in order, shining like two moons, like suns, and like lions, approached.

Therefore it was said, "The venerable Śāriputta saw," etc.

"Having seen the venerable Ānanda, he said this" means having seen him from afar, and this was accomplished by a gradual courteous conversation, "Come, venerable one," etc., he said these words.

"Ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso" means here there are two kinds of delightfulness: delightfulness of the forest and delightfulness of the person.

There, a forest, namely, covered with Nāga trees, Salaḷa trees, Sāla trees, Campaka trees, etc., having thick shade, frequented by flowers and fruits, having various trees, rich in water, set apart from the village, this is called delightfulness of the forest.

Referring to that it was said:

"Delightful are the forests, where the people do not delight; the passionless will delight, not those who seek sensual pleasures." (Dha. Pa. 99);

But a forest, even if it is in a remote place, waterless, having thin shade, crowded with thorns, if Buddhas and other noble ones dwell there, this is called delightfulness of the person.

Referring to that it was said:

"Whether in a village or in a forest, in a valley or on a hill, wherever arahants dwell, that land is delightful." (Dha. Pa. 98);

Here, however, both of these are obtained.

At that time, indeed, the Gosiṅga Sāla forest was entirely covered with Pāli flowers, having the fragrance of flowers, and the foremost person, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, dwells there with thirty thousand well-known monks together with the world of gods.

Referring to that it was said: "Delightful, friend Ānanda, is the Gosiṅga Sāla forest."

"Dosinā" means free from faults, it is said to be free from these five defilements: cloud, mist, smoke, dust, and Rāhu.

"Sabbapāliphullā" means everywhere covered with Pāli flowers, there is no place without flowers from the root up to the tip.

"Dibbā maññe gandhā sampavantī" means divine fragrances of Mandāra flowers, Koviḷāra flowers, Pāricchattaka flowers, and Candana powder, spread around, like a place attained by Sakka, Suyāma, Santusita, Nimmānarati, and Paranimmita Mahābrahmā, it is said.

"Dosinā Sabbapāliphullā Dibbā maññe gandhā sampavantī Kathaṃrūpena", friend Ānanda, means Ānanda Thera was only a novice in the Sangha of those five Theras.

Why does the Thera ask him first? Because of affection.

Indeed, those two Theras cherished each other.

Sāriputta Thera cherished Ānanda Thera, [thinking,] "The attendance on the Teacher must be done by me."

Ānanda Thera cherished Sāriputta Thera, [thinking,] "He is the foremost of the Blessed One's disciples," having ordained young men from good families, he had them accept him as their preceptor in the presence of Sāriputta Thera.

Sāriputta Thera also did likewise.

Thus, having given their own bowl and robe, having ordained [them], and having had [them] accept [him] as their preceptor, there were five hundred monks.

The venerable Ānanda, having obtained excellent robes etc., gives [them] to the Thera himself.

"Kathaṃrūpena Āvuso Ānandā"

A certain brahmin thought: "The worship of the Buddha Jewel and the Sangha Jewel is known, but how indeed is the Dhamma Jewel worshipped?" So he approached the Blessed One and asked this matter.

The Blessed One said: "If, brahmin, you wish to worship the Dhamma Jewel, worship one who is very learned." "Tell me, venerable one, who is very learned," he asks the Sangha of monks.

So he approached the Sangha of monks and said: "Tell me, venerable ones, who is very learned."The Elder Ānanda [was] with the Brahman.
The Brahman honored the Elder with a cloth worth a thousand [coins].
The Elder took it and went to the Blessed One's presence.
The Blessed One said, "From where, Ānanda, [was this] obtained?"
"Venerable Sir, it was given by a certain Brahman; I intend to give this to the venerable Śāriputta."
"Give [it], Ānanda."
"He has departed for a journey, venerable sir."
"Give [it to him] when he returns."
"A precept, venerable sir, has been established."
"When, then, will Śāriputta come?" "In ten days approximately, venerable sir."
"I allow, Ānanda, that an extra robe may be kept for up to ten days" (Pārā.
461; Mahāva.
347). He established a precept.
The Elder Śāriputta also, in the same way, whatever is pleasing that he obtains, he gives that to the Elder Ānanda.
Thus, those elders cherished one another; thus, because of that cherishing, he asked first.

Moreover, this request for permission should be asked beginning from a young age.
Therefore, the Elder thought, "I will first ask Ānanda; Ānanda will explain his insight.
Then I will ask Revata, Anuruddha, Mahākassapa, and Mahāmoggallāna.
Mahāmoggallāna will explain his insight.
Then the five elders will ask me, and I also will explain my insight."
Even with this, this teaching of the Dhamma will not reach the peak [of understanding], will not attain abundance; then, we all, approaching the One with Ten Powers, will ask; the Teacher will explain with the knowledge of omniscience.
With just this, this teaching of the Dhamma will reach the peak, will attain abundance.
Just as, indeed, in a district, a dispute that has arisen reaches the village headman; if he is unable to decide it, it reaches the district headman; if he is unable, [it reaches] the great judging minister; if he is unable, [it reaches] the commander of the army; if he is unable, [it reaches] the viceroy; if he is unable to decide it, [it reaches] the king; from the time of the decision by the king, the dispute does not circulate further; it is cut off by the king's word itself.
Just so, I will first ask Ānanda... and so on... then, we all, approaching the One with Ten Powers, will ask; the Teacher will explain with the knowledge of omniscience.
Just with this, this teaching of the Dhamma will reach the peak, will attain abundance.
Thus, asking for permission, the Elder first asked the Elder Ānanda.

<hi rend="bold">He is very learned</hi> means he has heard much, the Teacher's teaching, with its nine parts, is well-grasped in accordance with the sequence of the text and the preceding and following [context]; this is the meaning.
<hi rend="bold">Sutadhara</hi> means he is the support of what is heard.
For, if what is grasped here flees from here, it does not remain like water in a leaky pot; in the middle of the assembly, he is not able to tell or recite a discourse or a Jātaka; this is called <hi rend="bold">not a Sutadhara</hi>.
But for whom the Buddha's word that is grasped is just like the time it was grasped, even if he does not recite [it] for ten or twenty years, it does not perish; this is called <hi rend="bold">Sutadhara</hi>.
<hi rend="bold">Sutasannicaya</hi> means he is a collection of what is heard.
Just as what is heard, collected in the heart's casket, stands firmly like a line on stone, like ghee from a lion in a golden pot, this is called <hi rend="bold">Sutasannicaya</hi>.
<hi rend="bold">Dhātā</hi> means he is firm [and] skilled.
For some, the Buddha's word that is grasped is not firm, skilled, [or] unmoving; when it is said, "Tell such-and-such a discourse or a Jātaka," having recited, having compared, having taught, he says, "I will know."
For one, the qualities are suitable, like the continuity of existence; when asked to tell a certain *sutta* or *jātaka*, he brings it to mind and tells just that.

This is said with reference to that: “he is a speaker.”

He has learned much, remembers what he has learned, does not remember what he has learned, remembers what he has learned, consolidates what he has learned, consolidates what he has learned, he is a speaker.

"Familiar with speech" means reciting the texts by means of the *sutta* decade, the category decade, the fifty decade.

"Not regarded in the mind" means not regarded by the mind; the Buddha's word that is recited by his speech becomes apparent there and there to one thinking about it in his mind.

Having lit a great lamp, it appears as if it has taken form.

This is said with reference to that: "Familiar with speech, not regarded in the mind."

"Thoroughly penetrated by view" means thoroughly penetrated by wisdom from the meaning and from the cause.

"With well-rounded..." Because the expression is made complete by the words and syllables, it's well-rounded. The meaning is that it is called well-rounded when the ten kinds of expression-related understandings are made without loss, having made the completion of the syllables.

Moreover, when a *bhikkhu* teaching the *dharma* dismisses a *sutta* or *jātaka* and brings forward another *sutta* that causes vexation, he tells a comparison, he sets forth its meaning, and taking this, throwing it in here, only avoiding one side, knowing the time, he rises.

However, the dismissed *sutta* is only as much as dismissed; his talk is called not well-rounded.

But when someone, dismissing a *sutta* or *jātaka*, without going outside even one word, not confusing the connection and the before and after of the *pāḷi*, standing in the manner given by the teachers, as if cutting around with a brush, as if sending water with a deep matrix, as if pounding a word, goes like a thoroughbred Sindh horse, his talk is called well-rounded.

With what kind of talk in mind was it said: "with well-rounded words and expressions"?

Familiar with speech, not regarded in the mind, thoroughly penetrated by view, with well-rounded words and expressions...

"With continuous connection..." Here, when a *bhikkhu* telling the *dharma* begins a *sutta* or *jātaka*, from the time of beginning onwards, quickly, quickly, as if churning fire with a fire-stick, as if eating hot food, grasping what is grasped in the connection before and after of the *pāḷi* as grasped, and what is ungrasped as ungrasped, striking there and there, wearing out, abandoning, he goes away.

Also, someone telling the *dharma* sometimes quickly, sometimes slowly, sometimes loudly, sometimes makes a small sound.

Just as a cremation fire sometimes burns, sometimes goes out, just so here he is called a speaker on the petaggi-dharma, he repeatedly begins for the assembly desiring to rise.

Also, someone speaking spreads out there and there, as if scolding, weeping, he speaks; the talk of all of these is called unconnected.

But someone beginning a *sutta*, standing in the manner given by the teachers, making an unbroken stream, as if causing a river's flow, as if constantly causing water flowing from the Ākāśa-ganga, his talk has continuous connection.

This was said with reference to that: "with continuous connection".

"For the eradication of predispositions" means for the purpose of eradicating the seven predispositions.

"With such-and-such a form" means with such-and-such a form, a learned *bhikkhu*, just as such-and-such a hundred *bhikkhus* or a thousand *bhikkhus*, with the corner of a robe rubbing against the corner of a robe, or with a seat rubbing against a seat, sitting down, would adorn the Gosinga Sal Forest.

In this way, the meaning in all cases should be understood.

mula_pali: 334. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavoca – ‘‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso revata, āyasmatā ānandena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ revataṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso revata, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso revata, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti? ‘‘Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu paṭisallānārāmo hoti paṭisallānarato, ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno, vipassanāya samannāgato, brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti.
mula_english: When this was said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the venerable Revata thus: “Friend Revata, the venerable Ānanda has spoken according to his own inspiration. Now, we ask the venerable Revata: ‘Friend Revata, the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, the night is moonlit, the Sāla trees are all in full bloom, and heavenly scents, I think, are wafting about. What kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Revata, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’” “Here, friend Śāriputra, a *bhikkhu* delights in seclusion, is devoted to seclusion, is committed to inner tranquility of mind, has not rejected *jhāna*, is endowed with *vipassanā*, and develops empty dwellings. That kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Śāriputra, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.”
commentary_pali: 334. Paṭisallānaṃ assa ārāmoti paṭisallānārāmo. Paṭisallāne ratoti paṭisallānarato.
commentary_english: 334. *Paṭisallānaṃ* *assa* *ārāmoti* *paṭisallānārāmo*. *Paṭisallāne* *ratoti* *paṭisallānarato*.

mula_pali: 335. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso anuruddha, āyasmatā revatena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso anuruddha, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso anuruddha, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti? ‘‘Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi. Seyyathāpi, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhumā puriso uparipāsādavaragato sahassaṃ nemimaṇḍalānaṃ volokeyya; evameva kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti.
mula_english: When this was said, the venerable Sāriputta addressed the venerable Anuruddha thus: “Friend Anuruddha, the venerable Revata has spoken according to his own inspiration ( *yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ*). Now we ask the venerable Anuruddha: ‘Friend Anuruddha, Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, it is a moonlit night, the Sāla trees are all in full bloom, I think divine fragrances are wafting; in what way could a bhikkhu illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’” “Here, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), which is purified and surpasses the human, surveys a thousand worlds. Just as a man with good sight, when he has ascended to the upper palace chamber, might survey a thousand wheel-rims, so too, friend Sāriputta, with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), which is purified and surpasses the human, a *bhikkhu* surveys a thousand worlds. That kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.”
commentary_pali: 335.Sahassaṃlokānanti sahassaṃ lokadhātūnaṃ. Ettakañhi therassa dhuvasevanaṃ āvajjanapaṭibaddhaṃ, ākaṅkhamāno pana thero anekānipi cakkavāḷasahassāni voloketiyeva. Uparipāsādavaragatoti sattabhūmakassa vā navabhūmakassa vā pāsādavarassa upari gato. Sahassaṃ nemimaṇḍalānaṃ volokeyyāti pāsādapariveṇe nābhiyā patiṭṭhitānaṃ nemivaṭṭiyā nemivaṭṭiṃ āhacca ṭhitānaṃ nemimaṇḍalānaṃ sahassaṃ vātapānaṃ vivaritvā olokeyya, tassa nābhiyopi pākaṭā honti, arāpi arantarānipi nemiyopi. Evameva kho, āvusoti, āvuso, evaṃ ayampi dibbacakkhuko bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi. Tassa pāsāde ṭhitapurisassa cakkanābhiyo viya cakkavāḷasahasse sinerusahassaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti. Arā viya dīpā pākaṭā honti. Arantarāni viya dīpaṭṭhitamanussā pākaṭā honti. Nemiyo viya cakkavāḷapabbatā pākaṭā honti.
commentary_english: " *sahassaṃ lokāna* means a thousand world-spheres. For the elder, this much is constantly connected with attending [to things] and considering [them]; but if the elder wishes, he may look upon even many thousands of world-spheres. *uparipāsādavaragato* means gone to the top of a superior palace of seven or nine stories. *sahassaṃ nemimaṇḍalānaṃ volokeyya* means he might open a thousand windows in the palace enclosure, where the wheel-circles are established at the navel, striking rim against rim, and look out; the hubs of those [windows] become evident to him, as do the spokes, the spaces between the spokes, and the rims. *evameva kho, āvuso* means, friend, just so, this bhikkhu with the divine eye, by means of the divine eye that transcends the human, looks upon a thousand worlds. To that man standing in the palace, a thousand Mount Merus in a thousand world-spheres become evident, like the hubs of wheels. The continents become evident, like the spokes. The humans dwelling on the continents become evident, like the spaces between the spokes. The world-mountains become evident, like the rims.

mula_pali: 336. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso kassapa, āyasmatā anuruddhena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso kassapa, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso kassapa, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti? ‘‘Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu attanā ca āraññiko hoti āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca piṇḍapātiko hoti piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paṃsukūliko hoti paṃsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca tecīvariko hoti tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca appiccho hoti appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca santuṭṭho hoti santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca pavivitto hoti pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho hoti asaṃsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca āraddhavīriyo hoti vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca sīlasampanno hoti sīlasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca samādhisampanno hoti samādhisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paññāsampanno hoti paññāsampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttisampanno hoti vimuttisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta , bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus, when this was said, the venerable Sāriputta said to the venerable Mahākassapa: “Friend Kassapa, the venerable Anuruddha has spoken according to his own inspiration.

Now we ask the venerable Mahākassapa: ‘Friend Kassapa, the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, the night is moonlit, the *sāla* trees are all in blossom, and heavenly scents seem to be floating in the air. What kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Kassapa, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’”

“Here, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* is a forest-dweller (*āraññika*) himself and speaks in praise of forest dwelling (*āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī*), is an alms-food eater (*piṇḍapātika*) himself and speaks in praise of alms-food eating, is a rag-robe wearer (*paṃsukūlika*) himself and speaks in praise of rag-robe wearing, is a triple-rober (*tecīvarika*) himself and speaks in praise of being a triple-rober, is of few desires (*appiccho*) himself and speaks in praise of having few desires, is content (*santuṭṭho*) himself and speaks in praise of contentment, is secluded (*pavivitto*) himself and speaks in praise of seclusion, is unassociated (*asaṃsaṭṭho*) himself and speaks in praise of unassociation, is energetic (*āraddhavīriyo*) himself and speaks in praise of the instigation of energy, is accomplished in virtue (*sīlasampanno*) himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in virtue (*sīlasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī*), is accomplished in concentration (*samādhisampanno*) himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in concentration (*samādhisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī*), is accomplished in wisdom (*paññāsampanno*) himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in wisdom (*paññāsampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī*), is accomplished in liberation (*vimuttisampanno*) himself and speaks in praise of accomplishment in liberation (*vimuttisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī*), has attained to the knowledge and vision of deliverance (*vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno*) himself and speaks in praise of the attainment of the knowledge and vision of deliverance.

That kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Sāriputta, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.”
commentary_pali: 336.Āraññikoti samādiṇṇaaraññadhutaṅgo. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.
commentary_english: "āraññiko" means one who has undertaken the ascetic practice of dwelling in the forest (āraññadhutaṅgo). And so with the other words (sesapadesupi) (esseva nayo).

mula_pali: 337. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso moggallāna, āyasmatā mahākassapena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso moggallāna, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti? ‘‘Idhāvuso sāriputta, dve bhikkhū abhidhammakathaṃ kathenti, te aññamaññaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, aññamaññassa pañhaṃ puṭṭhā vissajjenti, no ca saṃsādenti saṃsārenti (ka.), dhammī ca nesaṃ kathā pavattinī hoti. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti.
mula_english:
When this was said, the venerable Sāriputta said to the venerable Mahā Moggallāna: “Friend Moggallāna, the venerable Mahā Kassapa has spoken according to his own inspiration ( *yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ*). Now, let us ask the venerable Mahā Moggallāna: ‘Friend Moggallāna, the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, the night is moonlit, the *sāla* trees are all in full bloom, and heavenly scents, I think, are wafting about. In what way, friend Moggallāna, could a *bhikkhu* illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’

“Here, friend Sāriputta, two *bhikkhus* are giving a discourse on the Abhidhamma. They ask each other questions, and questioned by each other, they explain, but they do not cause doubt, and their talk is in accordance with the Dharma. In that way, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.”
commentary_pali: 337.No ca saṃsādentīti na osādenti. Sahetukañhi sakāraṇaṃ katvā pañhaṃ pucchituṃ vissajjitumpi asakkonto saṃsādeti nāma. Evaṃ na karontīti attho. Pavattinī hotīti nadīsotodakaṃ viya pavattati.
commentary_english:
They do not cause to break down, thus they do not sink down.

Indeed, having made a question with a cause ( *sahetuka*) and with a reason (*sakāraṇaṃ*), someone who is unable to ask the question or to answer it causes to break down, it is said.

Thus, they do not do (*karonti*) this, this is the meaning (*attho*).

"She is flowing" (*pavattinī hotī*), that is, she flows like river water (*nadīsotodakaṃ viya pavattati*).

mula_pali: 338. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso sāriputta, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ pucchāma – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti? ‘‘Idhāvuso moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti, no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ majjhantikasamayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Seyyathāpi, āvuso moggallāna, rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā nānārattānaṃ dussānaṃ dussakaraṇḍako pūro assa. So yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupeyya. Evameva kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti, no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Evarūpena kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti.
mula_english:
338. Then the venerable Mahā Moggallāna addressed the venerable Sāriputta, saying: “Friend Sāriputta, we have all spoken according to our own inspiration.

Now we ask the venerable Sāriputta: ‘Friend Sāriputta, the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, it is a moonlit night, the Sālas are all in full bloom, divine scents seem to be blowing by. What kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Sāriputta, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’”

“Here, friend Moggallāna, a *bhikkhu* wields mastery over his mind, he does not let the mind wield mastery over him.

In the morning he abides in whatever abiding or attainment (*vihārasamāpatti*) he wants to abide in during the morning; at midday he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in at midday; in the evening he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the evening.

Suppose, friend Moggallāna, a king or a king’s minister had a chest full of variously coloured garments.

In the morning he could put on whatever pair of garments he wanted to put on in the morning; at midday he could put on whatever pair of garments he wanted to put on at midday; in the evening he could put on whatever pair of garments he wanted to put on in the evening.

So too, friend Moggallāna, a *bhikkhu* wields mastery over his mind, he does not let the mind wield mastery over him.

In the morning he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the morning; at midday he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in at midday; in the evening he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the evening.

That kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.”
commentary_pali: 338.Yāyavihārasamāpattiyāti yāya lokiyāya vihārasamāpattiyā, yāya lokuttarāya vihārasamāpattiyā.
commentary_english: For, namely, that absorption in abiding (*vihārasamāpatti*)—namely, that worldly (*lokiya*) absorption in abiding, that supramundane (*lokuttara*) absorption in abiding.

mula_pali: 339. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto te āyasmante etadavoca – ‘‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Āyāmāvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ bhagavato ārocessāma. Yathā no bhagavā byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te āyasmanto āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Atha kho te āyasmanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantañca revataṃ āyasmantañca ānandaṃ dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘etu kho āyasmā ānando! Svāgataṃ āyasmato ānandassa bhagavato upaṭṭhākassa bhagavato santikāvacarassa! Ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso ānanda, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti; kathaṃrūpena, āvuso ānanda, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā ānando maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso, sāriputta, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo…pe… anusayasamugghātāya. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yathā taṃ ānandova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Ānando hi, sāriputta, bahussuto sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā; kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti, dhātā, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. So catassannaṃ parisānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi anuppabandhehi anusayasamugghātāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
339. Then the venerable Sāriputta addressed those venerable ones thus: “Friends, we have all spoken according to our own inspiration.

Come, friends, let us go to where the Blessed One is; having gone there, we shall report this matter to the Blessed One. As the Blessed One explains it to us, so we shall bear it in mind.”

“Yes, friend,” the venerable ones replied to venerable Sāriputta.

Then those venerable ones went to the Blessed One; and after paying homage to the Blessed One, they sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, the venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I saw the venerable Revata and the venerable Ānanda coming from afar.

Having seen the venerable Ānanda, I said to him: ‘Come, venerable Ānanda! Welcome to venerable Ānanda, the Blessed One’s attendant, the Blessed One’s constant companion! Delightful, friend Ānanda, is the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood, the night is moonlit, the sāla trees are all in full bloom, heavenly, I think, are the scents wafting around; in what way, friend Ānanda, could a *bhikkhu* illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Ānanda said to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* has learned much, remembers what he has learned…for the eradication of the underlying tendencies.

That kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.’

“Good, good, Sāriputta! Ānanda, speaking rightly, should speak just as he did.

For Ānanda, Sāriputta, has learned much, remembers what he has learned, and consolidates what he has learned.

Those teachings that are good in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇā*), good in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇā*), and good in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇā*), with the right meaning and phrasing (*sātthā sabyañjanā*); which proclaim the perfectly complete and pure holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*)—such teachings as these he has learned much of, retained in mind, recited verbally (*vacasā paricitā*), mentally investigated (*manasānupekkhitā*), and penetrated well by view (*diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā*).

He teaches the *Dhamma* to the four assemblies with well-rounded and coherent statements and phrases (*parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi anuppabandhehi*) for the eradication of the underlying tendencies (*anusayasamugghātāyā*).”
commentary_pali: 339.Sādhu sādhu sāriputtāti ayaṃ sādhukāro ānandattherassa dinno. Sāriputtattherena pana saddhiṃ bhagavā ālapati. Esa nayo sabbattha. Yathā taṃ ānandovāti yathā ānandova sammā byākaraṇamāno byākareyya, evaṃ byākataṃ ānandena attano anucchavikameva, ajjhāsayānurūpameva byākatanti attho. Ānandatthero hi attanāpi bahussuto, ajjhāsayopissa evaṃ hoti – ‘‘aho vata sāsane sabrahmacārī bahussutā bhaveyyu’’nti. Kasmā? Bahussutassa hi kappiyākappiyaṃ sāvajjānavajjaṃ, garukalahukaṃ satekicchātekicchaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti. Bahussuto uggahitabuddhavacanaṃ āvajjitvā imasmiṃ ṭhāne sīlaṃ kathitaṃ, imasmiṃ samādhi, imasmiṃ vipassanā, imasmiṃ maggaphalanibbānānīti sīlassa āgataṭṭhāne sīlaṃ pūretvā, samādhissa āgataṭṭhāne samādhiṃ pūretvā vipassanāya āgataṭṭhāne vipassanāgabbhaṃ gaṇhāpetvā maggaṃ bhāvetvā phalaṃ sacchikaroti. Tasmā therassa evaṃ ajjhāsayo hoti – ‘‘aho vata sabrahmacārī ekaṃ vā dve vā tayo vā cattāro vā pañca vā nikāye uggahetvā āvajjantā sīlādīnaṃ āgataṭṭhānesu sīlādīni paripūretvā anukkamena maggaphalanibbānāni sacchikareyyu’’nti. Sesavāresupi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
339. "Excellent, excellent, Sāriputta," this praise was given to Ānanda Thera.

Then, the Blessed One converses with Sāriputta Thera.

This is the method everywhere.

"Just as Ānanda would explain it," just as Ānanda would explain it correctly, thus Ānanda explained it in accordance with his own capacity and in accordance with his own inclination. This is the meaning.

Ānanda Thera was indeed very learned himself, and his inclination was thus: "Oh, that the spiritual practitioners in the teaching might be very learned!"

Why? Because for the very learned, what is permissible and impermissible, what is blameworthy and blameless, what is weighty and light, what has a remedy and what is without remedy is clear.

Having learned the Buddha's teachings, the very learned one, reflecting, knows, "In this place, morality is spoken of; in this place, concentration; in this place, insight; in this place, the path, the fruit, and nirvāṇa." Having fulfilled morality in the place where morality is appropriate, having fulfilled concentration in the place where concentration is appropriate, having taken up the essence of insight in the place where insight is appropriate, one develops the path and realizes the fruit.

Therefore, the Thera has this inclination: "Oh, that spiritual practitioners, having learned one, two, three, four, or five collections (of teachings), reflecting, fulfilling morality and so on in the places where morality and so on are appropriate, might realize the path, the fruit, and nirvāṇa in due order!"

And the same method applies in the remaining instances.

mula_pali: 340. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ revataṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso revata āyasmatā ānandena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ revataṃ pucchāma – ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso revata, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā maññe gandhā sampavanti. Kathaṃrūpena, āvuso revata, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā revato maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta bhikkhu paṭisallānārāmo hoti paṭisallānarato , ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto, anirākatajjhāno, vipassanāya samannāgato, brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yathā taṃ revatova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Revato hi, sāriputta, paṭisallānārāmo paṭisallānarato, ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno, vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārāna’’nti.
mula_english:
“When this was said, venerable sir, I addressed the venerable Revata thus: ‘Friend Revata, the venerable Ānanda has spoken according to his own inspiration. Now we ask the venerable Revata: Friend Revata, the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, the night is moonlit, the *sāla* trees are all in blossom, and heavenly scents seem to be floating in the air. What kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Revata, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’

When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Revata said to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* delights in solitary meditation (*pratisallānārāmo*), takes delight in solitary meditation (*pratisallānarato*), is devoted to internal serenity of mind (*ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto*), does not neglect meditation (*anirākatajjhāno*), possesses insight (*vipassanāya samannāgato*), and dwells in empty huts (*brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ*). That kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.’

“Good, good, Sāriputta. Revata, speaking rightly, should speak just as he did. For Revata delights in solitary meditation (*pratisallānārāmo*), takes delight in solitary meditation (*pratisallānarato*), is devoted to internal serenity of mind (*ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto*) does not neglect meditation (*anirākatajjhāno*), possesses insight (*vipassanāya samannāgato*), and dwells in empty huts (*brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ*).”
commentary_pali: 340. Āyasmā hi revato jhānajjhāsayo jhānābhirato, tasmāssa evaṃ hoti – ‘‘aho vata sabrahmacārī ekikā nisīditvā kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā aṭṭha samāpattiyo nibbattetvā jhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā lokuttaradhammaṃ sacchikareyyu’’nti. Tasmā evaṃ byākāsi.
commentary_english: Venerable Revata was one who meditated on absorption, delighted in absorption. Therefore, it occurred to him: "Oh, that my fellow monks, alone, sitting down, having done the preliminary kasina practice, developing the eight attainments, developing insight based on absorption, might realize the supramundane Dharma!" Therefore, he spoke thus.

mula_pali: 341. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho āvuso anuruddha āyasmatā revatena…pe… kathaṃrūpena, āvuso anuruddha, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā anuruddho maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi. Seyyathāpi, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhumā puriso…pe… evarūpena kho āvuso sāriputta bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, yathā taṃ anuruddhova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Anuruddho hi, sāriputta, dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketī’’ti.
mula_english:
“When that was said, venerable sir, I addressed the venerable Anuruddha thus: ‘Friend Anuruddha, it was declared by the venerable Revata…What kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Anuruddha, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’

“When that was said, venerable sir, the venerable Anuruddha said to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* with the divine eye (*dibba cakkhu*), which is purified and surpasses the human, surveys a thousand worlds.

Just as a man with good sight… That kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Sāriputta, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.’ ”

“Good, good, Sāriputta. Anuruddha, speaking rightly, should speak just as he did.

For with the divine eye (*dibba cakkhu*), which is purified and surpasses the human, Anuruddha surveys a thousand worlds.”
commentary_pali: 341. Āyasmā anuruddho dibbacakkhuko, tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘‘aho vata sabrahmacārī ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā dibbena cakkhunā anekesu cakkavāḷasahassesu cavamāne ca upapajjamāne ca satte disvā vaṭṭabhayena cittaṃ saṃvejetvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā lokuttaradhammaṃ sacchikareyyu’’nti. Tasmā evaṃ byākāsi.
commentary_english: Venerable Anuruddha, possessor of the divine eye ( *dibba-cakkhu* ), it occurred to him: "Oh, that my fellow *brahmacārins* ( *sabrahmacārī* ), by increasing ( *vaḍḍhetvā* ) the light ( *ālokaṃ* ), might, with the divine ( *dibbena* ) eye ( *cakkhunā* ), seeing ( *disvā* ) beings ( *satte* ) departing ( *cavamāne* ) and arising ( *upapajjamāne* ) in many thousands of world-systems ( *anekesu cakkavāḷasahassesu* ), and being agitated in mind ( *cittaṃ saṃvejetvā* ) by the fear of the round ( *vaṭṭabhayena* ), might realize ( *sacchikareyyu* ) the transcendental *dharma* ( *lokuttaradhammaṃ* ) by developing insight ( *vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā* )!" Therefore ( *tasmā* ), he spoke thus ( *evaṃ byākāsi* ).

mula_pali: 342. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso kassapa āyasmatā anuruddhena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ pucchāma…pe… kathaṃ rūpena kho, āvuso kassapa, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte bhante, āyasmā mahākassapo maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu attanā ca āraññiko hoti āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca piṇḍapātiko hoti…pe… attanā ca paṃsukūliko hoti…pe… attanā ca tecīvariko hoti…pe… attanā ca appiccho hoti…pe… attanā ca santuṭṭho hoti…pe… attanā ca pavivitto hoti…pe… attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho hoti…pe… attanā ca āraddhavīriyo hoti…pe… attanā ca sīlasampanno hoti…pe… attanā ca samādhisampanno hoti…pe… attanā ca paññāsampanno hoti… attanā ca vimuttisampanno hoti… attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti . ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yathā taṃ kassapova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Kassapo hi, sāriputta, attanā ca āraññiko āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca piṇḍapātiko piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paṃsukūliko paṃsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca tecīvariko tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca appiccho appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca santuṭṭho santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca pavivitto pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca asaṃsaṭṭho asaṃsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca āraddhavīriyo vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca sīlasampanno sīlasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca samādhisampanno samādhisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca paññāsampanno paññāsampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttisampanno vimuttisampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī, attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadāya ca vaṇṇavādī’’ti.
mula_english:
‘When this was said, venerable sir, I said this to the venerable Mahākassapa: “Friend Kassapa, the venerable Anuruddha has spoken according to his ability. Now we ask the venerable Mahākassapa… What kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Kassapa, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?” When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Mahākassapa said this to me: “Here, friend Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* is a forest-dweller (*āraññika*) himself and speaks in praise of forest dwelling (*āraññikatta*); he is an alms-goer (*piṇḍapātika*) himself… he is a rag-robe wearer (*paṃsukūlika*) himself… he is a wearer of three robes (*tecīvarika*) himself… he is of few desires (*appiccha*) himself… he is content (*santuṭṭha*) himself… he is secluded (*pavivitta*) himself… he is non-associated (*asaṃsaṭṭha*) himself… he has aroused energy (*āraddhavīriya*) himself… he is accomplished in virtue (*śīlasampanna*) himself… he is accomplished in concentration (*samādhisampanna*) himself… he is accomplished in wisdom (*prajñāsampanna*)… he is accomplished in deliverance (*vimuttisampanna*) himself… he is accomplished in the knowledge and vision of deliverance (*vimuttiñāṇadassana-sampanna*) and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of deliverance. That kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Sāriputta, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.”’

‘Good, good, Sāriputta! Kassapa, speaking rightly, should speak just as he did. For Kassapa is a forest-dweller (*āraññika*) himself and speaks in praise of forest dwelling (*āraññikatta*); he is an alms-goer (*piṇḍapātika*) himself and speaks in praise of alms-going (*piṇḍapātikatta*); he is a rag-robe wearer (*paṃsukūlika*) himself and speaks in praise of wearing rag-robes (*paṃsukūlikatta*); he is a wearer of three robes (*tecīvarika*) himself and speaks in praise of wearing three robes (*tecīvarikatta*); he is of few desires (*appiccha*) himself and speaks in praise of having few desires (*appicchatāya*); he is content (*santuṭṭha*) himself and speaks in praise of contentment (*santuṭṭhiyā*); he is secluded (*pavivitta*) himself and speaks in praise of seclusion (*pavivekassa*); he is non-associated (*asaṃsaṭṭha*) himself and speaks in praise of non-association (*asaṃsaggassa*); he has aroused energy (*āraddhavīriya*) himself and speaks in praise of the arousal of energy (*vīriyārambhassa*); he is accomplished in virtue (*śīlasampanna*) himself and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of virtue (*śīlasampadāya*); he is accomplished in concentration (*samādhisampanna*) himself and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of concentration (*samādhisampadāya*); he is accomplished in wisdom (*prajñāsampanna*) himself and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of wisdom (*prajñāsampadāya*); he is accomplished in deliverance (*vimuttisampanna*) himself and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of deliverance (*vimuttisampadāya*); he is accomplished in the knowledge and vision of deliverance (*vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanna*) himself and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of deliverance.’
commentary_pali: 342. Āyasmā mahākassapo dhutavādo, tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘‘aho vata sabrahmacārī dhutavādā hutvā dhutaṅgānubhāvena paccayataṇhaṃ milāpetvā aparepi nānappakāre kilese dhunitvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā lokuttaradhammaṃ sacchikareyyu’’nti. Tasmā evaṃ byākāsi.
commentary_english: The venerable Mahākassapa, an advocate of the ascetic practices (*dhutavāda*), thought to himself: "Oh, that my fellow monks, being advocates of the ascetic practices (*dhutavāda*), having become [adept] through the power of the qualities of asceticism (*dhutaṅgānubhāva*), having eliminated craving for requisites (*paccayataṇhā*), and shaking off other various defilements (*kilesa*), developing insight (*vipassanā*), might realize the supramundane Dharma (*lokuttaradhamma*)!" Therefore, he spoke thus.

mula_pali: 343. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ bhante āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso moggallāna, āyasmatā mahākassapena yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ pucchāma…pe… kathaṃrūpena, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā mahāmoggallāno maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso sāriputta, dve bhikkhū abhidhammakathaṃ kathenti. Te aññamaññaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, aññamaññassa pañhaṃ puṭṭhā vissajjenti, no ca saṃsādenti, dhammī ca nesaṃ kathā pavattinī hoti. Evarūpena kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, yathā taṃ moggallānova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Moggallāno hi, sāriputta, dhammakathiko’’ti.
mula_english:
“When this was said, venerable sir, I addressed the venerable Mahā Moggallāna thus: ‘Friend Moggallāna, venerable Mahākassapa has spoken according to his own inspiration. Now, in this matter, we ask the venerable Mahāmoggallāna…pe… In what way, friend Moggallāna, could a *bhikkhu* illuminate the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Mahā Moggallāna said this to me: ‘Here, friend Sāriputta, two *bhikkhus* give a discourse on the *Abhidhamma*. They ask each other questions, and questioned by each other, they explain [them], and they do not get confused, and their talk proceeds according to the Dhamma. That kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Sāriputta, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.’ ”

The Blessed One said: “Good, good, Sāriputta. Moggallāna, speaking rightly, should speak just as he did. For Moggallāna is one who talks on the Dhamma.”
commentary_pali: 343. Āyasmā mahāmoggallāno samādhipāramiyā matthakaṃ patto, sukhumaṃ pana cittantaraṃ khandhantaraṃ dhātvantaraṃ āyatanantaraṃ jhānokkantikaṃ ārammaṇokkantikaṃ aṅgavavatthānaṃ ārammaṇavavatthānaṃ aṅgasaṅkanti ārammaṇasaṅkanti ekatovaḍḍhanaṃ ubhatovaḍḍhananti ābhidhammikadhammakathikasseva pākaṭaṃ. Anābhidhammiko hi dhammaṃ kathento – ‘‘ayaṃ sakavādo ayaṃ paravādo’’ti na jānāti. Sakavādaṃ dīpessāmīti paravādaṃ dīpeti, paravādaṃ dīpessāmīti sakavādaṃ dīpeti, dhammantaraṃ visaṃvādeti. Ābhidhammiko sakavādaṃ sakavādaniyāmeneva , paravādaṃ paravādaniyāmeneva dīpeti, dhammantaraṃ na visaṃvādeti. Tasmā therassa evaṃ hoti – ‘‘aho vata sabrahmacārī ābhidhammikā hutvā sukhumesu ṭhānesu ñāṇaṃ otāretvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā lokuttaradhammaṃ sacchikareyyu’’nti. Tasmā evaṃ byākāsi.
commentary_english:
The venerable Mahāmoggallāna attained the height of the perfection of concentration (samādhi-pāramī). But subtle distinctions such as distinctions of mind (citta-antara), distinctions of aggregates (skandha-antara), distinctions of elements (dhātu-antara), distinctions of sense-fields (āyatana-antara), stages of jhāna (dhyāna), access to objects (ārammaṇa), analysis of factors (aṅga-vavatthāna), analysis of objects (ārammaṇa-vavatthāna), the progression of factors (aṅga-saṅkanti), the progression of objects (ārammaṇa-saṅkanti), development in one way (ekatovaḍḍhana), and development in two ways (ubhatovaḍḍhana) are clear only to one who is an Abhidhamma-preacher.

For one who is not an Abhidhamma-practitioner, while speaking about the Dharma, does not know “this is my own doctrine (saka-vāda), this is the doctrine of another (para-vāda).”

Thinking, “I will illuminate my own doctrine (saka-vādaṃ dīpessāmi),” he illuminates the doctrine of another (para-vādaṃ dīpeti); thinking, “I will illuminate the doctrine of another (para-vādaṃ dīpessāmi),” he illuminates his own doctrine (saka-vādaṃ dīpeti), he contradicts the other aspect of the Dharma (dhamma-antaraṃ visaṃvādeti).

The Abhidhamma-practitioner illuminates his own doctrine (saka-vādaṃ) just by the method of his own doctrine (saka-vāda-niyāmena), he illuminates the doctrine of another (para-vādaṃ) just by the method of the doctrine of another (para-vāda-niyāmena), and he does not contradict the other aspect of the Dharma (dhamma-antaraṃ na visaṃvādeti).

Therefore, it occurs to the elder (thera): “Oh, that the fellow practitioners (sabrahmacārī), having become Abhidhamma-practitioners (ābhidhammikā hutvā), having brought their knowledge (jñānaṃ) down into subtle places (sukhumessu ṭhānesu), having developed insight (vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā), would realize the supramundane Dharma (lokuttara-dhammaṃ sacchikareyyu).”

Therefore, he spoke thus (tasmā evaṃ byākāsi).

mula_pali: 344. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘atha khvāhaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘byākataṃ kho, āvuso sāriputta, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha dāni mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ pucchāma – ramaṇīyaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, gosiṅgasālavanaṃ, dosinā ratti, sabbaphāliphullā sālā, dibbā, maññe, gandhā sampavanti. Kathaṃrūpena, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘idhāvuso, moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Seyyathāpi, āvuso moggallāna, rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā nānārattānaṃ dussānaṃ dussakaraṇḍako pūro assa. So yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ , taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ majjhanhikasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupeyya. Evameva kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhu cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti, no ca bhikkhu cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharati. Evarūpena kho, āvuso moggallāna, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, moggallāna! Yathā taṃ sāriputtova sammā byākaramāno byākareyya. Sāriputto hi, moggallāna, cittaṃ vasaṃ vatteti no ca sāriputto cittassa vasena vattati. So yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā majjhanhikasamayaṃ viharati; yāya vihārasamāpattiyā ākaṅkhati sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tāya vihārasamāpattiyā sāyanhasamayaṃ viharatī’’ti.
mula_english:
344. When that was said, the venerable Mahā Moggallāna told the Blessed One: “Then, venerable sir, I addressed the venerable Sāriputta thus: ‘Friend Sāriputta, we have all declared our own inspiration.’

Now, venerable sir, we ask the venerable Sāriputta: ‘Friend Sāriputta, the Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood is delightful, the night is moonlit, the *sāla* trees are all in blossom, and heavenly scents seem to be floating in the air. What kind of *bhikkhu*, friend Sāriputta, could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood?’” When that was said, the venerable Sāriputta told me: “Here, friend Moggallāna, a *bhikkhu* wields mastery over his mind, and the *bhikkhu* does not let the mind wield mastery over him.

In the morning he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the morning; at midday he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in at midday; in the evening he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the evening.

Suppose a king or a king’s minister had a chest full of variously coloured garments.

In the morning he could put on whatever pair of garments he wanted to put on in the morning; at midday he could put on whatever pair of garments he wanted to put on at midday; in the evening he could put on whatever pair of garments he wanted to put on in the evening.

So too, friend Moggallāna, a *bhikkhu* wields mastery over his mind, he does not let the mind wield mastery over him.

In the morning he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the morning; at midday he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in at midday; in the evening he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the evening.

That kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.’ ”

“Good, good, Moggallāna! Sāriputta, speaking rightly, should speak just as he did.

For Sāriputta wields mastery over his mind, he does not let the mind wield mastery over him.

In the morning he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the morning; at midday he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in at midday; in the evening he abides in whatever abiding or attainment he wants to abide in during the evening.”
commentary_pali: 344. Āyasmā sāriputto paññāpāramiyā matthakaṃ patto, paññavāyeva ca cittaṃ attano vase vattetuṃ sakkoti, na duppañño. Duppañño hi uppannassa cittassa vase vattetvā ito cito ca vipphanditvāpi katipāheneva gihibhāvaṃ patvā anayabyasanaṃ pāpuṇāti. Tasmā therassa evaṃ hoti – ‘‘aho vata sabrahmacārī acittavasikā hutvā cittaṃ attano vase vattetvā sabbānassa visevitavipphanditāni bhañjitvā īsakampi bahi nikkhamituṃ adentā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā lokuttaradhammaṃ sacchikareyyu’’nti. Tasmā evaṃ byākāsi.
commentary_english:
Venerable Śāriputra has attained the summit of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and only the wise are able to control their minds, not the unwise.

Indeed, the unwise, being controlled by the arising mind, wandering here and there, even after a few days, attain the state of a householder and encounter misfortune and disaster.

Therefore, the Elder thought thus: "Oh, that fellow practitioners, being without control over the mind, controlling the mind, having broken all the diverse wanderings experienced by the mind, not allowing it to exit even a little, developing insight (vipaśyanā), might realize the supramundane dharma (lokuttaradharma)!"

Therefore, he explained thus.

mula_pali:
345. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kassa nu kho, bhante, subhāsita’’nti? ‘‘Sabbesaṃ vo, sāriputta, subhāsitaṃ pariyāyena. Api ca mamapi suṇātha yathārūpena bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyya. Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ pallaṅkaṃ bhindissāmi yāva me nānupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccissatī’ti. Evarūpena kho, sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te āyasmanto te bhikkhū (ka.) bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

te bhikkhū (ka.)

Mahāgosiṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
345. Thus spoken, the venerable Śāriputra said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, which of us has spoken well?” “In every way, Śāriputta, what has been spoken is well-said.

Hear also from me what kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.

Here, Sāriputta, when a *bhikkhu* has returned from his almsround, after his meal, he sits down, folds his legs crosswise, sets his body erect, and establishing mindfulness in front of him, resolves: ‘I shall not break this sitting position until through not clinging my mind is liberated from the taints.’

That kind of *bhikkhu* could illuminate this Gosinga Sāla-tree Wood.”

The Blessed One said this.

Elated, those venerable monks delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Mahāgosingasutta, the second, is complete.
commentary_pali:
345.Sabbesaṃ vo, sāriputta, subhāsitaṃ pariyāyenāti sāriputta, yasmā saṅghārāmassa nāma bahussutabhikkhūhipi sobhanakāraṇaṃ atthi, jhānābhiratehipi, dibbacakkhukehipi, dhutavādehipi, ābhidhammikehipi, acittavasikehipi sobhanakāraṇaṃ atthi. Tasmā sabbesaṃ vo subhāsitaṃ pariyāyena, tena tena kāraṇena subhāsitameva, no dubbhāsitaṃ. Apica mamapi suṇāthāti apica mamapi vacanaṃ suṇātha. Na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ pallaṅkaṃ bhindissāmīti na tāva ahaṃ imaṃ caturaṅgavīriyaṃ adhiṭṭhāya ābhujitaṃ pallaṅkaṃ bhindissāmi, na mocessāmīti attho. Idaṃ kira bhagavā paripākagate ñāṇe rajjasiriṃ pahāya katābhinikkhamano anupubbena bodhimaṇḍaṃ āruyha caturaṅgavīriyaṃ adhiṭṭhāya aparājitapallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā daḷhasamādāno hutvā nisinno tiṇṇaṃ mārānaṃ matthakaṃ bhinditvā paccūsasamaye dasasahassilokadhātuṃ unnādento sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ paṭivijjhi, taṃ attano mahābodhipallaṅkaṃ sandhāya evamāha. Apica pacchimaṃ janataṃ anukampamānopi paṭipattisāraṃ puthujjanakalyāṇakaṃ dassento evamāha. Passati hi bhagavā – ‘‘anāgate evaṃ ajjhāsayā kulaputtā iti paṭisañcikkhissanti, ‘bhagavā mahāgosiṅgasuttaṃ kathento idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ…pe… evarūpena kho, sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyāti āha, mayaṃ bhagavato ajjhāsayaṃ gaṇhissāmā’ti pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā caturaṅgavīriyaṃ adhiṭṭhāya daḷhasamādānā hutvā ‘arahattaṃ appatvā imaṃ pallaṅkaṃ na bhindissāmā’ti samaṇadhammaṃ kātabbaṃ maññissanti, te evaṃ paṭipannā katipāheneva jātijarāmaraṇassa antaṃ karissantī’’ti, imaṃ pacchimaṃ janataṃ anukampamāno paṭipattisāraṃ puthujjanakalyāṇakaṃ dassento evamāha. Evarūpena kho, sāriputta, bhikkhunā gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyāti, sāriputta, evarūpena bhikkhunā nippariyāyeneva gosiṅgasālavanaṃ sobheyyāti yathānusandhināva desanaṃ niṭṭhapesīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāgosiṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
345. "O Sāriputta, all of you have spoken well in different ways." Sāriputta, because in a *saṃghārāma*, there is a cause for excellence even with monks who are very learned, with those delighting in *jhāna*, with those having the divine eye, with those who are proponents of ascetic practices (*dhutavāda*), with those versed in the *Abhidhamma*, and with those who dwell on the absence of thought (*acittavasika*), there is a cause for excellence.

Therefore, all of you have spoken well in different ways; for that reason, it is well-spoken, not ill-spoken.

"Moreover, listen to me as well": moreover, listen to my words as well.

"I will not break this *pallaṅka*": I will not break this crossed-legged posture, having undertaken the fourfold exertion, and I will not release it. That is the meaning.

It is said that the Blessed One, having abandoned the glory of kingship when his knowledge had reached maturity, having gone forth, and having ascended the *bodhimaṇḍa* in due course, having undertaken the fourfold exertion, having sat down cross-legged in the unconquered posture, having become firm in resolve, having broken the head of the three *Māras*, and resounding the ten thousand world-systems at dawn, realized the knowledge of omniscience (*sabbaññutaññāṇa*). With reference to that great *bodhipallaṅka* of his own, he said thus.

Moreover, showing compassion to the later generation, displaying the essence of practice, which is auspicious for ordinary people, he said thus.

The Blessed One sees that – "In the future, *kulaputras* with such intentions will reflect thus: 'The Blessed One, while teaching the *Mahāgosiṅgasutta* here, said, "O Sāriputta, a monk after the meal…pe… in this way, O Sāriputta, a monk adorns the Gosiṅga Sāla Forest." We will grasp the Blessed One’s intention.' Having returned from the alms round after the meal, having undertaken the fourfold exertion, having become firm in resolve, and thinking, 'Without attaining *arhatship*, we will not break this *pallaṅka*,’ they will consider the ascetic life should be lived." For those who are practicing thus, within a few days, they will make an end to birth, aging, and death." Showing compassion to this later generation, displaying the essence of practice, which is auspicious for ordinary people, he said thus.

"In this way, O Sāriputta, a monk adorns the Gosiṅga Sāla Forest." Sāriputta, in this way, a monk adorns the Gosiṅga Sāla Forest without any other means. Thus, in accordance with the connection, he brought the teaching to a conclusion.

The *Mahāgosiṅgasuttavaṇṇanā* is finished in the *Papañcasūdanī*, a commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

mula_pali:
346. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Ekādasahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako abhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ phātikattuṃ (sī. pī.), phātikātuṃ (syā. kaṃ.). Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, gopālako na rūpaññū hoti, na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā sāṭetā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) hoti, na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, na titthaṃ jānāti, na pītaṃ jānāti, na vīthiṃ jānāti, na gocarakusalo hoti anavasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te usabhā gopitaro gopariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako abhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjituṃ. Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na rūpaññū hoti, na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti, na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, na titthaṃ jānāti, na pītaṃ jānāti, na vīthiṃ jānāti, na gocarakusalo hoti, anavasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti.

phātikattuṃ (sī. pī.), phātikātuṃ (syā. kaṃ.) sāṭetā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
346.
Thus have I heard: Once the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park (ārāma).
There the Blessed One addressed the monks (bhikkhū), saying: “Monks!”
“Venerable sir (bhadante),” those monks replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:

“When a cowherd (gopālako), monks, possesses eleven qualities, he is incapable of keeping and rearing a herd of cattle (gogaṇaṃ).
What are the eleven? Here, monks, a cowherd has no knowledge of form (rūpaññū), he is unskilled in characteristics (lakkhaṇakusalo), he fails to pick out flies’ eggs (āsāṭikaṃ hāretā), he fails to dress wounds (vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā), he fails to smoke out the sheds (dhūmaṃ kattā), he does not know the watering place (titthaṃ jānāti), he does not know what it is to have drunk (pītaṃ jānāti), he does not know the road (vīthiṃ jānāti), he is unskilled in pastures (gocarakusalo), he milks dry (anavasesadohī) and he shows no extra veneration (atirekapūjāya pūjetā) to those bulls (usabhā) who are fathers (gopitaro) and leaders (gopariṇāyakā) of the herd.
When a cowherd, monks, possesses these eleven qualities, he is incapable of keeping and rearing a herd of cattle.

"Just so, monks, when a bhikkhu possesses eleven qualities, he is incapable of growth (vuddhiṃ), increase (virūḷhiṃ), and fulfilment (vepullaṃ) in this Dhamma and Discipline (dhammavinaye).
What are the eleven? Here, monks, a bhikkhu has no knowledge of form (rūpaññū), he is unskilled in characteristics (lakkhaṇakusalo), he fails to pick out flies’ eggs (āsāṭikaṃ hāretā), he fails to dress wounds (vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā), he fails to smoke out the sheds (dhūmaṃ kattā), he does not know the watering place (titthaṃ jānāti), he does not know what it is to have drunk (pītaṃ jānāti), he does not know the road (vīthiṃ jānāti), he is unskilled in pastures (gocarakusalo), he milks dry (anavasesadohī) and he shows no extra veneration (atirekapūjāya pūjetā) to those elder bhikkhus (bhikkhū therā) of long-standing (rattaññū) who have long gone forth (cirapabbajitā), the fathers (saṅghapitaro) and leaders (saṅghapariṇāyakā) of the Saṅgha."
commentary_pali:
346.Evaṃme sutanti mahāgopālakasuttaṃ. Tattha tisso kathā ekanāḷikā, caturassā, nisinnavattikāti. Tattha pāḷiṃ vatvā ekekapadassa atthakathanaṃ ekanāḷikā nāma. Apaṇḍitaṃ gopālakaṃ dassetvā, apaṇḍitaṃ bhikkhuṃ dassetvā, paṇḍitaṃ gopālakaṃ dassetvā, paṇḍitaṃ bhikkhuṃ dassetvāti catukkaṃ bandhitvā kathanaṃ caturassā nāma. Apaṇḍitaṃ gopālakaṃ dassetvā pariyosānagamanaṃ, apaṇḍitaṃ bhikkhuṃ dassetvā pariyosānagamanaṃ, paṇḍitaṃ gopālakaṃ dassetvā pariyosānagamanaṃ, paṇḍitaṃ bhikkhuṃ dassetvā pariyosānagamananti ayaṃ nisinnavattikā nāma. Ayaṃ idha sabbācariyānaṃ āciṇṇā.

Ekādasahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehīti ekādasahi aguṇakoṭṭhāsehi. Gogaṇanti gomaṇḍalaṃ. Pariharitunti pariggahetvā vicarituṃ. Phātiṃ kātunti vaḍḍhiṃ āpādetuṃ. Idhāti imasmiṃ loke. Na rūpaññū hotīti gaṇanato vā vaṇṇato vā rūpaṃ na jānāti. Gaṇanato na jānāti nāma attano gunnaṃ sataṃ vā sahassaṃ vāti saṅkhyaṃ na jānāti. So gāvīsu haṭāsu vā palātāsu vā gogaṇaṃ gaṇetvā, ajja ettikā na dissantīti dve tīṇi gāmantarāni vā aṭaviṃ vā vicaranto na pariyesati, aññesaṃ gāvīsu attano gogaṇaṃ paviṭṭhāsupi gogaṇaṃ gaṇetvā, ‘‘imā ettikā gāvo na amhāka’’nti yaṭṭhiyā pothetvā na nīharati, tassa naṭṭhā gāviyo naṭṭhāva honti. Paragāviyo gahetvā vicarantaṃ gosāmikā disvā, ‘‘ayaṃ ettakaṃ kālaṃ amhākaṃ dhenuṃ gaṇhātī’’ti tajjetvā attano gāviyo gahetvā gacchanti. Tassa gogaṇopi parihāyati, pañcagorasaparibhogatopi paribāhiro hoti. Vaṇṇato na jānāti nāma – ‘‘ettikā gāvo setā, ettikā rattā, ettikā kāḷā, ettikā kabarā ettikā nīlā’’ti na jānāti, so gāvīsu haṭāsu vā…pe… pañcagorasaparibhogatopi paribāhiro hoti.

Ekādasahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehī Gogaṇa Pariharitu Phātiṃ kātu Idhā Na rūpaññū hotī Gaṇanato Vaṇṇato

Na lakkhaṇakusalo hotīti gāvīnaṃ sarīre kataṃ dhanusattisūlādibhedaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ na jānāti , so gāvīsu haṭāsu vā palātāsu vā ajja asukalakkhaṇā ca asukalakkhaṇā ca gāvo na dissanti…pe… pañcagorasaparibhogatopi paribāhiro hoti.

Na lakkhaṇakusalo hotī

Na āsāṭikaṃ hāretāti gunnaṃ khāṇukaṇṭakādīhi pahaṭaṭṭhānesu vaṇo hoti. Tattha nīlamakkhikā aṇḍakāni pātenti, tesaṃ āsāṭikāti nāma. Tāni daṇḍena apanetvā bhesajjaṃ dātabbaṃ hoti. Bālo gopālako tathā na karoti, tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hotī’’ti. Tassa gunnaṃ vaṇā vaḍḍhanti, gambhīrā honti, pāṇakā kucchiṃ pavisanti, gāvo gelaññābhibhūtā neva yāvadatthaṃ tiṇāni khādituṃ, na pānīyaṃ pātuṃ sakkonti. Tattha gunnaṃ khīraṃ chijjati, goṇānaṃ javo hāyati, ubhayesaṃ jīvitantarāyo hoti. Evamassa gogaṇopi parihāyati, pañcagorasatopi paribāhiro hoti.

Na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā

Na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hotīti gunnaṃ vuttanayeneva sañjāto vaṇo bhesajjaṃ datvā vākena vā cīrakena vā bandhitvā paṭicchādetabbo hoti. Bālo gopālako tathā na karoti, athassa gunnaṃ vaṇehi yūsā paggharanti, tā aññamaññaṃ nighaṃsenti, tena aññesampi vaṇā jāyanti. Evaṃ gāvo gelaññābhibhūtā neva yāvadatthaṃ tiṇāni khādituṃ…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hotī

Na dhūmaṃ kattā hotīti antovasse ḍaṃsamakasādīnaṃ ussannakāle gogaṇe vajaṃ paviṭṭhe tattha tattha dhūmo kātabbo hoti, apaṇḍito gopālako taṃ na karoti. Gogaṇo sabbarattiṃ ḍaṃsādīhi upadduto niddaṃ alabhitvā punadivase araññe tattha tattha rukkhamūlādīsu nipajjitvā niddāyati, neva yāvadatthaṃ tiṇāni khādituṃ…pe… pañcagorasaparibhogatopi paribāhiro hoti.

Na dhūmaṃ kattā hotī

Na titthaṃ jānātīti titthaṃ samanti vā visamanti vā sagāhanti vā niggāhanti vā na jānāti, so atitthena gāviyo otāreti. Tāsaṃ visamatitthe pāsāṇādīni akkamantīnaṃ pādā bhijjanti, sagāhaṃ gambhīraṃ titthaṃ otiṇṇā kumbhīlādayo gāhā gaṇhanti. Ajja ettikā gāvo naṭṭhā, ajja ettikāti vattabbataṃ āpajjati. Evamassa gogaṇopi parihāyati, pañcagorasatopi paribāhiro hoti.

Na titthaṃ jānātī

Napītaṃ jānātīti pītampi apītampi na jānāti. Gopālakena hi ‘‘imāya gāviyā pītaṃ, imāya na pītaṃ, imāya pānīyatitthe okāso laddho, imāya na laddho’’ti evaṃ pītāpītaṃ jānitabbaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ pana divasabhāgaṃ araññe gogaṇaṃ rakkhitvā pānīyaṃ pāyessāmīti nadiṃ vā taḷākaṃ vā gahetvā gacchati. Tattha mahāusabhā ca anuusabhā ca balavagāviyo ca dubbalāni ceva mahallakāni ca gorūpāni siṅgehi vā phāsukāhi vā paharitvā attano okāsaṃ katvā ūruppamāṇaṃ udakaṃ pavisitvā yathākāmaṃ pivanti. Avasesā okāsaṃ alabhamānā tīre ṭhatvā kalalamissakaṃ udakaṃ pivanti, apītā eva vā honti. Atha ne gopālako piṭṭhiyaṃ paharitvā puna araññaṃ paveseti, tattha apītagāviyo pipāsāya sukkhamānā yāvadatthaṃ tiṇāni khādituṃ na sakkonti, tattha gunnaṃ khīraṃ chijjati, goṇānaṃ javo hāyati…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na pītaṃ jānātī

Na vīthiṃ jānātīti ‘‘ayaṃ maggo samo khemo, ayaṃ visamo sāsaṅko sappaṭibhayo’’ti na jānāti. So samaṃ khemaṃ maggaṃ vajjetvā gogaṇaṃ itaraṃ maggaṃ paṭipādeti, tattha gāvo sīhabyagghādīnaṃ gandhena coraparissayena vā abhibhūtā bhantamigasappaṭibhāgā gīvaṃ ukkhipitvā tiṭṭhanti, neva yāvadatthaṃ tiṇāni khādanti, na pānīyaṃ pivanti, tattha gunnaṃ khīraṃ chijjati…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na vīthiṃ jānātī

Na gocarakusalo hotīti gopālakena hi gocarakusalena bhavitabbaṃ, pañcāhikavāro vā sattāhikavāro vā jānitabbo, ekadisāya gogaṇaṃ cāretvā punadivase tattha na cāretabbo. Mahatā hi gogaṇena ciṇṇaṭṭhānaṃ bheritalaṃ viya suddhaṃ hoti nittiṇaṃ, udakampi āluḷīyati. Tasmā pañcame vā sattame vā divase puna tattha cāretuṃ vaṭṭati, ettakena hi tiṇampi paṭiviruhati, udakampi pasīdati. Ayaṃ pana imaṃ pañcāhikavāraṃ vā sattāhikavāraṃ vā na jānāti, divase divase rakkhitaṭṭhāneyeva rakkhati. Athassa gogaṇo haritatiṇaṃ na labhati, sukkhatiṇaṃ khādanto kalalamissakaṃ udakaṃ pivati, tattha gunnaṃ khīraṃ chijjati…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na gocarakusalo hotī

Anavasesadohī ca hotīti paṇḍitagopālakena yāva vacchakassa maṃsalohitaṃ saṇṭhāti, tāva ekaṃ dve thane ṭhapetvā sāvasesadohinā bhavitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ vacchakassa kiñci anavasesetvā duhati, khīrapako vaccho khīrapipāsāya sukkhati, saṇṭhātuṃ asakkonto kampamāno mātu purato patitvā kālaṅkaroti. Mātā puttakaṃ disvā, ‘‘mayhaṃ puttako attano mātukhīraṃ pātumpi na labhatī’’ti puttasokena na yāvadatthaṃ tiṇāni khādituṃ, na pānīyaṃ pātuṃ sakkoti, thanesu khīraṃ chijjati. Evamassa gogaṇopi parihāyati, pañcagorasatopi paribāhiro hoti.

Anavasesadohī ca hotī

Gunnaṃ pituṭṭhānaṃ karontīti gopitaro. Gāvo pariṇayanti yathāruciṃ gahetvā gacchantīti gopariṇāyakā. Na atirekapūjāyāti paṇḍito hi gopālako evarūpe usabhe atirekapūjāya pūjeti, paṇītaṃ gobhattaṃ deti, gandhapañcaṅgulikehi maṇḍeti, mālaṃ pilandheti, siṅge suvaṇṇarajatakosake ca dhāreti, rattiṃ dīpaṃ jāletvā celavitānassa heṭṭhā sayāpeti. Ayaṃ pana tato ekasakkārampi na karoti, usabhā atirekapūjaṃ alabhamānā gogaṇaṃ na rakkhanti, parissayaṃ na vārenti. Evamassa gogaṇo parihāyati, pañcagorasato paribāhiro hoti.

gopitaro gopariṇāyakā. Na atirekapūjāyā
commentary_english:
346. Thus I have heard: the Mahāgopālaka Sūtra.

There, there are three discussions: ekanāḷikā, caturassā, and nisinnavattikā.

There, after stating the Pāḷi, the explanation of each and every word is called *ekanāḷikā*.

Having shown the unlearned cowherd, having shown the unlearned bhikkhu, having shown the learned cowherd, having shown the learned bhikkhu, the discussion by binding the quatrain is called *caturassā*.

Having shown the unlearned cowherd [and] the conclusion of the going, having shown the unlearned *bhikkhu* [and] the conclusion of the going, having shown the learned cowherd [and] the conclusion of the going, having shown the learned *bhikkhu* [and] the conclusion of the going, this is called *nisinnavattikā*.

This is practiced by all the teachers here.

By eleven factors, *bhikkhus*, that is, by eleven parts devoid of good qualities.

"*Gogaṇa* " means a herd of cows. (gomaṇḍalaṃ)
