"*Pariharitu*" means having taken up, to wander about.

"*Phātiṃ kātu*" means to bring about growth.

"*Idhā*" means in this world (imasmiṃ loke).

"*Na rūpaññū hoti*" means he does not know form by counting or by color.

"*Gaṇanato* na jānāti" means he does not know the number, thinking, "There are one hundred or one thousand of his qualities."

He, after counting the herd of cows when the cows have been carried off or have fled, thinking, "Today, so many are not seen," does not search around two or three villages or in the forest. Even when his herd of cows has entered into the cows of others, after counting the herd of cows, he does not drive them out, striking [them] with a stick, [thinking,] "These so many cows are not ours." His lost cows are simply lost.

The cow owners, seeing him wandering about having taken the cows of others, scolding him, [thinking,] "For so long, this one takes our cows," take their own cows and go away.

His herd of cows also diminishes, and he is excluded even from the enjoyment of the five products of the cow.

"*Vaṇṇato* na jānāti" means he does not know by color, [thinking,] "So many cows are white, so many are red, so many are black, so many are mottled, so many are blue." He, when the cows have been carried off or...pe...is excluded even from the enjoyment of the five products of the cow.

By eleven factors, *bhikkhus*, to tend the *gogaṇa*, to bring about growth, here, he is not knowledgable about the appearance, by counting, by color.

"*Na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti*" means he does not know the characteristics, the different marks such as bows, spears, and tridents made on the bodies of the cows. He, when the cows have been carried off or have fled, today such and such characteristics and such and such characteristics the cows are not seen...pe...he is excluded even from the enjoyment of the five products of the cow.

"*Na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti*.

"*Na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā*" means there is a wound in the places struck by stumps, thorns, etc. of the cows.

There, blue flies lay eggs; that is the meaning of *āsāṭika*.

Having removed those with a stick, medicine should be given.

The foolish cowherd does not do that; therefore it was said: "He is not one who removes the *āsāṭika*."

His wounds of the cows grow, they are deep, worms enter the stomach, the cows, overcome by illness, are not able to eat grass to their satisfaction, nor are they able to drink water.

There, the milk of the cows is cut off, the swiftness of the oxen decreases, there is danger to the life of both.

Thus, his herd of cows also diminishes, and he is excluded even from the five products of the cow.

"*Na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā*.

"*Na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti*" means the wound that has arisen in just the way said, after giving medicine, should be covered by binding with bark or with a bandage.

The foolish cowherd does not do that; then from the wounds of his cows, serum flows, those rub against each other, therefore other wounds also arise.

Thus the cows, overcome by illness, are not able to eat grass to their satisfaction...pe...he is excluded.

"*Na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti*.

"*Na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti*" means when the herd of cows has entered the pen in the inner rains, at the time when gnats, mosquitoes, etc. are abundant, smoke should be made there in that place; the unlearned cowherd does not do that.

The herd of cows, afflicted all night by gnats, etc., not obtaining sleep, on the next day, lying down in the forest there in that place at the roots of trees, etc., sleeps, [and is] not able to eat grass to their satisfaction...pe...he is excluded even from the enjoyment of the five products of the cow.
Not making smoke."

"He does not know the *tirtha* (bathing place or ford)." Because he does not know whether the *tirtha* is level or uneven, shallow or deep, he drives the cows down to an improper *tirtha*.
When they step on stones, etc. in the uneven *tirtha*, their feet are broken. Those who have gone down into a *tirtha* that is deep and has crocodiles, are seized by crocodiles, and so on.
Today this many cows are lost, today that many cows are lost, he is liable to be spoken of in this way.
Thus his herd of cows also declines, and he is excluded from the five products of the cow as well.

"He does not know the *tirtha* (watering place)."

"He does not know what has been drunk." He knows neither what has been drunk nor what has not been drunk.
Indeed, the cowherd should know thus: "By this cow water has been drunk; by this cow water has not been drunk; by this cow an opportunity has been obtained at the watering *tirtha*; by this cow an opportunity has not been obtained." Thus he should know what has been drunk and not drunk.
But this one, thinking, "Having protected the herd of cows in the forest during the day, I will give them water to drink," goes to a river or a pond, taking them there.
There, the great bulls, the lesser bulls, the strong cows, the weak ones, the old cows— striking each other with their horns or ribs, making an opportunity for themselves, entering water the measure of their thighs, drink as they please.
The remaining ones, not obtaining an opportunity, stand on the bank and drink muddy, mixed water, or they are just ones that have not drunk.
Then the cowherd strikes them on their backs and again drives them into the forest. There, the cows that have not drunk, languishing with thirst, are not able to eat grass to their satisfaction. There, the cows' milk is cut off, the bulls' vigor declines...and so on... he is excluded.

"He does not know what has been drunk."

"He does not know the *vīthi* (path)." Because he does not know, "This path is level and safe, this is uneven, dangerous, and full of fear."
Avoiding a level and safe path, he leads the herd of cows along another path. There, the cows, overcome by the smell of lions, tigers, and so on, or by the danger of thieves, stand with their necks raised up, sharing the nature of frightened deer, not eating grass to their satisfaction, not drinking water. There, the cows' milk is cut off...and so on... he is excluded.

"He does not know the path."

"He is not skilled in pasture." Indeed, the cowherd should be skilled in pasture. He should know whether it is a five-day turn or a seven-day turn. Having pastured the herd of cows in one direction, he should not pasture them there again on the following day.
Indeed, by a large herd of cows, a place that has been grazed is made clean like the surface of a drum, devoid of grass, and even the water is stirred up.
Therefore, it is fitting to pasture them there again on the fifth or seventh day. Indeed, by this much even the grass grows back, and the water becomes clear.
But this one does not know this five-day turn or seven-day turn. Day after day, he protects them in the same protected place.
Then his herd of cows does not obtain green grass. Eating dry grass, they drink muddy, mixed water. There, the cows' milk is cut off...and so on... he is excluded.

"He is not skilled in pasture."

"He is also one who milks without leaving any remainder." Indeed, the wise cowherd should, as long as the calf's flesh and blood remains, having left one or two teats, be one who milks leaving a remainder.
This one milks everything without leaving anything for the calf. The calf, who is to be nourished with milk, wastes away with thirst for milk, and being unable to stand, trembling, falls down in front of its mother and dies.
Seeing her little one, the mother, thinking, "My little one does not even obtain his own mother's milk to drink," because of sorrow for her little one, is not able to eat grass to her satisfaction, nor is she able to drink water. In her teats, the milk is cut off.
Thus his herd of cows also declines, and he is excluded from the five products of the cow as well.

"He is also one who milks without leaving any remainder."

They make the cows' drinking places: these are called "cow-fathers."
They lead the cows, taking them where they please: these are called "cow-leaders."
Not for excessive honoring." Indeed, the wise cowherd honors a bull of such a kind with excessive honoring. He gives choice food for the cows, he decorates it with fragrant five-finger marks, he places a garland on it, and he puts golden and silver coverings on its horns. At night, having lit a lamp, he lets it lie down under a cloth canopy.
But this one does not do even a single honor to it. The bulls, not obtaining excessive honoring, do not protect the herd of cows, they do not ward off danger.
Thus his herd of cows declines, and he is excluded from the five products of the cow.

Cow-fathers, cow-leaders, not for excessive honoring.

mula_pali:
347. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na rūpaññū hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘cattāri mahābhūtāni, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na rūpaññū hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘kammalakkhaṇo bālo, kammalakkhaṇo paṇḍito’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na lakkhaṇakusalo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ adhivāseti, nappajahati na vinodeti na byantī karoti na anabhāvaṃ gameti. Uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ…pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme adhivāseti, nappajahati na vinodeti na byantī karoti na anabhāvaṃ gameti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya nimittaggāhī hoti anubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya na paṭipajjati, na rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye na saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ na vitthārena paresaṃ desetā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na dhūmaṃ kattā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na titthaṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te kālena kālaṃ upasaṅkamitvā na paripucchati, na paripañhati – ‘idaṃ, bhante, kathaṃ? Imassa ko attho’ti? Tassa te āyasmanto avivaṭañceva na vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca na uttānī karonti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhānīyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṃ na paṭivinodenti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na titthaṃ jānāti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na pītaṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne na labhati atthavedaṃ, na labhati dhammavedaṃ, na labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na pītaṃ jānāti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na vīthiṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na vīthiṃ jānāti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na gocarakusalo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāro satipaṭṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave , bhikkhu na gocarakusalo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anavasesadohī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ saddhā gahapatikā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavārenti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi, tatra bhikkhu mattaṃ na jānāti paṭiggahaṇāya. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anavasesadohī hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā, tesu na mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca; na mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca; na mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti.

‘‘Imehi kho bhikkhave ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjituṃ.
mula_english:
347. “And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* (monk) have no knowledge of form (*rūpa*)? Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not understand as it actually is, that all form whatsoever is the four great elements (*cattāri mahābhūtāni*) and form derived from the four great elements (*catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa*).” That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* has no knowledge of form.

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* unskilled in characteristics (*lakkhana*)? Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not understand as it actually is, that ‘a fool has action as his characteristic, a wise man has action as his characteristic.’" That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* is unskilled in characteristics.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* fail to pick out flies’ eggs (*āsāṭikaṃ hāretā*)? Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* tolerates a sensual thought (*kāmavitakka*) that has arisen; he does not abandon it, remove it, do away with it, or annihilate it. When a thought of ill-will (*byāpādavitakka*) has arisen… when a thought of violence (*vihiṃsāvitakka*) has arisen… when evil unwholesome states (*pāpake akusale dhamme*) that have arisen again and again, he tolerates them; he does not abandon them, remove them, do away with them, or annihilate them." That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* fails to pick out flies’ eggs.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* fail to dress wounds (*vanaṃ paṭicchādetā*)? Here, monks, having seen a form with the eye (*cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā*), a *bhikkhu* grasps at its signs (*nimittaggāhī*) and details (*anubyañjanaggāhī*). Even though, when he leaves the eye faculty (*cakkhundriyaṃ*) unguarded, evil unwholesome states of covetousness (*abhijjhā*) and grief (*domanassā*) might invade him, he does not practice the way of its restraint (*saṃvarāya*), he does not guard the eye faculty (*cakkhundriyaṃ*), he does not undertake the restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… smelled an odour with the nose… tasted a flavour with the tongue… touched a tangible with the body… cognized a mind-object with the mind, he grasps at its signs and details. Even though, when he leaves the mind faculty unguarded, evil unwholesome states of covetousness and grief might invade him, he does not practice the way of its restraint, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not undertake the restraint of the mind faculty.” That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* fails to dress wounds.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* fail to smoke out the sheds (*dhūmaṃ kattā*)? Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not extensively teach the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) to others as he has heard and learned it.” That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* fails to smoke out the sheds.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* not know the watering place (*tittaṃ jānāti*)? Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not go from time to time to those *bhikkhus* who have learned much, who are well versed in the tradition, who maintain the Dharma, the Discipline (*vinaya*), and the Codes (*mātikā*), and he does not enquire and ask questions of them thus: ‘How is this, venerable sir? What is its meaning?’ Those venerable ones do not reveal what is unrevealed, they do not clarify what is unclarified, and they do not dispel doubt about the many points that cause doubt." That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not know the watering place.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* not know what it is to have drunk (*pītaṃ jānāti*)? Here, monks, when the Dharma and Discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata* is being taught, a *bhikkhu* does not gain inspiration in the meaning (*attha*), does not gain inspiration in the Dharma, does not gain gladness connected with the Dharma (*dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ*).” That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not know what it is to have drunk.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* not know the road (*vīthiṃ jānāti*)? Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not understand the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ*) as it actually is.” That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not know the road.

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* unskilled in pastures (*gocarakusalo*)? Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not understand the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhāne*) as they actually are.” That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* is unskilled in pastures.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* milk dry (*anavasesadohī*)? Here, monks, faithful householders invite a *bhikkhu* and offer him robes (*cīvara*), alms food (*piṇḍapāta*), lodging (*senāsana*), and medicine as the requisites for the sick (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi*), but in this matter the *bhikkhu* does not know moderation in accepting them.” That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* milks dry.

“And how, monks, does a *bhikkhu* show no extra veneration to those elder *bhikkhus* of long-standing who have long gone forth, the fathers and leaders of the *Saṃgha*?
Here, monks, a *bhikkhu* does not maintain bodily acts of loving-kindness (*mettā kāyakamma*) both openly and privately towards those elder *bhikkhus* who are senior, who have long been ordained, the fathers of the *Saṅgha*, the leaders of the *Saṅgha*; he does not maintain verbal acts of loving-kindness (*mettā vacīkamma*) towards them both openly and privately; he does not maintain mental acts of loving-kindness (*mettā manokamma*) towards them both openly and privately.

Thus, monks, a *bhikkhu* shows no extra veneration to those elder *bhikkhus* who are senior, who have long been ordained, the fathers and leaders of the *Saṅgha*.

Monks, a *bhikkhu* who possesses these eleven qualities is incapable of growth (*vuddhi*), increase (*virūḷhi*), and fulfilment (*vepulla*) in this *Dhamma* and *Vinaya* (teachings and discipline).
commentary_pali:
347.Idhāti imasmiṃ sāsane. Na rūpaññū hotīti, ‘‘cattāri mahābhūtāni catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa’’nti evaṃ vuttarūpaṃ dvīhākārehi na jānāti gaṇanato vā samuṭṭhānato vā. Gaṇanato na jānāti nāma, ‘‘cakkhāyatanaṃ, sota-ghāna-jivhā-kāyāyatanaṃ, rūpa-sadda-gandha-rasa-phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ, kāyaviññatti, vacīviññatti, ākāsadhātu, āpodhātu, rūpassa lahutā, mudutā, kammaññatā, upacayo, santati, jaratā, rūpassa aniccatā, kabaḷīkāro āhāro’’ti evaṃ pāḷiyaṃ āgatā pañcavīsati rūpakoṭṭhāsāti na jānāti. Seyyathāpi so gopālako gaṇanato gunnaṃ rūpaṃ na jānāti, tathūpamo ayaṃ bhikkhu. So gaṇanato rūpaṃ ajānanto rūpaṃ pariggahetvā arūpaṃ vavatthapetvā rūpārūpaṃ pariggahetvā paccayaṃ sallakkhetvā lakkhaṇaṃ āropetvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetuṃ na sakkoti. So yathā tassa gopālakassa gogaṇo na vaḍḍhati, evaṃ imasmiṃ sāsane sīlasamādhivipassanāmaggaphalanibbānehi na vaḍḍhati, yathā ca so gopālako pañcahi gorasehi paribāhiro hoti, evaṃ asekkhena sīlakkhandhena, asekkhena samādhi, paññā, vimutti, vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhenāti pañcahi dhammakkhandhehi paribāhiro hoti.

Samuṭṭhānato na jānāti nāma, ‘‘ettakaṃ rūpaṃ ekasamuṭṭhānaṃ, ettakaṃ dvisamuṭṭhānaṃ, ettakaṃ tisamuṭṭhānaṃ, ettakaṃ catusamuṭṭhānaṃ, ettakaṃ na kutocisamuṭṭhātī’’ti na jānāti. Seyyathāpi so gopālako vaṇṇato gunnaṃ rūpaṃ na jānāti, tathūpamo ayaṃ bhikkhu. So samuṭṭhānato rūpaṃ ajānanto rūpaṃ pariggahetvā arūpaṃ vavatthapetvā…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Samuṭṭhānato

Na lakkhaṇakusalo hotīti kammalakkhaṇo bālo, kammalakkhaṇo paṇḍitoti evaṃ vuttaṃ kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ paṇḍitabālalakkhaṇanti na jānāti. So evaṃ ajānanto bāle vajjetvā paṇḍite na sevati, bāle vajjetvā paṇḍite asevanto kappiyākappiyaṃ kusalākusalaṃ sāvajjānavajjaṃ garukalahukaṃ satekicchaatekicchaṃ kāraṇākāraṇaṃ na jānāti; taṃ ajānanto kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti. So yathā tassa gopālakassa gogaṇo na vaḍḍhati, evaṃ imasmiṃ sāsane yathāvuttehi sīlādīhi na vaḍḍhati, gopālako viya ca pañcahi gorasehi pañcahi dhammakkhandhehi paribāhiro hoti.

Na lakkhaṇakusalo hotī

Na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hotīti uppannaṃ kāmavitakkanti evaṃ vutte kāmavitakkādike na vinodeti, so imaṃ akusalavitakkaṃ āsāṭikaṃ ahāretvā vitakkavasiko hutvā vicaranto kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti, so yathā tassa gopālakassa…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hotī

Na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hotīti cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hotītiādinā nayena sabbārammaṇesu nimittaṃ gaṇhanto yathā so gopālako vaṇaṃ na paṭicchādeti, evaṃ saṃvaraṃ na sampādeti. So vivaṭadvāro vicaranto kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hotī

Na dhūmaṃ kattā hotīti so gopālako dhūmaṃ viya dhammadesanādhūmaṃ na karoti, dhammakathaṃ vā sarabhaññaṃ vā upanisinnakathaṃ vā anumodanaṃ vā na karoti . Tato naṃ manussā bahussuto guṇavāti na jānanti, te guṇāguṇaṃ ajānantā catūhi paccayehi saṅgahaṃ na karonti . So paccayehi kilamamāno buddhavacanaṃ sajjhāyaṃ kātuṃ vattapaṭipattiṃ pūretuṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na dhūmaṃ kattā hotī

Na titthaṃ jānātīti titthabhūte bahussutabhikkhū na upasaṅkamati, upasaṅkamanto, ‘‘idaṃ, bhante, byañjanaṃ kathaṃ ropetabbaṃ, imassa bhāsitassa ko attho, imasmiṃ ṭhāne pāḷi kiṃ vadeti, imasmiṃ ṭhāne attho kiṃ dīpetī’’ti evaṃ na paripucchati na paripañhati, na jānāpetīti attho. Tassa te evaṃ aparipucchato avivaṭañceva na vivaranti, bhājetvā na dassenti, anuttānīkatañca na uttānīkaronti, apākaṭaṃ na pākaṭaṃ karonti. Anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesūti anekavidhāsu kaṅkhāsu ekaṃ kaṅkhampi na paṭivinodenti. Kaṅkhā eva hi kaṅkhāṭhāniyā dhammā nāma. Tattha ekaṃ kaṅkhampi na nīharantīti attho. So evaṃ bahussutatitthaṃ anupasaṅkamitvā sakaṅkho kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti. Yathā ca so gopālako titthaṃ na jānāti, evaṃ ayampi bhikkhu dhammatitthaṃ na jānāti, ajānanto avisaye pañhaṃ pucchati, abhidhammikaṃ upasaṅkamitvā kappiyākappiyaṃ pucchati, vinayadharaṃ upasaṅkamitvā rūpārūpaparicchedaṃ pucchati. Te avisaye puṭṭhā kathetuṃ na sakkonti, so attanā sakaṅkho kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na titthaṃ jānātī Anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesū

Na pītaṃ jānātīti yathā so gopālako pītāpītaṃ na jānāti, evaṃ dhammūpasañhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ na jānāti na labhati, savanamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthuṃ nissāya ānisaṃsaṃ na vindati, dhammassavanaggaṃ gantvā sakkaccaṃ na suṇāti, nisinno niddāyati, kathaṃ katheti, aññavihitako hoti, so sakkaccaṃ dhammaṃ asuṇanto kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na pītaṃ jānātī

Na vīthiṃ jānātīti so gopālako maggāmaggaṃ viya, – ‘‘ayaṃ lokiyo ayaṃ lokuttaro’’ti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ yathābhūtaṃ na pajānāti. Ajānanto lokiyamagge abhinivisitvā lokuttaraṃ nibbattetuṃ na sakkoti…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na vīthiṃ jānātī

Na gocarakusalo hotīti so gopālako pañcāhikavāre sattāhikavāre viya cattāro satipaṭṭhāne , ‘‘ime lokiyā ime lokuttarā’’ti yathābhūtaṃ na pajānāti. Ajānanto sukhumaṭṭhānesu attano ñāṇaṃ carāpetvā lokiyasatipaṭṭhāne abhinivisitvā lokuttaraṃ nibbattetuṃ na sakkoti…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Na gocarakusalo hotī

Anavasesadohī ca hotīti paṭiggahaṇe mattaṃ ajānanto anavasesaṃ duhati. Niddesavāre panassa abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavārentīti abhiharitvā pavārenti. Ettha dve abhihārā vācābhihāro ca paccayābhihāro ca. Vācābhihāro nāma manussā bhikkhussa santikaṃ gantvā, ‘‘vadeyyātha, bhante, yenattho’’ti pavārenti. Paccayābhihāro nāma vatthādīni vā telaphāṇitādīni vā gahetvā bhikkhussa santikaṃ gantvā, ‘‘gaṇhatha, bhante, yāvatakena attho’’ti vadanti. Tatra bhikkhu mattaṃ na jānātīti bhikkhu tesu paccayesu pamāṇaṃ na jānāti, – ‘‘dāyakassa vaso veditabbo, deyyadhammassa vaso veditabbo, attano thāmo veditabbo’’ti rathavinīte vuttanayena pamāṇayuttaṃ aggahetvā yaṃ āharanti, taṃ sabbaṃ gaṇhātīti attho. Manussā vippaṭisārino na puna abhiharitvā pavārenti. So paccayehi kilamanto kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vaḍḍhetuṃ na sakkoti…pe… paribāhiro hoti.

Anavasesadohī ca hotī abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavārentī Vācābhihāro Paccayābhihāro Tatra bhikkhu mattaṃ na jānātī

Te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hotīti so gopālako mahāusabhe viya te there bhikkhū imāya āvi ceva raho ca mettāya kāyakammādikāya atirekapūjāya na pūjeti. Tato therā, – ‘‘ime amhesu garucittīkāraṃ na karontī’’ti navake bhikkhū dvīhi saṅgahehi na saṅgaṇhanti, na āmisasaṅgahena cīvarena vā pattena vā pattapariyāpannena vā vasanaṭṭhānena vā. Kilamante milāyantepi nappaṭijagganti. Pāḷiṃ vā aṭṭhakathaṃ vā dhammakathābandhaṃ vā guyhaganthaṃ vā na sikkhāpenti. Navakā therānaṃ santikā sabbaso ime dve saṅgahe alabhamānā imasmiṃ sāsane patiṭṭhātuṃ na sakkonti. Yathā tassa gopālakassa gogaṇo na vaḍḍhati, evaṃ sīlādīni na vaḍḍhanti. Yathā ca so gopālako pañcahi gorasehi paribāhiro hoti, evaṃ pañcahi dhammakkhandhehi paribāhirā honti. Sukkapakkho kaṇhapakkhe vuttavipallāsavasena yojetvā veditabboti.

Te na atirekapūjāya pūjetā hotī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāgopālakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
347. "Here" ( *idhā*) means in this teaching (*imasmiṃ sāsane*).

"He does not know form" (*na rūpaññū hotī*) means he does not know form as it has been described, namely, "the four great elements (*cattāri mahābhūtāni*) and the form derived from the four great elements (*catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa*)," in two ways, either by enumeration (*gaṇanato*) or by origin (*samuṭṭhānato*).

He does not know by enumeration (*gaṇanato*) means he does not know that "the eye-sphere (*cakkhāyatanaṃ*), the ear-nose-tongue-body-sphere (*sota-ghāna-jivhā-kāyāyatanaṃ*), the form-sound-smell-taste-tangible-sphere (*rūpa-sadda-gandha-rasa-phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ*), the woman-faculty (*itthindriyaṃ*), the man-faculty (*purisindriyaṃ*), the life-faculty (*jīvitindriyaṃ*), bodily communication (*kāyaviññatti*), verbal communication (*vacīviññatti*), the space-element (*ākāsadhātu*), the water-element (*āpodhātu*), lightness of form (*rūpassa lahutā*), pliancy (*mudutā*), adaptability (*kammaññatā*), integration (*upacayo*), continuity (*santati*), decay (*jaratā*), impermanence of form (*rūpassa aniccatā*), and edible food (*kabaḷīkāro āhāro*)," these twenty-five categories of form have come in the Pāli.

Just as a cowherd does not know the form of cows by enumeration (*gaṇanato gunnaṃ rūpaṃ na jānāti*), so too is this monk.

Not knowing form by enumeration (*gaṇanato rūpaṃ ajānanto*), having grasped form (*rūpaṃ pariggahetvā*), having determined the formless (*arūpaṃ vavatthapetvā*), having grasped form and the formless (*rūpārūpaṃ pariggahetvā*), having considered the conditions (*paccayaṃ sallakkhetvā*), having imposed the characteristics (*lakkhaṇaṃ āropetvā*), he is not able to bring the meditation subject (*kammaṭṭhānaṃ*) to the summit (*matthakaṃ pāpetuṃ na sakkoti*).

Just as the herd of cows of that cowherd does not grow (*yathā tassa gopālakassa gogaṇo na vaḍḍhati*), so too in this teaching he does not grow in ethical conduct (*sīla*), concentration (*samādhi*), insight (*vipassanā*), path (*magga*), fruit (*phala*), and nirvāṇa (*nibbānehi na vaḍḍhati*). And just as that cowherd is excluded from the five products of the cow (*pañcahi gorasehi paribāhiro hoti*), so too is he excluded from the five aggregates of qualities (*pañcahi dhammakkhandhehi paribāhiro hoti*), namely, the aggregate of flawless ethical conduct (*asekkhena sīlakkhandhena*), flawless concentration (*asekkhena samādhi*), wisdom (*paññā*), liberation (*vimutti*), and the aggregate of the vision of the knowledge of liberation (*vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena*).

By origin (*samuṭṭhānato*)…

He does not know means he does not know that "so much form has a single origin (*ettakaṃ rūpaṃ ekasamuṭṭhānaṃ*), so much has two origins (*ettakaṃ dvisamuṭṭhānaṃ*), so much has three origins (*ettakaṃ tisamuṭṭhānaṃ*), so much has four origins (*ettakaṃ catusamuṭṭhānaṃ*), so much does not originate from anywhere (*ettakaṃ na kutocisamuṭṭhātī*)."

Just as a cowherd does not know the form of cows by color (*vaṇṇato gunnaṃ rūpaṃ na jānāti*), so too is this monk.

Not knowing form by origin (*samuṭṭhānato rūpaṃ ajānanto*), having grasped form (*rūpaṃ pariggahetvā*), having determined the formless (*arūpaṃ vavatthapetvā*)…he is excluded.

He is not skilled in characteristics (*na lakkhaṇakusalo hotī*) means he does not know that "action has characteristics, a fool has characteristics, a wise person has characteristics," thus it is said, "skillful and unskillful action, the fool and the wise person have characteristics (*kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ paṇḍitabālalakkhaṇanti na jānāti*)."

Not knowing thus, avoiding fools he does not associate with the wise (*bāle vajjetvā paṇḍite na sevati*), avoiding fools and not associating with the wise, he does not know what is allowable and unallowable (*kappiyākappiyaṃ*), skillful and unskillful (*kusalākusalaṃ*), blameworthy and blameless (*sāvajNot knowing, having become fixed on the worldly path, he is not able to bring about the supramundane… he is excluded.

*He does not know the path.* *He is not skilled in the pasture*: that cowherd, like [one who reckons] a five-day period as a seven-day period, does not understand the four foundations of mindfulness, "these are worldly, these are supramundane," according to reality.

Not knowing, having roamed his knowledge in subtle places, having become fixed on the worldly foundations of mindfulness, he is not able to bring about the supramundane… he is excluded.

*He is not skilled in the pasture.* *He is an indiscriminate milker*: not knowing the proper measure in receiving, he milks indiscriminately.

But in the section on exposition, *they invite [him] to bring [offerings]*: they invite [him] having brought [offerings]. Here, there are two kinds of bringing: bringing by speech and bringing of requisites. *Bringing by speech* means people, having gone to the monk, invite [him], "Speak, venerable sir, by which [there is] benefit." *Bringing of requisites* means having taken cloths, etc., or ghee, molasses, etc., having gone to the monk, they say, "Take, venerable sir, as much as [there is] benefit." *There, the monk does not know the proper measure*: the monk does not know the measure in those requisites - "the patron's resources should be known, the value of the gift should be known, one's own strength should be known" - not taking [requisites] with proper measure in the way that was said in the Rathavinīta, he takes all that they bring, this is the meaning. People, being remorseful, do not invite [him] again having brought [offerings]. He, being exhausted by the requisites, is not able to take up a meditation subject and develop it… he is excluded.

*He is an indiscriminate milker.* *They invite [him] to bring [offerings].* *Bringing by speech.* *Bringing of requisites.* *There, the monk does not know the proper measure.* *They are not those who honor with excessive honor*: that cowherd, like a great bull, does not honor those elder monks with excessive honor by this loving-kindness of body-action, etc., both openly and in secret. Then the elders, [thinking], "these do not show respect to us," do not accept the new monks with the two acceptances, not with the acceptance of material things, with a robe, or a bowl, or what is connected with the bowl, or a dwelling place. Even when [they are] exhausted and withered, they do not care for [them]. They do not teach [them] the Pāḷi, or the commentary, or the arrangement of a Dhamma talk, or a secret text. The new monks, not obtaining these two acceptances entirely from the elders, are not able to be established in this Dispensation. Just as that cowherd's herd of cows does not grow, so sīla, etc., do not grow. And just as that cowherd is excluded from the five products of the cow, so they are excluded from the five aggregates of qualities. The bright side should be understood by connecting [it] in terms of the opposite of what was said in the dark side.

*They are not those who honor with excessive honor.*

The Mahāgopālakasuttavaṇṇanā is finished.

mula_pali: 348. ‘‘Ekādasahi , bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako bhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave , gopālako rūpaññū hoti, lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti, vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, titthaṃ jānāti, pītaṃ jānāti, vīthiṃ jānāti, gocarakusalo hoti, sāvasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te usabhā gopitaro gopariṇāyakā te atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako bhabbo gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjituṃ. Katamehi ekādasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaññū hoti, lakkhaṇakusalo hoti, āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti, vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti, dhūmaṃ kattā hoti, titthaṃ jānāti, pītaṃ jānāti, vīthiṃ jānāti, gocarakusalo hoti, sāvasesadohī ca hoti. Ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti.
mula_english:
348. "Bhikkhus, when a cowherd possesses eleven factors (ekādasahi aṅgehi), he is capable of keeping and rearing a herd of cattle.

What are the eleven? Here, bhikkhus, a cowherd has knowledge of form (rūpaññū), he is skilled in characteristics (lakkhaṇakusalo), he picks out flies’ eggs (āsāṭikaṃ hāretā), he dresses wounds (vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā), he smokes out the sheds (dhūmaṃ kattā), he knows the watering place (titthaṃ jānāti), he knows what it is to have drunk (pītaṃ jānāti), he knows the road (vīthiṃ jānāti), he is skilled in pastures (gocarakusalo), he does not milk dry (sāvasesadohī).

And he shows extra veneration to those bulls (usabhā) who are fathers (gopitaro) and leaders of the herd (gopariṇāyakā).

When a cowherd possesses these eleven factors (ekādasahi aṅgehi), he is capable of keeping and rearing a herd of cattle.

“So too, bhikkhus, when a *bhikṣu* possesses these eleven qualities (ekādasahi dhammehi), he is capable of growth (vuddhiṃ), increase (virūḷhiṃ), and fulfilment (vepullaṃ) in this Dhamma and Discipline (dhammavinaye).

What are the eleven? Here, bhikkhus, a *bhikṣu* has knowledge of form (rūpaññū), he is skilled in characteristics (lakkhaṇakusalo), he picks out flies’ eggs (āsāṭikaṃ hāretā), he dresses wounds (vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā), he smokes out the sheds (dhūmaṃ kattā), he knows the watering place (titthaṃ jānāti), he knows what it is to have drunk (pītaṃ jānāti), he knows the road (vīthiṃ jānāti), he is skilled in pastures (gocarakusalo), he does not milk dry (sāvasesadohī).

And he shows extra veneration to those elder *bhikkhus* (bhikkhū therā) of longstanding (rattaññū) who have long since gone forth (cirapabbajitā), the fathers (saṅghapitaro) and leaders of the Sangha (saṅghapariṇāyakā).

mula_pali:
349. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaññū hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘cattāri mahābhūtāni , catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rūpaññū hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu lakkhaṇakusalo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kammalakkhaṇo bālo, kammalakkhaṇo paṇḍitoti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu lakkhaṇakusalo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca , bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, pajahati vinodeti byantī karoti anabhāvaṃ gameti. Uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ…pe… uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ…pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti, pajahati vinodeti byantī karoti anabhāvaṃ gameti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsāṭikaṃ hāretā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vaṇaṃ paṭicchādetā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhūmaṃ kattā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ vitthārena paresaṃ desetā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhūmaṃ kattā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu titthaṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā te kālena kālaṃ upasaṅkamitvā paripucchati, paripañhati – ‘idaṃ, bhante, kathaṃ? Imassa ko attho’ti? Tassa te āyasmanto avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānī karonti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhānīyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṃ paṭivinodenti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu titthaṃ jānāti.

‘‘Kathañca bhikkhave, bhikkhu pītaṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pītaṃ jānāti.

‘‘Kathañca , bhikkhave, bhikkhu vīthiṃ jānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vīthiṃ jānāti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gocarakusalo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāro satipaṭṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gocarakusalo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca bhikkhave, bhikkhu sāvasesadohī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ saddhā gahapatikā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavārenti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi. Tatra bhikkhu mattaṃ jānāti paṭiggahaṇāya. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sāvasesadohī hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā, te atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā tesu mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpeti āvi ceva raho ca. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā te atirekapūjāya pūjetā hoti.

‘‘Imehi kho, bhikkhave, ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjitu’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Mahāgopālakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu have knowledge of form? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu understands as it actually is thus: ‘All material form of whatever kind consists of the four great elements (*cattāri mahābhūtāni*) and the material form derived from the four great elements (*catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyarūpa*).’ That is how a bhikkhu has knowledge of form.

“How, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu skilled in characteristics? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu understands as it actually is thus: ‘A fool is characterized by their actions; a wise person is characterized by their actions.’ That is how a bhikkhu is skilled in characteristics.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu pick out flies’ eggs? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not tolerate an arisen thought of sensual desire; he abandons it, dispels it, terminates it, and obliterates it. (He does not tolerate) an arisen thought of ill will… (He does not tolerate) an arisen thought of harming… (He does not tolerate) bad unwholesome states whenever they arise; he abandons them, dispels them, terminates them, and obliterates them. That is how a bhikkhu picks out flies’ eggs.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu dress wounds? Here, bhikkhus, having seen a form with the eye, the bhikkhu does not grasp at the sign or the details. Since, if he were to dwell without restraint over the faculty of the eye, evil unwholesome states such as covetousness and grief might assail him, he practises restraint, guards the faculty of the eye, and achieves restraint over the faculty of the eye. Having heard a sound with the ear … having smelled an odour with the nose … having tasted a flavour with the tongue … having touched a tangible object with the body … having cognized a mind-object with the mind, the bhikkhu does not grasp at the sign or the details. Since, if he were to dwell without restraint over the faculty of the mind, evil unwholesome states such as covetousness and grief might assail him, he practises restraint, guards the faculty of the mind, and achieves restraint over the faculty of the mind. That is how a bhikkhu dresses wounds.

“How, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu smoke out the sheds? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu teaches the Dhamma in detail to others just as he has heard it and learned it. That is how a bhikkhu smokes out the sheds.

“How, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu know the watering place? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu approaches those bhikkhus who are learned, versed in the scriptures, observers of the Dhamma, observers of the Vinaya, observers of the Codes, and when from time to time one asks them questions, ‘How is this, venerable sir? What is the meaning of this?’ then those venerable ones reveal the unrevealed, explain the unexplained, and remove doubt about the many things that raise doubts. That is how a bhikkhu knows the watering place.

“How, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu know what it is to have drunk? Here, bhikkhus, when the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata* is being taught, a bhikkhu gains inspiration in the meaning, gains inspiration in the Dhamma, gains gladness connected with the Dhamma. That is how a bhikkhu knows what it is to have drunk.

“How, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu understand the road? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu understands the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ*) as it actually is. That is how a bhikkhu understands the road.

“How, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu skilled in pastures? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu understands the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhāne*) as they actually are. That is how a bhikkhu is skilled in pastures.

“How, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu not milk dry? Here, bhikkhus, when faithful householders invite a bhikkhu to take as much as he likes of robes, almsfood, resting places, and medicinal requisites, the bhikkhu knows moderation in accepting. That is how a bhikkhu does not milk dry.
“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu show extra veneration to those elder bhikkhus of long-standing who have long gone forth, the fathers and leaders of the *saṅgha*? Here, a bhikkhu maintains bodily acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-kāyakarma*) towards those elder bhikkhus both openly and privately; he maintains verbal acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-vacīkarma*) towards them both openly and privately; he maintains mental acts of loving-kindness (*maitrī-manokarma*) towards them both openly and privately. That is how a bhikkhu shows extra veneration to those elder bhikkhus of long-standing who have long gone forth, the fathers and leaders of the *saṅgha*.

“When a bhikkhu possesses these eleven qualities (*ekādasahi dhammehi samannāgato*), he is capable of growth (*vṛddhi*), increase (*virūḷhi*), and fulfilment (*vepulla*) in this *dharma* and discipline (*dharma-vinaya*).”

The Blessed One said this.

Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Mahāgopālaka Sutta is finished, the third.

mula_pali:
350. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vajjīsu viharati ukkacelāyaṃ gaṅgāya nadiyā tīre. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ , bhikkhave, māgadhako gopālako duppaññajātiko, vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye, asamavekkhitvā gaṅgāya nadiyā orimaṃ tīraṃ, asamavekkhitvā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, atittheneva gāvo patāresi uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehānaṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, gāvo majjhegaṅgāya nadiyā sote āmaṇḍaliyaṃ karitvā tattheva anayabyasanaṃ āpajjiṃsu. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so, bhikkhave, māgadhako gopālako duppaññajātiko, vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye, asamavekkhitvā gaṅgāya nadiyā orimaṃ tīraṃ, asamavekkhitvā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, atittheneva gāvo patāresi uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehānaṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci ye keci (syā. kaṃ.) samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā akusalā imassa lokassa akusalā parassa lokassa, akusalā māradheyyassa akusalā amāradheyyassa, akusalā maccudheyyassa akusalā amaccudheyyassa, tesaṃ ye sotabbaṃ saddahātabbaṃ maññissanti, tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya.

ye keci (syā. kaṃ.)
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD. On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Vajjian country at Ukkacela on the banks of the river Ganges.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: “Bhikkhus!”

“Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“Bhikkhus, there was once a foolish Magadhan cowherd, who, in the last month of the rainy season, in the autumn, without examining the near shore or the further shore of the river Ganges, drove his cattle across to the other shore in the Videhan country at a place that had no ford.

Then the cattle bunched together in mid-stream in the river Ganges, and they met with calamity and disaster.

Why is that? Because that foolish Magadhan cowherd, in the last month of the rainy season, in the autumn, without examining the near shore or the further shore of the river Ganges, drove his cattle across to the other shore in the Videhan country at a place that had no ford.

Just so, monks, whichever *śramaṇas* or *brāhmaṇas* are unskilled in this world and the other world, unskilled in Māra's realm and what is outside Māra's realm, unskilled in the realm of Death and what is outside the realm of Death - it will lead to the harm and suffering for a long time of those who think they should listen to them and place faith in them.
commentary_pali:
350.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷagopālakasuttaṃ. Tattha ukkacelāyanti evaṃnāmake nagare. Tasmiṃ kira māpiyamāne rattiṃ gaṅgāsotato maccho thalaṃ patto. Manussā celāni telapātiyaṃ temetvā ukkā katvā macchaṃ gaṇhiṃsu. Nagare niṭṭhite tassa nāmaṃ karonte amhehi nagaraṭṭhānassa gahitadivase celukkāhi maccho gahitoti ukkacelā-tvevassa nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Bhikkhū āmantesīti yasmiṃ ṭhāne nisinnassa sabbā gaṅgā pākaṭā hutvā paññāyati, tādise vālikussade gaṅgātitthe sāyanhasamaye mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisīditvā mahāgaṅgaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ sandamānaṃ olokento, – ‘‘atthi nu kho imaṃ gaṅgaṃ nissāya koci pubbe vaḍḍhiparihāniṃ patto’’ti āvajjitvā, pubbe ekaṃ bālagopālakaṃ nissāya anekasatasahassā gogaṇā imissā gaṅgāya āvaṭṭe patitvā samuddameva paviṭṭhā, aparaṃ pana paṇḍitagopālakaṃ nissāya anekasatasahassagogaṇassa sotthi jātā vaḍḍhi jātā ārogyaṃ jātanti addasa. Disvā imaṃ kāraṇaṃ nissāya bhikkhūnaṃ dhammaṃ desessāmīti cintetvā bhikkhū āmantesi.

Māgadhakoti magadharaṭṭhavāsī. Duppaññajātikoti nippaññasabhāvo dandho mahājaḷo. Asamavekkhitvāti asallakkhetvā anupadhāretvā. Patāresīti tāretuṃ ārabhi. Uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehānanti gaṅgāya orime tīre magadharaṭṭhaṃ, pārime tīre videharaṭṭhaṃ, gāvo magadharaṭṭhato videharaṭṭhaṃ netvā rakkhissāmīti uttaraṃ tīraṃ patāresi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehāna’’nti. Āmaṇḍalikaṃ karitvāti maṇḍalikaṃ katvā. Anayabyasanaṃ āpajjiṃsūti avaḍḍhiṃ vināsaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu, mahāsamuddameva pavisiṃsu. Tena hi gopālakena gāvo otārentena gaṅgāya orimatīre samatitthañca visamatitthañca oloketabbaṃ assa, majjhe gaṅgāya gunnaṃ vissamaṭṭhānatthaṃ dve tīṇi vālikatthalāni sallakkhetabbāni assu. Tathā pārimatīre tīṇi cattāri titthāni, imasmā titthā bhaṭṭhā imaṃ titthaṃ gaṇhissanti, imasmā bhaṭṭhā imanti. Ayaṃ pana bālagopālako orimatīre gunnaṃ otaraṇatitthaṃ samaṃ vā visamaṃ vā anoloketvāva majjhe gaṅgāya gunnaṃ vissamaṭṭhānatthaṃ dve tīṇi vālikatthalānipi asallakkhetvāva paratīre cattāri pañca uttaraṇatitthāni asamavekkhitvāva atittheneva gāvo otāresi. Athassa mahāusabho javanasampannatāya ceva thāmasampannatāya ca tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā pārimaṃ tīraṃ patvā chinnataṭañceva kaṇṭakagumbagahanañca disvā, ‘‘dubbiniviṭṭhameta’’nti ñatvā dhuragga-patiṭṭhānokāsampi alabhitvā paṭinivatti. Gāvo mahāusabho nivatto mayampi nivattissāmāti nivattā. Mahato gogaṇassa nivattaṭṭhāne udakaṃ chijjitvā majjhe gaṅgāya āvaṭṭaṃ uṭṭhapesi. Gogaṇo āvaṭṭaṃ pavisitvā samuddameva patto. Ekopi goṇo arogo nāma nāhosi. Tenāha – ‘‘tattheva anayabyasanaṃ āpajjiṃsū’’ti.

Māgadhako Duppaññajātiko Asamavekkhitvā Patāresī Uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehāna Āmaṇḍalikaṃ karitvā Anayabyasanaṃ āpajjiṃsū

Akusalā imassa lokassāti idha loke khandhadhātāyatanesu akusalā achekā, paralokepi eseva nayo. Māradheyyaṃ vuccati tebhūmakadhammā. Amāradheyyaṃ nava lokuttaradhammā. Maccudheyyampi tebhūmakadhammāva. Amaccudheyyaṃ nava lokuttaradhammā. Tattha akusalā achekā. Vacanatthato pana mārassa dheyyaṃ māradheyyaṃ. Dheyyanti ṭhānaṃ vatthu nivāso gocaro. Maccudheyyepi eseva nayo. Tesanti tesaṃ evarūpānaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ, iminā cha satthāro dassitāti veditabbā.

Akusalā imassa lokassā Māradheyyaṃ Amāradheyyaṃ Maccudheyya Amaccudheyyaṃ akusalā māradheyyaṃ. Dheyya Maccudheyye Tesa
commentary_english:
350. Thus, as I have heard: the Cūḷagopālaka Sūtra.

Therein, "Ukkacelā" means in a city of that name.

When it was being measured, at night a fish from the Ganges stream arrived on dry land.

People, having soaked cloths in an oil-pot, made torches and caught the fish.

When the city was finished, while they were making a name for it, they named it "Ukkacelā" because we caught a fish with cloth-torches on the day of the city's founding.

"He addressed the monks" means all the Ganges is visible in whatever place one sits; having sat down on a sandy mound on a Ganges ford of that sort at evening time, surrounded by a great assembly of monks, while gazing at the great Ganges, completely flowing, – "Indeed, having relied on this Ganges, has anyone formerly met with increase or decrease?" Having reflected, formerly, relying on one foolish cowherd, hundreds of thousands of cattle, having fallen into a whirlpool of this Ganges, entered right into the ocean. But, relying on another wise cowherd, safety arose, increase arose, health arose for hundreds of thousands of cattle.

Having seen, thinking, "Having relied on this cause, I will teach the *dharma* to the monks," he addressed the monks.

"Māgadhaka" means a resident of the kingdom of Magadha.

"Duppaññajātiko" means one whose nature is without wisdom, slow, greatly dull.

"Asamavekkhitvā" means without considering, without examining, without pondering.

"Patāresi" means he began to carry across.

"Uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehāna" means, "Having led the cows from the kingdom of Magadha to the kingdom of Videha on this near shore of the Ganges, on that far shore, I will protect [them]," he carried [them] to the further shore.

With reference to that, it was said – "Uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehāna."

"Āmaṇḍalikaṃ karitvā" means having made a circle.

"Anayabyasanaṃ āpajjiṃsu" means they attained decrease [and] ruin, they entered right into the great ocean.

Therefore, the ford by which the cows are carried across the Ganges, whether it is level or uneven on the near shore of the Ganges, should be looked at; in the middle of the Ganges, two or three sandy resting places for the cattle should be examined.

Likewise, on the far shore, three [or] four fords. "Having strayed from this ford, they will seize this ford; having strayed from this, this."

But this foolish cowherd, without looking at whether the ford for leading down the cows on the near shore is level or uneven, and without examining two or three sandy resting places for the cattle in the middle of the Ganges, led the cows down at a non-ford on the far shore.

Then, a great bull, by means of completeness of swiftness, and also by means of completeness of strength, having cut the stream of the Ganges crosswise, having reached the far shore, and having seen a cut bank and a thicket of thorny bushes, knowing, "This is badly situated," and also not obtaining a place for the tip of the yoke to stand, turned back.

"The cows [and] the great bull have turned back; we also will turn back," they turned back.

In the place where the great herd of cattle turned back, having cut off the water, he stirred up a whirlpool in the middle of the Ganges.

The herd of cattle, having entered the whirlpool, arrived right at the ocean.

Not even one bull was without disease.

Therefore he said – "Right there, they met with misfortune [and] calamity."

Māgadhaka, duppaññajātiko, asamavekkhitvā, patāresi, uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehāna, āmaṇḍalikaṃ karitvā, anayabyasanaṃ āpajjiṃsu.

"Akusalā imassa lokassa" means unskilled in this world, unskilled in the aggregates, elements and sense-bases, the same is true in the next world.

"Māradheyyaṃ" is said to be the three-planed *dharmas*.

"Amāradheyyaṃ" [are] the nine supramundane *dharmas*.

"Maccudheyyaṃ" also, is just the three-planed *dharmas*.

"Amaccudheyyaṃ" [are] the nine supramundane *dharmas*.

Therein, "akusalā" [means] unskilled.
Because the meaning of the term *māradheyyaṃ* depends on the word, it means *māradheyyaṃ.* 

*Dheyya* means place, object, dwelling, or range.

The same method applies to *maccudheyye*.

*Tesa* means those *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s of such a form; by this, the teachers are shown and should be understood.

Unwholesome things are the *māradheyyaṃ* of this world, and *amāradheyyaṃ*, *maccudheyya*, and *amaccudheyyaṃ* are unwholesome and *māradheyyaṃ*.

*Dheyya*, *maccudheyye*, *tesa*.

mula_pali: 351. ‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, māgadhako gopālako sappaññajātiko, vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye, samavekkhitvā gaṅgāya nadiyā orimaṃ tīraṃ, samavekkhitvā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, tittheneva gāvo patāresi uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehānaṃ. So paṭhamaṃ patāresi ye te usabhā gopitaro gopariṇāyakā. Te tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu. Athāpare patāresi balavagāvo dammagāvo. Tepi tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu. Athāpare patāresi vacchatare vacchatariyo. Tepi tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu. Athāpare patāresi vacchake kisābalake kisabalake (sī. syā. pī.). Tepi tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, vacchako taruṇako tāvadeva jātako mātugoravakena vuyhamāno, sopi tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamāsi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi so, bhikkhave, māgadhako gopālako sappaññajātiko , vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye, samavekkhitvā gaṅgāya nadiyā orimaṃ tīraṃ, samavekkhitvā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, tittheneva gāvo patāresi uttaraṃ tīraṃ suvidehānaṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kusalā imassa lokassa kusalā parassa lokassa, kusalā māradheyyassa kusalā amāradheyyassa, kusalā maccudheyyassa kusalā amaccudheyyassa, tesaṃ ye sotabbaṃ saddahātabbaṃ maññissanti, tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya.
mula_english:
351. Bhikkhus, there was once a wise Magadhan cowherd, in the last month of the rainy season, in the autumn, after examining the near shore and the far shore of the river Ganges (Gaṅgā), drove his cattle across to the other shore in the Videhan country at a place that had a ford.

He made the bulls, the fathers and leaders of the herd, enter first.

They breasted the stream of the Ganges (Gaṅgā) and got safely across to the further shore.

He made the strong cattle and the cattle to be tamed enter next.

They too breasted the stream of the Ganges (Gaṅgā) and got safely across to the further shore.

He made the heifers and young oxen enter next.

They too breasted the stream of the Ganges (Gaṅgā) and got safely across to the further shore.

He made the calves, the weak ones, enter next.

They too breasted the stream of the Ganges (Gaṅgā) and got safely across to the further shore.

Bhikkhus, there was once a tender calf, just born, and being urged on by its mother’s lowing, it too breasted the stream of the Ganges (Gaṅgā) and got safely across to the further shore.

Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, that wise Magadhan cowherd, in the last month of the rainy season, in the autumn, after examining the near shore and the far shore of the river Ganges (Gaṅgā), drove his cattle across to the other shore in the Videhan country at a place that had a ford.

So too, bhikkhus, as to those *śramaṇas* (*samaṇā*) and *brāhmaṇas* (*brāhmaṇā*) who are skilled in this world and the other world, skilled in Māra's realm and what is outside Māra's realm, skilled in the realm of death and what is outside the realm of death - it will lead to the welfare and happiness for a long time of those who think they should listen to them and place faith in them.
commentary_pali: 351. Evaṃ kaṇhapakkhaṃ niṭṭhapetvā sukkapakkhaṃ dassento bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha balavagāvoti dantagoṇe ceva dhenuyo ca. Dammagāvoti dametabbagoṇe ceva avijātagāvo ca. Vacchatareti vacchabhāvaṃ taritvā ṭhite balavavacche. Vacchaketi dhenupake taruṇavacchake . Kisābalaketi appamaṃsalohite mandathāme. Tāvadeva jātakoti taṃdivase jātako. Mātugoravakena vuyhamānoti mātā purato purato huṃhunti goravaṃ katvā saññaṃ dadamānā urena udakaṃ chindamānā gacchati, vacchako tāya goravasaññāya dhenuyā vā urena chinnodakena gacchamāno ‘‘mātugoravakena vuyhamāno’’ti vuccati.
commentary_english:
351. Thus, having completed the dark fortnight and showing the bright fortnight, he said, "<hi rend="bold">Formerly, oh monks</hi>," and so forth.

There, "<hi rend="bold">balavagāvo</hi>" means oxen with developed teeth as well as cows.

"<hi rend="bold">dammagāvo</hi>" means oxen that should be tamed as well as untamed cattle.

"<hi rend="bold">vacchatare</hi>" means a strong calf that has crossed beyond the state of being a calf and is established.

"<hi rend="bold">vacchake</hi>" means a young calf in the care of a cow.

"<hi rend="bold">kisābalake</hi>" means having little flesh and blood, with weak strength.

"<hi rend="bold">tāvadeva jātako</hi>" means born on that very day.

"<hi rend="bold">mātugoravakena vuyhamāno</hi>" means being carried along by honoring one's mother: the mother goes in front, making a "hum hum" sound, showing respect and giving a signal, going along cutting the water with her chest; the calf, going along following that respectful signal of the cow or the water cut by the chest, is called "being carried along by honoring one's mother."

mula_pali:
352. ‘‘Seyyathāpi , bhikkhave, ye te usabhā gopitaro gopariṇāyakā te tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu, evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, te tiriyaṃ mārassa sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gatā.

‘‘Seyyathāpi te, bhikkhave, balavagāvo dammagāvo tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu, evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā, tepi tiriyaṃ mārassa sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gamissanti.

‘‘Seyyathāpi te, bhikkhave, vacchatarā vacchatariyo tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu, evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakiṃdeva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti, tepi tiriyaṃ mārassa sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gamissanti.

‘‘Seyyathāpi te, bhikkhave, vacchakā kisābalakā tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamaṃsu, evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyanā, tepi tiriyaṃ mārassa sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gamissanti.

‘‘Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, vacchako taruṇako tāvadeva jātako mātugoravakena vuyhamāno tiriyaṃ gaṅgāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ agamāsi, evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū dhammānusārino saddhānusārino, tepi tiriyaṃ mārassa sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gamissanti.

‘‘Ahaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, kusalo imassa lokassa kusalo parassa lokassa, kusalo māradheyyassa kusalo amāradheyyassa, kusalo maccudheyyassa kusalo amaccudheyyassa. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, ye sotabbaṃ saddahātabbaṃ maññissanti, tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvā sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Ayaṃ loko paro loko, jānatā suppakāsito;

Yañca mārena sampattaṃ, appattaṃ yañca maccunā.

‘‘Sabbaṃ lokaṃ abhiññāya, sambuddhena pajānatā;

Vivaṭaṃ amatadvāraṃ, khemaṃ nibbānapattiyā.

‘‘Chinnaṃ pāpimato sotaṃ, viddhastaṃ vinaḷīkataṃ;

Pāmojjabahulā hotha, khemaṃ pattattha patthetha (syā. kaṃ. ka. aṭṭhakathāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbapāṭho) bhikkhavo’’ti.

patthetha (syā. kaṃ. ka. aṭṭhakathāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbapāṭho)

Cūḷagopālakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
352. Just as the bulls, the fathers and leaders of the herd, breasted the stream of the Ganges and got safely across to the further shore, so too, those *bhikkhus* who are *arahants* with taints destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), who have lived the holy life, done what had to be done (*katakaraṇīya*), laid down the burden, reached the true goal, destroyed the fetters of being (*bhava-saṃyojanā*), and are completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammad-aññā*)- by breasting Mara’s stream they have gotten safely across to the further shore.

Just as the strong cattle and the cattle to be tamed breasted the stream of the Ganges and got safely across to the further shore, so too, those *bhikkhus* who, with the destruction of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*), will reappear spontaneously (*opapātikā*) in the Pure Abodes and there attain final *Nibbāna* without ever returning from that world - by breasting Mara’s stream they will get safely across to the further shore.

Just as the heifers and young oxen breasted the stream of the Ganges and got safely across to the further shore, so too, those *bhikkhus* who, with the destruction of three fetters (*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*) and with the attenuation of lust (*rāga*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*), are once-returners (*sakadāgāmino*), returning once to this world to make an end of suffering (*dukkha*) - by breasting Mara’s stream they too will get safely across to the further shore.

Just as the calves and the feeble cattle breasted the stream of the Ganges and got safely across to the further shore, so too, those *bhikkhus* who, with the destruction of three fetters (*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*), are stream-enterers (*sotāpannā*), no longer subject to perdition (*avinipātadhammā*), bound for deliverance, headed for enlightenment (*sambodhi-parāyanā*) - by breasting Mara’s stream they too will get safely across to the further shore.

Just as that tender calf just born, being urged on by its mother’s lowing, also breasted the stream of the Ganges and got safely across to the further shore, so too, those *bhikkhus* who are *Dhamma*-followers (*dhammānusārino*) and faith-followers (*saddhānusārino*) - by breasting Mara’s stream they too will get safely across to the further shore.

I, *bhikkhus*, am skilled in this world and in the other world, skilled in Mara’s realm (*māradheyyassa*) and in what is outside Mara’s realm (*amāradheyyassa*), skilled in the realm of Death (*maccudheyyassa*) and in what is outside the realm of Death (*amaccudheyyassa*).
It will lead to the welfare (*hitāya*) and happiness (*sukhāya*) for a long time of those who think they should listen to me and place faith in me.

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*bhagavā*).
Having said this, the Well-Gone (*sugato*), the Teacher (*satthā*) then said further:

This world, the other world, is well-proclaimed by the knowing one;
And what is reached by *Māra*, and what is not reached by death.

Having fully known all the world, by the fully awakened one (*sambuddhena*), the knowing one;
The door to the deathless (*amatadvāraṃ*) is opened, safety (*khemaṃ*) for the attainment of *Nibbāna*.

Cut off is the stream of the evil one (*pāpimato sotaṃ*), destroyed, made devoid of reeds;
Be abundant with joy (*pāmojjabahulā hotha*), attain safety (*khemaṃ*), *bhikkhus*.

The Lesser Cowherd Discourse (*cūḷagopālakasuttaṃ*), the fourth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
352.Mārassasotaṃ chetvāti arahattamaggena mārassa taṇhāsotaṃ chetvā. Pāraṃ gatāti mahāusabhā nadīpāraṃ viya saṃsārapāraṃ nibbānaṃ gatā. Pāraṃ agamaṃsūti mahāusabhānaṃ pāraṅgatakkhaṇe gaṅgāya sotassa tayo koṭṭhāse atikkamma ṭhitā mahāusabhe pāraṃ patte disvā tesaṃ gatamaggaṃ paṭipajjitvā pāraṃ agamaṃsu. Pāraṃ gamissantīti catumaggavajjhānaṃ kilesānaṃ tayo koṭṭhāse khepetvā ṭhitā idāni arahattamaggena avasesaṃ taṇhāsotaṃ chetvā balavagāvo viya nadīpāraṃ saṃsārapāraṃ nibbānaṃ gamissantīti. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo. Dhammānusārino, saddhānusārinoti ime dve paṭhamamaggasamaṅgino.

Jānatāti sabbadhamme jānantena buddhena. Suppakāsitoti sukathito. Vivaṭanti vivaritaṃ. Amatadvāranti ariyamaggo. Nibbānapattiyāti tadatthāya vivaṭaṃ. Vinaḷīkatanti vigatamānanaḷaṃ kataṃ. Khemaṃ patthethāti kattukamyatāchandena arahattaṃ patthetha, kattukāmā nibbattetukāmā hothāti attho. ‘‘Patta’tthā’’tipi pāṭho. Evarūpaṃ satthāraṃ labhitvā tumhe pattāyeva nāmāti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Bhagavā pana yathānusandhināva desanaṃ niṭṭhapesīti.

Jānatā Suppakāsito Vivaṭa Amatadvāra Nibbānapattiyā Vinaḷīkata Khemaṃ patthethā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷagopālakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
352.

*Mārassa sotaṃ chetvā* means having severed the stream of Māra, severing the stream of craving ( *taṇhā*) of Māra by the path of the Arhat ( *arahattamaggena*).

*Pāraṃ gatā* means having gone to the further shore of *saṃsāra*, like Mahāusabha having gone to the further shore of the river, [they] have gone to *nirvāṇa*.

*Pāraṃ agamaṃsū* means those who, at the moment Mahāusabha went to the further shore (*pāraṅgatakkhaṇe*), stood having crossed the three portions of the stream of the Ganges (*gaṅgāya sotassa tayo koṭṭhāse atikkamma ṭhitā*), seeing Mahāusabha having reached the further shore (*mahāusabhe pāraṃ patte disvā*), having followed the path he took (*tesaṃ gatamaggaṃ paṭipajjitvā*), they went to the further shore (*pāraṃ agamaṃsu*).

*Pāraṃ gamissantī* means those who, of the four paths (*catumaggavajjhānaṃ*), having destroyed the three portions of the defilements (*kilesānaṃ tayo koṭṭhāse khepetvā ṭhitā*), now, by the path of the Arhat (*arahattamaggena*), having severed the remaining stream of craving (*avasesaṃ taṇhāsotaṃ chetvā*), like strong cattle (*balavagāvo viya*), will go to the further shore of the river, to the further shore of *saṃsāra*, to *nirvāṇa* (*nadīpāraṃ saṃsārapāraṃ nibbānaṃ gamissantīti*).

In this way (*iminā nayena*), the meaning (*attho*) should be understood in all instances (*sabbavāresu veditabbo*).

*Dhammānusārino, saddhānusārino* means these two (*ime dve*) are complete with the first path (*paṭhamamaggasamaṅgino*).

*Jānatā* means by the Buddha, who knows all things (*sabbadhamme jānantena buddhena*).

*Suppakāsito* means well-spoken (*sukathito*).

*Vivaṭa* means opened (*vivaritaṃ*).

*Amatadvāra* means the noble path ( *ariyamaggo*).

*Nibbānapattiyā* means opened for that purpose (*tadatthāya vivaṭaṃ*).

*Vinaḷīkata* means *vigatamānanaḷaṃ kataṃ*.

*Khemaṃ patthethā* means you should aspire to Arhatship (*arahattaṃ patthetha*) with the desire to do (*kattukamyatāchandena*), the desire to produce, the desire to be (*kattukāmā nibbattetukāmā hothāti attho*).

There is also the reading, "attained meaning" (*patta'tthā'tipi pāṭho*).

Having obtained such a teacher ( *evarūpaṃ satthāraṃ labhitvā*), you have indeed attained [it] (*tumhe pattāyeva nāmāti attho*).

The rest is clear throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*), indeed, completed the teaching with accordance (*yathānusandhināva desanaṃ niṭṭhapesīti*).

*Jānatā suppakāsito vivaṭa amatadvāra nibbānapattiyā vinaḷīkata khemaṃ patthethā*

The Cūḷagopālakasuttavaṇṇanā, [a commentary] of the Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā, [belonging to] the Papañcasūdanī, is finished.

mula_pali:
353. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena saccako nigaṇṭhaputto vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati bhassappavādako paṇḍitavādo sādhusammato bahujanassa. So vesāliyaṃ parisati evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsati – ‘‘nāhaṃ taṃ passāmi samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā, saṅghiṃ gaṇiṃ gaṇācariyaṃ, api arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ paṭijānamānaṃ, yo mayā vādena vādaṃ samāraddho na saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampavedheyya, yassa na kacchehi sedā mucceyyuṃ. Thūṇaṃ cepāhaṃ acetanaṃ vādena vādaṃ samārabheyyaṃ, sāpi mayā vādena vādaṃ samāraddhā saṅkampeyya sampakampeyya sampavedheyya. Ko pana vādo manussabhūtassā’’ti?

Atha kho āyasmā assaji pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasā kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto vesāliyaṃ jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno āyasmantaṃ assajiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna yenāyasmā assaji tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā assajinā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto āyasmantaṃ assajiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kathaṃ pana, bho assaji, samaṇo gotamo sāvake vineti, kathaṃbhāgā ca pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakesu anusāsanī bahulā pavattatī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ kho, aggivessana, bhagavā sāvake vineti, evaṃbhāgā ca pana bhagavato sāvakesu anusāsanī bahulā pavattati – ‘rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ, vedanā aniccā, saññā aniccā, saṅkhārā aniccā, viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ. Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, anattā, vedanā anattā, saññā anattā, saṅkhārā anattā, viññāṇaṃ anattā. Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā, sabbe dhammā anattā’ti. Evaṃ kho, aggivessana, bhagavā sāvake vineti, evaṃbhāgā ca pana bhagavato sāvakesu anusāsanī bahulā pavattatī’’ti. ‘‘Dussutaṃ vata, bho assaji, assumha ye mayaṃ evaṃvādiṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ assumha. Appeva nāma mayaṃ kadāci karahaci tena bhotā gotamena saddhiṃ samāgaccheyyāma , appeva nāma siyā kocideva kathāsallāpo, appeva nāma tasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā viveceyyāmā’’ti.
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD.

On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Vesali in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.

At that time Saccaka, the son of Nigantha, a clever disputant, considered wise by many lived in Vesali.

He would go about Vesali saying. I do not see a recluse, a *śramaṇa*, or a *brāhmaṇa*, a leader of a crowd, a teacher of a crowd, or one acknowledging he is perfect and rightfully enlightened not shivering, trembling and sweating when invited to a dispute by me.

Even if I were to start a debate with an inanimate pillar, it would tremble, shake, and quake when engaged in debate by me.

What need be said of one who is human?"

Then the Venerable Assaji, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vesali for alms.

Saccaka the son of Nigantha walking and wandering for exercise saw venerable Assaji coming in the distance

and approached venerable Assaji. exchanged friendly greetings

After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies he stood to one side.

and standing on a side said: “Good Assaji, how are the disciples of the *śramaṇa* Gotama trained, and in what section are they given a lot of the training.

Then venerable Assaji said, Aggivessana, the Blessed One gives his disciples a lot of advice and trains the disciples much in this section:“Bhikkhus, matter (*rūpa*) is impermanent (*anitya*). Feelings (*vedanā*) are impermanent (*anitya*). Perceptions (*saṃjñā*) are impermanent (*anitya*). Determinations (*saṃskārā*) are impermanent (*anitya*) and consciousness (*vijñāna*) is impermanent (*anitya*).

Bhikkhus, matter (*rūpa*) is not self (*anātman*). Feelings (*vedanā*) are not self (*anātman*). Perceptions (*saṃjñā*) are not self (*anātman*). Determinations (*saṃskārā*) are not self (*anātman*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) is not self (*anātman*).

All determinations (*saṃskārā*) are impermanent (*anitya*). All things (*dharmā*) are not self (*anātman*).

Aggivessana, the Blessed One advises the *bhikkhus* much on this and the training is much on this.

Good Assaji, we heard something that should not be heard. If the *śramaṇa* Gotama is of this view,

indeed we should meet him for a conversation on this. To dispel doubts on this view.
commentary_pali:
353.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷasaccakasuttaṃ. Tattha mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyanti mahāvanaṃ nāma sayaṃjātaṃ aropimaṃ saparicchedaṃ mahantaṃ vanaṃ. Kapilavatthusāmantā pana mahāvanaṃ himavantena saha ekābaddhaṃ aparicchedaṃ hutvā mahāsamuddaṃ āhacca ṭhitaṃ. Idaṃ tādisaṃ na hoti. Saparicchedaṃ mahantaṃ vananti mahāvanaṃ. Kūṭāgārasālā pana mahāvanaṃ nissāya kate ārāme kūṭāgāraṃ antokatvā haṃsavaṭṭakacchannena katā sabbākārasampannā buddhassa bhagavato gandhakuṭi veditabbā.

Saccakonigaṇṭhaputtoti pubbe kira eko nigaṇṭho ca nigaṇṭhī ca pañca pañca vādasatāni uggahetvā, vādaṃ āropessāmāti jambudīpe vicarantā vesāliyaṃ samāgatā. Licchavirājāno disvā, – ‘‘tvaṃ ko, tvaṃ kā’’ti pucchiṃsu. Nigaṇṭho – ‘‘ahaṃ vādaṃ āropessāmīti jambudīpe vicarāmī’’ti āha. Nigaṇṭhīpi tathā āha. Licchavino, ‘‘idheva aññamaññaṃ vādaṃ āropethā’’ti āhaṃsu. Nigaṇṭhī attanā uggahitāni pañcavādasatāni pucchi, nigaṇṭho kathesi. Nigaṇṭhena pucchitepi nigaṇṭhī kathesiyeva. Ekassapi na jayo, na parājayo, ubho samasamāva ahesuṃ. Licchavino, – ‘‘tumhe ubhopi samasamā āhiṇḍitvā kiṃ karissatha, idheva vasathā’’ti gehaṃ datvā baliṃ paṭṭhapesuṃ. Tesaṃ saṃvāsamanvāya catasso dhītaro jātā, – ekā saccā nāma, ekā lolā nāma, ekā paṭācārā nāma, ekā ācāravatī nāma. Tāpi paṇḍitāva ahesuṃ, mātāpitūhi uggahitāni pañca pañca vādasatāni uggahesuṃ. Tā vayapattā mātāpitaro avocuṃ – ‘‘amhākaṃ ammā kule dārikā nāma hiraññasuvaṇṇādīni datvā kulagharaṃ pesitapubbā nāma natthi. Yo pana agāriko tāsaṃ vādaṃ maddituṃ sakkoti, tassa pādaparicārikā honti. Yo pabbajito tāsaṃ maddituṃ sakkoti, tassa santike pabbajanti. Tumhe kiṃ karissathā’’ti? Mayampi evameva karissāmāti. Catassopi paribbājikavesaṃ gahetvā, ‘‘ayaṃ jambudīpo nāma jambuyā paññāyatī’’ti jambusākhaṃ gahetvā cārikaṃ pakkamiṃsu. Yaṃ gāmaṃ pāpuṇanti, tassa dvāre paṃsupuñje vā vālikapuñje vā jambudhajaṃ ṭhapetvā, – ‘‘yo vādaṃ āropetuṃ sakkoti, so imaṃ maddatū’’ti vatvā gāmaṃ pavisanti. Evaṃ gāmena gāmaṃ vicarantiyo sāvatthiṃ pāpuṇitvā tatheva gāmadvāre jambudhajaṃ ṭhapetvā sampattamanussānaṃ ārocetvā antonagaraṃ paviṭṭhā.

Saccako nigaṇṭhaputto

Tena samayena bhagavā sāvatthiṃ nissāya jetavane viharati. Athāyasmā sāriputto gilāne pucchanto ajaggitaṭṭhānaṃ jagganto attano kiccamahantatāya aññehi bhikkhūhi divātaraṃ gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisanto gāmadvāre jambudhajaṃ disvā, – ‘‘kimida’’nti dārake pucchi. Te tamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Tena hi maddathāti. Na sakkoma, bhante, bhāyāmāti. ‘‘Kumārā mā bhāyatha, ‘kena amhākaṃ jambudhajo maddāpito’ti vutte, buddhasāvakena sāriputtattherena maddāpito, vādaṃ āropetukāmā jetavane therassa santikaṃ gacchathāti vadeyyāthā’’ti āha. Te therassa vacanaṃ sutvā jambudhajaṃ madditvā chaḍḍesuṃ. Thero piṇḍāya caritvā vihāraṃ gato. Paribbājikāpi gāmato nikkhamitvā, ‘‘amhākaṃ dhajo kena maddāpito’’ti pucchiṃsu. Dārakā tamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Paribbājikā puna gāmaṃ pavisitvā ekekaṃ vīthiṃ gahetvā, – ‘‘buddhasāvako kira sāriputto nāma amhehi saddhiṃ vādaṃ karissati, sotukāmā nikkhamathā’’ti ārocesuṃ. Mahājano nikkhami, tena saddhiṃ paribbājikā jetavanaṃ agamiṃsu.

Thero – ‘‘amhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne mātugāmassa āgamanaṃ nāma aphāsuka’’nti vihāramajjhe nisīdi. Paribbājikāyo gantvā theraṃ pucchiṃsu – ‘‘tumhehi amhākaṃ dhajo maddāpito’’ti? Āma, mayā maddāpitoti. Mayaṃ tumhehi saddhiṃ vādaṃ karissāmāti. Sādhu karotha, kassa pucchā kassa vissajjanaṃ hotūti? Pucchā nāma amhākaṃ pattā, tumhe pana mātugāmā nāma paṭhamaṃ pucchathāti āha. Tā catassopi catūsu disāsu ṭhatvā mātāpitūnaṃ santike uggahitaṃ vādasahassaṃ pucchiṃsu. Thero khaggena kumudanāḷaṃ chindanto viya pucchitaṃ pucchitaṃ nijjaṭaṃ niggaṇṭhiṃ katvā kathesi, kathetvā puna pucchathāti āha. Ettakameva, bhante, mayaṃ jānāmāti. Thero āha – ‘‘tumhehi vādasahassaṃ pucchitaṃ mayā kathitaṃ, ahaṃ pana ekaṃ yeva pañhaṃ pucchissāmi, taṃ tumhe kathethā’’ti. Tā therassa visayaṃ disvā, ‘‘pucchatha, bhante, byākarissāmā’’ti vattuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. ‘‘Vada, bhante, jānamānā byākarissāmā’’ti puna āhaṃsu.

Thero ayaṃ pana kulaputte pabbājetvā paṭhamaṃ sikkhāpetabbapañhoti vatvā, – ‘‘ekaṃ nāma ki’’nti pucchi. Tā neva antaṃ, na koṭiṃ addasaṃsu. Thero kathethāti āha. Na passāma, bhanteti. Tumhehi vādasahassaṃ pucchitaṃ mayā kathitaṃ, mayhaṃ tumhe ekaṃ pañhampi kathetuṃ na sakkotha, evaṃ sante kassa jayo kassa parājayoti? Tumhākaṃ, bhante, jayo, amhākaṃ parājayoti. Idāni kiṃ karissathāti? Tā mātāpitūhi vuttavacanaṃ ārocetvā, ‘‘tumhākaṃ santike pabbajissāmā’’ti āhaṃsu. Tumhe mātugāmā nāma amhākaṃ santike pabbajituṃ na vaṭṭati, amhākaṃ pana sāsanaṃ gahetvā bhikkhuniupassayaṃ gantvā pabbajathāti. Tā sādhūti therassa sāsanaṃ gahetvā bhikkhunisaṅghassa santikaṃ gantvā pabbajiṃsu. Pabbajitā ca pana appamattā ātāpiniyo hutvā nacirasseva arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu.

Ayaṃ saccako tāsaṃ catunnampi kaniṭṭhabhātiko. Tāhi catūhipi uttaritarapañño, mātāpitūnampi santikā vādasahassaṃ, tato bahutarañca bāhirasamayaṃ uggahetvā katthaci agantvā rājadārake sippaṃ sikkhāpento tattheva vesāliyaṃ vasati, paññāya atipūritattā kucchi me bhijjeyyāti bhīto ayapaṭṭena kucchiṃ parikkhipitvā carati, imaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘saccako nigaṇṭhaputto’’ti.

Bhassappavādakoti bhassaṃ vuccati kathāmaggo, taṃ pavadati kathetīti bhassappavādako. Paṇḍitavādoti ahaṃ paṇḍitoti evaṃ vādo. Sādhusammato bahujanassāti yaṃ yaṃ nakkhattacārena ādisati, taṃ taṃ yebhuyyena tatheva hoti, tasmā ayaṃ sādhuladdhiko bhaddakoti evaṃ sammato mahājanassa. Vādena vādaṃ samāraddhoti kathāmaggena dosaṃ āropito. Āyasmā assajīti sāriputtattherassa ācariyo assajitthero. Jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamānoti tato tato licchavirājagehato taṃ taṃ gehaṃ gamanatthāya anucaṅkamamāno. Yenāyasmā assaji tenupasaṅkamīti kasmā upasaṅkami? Samayajānanatthaṃ.

Bhassappavādako Paṇḍitavādo Sādhusammato bahujanassā Vādena vādaṃ samāraddho Āyasmā assajī Jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno Yenāyasmā assaji tenupasaṅkamī

Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ahaṃ ‘samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropessāmī’ti āhiṇḍāmi, ‘samayaṃ panassa na jānāmī’ti na āropesiṃ. Parassa hi samayaṃ ñatvā āropito vādo svāropito nāma hoti. Ayaṃ pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako paññāyati assajitthero ; so attano satthu samaye kovido, etāhaṃ pucchitvā kathaṃ patiṭṭhāpetvā samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropessāmī’’ti. Tasmā upasaṅkami. Vinetīti kathaṃ vineti, kathaṃ sikkhāpetīti pucchati. Thero pana yasmā dukkhanti vutte upārambhassa okāso hoti, maggaphalānipi pariyāyena dukkhanti āgatāni, ayañca dukkhanti vutte theraṃ puccheyya – ‘‘bho assaji, kimatthaṃ tumhe pabbajitā’’ti. Tato ‘‘maggaphalatthāyā’’ti vutte, – ‘‘nayidaṃ, bho assaji, tumhākaṃ sāsanaṃ nāma, mahāāghātanaṃ nāmetaṃ, nirayussado nāmesa, natthi tumhākaṃ sukhāsā, uṭṭhāyuṭṭhāya dukkhameva jirāpentā āhiṇḍathā’’ti dosaṃ āropeyya, tasmā paravādissa pariyāyakathaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Yathā esa appatiṭṭho hoti, evamassa nippariyāyakathaṃ kathessāmīti cintetvā, ‘‘rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, anicca’’nti imaṃ aniccānattavaseneva kathaṃ katheti. Dussutanti sotuṃ ayuttaṃ.

Vinetī Dussuta
commentary_english:
353. Thus have I heard: the Cūḷasaccakasuttaṃ.

There, *mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāya* means the great forest (mahāvanaṃ), which is self-grown (sayaṃjātaṃ), planted (aropimaṃ), having boundaries (saparicchedaṃ), [and] a large forest (mahantaṃ vanaṃ).

Kapilavatthusāmantā, furthermore, the great forest (mahāvanaṃ) is connected with the Himālaya (himavantena saha ekābaddhaṃ), without boundaries (aparicchedaṃ), having become (hutvā) [one with the] great ocean (mahāsamuddaṃ), striking (āhacca), [and] standing (ṭhitaṃ).

This is not like that (idaṃ tādisaṃ na hoti).

*Saparicchedaṃ mahantaṃ vananti* means *mahāvanaṃ*.
