*Kūṭāgārasālā*, furthermore, refers to the perfumed chamber (*gandhakuṭi*) of the Buddha, the Blessed One, in the *ārāma* park, which relies on the great forest (mahāvanaṃ nissāya kate), the *kūṭāgāraṃ* upper room having been made inside (antokatvā), [and] is complete in all ways, made with a covering of *haṃsavaṭṭaka*.

Saccaka Nigaṇṭhaputta: Formerly, it is said, a Nigaṇṭha and a Nigaṇṭhī, having grasped five hundred theses (pañca pañca vādāni), wandering in Jambudvīpa (jambudīpe vicarantā), came together in Vesālī.

The Licchavi kings (licchavirājāno) having seen [them], asked, "Who are you?" (tvaṃ ko, tvaṃ kā).

The Nigaṇṭha said, "I will establish [my] thesis (vādaṃ āropessāmi), [therefore] I wander in Jambudvīpa" (jambudīpe vicarāmī).

The Nigaṇṭhī also said thus (nigaṇṭhīpi tathā āha).

The Licchavis said, "Establish [your] thesis here, with each other!"

The Nigaṇṭhī asked the five hundred theses grasped by herself, [and] the Nigaṇṭha spoke.

Even when asked by the Nigaṇṭha, the Nigaṇṭhī spoke.

There was no victory for one, nor defeat, both were just the same.

The Licchavis, giving a house (gehaṃ datvā) said: “You both wandering about equally, what will you do? Reside here!", [and] set up offerings (baliṃ paṭṭhapesuṃ).

From their cohabitation (tesaṃ saṃvāsamanvāya) four daughters (catasso dhītaro) were born (jātā), named (nāma) Saccā, Lolā, Paṭācārā, [and] Ācāravatī.

They, too, were wise (paṇḍitāva ahesuṃ), [and] grasped the five hundred theses grasped by [their] mother and father (mātāpitūhi uggahitāni pañca pañca vādasatāni uggahesuṃ).

Those who were mature in age (vayapattā) said to [their] mother and father, “In our family (kule), there is no girl who, having given gold and silver etc. (hiraññasuvaṇṇādīni datvā), has been sent to a family home."

Whoever is a householder (agāriko) [and] can refute their thesis (tāsaṃ vādaṃ maddituṃ sakkoti), they will become his foot-attendants (pādaparicārikā honti).

Whoever is a renunciate (pabbajito) [and] can refute them, they will renounce in his presence.

What will you do (tumhe kiṃ karissatha)?” [They replied,] "We too will do just this (mayampi evameva karissāmāti)."

All four of them (catassopi), taking the guise of wandering female ascetics (paribbājikavesaṃ gahetvā), saying, "This Jambudīpa is known (jambudīpo nāma jambuyā paññāyati) [from] the rose-apple tree (jambuyā)," taking a branch of the rose-apple tree (jambusākhaṃ gahetvā), departed on a journey (cārikaṃ pakkamiṃsu).

To whatever village (yaṃ gāmaṃ) they reached (pāpuṇanti), at its gate (tassa dvāre), having erected a rose-apple banner (jambudhajaṃ ṭhapetvā) in a heap of dust (paṃsupuñje) or a heap of sand (vālikapuñje), they would say: "Whoever is able to establish [a] thesis (vādaṃ āropetuṃ sakkoti), let him refute this (so imaṃ maddatū)," and [then] enter the village (gāmaṃ pavisanti).

Thus, wandering from village to village (evaṃ gāmena gāmaṃ vicarantiyo), reaching Sāvatthī (sāvatthiṃ pāpuṇitvā), just so (tatheva), at the village gate (gāmadvāre), having erected a rose-apple banner (jambudhajaṃ ṭhapetvā), having announced it to the people who had arrived (sampattamanussānaṃ ārocetvā), they entered (paviṭṭhā) the inner city (antonagaraṃ).

Saccako Nigaṇṭhaputto.

At that time (tena samayena), the Blessed One (bhagavā), relying on Sāvatthī (sāvatthiṃ nissāya), was dwelling in Jetavana (jetavane viharati).

Then, venerable Sāriputta (āyasmā sāriputto), asking after the sick (gilāne pucchanto), waking up those who were not awake (ajaggitaṭṭhānaṃ jagganto), due to the greatness of his own duty (attano kiccamahantatāya), [and] monks (bhikkhūhi) [who were] entering the village at midday (divātaraṃ gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisanto), having seen a rose-apple banner (jambudhajaṃ disvā) at the village gate (gāmadvāre), asked the boys (dārake), "What is this?" (kimidaṃ).

They announced that matter (te tamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ).

"Then refute [it]!"

"We are not able, venerable one (bhante), we are afraid (bhāyāma)."

"Boys, do not be afraid (mā bhāyatha), [but] if [someone] says (vutte), 'By whom (kena) was our rose-apple banner (jambudhajo) refuted (maddāpito)?', [then say,] 'It was refuted (maddāpito) by Sāriputta, the elder, a disciple of the Buddha (buddhasāvakena sāriputtattherena), wishing to establish [a] thesis (vādaṃ āropetukāmā), go to the elder's presence (therassa santikaṃ gacchatha) in Jetavana,' thus (iti) you should speak (vadeyyātha)," he said (āha).
Having heard his words, they crushed the *jambudhaja* and threw it away.
The elder, having wandered for alms, went to the monastery.
The female wanderers, having left the village, asked, "Who had our flag crushed?"
The boys reported the matter.
The female wanderers, having entered the village again, and having taken each street, announced: "The Buddha's disciple, named Śāriputra, will debate with us; those desiring to hear, come out!"
A great crowd came out, and the female wanderers went with them to Jetavana.

The elder thought, "The coming of women to our dwelling is unpleasant," and sat down in the middle of the monastery.
The female wanderers, having gone to the elder, asked: "Did you crush our flag?" "Yes, I crushed it."
"We will debate with you."
"Good, do it. Whose question, whose explanation will there be?" "The question is ours; you, however, being women, should ask first," he said.
Those four, standing in the four directions, asked the thousand arguments learned in the presence of their mothers and fathers.
The elder, like cutting a lotus stalk with a sword, having made each question asked, a knotless riddle, spoke; having spoken, he said again, "Ask!"
"Only this much, venerable sir, do we know."
The elder said: "A thousand arguments were asked by you, spoken by me; however, I will ask only one question; you explain that."
Those women, having seen the elder's domain, were not able to say, "Ask, venerable sir, we will explain."
"Speak, venerable sir, knowing, we will explain," they said again.

The elder, after ordaining those sons of good family, saying, "The first question should be what is to be taught," asked, "What is *ekaṃ*?"
They did not see either the end, nor the limit.
The elder said, "Explain!"
"We do not see, venerable sir."
"A thousand arguments were asked by you, spoken by me; you are not able to explain even one question to me; thus being, whose victory, whose defeat?" "Your victory, venerable sir, our defeat."
"Now what will you do?" Those women, having announced the word spoken by their mothers and fathers, said, "We will ordain in your presence."
"You, being women, it is not fitting to ordain in our presence; however, having taken our instruction, go to a nuns' dwelling and ordain."
"Good," they, having taken the elder's instruction, having gone to the presence of the community of nuns, ordained.
And those ordained, unremitting, zealous, soon attained *arhatship*.

This Saccaka was the younger brother of those four.
More wise than those four, having learned a thousand arguments from the presence of his mother and father, and even more of the outer doctrines, not going anywhere, teaching the princes skill, he dwells there in Vaiśālī; because his wisdom is over-filled, fearing that his stomach would break, he wanders, having encircled his stomach with an iron band; with reference to him it was said, "Saccaka, the son of Nigaṇṭha."

*Bhassappavādako* means *bhassaṃ* is called the path of speech; he speaks that, therefore *bhassappavādako*.
*Paṇḍitavādo* means "I am wise," thus is the doctrine.
*Sādhusammato bahujanassa* means whatever he declares by the course of the constellations, that mostly is thus; therefore, this one is well-regarded, blessed; thus is he esteemed by the great crowd.
*Vādena vādaṃ samāraddho* means, by the path of speech, fault is imputed.
*Āyasmā Assaji* means Assaji, the elder, was the teacher of the elder Śāriputra.
*Jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno* means, from here and there, from the Licchavi royal house, wandering about for the sake of going to that house.
Because he went to the venerable Assaji, why did he go? In order to know the time.

He was a speaker of speeches, a scholar of debates, well-regarded by many people, the venerable Assaji, who had begun a debate with a debate, was walking back and forth in his walking meditation, he went to the venerable Assaji. Thus it occurred to him: "I will raise the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama," I wander about, "but I do not know his time," thus I did not raise it.

For, having known the time of another, the doctrine that is raised is truly raised, by name.

Now, this disciple of the ascetic Gotama appears as the venerable Assaji; he is skilled in the doctrine of his own teacher, "Having asked him, how can I establish and raise the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama?"

Therefore, he went.

"He trains," how does he train, how does he teach? he asks.

Because when the Elder says "suffering," there is an opportunity for reproach, the fruits of the path also come as suffering in a way, and if he were to say "suffering," he might ask the Elder - "Venerable Assaji, for what purpose have you gone forth?"

Then, when he says "for the sake of the fruits of the path," - "This is not, venerable Assaji, your teaching, this is a great slaughter, this is a hellish undertaking, there is no hope of happiness for you, you wander about only aging suffering by getting up and getting up," he would bring about anger, therefore, it is not fitting to make a roundabout story to another debater.

Just as this one is unestablished, so, thinking, "I will tell him a story without a roundabout way," how does he tell this "form, monks, is impermanent" only by way of impermanence and non-self?

"Ill-heard" means unfit to be heard.

mula_pali: 354. Tena kho pana samayena pañcamattāni licchavisatāni santhāgāre sandhāgāre (ka.) sannipatitāni honti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto yena te licchavī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te licchavī etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkamantu bhonto licchavī, abhikkamantu bhonto licchavī, ajja me samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo bhavissati. Sace me samaṇo gotamo tathā patiṭṭhissati yathā ca me yathāssa me (sī. pī.) ñātaññatarena sāvakena assajinā nāma bhikkhunā patiṭṭhitaṃ, seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso dīghalomikaṃ eḷakaṃ lomesu gahetvā ākaḍḍheyya parikaḍḍheyya samparikaḍḍheyya , evamevāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ vādena vādaṃ ākaḍḍhissāmi parikaḍḍhissāmi samparikaḍḍhissāmi. Seyyathāpi nāma balavā soṇḍikākammakāro mahantaṃ soṇḍikākiḷañjaṃ gambhīre udakarahade pakkhipitvā kaṇṇe gahetvā ākaḍḍheyya parikaḍḍheyya samparikaḍḍheyya, evamevāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ vādena vādaṃ ākaḍḍhissāmi parikaḍḍhissāmi samparikaḍḍhissāmi. Seyyathāpi nāma balavā soṇḍikādhutto vālaṃ thālaṃ (ka.) kaṇṇe gahetvā odhuneyya niddhuneyya nipphoṭeyya nicchādeyya (sī. pī. ka.), nicchoṭeyya (ka.), nippoṭheyya (syā. kaṃ.) evamevāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ vādena vādaṃ odhunissāmi niddhunissāmi nipphoṭessāmi. Seyyathāpi nāma kuñjaro saṭṭhihāyano gambhīraṃ pokkharaṇiṃ ogāhetvā sāṇadhovikaṃ nāma kīḷitajātaṃ kīḷati, evamevāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ sāṇadhovikaṃ maññe kīḷitajātaṃ kīḷissāmi. Abhikkamantu bhonto licchavī, abhikkamantu bhonto licchavī, ajja me samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo bhavissatī’’ti. Tatrekacce licchavī evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘kiṃ samaṇo gotamo saccakassa nigaṇṭhaputtassa vādaṃ āropessati, atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropessatī’’ti? Ekacce licchavī evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘kiṃ so bhavamāno saccako nigaṇṭhaputto yo bhagavato vādaṃ āropessati, atha kho bhagavā saccakassa nigaṇṭhaputtassa vādaṃ āropessatī’’ti? Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto pañcamattehi licchavisatehi parivuto yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkami.
mula_english:
354. Then, at that time, several hundred Licchavis were assembled in the meeting hall on some business.

Then Saccaka the son of the Nigaṇṭha approached those Licchavis; having approached, he said this to those Licchavis: "Come forward, Licchavis, come forward, Licchavis! Today, I will have a discussion with the *śramaṇa* Gotama.

If the *śramaṇa* Gotama stands firm in that way, just as my known disciple, the *bhikṣu* named Assaji, has established, just as a strong man, having seized a long-haired ram by the wool, might pull him, drag him about, and completely drag him about, so too, I will draw the *śramaṇa* Gotama into a debate, I will drag him about, I will completely drag him about.

Just as a strong brewer's workman might throw a large brewer's sieve into a deep water tank, and, having seized it by the corners, might pull it, drag it about, and completely drag it about, so too, I will draw the *śramaṇa* Gotama into a debate, I will drag him about, I will completely drag him about.

Just as a strong brewer's mixer, having seized a strainer by the corners, might shake it down, shake it up, and thump it about, so too, I will shake the *śramaṇa* Gotama down, shake him up, and thump him about in debate.

Just as an elephant, sixty years old, having entered a deep pond, enjoys playing the game of hemp-washing, so too, I think I will enjoy playing the game of hemp-washing with the *śramaṇa* Gotama.

Come forward, Licchavis, come forward, Licchavis! Today, I will have a discussion with the *śramaṇa* Gotama."

There some Licchavis said this: "Will the *śramaṇa* Gotama draw Saccaka the son of the Nigaṇṭha into a debate, or will Saccaka the son of the Nigaṇṭha draw the *śramaṇa* Gotama into a debate?" Some Licchavis said this: "Will that esteemed Saccaka the son of the Nigaṇṭha draw the *bhagavat* into a debate, or will the *bhagavat* draw Saccaka the son of the Nigaṇṭha into a debate?"

Then Saccaka the son of the Nigaṇṭha, surrounded by about five hundred Licchavis, approached the Great Forest, the hall with a peaked roof.
commentary_pali: 354.Santhāgāreti rājakulānaṃ atthānusāsanasanthāgārasālāyaṃ. Yena te licchavī tenupasaṅkamīti evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ahaṃ pubbe samayaṃ ajānanabhāvena samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ na āropesiṃ, idāni panassa mahāsāvakena kathitaṃ samayaṃ jānāmi, ime ca mama antevāsikā pañcasatā licchavī sannipatitā. Etehi saddhiṃ gantvā samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropessāmī’’ti tasmā upasaṅkami. Ñātaññatarenāti ñātesu abhiññātesu pañcavaggiyattheresu aññatarena. Patiṭṭhitanti yathā tena patiṭṭhitaṃ. Sace evaṃ patiṭṭhissati, atha pana aññadeva vakkhati, tatra mayā kiṃ sakkā kātunti idāneva piṭṭhiṃ parivattento āha. Ākaḍḍheyyāti attano abhimukhaṃ kaḍḍheyya. Parikaḍḍheyyāti purato paṭipaṇāmeyya. Samparikaḍḍheyyāti kālena ākaḍḍheyya, kālena parikaḍḍheyya. Soṇḍikākilañjanti surāghare piṭṭhakilañjaṃ. Soṇḍikādhuttoti surādhutto. Vālaṃ kaṇṇe gahetvāti surāparissāvanatthavikaṃ dhovitukāmo kasaṭanidhunanatthaṃ ubhosu kaṇṇesu gahetvā. Odhuneyyāti adhomukhaṃ katvā dhuneyya. Niddhuneyyāti uddhaṃmukhaṃ katvā dhuneyya. Nipphoṭeyyāti punappunaṃ papphoṭeyya. Sāṇadhovikaṃ nāmāti ettha manussā sāṇasāṭakakaraṇatthaṃ sāṇavāke gahetvā muṭṭhiṃ muṭṭhiṃ bandhitvā udake pakkhipanti. Te tatiyadivase suṭṭhu kilinnā honti. Atha manussā ambilayāgusurādīni ādāya tattha gantvā sāṇamuṭṭhiṃ gahetvā, dakkhiṇato vāmato sammukhā cāti tīsu phalakesu sakiṃ dakkhiṇaphalake, sakiṃ vāmaphalake, sakiṃ sammukhaphalake paharantā ambilayāgusurādīni bhuñjantā pivantā khādantā dhovanti. Mahantā kīḷā hoti. Rañño nāgo taṃ kīḷaṃ disvā gambhīraṃ udakaṃ anupavisitvā soṇḍāya udakaṃ gahetvā sakiṃ kumbhe sakiṃ piṭṭhiyaṃ sakiṃ ubhosu passesu sakiṃ antarasatthiyaṃ pakkhipanto kīḷittha. Tadupādāya taṃ kīḷitajātaṃ sāṇadhovikaṃ nāma vuccati , taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘sāṇadhovikaṃ nāma kīḷitajātaṃ kīḷatī’’ti. Kiṃ so bhavamāno saccako nigaṇṭhaputto, yo bhagavato vādaṃ āropessatīti yo saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavato vādaṃ āropessati, so kiṃ bhavamāno kiṃ yakkho bhavamāno udāhu indo, udāhu brahmā bhavamāno bhagavato vādaṃ āropessati? Na hi sakkā pakatimanussena bhagavato vādaṃ āropetunti ayamettha adhippāyo.
commentary_english:
354. *Santhāgāre* means in the assembly hall for instructing in the meaning in the royal families.

*Yena te licchavī tenupasaṅkamī* means thus it occurred to him: “Formerly, due to not knowing the agreement, I did not introduce the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama. Now, however, I know the agreement spoken by his great disciple, and these five hundred Licchavis, who are my pupils, have assembled. Having gone with them, I will introduce the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama.” Therefore, he approached.

*Ñātaññatarenā* means by one of the known and well-known elders of the group of five.

*Patiṭṭhita*nti means just as it was established by him.

If it will be established thus, but if he should say something else, what will I be able to do there? Thinking this, he turned his back right then and spoke.

*Ākaḍḍheyyā* means he should pull [it] towards himself.

*Parikaḍḍheyyā* means he should turn [it] around in front.

*Samparikaḍḍheyyā* means he should pull [it] at one time, and turn [it] around at another time.

*Soṇḍikākilañja* means a mat in a liquor shop.

*Soṇḍikādhutto* means a liquor swindler.

*Vālaṃ kaṇṇe gahetvā* means desiring to wash the straining cloth for liquor, having taken the hair in [his] ear, for the purpose of removing the sediment, having taken [it] in both ears.

*Odhuneyyā* means having made [it] face downward, he should shake [it].

*Niddhuneyyā* means having made [it] face upward, he should shake [it].

*Nipphoṭeyyā* means he should repeatedly snap [it].

*Sāṇadhovikaṃ nāmā* means here, people, for the purpose of making hempen cloths, take hemp plants, tie fistfuls, and throw [them] in the water.

They become well soaked on the third day.

Then, people, taking sour gruel, liquor, etc., having gone there, taking the hemp fistful, striking the three boards, sometimes on the right board, sometimes on the left board, sometimes on the front board, eating, drinking, and consuming the sour gruel, liquor, etc., wash [the hemp].

There is a great game.

The king’s elephant, seeing that game, having entered deep water, taking water with its trunk, sometimes sprinkling [it] on the pot, sometimes on the back, sometimes on both sides, sometimes throwing [it] on the inner thighs, played.

Depending on that, that kind of game is called *sāṇadhovika*. Referring to that, it was said: “He plays a game of the *sāṇadhovika* kind.”

*Kiṃ so bhavamāno Saccako Nigaṇṭhaputto, yo Bhagavato vādaṃ āropessatī* means that Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son who will introduce the Blessed One’s doctrine, is he becoming what? Is he becoming a *yakṣa*, or is he becoming Indra, or is he becoming Brahmā [that] he will introduce the Blessed One’s doctrine? For it is not possible for an ordinary human to introduce the Blessed One’s doctrine. This is the meaning here.

mula_pali: 355. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū abbhokāse caṅkamanti. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘kahaṃ nu kho, bho, etarahi so bhavaṃ gotamo viharati? Dassanakāmā hi mayaṃ taṃ bhavantaṃ gotama’’nti . ‘‘Esa, aggivessana, bhagavā mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisinno’’ti. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto mahatiyā licchaviparisāya saddhiṃ mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Tepi kho licchavī appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
mula_english:
355. Then, at that time, a large number of monks were doing walking meditation in the open.

Then Saccaka, the son of the Nigaṇṭha, approached those monks and said to them: “Where, indeed, venerable sirs, does the esteemed Gotama currently reside? For we wish to see that esteemed Gotama."

"Aggivessana, the Blessed One, having entered the great forest (mahāvana), is seated at the foot of a certain tree for the day's retreat (divāvihāra)."

Then Saccaka, the son of the Nigaṇṭha, together with a large assembly of Licchavis, entered the great forest (mahāvana) and approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.

Having concluded their courteous and amiable talk (sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā), he sat down at one side.

Then some of those Licchavis, having bowed to the Blessed One, sat down at one side; some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One (bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu), and having concluded their courteous and amiable talk (sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā), sat down at one side.

Some, having extended their hands in reverential salutation (añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā) towards the Blessed One, sat down at one side; some announced their name and clan (nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā) in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down at one side; some kept silent (tuṇhībhūtā) and sat down at one side.
commentary_pali:
355.Tena kho pana samayenāti yasmiṃ samaye saccako ārāmaṃ pāvisi, tasmiṃ. Kismiṃ pana samaye pāvisīti? Mahāmajjhanhikasamaye. Kasmā pana tasmiṃ samaye caṅkamantīti? Paṇītabhojanapaccayassa thinamiddhassa vinodanatthaṃ. Divāpadhānikā vā te. Tādisānañhi pacchābhattaṃ caṅkamitvā nhatvā sarīraṃ utuṃ gaṇhāpetvā nisajja samaṇadhammaṃ karontānaṃ cittaṃ ekaggaṃ hoti. Yena te bhikkhūti so kira kuhiṃ samaṇo gotamoti pariveṇato pariveṇaṃ gantvā pucchitvā pavisissāmīti vilokento araññe hatthī viya caṅkame caṅkamamāne paṃsukūlikabhikkhū disvā tesaṃ santikaṃ agamāsi. Taṃ sandhāya, ‘‘yena te bhikkhū’’tiādi vuttaṃ. Kahaṃnu kho, bhoti katarasmiṃ āvāse vā maṇḍape vāti attho. Esa, aggivessana, bhagavāti tadā kira bhagavā paccūsakāle mahākaruṇā samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā dasasahassacakkavāḷe sabbaññutaññāṇajālaṃ pattharitvā bodhaneyyasattaṃ olokento addasa – ‘‘sve saccako nigaṇṭhaputto mahatiṃ licchaviparisaṃ gahetvā mama vādaṃ āropetukāmo āgamissatī’’ti. Tasmā pātova sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā bhikkhusaṅghaparivāro vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto mahāparisāya nisīdituṃ sukhaṭṭhāne nisīdissāmīti gandhakuṭiṃ apavisitvā mahāvane aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Te bhikkhū bhagavato vattaṃ dassetvā āgatā, saccakena puṭṭhā dūre nisinnaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassentā, ‘‘esa aggivessana bhagavā’’ti āhaṃsu.

Mahatiyā licchaviparisāya saddhinti heṭṭhā pañcamattehi licchavisatehi parivutoti vuttaṃ. Te etassa antevāsikāyeva, antovesāliyaṃ pana saccako pañcamattāni licchavirājasatāni gahetvā, ‘‘vādatthiko bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamanto’’ti sutvā dvinnaṃ paṇḍitānaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ sossāmāti yebhuyyena manussā nikkhantā, evaṃ sā parisā mahatī aparicchinnagaṇanā ahosi. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Añjaliṃ paṇāmetvāti ete ubhatopakkhikā, te evaṃ cintesuṃ – ‘‘sace no micchādiṭṭhikā codessanti, ‘kasmā tumhe samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ vanditthā’ti, tesaṃ, ‘kiṃ añjalimattakaraṇenapi vanditaṃ hotī’ti vakkhāma. Sace no sammādiṭṭhikā codessanti, ‘kasmā bhagavantaṃ na vanditthā’ti, ‘kiṃ sīsena bhūmiṃ paharanteneva vanditaṃ hoti, nanu añjalikammampi vandanā evā’ti vakkhāmā’’ti. Nāma gottanti, bho gotama, ahaṃ asukassa putto datto nāma mitto nāma idha āgatoti vadantā nāmaṃ sāventi nāma. Bho gotama, ahaṃ vāsiṭṭho nāma kaccāno nāma idha āgatoti vadantā gottaṃ sāventi nāma. Ete kira daliddā jiṇṇakulaputtā parisamajjhe nāmagottavasena pākaṭā bhavissāmāti evaṃ akaṃsu. Ye pana tuṇhībhūtā nisīdiṃsu, te kerāṭikā ceva andhabālā ca. Tattha kerāṭikā, ‘‘ekaṃ dve kathāsallāpe karonto vissāsiko hoti, atha vissāse sati ekaṃ dve bhikkhā adātuṃ na yutta’’nti tato attānaṃ mocentā tuṇhī nisīdanti. Andhabālā aññāṇatāyeva avakkhittamattikāpiṇḍo viya yattha katthaci tuṇhībhūtā nisīdanti.

Mahatiyā licchaviparisāya saddhi Añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā Nāma gotta
commentary_english:
355. "Then, at that time" means at which time Saccaka entered the monastery.

What time did he enter? At high noon.

Why were they walking around at that time? To dispel the drowsiness of having eaten fine food.

Or they were daytime practitioners.

For those who are like that, after eating, having walked around, bathed, cooled their bodies, and sat down, their minds become one-pointed while practicing the ascetic life.

"By whom those monks" means he, looking around and wondering where the ascetic Gotama was, thinking, "I will go from enclosure to enclosure, ask, and then enter," saw monks wearing robes made of rags wandering in the forest like an elephant, and approached them.

Referring to that, it was said, "By whom those monks," and so on.

"Where, now, sir?" means what is the meaning of "in which dwelling or pavilion?"

"This, Aggivessana, is the Blessed One" means then, it is said, the Blessed One, at dawn, having attained the great compassion absorption, having spread the net of all-knowing knowledge in the ten thousand world-systems, seeing a being capable of enlightenment, saw – "Tomorrow Saccaka, the Nigaṇṭha's son, having taken a large Licchavi assembly, intending to raise a debate with me, will come."

Therefore, having gotten up early and taken care of his body, surrounded by a community of monks, having gone to Vesālī for alms, having returned from the alms round, thinking, "I will sit down in a pleasant place to sit for the great assembly," he entered the perfume chamber and sat down for the daytime retreat at the foot of a certain tree in the great forest.

Those monks, having shown the Blessed One's routine, came, and when asked by Saccaka, showing the Blessed One sitting at a distance, said, "This, Aggivessana, is the Blessed One."

"With a large Licchavi assembly" means it was said that he was surrounded by five hundred Licchavis below.

They were just his disciples. But Saccaka, in inner Vesālī, having taken about five hundred Licchavi kings, having heard that "the debater is approaching the Blessed One," thinking, "I will listen to the conversation of the two learned men," most of the people left, thus that assembly was large and its number was unlimited.

Referring to that, this was said.

"Having raised their joined hands" means these were on both sides, they thought thus - "If those of wrong view question us, 'Why did you venerate the ascetic Gotama?', we will say to them, 'Is it veneration even by just making the gesture of joined hands?'

If those of right view question us, 'Why did you not venerate the Blessed One?', we will say, 'Is it veneration only by striking the ground with your head? Surely, even the act of joined hands is veneration!' "

"Name and clan" means, "Sir Gotama, I am the son of so-and-so, named Datta, named Mitta, I have come here," thus those who say their name are announcing their name.

"Sir Gotama, I am Vāsiṭṭha by name, Kaccāna by name, I have come here," thus those who say their clan are announcing their clan.

It is said that these poor sons of worn-out families thought, "We will become known in the middle of the assembly by means of name and clan," thus they did so.

Those who sat silently were both deceitful and blindly foolish.

There, the deceitful ones, "One who engages in one or two friendly conversations becomes trustworthy, and when there is trust, it is not proper to give one or two alms," thus they free themselves and sit silently.

The blindly foolish, just because of ignorance, sit silently anywhere, like a lump of clay that has been thrown away.

With a large Licchavi assembly

Having raised their joined hands name and clan

mula_pali:
356. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘puccheyyāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ kiñcideva desaṃ, sace me bhavaṃ gotamo okāsaṃ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā’’ti. ‘‘Puccha, aggivessana , yadākaṅkhasī’’ti . ‘‘Kathaṃ pana bhavaṃ gotamo sāvake vineti, kathaṃbhāgā ca pana bhoto gotamassa sāvakesu anusāsanī bahulā pavattatī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, sāvake vinemi, evaṃbhāgā ca pana me sāvakesu anusāsanī bahulā pavattati – ‘rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, aniccaṃ, vedanā aniccā, saññā aniccā, saṅkhārā aniccā, viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ. Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, anattā, vedanā anattā, saññā anattā, saṅkhārā anattā, viññāṇaṃ anattā. Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā, sabbe dhammā anattā’ti. Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, sāvake vinemi, evaṃbhāgā ca pana me sāvakesu anusāsanī bahulā pavattatī’’ti.

‘‘Upamā maṃ, bho gotama, paṭibhātī’’ti. ‘‘Paṭibhātu taṃ, aggivessanā’’ti bhagavā avoca.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, ye kecime bījagāmabhūtagāmā vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjanti, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya. Evamete bījagāmabhūtagāmā vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjanti. Seyyathāpi vā pana, bho gotama, ye kecime balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya. Evamete balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti. Evameva kho, bho gotama, rūpattāyaṃ purisapuggalo rūpe patiṭṭhāya puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā pasavati, vedanattāyaṃ purisapuggalo vedanāyaṃ patiṭṭhāya puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā pasavati, saññattāyaṃ purisapuggalo saññāyaṃ patiṭṭhāya puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā pasavati, saṅkhārattāyaṃ purisapuggalo saṅkhāresu patiṭṭhāya puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā pasavati, viññāṇattāyaṃ purisapuggalo viññāṇe patiṭṭhāya puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā pasavatī’’ti.

‘‘Nanu tvaṃ, aggivessana, evaṃ vadesi – ‘rūpaṃ me attā, vedanā me attā, saññā me attā, saṅkhārā me attā, viññāṇaṃ me attā’’’ti? ‘‘Ahañhi, bho gotama , evaṃ vadāmi – ‘rūpaṃ me attā, vedanā me attā, saññā me attā, saṅkhārā me attā, viññāṇaṃ me attā’ti, ayañca mahatī janatā’’ti.

‘‘Kiñhi te, aggivessana, mahatī janatā karissati? Iṅgha tvaṃ, aggivessana, sakaññeva vādaṃ nibbeṭhehī’’ti. ‘‘Ahañhi, bho gotama, evaṃ vadāmi – ‘rūpaṃ me attā, vedanā me attā, saññā me attā, saṅkhārā me attā, viññāṇaṃ me attā’’’ti.
mula_english:
356. Saccaka the son of Nigaṇṭha, being seated to one side, then said this to the Blessed One: “I would ask a certain question from the esteemed Gotama. If the esteemed Gotama would grant me the opportunity and would explain the answer to my question.”

“Ask, Aggivessana, whenever you wish.”

“How, then, does the esteemed Gotama train his disciples, and in what aspects does the instruction that the esteemed Gotama gives to his disciples mostly proceed?”

“Aggivessana, I train my disciples in this way, and the instruction that I give to my disciples mostly proceeds in this manner: ‘Form *(rūpa)*, monks *(bhikkhave)*, is impermanent *(aniccaṃ)*, feeling *(vedanā)* is impermanent, perception *(saññā)* is impermanent, determinations *(saṅkhārā)* are impermanent, consciousness *(viññāṇaṃ)* is impermanent.

Form, monks, is not-self *(anattā)*, feeling is not-self, perception is not-self, determinations are not-self, consciousness is not-self.

All determinations are impermanent, all things *(dhammā)* are not-self.’

Aggivessana, I train my disciples in this way, and the instruction that I give to my disciples mostly proceeds in this manner.”

“A comparison occurs to me, esteemed Gotama."

“Say it, Aggivessana,” said the Blessed One.

“Just as, esteemed Gotama, whatever seed groups and vegetable groups come to growth, increase and maturity, all of them depend on the earth, established on the earth.

Just so, these seed groups and vegetable groups come to growth, increase, and maturity.

Or just as, esteemed Gotama, whatever powerful work that has to be done is done, all of it depends on the earth, established on the earth.

Just so, this powerful work that has to be done is done.

In the same manner, esteemed Gotama, this person with the material self, established in matter *(rūpe)*, accrues merit *(puññaṃ)* or demerit *(apuññaṃ)*; this person with feeling, established in feeling, accrues merit or demerit; this person with perception, established in perception, accrues merit or demerit; this person with determinations, established in determinations, accrues merit or demerit; this person with consciousness, established in consciousness, accrues merit or demerit.”

“Aggivessana, do you not say this: ‘Form is my self *(attā)*, feeling is my self, perception is my self, determinations are my self, consciousness is my self’?”

“Esteemed Gotama, I do say this: ‘Form is my self, feeling is my self, perception is my self, determinations are my self, consciousness is my self,’ and this large crowd also says this.”

“Aggivessana, what will this large crowd do for you? Come now, Aggivessana, just refute your own doctrine *(vādaṃ)*.”

“Esteemed Gotama, I do say this: ‘Form is my self, feeling is my self, perception is my self, determinations are my self, consciousness is my self.’”
commentary_pali:
356.Kiñcideva desanti kañci okāsaṃ kiñci kāraṇaṃ, athassa bhagavā pañhapucchane ussāhaṃ janento āha – puccha, aggivessana, yadākaṅkhasīti. Tassattho – ‘‘puccha yadi ākaṅkhasi, na me pañhavissajjane bhāro atthi’’. Atha vā ‘‘puccha yaṃ ākaṅkhasi, sabbaṃ te vissajjessāmī’’ti sabbaññupavāraṇaṃ pavāresi asādhāraṇaṃ paccekabuddhaaggasāvamahāsāvakehi. Te hi yadākaṅkhasīti na vadanti, sutvā vedissāmāti vadanti. Buddhā pana ‘‘pucchāvuso, yadākaṅkhasī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.237) vā, ‘‘puccha, mahārāja, yadākaṅkhasī’’ti (dī. ni. 1.162) vā,

‘‘Puccha vāsava maṃ pañhaṃ, yaṃ kiñci manasicchasi;

Tassa tasseva pañhassa, ahaṃ antaṃ karomi te’’ iti. (dī. ni. 2.356) vā,

‘‘Tena hi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, sake āsane nisīditvā puccha yadākaṅkhasī’’ti (ma. ni. 3.85) vā,

‘‘Bāvarissa ca tuyhaṃ vā, sabbesaṃ sabbasaṃsayaṃ;

Katāvakāsā pucchavho, yaṃ kiñci manasicchathā’’ti. (su. ni. 1036) vā,

‘‘Puccha maṃ sabhiya pañhaṃ, yaṃ kiñci manasicchasi;

Tassa tasseva pañhassa, ahaṃ antaṃ karomi te’’ iti. (su. ni. 517) vā –

Tesaṃ tesaṃ yakkhanarindadevasamaṇabrāhmaṇaparibbājakānaṃ sabbaññupavāraṇaṃ pavārenti. Anacchariyañcetaṃ, yaṃ bhagavā buddhabhūmiṃ patvā etaṃ pavāraṇaṃ pavāreyya. Yo bodhisattabhūmiyaṃ padesañāṇepi ṭhito

‘‘Koṇḍañña pañhāni viyākarohi,

Yācanti taṃ isayo sādhurūpā;

Koṇḍañña eso manujesu dhammo,

Yaṃ vuddhamāgacchati esa bhāro’’ti. (jā. 2.17.60) –

Evaṃ sakkādīnaṃ atthāya isīhi yācito

‘‘Katāvakāsā pucchantu bhonto,

Yaṃ kiñci pañhaṃ manasābhipatthitaṃ;

Ahañhi taṃ taṃ vo viyākarissaṃ,

Ñatvā sayaṃ lokamimaṃ parañcā’’ti. (jā. 2.17.61);

Evaṃ sarabhaṅgakāle, sambhavajātake ca sakalajambudīpaṃ tikkhattuṃ vicaritvā pañhānaṃ antakaraṃ adisvā suciratena brāhmaṇena pañhaṃ puṭṭho okāse kārite, jātiyā sattavasso rathikāyaṃ paṃsuṃ kīḷanto pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā antaravīthiyaṃ nisinnova –

‘‘Taggha te ahamakkhissaṃ, yathāpi kusalo tathā;

Rājā ca kho taṃ jānāti, yadi kāhati vā na vā’’ti. (jā. 1.16.172) –

Sabbaññupavāraṇaṃ pavāresi.

Evaṃ bhagavatā sabbaññupavāraṇāya pavāritāya attamano pañhaṃ pucchanto, ‘‘kathaṃ pana, bho gotamā’’tiādimāha.

Athassa bhagavā, ‘‘passatha, bho, aññaṃ sāvakena kathitaṃ, aññaṃ satthā katheti, nanu mayā paṭikacceva vuttaṃ, ‘sace tathā patiṭṭhissati, yathāssa sāvakena patiṭṭhitaṃ, evāhaṃ vādaṃ āropessāmī’ti. Ayaṃ pana aññameva katheti, tattha kiṃ mayā sakkā kātu’’nti evaṃ nigaṇṭhassa vacanokāso mā hotūti heṭṭhā assajittherena kathitaniyāmeneva kathento, evaṃ kho ahaṃ, aggivessanātiādimāha. Upamā maṃ, bho gotama, paṭibhātīti, bho gotama, mayhaṃ ekā upamā upaṭṭhāti, āharāmi taṃ upamanti vadati. Paṭibhātu taṃ, aggivessanāti upaṭṭhātu te, aggivessana, āhara taṃ upamaṃ visatthoti bhagavā avoca. Balakaraṇīyāti bāhubalena kattabbā kasivāṇijjādikā kammantā. Rūpattāyaṃ purisapuggaloti rūpaṃ attā assāti rūpattā, rūpaṃ attāti gahetvā ṭhitapuggalaṃ dīpeti. Rūpe patiṭṭhāyāti tasmiṃ attāti gahitarūpe patiṭṭhahitvā. Puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā pasavatīti kusalaṃ vā akusalaṃ vā paṭilabhati. Vedanattādīsupi eseva nayo. Iminā kiṃ dīpeti? Ime pañcakkhandhā imesaṃ sattānaṃ pathavī viya patiṭṭhā, te imesu pañcasu khandhesu patiṭṭhāya kusalākusalakammaṃ nāma āyūhanti. Tumhe evarūpaṃ vijjamānameva attānaṃ paṭisedhento pañcakkhandhā anattāti dīpethāti ativiya sakāraṇaṃ katvā upamaṃ āhari. Iminā ca nigaṇṭhena āhaṭaopammaṃ niyatameva , sabbaññubuddhato añño tassa kathaṃ chinditvā vāde dosaṃ dātuṃ samattho nāma natthi. Duvidhā hi puggalā buddhaveneyyā ca sāvakaveneyyā ca. Sāvakaveneyye sāvakāpi vinenti buddhāpi. Buddhaveneyye pana sāvakā vinetuṃ na sakkonti, buddhāva vinenti. Ayampi nigaṇṭho buddhaveneyyo, tasmā etassa vādaṃ chinditvā añño dosaṃ dātuṃ samattho nāma natthi. Tenassa bhagavā sayameva vāde dosadassanatthaṃ nanu tvaṃ, aggivessanātiādimāha.

evaṃ kho ahaṃ, aggivessanā Upamā maṃ, bho gotama, paṭibhātī Paṭibhātu taṃ, aggivessanā Balakaraṇīyā Rūpattāyaṃ purisapuggalo rūpattā, Rūpe patiṭṭhāyā Puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā pasavatī Vedanattādīsupi nanu tvaṃ, aggivessanā

Atha nigaṇṭho cintesi – ‘‘ativiya samaṇo gotamo mama vādaṃ patiṭṭhapeti, sace upari koci doso bhavissati, mamaṃ ekakaṃyeva niggaṇhissati. Handāhaṃ imaṃ vādaṃ mahājanassāpi matthake pakkhipāmī’’ti, tasmā evamāha – ahampi, bho gotama, evaṃ vadāmi rūpaṃ me attā…pe… viññāṇaṃ me attāti, ayañca mahatī janatāti. Bhagavā pana nigaṇṭhato sataguṇenapi sahassaguṇenapi satasahassaguṇenapi vādīvarataro, tasmā cintesi – ‘‘ayaṃ nigaṇṭho attānaṃ mocetvā mahājanassa matthake vādaṃ pakkhipati, nāssa attānaṃ mocetuṃ dassāmi, mahājanato nivattetvā ekakaṃyeva naṃ niggaṇhissāmī’’ti. Atha naṃ kiñhi te, aggivessanātiādimāha. Tassattho – nāyaṃ janatā mama vādaṃ āropetuṃ āgatā, tvaṃyeva sakalaṃ vesāliṃ saṃvaṭṭitvā mama vādaṃ āropetuṃ āgato, tasmā tvaṃ sakameva vādaṃ niveṭhehi, mā mahājanassa matthake pakkhipasīti. So paṭijānanto ahañhi, bho gotamātiādimāha.

ahampi, bho gotama, evaṃ vadāmi rūpaṃ me attā…pe… viññāṇaṃ me attāti, ayañca mahatī janatā kiñhi te, aggivessanā ahañhi, bho gotamā
commentary_english:
356. *kiñcideva desa* means some space, some opportunity, some reason. Then the Blessed One, generating enthusiasm for questioning, said: "Ask, Aggivessana, whatever you wish (yad ākaṅkhasi)."

Its meaning is: "Ask (puccha) if you wish (yadi ākaṅkhasi), there is no trouble to me in answering (pañhavissajjane) questions (bhāro atthi)."

Or else, "Ask (puccha) what (yaṃ) you wish (ākaṅkhasi), I will answer (vissajjessāmi) everything (sabbaṃ) for you (te)," thus he made an invitation including all knowledge (sabbaññupavāraṇaṃ), an invitation not shared by individual Buddhas, chief disciples and senior disciples (asādhāraṇaṃ paccekabuddhaaggasāvamahāsāvakehi).

For they do not say "Ask whatever you wish (yadākaṅkhasīti)," but they say, "Having heard, we will try to answer (sutvā vedissāmāti)."

Buddhas, however, say, "Ask, friend (pucchāvuso), whatever you wish (yadākaṅkhasi)" (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.237) or, "Ask, great king (mahārāja), whatever you wish (yadākaṅkhasi)" (Dīgha Nikāya 1.162) or,

"Ask (puccha), Vāsava, me (maṃ) a question (pañhaṃ), whatever (yaṃ kiñci) you desire (manasicchasi); I (ahaṃ) will make (karomi) an end (antaṃ) to that (tassa) very (tasseva) question (pañhassa) for you (te)" (Dīgha Nikāya 2.356) or,

"Therefore (tena), bhikkhu, having sat down (nisīditvā) in your (sake) own (āsane) seat (puccha), ask (yadākaṅkhasi) whatever you wish" (Majjhima Nikāya 3.85) or,

"To Bāvari (bāvarissa) and (ca) to you (tuyhaṃ) or (vā), regarding all (sabbesaṃ) doubts (sabbasaṃsayaṃ); having made an opportunity (katāvakāsā), questioners (pucchavho), ask (manasicchatha) whatever (yaṃ kiñci) you desire (āti)." (Sutta Nipāta 1036) or,

"Ask (puccha) me (maṃ), Sabhiya, a question (pañhaṃ), whatever (yaṃ kiñci) you desire (manasicchasi); I (ahaṃ) will make (karomi) an end (antaṃ) to that (tassa) very (tasseva) question (pañhassa) for you (te)" (Sutta Nipāta 517) –

To those (tesaṃ tesaṃ) *yakṣas*, *narindas*, *devas*, *śramaṇas*, *brāhmaṇas*, and *parivrājakas*, they offer the invitation that includes all knowledge (sabbaññupavāraṇaṃ pavārenti).

It is not wonderful (anacchariyañcetaṃ), that the Blessed One (bhagavā), having attained (patvā) Buddhahood (buddhabhūmiṃ), would offer (pavāreyya) this (etaṃ) invitation (pavāraṇaṃ).

He who is established (ṭhito) in the knowledge of a region (padesañāṇepi) in the *bodhisattva*-ground (bodhisattabhūmiyaṃ):

"Koṇḍañña, explain (viyākarohi) the questions (pañhāni), the seers (isayo) of good form (sādhurūpā) ask (yācanti) you (taṃ); Koṇḍañña, this (eso) is the *dharma* (dhammo) among humans (manujesu), that (yaṃ) this burden (esa bhāro) comes (āgacchati) to the elder (vuddha)." (Jātaka 2.17.60) –

Thus (evaṃ), for the sake of (atthāya) Sakka and others (sakkādīnaṃ), requested (yācito) by the seers (isīhi):

"Having made an opportunity (katāvakāsā), question (pucchantu), *bhonto*, whatever (yaṃ kiñci) question (pañhaṃ) is desired (manasābhipatthitaṃ); for I (ahañhi) will explain (viyākarissaṃ) that (taṃ taṃ) to you (vo), having known (ñatvā) this (imaṃ) world (lokaṃ) and (ca) the other (paraṃ) myself (sayaṃ)." (Jātaka 2.17.
Thus, at the time when Sarabhaṅga was a hermit, and also in the Sambhava Jātaka, after wandering about in the entire Jambudvīpa three times, Sucirata the *brāhmaṇa*, not finding anyone who could put an end to questions, having been asked a question by Sucirata the *brāhmaṇa* in an open space that was made, [and] being seven years of age by birth, while playing with dust on the road, having bent his legs into the lotus position, and being seated in the middle of the street –

“Indeed, I will explain it to you, just as [I am] skilled;
And the king knows you, whether he will do [it] or not.”
(Jā. 1.16.172) –

He declared the *sarvajñupavāraṇa*.

Thus, having been invited for the *sarvajñupavāraṇa* by the Blessed One, delighted in his mind, asking a question, he said, “How then, sir Gotama?” etc.

Then the Blessed One [said] to him, "See, sir, one thing is said by the disciple, another thing is said by the teacher; surely it was said by me from the outset, 'If it will stand in such a way as it is established by his disciple, then I will bring forward a claim.'"

But this one says something else; what can I do there?" Thus, while speaking just as the rule spoken by Assaji the Elder below [said] so that there might not be an opportunity for the speech of the *nigaṇṭha*, he said, "*Thus, indeed, I am, Aggivessana*," etc.

"*A simile occurs to me, sir Gotama*," he says, "Sir Gotama, a simile occurs to me, I will bring that simile," he says.

"*May it occur to you, Aggivessana*," the Blessed One said, "[May] that simile occur to you, Aggivessana, bring that simile confidently."

"*To be done by strength*," are those actions that are to be done by the strength of the arms, such as agriculture, trade, etc.

"*This person is the self of *rūpa**," means that *rūpa* is the self for him, therefore "*the self of *rūpa*," he indicates the person who stands having taken *rūpa* as the self.

"*Having stood in *rūpa**," means having stood in the *rūpa* that is taken as the self.

"*She gives birth to merit or demerit*," means she obtains merit or demerit.

"*Also in feelings, etc.*" this very method [is to be applied].

What does he indicate by this? These five aggregates are a support for these beings, like the earth; having stood in these five aggregates, they accumulate what is called meritorious and demeritorious action.

While you refute the self that exists in just this way, saying that the five aggregates are "*not-self*," having made a cause in a very excessive way, he brought forward a simile.

And by this *nigaṇṭha* the simile that was brought is indeed fixed, [since] other than the all-knowing Buddha, there is no one capable of cutting off his speech and giving a fault in the debate.

For there are two kinds of persons: those who are to be trained by the Buddha and those who are to be trained by the disciples.

In those who are to be trained by the disciples, the disciples also train [them], and the Buddhas also.

But in those who are to be trained by the Buddha, the disciples are not able to train [them]; only the Buddhas train [them].

This *nigaṇṭha* also is to be trained by the Buddha; therefore, there is no one capable of cutting off his speech and giving a fault in the debate.

Therefore, the Blessed One himself, for the purpose of showing a fault in the debate, said, "*Surely you are, Aggivessana*," etc.

Then the *nigaṇṭha* thought: "The *śramaṇa* Gotama establishes my speech excessively; if there will be some fault above, he will refute me alone.

Come, I will throw this speech onto the head even of the great crowd," therefore he spoke thus: "*I also, sir Gotama, say thus: *rūpa* is my self…pe… consciousness is my self, and this great crowd [says the same]*."

But the Blessed One was superior in debate by a hundred times, a thousand times, a hundred thousand times to the *nigaṇṭha*, therefore he thought: "This *nigaṇṭha*, having freed himself, throws the speech onto the head of the great crowd; I will not give [him] an opportunity to free himself, having turned [it] back from the great crowd, I will refute him alone."

Then he said to him, "*What is it to you, Aggivessana*," etc.

His meaning is: "This crowd has not come to bring forward my speech, but you alone, having gathered the whole of Vesālī, have come to bring forward my speech, therefore you yourself conclude your speech, do not throw [it] onto the head of the great crowd."

He, acknowledging, said, "*Indeed, sir Gotama*," etc.

"*I also, sir Gotama, say thus: *rūpa* is my self…pe… consciousness is my self, and this great crowd [says the same]*."

"*What is it to you, Aggivessana*." "*Indeed, sir Gotama*."

mula_pali:
357. ‘‘Tena hi, aggivessana, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi, yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ tathā taṃ (ka.) byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi , aggivessana, vatteyya rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa sakasmiṃ vijite vaso – ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetuṃ, jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetuṃ, pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetuṃ, seyyathāpi rañño pasenadissa kosalassa, seyyathāpi vā pana rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassā’’ti? ‘‘Vatteyya, bho gotama, rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa sakasmiṃ vijite vaso – ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetuṃ, jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetuṃ, pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetuṃ, seyyathāpi rañño pasenadissa kosalassa, seyyathāpi vā pana rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassa. Imesampi hi, bho gotama, saṅghānaṃ gaṇānaṃ – seyyathidaṃ, vajjīnaṃ mallānaṃ – vattati sakasmiṃ vijite vaso – ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetuṃ, jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetuṃ, pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetuṃ. Kiṃ pana rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa, seyyathāpi rañño pasenadissa kosalassa , seyyathāpi vā pana rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassa? Vatteyya, bho gotama, vattituñca marahatī’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘rūpaṃ me attā’ti, vattati te tasmiṃ rūpe vaso – evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, saccako nigaṇṭhaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā saccakaṃ nigaṇṭhaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘rūpaṃ me attā’ti, vattati te tasmiṃ rūpe vaso – evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’’ti? Dutiyampi kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Atha kho bhagavā saccakaṃ nigaṇṭhaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘byākarohi dāni, aggivessana, na dāni te tuṇhībhāvassa kālo. Yo koci, aggivessana tathāgatena yāvatatiyaṃ sahadhammikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho na byākaroti, etthevassa sattadhā muddhā phalatī’’ti.

Tena kho pana samayena vajirapāṇi yakkho āyasaṃ vajiraṃ ādāya ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ saccakassa nigaṇṭhaputtassa uparivehāsaṃ ṭhito hoti – ‘sacāyaṃ saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavatā yāvatatiyaṃ sahadhammikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho na byākarissati etthevassa sattadhā muddhaṃ phālessāmī’ti. Taṃ kho pana vajirapāṇiṃ yakkhaṃ bhagavā ceva passati saccako ca nigaṇṭhaputto. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhīto saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto bhagavantaṃyeva tāṇaṃ gavesī bhagavantaṃyeva leṇaṃ gavesī bhagavantaṃyeva saraṇaṃ gavesī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘pucchatu maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo, byākarissāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
357. “Then, Aggivessana, I will cross-question you on this matter. Answer as you see fit. What do you think, Aggivessana, would a head-anointed warrior king such as a king have power in his own kingdom to execute those that have to be executed, to produce those that have to be produced, and to banish those that have to be banished, such as King Pasenadi of Kosala, or King Ajātasattu, the son of the Videhi princess, of Magadha?”

“Yes, good Gotama, a head-anointed warrior king has power in his own kingdom to execute those that have to be executed, to produce those that have to be produced, and to banish those that have to be banished, such as King Pasenadi of Kosala, or King Ajātasattu, the son of the Videhi princess, of Magadha."

Even the leaders, gathered here, of the Vajjis and Mallas, wield power in their kingdoms to execute those that have to be executed, to produce those that have to be produced and to banish those that have to be banished.

What about a head-anointed warrior king such as King Pasenadi of Kosala, or King Ajātasattu, the son of the Videhi princess, of Magadha? Yes, good Gotama, it applies and is fitting."

“What do you think, Aggivessana, you that say, ‘*Rūpa* (form) is my *ātman* (self),’ do you wield power over that *rūpa*, as may my *rūpa* be thus, and not otherwise?” When this was said Saccaka the son of Nigantha became silent.

For the second time, the Blessed One said to Saccaka, the son of Nigantha, “What do you think, Aggivessana, you that say, ‘*Rūpa* (form) is my *ātman* (self),’ do you wield power over that *rūpa*, as may my *rūpa* be thus, and not otherwise?” For the second time Saccaka the son of Nigantha became silent.

Then the Blessed One said to Saccaka, the son of Nigantha, “Explain it now, Aggivessana. This is not the time for you to be silent. If someone does not reply a rightful question asked by the *Tathāgata* (Thus Gone One) up to the third time, his head splits into seven pieces.”

Then, at that time, Vajrapāṇi (*Vajrapāṇi*) the *yakṣa* (demon), holding an iron *vajra* (thunderbolt), blazing, thoroughly ablaze, and radiant, was standing in the sky above Saccaka, the son of Nigantha, [thinking,] “If Saccaka, the son of Nigantha, does not answer a fundamental question put to him by the Blessed One by the third asking, I will split his head into seven pieces right here!”

The Blessed One and Saccaka, the son of Nigantha, both saw that *Vajrapāṇi yakṣa* (*Vajrapāṇi* the demon).

Then Saccaka, the son of Nigantha, frightened, agitated, and with his hair standing on end, sought refuge, shelter and safety from the Blessed One, and said to the Blessed One: “Let the esteemed Gotama ask me, and I will explain.”
commentary_pali:
357. Iti bhagavā nigaṇṭhassa vādaṃ patiṭṭhapetvā, tena hi, aggivessanāti pucchaṃ ārabhi. Tattha tena hīti kāraṇatthe nipāto. Yasmā tvaṃ pañcakkhandhe attato paṭijānāsi, tasmāti attho. Sakasmiṃ vijiteti attano raṭṭhe. Ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetunti ghātārahaṃ ghātetabbayuttakaṃ ghātetuṃ . Jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetunti dhanajānirahaṃ jāpetabbayuttaṃ jāpetuṃ jiṇṇadhanaṃ kātuṃ. Pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetunti sakaraṭṭhato pabbājanārahaṃ pabbājetuṃ, nīharituṃ. Vattituñca arahatīti vattati ceva vattituñca arahati. Vattituṃ yuttoti dīpeti. Iti nigaṇṭho attano vādabhedanatthaṃ āhaṭakāraṇameva attano māraṇatthāya āvudhaṃ tikhiṇaṃ karonto viya visesetvā dīpeti, yathā taṃ bālo. Evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotūti mama rūpaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ hotu, pāsādikaṃ abhirūpaṃ alaṅkatappaṭiyattaṃ suvaṇṇatoraṇaṃ viya susajjitacittapaṭo viya ca manāpadassananti. Evaṃ me rūpaṃmā ahosīti mama rūpaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ mā hotu, dubbaṇṇaṃ dussaṇṭhitaṃ valitapalitaṃ tilakasamākiṇṇanti.

Tuṇhī ahosīti nigaṇṭho imasmiṃ ṭhāne viraddhabhāvaṃ ñatvā, ‘‘samaṇo gotamo mama vādaṃ bhindanatthāya kāraṇaṃ āhari, ahaṃ bālatāya tameva visesetvā dīpesiṃ, idāni naṭṭhomhi, sace vattatīti vakkhāmi, ime rājāno uṭṭhahitvā, ‘aggivessana, tvaṃ mama rūpe vaso vattatīti vadasi, yadi te rūpe vaso vattati, kasmā tvaṃ yathā ime licchavirājāno tāvatiṃsadevasadisehi attabhāvehi virocanti abhirūpā pāsādikā, evaṃ na virocasī’ti. Sace na vattatīti vakkhāmi, samaṇo gotamo uṭṭhahitvā, ‘aggivessana, tvaṃ pubbe vattati me rūpasmiṃ vasoti vatvā idāni paṭikkhipasī’ti vādaṃ āropessati. Iti vattatīti vuttepi eko doso, na vattatīti vuttepi eko doso’’ti tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi bhagavā pucchi, dutiyampi tuṇhī ahosi. Yasmā pana yāvatatiyaṃ bhagavatā pucchite abyākarontassa sattadhā muddhā phalati, buddhā ca nāma sattānaṃyeva atthāya kappasatasahassādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni pāramīnaṃ pūritattā sattesu balavaanuddayā honti. Tasmā yāvatatiyaṃ apucchitvā atha kho bhagavā saccakaṃ nigaṇṭhaputtaṃ etadavoca – etaṃ ‘‘byākarohī dānī’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca.

Tuṇhī ahosī

Tattha sahadhammikanti sahetukaṃ sakāraṇaṃ. Vajiraṃ pāṇimhi assāti vajirapāṇi. Yakkhoti na yo vā so vā yakkho, sakko devarājāti veditabbo. Ādittanti aggivaṇṇaṃ. Sampajjalitanti suṭṭhu pajjalitaṃ. Sajotibhūtanti samantato jotibhūtaṃ, ekaggijālabhūtanti attho. Ṭhito hotīti mahantaṃ sīsaṃ, kandalamakulasadisā dāṭhā, bhayānakāni akkhināsādīnīti evaṃ virūparūpaṃ māpetvā ṭhito. Kasmā panesa āgatoti? Diṭṭhivissajjāpanatthaṃ. Apica, ‘‘ahañceva kho pana dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, pare ca me na ājāneyyu’’nti evaṃ dhammadesanāya appossukkabhāvaṃ āpanne bhagavati sakko mahābrahmunā saddhiṃ āgantvā, ‘‘bhagavā dhammaṃ desetha, tumhākaṃ āṇāya avattamāne mayaṃ vattāpessāma, tumhākaṃ dhammacakkaṃ hotu, amhākaṃ āṇācakka’’nti paṭiññamakāsi. Tasmā ‘‘ajja saccakaṃ tāsetvā pañhaṃ vissajjāpessāmī’’ti āgato.

sahadhammika vajirapāṇi. Yakkho Āditta Sampajjalita Sajotibhūta Ṭhito hotī

Bhagavāceva passati, saccako ca nigaṇṭhaputtoti yadi hi taṃ aññepi passeyyuṃ. Taṃ kāraṇaṃ agaru assa, ‘‘samaṇo gotamo saccakaṃ attano vāde anotarantaṃ ñatvā yakkhaṃ āvāhetvā dassesi, tato saccako bhayena kathesī’’ti vadeyyuṃ. Tasmā bhagavā ceva passati saccako ca. Tassa taṃ disvāva sakalasarīrato sedā mucciṃsu, antokucchi viparivattamānā mahāravaṃ ravi. So ‘‘aññepi nu kho passantī’’ti olokento kassaci lomahaṃsamattampi na addasa. Tato – ‘‘idaṃ bhayaṃ mameva uppannaṃ. Sacāhaṃ yakkhoti vakkhāmi, ‘kiṃ tuyhameva akkhīni atthi, tvameva yakkhaṃ passasi, paṭhamaṃ yakkhaṃ adisvā samaṇena gotamena vādasaṅghāṭe khittova yakkhaṃ passasī’ti vadeyyu’’nti cintetvā – ‘‘na dāni me idha aññaṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ atthi, aññatra samaṇā gotamā’’ti maññamāno, atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto…pe… bhagavantaṃ etadavoca. Tāṇaṃ gavesīti tāṇanti gavesamāno. Leṇaṃ gavesīti leṇanti gavesamāno. Saraṇaṃ gavesīti saraṇanti gavesamāno. Ettha ca tāyati rakkhatīti tāṇaṃ. Nilīyanti etthāti leṇaṃ. Saratīti saraṇaṃ, bhayaṃ hiṃsati viddhaṃsetīti attho.

Bhagavā ceva passati, saccako ca nigaṇṭhaputto Tāṇaṃ gavesī Leṇaṃ gavesī Saraṇaṃ gavesī tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ,
commentary_english:
357. Thus, the Blessed One, having established the doctrine of the Nigaṇṭha, began the questioning, "Then, Aggivessana..."
There, *tena hi* means a particle in the sense of cause.
Because you acknowledge the five aggregates as self, therefore, that is the meaning.
*Sakasmiṃ vijite* means in one's own kingdom.
*Ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetu* means he should kill one worthy of being killed, appropriate to be killed.
*Jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetu* means he should cause loss of wealth, appropriate for causing loss, to make wealth old.
*Pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetu* means he should banish from his own kingdom one worthy of being banished, to drive out, to expel.
*Vattituñca arahatī* means he is fit to behave and is worthy to behave.
*Vattituṃ yutto* he demonstrates to be fit to behave.
Thus, the Nigaṇṭha, wishing to break his own doctrine, just as a fool sharpening a weapon for his own destruction, emphasizes and demonstrates the very cause that was brought forward for the purpose of refuting his own doctrine.
*Evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotū* means may my form be of such a kind, pleasing, handsome, adorned, prepared, like a golden arch, like a well-decorated painted cloth, and of delightful appearance.
*Evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī* means may my form not be of such a kind, ugly, ill-shaped, wrinkled, grey-haired, covered with moles.

*Tuṇhī ahosī* means the Nigaṇṭha, knowing the state of being refuted in this place, [thought,] "The *śramaṇa* Gotama has brought a cause for the sake of breaking my doctrine, and I, in my foolishness, have emphasized and demonstrated that very thing. Now I am lost. If I say it exists, these kings will rise up and say, 'Aggivessana, you say that there is mastery over your form, but if there is mastery over your form, why do you not shine like these Licchavi kings, who shine with beautiful and pleasing forms similar to the Tāvatiṃsa gods?'
If I say it does not exist, the *śramaṇa* Gotama will rise up and accuse me, saying, 'Aggivessana, you formerly said that there is mastery and control over my form, but now you deny it.'
Thus, whether he said it exists or does not exist, there is a fault," so he remained silent.
A second time the Blessed One asked, and a second time he remained silent.
Because, if asked a third time by the Blessed One and not answering, his head would split into seven pieces, and Buddhas are truly strongly compassionate toward beings, having fulfilled the *pāramīs* for hundreds of thousands of *kappas*.
Therefore, without asking a third time, the Blessed One said this to Saccaka, the Nigaṇṭha’s son – he spoke this statement beginning, “Speak now!”
*Tuṇhī ahosī*
There, *sahadhammika* means with a cause, with a reason.
*Vajiraṃ pāṇimhi assāti Vajirapāṇi* means one who has the *vajra* in his hand.
*Yakkho* means not just any *yakṣa*, but Sakka, the king of the gods, should be understood.
*Āditta* means like fire.
*Sampajjalita* means very blazing.
*Sajotibhūta* means blazing all around, meaning having become one mass of flames.
*Ṭhito hotī* means he stands having created a monstrous form: a large head, teeth like *kandala* buds, fearful eyes, nose, etc.
Why did he come? For the rejection of views.
Moreover, when the Blessed One was inclined to a lack of enthusiasm for teaching the Dharma, [thinking,] "If I were to teach the Dharma, others would not understand me," Sakka, together with Mahābrahmā, having come, said, "Blessed One, teach the Dharma! If those who are not amenable to your command, we will make them amenable. Let the Wheel of the Dharma be yours, and the Wheel of Command be ours," he made a promise.
Therefore, he came [thinking], "Today, having terrified Saccaka, I will make him abandon his question."

*Sahadhammika Vajirapāṇi*.
*Yakkho Āditta Sampajjalita Sajotibhūta Ṭhito hotī*
*Bhagavā ceva passati, Saccako ca nigaṇṭhaputto* means if others were to see it, that would be an offense, [thinking,] "The *śramaṇa* Gotama, knowing that Saccaka was not answering in his own doctrine, has invoked a *yakṣa* and shown it, and then Saccaka spoke out of fear."
Therefore, the Blessed One alone sees it, and Saccaka.
Having seen that, sweat broke out from his entire body; his insides churned, and he roared loudly.

He looked around, thinking, "Are others also seeing [this]?" but he did not see even the slightest sign of goosebumps on anyone.

Then—"This fear has arisen in me alone.

If I should say 'It's a *yakṣa*,' they would say, 'Do only you have eyes? Are you alone seeing a *yakṣa*? Having not seen a *yakṣa* before, are you now seeing a *yakṣa* because you've been thrown into a debate-gathering by the ascetic Gotama?'"—thinking thus, "Now, for me, there is no other refuge here than the ascetic Gotama," he thought, and then Saccaka, the Nigaṇṭha's son...pe...said this to the Blessed One (bhagavant).

*tāṇaṃ gavesī* means seeking a refuge.

*leṇaṃ gavesī* means seeking a shelter.

*saraṇaṃ gavesī* means seeking a protection.

Because here, it protects and preserves, therefore *tāṇaṃ* (refuge).

They hide here, therefore *leṇaṃ* (shelter).

Because it protects, therefore *saraṇaṃ* (protection); it injures fear, it destroys, is the meaning.

The Blessed One (bhagavā) sees, and Saccaka, the Nigaṇṭha's son, seeks refuge, seeks shelter, seeks protection, refuge, shelter, protection.

358. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘rūpaṃ me attā’ti, vattati te tasmiṃ rūpe vaso – evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Manasi karohi, aggivessana; manasi karitvā kho, aggivessana, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘vedanā me attā’ti, vattati te tissaṃ vedanāyaṃ tāyaṃ vedanāyaṃ (sī. syā.) vaso – evaṃ me vedanā hotu, evaṃ me vedanā mā ahosī’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

tāyaṃ vedanāyaṃ (sī. syā.)

‘‘Manasi karohi, aggivessana; manasi karitvā kho, aggivessana, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana , yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘saññā me attā’ti, vattati te tissaṃ saññāyaṃ vaso – evaṃ me saññā hotu, evaṃ me saññā mā ahosī’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Manasi karohi, aggivessana ; manasi karitvā kho, aggivessana, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘saṅkhārā me attā’ti, vattati te tesu saṅkhāresu vaso – evaṃ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṃ me saṅkhārā mā ahesu’’nti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Manasi karohi, aggivessana; manasi karitvā kho, aggivessana, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘viññāṇaṃ me attā’ti, vattati te tasmiṃ viññāṇe vaso – evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ hotu, evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ mā ahosī’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Manasi karohi, aggivessana; manasi karitvā kho, aggivessana, byākarohi. Na kho te sandhiyati purimena vā pacchimaṃ, pacchimena vā purimaṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Aniccaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Dukkhaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Aniccaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Dukkhaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, yo nu kho dukkhaṃ allīno dukkhaṃ upagato dukkhaṃ ajjhosito , dukkhaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati, api nu kho so sāmaṃ vā dukkhaṃ parijāneyya, dukkhaṃ vā parikkhepetvā vihareyyā’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi siyā, bho gotama? No hidaṃ, bho gotamā’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, nanu tvaṃ evaṃ sante dukkhaṃ allīno dukkhaṃ upagato dukkhaṃ ajjhosito, dukkhaṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasī’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, bho gotama? Evametaṃ bho gotamā’’ti.
mula_english:
358. “What do you think, Aggivessana? You say, ‘Matter is my self.’ Do you wield power over that matter, as may my matter be thus and not thus?”

“Attend carefully and reply, Aggivessana.

What you said earlier does not agree with what you say now.

What do you think, Aggivessana? You say, ‘Feeling is my self.’ Do you wield power over those feelings, as may my feelings be thus, and not otherwise?”

“Attend carefully, Aggivessana; attend carefully and reply, Aggivessana.

What you said before does not agree with what you said afterwards, nor does what you said afterwards agree with what you said before.

What do you think, Aggivessana, you that say, perceptions are your self, do you wield power over those perceptions, as may my perceptions be thus and not otherwise?"

Aggivessana, you, that say, consciousness is your self, do you wield power over that consciousness, as may my consciousness be thus and not otherwise.

Attend carefully, Aggivessana; attend carefully and reply, Aggivessana.

What you said before does not agree with what you said afterwards, nor does what you said afterwards agree with what you said before.

What do you think, Āggivessana, is matter permanent or impermanent?

“But that which is impermanent, (is) that unpleasant or pleasant?”

“And is it fitting to regard what is inconstant, stressful, subject to change as: ‘This is mine. This is my self. This is what I am’?”

What do you think, Aggivessana, are feelings-are perceptions, —are determinations, —is consciousness permanent or impermanent?

“But that which is impermanent, (is) that unpleasant or pleasant?”

“And is it fitting to regard what is inconstant, stressful, subject to change as: ‘This is mine. This is my self. This is what I am’?”

Aggivessana, a certain one clinging to unpleasantness, over powered by it, pressed down by it and reflecting it’s mine, would think it’s my self. Would he accurately understand unpleasāntness by himself or ward it off and abide?

What do you think, Aggivessana, a certain one clinging to unpleasantness, over powered by it, pressed down by it and reflecting it’s mine, would think it’s my self.
[p.]
commentary_pali: 358.Manasi karitvāti manamhi katvā paccavekkhitvā upadhāretvā. Evaṃ me vedanā hotūti kusalāva hotu, sukhāva hotu. Evaṃ me saññā hotūti kusalāva hotu, sukhāva hotu, somanassasampayuttāva hotūti. Saṅkhāraviññāṇesupi eseva nayo. Mā ahosīti ettha pana vuttavipariyāyena attho veditabbo. Kallaṃ nūti yuttaṃ nu. Samanupassitunti ‘‘etaṃ mama esohamasmi eso me attā’’ti evaṃ taṇhāmānadiṭṭhivasena passituṃ. No hidaṃ, bho gotamāti na yuttametaṃ, bho gotama. Iti bhagavā yathā nāma cheko ahituṇḍiko sappadaṭṭhavisaṃ teneva sappena puna ḍaṃsāpetvā ubbāheyya, evaṃ tassaṃyeva parisati saccakaṃ nigaṇṭhaputtaṃ teneva mukhena pañcakkhandhā aniccā dukkhā anattāti vadāpesi. Dukkhaṃ allīnoti imaṃ pañcakkhandhadukkhaṃ taṇhādiṭṭhīhi allīno. Upagato ajjhositotipi taṇhādiṭṭhivaseneva veditabbo. Dukkhaṃ etaṃ mamātiādīsu pañcakkhandhadukkhaṃ taṇhāmānadiṭṭhivasena samanupassatīti attho. Parijāneyyāti aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti tīraṇapariññāya parito jāneyya. Parikkhepetvāti khayaṃ vayaṃ anuppādaṃ upanetvā.
commentary_english:
358. "Having made up my mind" means having done it in the mind, having contemplated, having considered.

"Thus may feeling arise in me" means may it be wholesome, may it be pleasant.

"Thus may perception arise in me" means may it be wholesome, may it be pleasant, may it be associated with joy.

This is the method for formations and consciousness as well.

"May [it] not be" should be understood in terms of the meaning in the opposite way.

"Is [it] suitable?" means is it fitting?

"To investigate" means to see in terms of craving, pride, and views, thinking "This is mine, this I am, this is my self (ātman)."

"No, Reverend Gotama," means this is not fitting, Reverend Gotama.

Thus, the Blessed One, just as a clever snake charmer would cause a snake that had bitten someone to bite [them] again in order to draw out the poison, in that very assembly, he caused Saccaka, the son of the Nigaṇṭha, to declare with that very mouth that the five aggregates (*pañcakkhandhā*) are impermanent (*aniccā*), suffering (*dukkhā*), and selfless (*anattā*).

"Attached to suffering" means attached to this suffering of the five aggregates by craving and views.

"Approached and adhered to" should also be understood in terms of craving and views.

"Suffering, this is mine," and so forth, the meaning is that one investigates the suffering of the five aggregates in terms of craving, pride, and views.

"One should understand" means one should understand fully with the discernment of impermanence, suffering, and selflessness.

"Having diminished" means having brought about destruction, cessation, and non-arising.

mula_pali: 359. ‘‘Seyyathāpi , aggivessana, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno tiṇhaṃ kuṭhāriṃ kudhāriṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) ādāya vanaṃ paviseyya. So tattha passeyya mahantaṃ kadalikkhandhaṃ ujuṃ navaṃ akukkukajātaṃ akukkuṭajātaṃ (syā. kaṃ.). Tamenaṃ mūle chindeyya, mūle chetvā agge chindeyya, agge chetvā pattavaṭṭiṃ vinibbhujeyya vinibbhujjeyya (ka.). So tattha pattavaṭṭiṃ vinibbhujanto pheggumpi nādhigaccheyya, kuto sāraṃ? Evameva kho tvaṃ, aggivessana, mayā sakasmiṃ vāde samanuyuñjiyamāno samanugāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno ritto tuccho aparaddho. Bhāsitā kho pana te esā, aggivessana, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā – ‘nāhaṃ taṃ passāmi samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā, saṅghiṃ gaṇiṃ gaṇācariyaṃ, api arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ paṭijānamānaṃ, yo mayā vādena vādaṃ samāraddho na saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampavedheyya, yassa na kacchehi sedā mucceyyuṃ. Thūṇaṃ cepāhaṃ acetanaṃ vādena vādaṃ samārabheyyaṃ sāpi mayā vādena vādaṃ samāraddhā saṅkampeyya sampakampeyya sampavedheyya. Ko pana vādo manussabhūtassā’ti? Tuyhaṃ kho pana, aggivessana, appekaccāni sedaphusitāni nalāṭā muttāni, uttarāsaṅgaṃ vinibhinditvā bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhitāni. Mayhaṃ kho pana, aggivessana, natthi etarahi kāyasmiṃ sedo’’ti. Iti bhagavā tasmiṃ tassaṃ (?) parisati suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ kāyaṃ vivari. Evaṃ vutte, saccako nigaṇṭhaputto tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno nisīdi.
mula_english:
359. Just as, Aggivessana, a man needing heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, might enter a forest taking a sharp axe, there he would see a large plantain trunk, straight, fresh, without a *kukkuka* core. He would cut it down at the root ( *mūle chindeyya*), cutting it at the root ( *mūle chetvā*), he would cut off the top ( *agge chindeyya*), cutting off the top ( *agge chetvā*), he would unroll the coil ( *pattavaṭṭiṃ vinibbhujeyya*). As he unrolls the coil there, he would not even obtain the soft core ( *pheggu*), how could there be heartwood ( *sāraṃ*)? Just so, Aggivessana, when you are pressed by me in my own argument, cross-examined, and refuted, you are empty, void, and in the wrong.

Indeed, this statement of yours has been spoken in Vesālī in assembly: ‘I do not see any renunciant ( *samaṇaṃ* ) or Brahmin ( *brāhmaṇaṃ* ), a leader of a group, a teacher of a group, or even an *arhat*, a Fully Awakened Buddha ( *sammāsambuddhaṃ* ) claiming such, who, when drawn into a debate with me, would not tremble, shake, and quake, whose sweat would not pour from his armpits.’ If I were to engage a lifeless pillar in debate, even that, when drawn into debate by me, would tremble, shake, and quake. What need to speak of a human being? But as for you, Aggivessana, some drops of sweat have fallen from your forehead and, piercing your upper robe ( *uttarāsaṅgaṃ* ), have settled on the ground. But as for me, Aggivessana, at this moment there is no sweat on my body."

Thus, the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ) disclosed his golden-hued body to that gathering.

When this was said, Saccaka, the son of the Nigaṇṭha, sat silent, confused, his form drooping, face turned down, glum, and without response.
commentary_pali:
359.Navanti taruṇaṃ. Akukkukajātanti pupphaggahaṇakāle anto aṅguṭṭhappamāṇo eko ghanadaṇḍako nibbattati, tena virahitanti attho. Rittoti suñño antosāravirahito. Rittattāva tuccho. Aparaddhoti parājito. Bhāsitā kho pana teti idaṃ bhagavā tassa mukharabhāvaṃ pakāsetvā niggaṇhanto āha. So kira pubbe pūraṇādayo cha satthāro upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ pucchati. Te vissajjetuṃ na sakkonti. Atha nesaṃ parisamajjhe mahantaṃ vippakāraṃ āropetvā uṭṭhāya jayaṃ pavedento gacchati. So sammāsambuddhampi tatheva viheṭhessāmīti saññāya upasaṅkamitvā –

‘‘Ambho ko nāma yaṃ rukkho, sinnapatto sakaṇṭako;

Yattha ekappahārena, uttamaṅgaṃ vibhijjita’’nti.

Ayaṃ khadiraṃ āhacca asārakarukkhaparicito mudutuṇḍasakuṇo viya sabbaññutaññāṇasāraṃ āhacca ñāṇatuṇḍabhedaṃ patto sabbaññutaññāṇassa thaddhabhāvaṃ aññāsi. Tadassa parisamajjhe pakāsento bhāsitā kho pana tetiādimāha. Natthi etarahīti upādinnakasarīre sedo nāma natthīti na vattabbaṃ, etarahi pana natthīti vadati. Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ kāyaṃ vivarīti na sabbaṃ kāyaṃ vivari. Buddhā nāma gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā paṭicchannasarīrā parisati dhammaṃ desenti. Atha bhagavā galavāṭakasammukhaṭṭhāne cīvaraṃ gahetvā caturaṅgulamattaṃ otāresi. Otāritamatte pana tasmiṃ suvaṇṇavaṇṇā rasmiyo puñjapuñjā hutvā suvaṇṇaghaṭato rattasuvaṇṇarasadhārā viya, rattavaṇṇavalāhakato vijjulatā viya ca nikkhamitvā suvaṇṇamurajasadisaṃ mahākhandhaṃ uttamasiraṃ padakkhiṇaṃ kurumānā ākāse pakkhandiṃsu. Kasmā pana bhagavā evamakāsīti? Mahājanassa kaṅkhāvinodanatthaṃ. Mahājano hi samaṇo gotamo mayhaṃ sedo natthīti vadati, saccakassa tāva nigaṇṭhaputtassa yantāruḷhassa viya sedā paggharanti. Samaṇo pana gotamo ghanadupaṭṭacīvaraṃ pārupitvā nisinno, anto sedassa atthitā vā natthitā vā kathaṃ sakkā ñātunti kaṅkhaṃ kareyya, tassa kaṅkhāvinodanatthaṃ evamakāsi. Maṅkubhūtoti nittejabhūto. Pattakkhandhoti patitakkhandho. Appaṭibhānoti uttari appassanto. Nisīdīti pādaṅguṭṭhakena bhūmiṃ kasamāno nisīdi.

bhāsitā kho pana te Natthi etarahī Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ kāyaṃ vivarī Maṅkubhūto Pattakkhandho Appaṭibhāno Nisīdī
commentary_english:
359.
*Nava*nti taruṇaṃ: Young.

*Akukkukajāta*nti: At the time of taking flowers, inside, a solid rod the size of a thumb arises, meaning devoid of that.

*ritto*ti: Empty, devoid of inner essence.

Because of emptiness, *tuccho*: vain.

*aparaddho*ti: Defeated.

*bhāsitā kho pana te*ti: The Blessed One, revealing and rebuking his garrulousness, said.

It is said that formerly he approached six teachers, beginning with Pūraṇa, and asked questions.

They are not able to answer.

Then, having caused great discord in the midst of their assembly, he rises, proclaiming victory, and leaves.

Thinking, "I will harass even the perfectly enlightened Buddha in the same way," he approached with that intention.

"O, what is the name of that tree, with withered leaves and thorns;

Where with a single strike, the head would be split?"

This one, having struck the *khadira* tree, being familiar with trees without essence, like a bird with a soft beak, having struck the essence of the knowledge of omniscience, having attained a split in the beak of knowledge, understood the rigidity of the knowledge of omniscience.

Therefore, revealing in the midst of the assembly, he spoke, beginning with "*bhāsitā kho pana te*."

* natthi etarahī*ti: It should not be said that there is no sweat in a body sustained by grasping; rather, he says that there is none now.

*suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ kāyaṃ vivarī*ti: He did not uncover the entire body.

The Buddhas, having tied on a belt and with their bodies covered, sit and teach the *dharma*.

Then the Blessed One, having taken the robe at a place facing the throat, lowered it about four inches.

As soon as it was lowered, rays of golden color, becoming heaps and heaps, like streams of red-golden juice from a golden pot, like lightning from a red-colored cloud, having emerged and circumambulating the great trunk, the supreme head, similar to a golden drum, scattered in the sky.

Why did the Blessed One do this? For the sake of dispelling the doubt of the great multitude.

Indeed, the great multitude [thought], "The *śramaṇa* Gotama says, 'I have no sweat,' but for Saccaka, the son of Nigaṇṭha, sweat flows as for one riding in a chariot."

The *śramaṇa* Gotama, however, having wrapped himself in a thick double-layered robe, is sitting; how is it possible to know whether there is sweat inside or not? He might have doubt. For the sake of dispelling his doubt, he did this.

*maṅkubhūto*ti: Having become without energy.

*pattakkhandho*ti: Fallen aggregate.

*appaṭibhāno*ti: Further, not experiencing.

*nisīdī*ti: He sat down, scraping the ground with his toe.

*bhāsitā kho pana te natthi etarahī suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ kāyaṃ vivarī maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho appaṭibhāno nisīdī*

mula_pali: 360. Atha kho dummukho licchaviputto saccakaṃ nigaṇṭhaputtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ maṅkubhūtaṃ pattakkhandhaṃ adhomukhaṃ pajjhāyantaṃ appaṭibhānaṃ viditvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘upamā maṃ, bhagavā, paṭibhātī’’ti. ‘‘Paṭibhātu taṃ, dummukhā’’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhante, gāmassa vā nigamassa vā avidūre pokkharaṇī. Tatrāssa kakkaṭako. Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā kumārakā vā kumārikā vā tamhā gāmā vā nigamā vā nikkhamitvā yena sā pokkharaṇī tenupasaṅkameyyuṃ; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ ogāhetvā taṃ kakkaṭakaṃ udakā uddharitvā thale patiṭṭhāpeyyuṃ. Yaññadeva hi so, bhante, kakkaṭako aḷaṃ abhininnāmeyya taṃ tadeva te kumārakā vā kumārikā vā kaṭṭhena vā kathalena vā sañchindeyyuṃ sambhañjeyyuṃ sampalibhañjeyyuṃ. Evañhi so, bhante, kakkaṭako sabbehi aḷehi sañchinnehi sambhaggehi sampalibhaggehi abhabbo taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ puna otarituṃ, seyyathāpi pubbe. Evameva kho, bhante, yāni saccakassa nigaṇṭhaputtassa visūkāyitāni visevitāni vipphanditāni tānipi sabbāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici tāni (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhagavatā sañchinnāni sambhaggāni sampalibhaggāni; abhabbo ca dāni, bhante, saccako nigaṇṭhaputto puna bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamituṃ yadidaṃ vādādhippāyo’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, saccako nigaṇṭhaputto dummukhaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘āgamehi tvaṃ, dummukha, āgamehi tvaṃ, dummukha ( ) (mukharosi tvaṃ dummukha) (syā. kaṃ.) na mayaṃ tayā saddhiṃ mantema, idha mayaṃ bhotā gotamena saddhiṃ mantema.
mula_english:
Then Dummukha, the son of the Licchavis, having seen Saccaka, the son of the Nigantha, silent, confused, with drooping form, face turned down, and unable to reply, said this to the Blessed One: "An analogy occurs to me, venerable sir."

"Say it, Dummukha," the Blessed One said.

"Venerable sir, suppose there were a pond not far from a village or town.

In it lives a crab.

Then, venerable sir, many boys and girls would leave that village or town and approach that pond; having approached that pond, they would descend into it, and having lifted that crab out of the water, they would place it on dry land.

Venerable sir, whenever that crab puts out a limb, those boys and girls would cut it off, shatter it, and utterly break it with a stick or a stone.

Thus, venerable sir, that crab, with all its limbs cut off, shattered, and utterly broken, would be incapable of descending into that pond again as before.

In the same way, venerable sir, all the distortions, elaborations, and restless thoughts of Saccaka, the son of the Nigantha, have been cut off, shattered, and utterly broken by the Blessed One; and now, venerable sir, it is impossible for Saccaka, the son of the Nigantha, to approach the Blessed One again with the intention of disputing."

When this was said, Saccaka, the son of the Nigantha, said this to Dummukha, the son of the Licchavis: "Wait, Dummukha, wait, Dummukha! We are not discussing with you; here we are discussing with Master Gotama."
commentary_pali: 360.Dummukhoti na virūpamukho, abhirūpo hi so pāsādiko. Nāmaṃ panassa etaṃ. Abhabbo taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ puna otaritunti sabbesaṃ aḷānaṃ bhaggattā pacchinnagamano otarituṃ abhabbo, tattheva kākakulalādīnaṃ bhattaṃ hotīti dasseti. Visūkāyikānīti diṭṭhivisūkāni. Visevitānīti diṭṭhisañcaritāni. Vipphanditānīti diṭṭhivipphanditāni. Yadidaṃ vādādhippāyoti ettha yadidanti nipātamattaṃ; vādādhippāyo hutvā vādaṃ āropessāmīti ajjhāsayena upasaṅkamituṃ abhabbo; dhammassavanāya pana upasaṅkameyyāti dasseti. Dummukhaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocāti kasmā avoca ? Dummukhassa kirassa upamāharaṇakāle sesa licchavikumārāpi cintesuṃ – ‘‘iminā nigaṇṭhena amhākaṃ sippuggahaṇaṭṭhāne ciraṃ avamāno kato, ayaṃ dāni amittassa piṭṭhiṃ passituṃ kālo. Mayampi ekekaṃ upamaṃ āharitvā pāṇippahārena patitaṃ muggarena pothento viya tathā naṃ karissāma, yathā na puna parisamajjhe sīsaṃ ukkhipituṃ sakkhissatī’’ti, te opammāni karitvā dummukhassa kathāpariyosānaṃ āgamayamānā nisīdiṃsu. Saccako tesaṃ adhippāyaṃ ñatvā, ime sabbeva gīvaṃ ukkhipitvā oṭṭhehi calamānehi ṭhitā; sace paccekā upamā harituṃ labhissanti, puna mayā parisamajjhe sīsaṃ ukkhipituṃ na sakkā bhavissati, handāhaṃ dummukhaṃ apasādetvā yathā aññassa okāso na hoti, evaṃ kathāvāraṃ pacchinditvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pañhaṃ pucchissāmīti tasmā etadavoca. Tattha āgamehīti tiṭṭha, mā puna bhaṇāhīti attho.
commentary_english:
360. *Dummukho* means: "not ugly-faced; for he, the handsome one, is pleasing."
This is the name of Panassa.
*Abhabbo taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ puna otaritu* means: Because of the brokenness of all the bones, he is unable to go down again into that lotus pond, his gait is cut off. He is unfit to descend; he shows that right there he becomes food for crows, kites, and so on.
*Visūkāyikānī* means views that are like barbs.
*Visevitānī* means views that are practiced.
*Vipphanditānī* means views that are distorted.
