*Yadidaṃ vādādhippāyo* means: Here, *yadidaṃ* is merely an expletive; being of a disputatious intention, he is unfit to approach in order to cast blame; he shows that one should approach to hear the Dharma.
*Dummukhaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocā* means: Why did he say [this] to Dummukha, the Licchavi son? When Kira was giving an analogy about Dummukha, the remaining Licchavi princes thought: "For a long time, this Nigaṇṭha has been disrespectful in our place of learning the arts; now is the time to look at the back of an enemy.
We too, each bringing an analogy, just as one might strike down with a hand and beat with a club one who has fallen, so shall we do to him, so that he will not again be able to raise his head in the assembly." Having made those comparisons, they sat down, awaiting the conclusion of Dummukha’s speech.
Saccaka, knowing their intention, thought: "All of these are standing having raised their necks, their lips moving; if each one gets an opportunity to offer an analogy, I will not be able to raise my head again in the assembly. Come, I will humiliate Dummukha, and having cut off the opportunity of another in that way, I will ask the ascetic Gotama a question." Therefore, he said this.
There, *āgamehī* means "stand still; do not speak again!" is the meaning.

mula_pali:
361. ‘‘Tiṭṭhatesā, bho gotama, amhākañceva aññesañca puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ vācā. Vilāpaṃ vilapitaṃ maññe. Kittāvatā ca nu kho bhoto gotamassa sāvako sāsanakaro hoti ovādapatikaro tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane viharatī’’ti? ‘‘Idha, aggivessana, mama sāvako yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati; yā kāci vedanā…pe… yā kāci saññā…pe… ye keci saṅkhārā…pe… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā, yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Ettāvatā kho, aggivessana, mama sāvako sāsanakaro hoti ovādapatikaro tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane viharatī’’ti.

‘‘Kittāvatā pana, bho gotama, bhikkhu arahaṃ hoti khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto’’ti? ‘‘Idha, aggivessana, bhikkhu yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anupādā vimutto hoti; yā kāci vedanā…pe… yā kāci saññā…pe… ye keci saṅkhārā…pe… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anupādā vimutto hoti. Ettāvatā kho, aggivessana, bhikkhu arahaṃ hoti khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto. Evaṃ vimuttacitto kho, aggivessana, bhikkhu tīhi anuttariyehi samannāgato hoti – dassanānuttariyena, paṭipadānuttariyena, vimuttānuttariyena. Evaṃ vimuttacitto kho, aggivessana, bhikkhu tathāgataññeva sakkaroti garuṃ karoti māneti pūjeti – buddho so bhagavā bodhāya dhammaṃ deseti, danto so bhagavā damathāya dhammaṃ deseti, santo so bhagavā samathāya dhammaṃ deseti, tiṇṇo so bhagavā taraṇāya dhammaṃ deseti, parinibbuto so bhagavā parinibbānāya dhammaṃ desetī’’ti.
mula_english:
361. "That saying, good Gotama, is just ours and other wanderers, ascetics, and Brahmins' speech. I think it is idle talk (vilāpaṃ vilapitaṃ maññe). But to what extent is a follower of Master Gotama one who acts according to the teaching, who follows the advice, who has gone beyond doubt, is rid of uncertainty, has attained confidence, is not dependent on others in the Teacher's teaching, and abides in it?"

"Here, Aggivessana, my follower sees any form whatsoever that is past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: every form as it really is with right wisdom, thus: 'This is not mine. This I am not. This is not my self.' Any kind of feeling whatsoever… Any kind of perception whatsoever… Any kind of volitional formations whatsoever… Any kind of consciousness whatsoever, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, one sees all consciousness as it really is with correct wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’

Aggivessana, with this much, my disciple has done the work in my dispensation, followed the advice, dispelling doubts has become confident not relying on a teacher abide.

"But to what extent, good Gotama, is a monk an *arhat*, one with taints destroyed, who has lived the life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained the true goal, destroyed the fetter of becoming, and is released through right knowledge?"

"Here, Aggivessana, a monk, seeing any form whatsoever that is past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near, every form as it really is with right wisdom, is released without clinging; Any kind of feeling whatsoever… Any kind of perception whatsoever… Any kind of volitional formations whatsoever… Any kind of consciousness whatsoever, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, every consciousness as it really is with right wisdom, is released without clinging.

Aggivessana, when this much is done the *bhikkhu* is an *arhat* whose effluents have ended, who has reached fulfillment, finished the task, laid down the burden, attained the true goal, destroyed the fetter of becoming, and is released through right knowledge.

Aggivessana, the mind of the *bhīkkhu* so released is endowed with three nobilities: the nobility of vision, the nobility of practice, and the nobility of release.

Aggivessana, the *bhikkhu* so released honors, reveres, esteems, and worships the Thus Gone One (Tathāgata): 'The Blessed One is enlightened, preaches the *Dharma* for enlightenment; the Blessed One is tamed, preaches the *Dharma* for taming; the Blessed One is calmed, preaches the *Dharma* for calming; the Blessed One has crossed over, preaches the *Dharma* for crossing over; the Blessed One is extinguished, preaches the *Dharma* for extinguishing.'"
commentary_pali:
361.Tiṭṭhatesā, bho gotamāti, bho gotama, esā amhākañceva aññesañca puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ vācā tiṭṭhatu. Vilāpaṃ vilapitaṃ maññeti etañhi vacanaṃ vilapitaṃ viya hoti, vippalapitamattaṃ hotīti attho. Atha vā tiṭṭhatesāti ettha kathāti āharitvā vattabbā. Vācāvilāpaṃ vilapitaṃ maññeti ettha panidaṃ vācānicchāraṇaṃ vilapitamattaṃ maññe hotīti attho.

Idāni pañhaṃ pucchanto kittāvatātiādimāha. Tattha vesārajjapattoti ñāṇapatto. Aparappaccayoti aparappattiyo. Athassa bhagavā pañhaṃ vissajjento idha, aggivessanātiādimāha, taṃ uttānatthameva. Yasmā panettha passatīti vuttattā sekkhabhūmi dassitā. Tasmā uttari asekkhabhūmiṃ pucchanto dutiyaṃ pañhaṃ pucchi, tampissa bhagavā byākāsi . Tattha dassanānuttariyenātiādīsu dassanānuttariyanti lokiyalokuttarā paññā. Paṭipadānuttariyanti lokiyalokuttarā paṭipadā. Vimuttānuttariyanti lokiyalokuttarā vimutti. Suddhalokuttarameva vā gahetvā dassanānuttariyanti arahattamaggasammādiṭṭhi. Paṭipadānuttariyanti sesāni maggaṅgāni. Vimuttānuttariyanti aggaphalavimutti. Khīṇāsavassa vā nibbānadassanaṃ dassanānuttariyaṃ nāma. Maggaṅgāni paṭipadānuttariyaṃ. Aggaphalaṃ vimuttānuttariyanti veditabbaṃ. Buddho so bhagavāti so bhagavā sayampi cattāri saccāni buddho. Bodhāyāti paresampi catusaccabodhāya dhammaṃ deseti. Dantotiādīsu dantoti nibbisevano. Damathāyāti nibbisevanatthāya. Santoti sabbakilesavūpasamena santo. Samathāyāti kilesavūpasamāya. Tiṇṇoti caturoghatiṇṇo. Taraṇāyāti caturoghataraṇāya. Parinibbutoti kilesaparinibbānena parinibbuto. Parinibbānāyāti kilesaparinibbānatthāya.

kittāvatā vesārajjapatto Aparappaccayo idha, aggivessanā dassanānuttariyenā dassanānuttariya Paṭipadānuttariya Vimuttānuttariya dassanānuttariya Paṭipadānuttariya Vimuttānuttariya dassanānuttariyaṃ paṭipadānuttariyaṃ vimuttānuttariya Buddho so bhagavā Bodhāyā Danto danto Damathāyā Santo Samathāyā Tiṇṇo Taraṇāyā Parinibbuto Parinibbānāyā
commentary_english:
361. "Let it stand, venerable Gotama (*tiṭṭhatesā, bho gotamā*)," venerable Gotama, let this speech of ours, and that of other various *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s, stand.

"I consider it wailing and lamenting (*vilāpaṃ vilapitaṃ maññe*)," because that statement is like wailing and lamenting; the meaning is that it is merely disconnected babble (*vippalapitamattaṃ hotīti attho*).

Or else, "Let it stand (*tiṭṭhatesā*)," here a talk should be brought forward and spoken.

"I consider speech wailing and lamenting (*vācāvilāpaṃ vilapitaṃ maññe*)," here, however, the meaning is, I consider this involuntary utterance of speech to be merely wailing and lamenting.

Now, asking a question, he said, "How much (*kittāvatā*)," etc.

There, "having attained confidence (*vesārajjapatto*)," means having attained knowledge (*ñāṇapatto*).

"Not dependent on another (*aparappaccayo*)," means not dependent on others (*aparappattiyo*).

Then, the Lord, answering the question, said, "Here, Aggivessana (*idha, aggivessanā*)," etc., that meaning is plain.

Because here it was said, "he sees (*passatīti*)," the state of the trainee (*śaikṣa-bhūmi*) is shown.

Therefore, asking about the further state of the non-trainee (*aśaikṣa-bhūmi*), he asked a second question. To him, the Lord explained,

There, "by unsurpassed vision (*dassanānuttariyenā*)," etc., "unsurpassed vision (*dassanānuttariya*)" is mundane and supramundane wisdom (*lokiyalokuttarā prajñā*).

"Unsurpassed practice (*pratipadānuttariya*)", is mundane and supramundane practice (*lokiyalokuttarā pratipadā*).

"Unsurpassed liberation (*vimuktānuttariya*)," is mundane and supramundane liberation (*lokiyalokuttarā vimukti*).

Or else, having taken only the purely supramundane, "unsurpassed vision (*dassanānuttariya*)" is the right view of the path of *arhat*-ship (*arahattamagga-sammādiṭṭhi*).

"Unsurpassed practice (*pratipadānuttariya*)," are the remaining factors of the path (*śeṣāṇi mārgāṅgāni*).

"Unsurpassed liberation (*vimuktānuttariya*)," is the liberation that is the fruit of the highest (*aggaphalavimutti*).

Or, for one whose *āsrava*s are destroyed, the vision of *nirvāṇa* is called "unsurpassed vision (*dassanānuttariyaṃ*)."

The factors of the path (*mārgāṅgāni*) are "unsurpassed practice (*pratipadānuttariyaṃ*)."

The highest fruit (*aggaphalaṃ*) is to be understood as "unsurpassed liberation (*vimuktānuttariyaṃ*)."

"The Buddha, that Lord (*buddho so bhagavā*)," that Lord himself is awakened to the four noble truths (*cattāri satyāni buddho*).

"For awakening (*bodhāyā*)," he teaches the *dharma* for the awakening of others to the four noble truths (*catusaccabodhāya dharmaṃ deśeti*).

Among "tamed (*danto*)", etc., "tamed (*danto*)" means without indulgence (*nibbisevano*).

"For taming (*damathāyā*)," means for the sake of non-indulgence (*nibbisevanatthāya*).

"Tranquil (*śānto*)," means tranquil by the appeasement of all defilements (*sabbakilesavūpasamena śānto*).

"For tranquility (*śamathāyā*)," means for the appeasement of defilements (*kilesavūpasamāya*).

"Crossed over (*tīrṇo*)," means crossed over the four floods (*caturoghatīrṇo*).

"For crossing over (*taraṇāyā*)," means for crossing over the four floods (*caturoghataraṇāya*).

"Completely extinguished (*parinirvṛto*)," means completely extinguished by the *nirvāṇa* of defilements (*kilesaparinirvāṇena parinirvṛto*).

"For complete extinction (*parinirvāṇāyā*)," means for the sake of the *nirvāṇa* of defilements (*kilesaparinirvāṇatthāya*).

How much; having attained confidence; not dependent on another; here, Aggivessana

Unsurpassed vision; unsurpassed vision; unsurpassed practice; unsurpassed liberation; unsurpassed vision; unsurpassed practice; unsurpassed liberation; unsurpassed vision

unsurpassed practice; unsurpassed liberation; the Buddha, that Lord; for awakening; tamed; tamed; for taming; tranquil; for tranquility; crossed over; for crossing over; completely extinguished; for complete extinction

mula_pali: 362. Evaṃ vutte, saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mayameva, bho gotama, dhaṃsī, mayaṃ pagabbā, ye mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ vādena vādaṃ āsādetabbaṃ amaññimha. Siyā hi, bho gotama, hatthiṃ pabhinnaṃ āsajja purisassa sotthibhāvo, na tveva bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ āsajja siyā purisassa sotthibhāvo. Siyā hi, bho gotama, pajjalitaṃ jalantaṃ (sī. pī.) aggikkhandhaṃ āsajja purisassa sotthibhāvo , na tveva bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ āsajja siyā purisassa sotthibhāvo. Siyā hi, bho gotama, āsīvisaṃ ghoravisaṃ āsajja purisassa sotthibhāvo, na tveva bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ āsajja siyā purisassa sotthibhāvo. Mayameva, bho gotama, dhaṃsī, mayaṃ pagabbā, ye mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ vādena vādaṃ āsādetabbaṃ amaññimha. Adhivāsetu adhivāsetu ca (pī. ka.) me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.
mula_english:
Thus having been said, Saccaka, the son of the Nigaṇṭha, said this to the Blessed One:

“Indeed, good Gotama, we were bold and daring, and we thought to insult the honorable Gotama with a dispute.

There might be safety for a man insulting a furious elephant, but there is no safety for one insulting the honorable Gotama.

There might be safety for a man disturbing a burning flame, but there is no safety for one insulting the honorable Gotama.

There might be safety for a man insulting a venomous snake, but there is no safety for one insulting the honorable Gotama.

Indeed, good Gotama, we were bold and daring, and we thought to insult the honorable Gotama with a dispute.

May the honorable Gotama consent to accept a meal from me tomorrow, together with the *bhikkhu-saṃgha* (community of monks).”

The Blessed One consented by remaining silent (*tuṇhībhāvena*).
commentary_pali: 362.Dhaṃsīti guṇadhaṃsakā. Pagabbāti vācāpāgabbiyena samannāgatā. Āsādetabbanti ghaṭṭetabbaṃ. Āsajjāti ghaṭṭetvā. Natveva bhavantaṃ gotamanti bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ āsajja kassaci attano vādaṃ anupahataṃ sakalaṃ ādāya pakkamituṃ thāmo natthīti dasseti. Na hi bhagavā hatthiādayo viya kassaci jīvitantarāyaṃ karoti. Ayaṃ pana nigaṇṭho imā tisso upamā na bhagavato ukkaṃsanatthaṃ āhari, attukkaṃsanatthameva āhari. Yathā hi rājā kañci paccatthikaṃ ghātetvā evaṃ nāma sūro evaṃ thāmasampanno puriso bhavissatīti paccatthikaṃ thomentopi attānameva thometi. Evameva sopi siyā hi, bho gotama, hatthiṃ pabhinnantiādīhi bhagavantaṃ ukkaṃsentopi mayameva sūrā mayaṃ paṇḍitā mayaṃ bahussutāyeva evaṃ pabhinnahatthiṃ viya, jalitaaggikkhandhaṃ viya, phaṇakataāsīvisaṃ viya ca vādatthikā sammāsambuddhaṃ upasaṅkamimhāti attānaṃyeva ukkaṃseti. Evaṃ attānaṃ ukkaṃsetvā bhagavantaṃ nimantayamāno adhivāsetu metiādimāha. Tattha adhivāsetūti sampaṭicchatu. Svātanāyāti yaṃ me tumhesu kāraṃ karoto sve bhavissati puññañca pītipāmojjañca, tadatthāya. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvenāti bhagavā kāyaṅgaṃ vā vācaṅgaṃ vā acopetvā abbhantareyeva khantiṃ dhārento tuṇhībhāvena adhivāsesi. Saccakassa anuggahakaraṇatthaṃ manasāva sampaṭicchīti vuttaṃ hoti.
commentary_english:
362. *dhaṃsī* means those who destroy qualities.
*pagabbā* means endowed with impudence of speech.
*āsādetabba* means should be struck.
*āsajjā* means having struck.
"*natveva bhavantaṃ gotama*" means having approached you, Gotama, no one has the strength to leave taking away his own doctrine unimpaired and complete; this he shows.
The Blessed One does not cause an obstruction to the life of anyone, like elephants and so on.
However, this Nigaṇṭha brought these three similes not for the purpose of praising the Blessed One, but he brought [them] only for the purpose of praising himself.
Just as a king, having killed some enemy, even while praising the enemy [saying] "Thus, indeed, will the hero, thus the person endowed with strength, be," he praises only himself.
Even so, that person, even while praising the Blessed One with "*siyā hi, bho gotama, hatthiṃ pabhinna*," etc., [saying] "We alone are heroes, we are wise, we are very learned," thus, just like an elephant in rut, like a blazing mass of fire, like a venomous snake with raised hood, we, being debaters, approached the Sammāsambuddha, he praises only himself.
Having praised himself in this way, inviting the Blessed One, he said "*adhivāsetu me,*" etc.
There, *adhivāsetū* means may [he] accept.
"*svātanāyā*" means for the sake of the merit and joy and delight that will be mine tomorrow as I do service to you.
"*adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvenā*" means the Blessed One, without stirring either [his] bodily limb or [his] vocal limb, but maintaining forbearance within, accepted with silence.
It is said [that the Blessed One] accepted it in [his] mind alone for the sake of doing a favor to Saccaka.

mula_pali:
363. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā te licchavī āmantesi – ‘‘suṇantu me bhonto licchavī, samaṇo me gotamo nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Tena me abhihareyyātha yamassa patirūpaṃ maññeyyāthā’’ti. Atha kho te licchavī tassā rattiyā accayena saccakassa nigaṇṭhaputtassa pañcamattāni thālipākasatāni bhattābhihāraṃ abhihariṃsu. Atha kho nigaṇṭhaputto sake ārāme paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – ‘‘kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena saccakassa nigaṇṭhaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yamidaṃ, bho gotama, dāne puññañca puññamahī ca taṃ dāyakānaṃ sukhāya hotū’’ti. ‘‘Yaṃ kho, aggivessana, tādisaṃ dakkhiṇeyyaṃ āgamma avītarāgaṃ avītadosaṃ avītamohaṃ, taṃ dāyakānaṃ bhavissati. Yaṃ kho, aggivessana, mādisaṃ dakkhiṇeyyaṃ āgamma vītarāgaṃ vītadosaṃ vītamohaṃ, taṃ tuyhaṃ bhavissatī’’ti.

Cūḷasaccakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then Saccaka the son of Nigaṇṭha, knowing that the Blessed One had accepted, addressed the Licchavis: "Good Licchavis, listen! The *śramaṇa* Gotama has been invited by me for tomorrow's meal, together with the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* (community of monks). Therefore, you should bring to me whatever you deem suitable for him."

Then those Licchavis, at the end of that night, brought five hundred bowls filled with cooked rice as an offering of food to Saccaka the son of Nigaṇṭha.

Then Nigaṇṭha's son, having had prepared fine foods and edibles in his own monastery, announced the time to the Blessed One: "It is time, good Gotama, the meal is ready."

Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning time, taking his bowl and robe, went to the monastery of Saccaka the son of Nigaṇṭha; having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the *bhikkhu-saṅgha*.

Then Saccaka the son of Nigaṇṭha, with his own hands, served and satisfied the *bhikkhu-saṅgha*, with the Buddha at its head, with excellent foods and edibles.

Then Saccaka the son of Nigaṇṭha, seeing that the Blessed One had finished eating and had removed his hand from his bowl, took a low seat and sat down to one side.

Having sat down to one side, Saccaka the son of Nigaṇṭha said this to the Blessed One: "May this merit and ground of merit from this giving be for the happiness of the givers, good Gotama."

"[Whatever merit accrues from] offerings made to such a worthy recipient, Aggivessana, who is not free from greed (*rāga*), hatred (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*), will be for the benefit of the givers. [However, whatever merit accrues from] offerings made to such a worthy recipient like me, Aggivessana, who is free from greed, hatred, and delusion, that will be for your benefit."

The Cūḷasaccaka Sutta, the fifth [sutta], is finished.
commentary_pali:
363.Yamassa patirūpaṃ maññeyyāthāti te kira licchavī tassa pañcathālipākasatāni niccabhattaṃ āharanti . Tadeva sandhāya esa sve tumhe yaṃ assa samaṇassa gotamassa patirūpaṃ kappiyanti maññeyyātha, taṃ āhareyyātha; samaṇassa hi gotamassa tumhe paricārakā kappiyākappiyaṃ yuttāyuttaṃ jānāthāti vadati. Bhattābhihāraṃ abhihariṃsūti abhiharitabbaṃ bhattaṃ abhihariṃsu. Paṇītenāti uttamena. Sahatthāti sahatthena. Santappetvāti suṭṭhu tappetvā, paripuṇṇaṃ suhitaṃ yāvadatthaṃ katvā. Sampavāretvāti suṭṭhu pavāretvā, alaṃ alanti hatthasaññāya paṭikkhipāpetvā. Bhuttāvinti bhuttavantaṃ. Onītapattapāṇinti pattato onītapāṇiṃ, apanītahatthanti vuttaṃ hoti. ‘‘Onittapattapāṇi’’ntipi pāṭho, tassattho, onittaṃ nānābhūtaṃ pattaṃ pāṇito assāti onittapattapāṇī. Taṃ onittapattapāṇiṃ, hatthe ca pattañca dhovitvā ekamante pattaṃ nikkhipitvā nisinnanti attho. Ekamantaṃ nisīdīti bhagavantaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ ñatvā ekasmiṃ okāse nisīdīti attho. Puññañcāti yaṃ imasmiṃ dāne puññaṃ, āyatiṃ vipākakkhandhāti attho. Puññamahīti vipākakkhandhānaṃyeva parivāro. Taṃ dāyakānaṃ sukhāya hotūti taṃ imesaṃ licchavīnaṃ sukhatthāya hotu. Idaṃ kira so ahaṃ pabbajito nāma, pabbajitena ca na yuttaṃ attano dānaṃ niyyātetunti tesaṃ niyyātento evamāha. Atha bhagavā yasmā licchavīhi saccakassa dinnaṃ, na bhagavato. Saccakena pana bhagavato dinnaṃ, tasmā tamatthaṃ dīpento yaṃ kho, aggivessanātiādimāha. Iti bhagavā nigaṇṭhassa matena vināyeva attano dinnaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ nigaṇṭhassa niyyātesi, sā cassa anāgate vāsanā bhavissatīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷasaccakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
363. "yamassa patirūpaṃ maññeyyāthā"ti: So it is said that those Licchavīs regularly brought five hundred dishes of rice cooked in milk for him. tadeva sandhāya esa sve tumhe yaṃ assa samaṇassa gotamassa patirūpaṃ kappiyanti maññeyyātha, taṃ āhareyyātha; samaṇassa hi gotamassa tumhe paricārakā kappiyākappiyaṃ yuttāyuttaṃ jānāthāti vadati. "bhattābhihāraṃ abhihariṃsū"ti: They brought food that should be brought. "paṇītenā"ti: With excellent food. "sahatthā"ti: By their own hand. "santappetvā"ti: Having thoroughly satisfied [them], having made them full, happy, and according to their desire. "sampavāretvā"ti: Having thoroughly invited [them], having caused them to refuse with a gesture of the hand, saying, "Enough! Enough!". "bhuttāvi"nti: To one who has eaten. "onītapattapāṇi"nti: From whose bowl the hand has been removed, it is said that the hand has been withdrawn. “onittapattapāṇi”ntipi pāṭho, tassattho, onittaṃ nānābhūtaṃ pattaṃ pāṇito assāti onittapattapāṇī. taṃ onittapattapāṇiṃ, hatthe ca pattañca dhovitvā ekamante pattaṃ nikkhipitvā nisinnanti attho. "ekamantaṃ nisīdī"ti: Having known the Blessed One to be of such a kind, he sat down in a suitable place. "puññañcā"ti: The merit in this giving, in the future, is a mass of ripening results. "puññamahī"ti: It is simply a retinue of masses of ripening results. "taṃ dāyakānaṃ sukhāya hotū"ti: May that be for the happiness of the donors, may that be for the welfare of these Licchavīs. idaṃ kira so ahaṃ pabbajito nāma, pabbajitena ca na yuttaṃ attano dānaṃ niyyātetunti tesaṃ niyyātento evamāha. atha bhagavā yasmā licchavīhi saccakassa dinnaṃ, na bhagavato. saccakena pana bhagavato dinnaṃ, tasmā tamatthaṃ dīpento "yaṃ kho, aggivessanā"tiādimāha. iti bhagavā nigaṇṭhassa matena vināyeva attano dinnaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ nigaṇṭhassa niyyātesi, sā cassa anāgate vāsanā bhavissatīti.

papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

cūḷasaccakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

mula_pali: 364. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ sunivattho hoti pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pavisitukāmo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya… pavisitukāmo hoti (sī.). Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando saccakaṃ nigaṇṭhaputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ayaṃ, bhante, saccako nigaṇṭhaputto āgacchati bhassappavādako paṇḍitavādo sādhusammato bahujanassa. Eso kho, bhante, avaṇṇakāmo buddhassa, avaṇṇakāmo dhammassa, avaṇṇakāmo saṅghassa. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā muhuttaṃ nisīdatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Vesālī in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.

Now on that occasion, when it was morning, the Blessed One had finished dressing and had taken his bowl and outer robe, desiring to go into Vesālī for alms.

Then, as Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son was walking and wandering for exercise, he came to the Hall with the Peaked Roof in the Great Wood.

The venerable Ānanda saw Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son coming in the distance.

Seeing the Blessed One, he said this: “Venerable sir, this is Saccaka, the son of the Nigaṇṭha, who is coming, a fluent speaker, a sophist, considered by many to be a good man.

He wants to discredit the Buddha, discredit the *dharma* (Dhamma), and discredit the *sangha* (Saṅgha).

It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would sit down for a moment out of compassion."

The Blessed One sat down on the seat that was prepared for him.

Then Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son went up to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

Having sat down to one side, Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son said this to the Blessed One:
commentary_pali:
364.Evaṃme sutanti mahāsaccakasuttaṃ. Tattha ekaṃ samayanti ca tena kho pana samayenāti ca pubbaṇhasamayanti ca tīhi padehi ekova samayo vutto. Bhikkhūnañhi vattapaṭipattiṃ katvā mukhaṃ dhovitvā pattacīvaramādāya cetiyaṃ vanditvā kataraṃ gāmaṃ pavisissāmāti vitakkamāḷake ṭhitakālo nāma hoti. Bhagavā evarūpe samaye rattadupaṭṭaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ ekaṃsaṃ pārupitvā gandhakuṭito nikkhamma bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto gandhakuṭipamukhe aṭṭhāsi. Taṃ sandhāya, – ‘‘ekaṃ samayanti ca tena kho pana samayenāti ca pubbaṇhasamaya’’nti ca vuttaṃ. Pavisitukāmoti piṇḍāya pavisissāmīti evaṃ katasanniṭṭhāno. Tenupasaṅkamīti kasmā upasaṅkamīti? Vādāropanajjhāsayena. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘pubbepāhaṃ apaṇḍitatāya sakalaṃ vesāliparisaṃ gahetvā samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ gantvā parisamajjhe maṅku jāto. Idāni tathā akatvā ekakova gantvā vādaṃ āropessāmi. Yadi samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ parājetuṃ sakkhissāmi, attano laddhiṃ dīpetvā jayaṃ karissāmi. Yadi samaṇassa gotamassa jayo bhavissati, andhakāre naccaṃ viya na koci jānissatī’’ti niddāpañhaṃ nāma gahetvā iminā vādajjhāsayena upasaṅkami.

Anukampaṃ upādāyāti saccakassa nigaṇṭhaputtassa anukampaṃ paṭicca. Therassa kirassa evaṃ ahosi – ‘‘bhagavati muhuttaṃ nisinne buddhadassanaṃ dhammassavanañca labhissati. Tadassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya saṃvattissatī’’ti. Tasmā bhagavantaṃ yācitvā paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ catugguṇaṃ paññapetvā nisīdatu bhagavāti āha. ‘‘Kāraṇaṃ ānando vadatī’’ti sallakkhetvā nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Bhagavantaṃ etadavocāti yaṃ pana pañhaṃ ovaṭṭikasāraṃ katvā ādāya āgato taṃ ṭhapetvā passena tāva pariharanto etaṃ santi, bho gotamātiādivacanaṃ avoca.

Anukampaṃ upādāyā nisīdatu bhagavā Bhagavantaṃ etadavocā santi, bho gotamā
commentary_english:
364. Thus I have heard: the Mahāsaccakasuttaṃ.

Therein, the word " *ekaṃ samaya* " (one time), " *tena kho pana samayena* " (at that time), and " *pubbaṇhasamaya* " (morning time) refer to the same time in three phrases.

For monks, after performing the customary observances, washing their face, taking their robes and bowl, worshiping the stupa, thinking “Which village shall I enter for alms?” is known as the time of standing in the windbreak of thoughts.

The Blessed One, at such a time, having dressed in a red upper robe, tied his waistband, put on a robe made of rags from a dust heap, went out from the scented chamber surrounded by a community of monks, and stood in front of the scented chamber.

In reference to that, it was said, " *ekaṃ samayaṃ* " (one time), " *tena kho pana samayena* " (at that time), and " *pubbaṇhasamaya* " (morning time).

"*pavisitukāmo* " (desiring to enter) means resolving to enter for alms.

"*tenupasaṅkamī* " (then he approached): Why did he approach? With the intention of raising a debate.

Thus it occurred to him: "Formerly, due to my lack of wisdom, I took the entire Vesālī assembly, went to the presence of the ascetic Gotama, and became embarrassed in the midst of the assembly.

Now, without doing so, I will go alone and raise a debate.

If I am able to defeat the ascetic Gotama, I will make known my doctrine and achieve victory.

If the ascetic Gotama's victory will be, no one will know, like a dance in the dark," having taken a riddle question, he approached with this intention of debating.

"*anukampaṃ upādāyā* " (having taken compassion) means with compassion towards Saccaka, the son of Nigaṇṭha.

Thus it occurred to the Elder: "While the Blessed One is sitting for a moment, he will obtain the sight of the Buddha and the hearing of the Dhamma.

That will lead to their welfare and happiness for a long time."

Therefore, having requested the Blessed One, having spread out the rag-robe fourfold, he said, "*nisīdatu bhagavā* " (may the Blessed One sit down).

"'Ānanda speaks with a reason,' thinking thus, the Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat.

"*bhagavantaṃ etadavocā* " (he said this to the Blessed One) means setting aside the question that he had come to ask, turning the subject aside, he spoke these words, "*santi, bho Gotamā* " (are there, good Gotamas?).

*anukampaṃ upādāyā* (having taken compassion), *nisīdatu bhagavā* (may the Blessed One sit down), *bhagavantaṃ etadavocā* (he said this to the Blessed One), *santi, bho Gotamā* (are there, good Gotamas?).

mula_pali: 365. ‘‘Santi, bho gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kāyabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti, no cittabhāvanaṃ. Phusanti hi te, bho gotama, sārīrikaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bho gotama, sārīrikāya dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭhassa sato ūrukkhambhopi nāma bhavissati, hadayampi nāma phalissati, uṇhampi lohitaṃ mukhato uggamissati, ummādampi pāpuṇissati pāpuṇissanti (syā. kaṃ.) cittakkhepaṃ. Tassa kho etaṃ, bho gotama, kāyanvayaṃ cittaṃ hoti, kāyassa vasena vattati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Abhāvitattā cittassa. Santi pana, bho gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā cittabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti, no kāyabhāvanaṃ. Phusanti hi te, bho gotama, cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bho gotama, cetasikāya dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭhassa sato ūrukkhambhopi nāma bhavissati, hadayampi nāma phalissati, uṇhampi lohitaṃ mukhato uggamissati, ummādampi pāpuṇissati cittakkhepaṃ. Tassa kho eso, bho gotama, cittanvayo kāyo hoti, cittassa vasena vattati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Abhāvitattā kāyassa . Tassa mayhaṃ, bho gotama, evaṃ hoti – ‘addhā bhoto gotamassa sāvakā cittabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti, no kāyabhāvana’’’nti.
mula_english: 365. “Master Gotama, there are some ascetics and Brahmins who abide pursuing the practice of bodily development (kāyabhāvanā), but not mental development (cittabhāvanā). They are touched by bodily painful feeling (sārīrikaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ). In the past, when one was touched by bodily painful feeling, one’s thighs would become rigid (ūrukkhambha), one’s heart would burst, hot blood would gush from one’s mouth, and one would go mad (ummāda), go out of one’s mind (cittakkhepaṃ). So then the mind (cittaṃ) was subservient to the body (kāya), the body wielded mastery over it (kāyassa vasena vattati). What is the reason for that? Because the mind has not been developed. But there are some ascetics and Brahmins who abide pursuing development of mind (cittabhāvanā), but not development of body (kāyabhāvanā). They are touched by mental painful feeling (cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ). In the past, when one was touched by mental painful feeling, one’s thighs would become rigid, one’s heart would burst, hot blood would gush from one’s mouth, and one would go mad, go out of one’s mind. So then the body (kāyo) was subservient to the mind (cittaṃ), the mind wielded mastery over it (cittassa vasena vattati). What is the reason for that? Because the body has not been developed. It has occurred to me: ‘Surely Master Gotama’s disciples abide pursuing development of mind (cittabhāvanā), but not development of body (kāyabhāvanā).’”
commentary_pali:
365.Phusanti hi te, bho gotamāti te samaṇabrāhmaṇā sarīre uppannaṃ sārīrikaṃ dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ phusanti labhanti, anubhavantīti attho. Ūrukkhambhoti khambhakataūrubhāvo, ūruthaddhatāti attho. Vimhayatthavasena panettha bhavissatīti anāgatavacanaṃ kataṃ. Kāyanvayaṃ hotīti kāyānugataṃ hoti kāyassa vasavatti. Kāyabhāvanāti pana vipassanā vuccati, tāya cittavikkhepaṃ pāpuṇanto nāma natthi, iti nigaṇṭho asantaṃ abhūtaṃ yaṃ natthi, tadevāha. Cittabhāvanātipi samatho vuccati, samādhiyuttassa ca puggalassa ūrukkhambhādayo nāma natthi, iti nigaṇṭho idaṃ abhūtameva āha. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana vuttaṃ – ‘‘yatheva ‘bhūtapubbanti vatvā ūrukkhambhopi nāma bhavissatī’tiādīni vadato anāgatarūpaṃ na sameti, tathā atthopi na sameti, asantaṃ abhūtaṃ yaṃ natthi, taṃ kathetī’’ti.

No kāyabhāvananti pañcātapatappanādiṃ attakilamathānuyogaṃ sandhāyāha. Ayañhi tesaṃ kāyabhāvanā nāma. Kiṃ pana so disvā evamāha? So kira divādivassa vihāraṃ āgacchati, tasmiṃ kho pana samaye bhikkhū pattacīvaraṃ paṭisāmetvā attano attano rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānesu paṭisallānaṃ upagacchanti. So te paṭisallīne disvā cittabhāvanāmattaṃ ete anuyuñjanti, kāyabhāvanā panetesaṃ natthīti maññamāno evamāha.

No kāyabhāvana
commentary_english:
365. “*Phusanti hi te, bho Gotamā*” means those *śramaṇa* and *brāhmaṇa* experience, obtain, and feel bodily suffering (*śārīrikaṃ duḥkhaṃ vedanaṃ*). This is the meaning.

"*Ūrukkhambho*" means having thighs that are like pillars (*khambhakataūrubhāvo*), having stiff thighs. This is the meaning.

Because of the wonderful meaning, here, "*bhavissati*" is said, it is a statement about the future (*anāgatavacanaṃ kataṃ*).

"*Kāyanvayaṃ hoti*" means being in accordance with the body (*kāyānugataṃ*). It is mastery over the body (*kāyassa vasavatti*).

"*Kāyabhāvanā*" However, it is called *vipaśyanā*. There is no distraction of the mind (*cittavikkhepaṃ*) through that. Thus, the *nigaṇṭha* speaks of what is unreal and untrue, which does not exist.

"*Cittabhāvanā* " is also called *samatha*. For a person endowed with *samādhi*, there are no such things as thigh-pillars and so on. Thus, the *nigaṇṭha* speaks of what is simply unreal.

In the *Aṭṭhakathā*, however, it was said: "Just as by saying '*bhūtapubbanti vatvā ūrukkhambhopi nāma bhavissati*’ etc., the future form does not fit, so also the meaning does not fit. He speaks of what is unreal and untrue, which does not exist."

"*No kāyabhāvana*" means he speaks referring to self-mortification (*attakilamathānuyogaṃ*) such as the fivefold heating of oneself.

This is their practice of the body (*kāyabhāvanā*).

But why did he say this, having seen? He comes to the *vihāra* at the time of day. At that time, the *bhikkhus*, having put away their robes and bowls, go to their respective daytime and nighttime dwellings for seclusion (*paṭisallānaṃ upagacchanti*).

He, having seen them in seclusion, thinks that they are only engaged in mental cultivation (*cittabhāvanāmattaṃ ete anuyuñjanti*), and that there is no practice of the body (*kāyabhāvanā panetesaṃ natthīti*), and so he says this.

"*No kāyabhāvana*"

mula_pali:
366. ‘‘Kinti pana te, aggivessana, kāyabhāvanā sutā’’ti? ‘‘Seyyathidaṃ – nando vaccho, kiso saṃkicco, makkhali gosālo – etehi, bho gotama, acelakā muttācārā hatthāpalekhanā naehibhaddantikā natiṭṭhabhaddantikā naehibhadantikā, natiṭṭhabhadantikā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) na abhihaṭaṃ na uddissakataṃ na nimantanaṃ sādiyanti, te na kumbhimukhā paṭiggaṇhanti na kaḷopimukhā paṭiggaṇhanti na eḷakamantaraṃ na daṇḍamantaraṃ na musalamantaraṃ na dvinnaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ na gabbhiniyā na pāyamānāya na purisantaragatāya na saṅkittīsu na yattha sā upaṭṭhito hoti na yattha makkhikā saṇḍasaṇḍacārinī , na macchaṃ na maṃsaṃ na suraṃ na merayaṃ na thusodakaṃ pivanti. Te ekāgārikā vā honti ekālopikā, dvāgārikā vā honti dvālopikā…pe… sattāgārikā vā honti sattālopikā. Ekissāpi dattiyā yāpenti, dvīhipi dattīhi yāpenti…pe… sattahipi dattīhi yāpenti. Ekāhikampi āhāraṃ āhārenti, dvīhikampi āhāraṃ āhārenti…pe… sattāhikampi āhāraṃ āhārenti. Iti evarūpaṃ addhamāsikampi pariyāyabhattabhojanānuyogamanuyuttā viharantī’’ti.

‘‘Kiṃ pana te, aggivessana, tāvatakeneva yāpentī’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Appekadā, bho gotama, uḷārāni uḷārāni khādanīyāni khādanti, uḷārāni uḷārāni bhojanāni bhuñjanti, uḷārāni uḷārāni sāyanīyāni sāyanti, uḷārāni uḷārāni pānāni pivanti. Te imaṃ kāyaṃ balaṃ gāhenti nāma, brūhenti nāma, medenti nāmā’’ti.

‘‘Yaṃ kho te, aggivessana, purimaṃ pahāya pacchā upacinanti, evaṃ imassa kāyassa ācayāpacayo hoti. Kinti pana te, aggivessana, cittabhāvanā sutā’’ti? Cittabhāvanāya kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavatā puṭṭho samāno na sampāyāsi.
mula_english:
366. "Well then, Aggivessana, what sort of physical practices (*kāyabhāvanā*) are known to you?"

"For example, there are Nanda Vaccha, Kisa Sankicca, Makkhali Gosāla. These naked ascetics, rejecting conventions, licking their hands, not coming when asked, not stopping when asked, do not accept food brought or food specially made or an invitation to a meal; they receive nothing from a pot, from a bowl, across a threshold, across a stick, across a pestle, from two eating together, from a pregnant woman, from a woman giving suck, from a woman living with a man, from where food is advertised to be distributed, from where a dog is waiting, from where flies are buzzing; they eat no fish or meat and drink no rum or spirits or fermented rice-gruel. They keep to one house, to one morsel; they keep to two houses, to two morsels…they keep to seven houses, to seven morsels. They live on one saucerful a day, on two saucerfuls a day…on seven saucerfuls a day. They take food once a day, once every two days…once every seven days. Thus even up to once every fortnight, they dwell pursuing the practice of taking food at stated intervals."

"Well then, Aggivessana, do they live only on that much?"

"No, Gotama. Sometimes, Gotama, they consume excellent hard food, eat excellent soft food, taste excellent delicacies, drink excellent drinks. Thereby they again regain their strength (*balaṃ*), fortify themselves, and become fat."

"What they earlier abandoned, Aggivessana, they later gather together again. That is how there is increase (*ācaya*) and decrease (*apacaya*) of this body (*kāyassa*). Well then, Aggivessana, what sort of mental development (*cittabhāvanā*) is known to you?"

When Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son was asked by the Blessed One about development of mind, he was unable to answer.
commentary_pali: 366. Atha naṃ bhagavā anuyuñjanto kinti pana te, aggivessana, kāyabhāvanā sutāti āha. So taṃ vitthārento seyyathidaṃ, nando vacchotiādimāha. Tattha nandoti tassa nāmaṃ. Vacchoti gottaṃ. Kisoti nāmaṃ. Saṃkiccoti gottaṃ. Makkhaligosālo heṭṭhā āgatova. Eteti ete tayo janā, te kira kiliṭṭhatapānaṃ matthakapattā ahesuṃ. Uḷārāni uḷārānīti paṇītāni paṇītāni. Gāhenti nāmāti balaṃ gaṇhāpenti nāma. Brūhentīti vaḍḍhenti. Medentīti jātamedaṃ karonti. Purimaṃ pahāyāti purimaṃ dukkarakāraṃ pahāya. Pacchā upacinantīti pacchā uḷārakhādanīyādīhi santappenti, vaḍḍhenti. Ācayāpacayo hotīti vaḍḍhi ca avaḍḍhi ca hoti, iti imassa kāyassa kālena vaḍḍhi, kālena parihānīti vaḍḍhiparihānimattameva paññāyati, kāyabhāvanā pana na paññāyatīti dīpetvā cittabhāvanaṃ pucchanto, ‘‘kinti pana te, aggivessana, cittabhāvanā sutā’’ti āha. Na sampāyāsīti sampādetvā kathetuṃ nāsakkhi, yathā taṃ bālaputhujjano.
commentary_english:
Then, the Blessed One, questioning him, said, “So what body cultivation (kāyabhāvanā), Aggivessana, have you heard?”

He, elaborating on that, said, “That is to say, Nanda, Vaccha,” and so on.

There, *Nanda* means his name.

*Vaccha* means his lineage (gottaṃ).

*Kisa* means his name.

*Saṃkicca* means his lineage.

Makkhali Gosāla came down below.

*Ete* means these three people, they, it is said, were at the height of corrupted asceticism.

*Uḷārāni uḷārānī* means exquisite, exquisite.

*Gāhenti nāmā* means they cause strength (balaṃ) to be acquired, it is said.

*Brūhentī* means they increase.

*Medentī* means they make what has become fat (jātamedaṃ).

*Purimaṃ pahāyā* means having abandoned the former, having abandoned the former practice of austerity (dukkarakāraṃ).

*Pacchā upacinantī* means afterwards they satisfy and increase with exquisite food (uḷārakhādanīya) and so forth.

*Ācayāpacayo hotī* means there is increase (vaḍḍhi) and decrease (avaḍḍhi), thus with time there is increase of this body (kāyassa), and with time, decrease (parihānī), thus only the measure of increase and decrease is evident, but body cultivation (kāyabhāvanā) is not evident. Having shown this, asking about mind cultivation (cittabhāvanaṃ), he said, “So what mind cultivation (cittabhāvanā), Aggivessana, have you heard?”

*Na sampāyāsī* means he was not able to bring it about and tell it, like that childish ordinary person (bālaputhujjano).

mula_pali: 367. Atha kho bhagavā saccakaṃ nigaṇṭhaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yāpi kho te esā, aggivessana, purimā kāyabhāvanā bhāsitā sāpi ariyassa vinaye no dhammikā kāyabhāvanā. Kāyabhāvanampi kāyabhāvanaṃ hi (sī. pī. ka.) kho tvaṃ, aggivessana, na aññāsi, kuto pana tvaṃ cittabhāvanaṃ jānissasi ? Api ca, aggivessana, yathā abhāvitakāyo ca hoti abhāvitacitto ca, bhāvitakāyo ca hoti bhāvitacitto ca. Taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
Then, the Blessed One said this to Saccaka, the son of Nigaṇṭha: "Aggivessana, that former development of the body (kāyabhāvanā) you spoke of, that is not a righteous development of the body (kāyabhāvanā) in the Discipline of the Noble Ones.

Furthermore, Aggivessana, since you do not understand the development of the body (kāyabhāvanā), how will you understand the development of the mind (cittabhāvanā)? Moreover, Aggivessana, it is like this: one is undeveloped in body (abhāvitakāyo) and undeveloped in mind (abhāvitacitto), or one is developed in body (bhāvitakāyo) and developed in mind (bhāvitacitto).

Listen and pay close attention, I shall speak."

"Yes, sir (bho)," replied Saccaka, the son of Nigaṇṭha, to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:
commentary_pali: 367.Kutopana tvanti yo tvaṃ evaṃ oḷārikaṃ dubbalaṃ kāyabhāvanaṃ na jānāsi? So tvaṃ kuto saṇhaṃ sukhumaṃ cittabhāvanaṃ jānissasīti. Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne codanālayatthero, ‘‘abuddhavacanaṃ nāmetaṃ pada’’nti bījaniṃ ṭhapetvā pakkamituṃ ārabhi. Atha naṃ mahāsīvatthero āha – ‘‘dissati, bhikkhave, imassa cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa ācayopi apacayopi ādānampi nikkhepanampī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 2.62). Taṃ sutvā sallakkhesi – ‘‘oḷārikaṃ kāyaṃ pariggaṇhantassa uppannavipassanā oḷārikāti vattuṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti.
commentary_english:
367.
From where? Furthermore, "you" – do you not know such a gross, weak, physical cultivation (kāyabhāvana)? So, from where will you know a subtle, refined mental cultivation (cittabhāvana)?
In this situation, the elder Codanālaya, thinking, "This word is not the Buddha's teaching (abuddhavacana)," placed the fan (bījaniṃ) and began to leave.
Then the elder Mahāsīva said to him, "Monks (bhikkhave), growth (ācaya), decline (apacaya), taking up (ādāna), and laying down (nikkhepanam) of this body (kāyassa) composed of the four great elements (cātumahābhūtikassa) are seen (dissati)." (Saṃ.
Ni.
2.
62).
Having heard that, he considered, "It is fitting to say that the insight (vipassanā) that arises in one who grasps the gross body (oḷārikaṃ kāyaṃ) is gross (oḷārikā)."

mula_pali: 368. ‘‘Kathañca , aggivessana, abhāvitakāyo ca hoti abhāvitacitto ca? Idha, aggivessana, assutavato puthujjanassa uppajjati sukhā vedanā. So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno sukhasārāgī ca hoti sukhasārāgitañca āpajjati. Tassa sā sukhā vedanā nirujjhati. Sukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati dukkhā vedanā. So dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati kilamati paridevati urattāḷiṃ kandati sammohaṃ āpajjati. Tassa kho esā, aggivessana, uppannāpi sukhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati abhāvitattā kāyassa, uppannāpi dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati abhāvitattā cittassa. Yassa kassaci, aggivessana, evaṃ ubhatopakkhaṃ uppannāpi sukhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati abhāvitattā kāyassa, uppannāpi dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati abhāvitattā cittassa, evaṃ kho, aggivessana, abhāvitakāyo ca hoti abhāvitacitto ca.
mula_english: 368. How, Aggivessana, is one undeveloped in body and undeveloped in mind? Here, Aggivessana, pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*) arises in an uninstructed ordinary person (*assutavato puthujjanassa*). Touched by that pleasant feeling, he lusts after pleasure (*sukhasārāgī*) and continues to lust after pleasure (*sukhasārāgitañca āpajjati*). That pleasant feeling of his ceases. With the cessation of the pleasant feeling (*sukhāya vedanāya nirodhā*), painful feeling (* dukkhā vedanā*) arises. Touched by that painful feeling, he sorrows, grieves, and laments, he weeps beating his breast and becomes distraught (*sammohaṃ āpajjati*). When that pleasant feeling has arisen in him, Aggivessana, it invades his mind and remains because body is not developed, and when that painful feeling has arisen in him, it invades his mind and remains because mind is not developed. Anyone in whom, Aggivessana, in this double manner, arisen pleasant feeling invades his mind and remains because body is not developed, and arisen painful feeling invades his mind and remains because mind is not developed, is thus undeveloped in body (*abhāvitakāyo*) and undeveloped in mind (*abhāvitacitto*).
commentary_pali: 368.Sukhasārāgīti sukhasārāgena samannāgato. Sukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati dukkhā vedanāti na anantarāva uppajjati, sukhadukkhānañhi anantarapaccayatā paṭṭhāne (paṭṭhā. 1.2.45-46) paṭisiddhā. Yasmā pana sukhe aniruddhe dukkhaṃ nuppajjati, tasmā idha evaṃ vuttaṃ. Pariyādāya tiṭṭhatīti khepetvā gaṇhitvā tiṭṭhati. Ubhatopakkhanti sukhaṃ ekaṃ pakkhaṃ dukkhaṃ ekaṃ pakkhanti evaṃ ubhatopakkhaṃ hutvā.
commentary_english:
368.
*Sukhasārāgī*: endowed with the essence of happiness.
*Sukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati dukkhā vedanā*: "Due to the cessation of pleasant feeling, unpleasant feeling arises"—it does not arise immediately; for the condition of pleasant and unpleasant [feelings] being contiguous is refuted in the *Paṭṭhāna* (Paṭṭhā.
1.
2.
45-46).
Since displeasure (*duḥkhaṃ*) does not arise when pleasure (*sukhe*) is unstopped (*aniruddhe*), therefore it is said thus here.
*Pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī*: having consumed and grasped, he stands.
*Ubhatopakkha*: pleasure is one side (*pakṣaṃ*), displeasure is one side—thus, having become *ubhatopakkha*.

mula_pali: 369. ‘‘Kathañca, aggivessana, bhāvitakāyo ca hoti bhāvitacitto ca? Idha, aggivessana, sutavato ariyasāvakassa uppajjati sukhā vedanā. So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na sukhasārāgī ca hoti, na sukhasārāgitañca āpajjati. Tassa sā sukhā vedanā nirujjhati. Sukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati dukkhā vedanā. So dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati na kilamati na paridevati na urattāḷiṃ kandati na sammohaṃ āpajjati. Tassa kho esā, aggivessana, uppannāpi sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati bhāvitattā kāyassa, uppannāpi dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati bhāvitattā cittassa. Yassa kassaci, aggivessana, evaṃ ubhatopakkhaṃ uppannāpi sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati bhāvitattā kāyassa, uppannāpi dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati bhāvitattā cittassa. Evaṃ kho, aggivessana, bhāvitakāyo ca hoti bhāvitacitto cā’’ti.
mula_english:
‘‘And how, Aggivessana, is one developed in body (bhāvitakāyo) and developed in mind (bhāvitacitto)? Here, Aggivessana, a pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*) arises in an instructed noble disciple (*ariyasāvaka*).

Touched by that pleasant feeling (*sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno*), he does not lust after pleasure (*na sukhasārāgī*) or continue to lust after pleasure (*na sukhasārāgitañca āpajjati*).

That pleasant feeling (*sā sukhā vedanā*) of his ceases (*nirujjhati*).

With the cessation (*nirodhā*) of the pleasant feeling (*sukhāya vedanāya*), painful feeling (* dukkhā vedanā*) arises (*uppajjati*).

Touched by that painful feeling (*dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno*), he does not sorrow (*na socati*), grieve (*na kilamati*), and lament (*na paridevati*), he does not weep beating his breast (*na urattāḷiṃ kandati*) and become distraught (*na sammohaṃ āpajjati*).

When that pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*) has arisen in him, Aggivessana, it does not invade his mind (*cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati*) and remain because body (*kāyassa*) is developed (*bhāvitattā*). And when that painful feeling (* dukkhā vedanā*) has arisen in him, it does not invade his mind (*cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati*) and remain because mind (*cittassa*) is developed (*bhāvitattā*).

Anyone in whom, Aggivessana, in this double manner (*evaṃ ubhatopakkhaṃ*), arisen pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*) does not invade his mind (*cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati*) and remain because body (*kāyassa*) is developed (*bhāvitattā*), and arisen painful feeling (* dukkhā vedanā*) does not invade his mind (*cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati*) and remain because mind (*cittassa*) is developed (*bhāvitattā*).

Thus, Aggivessana, is one developed in body (bhāvitakāyo) and developed in mind (bhāvitacitto).’’
commentary_pali: 369.Uppannāpi sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, bhāvitattā kāyassa. Uppannāpi dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, bhāvitattā cittassāti ettha kāyabhāvanā vipassanā, cittabhāvanā samādhi. Vipassanā ca sukhassa paccanīkā, dukkhassa āsannā. Samādhi dukkhassa paccanīko, sukhassa āsanno. Kathaṃ? Vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā nisinnassa hi addhāne gacchante gacchante tattha tattha aggiuṭṭhānaṃ viya hoti, kacchehi sedā muccanti, matthakato usumavaṭṭiuṭṭhānaṃ viya hotīti cittaṃ haññati vihaññati vipphandati. Evaṃ tāva vipassanā sukhassa paccanīkā, dukkhassa āsannā. Uppanne pana kāyike vā cetasike vā dukkhe taṃ dukkhaṃ vikkhambhetvā samāpattiṃ samāpannassa samāpattikkhaṇe dukkhaṃ dūrāpagataṃ hoti, anappakaṃ sukhaṃ okkamati. Evaṃ samādhi dukkhassa paccanīko, sukhassa āsanno. Yathā vipassanā sukhassa paccanīkā, dukkhassa āsannā, na tathā samādhi. Yathā samādhi dukkhassa paccanīko, sukhassa āsanno, na ca tathā vipassanāti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘uppannāpi sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, bhāvitattā kāyassa. Uppannāpi dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, bhāvitattā cittassā’’ti.
commentary_english:
Even when a pleasant feeling has arisen, it does not invade the mind and remain, because the body is developed. Even when a painful feeling has arisen, it does not invade the mind and remain, because the mind is developed." Here, development of the body ( *kāyabhāvanā*) is insight (*vipassanā*), and development of the mind (*cittabhāvanā*) is concentration (*samādhi*).

Insight is the opposite of pleasure and close to suffering. Concentration is the opposite of suffering and close to pleasure.

How so? For someone sitting having established insight, while going along the path, here and there it is like a fire flares up; sweat pours from the armpits; it is like heat rises from the top of the head. Thus, the mind is struck, injured, and flutters. In this way, insight is the opposite of pleasure and close to suffering.

However, when physical or mental suffering has arisen, that suffering is warded off and one enters into concentration (*samāpatti*). At the moment of entering concentration, suffering is far away, and no small amount of pleasure descends. In this way, concentration is the opposite of suffering and close to pleasure.

Just as insight is the opposite of pleasure and close to suffering, concentration is not like that. Just as concentration is the opposite of suffering and close to pleasure, insight is not like that.

Therefore it was said: "Even when a pleasant feeling has arisen, it does not invade the mind and remain, because the body is developed. Even when a painful feeling has arisen, it does not invade the mind and remain, because the mind is developed."

mula_pali:
370. ‘‘Evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ bhoto gotamassa! Bhavañhi gotamo bhāvitakāyo ca hoti bhāvitacitto cā’’ti . ‘‘Addhā kho te ayaṃ, aggivessana, āsajja upanīya vācā bhāsitā, api ca te ahaṃ byākarissāmi . Yato kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, taṃ vata me uppannā vā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassati, uppannā vā dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ netaṃ khoṭhānaṃ (sī. pī.) vijjatī’’ti.

‘‘Na hi nūna na hanūna (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhoto gotamassa uppajjati tathārūpā sukhā vedanā yathārūpā uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭheyya; na hi nūna bhoto gotamassa uppajjati tathārūpā dukkhā vedanā yathārūpā uppannā dukkhā vedanā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭheyyā’’ti.

na hanūna (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
370. I am thus pleased with Master Gotama! For Master Gotama is thus developed in body and developed in mind.”

“Surely, Aggivessana, your words are offensive and discourteous, but still I will answer you.

Since I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and went forth from the home life into homelessness, it has not been possible for arisen pleasant feeling (**sukha vedanā**) to invade my mind and remain or for arisen painful feeling (**duḥkha vedanā**) to invade my mind and remain.

“Has there never arisen in Master Gotama a feeling so pleasant (**sukha vedanā**) that it could invade his mind and remain? Has there never arisen in Master Gotama a feeling so painful (**duḥkha vedanā**) that it could invade his mind and remain? ”
commentary_pali: 370.Āsajjaupanīyāti guṇe ghaṭṭetvā ceva upanetvā ca. Taṃ vata meti taṃ vata mama cittaṃ.
commentary_english: 370. āsajjaupanīyāti guṇe ghaṭṭetvā ceva upanetvā ca. taṃ vata meti taṃ vata mama cittam.

mula_pali:
371. ‘‘Kiñhi no siyā, aggivessana? Idha me, aggivessana, pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā. Nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, aparena samayena daharova samāno, susukāḷakeso bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato paṭhamena vayasā, akāmakānaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ assumukhānaṃ rudantānaṃ, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajiṃ. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno kiṃkusalagavesī anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ pariyesamāno yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘icchāmahaṃ, āvuso kālāma, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye brahmacariyaṃ caritu’nti. Evaṃ vutte, aggivessana, āḷāro kālāmo maṃ etadavoca – ‘viharatāyasmā, tādiso ayaṃ dhammo yattha viññū puriso nacirasseva sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, nacirasseva khippameva taṃ dhammaṃ pariyāpuṇiṃ. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, tāvatakeneva oṭṭhapahatamattena lapitalāpanamattena ñāṇavādañca vadāmi theravādañca, ‘jānāmi passāmī’ti ca paṭijānāmi, ahañceva aññe ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘na kho āḷāro kālāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ kevalaṃ saddhāmattakena sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedeti, addhā āḷāro kālāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ viharatī’’’ti.

‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, aggivessana, yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘kittāvatā no, āvuso kālāma, imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedesī’ti? Evaṃ vutte, aggivessana, āḷāro kālāmo ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ pavedesi. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi saddhā, mayhaṃpatthi saddhā; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi vīriyaṃ, mayhaṃpatthi vīriyaṃ; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi sati, mayhaṃpatthi sati; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi samādhi, mayhaṃpatthi samādhi; na kho āḷārasseva kālāmassa atthi paññā, mayhaṃpatthi paññā; yaṃnūnāhaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ āḷāro kālāmo sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedeti tassa dhammassa sacchikiriyāya padaheyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, nacirasseva khippameva taṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsiṃ.

‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, aggivessana, yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘ettāvatā no, āvuso kālāma , imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedesī’ti? ‘Ettāvatā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedemī’ti. ‘Ahampi kho, āvuso, ettāvatā imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmī’ti. ‘Lābhā no, āvuso, suladdhaṃ no, āvuso, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ tādisaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ passāma. Iti yāhaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedemi taṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharasi; yaṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharasi tamahaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedemi. Iti yāhaṃ dhammaṃ jānāmi taṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ jānāsi; yaṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ jānāsi tamahaṃ dhammaṃ jānāmi. Iti yādiso ahaṃ tādiso tuvaṃ, yādiso tuvaṃ tādiso ahaṃ. Ehi dāni, āvuso, ubhova santā imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharāmā’ti. Iti kho, aggivessana, āḷāro kālāmo ācariyo me samāno (attano) ( ) natthi (sī. pī.) antevāsiṃ maṃ samānaṃ attanā samasamaṃ ṭhapesi, uḷārāya ca maṃ pūjāya pūjesi. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘nāyaṃ dhammo nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati, yāvadeva ākiñcaññāyatanūpapattiyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, taṃ dhammaṃ analaṅkaritvā tasmā dhammā nibbijja apakkamiṃ.

( ) natthi (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
371. Aggivessana, why should it not be? Here, Aggivessana, before my enlightenment, while I was still only an unenlightened Bodhisatta, I thought: ‘Household life is crowded and dusty; life gone forth is wide open.
It is not easy while living in a home to lead the holy life utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell.
What if I were to shave off my hair & beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?’
Later, Aggivessana, while still young, a black-haired young man endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, though my mother and father wished otherwise and wept with tearful faces, I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and went forth from the home life into homelessness.
So, having gone forth in this way, seeking what is good, searching for the unsurpassed state of perfect peace, I went to Āḷāra Kālāma. Having gone to him, I said to Āḷāra Kālāma: ‘I wish, friend Kālāma, to lead the holy life in this Dharma and discipline.’
When this was said, Aggivessana, Āḷāra Kālāma said to me: ‘The venerable one may stay here. This *dharma* is such that a wise man can soon enter upon and abide in it, realising for himself through direct knowledge his own teacher’s doctrine.’
I soon quickly learned that Dhamma.
As far as mere lip-reciting and rehearsal of his teaching went, I could speak with knowledge and assurance, and I claimed, ‘I know and see’—and there were others who did likewise.“
I considered: ‘It is not through mere faith alone that Āḷāra Kālāma declares: “By realising for myself with direct knowledge, I enter upon and abide in this Dhamma.” Certainly Āḷāra Kālāma abides knowing and seeing this Dhamma.’

Then I went to Āḷāra Kālāma and asked him: ‘In what way, friend Kālāma, do you declare that by realising for yourself with direct knowledge you enter upon and abide in this *dharma*?’ When this was said, Aggivessana, Āḷāra Kālāma declared the base of nothingness.
I considered: ‘Not only Āḷāra Kālāma has faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. I too have faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. Suppose I were to strive for the realisation of that *dharma* which Āḷāra Kālāma declares he enters upon and abides in by realising for himself with direct knowledge.’
I soon quickly entered upon and abided in that *dharma* by realising for myself with direct knowledge.

Then I went to Āḷāra Kālāma and asked him: ‘In what way, friend Kālāma, do you declare that by realising for yourself with direct knowledge you enter upon and abide in this *dharma*?’ —‘It is in this way, friend, that I declare that I enter upon and abide in this Dhamma by realising for myself with direct knowledge.’
‘It is in this way, friend, that I also enter upon and abide in this Dhamma by realising for myself with direct knowledge.’
‘It is a gain for us, friend, it is a great gain for us that we have such a venerable one for our companion in the holy life.
And the *dharma* that you enter upon and abide in by realising for yourself with direct knowledge is the *dharma* that I declare I enter upon and abide in by realising for myself with direct knowledge.
So you know the *dharma* that I know and I know the *dharma* that you know.
As I am, so are you; as you are, so am I.
Come, friend, let us now lead this community together.’
Thus Āḷāra Kālāma, my teacher, placed me, his pupil, on an equal footing with himself and awarded me the highest honour.
But it occurred to me: ‘This *dharma* does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna, but only to reappearance in the base of nothingness.
Not being satisfied with that *dharma*, disappointed with it, I left.
commentary_pali: 371.Kiñhi no siyā, aggivessanāti, aggivessana, kiṃ na bhavissati, bhavissateva, mā evaṃ saññī hohi, uppajjiyeva me sukhāpi dukkhāpi vedanā, uppannāya panassā ahaṃ cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhātuṃ na demi. Idānissa tamatthaṃ pakāsetuṃ upari pasādāvahaṃ dhammadesanaṃ desetukāmo mūlato paṭṭhāya mahābhinikkhamanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha idha me, aggivessana, pubbeva sambodhā…pe… tattheva nisīdiṃ, alamidaṃ padhānāyāti idaṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā pāsarāsisutte vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ pana viseso, tattha bodhipallaṅke nisajjā, idha dukkarakārikā.
commentary_english:
371. ‘Why would it not be (so), Aggivessana?’ Aggivessana, how could it not be? It will certainly be so. Do not be so mindful! Even when pleasure, pain, and feeling arise in me, I do not allow the mind to remain overcome by them.

Now, in order to reveal this meaning, he began the Dharma talk that brings clarity, starting from the very beginning with the great renunciation (mahābhiniṣkramaṇa).

There, “Here, Aggivessana, before my enlightenment…pe… right there I sat down, this is sufficient for striving,” all of this should be understood in the same way as was said in the Pāsarāsi Sutta, below.

Now, this is the distinction: there, sitting on the bodhi-platform; here, the practice of difficult austerities (duṣkarakārikā).

mula_pali:
372. ‘‘So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, kiṃkusalagavesī anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ pariyesamāno yena udako rāmaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā udakaṃ rāmaputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘icchāmahaṃ, āvuso passa ma. ni. 1.278 pāsarāsisutte imasmiṃ dhammavinaye brahmacariyaṃ caritu’nti. Evaṃ vutte, aggivessana, udako rāmaputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘viharatāyasmā, tādiso ayaṃ dhammo yattha viññū puriso nacirasseva sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, nacirasseva khippameva taṃ dhammaṃ pariyāpuṇiṃ. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, tāvatakeneva oṭṭhapahatamattena lapitalāpanamattena ñāṇavādañca vadāmi theravādañca, ‘jānāmi passāmī’ti ca paṭijānāmi, ahañceva aññe ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘na kho rāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ kevalaṃ saddhāmattakena sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedesi. Addhā rāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ vihāsī’ti. Atha khvāhaṃ, aggivessana, yena udako rāmaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā udakaṃ rāmaputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘kittāvatā no, āvuso rāmo, imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedesī’ti? Evaṃ vutte, aggivessana, udako rāmaputto nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ pavedesi. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘na kho rāmasseva ahosi saddhā, mayhaṃpatthi saddhā; na kho rāmasseva ahosi vīriyaṃ, mayhaṃpatthi vīriyaṃ; na kho rāmasseva ahosi sati, mayhaṃpatthi sati; na kho rāmasseva ahosi samādhi, mayhaṃpatthi samādhi; na kho rāmasseva ahosi paññā, mayhaṃpatthi paññā; yaṃnūnāhaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ rāmo sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmīti pavedesi tassa dhammassa sacchikiriyāya padaheyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, nacirasseva khippameva taṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsiṃ.

‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, aggivessana, yena udako rāmaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā udakaṃ rāmaputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘ettāvatā no, āvuso, rāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedesī’ti? ‘Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, rāmo imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedesī’ti. ‘Ahampi kho, āvuso, ettāvatā imaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmī’ti. ‘Lābhā no, āvuso, suladdhaṃ no, āvuso, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ tādisaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ passāma. Iti yaṃ dhammaṃ rāmo sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedesi, taṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharasi; yaṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharasi, taṃ dhammaṃ rāmo sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja pavedesi. Iti yaṃ dhammaṃ rāmo abhiññāsi taṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ jānāsi; yaṃ tvaṃ dhammaṃ jānāsi taṃ dhammaṃ rāmo abhiññāsi. Iti yādiso rāmo ahosi tādiso tuvaṃ; yādiso tuvaṃ tādiso rāmo ahosi. Ehi dāni, āvuso, tuvaṃ imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharā’ti. Iti kho, aggivessana, udako rāmaputto sabrahmacārī me samāno ācariyaṭṭhāne ca maṃ ṭhapesi, uḷārāya ca maṃ pūjāya pūjesi. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘nāyaṃ dhammo nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati, yāvadeva nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpapattiyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, taṃ dhammaṃ analaṅkaritvā tasmā dhammā nibbijja apakkamiṃ.
mula_english:
372.

So, Aggivessana, I, seeking what is skillful, searching for the unsurpassed peaceful state, went to Udaka Rāmaputta; having gone, I said this to Udaka Rāmaputta: ‘I wish, friend, to live the holy life in this Dharma-Vinaya.’

When this was said, Aggivessana, Udaka Rāmaputta said this to me: ‘The venerable one may stay here. This *dharma* is such that a wise man can soon enter upon and abide in it, himself realizing through direct knowledge his own teacher’s doctrine.’

So, Aggivessana, I soon quickly mastered that *dharma*.

So, Aggivessana, to that extent I both speak the doctrine of knowledge and the doctrine of the elders by mere lip-reciting and rehearsal, and I claim, ‘I know and see’—and there were others who did likewise.

It occurred to me: ‘It was not through mere faith alone that Rāma declared: “I enter upon and abide in this *dharma* by realizing it for myself with direct knowledge.” Certainly Rāma abided knowing and seeing this *dharma*.’

Then I went to Udaka Rāmaputta and asked him: ‘Friend, in what way did Rāma declare that he entered upon and abided in this *dharma* by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge?’ When this was said, Aggivessana, Udaka Rāmaputta declared the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

It occurred to me: ‘Not only Rāma had faith; I too have faith. Not only Rāma had energy; I too have energy. Not only Rāma had mindfulness; I too have mindfulness. Not only Rāma had *samādhi*; I too have *samādhi*. Not only Rāma had wisdom (*prajñā*); I too have wisdom (*prajñā*). Suppose I endeavor to realize the *dharma* that Rāma declared he entered upon and abided in by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge.’

So, Aggivessana, I soon quickly entered upon and abided in that *dharma* by realizing it for myself with direct knowledge.

Then I went to Udaka Rāmaputta and asked him: ‘Friend, to what extent did Rāma declare that he entered upon and abided in this *dharma* by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge?’ ‘To this extent, friend, Rāma entered upon and abided in this *dharma* by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge.’

‘I too, friend, enter upon and abide in this *dharma* by realizing it for myself with direct knowledge.’

‘It is a gain for us, friend, it is a great gain for us that we have such a venerable one for our companion in the holy life.

So the *dharma* that Rāma declared he entered upon and abided in by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge is the *dharma* that you enter upon and abide in by realizing it for yourself with direct knowledge; and the *dharma* that you enter upon and abide in by realizing it for yourself with direct knowledge is the *dharma* that Rāma declared he entered upon and abided in by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge.

So you know the *dharma* that Rāma knew; and the *dharma* that you know is the *dharma* that Rāma knew.

Thus as Rāma was, so are you; as you are, so was Rāma.

Come, friend, now lead this community.’

Thus, Aggivessana, Udaka Rāmaputta, my companion in the holy life, placed me in the position of a teacher, and honored and revered me with the highest honor.

It occurred to me: ‘This *dharma* does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge (*abhijñā*), to enlightenment (*sambodha*), to *Nirvāṇa*, but only to reappearance in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.’

Not being satisfied with that *dharma*, disappointed with it, I left.

mula_pali: 373. ‘‘So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, kiṃkusalagavesī anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ pariyesamāno magadhesu anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena uruvelā senānigamo tadavasariṃ. Tatthaddasaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ bhūmibhāgaṃ, pāsādikañca vanasaṇḍaṃ, nadiñca sandantiṃ setakaṃ supatitthaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ, samantā ca gocaragāmaṃ. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘ramaṇīyo vata, bho, bhūmibhāgo, pāsādiko ca vanasaṇḍo, nadī ca sandati setakā supatitthā ramaṇīyā, samantā ca gocaragāmo. Alaṃ vatidaṃ kulaputtassa padhānatthikassa padhānāyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, tattheva nisīdiṃ ‘alamidaṃ padhānāyā’ti.
mula_english:
"So then, Aggivessana, still seeking what is wholesome (kuśala), searching for the unsurpassed state of sublime peace (anuttaraṃ śāntivarapadaṃ), I wandered by stages through Magadha until I arrived at Uruvelā, at Senānigama.

There I saw an agreeable piece of ground (ramaṇīyaṃ bhūmibhāgaṃ), a delightful grove (pāsādikañca vanasaṇḍaṃ), a river flowing with clear water (nadīñca sandantiṃ setakaṃ), with pleasant, smooth banks (supatitthaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ), and nearby a village for alms resort (samantā ca gocaragāmaṃ).

Then, Aggivessana, this occurred to me: ‘This is an agreeable piece of ground, a delightful grove, a river flowing with clear water, with pleasant, smooth banks, and nearby a village for alms resort.

This will serve for the striving of a clansman intent on striving (padhāna).’

So then, Aggivessana, I sat down there, thinking: ‘This will serve for striving.’"

mula_pali: 374. ‘‘Apissumaṃ, aggivessana, tisso upamā paṭibhaṃsu anacchariyā pubbe assutapubbā. Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ udake nikkhittaṃ. Atha puriso āgaccheyya uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya – ‘aggiṃ abhinibbattessāmi, tejo pātukarissāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, api nu so puriso amuṃ allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ, udake nikkhittaṃ , uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya abhimanthento aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Aduñhi, bho gotama, allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ, tañca pana udake nikkhittaṃ. Yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, aggivessana, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāyena ceva cittena ca kāmehi avūpakaṭṭhā viharanti, yo ca nesaṃ kāmesu kāmacchando kāmasneho kāmamucchā kāmapipāsā kāmapariḷāho, so ca ajjhattaṃ na suppahīno hoti, na suppaṭippassaddho, opakkamikā cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, abhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya. No cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, abhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya. Ayaṃ kho maṃ, aggivessana, paṭhamā upamā paṭibhāsi anacchariyā pubbe assutapubbā.
mula_english:
374. “Now, Aggivessana, these three similes occurred to me spontaneously, never heard before.

Suppose there were a wet sappy piece of wood lying in water.

Then a man came with an upper fire-stick, thinking: ‘I shall light a fire, I shall produce heat.’

What do you think, Aggivessana? Could the man light a fire and produce heat by taking the upper fire-stick and rubbing it against the wet sappy piece of wood lying in the water?” “No, Gotama.”

“What is the reason for that?” “Because it is a wet sappy piece of wood, and it is lying in water.

That man would only get a fair share of weariness and vexation.”

“So too, Aggivessana, as to those recluses (*śramaṇa*) and brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*) who still do not live bodily and mentally withdrawn from sensual pleasures (*kāma*), and whose sensual desire (*kāmacchanda*), affection (*kāmasneha*), infatuation (*kāmamucchā*), thirst (*kāmapipāsā*), and fever (*kāmapariḷāho*) for sensual pleasures has not been fully abandoned and suppressed internally, even if those good recluses and brahmins feel painful (*duḥkhā*), racking (*tibbā*), piercing (*kharā*), bitter (*kaṭukā*) feelings (*vedanā*), they are incapable of knowledge (*jñāna*) and vision (*darśana*) and supreme enlightenment (*anuttarāyāḥ sambodhāya*);

and even if those good recluses and brahmins do not feel painful, racking, piercing, bitter feelings, they are incapable of knowledge and vision and supreme enlightenment.

This was the first simile that occurred to me spontaneously, never heard before.
commentary_pali:
374.Allakaṭṭhanti allaṃ udumbarakaṭṭhaṃ. Sasnehanti sakhīraṃ. Kāmehīti vatthukāmehi. Avūpakaṭṭhāti anapagatā. Kāmacchandotiādīsu kilesakāmova chandakaraṇavasena chando. Sinehakaraṇavasena sneho. Mucchākaraṇavasena mucchā. Pipāsākaraṇavasena pipāsā. Anudahanavasena pariḷāhoti veditabbo. Opakkamikāti upakkamanibbattā. Ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāyāti sabbaṃ lokuttaramaggavevacanameva.

Idaṃ panettha opammasaṃsandanaṃ – allaṃ sakhīraṃ udumbarakaṭṭhaṃ viya hi kilesakāmena vatthukāmato anissaṭapuggalā. Udake pakkhittabhāvo viya kilesakāmena tintatā; manthanenāpi aggino anabhinibbattanaṃ viya kilesakāmena vatthukāmato anissaṭānaṃ opakkamikāhi vedanāhi lokuttaramaggassa anadhigamo. Amanthanenāpi aggino anabhinibbattanaṃ viya tesaṃ puggalānaṃ vināpi opakkamikāhi vedanāhi lokuttaramaggassa anadhigamo. Dutiyaupamāpi imināva nayena veditabbā. Ayaṃ pana viseso, purimā saputtabhariyapabbajjāya upamā; pacchimā brāhmaṇadhammikapabbajjāya.
commentary_english:
374.

*Allakaṭṭha* means fresh fig wood.

*Sasneha* means with ghee.

*Kāmehī* means with desirable things.

*Avūpakaṭṭha* means not departed.

In *kāmacchando*, etc., *chando* is desire because of the action of desiring defilements.

*Sneho* is affection because of the action of affection.

*Mucchā* is delusion because of the action of delusion.

*Pipāsā* is thirst because of the action of thirst.

*Pariḷāho* is anguish because of the action of burning.

*Opakkamikā* means produced by effort.

*Ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāyā* means it is simply a designation for the supramundane path (*lokottaramārga*).

Here, moreover, is a comparison: like fresh fig wood with ghee are persons not detached from sense-desires (*kilesakāma*) with respect to objects of desire (*vatthukāma*).

Like the state of being thrown into water is the immersion by sense-desires; like the non-origination of fire even by churning, there is no attainment (*anadhigama*) of the supramundane path by those who are not detached from sense-desires with respect to objects of desire, because of pains caused by effort.

Like the non-origination of fire even by not churning, there is no attainment of the supramundane path for those persons without pains caused by effort.

The second comparison should also be understood in this way.

But this is the distinction: the first is a comparison with the going forth of one with wife and children; the latter is with the going forth of a brahmin practicing the Dharma.

mula_pali: 375. ‘‘Aparāpi kho maṃ, aggivessana, dutiyā upamā paṭibhāsi anacchariyā pubbe assutapubbā. Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ, ārakā udakā thale nikkhittaṃ. Atha puriso āgaccheyya uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya – ‘aggiṃ abhinibbattessāmi, tejo pātukarissāmī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, aggivessana, api nu so puriso amuṃ allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ, ārakā udakā thale nikkhittaṃ, uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya abhimanthento aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya tejo pātukareyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Aduñhi, bho gotama, allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ, kiñcāpi ārakā udakā thale nikkhittaṃ. Yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assāti. Evameva kho, aggivessana, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāyena ceva cittena ca kāmehi vūpakaṭṭhā viharanti, yo ca nesaṃ kāmesu kāmacchando kāmasneho kāmamucchā kāmapipāsā kāmapariḷāho so ca ajjhattaṃ na suppahīno hoti, na suppaṭippassaddho, opakkamikā cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, abhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya. No cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, abhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya. Ayaṃ kho maṃ, aggivessana, dutiyā upamā paṭibhāsi anacchariyā pubbe assutapubbā’’.
mula_english:
375. Again, Aggivessana, a second simile occurred to me spontaneously, never heard before.

Suppose there were a wet sappy piece of wood lying on dry land far from water.

Then a man came with an upper fire-stick, thinking: ‘I shall light a fire, I shall produce heat.’

What do you think, Aggivessana? Could the man light a fire and produce heat by taking the upper fire-stick and rubbing it against the wet sappy piece of wood lying on dry land far from water? ” “No, Gotama.”

“What is the reason for that?” “Because it is a wet sappy piece of wood, even though it is lying on dry land far from water.

The man would only partake of weariness and frustration.”

“So too, Aggivessana, as to those *śramaṇas* or *brāhmaṇas* who live bodily and mentally withdrawn from sensual pleasures, but whose sensual desire, affection, infatuation, thirst, and fever for sensual pleasures has not been fully abandoned and suppressed internally, even if those good *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* feel painful, racking, piercing feelings due to exertion, they are incapable of knowledge (*jñāna*) and vision (*darśana*) and supreme enlightenment (*anuttarā saṃbodhā*);

and even if those good *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* do not feel painful, racking, piercing feelings due to exertion, they are incapable of knowledge (*jñāna*) and vision (*darśana*) and supreme enlightenment (*anuttarā saṃbodhā*).

This, Aggivessana, is the second wonderful simile that occurred to me, never heard before.”

mula_pali: 376. ‘‘Aparāpi kho maṃ, aggivessana, tatiyā upamā paṭibhāsi anacchariyā pubbe assutapubbā. Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, sukkhaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ koḷāpaṃ, ārakā udakā thale nikkhittaṃ. Atha puriso āgaccheyya uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya – ‘aggiṃ abhinibbattessāmi, tejo pātukarissāmī’ti.
