“I thought: ‘Suppose I practise further the breathingless meditation.

So I stopped the in-breaths and out-breaths through my mouth, nose, and ears.

While I did so, violent winds carved up my belly.

Just as if a skilled butcher or his apprentice were to carve up an ox’s belly with a sharp butcher’s knife, so too, while I stopped the in-breaths and out-breaths through my mouth, nose, and ears, violent winds carved up my belly.

But although tireless energy was aroused in me and unremitting mindfulness was established, my body was overwrought and uncalm because I was exhausted by the painful striving.

But such painful feeling that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.

“I thought: ‘Suppose I practise further the breathingless meditation.

So I stopped the in-breaths and out-breaths through my mouth, nose, and ears.

While I did so, there was a violent burning in my body.

Just as if two strong men were to seize a weaker man by both arms and roast him over a pit of hot coals, so too, while I stopped the in-breaths and out-breaths through my mouth, nose, and ears, there was a violent burning in my body.

But although tireless energy was aroused in me and unremitting mindfulness was established, my body was overwrought and uncalm because I was exhausted by the painful striving.

But such painful feeling that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.

Now when deities saw me, some said: ‘The recluse Gotama is dead.

Other deities said: ‘The recluse Gotama is not dead, he is dying.

And other deities said: ‘The recluse Gotama is not dead nor dying; he is an *arhat*, for such is the way *arhats* abide.’
commentary_pali:
378.Appāṇakanti nirassāsakaṃ. Kammāragaggariyāti kammārassa gaggaranāḷiyā. Sīsavedanā hontīti kutoci nikkhamituṃ alabhamānehi vātehi samuṭṭhāpitā balavatiyo sīsavedanā honti. Sīsaveṭhaṃ dadeyyāti sīsaveṭhanaṃ dadeyya. Devatāti bodhisattassa caṅkamanakoṭiyaṃ paṇṇasālapariveṇasāmantā ca adhivatthā devatā.

Tadā kira bodhisattassa adhimatte kāyadāhe uppanne mucchā udapādi. So caṅkameva nisinno hutvā papati. Taṃ disvā devatā evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘vihārotveva so arahato’’ti, ‘‘arahanto nāma evarūpā honti matakasadisā’’ti laddhiyā vadanti. Tattha yā devatā ‘‘kālaṅkato’’ti āhaṃsu, tā gantvā suddhodanamahārājassa ārocesuṃ – ‘‘tumhākaṃ putto kālaṅkato’’ti. Mama putto buddho hutvā kālaṅkato, no ahutvāti? Buddho bhavituṃ nāsakkhi, padhānabhūmiyaṃyeva patitvā kālaṅkatoti. Nāhaṃ saddahāmi, mama puttassa bodhiṃ apatvā kālaṅkiriyā nāma natthīti.

Aparabhāge sammāsambuddhassa dhammacakkaṃ pavattetvā anupubbena rājagahaṃ gantvā kapilavatthuṃ anuppattassa suddhodanamahārājā pattaṃ gahetvā pāsādaṃ āropetvā yāgukhajjakaṃ datvā antarābhattasamaye etamatthaṃ ārocesi – tumhākaṃ bhagavā padhānakaraṇakāle devatā āgantvā, ‘‘putto te, mahārāja, kālaṅkato’’ti āhaṃsūti. Kiṃ saddahasi mahārājāti? Na bhagavā saddahinti. Idāni, mahārāja, supinappaṭiggahaṇato paṭṭhāya acchariyāni passanto kiṃ saddahissasi? Ahampi buddho jāto, tvampi buddhapitā jāto, pubbe pana mayhaṃ aparipakke ñāṇe bodhicariyaṃ carantassa dhammapālakumārakālepi sippaṃ uggahetuṃ gatassa, ‘‘tumhākaṃ putto dhammapālakumāro kālaṅkato, idamassa aṭṭhī’’ti eḷakaṭṭhiṃ āharitvā dassesuṃ, tadāpi tumhe, ‘‘mama puttassa antarāmaraṇaṃ nāma natthi, nāhaṃ saddahāmī’’ti avocuttha, mahārājāti imissā aṭṭhuppattiyā bhagavā mahādhammapālajātakaṃ kathesi.
commentary_english:
378. *Appāṇaka* means without breath (*nirassāsakaṃ*).

*Kammāragaggariyā* means the blacksmith's blowing pipe (*kammārassa gaggaranāḷiyā*).

*Sīsavedanā hontī* means intense headaches arise, caused by winds that cannot escape from anywhere (*kutoci nikkhamituṃ alabhamānehi vātehi samuṭṭhāpitā balavatiyo sīsavedanā honti*).

*Sīsaveṭhaṃ dadeyyā* means one should give a head-covering (*sīsaveṭhanaṃ dadeyya*).

*Devatā* means deities dwelling around the Bodhisattva's walking place and the perimeter of the leaf-hut enclosure (*bodhisattassa caṅkamanakoṭiyaṃ paṇṇasālapariveṇasāmantā ca adhivatthā devatā*).

Then, when the Bodhisattva experienced exceedingly intense bodily heat, faintness arose.

He, seated while still pacing back and forth, fell down.

Having seen him, the deities said thus: "He is indeed a dwelling place for the Arhat!" "Arhats are indeed of such a nature, like corpses," they say, according to their views.

There, the deities who said, "He has passed away," went and announced to King Śuddhodana: "Your son has passed away."

"Did my son pass away after becoming a Buddha, or before becoming one?" He was not able to become a Buddha; having fallen on the practice ground itself, he passed away.

"I do not believe it; there is no death for my son without attaining enlightenment (bodhi)."

Later, after the Perfectly Awakened Buddha (sammāsambuddha) had set the Wheel of Dharma in motion, having gone to Rājagṛha in due course, and having arrived at Kapilavastu, King Śuddhodana, having taken the bowl, having had [the Buddha] ascend the palace, having given rice-gruel and solid food, at the time of an intermission in the meal, announced this matter: "Divine beings (devatā) came during the time of your Blessed One’s (bhagavā) striving, [saying,] ‘Your son, Great King, has passed away.’"

"Great King, do you believe it?" "The Blessed One does not believe it."

Now, Great King, since the acceptance of the dream, seeing wonders, what will you believe? I, too, was born a Buddha; you, too, were born a Buddha-father; formerly, however, when my knowledge was immature, while practicing the conduct of enlightenment (bodhicariya), even when I had gone to learn a craft in the time of Dharmapāla Kumāra, [they] brought an *eḷakaṭṭhi* and showed [it, saying,] "Your son, Dharmapāla Kumāra, has passed away; this is his bone." Even then, you said, "There is no premature death for my son; I do not believe it." Because of this origination of the bone, the Blessed One told the Great-Dharmapāla Jātaka.

mula_pali: 379. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ sabbaso āhārupacchedāya paṭipajjeyya’nti. Atha kho maṃ, aggivessana, devatā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘mā kho tvaṃ, mārisa, sabbaso āhārupacchedāya paṭipajji. Sace kho tvaṃ, mārisa, sabbaso āhārupacchedāya paṭipajjissasi, tassa te mayaṃ dibbaṃ ojaṃ lomakūpehi ajjhohāressāma ajjhoharissāma (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), tāya tvaṃ yāpessasī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘ahañceva kho pana sabbaso ajajjitaṃ ajaddhukaṃ (sī. pī.), jaddhukaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) paṭijāneyyaṃ, imā ca me devatā dibbaṃ ojaṃ lomakūpehi ajjhohāreyyuṃ ajjhohareyyuṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), tāya cāhaṃ yāpeyyaṃ, taṃ mamassa musā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, tā devatā paccācikkhāmi, ‘hala’nti vadāmi.
mula_english:
379.
"Then, Aggivessana, it occurred to me: ‘Suppose I were to practice the complete cessation of food (āhārupacchedāya paṭipajjeyya)’."

"Then, Aggivessana, deities approached me and said: ‘Do not, good sir (mārisa), practice the complete cessation of food (āhārupacchedāya paṭipajji). If you were to practice the complete cessation of food (āhārupacchedāya paṭipajjissasi), we would infuse heavenly sustenance (dibbaṃ ojaṃ) through the pores (lomakūpehi), and you would survive (yāpessasi) on that.’"

"Then, Aggivessana, it occurred to me: ‘If I were to claim to be completely fasting (ajajjitaṃ paṭijāneyyaṃ), and these deities were to infuse heavenly sustenance (dibbaṃ ojaṃ) through the pores (lomakūpehi), and I were to survive (yāpeyyaṃ) on that, that would be a falsehood (musā) for me.’"

"So, Aggivessana, I rejected those deities (devatā paccācikkhāmi), saying, ‘There is no need (hala)’."
commentary_pali: 379.Mākho tvaṃ mārisāti sampiyāyamānā āhaṃsu. Devatānaṃ kirāyaṃ piyamanāpavohāro, yadidaṃ mārisāti. Ajajjitanti abhojanaṃ. Halanti vadāmīti alanti vadāmi, alaṃ iminā evaṃ mā karittha, yāpessāmahanti evaṃ paṭisedhemīti attho.
commentary_english:
379.
*mā*, *kho tvaṃ mārisā* _iti_ sampiyāyamānā āhaṃsu.
_devatānaṃ kirāyaṃ piyamanāpavohāro, yadidaṃ mārisāti._
*ajajjita* _iti_ abhojanaṃ.
*halanti vadāmī* _iti_ alaṃti vadāmi, alaṃ iminā evaṃ mā karittha, yāpessāmahanti evaṃ paṭisedhemīti attho.

mula_pali:
380. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ thokaṃ thokaṃ āhāraṃ āhāreyyaṃ, pasataṃ pasataṃ, yadi vā muggayūsaṃ, yadi vā kulatthayūsaṃ, yadi vā kaḷāyayūsaṃ, yadi vā hareṇukayūsa’nti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, thokaṃ thokaṃ āhāraṃ āhāresiṃ, pasataṃ pasataṃ, yadi vā muggayūsaṃ, yadi vā kulatthayūsaṃ, yadi vā kaḷāyayūsaṃ, yadi vā hareṇukayūsaṃ. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, thokaṃ thokaṃ āhāraṃ āhārayato, pasataṃ pasataṃ, yadi vā muggayūsaṃ, yadi vā kulatthayūsaṃ, yadi vā kaḷāyayūsaṃ, yadi vā hareṇukayūsaṃ, adhimattakasimānaṃ patto kāyo hoti. Seyyathāpi nāma āsītikapabbāni vā kāḷapabbāni vā, evamevassu me aṅgapaccaṅgāni bhavanti tāyevappāhāratāya. Seyyathāpi nāma oṭṭhapadaṃ, evamevassu me ānisadaṃ hoti tāyevappāhāratāya. Seyyathāpi nāma vaṭṭanāvaḷī, evamevassu me piṭṭhikaṇṭako uṇṇatāvanato hoti tāyevappāhāratāya. Seyyathāpi nāma jarasālāya gopāṇasiyo oluggaviluggā bhavanti, evamevassu me phāsuḷiyo oluggaviluggā bhavanti tāyevappāhāratāya. Seyyathāpi nāma gambhīre udapāne udakatārakā gambhīragatā okkhāyikā dissanti, evamevassu me akkhikūpesu akkhitārakā gambhīragatā okkhāyikā dissanti tāyevappāhāratāya. Seyyathāpi nāma tittakālābu āmakacchinno vātātapena saṃphuṭito hoti sammilāto, evamevassu me sīsacchavi saṃphuṭitā hoti sammilātā tāyevappāhāratāya.

‘‘So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, udaracchaviṃ parimasissāmīti piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃyeva pariggaṇhāmi, piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ parimasissāmīti udaracchaviṃyeva pariggaṇhāmi, yāvassu me, aggivessana, udaracchavi piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ allīnā hoti tāyevappāhāratāya. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, vaccaṃ vā muttaṃ vā karissāmīti tattheva avakujjo papatāmi tāyevappāhāratāya. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, imameva kāyaṃ assāsento pāṇinā gattāni anumajjāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, pāṇinā gattāni anumajjato pūtimūlāni lomāni kāyasmā papatanti tāyevappāhāratāya. Apissu maṃ, aggivessana, manussā disvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘kāḷo samaṇo gotamo’ti. Ekacce manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘na kāḷo samaṇo gotamo, sāmo samaṇo gotamo’ti. Ekacce manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘na kāḷo samaṇo gotamo , napi sāmo, maṅguracchavi samaṇo gotamo’ti. Yāvassu me, aggivessana, tāva parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto upahato hoti tāyevappāhāratāya.
mula_english:
“380. I thought: ‘Suppose I take very little food, a handful each time, whether of green gram soup (*muggayūsaṃ*) or horse gram soup (*kulatthayūsaṃ*) or pea soup (*kaḷāyayūsaṃ*) or lentil soup (*hareṇukayūsaṃ*).’

So I took very little food, a handful each time, whether of green gram soup (*muggayūsaṃ*) or horse gram soup (*kulatthayūsaṃ*) or pea soup (*kaḷāyayūsaṃ*) or lentil soup (*hareṇukayūsaṃ*).

While I did so, my body reached a state of extreme emaciation.

Because of eating so little, my limbs became like the jointed segments of vine stems or bamboo stems (*āsītikapabbāni vā kāḷapabbāni vā*).

Because of eating so little my backside became like a camel’s hoof (*oṭṭhapadaṃ*).

Because of eating so little the projections on my spine stood forth like corded beads (*vaṭṭanāvaḷī uṇṇatāvanato*).

Because of eating so little my ribs jutted out as gaunt as the crazy rafters of an old roofless barn (*jarasālāya gopāṇasiyo oluggaviluggā*).

Because of eating so little the gleam of my eyes sank far down in their sockets, looking like a gleam of water that has sunk far down in a deep well (*gambhīre udapāne udakatārakā gambhīragatā okkhāyikā dissanti*).

Because of eating so little my scalp shrivelled and withered as a green bitter gourd (*tittakālābu āmakacchinno*) shrivels and withers in the wind and sun (*vātātapena saṃphuṭito hoti sammilāto*).

Because of eating so little, if I tried to ease my belly skin I encountered my backbone (*piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ*), and if I tried to ease my backbone (*piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ*) I encountered my belly skin (*udaracchaviṃ*); so much had my belly skin adhered to my backbone (*udaracchavi piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ allīnā hoti*).

Because of eating so little, if I defecated or urinated, I fell over on my face there (*avakujjo papatāmi*).

Because of eating so little, if I tried to ease this body (*kāyaṃ assāsento*) by rubbing my limbs with my hands (*pāṇinā gattāni anumajjāmi*),

the hair, rotted at its roots (*pūtimūlāni lomāni*), fell from my body (*kāyasmā papatanti*) as I rubbed. Because of eating so little.

Now when people saw me, some said: ‘The ascetic Gotama is dark-skinned (*kāḷo samaṇo gotamo*).’

Other people said: ‘The ascetic Gotama is not dark-skinned (*na kāḷo samaṇo gotamo*), he is brown (*sāmo samaṇo gotamo*).’

Other people said: ‘The ascetic Gotama is neither dark-skinned nor brown, he is golden-skinned (*maṅguracchavi samaṇo gotamo*).

So much had the clear, bright colour of my skin (*chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto*) deteriorated (*upahato*) through eating so little."

mula_pali: 381. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayiṃsu, etāvaparamaṃ, nayito bhiyyo. Yepi hi keci anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayissanti, etāvaparamaṃ, nayito bhiyyo. Yepi hi keci etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, etāvaparamaṃ, nayito bhiyyo. Na kho panāhaṃ imāya kaṭukāya dukkarakārikāya adhigacchāmi uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ. Siyā nu kho añño maggo bodhāyā’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ pitu sakkassa kammante sītāya jambucchāyāya nisinno vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharitā. Siyā nu kho eso maggo bodhāyā’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, satānusāri viññāṇaṃ ahosi – ‘eseva maggo bodhāyā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi, yaṃ taṃ sukhaṃ aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehī’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘na kho ahaṃ tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi, yaṃ taṃ sukhaṃ aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehī’ti.
mula_english:
381. “Then I thought: ‘Whatever ascetics or Brahmins in the past experienced painful, racking, piercing feelings due to exertion ( *opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā* ), this was the utmost; there is none beyond this.

And whatever ascetics or Brahmins in the future will experience painful, racking, piercing feelings due to exertion, this will be the utmost; there is none beyond this.

And whatever ascetics or Brahmins at present experience painful, racking, piercing feelings due to exertion, this is the utmost; there is none beyond this.

But even by undergoing this bitter austerity (*kaṭukāya dukkarakārikāya*), I did not attain any superhuman states, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones (*uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ*).

Could there be another path to enlightenment (*bodhāyā*)?’ Then I thought: ‘I recall that when my father the Sakyan was occupied, while I was sitting in the cool shade of a rose-apple tree, quite secluded from sensual pleasures (*kāmehi*), secluded from unwholesome states (*akusalehi dhammehi*), I entered upon and abided in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion (*savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharitā*).

Could this be the path to enlightenment (*maggo bodhāyā*)?’ Then, following on that memory, came the realisation: ‘That is indeed the path to enlightenment (*eseva maggo bodhāyā*).’

Then I thought: ‘Why then am I afraid of that pleasure (*tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi*) since it has nothing to do with sensual pleasures (*kāmehi*) and unwholesome states (*akusalehi dhammehi*)?’ Then I thought: ‘I am not afraid of that pleasure (*na kho ahaṃ tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi*), since it has nothing to do with sensual pleasures (*kāmehi*) and unwholesome states (*akusalehi dhammehi*)’."

mula_pali: 382. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etadahosi – ‘na kho taṃ sukaraṃ sukhaṃ adhigantuṃ evaṃ adhimattakasimānaṃ pattakāyena, yaṃnūnāhaṃ oḷārikaṃ āhāraṃ āhāreyyaṃ odanakummāsa’nti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, oḷārikaṃ āhāraṃ āhāresiṃ odanakummāsaṃ. Tena kho pana maṃ, aggivessana, samayena pañca pañcavaggiyā (aññasuttesu) bhikkhū paccupaṭṭhitā honti – ‘yaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ adhigamissati, taṃ no ārocessatī’ti. Yato kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, oḷārikaṃ āhāraṃ āhāresiṃ odanakummāsaṃ, atha me te pañca bhikkhū nibbijja pakkamiṃsu – ‘bāhulliko bāhuliko (sī. pī.) saṃghabhedasikkhāpadaṭīkāya sameti samaṇo gotamo, padhānavibbhanto, āvatto bāhullāyā’ti.
mula_english:
382. “Then it occurred to me, Aggivessana: ‘It is not easy to attain that pleasure with a body so excessively emaciated. Suppose I were to eat some coarse food—some boiled rice and porridge ( *odanakummāsa* ).’

And I, Aggivessana, ate some coarse food—boiled rice and porridge (*odanakummāsa*).

Now at that time, five monks were waiting upon me, thinking: ‘If the ascetic Gotama attains the Dharma, he will inform us.’

But when I, Aggivessana, ate coarse food—boiled rice and porridge (*odanakummāsa*)—the five monks were disgusted and left me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama lives luxuriously, he has given up his striving and has turned to luxury!’”
commentary_pali: 382.Paccupaṭṭhitā hontīti paṇṇasālapariveṇasammajjanādivattakaraṇena upaṭṭhitā honti. Bāhullikoti paccayabāhulliko. Āvatto bāhullāyāti rasagiddho hutvā paṇītapiṇḍapātādīnaṃ atthāya āvatto. Nibbijja pakkamiṃsūti ukkaṇṭhitvā dhammaniyāmeneva pakkantā bodhisattassa sambodhiṃ pattakāle kāyavivekassa okāsadānatthaṃ dhammatāya gatā. Gacchantā ca aññaṭṭhānaṃ agantvā bārāṇasimeva agamaṃsu. Bodhisatto tesu gatesu addhamāsaṃ kāyavivekaṃ labhitvā bodhimaṇḍe aparājitapallaṅke nisīditvā sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ paṭivijjhi.
commentary_english:
382.
"They attend" means they attend by doing such things as sweeping the leaf-hut enclosure.
"One who is excessive" means one who is excessive in requisites.
"Turning back for excess" means turning back, desiring flavors, for the sake of excellent alms food, and so on.
"Having become disgusted, they departed" means having become anxious, they departed according to the rule of the Dharma. They left according to the law of Dharma to give the bodhisattva an opportunity for physical solitude at the time of attaining complete enlightenment (saṃbodhi).
And going, without going to another place, they went to Bārāṇasī itself.
When they had gone, the bodhisattva, having obtained physical solitude for half a month, sat down on the unconquered seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), and penetrated all-knowing knowledge (sarvajñuta-jñāna).

mula_pali: 383. ‘‘So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, oḷārikaṃ āhāraṃ āhāretvā, balaṃ gahetvā, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati. Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca vihāsiṃ, sato ca sampajāno. Sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedesiṃ yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati. Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati.
mula_english:
383.
“Now, O Aggivessana, having taken solid food, I gained strength, and quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I entered upon and abided in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.

But such pleasant feeling that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.

With the stilling of directed thoughts & evaluations, I entered & remained in the second *jhāna*: rapture & pleasure born of composure, unification of awareness free from directed thought & evaluation — internal assurance.

But such pleasant feeling that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.

With the fading away as well of rapture I remained in equanimity, mindful & alert.

And experiencing pleasure with the body, I entered & remained in the third *jhāna*, of which the Noble Ones declare, ‘Equanimous & mindful, he has a pleasant abiding.’

But such pleasant feeling that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.

With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, I entered and remained in the fourth *jhāna*: purity of equanimity & mindfulness, neither pleasure nor pain.

But such pleasant feeling that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.
commentary_pali: 383.Vivicceva kāmehītiādi bhayabherave vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english: It should be understood in the same way as stated in the fearsome *vivicceva kāmehī* etc.

mula_pali: 384. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi , seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi. Ayaṃ kho me, aggivessana, rattiyā paṭhame yāme paṭhamā vijjā adhigatā; avijjā vihatā, vijjā uppannā; tamo vihato, āloko uppanno; yathā taṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato. Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati.
mula_english:
384. Thus, when the mind was concentrated ( *samāhite citte*), purified (*parisuddhe*), cleansed (*pariyodāte*), without blemish (*anaṅgaṇe*), free from defilement (*vigatūpakkilese*), pliable (*mudubhūte*), workable (*kammaniye*), steady (*ṭhite*), and had attained imperturbability (*āneñjappatte*), I directed (*abhininnāmesiṃ*) my mind to the knowledge of the recollection of past existences (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya*).

I recollected my manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi*), that is to say, one birth… and so forth… Thus, with their aspects and particulars (*sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ*), I recollected my manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi*).

This, Aggivessana, was the first true knowledge (*paṭhamā vijjā adhigatā*) attained by me in the first watch of the night (*rattiyā paṭhame yāme*); ignorance (*avijjā*) was banished (*vihatā*), and true knowledge (*vijjā*) arose (*uppannā*); darkness (*tamo*) was banished (*vihato*), and light (*āloko*) arose (*uppanno*), as happens in one who abides diligent (*appamattassa*), ardent (*ātāpino*), and resolute (*pahitattassa viharato*).

Even such pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*) that arose in me, Aggivessana, did not invade my mind and remain (*cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati*).

mula_pali: 385. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi…pe… ayaṃ kho me, aggivessana, rattiyā majjhime yāme dutiyā vijjā adhigatā; avijjā vihatā, vijjā uppannā; tamo vihato, āloko uppanno; yathā taṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato . Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana , uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati.
mula_english:
“When my concentrated mind was thus purified (parisuddhe), bright (pariyodāte), unblemished (anaṅgaṇe), rid of imperfection (vigatūpakkilese), malleable (mudubhūte), wieldy (kammaniye), steady (ṭhite), and attained to imperturbability (āneñjappatte), I directed it to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings (sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ).

Thus with the divine eye (so dibbena cakkhunā), which is purified (visuddhena) and surpasses the human (atikkantamānusakena), I saw beings passing away (cavamāne) and reappearing (upapajjamāne), inferior (hīne) and superior (paṇīte), fair (suvaṇṇe) and ugly (dubbaṇṇe), fortunate (sugate) and unfortunate (duggate), and I understood how beings pass on according to their actions (yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi)…pe… This was the second true knowledge (dutiyā vijjā) attained by me in the middle watch of the night. Ignorance (avijjā) was banished (vihatā) and true knowledge (vijjā) arose (uppannā), darkness (tamo) was banished (vihato) and light (āloko) arose (uppanno), as happens in one who abides diligent (appamattassa), ardent (ātāpino), and resolute (pahitattassa).

But such pleasant feeling (sukhā vedanā) that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain (cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati).

mula_pali: 386. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ. ‘Ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ. Tassa me evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ ahosi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsiṃ. Ayaṃ kho me, aggivessana, rattiyā pacchime yāme tatiyā vijjā adhigatā; avijjā vihatā, vijjā uppannā; tamo vihato, āloko uppanno; yathā taṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato. Evarūpāpi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati.
mula_english:
386. “When my mind was thus concentrated, purified, clear, without blemish, rid of imperfections, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, I directed it to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints (*āsava*).

I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘This is suffering (*duḥkha*)’; I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘This is the origin of suffering (*duḥkha*)’; I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering (*duḥkha*)’; I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering (*duḥkha*)’.

I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘These are the taints (*āsava*)’; I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘This is the origin of the taints (*āsava*)’; I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘This is the cessation of the taints (*āsava*)’; I directly knew, as it actually is: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of the taints (*āsava*)’.

When I knew and saw thus, my mind was liberated from the taint (*āsava*) of sensual desire (*kāma*), from the taint (*āsava*) of being (*bhava*), and from the taint (*āsava*) of ignorance (*avidyā*).

When it was liberated, there came the knowledge: ‘It is liberated.’

’ I directly knew: ‘Destroyed is birth (*jāti*), lived is the holy life (*brahmacariya*), done is what was to be done, now there is no more of being this or that.’

“This was the third true knowledge (*vidyā*) attained by me in the last watch of the night. Ignorance (*avidyā*) was banished and true knowledge (*vidyā*) arose; darkness (*tamas*) was banished and light (*āloka*) arose, as happens in one who abides diligent, ardent, and resolute.

But such pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*) that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.

mula_pali:
387. ‘‘Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, aggivessana, anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ desetā. Apissu maṃ ekameko evaṃ maññati – ‘mamevārabbha samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ desetī’ti. ‘Na kho panetaṃ, aggivessana, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ; yāvadeva viññāpanatthāya tathāgato paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti. So kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, tassāyeva kathāya pariyosāne, tasmiṃyeva purimasmiṃ samādhinimitte ajjhattameva cittaṃ saṇṭhapemi sannisādemi ekodiṃ karomi samādahāmi, yena sudaṃ niccakappaṃ viharāmī’’’ti.

‘‘Okappaniyametaṃ bhoto gotamassa yathā taṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Abhijānāti kho pana bhavaṃ gotamo divā supitā’’ti? ‘‘Abhijānāmahaṃ, aggivessana, gimhānaṃ pacchime māse pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā dakkhiṇena passena sato sampajāno niddaṃ okkamitā’’ti. ‘‘Etaṃ kho, bho gotama, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammohavihārasmiṃ vadantī’’ti ? ‘‘Na kho, aggivessana, ettāvatā sammūḷho vā hoti asammūḷho vā. Api ca, aggivessana, yathā sammūḷho ca hoti asammūḷho ca, taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
387. “Aggivessana, I recall teaching the *dharma* to an assembly of many hundreds. And even then each person thinks of me: ‘The *śramaṇa* Gotama is teaching the *dharma* especially for me.’

‘It is not in such a way that one is to see it, Aggivessana; the *Tathāgata* teaches the *dharma* to others only for the sake of communicating.

When the talk is finished, Aggivessana, then I steady my mind internally, quieten it, bring it to singleness, and concentrate it on that same sign of concentration as before, in which I constantly abide.’"

“This is acceptable for the *bhoto* Gotama, as it is for the *arhat* *sammāsambuddha*."

"Does the esteemed Gotama recognize sleeping during the day?" "Aggivessana, I recognize that in the last month of summer, after the meal, returning from alms, having folded the robe four times, I lie down on my right side, mindful and fully aware."

“Some *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s speak of this as dwelling in delusion, esteemed Gotama?" "It is not in such a way that one is deluded or undeluded, Aggivessana. As to how one is deluded or undeluded, Aggivessana, listen and attend closely to what I shall say."

“Yes, sir,” Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son replied.

The Bhagavān said this:
commentary_pali:
387.Abhijānāmi kho panāhanti ayaṃ pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Nigaṇṭho kira cintesi – ‘‘ahaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ ekaṃ pañhaṃ pucchiṃ. Samaṇo gotamo ‘aparāpi maṃ, aggivessana, aparāpi maṃ, aggivessanā’ti pariyosānaṃ adassento kathetiyeva. Kupito nu kho’’ti? Atha bhagavā, aggivessana , tathāgate anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ desente kupito samaṇo gotamoti ekopi vattā natthi, paresaṃ bodhanatthāya paṭivijjhanatthāya eva tathāgato dhammaṃ desetīti dassento imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha ārabbhāti sandhāya. Yāvadevāti payojanavidhi paricchedaniyamanaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – paresaṃ viññāpanameva tathāgatassa dhammadesanāya payojanaṃ, tasmā na ekasseva deseti, yattakā viññātāro atthi, sabbesaṃ desetīti. Tasmiṃyeva purimasminti iminā kiṃ dassetīti? Saccako kira cintesi – ‘‘samaṇo gotamo abhirūpo pāsādiko suphusitaṃ dantāvaraṇaṃ, jivhā mudukā, madhuraṃ vākkaraṇaṃ, parisaṃ rañjento maññe vicarati, anto panassa cittekaggatā natthī’’ti. Atha bhagavā, aggivessana, na tathāgato parisaṃ rañjento vicarati, cakkavāḷapariyantāyapi parisāya tathāgato dhammaṃ deseti, asallīno anupalitto ettakaṃ ekavihārī, suññataphalasamāpattiṃ anuyuttoti dassetuṃ evamāha.

Ajjhattamevāti gocarajjhattameva. Sannisādemīti sannisīdāpemi, tathāgato hi yasmiṃ khaṇe parisā sādhukāraṃ deti, tasmiṃ khaṇe pubbābhogena paricchinditvā phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjati, sādhukārasaddassa nigghose avicchinneyeva samāpattito vuṭṭhāya ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya dhammaṃ deseti, buddhānañhi bhavaṅgaparivāso lahuko hotīti assāsavāre passāsavāre samāpattiṃ samāpajjanti. Yena sudaṃ niccakappanti yena suññena phalasamādhinā niccakālaṃ viharāmi, tasmiṃ samādhinimitte cittaṃ saṇṭhapemi samādahāmīti dasseti.

Ajjhattamevā Sannisādemī Yena sudaṃ niccakappa

Okappaniyametanti saddahaniyametaṃ. Evaṃ bhagavato ekaggacittataṃ sampaṭicchitvā idāni attano ovaṭṭikasāraṃ katvā ānītapañhaṃ pucchanto abhijānāti kho pana bhavaṃ gotamo divā supitāti āha. Yathā hi sunakho nāma asambhinnakhīrapakkapāyasaṃ sappinā yojetvā udarapūraṃ bhojitopi gūthaṃ disvā akhāditvā gantuṃ na sakkā, akhādamāno ghāyitvāpi gacchati, aghāyitvāva gatassa kirassa sīsaṃ rujjati; evamevaṃ imassapi satthā asambhinnakhīrapakkapāyasasadisaṃ abhinikkhamanato paṭṭhāya yāva āsavakkhayā pasādanīyaṃ dhammadesanaṃ deseti. Etassa pana evarūpaṃ dhammadesanaṃ sutvā satthari pasādamattampi na uppannaṃ, tasmā ovaṭṭikasāraṃ katvā ānītapañhaṃ apucchitvā gantuṃ asakkonto evamāha. Tattha yasmā thinamiddhaṃ sabbakhīṇāsavānaṃ arahattamaggeneva pahīyati, kāyadaratho pana upādinnakepi hoti anupādinnakepi. Tathā hi kamaluppalādīni ekasmiṃ kāle vikasanti, ekasmiṃ makulāni honti, sāyaṃ kesañci rukkhānampi pattāni patilīyanti, pāto vipphārikāni honti. Evaṃ upādinnakassa kāyassa darathoyeva darathavasena bhavaṅgasotañca idha niddāti adhippetaṃ, taṃ khīṇāsavānampi hoti. Taṃ sandhāya, ‘‘abhijānāmaha’’ntiādimāha. Sammohavihārasmiṃ vadantīti sammohavihāroti vadanti.

Okappaniyameta abhijānāti kho pana bhavaṃ gotamo divā supitā Sammohavihārasmiṃ vadantī
commentary_english:
387. "I recognize," this is a distinct connection.

The *nigaṇṭha* (Jain ascetic) thought, "I asked the *śramaṇa* (mendicant) *Gautama* (Gotama) a question.

The *śramaṇa* *Gautama*, without showing the end, says only, 'Again to me, *Aggivessana*, again to me, *Aggivessana*.’

Is he angry?" Then, the Blessed One, *Aggivessana*, to the *tathāgata* (the thus-gone one, the Buddha) teaching the Dharma to an assembly of many hundreds, is the *śramaṇa* *Gautama* angry? There is not even one speaker [who would say that]. The *tathāgata*, showing that he teaches the Dharma only for the purpose of awakening others, for the purpose of insight, began this Dharma teaching.

There, "having begun" refers to.

"Only as long as" is the determination and restriction of the purpose.

This is what was said: The purpose of the *tathāgata*'s Dharma teaching is only to inform others. Therefore, he does not teach to only one person. As many knowers as there are, he teaches to all of them.

"In that very former one," what does he show with this? *Saccaka* thought: "The *śramaṇa* *Gautama* is handsome, pleasing, with well-formed teeth, a soft tongue, sweet speech, I think he wanders about delighting the assembly, but inwardly he has no one-pointedness of mind."

Then, the Blessed One, *Aggivessana*, the *tathāgata* does not wander about delighting the assembly, the *tathāgata* teaches the Dharma to an assembly even as far as the *cakkavāḷa* (wheel-circle, world-system), he abides alone, without clinging, without attachment, devoted to the *suññatā* (emptiness) attainment of fruition, to show this, he said thus.

Internally, only internally as to the range of object.

"I seat myself" means I cause to be seated. For the *tathāgata*, indeed, in whatever moment the assembly gives approval, in that moment, having cut off with prior practice, he attains the fruition attainment. In the sound of the approval, without even interrupting, having arisen from the attainment, having begun from the place where he stood, he teaches the Dharma. For the Buddhas, indeed, the dependence on the life-continuum is light. They attain the attainment in the in-breath and the out-breath.

"By which, indeed, constantly" means, by which emptiness, by the fruition *samādhi* (concentration) I constantly abide, in that *samādhi* sign, I fix and concentrate the mind, this he shows.

Internally, I seat myself by which, indeed, constantly.

"To be assented to," means to be believed.

Having approved the one-pointedness of mind of the Blessed One in this way, now, making his own question brought forward into a *ovaṭṭika* core, asking, "Does the esteemed *Gautama* know [that I] slept during the day?" he said.

Just as a dog, having been fed to the full with milk-rice mixed with ghee, not having eaten it, is not able to go, and even smelling it, goes; and even without smelling it, the head of the one who has gone cracks; even so, for this one also, the teacher teaches a Dharma teaching that is pleasing from the going forth until the destruction of the *āsavas* (influxes), like milk-rice.

But having heard such a Dharma teaching of his, not even a little faith arose in the teacher. Therefore, making a *ovaṭṭika* core, without asking the question brought forward, being unable to go, he said thus.

There, since drowsiness and sleep are abandoned only by the path of *arahatta* (worthiness) of all those with destroyed *āsavas*, but physical fatigue is both clung to and not clung to.

Just as lotuses and water lilies blossom at one time, are buds at one time, and in the evening even the leaves of some trees are concealed, and in the morning they are expanded.

Thus, for the body of one who has clung, fatigue itself, by way of fatigue, and the stream of the life-continuum here are sleep, this is intended. That is also for those with destroyed *āsavas*.

Referring to that, he said, "We know," etc.

"Speaking in a state of bewilderment," means they speak of a state of bewilderment.

To be assented to, Does the esteemed *Gautama* know [that I] slept during the day? Speaking in a state of bewilderment.

mula_pali:
388. ‘‘Yassa kassaci, aggivessana, ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā appahīnā, tamahaṃ ‘sammūḷho’ti vadāmi. Āsavānañhi, aggivessana, appahānā sammūḷho hoti. Yassa kassaci, aggivessana, ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā pahīnā, tamahaṃ ‘asammūḷho’ti vadāmi. Āsavānañhi, aggivessana, pahānā asammūḷho hoti.

‘‘Tathāgatassa kho, aggivessana, ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā . Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna virūḷhiyā, evameva kho, aggivessana, tathāgatassa ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā’’ti.
mula_english:
388. "Him I call deluded, Aggivessana, who has not abandoned the *āsavas* (taints) that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth (*jāti*), ageing (*jarā*), and death (*maraṇa*); for it is with the non-abandoning of the taints (*āsavas*) that one is deluded. Him I call undeluded who has abandoned the taints (*āsavas*) that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth (*jāti*), ageing (*jarā*), and death (*maraṇa*); for it is with the abandoning of the taints (*āsavas*) that one is undeluded.

"The *Tathāgata*, Aggivessana, has abandoned the taints (*āsavas*) that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth (*jāti*), ageing (*jarā*), and death (*maraṇa*); he has cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, done away with them so that they are no longer subject to future arising. Just as a palm tree whose crown is cut off is incapable of further growth, so too, the *Tathāgata* has abandoned the taints (*āsavas*) that defile…cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, done away with them so that they are no longer subject to future arising."

mula_pali:
389. Evaṃ vutte, saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bho gotama, abbhutaṃ, bho gotama! Yāvañcidaṃ bhoto gotamassa evaṃ āsajja āsajja vuccamānassa, upanītehi vacanappathehi samudācariyamānassa, chavivaṇṇo ceva pariyodāyati, mukhavaṇṇo ca vippasīdati, yathā taṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Abhijānāmahaṃ, bho gotama, pūraṇaṃ kassapaṃ vādena vādaṃ samārabhitā. Sopi mayā vādena vādaṃ samāraddho aññenaññaṃ paṭicari, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmesi, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Bhoto pana bhoto kho pana (sī.) gotamassa evaṃ āsajja āsajja vuccamānassa, upanītehi vacanappathehi samudācariyamānassa, chavivaṇṇo ceva pariyodāyati, mukhavaṇṇo ca vippasīdati, yathā taṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Abhijānāmahaṃ, bho gotama, makkhaliṃ gosālaṃ…pe… ajitaṃ kesakambalaṃ… pakudhaṃ kaccāyanaṃ… sañjayaṃ belaṭṭhaputtaṃ… nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ vādena vādaṃ samārabhitā . Sopi mayā vādena vādaṃ samāraddho aññenaññaṃ paṭicari, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmesi, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Bhoto pana gotamassa evaṃ āsajja āsajja vuccamānassa, upanītehi vacanappathehi samudācariyamānassa, chavivaṇṇo ceva pariyodāyati, mukhavaṇṇo ca vippasīdati, yathā taṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Handa ca dāni mayaṃ, bho gotama, gacchāma. Bahukiccā mayaṃ, bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni tvaṃ, aggivessana, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti.

Atha kho saccako nigaṇṭhaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti.

Mahāsaccakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
389.
When this was said, Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha's son said this to the Blessed One: "Wonderful, Master Gotama, amazing, Master Gotama! As much as the color of the skin brightens and the color of the face clears when Master Gotama is spoken to offensively again and again, assailed by discourteous courses of speech, as is to be expected of an *arhat*, a *sammāsambuddha* (perfectly awakened one).

I recall, Master Gotama, engaging Pūraṇa Kassapa in debate.

And then he prevaricated with me, led the talk aside, and showed anger, hate, and bitterness.

But when Master Gotama is spoken to offensively again and again, assailed by discourteous courses of speech, the colour of his skin brightens and the colour of his face clears, as is to be expected of an *arhat*, a *sammāsambuddha* (perfectly awakened one).

I recall, Master Gotama, engaging Makkhali Gosāla… Ajita Kesakambalin… Pakudha Kaccāyana… Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta… the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta in debate.

And then he prevaricated with me, led the talk aside, and showed anger, hate, and bitterness.

But when Master Gotama is spoken to offensively again and again, assailed by discourteous courses of speech, the colour of his skin brightens and the colour of his face clears, as is to be expected of an *arhat*, a *sammāsambuddha* (perfectly awakened one).

And now, Master Gotama, we depart.
We are busy and have much to do.

“Now is the time, Aggivessana, to do as you think fit.”

Then Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha’s son, having delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words, got up from his seat and departed.

The Mahāsaccaka Sutta, the sixth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
389.Āsajja āsajjāti ghaṭṭetvā ghaṭṭetvā. Upanītehīti upanetvā kathitehi. Vacanappathehīti vacanehi. Abhinanditvā anumoditvāti alanti cittena sampaṭicchanto abhinanditvā vācāyapi pasaṃsanto anumoditvā. Bhagavatā imassa nigaṇṭhassa dve suttāni kathitāni. Purimasuttaṃ eko bhāṇavāro, idaṃ diyaḍḍho, iti aḍḍhatiye bhāṇavāre sutvāpi ayaṃ nigaṇṭho neva abhisamayaṃ patto, na pabbajito, na saraṇesu patiṭṭhito. Kasmā etassa bhagavā dhammaṃ desesīti? Anāgate vāsanatthāya. Passati hi bhagavā, ‘‘imassa idāni upanissayo natthi, mayhaṃ pana parinibbānato samadhikānaṃ dvinnaṃ vassasatānaṃ accayena tambapaṇṇidīpe sāsanaṃ patiṭṭhahissati. Tatrāyaṃ kulaghare nibbattitvā sampatte kāle pabbajitvā tīṇi piṭakāni uggahetvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ patvā kāḷabuddharakkhito nāma mahākhīṇāsavo bhavissatī’’ti. Idaṃ disvā anāgate vāsanatthāya dhammaṃ desesi.

Sopi tattheva tambapaṇṇidīpamhi sāsane patiṭṭhite devalokato cavitvā dakkhiṇagirivihārassa bhikkhācāragāme ekasmiṃ amaccakule nibbatto pabbajjāsamatthayobbane pabbajitvā tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ uggahetvā gaṇaṃ pariharanto mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivuto upajjhāyaṃ passituṃ agamāsi. Athassa upajjhāyo saddhivihārikaṃ codessāmīti tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ uggahetvā āgatena tena saddhiṃ mukhaṃ datvā kathāmattampi na akāsi. So paccūsasamaye vuṭṭhāya therassa santikaṃ gantvā, – ‘‘tumhe, bhante, mayi ganthakammaṃ katvā tumhākaṃ santikaṃ āgate mukhaṃ datvā kathāmattampi na karittha, ko mayhaṃ doso’’ti pucchi. Thero āha – ‘‘tvaṃ, āvuso, buddharakkhita ettakeneva ‘pabbajjākiccaṃ me matthakaṃ patta’nti saññaṃ karosī’’ti. Kiṃ karomi, bhanteti? Gaṇaṃ vinodetvā tvaṃ papañcaṃ chinditvā cetiyapabbatavihāraṃ gantvā samaṇadhammaṃ karohīti. So upajjhāyassa ovāde ṭhatvā saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ patvā puññavā rājapūjito hutvā mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivāro cetiyapabbatavihāre vasi.

Tasmiñhi kāle tissamahārājā uposathakammaṃ karonto cetiyapabbate rājaleṇe vasati. So therassa upaṭṭhākabhikkhuno saññaṃ adāsi – ‘‘yadā mayhaṃ ayyo pañhaṃ vissajjeti, dhammaṃ vā katheti, tadā me saññaṃ dadeyyāthā’’ti. Theropi ekasmiṃ dhammassavanadivase bhikkhusaṅghaparivāro kaṇṭakacetiyaṅgaṇaṃ āruyha cetiyaṃ vanditvā kāḷatimbarurukkhamūle aṭṭhāsi. Atha naṃ eko piṇḍapātikatthero kāḷakārāmasuttante pañhaṃ pucchi. Thero nanu, āvuso, ajja dhammassavanadivasoti āha. Āma, bhante, dhammassavanadivasoti. Tena hi pīṭhakaṃ ānetha, idheva nisinnā dhammassavanaṃ karissāmāti. Athassa rukkhamūle āsanaṃ paññapetvā adaṃsu. Thero pubbagāthā vatvā kāḷakārāmasuttaṃ ārabhi. Sopissa upaṭṭhākadaharo rañño saññaṃ dāpesi. Rājā pubbagāthāsu aniṭṭhitāsuyeva pāpuṇi. Patvā ca aññātakaveseneva parisante ṭhatvā tiyāmarattiṃ ṭhitakova dhammaṃ sutvā therassa, idamavoca bhagavāti vacanakāle sādhukāraṃ adāsi. Thero ñatvā, kadā āgatosi, mahārājāti pucchi. Pubbagāthā osāraṇakāleyeva, bhanteti. Dukkaraṃ te mahārāja, katanti. Nayidaṃ, bhante, dukkaraṃ, yadi pana me ayyassa dhammakathaṃ āraddhakālato paṭṭhāya ekapadepi aññavihitabhāvo ahosi, tambapaṇṇidīpassa patodayaṭṭhinitudanamattepi ṭhāne sāmibhāvo nāma me mā hotūti sapathamakāsi.

Tasmiṃ pana sutte buddhaguṇā paridīpitā, tasmā rājā pucchi – ‘‘ettakāva, bhante, buddhaguṇā, udāhu aññepi atthī’’ti. Mayā kathitato, mahārāja, akathitameva bahu appamāṇanti. Upamaṃ, bhante, karothāti. Yathā, mahārāja , karīsasahassamatte sālikkhette ekasālisīsato avasesasālīyeva bahū, evaṃ mayā kathitaguṇā appā, avasesā bahūti. Aparampi, bhante, upamaṃ karothāti. Yathā, mahārāja, mahāgaṅgāya oghapuṇṇāya sūcipāsaṃ sammukhaṃ kareyya, sūcipāsena gataudakaṃ appaṃ, sesaṃ bahu, evameva mayā kathitaguṇā appā, avasesā bahūti. Aparampi, bhante, upamaṃ karothāti. Idha, mahārāja, cātakasakuṇā nāma ākāse kīḷantā vicaranti. Khuddakā sā sakuṇajāti, kiṃ nu kho tassa sakuṇassa ākāse pakkhapasāraṇaṭṭhānaṃ bahu, avaseso ākāso appoti? Kiṃ, bhante, vadatha, appo tassa pakkhapasāraṇokāso, avasesova bahūti. Evameva, mahārāja, appakā mayā buddhaguṇā kathitā, avasesā bahū anantā appameyyāti. Sukathitaṃ, bhante, anantā buddhaguṇā ananteneva ākāsena upamitā. Pasannā mayaṃ ayyassa, anucchavikaṃ pana kātuṃ na sakkoma. Ayaṃ me duggatapaṇṇākāro imasmiṃ tambapaṇṇidīpe imaṃ tiyojanasatikaṃ rajjaṃ ayyassa demāti. Tumhehi, mahārāja, attano pasannākāro kato, mayaṃ pana amhākaṃ dinnaṃ rajjaṃ tumhākaṃyeva dema, dhammena samena rajjaṃ kārehi mahārājāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāsaccakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
389. *Āsajja āsajjā*: striking and striking. *Upanītehī*: having brought near, with words. *Vacanappathehī*: with words. *Abhinanditvā anumoditvā*: being pleased at heart, accepting, rejoicing, praising with speech, and approving. The Blessed One spoke two *sūtras* to this *Nigaṇṭha*. The first *sūtra* is one recitation section, this [next] is one and a half. Even after hearing one and a half recitation sections, this *Nigaṇṭha* neither attained clear understanding, nor went forth [as a monk], nor was established in the refuges. Why did the Blessed One teach the *dharma* to him? For the sake of habituation in the future. For the Blessed One sees, "Now, this one has no support. But after the passing away into complete nirvāṇa of me, after the lapse of two hundred years, the teaching will be established in Tambapaṇṇidīpa. There, this one, having been born in a family home, when the time has come, having gone forth [as a monk], having grasped the three *piṭakas*, having increased insight, together with the *paṭisambhidās*, having attained arhatship, will become a great one whose defilements are destroyed, by the name of Kāḷabuddharakkhita." Having seen this, he taught the *dharma* for the sake of habituation in the future. And that one, in that very Tambapaṇṇidīpa, when the teaching was established, having passed away from the world of the gods, having been born in a minister's family in a village for alms in the Dakkhiṇagirivihāra, having gone forth [as a monk] in youth capable of going forth, having grasped the three *piṭakas*, the word of the Buddha, protecting the community, surrounded by a great community of monks, went to see [his] preceptor. Then his preceptor, thinking, "I will rebuke the co-resident," having grasped the three *piṭakas*, the word of the Buddha, with that one who had come, having given [him] a face, he did not speak even a word. He, at dawn, having arisen, went to the elder, saying, "Venerable sir, having done the work of tying a knot in me, having come to your presence, having given [me] a face, you did not speak even a word. What is my fault?" The elder said, "You, friend Buddharakkhita, with just this much, do you make the notion, 'The duties of going forth have reached my peak'?" What should I do, venerable sir? Having gladdened the community, having cut off proliferation, having gone to the Cetiyapabbatavihāra, do the *śramaṇa-dharma*! He, having stood in the preceptor's instruction, together with the *paṭisambhidās*, having attained arhatship, being meritorious, being honored by the king, having become surrounded by a great community of monks, lived in the Cetiyapabbatavihāra. At that time, Tissamahārāja, while doing the *uposatha* work, lived in the royal cave in Cetiyapabbata. He gave a sign to the attendant monk of the elder, "When my lord answers a question or speaks *dharma*, then give me a sign." The elder, on a certain day for hearing the *dharma*, surrounded by a community of monks, having ascended the Kaṇṭakacetiyangaṇa, having worshiped the *cetiya*, stood at the root of the Kāḷatimbarurukkha. Then a certain alms-goer elder asked him a question in the Kāḷakārāmasuttanta. The elder said, "Friend, is today the day for hearing the *dharma*?" "Yes, venerable sir, it is the day for hearing the *dharma*." "Then bring a seat. Having sat down right here, we will do the hearing of the *dharma*." Then they prepared a seat at the root of the tree and gave [it to him]. The elder, having spoken the preliminary verses, began the Kāḷakārāmasutta. That attendant youth gave the sign to the king. The king arrived while the preliminary verses were not yet finished. Having arrived, and having stood at the edge, with the appearance of a stranger, having heard the *dharma* for three watches of the night, at the time of the words "The Blessed One said this," he gave applause. The elder, having known, asked, "When did you come, great king?" "At the very time of the utterance of the preliminary verses, venerable sir." "Difficult is that which you, great king, have done." "This is not difficult, venerable sir. But if there was even one word of different intention, from the time when my lord's *dharma* talk was begun, may I not have ownership in a place even as small as the prick of a goad in Tambapaṇṇidīpa." Thus he swore an oath. In that *sūtra*, the qualities of the Buddha are clearly explained. Therefore, the king asked: “Are these all the qualities of the Buddha, venerable sir, or are there others as well?” [The Buddha replied:] "Mahārāja, what I have not spoken of is truly much, immeasurable." [The king asked:] "Venerable sir, is it possible to give a simile?" [The Buddha said:] “Mahārāja, just as in a rice field of a thousand *karīsa*s, there are many more grains of rice than on a single rice stalk, so too, the qualities I have spoken of are few, while those remaining are many." [The king asked:] "Venerable sir, is it possible to give another simile?" [The Buddha said:] "Mahārāja, imagine someone were to make an opening with a needle near the great Ganges river, which is filled with floodwater. The water that passes through the needle's opening would be little, while the remaining [water] would be much. In the same way, the qualities I have spoken of are few, while those remaining are many." [The king asked:] "Venerable sir, is it possible to give another simile?" [The Buddha said:] "Here, Mahārāja, there are birds called *cātakas* that wander about playing in the sky. That species of bird is small. Now, is the space where that bird extends its wings in the sky large, or is the remaining sky small?" [The king asked:] "What do you say, venerable sir? Is the space where it extends its wings small, while the remaining [sky] is very much?" [The Buddha said:] “In the same way, Mahārāja, the qualities of the Buddha that I have spoken of are few, while those remaining are many, endless, and immeasurable.” [The king said:] "Well spoken, venerable sir. The endless qualities of the Buddha are comparable to the endless sky." "We are pleased with the venerable one, but we are unable to do what is fitting. This humble gift of leaves is [offered so that] he might rule this kingdom of three hundred *yojana*s in this *Tambapaṇṇi* island." [The Buddha said:] “Mahārāja, you have shown your pleasure, but we will give back to you the kingdom you have given us. Rule the kingdom with righteousness and justice, Mahārāja!”

Here ends the *Mahāsaccakasuttavaṇṇanā* in the *Papañcasūdanī*, a commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

mula_pali:
390. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Atha kho sakko devānamindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hoti accantaniṭṭho accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussāna’’nti?

‘‘Idha, devānaminda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti – ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. Evañcetaṃ, devānaminda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti – ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. So sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti; sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti; sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti – sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, so tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharati, virāgānupassī viharati, nirodhānupassī viharati, paṭinissaggānupassī viharati. So tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharanto, virāgānupassī viharanto, nirodhānupassī viharanto, paṭinissaggānupassī viharanto na kiñci loke upādiyati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassati, aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Ettāvatā kho, devānaminda, bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hoti accantaniṭṭho accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussāna’’nti.

Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
mula_english:
390. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park in Migāramātā’s mansion.

Then Sakka, ruler of gods, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, stood to one side. Standing to one side, Sakka, ruler of gods, said to the Blessed One: “In how short a time, venerable sir, is a bhikkhu liberated by the destruction of craving, one who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate security from bondage, the ultimate holy life, the ultimate goal, one who is foremost among gods and humans?”

“Here, ruler of gods, a *bhikkhu* has heard that nothing is worth adhering to. Thus, ruler of gods, a *bhikkhu* has heard that nothing is worth adhering to. He directly knows everything; having directly known everything, he fully understands everything; having fully understood everything, whatever feeling (*vedanā*) he feels, whether pleasant (*sukhaṃ*) or painful (*dukkhaṃ*) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*), he abides contemplating impermanence (*anicānupassī*) in those feelings, contemplating fading away (*virāgānupassī*), contemplating cessation (*nirodhānupassī*), contemplating relinquishment (*paṭinissaggānupassī*). Contemplating thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. When he does not cling, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains *nibbana* – ‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the spiritual life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā*)’ he understands. Briefly, it is in this way, ruler of gods, that a *bhikkhu* is liberated by the destruction of craving…one who is foremost among gods and humans.”

Then Sakka, ruler of gods, delighting and rejoicing in the Blessed One’s words, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him on his right, he vanished at once.
commentary_pali:
390.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasuttaṃ. Tattha pubbārāme migāramātupāsādeti pubbārāmasaṅkhāte vihāre migāramātuyā pāsāde. Tatrāyaṃ anupubbīkathāatīte satasahassakappamatthake ekā upāsikā padumuttaraṃ bhagavantaṃ nimantetvā buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa satasahassaṃ dānaṃ datvā bhagavato pādamūle nipajjitvā, ‘‘anāgate tumhādisassa buddhassa aggupaṭṭhāyikā homī’’ti patthanamakāsi. Sā kappasatasahassaṃ devesu ceva manussesu ca saṃsaritvā amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle bhaddiyanagare meṇḍakaseṭṭhiputtassa dhanañjayassa seṭṭhino gahe sumanadeviyā kucchimhi paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhi. Jātakāle cassā visākhāti nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Sā yadā bhagavā bhaddiyanagaraṃ agamāsi, tadā pañcahi dārikāsatehi saddhiṃ bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ katvā paṭhamadassanamhiyeva sotāpannā ahosi. Aparabhāge sāvatthiyaṃ migāraseṭṭhiputtassa puṇṇavaḍḍhanakumārassa gehaṃ gatā, tattha naṃ migāraseṭṭhi mātiṭṭhāne ṭhapesi, tasmā migāramātāti vuccati.

Patikulaṃ gacchantiyā cassā pitā mahālatāpiḷandhanaṃ nāma kārāpesi. Tasmiṃ piḷandhane catasso vajiranāḷiyo upayogaṃ agamaṃsu, muttānaṃ ekādasa nāḷiyo, pavāḷānaṃ dvāvīsati nāḷiyo, maṇīnaṃ tettiṃsa nāḷiyo, iti etehi ca aññehi ca sattavaṇṇehi ratanehi niṭṭhānaṃ agamāsi. Taṃ sīse paṭimukkaṃ yāva pādapiṭṭhiyā bhassati, pañcannaṃ hatthīnaṃ balaṃ dhārayamānāva naṃ itthī dhāretuṃ sakkoti. Sā aparabhāge dasabalassa aggupaṭṭhāyikā hutvā taṃ pasādhanaṃ vissajjetvā navahi koṭīhi bhagavato vihāraṃ kārayamānā karīsamatte bhūmibhāge pāsādaṃ kāresi. Tassa uparibhūmiyaṃ pañca gabbhasatāni honti, heṭṭhābhūmiyaṃ pañcāti gabbhasahassappaṭimaṇḍito ahosi. Sā ‘‘suddhapāsādova na sobhatī’’ti taṃ parivāretvā pañca dvikūṭagehasatāni, pañca cūḷapāsādasatāni, pañca dīghasālasatāni ca kārāpesi. Vihāramaho catūhi māsehi niṭṭhānaṃ agamāsi.

mahālatāpiḷandhanaṃ

Mātugāmattabhāve ṭhitāya visākhāya viya aññissā buddhasāsane dhanapariccāgo nāma natthi, purisattabhāve ṭhitassa ca anāthapiṇḍikassa viya aññassa buddhasāsane dhanapariccāgo nāma natthi. So hi catupaññāsakoṭiyo vissajjetvā sāvatthiyā dakkhiṇabhāge anurādhapurassa mahāvihārasadise ṭhāne jetavanamahāvihāraṃ nāma kāresi. Visākhā, sāvatthiyā pācīnabhāge uttamadevīvihārasadise ṭhāne pubbārāmaṃ nāma kāresi. Bhagavā imesaṃ dvinnaṃ kulānaṃ anukampāya sāvatthiṃ nissāya viharanto imesu dvīsu vihāresu nibaddhavāsaṃ vasi. Ekaṃ antovassaṃ jetavane vasati, ekaṃ pubbārāme, etasmiṃ pana samaye bhagavā pubbārāme viharati. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde’’ti.

pubbārāmaṃ

Kittāvatānu kho, bhanteti kittakena nu kho, bhante. Saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hotīti taṇhāsaṅkhaye nibbāne taṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā vimuttacittatāya taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto nāma saṃkhittena kittāvatā hoti? Yāya paṭipattiyā taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hoti, taṃ me khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pubbabhāgappaṭipadaṃ saṃkhittena desethāti pucchati. Accantaniṭṭhoti khayavayasaṅkhātaṃ antaṃ atītāti accantā. Accantā niṭṭhā assāti accantaniṭṭho, ekantaniṭṭho satataniṭṭhoti attho. Accantaṃ yogakkhemīti accantayogakkhemī, niccayogakkhemīti attho. Accantaṃ brahmacārīti accantabrahmacārī, niccabrahmacārīti attho. Accantaṃ pariyosānamassāti purimanayeneva accantapariyosāno. Seṭṭho devamanussānanti devānañca manussānañca seṭṭho uttamo. Evarūpo bhikkhu kittāvatā hoti, khippametassa saṅkhepeneva paṭipattiṃ kathethāti bhagavantaṃ yācati. Kasmā panesa evaṃ vegāyatīti? Kīḷaṃ anubhavitukāmatāya.

Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante Saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hotī Accantaniṭṭho accantaniṭṭho, accantayogakkhemī, accantabrahmacārī, accantapariyosāno. Seṭṭho devamanussāna

Ayaṃ kira uyyānakīḷaṃ āṇāpetvā catūhi mahārājūhi catūsu disāsu ārakkhaṃ gāhāpetvā dvīsu devalokesu devasaṅghena parivuto aḍḍhatiyāhi nāṭakakoṭīhi saddhiṃ erāvaṇaṃ āruyha uyyānadvāre ṭhito imaṃ pañhaṃ sallakkhesi – ‘‘kittakena nu kho taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttassa khīṇāsavassa saṅkhepato āgamaniyapubbabhāgapaṭipadā hotī’’ti. Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ pañho ativiya sassiriko, sacāhaṃ imaṃ pañhaṃ anuggaṇhitvāva uyyānaṃ pavisissāmi, chadvārikehi ārammaṇehi nimmathito na puna imaṃ pañhaṃ sallakkhessāmi , tiṭṭhatu tāva uyyānakīḷā, satthu santikaṃ gantvā imaṃ pañhaṃ pucchitvā uggahitapañho uyyāne kīḷissāmī’’ti hatthikkhandhe antarahito bhagavato santike pāturahosi. Tepi cattāro mahārājāno ārakkhaṃ gahetvā ṭhitaṭṭhāneyeva ṭhitā, paricārikadevasaṅghāpi nāṭakānipi erāvaṇopi nāgarājā tattheva uyyānadvāre aṭṭhāsi, evamesa kīḷaṃ anubhavitukāmatāya vegāyanto evamāha.

Sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyāti ettha sabbe dhammā nāma pañcakkhandhā dvādasāyatanāni aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo. Te sabbepi taṇhādiṭṭhivasena abhinivesāya nālaṃ na pariyattā na samatthā na yuttā, kasmā? Gahitākārena atiṭṭhanato. Te hi niccāti gahitāpi aniccāva sampajjanti, sukhāti gahitāpi dukkhāva sampajjanti, attāti gahitāpi anattāva sampajjanti, tasmā nālaṃ abhinivesāya. Abhijānātīti aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti ñātapariññāya abhijānāti. Parijānātīti tatheva tīraṇapariññāya parijānāti. Yaṃkiñci vedananti antamaso pañcaviññāṇasampayuttampi yaṃkiñci appamattakampi vedanaṃ anubhavati. Iminā bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa vedanāvasena nibbattetvā arūpapariggahaṃ dasseti. Sace pana vedanākammaṭṭhānaṃ heṭṭhā na kathitaṃ bhaveyya, imasmiṃ ṭhāne kathetabbaṃ siyā. Heṭṭhā pana kathitaṃ, tasmā satipaṭṭhāne vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Aniccānupassīti ettha aniccaṃ veditabbaṃ, aniccānupassanā veditabbā, aniccānupassī veditabbo. Tattha aniccanti pañcakkhandhā, te hi uppādavayaṭṭhena aniccā. Aniccānupassanāti pañcakkhandhānaṃ khayato vayato dassanañāṇaṃ. Aniccānupassīti tena ñāṇena samannāgato puggalo . Tasmā ‘‘aniccānupassī viharatī’’ti aniccato anupassanto viharatīti ayamettha attho.

Sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā Abhijānātī Parijānātī Yaṃkiñci vedana Aniccānupassī anicca Aniccānupassanā Aniccānupassī

Virāgānupassīti ettha dve virāgā khayavirāgo ca accantavirāgo ca. Tattha saṅkhārānaṃ khayavayato anupassanāpi, accantavirāgaṃ nibbānaṃ virāgato dassanamaggañāṇampi virāgānupassanā. Tadubhayasamāṅgīpuggalo virāgānupassī nāma, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘virāgānupassī’’ti, virāgato anupassantoti attho. Nirodhānupassimhipi eseva nayo, nirodhopi hi khayanirodho ca accantanirodho cāti duvidhoyeva. Paṭinissaggānupassīti ettha paṭinissaggo vuccati vossaggo, so ca pariccāgavossaggo pakkhandanavossaggoti duvidho hoti . Tattha pariccāgavossaggoti vipassanā, sā hi tadaṅgavasena kilese ca khandhe ca vossajjati. Pakkhandanavossaggoti maggo, so hi nibbānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ ārammaṇato pakkhandati. Dvīhipi vā kāraṇehi vossaggoyeva, samucchedavasena khandhānaṃ kilesānañca vossajjanato, nibbānañca pakkhandanato. Tasmā kilese ca khandhe ca pariccajatīti pariccāgavossaggo, nirodhe nibbānadhātuyā cittaṃ pakkhandatīti pakkhandanavossaggoti ubhayampetaṃ magge sameti. Tadubhayasamaṅgīpuggalo imāya paṭinissaggānupassanāya samannāgatattā paṭinissaggānupassī nāma hoti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘paṭinissaggānupassī’’ti. Na kiñci loke upādiyatīti kiñci ekampi saṅkhāragataṃ taṇhāvasena na upādiyati na gaṇhāti na parāmasati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassatīti aggaṇhanto taṇhāparitassanāya na paritassati. Paccattaññeva parinibbāyatīti sayameva kilesaparinibbānena parinibbāyati. Khīṇā jātītiādinā panassa paccavekkhaṇāva dassitā. Iti bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa saṃkhittena khīṇāsavassa pubbabhāgappaṭipadaṃ pucchito sallahukaṃ katvā saṃkhitteneva khippaṃ kathesi.

Virāgānupassī virāgānupassanā Nirodhānupassi Paṭinissaggānupassī paṭinissaggo pariccāgavossaggo Pakkhandanavossaggo Na kiñci loke upādiyatī Anupādiyaṃ na paritassatī Paccattaññeva parinibbāyatī Khīṇā jātī
commentary_english:
390. Thus I have heard: the Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasuttaṃ.

There, Pubbārāme Migāramātupāsāde means in the monastery known as Pūrvārāma, in the palace of Migāramātā.

There, this sequential account [begins]: In the distant past, hundreds of thousands of eons ago, a female lay follower invited the Blessed One Padumuttara and, having given a hundred thousand donations to the Saṃgha of monks with the Buddha at its head, knelt at the feet of the Blessed One, and made the aspiration, “In the future, may I become the foremost attendant of a Buddha like you."

Having transmigrated among gods and humans for hundreds of thousands of eons, at the time of our Blessed One, she took rebirth in Bhaddiyanagara, in the womb of Sumanadevī, the wife of the wealthy merchant Dhanañjaya, son of Meṇḍaka.

At the time of her birth, they gave her the name Visākhā.

When the Blessed One arrived in Bhaddiyanagara, she went to greet the Blessed One with five hundred girls, and at her first sight, she became a stream-enterer (sotāpanna).

Later, she went to the house of Puṇṇavaḍḍhanakumāra, the son of the wealthy merchant Migāra, in Śrāvastī. There, Migāra the merchant placed her in the position of a mother, therefore she is called Migāramātā.

When she went to her husband's family, her father had a Mahālatāpiḷandhana made.

In that Piḷandhana, four diamond pipes were used, eleven pipes of pearls, twenty-two pipes of corals, thirty-three pipes of jewels, thus it reached completion with these and other seven-colored jewels.

When it was placed on her head, it reached down to the surface of her feet; only a woman possessing the strength of five elephants could bear it.

Later, having become the chief attendant of the Ten-Powered One, she spent that adornment, and while having a monastery built for the Blessed One with nine koṭis, she had a palace built on an area equal to a karīsa.

In the upper story of that, there were five hundred chambers; on the lower story, there were five, so it was adorned with a thousand chambers.

Thinking, "A mere palace does not look good," she surrounded it with five hundred two-peaked houses, five hundred smaller palaces, and five hundred long halls.

The monastery festival reached completion in four months.

Mahālatāpiḷandhana

In the state of being a woman, there was no other in the Buddha’s Dispensation like Visākhā who gave donations of wealth, and in the state of being a man, there was no other in the Buddha’s Dispensation like Anāthapiṇḍika who gave donations of wealth.

For he, having spent fifty-four koṭis, had a monastery built called Jetavanamahāvihāra in the southern part of Śrāvastī, in a place similar to the Mahāvihāra of Anurādhapura.

Visākhā had a monastery built called Pūrvārāma in the eastern part of Śrāvastī, in a place similar to the Uttamadevī Monastery.

The Blessed One, out of compassion for these two families, dwelling near Śrāvastī, spent the rainy season in these two monasteries.

One rainy season he dwells in Jetavana, one in Pūrvārāma. In this time, the Blessed One dwells in Pūrvārāma.

Therefore it was said - "In Pūrvārāma, in the palace of Migāramātā."

Pūrvārāma

"How much, O Bhante?" means by how much, O Bhante.

"In brief, he is liberated by the cessation of craving," means by making that cessation of craving, Nirvāṇa, the object [of his meditation], by the liberation of his mind, how much is he liberated by the cessation of craving in brief? With whatever practice he is liberated by the cessation of craving, please teach me that preliminary practice of a monk who has destroyed the āsavas in brief," he asks.

"Accantaniṭṭho" means because it has gone beyond the end defined by decay and destruction, it is accantā.

Because accantā is the niṭṭhā, it is Accantaniṭṭho, Ekantaniṭṭho, Satataniṭṭho, is the meaning.

"Accantaṃ yogakkhemīti" means "Accantayogakkhemī," "niccayogakkhemīti," is the meaning.

"Accantaṃ brahmacārīti" means "Accantabrahmacārī," "niccabrahmacārīti," is the meaning.

"Accantaṃ pariyosānamassāti" means "Accantapariyosāno" by the same method as before.

"Seṭṭho devamanussāna" means "Seṭṭho uttamo" of gods and humans.

"How much is a monk of such a form, quickly tell me about his practice in brief," he asks the Blessed One.

Why does he hasten thus? Because of his desire to experience play.
"Surely, venerable sir, is one succinctly liberated through the destruction of craving," utterly complete, utterly complete, utterly secure from bondage, utterly practicing the holy life, utterly perfect.

The best of gods and humans, this one, having ordered a pleasure garden and having had the four great kings take charge of protection in the four directions, surrounded by a host of deities in the two celestial realms, together with two and a half million troupes of actors, mounted Erāvaṇa, ascended to the garden gate, stood there, and reflected on this question: "By how much is the practice leading to the prior part of the path attainable in summary by one liberated through the destruction of craving, whose āsavas are destroyed?"

Then this occurred to him: "This question is exceedingly splendid. If, without first grasping this question, I enter the pleasure garden, overwhelmed by objects through the six doorways, I will not again reflect on this question.

Let the pleasure garden remain for now. Having gone to the presence of the Teacher, having asked this question, and having understood the question, I will enjoy myself in the pleasure garden." Immediately, having vanished from the elephant's shoulder, he appeared in the presence of the Blessed One.

Those four great kings, too, having taken charge of protection, stood right there in their respective places. The retinues of serving deities, the troupes of actors, Erāvaṇa, and the Nāga king all stood right there at the garden gate. Thus, eager to experience the pleasure, hurrying, he spoke thus:

All phenomena are not worth adhering to," here, all phenomena, namely, are the five aggregates (pañcakkhandhā), the twelve sources (dvādasāyatanāni), and the eighteen elements (aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo).

All of those, too, are not adequate, not sufficient, not capable, not fit for adhering to due to not remaining in the manner they are grasped. Why? Because they do not persist in the way they are grasped.

Those phenomena, even grasped as permanent (nicca), become impermanent (anicca); even grasped as pleasure (sukha), become suffering (dukkha); even grasped as self (attā), become not-self (anattā). Therefore, they are not worth adhering to.

"He understands completely (abhijānātī)," means he understands completely through the knowledge of discernment that they are impermanent (aniccaṃ), suffering (dukkhaṃ), and not-self (anattā).

"He comprehends completely (parijānātī)," means he comprehends completely through the determining comprehension in just that way.

"Whatever feeling (yaṃkiñci vedana)," means whatever feeling, even the slightest, that one experiences, even connected with the five types of sensory consciousness.

By this, the Blessed One, having manifested it through the feeling-aspect of Śakka, the lord of the gods, shows the non-apprehension of form.

If, however, the feeling-contemplation had not been spoken of below, it would be appropriate to speak of it in this place.

However, it was spoken of below; therefore, it should be understood in just the manner spoken of in the mindfulness foundations.

"Observing impermanence (aniccānupassī)," here, impermanence (aniccaṃ) should be understood, the observation of impermanence (aniccānupassanā) should be understood, and the one observing impermanence (aniccānupassī) should be understood.

There, "impermanence (aniccaṃ)" refers to the five aggregates (pañcakkhandhā). They are impermanent due to having the characteristic of arising and passing away (uppādavayaṭṭhena).

"The observation of impermanence (aniccānupassanā)" is the knowledge of seeing the aggregates as decaying and vanishing.

"The one observing impermanence (aniccānupassī)" is the person who is endowed with that knowledge.

Therefore, "he dwells observing impermanence (aniccānupassī viharati)," means he dwells observing impermanence from [the perspective of] impermanence. This is the meaning here.

All phenomena are not worth adhering to.

He understands completely. He comprehends completely. Whatever feeling. He observes impermanence. Impermanence. Observation of impermanence. He observes impermanence.

"Observing dispassion (virāgānupassī)," here, there are two kinds of dispassion: the dispassion of destruction (khayavirāgo) and the ultimate dispassion (accantavirāgo).

There, the observation of the passing away and vanishing of conditioned phenomena (saṅkhārānaṃ), and the knowledge of the path seeing nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ), the ultimate dispassion, from dispassion, is "observing dispassion (virāgānupassanā)."

A person complete with both of those is called one who observes dispassion (virāgānupassī). With reference to that, it was said, "observing dispassion (virāgānupassī)," meaning he observes dispassion from [the perspective of] dispassion.

The same method applies to "observing cessation (nirodhānupassī)," for cessation (nirodho), too, is just twofold: cessation by destruction (khayanirodho) and ultimate cessation (accantanirodho).

"Observing relinquishment (paṭinissaggānupassī)," here, relinquishment (paṭinissaggo) is said to be abandonment (vossaggo), and that is twofold: abandonment by renunciation (pariccāgavossaggo) and abandonment by ejection (pakkhandanavossaggoti).

There, "abandonment by renunciation (pariccāgavossaggo)" is insight (vipassanā), for that abandons both the defilements (kilese) and the aggregates (khandhe) by way of their respective aspects.

"Abandonment by ejection (pakkhandanavossaggo)" is the path (maggo), for that ejects toward nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ) as its object (ārammaṇaṃ), from [the perspective of] its object.

Abandonment is indeed [accomplished] by those two causes: by abandoning the aggregates and defilements through the force of complete destruction, and by ejecting toward nirvāṇa.

Therefore, "he relinquishes both the defilements and the aggregates," [this] is abandonment by renunciation (pariccāgavossaggo). "In cessation (nirodhe), consciousness (cittaṃ) ejects toward the element of nirvāṇa (nibbānadhātuyā)," [this] is abandonment by ejection (pakkhandanavossaggoti). Both of these come together in the path (magge).

A person complete with both of those, due to being endowed with this observation of relinquishment (paṭinissaggānupassanāya), is called one who observes relinquishment (paṭinissaggānupassī).

With reference to that, it was said, "observing relinquishment (paṭinissaggānupassī)."

"He clings to nothing in the world (na kiñci loke upādiyatī)," means he does not cling to, grasp, or touch anything at all pertaining to conditioned phenomena (saṅkhāragataṃ) through the force of craving (taṇhāvasena).
<hi rend="bold">Anupādiyaṃ na paritassatī</hi>ti, because he does not grasp, he is not disturbed by the disturbance of craving.

<hi rend="bold">Paccattaññeva parinibbāyatī</hi>ti, he himself attains *Nirvāṇa* by the *Nirvāṇa* of defilements.

<hi rend="bold">Khīṇā jātī</hi>tiādinā panassa paccavekkhaṇāva dassitā.

Thus, the Blessed One, being asked by Śakra, the lord of the gods, about the preliminary practice of one whose *āsavas* are destroyed, having made it light, quickly spoke in brief.
