mula_pali: 391. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti. Atha kho āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa etadahosi – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho so yakkho bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhisamecca anumodi udāhu no; yaṃnūnāhaṃ taṃ yakkhaṃ jāneyyaṃ – yadi vā so yakkho bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhisamecca anumodi yadi vā no’’ti? Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde antarahito devesu tāvatiṃsesu pāturahosi. Tena kho pana samayena sakko devānamindo ekapuṇḍarīke uyyāne dibbehi pañcahi tūriyasatehi turiyasatehi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Addasā kho sakko devānamindo āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna tāni dibbāni pañca tūriyasatāni paṭippaṇāmetvā yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ehi kho, mārisa moggallāna, svāgataṃ, mārisa moggallāna! Cirassaṃ kho, mārisa moggallāna, imaṃ pariyāyaṃ akāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīda, mārisa moggallāna, idamāsanaṃ paññatta’’nti. Nisīdi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno paññatte āsane. Sakkopi kho devānamindo aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca – ‘‘yathā kathaṃ pana kho, kosiya, bhagavā saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṃ abhāsi? Sādhu mayampi etissā kathāya bhāgino assāma savanāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
Now on that occasion the venerable Mahā Moggallāna was sitting not far from the Blessed One.

Then it occurred to the venerable Mahā Moggallāna: “Did that spirit penetrate to the meaning of the Blessed One’s words when he rejoiced, or did he not? Suppose I found out whether he did or not.” Then, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, the venerable Maha Moggallana vanished from the Palace of Migara’s Mother in the Eastern Park and appeared among the gods of the Thirty-three.

Now on that occasion Sakka, ruler of gods, was furnished and endowed a hundredfold with the five kinds of heavenly music, and he was enjoying it in the Pleasure Park of the Single Lotus.

When he saw the venerable Maha Moggallana coming in the distance, he dismissed the music, went to the venerable Maha Moggallana, and said to him: “Come, good sir Moggallana! Welcome, good sir Moggallana! It is long, good sir Moggallana, since you found an opportunity to come here. Sit down, good sir Moggallana; this seat is ready.”

The venerable Maha Moggallana sat down on the seat made ready. And Sakka, ruler of gods, took a low seat and sat down at one side.

The venerable Maha Moggallana then asked Sakka, ruler of gods, who was sitting to one side: “Kosiya, how did the Blessed One state to you in brief deliverance through the destruction of craving (**taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutti**)? It would be good if we too might have a share in this talk, for listening.”
commentary_pali:
391.Avidūre nisinno hotīti anantare kūṭāgāre nisinno hoti. Abhisameccāti ñāṇena abhisamāgantvā, jānitvāti attho. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – kiṃ nu kho esa jānitvā anumodi, udāhu ajānitvā vāti. Kasmā panassa evamahosīti? Thero kira na bhagavato pañhavissajjanasaddaṃ assosi, sakkassa pana devarañño, ‘‘evametaṃ bhagavā evametaṃ sugatā’’ti anumodanasaddaṃ assosi. Sakko kira devarājā mahatā saddena anumodi. Atha kasmā na bhagavato saddaṃ assosīti? Yathāparisaviññāpakattā. Buddhānañhi dhammaṃ kathentānaṃ ekābaddhāya cakkavāḷapariyantāyapi parisāya saddo suyyati, pariyantaṃ pana muñcitvā aṅgulimattampi bahiddhā na niccharati. Kasmā? Evarūpā madhurakathā mā niratthakā agamāsīti. Tadā bhagavā migāramātupāsāde sattaratanamaye kūṭāgāre sirigabbhamhi nisinno hoti, tassa dakkhiṇapasse sāriputtattherassa vasanakūṭāgāraṃ, vāmapasse mahāmoggallānassa, antare chiddavivarokāso natthi, tasmā thero na bhagavato saddaṃ assosi, sakkasseva assosīti.

Pañcahitūriyasatehīti pañcaṅgikānaṃ tūriyānaṃ pañcahi satehi. Pañcaṅgikaṃ tūriyaṃ nāma ātataṃ vitataṃ ātatavitataṃ susiraṃ ghananti imehi pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgataṃ. Tattha ātataṃ nāma cammapariyonaddhesu bheriādīsu ekatalatūriyaṃ. Vitataṃ nāma ubhayatalaṃ. Ātatavitataṃ nāma tantibaddhapaṇavādi. Susiraṃ vaṃsādi. Ghanaṃ sammādi. Samappitoti upagato. Samaṅgībhūtoti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Paricāretīti taṃ sampattiṃ anubhavanto tato tato indriyāni cāreti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – parivāretvā vajjamānehi pañcahi tūriyasatehi samannāgato hutvā dibbasampattiṃ anubhavatī. Paṭipaṇāmetvāti apanetvā, nissaddāni kārāpetvāti attho. Yatheva hi idāni saddhā rājāno garubhāvaniyaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā – ‘‘asuko nāma ayyo āgacchati, mā, tātā, gāyatha, mā vādetha, mā naccathā’’ti nāṭakāni paṭivinenti, sakkopi theraṃ disvā evamakāsi. Cirassaṃ kho, mārisa moggallāna, imaṃ pariyāyamakāsīti evarūpaṃ loke pakatiyā piyasamudāhāravacanaṃ hoti, lokiyā hi cirassaṃ āgatampi anāgatapubbampi manāpajātiyaṃ āgataṃ disvā, – ‘‘kuto bhavaṃ āgato, cirassaṃ bhavaṃ āgato, kathaṃ te idhāgamanamaggo ñāto maggamūḷhosī’’tiādīni vadanti. Ayaṃ pana āgatapubbattāyeva evamāha. Thero hi kālena kālaṃ devacārikaṃ gacchatiyeva. Tattha pariyāyamakāsīti vāramakāsi. Yadidaṃ idhāgamanāyāti yo ayaṃ idhāgamanāya vāro, taṃ, bhante, cirassamakāsīti vuttaṃ hoti. Idamāsanaṃ paññattanti yojanikaṃ maṇipallaṅkaṃ paññapāpetvā evamāha.

Pañcahi tūriyasatehī ātataṃ Vitataṃ Ātatavitataṃ Susiraṃ Ghanaṃ Samappito Samaṅgībhūto Paricāretī Paṭipaṇāmetvā Cirassaṃ kho, mārisa moggallāna, imaṃ pariyāyamakāsī pariyāyamakāsī Yadidaṃ idhāgamanāyā Idamāsanaṃ paññatta
commentary_english:
391. "Having sat not far away (avidūre nisinno hotī)" means having sat in a nearby upper chamber (anantare kūṭāgāre nisinno hoti).

"Having understood (abhisameccā)" means having approached with knowledge (ñāṇena abhisamāgantvā), the meaning is "having known (jānitvāti attho)."

This was said: "Did he approve having known (jānitvā anumodi), or, having not known (ajānitvā vāti)?"

Why did that happen to him (kasmā panassa evamahosīti)? The elder (thero) did not hear the sound of the Blessed One's (bhagavato) answering of the question (pañhavissajjanasaddaṃ assosi), but he heard the approving sound (anumodanasaddaṃ assosi) of Sakka (sakkassa), the king of the gods (devarañño), [saying,] "Thus it is, Blessed One (evametaṃ bhagavā), thus it is, Sugata (evametaṃ sugatā)!"

Sakka (sakko), the king of the gods (devarājā), approved with a great sound (mahatā saddena anumodi).

Then why (atha kasmā) did he not hear the sound (saddaṃ assosīti) of the Blessed One (bhagavato)? Because of [his] capacity to make known (yathāparisaviññāpakattā) to the assembly (parisa).

For when Buddhas (buddhānañhi) are teaching the Dharma (dhammaṃ kathentānaṃ), the sound (saddo) is heard (suyyati) by an assembly (parisāya) contained within a single, unbroken (ekābaddhāya) *cakravāḷa*; but having released the boundary (pariyantaṃ pana muñcitvā), not even an *aṅguli*’s worth (aṅgulimattampi) goes forth outside (bahiddhā na niccharati).

Why (kasmā)? [It is] so that such sweet talk (evarūpā madhurakathā) might not go without meaning (mā niratthakā agamāsīti).

At that time (tadā) the Blessed One (bhagavā) was sitting (nisinno hoti) in the *Migāramātupāsāda* (migāramātupāsāde), in the jeweled (sattaratanamaye) upper chamber (kūṭāgāre), in the *sirigabbha* (sirigabbhamhi); on his right side (dakkhiṇapasse) was the dwelling-upper chamber (vasanakūṭāgāraṃ) of the elder (therassa) Sāriputta (sāriputtattherassa), on the left side (vāmapasse) [was that] of Mahāmoggallāna (mahāmoggallānassa); in between (antare) there was no (natthi) opportunity for a hole or opening (chiddavivarokāso), therefore (tasmā) the elder (thero) did not hear (na bhagavato saddaṃ assosi) the sound (saddaṃ assosi) of the Blessed One (bhagavato), but he heard (sakkasseva assosīti) [that] of Sakka (sakkassa).

With the five (pañcahi) [kinds of] instruments (tūriyasatehī): *pañcaṅgika*, with the five hundred (pañcahi satehi) instruments (tūriyānaṃ).

The *pañcaṅgika tūriya* (pañcaṅgikaṃ tūriyaṃ) is named (nāma): *ātataṃ, vitataṃ, ātatavitataṃ, susiraṃ, ghananti*; it is endowed (samannāgataṃ) with these five (imehi pañcahi) limbs (aṅgehi).

There (tattha), *ātataṃ* (ātataṃ) is named (nāma) [as] the single-sided (ekatalatūriyaṃ) instrument (tūriyaṃ) in drums (bheriādīsu) covered with hide (cammapariyonaddhesu).

*Vitataṃ* (vitataṃ) is named (nāma) [as] two-sided (ubhayatalaṃ).

*Ātatavitataṃ* (ātatavitataṃ) is named (nāma) [as] a stringed (tantibaddha) instrument (paṇavādi).

*Susiraṃ* (susiraṃ) [is] flute (vaṃsādi).

*Ghanaṃ* (ghanaṃ) [is] cymbals (sammādi).

*Samappito* (samappito) means (ti) approached (upagato).

*Samaṅgībhūto* (samaṅgībhūto) means (ti) a synonym (tasseva vevacanaṃ) of that.

*Paricāretī* (paricāretī) means (ti) experiencing (anubhavanto) that (taṃ) success (sampattiṃ), he moves (cāreti) the senses (indriyāni) from here and there (tato tato).

This was said (idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti): having surrounded (parivāretvā), having become one who possesses (samannāgato hutvā) the five hundred (pañcahi tūriyasatehi) instruments (vajjamānehi tūriyasatehi), she experiences (anubhavatī) divine success (dibbasampattiṃ).

*Paṭipaṇāmetvā* (paṭipaṇāmetvā) means (ti) having removed (apanetvā), having caused (kārāpetvāti) [them] to be without sound (nissaddāni), [this is the] meaning (attho).

Just as (yatheva hi) now (idāni) faithful (saddhā) kings (rājāno), having seen (disvā) a monk (bhikkhuṃ) worthy of respect (garubhāvaniyaṃ) – "A certain (asuko) *ayya* (nāma ayyo) is coming (āgacchati), don't, dear ones (mā, tātā), sing (gāyatha), don't play (mā vādetha), don't dance (mā naccathā)" – they stop (paṭivinenti) the plays (nāṭakāni), just so (evam) Sakka (sakkopi), having seen (disvā) the elder (theraṃ), did (akāsi).

"For a long time (cirassaṃ kho), *mārisa* Moggallāna (moggallāna), [you] made (pariyāyamakāsī) this turn (imaṃ pariyāyaṃ)!" Thus (iti) is (hoti) a word of affectionate greeting (piyasamudāhāravacanaṃ) according to nature (pakatiyā) in the world (loke), for worldly people (lokiyā hi), having seen (disvā) one who has come (āgatampi) after a long time (cirassaṃ), or one who has never come before (anāgatapubbampi), [or] one who has come (āgataṃ) of a pleasing sort (manāpajātiyaṃ), – "From where (kuto) have you (bhavaṃ) come (āgato), for a long time (cirassaṃ) [you] (bhavaṃ) have come (āgato), how (kathaṃ) is this path (maggo) of your coming here (idhāgamanamaggo) known (ñāto), [or] have you become lost (maggamūḷhosī)?" – they say (vadanti) things such as (ādīni) this.

But (pana) this one (ayaṃ) speaks thus (evamāha) just because of [his] having come before (āgatapubbattāyeva).

For the elder (thero hi) goes (gacchatiyeva) to the world of the gods (devacārikaṃ) from time to time (kālena kālaṃ).

There (tattha), "*pariyāyamakāsī*" (pariyāyamakāsī) means (ti) he made (akāsi) a turn (vāraṃ).

"*yadidaṃ idhāgamanāyā*" (yadidaṃ idhāgamanāyā) means (ti): "this (yo ayaṃ) turn (vāro) for coming here (idhāgamanāya), that (taṃ), *bhante*, [you] made (cirassamakāsīti vuttaṃ hoti) after a long time (cirassaṃ)!"

"*idamāsanaṃ paññatta*" (idamāsanaṃ paññatta) means (nti) having prepared (paññapāpetvā) a jeweled couch (maṇipallaṅkaṃ) [that is] a *yojanika* (yojanikaṃ), he speaks thus (evamāha).

mula_pali: 392. ‘‘Mayaṃ kho, mārisa moggallāna, bahukiccā bahukaraṇīyā – appeva sakena karaṇīyena, api ca devānaṃyeva tāvatiṃsānaṃ karaṇīyena. Api ca, mārisa moggallāna, sussutaṃyeva hoti suggahitaṃ sumanasikataṃ sūpadhāritaṃ, yaṃ no khippameva antaradhāyati. Bhūtapubbaṃ, mārisa moggallāna, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho samūpabyuḷho (syā. kaṃ.), samūpabbūḷho (sī.) ahosi. Tasmiṃ kho pana, mārisa moggallāna, saṅgāme devā jiniṃsu, asurā parājiniṃsu. So kho ahaṃ, mārisa moggallāna, taṃ saṅgāmaṃ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tato paṭinivattitvā vejayantaṃ nāma pāsādaṃ māpesiṃ. Vejayantassa kho, mārisa moggallāna, pāsādassa ekasataṃ niyyūhaṃ. Ekekasmiṃ niyyūhe satta satta kūṭāgārasatāni. Ekamekasmiṃ kūṭāgāre satta satta accharāyo . Ekamekissā accharāya satta satta paricārikāyo. Iccheyyāsi no tvaṃ , mārisa moggallāna, vejayantassa pāsādassa rāmaṇeyyakaṃ daṭṭhu’’nti? Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno tuṇhībhāvena.
mula_english:
“Good sir Moggallāna, we are so busy, we have so much to do, not only with our own business, but also with the business of the gods of the Thirty-three.

And furthermore, good sir Moggallāna, it is well-heard, well-grasped, well-considered, and well-understood, which does not quickly disappear.

Good sir Moggallana, it once happened that war broke out between the gods (**deva**) and the titans (**asura**).

In that war the gods (**deva**) won and the titans (**asura**) were defeated.

So, good sir Moggallāna, having completely conquered that war, a victor in battle, then returning from there, I had the Vejayanta Palace built.

Good sir Moggallana, the Vejayanta Palace has one hundred towers (**niyyūhaṃ**).

Each tower (**niyyūhe**) has seven hundred upper chambers (**kūṭāgārasatāni**).

Each upper chamber (**kūṭāgāre**) has seven nymphs (**accharāyo**).

Each nymph (**accharāya**) has seven maids (**paricārikāyo**).

Would you like, good sir Moggallāna, to see the beauty (**rāmaṇeyyakaṃ**) of the Vejayanta Palace?" The venerable Mahāmoggallāna consented in silence (**tuṇhībhāvena**).
commentary_pali:
392.Bahukiccā bahukaraṇīyāti ettha yesaṃ bahūni kiccāni, te bahukiccā. Bahukaraṇīyāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Appeva sakena karaṇīyenāti sakaraṇīyameva appaṃ mandaṃ, na bahu, devānaṃ karaṇīyaṃ pana bahu, pathavito paṭṭhāya hi kapparukkhamātugāmādīnaṃ atthāya aṭṭā sakkassa santike chijjanti, tasmā niyamento āha – apica devānaṃyeva tāvatiṃsānaṃ karaṇīyenāti. Devānañhi dhītā ca puttā ca aṅke nibbattanti, pādaparicārikā itthiyo sayane nibbattanti, tāsaṃ maṇḍanapasādhanakārikā devadhītā sayanaṃ parivāretvā nibbattanti, veyyāvaccakarā antovimāne nibbattanti, etesaṃ atthāya aṭṭakaraṇaṃ natthi. Ye pana sīmantare nibbattanti, te ‘‘mama santakā tava santakā’’ti nicchetuṃ asakkontā aṭṭaṃ karonti, sakkaṃ devarājānaṃ pucchanti, so yassa vimānaṃ āsannataraṃ, tassa santakoti vadati. Sace dvepi samaṭṭhāne honti, yassa vimānaṃ olokento ṭhito, tassa santakoti vadati. Sace ekampi na oloketi, taṃ ubhinnaṃ kalahupacchedanatthaṃ attano santakaṃ karoti. Taṃ sandhāya, ‘‘devānaṃyeva tāvatiṃsānaṃ karaṇīyenā’’ti āha. Apicassa evarūpaṃ kīḷākiccampi karaṇīyameva.

Yaṃno khippameva antaradhāyatīti yaṃ amhākaṃ sīghameva andhakāre rūpagataṃ viya na dissati. Iminā – ‘‘ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ pañhavissajjanaṃ na sallakkhemī’’ti dīpeti. Thero – ‘‘kasmā nu kho ayaṃ yakkho asallakkhaṇabhāvaṃ dīpeti, passena pariharatī’’ti āvajjanto – ‘‘devā nāma mahāmūḷhā honti. Chadvārikehi ārammaṇehi nimmathīyamānā attano bhuttābhuttabhāvampi pītāpītabhāvampi na jānanti, idha katamettha pamussantī’’ti aññāsi. Keci panāhu – ‘‘thero etassa garu bhāvaniyo, tasmā ‘idāneva loke aggapuggalassa santike pañhaṃ uggahetvā āgato, idāneva nāṭakānaṃ antaraṃ paviṭṭhoti evaṃ maṃ thero tajjeyyā’ti bhayena evamāhā’’ti. Etaṃ pana kohaññaṃ nāma hoti, na ariyasāvakassa evarūpaṃ kohaññaṃ nāma hoti, tasmā mūḷhabhāveneva na sallakkhesīti veditabbaṃ. Upari kasmā sallakkhesīti? Thero tassa somanassasaṃvegaṃ janayitvā tamaṃ nīhari, tasmā sallakkhesīti.

Yaṃ no khippameva antaradhāyatī

Idāni sakko pubbe attano evaṃ bhūtakāraṇaṃ therassa ārocetuṃ bhūtapubbantiādimāha. Tattha samupabyūḷhoti sannipatito rāsibhūto. Asurā parājiniṃsūti asurā parājayaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Kadā panete parājitāti? Sakkassa nibbattakāle. Sakko kira anantare attabhāve magadharaṭṭhe macalagāme magho nāma māṇavo ahosi, paṇḍito byatto, bodhisattacariyā viyassa cariyā ahosi. So tettiṃsa purise gahetvā kalyāṇamakāsi. Ekadivasaṃ attanova paññāya upaparikkhitvā gāmamajjhe mahājanassa sannipatitaṭṭhāne kacavaraṃ ubhayato apabbahitvā taṃ ṭhānaṃ atiramaṇīyamakāsi, puna tattheva maṇḍapaṃ kāresi, puna gacchante kāle sālaṃ kāresi. Gāmato ca nikkhamitvā gāvutampi aḍḍhayojanampi tigāvutampi yojanampi vicaritvā tehi sahāyehi saddhiṃ visamaṃ samaṃ akāsi. Te sabbepi ekacchandā tattha tattha setuyuttaṭṭhānesu setuṃ, maṇḍapasālāpokkharaṇīmālāgaccharopanādīnaṃ yuttaṭṭhānesu maṇḍapādīni karontā bahuṃ puññamakaṃsu . Magho satta vatapadāni pūretvā kāyassa bhedā saddhiṃ sahāyehi tāvatiṃsabhavane nibbatti.

bhūtapubba samupabyūḷho Asurā parājiniṃsū magho

Tasmiṃ kāle asuragaṇā tāvatiṃsadevaloke paṭivasanti. Sabbe te devānaṃ samānāyukā samānavaṇṇā ca honti, te sakkaṃ saparisaṃ disvā adhunā nibbattā navakadevaputtā āgatāti mahāpānaṃ sajjayiṃsu. Sakko devaputtānaṃ saññaṃ adāsi – ‘‘amhehi kusalaṃ karontehi na parehi saddhiṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kataṃ, tumhe gaṇḍapānaṃ mā pivittha pītamattameva karothā’’ti. Te tathā akaṃsu. Bālaasurā gaṇḍapānaṃ pivitvā mattā niddaṃ okkamiṃsu. Sakko devānaṃ saññaṃ datvā te pādesu gāhāpetvā sinerupāde khipāpesi, sinerussa heṭṭhimatale asurabhavanaṃ nāma atthi, tāvatiṃsadevalokappamāṇameva. Tattha asurā vasanti. Tesampi cittapāṭali nāma rukkho atthi. Te tassa pupphanakāle jānanti – ‘‘nāyaṃ tāvatiṃsā, sakkena vañcitā maya’’nti. Te gaṇhatha nanti vatvā sineruṃ pariharamānā deve vuṭṭhe vammikapādato vammikamakkhikā viya abhiruhiṃsu. Tattha kālena devā jinanti, kālena asurā. Yadā devānaṃ jayo hoti, asure yāva samuddapiṭṭhā anubandhanti. Yadā asurānaṃ jayo hoti, deve yāva vedikapādā anubandhanti. Tasmiṃ pana saṅgāme devānaṃ jayo ahosi, devā asure yāva samuddapiṭṭhā anubandhiṃsu. Sakko asure palāpetvā pañcasu ṭhānesu ārakkhaṃ ṭhapesi. Evaṃ ārakkhaṃ datvā vedikapāde vajirahatthā indapaṭimāyo ṭhapesi. Asurā kālena kālaṃ uṭṭhahitvā tā paṭimāyo disvā, ‘‘sakko appamatto tiṭṭhatī’’ti tatova nivattanti. Tato paṭinivattitvāti vijitaṭṭhānato nivattitvā. Paricārikāyoti mālāgandhādikammakārikāyo.

asurabhavanaṃ cittapāṭali Tato paṭinivattitvā Paricārikāyo
commentary_english:
392. “*Bahukiccā bahukaraṇīyā*”: Here, those who have many tasks are *bahukiccā*.
"*Bahukaraṇīyā*" is a synonym of that.
"*Appeva sakena karaṇīyenā*": *Sakaraniīyameva* is a little, weak, not much. But the tasks of the gods are many. For, starting from the earth, in the vicinity of Śakra, judgments are made for the sake of wish-fulfilling trees, women, and so on. Therefore, defining it, he said: “Moreover, the tasks of the *Trāyastriṃśa* gods themselves [are many]."
For daughters and sons are born in the lap of the gods; women as attendants are born in beds; goddesses who beautify and adorn them are born surrounding the bed; those who do service are born in inner palaces. There is no judgment-making for the sake of these.
But those who are born at the boundary, being unable to decide “Mine, yours,” make a judgment. They ask Śakra, the king of gods. He says, “Whose chariot is nearer, that is whose.”
If two are in the same location, [he says,] “Whose chariot he is looking at, standing, that is whose."
If he does not look at even one, he makes that his own, for the sake of cutting off quarrel between the two.
Referring to that, he said, "The tasks of the *Trāyastriṃśa* gods themselves [are many].”
Moreover, even such sport-tasks are to be done by him.

That which quickly disappears": That which does not appear to us, quickly, in the darkness, as having form.
By this, he indicates, "I, venerable sir, do not consider that question and answer."
The Elder, considering, "Why does this *yakṣa* indicate un-considering, shirking the question?", says, "The gods are truly greatly confused.
Being churned by the six-doored objects, they do not know their own state of having been eaten or not eaten, having been drunk or not drunk. Here, they are forgetting which is appropriate," he realized.
Some say, “The Elder is to be respected by him, therefore, ‘Just now, in the world, having taken a question from the vicinity of the foremost individual, he has come; just now he has entered the midst of actors, thus the Elder might rebuke me,’ out of fear, he said thus."
But that is called deceit. Such deceit is not in an *arya*-disciple. Therefore, it should be known that, just by being confused, he did not consider.
Why did he consider later? The Elder, having generated joy and agitation, expelled the darkness. Therefore, he considered.

Now, Śakra, in order to announce to the Elder the reason for what happened to him in the past, begins by saying "In the past."
There, "*Samupabyūḷho*" means gathered together, massed.
"*Asurā parājiniṃsū*" means the *asuras* suffered defeat.
When were they defeated? At the time of Śakra's birth.
It is said that Śakra, in a previous existence, in the Magadha country, in Macalagama, was a youth named *Magha*, learned, astute, whose conduct was like the conduct of a *bodhisattva*.
Taking thirty-three men, he did good.
One day, having examined it by his own wisdom, in the middle of the village, in a place where many people gathered, having removed the rubbish from both sides, he made that place very delightful. Again, there he had a pavilion made. Again, as time went on, he had a hall made.
And going out from the village, traveling a *gāvuta*, a half-league, three *gāvutas*, and a league, together with those friends, he made the uneven even.
All of them, being of one mind, there, in places fit for bridges, building bridges, in suitable places for pavilions, halls, ponds, garlands, groves, and so on, they did much merit.

Magha, having fulfilled seven vows, at the breaking up of his body, together with his friends, was born in the *Trāyastriṃśa* heaven.

"*Bhūtapubba*, *samupabyūḷho*, *asurā parājiniṃsū*, *Magha*."

At that time, the hosts of *asuras* dwelt in the *Trāyastriṃśa* world.
All those were of equal lifespan, of equal color to the gods. Seeing Śakra with his retinue, "Just now born, new sons of gods have come," they prepared great drink.
Śakra gave a sign to the sons of gods: "Having done skillful deeds, we have not done common deeds with others. You all should not drink intoxicating drinks; do only what is moderate."
They did thus.The young *asuras*, having drunk cheek-liquor, became intoxicated and succumbed to sleep.

Śakra, having given the gods a sign, made them grasp his feet and hurled them at the foot of Mount Sumeru. At the lower level of Sumeru, there exists a place called *Asurabhavana*—the abode of the *asuras*—which is the same size as the Tāvatiṃsa heaven.

There the *asuras* dwell.

For them, there is also a tree called *Cittapāṭali*.

They know when it is the flowering season for it: "This is not Tāvatiṃsa; we have been deceived by Śakra."

Saying, "Seize [them]!" they, while encircling Sumeru, ascended like white ants from an anthill's base as the gods looked on.

There, at times, the gods are victorious; at times, the *asuras*.

When the gods are victorious, they pursue the *asuras* as far as the surface of the ocean.

When the *asuras* are victorious, they pursue the gods as far as the foot of the altar.

In that battle, however, the gods were victorious; the gods pursued the *asuras* as far as the surface of the ocean.

Śakra, having driven away the *asuras*, placed a guard in five places.

Having thus given protection, he placed images of Indra holding a *vajra* at the foot of the altar.

The *asuras*, having risen up from time to time and seeing those images, think, "Śakra is standing watchful," and from that very spot, they turn back.

"*Tato paṭinivattitvā*": having turned back from the conquered place.

"*Paricārikāyo*": those who perform tasks such as [providing] garlands and scents.

0303"/> *Asurabhavanaṃ* *Cittapāṭali* *Tato paṭinivattitvā* *Paricārikāyo*

mula_pali: 393. Atha kho sakko ca devānamindo vessavaṇo ca mahārājā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ purakkhatvā yena vejayanto pāsādo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Addasaṃsu kho sakkassa devānamindassa paricārikāyo āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ; disvā ottappamānā hirīyamānā sakaṃ sakaṃ ovarakaṃ pavisiṃsu. Seyyathāpi nāma suṇisā sasuraṃ disvā ottappati hirīyati, evameva sakkassa devānamindassa paricārikāyo āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ disvā ottappamānā hirīyamānā sakaṃ sakaṃ ovarakaṃ pavisiṃsu. Atha kho sakko ca devānamindo vessavaṇo ca mahārājā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ vejayante pāsāde anucaṅkamāpenti anuvicarāpenti – ‘‘idampi, mārisa moggallāna, passa vejayantassa pāsādassa rāmaṇeyyakaṃ; idampi, mārisa moggallāna, passa vejayantassa pāsādassa rāmaṇeyyaka’’nti. ‘‘Sobhati idaṃ āyasmato kosiyassa, yathā taṃ pubbe katapuññassa. Manussāpi kiñcideva rāmaṇeyyakaṃ disvā diṭṭhā (sī. pī. ka.) evamāhaṃsu – ‘sobhati vata bho yathā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsāna’nti. Tayidaṃ āyasmato kosiyassa sobhati, yathā taṃ pubbe katapuññassā’’ti. Atha kho āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa etadahosi – ‘‘atibāḷhaṃ kho ayaṃ yakkho pamatto viharati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ yakkhaṃ saṃvejeyya’’nti. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsi abhisaṅkhāresi (ka.), abhisaṅkhāreti (syā. kaṃ.) yathā vejayantaṃ pāsādaṃ pādaṅguṭṭhakena saṅkampesi sampakampesi sampavedhesi . Atha kho sakko ca devānamindo, vessavaṇo ca mahārājā, devā ca tāvatiṃsā acchariyabbhutacittajātā ahesuṃ – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho, samaṇassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāma dibbabhavanaṃ pādaṅguṭṭhakena saṅkampessati sampakampessati sampavedhessatī’’ti! Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ saṃviggaṃ lomahaṭṭhajātaṃ viditvā sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yathā kathaṃ pana kho, kosiya, bhagavā saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṃ abhāsi? Sādhu mayampi etissā kathāya bhāgino assāma savanāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
Then Sakka, the ruler of the gods, and the great King Vessavaṇa, giving precedence to the venerable Mahā Moggallāna, went to the Vejayanta Palace.

The maids of Sakka, the ruler of the gods, saw the venerable Mahā Moggallāna coming from afar; seeing him, they were embarrassed and ashamed, and each went into her own chamber.

Just as a daughter-in-law is embarrassed and ashamed on seeing her father-in-law, so too, when the maids of Sakka, the ruler of the gods, saw the venerable Mahā Moggallāna coming, they were embarrassed and ashamed, and each went into her own chamber.

Then Sakka, the ruler of the gods, and the great King Vessavaṇa had the venerable Mahā Moggallāna walk all over and explore the Vejayanta Palace: "See, good sir Moggallāna, this loveliness ( *rāmaṇeyyaka*) of the Vejayanta Palace! See, good sir Moggallāna, this loveliness of the Vejayanta Palace!"

"It does the venerable Kosiya credit as one who has formerly made merit.

And whenever human beings see anything lovely, they say: ‘Sirs, it does credit to the gods of the Thirty-three!’"

It does the venerable Kosiya credit as one who has formerly made merit.

Then the venerable Mahā Moggallāna considered thus: "This spirit is living much too negligently.

What if I stirred up a sense of urgency in him?"

Then the venerable Mahā Moggallāna performed such a feat of supernormal power ( *iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ*) that with the point of his toe he made the Vejayanta Palace shake and quake and tremble.

Then Sakka, the ruler of the gods, and Vessavaṇa, the great king, and the gods of the Thirty-three were filled with wonder and amazement: "It is wonderful, indeed! It is amazing, indeed, how powerful and mighty is this *samaṇa*, that he can make a divine dwelling shake, quake, and tremble with the point of his toe!" Then the venerable Mahā Moggallāna, knowing that Sakka, the ruler of the gods, was agitated and his hair stood on end, said to Sakka, the ruler of the gods: “How, Kosiya, did the Blessed One briefly describe the deliverance through the destruction of craving ( *taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṃ*)? It would be good if we too could share in that teaching, for the sake of hearing it.”
commentary_pali:
393.Vessavaṇo ca mahārājāti so kira sakkassa vallabho, balavavissāsiko, tasmā sakkena saddhiṃ agamāsi. Purakkhatvāti purato katvā. Pavisiṃsūti pavisitvā pana upaḍḍhapihitāni dvārāni katvā olokayamānā aṭṭhaṃsu. Idampi, mārisa moggallāna, passa vejayantassa pāsādassa rāmaṇeyyakanti, mārisa moggallāna, idampi vejayantassa pāsādassa rāmaṇeyyakaṃ passa, suvaṇṇatthambhe passa, rajatatthambhe maṇitthambhe pavāḷatthambhe lohitaṅgatthambhe masāragallatthambhe muttatthambhe sattaratanatthambhe, tesaṃyeva suvaṇṇādimaye ghaṭake vāḷarūpakāni ca passāti evaṃ thambhapantiyo ādiṃ katvā rāmaṇeyyakaṃ dassento evamāha. Yathā taṃ pubbekatapuññassāti yathā pubbe katapuññassa upabhogaṭṭhānena sobhitabbaṃ, evamevaṃ sobhatīti attho. Atibāḷhaṃkho ayaṃ yakkho pamatto viharatīti attano pāsāde nāṭakaparivārena sampattiyā vasena ativiya matto.

Iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsīti iddhimakāsi. Āpokasiṇaṃ samāpajjitvā pāsādapatiṭṭhitokāsaṃ udakaṃ hotūti iddhiṃ adhiṭṭhāya pāsādakaṇṇike pādaṅguṭṭhakena pahari. So pāsādo yathā nāma udakapiṭṭhe ṭhapitapattaṃ mukhavaṭṭiyaṃ aṅguliyā pahaṭaṃ aparāparaṃ kampati calati na santiṭṭhati. Evamevaṃ saṃkampi sampakampi sampavedhi, thambhapiṭṭhasaṅghāṭakaṇṇikagopānasiādīni karakarāti saddaṃ muñcantāni patituṃ viya āraddhāni. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘saṅkampesi sampakampesi sampavedhesī’’ti. Acchariyabbhutacittajātāti aho acchariyaṃ, aho abbhutanti evaṃ sañjātaacchariyaabbhutā ceva sañjātatuṭṭhino ca ahesuṃ uppannabalavasomanassā. Saṃvigganti ubbiggaṃ. Lomahaṭṭhajātanti jātalomahaṃsaṃ, kañcanabhittiyaṃ ṭhapitamaṇināgadantehi viya uddhaggehi lomehi ākiṇṇasarīranti attho. Lomahaṃso ca nāmesa somanassenapi hoti domanassenapi, idha pana somanassena jāto. Thero hi sakkassa somanassavegena saṃvejetuṃ taṃ pāṭihāriyamakāsi. Tasmā somanassavegena saṃviggalomahaṭṭhaṃ viditvāti attho.

Iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsī Acchariyabbhutacittajātā Saṃvigga Lomahaṭṭhajāta
commentary_english:
393. *Vessavaṇo ca mahārājā* means he was dear to Śakka, trustworthy and strong, therefore he went with Śakka.

*Purakkhatvā* means having placed in front, or having done in front.

*Pavisiṃsū* means having entered, they made the doors half-closed and stood looking around.

*Idampi, mārisa moggallāna, passa vejayantassa pāsādassa rāmaṇeyyaka* means, "Venerable Maudgalyāyana, see the beauty of the Vejayanta palace." Venerable Maudgalyāyana, see this beauty of the Vejayanta palace, see the golden pillars, see the silver pillars, the jewel pillars, the coral pillars, the red pillars, the crystal pillars, the pearl pillars, the seven-jeweled pillars, and see the various animal shapes in the golden containers. Thus, showing the beauty after making the rows of pillars and so on, he said this.

*Yathā taṃ pubbekatapuññassā* means as if by merit previously acquired. As something is beautiful by reason of being a place for enjoying the merit previously acquired, just so it is beautiful, this is the meaning.

*Atibāḷhaṃ* this Yakṣa is exceedingly intoxicated because he is reckless and living in his own palace with a retinue of actors due to his prosperity.

*Iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsī* means he performed a miracle.

Having entered the water kasina, he struck the palace pinnacle with his big toe, resolving that the place established in the palace should become water.

That palace, as if a bowl placed on a surface of water, when struck with a finger on the edge, trembles, shakes, and does not stand still.

Just so, it shook greatly, trembled intensely, and quaked exceedingly; the pillar bases, the joining rafters, the pinnacles, the eaves and so on emitted a cracking sound, as if about to fall.

Therefore it was said, "He caused to shake, he caused to tremble, he caused to quake."

*Acchariyabbhutacittajātā* means "Oh, it is wonderful! Oh, it is marvelous!" Thus, they were filled with wonder and amazement, filled with delight, and had strong joy arisen.

*Saṃvigga* means agitated.

*Lomahaṭṭhajāta* means having hair standing on end, like hairs standing upright like jewel-encrusted Nāga teeth set in a golden wall, this is the meaning.

The hair standing on end is associated with joy as well as sorrow, but here it is born of joy.

The elder performed that miracle in order to agitate Śakka with the force of joy.

Therefore, knowing it to be agitation and hair standing on end due to the force of joy, this is the meaning.

*Iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsī, acchariyabbhutacittajātā, saṃvigga, lomahaṭṭhajāta*

mula_pali:
394. ‘‘Idhāhaṃ , mārisa moggallāna, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsiṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho ahaṃ, mārisa moggallāna, bhagavantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hoti accantaniṭṭho accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussāna’’’nti?

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, mārisa moggallāna, bhagavā maṃ etadavoca – ‘idha, devānaminda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti – sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. Evaṃ cetaṃ devānaminda bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. So sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā. So tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharati, virāgānupassī viharati, nirodhānupassī viharati, paṭinissaggānupassī viharati. So tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharanto, virāgānupassī viharanto, nirodhānupassī viharanto, paṭinissaggānupassī viharanto na kiñci loke upādiyati, anupādiyaṃ na paritassati, aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Ettāvatā kho, devānaminda, bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hoti accantaniṭṭho accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussānanti. Evaṃ kho me, mārisa moggallāna, bhagavā saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṃ abhāsī’’ti.

Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sakkassa devānamindassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – devesu tāvatiṃsesu antarahito pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde pāturahosi. Atha kho sakkassa devānamindassa paricārikāyo acirapakkante āyasmante mahāmoggallāne sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘eso nu te, mārisa, so bhagavā satthā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho me, mārisa, so bhagavā satthā. Sabrahmacārī me eso āyasmā mahāmoggallāno’’ti. ‘‘Lābhā te, mārisa, (suladdhaṃ te, mārisa) ( ) natthi (sī. pī.) yassa te sabrahmacārī evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo! Aho nūna te so bhagavā satthā’’ti.

( ) natthi (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
394. “Good sir Moggallana, I went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, I stood at one side. Standing at one side, good sir Moggallana, I said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, how in brief is a *bhikkhu* liberated by the destruction of craving, one who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate security from bondage, the ultimate holy life, the ultimate goal, one who is foremost among gods and humans?’”

“When this was said, good sir Moggallana, the Blessed One told me: ‘Here, ruler of gods, a *bhikkhu* has heard that nothing is worth adhering to ( *abhinivesāya*). When a *bhikkhu*, ruler of gods, has heard that nothing is worth adhering to, he directly knows everything ( *sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti*); having directly known everything, he fully understands everything ( *sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti*); having fully understood everything, whatever feeling (*vedanā*) he feels, whether pleasant (*sukhaṃ*) or painful (*dukkhaṃ*) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*), he abides contemplating impermanence (*anicca-anupassī*) in those feelings, contemplating fading away (*virāga-anupassī*), contemplating cessation (*nirodha-anupassī*), contemplating relinquishment (*paṭinissagga-anupassī*). Contemplating thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. When he does not cling, he is not agitated. When he is not agitated, he personally attains *nirvāṇa* (*parinibbāyati*). He understands: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.” Briefly, it is in this way, ruler of gods, that a *bhikkhu* is liberated by the destruction of craving, one who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate security from bondage, the ultimate holy life, the ultimate goal, one who is foremost among gods and humans.’ That is how the Blessed One stated to me in brief deliverance through the destruction of craving, good sir Moggallana.”

Then the venerable Mahāmoggallāna, delighted and rejoiced in the words of Śakka, ruler of gods. Then, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, he vanished from among the gods of the Thirty-three (*tāvatiṃsa*) and appeared in the Eastern Park in the Palace of Migāra’s Mother. Then, soon after the venerable Mahāmoggallāna had gone, the attendants of Śakka, ruler of gods, asked him: “Good sir, was that your teacher, the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), the Teacher (*satthā*)?” “No, good sirs, that Blessed One is not my Teacher. That venerable Mahāmoggallāna is one of my companions in the holy life (*sabrahmacārī*).” “Good for you, good sir, so very good for you, good sir, that you have a companion in the holy life of such great power and such great influence! How much more so must that Blessed One, your Teacher, be!”
commentary_pali: 394.Idhāhaṃ, mārisāti idānissa yasmā therena somanassasaṃvegaṃ janayitvā tamaṃ vinoditaṃ, tasmā sallakkhetvā evamāha. Eso nu te, mārisa, so bhagavā satthāti, mārisa, tvaṃ kuhiṃ gatosīti vutte mayhaṃ satthu santikanti vadesi, imasmiṃ devaloke ekapādakena viya tiṭṭhasi, yaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi, eso nu te, mārisa, so bhagavā satthāti pucchiṃsu. Sabrahmacārī me esoti ettha kiñcāpi thero anagāriyo abhinīhārasampanno aggasāvako, sakko agāriyo, maggabrahmacariyavasena panete sabrahmacārino honti, tasmā evamāha. Ahonūna te so bhagavā satthāti sabrahmacārī tāva te evaṃmahiddhiko, so pana te bhagavā satthā aho nūna mahiddhikoti satthu iddhipāṭihāriyadassane jātābhilāpā hutvā evamāhaṃsu.
commentary_english:
"Here I am, friend," because now, since the Elder, having generated joy and agitation, dispelled the darkness, therefore, reflecting, he spoke thus.

"Is this, friend, your Lord, the Teacher?" When it was said, "Friend, where have you gone?" he replied, "I dwell near my Teacher," in this divine world you stand as if on one foot. Because you speak thus, they asked, "Is this, friend, your Lord, the Teacher?"

"This is my fellow practitioner." Here, although the Elder is homeless, endowed with aspiration, the foremost disciple, Śakka is a householder, yet by way of the path of ব্রহ্মচर्या, these are fellow practitioners, therefore he spoke thus.

"Alas! Surely your Lord is the Teacher!" Since a fellow practitioner of yours is so mighty, and your Lord is the Teacher, alas, surely he is mighty," having become of manifested speech at the sight of the Teacher's magical display, they spoke thus.

mula_pali:
395. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhijānāti no, bhante, bhagavā ahu ahunaññeva (sī. syā. kaṃ.) ñātaññatarassa mahesakkhassa yakkhassa saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṃ bhāsitā’’ti abhāsitthāti (ka.)? ‘‘Abhijānāmahaṃ, moggallāna, idha sakko devānamindo yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, moggallāna, sakko devānamindo maṃ etadavoca – ‘kittāvatā nu kho, bhante , bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hoti accantaniṭṭho accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussāna’’nti.

Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, moggallāna, sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavocaṃ ‘‘idha devānaminda bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. Evaṃ cetaṃ devānaminda bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. So sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti , sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā. So tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharati, virāgānupassī viharati, nirodhānupassī viharati, paṭinissaggānupassī viharati. So tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharanto, virāgānupassī viharanto, nirodhānupassī viharanto, paṭinissaggānupassī viharanto na kiñci loke upādiyati, anupādiyaṃ na paritassati, aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ , kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Ettāvatā kho, devānaminda, bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimutto hoti accantaniṭṭho accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussānanti. Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, moggallāna, abhijānāmi sakkassa devānamindassa saṃkhittena taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttiṃ bhāsitā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
395. Then the venerable Mahāmoggallāna approached the Lord; having approached, having greeted the Lord, he sat down at a respectful distance. Seated at a respectful distance, the venerable Mahāmoggallāna said to the Lord: “Venerable sir, does the Blessed One recall stating in brief - to a certain one of the renowned spirits with a great following - deliverance through the destruction of craving?” “I do recall doing so, Moggallana. Here Sakka, ruler of gods, came to me, and after paying homage to me, he stood at one side. As he was standing there, Sakka, ruler of gods, said to me: ‘In what way, venerable sir, is a bhikkhu liberated by the destruction of craving in brief, one who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate security from bondage, the ultimate holy life, the ultimate goal, one who is foremost among gods and humans?’”

When this was said, I told Sakka, ruler of gods: ‘Here, ruler of gods, a bhikkhu has heard that nothing is worth adhering to. When a bhikkhu has heard that nothing is worth adhering to, he directly knows everything; having directly known everything, he fully understands everything; having fully understood everything, whatever feeling he feels, whether pleasant or painful or neitherpainful- nor-pleasant. he abides contemplating impermanence in those feelings, contemplating fading away, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment. Contemplating thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. When he does not cling, he is not agitated. When he is not agitated, he personally attains Nibbana. He understands: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.” Briefly, it is in this way, ruler of gods, that a *bhikkhu* is liberated by the destruction of craving, one who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate security from bondage, the ultimate holy life, the ultimate goal, one who is foremost among gods and humans.’ That is how I recall stating in brief to Sakka, ruler of gods, deliverance through the destruction of craving.”

Thus spoke the Lord. The venerable Maha Moggallana was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasuttaṃ, the seventh, is finished.
commentary_pali:
395.Ñātaññatarassāti paññātaññatarassa, sakko hi paññātānaṃ aññataro. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva, desanaṃ pana bhagavā yathānusandhināva niṭṭhāpesīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
"ñātaññatarassā" means "paññātaññatarassa," because Sakka is one of the known ones.

The rest is clear everywhere. However, the Blessed One completed the teaching according to the connection.

The commentary on the *Cūḷataṇhāsaṅkhayasutta*, from the *Papañcasūdanī Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā*, is finished.

mula_pali: 396. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sātissa nāma bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – ‘‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati anañña’’nti. Assosuṃ kho sambahulā bhikkhū – ‘‘sātissa kira nāma bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’’’nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘saccaṃ kira te, āvuso sāti, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ byā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’’nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetukāmā samanuyuñjanti samanugāhanti samanubhāsanti – ‘‘mā evaṃ, āvuso sāti, avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ, na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyenāvuso sāti, paṭiccasamuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, aññatra paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavo’’ti. Evampi kho sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tehi bhikkhūhi samanuyuñjiyamāno samanugāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno tadeva pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharati – ‘‘evaṃ byā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati anañña’’nti.
mula_english:
396. Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One was dwelling at Anāthapindika’s monastery, in the Jeta Grove, near Sāvatthi.

Now on that occasion a pernicious view had arisen in a bhikkhu named Sāti, son of a fisherman, thus: “As I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāna*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another.”

Several *bhikkhus*, having heard about this, [went to the bhikkhu Sāti and asked him]: “Friend Sāti, is it true that such a pernicious view has arisen in you? ‘As I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāna*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another?’” “Yes, friend, as I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāna*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another.”

Then those *bhikkhus*, desiring to detach him from that pernicious view, pressed and questioned and cross-questioned him thus: “Friend Sāti, do not say so. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One; it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not speak thus.

Friend Sāti, in many discourses the Blessed One has stated consciousness (*vijñāna*) to be dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppanna*), since without a condition there is no origination of consciousness (*vijñāna*).”

Yet although pressed and questioned and cross-questioned by those *bhikkhus* in this way, the bhikkhu Sāti, son of a fisherman, still obstinately adhered to that pernicious view and continued to insist upon it: “Yes, friend, as I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāna*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another.”
commentary_pali:
396.Evaṃme sutanti mahātaṇhāsaṅkhayasuttaṃ. Tattha diṭṭhigatanti alagaddūpamasutte laddhimattaṃ diṭṭhigatanti vuttaṃ, idha sassatadiṭṭhi. So ca bhikkhu bahussuto, ayaṃ appassuto, jātakabhāṇako bhagavantaṃ jātakaṃ kathetvā, ‘‘ahaṃ, bhikkhave, tena samayena vessantaro ahosiṃ, mahosadho, vidhurapaṇḍito, senakapaṇḍito, mahājanako rājā ahosi’’nti samodhānentaṃ suṇāti. Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘ime rūpavedanāsaññāsaṅkhārā tattha tattheva nirujjhanti, viññāṇaṃ pana idhalokato paralokaṃ, paralokato imaṃ lokaṃ sandhāvati saṃsaratī’’ti sassatadassanaṃ uppannaṃ. Tenāha – ‘‘tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati anañña’’nti.

Sammāsambuddhena pana, ‘‘viññāṇaṃ paccayasambhavaṃ, sati paccaye uppajjati, vinā paccayaṃ natthi viññāṇassa sambhavo’’ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā ayaṃ bhikkhu buddhena akathitaṃ katheti, jinacakke pahāraṃ deti, vesārajjañāṇaṃ paṭibāhati, sotukāmaṃ janaṃ visaṃvādeti, ariyapathe tiriyaṃ nipatitvā mahājanassa ahitāya dukkhāya paṭipanno. Yathā nāma rañño rajje mahācoro uppajjamāno mahājanassa ahitāya dukkhāya uppajjati, evaṃ jinasāsane coro hutvā mahājanassa ahitāya dukkhāya uppannoti veditabbo. Sambahulā bhikkhūti janapadavāsino piṇḍapātikabhikkhū. Tenupasaṅkamiṃsūti ayaṃ parisaṃ labhitvā sāsanampi antaradhāpeyya, yāva pakkhaṃ na labhati, tāvadeva naṃ diṭṭhigatā vivecemāti sutasutaṭṭhānatoyeva aṭṭhatvā anisīditvā upasaṅkamiṃsu.

Sambahulā bhikkhū Tenupasaṅkamiṃsū
commentary_english:
396. Thus, I have heard: the Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhayasutta.

There, "diṭṭhigata" means that in the Alagaddūpamasutta, diṭṭhigata means holding a view, here it is the eternalist view ( *sassatadiṭṭhi*).

That monk is very learned, this one is not very learned. The Jātaka reciter, having related a Jātaka of the Blessed One, hears him clarifying, "I, monks, at that time was Vessantara, Mahosadha, Vidhurapaṇḍita, Senakapaṇḍita, King Mahājanaka."

Then it occurred to him: "These *rūpa*, *vedanā*, *saññā*, and *saṃkhāra* cease right there, but consciousness (*vijñāṇa*) wanders and transmigrates from this world to the next world, and from the next world to this world." Thus, an eternalist view arose.

Therefore, he said: "It is this same consciousness (*vijñāṇa*) that wanders and transmigrates, not another."

Moreover, the Sammāsambuddha said, "Consciousness (*vijñāṇa*) is conditioned, it arises when there is a condition, without a condition, there is no arising of consciousness (*vijñāṇa*)."

Therefore, this monk speaks what was not spoken by the Buddha, he strikes the Jina's wheel, he opposes the knowledge of self-confidence (*vesārajjañāṇa*), he causes those who wish to hear to disagree, having fallen across the noble path, he is committed to the harm and suffering of the great mass of people.

Just as, in a king's kingdom, a great thief, arising, arises for the harm and suffering of the great mass of people, so too, in the Jina's teaching, a thief, having become [like that], is understood to have arisen for the harm and suffering of the great mass of people.

"Many monks (*sambahulā bhikkhū*)" means monks who live in the country, who live on alms.

"They approached him (*tenupasaṅkamiṃsū*)" means: "Having gained a following, this one might even cause the teaching to disappear; before he gains a faction, let us refute his view." Thus, having stood only where they had heard and learned, without sitting down, they approached him.

Many monks (*sambahulā bhikkhū*) They approached him (*tenupasaṅkamiṃsū*).

mula_pali: 397. Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṃ, atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘sātissa nāma, bhante, bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’nti. Assumha kho mayaṃ, bhante, sātissa kira nāma bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’nti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yena sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etadavocumha – ‘saccaṃ kira te, āvuso sāti, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’’nti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto amhe etadavoca – ‘evaṃ byā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’nti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetukāmā samanuyuñjimha samanugāhimha samanubhāsimha – ‘mā evaṃ, āvuso sāti, avaca, mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ, na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya. Anekapariyāyenāvuso sāti, paṭiccasamuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, aññatra paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavo’ti. Evampi kho, bhante, sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto amhehi samanuyuñjiyamāno samanugāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno tadeva pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ thāmasā parāmasā abhinivissa voharati – ‘evaṃ byā kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’nti. Yato kho mayaṃ, bhante, nāsakkhimha sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṃ, atha mayaṃ etamatthaṃ bhagavato ārocemā’’ti.
mula_english:
397. Since the *bhikkhus* were unable to detach the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman, from that pernicious view (*pāpakā diṭṭhigatā*), they went to the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side.

Sitting down at a respectful distance, the *bhikkhus* said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir (*bhante*), a pernicious view has arisen in the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman: ‘As I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāṇa*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another.’

“We heard, venerable sir, that such a pernicious view had arisen in the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman: ‘As I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāṇa*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another.’

"Then, venerable sir, we went to the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman; and having gone, we said this to the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman: ‘Friend Sāti, is it true that such a pernicious view has arisen in you: "As I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāṇa*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another"?’ When this was said, venerable sir, the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman, said this to us: ‘Exactly so, friend, as I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāṇa*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another.’

“Then, venerable sir, desiring to detach the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman, from this pernicious view, we questioned, pressed, and cross-examined him, saying: ‘Do not speak thus, friend Sāti. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One (*bhagavantam*); it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One (*bhagavato*). The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) would not speak thus. For in many ways, friend Sāti, the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) has declared consciousness (*vijñāṇaṃ*) to be dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannaṃ*); for without a condition (*paccaya*), there is no origination (*sambhava*) of consciousness (*vijñāṇassa*).’

“Yet although we questioned, pressed, and cross-examined the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman, in this way, venerable sir, he still obstinately adhered to that same pernicious view, insisting: ‘Exactly so, friend, as I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, it is this same consciousness (*vijñāṇaṃ*) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another.’

“Since, venerable sir, we were unable to detach the *bhikkhu* Sāti, son of a fisherman, from this pernicious view (*pāpakā diṭṭhigatā*), we have reported this matter to the Blessed One (*bhagavato*)".

mula_pali: 398. Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ bhikkhu, mama vacanena sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ āmantehi – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso sāti, āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yena sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘satthā taṃ, āvuso sāti, āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘saccaṃ kira, te, sāti, evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – ‘tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ byā kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati, anañña’’nti. ‘‘Katamaṃ taṃ, sāti, viññāṇa’’nti? ‘‘Yvāyaṃ, bhante, vado vedeyyo tatra tatra kalyāṇapāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ vipākaṃ paṭisaṃvedetī’’ti. ‘‘Kassa nu kho nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi? Nanu mayā, moghapurisa, anekapariyāyena paṭiccasamuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ vuttaṃ, aññatra paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavoti? Atha ca pana tvaṃ, moghapurisa, attanā duggahitena amhe ceva abbhācikkhasi, attānañca khaṇasi, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavasi. Tañhi te, moghapurisa, bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed a certain *bhikkhu* (monk) thus: "Come, *bhikkhu* (monk), tell the *bhikkhu* (monk) Sāti, son of a fisherman, in my name that the Teacher calls him."

"Yes, venerable sir," replied that *bhikkhu* (monk) to the Blessed One, and he went to where the *bhikkhu* (monk) Sāti, son of a fisherman, was; having gone there, he said to the *bhikkhu* (monk) Sāti, son of a fisherman: "The Teacher calls you, friend Sāti."

"Very well, friend," replied the *bhikkhu* (monk) Sāti, son of a fisherman, to that *bhikkhu* (monk), and he went to where the Blessed One was; having gone there, he greeted the Blessed One, and sat down on one side.

The Blessed One then asked the *bhikkhu* (monk) Sāti, son of a fisherman, who was sitting on one side: "Sāti, is it true that the following pernicious view has arisen in you: ‘As I understand the *dharma* (Dhamma) taught by the Blessed One, it is this same *vijñāna* (consciousness) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another’?"

"Yes, venerable sir, as I understand the *dharma* (Dhamma) taught by the Blessed One, it is this same *vijñāna* (consciousness) that runs and wanders through the round of rebirths, not another."

"What is that *vijñāna* (consciousness), Sāti?"

"Venerable sir, it is that which speaks and feels, and experiences the *vipāka* (result) of good and bad actions in various places."

"Whom do you know, foolish man, to whom I have taught the *dharma* (Dhamma) in that way? Foolish man, have I not stated in many ways that *pratītyasamutpāda* (dependent origination) is *vijñāna* (consciousness), and that there is no arising of *vijñāna* (consciousness) without a cause? But you, foolish man, through your own wrong grasp, both misrepresent me and dig yourself up, and beget much demerit. This, foolish man, will be for your long-lasting harm and suffering."
commentary_pali: 398.Katamaṃ taṃ sāti viññāṇanti sāti yaṃ tvaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāya vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ viññāṇanti? Yvāyaṃ, bhante, vado vedeyyo tatra tatra kalyāṇapāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ vipākaṃ paṭisaṃvedetīti, bhante, yo ayaṃ vadati vedayati, yo cāyaṃ tahiṃ tahiṃ kusalākusalakammānaṃ vipākaṃ paccanubhoti. Idaṃ, bhante, viññāṇaṃ, yamahaṃ sandhāya vademīti . Kassa nu kho nāmāti kassa khattiyassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā vessasuddagahaṭṭhapabbajitadevamanussānaṃ vā aññatarassa.
commentary_english:
398. What is that consciousness, which you refer to when you speak referring to consciousness? What is that consciousness? That which, venerable sir, is the speaker who experiences in each and every instance the ripening of the actions that are wholesome and unwholesome. That which, venerable sir, speaks and experiences, that which experiences the ripening of wholesome and unwholesome actions in each and every instance.

This, venerable sir, is the consciousness I speak of, referring to it.

Whose name is it? To which kṣatriya, or to which brāhmaṇa, or to which vaiśya, śūdra, householder, renunciate, god, human, or to any other.

mula_pali: 399. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nāyaṃ sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto usmīkatopi imasmiṃ dhammavinaye’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi siyā bhante? No hetaṃ, bhante’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno nisīdi. Atha kho bhagavā sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ maṅkubhūtaṃ pattakkhandhaṃ adhomukhaṃ pajjhāyantaṃ appaṭibhānaṃ viditvā sātiṃ bhikkhuṃ kevaṭṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘paññāyissasi kho tvaṃ, moghapurisa, etena sakena pāpakena diṭṭhigatena. Idhāhaṃ bhikkhū paṭipucchissāmī’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘tumhepi me, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha yathāyaṃ sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto attanā duggahitena amhe ceva abbhācikkhati, attānañca khaṇati, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavatī’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante! Anekapariyāyena hi no, bhante, paṭiccasamuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, aññatra paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavo’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave! Sādhu kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānātha. Anekapariyāyena hi vo, bhikkhave, paṭiccasamuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ vuttaṃ mayā, aññatra paccayā natthi viññāṇassa sambhavoti. Atha ca panāyaṃ sāti bhikkhu kevaṭṭaputto attanā duggahitena amhe ceva abbhācikkhati, attānañca khaṇati, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavati pasavati. Tañhi tassa moghapurisassa bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “What do you think, monks? Has this monk Sāti, son of a fisherman, kindled even a spark of wisdom in this Dharma and Discipline?” “What could it be, Lord? No, Lord.”

When this was said, the monk Sāti, son of a fisherman, sat silent, dismayed, with shoulders drooping and head down, glum, and without response.

Then, knowing this, the Blessed One told Sāti, the monk, son of a fisherman: “Misguided man, you will be recognised by your own pernicious view. I shall question the monks on this matter.”

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Bhikkhus, do you understand the Dhamma taught by me as this monk Sāti, son of a fisherman, misrepresents us by his wrong grasp and injures himself and stores up much demerit?” “No, Lord! For in many discourses, Lord, the Blessed One has stated consciousness to be dependently arisen, since without a condition there is no origination of consciousness.”

“Good, good, monks! It is good that you understand the Dhamma taught by me thus. For in many discourses I have stated consciousness to be dependently arisen, since without a condition there is no origination of consciousness. But this monk Sāti, son of a fisherman, misrepresents us by his wrong grasp and injures himself and stores up much demerit; for this will lead to this misguided man’s harm and suffering for a long time.
commentary_pali: 399.Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesīti kasmā āmantesi? Sātissa kira evaṃ ahosi – ‘‘satthā maṃ ‘moghapuriso’ti vadati, na ca moghapurisoti vuttamatteneva maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo na hoti. Upasenampi hi vaṅgantaputtaṃ, ‘atilahuṃ kho tvaṃ moghapurisa bāhullāya āvatto’ti (mahāva. 75) bhagavā moghapurisavādena ovadi. Thero aparabhāge ghaṭento vāyamanto cha abhiññā sacchākāsi. Ahampi tathārūpaṃ vīriyaṃ paggaṇhitvā maggaphalāni nibbattessāmī’’ti. Athassa bhagavā chinnapaccayo ayaṃ sāsane aviruḷhadhammoti dassento bhikkhū āmantesi. Usmīkatotiādi heṭṭhā vuttādhippāyameva. Atha kho bhagavāti ayampi pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Sātissa kira etadahosi – ‘‘bhagavā mayhaṃ maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo natthīti vadati, kiṃ sakkā upanissaye asati kātuṃ? Na hi tathāgatā saupanissayasseva dhammaṃ desenti, yassa kassaci desentiyeva. Ahaṃ buddhassa santikā sugatovādaṃ labhitvā saggasampattūpagaṃ kusalaṃ karissāmī’’ti. Athassa bhagavā, ‘‘nāhaṃ, moghapurisa, tuyhaṃ ovādaṃ vā anusāsaniṃ vā demī’’ti sugatovādaṃ paṭippassambhento imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tassattho heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Idāni parisāya laddhiṃ sodhento, ‘‘idhāhaṃ bhikkhū paṭipucchissāmī’’tiādimāha. Taṃ sabbampi heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus": Why did he address [them]? Sāti thought to himself: "The Teacher says, 'He is a useless man', but merely by saying 'useless man' the basis for the paths and their fruits does not come to be.

Upasena also [said] to Vaṅgantaputta, 'You are very frivolous, a useless man, turned to extravagance' (Mahāva.

75) The Blessed One admonished him with the term "useless man."

The Elder, striving and exerting himself later, realized the six superknowledges.

"I, too, having taken up such energy, will produce the paths and their fruits."

Then the Blessed One, showing that his basis was destroyed and his Dhamma did not grow in the Dispensation, addressed the bhikkhus.

"Usmīkato" etc., the meaning is just as previously stated.

"Then the Blessed One": this also is a distinct connection.

Sāti thought to himself: "The Blessed One says that the basis for the paths and their fruits does not exist for me. What can be done when there is no basis? For the Tathāgatas teach the Dhamma only to one who has a basis, not to just anyone.

"I, having obtained the Sugata's teaching from the Buddha's presence, will do skillful deeds that lead to the attainment of heavenly prosperity."

Then the Blessed One, rejecting his acceptance of the Sugata's teaching, said to him, "I do not give you advice or instruction, you useless man," and began this discourse.

Its meaning should be understood in the same way as previously stated.

Now, purifying the assembly's view, he said, "Here I will question the bhikkhus," etc.

All that should be understood in the same way as previously stated.

mula_pali:
400. ‘‘Yaṃ yadeva, bhikkhave, paccayaṃ paṭicca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, tena teneva viññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati saṅkhaṃ gacchati (sī. pī.). Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; sotañca paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; ghānañca paṭicca gandhe ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, ghānaviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; kāyañca paṭicca phoṭṭhabbe ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yaṃ yadeva paccayaṃ paṭicca aggi jalati tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Kaṭṭhañca paṭicca aggi jalati, kaṭṭhaggitveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; sakalikañca paṭicca aggi jalati, sakalikaggitveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; tiṇañca paṭicca aggi jalati, tiṇaggitveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; gomayañca paṭicca aggi jalati, gomayaggitveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; thusañca paṭicca aggi jalati, thusaggitveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; saṅkārañca paṭicca aggi jalati, saṅkāraggitveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ yadeva paccayaṃ paṭicca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; sotañca paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, sotaviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati, ghānañca paṭicca gandhe ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ , ghāṇaviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati, jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, jivhāviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Kāyañca paṭicca phoṭṭhabbe ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, kāyaviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati viññāṇaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃtveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.
mula_english:
400. “Bhikkhus, consciousness is reckoned by the particular condition dependent upon which it arises.

When consciousness arises dependent on the eye (cakṣu) and forms (rūpa), it is reckoned as eye-consciousness (cakṣurvijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the ear (śrotra) and sounds (śabda), it is reckoned as ear-consciousness (śrotravijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the nose (ghrāṇa) and odours (gandha), it is reckoned as nose-consciousness (ghrāṇavijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the tongue (jihvā) and flavours (rasa), it is reckoned as tongue-consciousness (jihvavijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the body (kāya) and tangibles (sparśa), it is reckoned as body-consciousness (kāyavijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the mind (manas) and mind-objects (dharma), it is reckoned as mind-consciousness (manovijñāna).

Just as fire is reckoned by the particular condition dependent on which it burns - when fire burns dependent on logs (kāṣṭha), it is reckoned as a log fire; when fire burns dependent on faggots (sakalika), it is reckoned as a faggot fire; when fire burns dependent on grass (tṛṇa), it is reckoned as a grass fire; when fire burns dependent on cowdung (gomaya), it is reckoned as a cowdung fire; when fire burns dependent on chaff (thuṣa), it is reckoned as a chaff fire; when fire burns dependent on rubbish (saṅkāra), it is reckoned as a rubbish fire - so too, consciousness is reckoned by the particular condition dependent on which it arises.

When consciousness arises dependent on the eye (cakṣu) and forms (rūpa), it is reckoned as eye-consciousness (cakṣurvijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the ear (śrotra) and sounds (śabda), it is reckoned as ear-consciousness (śrotravijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the nose (ghrāṇa) and odours (gandha), it is reckoned as nose-consciousness (ghrāṇavijñāna), when consciousness arises dependent on the tongue (jihvā) and flavours (rasa), it is reckoned as tongue-consciousness (jihvavijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the body (kāya) and tangibles (sparśa), it is reckoned as body-consciousness (kāyavijñāna); when consciousness arises dependent on the mind (manas) and mind-objects (dharma), it is reckoned as mind-consciousness (manovijñāna).
commentary_pali: 400. Idāni viññāṇassa sappaccayabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ yaṃ yadeva, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha manañca paṭicca dhamme cāti sahāvajjanena bhavaṅgamanañca tebhūmakadhamme ca paṭicca. Kaṭṭhañca paṭiccātiādi opammanidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tena kiṃ dīpeti? Dvārasaṅkantiyā abhāvaṃ. Yathā hi kaṭṭhaṃ paṭicca jalamāno aggi upādānapaccaye satiyeva jalati, tasmiṃ asati paccayavekallena tattheva vūpasammati, na sakalikādīni saṅkamitvā sakalikaggītiādisaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, evameva cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ tasmiṃ dvāre cakkhurūpaālokamanasikārasaṅkhāte paccayamhi satiyeva uppajjati, tasmiṃ asati paccayavekallena tattheva nirujjhati, na sotādīni saṅkamitvā sotaviññāṇantiādisaṅkhyaṃ gacchati . Esa nayo sabbavāresu. Iti bhagavā nāhaṃ viññāṇappavatte dvārasaṅkantimattampi vadāmi, ayaṃ pana sāti moghapuriso bhavasaṅkantiṃ vadatīti sātiṃ niggahesi.
commentary_english:
400. Now, in order to show the conditionality of consciousness, he says, "<hi rend="bold">Whatever it may be, monks</hi>," etc.

There, "<hi rend="bold">depending on the mind and also on the objects</hi>" means depending on the mind together with initial attention, and also depending on the three-planes-of-existence phenomena.

"<hi rend="bold">Depending on the wood</hi>" etc., is said for the purpose of simile and illustration.

By that, on what does it shed the light? On the absence of transference through a doorway.

Just as fire, when blazing, depends on wood and burns only when there is a fuel condition, [and] subsides right there when that is absent due to lack of a condition, and does not go to the enumeration of *sakalikā*, etc. by transferring to *sakalikaggi*, etc.; in the same way, consciousness, having arisen depending on the eye and also on forms, arises only when there is a condition counted as the doorway, eye, form, light, and attention; [and] ceases right there when that is absent due to lack of a condition, and does not go to the enumeration of ear-consciousness, etc. by transferring to ear, etc..

And so in each section.

Thus, the Blessed One [said:] "I do not speak of even the slightest transference through a doorway in the process of consciousness; but this Sāti, foolish man, speaks of transference of existence," thus he rebuked Sāti.

mula_pali:
401. ‘‘Bhūtamidanti , bhikkhave, passathā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhārasambhavanti, bhikkhave, passathā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ, taṃ nirodhadhammanti, bhikkhave, passathā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Bhūtamidaṃ nossūti, bhikkhave, kaṅkhato uppajjati vicikicchā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhārasambhavaṃ nossūti, bhikkhave , kaṅkhato uppajjati vicikicchā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ, taṃ nirodhadhammaṃ nossūti, bhikkhave, kaṅkhato uppajjati vicikicchā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Bhūtamidanti, bhikkhave, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato yā vicikicchā sā pahīyatī’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhārasambhavanti, bhikkhave, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato yā vicikicchā sā pahīyatī’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ, taṃ nirodhadhammanti, bhikkhave, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato yā vicikicchā sā pahīyatī’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’.

‘‘Bhūtamidanti, bhikkhave, itipi vo ettha nibbicikicchā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhārasambhavanti, bhikkhave, itipi vo ettha nibbicikicchā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti, bhikkhave, itipi vo ettha nibbicikicchā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Bhūtamidanti, bhikkhave, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭha’’nti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhārasambhavanti, bhikkhave, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭha’’nti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti, bhikkhave, yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭha’’nti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Imaṃ ce tumhe, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ allīyetha kelāyetha dhanāyetha mamāyetha, api nu me tumhe, bhikkhave, kullūpamaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājāneyyātha nittharaṇatthāya no gahaṇatthāyā’’ti?

‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Imaṃ ce tumhe, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ na allīyetha na kelāyetha na dhanāyetha na mamāyetha, api nu me tumhe, bhikkhave, kullūpamaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājāneyyātha nittharaṇatthāya no gahaṇatthāyā’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.
mula_english:
401. “Monks, do you see that this has come to be (bhūtam idaṃ)?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, do you see that it arises from nutriment (tadāhārasambhavaṃ)?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, do you see that what has come to be, with the cessation of that nutriment, is subject to cessation (tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ, taṃ nirodhadhammaṃ)?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, does doubt arise in one who wonders, ‘Has this come to be (bhūtam idaṃ) or not?’”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, does doubt arise in one who wonders, ‘Does it arise from nutriment (tadāhārasambhavaṃ) or not?’”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, does doubt arise in one who wonders, ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, is what has come to be subject to cessation (tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ, taṃ nirodhadhammaṃ) or not?’”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, is doubt abandoned in one who sees as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This has come to be (bhūtam idaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, is doubt abandoned in one who sees as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘It arises from nutriment (tadāhārasambhavaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, is doubt abandoned in one who sees as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation (tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ, taṃ nirodhadhammaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, are you free from doubt here: ‘This has come to be (bhūtam idaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, are you free from doubt here: ‘It arises from nutriment (tadāhārasambhavaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, are you free from doubt here: ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation (tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, has it been seen well by you as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This has come to be (bhūtam idaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, has it been seen well by you as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘It arises from nutriment (tadāhārasambhavaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, has it been seen well by you as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation (tadāhāranirodhā yaṃ bhūtaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammaṃ)’?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Monks, if you were to cling to this view, so purified, so bright, caressing it, cherishing it, and possessing it, would you understand that the Dhamma I have taught is similar to a raft, meant for crossing over, not for holding onto?”

“Certainly not, Lord.”

“Monks, if you were not to cling to this view, so purified, so bright, not caressing it, not cherishing it, not possessing it, would you understand that the Dhamma I have taught is similar to a raft, meant for crossing over, not for holding onto?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”
commentary_pali:
401. Evaṃ viññāṇassa sappaccayabhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni pana pañcannampi khandhānaṃ sappaccayabhāvaṃ dassento, bhūtamidantiādimāha. Tattha bhūtamidanti idaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ nibbattaṃ, tumhepi taṃ bhūtamidanti, bhikkhave, passathāti. Tadāhārasambhavanti taṃ panetaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ āhārasambhavaṃ paccayasambhavaṃ, sati paccaye uppajjati evaṃ passathāti pucchati. Tadāhāranirodhāti tassa paccayassa nirodhā. Bhūtamidaṃ nossūti bhūtaṃ nu kho idaṃ, na nu kho bhūtanti. Tadāhārasambhavaṃ nossūti taṃ bhūtaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ paccayasambhavaṃ nu kho, na nu khoti. Tadāhāranirodhāti tassa paccayassa nirodhā. Nirodhadhammaṃ nossūti taṃ dhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ nu kho, na nu khoti. Sammappaññāya passatoti idaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ nibbattanti yāthāvasarasalakkhaṇato vipassanāpaññāya sammā passantassa. Paññāya sudiṭṭhanti vuttanayeneva vipassanāpaññāya suṭṭhu diṭṭhaṃ. Evaṃ ye ye taṃ pucchaṃ sallakkhesuṃ, tesaṃ tesaṃ paṭiññaṃ gaṇhanto pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ sappaccayabhāvaṃ dasseti.

Idāni yāya paññāya tehi taṃ sappaccayaṃ sanirodhaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ, tattha nittaṇhabhāvaṃ pucchanto imaṃ ce tumhetiādimāha. Tattha diṭṭhinti vipassanāsammādiṭṭhiṃ . Sabhāvadassanena parisuddhaṃ. Paccayadassanena pariyodātaṃ. Allīyethāti taṇhādiṭṭhīhi allīyitvā vihareyyātha. Kelāyethāti taṇhādiṭṭhīhi kīḷamānā vihareyyātha . Dhanāyethāti dhanaṃ viya icchantā gedhaṃ āpajjeyyātha. Mamāyethāti taṇhādiṭṭhīhi mamattaṃ uppādeyyātha. Nittharaṇatthāya no gahaṇatthāyāti yo so mayā caturoghanittharaṇatthāya kullūpamo dhammo desito, no nikantivasena gahaṇatthāya. Api nu taṃ tumhe ājāneyyāthāti. Vipariyāyena sukkapakkho veditabbo.

imaṃ ce tumhe diṭṭhi parisuddhaṃ pariyodātaṃ. Allīyethā Kelāyethā Dhanāyethā Mamāyethā Nittharaṇatthāya no gahaṇatthāyā
commentary_english:
Thus, having shown that consciousness has conditions, and now, showing that the five aggregates also have conditions, he says, "<hi rend="bold">bhūtamida</hi>nti," and so forth.

There, "<hi rend="bold">bhūtamida</hi>nti" means this aggregate of five is born, has become, has arisen; you too, monks, see it as "bhūtamidaṃ."

"<hi rend="bold">tadāhārasambhava</hi>nti" means that aggregate of five has food as its origin, conditions as its origin; with conditions, it arises; thus he asks, "Do you see it?"

"<hi rend="bold">tadāhāranirodhā</hi>ti" means from the cessation of those conditions.

"<hi rend="bold">bhūtamidaṃ nossū</hi>ti" means is this born, or is it not born?

"<hi rend="bold">tadāhārasambhavaṃ nossū</hi>ti" means is that born aggregate of five of conditions as its origin, or is it not?

"<hi rend="bold">tadāhāranirodhā</hi>ti" means from the cessation of those conditions.

"<hi rend="bold">nirodhadhammaṃ nossū</hi>ti" means is that a phenomenon of cessation, or is it not?

"<hi rend="bold">sammappaññāya passato</hi>ti" means to one who sees correctly with right wisdom, this aggregate of five is born, has become, has arisen, according to the characteristics of each occasion, with wisdom of insight.

"<hi rend="bold">paññāya sudiṭṭha</hi>nti" means it is well seen with the wisdom of insight, just as has been said.

Thus, to those who considered that question, taking their agreement, he shows that the five aggregates have conditions.

Now, with whatever wisdom they have well seen that aggregate of five with its conditions and its cessation, asking about the state of being without craving there, he says, "<hi rend="bold">imaṃ ce tumhe</hi>tiādi."

There, "<hi rend="bold">diṭṭhi</hi>nti" means insight, right view through insight.

Through seeing its own nature, it is "<hi rend="bold">parisuddhaṃ</hi>" (perfectly pure).

Through seeing its conditions, it is "<hi rend="bold">pariyodātaṃ</hi>" (perfectly cleansed).
