mula_pali: 429. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati, sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So imameva kāyaṃ nippītikena sukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa nippītikena sukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni antonimuggaposīni, tāni yāva caggā yāva ca mūlā sītena vārinā abhisannāni parisannāni paripūrāni paripphuṭāni, nāssa na nesaṃ (sī.) kiñci sabbāvataṃ uppalānaṃ vā padumānaṃ vā puṇḍarīkānaṃ vā sītena vārinā apphuṭaṃ assa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ nippītikena sukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa nippītikena sukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti.
mula_english:
429. Again, O monks, a *bhikkhu*, with the fading away of joy (*pīti*) dwells in equanimity (*upekkhā*), mindful and fully aware, and experiences pleasure (*sukha*) with the body (*kāya*). That which the noble ones (*ariyā*) declare, 'Dwelling in equanimity, mindful, and having a pleasant abiding (*sukhavihārī*)', he enters and abides in the third *jhāna*.

He drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses this very body (*kāya*) with happiness (*sukha*) free from joy (*nippītika*), so that there is no part of his entire body (*kāya*) which is not suffused by this happiness (*sukha*) free from joy (*nippītika*).

Just as, O monks, in a pond of blue lotuses (*uppala*), or red lotuses (*paduma*), or white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*), some lotuses (*uppala, paduma, puṇḍarīka*) are born in the water (*udaka*), grow in the water (*udaka*), thrive without rising out of the water (*udakānuggata*), and are nourished immersed within (the water) (*antonimuggaposīni*); and cool water (*sītena vārinā*) drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades them from their tips to their roots (*mūlā*), so that there is no part of all those blue lotuses (*uppala*), or red lotuses (*paduma*), or white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*) unpervaded by cool water (*sītena vārinā*);

Even so, O monks, a *bhikkhu* drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses this very body (*kāya*) with happiness (*sukha*) free from joy (*nippītika*), so that there is no part of his entire body (*kāya*) which is not suffused by this happiness (*sukha*) free from joy (*nippītika*).
commentary_pali: 429. Tatiyajjhānasukhaupamāyaṃ uppalāni ettha santīti uppalinī. Sesapadadvayesupi eseva nayo. Ettha ca setarattanīlesu yaṃkiñci uppalaṃ uppalameva, ūnakasatapattaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ, satapattaṃ padumaṃ. Pattaniyamaṃ vā vināpi setaṃ padumaṃ, rattaṃ puṇḍarīkanti ayamettha vinicchayo. Udakānuggatānīti udakato na uggatāni. Antonimuggaposīnīti udakatalassa anto nimuggāniyeva hutvā posīni, vaḍḍhīnīti attho. Sesaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
429. tatiyajjhānasukhaupamāyaṃ uppalāni ettha santīti *uppalinī*.

And the same rule applies to the other two sections.

Furthermore, in this context, any *uppala*, whether white (*śeta*), red (*ratta*), or blue (*nīla*), is simply an *uppala*. An *ūnakasatapattaṃ* is a *puṇḍarīka*, and a *satapattaṃ* is a *paduma*.

This is the distinction here: *paduma* can be white (*śetaṃ*), or *puṇḍarīka* can be red (*rattaṃ*) even without fixed rules.

*Udakānuggatānī* means not risen from the water (*udakato na uggatāni*).

*Antonimuggaposīnī* means having become submerged inside the water's surface (*udakatalassa anto nimuggāniyeva hutvā posīni*), meaning nourishing (*vaḍḍhīnīti attho*).

The rest should be understood in the way already described (*sesaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ*).

mula_pali: 430. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So imameva kāyaṃ parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena pharitvā nisinno hoti , nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena apphuṭaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso odātena vatthena sasīsaṃ pārupetvā nisinno assa, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa odātena vatthena apphuṭaṃ assa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena pharitvā nisinno hoti, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena apphuṭaṃ hoti.
mula_english:
"Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, with the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a *bhikkhu* enters and abides in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity (*upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*).

He sits, having pervaded this very body with pure, bright awareness (*parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena pharitvā nisinno hoti*), so that there is no part of his entire body that is not suffused with pure, bright awareness.

Just as, *bhikkhus*, a man might sit having wrapped himself from the head down in a white cloth, so that there would be no part of his entire body not covered by the white cloth; even so, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* sits, having pervaded this very body with pure, bright awareness, so that there is no part of his entire body that is not suffused with pure, bright awareness."
commentary_pali: 430. Catutthajjhānasukhaupamāyaṃ parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātenāti ettha nirupakkilesaṭṭhena parisuddhaṃ. Pabhassaraṭṭhena pariyodātaṃ veditabbaṃ. Odātena vatthenāti idaṃ utupharaṇatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiliṭṭhavatthena hi utupharaṇaṃ na hoti, taṅkhaṇadhotaparisuddhena utupharaṇaṃ balavaṃ hoti. Imissā hi upamāya vatthaṃ viya karajakāyo. Utupharaṇaṃ viya catutthajjhānasukhaṃ. Tasmā yathā sunhātassa purisassa parisuddhaṃ vatthaṃ sasīsaṃ pārupitvā nisinnassa sarīrato utu sabbameva vatthaṃ pharati, na koci vatthassa aphuṭokāso hoti. Evaṃ catutthajjhānasukhena bhikkhuno karajakāyassa na koci okāso aphuṭo hotīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Catutthajjhānacittameva vā vatthaṃ viya, taṃsamuṭṭhānarūpaṃ utupharaṇaṃ viya. Yathā hi katthaci odātavatthe kāyaṃ apphusantepi taṃsamuṭṭhānena utunā sabbatthakameva kāyo phuṭṭho hoti. Evaṃ catutthajjhānasamuṭṭhitena sukhumarūpena sabbatthakameva bhikkhuno karajakāyo phuṭo hotīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo.
commentary_english:
430. In the simile of the happiness of the fourth *jhāna*, "with a **pure and cleansed mind**" ( *parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātenā*), *parisuddha* should be understood in the sense of being free from defilements (*nirupakkilesaṭṭhena*), and *pariyodāta* in the sense of being radiant (*pabhassaraṭṭhena*).

"**With a clean cloth**" (*odātena vatthenā*) was said for the sake of suffusion by heat (*utupharaṇatthaṃ*). For there is no suffusion by heat with a soiled cloth (*kiliṭṭhavatthena*); with a clean cloth that has just been washed, the suffusion by heat is strong (*taṅkhaṇadhotaparisuddhena utupharaṇaṃ balavaṃ hoti*). For in this simile, the material body (*karajakāyo*) is like the cloth (*vatthaṃ viya*), and the happiness of the fourth *jhāna* (*catutthajjhānasukhaṃ*) is like the suffusion by heat (*utupharaṇaṃ viya*).

Therefore, just as when a man has bathed well (*sunhātassa purisassa*) and is sitting covered from the head down by a clean cloth (*parisuddhaṃ vatthaṃ sasīsaṃ pārupitvā nisinnassa*), the heat (*utu*) from his body suffuses the entire cloth (*sabbameva vatthaṃ pharati*), and there is no part of the cloth that is not suffused (*na koci vatthassa aphuṭokāso hoti*), similarly, there is no part of the *bhikkhu*'s material body that is not suffused by the happiness of the fourth *jhāna* (*evaṃ catutthajjhānasukhena bhikkhuno karajakāyassa na koci okāso aphuṭo hoti*). Thus, the meaning should be understood here.

Or, the mind of the fourth *jhāna* itself is like the cloth (*vatthaṃ viya*), and the matter (*rūpaṃ*) arisen from it is like the suffusion by heat (*utupharaṇaṃ viya*). Just as even without the body touching the clean cloth anywhere (*kathaci odātavatthe kāyaṃ apphusantepi*), the body is entirely suffused by the heat arisen from it (*taṃsamuṭṭhānena utunā sabbatthakameva kāyo phuṭṭho hoti*), similarly, the *bhikkhu*'s material body is entirely suffused by the subtle matter (*sukhumarūpena*) arisen from the fourth *jhāna* (*evaṃ catutthajjhānasamuṭṭhitena sukhumarūpena sabbatthakameva bhikkhuno karajakāyo phuṭo hoti*). Thus, the meaning should be understood here.

mula_pali: 431. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ, dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso sakamhā gāmā aññaṃ gāmaṃ gaccheyya, tamhāpi gāmā aññaṃ gāmaṃ gaccheyya, so tamhā gāmā sakaṃyeva gāmaṃ paccāgaccheyya. Tassa evamassa – ‘ahaṃ kho sakamhā gāmā amuṃ gāmaṃ agacchiṃ agacchiṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), tatrapi evaṃ aṭṭhāsiṃ evaṃ nisīdiṃ evaṃ abhāsiṃ evaṃ tuṇhī ahosiṃ; tamhāpi gāmā amuṃ gāmaṃ agacchiṃ, tatrapi evaṃ aṭṭhāsiṃ evaṃ nisīdiṃ evaṃ abhāsiṃ evaṃ tuṇhī ahosiṃ; somhi tamhā gāmā sakaṃyeva gāmaṃ paccāgato’ti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati.
mula_english:
431. “When his concentrated mind is thus purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to knowledge of the recollection of past lives.

He recollects his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births…Thus with their aspects and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives.

Just as, monks, a man might go from his own village to another village, and from that village to still another village, and then back again to his own village,

he might think: ‘I went from my own village to that village, and there I stood in such a way, sat in such a way, spoke in such a way, kept silent in such a way; and from that village I went to that other village, and there I stood in such a way, sat in such a way, spoke in such a way, kept silent in such a way; and from that village I came back again to my own village.’

So too, monks, a *bhikṣu* recollects his manifold past lives… Thus with their aspects and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives.
commentary_pali: 431. Pubbenivāsañāṇaupamāyaṃ taṃdivasaṃ katakiriyā pākaṭā hotīti taṃdivasaṃ gatagāmattayameva gahitaṃ. Tattha gāmattayaṃ gatapuriso viya pubbenivāsañāṇalābhī daṭṭhabbo. Tayo gāmā viya tayo bhavā daṭṭhabbā. Tassa purisassa tīsu gāmesu taṃdivasaṃ katakiriyāya āvibhāvo viya pubbenivāsāya cittaṃ abhinīharitvā nisinnassa bhikkhuno tīsu bhavesu katakiriyāya āvibhāvo daṭṭhabbo.
commentary_english: In the simile of the knowledge of recollecting past lives, "the action done that day becomes clear," this refers to only the three villages visited that day. Therein, the man who has gone to the three villages is to be seen as one who gains the knowledge of recollecting past lives. The three villages are to be seen as three existences. Just as the manifestation of the actions done that day in the three villages to that man, so should the manifestation of the actions done in the three existences be seen by the *bhikṣu* sitting having directed his mind to the knowledge of recollecting past lives.

mula_pali: 432. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate, yathākammūpage satte pajānāti…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dve agārā sadvārā sannadvārā (ka.). Tattha cakkhumā puriso majjhe ṭhito passeyya manusse gehaṃ pavisantepi nikkhamantepi, anucaṅkamantepi anuvicarantepi . Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti…pe….
mula_english:
432. "When his concentrated mind is thus purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings.

He sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human…and he understands how beings pass on according to their actions...

Just as, monks, there were two houses with doors. And a man with good sight standing in the middle saw people entering the house, leaving, walking back and forth, and wandering around.

In the same way, monks, a bhikkhu with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands how beings pass on according to their actions...
commentary_pali: 432. Dibbacakkhuupamāyaṃ dve agārāti dve gharā. Sadvārāti sammukhadvārā. Anucaṅkamanteti aparāparaṃ sañcarante. Anuvicaranteti ito cito ca vicarante, ito pana gehā nikkhamitvā etaṃ gehaṃ, etasmā vā nikkhamitvā imaṃ gehaṃ pavisanavasenapi daṭṭhabbā. Tattha dve agārā sadvārā viya cutipaṭisandhiyo, cakkhumā puriso viya dibbacakkhuñāṇalābhī, cakkhumato purisassa dvinnaṃ gehānaṃ antare ṭhatvā passato dve agāre pavisanakanikkhamanakapurisānaṃ pākaṭakālo viya dibbacakkhulābhino ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā olokentassa cavanakaupapajjanakasattānaṃ pākaṭakālo. Kiṃ pana te ñāṇassa pākaṭā, puggalassāti? Ñāṇassa. Tassa pākaṭattā pana puggalassa pākaṭāyevāti.
commentary_english:
432.
By means of the simile of divine vision: *dve agārā* means two houses.
*sadvārā* means *sammukhadvārā* (facing doors).
*anucaṅkamante* means *aparāparaṃ sañcarante* (walking back and forth).
*anuvicarante* means *ito cito ca vicarante* (wandering here and there); here, however, having left one house and entered another, they should be seen in terms of entering.
There, *dve agārā sadvārā* are like death and rebirth. A person with vision is like one who has obtained divine wisdom. Just as the time of entering and exiting of people in two houses is clear to a person with vision standing between the two houses and looking on, so is the time of the passing away and arising of beings clear to one who has obtained divine vision, increasing the light and looking on.
What is clear to you, is it the knowledge or the individual? The knowledge.
Because of the clarity of that, it is indeed clear to the individual.

mula_pali:
433. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. ‘Ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pabbatasaṅkhepe udakarahado accho vippasanno anāvilo. Tattha cakkhumā puriso tīre ṭhito passeyya sippisambukampi sippikasambukampi (syā. kaṃ. ka.) sakkharakathalampi macchagumbampi, carantampi tiṭṭhantampi. Tassa evamassa – ‘ayaṃ kho udakarahado accho vippasanno anāvilo. Tatrime sippisambukāpi sakkharakathalāpi macchagumbāpi carantipi tiṭṭhantipīti . Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāti.

sippikasambukampi (syā. kaṃ. ka.)
mula_english:
433. “When his mind is thus concentrated (samāhite), purified (parisuddhe), cleansed (pariyodāte), unblemished (anaṅgaṇe), rid of defilement (vigatūpakkilese), malleable (mudubhūte), wieldy (kammaniye), steady (ṭhite), and attained to imperturbability (āneñjappatte), he directs his mind to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints (āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti).

He understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering (idaṃ dukkha)’; ‘This is the origin of suffering (ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo)’; ‘This is the cessation of suffering (ayaṃ dukkhanirodho)’; ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering (ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā)’.

He understands as it really is: ‘These are the taints (ime āsavā)’; ‘This is the origin of the taints (ayaṃ āsavasamudayo)’; ‘This is the cessation of the taints (ayaṃ āsavanirodho)’; ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of the taints (ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā)’.

When he knows and sees thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire (kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati), from the taint of being (bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati), and from the taint of ignorance (avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati).

When it is liberated, there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated (vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti).’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed (khīṇā jāti), the spiritual life has been lived (vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ), what had to be done has been done (kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ), there is no more coming to any state of being (nāparaṃ itthattāyā)’.

“Just as if there were a lake in a mountain recess (pabbatasaṅkhepe udakarahado), clear (acchho), limpid (vippasanno), and undisturbed (anāvilo), so that a man with good sight (cakkhumā puriso) standing on the bank (tīre ṭhito) could see shells (sippisambukampi), gravel and pebbles (sakkharakathalampi), and shoals of fish (macchagumbampi), moving about (carantampi) and keeping still (tiṭṭhantampi).

He would think to himself: ‘This is a lake (ayaṃ kho udakarahado) with clear water (acchho), limpid (vippasanno) and unsullied (anāvilo). There are these shells (sippisambukāpi), these gravel and pebbles (sakkharakathalāpi), these shoals of fish (macchagumbāpi) moving about (carantipi) and keeping still (tiṭṭhantipīti).’

So too, a bhikkhu understands as it actually is: ‘This is suffering (idaṃ dukkha)’…pe…He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed (nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāti).’
commentary_pali: 433. Āsavakkhayañāṇaupamāyaṃ pabbatasaṅkhepeti pabbatamatthake. Anāviloti nikkaddamo. Sippiyo ca sambukā ca sippisambukaṃ. Sakkharā ca kathalā ca sakkharakathalaṃ. Macchānaṃ gumbā ghaṭāti macchagumbaṃ. Tiṭṭhantampi carantampīti ettha sakkharakathalaṃ tiṭṭhatiyeva, itarāni carantipi tiṭṭhantipi. Yathā pana antarantarā ṭhitāsupi nisinnāsupi vijjamānāsupi, ‘‘etā gāvo carantī’’ti carantiyo upādāya itarāpi carantīti vuccanti. Evaṃ tiṭṭhantameva sakkharakathalaṃ upādāya itarampi dvayaṃ tiṭṭhantanti vuttaṃ. Itarañca dvayaṃ carantaṃ upādāya sakkharakathalampi carantanti vuttaṃ. Tattha cakkhumato purisassa tīre ṭhatvā passato sippisambukādīnaṃ vibhūtakālo viya āsavānaṃ khayāya cittaṃ nīharitvā nisinnassa bhikkhuno catunnaṃ saccānaṃ vibhūtakālo daṭṭhabbo.
commentary_english:
433. Regarding the simile of the knowledge of the destruction of the āsavas, *pabbatasaṅkhepe* means on the summit of the mountain.

*anāvilo* means *nikkaddamo* (free from mud).

*sippiyo ca sambukā ca* means *sippisambukaṃ* (shells and snails).

*sakkharā ca kathalā ca* means *sakkharakathalaṃ* (gravel and potsherds).

*macchānaṃ gumbā ghaṭāti* means *macchagumbaṃ* (a cluster of fish).

*tiṭṭhantampi carantampī* means here, *sakkharakathalaṃ* only stands, the others both move and stand.

Just as, however, even though some are standing, some are sitting, and some are moving, taking those which are moving, the others also are said to be moving.

Likewise, taking just the standing *sakkharakathalaṃ*, the other pair also is said to be standing.

And taking the moving pair, the *sakkharakathalaṃ* is also said to be moving.

There, just as the time when shells and snails etc. become clear to a man with eyes standing on the bank, so the time when the four truths become clear to a *bhikkhu* sitting having drawn his mind to the destruction of the *āsavas* should be seen.

mula_pali:
434. ‘‘Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘samaṇo’ itipi ‘brāhmaṇo’itipi ‘nhātako’itipi ‘vedagū’itipi ‘sottiyo’itipi ‘ariyo’itipi ‘arahaṃ’itipi. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samaṇo hoti? Samitāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, saṃkilesikā, ponobbhavikā, sadarā, dukkhavipākā , āyatiṃ, jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samaṇo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu brāhmaṇo hoti? Bāhitāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā , saṃkilesikā, ponobbhavikā, sadarā, dukkhavipākā, āyatiṃ, jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu brāhmaṇo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nhātako nahātako (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) hoti? Nhātāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, saṃkilesikā, ponobbhavikā, sadarā, dukkhavipākā, āyatiṃ, jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nhātako hoti.

nahātako (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedagū hoti? Viditāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, saṃkilesikā, ponobbhavikā, sadarā, dukkhavipākā, āyatiṃ, jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedagū hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sottiyo hoti? Nissutāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, saṃkilesikā, ponobbhavikā, sadarā, dukkhavipākā, āyatiṃ, jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sottiyo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo hoti ? Ārakāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, saṃkilesikā, ponobbhavikā, sadarā, dukkhavipākā, āyatiṃ, jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ hoti? Ārakāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā, saṃkilesikā, ponobbhavikā, sadarā, dukkhavipākā, āyatiṃ, jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ hotī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Mahāassapurasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
434. “Thus, monks, a *bhikkhu* is called a recluse (*śramaṇa*), a Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*), one who has been washed (*nhātaka*), one who has attained to knowledge (*vedagū*), a holy scholar (*sottiyo*), a noble one (*āriya*), and an arahant (*arahaṃ*).

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* a recluse (*śramaṇa*)? He has quieted down evil unwholesome states (*akusalā dhammā*) that defile (*saṃkilesikā*), bring renewal of being (*ponobbhavikā*), give trouble (*sadarā*), ripen in suffering (*dukkhavipākā*), and lead to future birth, ageing, and death (*jātijarāmaraṇiyā*). That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* is a recluse (*śramaṇa*).

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* a Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*)? He has banished evil unwholesome states that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth, ageing, and death. That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* is a Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*).

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* one who has been washed (*nhātaka*)? He has washed off evil unwholesome states that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth, ageing, and death. That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* is one who has been washed (*nhātaka*).

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* one who has attained to knowledge (*vedagū*)? He has known evil unwholesome states that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth, ageing, and death. That is how, monks, a *bhikkhu* is one who has attained to knowledge (*vedagū*).

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* a holy scholar (*sottiyo*)? The evil unwholesome states that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth, ageing, and death, have streamed away from him. That is how a *bhikkhu* is a holy scholar (*sottiyo*).

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* a noble one (*āriya*)? Evil unwholesome states that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth, ageing, and death, are far away from him. That is how a *bhikkhu* is a noble one (*āriya*).

“And how, monks, is a *bhikkhu* an arahant (*arahaṃ*)? Evil unwholesome states that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth, ageing, and death, are far away from him. That is how a *bhikkhu* is an arahant (*arahaṃ*).”

The Blessed One said this. Gratified, the monks delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Mahāassapura Sutta, the ninth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
434. Idāni sattahākārehi saliṅgato saguṇato khīṇāsavassa nāmaṃ gaṇhanto, ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samaṇo itipītiādimāha. Tattha evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samaṇohotītiādīsu, bhikkhave, evaṃ bhikkhu samitapāpattā samaṇo hoti. Bāhitapāpattā brāhmaṇo hoti. Nhātakilesattā nhātako hoti, dhotakilesattāti attho. Catumaggañāṇasaṅkhātehi vedehi akusaladhammānaṃ gatattā vedagū hoti, viditattāti attho. Teneva viditāssa hontītiādimāha. Kilesānaṃ sutattā sottiyo hoti, nissutattā apahatattāti attho. Kilesānaṃ ārakattā ariyo hoti, hatattāti attho. Tehi ārakattā arahaṃ hoti, dūrībhūtattāti attho. Sesaṃ sabattha pākaṭamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāassapurasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
Now, while taking up the name of the *khīṇāsava* (one who has destroyed the āsavas), with seven aspects, with the *liṅga*, and with the qualities, he says, “This is called, O monks, a *bhikkhu*, a *samaṇa*,” etc.

There, in “It is in this way, O monks, that a *bhikkhu* is a *samaṇa*,” etc., O monks, in this way a *bhikkhu*, because he has calmed evil (*samita-pāpattā*), is a *samaṇa* (ascetic). Because he has warded off evil (*bāhita-pāpattā*), he is a *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin). Because he has washed away defilements (*nhāta-kilesattā*), he is a *nhātako* (one who has bathed), that is, the meaning is, because he has cleansed away defilements. Because he has gone to the Vedas (*vedagū*)—in the sense of the four paths' knowledge—gone to unwholesome things, he is a *vedagū*, that is, the meaning is, because he has known it. Just because of that, he says, “They are known to him,” etc. Because he has heard the defilements (*kilesānaṃ sutattā*), he is a *sottiyo* (one who has heard), that is, the meaning is, because he has completely heard, because he has warded off. Because he is far from the defilements (*kilesānaṃ ārakattā*), he is an *ariya* (noble one), that is, the meaning is, because he has destroyed. Because he is far from them (*tehi ārakattā*), he is an *arahaṃ* (worthy one), that is, the meaning is, because he has become distant. The rest is clear everywhere.

The Great Assapura Sutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, the commentary to the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 435. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā aṅgesu viharati assapuraṃ nāma aṅgānaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘samaṇā samaṇāti vo, bhikkhave, jano sañjānāti. Tumhe ca pana ‘ke tumhe’ti puṭṭhā samānā ‘samaṇāmhā’ti paṭijānātha. Tesaṃ vo, bhikkhave, evaṃsamaññānaṃ sataṃ evaṃpaṭiññānaṃ sataṃ – ‘yā samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadā taṃ paṭipajjissāma; evaṃ no ayaṃ amhākaṃ samaññā ca saccā bhavissati paṭiññā ca bhūtā; yesañca mayaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ paribhuñjāma, tesaṃ te kārā amhesu mahapphalā bhavissanti mahānisaṃsā, amhākañcevāyaṃ pabbajjā avañjhā bhavissati saphalā saudrayā’ti. Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
435. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Aṅga country at a town of the Aṅgas named Assapura.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks (saying): "Bhikkhus."

"Venerable sir," those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this: "'Recluses, recluses,' monks, that is how people perceive you.

And when you are asked, ‘What are you? ‘, you claim that you are recluses.

Since that is what you are designated and what you claim to be : ‘We will undertake and practise that good conduct that makes one a recluse; thus our designation will be true and our claims genuine; and those from whom we receive robes, alms food, lodging, and medicine for the sick will have great reward and great benefit from us, and this going forth of ours will not be in vain, but fruitful and blessed.’

That is how you should train, bhikkhus.
commentary_pali: 435.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷaassapurasuttaṃ. Tassa desanākāraṇaṃ purimasadisameva. Samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadāti samaṇānaṃ anucchavikā samaṇānaṃ anulomappaṭipadā.
commentary_english: 435. *evaṃ me suta* is the Cūḷaassapurasuttaṃ. The reason for its teaching is just like the previous one. *samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadā* means conduct befitting ascetics, conduct in accordance with ascetics.

mula_pali: 436. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno hoti? Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno abhijjhālussa abhijjhā appahīnā hoti, byāpannacittassa byāpādo appahīno hoti, kodhanassa kodho appahīno hoti, upanāhissa upanāho appahīno hoti, makkhissa makkho appahīno hoti, paḷāsissa paḷāso appahīno hoti, issukissa issā appahīnā hoti, maccharissa macchariyaṃ appahīnaṃ hoti , saṭhassa sāṭheyyaṃ appahīnaṃ hoti, māyāvissa māyā appahīnā hoti, pāpicchassa pāpikā icchā appahīnā hoti, micchādiṭṭhikassa micchādiṭṭhi appahīnā hoti – imesaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, samaṇamalānaṃ samaṇadosānaṃ samaṇakasaṭānaṃ āpāyikānaṃ ṭhānānaṃ duggativedaniyānaṃ appahānā ‘na samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno’ti vadāmi. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, matajaṃ nāma āvudhajātaṃ ubhatodhāraṃ pītanisitaṃ. Tadassa saṅghāṭiyā sampārutaṃ sampaliveṭhitaṃ. Tathūpamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imassa bhikkhuno pabbajjaṃ vadāmi.
mula_english:
“And how, *bhikkhus*, is a *bhikkhu* not practicing the proper course of a *samaṇa*? In the case of whatever *bhikkhu*, *bhikkhus*, whose covetousness (*abhijjhā*) is not abandoned (*appahīna*), whose ill-will (*byāpāda*) is not abandoned, whose anger (*kodha*) is not abandoned, whose hostility (*upanāha*) is not abandoned, whose detraction (*makkha*) is not abandoned, whose insolence (*paḷāsa*) is not abandoned, whose envy (*issā*) is not abandoned, whose stinginess (*macchariya*) is not abandoned, whose deceit (*sāṭheyya*) is not abandoned, whose hypocrisy (*māyā*) is not abandoned, whose evil desires (*pāpikā icchā*) are not abandoned, whose wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*) is not abandoned—because of the non-abandonment (*appahāna*) of these defilements of a *samaṇa* (*samaṇamala*), faults of a *samaṇa* (*samaṇadosa*), impurities of a *samaṇa* (*samaṇakasaṭa*), things leading to misfortune (*āpāyika*), and resulting in suffering (*duggativedanīya*), I say [of such a *bhikkhu*] that he is ‘not practicing the proper course of a *samaṇa*.

“Just as, *bhikkhus*, a weapon (*āvudha*) called a *mataja*, sharpened on both sides and keen-edged, might be completely wrapped and swathed in a cloak (*saṅghāṭī*), so too, *bhikkhus*, do I declare the going forth (*pabbajja*) of this *bhikkhu*."
commentary_pali: 436.Samaṇamalānantiādīsu ete dhammā uppajjamānā samaṇe maline karonti malaggahite, tasmā ‘‘samaṇamalā’’ti vuccanti. Etehi samaṇā dussanti, padussanti, tasmā samaṇadosāti vuccanti. Ete uppajjitvā samaṇe kasaṭe niroje karonti milāpenti, tasmā samaṇakasaṭāti vuccanti. Āpāyikānaṃ ṭhānānanti apāye nibbattāpakānaṃ kāraṇānaṃ. Duggativedaniyānanti duggatiyaṃ vipākavedanāya paccayānaṃ. Matajaṃ nāmāti manussā tikhiṇaṃ ayaṃ ayena sughaṃsitvā taṃ ayacuṇṇaṃ maṃsena saddhiṃ madditvā koñcasakuṇe khādāpenti. Te uccāraṃ kātuṃ asakkontā maranti. No ce maranti, paharitvā mārenti. Atha tesaṃ kucchiṃ phāletvā naṃ udakena dhovitvā cuṇṇaṃ gahetvā maṃsena saddhiṃ madditvā puna khādāpentīti evaṃ satta vāre khādāpetvā gahitena ayacuṇṇena āvudhaṃ karonti. Susikkhitā ca naṃ ayakārā bahuhatthakammamūlaṃ labhitvā karonti. Taṃ matasakuṇato jātattā ‘‘mataja’’nti vuccati, atitikhiṇaṃ hoti. Pītanisitanti udakapītañceva silāya ca sunighaṃsitaṃ. Saṅghāṭiyāti kosiyā. Sampārutanti pariyonaddhaṃ. Sampaliveṭhitanti samantato veṭhitaṃ.
commentary_english:
436. *Samaṇamalānaṃ* etc.: These things, when arising, make ascetics impure, [and] are seized by impurity. Therefore, they are called "impurities of ascetics" (*samaṇamalā*).

By these, ascetics are corrupted and completely corrupted. Therefore, they are called "faults of ascetics" (*samaṇadosā*).

Having arisen, these make ascetics rough and unrefined, [and] cause [them to] wither. Therefore, they are called "roughness of ascetics" (*samaṇakasaṭā*).

*Āpāyikānaṃ ṭhānānaṃ*: Of the causes that bring about rebirth in states of loss (*apāya*).

*Duggativedaniyānaṃ*: Of the conditions for the experience of the result in a bad state (*duggati*).

*Matajaṃ nāmā*: People sharpen a very sharp iron [tool] with iron, and having crushed that iron powder together with meat, they feed it to herons.

Unable to excrete, they die.

If they do not die, they strike and kill [them].

Then, having cut open their stomachs, washed [the contents] with water, taken the powder, crushed it together with meat, and fed it again, they make a weapon with the iron powder taken after feeding [it to the bird] in this way seven times.

And skilled ironworkers, having obtained the means for much handwork, make it.

Because it is born from a dead bird, it is called *mataja*, and it is very sharp.

*Pītanisitaṃ*: Having been drunk with water and well-sharpened on a stone.

*Saṅghāṭiyā*: Of the cloak. ( *kosiya* )

*Sampārutaṃ*: Completely bound. ( *pariyonaddhaṃ* )

*Sampaliveṭhitaṃ*: Completely wrapped around. ( *samantato veṭhitaṃ* )

mula_pali:
437. ‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, saṅghāṭikassa saṅghāṭidhāraṇamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, acelakassa acelakamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, rajojallikassa rajojallikamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave , udakorohakassa udakorohaṇamattena udakorohakamattena (sī. pī.) sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, rukkhamūlikassa rukkhamūlikamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, abbhokāsikassa abbhokāsikamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ubbhaṭṭhakassa ubbhaṭṭhakamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pariyāyabhattikassa pariyāyabhattikamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, mantajjhāyakassa mantajjhāyakamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, jaṭilakassa jaṭādhāraṇamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi.

‘‘Saṅghāṭikassa ce, bhikkhave, saṅghāṭidhāraṇamattena abhijjhālussa abhijjhā pahīyetha, byāpannacittassa byāpādo pahīyetha, kodhanassa kodho pahīyetha, upanāhissa upanāho pahīyetha, makkhissa makkho pahīyetha, paḷāsissa paḷāso pahīyetha, issukissa issā pahīyetha, maccharissa macchariyaṃ pahīyetha, saṭhassa sāṭheyyaṃ pahīyetha, māyāvissa māyā pahīyetha, pāpicchassa pāpikā icchā pahīyetha, micchādiṭṭhikassa micchādiṭṭhi pahīyetha, tamenaṃ mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā jātameva naṃ saṅghāṭikaṃ kareyyuṃ, saṅghāṭikattameva saṃghāṭīkatte ceva (ka.) samādapeyyuṃ – ‘ehi tvaṃ, bhadramukha, saṅghāṭiko hohi, saṅghāṭikassa te sato saṅghāṭidhāraṇamattena abhijjhālussa abhijjhā pahīyissati, byāpannacittassa byāpādo pahīyissati, kodhanassa kodho pahīyissati, upanāhissa upanāho pahīyissati, makkhissa makkho pahīyissati, paḷāsissa paḷāso pahīyissati, issukissa issā pahīyissati, maccharissa macchariyaṃ pahīyissati, saṭhassa sāṭheyyaṃ pahīyissati, māyāvissa māyā pahīyissati, pāpicchassa pāpikā icchā pahīyissati, micchādiṭṭhikassa micchādiṭṭhi pahīyissatī’ti. Yasmā ca kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, saṅghāṭikampi idhekaccaṃ passāmi abhijjhāluṃ byāpannacittaṃ kodhanaṃ upanāhiṃ makkhiṃ paḷāsiṃ issukiṃ macchariṃ saṭhaṃ māyāviṃ pāpicchaṃ micchādiṭṭhikaṃ, tasmā na saṅghāṭikassa saṅghāṭidhāraṇamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi.

saṃghāṭīkatte ceva (ka.)

‘‘Acelakassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… rajojallikassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… udakorohakassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… rukkhamūlikassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… abbhokāsikassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… ubbhaṭṭhakassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… pariyāyabhattikassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… mantajjhāyakassa ce, bhikkhave…pe… jaṭilakassa ce, bhikkhave, jaṭādhāraṇamattena abhijjhālussa abhijjhā pahīyetha, byāpannacittassa byāpādo pahīyetha , kodhanassa kodho pahīyetha, upanāhissa upanāho pahīyetha, makkhissa makkho pahīyetha, paḷāsissa paḷāso pahīyetha, issukissa issā pahīyetha, maccharissa macchariyaṃ pahīyetha, saṭhassa sāṭheyyaṃ pahīyetha, māyāvissa māyā pahīyetha, pāpicchassa pāpikā icchā pahīyetha, micchādiṭṭhikassa micchādiṭṭhi pahīyetha, tamenaṃ mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā jātameva naṃ jaṭilakaṃ kareyyuṃ, jaṭilakattameva jaṭilakatte ceva (ka.) samādapeyyuṃ – ‘ehi tvaṃ, bhadramukha, jaṭilako hohi, jaṭilakassa te sato jaṭādhāraṇamattena abhijjhālussa abhijjhā pahīyissati byāpannacittassa byāpādo pahīyissati, kodhanassa kodho pahīyissati…pe… pāpicchassa pāpikā icchā pahīyissati micchādiṭṭhikassa micchādiṭṭhi pahīyissatī’ti. Yasmā ca kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, jaṭilakampi idhekaccaṃ passāmi abhijjhāluṃ byāpannacittaṃ kodhanaṃ upanāhiṃ makkhiṃ palāsiṃ issukiṃ macchariṃ saṭhaṃ māyāviṃ pāpicchaṃ micchādiṭṭhiṃ, tasmā na jaṭilakassa jaṭādhāraṇamattena sāmaññaṃ vadāmi.

jaṭilakatte ceva (ka.)
mula_english:
“Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of wearing the outer robe (saṃghāṭī).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of being naked (acelaka).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of being covered in dust and grime (rajojallika).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of plunging into water periodically (udakorohaka).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of dwelling at the root of a tree (rukkh mūlika).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of dwelling in the open air (abbhokāsika).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of dwelling in a cemetery (ubbhaṭṭhaka).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of eating food obtained by gleaning (pariyāyabhattika).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of reciting mantras (mantajjhāyaka).
Monks, I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of wearing matted hair (jaṭilaka).

If, monks, by merely wearing the outer robe, one who is greedy (abhijjhālu) were to abandon greed (abhijjhā), one whose mind is malevolent (byāpannacitta) were to abandon malevolence (byāpāda), one who is angry (kodhana) were to abandon anger (kodha), one who is resentful (upanāhi) were to abandon resentment (upanāha), one who is denigrating (makkhi) were to abandon denigration (makkha), one who is controlling (palāsi) were to abandon being controlling (palāsa), one who is envious (issuki) were to abandon envy (issā), one who is miserly (macchari) were to abandon miserliness (macchariyaṃ), one who is deceitful (saṭha) were to abandon deceit (sāṭheyyaṃ), one who is deceptive (māyāvi) were to abandon deception (māyā), one who has evil desires (pāpiccha) were to abandon evil desires (pāpikā icchā), one who has wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi) were to abandon wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi), then their friends, companions, relatives, and kin would make them wear the outer robe from birth, urging them simply to wear the outer robe, saying: ‘Come, good sir, be a wearer of the outer robe. While you are wearing the outer robe, by merely wearing it, the greed of the greedy will be abandoned, the malevolence of the malevolent-minded will be abandoned, the anger of the angry will be abandoned, the resentment of the resentful will be abandoned, the denigration of the denigrating will be abandoned, the controlling nature of the controlling will be abandoned, the envy of the envious will be abandoned, the miserliness of the miserly will be abandoned, the deceit of the deceitful will be abandoned, the deception of the deceptive will be abandoned, the evil desires of those with evil desires will be abandoned, and the wrong view of those with wrong view will be abandoned.’ But since I see some wearers of the outer robe here who are greedy, malevolent-minded, angry, resentful, denigrating, controlling, envious, miserly, deceitful, deceptive, having evil desires, and having wrong view, therefore I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of wearing the outer robe.

If, monks, by merely being naked… If, monks, by merely being covered in dust and grime… If, monks, by merely plunging into water periodically… If, monks, by merely dwelling at the root of a tree… If, monks, by merely dwelling in the open air… If, monks, by merely dwelling in a cemetery… If, monks, by merely eating food obtained by gleaning… If, monks, by merely reciting mantras… If, monks, by merely wearing matted hair, one who is greedy were to abandon greed, one whose mind is malevolent were to abandon malevolence, one who is angry were to abandon anger, one who is resentful were to abandon resentment, one who is denigrating were to abandon denigration, one who is controlling were to abandon being controlling, one who is envious were to abandon envy, one who is miserly were to abandon miserliness, one who is deceitful were to abandon deceit, one who is deceptive were to abandon deception, one who has evil desires were to abandon evil desires, one who has wrong view were to abandon wrong view, then their friends, companions, relatives, and kin would make them wear matted hair from birth, urging them simply to wear matted hair, saying: ‘Come, good sir, be a wearer of matted hair. While you are wearing matted hair, by merely wearing it, the greed of the greedy will be abandoned, the malevolence of the malevolent-minded will be abandoned, the anger of the angry will be abandoned… the evil desires of those with evil desires will be abandoned, and the wrong view of those with wrong view will be abandoned.’ But since I see some wearers of matted hair here who are greedy, malevolent-minded, angry, resentful, denigrating, controlling, envious, miserly, deceitful, deceptive, having evil desires, and having wrong view, therefore I do not call someone a true ascetic simply because of wearing matted hair."
commentary_pali: 437.Rajojallikassāti rajojalladhārino. Udakorohakassāti divasassa tikkhattuṃ udakaṃ orohantassa. Rukkhamūlikassāti rukkhamūlavāsino. Abbhokāsikassāti abbhokāsavāsino. Ubbhaṭṭhakassāti uddhaṃ ṭhitakassa. Pariyāyabhattikassāti māsavārena vā aḍḍhamāsavārena vā bhuñjantassa. Sabbametaṃ bāhirasamayeneva kathitaṃ. Imasmiñhi sāsane cīvaradharo bhikkhu saṅghāṭikoti na vuccati. Rajojalladhāraṇādivatāni imasmiṃ sāsane natthiyeva. Buddhavacanassa buddhavacanameva nāmaṃ, na mantāti. Rukkhamūliko, abbhokāsikoti ettakaṃyeva pana labbhati. Tampi bāhirasamayeneva kathitaṃ. Jātamevananti taṃdivase jātamattaṃyeva naṃ. Saṅghāṭikaṃ kareyyunti saṅghāṭikaṃ vatthaṃ nivāsetvā ca pārupitvā ca saṅghāṭikaṃ kareyyuṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha.
commentary_english:
437.
"rajojallikassā": "one who possesses the *rajojalla*."
"udakorohakassā": "one who descends into the water three times a day."
"rukkhamūlikassā": "one who dwells at the root of a tree (ṛukkhamūlavāsin)."
"abbhokāsikassā": "one who dwells in the open air."
"ubbhaṭṭhakassā": "one who is standing upright."
"pariyāyabhattikassā": "one who eats according to a monthly or half-monthly rotation."
All this has been said according to external conventions.
In this teaching (*sāsana*), a monk who wears robes (*cīvaradharaḥ bhikṣu*) is not called a *saṅghāṭika*.
Practices such as wearing the *rajojalla*, etc., do not exist in this teaching (*sāsane*).
The word of the Buddha (*buddhavacana*) is only called the word of the Buddha, not a mantra.
Only the tree-root dweller (*ṛukkhamūliko*), and the open-air dweller (*abbhokāsiko*) are obtained thus.
That too has been said according to external conventions.
"jātameva": "as soon as [he is] born."
"na": on that day, just as [he is] born.
"saṅghāṭikaṃ kareyyuṃ": they should make a *saṅghāṭika*, having put on and wrapped the cloth of the *saṅghāṭika*, they should make a *saṅghāṭika*.
This method applies everywhere (*esa nayo sabbattha*).

mula_pali:
438. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno hoti? Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno abhijjhālussa abhijjhā pahīnā hoti, byāpannacittassa byāpādo pahīno hoti, kodhanassa kodho pahīno hoti, upanāhissa upanāho pahīno hoti, makkhissa makkho pahīno hoti, paḷāsissa paḷāso pahīno hoti, issukissa issā pahīnā hoti, maccharissa macchariyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, saṭhassa sāṭheyyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, māyāvissa māyā pahīnā hoti, pāpicchassa pāpikā icchā pahīnā hoti, micchādiṭṭhikassa micchādiṭṭhi pahīnā hoti – imesaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, samaṇamalānaṃ samaṇadosānaṃ samaṇakasaṭānaṃ āpāyikānaṃ ṭhānānaṃ duggativedaniyānaṃ pahānā ‘samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno’ti vadāmi. So sabbehi imehi pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi visuddhamattānaṃ samanupassati ( ) (vimuttamattānaṃ samanupassati) (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Tassa sabbehi imehi pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi visuddhamattānaṃ samanupassato ( ) (vimuttamattānaṃ samanupassato) (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pāmojjaṃ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedeti, sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati.

‘‘So mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pokkharaṇī acchodakā sātodakā sītodakā setakā supatitthā ramaṇīyā. Puratthimāya cepi disāya puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito. So taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ āgamma vineyya udakapipāsaṃ vineyya ghammapariḷāhaṃ…pe… pacchimāya cepi disāya puriso āgaccheyya…pe… uttarāya cepi disāya puriso āgaccheyya…pe… dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya puriso āgaccheyya. Yato kuto cepi naṃ puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto, kilanto tasito pipāsito. So taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ āgamma vineyya udakapipāsaṃ, vineyya ghammapariḷāhaṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma, evaṃ mettaṃ karuṇaṃ muditaṃ upekkhaṃ bhāvetvā labhati ajjhattaṃ tamahaṃ (ka.) vūpasamaṃ tamahaṃ (ka.). Ajjhattaṃ vūpasamā ‘samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno’ti vadāmi. Brāhmaṇakulā cepi…pe… vessakulā cepi…pe… suddakulā cepi…pe… yasmā kasmā cepi kulā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti , so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma, evaṃ mettaṃ karuṇaṃ muditaṃ upekkhaṃ bhāvetvā labhati ajjhattaṃ vūpasamaṃ. Ajjhattaṃ vūpasamā ‘samaṇasāmīcippaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno’ti vadāmi.

tamahaṃ (ka.) tamahaṃ (ka.)

‘‘Khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti. So ca āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Āsavānaṃ khayā samaṇo hoti. Brāhmaṇakulā cepi…pe… vessakulā cepi… suddakulā cepi… yasmā kasmā cepi kulā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Āsavānaṃ khayā samaṇo hotī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Cūḷaassapurasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Mahāyamakavaggo niṭṭhito catuttho.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Giñjakasālavanaṃ pariharituṃ, paññavato puna saccakanisedho;

Mukhavaṇṇapasīdanatāpindo, kevaṭṭaassapurajaṭilena.
mula_english:
438. And how, monks, does a monk practice the proper course of conduct befitting a *samaṇa*? In whatsoever monk, monks, greed has been eliminated in one who is greedy, ill-will has been eliminated in one whose mind is full of ill-will, anger has been eliminated in one who is angry, hostility has been eliminated in one who is hostile, contempt has been eliminated in one who is contemptuous, insolence has been eliminated in one who is insolent, envy has been eliminated in one who is envious, stinginess has been eliminated in one who is stingy, deceit has been eliminated in one who is deceitful, hypocrisy has been eliminated in one who is hypocritical, evil desires have been eliminated in one with evil desires, wrong view has been eliminated in one with wrong view—it is through the elimination of these corruptions of a *samaṇa*, these faults of a *samaṇa*, these stains of a *samaṇa*, states that lead to misery, that lead to suffering, that I say [he] practices the proper course of conduct befitting a *samaṇa*.

He sees himself as purified of all these evil, unwholesome qualities. As he sees himself purified of all these evil, unwholesome qualities, gladness (*prāmojjaṃ*) arises. When he is gladdened, rapture (*pīti*) arises. When his mind is filled with rapture, his body becomes tranquil (*passaddhi*); tranquil in body, he experiences happiness (*sukhaṃ*); being happy, his mind becomes concentrated (*samādhi*).

He abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (*mettāsahagatena cetasā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, around, everywhere, in its entirety, he abides pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility (*averena*) and without ill-will (*abyābajjhena*). With a mind imbued with compassion (*karuṇāsahagatena cetasā*)… with a mind imbued with appreciative joy (*muditāsahagatena cetasā*)… with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekkhāsahagatena cetasā*) he abides pervading one quarter, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, around, everywhere, in its entirety, he abides pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility and without ill-will.

Suppose there were a pond with clean, agreeable, cool water, transparent, with smooth banks, delightful. And a man came from the east scorched and exhausted by hot weather, weary, parched, and thirsty. Having come to that pond, he would get rid of his thirst for water and the burning heat…. And a man came from the west…. And a man came from the north…. And a man came from the south. From whatever direction a man came, scorched and exhausted by hot weather, weary, parched, and thirsty, having come to that pond, he would get rid of his thirst for water and the burning heat.

In the same way, monks, if someone from a noble family has gone forth from the house life into homelessness, and having come to the *dhamma* and discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, thus cultivates loving-kindness, compassion, appreciative joy, and equanimity, he attains inner peace (*ajjhattaṃ vūpasamaṃ*). Through inner peace, I say [he] practices the proper course of conduct befitting a *samaṇa*. If someone from a brahmin family…if someone from a merchant family…if someone from a worker family…if someone from whatever family has gone forth from the house life into homelessness, and having come to the *dhamma* and discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, thus cultivates loving-kindness, compassion, appreciative joy, and equanimity, he attains inner peace. Through inner peace, I say [he] practices the proper course of conduct befitting a *samaṇa*.

If someone from a noble family has gone forth from the house life into homelessness…
And he, through the destruction of the *āsavas* (influxes, taints, defilements), having realized it himself with direct knowledge, in this very life enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind (*anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ*), liberation by wisdom (*paññāvimuttiṃ*).

Through the destruction of the *āsavas*, one becomes a *samaṇa* (ascetic).

Even from a Brahmin family... or a *Vessa* (merchant) family... or a *Suddha* (laborer) family... from whatever family he has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, he, through the destruction of the *āsavas*, having realized it himself with direct knowledge, in this very life enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind (*anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ*), liberation by wisdom (*paññāvimuttiṃ*).

Through the destruction of the *āsavas*, one becomes a *samaṇa* (ascetic).

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*bhagavān*). Those monks, uplifted, rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words.
commentary_pali:
438.Visuddhamattānaṃ samanupassatīti attānaṃ visujjhantaṃ passati. Visuddhoti pana na tāva vattabbo. Pāmojjaṃ jāyatīti tuṭṭhākāro jāyati. Pamuditassa pītīti tuṭṭhassa sakalasarīraṃ khobhayamānā pīti jāyati. Pītimanassa kāyoti pītisampayuttassa puggalassa nāmakāyo. Passambhatīti vigatadaratho hoti. Sukhaṃ vedetīti kāyikampi cetasikampi sukhaṃ vediyati. Cittaṃ samādhiyatīti iminā nekkhammasukhena sukhitassa cittaṃ samādhiyati, appanāpattaṃ viya hoti. So mettāsahagatena cetasāti heṭṭhā kilesavasena āraddhā desanā pabbate vuṭṭhavuṭṭhi viya nadiṃ yathānusandhinā brahmavihārabhāvanaṃ otiṇṇā. Tattha yaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, taṃ sabbaṃ visuddhimagge vuttameva. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pokkharaṇīti mahāsīhanādasutte maggo pokkharaṇiyā upamito, idha sāsanaṃ upamitanti veditabbaṃ. Āsavānaṃ khayā samaṇo hotīti sabbakilesānaṃ samitattā paramatthasamaṇo hotīti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷaassapurasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Catutthavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
438. “He observes himself as pure (visuddhamattānaṃ samanupassatī)” means he sees himself becoming pure.

However, it is not yet to be called pure.

“Joy arises (pāmojjaṃ jāyatī)” means a state of satisfaction arises.

“For the joyful, rapture (pītī) [comes] (pamuditassa pītī)” means for the satisfied, rapture arises, agitating the whole body.

“The body of one with rapture (pītimanassa kāyo)” means the mental body (*nāmakāya*) of a person endowed with rapture.

“Becomes tranquil (passambhatī)” means he is without agitation.

“He experiences happiness (sukhaṃ vedetī)” means he experiences bodily happiness (kāyikampi) and mental happiness (cetasikampi).

“The mind becomes concentrated (cittaṃ samādhiyatī)” means the mind of one who is happy with this happiness of renunciation (nekkhamma-sukhena) becomes concentrated; it is as if it has attained absorption (*appanā*).

“He, with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness (so mettāsahagatena cetasā)” means the teaching begun below in terms of defilements, like rain falling on a mountain, has descended into the development (*bhāvana*) of the divine abodes (*brahmavihāra*) in accordance with the connection [of the text].

Whatever should be said there, all that has been said in the *Visuddhimagga* itself.

"Just as, monks, a lotus pond (seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pokkharaṇī)" in the Mahāsīhanāda Sutta, the path is compared to a lotus pond; here, the dispensation (*sāsana*) is to be understood as compared.

“Through the destruction of the corruptions, he becomes a *samaṇa* (āsavānaṃ khayā samaṇo hotī)” means because of the calming (*samatattā*) of all defilements, he becomes a *samaṇa* in the ultimate sense (*paramattha*).

The rest is clear throughout.

The Cūḷaassapura Sutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

The Fourth Varga Commentary is finished.

mula_pali:
439. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena sālā nāma kosalānaṃ brāhmaṇagāmo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā – ‘‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ sālaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ; kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti’. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’’ti.

Atha kho sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti ? Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī’’ti?

‘‘Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, gahapatayo, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti. Dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, gahapatayo, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī’’ti .

‘‘Na kho mayaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa, vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa, vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāma. Sādhu no bhavaṃ gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetu, yathā mayaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa, vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa, vitthārena atthaṃ ājāneyyāmā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, gahapatayo, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
439. Thus I have heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kosala country with a large Saṅgha of monks, and he arrived at a town of Kosala called Sāla, a Brahmin village.

The brahmin householders of Sāla heard: “The recluse Gotama, the son of the Sakyans, who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the Kosalan country with a large Sangha of *bhikkhus* and has come to Sāla.

And concerning this Blessed Lord Gotama, a good report has been spread about: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an *Arhat*, a Fully Enlightened One (*sammāsambuddho*), endowed with knowledge and good conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), a Well-Gone One (*sugato*), knower of the world (*lokavidū*), unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed (*anuttaro purisadammasārathi*), teacher of gods and humans (*satthā devamanussānaṃ*), the Awakened One (*buddho*), the Blessed One (*bhagavā*)’.

He, having realized it by his own super-knowledge (*abhiññā*), proclaims this world with its gods (*sadevakaṃ*), with its *Māras* (*samārakaṃ*), and with its *Brahmās* (*sabrahmakaṃ*), this generation with its ascetics and Brahmins (*sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ*), its princes and people (*sadevamanussaṃ*).

He teaches the *Dhamma* (*dhammaṃ*) which is good in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇaṃ*), good in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇaṃ*), and good in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ*), with the right meaning (*sātthaṃ*) and phrasing (*sabyañjanaṃ*); he reveals a life of purity (*brahmacariyaṃ*) that is utterly perfect (*kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ*) and purified (*parisuddhaṃ*)’.

It is good to see such *arahants*."

Then the Sāleyyakā Brahmin householders went to the Blessed One. On arrival, some bowed down to the Blessed One and sat to one side; some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and when this courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down to one side; some extended their hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some pronounced their name and clan in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down to one side; some kept silent and sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the Sāleyyakā Brahmin householders said to the Blessed One: “What is the cause and condition, Master Gotama, why some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in states of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), in an unhappy destination (*duggatiṃ*), in perdition (*vinipātaṃ*), even in hell (*nirayaṃ*)? Or what is the cause and condition, Master Gotama, why some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), even in the heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ*)?”

“Householders, it is by reason of conduct not in accordance with the *Dhamma* (*adhamma cariyā*) and unrighteous conduct (*visama cariyā*) that some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in states of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), in an unhappy destination (*duggatiṃ*), in perdition (*vinipātaṃ*), even in hell (*nirayaṃ*).

Householders, it is by reason of conduct in accordance with the *Dhamma* (*dhamma cariyā*) and righteous conduct (*sama cariyā*) that some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), even in the heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ*).”

“We do not understand the detailed meaning of Master Gotama’s utterance, which he has spoken in brief without expounding the detailed meaning.

It would be good if Master Gotama would teach us the *Dhamma* (*dhammaṃ*) so that we might understand the detailed meaning of his utterance."

“Then, householders, listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” they replied.

The Blessed One said this:
commentary_pali:
439.Evaṃme sutanti sāleyyakasuttaṃ. Tattha kosalesūti kosalā nāma jānapadino rājakumārā. Tesaṃ nivāso ekopi janapado ruḷhīsaddena kosalāti vuccati, tasmiṃ kosalesu janapade. Porāṇā panāhu – yasmā pubbe mahāpanādaṃ rājakumāraṃ nānānāṭakāni disvā sitamattampi akarontaṃ sutvā rājā āha – ‘‘yo mama puttaṃ hasāpeti, sabbālaṅkārena naṃ alaṅkaromī’’ti. Tato naṅgalānipi chaḍḍetvā mahājanakāye sannipatite manussā sātirekāni sattavassāni nānākīḷikāyo dassetvā naṃ hasāpetuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Tato sakko devanaṭaṃ pesesi. So dibbanāṭakaṃ dassetvā hasāpesi. Atha te manussā attano attano vasanokāsābhimukhā pakkamiṃsu. Te paṭipathe mittasuhajjādayo disvā paṭisanthāraṃ karontā, ‘‘kacci, bho, kusalaṃ, kacci, bho, kusala’’nti āhaṃsu. Tasmā taṃ ‘‘kusalaṃ kusala’’nti vacanaṃ upādāya so padeso kosalāti vuccatīti.

Cārikaṃ caramānoti aturitacārikaṃ caramāno. Mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhinti sataṃ vā sahassaṃ vā satasahassaṃ vāti evaṃ aparicchinnena mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Brāhmaṇagāmoti brāhmaṇānaṃ samosaraṇagāmopi brāhmaṇagāmoti vuccati brāhmaṇānaṃ bhogagāmopi. Idha samosaraṇagāmo adhippeto. Tadavasarīti taṃ avasari, sampattoti attho. Vihāro panettha aniyāmito; tasmā tassa avidūre buddhānaṃ anucchaviko eko vanasaṇḍo bhavissati, satthā taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ gatoti veditabbo. Assosunti suṇiṃsu upalabhiṃsu. Sotadvārasampattavacananigghosānusārena jāniṃsu. Khoti avadhāraṇatthe padapūraṇamatte vā nipāto. Tattha avadhāraṇatthena assosuṃyeva , na nesaṃ koci savanantarāyo ahosīti ayamattho veditabbo. Padapūraṇena byañjanasiliṭṭhatāmattameva.

Cārikaṃ caramāno Mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhi Brāhmaṇagāmo Tadavasarī Assosu Kho

Idāni yamatthaṃ assosuṃ, taṃ pakāsetuṃ samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamotiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha samitapāpattā samaṇoti veditabbo. Khalūti anussavanatthe nipāto. Bhoti tesaṃ aññamaññaṃ ālapanamattaṃ. Gotamoti bhagavato gottavasena paridīpanaṃ. Tasmā samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamoti ettha samaṇo kira, bho, gotamagottoti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Sakyaputtoti idaṃ pana bhagavato uccākulaparidīpanaṃ. Sakyakulā pabbajitoti saddhāpabbajitabhāvadīpanaṃ. Kenaci pārijuññena anabhibhūto aparikkhīṇaṃyeva taṃ kulaṃ pahāya saddhāpabbajitoti vuttaṃ hoti. Tato paraṃ vuttatthameva. Taṃ kho panāti itthambhūtākhyānatthe upayogavacanaṃ, tassa kho pana bhoto gotamassāti attho. Kalyāṇoti kalyāṇaguṇasamannāgato, seṭṭhoti vuttaṃ hoti. Kittisaddoti kittiyeva, thutighoso vā. Abbhuggatoti sadevakaṃ lokaṃ ajjhottharitvā uggato. Kinti? ‘‘Itipi so bhagavā…pe… buddho bhagavā’’ti.

samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo samaṇo Khalū Bho Gotamo samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo Sakyaputto Sakyakulā pabbajito Taṃ kho panā Kalyāṇo Kittisaddo Abbhuggato

Tatrāyaṃ padasambandho – so bhagavā itipi arahaṃ, itipi sammāsambuddho…pe… itipi bhagavāti. Iminā ca iminā ca kāraṇenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha ārakattā, arīnaṃ arānañca hatattā, paccayādīnaṃ arahattā, pāpakaraṇe rahābhāvāti imehi tāva kāraṇehi so bhagavā arahanti veditabbotiādinā nayena mātikaṃ nikkhipitvā sabbāneva etāni padāni visuddhimagge buddhānussatiniddese vitthāritānīti tato tesaṃ vitthāro gahetabbo.

Sādhu kho panāti sundaraṃ kho pana; atthāvahaṃ sukhāvahanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tathārūpānaṃ arahatanti yathārūpo so bhavaṃ gotamo, evarūpānaṃ anekehipi kappakoṭisatasahassehi dullabhadassanānaṃ byāmappabhāparikkhittehi asītianubyañjanaratanapaṭimaṇḍitehi dvattiṃsmahāpurisalakkhaṇavarehi samākiṇṇamanoramasarīrānaṃ atappakadassanānaṃ atimadhuradhammanigghosānaṃ, yathābhūtaguṇādhigamena loke arahantoti laddhasaddānaṃ arahataṃ. Dassanaṃ hotīti pasādasommāni akkhīni ummīletvā dassanamattampi sādhu hoti. Sace pana aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatena brahmassarena dhammaṃ desentassa ekaṃ padampi sotuṃ labhissāma, sādhutaraṃyeva bhavissatīti evaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ katvā.

Sādhu kho panā Tathārūpānaṃ arahata Dassanaṃ hotī

Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsūti sabbakiccāni pahāya tuṭṭhamānasā āgamaṃsu. Etadavocunti duvidhā hi pucchā agārikapucchā anagārikapucchā ca. Tattha ‘‘kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusala’’nti iminā nayena agārikapucchā āgatā. ‘‘Ime kho, bhante, pañcupādānakkhandhā’’ti iminā nayena anagārikapucchā. Ime pana attano anurūpaṃ agārikapucchaṃ pucchantā etaṃ, ‘‘ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo’’tiādivacanaṃ avocuṃ. Tesaṃ bhagavā yathā na sakkonti sallakkhetuṃ, evaṃ saṃkhitteneva tāva pañhaṃ vissajjento, adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho gahapatayotiādimāha. Kasmā pana bhagavā yathā na sallakkhenti, evaṃ vissajjesīti? Paṇḍitamānikā hi te; āditova mātikaṃ aṭṭhapetvā yathā sallakkhenti, evaṃ atthe vitthārite, desanaṃ uttānikāti maññantā avajānanti, mayampi kathentā evameva katheyyāmāti vattāro bhavanti. Tena nesaṃ bhagavā yathā na sakkonti sallakkhetuṃ, evaṃ saṃkhitteneva tāva pañhaṃ vissajjesi. Tato sallakkhetuṃ asakkontehi vitthāradesanaṃ yācito vitthārena desetuṃ, tena hi gahapatayotiādimāha. Tattha tena hīti kāraṇatthe nipāto. Yasmā maṃ tumhe yācatha, tasmāti attho.

Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsū Etadavocu adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho gahapatayo tena hi gahapatayo tena hī
commentary_english:
439. Thus have I heard: the Sāleyyakasutta.

Therein, *kosalesū* means Kosala, namely, princes of a rural district. Their dwelling place, even a single district, is called Kosala by way of established convention. In that Kosala district, the elders said: "Because formerly, upon seeing Prince Mahāpanāda watching various dramas without even a slight smile, the king said, 'Whoever makes my son laugh, I will adorn him with all ornaments.'" Then, having cast aside even their plows, men gathered in the great assembly tried for seven years, displaying various games, but they were not able to make him laugh.

Then Sakka sent the divine dancer. He made him laugh by showing a divine drama. Then those men departed, each heading towards their own dwelling place. On the road, seeing friends and companions, they exchanged greetings, saying, "Is it well, friend? Is it well?" Therefore, taking up that saying, "Is it well? Is it well?", that region is called Kosala.

*cārikaṃ caramāno* means wandering on a journey without haste. *mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhi* means with a great community of monks, whether a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand, thus with an immeasurable great community of monks. *brāhmaṇagāmo* means a village of Brahmins, a village where Brahmins assemble, or a village for the enjoyment of Brahmins. Here, a village of assembly is intended. *tadavasarī* means he approached that, the meaning is, he attained it.

Here, the monastery is unrestricted; therefore, not far from it, there will be an appropriate grove for the Buddhas; the teacher should be understood to have gone to that grove. *assosu* means they heard, they perceived. They knew according to the sound of the words arriving at the ear-door. *kho* is a particle used for emphasis or merely to fill out the line.

There, with emphasis, they only heard, and there was no obstruction to their hearing, this meaning should be understood. By filling out the line, there is only elegance of expression.

*cārikaṃ caramāno*, *mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhi*, *brāhmaṇagāmo*, *tadavasarī*, *assosu*, *kho*.

Now, in order to reveal what meaning they heard, *samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo* etc. is said. There, *samaṇo* should be understood as one who has calmed down evil deeds. *khalū* is a particle indicating hearsay. *bho* is merely an address to one another. *gotamo* is a designation according to the family lineage of the Blessed One (Bhagavat). Therefore, *samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo* here means, "It is said that the *śramaṇa* is of the Gotama lineage," this is how the meaning should be understood. *sakyaputto* means that this is a declaration of the Blessed One's high lineage. *sakyakulā pabbajito* means a declaration of having gone forth out of faith.

It is said that having abandoned that family without being overcome by any deprivation and while it was not yet diminished, he went forth out of faith. Thereafter, the meaning is the same as previously stated. *taṃ kho panā* is a word of use in the meaning of describing such a state, the meaning is, "of that venerable Gotama."
*Kalyāṇo* means endowed with auspicious qualities, excellent.

*Kittisaddo* means just fame, or a sound of praise.

*Abbhuggato* means having risen, having risen pervading the world with its deities.

What is it? "[He] is such, the Blessed One…pe…the Buddha, the Blessed One."

The ascetic Gotama, indeed, sirs. The ascetic, indeed, sirs, Gotama, the ascetic Gotama, indeed, sirs, is a son of the Śākya, gone forth from the Śākya clan, that indeed, is auspicious.

*Kittisaddo abbhuggato*

Here is the connection of words: "That Blessed One is such, since he is an Arhat, he is such, since he is a perfectly awakened one...pe...he is such, since he is a Blessed One."

It is said: By this reason and by this reason.

There, because of being far away, because of the killing of enemies and what should not be given, because of being worthy of offerings etc., because of the absence of secrecy in evil actions, by these reasons that Blessed One is worthy of offerings should be known. Having placed the outline in such a way, all these words have been expanded in the chapter on mindfulness of the Buddha in the *Visuddhimagga*, therefore their expansion should be taken from there.

*Sādhu kho panā* means beautiful indeed; it is said to bring benefit and happiness.

*Tathārūpānaṃ arahata* means the Arahants of such a form; as the Blessed Gotama is, the Arahants in the world who have obtained such fame, whose sight is difficult to obtain even in hundreds of thousands of millions of aeons, who are surrounded by a fathom's extent of light, who are adorned with eighty minor marks, jewel-like, who have bodies that are crowded with the best of the thirty-two marks of a great man, whose sight is pleasing, whose exceedingly sweet voice is like the sound of the Dharma, through the attainment of qualities that are in accordance with reality.

*Dassanaṃ hotī* means even just seeing is good, having opened eyes that are delightful and gentle.

If, with a voice complete with the eight qualities of Brahmā, we will be able to hear even one word of him teaching the Dharma, it will be even better, having made such an intention.

*Sādhu kho panā tathārūpānaṃ arahata dassanaṃ hotī*

*Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsū* means having abandoned all their duties, they came with joyful minds.

*Etadavocu* means indeed there are two kinds of questions, questions of householders and questions of those who have gone forth.

There, "What, venerable sir, is skillful, what is unskillful?" In this way, the question of householders has come.

"These, venerable sir, are the five aggregates of clinging." In this way, the question of those who have gone forth.

But these, asking a question of householders that was appropriate to themselves, said this: "What now, venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition?" etc.

As the Blessed One was unable to make them understand, in that way, briefly answering the question, he said, "*adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho gahapatayo*" etc.

But why did the Blessed One answer in such a way that they were unable to understand? Because they were conceited know-it-alls; for if he established the outline from the beginning and then expanded the meaning in such a way that they could understand, they would despise the teaching, thinking, "The teaching is obvious, we ourselves, if we were speaking, would speak in just this way."

Therefore, as the Blessed One was unable to make them understand, in that way, he briefly answered the question.

Then, when those who were unable to understand requested an expanded teaching, he said in order to teach in detail, "*tena hi gahapatayo*" etc.

There, *tena hī* is a particle in the sense of cause.

Because you ask me, therefore it means.

*Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsū etadavocu adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho gahapatayo tena hi gahapatayo tena hī*

mula_pali:
440. ‘‘Tividhaṃ kho, gahapatayo, kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti, catubbidhaṃ vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti, tividhaṃ manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, luddo luddo dāruṇo (ka.) ṭīkā oloketabbā lohitapāṇi hatappahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu sabbapāṇabhūtesu (syā. kaṃ. ka.).

luddo dāruṇo (ka.) ṭīkā oloketabbā sabbapāṇabhūtesu (syā. kaṃ. ka.)

‘‘Adinnādāyī kho pana hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ, gāmagataṃ vā araññagataṃ vā, taṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti.

‘‘Kāmesumicchācārī kho pana hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā dhammarakkhitā sassāmikā saparidaṇḍā antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca , gahapatayo, catubbidhaṃ vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco musāvādī hoti. Sabhāgato vā parisāgato vā, ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā, abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho – ‘ehambho purisa, yaṃ jānāsi taṃ vadehī’ti , so ajānaṃ vā āha – ‘jānāmī’ti, jānaṃ vā āha – ‘na jānāmī’ti, apassaṃ vā āha – ‘passāmī’ti, passaṃ vā āha – ‘na passāmī’ti so āha ajānaṃ vā ahaṃ jānāmīti jānaṃ vā ahaṃ na jānāmīti apassaṃ vā ahaṃ passāmīti passaṃ vā ahaṃ na passāmīti (ka.). Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.

so āha ajānaṃ vā ahaṃ jānāmīti jānaṃ vā ahaṃ na jānāmīti apassaṃ vā ahaṃ passāmīti passaṃ vā ahaṃ na passāmīti (ka.)

‘‘Pisuṇavāco kho pana hoti. Ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti samaggānaṃ vā bhettā bhedakā (ka.), bhedetā (syā. kaṃ.), tadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana bhettāti dissati, bhinnānaṃ vā anuppadātā, vaggārāmo vaggarato vagganandī vaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

bhedakā (ka.), bhedetā (syā. kaṃ.), tadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana bhettāti dissati

‘‘Pharusavāco kho pana hoti. Yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kaṇḍakā (ka.) kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā asamādhisaṃvattanikā , tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

kaṇḍakā (ka.)

‘‘Samphappalāpī kho pana hoti. Akālavādī abhūtavādī anatthavādī adhammavādī avinayavādī. Anidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti akālena anapadesaṃ apariyantavatiṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, catubbidhaṃ vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti? Idha, gahapatayo, ekacco abhijjhālu hoti, yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ abhijjhātā hoti – ‘aho vata yaṃ parassa taṃ mamassā’’’ti!

‘‘Byāpannacitto kho pana hoti paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā haññantu vā vajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesu’’’nti mā vā ahesuṃ iti vāti (sī. pī. ka.).

mā vā ahesuṃ iti vāti (sī. pī. ka.)

‘‘Micchādiṭṭhiko kho pana hoti viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ natthi yiṭṭhaṃ natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko natthi paro loko, natthi mātā natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā , natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, gahapatayo, tividhaṃ manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti.

‘‘Evaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, gahapatayo, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti.
mula_english:
440.” Householders, there are three kinds of bodily conduct not in accordance with the Dharma, unrighteous conduct. There are four kinds of verbal conduct not in accordance with the Dharma, unrighteous conduct. There are three kinds of mental conduct not in accordance with the Dharma, unrighteous conduct.

“And how, householders, are there three kinds of bodily conduct not in accordance with the *dharma*, unrighteous conduct? Here, householders, someone kills living beings; he is murderous, bloody-handed, given to blows and violence, merciless to living beings.

“He takes what is not given. He takes, in the manner of a thief, things in a village or a wilderness that belong to others and have not been given by them.

“He misconducts himself in sensual pleasures. He gets sexually involved with those who are protected by their mothers, their fathers, their brothers, their sisters, their relatives, or their *dharma*; those with husbands, those who entail punishments, or even those crowned with flowers by another man. That is how there are three kinds of bodily conduct not in accordance with the *dharma*, unrighteous conduct.

“And how, householders, are there four kinds of verbal conduct not in accordance with the *dharma*, unrighteous conduct? Here, householders, someone speaks falsehood; when summoned to a court, or to a meeting, or to his relatives’ presence, or to his guild, or to the royal family’s presence, and questioned as a witness thus: ‘So, good man, tell what you know,’ not knowing, he says, ‘I know,’ or knowing, he says, ‘I do not know’; not seeing, he says, ‘I see,’ or seeing, he says, ‘I do not see.’ Thus he consciously tells lies for his own sake, for the sake of another, or for the sake of a certain reward.

“He speaks maliciously; he repeats elsewhere what he has heard here in order to divide those people from these, or he repeats to these people what he has heard elsewhere in order to divide these people from those; thus he is a disruptor of those who are harmonious or an instigator of those who are divided, he enjoys discord, delights in discord, finds pleasure in discord, speaks words that create discord.

“He speaks harshly. He utters such words as are rough, hard, hurtful to others, offensive to others, bordering on anger, unconducive to concentration.
[Note: kaṇḍakā (ka.)]
[Page break p. 1.0287]
He engages in idle chatter (samphappalāpī). He speaks at the wrong time (*akālavādī*), speaks what is not fact (*abhūtavādī*), speaks what is useless (*anatthavādī*), speaks contrary to the *Dhamma* (*adhammavādī*) and the Discipline (*avinayavādī*). At the wrong time he speaks such words as are worthless (*anidhānavatiṃ*), unreasonable (*anapadesaṃ*), immoderate (*apariyantavatiṃ*), and unbeneficial (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*). That is how, householders (*gahapatayo*), there are four kinds of verbal conduct not in accordance with the *Dhamma* (*adhamma*), unrighteous conduct (*visamacariyā*).

And how, householders (*gahapatayo*), is there threefold conduct of mind not in accordance with the *Dhamma* (*adhamma*), unrighteous conduct (*visamacariyā*)? Here, householders (*gahapatayo*), someone is covetous (*abhijjhālu*). They are coveting the property of others, things that belong to others, [thinking:] 'Oh, that what belongs to others would be mine (*mamassā*)!'
