They divert themselves with women wanderers (*paribbājikāhi*) who wear their hair bound in a topknot (*moḷibaddhāhi*).

They say thus: ‘What future fear (*anāgatabhayaṃ*) do these good ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā*) see in sensual pleasures (*kāmesu*) when they speak of abandoning sensual pleasures (*kāmānaṃ pahānaṃ*) and describe the full understanding (*pariññaṃ*) of sensual pleasures (*kāmānaṃ*)? Pleasant is the touch of this young, tender, soft, hairy arm of the female wanderer (*paribbājikāya*)’.

They take to gulping down sensual pleasures (*kāmesu*).

Having taken to gulping down sensual pleasures (*kāmesu*), on the dissolution (*bhedā*) of the body (*kāyassa*), after death (*maraṇā*), they reappear in a state of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), in an unhappy destination (*duggatiṃ*), in perdition (*vinipātaṃ*), even in hell (*nirayaṃ*).

There they feel painful (*dukkha*), racking (*tibba*), piercing (*khara*), and bitter (*kaṭuka*) sensations (*vedanā*).

They say thus: ‘This is the future fear (*anāgatabhayaṃ*) those good ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā*) saw in sensual pleasures (*kāmesu*) when they spoke of abandoning sensual pleasures (*kāmānaṃ pahānaṃ*) and described the full understanding (*pariññaṃ*) of sensual pleasures (*kāmānaṃ*).

For it is by reason of sensual pleasures (*kāmahetu*), owing to sensual pleasures (*kāmanidānaṃ*), that we are now feeling painful (*dukkha*), racking (*tibba*), piercing (*khara*), and bitter (*kaṭuka*) sensations (*vedanā*)’.

This, mendicants (*bhikkhave*), is called the way of undertaking things (*dhammasamādānaṃ*) that is pleasant (*sukhaṃ*) now (*paccuppannaṃ*) and ripens in the future (*āyatiṃ*) as pain (*dukkhavipākaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
469.Natthi kāmesu dosoti vatthukāmesupi kilesakāmesupi doso natthi. Pātabyataṃ āpajjantīti te vatthukāmesu kilesakāmena pātabyataṃ pivitabbataṃ, yathāruci paribhuñjitabbataṃ āpajjantīti attho. Moḷibaddhāhīti moḷiṃ katvā baddhakesāhi. Paribbājikāhīti tāpasaparibbājikāhi. Evamāhaṃsūti evaṃ vadanti. Pariññaṃ paññapentīti pahānaṃ samatikkamaṃ paññapenti. Māluvāsipāṭikāti dīghasaṇṭhānaṃ māluvāpakkaṃ. Phaleyyāti ātapena sussitvā bhijjeyya. Sālamūleti sālarukkhassa samīpe. Santāsaṃ āpajjeyyāti kasmā āpajjati? Bhavanavināsabhayā. Rukkhamūle patitamāluvābījato hi latā uppajjitvā rukkhaṃ abhiruhati. Sā mahāpattā ceva hoti bahupattā ca, koviḷārapattasadisehi pattehi samannāgatā. Atha taṃ rukkhaṃ mūlato paṭṭhāya vinandhamānā sabbaviṭapāni sañchādetvā mahantaṃ bhāraṃ janetvā tiṭṭhati. Sā vāte vā vāyante deve vā vassante oghanaṃ janetvā tassa rukkhassa sabbasākhāpasākhaṃ bhañjati, bhūmiyaṃ nipāteti. Tato tasmiṃ rukkhe patiṭṭhitavimānaṃ bhijjati nassati. Iti sā bhavanavināsabhayā santāsaṃ āpajjati.

Ārāmadevatāti tattha tattha pupphārāmaphalārāmesu adhivatthā devatā. Vanadevatāti andhavanasubhagavanādīsu vanesu adhivatthā devatā. Rukkhadevatāti abhilakkhitesu naḷerupucimandādīsu rukkhesu adhivatthā devatā. Osadhitiṇavanappatīsūti harītakīāmalakīādīsu osadhīsu tālanāḷikerādīsu tiṇesu vanajeṭṭhakesu ca vanappatirukkhesu adhivatthā devatā. Vanakammikāti vane kasanalāyanadāruāharaṇagorakkhādīsu kenacideva kammena vā vicarakamanussā. Uddhareyyunti khādeyyuṃ. Vilambinīti vātena pahatapahataṭṭhānesu keḷiṃ karontī viya vilambantī. Sukho imissāti evarūpāya māluvālatāya samphassopi sukho, dassanampi sukhaṃ. Ayaṃ me dārakānaṃ āpānamaṇḍalaṃ bhavissati, kīḷābhūmi bhavissati, dutiyaṃ me vimānaṃ paṭiladdhanti latāya dassanepi samphassepi somanassajātā evamāha.

Ārāmadevatā Vanadevatā Rukkhadevatā Osadhitiṇavanappatīsū Vanakammikā Uddhareyyu Vilambinī Sukho imissā

Viṭabhiṃ kareyyāti sākhānaṃ upari chattākārena tiṭṭheyya. Oghanaṃ janeyyāti heṭṭhā ghanaṃ janeyya. Upari āruyha sakalaṃ rukkhaṃ paliveṭhetvā puna heṭṭhā bhassamānā bhūmiṃ gaṇheyyāti attho. Padāleyyāti evaṃ oghanaṃ katvā puna tato paṭṭhāya yāva mūlā otiṇṇasākhāhi abhiruhamānā sabbasākhā paliveṭhentī matthakaṃ patvā teneva niyāmena puna orohitvā ca abhiruhitvā ca sakalarukkhaṃ saṃsibbitvā ajjhottharantī sabbasākhā heṭṭhā katvā sayaṃ upari ṭhatvā vāte vā vāyante deve vā vassante padāleyya. Bhindeyyāti attho. Khāṇumattameva tiṭṭheyya, tattha yaṃ sākhaṭṭhakavimānaṃ hoti, taṃ sākhāsu bhijjamānāsu tattha tattheva bhijjitvā sabbasākhāsu bhinnāsu sabbaṃ bhijjati. Rukkhaṭṭhakavimānaṃ pana yāva rukkhassa mūlamattampi tiṭṭhati, tāva na nassati. Idaṃ pana vimānaṃ sākhaṭṭhakaṃ, tasmā sabbasākhāsu saṃbhijjamānāsu bhijjittha. Devatā puttake gahetvā khāṇuke ṭhitā paridevituṃ āraddhā.

Viṭabhiṃ kareyyā Oghanaṃ janeyyā Padāleyyā
commentary_english:
469. "'There is no fault in sensual pleasures'—that is, there is no fault in material sensual pleasures or defilement-sensual pleasures.

"'They obtain what should be drunk'—that is, in those material sensual pleasures, through defilement-sensual pleasure, they obtain what should be drunk, what should be drunk according to their desire, what should be enjoyed, this is the meaning.

"'With hair braided'—having made a crest, with hair tied up.

"'By female wanderers'—by female ascetic wanderers.

"'Thus they said'—thus they speak.

"'Proclaiming full knowledge'—they proclaim abandonment, transcendence.

"'*Māluvāsipāṭikā*'—of long shape, *māluvāpakka*.

"'It would split'—dried by the heat, it would break.

"'At the root of the *sāla* tree'—near the *sāla* tree.

"'He would experience terror'—why would he experience it? Because of the fear of the destruction of his dwelling.

Indeed, a vine having sprung up from a *māluvā* seed fallen at the root of a tree, 2. 0372 ascends the tree.

It is very leafy and also has many leaves, endowed with leaves similar to *koviḷāra* leaves.

Then, having wound around that tree from the root onwards, covering all the branches, having created a great weight, it stands.

When the wind blows or the gods rain, having created a mass, it breaks every branch and twig of that tree, it throws [them] on the ground.

Then the established aerial mansion on that tree is broken and destroyed.

Thus, because of the fear of the destruction of [her] dwelling, she experiences terror.

"***Ārāmadevatā***"—a deity dwelling in the various flower gardens and fruit gardens.

"***Vanadevatā***"—a deity dwelling in the forests, such as the Blind Forest, the Auspicious Forest, and so on.

"***Rukkhadevatā***"—a deity dwelling in the trees distinguished as *naḷeru*, *pucimanda*, and so on.

"***Osadhitiṇavanappatīsū***"—a deity dwelling in the herbs such as *harītakī*, *āmalakī*, and so on, in the grasses such as *tāla*, *nāḷikera*, and so on, in the *vanajeṭṭhaka* trees and in the forest trees.

"***Vanakammikā***"—forest workers, 2. 0266 people wandering due to work in the forest, such as plowing, guarding, gathering wood, tending cattle, and so on.

"'They would take out'—they would eat.

"'*Vilambinī*'"—lingering, as if sporting in places struck by the wind.

"'Pleasant is this'—contact with this kind of *māluvā* vine is also pleasant, seeing [it] is also pleasant.

"This will be a drinking-hall for my children, it will be a playground, a second 2. 0271 aerial mansion has been obtained by me," thus she speaks, experiencing joy upon seeing and touching the vine.

***Ārāmadevatā*** ***Vanadevatā*** ***Rukkhadevatā*** ***Osadhitiṇavanappatīsū*** ***Vanakammikā*** 2. 0266 ***Uddhareyyu*** ***Vilambinī*** ***Sukho imissā*** 2. 071

"'He would make a canopy'—he should stand above the branches in the shape of a parasol.

"'He would create a mass'—he should create a dense mass below.

Having ascended above, having completely surrounded the entire tree, and again remaining below, he would take the ground, this is the meaning.

"'He would cause to fall'—having thus created a mass, and again, from there onwards, as far as the root, with hanging branches, while ascending, completely surrounding all the branches, having reached the top, by that very method, again having descended and again having ascended, intertwining the entire tree, while covering [it], having placed all the branches below, himself standing above, 2. 0373 he would cause [it] to fall when the wind blows or the gods rain.

"It would break," this is the meaning.

Only the stump would remain; there, whatever branch-aerial mansion there is, when the branches are being broken, having been broken right there, when all the branches have been broken, everything is broken.

However, the tree-aerial mansion remains as long as even the root of the tree remains; it does not perish as long as that lasts.

But this aerial mansion is a branch one; therefore, when all the branches were being completely broken, it was broken.
Having taken the young *devatā*s, standing at the post, they began to lament.
"May (he) make a split! May (he) produce a flood! May (he) burst (it) open!"

mula_pali: 470. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco acelako hoti muttācāro hatthāpalekhano, naehibhaddantiko, natiṭṭhabhaddantiko, nābhihaṭaṃ, na uddissakataṃ, na nimantanaṃ sādiyati, so na kumbhimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na kaḷopimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na eḷakamantaraṃ, na daṇḍamantaraṃ, na musalamantaraṃ, na dvinnaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ, na gabbhiniyā, na pāyamānāya, na purisantaragatāya, na saṅkittīsu, na yattha sā upaṭṭhito hoti, na yattha makkhikā saṇḍasaṇḍacārinī, na macchaṃ, na maṃsaṃ, na suraṃ, na merayaṃ, na thusodakaṃ pivati. So ekāgāriko vā hoti ekālopiko, dvāgāriko vā hoti dvālopiko…pe… sattāgāriko vā hoti sattālopiko. Ekissāpi dattiyā yāpeti, dvīhipi dattīhi yāpeti… sattahipi dattīhi yāpeti. Ekāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti, dvīhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti… sattāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti. Iti evarūpaṃ addhamāsikampi pariyāyabhattabhojanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. So sākabhakkho vā hoti , sāmākabhakkho vā hoti, nīvārabhakkho vā hoti, daddulabhakkho vā hoti, haṭabhakkho vā hoti, kaṇabhakkho vā hoti, ācāmabhakkho vā hoti, piññākabhakkho vā hoti, tiṇabhakkho vā hoti, gomayabhakkho vā hoti, vanamūlaphalāhāro yāpeti pavattaphalabhojī. So sāṇānipi dhāreti, masāṇānipi dhāreti, chavadussānipi dhāreti, paṃsukūlānipi dhāreti, tirīṭānipi dhāreti, ajinampi dhāreti, ajinakkhipampi dhāreti, kusacīrampi dhāreti, vākacīrampi dhāreti, phalakacīrampi dhāreti, kesakambalampi dhāreti, vāḷakambalampi dhāreti, ulūkapakkhampi dhāreti, kesamassulocakopi hoti, kesamassulocanānuyogamanuyutto, ubbhaṭṭhakopi hoti, āsanapaṭikkhitto, ukkuṭikopi hoti ukkuṭikappadhānamanuyutto, kaṇṭakāpassayikopi hoti, kaṇṭakāpassaye seyyaṃ kappeti passa ma. ni. 1.155 mahāsīhanādasutte, sāyatatiyakampi udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Iti evarūpaṃ anekavihitaṃ kāyassa ātāpanaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto viharati . So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
470. And what, bhikkhus, is the way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pain? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person goes naked, rejecting conventions, licking his hands, not coming when asked, not stopping when asked; he does not accept food brought or food specially made or an invitation to a meal; he receives nothing from a pot, from a bowl, across a threshold, across a stick, across a pestle, from two eating together, from a pregnant woman, from a woman giving suck, from a woman lying with a man, from where food is advertised to be distributed, from where a dog is waiting, from where flies are swarming; he eats no fish or meat and drinks no rum or spirits or fermented rice-gruel.

He is a one-house man or a one-morsel man, a two-house man or a two-morsel man... he is a seven-house man or a seven-morsel man.

He lives on one saucerful a day, on two saucerfuls a day… on seven saucerfuls a day.

He takes food once a day, once every two days… once every seven days.

Thus, he dwells pursuing the practice of taking food at stated intervals, even up to once every fortnight.

He is an eater of greens or millet or wild rice or hide-parings or moss or rice-bran or rice-scum or sesamum flour or grass or cow-dung. He lives on forest roots and fruits, he feeds on fallen fruits.

He wears coarse hemp or mixed material, shrouds from corpses, rags from the dust-heap, garments of bark-fibre, antelope-skins, grass, bark, shavings, blankets of human hair or horse-hair, the wings of owls. He is a plucker-out of hair and beard, devoted to this practice; he is one who stands continuously, rejecting seats. He is one who squats continuously, devoted to maintaining the squatting position. He is one who uses a mattress of spikes; he makes a mattress of spikes his bed. He dwells pursuing the practice of bathing in water three times daily, including the evening.

Thus, in such a variety of ways, he dwells pursuing the practice of tormenting and mortifying the body.

On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, perdition, even in hell.

This is called the way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pain.

mula_pali: 471. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ? Idha , bhikkhave, ekacco pakatiyā tibbarāgajātiko hoti, so abhikkhaṇaṃ rāgajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; pakatiyā tibbadosajātiko hoti, so abhikkhaṇaṃ dosajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; pakatiyā tibbamohajātiko hoti, so abhikkhaṇaṃ mohajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. So sahāpi dukkhena, sahāpi domanassena, assumukhopi rudamāno paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
471.
“And what, bhikkhus, is the way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pleasure? Here, bhikkhus, someone by nature has strong lust ( *rāga* ), and he constantly experiences pain ( *duḥkha* ) and grief born of lust; by nature he has strong hate (*dveṣa*), and he constantly experiences pain and grief born of hate; by nature he has strong delusion ( *moha* ), and he constantly experiences pain and grief born of delusion.

Yet in pain and grief, weeping with tearful face, he leads the perfect and pure holy life ( *brahmacarya* ).

On the dissolution of the body ( *kāya* ), after death ( *maraṇa* ), he reappears in a happy destination ( *sugati* ), even in the heavenly world ( *svarga* ).

This is called the way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pleasure."
commentary_pali: 471.Tibbarāgajātikoti bahalarāgasabhāvo. Rāgajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedetīti tibbarāgajātikattā diṭṭhe diṭṭhe ārammaṇe nimittaṃ gaṇhāti. Athassa ācariyupajjhāyā daṇḍakammaṃ āṇāpenti. So abhikkhaṇaṃ daṇḍakammaṃ karonto dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti, natveva vītikkamaṃ karoti. Tibbadosajātikoti appamattikeneva kuppati, daharasāmaṇerehi saddhiṃ hatthaparāmāsādīni karontova katheti. Sopi daṇḍakammapaccayā dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Mohajātiko pana idha kataṃ vā katato akataṃ vā akatato na sallakkheti, tāni tāni kiccāni virādheti. Sopi daṇḍakammapaccayā dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.
commentary_english:
471. *Tibbarāgajātiko* means one whose nature is abundant in passion ( *bahalarāgasabhāvo*).

*Rāgajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti* means due to being by nature strongly passionate (*tibbarāgajātikattā*), he seizes upon the appearance (*nimittaṃ gaṇhāti*) in each and every object (*diṭṭhe diṭṭhe ārammaṇe*).

Then his teachers and preceptors (*ācariyupajjhāyā*) impose a penalty (*daṇḍakammaṃ āṇāpenti*).

He, constantly engaging in the penalty (*abhikkhaṇaṃ daṇḍakammaṃ karonto*), experiences suffering (*dukkhaṃ*), grief (*domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti*), but does not transgress (*natveva vītikkamaṃ karoti*).

*Tibbadosajātiko* means he becomes angry with even a small matter (*appamattikeneva kuppati*), and he speaks while engaging in such things as touching hands with young novices (*daharasāmaṇerehi saddhiṃ hatthaparāmāsādīni karontova katheti*).

He also experiences suffering and grief due to the penalty (*sopi daṇḍakammapaccayā dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti*).

Furthermore, one who is by nature deluded (*mohajātiko pana idha*) does not consider what is done (*kataṃ*) or what is not done (*akataṃ*), or the cause of what is done or not done (*katato akatato na sallakkheti*), and he spoils those very tasks (*tāni tāni kiccāni virādheti*).

He also experiences suffering and grief due to the penalty (*sopi daṇḍakammapaccayā dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti*).

mula_pali:
472. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pakatiyā na tibbarāgajātiko hoti, so na abhikkhaṇaṃ rāgajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; pakatiyā na tibbadosajātiko hoti, so na abhikkhaṇaṃ dosajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; pakatiyā na tibbamohajātiko hoti , so na abhikkhaṇaṃ mohajaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. So vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri dhammasamādānānī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Cūḷadhammasamādānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
472. Bhikkhus, what is the way of undertaking things that is pleasant at present and ripens as pleasure in the future? Here, bhikkhus, someone by nature does not have a strong inclination to lust ( *rāga*), and so he does not constantly experience pain (*duḥkha*) and grief (*daurmanasya*) born of lust. By nature, he does not have a strong inclination to hate ( *dveṣa*), and so he does not constantly experience pain and grief born of hate. By nature, he does not have a strong inclination to delusion (*moha*), and so he does not constantly experience pain and grief born of delusion.

Quite secluded from sensuality (*kāma*), secluded from unskillful qualities (*akuśala dharma*), he dwells, having attained the first *jhāna*: rapture (*prīti*) and pleasure (*sukha*) born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought (*vitarka*) and evaluation (*vicāra*).

With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, with internal assurance, unification of awareness, free from directed thought & evaluation, he enters and remains in the second *jhāna*: rapture and pleasure born of concentration (*samādhija*). …the third *jhāna*…the fourth *jhāna*.

At the dissolution of the body (*kāya*) after death (*maraṇa*), he reappears in a happy destination (*sugati*), even in the heavenly world (*svarga loka*).

This, bhikkhus, is called the way of undertaking things that is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pleasure.

These, bhikkhus, are the four ways of undertaking things.”

The Blessed One said this.

Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The *Cūḷadhammasamādānasutta* the fifth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
472.Na tibbarāgajātikotiādīni vuttapaṭipakkhanayena veditabbāni. Kasmā panettha koci tibbarāgādijātiko hoti, koci na tibbarāgādijātiko? Kammaniyāmena. Yassa hi kammāyūhanakkhaṇe lobho balavā hoti, alobho mando, adosāmohā balavanto, dosamohā mandā, tassa mando alobho lobhaṃ pariyādātuṃ na sakkoti, adosāmohā pana balavanto dosamohe pariyādātuṃ sakkonti. Tasmā so tena kammena dinnapaṭisandhivasena nibbatto luddho hoti, sukhasīlo akkodhano paññavā vajirūpamañāṇo.

Yassa pana kammāyūhanakkhaṇe lobhadosā balavanto honti, alobhādosā mandā, amoho balavā, moho mando, so purimanayeneva luddho ceva hoti duṭṭho ca, paññavā pana hoti vajirūpamañāṇo dattābhayatthero viya.

Yassa pana kammāyūhanakkhaṇe lobhādosamohā balavanto honti, itare mandā, so purimanayeneva luddho ceva hoti dandho ca, sukhasīlako pana hoti akkodhano.

Tathā yassa kammāyūhanakkhaṇe tayopi lobhadosamohā balavanto honti, alobhādayo mandā, so purimanayeneva luddho ceva hoti duṭṭho ca mūḷho ca.

Yassa pana kammāyūhanakkhaṇe alobhadosamohā balavanto honti, itare mandā, so purimanayeneva appakileso hoti, dibbārammaṇampi disvā niccalo, duṭṭho pana hoti dandhapañño ca.

Yassa pana kammāyūhanakkhaṇe alobhādosamohā balavanto honti, itare mandā, so purimanayeneva aluddho ceva hoti sukhasīlako ca, mūḷho pana hoti.

Tathā yassa kammāyūhanakkhaṇe alobhadosāmohā balavanto honti, itare mandā, so purimanayeneva aluddho ceva hoti paññavā ca, duṭṭho pana hoti kodhano.

Yassa pana kammāyūhanakkhaṇe tayopi alobhādayo balavanto honti, lobhādayo mandā, so mahāsaṅgharakkhitatthero viya aluddho aduṭṭho paññavā ca hoti.

Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷadhammasamādānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
472. The *na tibbarāgajātiko* etc. should be understood by way of the stated counter-positions.

Why is it that here, one is of the nature of intense attachment, etc., and one is not of the nature of intense attachment, etc.? Because of the law of karma (*kammaniyāmena*).

For when, at the moment of accumulating kamma, greed (*lobha*) is strong and non-greed (*alobha*) is weak, non-hate (*adosa*) and non-delusion (*amoha*) are strong, and hate (*dosa*) and delusion (*moha*) are weak, then his weak non-greed (*alobha*) is unable to prevail over his greed (*lobha*), [but] non-hate (*adosa*) and non-delusion (*amoha*) are strong [and] are able to prevail over hate (*dosa*) and delusion (*moha*).

That is why, on being reborn through rebirth-linking given by that kamma, he has greed (*luddho*), is good-natured (*sukhasīlo*), unangry (*akkodhano*), and possesses understanding with knowledge like a lightning flash (*paññavā vajirūpamañāṇo*).

When, at the moment of another’s accumulating kamma, greed (*lobha*) and hate (*dosa*) are strong and non-greed (*alobha*) and non-hate (*adosa*) weak, and non-delusion (*amoha*) is strong and delusion (*moha*) weak, then in the way already stated he has both greed (*luddho*) and hate (*duṭṭho*), but he possesses understanding with knowledge like a lightning flash (*paññavā vajirūpamañāṇo*), like the Elder Dattābhaya.

“When, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, greed (*lobhā*), non-hate (*adosa*), and delusion (*moha*) are strong and the others are weak, then in the way already stated he both has greed (*luddho*) and is dull (*dandha*) but is good-tempered (*sukhasīlako*) and unangry (*akkodhano*).

Likewise when, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, the three, namely, greed (*lobha*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*) are strong and non-greed (*alobhā*), etc., are weak, then in the way already stated he has both greed (*luddho*) and hate (*duṭṭho*) and is deluded (*mūḷho*).

When, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, non-greed (*alobha*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*) are strong and the others are weak, then in the way already stated he has little defilement (*appakileso*) and is unshakable (*niccalo*) even on seeing a heavenly object (*dibbārammaṇampi disvā*), but he has hate (*duṭṭho*) and is slow in understanding (*dandhapañño*).

When, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, non-greed (*alobhā*), non-hate (*adosa*), and delusion (*moha*) are strong and the rest are weak, then in the way already stated he has no greed (*aluddho*) and is good-tempered (*sukhasīlako*), but is deluded (*mūḷho*).

Likewise when, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, non-greed (*alobha*), hate (*dosa*), and non-delusion (*amohā*) are strong and the rest are weak, then in the way already stated he has no greed (*aluddho*) and possesses understanding (*paññavā*), but has hate (*duṭṭho*) and is irascible (*kodhano*).

When, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, the three, that is, non-greed (*alobhā*), etc., are strong and greed (*lobhā*), etc., are weak, then in the way already stated he has no greed (*aluddho*), no hate (*aduṭṭho*), and possesses understanding (*paññavā*), like the Elder Mahā-Saṅgharakkhita.

The rest is easy to understand everywhere.

The Cūḷadhammasamādāna Sutta Commentary of the Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

mula_pali: 473. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, sattā evaṃkāmā evaṃchandā evaṃadhippāyā – ‘aho vata aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā parihāyeyyuṃ, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍheyyu’nti. Tesaṃ, bhikkhave, sattānaṃ evaṃkāmānaṃ evaṃchandānaṃ evaṃadhippāyānaṃ aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā parihāyanti. Tatra tumhe, bhikkhave, kaṃ hetuṃ paccethā’’ti? ‘‘Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā, bhagavaṃnettikā, bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaññeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho; bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
473. Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, in the Jeta Grove, near Śrāvastī (sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks (bhikkhū), saying: “Monks (bhikkhavo)!”

“Venerable sir (bhadante),” those monks (bhikkhū) replied to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said this: “Bhikkhus (bhikkhave), for the most part beings (sattā) have this wish (evaṃkāmā), desire (evaṃchandā), and longing (evaṃadhippāyā): ‘If only unwished for (aniṭṭhā), undesired (akantā), disagreeable things (amanāpā dhammā) would diminish (parihāyeyyuṃ), and wished for (iṭṭhā), desired (kantā), agreeable things (manāpā dhammā) would increase (abhivaḍḍheyyuṃ’nti)!’

Yet although beings (sattānaṃ), bhikkhus (bhikkhave), have this wish (evaṃkāmānaṃ), desire (evaṃchandānaṃ), and longing (evaṃadhippāyānaṃ), unwished for (aniṭṭhā), undesired (akantā), disagreeable things (amanāpā dhammā) increase (abhivaḍḍhanti) for them, and wished for (iṭṭhā), desired (kantā), agreeable things (manāpā dhammā) diminish (parihāyanti).

Now, bhikkhus (bhikkhave), what do you think is the reason (hetuṃ) for that?”

“Venerable sir (bhante), our teachings (dhammā) are rooted in the Blessed One (bhagavaṃmūlakā), guided by the Blessed One (bhagavaṃnettikā), have the Blessed One as their resort (bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā). It would be good (sādhu vata), venerable sir (bhante), if the Blessed One (bhagavantaññeva) would explain the meaning (attho) of these words (bhāsitassa). Having heard it from the Blessed One (bhagavato sutvā), the bhikkhus (bhikkhū) will remember it (dhāressantī’ti).”

“Then listen (suṇātha), bhikkhus (bhikkhave), and attend carefully (sādhukaṃ manasi karotha). I shall speak (bhāsissāmī’ti).”

“As you say, lord (evaṃ, bhante),” those monks (bhikkhū) responded to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said this:
commentary_pali: 473.Evaṃme suttanti mahādhammasamādānasuttaṃ. Tattha evaṃkāmāti evaṃicchā. Evaṃchandāti evaṃajjhāsayā. Evaṃadhippāyāti evaṃladdhikā. Tatrāti tasmiṃ aniṭṭhavaḍḍhane ceva iṭṭhaparihāne ca. Bhagavaṃmūlakāti bhagavā mūlaṃ etesanti bhagavaṃmūlakā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ime, bhante, amhākaṃ dhammā pubbe kassapasammāsambuddhena uppāditā, tasmiṃ parinibbute ekaṃ buddhantaraṃ añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ime dhamme uppādetuṃ samattho nāma nāhosi, bhagavatā pana no ime dhammā uppāditā. Bhagavantañhi nissāya mayaṃ ime dhamme ājānāma paṭivijjhāmāti evaṃ bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammāti. Bhagavaṃnettikāti bhagavā hi dhammānaṃ netā vinetā anunetāti. Yathāsabhāvato pāṭiyekkaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā dassitā dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā nāma honti. Bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇāti catubhūmakā dhammā sabbaññutaññāṇassa āpāthaṃ āgacchamānā bhagavati paṭisaranti nāmāti bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Paṭisarantīti osaranti samosaranti. Apica mahābodhimaṇḍe nisinnassa bhagavato paṭivedhavasena phasso āgacchati, ahaṃ bhagavā kinnāmoti? Tvaṃ phusanaṭṭhena phasso nāma. Vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ āgacchati. Ahaṃ bhagavā kinnāmanti? Tvaṃ vijānanaṭṭhena viññāṇaṃ nāmāti evaṃ catubhūmakadhammānaṃ yathāsabhāvato pāṭiyekkaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ nāmaṃ gaṇhanto bhagavā dhamme paṭisaratītipi bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Bhagavantaññeva paṭibhātūti bhagavatoyeva etassa bhāsitassa attho upaṭṭhātu, tumheyeva no kathetvā dethāti attho.
commentary_english:
473.
Thus, "my *sutta*," means the *Mahādhammasamādānasutta*.

There, *evaṃkāmā* means *evaṃicchā* (having such a desire).

*Evaṃchandā* means *evaṃajjhāsayā* (having such an aspiration).

*Evaṃadhippāyā* means *evaṃladdhikā* (having such an aim).

*Tatrā* means in that un-wished increase and in the wished decrease.

*Bhagavaṃmūlakā* means the Blessed One is the root of these, thus *bhagavaṃmūlakā*.

This was said - These, venerable sir, are the *dharmas* produced by the former *Kassapasammāsambuddha*. When he had completely passed away, for one Buddha-interval, no other *samaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* was able to produce these *dharmas*. But these *dharmas* were produced for us by the Blessed One.

Because we understand and penetrate these *dharmas* relying on the Blessed One, thus we are *bhagavaṃmūlakā*, venerable sir, regarding the *dharmas*.

*Bhagavaṃnettikā* means the Blessed One is the leader, trainer, and subduer of the *dharmas*.

According to their own nature, taking each and every name, the *dharmas* shown are called *bhagavaṃnettikā*.

*Bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā* means the four-level *dharmas*, coming into the range of the knowledge of omniscience, resort to the Blessed One, thus *bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā*.

*Paṭisarantīti* means they approach, they completely approach.

Moreover, for the Blessed One seated at the great *bodhimaṇḍa*, contact (*phassa*) arises by way of penetration: "What am I called, Blessed One?" "You are called contact (*phassa*) by way of the function of touching."

Feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saññā*), volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*), consciousness (*viññāṇa*) arise.

"What am I called, Blessed One?" "You are called consciousness (*viññāṇa*) by way of the function of cognizing." Thus, the Blessed One, taking each and every name of the four-level *dharmas* according to their own nature, resorts to the *dharmas*; therefore, also *bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā*.

*Bhagavantaññeva paṭibhātū* means may the meaning of this speech occur to the Blessed One alone; the meaning is, "May you alone explain and give it to us."

mula_pali:
474. ‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano, ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto, sevitabbe dhamme na jānāti asevitabbe dhamme na jānāti, bhajitabbe dhamme na jānāti abhajitabbe dhamme na jānāti. So sevitabbe dhamme ajānanto asevitabbe dhamme ajānanto, bhajitabbe dhamme ajānanto abhajitabbe dhamme ajānanto, asevitabbe dhamme sevati sevitabbe dhamme na sevati, abhajitabbe dhamme bhajati bhajitabbe dhamme na bhajati. Tassa asevitabbe dhamme sevato sevitabbe dhamme asevato, abhajitabbe dhamme bhajato bhajitabbe dhamme abhajato aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā parihāyanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ aviddasuno.

‘‘Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako, ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto, sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto, sevitabbe dhamme jānāti asevitabbe dhamme jānāti, bhajitabbe dhamme jānāti abhajitabbe dhamme jānāti. So sevitabbe dhamme jānanto asevitabbe dhamme jānanto, bhajitabbe dhamme jānanto abhajitabbe dhamme jānanto, asevitabbe dhamme na sevati sevitabbe dhamme sevati, abhajitabbe dhamme na bhajati bhajitabbe dhamme bhajati. Tassa asevitabbe dhamme asevato sevitabbe dhamme sevato, abhajitabbe dhamme abhajato bhajitabbe dhamme bhajato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā parihāyanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ viddasuno.
mula_english:
Here, bhikkhus, an untaught ordinary person who has no regard for noble ones (*ariyas*) and is unskilled and undisciplined in their *Dhamma*, who has no regard for true men and is unskilled and undisciplined in their *Dhamma*, does not know what things should be cultivated and what things should not be cultivated, he does not know what things should be followed and what things should not be followed.

Not knowing this, he cultivates things that should not be cultivated and does not cultivate things that should be cultivated, he follows things that should not be followed and does not follow things that should be followed.

It is because he does this that unwished for, undesired, disagreeable things increase for him and wished for, desired, agreeable things diminish.

What is the reason? That is what happens to one who does not see.

The well-taught noble disciple (*ariyasāvaka*) who has regard for noble ones (*ariyas*) and is skilled and disciplined in their *Dhamma*, who has regard for true men and is skilled and disciplined in their *Dhamma*, knows what things should be cultivated and what things should not be cultivated, he knows what things should be followed and what things should not be followed.

Knowing this, he cultivates things that should be cultivated and does not cultivate things that should not be cultivated, he follows things that should be followed and does not follow things that should not be followed.

It is because he does this that unwished for, undesired, disagreeable things diminish for him and wished for, desired, agreeable things increase.

What is the reason? That is what happens to one who sees.
commentary_pali: 474.Sevitabbeti nissayitabbe. Bhajitabbeti upagantabbe. Yathā taṃ aviddasunoti yathā aviduno bālassa andhaputhujjanassa. Yathā taṃ viddasunoti yathā viduno medhāvino paṇḍitassa.
commentary_english: 474. *Sevitabbe* means to be relied upon. *Bhajitabbe* means to be approached. *Yathā taṃ aviddasuno* means like an ignorant, foolish, blind ordinary person. *Yathā taṃ viddasuno* means like a wise, intelligent, learned person.

mula_pali: 475. ‘‘Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānāni. Katamāni cattāri? Atthi, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ; atthi, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ; atthi, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ; atthi, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
“Monks, there are these four ways of undertaking things ( *dhammasamādānāni*).

Which four? There is a way of undertaking things that is presently painful and ripens in the future as pain ( *paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ*). There is a way of undertaking things that is presently pleasant and ripens in the future as pain ( *paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ*). There is a way of undertaking things that is presently painful and ripens in the future as pleasure ( *paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ*). There is a way of undertaking things that is presently pleasant and ripens in the future as pleasure ( *paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ*)."
commentary_pali: 475.Atthi, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānanti purimasutte uppaṭipāṭiākārena mātikā ṭhapitā , idha pana yathādhammaraseneva satthā mātikaṃ ṭhapesi. Tattha dhammasamādānanti pāṇātipātādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ gahaṇaṃ.
commentary_english: 475. atthi, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānanti, in the previous *sūtra*, the outline (mātikā) was established in reverse order. Here, however, the Teacher established the outline according to the flavor of the Dharma itself. There, dhammasamādānanti means the acceptance (grahaṇaṃ) of *dharmas* such as taking life (pāṇātipāta) and so forth.

mula_pali:
476. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ yadidaṃ (sī.) dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ, taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipāka’nti. Taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ appajānanto taṃ sevati, taṃ na parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ sevato, taṃ aparivajjayato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā parihāyanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ aviddasuno.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipāka’nti. Taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ appajānanto taṃ sevati, taṃ na parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ sevato, taṃ aparivajjayato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā parihāyanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ aviddasuno.

‘‘Tatra , bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ, taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipāka’nti. Taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ appajānanto taṃ na sevati, taṃ parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ asevato, taṃ parivajjayato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā parihāyanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ aviddasuno.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ, taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipāka’nti. Taṃ avidvā avijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ appajānanto taṃ na sevati, taṃ parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ asevato, taṃ parivajjayato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā parihāyanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ aviddasuno.
mula_english:
476. “Now, bhikkhus, one who is ignorant, not knowing this way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pain ( *duḥkhavipākaṃ*), does not understand it as it actually is thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is painful now and ripens in the future as pain.’
Not knowing it, not understanding it as it actually is, the ignorant one cultivates it and does not avoid it; because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* increase for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* diminish.
What is the reason for that? That is what happens to one who does not see.

“Now, bhikkhus, one who is ignorant, not knowing the way of undertaking things that is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pain (*duḥkhavipākaṃ*), does not understand it as it actually is thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pain.’
Not knowing it, not understanding it as it actually is, the ignorant one cultivates it and does not avoid it; because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* increase for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* diminish.
What is the reason for that? That is what happens to one who does not see.

“Now, bhikkhus, one who is ignorant, not knowing this way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pleasure, does not understand it as it actually is thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is painful now and ripens in the future as pleasure.’
Not knowing it, not understanding it as it actually is, the ignorant one does not cultivate it but avoids it; because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* increase for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* diminish.
What is the reason for that? That is what happens to one who does not see.

“Now, bhikkhus, one who is ignorant, not knowing the way of undertaking things that is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pleasure (*sukhavipākaṃ*), does not understand it as it actually is thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pleasure.’
Not knowing it, not understanding it as it actually is, the ignorant one does not cultivate it but avoids it; because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* diminish for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* increase.
What is the reason for that? That is what happens to one who does not see.
commentary_pali: 476.Avijjāgatoti avijjāya samannāgato.
commentary_english: *avijjāgato* means endowed with ignorance.

mula_pali:
477. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipāka’nti. Taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānanto taṃ na sevati, taṃ parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ asevato, taṃ parivajjayato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā parihāyanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ viddasuno.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipāka’nti. Taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānanto taṃ na sevati, taṃ parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ asevato, taṃ parivajjayato , aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā parihāyanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ viddasuno.

‘‘Tatra , bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipāka’nti. Taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānanto taṃ sevati, taṃ na parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ sevato, taṃ aparivajjayato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā parihāyanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ viddasuno.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti – ‘idaṃ kho dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipāka’nti. Taṃ vidvā vijjāgato yathābhūtaṃ pajānanto taṃ sevati, taṃ na parivajjeti. Tassa taṃ sevato, taṃ aparivajjayato, aniṭṭhā akantā amanāpā dhammā parihāyanti, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yathā taṃ viddasuno.
mula_english:
477. Monks, when one who is wise understands as it actually is this way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pain—understands it thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is painful now and ripens in the future as pain’—knowing it, understanding it as it actually is, the wise one does not cultivate it but avoids it. Because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* diminish for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* increase. Why is that? That is what happens to one who sees.

Monks, when one who is wise understands as it actually is this way of undertaking things that is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pain—understands it thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pain’—knowing it, understanding it as it actually is, the wise one does not cultivate it but avoids it. Because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* diminish for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* increase. Why is that? That is what happens to one who sees.

Monks, when one who is wise understands as it actually is this way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pleasure—understands it thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is painful now and ripens in the future as pleasure’—knowing it, understanding it as it actually is, the wise one cultivates it and does not avoid it. Because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* diminish for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* increase. Why is that? That is what happens to one who sees.

Monks, when one who is wise understands as it actually is this way of undertaking things that is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pleasure—understands it thus: ‘This way of undertaking things is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pleasure’—knowing it, understanding it as it actually is, the wise one cultivates it and does not avoid it. Because he does so, unwished for, undesired, disagreeable *dharmas* diminish for him and wished for, desired, agreeable *dharmas* increase. Why is that? That is what happens to one who sees.
commentary_pali: 477.Vijjāgatoti vijjāya samannāgato paññavā.
commentary_english: " *Vijjāgato* means endowed with knowledge (*vidyā*), wise (*prajñavān*)."

mula_pali: 478. ‘‘Katamañca , bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena pāṇātipātī hoti, pāṇātipātapaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena adinnādāyī hoti, adinnādānapaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena kāmesu micchācārī hoti, kāmesu micchācārapaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena musāvādī hoti, musāvādapaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena pisuṇavāco hoti, pisuṇavācāpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena pharusavāco hoti, pharusavācāpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena samphappalāpī hoti, samphappalāpapaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena abhijjhālu hoti, abhijjhāpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena byāpannacitto hoti, byāpādapaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena micchādiṭṭhi hoti, micchādiṭṭhipaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
478. What, bhikkhus, is the way of undertaking things that is painful now and ripens in the future as pain? Here, bhikkhus, someone in pain and grief kills living beings (pāṇātipātī), and he experiences pain and grief that have killing of living beings as condition. In pain and grief he takes what is not given (adinnādāyī)…misconducts himself in sensual pleasures (kāmesu micchācārī)…speaks falsehood (musāvādī)…speaks maliciously (pisuṇavāco)… speaks harshly (pharusavāco)…gossips (samphappalāpī)…is covetous (abhijjhālu)…has a mind of ill will (byāpannacitto)…holds wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi), and he experiences pain and grief that have wrong view as condition.

On the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ) .

This is called the way of undertaking things (dhammasamādānaṃ) that is painful now (paccuppannadukkhañceva) and ripens in the future as pain (āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ).
commentary_pali: 478.Sahāpi dukkhenāti ettha micchācāro abhijjhā micchādiṭṭhīti ime tāva tayo pubbacetanāya ca aparacetanāya cāti dvinnaṃ cetanānaṃ vasena dukkhavedanā honti. Sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā pana sukhasampayuttā vā upekkhāsampayuttā vā hoti. Sesā pāṇātipātādayo satta tissannampi cetanānaṃ vasena dukkhavedanā honti. Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassenā’’ti. Domanassameva cettha dukkhanti veditabbaṃ. Pariyeṭṭhiṃ vā āpajjantassa pubbabhāgaparabhāgesu kāyikaṃ dukkhampi vaṭṭatiyeva.
commentary_english:
Here, "accompanied by suffering" means that these three—wrong conduct (*micchācāra*), covetousness (*abhijjhā*), and wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*)—cause painful sensations due to the two kinds of intention: prior intention and subsequent intention.

Furthermore, conclusive intention (*sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā*) is associated with either pleasure (*sukhasampayuttā*) or equanimity (*upekkhāsampayuttā*).

The remaining seven, starting with killing living beings (*pāṇātipātādayo*), also cause painful sensations due to these three intentions.

This was stated in reference to "accompanied by suffering, accompanied by sadness" (*sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassenā*).

Here, it should be understood that sadness (*domanassa*) itself is suffering (*dukkha*).

Even physical suffering (*kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ*) befalls one who undertakes a search (*pariyeṭṭhiṃ*), in the prior and subsequent stages.

mula_pali: 479. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena pāṇātipātī hoti, pāṇātipātapaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena adinnādāyī hoti, adinnādānapaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena kāmesumicchācārī hoti, kāmesumicchācārapaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena musāvādī hoti, musāvādapaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena pisuṇavāco hoti, pisuṇavācāpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena pharusavāco hoti, pharusavācāpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena samphappalāpī hoti, samphappalāpapaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena abhijjhālu hoti, abhijjhāpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena byāpannacitto hoti, byāpādapaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena micchādiṭṭhi hoti, micchādiṭṭhipaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
479. What, monks, is the way of undertaking things that is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pain (paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ)? Here, monks, someone, while experiencing pleasure (sukha) and joy (somanassa), kills living beings (pāṇātipātī), and due to killing living beings, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he takes what is not given (adinnādāyī), and due to taking what is not given, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he engages in sexual misconduct (kāmesumicchācārī), and due to engaging in sexual misconduct, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he speaks falsely (musāvādī), and due to speaking falsely, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he speaks maliciously (pisuṇavāco), and due to malicious speech, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he speaks harshly (pharusavāco), and due to harsh speech, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he engages in idle chatter (samphappalāpī), and due to idle chatter, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he is covetous (abhijjhālu), and due to covetousness, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he has a mind of ill-will (byāpannacitto), and due to ill-will, he experiences pleasure and joy; while experiencing pleasure and joy, he holds wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi), and due to wrong view, he experiences pleasure and joy.

On the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in the downfall (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ).

This, monks, is called the way of undertaking things that is pleasant now and ripens in the future as pain (idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ).
commentary_pali: 479.Sahāpisukhenāti ettha pāṇātipāto pharusavācā byāpādoti ime tāva tayo pubbacetanāya ca aparacetanāya cāti dvinnaṃ cetanānaṃ vasena sukhavedanā honti. Sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā pana dukkhasampayuttāva hoti. Sesā satta tissannampi cetanānaṃ vasena sukhavedanā hontiyeva. Sahāpi somanassenāti somanassameva cettha sukhanti veditabbaṃ. Iṭṭhaphoṭṭhabbasamaṅgino vā pubbabhāgaparabhāgesu kāyikaṃ sukhampi vaṭṭatiyeva.
commentary_english:
479.
"Along with pleasure" ( *sukhena*) here [means:] injury to living beings (*pāṇātipāta*), harsh speech (*pharusavācā*), malicious intent (*byāpāda*); these three, indeed, arise from both prior intention (*pubbacetanā*) and subsequent intention (*aparacetanā*), through the force of two intentions, [and bring about] pleasant sensation (*sukhavedanā*).

The establishing intention (*sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā*), however, is associated with suffering (*dukkha*).

The remaining seven also produce pleasant sensation (*sukhavedanā*) through the force of the three intentions.

"Along with joy" (*sahāpi somanassenā*) means that here joy (*somanassa*) itself should be understood as pleasure (*sukha*).

Or, in the preliminary and subsequent stages, pleasure (*sukha*) also exists for those endowed with desirable tangible objects (*iṭṭhaphoṭṭhabbasamaṅgino*), physical pleasure (*kāyikaṃ sukha*) certainly exists.

mula_pali: 480. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇīpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti ; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā veramaṇīpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇīpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā veramaṇīpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti , pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇīpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti ; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇīpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā veramaṇīpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena anabhijjhālu hoti, anabhijjhāpaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena abyāpannacitto hoti, abyāpādapaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassena sammādiṭṭhi hoti, sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ.
mula_english: What, O monks, is the undertaking of things that is painful in the present, but has a pleasant result in the future? Here, O monks, some person, while [still] in pain and grief, abstains from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā), and because of abstaining from killing, he experiences pain and grief. While in pain and grief, he abstains from taking what is not given (adinnādānā)…from misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārā)…from speaking falsehood (musāvādā)…from malicious speech (pisuṇāya vācāya)… from harsh speech (pharusāya vācāya)… from idle chatter (samphappalāpā)… While in pain and grief, he is without covetousness (anabhijjhālu)…he has a mind without ill will (abyāpannacitto)…while in pain and grief, he has right view (sammādiṭṭhi), and because of right view, he experiences pain and grief. At the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world (sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati). This is called, O monks, the undertaking of things that is painful in the present, but has a pleasant result in the future (dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ).
commentary_pali: 480. Tatiyadhammasamādāne idhekacco macchabandho vā hoti, māgaviko vā, pāṇupaghātaṃyeva nissāya jīvikaṃ kappeti. Tassa garuṭṭhāniyo bhikkhu akāmakasseva pāṇātipāte ādīnavaṃ, pāṇātipātaviratiyā ca ānisaṃsaṃ kathetvā sikkhāpadaṃ deti. So gaṇhantopi dukkhito domanassitova hutvā gaṇhāti. Aparabhāge katipāhaṃ vītināmetvā rakkhituṃ asakkontopi dukkhitova hoti, tassa pubbāparacetanā dukkhasahagatāva honti. Sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā pana sukhasahagatā vā upekkhāsahagatā vāti evaṃ sabbattha attho veditabbo . Iti pubbabhāgaparabhāgacetanāva sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ – ‘‘sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassenā’’ti. Domanassameva cettha dukkhanti veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english: 480. In the third taking-up of the Dhamma, here a certain fisherman or hunter makes a living relying solely on the killing of living beings. A venerable monk explains to him, even against his will, the danger in the taking of life (*prāṇātipāte ādīnavaṃ*), and after telling him the benefit of abstaining from the taking of life (*prāṇātipātaviratiyā ca ānisaṃsaṃ kathetvā*), gives him the training. Even accepting it, he accepts it being miserable and afflicted. Later, after spending a few days, unable to protect it, he is miserable. His previous and subsequent thoughts are associated with suffering (*dukkhasahagatāva honti*). However, the conclusive thought is associated with happiness or associated with equanimity. Thus, the meaning should be understood everywhere. Thus, with reference to the previous and subsequent thoughts, this was said: "Together with suffering, together with sadness" (*sahāpi dukkhena sahāpi domanassenā’ti*). Here, sadness itself should be understood as suffering (*domanassameva cettha dukkhanti veditabbaṃ*).

mula_pali: 481. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇīpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā veramaṇīpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇīpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā veramaṇīpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇīpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇīpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā veramaṇīpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena anabhijjhālu hoti, anabhijjhāpaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena abyāpannacitto hoti, abyāpādapaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassena sammādiṭṭhi hoti, sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Idaṃ, vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri dhammasamādānāni.
mula_english:
481.
‘‘And what, bhikkhus, is the way of undertaking things that is pleasant in the present and results in pleasure in the future? Here, bhikkhus, someone in pleasure and joy abstains from killing living beings (prāṇātipātā), and he experiences pleasure (sukhaṃ) and joy (somanassaṃ) that have abstention from killing living beings as condition. In pleasure and joy he abstains from taking what is not given (adinnādānā)…In pleasure and joy he abstains from false speech (musāvādā)… In pleasure and joy he abstains from malicious speech (pisuṇāya vācāya)…In pleasure and joy he abstains from harsh speech (pharusāya vācāya)…In pleasure and joy he abstains from idle chatter (samphappalāpā)…In pleasure and joy, he is without covetousness (anabhijjhālu)…In pleasure and joy, his mind is without ill will (abyāpannacitto)…In pleasure and joy he holds right view (sammādiṭṭhi), and he experiences pleasure and joy that have right view as condition.

On the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a happy destination (sugatiṃ), even in the heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ).

This, bhikkhus, is called the way of undertaking things (dhammasamādānaṃ) that is pleasant in the present and results in pleasure in the future (sukhavipākaṃ).

These, bhikkhus, are the four ways of undertaking things (dhammasamādānāni).
commentary_pali: 481. Catutthadhammasamādāne dasasupi padesu tissopi pubbabhāgāparabhāgasanniṭṭhāpakacetanā sukhasampayuttā hontiyeva, taṃ sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ – ‘‘sahāpi sukhena sahāpi somanassenā’’ti. Somanassameva cettha sukhanti veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english: In the attainment of the fourth state, even in the ten stages, the three thoughts that establish the preceding and subsequent parts are connected with pleasure (sukha); referring to that, this was said: "together with pleasure (sukhena), together with joy (somanassena)." Here, joy (somanassa) should be understood as pleasure (sukha).

mula_pali: 482. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, tittakālābu visena saṃsaṭṭho. Atha puriso āgaccheyya jīvitukāmo amaritukāmo sukhakāmo dukkhappaṭikūlo. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, ayaṃ tittakālābu visena saṃsaṭṭho, sace ākaṅkhasi piva pipa (sī. pī.). Tassa te pivato pipato (sī. pī.) ceva nacchādessati vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā pītvā (sī.) ca pana maraṇaṃ vā nigacchasi maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkha’nti. So taṃ appaṭisaṅkhāya piveyya, nappaṭinissajjeyya. Tassa taṃ pivato ceva nacchādeyya vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Tathūpamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ vadāmi, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhañceva āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
482. Bhikkhus, suppose there were a bitter gourd (*tittakālābu*) mixed with poison (*visena saṃsaṭṭho*).

Then a man would come along wanting to live (*jīvitukāmo*), not wanting to die (*amaritukāmo*), desiring happiness (*sukhakāmo*) and averse to suffering (*dukkhappaṭikūlo*).

They might say to him, ‘Good man (*ambho purisa*), this bitter gourd (*tittakālābu*) is mixed with poison (*visena saṃsaṭṭho*). Drink from it if you wish (*sace ākaṅkhasi piva*).’

As he drank it, its color, smell (*gandhenapi*), and taste (*rasenapi*) would not agree with him, and after drinking it, he would meet with death (*maraṇaṃ*) or deadly suffering (*maraṇamattaṃ...dukkhaṃ*).

Then he would drink from it without reflecting and would not relinquish it.

As he drank it, its color, smell (*gandhenapi*), and taste (*rasenapi*) would not agree with him, and after drinking it, he would come to death (*maraṇaṃ*) or deadly suffering (*maraṇamattaṃ...dukkhaṃ*).

Bhikkhus, I declare that the undertaking of things (*dhammasamādānaṃ*) is similar to this, namely, the undertaking of things (*dhammasamādānaṃ*) that is painful in the present (*paccuppannadukkhañceva*) and ripens in the future as pain (*āyatiñca dukkhavipākaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 482.Tittakālābūti tittakarasaalābu. Visena saṃsaṭṭhoti halāhalavisena sampayutto missito luḷito. Nacchādessatīti na ruccissati na tuṭṭhiṃ karissati. Nigacchasīti gamissasi. Appaṭisaṅkhāya piveyyāti taṃ appaccavekkhitvā piveyya.
commentary_english:
482. *tittakālābū* means *tittakarasaalābu.*
*visena saṃsaṭṭho* means mixed, mingled, and stirred with halāhala poison, joined with poison.
*nacchādessatī* means will not like, will not give satisfaction.
*nigacchasī* means you will go.
*appaṭisaṅkhāya piveyyā* means one should drink without considering it, without reflecting on it.

mula_pali: 483. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āpānīyakaṃso vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno. So ca kho visena saṃsaṭṭho. Atha puriso āgaccheyya jīvitukāmo amaritukāmo sukhakāmo dukkhappaṭikūlo. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, ayaṃ āpānīyakaṃso vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno. So ca kho visena saṃsaṭṭho, sace ākaṅkhasi piva. Tassa te pivatohi pivatopi (ka.) kho chādessati vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana maraṇaṃ vā nigacchasi maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkha’nti. So taṃ appaṭisaṅkhāya piveyya, nappaṭinissajjeyya. Tassa taṃ pivatohi kho chādeyya vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Tathūpamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ vadāmi, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhaṃ āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
“Suppose, monks, there were a bronze cup of beverage possessing a good colour (varṇa), smell (gandha), and taste (rasa).

But it was mixed with poison (viṣa).

A man would come along wanting to live (jīvitukāma), not wanting to die (amaritukāma), desiring happiness (sukhakāma) and averse to suffering (duḥkhappaṭikūla).

And they told him: ‘Good man (ambho purisa), this bronze cup of beverage possesses a good colour (varṇa), smell (gandha), and taste (rasa).

But it is mixed with poison (viṣa). Drink from it if you want;

as you drink from it, its colour (varṇa), smell (gandha), and taste (rasa) will agree with you, but after drinking from it, you will come to death (maraṇa) or deadly suffering (maraṇamattaṃ dukkha).’

Then he drank from it without reflecting (appaṭisaṅkhāya), and did not relinquish it.

As he drank from it, its colour (varṇa), smell (gandha), and taste (rasa) agreed with him, but after drinking from it, he came to death (maraṇa) or deadly suffering (maraṇamattaṃ dukkha).

Similar to that, I say, monks, is this way of undertaking things (dhammasamādāna) that is pleasant now (paccuppannasukha) and ripens in the future as pain (āyatiṃ dukkhavipākaṃ).
commentary_pali: 483.Āpānīyakaṃsoti āpānīyassa madhurapānakassa bharitakaṃso. Vaṇṇasampannoti pānakavaṇṇādīhi sampannavaṇṇo, kaṃse pakkhittapānakavasena pānakakaṃsopi evaṃ vutto. Chādessatīti tañhi halāhalavisaṃ yattha yattha pakkhittaṃ hoti, tassa tasseva rasaṃ deti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘chādessatī’’ti.
commentary_english:
483. *āpānīyakaṃso* means a *bharitakaṃsa* (filled vessel) of sweet drink, *āpānīya*.

*vaṇṇasampanno* means having an excellent color due to the color of the drink, etc.; because of the drink placed in the vessel, the drink-vessel is also spoken of thus.

*chādessatī* -- just as the *halāhalavisaṃ* (deadly poison), wherever it is placed, gives its own taste, therefore it is said "*chādessatī*."

mula_pali: 484. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pūtimuttaṃ nānābhesajjehi saṃsaṭṭhaṃ. Atha puriso āgaccheyya paṇḍukarogī. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, idaṃ pūtimuttaṃ nānābhesajjehi saṃsaṭṭhaṃ, sace ākaṅkhasi piva. Tassa te pivatohi kho nacchādessati vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana sukhī bhavissasī’ti. So taṃ paṭisaṅkhāya piveyya, nappaṭinissajjeyya. Tassa taṃ pivatohi kho nacchādeyya vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana sukhī assa. Tathūpamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ vadāmi, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
484. Suppose, *bhikkhus*, there was fermented urine (*pūtimuttaṃ*) mixed with various medicines (*nānābhesajjehi saṃsaṭṭhaṃ*).

Then a man came sick with jaundice (*paṇḍukarogī*).

They might say to him, 'Good man, this fermented urine (*pūtimuttaṃ*) is mixed with various medicines (*nānābhesajjehi saṃsaṭṭhaṃ*). Drink from it if you want.

As you drink from it, its color, smell (*gandhena*), and taste (*rasena*) will not agree with you, but after drinking from it, you will be well.'

Then he drank from it after reflecting (*paṭisaṅkhāya*), and did not relinquish it.

As he drank from it, its color, smell (*gandhena*), and taste (*rasena*) did not agree with him, but after drinking from it, he became well.

Similarly, *bhikkhus*, I speak of this undertaking of things (*dhammasamādānaṃ*) that is painful now and ripens in the future as pleasure (*paccuppannadukkhaṃ āyatiṃ sukhavipākaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 484.Pūtimuttanti muttameva. Yathā hi manussabhāvo suvaṇṇavaṇṇo pūtikāyotveva, tadahujātāpi galocilatā pūtilatātveva vuccati. Evaṃ taṅkhaṇaṃ gahitaṃ taruṇampi muttaṃ pūtimuttameva. Nānābhesajjehīti harītakāmalakādīhi nānosadhehi. Sukhī assāti arogo suvaṇṇavaṇṇo sukhī bhaveyya.
commentary_english: 484. pūtimuttanti *muttameva*. Just as the human state (*manussabhāvo*) [can be] golden-colored (*suvaṇṇavaṇṇo*) even as a putrid body (*pūtikāyotveva*), so too *galocilatā*, though born from that, is called *pūtilatātveva*. Thus, that which is taken at that moment, even fresh (*taruṇampi*) *muttam*, is truly *pūtimuttameva*. nānābhesajjehīti with various medicines, such as *harītakāmalakādīhi*, with various remedies (*nānosadhehi*). sukhī assāti may [one] be happy (*arogo sukhī bhaveyya*), healthy and golden-colored (*suvaṇṇavaṇṇo*).

mula_pali: 485. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dadhi ca madhu ca sappi ca phāṇitañca ekajjhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ. Atha puriso āgaccheyya lohitapakkhandiko. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ambho purisa, idaṃ dadhiṃ ca madhuṃ ca sappiṃ ca phāṇitañca ekajjhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ, sace ākaṅkhasi piva. Tassa te pivato ceva chādessati vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana sukhī bhavissasī’ti. So taṃ paṭisaṅkhāya piveyya, nappaṭinissajjeyya. Tassa taṃ pivato ceva chādeyya vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana sukhī assa. Tathūpamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ vadāmi, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ.
mula_english:
485. Suppose, mendicants, there were curd (*dadhi*), honey (*madhu*), ghee (*sarpi*), and molasses (*phāṇita*) mixed together.

Then a man with dysentery (*lohitapakkhandiko*) came.

They might say to him, ‘Good man (*ambho purisa*), this is curd (*dadhi*), honey (*madhu*), ghee (*sarpi*), and molasses (*phāṇita*) mixed together. Drink from it if you want.

As you drink from it, its colour, smell, and taste will agree with you, and after drinking from it you will be well.’

Then he drank from it after reflecting, and did not relinquish it.

As he drank from it, its colour, smell, and taste agreed with him, and after drinking from it, he became well.

Similar to that, I say, is this undertaking of the Dhamma (*dhammasamādāna*), this undertaking of the Dhamma (*dhammasamādāna*) which is pleasant in the present and ripens in the future as pleasure.
commentary_pali: 485.Dadhi ca madhu cāti suparisuddhaṃ dadhi ca sumadhuraṃ madhu ca. Ekajjhaṃ saṃsaṭṭhanti ekato katvā missitaṃ āluḷitaṃ. Tassa tanti tassa taṃ catumadhurabhesajjaṃ pivato rucceyya. Idañca yaṃ bhagandarasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ lohitaṃ pakkhandati, na tassa bhesajjaṃ, āhāraṃ thambhetvā maggaṃ avalañjaṃ karoti. Yaṃ pana pittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ lohitaṃ, tassetaṃ bhesajjaṃ sītalakiriyāya pariyattabhūtaṃ.
commentary_english:
485.
"Curd and honey," namely, very pure curd and very sweet honey.
"Being in one mass and mixed together," namely, having made it one, mixed and stirred.
"To him, that," namely, that quadruple sweet medicine would be pleasing to one who drinks it.
And that blood which flows out, mixed with a fistula, there is no medicine for that; having stopped the food, it makes the path obstructed.
But that blood which is mixed with bile, that is a medicine that is suitable for a cooling action.

mula_pali:
486. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vassānaṃ pacchime māse saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṃ abbhussakkamāno sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocate ca; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ dhammasamādānaṃ paccuppannasukhañceva āyatiñca sukhavipākaṃ tadaññe puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇaparappavāde abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocate cā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Mahādhammasamādānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
“Just as, monks, in the last month of the rainy season, in autumn, when the sky is clear and cloudless, the sun rises up into the sky, dispelling all the darkness in space, and shines, blazes, and radiates; so too, monks, this undertaking of the Dharma, which is pleasant in the present and ripens as pleasure in the future, dispels, shines, blazes, and radiates over any other doctrines of ordinary ascetics and Brahmins.”

This the Blessed One said. Elated, those monks delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Great Discourse on the Undertaking of the Dharma is finished, the sixth.
commentary_pali:
486.Viddheti ubbiddhe. Meghavigamena dūrībhūteti attho. Vigatavalāhaketi apagatameghe, deveti ākāse. Ākāsagataṃ tamagatanti ākāsagataṃ tamaṃ. Puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇaparappavādeti puthūnaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇasaṅkhātānaṃ paresaṃ vāde. Abhivihaccāti abhihantvā. Bhāsate ca tapate ca virocate cāti saradakāle majjhanhikasamaye ādiccova obhāsaṃ muñcati tapati vijjotatīti.

Idaṃ pana suttaṃ devatānaṃ ativiya piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Tatridaṃ vatthu – dakkhiṇadisāyaṃ kira hatthibhogajanapade saṅgaravihāro nāma atthi. Tassa bhojanasāladvāre saṅgararukkhe adhivatthā devatā rattibhāge ekassa daharassa sarabhaññavasena idaṃ suttaṃ osārentassa sutvā sādhukāraṃ adāsi. Daharo kiṃ esoti āha. Ahaṃ, bhante, imasmiṃ rukkhe adhivatthā devatāti. Kasmiṃ devate pasannāsi, kiṃ sadde, udāhu sutteti? Saddo nāma, bhante, yassa kassaci hotiyeva, sutte pasannāmhi. Satthārā jetavane nisīditvā kathitadivase ca ajja ca ekabyañjanepi nānaṃ natthīti. Assosi tvaṃ devate satthārā kathitadivaseti? Āma, bhante. Kattha ṭhitā assosīti? Jetavanaṃ, bhante, gatāmhi, mahesakkhāsu pana devatāsu āgacchantīsu tattha okāsaṃ alabhitvā idheva ṭhatvā assosinti. Ettha ṭhitāya sakkā sutthu saddo sotunti? Tvaṃ pana, bhante, mayhaṃ saddaṃ suṇasīti? Āma devateti. Dakkhiṇakaṇṇapasse nisīditvā kathanakālo viya, bhante, hotīti. Kiṃ pana devate satthu rūpaṃ passasīti? Satthā mameva oloketīti maññamānā saṇṭhātuṃ na sakkomi, bhanteti. Visesaṃ pana nibbattetuṃ asakkhittha devateti. Devatā tattheva antaradhāyi. Taṃ divasaṃ kiresa devaputto sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhito. Evamidaṃ suttaṃ devatānaṃ piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahādhammasamādānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
486. Viddheti ubbiddhe. The meaning is, "having become distant" through the disappearance of the clouds. Vigatavalāhaketi, [means] *apagatameghe*, [namely:] in the sky (*ākāse*). Ākāsagataṃ tamagatanti: *ākāsagataṃ tamaṃ*. Puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇaparappavādeti: in the speech of others, who are numerous, reckoned as ascetics and Brahmins. Abhivihaccāti: having struck. Bhāsate ca tapate ca virocate cāti: in the autumn season, at midday, just like the sun, it releases light, burns, and shines brightly.

Now, this *sūtra* is exceedingly dear and pleasing to the gods (*devatānaṃ*). In that regard, this is the story: in the southern direction, in the country of Hatthibhoga, there was a monastery called Saṅgara. At the door of its refectory, a deity (*devatā*) dwelling in the Saṅgara tree, in the night, having heard this *sūtra* being recited by a certain young man in the manner of reciting the *sarabhañña*, gave approval. He said, "Young man, what is this?" "Venerable sir, I am a deity (*devatā*) dwelling in this tree." "In what are you pleased, O deity (*devate*)? In the sound or in the *sūtra*?" "Sound, venerable sir, is just whatever it may be for anyone, [but] in the *sūtra* I am pleased." "Venerable sir, there is no difference, even in a single consonant, between what the Teacher spoke when sitting in Jeta's Grove and what was spoken today." "O deity (*devate*), did you hear what the Teacher spoke?" "Yes, venerable sir." "Where were you standing when you heard it?" "Venerable sir, I had gone to Jeta's Grove, but since powerful deities (*devatāsu*) were coming, not obtaining space there, I stood right here and heard it." "Is it possible to hear the sound well while standing here?" "Venerable sir, do you hear my sound?" "Yes, O deity (*devateti*)." "It is just as if the time for speaking were when [you are] sitting beside [my] right ear, venerable sir." "O deity (*devate*), do you see the Teacher's form?" "Thinking, 'The Teacher is looking right at me,' I am not able to remain still, venerable sir." "O deity (*devateti*), were you not able to produce distinction?" The deity (*devatā*) disappeared right there. It is said that on that day, that divine son (*devaputto*) was established in the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphale*). In this way, this *sūtra* is dear and pleasing to the gods (*devatānaṃ*). The rest is clear throughout.

The Mahādhammasamādānasuttavaṇṇanā in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary on the Majjhimanikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 487. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘vīmaṃsakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā parassa cetopariyāyaṃ ajānantena ājānantena (pī. ka.), ajānantena kinti (?) tathāgate samannesanā kātabbā ‘sammāsambuddho vā no vā’ iti viññāṇāyā’’ti. ‘‘Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā, bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā; sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho; bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti . ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying at Sāvatthī (sāvatthiyaṃ) in Jeta's Grove (jetavane), Anāthapindika's Park (anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

There the Blessed One (bhagavā) addressed the monks (bhikkhū), saying: "Monks (bhikkhavo)!"

"Venerable Sir (bhadante)," those monks (bhikkhū) replied to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said this: "Monks (bhikkhave), a monk (bhikkhunā) who is an inquirer (vīmaṃsakena), not knowing how to gauge another’s mind (parassa cetopariyāyaṃ ajānantena), should make an investigation (samannesanā kātabbā) of the *Tathāgata* (tathāgate) in order to find out whether or not he is a *sammāsambuddha* (sammāsambuddho vā no vā) for the purpose of understanding (viññāṇāya)."

"Venerable Sir (bhante), our teachings (*dhammā*) are rooted in the Blessed One (bhagavaṃmūlakā no), guided by the Blessed One (bhagavaṃnettikā), have the Blessed One as their resort (bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā); it would be good (sādhu vata), Venerable Sir (bhante), if the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃyeva) would explain (paṭibhātu) the meaning (attho) of these words (etassa bhāsitassa); having heard (sutvā) it from the Blessed One (bhagavato), the monks (bhikkhū) will remember (dhāressantī)."

"Then listen (suṇātha), monks (bhikkhave), and attend carefully (sādhukaṃ manasi karotha). I shall speak (bhāsissāmī)."

"As you say, lord (evaṃ, bhante)," those monks (bhikkhū) replied to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said:
commentary_pali: 487.Evaṃme sutanti vīmaṃsakasuttaṃ. Tattha vīmaṃsakenāti tayo vīmaṃsakā – atthavīmaṃsako saṅkhāravīmaṃsako satthuvīmaṃsakoti. Tesu, ‘‘paṇḍitā hāvuso, manussā vīmaṃsakā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 3.2) ettha atthavīmaṃsako āgato. ‘‘Yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu dhātukusalo ca hoti, āyatanakusalo ca hoti, paṭiccasamuppādakusalo ca hoti, ṭhānāṭṭhānakusalo ca hoti, ettāvatā kho, ānanda, paṇḍito bhikkhu vīmaṃsakoti alaṃ vacanāyā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.124) ettha saṅkhāravīmaṃsako āgato. Imasmiṃ pana sutte satthuvīmaṃsako adhippeto. Cetopariyāyanti cittavāraṃ cittaparicchedaṃ. Samannesanāti esanā pariyesanā upaparikkhā. Iti viññāṇāyāti evaṃ vijānanatthāya.
commentary_english:
487. Thus have I heard, is the *Vīmaṃsaka Sutta*.

Therein, *vīmaṃsakenā* (by an investigator) refers to three types of investigators: an investigator of meaning (*attha-vīmaṃsako*), an investigator of formations (*saṅkhāra-vīmaṃsako*), and an investigator of the teacher (*satthu-vīmaṃsako*).

Among these, "Wise men, friends, are investigators" (SN 3.2) refers to the investigator of meaning.
