"When, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* is skilled in the elements (*dhātukusalo*), skilled in the bases (*āyatanakusalo*), skilled in dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppādakusalo*), skilled in what is possible and what is impossible (*ṭhānāṭṭhānakusalo*), in that way he can be called a wise man and an investigator" (MN 3.124) refers to the investigator of formations.

But in this *sutta*, the investigator of the teacher is intended.

*cetopariyāya* (awareness of the minds of others) means an occasion of mind (*cittavāraṃ*), a delimitation of mind (*cittaparicchedaṃ*).

*samannesanā* (investigation) means searching (*esanā*), seeking (*pariyesanā*), examination (*upaparikkhā*).

*iti viññāṇāya* (for the sake of knowing) means thus for the sake of understanding (*evaṃ vijānanatthāya*).

mula_pali:
488. ‘‘Vīmaṃsakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā parassa cetopariyāyaṃ ajānantena dvīsu dhammesu tathāgato samannesitabbo cakkhusotaviññeyyesu dhammesu – ‘ye saṃkiliṭṭhā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti vā te tathāgatassa no vā’ti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ye saṃkiliṭṭhā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantī’ti.

‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ye saṃkiliṭṭhā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantī’ti, tato naṃ uttariṃ samannesati – ‘ye vītimissā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti vā te tathāgatassa no vā’ti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ye vītimissā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantī’ti.

‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ye vītimissā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantī’ti, tato naṃ uttariṃ samannesati – ‘ye vodātā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti vā te tathāgatassa no vā’ti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ye vodātā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti te tathāgatassā’ti.

‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ye vodātā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti te tathāgatassā’ti, tato naṃ uttariṃ samannesati – ‘dīgharattaṃ samāpanno ayamāyasmā imaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, udāhu ittarasamāpanno’ti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘dīgharattaṃ samāpanno ayamāyasmā imaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, nāyamāyasmā ittarasamāpanno’ti.

‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘dīgharattaṃ samāpanno ayamāyasmā imaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, nāyamāyasmā ittarasamāpanno’ti, tato naṃ uttariṃ samannesati – ‘ñattajjhāpanno ayamāyasmā bhikkhu yasappatto, saṃvijjantassa idhekacce ādīnavā’ti? Na tāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno idhekacce ādīnavā saṃvijjanti yāva na ñattajjhāpanno hoti yasappatto. Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ñattajjhāpanno hoti yasappatto , athassa idhekacce ādīnavā saṃvijjanti. Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ñattajjhāpanno ayamāyasmā bhikkhu yasappatto, nāssa idhekacce ādīnavā saṃvijjantī’ti.

‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘ñattajjhāpanno ayamāyasmā bhikkhu yasappatto, nāssa idhekacce ādīnavā saṃvijjantī’ti, tato naṃ uttariṃ samannesati – ‘abhayūparato ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā bhayūparato; vītarāgattā kāme na sevati khayā rāgassā’ti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhayūparato ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā bhayūparato; vītarāgattā kāme na sevati khayā rāgassā’ti. Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ pare evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘ke panāyasmato ākārā, ke anvayā, yenāyasmā evaṃ vadesi – abhayūparato ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā bhayūparato; vītarāgattā kāme na sevati khayā rāgassā’ti. Sammā byākaramāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ byākareyya – ‘tathā hi pana ayamāyasmā saṅghe vā viharanto eko vā viharanto, ye ca tattha sugatā ye ca tattha duggatā, ye ca tattha gaṇamanusāsanti, ye ca idhekacce āmisesu saṃdissanti, ye ca idhekacce āmisena anupalittā, nāyamāyasmā taṃ tena avajānāti . Sammukhā kho pana metaṃ bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – abhayūparatohamasmi, nāhamasmi bhayūparato, vītarāgattā kāme na sevāmi khayā rāgassā’ti.
mula_english:
488.
"Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is an inquirer, not knowing how to gauge another’s mind, should investigate the *Tathāgata* with respect to two kinds of states, states cognizable through the eye (*cakṣu*) and through the ear (*śrotra*) thus: ‘Are there found in the *Tathāgata* or not any defiled (*saṃkiliṣṭhā*) states cognizable through the eye or through the ear?’ When he investigates him, he comes to know: ‘No defiled (*saṃkiliṣṭhā*) states cognizable through the eye or through the ear are found in the *Tathāgata*.’

"When he comes to know this, he investigates him further thus: ‘Are there found in the *Tathāgata* or not any mixed (*vītimissā*) states cognizable through the eye or through the ear?’ When he investigates him, he comes to know: ‘No mixed (*vītimissā*) states cognizable through the eye or through the ear are found in the *Tathāgata*.’

"When he comes to know this, he investigates him further thus: ‘Are there found in the *Tathāgata* or not cleansed (*vodātā*) states cognizable through the eye or through the ear?’ When he investigates him, he comes to know: ‘Cleansed (*vodātā*) states cognizable through the eye or through the ear are found in the *Tathāgata*.’

"When he comes to know this, he investigates him further thus: ‘Has this venerable one attained this wholesome (*kuśalaṃ*) state over a long time (*dīgharattaṃ*) or did he attain it recently (*ittarasamāpanno*)?’ When he investigates him, he comes to know: ‘This venerable one has attained this wholesome (*kuśalaṃ*) state over a long time (*dīgharattaṃ*), he did not attain it recently (*ittarasamāpanno*).’

"When he comes to know this, he investigates him further thus: ‘This venerable one has acquired renown (*ñattajjhāpanno*) and attained fame (*yasappatto*), are there found in him any dangers (*ādīnavā*)?’ As long as a *bhikkhu* has not acquired renown (*ñattajjhāpanno*) and attained fame (*yasappatto*), those dangers (*ādīnavā*) are not found in him.
But when, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* has acquired renown (*ñattajjhāpanno*) and attained fame (*yasappatto*), then those dangers (*ādīnavā*) are found in him.
When he investigates him, he comes to know: ‘This venerable *bhikkhu* has acquired renown (*ñattajjhāpanno*) and attained fame (*yasappatto*), but the dangers (*ādīnavā*) are not found in him.’

"When he comes to know this, he investigates him further thus: ‘Is this venerable one restrained without fear (*abhayūparato*), not restrained by fear (*bhayūparato*), and does he avoid indulging in sensual pleasures (*kāme*) because he is without lust (*vītarāgattā*) through the destruction (*khayā*) of lust (*rāgassa*)?’ When he investigates him, he comes to know: ‘This venerable one is restrained without fear (*abhayūparato*), not restrained by fear (*bhayūparato*), and he avoids indulging in sensual pleasures (*kāme*) because he is without lust (*vītarāgattā*) through the destruction (*khayā*) of lust (*rāgassa*).’
“Now, *bhikkhus*, if others should ask that *bhikkhu* thus: ‘What are the venerable one’s reasons (*ākārā*) and what is his evidence (*anvayā*) whereby he says: “That venerable one is restrained without fear (*abhayūparato*), not restrained by fear (*bhayūparato*), and he avoids indulging in sensual pleasures (*kāme*) because he is without lust (*vītarāgattā*) through the destruction (*khayā*) of lust (*rāgassa*)”?’
- answering rightly, that *bhikkhu* would answer thus: ‘Whether that venerable one dwells in the *Saṅgha* or alone, while some there are well-behaved (*sugatā*) and some are ill-behaved (*duggatā*) and some there teach a group (*gaṇamanusāsanti*), while some here are seen concerned about material things (*āmisesu saṃdissanti*) and some are unsullied by material things (*āmisena anupalittā*), still that venerable one does not despise anyone because of that.
And I have heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: “I am restrained without fear (*abhayūparato*), not restrained by fear (*bhayūparato*), and I avoid indulging in sensual pleasures (*kāme*) because I am without lust (*vītarāgattā*) through the destruction (*khayā*) of lust (*rāgassa*).’“
commentary_pali:
488.Dvīsu dhammesu tathāgato samannesitabboti idha kalyāṇamittūpanissayaṃ dasseti. Mahā hi esa kalyāṇamittūpanissayo nāma. Tassa mahantabhāvo evaṃ veditabbo – ekasmiṃ hi samaye āyasmā ānando upaḍḍhaṃ attano ānubhāvena hoti, upaḍḍhaṃ kalyāṇamittānubhāvenāti cintetvā attano dhammatāya nicchetuṃ asakkonto bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchi, – ‘‘upaḍḍhamidaṃ, bhante, brahmacariyassa, yadidaṃ kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā’’ti. Bhagavā āha – ‘‘mā hevaṃ, ānanda, mā hevaṃ, ānanda, sakalamevidaṃ, ānanda, brahmacariyaṃ yadidaṃ kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā, kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañcānanda, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto…pe… ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti. Idhānanda, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto…pe… bahulīkaroti, tadamināpetaṃ, ānanda, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ. Yathā sakalamevidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ yadidaṃ kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā. Mamañhi, ānanda, kalyāṇamittaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti. Jarādhammā…pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.2).

Bhikkhūnaṃ bāhiraṅgasampattiṃ kathentopi āha – ‘‘bāhiraṃ, bhikkhave, aṅganti karitvā nāññaṃ ekaṅgampi samanupassāmi, yaṃ evaṃ mahato atthāya saṃvattati, yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, kalyāṇamittatā. Kalyāṇamittatā, bhikkhave, mahato atthāya saṃvattatī’’ti (a. ni. 1.113). Mahācundassa kilesasallekhapaṭipadaṃ kathentopi, ‘‘pare pāpamittā bhavissanti, mayamettha kalyāṇamittā bhavissāmāti sallekho karaṇīyo’’ti (ma. ni. 1.83) āha. Meghiyattherassa vimuttiparipācaniyadhamme kathentopi, ‘‘aparipakkāya, meghiya, cetovimuttiyā pañca dhammā paripākāya saṃvattanti. Katame pañca? Idha, meghiya, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti’’ti (udā. 31) kalyāṇamittūpanissayameva visesesi. Piyaputtassa rāhulattherassa abhiṇhovādaṃ dentopi –

‘‘Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe, pantañca sayanāsanaṃ;

Vivittaṃ appanigghosaṃ, mattaññū hohi bhojane.

Cīvare piṇḍapāte ca, paccaye sayanāsane;

Etesu taṇhaṃ mākāsi, mā lokaṃ punarāgamī’’ti. (su. ni. 340, 341) –

Kalyāṇamittūpanissayameva sabbapaṭhamaṃ kathesi. Evaṃ mahā esa kalyāṇamittūpanissayo nāma. Idhāpi taṃ dassento bhagavā dvīsu dhammesu tathāgato samannesitabboti desanaṃ ārabhi. Paṇḍito bhikkhu dvīsu dhammesu tathāgataṃ esatu gavesatūti attho. Etena bhagavā ayaṃ mahājaccoti vā, lakkhaṇasampannoti vā, abhirūpo dassanīyoti vā, abhiññāto abhilakkhitoti vā, imaṃ nissāyāhaṃ cīvarādayo paccaye labhissāmīti vā, evaṃ cintetvā maṃ nissāya vasanakiccaṃ natthi. Yo pana evaṃ sallakkheti, ‘‘pahoti me esa satthā hutvā satthukiccaṃ sādhetu’’nti, so maṃ bhajatūti sīhanādaṃ nadati. Buddhasīhanādo kira nāmesa suttantoti.

dvīsu dhammesu tathāgato samannesitabbo

Idāni te dve dhamme dassento cakkhusotaviññeyyesūti āha. Tattha satthu kāyiko samācāro vīmaṃsakassa cakkhuviññeyyo dhammo nāma. Vācasiko samācāro sotaviññeyyo dhammo nāma. Idāni tesu samannesitabbākāraṃ dassento ye saṃkiliṭṭhātiādimāha. Tattha saṃkiliṭṭhāti kilesasampayuttā. Te ca na cakkhusotaviññeyyā. Yathā pana udake calante vā pupphuḷake vā muñcante anto maccho atthīti viññāyati, evaṃ pāṇātipātādīni vā karontassa, musāvādādīni vā bhaṇantassa kāyavacīsamācāre disvā ca sutvā ca taṃsamuṭṭhāpakacittaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhanti viññāyati. Tasmā evamāha. Saṃkiliṭṭhacittassa hi kāyavacīsamācārāpi saṃkiliṭṭhāyeva nāma. Na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantīti na te tathāgatassa atthi. Na upalabbhantīti evaṃ jānātīti attho. Natthitāyeva hi te na upalabbhanti na paṭicchannatāya. Tathā hi bhagavā ekadivasaṃ imesu dhammesu bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pavārento āha – ‘‘handa dāni, bhikkhave, pavāremi vo, na ca me kiñci garahatha kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā sāriputto uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘na kho mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato kiñci garahāma kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā. Bhagavā hi, bhante, anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā, asañjātassa maggassa sañjānetā, anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā, maggaññū maggavidū maggakovido. Maggānugā ca, bhante, etarahi sāvakā viharanti pacchāsamannāgatā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.215). Evaṃ parisuddhā tathāgatassa kāyavacīsamācārā. Uttaropi sudaṃ māṇavo tathāgatassa kāyavacīdvāre anārādhanīyaṃ kiñci passissāmīti satta māse anubandhitvā likkhāmattampi na addasa. Manussabhūto vā esa buddhabhūtassa kāyavacīdvāre kiṃ anārādhanīyaṃ passissati? Māropi devaputto bodhisattassa sato mahābhinikkhamanato paṭṭhāya chabbassāni gavesamāno kiñci anārādhanīyaṃ nāddasa, antamaso cetoparivitakkamattampi. Māro kira cintesi – ‘‘sacassa vitakkitamattampi akusalaṃ passissāmi, tattheva naṃ muddhani paharitvā pakkamissāmī’’ti. So chabbassāni adisvā buddhabhūtampi ekaṃ vassaṃ anubandhitvā kiñci vajjaṃ apassanto gamanasamaye vanditvā –

cakkhusotaviññeyyesū ye saṃkiliṭṭhā saṃkiliṭṭhā Na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantī

‘‘Mahāvīra mahāpuññaṃ, iddhiyā yasasā jalaṃ;

Sabbaverabhayātītaṃ, pāde vandāmi gotama’’nti. (saṃ. ni. 1.159) –

Gāthaṃ vatvā gato.

Vītimissāti kāle kaṇhā, kāle sukkāti evaṃ vomissakā. Vodātāti parisuddhā nikkilesā. Saṃvijjantīti vodātā dhammā atthi upalabbhanti. Tathāgatassa hi parisuddhā kāyasamācārādayo. Tenāha – ‘‘cattārimāni, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arakkheyyāni. Katamāni cattāri? Parisuddhakāyasamācāro, bhikkhave, tathāgato, natthi tathāgatassa kāyaduccaritaṃ, yaṃ tathāgato rakkheyya, ‘mā me idaṃ paro aññāsī’ti. Parisuddhavacīsamācāro… parisuddhamanosamācāro… parisuddhājīvo, bhikkhave, tathāgato , natthi tathāgatassa micchājīvo, yaṃ tathāgato rakkheyya, mā me idaṃ paro aññāsī’’ti (a. ni. 7.58).

Vītimissā Vodātā Saṃvijjantī

Imaṃ kusalaṃ dhammanti imaṃ anavajjaṃ ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ. ‘‘Ayamāyasmā satthā kiṃ nu kho dīgharattaṃ samāpanno aticirakālato paṭṭhāya iminā samannāgato, udāhu ittarasamāpanno hiyyo vā pare vā parasuve vā divase samāpanno’’ti evaṃ gavesatūti attho. Ekaccena hi ekasmiṃ ṭhāne vasantena bahu micchājīvakammaṃ kataṃ, taṃ tattha kālātikkame paññāyati, pākaṭaṃ hoti. So aññataraṃ paccantagāmaṃ vā samuddatīraṃ vā gantvā paṇṇasālaṃ kāretvā āraññako viya hutvā viharati. Manussā sambhāvanaṃ uppādetvā tassa paṇīte paccaye denti. Janapadavāsino bhikkhū tassa parihāraṃ disvā, ‘‘atidappito vatāyaṃ āyasmā, ko nu kho eso’’ti pariggaṇhantā, ‘‘asukaṭṭhāne asukaṃ nāma micchājīvaṃ katvā pakkantabhikkhū’’ti ñatvā na sakkā iminā saddhiṃ uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā kātunti sannipatitvā dhammena samena ukkhepanīyādīsu aññataraṃ kammaṃ karonti. Evarūpāya paṭicchannapaṭipattiyā atthibhāvaṃ vā natthibhāvaṃ vā vīmaṃsāpetuṃ evamāha.

Imaṃ kusalaṃ dhamma

Evaṃjānātīti dīgharattaṃ samāpanno, na ittarasamāpannoti jānāti. Anacchariyaṃ cetaṃ. Yaṃ tathāgatassa etarahi sabbaññutaṃ pattassa dīgharattaṃ ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ parisuddhaṃ bhaveyya. Yassa bodhisattakālepi evaṃ ahosi.

Evaṃ jānātī

Atīte kira gandhārarājā ca vedeharājā ca dvepi sahāyakā hutvā kāmesu ādīnavaṃ disvā rajjāni puttānaṃ niyyātetvā isipabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā ekasmiṃ araññagāmake piṇḍāya caranti. Paccanto nāma dullabhaloṇo hoti. Tato aloṇaṃ yāguṃ labhitvā ekissāya sālāya nisīditvā pivanti. Antarantare manussā loṇacuṇṇaṃ āharitvā denti. Ekadivasaṃ eko vedehisissa paṇṇe pakkhipitvā loṇacuṇṇaṃ adāsi . Vedehisi gahetvā upaḍḍhaṃ gandhārisissa-santike ṭhapetvā upaḍḍhaṃ attano santike ṭhapesi. Tato thokaṃ paribhuttāvasesaṃ disvā, ‘‘mā idaṃ nassī’’ti paṇṇena veṭhetvā tiṇagahane ṭhapesi. Puna ekasmiṃ divase yāgupānakāle satiṃ katvā olokento taṃ disvā gandhārisiṃ upasaṅkamitvā, ‘‘ito thokaṃ gaṇhatha ācariyā’’ti āha. Kuto te laddhaṃ vedehisīti? Tasmiṃ divase paribhuttāvasesaṃ ‘‘mā nassī’’ti mayā ṭhapitanti. Gandhārisi gahetuṃ na icchati, aloṇakaṃyeva yāguṃ pivitvā vedehaṃ isiṃ avoca –

‘‘Hitvā gāmasahassāni, paripuṇṇāni soḷasa;

Koṭṭhāgārāni phītāni, sannidhiṃ dāni kubbasī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.76);

Vedehisi avoca – ‘‘tumhe rajjaṃ pahāya pabbajitā, idāni kasmā loṇacuṇṇamattasannidhikāraṇā pabbajjāya anucchavikaṃ na karothā’’ti? Kiṃ mayā kataṃ vedehisīti? Atha naṃ āha –

‘‘Hitvā gandhāravisayaṃ, pahūtadhanadhāriyaṃ;

Pasāsanato nikkhanto, idha dāni pasāsasī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.77);

Gandhāro āha –

‘‘Dhammaṃ bhaṇāmi vedeha, adhammo me na ruccati;

Dhammaṃ me bhaṇamānassa, na pāpamupalimpatī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.78);

Vedeho āha –

‘‘Yena kenaci vaṇṇena, paro labhati ruppanaṃ;

Mahatthiyampi ce vācaṃ, na taṃ bhāseyya paṇḍito’’ti. (jā. 1.7.79);

Gandhāro āha –

‘‘Kāmaṃ ruppatu vā mā vā, bhusaṃva vikirīyatu;

Dhammaṃ me bhaṇamānassa, na pāpamupalimpatī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.80);

Tato vedehisi yassa sakāpi buddhi natthi, ācariyasantike vinayaṃ na sikkhati, so andhamahiṃso viya vane caratīti cintetvā āha –

‘‘No ce assa sakā buddhi, vinayo vā susikkhito;

Vane andhamahiṃsova, careyya bahuko jano.

Yasmā ca panidhekacce, āceramhi susikkhitā;

Tasmā vinītavinayā, caranti susamāhitā’’ti. (jā. 1.7.81-82);

Evañca pana vatvā vedehisi ajānitvā mayā katanti gandhārisiṃ khamāpesi. Te ubhopi tapaṃ caritvā brahmalokaṃ agamaṃsu. Evaṃ tathāgatassa bodhisattakālepi dīgharattaṃ ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ parisuddhaṃ ahosi.

Uttajjhāpanno ayamāyasmā bhikkhu yasapattoti ayamāyasmā amhākaṃ satthā bhikkhu ñattaṃ paññātabhāvaṃ pākaṭabhāvaṃ ajjhāpanno nu kho, sayañca parivārasampattiṃ patto nu kho noti. Tena cassa paññātajjhāpannabhāvena yasasannissitabhāvena ca kiṃ ekacce ādīnavā sandissanti udāhu noti evaṃ samannesantūti dasseti. Na tāva, bhikkhaveti, bhikkhave, yāva bhikkhu na rājarājamahāmattādīsu abhiññātabhāvaṃ vā parivārasampattiṃ vā āpanno hoti, tāva ekacce mānātimānādayo ādīnavā na saṃvijjanti upasantūpasanto viya sotāpanno viya sakadāgāmī viya ca viharati. Ariyo nu kho puthujjano nu khotipi ñātuṃ na sakkā hoti.

Uttajjhāpanno ayamāyasmā bhikkhu yasapatto Na tāva, bhikkhave

Yatoca kho, bhikkhaveti yadā pana idhekacco bhikkhu ñāto hoti parivārasampanno vā, tadā tiṇhena siṅgena gogaṇaṃ vijjhanto duṭṭhagoṇo viya, migasaṅghaṃ abhimaddamāno dīpi viya ca aññe bhikkhū tattha tattha vijjhanto agāravo asabhāgavutti aggapādena bhūmiṃ phusanto viya carati. Ekacco pana kulaputto yathā yathā ñāto hoti yasassī, tathā tathā phalabhārabharito viya sāli suṭṭhutaraṃ onamati, rājarājamahāmattādīsu upasaṅkamantesu akiñcanabhāvaṃ paccavekkhitvā samaṇasaññaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā chinnavisāṇausabho viya, caṇḍāladārako viya ca sorato nivāto nīcacitto hutvā bhikkhusaṅghassa ceva sadevakassa ca lokassa, hitāya sukhāya paṭipajjati. Evarūpaṃ paṭipattiṃ sandhāya ‘‘nāssa idhekacce ādīnavā’’ti āha.

Yato ca kho, bhikkhave

Tathāgato pana aṭṭhasu lokadhammesu tādī, so hi lābhepi tādī, alābhepi tādī, yasepi tādī, ayasepi tādī, pasaṃsāyapi tādī, nindāyapi tādī, sukhepi tādī, dukkhepi tādī, tasmā sabbākārena nāssa idhekacce ādīnavā saṃvijjanti. Abhayūparatoti abhayo hutvā uparato, accantūparato satatūparatoti attho. Na vā bhayena uparatotipi abhayūparato. Cattāri hi bhayāni kilesabhayaṃ vaṭṭabhayaṃ duggatibhayaṃ upavādabhayanti. Puthujjano catūhipi bhayehi bhāyati. Sekkhā tīhi, tesañhi duggatibhayaṃ pahīnaṃ, iti satta sekkhā bhayūparatā, khīṇāsavo abhayūparato nāma, tassa hi ekampi bhayaṃ natthi. Kiṃ paravādabhayaṃ natthīti? Natthi. Parānuddayaṃ pana paṭicca, ‘‘mādisaṃ khīṇāsavaṃ paṭicca sattā mā nassantū’’ti upavādaṃ rakkhati. Mūluppalavāpivihāravāsī yasatthero viya.

Abhayūparato

Thero kira mūluppalavāpigāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Athassa upaṭṭhākakuladvāraṃ pattassa pattaṃ gahetvā thaṇḍilapīṭhakaṃ nissāya āsanaṃ paññapesuṃ. Amaccadhītāpi taṃyeva pīṭhakaṃ nissāya paratobhāge nīcataraṃ āsanaṃ paññāpetvā nisīdi. Eko nevāsiko bhikkhu pacchā piṇḍāya paviṭṭho dvāre ṭhatvāva olokento thero amaccadhītarā saddhiṃ ekamañce nisinnoti sallakkhetvā, ‘‘ayaṃ paṃsukūliko vihāreva upasantūpasanto viya viharati, antogāme pana upaṭṭhāyikāhi saddhiṃ ekamañce nisīdatī’’ti cintetvā, ‘‘kiṃ nu kho mayā duddiṭṭha’’nti punappunaṃ oloketvā tathāsaññīva hutvā pakkāmi. Theropi bhattakiccaṃ katvā vihāraṃ gantvā vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisitvā dvāraṃ pidhāya nisīdi. Nevāsikopi katabhattakicco vihāraṃ gantvā, ‘‘taṃ paṃsukūlikaṃ niggaṇhitvā vihārā nikkaḍḍhissāmī’’ti asaññatanīhārena therassa vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā paribhogaghaṭato uluṅkena udakaṃ gahetvā mahāsaddaṃ karonto pāde dhovi. Thero, ‘‘ko nu kho ayaṃ asaññatacāriko’’ti āvajjanto sabbaṃ ñatvā, ‘‘ayaṃ mayi manaṃ padosetvā apāyūpago mā ahosī’’ti vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā kaṇṇikāmaṇḍalasamīpe pallaṅkena nisīdi. Nevāsiko duṭṭhākārena ghaṭikaṃ ukkhipitvā dvāraṃ vivaritvā anto paviṭṭho theraṃ apassanto, ‘‘heṭṭhāmañcaṃ paviṭṭho bhavissatī’’ti oloketvā tatthāpi apassanto nikkhamituṃ ārabhi. Thero ukkāsi. Itaro uddhaṃ olokento disvā adhivāsetuṃ asakkonto evamāha – ‘‘patirūpaṃ te, āvuso, paṃsukūlika evaṃ ānubhāvasampannassa upaṭṭhāyikāya saddhiṃ ekamañce nisīditu’’nti. Pabbajitā nāma, bhante, mātugāmena saddhiṃ na ekamañce nisīdanti, tumhehi pana duddiṭṭhametanti. Evaṃ khīṇāsavā parānuddayāya upavādaṃ rakkhanti.

Khayā rāgassāti rāgassa khayeneva. Vītarāgattā kāme na paṭisevati, na paṭisaṅkhāya vāretvāti. Tañceti evaṃ tathāgatassa kilesappahānaṃ ñatvā tattha tattha ṭhitanisinnakālādīsupi catuparisamajjhe alaṅkatadhammāsane nisīditvāpi itipi satthā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho vantakileso pahīnamalo abbhā muttapuṇṇacando viya suparisuddhoti evaṃ tathāgatassa kilesappahāne vaṇṇaṃ kathayamānaṃ taṃ vīmaṃsakaṃ bhikkhuṃ pare evaṃ puccheyyuṃ ceti attho.

Khayā rāgassā Tañce

Ākārāti kāraṇāni. Anvayāti anubuddhiyo. Saṅghe vā viharantoti appekadā aparicchinnagaṇanassa bhikkhusaṅghassa majjhe viharanto. Eko vā viharantoti icchāmahaṃ, bhikkhave , aḍḍhamāsaṃ paṭisallīyitunti, temāsaṃ paṭisallīyitunti evaṃ paṭisallāne ceva pālileyyakavanasaṇḍe ca ekako viharanto. Sugatāti suṭṭhugatā suppaṭipannā kārakā yuttapayuttā. Evarūpāpi hi ekacce bhikkhū atthi. Duggatāti duṭṭhugatā duppaṭipannā kāyadaḷhibahulā vissaṭṭhakammaṭṭhānā. Evarūpāpi ekacce atthi. Gaṇamanusāsantīti gaṇabandhanena baddhā gaṇārāmā gaṇabahulikā hutvā gaṇaṃ pariharanti. Evarūpāpi ekacce atthi. Tesaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtā gaṇato nissaṭā visaṃsaṭṭhā vippamuttavihārinopi atthi.

Ākārā Anvayā Saṅghe vā viharanto Eko vā viharanto Sugatā Duggatā Gaṇamanusāsantī

Āmisesu sandissantīti āmisagiddhā āmisacakkhukā catupaccayaāmisatthameva āhiṇḍamānā āmisesu sandissamānakabhikkhūpi atthi. Āmisena anupalittā catūhi paccayehi vinivattamānasā abbhā muttacandasadisā hutvā viharamānāpi atthi. Nāyamāyasmā taṃ tena avajānātīti ayaṃ āyasmā satthā tāya tāya paṭipattiyā taṃ taṃ puggalaṃ nāvajānāti, ayaṃ paṭipanno kārako, ayaṃ gaṇato nissaṭo visaṃsaṭṭho. Ayaṃ āmisena anupalitto paccayehi vinivattamānaso abbhā mutto candimā viyāti evamassa gehasitavasena ussādanāpi natthi. Ayaṃ duppaṭipanno akārako kāyadaḷhibahulo vissaṭṭhakammaṭṭhāno, ayaṃ gaṇabandhanabaddho, ayaṃ āmisagiddho lolo āmisacakkhukoti evamassa gehasitavasena apasādanāpi natthīti attho. Iminā kiṃ kathitaṃ hoti? Tathāgatassa sattesu tādibhāvo kathito hoti. Ayañhi –

Āmisesu sandissantī Nāyamāyasmā taṃ tena avajānātī

‘‘Vadhakassa devadattassa, corassaṅgulimālino;

Dhanapāle rāhule ca, sabbesaṃ samako munī’’ti. (mi. pa. 6.6.5);
commentary_english:
488. Here, [it] shows the dependence on good friendship, that the *Tathāgata* is to be inferred by means of two qualities (*dvīsu dhammesu tathāgato samannesitabbo*). Indeed, great is this dependence on good friendship, named. Thus its greatness should be understood: once, venerable Ānanda, thinking, "Half of me is due to my own power, [and] half is due to the power of good friendship," and being unable to decide through his own nature, approached the Blessed One and asked: "This is half of the holy life (*brahmacariyassa*), namely, good friendship (*kalyāṇamittatā*), good companionship (*kalyāṇasahāyatā*), [and] good comradeship (*kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā*)." The Blessed One said: "Not so, Ānanda, not so, Ānanda, this entire holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) is this, Ānanda, good friendship (*kalyāṇamittatā*), good companionship (*kalyāṇasahāyatā*), [and] good comradeship (*kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā*). It is to be expected of a monk (*bhikkhuno*), Ānanda, who has a good friend, a good companion, a good comrade, that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati*), he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati*)." And how, Ānanda, does a monk who has a good friend... develop the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti*), [and] cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti*)? Here, Ānanda, a monk develops right view (*sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti*) ... develops right concentration (*sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti*) based on seclusion. Thus, Ānanda, a monk [who has] a good friend... cultivates [the path], thus it should be understood by this method, Ānanda. Just as this entire holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) is this: good friendship (*kalyāṇamittatā*), good companionship (*kalyāṇasahāyatā*), [and] good comradeship (*kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā*). For indeed, Ānanda, by relying on a good friend, beings subject to birth are freed from birth (*jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti*). Beings subject to old age... beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair (*sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā*) are freed from sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair (*sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī*)."

Speaking of the external accomplishment of monks, he said: "Having made an external factor, monks, what else do I see as a single factor that leads to such great benefit, as this, monks, good friendship (*kalyāṇamittatā*). Good friendship (*kalyāṇamittatā*), monks, leads to great benefit." Speaking of Mahācunda's course of effacement of defilements, he said: "Others will have bad friends (*pāpamittā bhavissanti*); we shall have good friends (*kalyāṇamittā bhavissāma*) here': effacement (*sallekho*) should be practiced thus." Speaking of the qualities conducive to liberation of Meghiya Thera, [the Buddha said]: "For one whose awareness-release (*cetovimuttiyā*) is still immature, Meghiya, five qualities lead to maturity (*paripākāya saṃvattanti*). Which five? Here, Meghiya, a monk is a good friend (*kalyāṇamitto hoti*)," he emphasized only the dependence on good friendship (*kalyāṇamittūpanissayameva*). Even giving frequent advice to his dear son, Rāhula Thera – "Cultivate good friends (*mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe*), [and] a secluded resting place; A solitary, quiet place, be moderate in eating. In robes, alms food, requisites, [and] a resting place; Do not create craving in these, do not come again to the world." He spoke of good friendship as the very first thing. Thus, great is this dependence on good friendship named. Here too, showing that, the Blessed One began the teaching: "The *Tathāgata* is to be inferred by means of two qualities (*dvīsu dhammesu tathāgato samannesitabbo*)." The meaning is: "A wise monk should seek and investigate the *Tathāgata* by means of two qualities (*dvīsu dhammesu tathāgataṃ esatu gavesatūti attho*)." By this, "The Blessed One is of great birth (*mahājaccoti*)," or "is endowed with marks (*lakkhaṇasampannoti*)," or "is beautiful [and] pleasing (*abhirūpo dassanīyoti*)," or "is known [and] distinguished (*abhiññāto abhilakkhitoti*)," or "relying on him, I will obtain robes and other requisites (*cīvarādayo paccaye labhissāmi*)," thus thinking, the business of dwelling relying on me There is no such thing. However, if anyone thinks thus, "This teacher is capable of achieving the task of a teacher," let him attend to me," he roars a lion's roar. The *Buddha-sīhanāda* (Buddha's Lion's Roar) is said to be the name of the *sūtra*. [A *Tathāgata*] is to be investigated in two qualities. Now, showing those two qualities, he says, "Cognizable through the eye and ear." Therein, the teacher's physical conduct is called a state cognizable through the eye for one who investigates. The verbal conduct is called a state cognizable through the ear. Now, showing the way it is to be investigated in those, he says, "Those that are defiled," and so on. Therein, "defiled" means associated with defilements. And those are not cognizable through the eye and ear. Just as it is known that there is a fish inside when water is moving or bubbles are rising, so it is known that the mind that arises together with it is defiled when one sees or hears bodily or verbal conduct of one who is doing such things as killing living beings, or speaking such things as false speech. Therefore, he said thus. For the bodily and verbal conduct of one whose mind is defiled is indeed defiled. "They are not found in the *Tathāgata*" means they are not in the *Tathāgata*. It means he knows thus, "They are not apprehended." For they are not apprehended because of non-existence, not because of concealment. Thus, indeed, the Fortunate One, on one day, addressing the community of monks on these states, said, "Come now, monks, I invite you [to speak], and do you not blame me in any way, bodily or verbally." When this was said, the venerable Śāriputra, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe on one shoulder, prostrating with joined palms in the direction of the Fortunate One, said this to the Fortunate One: "We, venerable sir, do not blame the Fortunate One in any way, bodily or verbally. For the Fortunate One, venerable sir, is the originator of the path unarisen before, the producer of the path unproduced before, the declarer of the path undeclared before; he is the knower of the path, the finder of the path, the one skilled in the path. And his disciples now abide following that path and become possessed of it afterwards" (Saṃ. Ni. 1. 215). Thus, the bodily and verbal conduct of the *Tathāgata* is completely pure. Uttara also, it is said, a youth, following the *Tathāgata* for seven months, thinking, "I will see something unappealing in the bodily and verbal door of the *Tathāgata*," did not see even the amount of a louse. What unappealing thing will a human being see in the bodily and verbal door of one who has become a Buddha? Māra also, the divine son, searching for six years from the time of the Great Renunciation of the Bodhisattva, did not see anything unappealing, not even the slightest thought that arises in the mind. Māra, it is said, thought, "If I see even the slightest unwholesome thought in him, I will strike him on the head right there and depart." He, not seeing [any fault] for six years, following even the one who had become a Buddha for one year, seeing no fault, at the time of departure, after venerating, Cognizable through the eye and ear. Those that are defiled. Defiled. They are not found in the *Tathāgata*. "Great hero, great merit, radiant with power and fame; Having passed beyond all enmity and fear, I venerate the feet of Gotama." (Saṃ. Ni. 1. 159) – Having spoken the verse, he departed. Vītimissā means mixed, at times dark, at times light. Vodātā means completely pure, without defilements ( *kilesa*). Saṃvijjantī means the pure *dharmas* are present and can be found. The *tathāgata*'s bodily conduct, etc. is completely pure. Therefore, he said: "These four, monks, are the confidences (*arakkheyyāni*) of a *tathāgata*. Which four? The *tathāgata*, monks, has completely pure bodily conduct; there is no bodily misconduct of the *tathāgata* that the *tathāgata* would need to guard against, [thinking,] 'May another not know this of me.' [He has] completely pure verbal conduct… [He has] completely pure mental conduct… The *tathāgata*, monks, has completely pure livelihood ; there is no wrong livelihood of the *tathāgata* that the *tathāgata* would need to guard against, [thinking,] 'May another not know this of me'" (A. Ni. 7. 58). Vītimissā Vodātā Saṃvijjantī

Imaṃ kusalaṃ dhamma means this wholesome *dharma*, this faultless livelihood, the eighth factor of the path (*ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ*). "'Is this venerable teacher one who has attained to prolonged meditative absorption (*dīgharattaṃ samāpanno*) and has been endowed with this from a very long time, or is he one who has attained to a lesser meditative absorption, having attained it yesterday, the day before, or the day before that?' Such is the meaning of investigating." For some one living in a certain place, much wrong livelihood (*micchājīvakammaṃ*) has been done; that becomes known there after the passage of time; it becomes evident. He goes to some frontier village (*paccantagāmaṃ*) or to the seashore, has a leaf hut (*paṇṇasālaṃ*) built, and lives as if he were a forest dweller (*āraññako*). People create respect (*sambhāvanaṃ*) and give him excellent requisites (*paccaye*). Monks living in the district, seeing his behavior (*parihāraṃ*), [and] suspecting, "This venerable one is very arrogant, who could this be?" knowing, "He is a monk who has gone forth (*pakkantabhikkhū*) having committed such-and-such wrong livelihood (*micchājīvaṃ*) in such-and-such place," coming together, they perform some act of expulsion (*ukkhepanīyādīsu*) with the *dharma*, fairly and equally. In order to investigate the existence or non-existence of such concealed practice (*paṭicchannapaṭipattiyā*), he spoke thus. Imaṃ kusalaṃ dhamma

EvaṃJānātī means one who has attained to prolonged meditative absorption knows, "He has not attained to a lesser meditative absorption." This is not amazing. The fact that the eight-factored path of livelihood (*ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ*) of the *tathāgata*, who has now attained omniscience (*sabbaññutaṃ*), might be completely pure occurred even in his time as a *bodhisattva*. Evaṃ Jānātī

In the past, it is said, the king of Gandhāra and the king of Videha, both being friends, seeing the danger in sensual pleasures (*kāmesu ādīnavaṃ*), entrusting their kingdoms (*rajjāni*) to their sons, went forth into the ascetic life (*isipabbajjaṃ*), wandering for alms (*piṇḍāya caranti*) in a certain forest village (*araññagāmake*). A frontier area (*paccanto*) is said to be a place where salt is hard to find (*dullabhaloṇo*). Then, obtaining unsalted rice gruel (*aloṇaṃ yāguṃ*), they sit down in a certain hall (*sālāya*) and drink. From time to time, people bring salt powder (*loṇacuṇṇaṃ*) and give it to them. One day, a certain person from Videha, putting it in a leaf, gave salt powder (*loṇacuṇṇaṃ*) to the Videhan ascetic . The Videhan ascetic, taking [it], setting aside half near the Gandhāran ascetic, set aside half near himself. Then, seeing a little bit left over from what had been eaten, [thinking,] "May this not be destroyed," wrapping it in a leaf, he put it in a grassy thicket (*tiṇagahane*). Again, one day, remembering it at the time for drinking rice gruel (*yāgupānakāle*), looking around, seeing that, approaching the Gandhāran ascetic, he said, "Take a little bit from here, teacher (*ācariyā*)." "From where did you obtain it, Videhan ascetic?" On that day, [it was] what was left over from what had been eaten, [and] was set aside by me [thinking,] 'May it not be destroyed.'" The Gandhāran ascetic does not want to take [it], drinking the unsalted rice gruel, he spoke to the Videhan ascetic – "Having abandoned sixteen thousand villages (*gāmasahassāni*), completely full, storehouses (*koṭṭhāgārāni*) abounding, do you now amass a store (*sannidhiṃ*)?" (Jā. 1. 7. 76); Vedehisi said, “You renounced the kingdom and went forth. Now, why don't you do what is inappropriate for the going forth, because of the mere presence of salt and flour?" "What have I done, Vedehisi?" Then he said to him: "Having abandoned the Gandhara country, abundant in wealth and resources, Having gone forth from governance, now you govern here." (jā. 1.7.77); Gandhāro said: "I speak the *dharma*, Vedeha, the *adharma* is not pleasing to me; While I am speaking the *dharma*, evil does not cling to me." (jā. 1.7.78); Vedeho said: "By whatever manner, another obtains vexation, Even if the speech is of great meaning, a wise man should not speak it." (jā. 1.7.79); Gandhāro said: "Let it vex or not, let it be scattered greatly; While I am speaking the *dharma*, evil does not cling to me." (jā. 1.7.80); Then Vedehisi, thinking, "He who has no intelligence of his own, does not learn the discipline from a teacher, he wanders in the forest like a blind buffalo," said: "If he had intelligence of his own, or the discipline was well learned; Like a blind buffalo in the forest, many people would wander. Because some here are well trained in conduct; Therefore, with subdued discipline, they live well composed." (jā. 1.7.81-82); Having said this, Vedehisi apologized to Gandharisi, saying, "I did not know, I did it." Both of them, practicing austerity, went to the Brahma world. Thus, even in the time of the Tathāgata, in the time of the Bodhisattva, for a long time, the morality of the eighth means of livelihood was completely pure. "*Uttajjhāpanno ayamāyasmā bhikkhu yasapatto*," this venerable monk, our teacher, the monk, has attained the state of being known and recognized, or has attained the acquisition of a retinue, or not. Therefore, due to his state of being known and recognized, and due to his state of dependence on fame, does he show whether some faults appear or not, thus he shows by considering together. "*Na tāva, bhikkhave*," monks, as long as a monk has not attained the state of being known among kings, royal ministers, and others, or has not attained the acquisition of a retinue, so long some faults, such as pride and excessive pride, do not exist; he lives as if calmed, as if a *sotāpanna*, as if a *sakadāgāmī*. It is not possible to know whether he is an *ariya* or an ordinary person. "*Uttajjhāpanno ayamāyasmā bhikkhu yasapatto* *na tāva, bhikkhave* *yato* *ca kho, bhikkhave*," when, however, a certain monk here is known or has acquired a retinue, then, like a rogue bull piercing the herd of cows with a sharp horn, like a leopard crushing the flock of deer, he wanders here and there piercing other monks, being disrespectful, behaving inappropriately, touching the ground with the tip of his foot. But some son of a good family, as he becomes known and famous, so does he bow down even better, like a rice plant laden with the burden of fruit. When approaching kings, royal ministers, and the like, reflecting on his own lack of possessions, establishing the perception of a *śramaṇa*, like a bull with severed horns, like an outcaste boy, he is gentle, humble, and low-minded, and thus practices for the benefit and happiness of the *bhikṣu*-*saṅgha* and the world with its gods. Referring to such practice, he said, "For him, some dangers do not exist here." And because, *bhikṣus*, the *Tathāgata* is the same in the eight worldly *dharmas*, he is indeed the same in gain, the same in loss, the same in fame, the same in disgrace, the same in praise, the same in blame, the same in happiness, the same in suffering. Therefore, in every way, some dangers do not exist for him. "One who has ceased from fear" means one who has become fearless and has ceased, utterly ceased, constantly ceased. Or, one who has ceased not by fear is also one who has ceased from fear. For there are four fears: the fear of defilements, the fear of the round, the fear of bad destinies, and the fear of blame. An ordinary person is afraid of all four fears. A trainee [is afraid] of three, for the fear of bad destinies is abandoned by them. Thus, seven trainees are those who have ceased from fear. An *arhat* is called one who has ceased from fear, for he has not even one fear. Is there no fear of the views of others? No, there is not. But out of compassion for others, he protects himself from blame, thinking, "Lest beings be ruined on account of an *arhat* like me." Like the venerable Yasatthera, who lived at the Mūluppalavāpi monastery. It seems that the venerable one entered the village of Mūluppalavāpi for alms. Then, having reached the door of his patron's family, they took his bowl and prepared a seat, relying on a *thaṇḍila* seat. The daughter of a minister also prepared a lower seat behind the same seat and sat down. A resident *bhikṣu*, having entered for alms later, standing at the door and looking, noticed that the venerable one was sitting on the same seat with the minister's daughter. Thinking, "This rag-robe wearer behaves in the monastery as if he were peaceful and calm, but in the village he sits on the same seat with his female attendant," and looking again and again, thinking, "Have I seen wrongly?", he departed. The venerable one also, having finished his meal, went to the monastery, entered his dwelling, and closed the door and sat down. The resident one also, having finished his meal, went to the monastery, thinking, "I will rebuke that rag-robe wearer and drag him out of the monastery," and with unrestrained craving, went to the venerable one's dwelling, took water from the bathing pot with a scoop, and washed his feet, making a great noise. The venerable one, considering, "Who is this unrestrained wanderer?", knowing everything, thinking, "Lest this one, having corrupted his mind towards me, go to a bad destiny," rose into the sky and sat cross-legged near the circle of the eave. The resident one, raising the pot with a bad attitude, opened the door and entered, not seeing the venerable one, thinking, "He must have entered under the bed," looked there too, and not seeing him, began to leave. The venerable one cleared his throat. The other, looking upwards and seeing him, unable to bear it, said thus: "It is fitting for you, friend, a rag-robe wearer with such great power, to sit on the same seat with a female attendant." "Those gone forth, *bhante*, do not sit on the same seat with a woman. You have seen wrongly." Thus, *arhat*s protect themselves from blame out of compassion for others. "By the destruction of passion" means by the very destruction of passion. Being without passion, he does not indulge in sensual pleasures, he does not ward them off by reflection. "And if" means, having known thus the abandonment of defilements by the *Tathāgata*, even in the various situations of standing, sitting, time, etc., even sitting on an adorned *dharma* seat in the midst of the four assemblies, [one might say,] "Thus, the Teacher is without passion, without hatred, without delusion, rid of defilements, with abandoned impurity, like the full moon freed from clouds, utterly pure." Thus, while telling the virtues of the *Tathāgata's* abandonment of defilements, others might ask that investigating *bhikṣu* thus. "Causes" means reasons. "Understanding" means subsequent realizations. "Dwelling in the *saṅgha*" means dwelling in the midst of the *bhikṣu*-*saṅgha*, whose number is sometimes not fixed. "Dwelling alone" means, "I desire, *bhikṣus*, to go into seclusion for half a month," "to go into seclusion for three months." Thus, dwelling alone both in seclusion and in the Pārileyyaka forest grove. "Sugatā" means "gone well," "gone rightly," those who are accomplished, proper, and engaged in appropriate conduct. Indeed, there are some monks of this kind. "Duggatā" means "gone badly," "gone wrongly," those who are ill-conducted, rigid in their ways, and of dissipated practice. Indeed, there are some of this kind as well. "Gaṇamanusāsantī" means those who, bound by group ties, delight in groups, are fond of groups, and, having become numerous, care for the group. Indeed, there are some of this kind as well. Opposed to these are those who, cast out from the group, are detached, live in freedom, and are without attachment to the group.

Ākārā anvayā saṅghe vā viharanto eko vā viharanto Sugatā duggatā Gaṇamanusāsantī

Āmisesu sandissantī means those monks who are greedy for material things, focused on material things, constantly wandering about just for the sake of the four requisites, and attached to material things. Those whose minds are averse to material things, who are like the moon freed from clouds, live detached from the four requisites. Nāyamāyasmā taṃ tena avajānātī means this venerable one, the teacher, does not despise this or that person because of this or that practice, saying, "This one is accomplished, this one is a doer, this one is cast out from the group, this one is detached." This one is not attached to material things, his mind is averse to the requisites, he is like the moon freed from clouds; thus, for him, there is no elation due to dwelling in a house. This one is ill-conducted, not a doer, rigid in his ways, of dissipated practice, this one is bound by group ties, this one is greedy for material things, fickle, focused on material things; thus, for him, there is no depression due to dwelling in a house—this is the meaning. What is said by this? The suchness (tādibhāva) of the Tathāgata in beings is said. This is because –

āmisesu sandissantī Nāyamāyasmā taṃ tena avajānātī ‘‘For the murderer Devadatta, for the thief Aṅgulimāla, for Dhanapāla, for Rāhula, the sage is equal to all.’’

mula_pali:
489. ‘‘Tatra , bhikkhave, tathāgatova uttariṃ paṭipucchitabbo – ‘ye saṃkiliṭṭhā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti vā te tathāgatassa no vā’ti? Byākaramāno, bhikkhave, tathāgato evaṃ byākareyya – ‘ye saṃkiliṭṭhā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantī’’’ti.

‘‘Ye vītimissā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti vā te tathāgatassa no vāti? Byākaramāno, bhikkhave, tathāgato evaṃ byākareyya – ‘ye vītimissā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, na te tathāgatassa saṃvijjantī’ti.

‘‘Ye vodātā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti vā te tathāgatassa no vāti? Byākaramāno, bhikkhave, tathāgato evaṃ byākareyya – ‘ye vodātā cakkhusotaviññeyyā dhammā, saṃvijjanti te tathāgatassa; etaṃpathohamasmi, etaṃgocaro etapathohamasmi etagocaro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), no ca tena tammayo’ti.

etapathohamasmi etagocaro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Evaṃvādiṃ kho, bhikkhave, satthāraṃ arahati sāvako upasaṅkamituṃ dhammassavanāya. Tassa satthā dhammaṃ deseti uttaruttariṃ paṇītapaṇītaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ. Yathā yathā kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṃ deseti uttaruttariṃ paṇītapaṇītaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ tathā tathā so tasmiṃ dhamme abhiññāya idhekaccaṃ dhammaṃ dhammesu niṭṭhaṃ gacchati, satthari pasīdati – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno saṅgho’ti. Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ pare evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘ke panāyasmato ākārā, ke anvayā, yenāyasmā evaṃ vadesi – sammāsambuddho bhagavā , svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno saṅgho’ti? Sammā byākaramāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ byākareyya – ‘idhāhaṃ, āvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃ dhammassavanāya. Tassa me bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti uttaruttariṃ paṇītapaṇītaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ. Yathā yathā me, āvuso , bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti uttaruttariṃ paṇītapaṇītaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ tathā tathāhaṃ tasmiṃ dhamme abhiññāya idhekaccaṃ dhammaṃ dhammesu niṭṭhamagamaṃ, satthari pasīdiṃ – sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā, dhammo, suppaṭipanno saṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
489. Monks, in that case, the *Tathāgata* should be asked further: ‘Are there defiled phenomena cognizable by the eye and ear for the *Tathāgata*, or not?’ If the *Tathāgata* were to answer, monks, he would answer thus: ‘There are no defiled phenomena cognizable by the eye and ear for the *Tathāgata*.’

‘Are there mixed phenomena cognizable by the eye and ear for the *Tathāgata*, or not?’ If the *Tathāgata* were to answer, monks, he would answer thus: ‘There are no mixed phenomena cognizable by the eye and ear for the *Tathāgata*.’

‘Are there pure phenomena cognizable by the eye and ear for the *Tathāgata*, or not?’ If the *Tathāgata* were to answer, monks, he would answer thus: ‘There are pure phenomena cognizable by the eye and ear for the *Tathāgata*; I am on this path, this is my domain, but I am not made of that.’

Monks, a disciple is worthy to approach a teacher who speaks thus, to hear the *Dhamma*. The Teacher teaches him the *Dhamma* with its higher and higher levels, with its more and more sublime levels, with its dark and bright counterparts (*kṛṣṇa-śukla-saprati-bhāgam*). As the Teacher teaches the *Dhamma* to a *bhikkhu* in this way, through direct knowledge (*abhijñāya*) of a certain teaching here in that *Dhamma*, the *bhikkhu* comes to a conclusion (*niṭṭhaṃ gacchati*) about the teachings. He places confidence (*prasīdati*) in the Teacher thus: ‘The Blessed One is fully enlightened (*sammāsambuddho bhagavā*), the *Dhamma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One (*svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo*), the *Saṅgha* is practising the good way (*suppaṭipanno saṅgho*)’.

“Now if others should ask that *bhikkhu* thus: ‘What are the venerable one’s reasons (*ākārā*), and what is his evidence (*anvayā*), whereby he says, “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the *Dhamma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, the *Saṅgha* is practising the good way”?’ If he is answering rightly, monks, a *bhikkhu* should answer thus: ‘Here, friends, I approached the Blessed One to hear the *Dhamma*. The Blessed One taught me the *Dhamma* with its higher and higher levels, with its more and more sublime levels, with its dark and bright counterparts. As the Blessed One taught the *Dhamma* to me in this way, through direct knowledge of a certain teaching here in that *Dhamma*, I came to a conclusion about the teachings. I placed confidence in the Teacher thus: “The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the *Dhamma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, the *Saṅgha* is practising the good way.”’
commentary_pali:
489.Tatra, bhikkhaveti tesu dvīsu vīmaṃsakesu. Yo, ‘‘ke panāyasmato ākārā’’ti pucchāyaṃ āgato gaṇṭhivīmaṃsako ca, yo ‘‘abhayūparato ayamāyasmā’’ti āgato mūlavīmaṃsako ca. Tesu mūlavīmaṃsakena tathāgatova uttari paṭipucchitabbo. So hi pubbe parasseva kathāya niṭṭhaṅgato. Paro ca nāma jānitvāpi katheyya ajānitvāpi. Evamassa kathā bhūtāpi hoti abhūtāpi, tasmā parasseva kathāya niṭṭhaṃ agantvā tato uttari tathāgatova paṭipucchitabboti attho.

Byākaramānoti ettha yasmā tathāgatassa micchābyākaraṇaṃ nāma natthi, tasmā sammā micchāti avatvā byākaramānotveva vuttaṃ. Etaṃ pathohamasmietaṃ gocaroti esa mayhaṃ patho esa gocaroti attho. ‘‘Etāpātho’’tipi pāṭho, tassattho mayhaṃ ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ parisuddhaṃ, svāhaṃ tassa parisuddhabhāvena vīmaṃsakassa bhikkhuno ñāṇamukhe etāpātho, evaṃ āpāthaṃ gacchāmīti vuttaṃ hoti. No ca tena tammayoti tenapi cāhaṃ parisuddhena sīlena na tammayo, na sataṇho, parisuddhasīlattāva nittaṇhohamasmīti dīpeti.

Byākaramāno Etaṃ pathohamasmi etaṃ gocaro No ca tena tammayo

Uttaruttariṃpaṇītapaṇītanti uttaruttariṃ ceva paṇītatarañca katvā deseti. Kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāganti kaṇhaṃ ceva sukkañca, tañca kho sappaṭibhāgaṃ savipakkhaṃ katvā, kaṇhaṃ paṭibāhitvā sukkanti sukkaṃ paṭibāhitvā kaṇhanti evaṃ sappaṭibhāgaṃ katvā kaṇhasukkaṃ deseti. Kaṇhaṃ desentopi saussāhaṃ savipākaṃ deseti, sukkaṃ desentopi saussāhaṃ savipākaṃ deseti. Abhiññāya idhekaccaṃ dhammaṃ dhammesu niṭṭhaṃ gacchatīti tasmiṃ desite dhamme ekaccaṃ paṭivedhadhammaṃ abhiññāya tena paṭivedhadhammena desanādhamme niṭṭhaṃ gacchati. Satthari pasīdatīti evaṃ dhamme niṭṭhaṃ gantvā bhiyyosomattāya sammāsambuddho so bhagavāti satthari pasīdati. Tena pana bhagavatā yo dhammo akkhāto, sopi svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo niyyānikattā. Yvāssa taṃ dhammaṃ paṭipanno saṅgho, sopi suppaṭipanno vaṅkādidosarahitaṃ paṭipadaṃ paṭipannattāti evaṃ dhamme saṅghepi pasīdati. Tañceti taṃ evaṃ pasannaṃ tattha tattha tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ vaṇṇaṃ kathentaṃ bhikkhuṃ.

Uttaruttariṃ paṇītapaṇīta Kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga Abhiññāya idhekaccaṃ dhammaṃ dhammesu niṭṭhaṃ gacchatī Satthari pasīdatī Tañce
commentary_english:
489. Bhikkhus, "tatra," [means] among those two investigators.

One, "What are the venerable one’s characteristics?" having come with this question, is a knot-investigator (gaṇṭhivīmaṃsako); and one, "This venerable one is without fear and cessation," having come, is a root-investigator (mūlavīmaṃsako).

Among them, the *tathāgata* should be questioned further by the root-investigator.

For he previously reached a conclusion through the words of another.

And another might speak having known [something], or without having known [it].

Thus, his speech might be true or untrue, therefore, without having reached a conclusion through the words of another, the *tathāgata* should be questioned further, this is the meaning.

*Byākaramāno* means: Here, because there is no false explanation (micchābyākaraṇaṃ) of a *tathāgata*, therefore, without saying "wrongly," it is said "explaining" (byākaramāno).

*Etaṃ pathohamasmi* means: This is my path, this is my range, this is the meaning.

"Etāpātho" is also a reading. Its meaning is: my livelihood-eighth-precept morality (ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ) is purified; therefore, I am in the face of the wisdom of the investigating bhikkhu through the purified state of that, thus I go to that path, this is said.

*No ca tena tammayo* means: I am not made of that even by that purified morality, I am without craving, because of purified morality, I am without craving, he illuminates.

*Byākaramāno*

*Etaṃ pathohamasmi*

*Etaṃ gocaro no ca tena tammayo*

*Uttaruttariṃ paṇītapaṇīta* means: having made it more and more excellent (paṇītataraṃ), he teaches.

*Kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga* means: both dark (kaṇhaṃ) and bright (sukkaṃ), and having made that with a counterpart (sappaṭibhāgaṃ) and with an opponent (savipakkhaṃ), having rejected the dark, [he teaches] "bright," and having rejected the bright, [he teaches] "dark," thus, having made [them] with a counterpart, he teaches dark and bright.

Even teaching the dark, he teaches with enthusiasm (saussāhaṃ) and with result (savipākaṃ); even teaching the bright, he teaches with enthusiasm and with result.

*Abhiññāya idhekaccaṃ dhammaṃ dhammesu niṭṭhaṃ gacchatī* means: in that dharma that was taught, one, having directly known (abhiññāya) the dharma of penetration (paṭivedhadhammaṃ), by that dharma of penetration, he goes to completion (niṭṭhaṃ gacchati) in the dharma of teaching (desanādhamme).

*Satthari pasīdatī* means: having gone to completion (niṭṭhaṃ gantvā) in the dharma in this way, he is pleased (pasīdati) with the teacher (satthari), "the *sammāsambuddha* is the *bhagavat*," to a greater extent (bhiyyosomattāya).

Moreover, the dharma that was declared by that *bhagavat*, that dharma is well-declared (svākkhāto) by the *bhagavat* because it leads to liberation (niyyānikattā).

The *saṅgha* that has undertaken that dharma, that is also well-practiced (suppaṭipanno), because it has undertaken the practice free from crookedness and faults (vaṅkādidosarahitaṃ paṭipadaṃ paṭipannattā), thus he is pleased with the dharma and the *saṅgha* as well.

*Tañce* means: that bhikkhu who is thus pleased, telling the qualities of the three jewels there and there.

*Uttaruttariṃ paṇītapaṇīta kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga abhiññāya idhekaccaṃ dhammaṃ dhammesu niṭṭhaṃ gacchatī satthari pasīdatī tañce*

mula_pali:
490. ‘‘Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, imehi ākārehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi tathāgate saddhā niviṭṭhā hoti mūlajātā patiṭṭhitā, ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ākāravatī saddhā dassanamūlikā, daḷhā; asaṃhāriyā samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tathāgate dhammasamannesanā hoti. Evañca pana tathāgato dhammatāsusamanniṭṭho hotī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Vīmaṃsakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Monks, when anyone’s faith has been planted, rooted (mūlajātā), and established in the Thus Gone One (Tathāgata) through these reasons, terms (padehi), and phrases (byañjanehi), his faith (saddhā) is said to be supported by reasons (ākāravatī saddhā), rooted in vision (dassanamūlikā), firm (daḷhā); it is invincible (asaṃhāriyā) by any recluse (samaṇena) or Brahmin (brāhmaṇena) or god (devena) or Māra or Brahmā or by anyone in the world (lokasmiṃ). That is how, monks, there is an investigation of the Thus Gone One (Tathāgata) in accordance with the Dhamma (dhammasamannesanā hoti), and that is how the Thus Gone One (Tathāgata) is well investigated in accordance with the Dhamma (dhammatāsusamanniṭṭho hotī’’ti).”

This was said by the Blessed One (bhagavā). Elated (attamanā), those monks (bhikkhū) delighted in the Blessed One’s (bhagavato) statement (bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti).

The seventh, the Vīmaṃsaka Sutta, is finished.
commentary_pali:
490.Imehi ākārehīti imehi satthuvīmaṃsanakāraṇehi. Imehi padehīti imehi akkharasampiṇḍanapadehi. Imehi byañjanehīti imehi idha vuttehi akkharehi. Saddhā niviṭṭhāti okappanā patiṭṭhitā. Mūlajātāti sotāpattimaggavasena sañjātamūlā. Sotāpattimaggo hi saddhāya mūlaṃ nāma. Ākāravatīti kāraṇaṃ pariyesitvā gahitattā sakāraṇā. Dassanamūlikāti sotāpattimaggamūlikā. So hi dassananti vuccati. Daḷhāti thirā. Asaṃhāriyāti harituṃ na sakkā. Samaṇena vāti samitapāpasamaṇena vā. Brāhmaṇena vāti bāhitapāpabrāhmaṇena vā. Devena vāti upapattidevena vā. Mārena vāti vasavattimārena vā, sotāpannassa hi vasavattimārenāpi saddhā asaṃhāriyā hoti sūrambaṭṭhassa viya.

So kira satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā sotāpanno hutvā gehaṃ āgato. Atha māro dvattiṃsavaralakkhaṇappaṭimaṇḍitaṃ buddharūpaṃ māpetvā tassa gharadvāre ṭhatvā – ‘‘satthā āgato’’ti sāsanaṃ pahiṇi. Sūro cintesi, ‘‘ahaṃ idāneva satthu santikā dhammaṃ sutvā āgato, kiṃ nu kho bhavissatī’’ti upasaṅkamitvā satthusaññāya vanditvā aṭṭhāsi. Māro āha – ‘‘yaṃ te mayā, sūrambaṭṭha, rūpaṃ aniccaṃ…pe… viññāṇaṃ aniccanti kathitaṃ, taṃ anupadhāretvāva sahasā mayā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā tvaṃ rūpaṃ niccaṃ…pe… viññāṇaṃ niccanti gaṇhāhī’’ti. Sūro cintesi – ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ, yaṃ buddhā anupadhāretvā apaccakkhaṃ katvā kiñci katheyyuṃ, addhā ayaṃ mayhaṃ vibādhanatthaṃ māro āgato’’ti. Tato naṃ tvaṃ māroti āha. So musāvādaṃ kātuṃ nāsakkhi, āma mārosmīti paṭijāni. Kasmā āgatosīti vutte tava saddhācālanatthanti āha. Kaṇha pāpima, tvaṃ tāva ekako tiṭṭha, tādisānaṃ mārānaṃ satampi sahassampi mama saddhaṃ cāletuṃ asamatthaṃ, maggena āgatā saddhā nāma silāpathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhitasineru viya acalā hoti, kiṃ tvaṃ etthāti accharaṃ pahari. So ṭhātuṃ asakkonto tatthevantaradhāyi. Brahmunā vāti brahmakāyikādīsu aññatarabrahmunā vā. Kenaci vā lokasminti ete samaṇādayo ṭhapetvā aññenapi kenaci vā lokasmiṃ harituṃ na sakkā. Dhammasamannesanāti sabhāvasamannesanā. Dhammatāsusamanniṭṭhoti dhammatāya susamanniṭṭho, sabhāveneva suṭṭhu samannesito hotīti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Brahmunā vā Kenaci vā lokasmi Dhammasamannesanā Dhammatāsusamanniṭṭho

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Vīmaṃsakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
490.
"Because of these characteristics ( *imehi ākārehī* )" means because of these reasons for investigating the Teacher.
"Because of these words ( *imehi padehī* )" means because of these words consisting of a collection of syllables.
"Because of these consonants ( *imehi byañjanehī* )" means because of these syllables stated here.
"Faith is fixed ( *saddhā niviṭṭhā* )" means conviction is established.
"Having a root ( *mūlajātā* )" means having a root that has arisen through the way of stream-entry ( *sotāpattimagga* ).
The way of stream-entry ( *sotāpattimagga* ) is called the root of faith ( *saddhā* ).
"Having characteristics ( *ākāravatī* )" means having a cause ( *kāraṇa* ) because of taking it after seeking a cause.
"Having the stream-entry way as its root ( *dassanamūlikā* )" means having the *sotāpattimagga* as its root.
That is called insight ( *dassana* ).
"Firm ( *daḷhā* )" means stable ( *thirā* ).
"Unshakeable ( *asaṃhāriyā* )" means it is not possible to take away ( *harituṃ na sakkā* ).
"By a *śramaṇa* ( *samaṇena vā* )" means by a *śramaṇa* whose evil has been calmed.
"By a *brāhmaṇa* ( *brāhmaṇena vā* )" means by a *brāhmaṇa* who has discarded evil.
"By a *deva* ( *devena vā* )" means by a *deva* who has arisen.
"By a *māra* ( *mārena vā* )" means by a *māra* who has power, or, for a stream-enterer ( *sotāpanna* ), even by a *māra* who has power, faith is unshakeable, like that of Sūrambaṭṭha.

Then he, having heard the Dharma teaching of the Teacher, having become a stream-enterer, came to his house.
Then Māra, having created a Buddha-image adorned with the thirty-two excellent marks, having stood at the door of his house, sent the message, "The Teacher has arrived."
Sūra thought, "I have just now heard the Dharma from the Teacher, what will happen?", having approached, having saluted with the perception of the Teacher, he stood aside.
Māra said, "That which was said by me to you, Sūrambaṭṭha, that form is impermanent...etc...consciousness is impermanent, that was said by me rashly, without considering it."
Therefore, you should grasp that form is permanent...etc...consciousness is permanent.
Sūra thought, "This is not a possibility, that Buddhas would say something without considering it, having made it non-manifest, truly this Māra has come to disturb me."
Then he said to him, "You are Māra."
He was not able to speak falsely, he acknowledged, "Yes, I am Māra."
When asked, "Why have you come?", he said, "To shake your faith."
"Kanhha, evil one, you just stand alone, even a hundred or a thousand of such Māras are unable to shake my faith, the faith that has come by the path is unmoving like Sineru established on the stone earth, what are you here?", he uttered a verse.
He, being unable to stand, disappeared right there.
"By a *brahmā* ( *brahmunā vā* )" means by some *brahmā* or other among those beginning with the *brahmakāyika*s.
"By someone in the world ( *kenaci vā lokasmi* )" means that these *śramaṇa*s and the rest having been set aside, by someone else in the world it is not possible to take it away.
"*Dhammasamannesanā*" means investigation of intrinsic nature.
"*Dhammatāsusamanniṭṭho*" means well-established in the nature of phenomena, meaning he is well investigated by intrinsic nature itself.
The rest is clear everywhere.

The *Papañcasūdanī* commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*
The exposition of the *Vīmaṃsakasutta* is finished.

mula_pali:
491. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena kosambiyaṃ bhikkhū bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti. Te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpenti na ca saññattiṃ upenti, na ca aññamaññaṃ nijjhāpenti, na ca nijjhattiṃ upenti. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idha, bhante, kosambiyaṃ bhikkhū bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti, te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpenti, na ca saññattiṃ upenti, na ca aññamaññaṃ nijjhāpenti, na ca nijjhattiṃ upentī’’ti.

Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena te bhikkhū āmantehi – ‘satthā vo āyasmante āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘satthā āyasmante āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘saccaṃ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharatha, te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpetha, na ca saññattiṃ upetha, na ca aññamaññaṃ nijjhāpetha, na ca nijjhattiṃ upethā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ tumhe samaye bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharatha, api nu tumhākaṃ tasmiṃ samaye mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ…pe… mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho cā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Iti kira, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ tumhe samaye bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharatha, neva tumhākaṃ tasmiṃ samaye mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, na mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ…pe… na mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca. Atha kiñcarahi tumhe, moghapurisā, kiṃ jānantā kiṃ passantā bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharatha, te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpetha, na ca saññattiṃ upetha, na ca aññamaññaṃ nijjhāpetha, na ca nijjhattiṃ upetha ? Tañhi tumhākaṃ, moghapurisā, bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kosambi in Ghosita’s Park.

Now on that occasion the monks at Kosambi had taken to quarrelling and brawling and were deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers.

They could neither convince each other nor be convinced by others; they could neither persuade each other nor be persuaded by others.

Then a certain monk went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: “Here, venerable sir, at Kosambi the monks have taken to quarrelling and brawling and are deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers; they can neither convince each other nor be convinced by others, nor can they persuade each other nor be persuaded by others.”

Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk: “Go, monk, tell those monks in my name that the Teacher summons the venerable ones.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” replied that monk to the Blessed One, and he went to those monks; on arrival, he told the monks: “The Teacher summons the venerable ones.”

“Very well, friend,” replied those monks to that monk, and they went to the Blessed One; on arrival, having paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to those monks: “Is it true, as is said, that you, monks, have taken to quarrelling and brawling and are deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers; that you can neither convince each other nor be convinced by others, that you can neither persuade each other nor be persuaded by others?” “Yes, venerable sir.”

“What do you think, monks, when you have taken to quarrelling and brawling and are deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers, do you on that occasion maintain loving-kindness through bodily action towards your companions in the holy life, both in public and in private; and loving-kindness through speech…and… loving-kindness through mental action towards your companions in the holy life, both in public and in private?” “No, venerable sir.”

“So, monks, when you have taken to quarrelling and brawling and are deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers, on that occasion you do not maintain loving-kindness through bodily action towards your companions in the holy life, both in public and in private; nor loving-kindness through speech…and… nor loving-kindness through mental action towards your companions in the holy life, both in public and in private.

Misguided men, what can you possibly know, what can you see, that you take to quarrelling and brawling and are deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers? That you can neither convince each other nor be convinced by others, that you can neither persuade each other nor be persuaded by others? This will lead to your harm and suffering for a long time.”
commentary_pali:
491.Evaṃme sutanti kosambiyasuttaṃ. Tattha kosambiyanti evaṃnāmake nagare. Tassa kira nagarassa ārāmapokkharaṇīādīsu tesu tesu ṭhānesu kosambarukkhāva ussannā ahesuṃ, tasmā kosambīti saṅkhaṃ agamāsi. Kusambassa nāma isino assamato avidūre māpitattātipi eke. Ghositārāmeti ghositaseṭṭhinā kārite ārāme.

Pubbe kira addilaraṭṭhaṃ nāma ahosi. Tato kotūhalako nāma daliddo chātakabhayena saputtadāro kedāraparicchinnaṃ subhikkhaṃ raṭṭhaṃ gacchanto puttaṃ vahituṃ asakkonto chaḍḍetvā agamāsi. Mātā nivattitvā taṃ gahetvā gatā. Te ekaṃ gopālakagāmakaṃ pavisiṃsu, gopālakānañca tadā pahatapāyaso paṭiyatto hoti, tato pāyasaṃ labhitvā bhuñjiṃsu. Atha so puriso pahūtapāyasaṃ bhuñjitvā jirāpetuṃ asakkonto rattibhāge kālaṃ katvā tattheva sunakhiyā kucchimhi paṭisandhiṃ gahetvā kukkuro jāto. So gopālakassa piyo ahosi manāpo, gopālako ca paccekabuddhaṃ upaṭṭhāsi. Paccekabuddhopi bhattakiccāvasāne kukkurassa ekaṃ piṇḍaṃ deti. So paccekabuddhe sinehaṃ uppādetvā gopālakena saddhiṃ paṇṇasālampi gacchati.

So gopālake asannihite bhattavelāya sayameva gantvā kālārocanatthaṃ paṇṇasāladvāre bhussati, antarāmaggepi caṇḍamige disvā bhussitvā palāpeti. So paccekabuddhe mudukena cittena kālaṃ katvā devaloke nibbatti. Tatrassa ghosakadevaputtotveva nāmaṃ ahosi. So devalokato cavitvā kosambiyaṃ ekasmiṃ kulaghare nibbatti. Taṃ aputtako seṭṭhi tassa mātāpitūnaṃ dhanaṃ datvā puttaṃ katvā aggahesi. Atha so attano putte jāte sattakkhattuṃ mārāpetuṃ upakkami. So puññavantatāya sattasupi ṭhānesu maraṇaṃ appatvā avasāne ekāya seṭṭhidhītāya veyyattiyena laddhajīviko aparabhāge pituaccayena seṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ patvā ghositaseṭṭhi nāma jāto. Aññepi kosambiyaṃ kukkuṭaseṭṭhi pāvārikaseṭṭhīti dve seṭṭhino santi. Imehi saddhiṃ tayo ahesuṃ.

ghositaseṭṭhi

Tena ca samayena tesaṃ sahāyakānaṃ seṭṭhīnaṃ kulūpakā pañcasatā isayo pabbatapāde vasiṃsu. Te kālena kālaṃ loṇambilasevanatthāya manussapathaṃ āgacchanti. Athekasmiṃ vāre gimhasamaye manussapathaṃ āgacchantā nirudakamahākantāraṃ atikkamitvā kantārapariyosāne mahantaṃ nigrodharukkhaṃ disvā cintesuṃ – ‘‘yādiso ayaṃ rukkho, addhā ettha mahesakkhāya devatāya bhavitabbaṃ, sādhu vatassa, sace no pānīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dadeyyā’’ti. Devatā isīnaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā imesaṃ saṅgahaṃ karissāmīti attano ānubhāvena viṭapantarato naṅgalasīsamattaṃ udakadhāraṃ pavattesi. Isigaṇo rajatakkhandhasadisaṃ udakavaṭṭiṃ disvā attano bhājanehi udakaṃ gahetvā paribhogaṃ katvā cintesi – ‘‘devatāya amhākaṃ paribhogaudakaṃ dinnaṃ, idaṃ pana agāmakaṃ mahāaraññaṃ, sādhu vatassa, sace no āhārampi dadeyyā’’ti. Devatā isīnaṃ upasaṃkappanavasena dibbāni yāgukhajjakādīni datvā santappesi. Isayo cintayiṃsu – ‘‘devatāya amhākaṃ paribhogaudakampi bhojanampi sabbaṃ dinnaṃ, sādhu vatassa, sace no attānaṃ dasseyyā’’ti.

Devatā tesaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā upaḍḍhakāyaṃ dassesi. Te āhaṃsu – ‘‘devate, mahatī te sampatti, kiṃ kammaṃ katvā imaṃ sampattiṃ adhigatāsī’’ti? Bhante, nātimahantaṃ parittakaṃ kammaṃ katvāti. Upaḍḍhauposathakammaṃ nissāya hi devatāya sā sampatti laddhā.

Anāthapiṇḍikassa kira gehe ayaṃ devaputto kammakāro ahosi. Seṭṭhissa hi gehe uposathadivasesu antamaso dāsakammakāre upādāya sabbo jano uposathiko hoti. Ekadivasaṃ ayaṃ kammakāro ekakova pāto uṭṭhāya kammantaṃ gato. Mahāseṭṭhi nivāpaṃ labhanamanusse sallakkhento etassevekassa araññaṃ gatabhāvaṃ ñatvā assa sāyamāsatthāya nivāpaṃ adāsi. Bhattakārikā dāsī ekasseva bhattaṃ pacitvā araññato āgatassa bhattaṃ vaḍḍhetvā adāsi, kammakāro āha – ‘‘aññesu divasesu imasmiṃ kāle gehaṃ ekasaddaṃ ahosi, ajja ativiya sannisinnaṃ, kiṃ nu kho eta’’nti ? Tassa sā ācikkhi – ‘‘ajja imasmiṃ gehe sabbe manussā uposathikā, mahāseṭṭhi tuyhevekassa nivāpaṃ adāsī’’ti. Evaṃ ammāti? Āma sāmīti. Imasmiṃ kāle uposathaṃ samādinnassa uposathakammaṃ hoti na hotīti mahāseṭṭhiṃ puccha ammāti? Tāya gantvā pucchito mahāseṭṭhi āha – ‘‘sakalauposathakammaṃ na hoti, upaḍḍhakammaṃ pana hoti, uposathiko hotū’’ti . Kammakāro bhattaṃ abhuñjitvā mukhaṃ vikkhāletvā uposathiko hutvā vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā nipajji. Tassa āhāraparikkhīṇakāyassa rattiṃ vāto kuppi. So paccūsasamaye kālaṃ katvā upaḍḍhauposathakammanissandena mahāvaṭṭaniaṭaviyaṃ nigrodharukkhe devaputto hutvā nibbatti. So taṃ pavattiṃ isīnaṃ ārocesi.

Isayo tumhehi mayaṃ buddho, dhammo, saṅghoti asutapubbaṃ sāvitā, uppanno nu kho loke buddhoti? Āma, bhante, uppannoti. Idāni kuhiṃ vasatīti? Sāvatthiṃ nissāya jetavane, bhanteti. Isayo tiṭṭhatha tāva tumhe mayaṃ satthāraṃ passissāmāti haṭṭhatuṭṭhā nikkhamitvā anupubbena kosambinagaraṃ sampāpuṇiṃsu. Mahāseṭṭhino, ‘‘isayo āgatā’’ti paccuggamanaṃ katvā, ‘‘sve amhākaṃ bhikkhaṃ gaṇhatha, bhante’’ti nimantetvā punadivase isigaṇassa mahādānaṃ adaṃsu. Isayo bhuñjitvāva gacchāmāti āpucchiṃsu. Tumhe, bhante, aññasmiṃ kāle ekampi māsaṃ dvepi tayopi cattāropi māse vasitvā gacchatha. Imasmiṃ pana vāre hiyyo āgantvā ajjeva gacchāmāti vadatha, kimidanti? Āma gahapatayo buddho loke uppanno, na kho pana sakkā jīvitantarāyo vidituṃ, tena mayaṃ turitā gacchāmāti. Tena hi, bhante, mayampi gacchāma, amhehi saddhiṃyeva gacchathāti. Tumhe agāriyā nāma mahājaṭā, tiṭṭhatha tumhe, mayaṃ puretaraṃ gamissāmāti nikkhamitvā ekasmiṃ ṭhāne dvepi divasāni avasitvā turitagamaneneva sāvatthiṃ patvā jetavanavihāre satthu santikameva agamaṃsu. Satthu madhuradhammakathaṃ sutvā sabbeva pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu.

Tepi tayo seṭṭhino pañcahi pañcahi sakaṭasatehi sappimadhuphāṇitādīni ceva paṭṭunnadukūlādīni ca ādāya kosambito nikkhamitvā anupubbena sāvatthiṃ patvā jetavanasāmante khandhāvāraṃ bandhitvā satthu santikaṃ gantvā vanditvā paṭisanthāraṃ katvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Satthā tiṇṇampi sahāyakānaṃ madhuradhammakathaṃ kathesi. Te balavasomanassajātā satthāraṃ nimantetvā punadivase mahādānaṃ adaṃsu. Puna nimantetvā punadivaseti evaṃ aḍḍhamāsaṃ dānaṃ datvā, ‘‘amhākaṃ janapadaṃ āgamanāya paṭiññaṃ dethā’’ti pādamūle nipajjiṃsu. Bhagavā, ‘‘suññāgāre kho gahapatayo tathāgatā abhiramantī’’ti āha. Ettāvatā paṭiññā dinnā nāma hotīti gahapatayo sallakkhetvā dinnā no bhagavatā paṭiññāti dasabalaṃ vanditvā nikkhamitvā antarāmagge yojane yojane ṭhāne vihāraṃ kāretvā anupubbena kosambiṃ patvā, ‘‘loke buddho uppanno’’ti kathayiṃsu. Tayopi janā attano attano ārāme mahantaṃ dhanapariccāgaṃ katvā bhagavato vasanatthāya vihāre kārāpayiṃsu. Tattha kukkuṭaseṭṭhinā kārito kukkuṭārāmo nāma ahosi. Pāvārikaseṭṭhinā ambavane kārito pāvārikambavano nāma ahosi. Ghositena kārito ghositārāmo nāma ahosi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘ghositaseṭṭhinā kārite ārāme’’ti.

kukkuṭārāmo pāvārikambavano ghositārāmo

Bhaṇḍanajātātiādīsu kalahassa pubbabhāgo bhaṇḍanaṃ nāma, taṃ jātaṃ etesanti bhaṇḍanajātā. Hatthaparāmāsādivasena matthakaṃ patto kalaho jāto etesanti kalahajātā. Viruddhabhūtaṃ vādanti vivādaṃ, taṃ āpannāti vivādāpannā. Mukhasattīhīti vācāsattīhi. Vitudantāti vijjhantā. Te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpenti na ca saññattiṃ upentīti te atthañca kāraṇañca dassetvā neva aññamaññaṃ jānāpenti. Sacepi saññāpetuṃ ārabhanti, tathāpi saññattiṃ na upenti, jānituṃ na icchantīti attho. Nijjhattiyāpi eseva nayo. Ettha ca nijjhattīti saññattivevacanamevetaṃ. Kasmā panete bhaṇḍanajātā ahesunti? Appamattakena kāraṇena.

Bhaṇḍanajātā bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā. Mukhasattīhī Vitudantā Te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpenti na ca saññattiṃ upentī nijjhattī

Dve kira bhikkhū ekasmiṃ āvāse vasanti vinayadharo ca suttantiko ca. Tesu suttantiko bhikkhu ekadivasaṃ vaccakuṭiṃ paviṭṭho ācamanaudakāvasesaṃ bhājane ṭhapetvāva nikkhami. Vinayadharo pacchā paviṭṭho taṃ udakaṃ disvā nikkhamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchi, āvuso, tayā idaṃ udakaṃ ṭhapitanti? Āma, āvusoti. Tvamettha āpattibhāvaṃ na jānāsīti? Āma na jānāmīti. Hoti, āvuso, ettha āpattīti. Sace hoti desessāmīti. Sace pana te, āvuso, asañcicca asatiyā kataṃ, natthi te āpattīti. So tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi ahosi.

Vinayadharo attano nissitakānaṃ, ‘‘ayaṃ suttantiko āpattiṃ āpajjamānopi na jānātī’’ti ārocesi. Te tassa nissitake disvā – ‘‘tumhākaṃ upajjhāyo āpattiṃ āpajjitvāpi āpattibhāvaṃ na jānātī’’ti āhaṃsu. Te gantvā attano upajjhāyassa ārocesuṃ. So evamāha – ‘‘ayaṃ vinayadharo pubbe ‘anāpattī’ti vatvā idāni ‘āpattī’ti vadati, musāvādī eso’’ti. Te gantvā, ‘‘tumhākaṃ upajjhāyo musāvādī’’ti evaṃ aññamaññaṃ kalahaṃ vaḍḍhayiṃsu, taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Bhagavantaṃ etadavocāti etaṃ, ‘‘idha, bhante, kosambiyaṃ bhikkhū bhaṇḍanajātā’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tañca kho neva piyakamyatāya na bhedādhippāyena, atha kho atthakāmatāya hitakāmatāya. Sāmaggikārako kiresa bhikkhu, tasmāssa etadahosi – ‘‘yathā ime bhikkhū vivādaṃ āraddhā, na sakkā mayā, nāpi aññena bhikkhunā samaggā kātuṃ, appeva nāma sadevake loke appaṭipuggalo bhagavā sayaṃ vā gantvā, attano vā santikaṃ pakkosāpetvā etesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ khantimettāpaṭisaṃyuttaṃ sāraṇīyadhammadesanaṃ kathetvā sāmaggiṃ kareyyā’’ti atthakāmatāya hitakāmatāya gantvā avoca.

Bhagavantaṃ etadavocā
commentary_english:
491. Thus have I heard: the Kosambiya Sūtra.

There, "Kosambī" refers to a city of that name.

It is said that in that city, in various places such as parks and ponds, Kosamba trees grew densely. Therefore, it came to be known as Kosambī.

Some say [it was named] after the hermitage of a sage named Kusamba, not far from [the city].

Ghoṣitārāma refers to a park caused to be made by Ghoṣita the merchant.

Formerly, it was known as Addilarattha.

Then, a poor man named Kotūhalaka, fearing starvation, was going to a prosperous country with his wife and child. Unable to carry his son, he abandoned him and went away.

The mother returned, took the child, and left.

They entered a village of cowherds. At that time, milk-rice mixed with pounded grain had been prepared for the cowherds. Having obtained the milk-rice, they ate it.

Then that man, having eaten a large amount of milk-rice, was unable to digest it. At night, he died and was reborn as a dog in the womb of a bitch in that very place.

He was dear and pleasing to the cowherd, and the cowherd attended upon a solitary Buddha.

The solitary Buddha also gave the dog a morsel of food after the meal was finished.

Having developed affection for the solitary Buddha, he went with the cowherd to the leaf hut as well.

When the cowherd was away, at mealtime, he himself would go and bark at the door of the leaf hut to announce the time. Even on the road in between, having seen a fierce animal, he would bark and chase it away.

Having passed away from the solitary Buddha with a tender mind, he was reborn in the world of the gods.

There, his name was Ghosakadevaputta.

Having passed away from the world of the gods, he was reborn in a respectable family in Kosambī.

A childless merchant, having given wealth to his parents, adopted him as his son.

Then, when his own sons were born, he attempted to kill him seven times.

Due to his merit, not meeting death in even seven places, at the end, having obtained a livelihood through the shrewdness of a merchant’s daughter, and having obtained the position of merchant upon the death of his father, he became known as Ghoṣita the merchant.

Moreover, in Kosambī, there were two other merchants: Kukkuṭa the merchant and Pāvārika the merchant.

With these, there were three.

Ghoṣita the merchant

And at that time, five hundred ascetics who were family priests of those merchants lived at the foot of a mountain.

From time to time, they would come to the path of humans for the sake of obtaining salt and sour gruel.

Then, on one occasion, in the summer season, while coming to the path of humans, having crossed a great wilderness without water, and having seen a large banyan tree at the end of the wilderness, they thought, "Since this tree is like this, surely a deity of great power must live here. It would be good if he would give us drinking water or food."

The deity, having known the intention of the ascetics, [thought,] "I will do a favor for these," and by his own power, he caused a stream of water the size of a ploughshare to flow from within a branch.

The group of ascetics, having seen the stream of water resembling a silver trunk, having taken the water with their own vessels, and having used it, they thought, "The deity has given us water for use. However, this is a great forest without villages. It would be good if he would give us food as well."

The deity, according to the thought of the ascetics, gave divine rice gruel, cakes, and the like, and satisfied them.

The ascetics thought, "The deity has given us all things—water for use, and food. It would be good if he would show us himself."

The deity, having known their intention, showed half of his body.
They said, "O goddess, great is your prosperity. What *karma* did you do to attain this prosperity?" "Venerable sir, I did not do a very great or trifling *karma*."

That prosperity was obtained by the goddess on account of undertaking the half-observance of the *uposatha*.

It seems that this *devaputta* was a worker in Anāthapiṇḍika's house.
