Indeed, in the treasurer's house, on the *uposatha* days, all the people, even including the slave workers, observe the *uposatha*.

One day this worker, alone, early in the morning, went to work.

The great treasurer, considering the men who deserved an oblation, knowing that he alone had gone to the forest, gave him an oblation for his evening meal.

A serving-maid slave, having cooked food for him alone and having served the food to him who had come from the forest, the worker said, "On other days, at this time the house is noisy; today it is very quiet. What is this?"

She told him, "Today all the people in this house are observing the *uposatha*. The great treasurer gave an oblation to you alone."

"Is that so, mother?" "Yes, master."

"In this time, for one who has undertaken the *uposatha*, is there *uposatha-karma* or not?" he asked the great treasurer, "Mother?" Having gone and asked, the great treasurer said, "There is no complete *uposatha-karma*, but there is half-*karma*. Let him be an *uposathika*."

The worker, not having eaten food, having washed his face, having become an *uposathika*, went to his dwelling place and lay down.

For him, whose body was weakened by lack of food, the wind was disturbed in the night.

He, at dawn, having done his time, by the power of the half-*uposatha-karma*, was reborn as a *devaputta* in a *nigrodha* tree in the great Vaṭṭani forest.

He announced that event to the seers.

The seers, having never previously heard it said by you, "The Buddha, the *dharma*, the *sangha*", asked, "Has a Buddha arisen in the world?" "Yes, venerable sir, he has arisen."

"Where does he live now?" "Relying on Śrāvastī, in Jētavana, venerable sir."

The seers, delighted and pleased, having gone out, "Wait there for us, you. We will see the teacher," gradually arrived at the city of Kosambi.

The great treasurers, having gone to meet them, "The seers have come," having invited them, "Tomorrow, accept our alms, venerable sirs," on the next day gave a great gift to the group of seers.

The seers asked, "Having eaten, may we go?"

"Venerable sirs, at another time you stay for one month, two, three, or four months and then go.

But in this turn, having come yesterday, you say, 'We will go today.' What is this?" "Yes, householders, a Buddha has arisen in the world. It is not possible to know the danger to life; therefore we are going quickly."

"Then, venerable sirs, we too will go. Go together with us."

"You are householders named great ascetics, stay here you, we will go ahead," having gone out, having stayed for two days in one place, by the same quick journey, having arrived at Śrāvastī, they went to the presence of the teacher in the Jētavana monastery.

Having heard the teacher's sweet *dharma*-talk, all of them, having gone forth, attained *arhatship*.

Those three treasurers too, with five hundred carts each, having taken ghee, honey, molasses, etc., and linen cloth and fine cloth, etc., having gone out from Kosambi, gradually having arrived at Śrāvastī, having made a camp near Jētavana, having gone to the presence of the teacher, having bowed, having exchanged polite greetings, sat down on one side.

The teacher told the sweet *dharma*-talk to the three friends.

They, having become strong and joyful, having invited the teacher, on the next day gave a great gift.

Having invited [him] again, and again on the next day, in this way having given a gift for half a month, "Give a promise for coming to our country," they lay down at his feet.

The Blessed One said, "In empty dwellings, householders, *tathāgatas* delight."

"To this extent, a promise has been given," the householders, considering, "Has a promise been given to us by the Blessed One?" having bowed to the Ten-Powered One, having gone out, having made a monastery in a place at each *yojana* along the way, gradually having arrived at Kosambi, they said, "A Buddha has arisen in the world."

Those three people too, in their own *arama*s, having made a great outlay of wealth, had monasteries built for the Blessed One's dwelling.

There, the *Kukkuṭaseṭṭhi* had the *Kukkuṭārāma* built.
Pāvārika-seṭṭhi had the Pāvārikambavana built in the mango grove, so it was named.
Ghoṣita had the Ghoṣitārāma built, so it was named.
With that in mind, it was said: "In the ārāma built by Ghoṣita-seṭṭhi."

Kukkuṭārāma, Pāvārikambavana, Ghoṣitārāma.
*Bhaṇḍanajātā* means, among others, the first part of strife (kalahassa) is called mischief (bhaṇḍana), thus they are born of that.
*Kalahajātā* means, due to touching etc., the peak of strife (kalaho) is reached, thus they are born of strife.
*Vivādāpannā* means, they speak contradictory things, [and] they have gotten into dispute (vivāda).
*Mukhasattīhi* means with verbal attacks.
*Vitudantā* means piercing.
*Te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpenti na ca saññattiṃ upentī* means, showing the meaning and the cause, they do not make each other know.
Even if they start to make [it] known, still they do not go to an agreement, they do not want to know, is the meaning.
The same method applies in the case of *nijjhattī* too.
And here, *nijjhattī* means just a synonym of agreement (saññatti).
Why were these born of mischief? Because of a small cause.

Born of mischief, born of mischief, born of strife, involved in dispute.
With verbal attacks, piercing, *te na ceva aññamaññaṃ saññāpenti na ca saññattiṃ upentī*, agreement.

Two monks live in one monastery (āvāsa): one who adheres to the monastic discipline (vinayadhara), and one who is an expert in the discourses (suttantika).
Among them, the expert in the discourses (suttantika) monk, one day, having entered the toilet (vaccakuṭi), after having put the remainder of the rinsing water (ācamanaudakāvasesa) in a vessel, he left.
The monastic discipline adherent (vinayadhara) then entered, and having seen that water, having left, he asked that monk: "Friend, was this water put here by you?" "Yes, friend."
"You do not know the state of offense (āpattibhāva) here?" "Yes, I do not know."
"Friend, there is an offense here!"
"If there is, I will confess it!"
"But if it was done unintentionally and through lack of mindfulness, friend, there is no offense for you."
He had the view that there was no offense (anāpattidiṭṭhi) in that offense (āpatti).

The monastic discipline adherent (vinayadhara), told his students (nissitaka): "This expert in the discourses (suttantika), even when incurring an offense (āpatti), does not know [it]."
Those students (nissitaka) of his, having seen [this], said: "Your preceptor (upajjhāyo), even after incurring an offense (āpatti), does not know the state of offense (āpattibhāva)."
They went and told their preceptor (upajjhāyassa).
He said thus: "This monastic discipline adherent (vinayadhara), formerly having said 'there is no offense', now says 'there is an offense,' he is a liar!"
They went, "Your preceptor (upajjhāyo) is a liar!" Thus, they increased the quarrel (kalaha) with each other, with that in mind, this was said.

*Bhagavantaṃ etadavocā* means, he told this statement (vacana): "Here, venerable sir (bhante), in Kosambi, the monks are born of mischief (bhaṇḍanajātā)" etc.
And that, indeed, [was] not for the sake of pleasing (piyakamyatāya), nor with the intention of division (bhedādhippāyena), but rather for the sake of benefit (atthakāmatāya), for the sake of welfare (hitakāmatāya).
That monk was a maker of harmony (sāmaggikārako), so this occurred to him: "Just as these monks have started a dispute (vivādaṃ), it is not possible for me, nor for another monk, to make [them] harmonious (samaggā kātuṃ), perhaps the Blessed One (bhagavā), unrivaled (appaṭipuggalo) in the world with the gods (sadevake loke), having gone himself, or having had [them] summoned to his presence, having spoken a sermon on the Teaching that is connected with forbearance (khanti), loving-kindness (mettā), and friendliness (sāraṇīyadhammadesanaṃ), would create harmony (sāmaggiṃ kareyyā)", for the sake of benefit (atthakāmatāya), for the sake of welfare (hitakāmatāya) he went and spoke.

*Bhagavantaṃ etadavocā*

mula_pali:
492. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sāraṇīyā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattanti. Katame cha? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekibhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi, tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī hoti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṃvattanikāni tathārūpesu sīlesu sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāyaṃ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhisāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Ime kho, bhikkhave, cha sāraṇīyā dhammā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattanti. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, channaṃ sāraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ etaṃ aggaṃ etaṃ saṅgāhikaṃ saṅgāhakaṃ (?) etaṃ saṅghāṭanikaṃ – yadidaṃ yāyaṃ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa etaṃ aggaṃ etaṃ saṅgāhikaṃ etaṃ saṅghāṭanikaṃ yadidaṃ kūṭaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave , imesaṃ channaṃ sāraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ etaṃ aggaṃ etaṃ saṅgāhikaṃ etaṃ saṅghāṭanikaṃ yadidaṃ yāyaṃ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya.

saṅgāhakaṃ (?)
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: “*Bhikkhus*, there are these six qualities which encourage being mindful, create love and respect, and conduce to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

What are the six? Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* maintains bodily acts of loving-kindness (*mettā kāyakamma*) both in public and in private towards his companions in the holy life (*sabrahmacārī*). This quality encourages being mindful, creates love and respect, and conduces to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* maintains verbal acts of loving-kindness both in public and in private towards his companions in the holy life. This quality encourages being mindful, creates love and respect, and conduces to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* maintains mental acts of loving-kindness both in public and in private towards his companions in the holy life. This quality encourages being mindful, creates love and respect, and conduces to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, whatever righteous gains (*lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā*) the *bhikkhu* may obtain in a righteous way—even if only the alms in his bowl—he does not consume them alone. He consumes them after sharing them in common with his virtuous companions in the holy life (*sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī*). This quality encourages being mindful, creates love and respect, and conduces to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, with reference to the virtues (*sīlāni*) that are unbroken, untorn, unspotted, unsplattered, liberating, praised by the observant, ungrasped at, leading to concentration—the *bhikkhu* dwells with his virtue in tune with that of his companions in the holy life, to their faces & behind their backs. This quality encourages being mindful, creates love and respect, and conduces to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, with reference to the view (*dṭṭhi*) that is noble (*ariyā*), leading outward (*niyyānikā*), that leads those who act in accordance with it to the right ending of suffering (*dukkhakkhayāya*)—the *bhikkhu* dwells with his view in tune with that of his companions in the holy life, to their faces & behind their backs. This quality encourages being mindful, creates love and respect, and conduces to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

“These are the six qualities which encourage being mindful, create love and respect, and conduce to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity. Of these six qualities which encourage being mindful, the highest, the most comprehensive, the most conclusive is this view that is noble and emancipating, and leads the one who practises in accordance with it to the complete destruction of suffering. Just as the highest, the most comprehensive, the most conclusive part of a pinnacled building is the pinnacle itself, so too, of these six qualities which encourage being mindful, the highest…is this view that is noble and emancipating…
commentary_pali:
492.Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sāraṇīyāti heṭṭhā kalahabhaṇḍanavasena desanā āraddhā. Imasmiṃ ṭhāne cha sāraṇīyā dhammā āgatāti evamidaṃ kosambiyasuttaṃ yathānusandhināva gataṃ hoti. Tattha sāraṇīyāti saritabbayuttā addhāne atikkantepi na pamussitabbā. Yo te dhamme pūreti, taṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ piyaṃ karontīti piyakaraṇā. Garuṃ karontīti garukaraṇā. Saṅgahāyāti saṅgahaṇatthāya. Avivādāyāti avivādanatthāya. Sāmaggiyāti samaggabhāvatthāya . Ekībhāvāyāti ekībhāvatthāya ninnānākaraṇāya. Saṃvattantīti bhavanti. Mettaṃ kāyakammanti mettacittena kattabbaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Vacīkammamanokammesupi eseva nayo. Imāni bhikkhūnaṃ vasena āgatāni, gihīsupi labbhantiyeva. Bhikkhūnañhi mettacittena ābhisamācārikadhammapūraṇaṃ mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Gihīnaṃ cetiyavandanatthāya bodhivandanatthāya saṅghanimantanatthāya gamanaṃ gāmaṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭhe bhikkhū disvā paccuggamanaṃ pattapaṭiggahaṇaṃ āsanapaññāpanaṃ anugamananti evamādikaṃ mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma.

Bhikkhūnaṃ mettacittena ācārapaññattisikkhāpadaṃ, kammaṭṭhānakathanaṃ dhammadesanā tepiṭakampi buddhavacanaṃ mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma. Gihīnañca, ‘‘cetiyavandanatthāya gacchāma, bodhivandanatthāya gacchāma, dhammassavanaṃ karissāma, padīpamālāpupphapūjaṃ karissāma, tīṇi sucaritāni samādāya vattissāma, salākabhattādīni dassāma, vassāvāsikaṃ dassāma, ajja saṅghassa cattāro paccaye dassāma, saṅghaṃ nimantetvā khādanīyādīni saṃvidahatha, āsanāni paññāpetha, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhapetha, saṅghaṃ paccuggantvā ānetha, paññattāsane nisīdāpetvā chandajātā ussāhajātā veyyāvaccaṃ karothā’’tiādikathanakāle mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma.

mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ

Bhikkhūnaṃ pātova uṭṭhāya sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ cetiyaṅgaṇavattādīni ca katvā vivittāsane nisīditvā, ‘‘imasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū sukhī hontu, averā abyāpajjhā’’ti cintanaṃ mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma. Gihīnaṃ ‘‘ayyā sukhī hontu, averā abyāpajjhā’’ti cintanaṃ mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma.

mettaṃ manokammaṃ

Āvi ceva raho cāti sammukhā ca parammukhā ca. Tattha navakānaṃ cīvarakammādīsu sahāyabhāvūpagamanaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Therānaṃ pana pādadhovanavandanabījanadānādibhedampi sabbaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Ubhayehipi dunnikkhittānaṃ dārubhaṇḍādīnaṃ tesu avamaññaṃ akatvā attanā dunnikkhittānaṃ viya paṭisāmanaṃ parammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Devatthero tissattheroti evaṃ paggayha vacanaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma. Vihāre asantaṃ pana paripucchantassa, kuhiṃ amhākaṃ devatthero, amhākaṃ tissatthero kadā nu kho āgamissatīti evaṃ mamāyanavacanaṃ parammukhā mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma. Mettāsinehasiniddhāni pana nayanāni ummīletvā suppasannena mukhena olokanaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma. Devatthero, tissatthero arogo hotu appābādhoti samannāharaṇaṃ parammukhā mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma.

Āvi ceva raho cā

Lābhāti cīvarādayo laddhapaccayā. Dhammikāti kuhanādibhedaṃ micchājīvaṃ vajjetvā dhammena samena bhikkhācariyavattena uppannā. Antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampīti pacchimakoṭiyā patte pariyāpannaṃ pattassa antogataṃ dvattikaṭacchubhikkhāmattampi. Appaṭivibhattabhogīti ettha dve paṭivibhattāni nāma āmisapaṭivibhattaṃ puggalapaṭivibhattañca. Tattha, ‘‘ettakaṃ dassāmi, ettakaṃ na dassāmī’’ti evaṃ cittena vibhajanaṃ āmisapaṭivibhattaṃ nāma. ‘‘Asukassa dassāmi, asukassa na dassāmī’’ti evaṃ cittena vibhajanaṃ pana puggalapaṭivibhattaṃ nāma. Tadubhayampi akatvā yo appaṭivibhattaṃ bhuñjati, ayaṃ appaṭivibhattabhogī nāma.

Lābhā Dhammikā Antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampī Appaṭivibhattabhogī appaṭivibhattabhogī

Sīlavantehisabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogīti ettha sādhāraṇabhogino idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ, yaṃ yaṃ paṇītaṃ labbhati, taṃ taṃ neva lābhena lābhaṃ jigīsanāmukhena gihīnaṃ deti, na attanā paribhuñjati; paṭiggaṇhantova saṅghena sādhāraṇaṃ hotūti gahetvā gaṇḍiṃ paharitvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ saṅghasantakaṃ viya passati. Idaṃ pana sāraṇīyadhammaṃ ko pūreti, ko na pūretīti? Dussīlo tāva na pūreti. Na hi tassa santakaṃ sīlavantā gaṇhanti. Parisuddhasīlo pana vattaṃ akhaṇḍento pūreti.

Sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī

Tatridaṃ vattaṃ – yo hi odissakaṃ katvā mātu vā pitu vā ācariyupajjhāyādīnaṃ vā deti, so dātabbaṃ deti, sāraṇīyadhammo panassa na hoti, palibodhajagganaṃ nāma hoti. Sāraṇīyadhammo hi muttapalibodhasseva vaṭṭati, tena pana odissakaṃ dentena gilānagilānupaṭṭhākaāgantukagamikānañceva navapabbajitassa ca saṅghāṭipattaggahaṇaṃ ajānantassa dātabbaṃ. Etesaṃ datvā avasesaṃ therāsanato paṭṭhāya thokaṃ thokaṃ adatvā yo yattakaṃ gaṇhāti, tassa tattakaṃ dātabbaṃ. Avasiṭṭhe asati puna piṇḍāya caritvā therāsanato paṭṭhāya yaṃ yaṃ paṇītaṃ, taṃ taṃ datvā sesaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ, ‘‘sīlavantehī’’ti vacanato dussīlassa adātumpi vaṭṭati.

Ayaṃ pana sāraṇīyadhammo susikkhitāya parisāya supūro hoti, no asikkhitāya parisāya. Susikkhitāya hi parisāya yo aññato labhati, so na gaṇhāti, aññato alabhantopi pamāṇayuttameva gaṇhāti, na atirekaṃ. Ayañca pana sāraṇīyadhammo evaṃ punappunaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā laddhaṃ laddhaṃ dentassāpi dvādasahi vassehi pūrati, na tato oraṃ. Sace hi dvādasamepi vasse sāraṇīyadhammapūrako piṇḍapātapūraṃ pattaṃ āsanasālāyaṃ ṭhapetvā nahāyituṃ gacchati, saṅghatthero ca kasseso pattoti? Sāraṇīyadhammapūrakassāti vutte – ‘‘āharatha na’’nti sabbaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ vicāretvā bhuñjitvā ca rittapattaṃ ṭhapeti. Atha so bhikkhu rittapattaṃ disvā, ‘‘mayhaṃ asesetvāva paribhuñjiṃsū’’ti domanassaṃ uppādeti, sāraṇīyadhammo bhijjati, puna dvādasa vassāni pūretabbo hoti, titthiyaparivāsasadiso hesa. Sakiṃ khaṇḍe jāte puna pūretabbova. Yo pana, ‘‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me pattagataṃ anāpucchāva sabrahmacārī paribhuñjantī’’ti somanassaṃ janeti, tassa puṇṇo nāma hoti.

Evaṃ pūritasāraṇīyadhammassa pana neva issā, na macchariyaṃ hoti, so manussānaṃ piyo hoti, sulabhapaccayo; pattagatamassa dīyamānampi na khīyati, bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṭṭhāne aggabhaṇḍaṃ labhati, bhaye vā chātake vā sampatte devatā ussukkaṃ āpajjanti.

Tatrimāni vatthūni – leṇagirivāsī tissatthero kira mahāgirigāmaṃ upanissāya vasati. Paññāsa mahātherā nāgadīpaṃ cetiyavandanatthāya gacchantā girigāme piṇḍāya caritvā kiñci aladdhā nikkhamiṃsu. Thero pavisanto te disvā pucchi – ‘‘laddhaṃ, bhante’’ti? Vicarimhā, āvusoti. So aladdhabhāvaṃ ñatvā āha – ‘‘yāvāhaṃ, bhante, āgacchāmi, tāva idheva hothā’’ti. Mayaṃ, āvuso, paññāsa janā pattatemanamattampi na labhimhāti. Nevāsikā nāma, bhante, paṭibalā honti, alabhantāpi bhikkhācāramaggasabhāvaṃ jānantīti. Therā āgamiṃsu. Thero gāmaṃ pāvisi. Dhurageheyeva mahāupāsikā khīrabhattaṃ sajjetvā theraṃ olokayamānā ṭhitā therassa dvāraṃ sampattasseva pattaṃ pūretvā adāsi. So taṃ ādāya therānaṃ santikaṃ gantvā, ‘‘gaṇhatha, bhante’’ti saṅghattheramāha. Thero, ‘‘amhehi ettakehi kiñci na laddhaṃ, ayaṃ sīghameva gahetvā āgato, kiṃ nu kho’’ti sesānaṃ mukhaṃ olokesi. Thero olokanākāreneva ñatvā – ‘‘dhammena samena laddhapiṇḍapāto, nikkukkuccā gaṇhatha bhante’’tiādito paṭṭhāya sabbesaṃ yāvadatthaṃ datvā attanāpi yāvadatthaṃ bhuñji.

Atha naṃ bhattakiccāvasāne therā pucchiṃsu – ‘‘kadā, āvuso, lokuttaradhammaṃ paṭivijjhī’’ti? Natthi me, bhante, lokuttaradhammoti. Jhānalābhīsi, āvusoti? Etampi me, bhante, natthīti. Nanu, āvuso, pāṭihāriyanti? Sāraṇīyadhammo me, bhante, pūrito, tassa me dhammassa pūritakālato paṭṭhāya sacepi bhikkhusatasahassaṃ hoti, pattagataṃ na khīyatīti. Sādhu sādhu, sappurisa, anucchavikamidaṃ tuyhanti. Idaṃ tāva pattagataṃ na khīyatīti ettha vatthu.

pattagataṃ na khīyatī

Ayameva pana thero cetiyapabbate giribhaṇḍamahāpūjāya dānaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā, ‘‘imasmiṃ ṭhāne kiṃ varabhaṇḍa’’nti pucchati. Dve sāṭakā, bhanteti. Ete mayhaṃ pāpuṇissantīti. Taṃ sutvā amacco rañño ārocesi – ‘‘eko daharo evaṃ vadatī’’ti. ‘‘Daharassevaṃ cittaṃ, mahātherānaṃ pana sukhumasāṭakā vaṭṭantī’’ti vatvā, ‘‘mahātherānaṃ dassāmī’’ti ṭhapesi. Tassa bhikkhusaṅghe paṭipāṭiyā ṭhite dentassa matthake ṭhapitāpi te sāṭakā hatthaṃ nārohanti, aññeva ārohanti. Daharassa dānakāle pana hatthaṃ āruḷhā. So tassa hatthe ṭhapetvā amaccassa mukhaṃ oloketvā daharaṃ nisīdāpetvā dānaṃ datvā saṅghaṃ vissajjetvā daharassa santike nisīditvā, ‘‘kadā, bhante, imaṃ dhammaṃ paṭivijjhitthā’’ti āha. So pariyāyenapi asantaṃ avadanto, ‘‘natthi mayhaṃ, mahārāja, lokuttaradhammo’’ti āha. Nanu, bhante, pubbeva avacutthāti? Āma, mahārāja, sāraṇīyadhammapūrako ahaṃ, tassa me dhammassa pūritakālato paṭṭhāya bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṭṭhāne aggabhaṇḍaṃ pāpuṇātīti. Sādhu sādhu, bhante, anucchavikamidaṃ tumhākanti vanditvā pakkāmi. Idaṃ bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṭṭhāne aggabhaṇḍaṃ pāpuṇātīti ettha vatthu.

bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṭṭhāne aggabhaṇḍaṃ pāpuṇātī

Brāhmaṇatissabhaye pana bhātaragāmavāsino nāgattheriyā anārocetvāva palāyiṃsu. Therī paccūsakāle, ‘‘ativiya appanigghoso gāmo, upadhāretha tāvā’’ti daharabhikkhuniyo āha. Tā gantvā sabbesaṃ gatabhāvaṃ ñatvā āgamma theriyā ārocesuṃ. Sā sutvā, ‘‘mā tumhe tesaṃ gatabhāvaṃ cintayittha, attano uddesaparipucchāyonisomanasikāresuyeva yogaṃ karothā’’ti vatvā bhikkhācāravelāya pārupitvā attadvādasamā gāmadvāre nigrodharukkhamūle aṭṭhāsi. Rukkhe adhivatthā devatā dvādasannampi bhikkhunīnaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ datvā, ‘‘ayye, aññattha mā gacchatha, niccaṃ idheva ethā’’ti āha. Theriyā pana kaniṭṭhabhātā nāgatthero nāma atthi. So, ‘‘mahantaṃ bhayaṃ, na sakkā idha yāpetuṃ, paratīraṃ gamissāmāti attadvādasamova attano vasanaṭṭhānā nikkhanto theriṃ disvā gamissāmī’’ti bhātaragāmaṃ āgato. Therī, ‘‘therā āgatā’’ti sutvā tesaṃ santikaṃ gantvā, kiṃ ayyāti pucchi. So taṃ pavattiṃ ācikkhi. Sā, ‘‘ajja ekadivasaṃ vihāreyeva vasitvā sveva gamissathā’’ti āha. Therā vihāraṃ agamaṃsu.

Therī punadivase rukkhamūle piṇḍāya caritvā theraṃ upasaṅkamitvā, ‘‘imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjathā’’ti āha. Thero, ‘‘vaṭṭissati therī’’ti vatvā tuṇhī aṭṭhāsi. Dhammiko tātā piṇḍapāto kukkuccaṃ akatvā paribhuñjathāti. Vaṭṭissati therīti. Sā pattaṃ gahetvā ākāse khipi, patto ākāse aṭṭhāsi. Thero, ‘‘sattatālamatte ṭhitampi bhikkhunībhattameva, therīti vatvā bhayaṃ nāma sabbakālaṃ na hoti, bhaye vūpasante ariyavaṃsaṃ kathayamāno, ‘bho piṇḍapātika bhikkhunībhattaṃ bhuñjitvā vītināmayitthā’ti cittena anuvadiyamāno santhambhetuṃ na sakkhissāmi, appamattā hotha theriyo’’ti maggaṃ āruhi.

Rukkhadevatāpi, ‘‘sace thero theriyā hatthato piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjissati, na naṃ nivattessāmi, sace pana na paribhuñjissati, nivattessāmī’’ti cintayamānā ṭhatvā therassa gamanaṃ disvā rukkhā oruyha pattaṃ, bhante, dethāti pattaṃ gahetvā theraṃ rukkhamūlaṃyeva ānetvā āsanaṃ paññāpetvā piṇḍapātaṃ datvā katabhattakiccaṃ paṭiññaṃ kāretvā dvādasa bhikkhuniyo, dvādasa ca bhikkhū satta vassāni upaṭṭhahi. Idaṃ devatā ussukkaṃ āpajjantīti ettha vatthu, tatra hi therī sāraṇīyadhammapūrikā ahosi.

devatā ussukkaṃ āpajjantī

Akhaṇḍānītiādīsu yassa sattasu āpattikkhandhesu ādimhi vā ante vā sikkhāpadaṃ bhinnaṃ hoti, tassa sīlaṃ pariyante chinnasāṭako viya khaṇḍaṃ nāma. Yassa pana vemajjhe bhinnaṃ, tassa majjhe chiddasāṭako viya chiddaṃ nāma hoti. Yassa pana paṭipāṭiyā dve tīṇi bhinnāni, tassa piṭṭhiyaṃ vā kucchiyaṃ vā uṭṭhitena visabhāgavaṇṇena kāḷarattādīnaṃ aññataravaṇṇā gāvī viya sabalaṃ nāma hoti. Yassa pana antarantarā bhinnāni, tassa antarantarā visabhāgabinducitrā gāvī viya kammāsaṃ nāma hoti. Yassa pana sabbena sabbaṃ abhinnāni, tassa tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni nāma honti. Tāni panetāni taṇhādāsabyato mocetvā bhujissabhāvakaraṇato bhujissāni. Buddhādīhi viññūhi pasatthattā viññuppasatthāni. Taṇhādiṭṭhīhi aparāmaṭṭhattā, ‘‘idaṃ nāma tvaṃ āpannapubbo’’ti kenaci parāmaṭṭhuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā ca aparāmaṭṭhāni. Upacārasamādhiṃ vā appanāsamādhiṃ vā saṃvattayantīti samādhisaṃvattanikānīti vuccanti. Sīlasāmaññagatoviharatīti tesu tesu disābhāgesu viharantehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ samānabhāvūpagatasīlo viharati . Sotāpannādīnañhi sīlaṃ samuddantarepi devalokepi vasantānaṃ aññesaṃ sotāpannādīnaṃ sīlena samānameva hoti, natthi maggasīle nānattaṃ, taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Akhaṇḍānī khaṇḍaṃ chiddaṃ sabalaṃ kammāsaṃ akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṃvattanikānī Sīlasāmaññagato viharatī

Yāyaṃ diṭṭhīti maggasampayuttā sammādiṭṭhi. Ariyāti niddosā. Niyyātīti niyyānikā. Takkarassāti yo tathākārī hoti. Dukkhakkhayāyāti sabbadukkhakkhayatthaṃ. Diṭṭhisāmaññagatoti samānadiṭṭhibhāvaṃ upagato hutvā viharati. Agganti jeṭṭhakaṃ. Sabbagopānasiyo saṅgaṇhātīti saṅgāhikaṃ. Sabbagopānasīnaṃ saṅghāṭaṃ karotīti saṅghāṭanikaṃ. Saṅghāṭaniyanti attho. Yadidaṃ kūṭanti yametaṃ kūṭāgārakaṇṇikāsaṅkhātaṃ kūṭaṃ nāma. Pañcabhūmikādipāsādā hi kūṭabaddhāva tiṭṭhanti. Yasmiṃ patite mattikaṃ ādiṃ katvā sabbe patanti. Tasmā evamāha. Evameva khoti yathā kūṭaṃ kūṭāgārassa, evaṃ imesampi sāraṇīyadhammānaṃ yā ayaṃ ariyā diṭṭhi, sā aggā ca saṅgāhikā ca saṅghāṭaniyā cāti daṭṭhabbā.

Yāyaṃ diṭṭhī Ariyā Niyyātī niyyānikā. Takkarassā Dukkhakkhayāyā Diṭṭhisāmaññagato Agga saṅgāhikaṃ saṅghāṭanikaṃ Yadidaṃ kūṭa Evameva kho
commentary_english:
492. “*Chayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sāraṇīyā*,” thus, below, the teaching was begun in terms of strife, quarrel, and cause of dispute. In this place, [there are] six memorable *dharmas* that have come, thus this *Kosambiya Sutta* accords with what follows. There, *sāraṇīyā* means proper to be remembered, not to be forgotten even when gone far away. "He fulfills these *dharmas*, he makes [himself] dear to his fellow practitioners," [this is] *piyakaraṇā*. They make [him] heavy [with respect], [this is] *garukaraṇā*. *Saṅgahāyā* means for the purpose of harmony. *Avivādāyā* means for the purpose of non-dispute. *Sāmaggiyā* means for the purpose of harmonious being. *Ekībhāvāyā* means for the sake of unity, for the sake of non-differentiation. *Saṃvattantī* means they become. *Mettaṃ kāyakamma* means bodily action to be done with a mind of loving-kindness. *Vacīkammamanokammesupi*—the same is the method for verbal and mental action. These have come in dependence on the monks, they are also obtained by householders. For monks, the fulfillment of the practice of conduct that accords with loving-kindness with a mind of loving-kindness is called *mettaṃ kāyakamma*. For householders, going for the purpose of venerating a *cetiya*, going for the purpose of venerating the *bodhi* tree, going for the purpose of inviting the *saṅgha*, seeing monks who have entered the village for alms, going out to meet [them], receiving [their] bowls, preparing seats, following after—such things as these are called *mettaṃ kāyakamma*.

For monks, with a mind of loving-kindness, the code of monastic discipline, the telling of the place for meditation, a *dharma* talk, even the Three Baskets, the Buddha's word, is called *mettaṃ vacīkamma*. And for householders, [saying,] "Let us go for the purpose of venerating a *cetiya*, let us go for the purpose of venerating a *bodhi* tree, let us perform the hearing of the *dharma*, let us make an offering of a garland of lamps and flowers, let us undertake and maintain the three kinds of good conduct, let us give food offered by ticket," and so on, "let us give robes for the rainy season retreat, today let us give the four requisites to the *saṅgha*," inviting the *saṅgha*, preparing consumable things and so on, preparing seats, providing water, going out to meet the *saṅgha* and bringing [them] in, having seated [them] on prepared seats, at the time of speaking about things like being born from desire, being born from enthusiasm, doing service—this is called *mettaṃ vacīkamma*.

mettaṃ vacīkamma

For monks, rising up early in the morning, having attended to [their] bodies, and having made the practice of the *cetiya* courtyard and so on, and having sat down on a secluded seat, thinking, "May the monks in this monastery be happy, free from enmity, free from oppression," this thought is called *mettaṃ manokamma*. For householders, the thought, "May the noble ones be happy, free from enmity, free from oppression," is called *mettaṃ manokamma*.

mettaṃ manokamma

*Āvi ceva raho cā* means both in public and in private. There, going for companionship to new monks in things like robe-making and so on, is called *sammukhā mettaṃ kāyakamma*. But for elder monks, even the distinction of washing the feet, venerating, giving fans, and so on, all this proper action is called *sammukhā mettaṃ kāyakamma*. Even for both, not making light of wooden utensils and so on that are badly put away, but [rather] arranging what has been badly put away by oneself is called *parammukhā mettaṃ kāyakamma*. Saying things like "Devatthera, Tissatthera," and so on, with respect, is called *sammukhā mettaṃ vacīkamma*. But in the monastery, to one who asks about one who is not there, [saying,] "Where is our Devatthera? When will our Tissatthera come?" Such speech of possessiveness is called *parammukhā mettaṃ vacīkamma*. But opening the eyes, which are sticky with loving affection, and looking with a very clear face, is called *sammukhā mettaṃ manokamma*. The thought, "Devatthera, Tissatthera, may [they] be free from disease, free from affliction," is called *parammukhā mettaṃ manokamma*.

āvi ceva raho cā

*Lābhā* means requisites that have been obtained, like robes and so on. *Dhammikā* means arisen from proper conduct by avoiding wrong livelihood which is different from hypocrisy and so on, by [means of] the alms-begging life, which is even and in accordance with the *dharma*. *Antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampī* means even a little food that has been completely filled in a bowl at the last edge, that is contained within the bowl, two or three spoonfuls. *Appaṭivibhattabhogī*—here, there are two kinds of sharing: sharing of material things and sharing with individuals. Therein, the distribution with the thought, “I will give this much; I will not give this much,” is called distribution based on material (*āmisapaṭivibhatta*). The distribution with the thought, “I will give to this person; I will not give to that person,” is called distribution based on the individual (*puggalapaṭivibhatta*). But one who, without doing either of those two, enjoys [something] undivided—this one is called an enjoyer of the undivided (*appaṭivibhattabhogī*). The gains that are righteous (*lābhā dhammikā*)—even as little as would fill a bowl—[belong to] the enjoyer of the undivided (*appaṭivibhattabhogī*). An enjoyer of the undivided… …[is] one who shares in common with his fellow-practitioners (*sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī*). Here is the characteristic of the one who shares in common: whatever is excellent that he obtains, that he does not give to householders with a desire to conquer gain with gain in a deceiving way, nor does he enjoy it himself; but receiving it, thinking, “Let it be shared in common by the *saṅgha*,” having taken it, struck the gong, he sees [it] as if [it were] the property of the *saṅgha* to be enjoyed. Who fulfills this practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhamma*), and who does not fulfill it? A person of immoral character, of course, does not fulfill it. For virtuous people do not accept what belongs to him. But a person of completely pure virtue, not breaking his observance, fulfills it. [Is] one who shares in common with his fellow-practitioners (*sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī*). Therein, this is the observance: the one who, indeed, having made a specific allocation (*odissaka*), gives to his mother, or father, or teachers, preceptors, etc., this one gives what should be given. The practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhamma*) does not exist for him; it is called an impediment of worldliness (*palibodhajagganaṃ nāma hoti*). The practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhamma*) is suitable only for one freed from the impediments of worldliness (*muttapalibodha*). Therefore, through giving a specific allocation, it should be given to the sick, to those who attend to the sick, to visitors, to travelers, and also to a newly ordained monk who does not know the robe, bowl, and acceptance. Having given to these, and not giving the remainder little by little from the seat of the elders onward, the one who takes whatever amount, that much should be given to him. If there is no remainder, having again gone for alms, having given whatever is excellent from the seat of the elders onward, the remainder should be enjoyed, “Because of the saying, ‘by virtuous ones,’” it is also suitable not to give to an immoral person. This practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhamma*), however, is easily fulfilled by a well-trained community, not by an untrained community. For in a well-trained community, the one who obtains [something] from elsewhere, this one does not take [it]; even though not obtaining [it] from elsewhere, he takes only what is in accordance with measure, not an excess. And this practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhamma*), even for one who, having thus repeatedly gone for alms, gives what he has obtained, is fulfilled in twelve years; not less than that. If, indeed, even in the twelfth year, one fulfilling the practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhammapūrako*), having filled his bowl with alms food, places [it] in the alms hall and goes to bathe, and the *saṅgha* elder asks, “Whose bowl is this?” if it is said, “Of the one fulfilling the practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhammapūraka*),” [they will say] “Bring it here!” and all… …having reflected upon the alms food, and having eaten, puts away the empty bowl. Then that monk, having seen the empty bowl, if he produces displeasure, [thinking], “They have enjoyed [it] all, without leaving anything for me!” the practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhamma*) is broken; again, twelve years must be fulfilled. It is like the probationary period of members of other sects (*titthiya*); that is how it is. Once a break has occurred, it must be fulfilled again. But the one who generates joy, [thinking], “It is a gain for me, it is well gained for me, that my fellow-practitioners enjoy what has gone into my bowl without asking me!” this one is said to be full (*puṇṇo*). The one whose practice conducive to amiability (*sāraṇīyadhamma*) is thus fulfilled, however, has neither envy nor stinginess; that one is dear to people, [and has] easily obtained requisites. Even though [something] is being given to the one into whose bowl [food] has gone, it does not diminish; in the place of disposable goods, he obtains excellent goods; when fear or hunger has befallen [him], the gods become eager. These are the stories therein: Tissa, an elder dwelling on Leṇagiri, it seems, lived depending on the village of Mahāgiri. Fifty great elders, going to Nāgadīpa for the purpose of worshiping a shrine, having gone for alms in the village of Giri, having obtained nothing, departed. An elder, entering, having seen them, asked, “Did you obtain [anything], *bhante*?” “We went around, *āvuso*.” That one, having known the state of not obtaining, said, “As long as I, *bhante*, come [back], remain right here!” “We, *āvuso*, fifty people, did not obtain even as much as would fill the bottom of a bowl!” “The residents (*nevāsikā*), *bhante*, are very powerful; even without obtaining [anything], they know the nature of the path of the alms round.” The elders came. The elder entered the village. A great female lay follower, right there at the entrance of the house, having prepared milk-rice, standing looking at the elder, having filled the bowl right as the elder had arrived at the door, gave [it to him]. He, having taken that, having gone to the elders, said to the *saṅgha* elder, “Take [this], *bhante*!” The elder, “We have not obtained anything with so many people, this one has quickly taken [it] and come, what now?” looked at the faces of the others. The elder, having known the form of looking only, having given to all as long as was needed, beginning from “alms obtained righteously, take [it] without hesitation, Venerable Sir!”, he himself also enjoyed as much as was needed. Then, at the end of the meal, the elders asked him: "When, friend, did you penetrate the supramundane Dharma?" "There is no supramundane Dharma for me, Venerable Sir." "Are you a gainer of absorption, friend?" "This too, Venerable Sir, is not for me." "Surely, friend, [are there] miracles?" "The Dharma that is to be recollected, Venerable Sir, is fulfilled by me; from the time of the fulfillment of that Dharma, if there are even one hundred thousand monks, [the food] in the bowl does not diminish." "Well done, well done, superior man, this is fitting for you." Here is the story of "the food in the bowl does not diminish." Now, that elder, having gone to the alms-giving place at the Giribhaṇḍa Great Festival on Cetiyapabbata, asks, "In this place, what is the best ware?" "Two cloaks, Venerable Sir." "These will come to me." Having heard that, the minister announced to the king: "A certain young man speaks thus." "The mind of the young man is thus; fine cloaks are fitting for the great elders," having said, "[I] will give to the great elders," he set [them] aside. When the Saṭakas are placed on the head of a giver standing in order of the community of monks, they do not come into the hand, they come on something else. But at the time of the young man's giving, they came into [his] hand. He, having placed [the Saṭakas] in that hand, having looked at the face of the minister, having seated the young man, having given the alms, having dismissed the Sangha, having sat down near the young man, said: "When, Venerable Sir, did you penetrate this Dharma?" He, not speaking falsely even by a circumlocution, said, "There is no supramundane Dharma for me, great king." "Surely, Venerable Sir, you spoke falsely before?" "Yes, great king, I am a fulfiller of the Dharma that is to be recollected; from the time of the fulfillment of that Dharma, in the place of things to be shared, the best thing is obtained." "Well done, well done, Venerable Sir, this is fitting for you," having worshiped, he departed. Here is the story of "in the place of things to be shared, the best thing is obtained." In the Brāhmaṇatissa fear, the inhabitants of Bhātaragāma fled without even announcing it to Nāgattherī. The Theri, at dawn, [thinking], "The village is extremely quiet, you should investigate," said to the young nuns. Having gone, having known the state of all having gone, having come back, they announced to the Theri. She, having heard, having said, "Do not think about the state of their having gone, but do only yoga in the matters of learning, questioning, and appropriate attention," having dressed at the time for alms-wandering, stood, attended by twelve, at the village gate, at the foot of a banyan tree (nigrodha). A *devatā* dwelling in the tree, having given alms to the twelve nuns, said: "Ladies, do not go elsewhere, but always come here." Now, the younger brother of the Theri, named Nāgatthera, exists. He, [thinking], "There is great fear, it is not possible to live here, I will go to the further shore," attended by twelve, having left from his own dwelling place, [thinking], "I will go after seeing the Theri," came to Bhātaragāma. The Theri, having heard, "The elders have come," having gone to their presence, asked, "What is it, lady?" He told that story. She said, "Today, having lived in the monastery for one day only, you will go tomorrow." The elders went to the monastery. The Theri, on the following day, having wandered for alms at the foot of the tree, having approached the Thera, said, "Enjoy this alms-food." The elder said, “She will be a *therī*,” and then he was silent. “Dear fathers, you should partake of this alms food without any misgivings.” “She will be a *therī*.” She took the bowl and threw it into the sky, and the bowl remained in the sky. The elder thought, “Even if she stays at a height of seven tāla trees, this is just nun's food. If I say, ‘She is a *therī,*’ fear will not exist at all times. When fear has subsided, while I am relating the lineage of the Noble Ones, if I am slighted in my mind, thinking, ‘This alms-mendicant partook of the nun's food and passed the time,’ I will not be able to calm [myself]. Be diligent, *therīs*!” and he went on his way.

The tree deity also, thinking, “If this elder partakes of alms food from the hand of the *therī*, I will not turn him back, but if he does not partake, I will turn him back,” stood there, and seeing the elder's departure, descended from the tree, and having taken the bowl, saying, “Venerable sir, give [me] the bowl,” brought the elder to the foot of the tree, and having prepared a seat, and having given the alms food, and having made [him] acknowledge the completed meal duties, attended upon twelve nuns and twelve monks for seven years. This is the story about the deity becoming eager. There, the *therī* was filled with things worthy of remembrance.

About the deity becoming eager. In “unbroken,” etc., if a training rule is broken in the beginning or the end in his seven aggregates of offenses, his morality is called "rent" (*khaṇḍa*) like a torn cloth at the end. But when he has broken it in the middle, it is called "hole" (*chiddaṃ*), like a cloth that is rent in the middle. When he has broken it twice or thrice in succession, it is called "blotched" (*sabalaṃ*), like a cow whose body is some such color as black or red with a discrepant color appearing on the back or the belly. When he has broken it intermittently, it is called "blemished" (*kammāsaṃ*), like a cow with a different color of spotted patches. When all of them are unbroken in every way, those moralities are called “unbroken, unperforated, unblotched, unblemished” (*akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni*). Having freed those [moralities] from being slaves to craving, on account of making them free, [they are] "free" (*bhujissāni*). Because they are praised by the wise, such as the Buddhas, [they are] "praised by the wise" (*viññuppasatthāni*). Because they are untouched by craving and views, and because no one can touch them, saying, “You were formerly subject to this,” [they are] "untouchable" (*aparāmaṭṭhāni*). Because they promote approach-concentration or attainment-concentration, they are called “promoters of concentration” (*samādhisaṃvattanikāni*). Being one who has gone to the same morality. He lives with the monks who are living in those various directions, with morality that has approached a state of sameness. Indeed, the morality of the stream-enterers, even when they are living in the ocean's interior or in the world of the gods, is just the same as the morality of the other stream-enterers. There is no diversity in the morality of the path. This was said having in mind that.

Unbroken, rent, perforated, blotched, blemished, unbroken, unperforated, unblotched, unblemished, free, praised by the wise, untouched, promoters of concentration, one who has gone to the same morality. Being one who has gone to the same morality. That is right view associated with the path. Noble, means without defects. Leading out, means leading out. Of the doer of that, means he is doing like that. For the destruction of suffering, means for the sake of the destruction of all suffering. Being one who has gone to the same view, means having approached a state of the same view, he lives. Highest, means eldest. He holds all rafters, therefore holding together. He makes a union of all the rafters, therefore to be joined together. The meaning is to be joined together. That which is false, means that which is known as the peak of a false house, is called false. Indeed, palaces with five stories etc. stand only connected by falsehood. When that falls, all fall, having made clay etc. the beginning.Therefore, he spoke thus. Just as a peaked roof for a peaked house, even so, this noble view (ariyā diṭṭhi) regarding these memorable qualities (sāraṇīyadhammānaṃ) should be regarded as chief (aggā), comprehensive (saṅgāhikā), and unifying (saṅghāṭaniyā). This noble (ariyā) view (diṭṭhi) leads out (niyyātī), is a vehicle of deliverance (niyyānikā). Connected to the destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayāyā), attained to agreement in view (diṭṭhisāmaññagato), supreme (agga), comprehensive (saṅgāhikaṃ), unifying (saṅghāṭanikaṃ), namely this peaked roof (kūṭa), just so (evameva).

mula_pali: 493. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, yāyaṃ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘atthi nu kho me taṃ pariyuṭṭhānaṃ ajjhattaṃ appahīnaṃ, yenāhaṃ pariyuṭṭhānena pariyuṭṭhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ nappajāneyyaṃ na passeyya’nti? Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhito hoti, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu byāpādapariyuṭṭhito hoti, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu thīnamiddhapariyuṭṭhito hoti, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhito hoti, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhito hoti, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu idhalokacintāya pasuto hoti, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paralokacintāya pasuto hoti, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanajāto kalahajāto vivādāpanno aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudanto viharati, pariyuṭṭhitacittova hoti . So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘natthi kho me taṃ pariyuṭṭhānaṃ ajjhattaṃ appahīnaṃ, yenāhaṃ pariyuṭṭhānena pariyuṭṭhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ nappajāneyyaṃ na passeyyaṃ. Suppaṇihitaṃ me mānasaṃ saccānaṃ bodhāyā’ti. Idamassa paṭhamaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi.
mula_english:
493. “And how, *bhikkhus*, does that view lead out, being noble, leading to the destruction of suffering, for one who reasons rightly? Here, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu*, gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, considers thus: ‘Is there any obsession unabandoned in myself that might so obsess my mind that I cannot know or see things as they actually are?’ If, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is obsessed by sensual lust (kāmarāga-pariyuṭṭhito), then his mind is obsessed. If, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is obsessed by ill will (byāpāda-pariyuṭṭhito), then his mind is obsessed. If, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is obsessed by sloth and torpor (thīnamiddha-pariyuṭṭhito), then his mind is obsessed. If, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is obsessed by restlessness and remorse (uddhaccakukkucca-pariyuṭṭhito), then his mind is obsessed. If, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is obsessed by doubt (vicikicchā-pariyuṭṭhito), then his mind is obsessed. If, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is absorbed in speculation about this world (idhalokacintāya pasuto), then his mind is obsessed. If, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* is absorbed in speculation about the other world (paralokacintāya pasuto), then his mind is obsessed. If a *bhikkhu* takes to quarrelling and brawling and is deep in disputes, stabbing others with verbal daggers, then his mind is obsessed.

He understands thus: ‘There is no obsession unabandoned in myself that might so obsess my mind that I cannot know and see things as they actually are.’ My mind is well disposed for awakening to the truths (saccānaṃ bodhāyā’ti). This is the first knowledge (ñāṇaṃ) attained by him that is noble (ariyaṃ), supramundane (lokuttaraṃ), not shared by ordinary people (puthujjanehi).
commentary_pali: 493.Kathañca, bhikkhave, yāyaṃ diṭṭhīti ettha, bhikkhave, yāyaṃ sotāpattimaggadiṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyāti vuttā, sā kathaṃ kena kāraṇena niyyātīti attho. Pariyuṭṭhitacittova hotīti ettāvatāpi pariyuṭṭhitacittoyeva nāma hotīti attho. Esa nayo sabbattha. Suppaṇihitaṃ me mānasanti mayhaṃ cittaṃ suṭṭhu ṭhapitaṃ. Saccānaṃ bodhāyāti catunnaṃ saccānaṃ bodhatthāya. Ariyantiādīsu taṃ ñāṇaṃ yasmā ariyānaṃ hoti, na puthujjanānaṃ, tasmā ariyanti vuttaṃ. Yesaṃ pana lokuttaradhammopi atthi, tesaṃyeva hoti, na aññesaṃ, tasmā lokuttaranti vuttaṃ. Puthujjanānaṃ pana abhāvato asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehīti vuttaṃ. Esa nayo sabbavāresu.
commentary_english:
493. “And how, monks, is this view?” namely, here, monks, that path of stream-entry ( *sotāpatti-magga*) which is noble (*ārya*), which leads out (*niyyānika*), leads to the destruction of suffering (*duḥkhakṣaya*), as has been said, how and by what cause does it lead out? This is the meaning.

“His mind is obsessed” namely, even by that much, it is said to be obsessed; this is the meaning.

This method applies to all instances.

“My mind is well-composed” namely, my mind (*citta*) is well-established (*suṣṭhu* *sthāpitaṃ*).

“For the understanding of the truths” namely, for the purpose of understanding the four truths (*caturnaṃ* *satyānām* *bodhārthāya*).

"Noble" etc., because that knowledge (*jñāna*) belongs to the noble ones (*ārya*), not to ordinary people (*pṛthagjana*), therefore it is called "noble" (*ārya*).

But that which also has supramundane phenomena (*lokottaradharma*), belongs only to them, not to others, therefore it is called "supramundane" (*lokottara*).

Because of the absence of ordinary people (*pṛthagjana*), it is said to be "uncommon to ordinary people" (*asādhāraṇaṃ* *pṛthagjanehi*).

This method applies to all sections.

mula_pali: 494. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘imaṃ nu kho ahaṃ diṭṭhiṃ āsevanto bhāvento bahulīkaronto labhāmi paccattaṃ samathaṃ, labhāmi paccattaṃ nibbuti’nti? So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘imaṃ kho ahaṃ diṭṭhiṃ āsevanto bhāvento bahulīkaronto labhāmi paccattaṃ samathaṃ, labhāmi paccattaṃ nibbuti’nti. Idamassa dutiyaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi.
mula_english: Furthermore, O monks, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘Indeed, by cultivating, developing, and pursuing this view, do I attain inner calm ( *samatha*), do I attain inner liberation (*nirvutti*)?’ He understands thus: ‘Indeed, by cultivating, developing, and pursuing this view, I attain inner calm (*samatha*), I attain inner liberation (*nirvutti*).’ This is his second knowledge, which is noble (*ariya*), supramundane (*lokuttara*), and not shared by ordinary people (*puthujjanehi*).
commentary_pali: 494.Labhāmi paccattaṃ samathanti attano citte samathaṃ labhāmīti attho. Nibbutiyampi eseva nayo. Ettha ca samathoti ekaggatā. Nibbutīti kilesavūpasamo.
commentary_english: " *labhāmi paccattaṃ samatha* means "I obtain calm (*samatha*) in my own mind." *nibbutiyampi* the same method applies. Here, *samatho* means one-pointedness ( *ekaggatā*). *nibbutī* means the subsiding of defilements (*kilesavūpasamo*).

mula_pali: 495. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yathā rūpāyāhaṃ diṭṭhiyā samannāgato, atthi nu kho ito bahiddhā añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato’ti? So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yathārūpāyāhaṃ diṭṭhiyā samannāgato, natthi ito bahiddhā añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato’ti. Idamassa tatiyaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi.
mula_english: “Furthermore, O monks, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘Is there any other recluse (śramaṇa) or *brāhmaṇa* outside the Buddha’s Dispensation possessed of a view such as I possess?’ He understands thus: ‘There is no other recluse (śramaṇa) or *brāhmaṇa* outside the Buddha’s Dispensation possessed of a view such as I possess.’ This is the third knowledge (*jñāna*) attained by him that is noble (*ārya*), supramundane (*lokottara*), not shared by ordinary people (*pṛthagjana*).
commentary_pali: 495.Tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyāti evarūpāya sotāpattimaggadiṭṭhiyā.
commentary_english: " *tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā* means to a view of such a nature," that is, to a view of the path of stream-entry (*sotāpattimārga-dṛṣṭi*), of such a form.

mula_pali: 496. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yathārūpāya dhammatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya dhammatāya samannāgato’ti. Kathaṃrūpāya ca, bhikkhave, dhammatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato? Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa – ‘kiñcāpi tathārūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, yathārūpāya āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyati, atha kho naṃ khippameva satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu deseti vivarati uttānīkaroti; desetvā vivaritvā uttānīkatvā āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjati’. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, daharo kumāro mando uttānaseyyako hatthena vā pādena vā aṅgāraṃ akkamitvā khippameva paṭisaṃharati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dhammatā esā diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa – ‘kiñcāpi tathārūpiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati yathārūpāya āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyati, atha kho naṃ khippameva satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu deseti vivarati uttānīkaroti; desetvā vivaritvā uttānīkatvā āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjati’. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yathārūpāya dhammatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya dhammatāya samannāgato’ti. Idamassa catutthaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi.
mula_english:
“Again, bhikkhus, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘Do I possess the character (dhammatā) of a person who possesses right view (diṭṭhisampanno puggalo)?’

And how, bhikkhus, does a person possess the character of one who possesses right view? This is the character of a person who possesses right view: although he may commit some kind of offense (āpattiṃ) for which a means of rehabilitation (vuṭṭhānaṃ) has been laid down, still he at once confesses (deseti), reveals (vivarati), and discloses (uttānīkaroti) it to the Teacher (satthari) or to wise (viññūsu) companions in the holy life (sabrahmacārīsu), and having done that, he enters upon restraint (saṃvaraṃ) for the future (āyatiṃ).

Bhikkhus, just as a young, tender infant (daharo kumāro mando) lying prone (uttānaseyyako) at once draws back (paṭisaṃharati) when he puts his hand or his foot on a live coal (aṅgāraṃ akkamitvā), so too, bhikkhus, that is the character of a person who possesses right view: although he may commit an offense for which a means of rehabilitation has been laid down, still he at once confesses, reveals and discloses it to the Teacher or to wise companions in the holy life, and having done that, he enters upon restraint for the future.

He understands thus: ‘I possess the character of a person who possesses right view.’

This is the fourth knowledge (ñāṇaṃ) attained by him that is noble (ariyaṃ), supramundane (lokuttaraṃ), not shared by ordinary people (asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi).
commentary_pali: 496.Dhammatāyāti sabhāvena. Dhammatā esāti sabhāvo esa. Vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyatīti saṅghakammavasena vā desanāya vā vuṭṭhānaṃ dissati. Ariyasāvako hi āpattiṃ āpajjanto garukāpattīsu kuṭikārasadisaṃ, lahukāpattīsu sahaseyyādisadisaṃ acittakāpattiṃyeva āpajjati, tampi asañcicca, no sañcicca, āpannaṃ na paṭicchādeti. Tasmā atha kho naṃ khippamevātiādimāha. Daharoti taruṇo. Kumāroti na mahallako. Mandoti cakkhusotādīnaṃ mandatāya mando. Uttānaseyyakoti atidaharatāya uttānaseyyako, dakkhiṇena vā vāmena vā passena sayituṃ na sakkotīti attho. Aṅgāraṃ akkamitvāti ito cito ca pasāritena hatthena vā pādena vā phusitvā. Evaṃ phusantānaṃ pana manussānaṃ na sīghaṃ hattho jhāyati, tathā hi ekacce hatthena aṅgāraṃ gahetvā parivattamānā dūrampi gacchanti. Daharassa pana hatthapādā sukhumālā honti, so phuṭṭhamatteneva dayhamāno cirīti saddaṃ karonto khippaṃ paṭisaṃharati, tasmā idha daharova dassito. Mahallako ca dayhantopi adhivāseti, ayaṃ pana adhivāsetuṃ na sakkoti. Tasmāpi daharova dassito. Desetīti āpattipaṭiggāhake sabhāgapuggale sati ekaṃ divasaṃ vā rattiṃ vā anadhivāsetvā rattiṃ caturaṅgepi tame sabhāgabhikkhuno vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā desetiyeva.
commentary_english: 496. *Dhammatāyā* means by nature (*sabhāvena*). *Dhammatā esā* means its nature (*sabhāvo esa*). *Vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyatī* means by means of the Saṅgha's action (*saṅghakammavasena*) or by means of teaching (*desanāya*), uprising (*vuṭṭhānaṃ*) is seen (*dissati*). An noble disciple, incurring an offense (*āpattiṃ āpajjanto*), in the case of serious offenses (*garukāpattīsu*) [commits an offense] similar to the construction of a hut (*kuṭikārasadisaṃ*), in the case of light offenses (*lahukāpattīsu*) [commits an offense] similar to sharing a bed (*sahaseyyādisadisaṃ*), incurs only an unintentional offense (*acittakāpattiṃyeva āpajjati*), and even that unintentionally (*tampi asañcicca*), not intentionally (*no sañcicca*), and does not conceal the offense (*āpannaṃ na paṭicchādeti*). Therefore, he said, beginning with "*atha kho naṃ khippamevā*." *Daharo* means young (*taruṇo*). *Kumāro* means not old (*na mahallako*). *Mando* means dull (*mando*) due to the dullness (*mandatāya*) of the eyes, ears, etc. (*cakkhusotādīnaṃ*). *Uttānaseyyako* means, due to excessive youthfulness (*atidaharatāya*), [he is] one who lies on his back (*uttānaseyyako*), that is, he is not able (*na sakkoti*) to lie down (*sayituṃ*) on his right (*dakkhiṇena*) or left (*vāmena*) side (*passena*), this is the meaning (*attho*). *Aṅgāraṃ akkamitvā* means having touched (*phusitvā*) the embers (*aṅgāraṃ*) with a hand (*hatthena*) or foot (*pādena*) that has been stretched out (*pasāritena*) from here and there (*ito cito ca*). However, for people (*manussānaṃ*) who are thus touching (*evaṃ phusantānaṃ*), the hand (*hattho*) does not burn (*na sīghaṃ jhāyati*) quickly (*sīghaṃ*), for thus (*tathā hi*) some (*ekacce*) take (*gahetvā*) the embers (*aṅgāraṃ*) with their hand (*hatthena*) and, while moving around (*parivattamānā*), go (*gacchanti*) even far away (*dūrampi*). However, the hands and feet (*hatthapādā*) of a young person (*daharassa*) are very tender (*sukhumālā honti*), so (*so*) when touched (*phuṭṭhamattena eva*) he burns (*dayhamāno*) and, making the sound "*cirīti saddaṃ karonto*," quickly withdraws (*khippaṃ paṭisaṃharati*), therefore (*tasmā*) here (*idha*) only a young person (*daharova*) is shown (*dassito*). And an old person (*mahallako ca*), even while burning (*dayhantopi*), endures (*adhivāseti*), but (*pana*) this one (*ayaṃ*) is not able (*na sakkoti*) to endure (*adhivāsetuṃ*). Therefore also (*tasmāpi*) only a young person (*daharova*) is shown (*dassito*). *Desetī* means, when there is a co-participating individual (*sabhāgapuggale sati*) who receives offenses (*āpattipaṭiggāhake*), having not spent (*anadhivāsetvā*) one day (*ekaṃ divasaṃ*) or night (*rattiṃ vā*), even on the fourth night (*rattiṃ caturaṅgepi tame*), having gone (*gantvā*) to the dwelling place (*vasanaṭṭhānaṃ*) of the co-participating monk (*sabhāgabhikkhuno*), he should declare (*deseti eva*).

mula_pali: 497. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yathārūpāya dhammatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya dhammatāya samannāgato’ti. Kathaṃrūpāya ca, bhikkhave, dhammatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato? Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa – ‘kiñcāpi yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni tattha ussukkaṃ āpanno hoti, atha khvāssa tibbāpekkhā hoti adhisīlasikkhāya adhicittasikkhāya adhipaññāsikkhāya’. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gāvī taruṇavacchā thambañca ālumpati vacchakañca apacinati; evameva kho, bhikkhave , dhammatā esā diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa – ‘kiñcāpi yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni tattha ussukkaṃ āpanno hoti, atha khvāssa tibbāpekkhā hoti adhisīlasikkhāya adhicittasikkhāya adhipaññāsikkhāya’. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yathārūpāya dhammatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya dhammatāya samannāgato’ti. Idamassa pañcamaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi.
mula_english:
Again, O monks, a noble disciple considers thus: ‘Do I possess the character of a person who possesses right view (dṛṣṭisampanna)?’

And what, O monks, is the character of a person who possesses right view (dṛṣṭisampanna)? It is this, O monks, the character of a person who possesses right view (dṛṣṭisampanna): ‘Although there may be various duties, great and small, for his fellow religious practitioners (sabrahmacārī), he is keen to perform them, and furthermore, he has intense aspiration for higher training in morality (adhiśīlasikkhā), higher training in mind (adhicittasikkhā), and higher training in wisdom (adhiprajñāsikkhā).’

Just as, O monks, a cow with a young calf both licks a post and pays attention to her calf; even so, O monks, it is the character of a person who possesses right view (dṛṣṭisampanna): ‘Although there may be various duties, great and small, for his fellow religious practitioners (sabrahmacārī), he is keen to perform them, and furthermore, he has intense aspiration for higher training in morality (adhiśīlasikkhā), higher training in mind (adhicittasikkhā), and higher training in wisdom (adhiprajñāsikkhā).’

He understands thus: ‘I possess the character of a person who possesses right view (dṛṣṭisampanna).’

This is the fifth knowledge (jñāna) attained by him that is noble (ariya), supramundane (lokuttara), unshared (asādhāraṇa) by ordinary people (pṛthujjana).
commentary_pali:
497.Uccāvacānīti uccanīcāni. Kiṃ karaṇīyānīti kiṃ karomīti evaṃ vatvā kattabbakammāni. Tattha uccakammaṃ nāma cīvarassa karaṇaṃ rajanaṃ cetiye sudhākammaṃ uposathāgāracetiyagharabodhigharesu kattabbakammanti evamādi. Avacakammaṃ nāma pādadhovanamakkhanādikhuddakakammaṃ, atha vā cetiye sudhākammādi uccakammaṃ nāma. Tattheva kasāvapacanaudakānayanakucchakaraṇa niyyāsabandhanādi avacakammaṃ nāma. Ussukkaṃ āpanno hotīti ussukkabhāvaṃ kattabbataṃ paṭipanno hoti. Tibbāpekkho hotīti bahalapatthano hoti. Thambañcaālumpatīti tiṇañca ālumpamānā khādati. Vacchakañca apacinātīti vacchakañca apaloketi. Taruṇavacchā hi gāvī araññe ekato āgataṃ vacchakaṃ ekasmiṃ ṭhāne nipannaṃ pahāya dūraṃ na gacchati, vacchakassa āsannaṭṭhāne caramānā tiṇaṃ ālumpitvā gīvaṃ ukkhipitvā ekantaṃ vacchakameva ca viloketi, evameva sotāpanno uccāvacāni kiṃ karaṇīyāni karonto tanninno hoti, asithilapūrako tibbacchando bahalapatthano hutvāva karoti.

Tatridaṃ vatthu – mahācetiye kira sudhākamme kariyamāne eko ariyasāvako ekena hatthena sudhābhājanaṃ, ekena kucchaṃ gahetvā sudhākammaṃ karissāmīti cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ āruḷho. Eko kāyadaḷhibahulo bhikkhu gantvā therassa santike aṭṭhāsi. Thero aññasmiṃ sati papañco hotīti tasmā ṭhānā aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ gato. Sopi bhikkhu tattheva agamāsi. Thero puna aññaṃ ṭhānanti evaṃ katipayaṭṭhāne āgataṃ, – ‘‘sappurisa mahantaṃ cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ kiṃ aññasmiṃ ṭhāne okāsaṃ na labhathā’’ti āha. Na itaro pakkāmīti.
commentary_english:
497. "Uccāvacānī" means high and low.
"Kiṃ karaṇīyānī" means saying "What shall I do?" are the things to be done.

There, "uccakammaṃ" means making robes, dyeing, whitewashing the *cetiya*, things to be done in the *uposatha* hall, *cetiyaghara*, and *bodhighara*, and so on.

"Avacakammaṃ" means minor tasks such as washing feet and anointing, or whitewashing the *cetiya*, etc., is called "uccakammaṃ."

Right there, tasks such as setting out astringent medicine, fetching water, making a *kuccha*, applying resin, etc., are called "avacakammaṃ".

"Ussukkaṃ āpanno hotī" means he has undertaken the state of eagerness, the duty.

"Tibbāpekkho hotī" means he is one with intense longing, being very desirous.

"Thambañca ālumpatī" means she grazes on grass, chewing as she grazes.

"Vacchakañca apacinātī" means she observes the calf.

Indeed, a young cow, having left her calf who has come to the forest from one side and is lying down in one place, does not go far away. While wandering in a place near the calf, having grazed on grass, having raised her neck, she only looks at the calf, in the same way, a stream-enterer, while doing various things to be done, is inclined to that, he does [them] having become one with unfailing effort, intense desire, and great longing.

Here is the story: While whitewashing was being done at the great *cetiya*, a certain noble disciple, having taken a whitewash vessel in one hand and a *kuccha* in the other, ascended the *cetiyaṅgaṇa*, thinking "I will do the whitewashing".

A certain bhikkhu, strong and stout in body, went and stood near the elder.

The elder thought, "If there is association, there will be proliferation," therefore, he went from that place to another place.

That bhikkhu also went right there.

The elder again [went] to another place. Thus, [they] came to several places. [The elder] said, "Good sir, why don't you find a place in another place, [this] great *cetiyaṅgaṇa*?"

The other one did not leave.

mula_pali: 498. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yathārūpāya balatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya balatāya samannāgato’ti. Kathaṃrūpāya ca, bhikkhave, balatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato? Balatā esā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa yaṃ tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne aṭṭhiṃkatvā manasikatvā sabbacetasā sabbacetaso (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sabbaṃ cetasā (ka.) samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yathārūpāya balatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya balatāya samannāgato’ti. Idamassa chaṭṭhaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi.
mula_english:
“Again, O monks, a noble disciple considers thus: ‘I possess the strength of a person who possesses right view ( *dṛṣṭisampanno puggalaḥ* ).’

“And how, O monks, does a person who possesses right view possess strength? This is the strength, O monks, of a person who possesses right view: when the *dharmavinaya* (teachings) proclaimed by the *tathāgata* is being taught, he heeds it, gives it attention, engages it with all his mind (*sabbacetasā*), hears the Dharma with eager ears (*ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti*).

“He understands thus: ‘I possess the strength of a person who possesses right view.’

This is the sixth knowledge attained by him that is noble (*ariyaṃ*), supramundane (*lokuttaraṃ*), not shared by ordinary people (*puthujjanehi*).
commentary_pali: 498.Balatāya samannāgatoti balena samannāgato. Aṭṭhiṃ katvāti atthikabhāvaṃ katvā, atthiko hutvāti attho. Manasikatvāti manasmiṃ karitvā. Sabbacetasā samannāharitvāti appamattakampi vikkhepaṃ akaronto sakalacittena samannāharitvā. Ohitasototi ṭhapitasoto. Ariyasāvakā hi piyadhammassavanā honti, dhammassavanaggaṃ gantvā niddāyamānā vā yena kenaci saddhiṃ sallapamānā vā vikkhittacittā vā na nisīdanti, atha kho amataṃ paribhuñjantā viya atittāva honti dhammassavane, atha aruṇaṃ uggacchati. Tasmā evamāha.
commentary_english:
498. "balatāya samannāgato" means samannāgato with strength.

"aṭṭhiṃ katvā" means having done atthikabhāvaṃ, atthiko hutvāti is the meaning.

"manasikatvā" means having done manasmiṃ.

"sabbacetasā samannāharitvā" means samannāharitvā with sakalacittena, not doing even a little vikkhepaṃ.

"ohitasoto" means ṭhapitasoto.

Ariyasāvakās are indeed fond of hearing the Dhamma. Having gone to a place for hearing the Dhamma, they do not sit down drowsing, or conversing with anyone, or with distracted minds; rather, they are as if enjoying amata, not being satiated in hearing the Dhamma, and then aruṇaṃ rises.

Therefore, he said this.

mula_pali: 499. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yathārūpāya balatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya balatāya samannāgato’ti. Kathaṃrūpāya ca, bhikkhave, balatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato? Balatā esā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa yaṃ tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yathārūpāya balatāya diṭṭhisampanno puggalo samannāgato, ahampi tathārūpāya balatāya samannāgato’ti. Idamassa sattamaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ puthujjanehi.
mula_english:
Again, O monks, a noble disciple considers thus: ‘Do I possess the strength (balatā) of a person who possesses right view (dṛṣṭisampanna)?’

What is the strength (balatā) with which a person possessing right view (dṛṣṭisampanna) is endowed, O monks? This is the strength (balatā), O monks, of a person possessing right view (dṛṣṭisampanna): when the *dharma* and *vinaya* proclaimed by the *Tathāgata* are being taught, he gains inspiration in the meaning (*arthaveda*), gains inspiration in the *dharma* (*dharmaveda*), gains gladness connected with the *dharma* (*dharmūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ*).

He understands thus: ‘I possess the strength (balatā) of a person who possesses right view (dṛṣṭisampanna).’

This is the seventh knowledge (*jñāna*) attained by him that is noble (*ārya*), supramundane (*lokottara*), not shared by ordinary people (*pṛthagjana*).

mula_pali:
500. ‘‘Evaṃ sattaṅgasamannāgatassa kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa dhammatā susamanniṭṭhā hoti sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya. Evaṃ sattaṅgasamannāgato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpattiphalasamannāgato hotī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Kosambiyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
"Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple is thus possessed of seven factors, it is fitting that he has well sought the character for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry. Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple is thus possessed of seven factors, he possesses the fruit of stream-entry."

The Blessed One said this. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Kosambiya Discourse, the eighth, is concluded.
commentary_pali:
500.Dhammatāsusamanniṭṭhā hotīti sabhāvo suṭṭhu samannesito hoti. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāyāti karaṇavacanaṃ , sotāpattiphalasacchikatañāṇenāti attho. Evaṃ sattaṅgasamannāgatoti evaṃ imehi sattahi mahāpaccavekkhaṇañāṇehi samannāgato. Ayaṃ tāva ācariyānaṃ samānakathā. Lokuttaramaggo hi bahucittakkhaṇiko nāma natthi.

Vitaṇḍavādī pana ekacittakkhaṇiko nāma maggo natthi, ‘‘evaṃ bhāveyya satta vassānī’’ti hi vacanato sattapi vassāni maggabhāvanā honti. Kilesā pana lahu chijjantā sattahi ñāṇehi chijjantīti vadati. So suttaṃ āharāti vattabbo, addhā aññaṃ suttaṃ apassanto, ‘‘idamassa paṭhamaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti, idamassa dutiyaṃ ñāṇaṃ…pe… idamassa sattamaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hotī’’ti imameva āharitvā dassessati. Tato vattabbo kiṃ panidaṃ suttaṃ neyyatthaṃ nītatthanti. Tato vakkhati – ‘‘nītatthatthaṃ, yathāsuttaṃ tatheva attho’’ti. So vattabbo – ‘‘dhammatā susamanniṭṭhā hoti sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāyāti ettha ko attho’’ti? Addhā sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāyatthoti vakkhati. Tato pucchitabbo, ‘‘maggasamaṅgī phalaṃ sacchikaroti, phalasamaṅgī’’ti. Jānanto, ‘‘phalasamaṅgī sacchikarotī’’ti vakkhati. Tato vattabbo, – ‘‘evaṃ sattaṅgasamannāgato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpattiphalasamannāgato hotīti idha maggaṃ abhāvetvā maṇḍūko viya uppatitvā ariyasāvako phalameva gaṇhissati. Mā suttaṃ me laddhanti yaṃ vā taṃ vā avaca. Pañhaṃ vissajjentena nāma ācariyasantike vasitvā buddhavacanaṃ uggaṇhitvā attharasaṃ viditvā vattabbaṃ hotī’’ti. ‘‘Imāni satta ñāṇāni ariyasāvakassa paccavekkhaṇañāṇāneva, lokuttaramaggo bahucittakkhaṇiko nāma natthi, ekacittakkhaṇikoyevā’’ti saññāpetabbo. Sace sañjānāti sañjānātu. No ce sañjānāti, ‘‘gaccha pātova vihāraṃ pavisitvā yāguṃ pivāhī’’ti uyyojetabbo. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Kosambiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
500. *Dhammatā susamanniṭṭhā hotī* means that the nature is well ascertained.

*Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāyā* means the statement of the cause, the meaning is the knowledge of realizing the fruit of stream-entry ( *sotāpatti-phala*).

*Evaṃ sattaṅgasamannāgato* means thus, endowed with these seven great knowledges of retrospection.

This, firstly, is the similar talk of the teachers.

There is certainly no supramundane path ( *lokuttara-maggo*) that is of many moments of consciousness.

But the sophist says, "There is no path that is a single moment of consciousness, because according to the statement, 'Thus he should cultivate for seven years,' even seven years are the cultivation of the path."

But the defilements, quickly being cut off, he speaks of being cut off by seven knowledges.

He should be told to bring the sutra, for sure, not seeing another sutra, he will show by bringing this very one, "This is his first knowledge attained, this is his second knowledge...pe...this is his seventh knowledge attained."

Then he should be told, "What then is this sutra, is it interpretable or definitive?"

Then he will say - "It is of definitive meaning, the meaning is just as in the sutra."

He should be told - "What is the meaning of *dhammatā susamanniṭṭhā hoti sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāyāti ettha ko attho*?" Surely, he will say, "The meaning is the realization of the fruit of stream-entry ( *sotāpatti-phala*)."

Then he should be asked, "The one endowed with the path realizes the fruit, the one endowed with the fruit?"

Knowing, he will say, "The one endowed with the fruit realizes it."

Then he should be told - "Thus, endowed with seven factors, monks, the noble disciple is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry ( *sotāpatti-phala*), here, without cultivating the path, like a frog having jumped up, the noble disciple will only take hold of the fruit."

"May you not have found the sutra for me," or whatever he said.

The one releasing the question, having lived near the teacher, having learned the word of the Buddha, having known the taste of the meaning, should be told.

"These seven knowledges are indeed the knowledges of retrospection of the noble disciple, there is certainly no supramundane path ( *lokuttara-maggo*) that is of many moments of consciousness, it is only of one moment of consciousness," he should be made to understand.

If he understands, let him understand.

If he does not understand, he should be dismissed, "Go early in the morning, having entered the monastery, drink rice gruel."

The rest is clear throughout.

The Kosambiyasutta Commentary is finished in the *Papañcasūdanī*, a commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

mula_pali:
501. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, bhikkhave, samayaṃ ukkaṭṭhāyaṃ viharāmi subhagavane sālarājamūle. Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena bakassa brahmuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – ‘idaṃ niccaṃ, idaṃ dhuvaṃ, idaṃ sassataṃ, idaṃ kevalaṃ, idaṃ acavanadhammaṃ, idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, ito ca panaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ natthī’ti. Atha khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bakassa brahmuno cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – ukkaṭṭhāyaṃ subhagavane sālarājamūle antarahito tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahosiṃ. Addasā kho maṃ, bhikkhave, bako brahmā dūratova āgacchantaṃ; disvāna maṃ etadavoca – ‘ehi kho, mārisa, svāgataṃ, mārisa! Cirassaṃ kho, mārisa, imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Idañhi, mārisa, niccaṃ, idaṃ dhuvaṃ, idaṃ sassataṃ, idaṃ kevalaṃ, idaṃ acavanadhammaṃ, idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati. Ito ca panaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ natthī’’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bakaṃ brahmānaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘‘avijjāgato vata, bho, bako brahmā; avijjāgato vata, bho, bako brahmā; yatra hi nāma aniccaṃyeva samānaṃ niccanti vakkhati, addhuvaṃyeva samānaṃ dhuvanti vakkhati, asassataṃyeva samānaṃ sassatanti vakkhati, akevalaṃyeva samānaṃ kevalanti vakkhati, cavanadhammaṃyeva samānaṃ acavanadhammanti vakkhati; yattha ca pana jāyati jīyati mīyati cavati upapajjati tañca vakkhati – ‘idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjatī’ti; santañca panaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ ‘natthaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇa’nti vakkhatī’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, in the Jeta Grove, near Sāvatthi.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks.”

“Venerable sir,” they replied.

The Blessed One said this:

“Once, monks, I was staying at Ukkaṭṭha in the Subhaga forest, at the root of the royal sal tree.

Now on that occasion an evil viewpoint had arisen to Baka Brahma: ‘This is constant (niccaṃ). This is permanent (dhuvaṃ). This is eternal (sassataṃ). This is total (kevalaṃ). This is not subject to falling away (acavanadhammaṃ)—for this does not take birth (na jāyati), does not age (na jīyati), does not die (na mīyati), does not fall away (na cavati), does not reappear (na upapajjati). And there is no other, higher escape (nissaraṇaṃ).’

“So I—having known with my awareness the train of thought in Baka Brahma’s awareness—as a strong man would extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, vanished into the root of the royal sala tree in the Subhaga forest in Ukkaṭṭha and appeared in that Brahma world (brahmaloke).

Baka Brahma saw me coming in the distance and, on seeing me, said, ‘Come, good sir (mārisa). You are welcome (svāgataṃ), good sir! It has been long, good sir, since you took the trouble to come here.

For here, good sir, is constant (niccaṃ). This is permanent (dhuvaṃ). This is eternal (sassataṃ). This is total (kevalaṃ). This is not subject to falling away (acavanadhammaṃ)—for here one does not take birth (na jāyati), does not age (na jīyati), does not die (na mīyati), does not fall away (na cavati), does not reappear (na upapajjati). And there is no other, higher escape (nissaraṇaṃ).’

“When this was said, I told Baka Brahma, ‘How immersed in ignorance (avijjāgato) is Baka Brahma! How immersed in ignorance (avijjāgato) is Baka Brahma!—in that what is actually inconstant (aniccaṃ) he calls “constant” (niccanti). What is actually impermanent (addhuvaṃ) he calls “permanent” (dhuvanti). What is actually non-eternal (asassataṃ) he calls “eternal” (sassatanti). What is actually partial (akevalaṃ) he calls “total” (kevalanti). What is actually subject to falling away (cavanadhammaṃ) he calls “not subject to falling away” (acavanadhammanti). Where one takes birth (jāyati), ages (jīyati), dies (mīyati), falls away (cavati), and reappears (upapajjati), he says, “For here one does not take birth (na jāyati), does not age (na jīyati), does not die (na mīyati), does not fall away (na cavati), does not reappear (na upapajjati).” Though there is another, higher escape (nissaraṇaṃ), he says, “There is no other, higher escape (natthaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇa).”’”
commentary_pali: 501.Evaṃme sutanti brahmanimantanikasuttaṃ. Tattha pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigatanti lāmakā sassatadiṭṭhi. Idaṃ niccanti idaṃ saha kāyena brahmaṭṭhānaṃ aniccaṃ ‘‘nicca’’nti vadati. Dhuvādīni tasseva vevacanāni. Tattha dhuvanti thiraṃ. Sassatanti sadā vijjamānaṃ. Kevalanti akhaṇḍaṃ sakalaṃ. Acavanadhammanti acavanasabhāvaṃ.
