Idañhi na jāyatītiādīsu imasmiṃ ṭhāne koci jāyanako vā jīyanako vā mīyanako vā cavanako vā upapajjanako vā natthīti sandhāya vadati. Ito ca panaññanti ito saha kāyakā brahmaṭṭhānā uttari aññaṃ nissaraṇaṃ nāma natthīti evamassa thāmagatā sassatadiṭṭhi uppannā hoti. Evaṃvādī pana so upari tisso jhānabhūmiyo cattāro maggā cattāri phalāni nibbānanti sabbaṃ paṭibāhati. Avijjāgatoti avijjāya gato samannāgato aññāṇī andhībhūto. Yatra hi nāmāti yo nāma.

mula_pali:
502. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā aññataraṃ brahmapārisajjaṃ anvāvisitvā maṃ etadavoca – ‘bhikkhu, bhikkhu, metamāsado metamāsado, eso hi, bhikkhu, brahmā mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī issaro kattā nimmātā seṭṭho sajitā sajjitā (syā. kaṃ. ka.), sañjitā (sī. pī.) vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānaṃ. Ahesuṃ kho ye, bhikkhu, tayā pubbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā lokasmiṃ pathavīgarahakā pathavījigucchakā, āpagarahakā āpajigucchakā, tejagarahakā tejajigucchakā, vāyagarahakā vāyajigucchakā, bhūtagarahakā bhūtajigucchakā, devagarahakā devajigucchakā, pajāpatigarahakā pajāpatijigucchakā, brahmagarahakā brahmajigucchakā – te kāyassa bhedā pāṇupacchedā hīne kāye patiṭṭhitā ahesuṃ. Ye pana, bhikkhu, tayā pubbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā lokasmiṃ pathavīpasaṃsakā pathavābhinandino, āpapasaṃsakā āpābhinandino, tejapasaṃsakā tejābhinandino, vāyapasaṃsakā vāyābhinandino, bhūtapasaṃsakā bhūtābhinandino, devapasaṃsakā devābhinandino, pajāpatipasaṃsakā pajāpatābhinandino, brahmapasaṃsakā brahmābhinandino – te kāyassa bhedā pāṇupacchedā paṇīte kāye patiṭṭhitā. Taṃ tāhaṃ, bhikkhu, evaṃ vadāmi – ‘iṅgha tvaṃ, mārisa, yadeva te brahmā āha tadeva tvaṃ karohi, mā tvaṃ brahmuno vacanaṃ upātivattittho’. Sace kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, brahmuno vacanaṃ upātivattissasi, seyyathāpi nāma puriso siriṃ āgacchantiṃ daṇḍena paṭippaṇāmeyya, seyyathāpi vā pana, bhikkhu, puriso narakappapāte papatanto hatthehi ca pādehi ca pathaviṃ virādheyya, evaṃ sampadamidaṃ, bhikkhu, tuyhaṃ bhavissati. ‘Iṅghaṃ tvaṃ, mārisa, yadeva te brahmā āha tadeva tvaṃ karohi, mā tvaṃ brahmuno vacanaṃ upātivattittho. Nanu tvaṃ, bhikkhu, passasi brahmaparisaṃ sannipatita’nti? Iti kho maṃ, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā brahmaparisaṃ upanesi.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘jānāmi kho tāhaṃ, pāpima; mā tvaṃ maññittho – na maṃ jānātī’ti. Māro tvamasi, pāpima. Yo ceva, pāpima, brahmā, yā ca brahmaparisā, ye ca brahmapārisajjā, sabbeva tava hatthagatā sabbeva tava vasaṃgatā. Tuyhañhi, pāpima, evaṃ hoti – ‘esopi me assa hatthagato, esopi me assa vasaṃgato’ti. Ahaṃ kho pana, pāpima, neva tava hatthagato neva tava vasaṃgato’’ti.
mula_english:
“Then, monks, Māra the Evil One, taking possession of an attendant of the Brahma assembly, said to me, ‘Monk! Monk! Don’t attack him! Don’t attack him! For this Brahmā, monk, is the Great Brahmā, the Conqueror, the Unconquered, the All-Seeing, All-Powerful, the Sovereign Lord, the Maker, Creator, Chief, Appointer and Ruler, Father of All That Have Been and Shall Be.

There were, monk, before your time, *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* in the world who found fault with earth and were disgusted with earth, who found fault with liquid and were disgusted with liquid, who found fault with fire and were disgusted with fire, who found fault with wind and were disgusted with wind, who found fault with beings and were disgusted with beings, who found fault with *devas* and were disgusted with *devas*, who found fault with *Pajāpati* and were disgusted with *Pajāpati*, who found fault with *Brahmā* and were disgusted with *Brahmā*—they, with the break-up of the body, after death, were established in an inferior body.

There were, monk, before your time, *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* in the world who praised earth and were delighted with earth, who praised liquid and were delighted with liquid, who praised fire and were delighted with fire, who praised wind and were delighted with wind, who praised beings and were delighted with beings, who praised *devas* and were delighted with *devas*, who praised *Pajāpati* and were delighted with *Pajāpati*, who praised *Brahmā* and were delighted with *Brahmā*—they, with the break-up of the body, after death, were established in a superior body.

So I tell you, monk, “Please, good sir (*mārisa*), do only as *Brahmā* says. Don’t defy the word of *Brahmā*.”

If you defy the word of *Brahmā*, then—as a man, when the goddess of fortune approaches, chases her away with a stick, or as a man, falling into hell, loses hold of the earth with his hands and feet—that will be what you have accomplished.

Please, good sir (*mārisa*), do only as *Brahmā* says. Don’t defy the word of *Brahmā*.

“Surely, monk, you see the Brahma assembly gathered together?” In this way, monks, Māra the Evil One led me to the Brahma assembly.

When this was said, I told Māra the Evil One, ‘I know you, Evil One (*pāpima*). Don’t assume, “He doesn’t know me.”’

You are Māra, Evil One (*pāpima*).

And Brahmā, and Brahma’s assembly, and the attendants of Brahma’s assembly have all fallen into your hands. They have all fallen into your power.

And you think, “This one, too, has come into my hands, has come under my control.”

But, Evil One (*pāpima*), I have neither come into your hands nor have I come under your control.’
commentary_pali:
502.Atha kho, bhikkhave, māro pāpimāti māro kathaṃ bhagavantaṃ addasa? So kira attano bhavane nisīditvā kālena kālaṃ satthāraṃ āvajjeti – ‘‘ajja samaṇo gotamo katarasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā vasatī’’ti. Imasmiṃ pana kāle āvajjanto, ‘‘ukkaṭṭhaṃ nissāya subhagavane viharatī’’ti ñatvā, ‘‘kattha nu kho gato’’ti olokento brahmalokaṃ gacchantaṃ disvā, ‘‘samaṇo gotamo brahmalokaṃ gacchati, yāva tattha dhammakathaṃ kathetvā brahmagaṇaṃ mama visayā nātikkameti, tāva gantvā dhammadesanāyaṃ vichandaṃ karissāmī’’ti satthu padānupadiko gantvā brahmagaṇassa antare adissamānena kāyena aṭṭhāsi. So, ‘‘satthārā bakabrahmā apasādito’’ti ñatvā brahmuno upatthambho hutvā aṭṭhāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā’’ti.

Brahmapārisajjaṃ anvāvisitvāti ekassa brahmapārisajjassa sarīraṃ pavisitvā. Mahābrahmānaṃ pana brahmapurohitānaṃ vā anvāvisituṃ na sakkoti. Metamāsadoti mā etaṃ apasādayittha. Abhibhūti abhibhavitvā ṭhito jeṭṭhako. Anabhibhūtoti aññehi anabhibhūto. Aññadatthūti ekaṃsavacane nipāto. Dassanavasena daso, sabbaṃ passatīti dīpeti. Vasavattīti sabbajanaṃ vase vatteti. Issaroti loke issaro. Kattā nimmātāti lokassa kattā ca nimmātā ca, pathavīhimavantasinerucakkavāḷamahāsamuddacandimasūriyā ca iminā nimmitāti dīpeti.

Brahmapārisajjaṃ anvāvisitvā Metamāsado Abhibhū Anabhibhūto Aññadatthū daso, Vasavattī Issaro Kattā nimmātā

Seṭṭho sajitāti ayaṃ lokassa uttamo ca sajitā ca. ‘‘Tvaṃ khattiyo nāma hohi, tvaṃ brāhmaṇo nāma, vesso nāma, suddo nāma, gahaṭṭho nāma, pabbajito nāma, antamaso oṭṭho hohi, goṇo hohī’’ti evaṃ sattānaṃ visajjetā ayanti dasseti. Vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānanti ayaṃ ciṇṇavasitāya vasī, ayaṃ pitā bhūtānañca bhabyānañcāti vadati. Tattha aṇḍajajalābujā sattā antoaṇḍakose ceva antovatthimhi ca bhabyā nāma, bahi nikkhantakālato paṭṭhāya bhūtā. Saṃsedajā paṭhamacittakkhaṇe bhabyā, dutiyato paṭṭhāya bhūtā. Opapātikā paṭhamairiyāpathe bhabyā, dutiyato paṭṭhāya bhūtāti veditabbā. Te sabbepi etassa puttāti saññāya, ‘‘pitā bhūtabhabyāna’’nti āha.

Seṭṭho sajitā Vasī pitā bhūtabhabyāna bhabyā bhūtā

Pathavīgarahakāti yathā tvaṃ etarahi, ‘‘aniccā dukkhā anattā’’ti pathaviṃ garahasi jigucchasi, evaṃ tepi pathavīgarahakā ahesuṃ, na kevalaṃ tvaṃyevāti dīpeti. Āpagarahakātiādīsupi eseva nayo. Hīne kāye patiṭṭhitāti catūsu apāyesu nibbattā. Pathavīpasaṃsakāti yathā tvaṃ garahasi, evaṃ agarahitvā, ‘‘niccā dhuvā sassatā acchejjā abhejjā akkhayā’’ti evaṃ pathavīpasaṃsakā pathaviyā vaṇṇavādino ahesunti vadati. Pathavābhinandinoti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena pathaviyā abhinandino. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Paṇīte kāye patiṭṭhitāti brahmaloke nibbattā. Taṃ tāhanti tena kāraṇena taṃ ahaṃ. Iṅghāti codanatthe nipāto. Upātivattitthoti atikkamittha. ‘‘Upātivattito’’tipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Daṇḍena paṭippaṇāmeyyāti catuhatthena muggaradaṇḍena pothetvā palāpeyya. Narakapapāteti sataporise mahāsobbhe. Virādheyyāti hatthena gahaṇayutte vā pādena patiṭṭhānayutte vā ṭhāne gahaṇapatiṭṭhānāni kātuṃ na sakkuṇeyya. Nanu tvaṃ bhikkhu passasīti bhikkhu nanu tvaṃ imaṃ brahmaparisaṃ sannipatitaṃ obhāsamānaṃ virocamānaṃ jotayamānaṃ passasīti brahmuno ovāde ṭhitānaṃ iddhānubhāvaṃ dasseti. Iti kho maṃ, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā brahmaparisaṃ upanesīti, bhikkhave , māro pāpimā nanu tvaṃ bhikkhu passasi brahmaparisaṃ yasena ca siriyā ca obhāsamānaṃ virocamānaṃ jotayamānaṃ, yadi tvampi mahābrahmuno vacanaṃ anatikkamitvā yadeva te brahmā vadati, taṃ kareyyāsi, tvampi evamevaṃ yasena ca siriyā ca viroceyyāsīti evaṃ vadanto maṃ brahmaparisaṃ upanesi upasaṃhari. Mā tvaṃ maññitthoti mā tvaṃ maññi. Māro tvamasi pāpimāti pāpima tvaṃ mahājanassa māraṇato māro nāma, pāpakaṃ lāmakaṃ mahājanassa ayasaṃ karaṇato pāpimā nāmāti jānāmi.

Pathavīgarahakā Āpagarahakā Hīne kāye patiṭṭhitā Pathavīpasaṃsakā Pathavābhinandino Paṇīte kāye patiṭṭhitā Taṃ tāha Iṅghā Upātivattittho Daṇḍena paṭippaṇāmeyyā Narakapapāte Virādheyyā Nanu tvaṃ bhikkhu passasī Iti kho maṃ, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā brahmaparisaṃ upanesī Mā tvaṃ maññittho Māro tvamasi pāpimā māro pāpimā
commentary_english:
502. Then, monks, Māra the Evil One: How did Māra see the Blessed One? It seems that he, sitting in his own palace, would periodically turn his attention to the Teacher, thinking, “Today, in which village or town does the ascetic Gotama reside?”

However, while turning his attention at this time, having realized that "[he] dwells in Subhaga Grove, relying on Ukkaṭṭha," and looking to see "where has he gone?" he saw him going to the Brahma world. [Māra thought:] "The ascetic Gotama is going to the Brahma world. Before he can preach the Dharma there and lead the Brahma host beyond my domain, I will go and disrupt his Dharma teaching." Following closely behind the Teacher, he stood within the Brahma host with an invisible body.

Realizing that "the Teacher has displeased Baka Brahma," he stood as a support for Brahma.

Therefore it was said: "Then, monks, Māra the Evil One."

"Having possessed a member of Brahmā’s retinue": Having entered the body of one of Brahmā’s attendants.

But he cannot possess Mahābrahmā or the chaplains of Brahmā.

"Métaṃ āsado": He did not please him.

"Abhibhū": Having overcome, the chief one stands.

"Anabhibhūto": Unvanquished by others.

"Aññadatthū": The particle *aññadatthū* is used in the sense of the একṃsa-vacana.

"Dasa" in terms of seeing indicates that he sees everything.

"Vasavattī": He controls all people.

"Issaro": The lord in the world.

"Kattā nimmātā": The creator and maker of the world. He indicates that the earth, Himavant, Sineru, the circle of the world, the great ocean, the moon, and the sun were created by him.

Having possessed a member of Brahmā’s retinue, not pleasing him, having overcome, unvanquished by others, *aññadatthū*, *dasa*, *vasavattī*, *issaro*, creator and maker.

"Seṭṭho sajitā": He is the highest and the conqueror of the world. He shows that he is the one who assigns beings, saying, "You be a Khattiya, you be a Brāhmaṇa, a Vessa, a Sudda, a householder, a renunciant, even be a camel or an ox."

"Vasī pitā bhūtabhabyāna": He is a master by habitual mastery; he says that he is the father of beings that have come to be and will come to be.

There, beings born from eggs, wombs, and moisture are called "will come to be" while still inside the eggshell and inside the womb, but from the time they emerge, they are "have come to be".

Beings born spontaneously are "will come to be" at the first moment of consciousness, but from the second moment on, they "have come to be".

It should be understood that beings born through spontaneous appearance are "will come to be" at the first arising of movement, but from the second arising on, they "have come to be."

Because all of these are called his children, he says, "father of beings that have come to be and will come to be."

Highest and conqueror, master, father of beings that have come to be and will come to be, will come to be, have come to be.

"Pathavīgarahakā": Just as you now despise and revile the earth, saying "impermanent, suffering, not-self," so were those who despised the earth; he indicates that it is not only you.

The same method applies to "āpagarahakā" and so on.

"Hīne kāye patiṭṭhitā": Born in the four woeful states.

"Pathavīpasaṃsakā": Just as you revile it, without reviling it, saying, "permanent, stable, eternal, unbreakable, impenetrable, indestructible," so those who praised the earth, who spoke well of the earth, were.

"Pathavābhinandino": Those who rejoiced in the earth through craving and wrong view. The same method applies to the rest.

"Paṇīte kāye patiṭṭhitā": Born in the Brahma world.

"Taṃ tāha": Therefore, I say that.

"Iṅgha": The particle *iṅgha* is used in the sense of exhortation.

"Upātivattittho": He transgressed.

"Upātivattito" is also a reading, the meaning is the same.

"Daṇḍena paṭippaṇāmeyya": He should drive them away by striking them with a club four cubits long.
*Narakapapāte* means in the *sataporisa mahāsobbha* [hell].

*Virādheyyā*, at [page number 2.0407], by hand, being yoked to grasping, or by foot, being yoked to a place of standing, is unable to do grasping or standing in that place.

*Nanu tvaṃ bhikṣu passasī* means, "Bhikkhu, do you see this assembly of Brahmā, gathered together, shining, radiant, and gleaming?" Thus, he shows the power of splendor to those standing by the instruction of Brahmā, at [page number 2.0304].

*Iti kho maṃ, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā brahmaparisaṃ upanesī* means, "Thus, monks, Māra the Evil One led me to the assembly of Brahmā," at [page number 2.0300]. Māra the Evil One [asked], "Bhikkhu, do you see the assembly of Brahmā shining with glory and splendor, radiant and gleaming? If you, too, without transgressing the word of the Great Brahmā, would do as Brahmā tells you, you too would shine with glory and splendor!" Thus, saying this, he brought me near and introduced me to the assembly of Brahmā.

*Mā tvaṃ maññittho* means, do not think yourself.

*Māro tvamasi pāpimā* means, "Evil one, you are called *Māra* because you cause the death of the great multitude; I know that you are called *Pāpimā* because you cause what is evil and worthless to the great multitude, [causing them] misfortune."

Those who despise the earth, those who despise water, those who are established in a base body, those who praise the earth, those who rejoice in the earth, those who are established in a refined body—so he says. "Come, do not defy! He would chase [her] away with a stick; in the hellish fall, he would lose hold."

*Nanu tvaṃ bhikṣu passasī*, at [page number 2.0407].

*Iti kho maṃ, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā brahmaparisaṃ upanesī*, at [page number 2.0304].

*Mā tvaṃ maññittho*, *Māro tvamasi pāpimā*, *Māro*, *Pāpimā*, at [page number 2.0300].

mula_pali:
503. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, bako brahmā maṃ etadavoca – ‘ahañhi, mārisa, niccaṃyeva samānaṃ niccanti vadāmi, dhuvaṃyeva samānaṃ dhuvanti vadāmi, sassataṃyeva samānaṃ sassatanti vadāmi, kevalaṃyeva samānaṃ kevalanti vadāmi, acavanadhammaṃyeva samānaṃ acavanadhamma’nti vadāmi, yattha ca pana na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati tadevāhaṃ vadāmi – ‘idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjatī’ti. Asantañca panaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ ‘natthaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇa’nti vadāmi. Ahesuṃ kho, bhikkhu, tayā pubbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā lokasmiṃ yāvatakaṃ tuyhaṃ kasiṇaṃ āyu tāvatakaṃ tesaṃ tapokammameva ahosi. Te kho evaṃ jāneyyuṃ – ‘santañca panaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ atthaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇanti, asantaṃ vā aññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ natthaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇa’nti. Taṃ tāhaṃ, bhikkhu, evaṃ vadāmi – ‘na cevaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ dakkhissasi, yāvadeva ca pana kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī bhavissasi. Sace kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, pathaviṃ ajjhosissasi, opasāyiko me bhavissasi vatthusāyiko, yathākāmakaraṇīyo bāhiteyyo. Sace āpaṃ… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ ajjhosissasi, opasāyiko me bhavissasi vatthusāyiko, yathākāmakaraṇīyo bāhiteyyo’ti.

‘‘Ahampi kho evaṃ, brahme, jānāmi – sace pathaviṃ ajjhosissāmi, opasāyiko te bhavissāmi vatthusāyiko, yathākāmakaraṇīyo bāhiteyyo. ‘Sace āpaṃ… tejaṃ… vāyaṃ… bhūte… deve… pajāpatiṃ… brahmaṃ ajjhosissāmi, opasāyiko te bhavissāmi vatthusāyiko, yathākāmakaraṇīyo bāhiteyyo’ti api ca te ahaṃ, brahme, gatiñca pajānāmi, jutiñca pajānāmi – evaṃ mahiddhiko bako brahmā, evaṃ mahānubhāvo bako brahmā, evaṃ mahesakkho bako brahmā’’ti.

‘‘Yathākathaṃ pana me tvaṃ, mārisa, gatiñca pajānāsi, jutiñca pajānāsi – ‘evaṃ mahiddhiko bako brahmā, evaṃ mahānubhāvo bako brahmā, evaṃ mahesakkho bako brahmā’ti?

‘‘Yāvatā candimasūriyā, pariharanti disā bhanti virocanā;

Tāva sahassadhā loko, ettha te vattate vattatī (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vaso.

vattatī (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Paroparañca parovarañca (sī. pī.) jānāsi, atho rāgavirāginaṃ;

parovarañca (sī. pī.)

Itthabhāvaññathābhāvaṃ, sattānaṃ āgatiṃ gati’’nti.

‘‘Evaṃ kho te ahaṃ, brahme, gatiñca pajānāmi jutiñca pajānāmi – ‘evaṃ mahiddhiko bako brahmā, evaṃ mahānubhāvo bako brahmā, evaṃ mahesakkho bako brahmā’ti.
mula_english:
503. “When this was said, venerable monks, Baka Brahmā said this to me: ‘Indeed, dear sir, what is actually constant ( *nicca*) I call “constant ( *nicca*) .” What is actually permanent (*dhruva*) I call “permanent (*dhruva*).” What is actually eternal (*sassata*) I call “eternal (*sassata*).” What is actually total (*kevala*) I call “total (*kevala*).” What is actually not subject to falling away (*acavanadhamma*) I call “not subject to falling away (*acavanadhamma*).” And where one does not take birth (*jāyati*), age (*jīyati*), die (*mīyati*), fall away (*cavati*), or reappear (*upapajjati*), that I call – ‘For this does not take birth (*jāyati*), does not age (*jīyati*), does not die (*mīyati*), does not fall away (*cavati*), does not reappear (*upapajjati*)’.’

And there being no other, higher escape, I say, “There is no other, higher escape.”

“There were, monk, before your time, *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s in the world whose ascetic practice lasted as long as your entire life span.

They knew, when there was another, higher escape, that there was another, higher escape; or, when there was no other, higher escape, that there was no other, higher escape.”

So I tell you, monk, both that you will not find another, higher escape, and that, to that extent, you will reap your share of trouble & weariness.

Monk, if you relish earth ( *pathavī*), you will lie close to me, lie within my domain, for me to banish and to do with as I like.

If you relish water (*āpa*), fire (*teja*), wind (*vāyu*), beings (*bhūta*), gods (*deva*), *prajāpati*, *brahman*, you will lie close to me, lie within my domain, for me to banish and to do with as I like.’

“I, too, Brahmā, know this: If I relish earth (*pathavī*), I will lie close to you, lie within your domain, for you to banish and to do with as you like.

If I relish water (*āpa*), fire (*teja*), wind (*vāyu*), beings (*bhūta*), gods (*deva*), *prajāpati*, *brahman*, I will lie close to you, lie within your domain, for you to banish and to do with as you like. Moreover, I discern your sphere, I discern your splendor: “Baka Brahmā has this much great power. Baka Brahmā has this much great might. Baka Brahmā has this much great influence.” ‘

“Well, how do you discern my sphere, how do you discern my splendor: “Baka Brahmā has this much great power. Baka Brahmā has this much great might. Baka Brahmā has this much great influence”?

As far as the moon and sun revolve, illuminating the directions with their light,

over a thousand-fold world your control holds sway, radiant one.

You know what is higher and lower, and also those with and without passion;

the state of being thus and otherwise, and the coming and going of beings.”

“That, Brahmā, is how I discern your sphere, that is how I discern your splendor: “Baka Brahmā has this much great power. Baka Brahmā has this much great might. Baka Brahmā has this much great influence.”
commentary_pali:
503.Kasiṇaṃ āyunti sakalaṃ āyuṃ. Te kho evaṃ jāneyyunti te evaṃ mahantena tapokammena samannāgatā, tvaṃ pana purimadivase jāto, kiṃ jānissasi, yassa te ajjāpi mukhe khīragandho vāyatīti ghaṭṭento vadati. Pathaviṃ ajjhosissasīti pathaviṃ ajjhosāya gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā taṇhāmānadiṭṭhīhi gaṇhissasi. Opasāyiko me bhavissasīti mayhaṃ samīpasayo bhavissasi, maṃ gacchantaṃ anugacchissasi, ṭhitaṃ upatiṭṭhissasi, nisinnaṃ upanisīdissasi, nipannaṃ upanipajjissasīti attho. Vatthusāyikoti mama vatthusmiṃ sayanako. Yathākāmakaraṇīyo bāhiteyyoti mayā attano ruciyā yaṃ icchāmi, taṃ kattabbo, bāhitvā ca pana jajjharikāgumbatopi nīcataro lakuṇḍaṭakataro kātabbo bhavissasīti attho.

Iminā esa bhagavantaṃ upalāpeti vā apasādeti vā. Upalāpeti nāma sace kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, taṇhādīhi pathaviṃ ajjhosissasi, opasāyiko me bhavissasi, mayi gacchante gamissasi, tiṭṭhante ṭhassasi, nisinne nisīdissasi, nipanne nipajjissasi, ahaṃ taṃ sesajanaṃ paṭibāhitvā vissāsikaṃ abbhantarikaṃ karissāmīti evaṃ tāva upalāpeti nāma. Sesapadehi pana apasādeti nāma. Ayañhettha adhippāyo – sace tvaṃ pathaviṃ ajjhosissasi, vatthusāyiko me bhavissasi, mama gamanādīni āgametvā gamissasi vā ṭhassasi vā nisīdissasi vā nipajjissasi vā, mama vatthusmiṃ mayhaṃ ārakkhaṃ gaṇhissasi, ahaṃ pana taṃ yathākāmaṃ karissāmi bāhitvā ca jajjharikāgumbatopi lakuṇḍakataranti evaṃ apasādeti nāma. Ayaṃ pana brahmā mānanissito, tasmā idha apasādanāva adhippetā. Āpādīsupi eseva nayo.

Upalāpeti upalāpeti apasādeti Āpādīsupi

Apicate ahaṃ brahmeti idāni bhagavā, ‘‘ayaṃ brahmā mānanissito ‘ahaṃ jānāmī’ti maññati, attano yasena sammatto sarīraṃ phusitumpi samatthaṃ kiñci na passati, thokaṃ niggahetuṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti cintetvā imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha gatiñca pajānāmīti nipphattiñca pajānāmi. Jutiñcāti ānubhāvañca pajānāmi. Evaṃ mahesakkhoti evaṃ mahāyaso mahāparivāro.

Apica te ahaṃ brahme gatiñca pajānāmī Jutiñcā Evaṃ mahesakkho

Yāvatā candimasūriyā pariharantīti yattake ṭhāne candimasūriyā vicaranti. Disā bhanti virocanāti disāsu virocamānā obhāsanti, disā vā tehi virocamānā obhāsanti. Tāva sahassadhā lokoti tattakena pamāṇena sahassadhā loko, iminā cakkavāḷena saddhiṃ cakkavāḷasahassanti attho. Ettha te vattate vasoti ettha cakkavāḷasahasse tuyhaṃ vaso vattati. Paroparañca jānāsīti ettha cakkavāḷasahasse paropare uccanīce hīnappaṇīte satte jānāsi. Atho rāgavirāginanti na kevalaṃ, ‘‘ayaṃ iddho ayaṃ pakatimanusso’’ti paroparaṃ, ‘‘ayaṃ pana sarāgo ayaṃ vītarāgo’’ti evaṃ rāgavirāginampi janaṃ jānāsi. Itthaṃbhāvaññathābhāvanti itthaṃbhāvoti idaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ. Aññathābhāvoti ito sesaṃ ekūnasahassaṃ. Sattānaṃ āgatiṃ gatinti ettha cakkavāḷasahasse paṭisandhivasena sattānaṃ āgatiṃ, cutivasena gatiṃ ca jānāsi. Tuyhaṃ pana atimahantohamasmīti saññā hoti, sahassibrahmā nāma tvaṃ, aññesaṃ pana tayā uttari dvisahassānaṃ tisahassānaṃ catusahassānaṃ pañcasahassānaṃ dasasahassānaṃ satasahassānañca brahmānaṃ pamāṇaṃ natthi, catuhatthāya pilotikāya paṭappamāṇaṃ kātuṃ vāyamanto viya mahantosmīti saññaṃ karosīti niggaṇhāti.

Yāvatā candimasūriyā pariharantī Disā bhanti virocanā Tāva sahassadhā loko Ettha te vattate vaso Paroparañca jānāsī Atho rāgavirāgina Itthaṃbhāvaññathābhāva itthaṃbhāvo Aññathābhāvo Sattānaṃ āgatiṃ gati
commentary_english:
503. *Kasiṇaṃ āyu* means the entirety of life.

*Te kho evaṃ jāneyyu* means they are endowed with such great ascetic practice. But you were born just the other day. What will you know? Even now, the smell of milk wafts from your mouth," he says, rebuking him.

*Pathaviṃ ajjhosissasi* means you will take hold of the earth, swallowing it, having completely determined [it] with craving, conceit, and views.

*Opasāyiko me bhavissasi* means you will be one who lies near to me. You will follow me as I go; you will attend me standing; you will sit down close when I am sitting; you will lie down close when I am lying down. This is the meaning.

*Vatthusāyiko* means one who lies in my territory.

*Yathākāmakaraṇīyo bāhiteyyo* means I will do what I want by the inclination of my own heart. And having driven [you] out, you will be made lower, even, than a dilapidated hut, even more insignificant than a *lakuṇḍaka* plant. This is the meaning.

By this, he either flatters or disparages the Blessed One.

*Upalāpeti* means, "Indeed, if you, *bhikkhu*, take hold of the earth with craving, etc., you will be one who lies near to me. As I go, you will go; standing, you will stand; sitting, you will sit; lying down, you will lie down. Having driven away the rest of the people, I will make you a confidant, an intimate," thus, to this extent, he flatters.

By the remaining words, however, he disparages.

Here, the intention is this: If you take hold of the earth, you will be one who lies in my territory. Having awaited my going, etc., you will go, or you will stand, or you will sit down, or you will lie down. In my territory, you will take up the protection for me. But I, having driven [you] out, will do as I please, even lower than a dilapidated hut, even more insignificant than a *lakuṇḍaka* plant," thus he disparages.

Now, this Brahmā is dependent on conceit. Therefore, here, only disparagement is intended.

*Āpādīsupi*, the same is the method.

*Upalāpeti*.

*Upalāpeti*, *apasādeti*.

*Āpādīsupi*. Moreover,

*Te ahaṃ brahme* means now, the Blessed One [thought], "This Brahmā is dependent on conceit, thinking, 'I know.' Intoxicated by his own glory, he does not see anything capable even of touching [his] body. It is fitting to restrain [him] a little," and having thought [this], he began this teaching.

There, *gatiñca pajānāmi* means I know also the rebirth.

*Jutiñcā* means I know also the power.

*Evaṃ mahesakkho* means thus, of great fame, of a great retinue.

Moreover,

*Te ahaṃ brahme*, *gatiñca pajānāmi*, *jutiñcā*, *evaṃ mahesakkho*.

*Yāvatā candimasūriyā pariharantī* means in whatever place the moon and sun move about.

*Disā bhanti virocanā* means the directions shine, illuminating, or the directions shine, illuminated by them.

*Tāva sahassadhā loko* means with that much extent, a thousandfold world, together with this *cakkavāḷa*, a thousand *cakkavāḷas*. This is the meaning.

*Ettha te vattate vaso* means here, in [this] thousandfold *cakkavāḷa*, your power prevails.

*Paroparañca jānāsī* means here, in [this] thousandfold *cakkavāḷa*, you know beings high and low, inferior and excellent.

*Atho rāgavirāgina* means not only *paroparaṃ*, [thinking], "This one is prosperous, this one is a natural human," but also, "This one is passionate, this one is without passion," thus, you know also people with and without passion.

*Itthaṃbhāvaññathābhāva* means *itthaṃbhāvo* is this *cakkavāḷa*.

*Aññathābhāvo* means the remainder, one less than a thousand.

*Sattānaṃ āgatiṃ gati* means here, in [this] thousandfold *cakkavāḷa*, you know the coming of beings in terms of rebirth, and the going in terms of decease.

But to you, there is the idea, "I am exceedingly great!" You are named Sahassibrahmā, but by you, furthermore, the measure of the Brahmās of two thousand, three thousand, four thousand, five thousand, ten thousand, [and] one hundred thousand is not reached. Like one striving to make a likeness with a four-cubit doll, you make the idea, "I am great!" Thus, he restrains [him].

*Yāvatā candimasūriyā pariharantī*, *disā bhanti virocanā*, *tāva sahassadhā loko*, *ettha te vattate vaso*, *paroparañca jānāsī*, *atho rāgavirāgina*, *itthaṃbhāvaññathābhāva*, *itthaṃbhāvo*, *aññathābhāvo*, *sattānaṃ āgatiṃ gati*.

mula_pali:
504. ‘‘Atthi kho, brahme, añño kāyo, taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi; tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. Atthi kho, brahme, ābhassarā nāma kāyo yato tvaṃ cuto idhūpapanno. Tassa te aticiranivāsena sā sati pamuṭṭhā, tena taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi; tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. Evampi kho ahaṃ, brahme, neva te samasamo abhiññāya, kuto nīceyyaṃ? Atha kho ahameva tayā bhiyyo. Atthi kho, brahme, subhakiṇho nāma kāyo, vehapphalo nāma kāyo, abhibhū nāma kāyo, taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi na passasi; tamahaṃ jānāmi passāmi. Evampi kho ahaṃ, brahme, neva te samasamo abhiññāya, kuto nīceyyaṃ? Atha kho ahameva tayā bhiyyo. Pathaviṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme, pathavito abhiññāya yāvatā pathaviyā pathavattena ananubhūtaṃ tadabhiññāya pathaviṃ nāpahosiṃ, pathaviyā nāpahosiṃ, pathavito nāpahosiṃ, pathaviṃ meti nāpahosiṃ, pathaviṃ nābhivadiṃ. Evampi kho ahaṃ, brahme, neva te samasamo abhiññāya, kuto nīceyyaṃ? Atha kho ahameva tayā bhiyyo. Āpaṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… tejaṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… vāyaṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… bhūte kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… deve kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… pajāpatiṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… brahmaṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… ābhassare kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… subhakiṇhe kho ahaṃ, brahme… …pe… vehapphale kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… abhibhuṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme…pe… sabbaṃ kho ahaṃ, brahme, sabbato abhiññāya yāvatā sabbassa sabbattena ananubhūtaṃ tadabhiññāya sabbaṃ nāpahosiṃ sabbasmiṃ nāpahosiṃ sabbato nāpahosiṃ sabbaṃ meti nāpahosiṃ, sabbaṃ nābhivadiṃ. Evampi kho ahaṃ, brahme, neva te samasamo abhiññāya, kuto nīceyyaṃ? Atha kho ahameva tayā bhiyyo’’ti.

‘‘Sace kho, mārisa, sabbassa sabbattena ananubhūtaṃ, tadabhiññāya mā heva te rittakameva ahosi, tucchakameva ahosī’’ti .

‘‘‘Viññāṇaṃ anidassanaṃ anantaṃ sabbato pabhaṃ’, taṃ pathaviyā pathavattena ananubhūtaṃ, āpassa āpattena ananubhūtaṃ, tejassa tejattena ananubhūtaṃ, vāyassa vāyattena ananubhūtaṃ, bhūtānaṃ bhūtattena ananubhūtaṃ, devānaṃ devattena ananubhūtaṃ, pajāpatissa pajāpatittena ananubhūtaṃ, brahmānaṃ brahmattena ananubhūtaṃ, ābhassarānaṃ ābhassarattena ananubhūtaṃ, subhakiṇhānaṃ subhakiṇhattena ananubhūtaṃ, vehapphalānaṃ vehapphalatte ananubhūtaṃ, abhibhussa abhibhuttena ananubhūtaṃ, sabbassa sabbattena ananubhūtaṃ’’.

‘‘Handa carahi handa ca hi (sī. pī.) te, mārisa, passa antaradhāyāmī’’ti. ‘Handa carahi me tvaṃ, brahme, antaradhāyassu, sace visahasī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, bako brahmā ‘antaradhāyissāmi samaṇassa gotamassa, antaradhāyissāmi samaṇassa gotamassā’ti nevassu me sakkoti antaradhāyituṃ.

handa ca hi (sī. pī.)

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bakaṃ brahmānaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘handa carahi te brahme antaradhāyāmī’ti. ‘Handa carahi me tvaṃ, mārisa, antaradhāyassu sace visahasī’ti. Atha kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsiṃ – ‘ettāvatā brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā ca saddañca me sossanti saddameva suyyanti (ka.), na ca maṃ dakkhantī’ti. Antarahito imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsiṃ –

saddameva suyyanti (ka.)

‘‘Bhavevāhaṃ bhayaṃ disvā, bhavañca vibhavesinaṃ;

Bhavaṃ nābhivadiṃ kiñci, nandiñca na upādiyi’’nti.

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā ca acchariyabbhutacittajātā ahesuṃ – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho! Samaṇassa gotamassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, na ca vata no ito pubbe diṭṭho vā, suto vā, añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃ mahiddhiko evaṃ mahānubhāvo yathāyaṃ samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito. Bhavarāmāya vata, bho, pajāya bhavaratāya bhavasammuditāya samūlaṃ bhavaṃ udabbahī’ti.
mula_english:
504. “‘There is, brahma, another body that you don’t know, don’t see, but that I know, I see.

There is, brahma, the body named Ābhassarā from which you fell away and reappeared here.

From your having lived here so long, your memory of that has become muddled. That is why you don’t know it, don’t see it, but I know it, I see it.

Thus I am not your mere equal in terms of direct knowing, so how could I be inferior? Now, I am actually superior to you.

“‘There is, brahma, the body named Subhakiṇha, the body named Vehapphala, {the body named Abhibhu} which you don’t know, don’t see, but that I know, I see.

Thus I am not your mere equal in terms of direct knowing, so how could I be inferior? Now, I am actually superior to you.

‘Having directly known earth as earth, and having directly known the extent of what has not been experienced through the earthness of earth, I wasn’t earth, I wasn’t in earth, I wasn’t coming from earth, I wasn’t “Earth is mine.” I didn’t affirm earth.

Thus I am not your mere equal in terms of direct knowing, so how could I be inferior? Now, I am actually superior to you.

‘Having directly known liquid as liquid … fire as fire … wind as wind … beings as beings … devas as devas … Pajāpati as Pajāpati … Brahmā as Brahmā … the radiant as radiant … the beautiful black as the beautiful black … the sky-fruit as the sky-fruit … the conqueror as the conqueror … “‘Having directly known the all as the all, and having directly known the extent of what has not been experienced through the allness of the all, I wasn’t the all, I wasn’t in the all, I wasn’t coming forth from the all, I wasn’t “The all is mine.” I didn’t affirm the all.

Thus I am not your mere equal in terms of direct knowing, so how could I be inferior? Now, I am actually superior to you.’”

“‘If, good sir, what has not been experienced through the allness of the all, through directly knowing that, may it not be that you were just empty, you were just hollow?’”

‘‘‘Consciousness without surface, endless, radiant all around, has not been experienced through the earthness of earth … the liquidity of liquid … the fieriness of fire … the windiness of wind … the allness of the all.’

“‘Well then, good sir, I will disappear from you.’

‘Well then, brahma, disappear from me if you can.’

“Then, monks, Baka Brahmā, thinking, ‘I will disappear from Gotama the contemplative. I will disappear from Gotama the contemplative,’ was not able to disappear from me.

“When this was said, I, monks, said this to Baka Brahmā: ‘Well then, brahma, I will disappear from you.’

‘Well then, good sir, disappear from me if you can.’

“So then, monks, I fabricated a fabrication of psychic power to the extent that Brahmā, the Brahmā assembly, and the attendants of the Brahmā assembly heard my voice but did not see me.

Having disappeared, I spoke this verse:

‘‘Having seen fear in becoming, and those set on becoming,

I affirmed nothing in becoming, and I didn’t appropriate delight.’’

“Then, monks, Brahmā, the Brahmā assembly, and the attendants of the Brahmā assembly were amazed, awestruck: ‘Amazing, truly, sir! Astounding, truly, sir! — The great power, the great might of Gotama the contemplative! Never before have we seen or heard of any other contemplative or *brāhmaṇa* of such great power, such great might as that of this Gotama the contemplative, who went forth from a Sakyan clan!

Living in a generation that so delights in becoming, so rejoices in becoming, is so fond of becoming, he has pulled out becoming by the root!’”

commentary_pali:
504.Idhūpapannoti idha paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyaṃ upapanno. Tena taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsīti tena kāraṇena taṃ kāyaṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi. Neva te samasamoti jānitabbaṭṭhānaṃ patvāpi tayā samasamo na homi. Abhiññāyāti aññāya. Kuto nīceyyanti tayā nīcatarabhāvo pana mayhaṃ kuto.

Heṭṭhūpapattiko kiresa brahmā anuppanne buddhuppāde isipabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā samāpattiyo nibbattetvā aparihīnajjhāno kālaṃ katvā catutthajjhānabhūmiyaṃ vehapphalabrahmaloke pañcakappasatikaṃ āyuṃ gahetvā nibbatti. Tattha yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā heṭṭūpapattikaṃ katvā tatiyajjhānaṃ paṇītaṃ bhāvetvā subhakiṇhabrahmaloke catusaṭṭhikappaṃ āyuṃ gahetvā nibbatti. Tattha dutiyajjhānaṃ bhāvetvā ābhassaresu aṭṭhakappaṃ āyuṃ gahetvā nibbatti. Tattha paṭhamajjhānaṃ bhāvetvā paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyaṃ kappāyuko hutvā nibbatti, so paṭhamakāle attanā katakammañca nibbattaṭṭhānañca aññāsi, kāle pana gacchante ubhayaṃ pamussitvā sassatadiṭṭhiṃ uppādesi. Tena naṃ bhagavā, ‘‘tena taṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi…pe… kuto nīceyya’’nti āha.

Atha brahmā cintesi – ‘‘samaṇo gotamo mayhaṃ āyuñca nibbattaṭṭhānañca pubbekatakammañca jānāti, handa naṃ pubbe katakammaṃ pucchāmī’’ti satthāraṃ attano pubbekatakammaṃ pucchi. Satthā kathesi.

Pubbe kiresa kulaghare nibbattitvā kāmesu ādīnavaṃ disvā, ‘‘jātijarābyādhimaraṇassa antaṃ karissāmī’’ti nikkhamma isipabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā samāpattiyo nibbattetvā abhiññāpādakajjhānalābhī hutvā gaṅgātīre paṇṇasālaṃ kāretvā jhānaratiyā vītināmeti. Tadā ca kālena kālaṃ satthavāhā pañcahi sakaṭasatehi marukantāraṃ paṭipajjanti. Marukantāre pana divā na sakkā gantuṃ, rattiṃ gamanaṃ hoti. Atha purimasakaṭassa aggayuge yuttabalibaddā gacchantā nivattitvā āgatamaggābhimukhāva ahesuṃ. Itarasakaṭāni tatheva nivattitvā aruṇe uggate nivattitabhāvaṃ jāniṃsu. Tesañca tadā kantāraṃ atikkamanadivaso ahosi. Sabbaṃ dārudakaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ, tasmā, ‘‘natthi dāni amhākaṃ jīvita’’nti cintetvā goṇe cakkesu bandhitvā manussā sakaṭapacchāyāyaṃ pavisitvā nipajjiṃsu . Tāpasopi kālasseva paṇṇasālato nikkhamitvā paṇṇasāladvāre nisinno gaṅgaṃ olokayamāno addasa gaṅgaṃ mahatā udakoghena vuyhamānaṃ pavattitamaṇikkhandhaṃ viya āgacchantiṃ. Disvā cintesi – ‘‘atthi nu kho imasmiṃ loke evarūpassa madhurodakassa alābhena kilissamānā sattā’’ti. So evaṃ āvajjanto marukantāre taṃ satthaṃ disvā, ‘‘ime sattā mā nassantū’’ti, ‘‘ito mahā udakakkhandho chijjitvā marukantāre satthābhimukho gacchatū’’ti abhiññācittena adhiṭṭhāsi. Sahacittuppādena mātikāruḷhaṃ viya udakaṃ tattha agamāsi. Manussā udakasaddena vuṭṭhāya udakaṃ disvā hatthatuṭṭhā nhāyitvā pivitvā goṇepi pāyetvā sotthinā icchitaṭṭhānaṃ agamaṃsu. Satthā taṃ brahmuno pubbakammaṃ dassento –

‘‘Yaṃ tvaṃ apāyesi bahū manusse,

Pipāsite ghammani samparete;

Taṃ te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.71) –

Imaṃ gāthamāha.

Aparasmiṃ samaye tāpaso gaṅgātīre paṇṇasālaṃ māpetvā āraññakaṃ gāmaṃ nissāya vasati. Tena ca samayena corā taṃ gāmaṃ paharitvā hatthasāraṃ gahetvā gāviyo ca karamare ca gahetvā gacchanti. Gāvopi sunakhāpi manussāpi mahāviravaṃ viravanti. Tāpaso taṃ saddaṃ sutvā ‘‘kiṃ nu kho eta’’nti āvajjanto, ‘‘manussānaṃ bhayaṃ uppanna’’nti ñatvā, ‘‘mayi passante ime sattā mā nassantū’’ti abhiññāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya abhiññācittena corānaṃ paṭipathe caturaṅginisenaṃ māpesi kammasajjaṃ āgacchantiṃ. Corā disvā, ‘‘rājā’’ti te maññamānā vilopaṃ chaḍḍetvā pakkamiṃsu. Tāpaso ‘‘yaṃ yassa santakaṃ, taṃ tasseva hotū’’ti adhiṭṭhāsi, taṃ tatheva ahosi. Mahājano sotthibhāvaṃ pāpuṇi. Satthā idampi tassa pubbakammaṃ dassento –

‘‘Yaṃ eṇikūlasmiṃ janaṃ gahītaṃ,

Amocayī gayhaka nīyamānaṃ;

Taṃ te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.72) –

Imaṃ gāthamāha. Ettha eṇikūlasminti gaṅgātīre.

eṇikūlasmi

Puna ekasmiṃ samaye uparigaṅgāvāsikaṃ kulaṃ heṭṭhāgaṅgāvāsikena kulena saddhiṃ mittasanthavaṃ katvā nāvāsaṅghāṭaṃ bandhitvā bahuṃ khādanīyabhojanīyañceva gandhamālādīni ca āropetvā gaṅgāsotena āgacchati. Manussā khādamānā bhuñjamānā naccantā gāyantā devavimānena gacchantā viya balavasomanassā ahesuṃ. Gaṅgeyyako nāgo disvā kupito, ‘‘ime mayi saññampi na karonti, idāni ne samuddameva pāpessāmī’’ti mahantaṃ attabhāvaṃ māpetvā udakaṃ dvidhā bhinditvā uṭṭhāya phaṇaṃ katvā sussūkāraṃ karonto aṭṭhāsi. Mahājano disvā bhīto vissaramakāsi. Tāpaso paṇṇasālāya nisinno sutvā, ‘‘ime gāyantā naccantā somanassajātā āgacchanti, idāni pana bhayaravaṃ raviṃsu, kiṃ nu kho’’ti āvajjanto nāgarājaṃ disvā, ‘‘mayi passante ime sattā mā nassantū’’ti abhiññāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā attabhāvaṃ vijahitvā supaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ māpetvā nāgarājassa dassesi. Nāgarājā bhīto phaṇaṃ saṃharitvā udakaṃ paviṭṭho. Mahājano sotthibhāvaṃ pāpuṇi. Satthā idampi tassa pubbakammaṃ dassento –

‘‘Gaṅgāya sotasmiṃ gahītanāvaṃ,

Luddena nāgena manussakappā;

Amocayittha balasā pasayha,

Taṃ te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ;

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.73) –

Imaṃ gāthamāha.

Aparasmiṃ samaye esa isipabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā kesavo nāma tāpaso ahosi. Tena samayena amhākaṃ bodhisatto kappo nāma māṇavo kesavassa baddhacaro antevāsiko hutvā ācariyassa kiṃkārapaṭissāvī manāpacārī buddhisampanno atthacaro ahosi. Kesavo taṃ vinā vattituṃ nāsakkhi, taṃ nissāyeva jīvikaṃ kappesi. Satthā idampi tassa pubbakammaṃ dassento –

kesavo kappo

‘‘Kappo ca te baddhacaro ahosi,

Sambuddhimantaṃ vatinaṃ amaññi;

Taṃ te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmī’’ti. (jā. 1.7.74) –

Imaṃ gāthamāha.

Evaṃ brahmuno nānattabhāvesu katakammaṃ satthā pakāsesi. Satthari kathenteyeva brahmā sallakkhesi, dīpasahasse ujjalite rūpāni viya sabbakammānissa pākaṭāni ahesuṃ. So pasannacitto imaṃ gāthamāha –

‘‘Addhā pajānāsi mametamāyuṃ,

Aññampi jānāsi tathā hi buddho;

Tathā hi tāyaṃ jalitānubhāvo,

Obhāsayaṃ tiṭṭhati brahmaloka’’nti. (jā. 1.7.75);

Athassa bhagavā uttari asamasamataṃ pakāsento pathaviṃ kho ahaṃ brahmetiādimāha. Tattha pathaviyā pathavattena ananubhūtanti pathaviyā pathavisabhāvena ananubhūtaṃ appattaṃ. Kiṃ pana tanti? Nibbānaṃ. Tañhi sabbasmā saṅkhatā nissaṭattā pathavisabhāvena appattaṃ nāma. Tadabhiññāyāti taṃ nibbānaṃ jānitvā sacchikatvā. Pathaviṃ nāpahosinti pathaviṃ taṇhādiṭṭhimānagāhehi na gaṇhiṃ. Āpādīsupi eseva nayo. Vitthāro pana mūlapariyāye vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

pathaviṃ kho ahaṃ brahme pathaviyā pathavattena ananubhūta Tadabhiññāyā Pathaviṃ nāpahosi Āpādīsupi

Sace kho te, mārisa, sabbassa sabbattenāti idameva brahmā attano vāditāya sabbanti akkharaṃ niddisitvā akkhare dosaṃ gaṇhanto āha. Satthā pana sakkāyaṃ sandhāya ‘‘sabba’’nti vadati, brahmā sabbasabbaṃ sandhāya. Tvaṃ ‘‘sabba’’nti vadasi, ‘‘sabbassa sabbattena ananubhūta’’nti vadasi, yadi sabbaṃ ananubhūtaṃ natthi, athassa ananubhūtaṃ atthi. Mā heva te rittakamevaahositucchakameva ahosīti tuyhaṃ vacanaṃ rittakaṃ mā hotu, tucchakaṃ mā hotūti satthāraṃ musāvādena niggaṇhāti.

Sace kho te, mārisa, sabbassa sabbattenā Mā heva te rittakameva ahosi tucchakameva ahosī

Satthā pana etasmā brahmunā sataguṇena sahassaguṇena satasahassaguṇena vādītaro, tasmā ahaṃ sabbañca vakkhāmi, ananubhūtañca vakkhāmi, suṇāhi meti tassa vādamaddanatthaṃ kāraṇaṃ āharanto viññāṇantiādimāha. Tattha viññāṇanti vijānitabbaṃ. Anidassananti cakkhuviññāṇassa āpāthaṃ anupagamanato anidassanaṃ nāma, padadvayenapi nibbānameva vuttaṃ. Anantanti tayidaṃ uppādavayaantarahitattā anantaṃ nāma. Vuttampi hetaṃ –

viññāṇa viññāṇa Anidassana Ananta

‘‘Antavantāni bhūtāni, asambhūtaṃ anantakaṃ;

Bhūte antāni dissanti, bhūte antā pakāsitā’’ti.

Sabbatopabhanti sabbaso pabhāsampannaṃ. Nibbānato hi añño dhammo sapabhataro vā jotivantataro vā parisuddhataro vā paṇḍarataro vā natthi. Sabbato vā tathā pabhūtameva, na katthaci natthīti sabbatopabhaṃ. Puratthimadisādīsu hi asukadisāya nāma nibbānaṃ natthīti na vattabbaṃ. Atha vā pabhanti titthassa nāmaṃ, sabbato pabhamassāti sabbatopabhaṃ. Nibbānassa kira yathā mahāsamuddassa yato yato otaritukāmā honti, taṃ tadeva titthaṃ, atitthaṃ nāma natthi. Evamevaṃ aṭṭhatiṃsāya kammaṭṭhānesu yena yena mukhena nibbānaṃ otaritukāmā honti, taṃ tadeva titthaṃ. Nibbānassa atitthaṃ nāma kammaṭṭhānaṃ natthi. Tena vuttaṃ sabbatopabhanti. Taṃ pathaviyā pathavattenāti taṃ nibbānaṃ pathaviyā pathavīsabhāvena tato paresaṃ āpādīnaṃ āpādisabhāvena ca ananubhūtaṃ. Iti yaṃ tumhādisānaṃ visayabhūtaṃ sabbatebhūmakadhammajātaṃ tassa sabbattena taṃ viññāṇaṃ anidassanaṃ anantaṃ sabbatopataṃ ananubhūtanti vādaṃ patiṭṭhapesi.

Sabbatopabha pabha sabbatopabhaṃ sabbatopabha

Tato brahmā gahitagahitaṃ satthārā vissajjāpito kiñci gahetabbaṃ adisvā laḷitakaṃ kātukāmo handa carahi te, mārisa, antaradhāyāmīti āha. Tattha antaradhāyāmīti adissamānakapāṭihāriyaṃ karomīti āha. Sace visahasīti yadi sakkosi mayhaṃ antaradhāyituṃ, antaradhāyasi , pāṭihāriyaṃ karohīti. Nevassu me sakkoti antaradhāyitunti mayhaṃ antaradhāyituṃ neva sakkoti. Kiṃ panesa kātukāmo ahosīti? Mūlapaṭisandhiṃ gantukāmo ahosi. Brahmānañhi mūlapaṭisandhikaattabhāvo sukhumo, aññesaṃ anāpātho, abhisaṅkhatakāyeneva tiṭṭhanti. Satthā tassa mūlapaṭisandhiṃ gantuṃ na adāsi. Mūlapaṭisandhiṃ vā agantvāpi yena tamena attānaṃ antaradhāpetvā adissamānako bhaveyya, satthā taṃ tamaṃ vinodesi, tasmā antaradhāyituṃ nāsakkhi. So asakkonto vimāne nilīyati, kapparukkhe nilīyati, ukkuṭiko nisīdati. Brahmagaṇo keḷimakāsi – ‘‘esa kho bako brahmā vimāne nilīyati, kapparukkhe nilīyati, ukkuṭiko nisīdati, brahme tvaṃ antarahitomhī’’ti saññaṃ uppādesi nāmāti. So brahmagaṇena uppaṇḍito maṅku ahosi.

handa carahi te, mārisa, antaradhāyāmī antaradhāyāmī Sace visahasī Nevassu me sakkoti antaradhāyitu

Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhikkhaveti, bhikkhave, etena brahmunā, ‘‘handa carahi te, mārisa, antaradhāyāmī’’ti evaṃ vutte taṃ antaradhāyituṃ asakkontaṃ disvā ahaṃ etadavocaṃ. Imaṃ gāthamabhāsinti kasmā bhagavā gāthamabhāsīti? Samaṇassa gotamassa imasmiṃ ṭhāne atthibhāvo vā natthibhāvo vā kathaṃ sakkā jānitunti evaṃ brahmagaṇassa vacanokāso mā hotūti antarahitova gāthamabhāsi.

Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhikkhave Imaṃ gāthamabhāsi

Tattha bhavevāhaṃ bhayaṃ disvāti ahaṃ bhave bhayaṃ disvāyeva. Bhavañca vibhavesinanti imañca kāmabhavāditividhampi sattabhavaṃ vibhavesinaṃ vibhavaṃ gavesamānaṃ pariyesamānampi punappunaṃ bhaveyeva disvā. Bhavaṃ nābhivadinti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena kiñci bhavaṃ na abhivadiṃ, na gavesinti attho. Nandiñca na upādiyinti bhavataṇhaṃ na upagañchiṃ, na aggahesinti attho. Iti cattāri saccāni pakāsento satthā dhammaṃ desesi. Desanāpariyosāne desanānusārena vipassanāgabbhaṃ gāhāpetvā dasamattāni brahmasahassāni maggaphalāmatapānaṃ piviṃsu.

bhavevāhaṃ bhayaṃ disvā Bhavañca vibhavesina Bhavaṃ nābhivadi Nandiñca na upādiyi

Acchariyabbhutacittajātāti acchariyajātā abbhutajātā tuṭṭhijātā ca ahesuṃ. Samūlaṃ bhavaṃ udabbahīti bodhimaṇḍe attano tāya tāya desanāya aññesampi bahūnaṃ devamanussānaṃ samūlakaṃ bhavaṃ udabbahi, uddhari uppāṭesīti attho.

Acchariyabbhutacittajātā Samūlaṃ bhavaṃ udabbahī
commentary_english:
504. "Having arisen here" means having arisen here in the first *jhāna* level.

"Because you do not know that" means because of that reason, you do not know that body.

"There is not even an equal to you" means, reaching a place to be understood, I am not an equal to you.

"For thorough knowledge" means for knowledge.

"From where, lowliness?" means by you, a lower state, however, from where is that for me?

The *brahmā*, a lower attainer, it seems, in a time when a Buddha has not arisen, having gone forth into the ascetic life, having done the preliminary work for the *kasiṇa*, having brought about the *samāpatti*s, not having lost the *jhāna*, having made time, in the fourth *jhāna* level, having arisen in the *Vēhapphala Brahma* world, having taken life for five kalpas.

There, having remained as long as life lasts, having made the lower attainment, having cultivated the excellent third *jhāna*, in the *Subhakiṇha Brahma* world, having taken life for sixty-four kalpas, he was reborn.

There, having cultivated the second *jhāna*, in the *Ābhassara* realm, having taken life for eight kalpas, he was reborn.

There, having cultivated the first *jhāna*, in the first *jhāna* level, having been one whose life lasts for a *kappa*, he was reborn; he, in the first time, knew his own past action and the place of rebirth, but as time went on, forgetting both, he produced the eternalist view.

Therefore, the Blessed One said to him, "Because you do not know that…pe…from where, lowliness?"

Then the *brahmā* thought, "The *samaṇa* Gotama knows my life, the place of rebirth, and past action. Come, let me ask him about my past action." He asked the Teacher about his own past action.

The Teacher related:

"In the past, it seems, having been born in a family, seeing the wretchedness in desires, thinking, 'I will make an end to birth, old age, sickness, and death,' having gone forth, having gone forth into the ascetic life, having brought about the *samāpatti*s, having been a gainer of *jhāna*s that are the basis for higher knowledge, on the bank of the Ganges, having built a leaf hut, he passed his time in the joy of *jhāna*.

And at that time, from time to time, caravan leaders with five hundred cartloads would set out for the desert wilderness.

However, in the desert wilderness, it is not possible to go during the day; the journey is at night.

Then, the oxen yoked to the front cart, while going, turned back and faced the road they had come from.

The other carts also turned back in the same way. When dawn broke, they knew that they had turned back.

For them, then, that day was one of crossing the wilderness.

All the wood and water were exhausted. Therefore, thinking, "Now there is no life for us," they tied the oxen to the wheels, and the people entered the shade of the carts and lay down.

The ascetic, too, in the evening, having gone out from his leaf hut, sitting at the door of his leaf hut, looking at the Ganges, saw the Ganges being carried along by a great flood of water, like a heap of jewels that had arisen coming along.

Having seen this, he thought, "Are there beings in this world who are distressed by not obtaining such sweet water?"

He, thus considering, seeing that caravan in the desert wilderness, thinking, "May these beings not perish," with his mind of higher knowledge, he resolved, "From here, may a great mass of water be cut off and go towards the caravan in the desert wilderness."

With the arising of that thought, like water let loose on a slope, the water went there.

The people, rising at the sound of the water, seeing the water, delighted in their hearts, having bathed, having drunk, having given the oxen also to drink, with safety, they went to the place they desired.

The Teacher, showing that past action of the *brahmā*—

"You gave water to many people,

thirsty, exhausted by the heat;

that ancient practice of virtuous conduct,

like one awakened from sleep, I remember."

(Jā. 1.7.71)—

He spoke this verse.

At another time, the ascetic, having built a leaf hut on the bank of the Ganges, living dependent on a forest village, dwells there.
At that time, thieves attacked that village, took valuables and drove away the cows and the *karamara* carts.

Cows, dogs, and humans alike cried out with a great roar.

Hearing that sound, the ascetic reflected, "What is this?" Knowing that "Fear has arisen for the humans," and thinking "While I am watching, may these beings not perish," he entered the meditation that is the basis of super-knowledge (*abhijñāpādakajjhānaṃ*), arose, and by means of his super-knowledge mind, created a four-division army (*caturaṅginisenaṃ*) in the path of the thieves who were approaching, fully equipped for battle (*kammasajjaṃ*).

The thieves, seeing it and thinking "It is the king!", abandoned their loot and fled.

The ascetic made a resolution: "Whatever belongs to whomever, may it belong to that person!" and it was just so.

The great multitude attained a state of well-being (*sotthibhāvaṃ*).

The Teacher, showing this as his former deed, [said]:

"That person, who was seized at the bank of the *eṇikūla*,

You freed him, Gayhaka, as he was being led away.

That ancient practice of virtuous conduct of yours,

Awakened from sleep, I recall."

(Jā. 1.7.72)

He spoke this verse.

Here, *eṇikūlasmi* means on the bank of the Ganges.

Again, at one time, a family residing upstream on the Ganges, having made a friendship pact (*mittasanthavaṃ katvā*) with a family residing downstream on the Ganges, tied together a raft of boats (*nāvāsaṅghāṭaṃ bandhitvā*) and, loading many edible and enjoyable things, along with perfumes, garlands, and so on (*gandhamālādīni ca āropetvā*), came along the Ganges river current.

The humans, eating, enjoying, dancing, and singing, were very strong and happy, as if they were traveling in a divine chariot (*devavimānena gacchantā viya balavasomanassā ahesuṃ*).

A Nāga named Gangeyyaka, seeing them, became angry: "These ones do not even pay attention to me!" and thinking, "Now I will send them to the ocean itself!", he created a great self-body, split the water in two, rose up, made a hood, and making a hissing sound (*sussūkāraṃ karonto aṭṭhāsi*), he stood there.

The great multitude, seeing it, became frightened and made a great outcry.

The ascetic, sitting in his leaf hut, hearing it, [thought,] "These ones were singing, dancing, and coming along with happiness, and now they are crying out with fearful sounds (*bhayaravaṃ raviṃsu*). What is this?" Reflecting and seeing the Nāga-king, [and thinking,] "While I am watching, may these beings not perish," he entered the meditation that is the basis of super-knowledge (*abhijñāpādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā*), gave up his own body, created the color of a *supaṇṇa*, and showed it to the Nāga-king.

The Nāga-king, frightened, contracted his hood, and entered the water.

The great multitude attained a state of well-being (*sotthibhāvaṃ pāpuṇi*).

The Teacher, showing this as his former deed, [said]:

"On the Ganges river current, you released the seized boat,

[Seized] by the cruel Nāga, [endangering] humans;

You freed it by force, overpowering [him].

That ancient practice of virtuous conduct of yours,

Awakened from sleep, I recall."

(Jā. 1.7.73)

He spoke this verse.

At another time, he, having gone forth into the ascetic life, became an ascetic named Keśava.

At that time, our Bodhisattva, a young man named Kappa, became the constant attendant (*baddhacaro*) and pupil (*antevāsiko*) of Keśava, a doer of what the teacher requested (*kiṃkārapaṭissāvī*), a pleasant practitioner (*manāpacārī*), endowed with intelligence (*buddhisampanno*), and a practitioner of the goal (*atthacaro*).

Keśava was unable to live without him; he made his living dependent on him.

The Teacher, showing this as his former deed, [said]:

"Keśava, Kappa was your constant attendant,

You did not consider [anyone] as having equal intelligence.

That ancient practice of virtuous conduct of yours,

Awakened from sleep, I recall."
(jā. 1.7.74) –
This verse was spoken.

Thus, the Teacher (satthā) revealed the accomplished deed (katakammaṃ) in the various states (nānattabhāvesu) of Brahmā (brahmuno). As the Teacher (satthari) was speaking, Brahmā (brahmā) considered (sallakkhesi): "Just as when a thousand lamps (dīpasahasse) are lit, forms (rūpāni) become clear (pākaṭāni), so too are all his deeds (sabbakammānissa)."

So, with a pleased mind (pasannacitto), he spoke this verse:

"Indeed (addhā), you know (pajānāsi) my (mama) life (āyuṃ),
And you also know (jānāsi) another (aññampi), for (hi) you are the awakened one (buddho);
Thus (tathā hi), this (tāyaṃ) radiant power (jalitānubhāvo)
Illuminating (obhāsayaṃ) remains (tiṭṭhati) in the Brahma-world (brahmaloka)."

(jā. 1.7.75);
Then, the Blessed One (bhagavā), revealing further the unequaled equality (asamasamataṃ), spoke, beginning with: "<hi rend="bold">O Brahmā, I am the earth (pathaviṃ kho ahaṃ brahme)</hi>."

There (tattha), "<hi rend="bold">unanubūta by the earth through earthness (pathaviyā pathavattena ananubhūta)</hi>" means (nti): unreached (appattaṃ), unexperienced (ananubhūtaṃ) by the earth through the state of being earth (pathavisabhāvena).

What then (kiṃ pana) is that (tanti)? Nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ).
Indeed (hi), because it (taṃ) is free (nissaṭattā) from all conditioned things (sabbasmā saṅkhatā), it is called (nāma) unreached (appattaṃ) through the state of being earth (pathavisabhāvena).

"<hi rend="bold">Through its highest knowledge (tadabhiññāyā)</hi>" means (ti): having known (jānitvā) and realized (sacchikatvā) that Nirvāṇa (taṃ nibbānaṃ).

"<hi rend="bold">He did not abandon the earth (pathaviṃ nāpahosi)</hi>" means (nti): he did not grasp (na gaṇhiṃ) the earth (pathaviṃ) with craving (taṇhā), views (diṭṭhi), and the conceit of self (mānagāhehi).

"<hi rend="bold">Even for water, etc. (āpādīsupi)</hi>" the method (nayo) is the same (eseva).
But (pana) the detailed exposition (vitthāro) should be understood (veditabbo) by the method stated (vuttanayeneva) in the Root Discourse (mūlapariyāye).

<hi rend="bold">O Brahmā, I am the earth (pathaviṃ kho ahaṃ brahme)</hi> <hi rend="bold">unanubūta by the earth through earthness (pathaviyā pathavattena ananubhūta)</hi> <hi rend="bold">Through its highest knowledge (tadabhiññāyā)</hi> <hi rend="bold">He did not abandon the earth (pathaviṃ nāpahosi)</hi> <hi rend="bold">Even for water, etc. (āpādīsupi)</hi>
"<hi rend="bold">If indeed (sace kho), Mārisa, everything through allness (sabbassa sabbattenā)</hi>" means (ti): Brahmā (brahmā) himself (attano), pointing out (niddisitvā) the syllable (akkharaṃ) "all (sabba)" as his (vāditāya) doctrine (idameva), and finding fault (dosam gaṇhanto) with the syllable (akkhare), spoke (āha).

But (pana) the Teacher (satthā), referring (sandhāya) to self-identity (sakkāyaṃ), speaks (vadati) "all (sabba)," while (brahmā) Brahmā (sandhāya) refers to all of everything (sabbasabbaṃ).

You (tvaṃ) <pb ed="p" n="2.0413"/> say (vadasi), "all (sabba)," you say (vadasi), "unanubūta by everything through allness (sabbassa sabbattena ananubhūta)," if (yadi) all (sabbaṃ) is unexperienced (ananubhūtaṃ), [then] nothing (natthi), otherwise (atha), it has (assa) unexperienced (ananubhūtaṃ) existence (atthi).

"<hi rend="bold">May it not be (mā heva te) merely empty (rittakameva)</hi>"<pb ed="v" n="2.0306"/><hi rend="bold">it was (ahosi)</hi><pb ed="m" n="2.0310"/><hi rend="bold">merely vain (tucchakameva) it was (ahosī)</hi>" means (ti): he refutes (niggaṇhāti) the Teacher (satthāraṃ) with false speech (musāvādena), [saying] "may your (tuyhaṃ) speech (vacanaṃ) not be (mā hotu) empty (rittakaṃ), may it not be (mā hotūti) vain (tucchakaṃ)."

<hi rend="bold">If indeed (sace kho) to you (te), Mārisa, everything through allness (sabbassa sabbattenā)</hi> <pb ed="p" n="2.0413"/> <hi rend="bold">May it not be (mā heva te) merely empty (rittakameva)</hi> <pb ed="v" n="2.0306"/> <hi rend="bold">it was (ahosi)</hi> <pb ed="m" n="2.0310"/> <hi rend="bold">merely vain (tucchakameva) it was (ahosī)</hi>
But (pana) the Teacher (satthā), [being] superior (vādītaro) to this (etasmā) Brahmā (brahmunā) by a hundredfold (sataguṇena), a thousandfold (sahassaguṇena), a hundred thousandfold (satasahassaguṇena), therefore (tasmā), declaring (āharanto) a reason (kāraṇaṃ) for the subduing (vādamaddanatthaṃ) of his (tassa) doctrine (vādaṃ), spoke (āha), beginning with "<hi rend="bold">consciousness (viññāṇa)</hi>."

There (tattha), "<hi rend="bold">consciousness (viññāṇa)</hi>" means (nti) should be understood (vijānitabbaṃ).

"<hi rend="bold">invisible (anidassana)</hi>" means (nti): because of the non-access (anupagamanato) of the range (āpāthaṃ) of eye-consciousness (cakkhuviññāṇassa), it is called (nāma) invisible (anidassanaṃ), even (api) by the two terms (padadvayena) Nirvāṇa (nibbānameva) is stated (vuttaṃ).

"<hi rend="bold">endless (ananta)</hi>" means (nti): because it (tayidaṃ) is without (rahitattā) arising (uppāda), passing away (vaya), and the intermediate state (antara), it is called (nāma) endless (anantaṃ).
This (hetaṃ) was also spoken (vuttampi) –

<hi rend="bold">Consciousness (viññāṇa)</hi> <hi rend="bold">Consciousness (viññāṇa)</hi> <hi rend="bold">Invisible (anidassana)</hi> <hi rend="bold">Endless (ananta)</hi>

‘‘Beings (bhūtāni) are finite (antavantāni), the unbecome (asambhūtaṃ) is endless (anantakaṃ);
In beings (bhūte) ends (antāni) are seen (dissantī), in beings (bhūte) ends (antā) are declared (pakāsitā).’’

<hi rend="bold">All-illuminating (sabbatopabha)</hi>" means (nti): endowed with light (pabhāsampannaṃ) in every way (sabbaso).

Indeed (hi), there is no other (añño) dharma (dhammo) more radiant (sapabhataro vā), more shining (jotivantataro vā), more purified (parisuddhataro vā), or more brilliant (paṇḍarataro vā) than (nibbānato) Nirvāṇa (natthi).

Or (vā) everywhere (sabbato) it is (eva) thus (tathā) shining (pabhūtaṃ), there is no (na) place where it is not (katthaci natthīti), [therefore it is] all-illuminating (sabbatopabhaṃ).

Indeed (hi), it should not be said (na vattabbaṃ) that (iti) there is no (natthi) Nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ) by name (nāma) in such and such a direction (asukadisāya) among (ādīsu) the eastern directions (puratthimadisā).

Or (atha vā) "<hi rend="bold">light (pabha)</hi>" is (nti) the name (nāmaṃ) of a ford (titthassa), the all-shining (sabbato pabhamassāti) [is] <hi rend="bold">all-illuminating (sabbatopabhaṃ)</hi>.

It is said (kira) that (yathā) just as (nibbānassa) for Nirvāṇa (mahāsamuddassa) for the great ocean (yato yato), from wherever (hotī), they wish to descend (otaritukāmā), that (taṃ) itself (tadeva) is a ford (titthaṃ), there is no (natthi) place that is not a ford (atitthaṃ nāma).

Even so (evamevaṃ), in the thirty-eight (aṭṭhatiṃsāya) meditation subjects (kammaṭṭhānesu), by whatever (yena yena) means (mukhena) they wish to descend (otaritukāmā honti) to Nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ), that (taṃ) itself (tadeva) is a ford (titthaṃ).
There is no meditation subject called *nibbāna* that is unequalled. Therefore, it is called "all-illuminating." That *nibbāna* is not experienced by earth through its earth-nature, nor by water and the others through their respective natures. Thus, by virtue of its all-illuminating nature, that consciousness, which is the object of your kind and the aggregate of all ten-world-dharmas, establishes the doctrine that it is invisible, endless, all-pervading, and unexperienced.

Then Brahmā, being dismissed by the Teacher after having been repeatedly pressed but seeing nothing that should be taken, desiring to make a jest, said, "Come now, venerable sir, I will disappear." There, "I will disappear" means "I will perform the miracle of invisibility."

"If you are able" means, "If you are able to disappear from me, perform the miracle of disappearing." "He is not able to disappear from me" means that he is simply not able to disappear from me. What did he desire to do? He desired to return to the original state of rebirth. For the Brahmās, indeed, the state of having the original rebirth is subtle, unapproachable to others, and they abide merely with a body that is compounded.

The Teacher did not allow him to return to the original rebirth. Even without going to the original rebirth, by whatever darkness he could make himself unseeable by disappearing, the Teacher dispelled that darkness. Therefore, he was not able to disappear. Being unable, he hid in a celestial mansion, he hid in a wish-fulfilling tree, he sat squatting on his heels.

The Brahma-host made sport, "This Brahmā, indeed, is hiding in a celestial mansion, he is hiding in a wish-fulfilling tree, he is sitting squatting on his heels, O Brahmā, I have disappeared from you!" Thus they produced a perception, so it is said. Humiliated by the Brahma-host, he felt disgraced.

"Thus spoke I, monks" means, "O monks, when thus addressed by that Brahmā, 'Come now, venerable sir, I will disappear,' when he was thus addressed, seeing that he was unable to disappear, I spoke thus."

"I spoke this verse" means, "Why did the Blessed One speak a verse?" In order that there should not be an opportunity for the Brahma-host to say, "How can the existence or non-existence of the ascetic Gotama in this place be known?" the Teacher, being invisible, spoke a verse.

"Thus spoke I, monks," "I spoke this verse." There, "Having seen fear in existence" means "I alone have seen fear in existence." "And the seeker of becoming" means "Having seen this becoming, and also the seven kinds of existence, beginning with desire-existence, in its various forms, as a seeker of becoming, searching and seeking for prosperity again and again in existence..." "I did not address becoming" means "I did not address any becoming by way of craving and views; I did not seek it," is the meaning. "And I did not take up delight" means "I did not approach craving for existence; I did not grasp it," is the meaning.

Thus, the Teacher, proclaiming the four noble truths, taught the Dharma. At the end of the teaching, having established them in the chamber of insight in accordance with the teaching, ten measures of thousands of Brahmās drank the nectar of the path and its fruit.

"Having seen fear in existence," "And the seeker of becoming," "I did not address becoming," "And I did not take up delight." "Having minds of wonder and amazement" means that they were those who had wonder, those who had amazement, and those who had joy. "He uprooted becoming together with its root" means that at the *bodhimaṇḍa*, by that teaching of his, he uprooted, eradicated, and tore up becoming, together with its root, from many other gods and humans as well, is the meaning.

"Having minds of wonder and amazement," "He uprooted becoming together with its root."

mula_pali:
505. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā aññataraṃ brahmapārisajjaṃ anvāvisitvā maṃ etadavoca – ‘sace kho tvaṃ, mārisa, evaṃ pajānāsi, sace tvaṃ evaṃ anubuddho, mā sāvake upanesi, mā pabbajite; mā sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ desesi, mā pabbajitānaṃ; mā sāvakesu gedhimakāsi, mā pabbajitesu. Ahesuṃ kho, bhikkhu, tayā pubbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā lokasmiṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā paṭijānamānā . Te sāvake upanesuṃ pabbajite, sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ desesuṃ pabbajitānaṃ, sāvakesu gedhimakaṃsu pabbajitesu, te sāvake upanetvā pabbajite, sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ desetvā pabbajitānaṃ, sāvakesu gedhitacittā pabbajitesu, kāyassa bhedā pāṇupacchedā hīne kāye patiṭṭhitā. Ahesuṃ ye pana, bhikkhu, tayā pubbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā lokasmiṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā paṭijānamānā. Te na sāvake upanesuṃ na pabbajite, na sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ desesuṃ na pabbajitānaṃ, na sāvakesu gedhimakaṃsu na pabbajitesu, te na sāvake upanetvā na pabbajite, na sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ desetvā na pabbajitānaṃ, na sāvakesu gedhitacittā na pabbajitesu, kāyassa bhedā pāṇupacchedā paṇīte kāye patiṭṭhitā. Taṃ tāhaṃ, bhikkhu, evaṃ vadāmi – iṅgha tvaṃ, mārisa, appossukko diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāramanuyutto viharassu, anakkhātaṃ kusalañhi, mārisa, mā paraṃ ovadāhī’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘jānāmi kho tāhaṃ, pāpima, mā tvaṃ maññittho – na maṃ jānātī’ti. Māro tvamasi, pāpima. Na maṃ tvaṃ, pāpima, hitānukampī evaṃ vadesi; ahitānukampī maṃ tvaṃ, pāpima, evaṃ vadesi. Tuyhañhi, pāpima, evaṃ hoti – ‘yesaṃ samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ desessati, te me visayaṃ upātivattissantī’ti. Asammāsambuddhāva pana te , pāpima, samānā sammāsambuddhāmhāti paṭijāniṃsu. Ahaṃ kho pana, pāpima, sammāsambuddhova samāno sammāsambuddhomhīti paṭijānāmi. Desentopi hi, pāpima, tathāgato sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ tādisova adesentopi hi, pāpima, tathāgato sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ tādisova. Upanentopi hi, pāpima, tathāgato sāvake tādisova, anupanentopi hi, pāpima, tathāgato sāvake tādisova. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāgatassa, pāpima, ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā – te pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Seyyathāpi, pāpima, tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna virūḷhiyā; evameva kho, pāpima, tathāgatassa ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā – te pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammāti.

‘‘Iti hidaṃ mārassa ca anālapanatāya brahmuno ca abhinimantanatāya, tasmā imassa veyyākaraṇassa brahmanimantanikaṃteva adhivacana’’nti.

Brahmanimantanikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
505. Then, monks, Māra the Evil One, taking possession of a certain attendant of the Brahma assembly, said this to me: ‘If, good sir, you understand thus, if you are awakened thus, do not lead disciples, do not lead those gone forth; do not teach the Dhamma to disciples, do not teach it to those gone forth; do not create desire among disciples, do not create it among those gone forth.’

There were, monk, before your time, ascetics and Brahmins in the world claiming to be worthy and rightly self-awakened.

They led disciples and those gone forth; they taught the Dhamma to disciples and those gone forth; they created desire among disciples and those gone forth; having led disciples and those gone forth, having taught the Dhamma to disciples and those gone forth, with minds full of desire among disciples and those gone forth, on the breakup of the body, after death, they were established in a lower body.

There were those, monk, before your time, ascetics and Brahmins in the world claiming to be worthy and rightly self-awakened.

They did not lead disciples or those gone forth; they did not teach the Dhamma to disciples or those gone forth; they did not create desire among disciples or those gone forth; not having led disciples or those gone forth, not having taught the Dhamma to disciples or those gone forth, with minds free of desire among disciples and those gone forth, on the breakup of the body, after death, they were established in a refined body.

So, monk, I say this to you: Come now, good sir, be without concern, dwell devoted to a pleasant abiding in the here-and-now; for skillfulness is undeclared, good sir, do not instruct others.’

When this was said, I said this to Māra the Evil One: ‘I know you, Evil One; do not think, “He does not know me.”

You are Māra, Evil One.

You do not speak to me thus out of sympathy for welfare; you speak to me thus out of sympathy for what is not welfare.

For you think thus, Evil One: “Those to whom Gotama the ascetic will teach the Dhamma will transgress my domain.”

Those ascetics and Brahmins, Evil One, who were not rightly self-awakened claimed to be rightly self-awakened.

But I, Evil One, being rightly self-awakened, claim to be rightly self-awakened ( *sammāsambuddho’va samāno sammāsambuddho’mhīti paṭijānāmi* ).

Even when teaching the Dhamma to his disciples, Evil One, the *Tathāgata* is Such; even when not teaching the Dhamma to his disciples, Evil One, the *Tathāgata* is Such.

Even when leading his disciples, Evil One, the *Tathāgata* is Such; even when not leading his disciples, Evil One, the *Tathāgata* is Such.

Why is that? Because, Evil One, the corruptions of the *Tathāgata*—defiling, leading to renewed existence, distressing, resulting in suffering, tending to future birth, aging, and death—are abandoned, their root cut off, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and subject to no future arising.

Just as a palm tree with its crown severed is incapable of growing again, so too, Evil One, the corruptions of the *Tathāgata*—defiling, leading to renewed existence, distressing, resulting in suffering, tending to future birth, aging, and death—are abandoned, their root cut off, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and subject to no future arising.’

Thus, because of the silencing of Māra and because of the invitation of Brahmā, therefore this exposition is entitled “The Brahmā Invitation.”

The *Brahma-nimantanika Sutta* is finished, the ninth.
commentary_pali:
505. Tasmiṃ pana samaye māro pāpimā kodhābhibhūto hutvā, ‘‘mayi vicaranteyeva samaṇena gotamena dhammakathaṃ kathetvā dasamattāni brahmasahassāni mama vasaṃ ativattitānī’’ti kodhābhibhūtatāya aññatarassa brahmapārisajjassa sarīre adhimucci, taṃ dassetuṃ atha kho, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha sace tvaṃ evaṃ anubuddhoti sace tvaṃ evaṃ attanāva cattāri saccāni anubuddho. Mā sāvake upanesīti gihisāvake vā pabbajitasāvake vā taṃ dhammaṃ mā upanayasi. Hīne kāye patiṭṭhitāti catūsu apāyesu patiṭṭhitā. Paṇīte kāye patiṭṭhitāti brahmaloke patiṭṭhitā. Idaṃ ke sandhāya vadati? Bāhirapabbajjaṃ pabbajite tāpasaparibbājake. Anuppanne hi buddhuppāde kulaputtā tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā kassaci kiñci avicāretvā ekacarā hutvā samāpattiyo nibbattetvā brahmaloke uppajjiṃsu, te sandhāya evamāha. Anakkhātaṃ kusalañhi mārisāti paresaṃ anakkhātaṃ anovadanaṃ dhammakathāya akathanaṃ kusalaṃ etaṃ seyyo. Mā paraṃ ovadāhīti kālena manussalokaṃ, kālena devalokaṃ, kālena brahmalokaṃ, kālena nāgalokaṃ āhiṇḍanto mā vicari, ekasmiṃ ṭhāne nisinno jhānamaggaphalasukhena vītināmehīti. Anālapanatāyāti anullapanatāya. Brahmuno ca abhinimantanatāyāti bakabrahmuno ca idañhi, mārisa, niccantiādinā nayena saha kāyakena brahmaṭṭhānena nimantanavacanena. Tasmāti tena kāraṇena. Imassa veyyākaraṇassa brahmanimantanikaṃtveva adhivacanaṃ saṅkhā samaññā paññatti jātā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Brahmanimantanikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
505. Then, at that time, Māra the Evil One, being overwhelmed with anger, [thought:] “While I was wandering around, the ascetic Gotama, by telling a Dhamma talk, caused about ten thousand Brahma-worlds to go beyond my control.” Overwhelmed by anger, he possessed the body of a certain Brahma-attendant in order to show that.

"Then, monks..." etc., he said, beginning thus.

There, "If you have awakened in this way..." means, "If you yourself have awakened to the four truths in this way."

"Do not lead disciples" means, "Do not lead either lay disciples or ordained disciples to that Dhamma."

"Established in a base body" means, "Established in the four woeful states."

"Established in a refined body" means, "Established in the Brahma-world."

With what in mind does he speak this? With the renunciants who have gone forth into external renunciations, ascetics and wanderers.

For, before the arising of a Buddha, clansmen, having gone forth into the ascetic life, without consulting anyone about anything, becoming solitary wanderers, having produced attainments, were reborn in the Brahma-world. With them in mind, he spoke thus.

"Indeed, unproclaimed is skill, sir" means, "This is better: skill that is unproclaimed to others, not advising, not speaking a Dhamma talk."

"Do not advise others" means, "Wandering from time to time to the human world, from time to time to the deva-world, from time to time to the Brahma-world, from time to time to the nāga-world, do not wander. Sit in one place and pass the time with the bliss of jhāna, path and fruition."

"Because of non-addressing" means, "Because of non-utterance."

"And because of Brahma's invitation" means, "And because of the invitation-speech of Baka Brahma, together with his embodied Brahma-state, by the means of the line, 'Indeed, sir, this is permanent,' etc."

"Therefore" means, "For that reason."

"Of this exposition, 'Brahma-invitation' is indeed the designation, the reckoning, the convention, the term."

The rest is clear throughout.

* * *

The Brahma-invitation Discourse Commentary,
from the Papañcasūdanī, Commentary on the Middle Length Discourses, is finished.

mula_pali:
506. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahāmoggallāno abbhokāse caṅkamati. Tena kho pana samayena māro pāpimā āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa kucchigato hoti koṭṭhamanupaviṭṭho. Atha kho āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa etadahosi – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho me kucchi garugaro viya garu garu viya (sī. pī. ṭīkāyaṃ pāṭhantaraṃ)? Māsācitaṃ maññe’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno caṅkamā orohitvā vihāraṃ pavisitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno paccattaṃ yoniso manasākāsi. Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno māraṃ pāpimantaṃ kucchigataṃ koṭṭhamanupaviṭṭhaṃ. Disvāna māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘nikkhama, pāpima; nikkhama, pāpima! Mā tathāgataṃ vihesesi, mā tathāgatasāvakaṃ. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’’ti. Atha kho mārassa pāpimato etadahosi – ‘‘ajānameva kho maṃ ayaṃ samaṇo apassaṃ evamāha – ‘nikkhama, pāpima; nikkhama, pāpima! Mā tathāgataṃ vihesesi, mā tathāgatasāvakaṃ. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’ti. Yopissa so satthā sopi maṃ neva khippaṃ jāneyya, kuto pana kuto ca pana (syā.) maṃ ayaṃ sāvako jānissatī’’ti? Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘evampi kho tāhaṃ, pāpima, jānāmi, mā tvaṃ maññittho – ‘na maṃ jānātī’ti. Māro tvamasi, pāpima; tuyhañhi, pāpima, evaṃ hoti – ‘ajānameva kho maṃ ayaṃ samaṇo apassaṃ evamāha – nikkhama, pāpima; nikkhama, pāpima! Mā tathāgataṃ vihesesi, mā tathāgatasāvakaṃ. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti. Yopissa so satthā sopi maṃ neva khippaṃ jāneyya, kuto pana maṃ ayaṃ sāvako jānissatī’’’ti?

Atha kho mārassa pāpimato etadahosi – ‘‘jāname kho maṃ ayaṃ samaṇo passaṃ evamāha – ‘nikkhama, pāpima; nikkhama, pāpima! Mā tathāgataṃ vihesesi, mā tathāgatasāvakaṃ. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’’’ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa mukhato uggantvā paccaggaḷe aṭṭhāsi.
mula_english:
506.
Thus I have heard. On one occasion the venerable Mahāmoggallāna was living in the Bhagga country at Susumāragiri in the Bhesakaḷāvana Deer Park.
Then, at that time, the venerable Mahāmoggallāna was walking up and down in the open.
Then, at that time, Māra the Evil One had gone into the belly of the venerable Mahāmoggallāna and was sitting inside his bowels.
Then the venerable Mahāmoggallāna considered thus: “Why is my belly so heavy, as if it were full [of beans]?”
Then the venerable Mahāmoggallāna descended from the walking place, entered his dwelling, and sat down on the prepared seat.
Having sat down, the venerable Mahāmoggallāna gave thorough attention to himself.
The venerable Mahāmoggallāna saw Māra the Evil One gone into his belly and sitting inside his bowels.
Having seen Māra the Evil One, he said this: “Get out, Evil One! Get out, Evil One! Do not harass the *Tathāgata*, do not harass the *Tathāgata*'s disciple.
Do not let it be to your harm and suffering for a long time.”
Then Māra the Evil One thought: “This *samaṇa* does not know me, he does not see me, when he says thus: ‘Get out, Evil One! Get out, Evil One! Do not harass the *Tathāgata*, do not harass the *Tathāgata*'s disciple.
Do not let it be to your harm and suffering for a long time.’”
“Even his teacher would not know me so quickly, so how could this disciple know me?” Then the venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to Māra the Evil One: “Even so, Evil One, I know you. Do not think, ‘He does not know me.’
You are Māra, Evil One; for you it occurs thus: ‘This *samaṇa* does not know me, he does not see me, when he says thus: Get out, Evil One! Get out, Evil One! Do not harass the *Tathāgata*, do not harass the *Tathāgata*'s disciple.
Do not let it be to your harm and suffering for a long time.’"
“Even his teacher would not know me so quickly, so how could this disciple know me?”
Then Māra the Evil One thought: “This *samaṇa* knows me, he sees me, when he says thus: ‘Get out, Evil One! Get out, Evil One! Do not harass the *Tathāgata*, do not harass the *Tathāgata*'s disciple.
Do not let it be to your harm and suffering for a long time.’”
Then Māra the Evil One came out of the mouth of the venerable Mahāmoggallāna and stood against the door bar.
commentary_pali:
506.Evaṃme sutanti māratajjanīyasuttaṃ. Tattha koṭṭhamanupaviṭṭhoti kucchiṃ pavisitvā antānaṃ anto anupaviṭṭho, pakkāsayaṭṭhāne nisinno. Garugaro viyāti garukagaruko viya thaddho pāsāṇapuñjasadiso. Māsācitaṃmaññeti māsabhattaṃ bhuttassa kucchi viya māsapūritapasibbako viya tintamāso viya cāti attho. Vihāraṃ pavisitvāti sace āhāradosena esa garubhāvo, abbhokāse caṅkamituṃ na sappāyanti caṅkamā orohitvā paṇṇasālaṃ pavisitvā pakatipaññatte āsane nisīdi. Paccattaṃ yoniso manasākāsīti, ‘‘kiṃ nu kho eta’’nti āvajjamāno attanoyeva upāyena manasi akāsi. Sace pana thero attano sīlaṃ āvajjetvā, ‘‘yaṃ hiyyo vā pare vā parasuve vā paribhuttaṃ avipakkamatthi, añño vā koci visabhāgadoso, sabbaṃ jīratu phāsukaṃ hotū’’ti hatthena kucchiṃ parāmasissa, māro pāpimā vilīyitvā agamissa. Thero pana tathā akatvā yoniso manasi akāsi. Mā tathāgataṃ vihesesīti yathā hi puttesu vihesitesu mātāpitaro vihesitāva honti, saddhivihārikaantevāsikesu vihesitesu ācariyupajjhāyā vihesitāva, janapade vihesite rājā vihesitova hoti, evaṃ tathāgatasāvake vihesite tathāgato vihesitova hoti. Tenāha – ‘‘mā tathāgataṃ vihesesī’’ti.

Paccaggaḷe aṭṭhāsīti patiaggaḷeva aṭṭhāsi. Aggaḷaṃ vuccati kavāṭaṃ, mukhena uggantvā paṇṇasālato nikkhamitvā bahipaṇṇasālāya kavāṭaṃ nissāya aṭṭhāsīti attho.

Paccaggaḷe aṭṭhāsī Aggaḷaṃ
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard: The Māratajjanīya Sutta.

There, "having sat down inside the *koṭṭha*" means having entered the stomach and sat down inside the intestines, having sat in the place of the digested matter.

"*Garugaro viyā*" means like something very heavy, stiff, like a heap of stones.

"*Māsācitaṃ maññe*" means like the stomach of one who has eaten a month's worth of food, like a bag filled with month-old food, like month-old curds, such is the meaning.
