"*Vihāraṃ pavisitvā*" means if this heaviness is due to a fault of the food, and walking in the open air is not suitable, having descended from the walking place, having entered the leaf-hut, he sits down on the seat prepared by custom.

"*Paccattaṃ yoniso manasākāsī*" means, reflecting, "What could this be?", he applied his mind by his own means.

If the Elder, reflecting on his own morality, were to touch his stomach with his hand [thinking], "May whatever undigested food was consumed yesterday, the day before yesterday, or the day before that, or any other disturbing fault, be digested and comfortable," Māra the Evil One would dissolve and depart.

But the Elder, not doing so, wisely applied his mind.

"*Mā tathāgataṃ vihesesī*" means just as parents are harmed when their children are harmed, teachers and preceptors are harmed when their co-residents and disciples are harmed, and a king is harmed when his kingdom is harmed, so too the *tathāgata* is harmed when a disciple of the *tathāgata* is harmed.

Therefore, he said, "Do not harm the *tathāgata*."

"*Paccaggaḷe aṭṭhāsī*" means he stood right at the bolt.

"*Aggaḷaṃ*" is said to be the door; having opened [it] with his mouth, having left the leaf-hut, he stood leaning on the door of the outer leaf-hut, such is the meaning.

"*Paccaggaḷe aṭṭhāsī* *Aggaḷaṃ*"

mula_pali:
507. Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno māraṃ pāpimantaṃ paccaggaḷe ṭhitaṃ; disvāna māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavoca – ‘etthāpi kho tāhaṃ, pāpima, passāmi; mā tvaṃ maññittho ‘‘na maṃ passatī’’ti. Eso tvaṃ, pāpima, paccaggaḷe ṭhito. Bhūtapubbāhaṃ, pāpima, dūsī nāma māro ahosiṃ, tassa me kāḷī nāma bhaginī. Tassā tvaṃ putto. So me tvaṃ bhāgineyyo ahosi. Tena kho pana, pāpima, samayena kakusandho bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti. Kakusandhassa kho pana, pāpima, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa vidhurasañjīvaṃ nāma sāvakayugaṃ ahosi aggaṃ bhaddayugaṃ. Yāvatā kho pana, pāpima, kakusandhassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa sāvakā. Tesu na ca koci āyasmatā vidhurena samasamo hoti yadidaṃ dhammadesanāya. Iminā kho evaṃ etaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), pāpima, pariyāyena āyasmato vidhurassa vidhuroteva vidhurassa vidhuro vidhurotveva (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) samaññā udapādi.

‘‘Āyasmā pana, pāpima, sañjīvo araññagatopi rukkhamūlagatopi suññāgāragatopi appakasireneva saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjati. Bhūtapubbaṃ, pāpima, āyasmā sañjīvo aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno nisinno hoti. Addasaṃsu kho, pāpima, gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino āyasmantaṃ sañjīvaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannaṃ nisinnaṃ; disvāna tesaṃ etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ayaṃ samaṇo nisinnakova kālaṅkato! Handa naṃ dahāmā’ti. Atha kho te, pāpima, gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino tiṇañca kaṭṭhañca gomayañca saṃkaḍḍhitvā āyasmato sañjīvassa kāye upacinitvā aggiṃ datvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho, pāpima, āyasmā sañjīvo tassā rattiyā accayena tāya samāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā cīvarāni papphoṭetvā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasaṃsu kho te, pāpima, gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino āyasmantaṃ sañjīvaṃ piṇḍāya carantaṃ; disvāna nesaṃ etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ayaṃ samaṇo nisinnakova kālaṅkato, svāyaṃ paṭisañjīvito’ti . Iminā kho evaṃ, pāpima, pariyāyena āyasmato sañjīvassa sañjīvoteva sañjīvo sañjīvotveva (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) samaññā udapādi.

sañjīvo sañjīvotveva (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
507. The venerable Mahāmoggallāna saw Māra the Evil One standing against the door bar; having seen Māra the Evil One, he said this: “I see you there too, Evil One; do not think ‘he does not see me.’”

“You are standing against the door bar, Evil One.”

“It happened once, Evil One, that I was a Māra named Dusi, and I had a sister named Kali. You were her son. So you were my nephew.”

“Now on that occasion, Evil One, the Blessed One Kakusandha, the worthy, the perfectly enlightened one, had arisen in the world. The Blessed One Kakusandha, the worthy, the perfectly enlightened one, had a pair of disciples named Vidhura and Sañjīva, an excellent and auspicious pair. As many disciples as the Blessed One Kakusandha, the worthy, the perfectly enlightened one, had, among them there was none equal to the venerable Vidhura in teaching the Dharma. In this way, Evil One, the designation ‘Vidhura like Vidhura’ arose for the venerable Vidhura.

“Furthermore, Evil One, the venerable Sañjīva, whether gone to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, easily attains the cessation of perception and feeling. It happened once, Evil One, that the venerable Sañjīva was sitting at the root of a certain tree, having attained the cessation of perception and feeling. Cowherds, shepherds, ploughmen, and travelers saw the venerable Sañjīva sitting at the root of a certain tree, having attained the cessation of perception and feeling; having seen him, they thought, ‘It is wonderful, sirs, it is marvelous! This ascetic has died while sitting! Come, let us burn him!’ Then those cowherds, shepherds, ploughmen, and travelers gathered grass, wood, and cow dung, piled it on the body of the venerable Sañjīva, set fire to it, and departed. Then, Evil One, the venerable Sañjīva, at the end of that night, having risen from that attainment, shook his robes, and having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered the village for alms. Those cowherds, shepherds, ploughmen, and travelers saw the venerable Sañjīva wandering for alms; having seen him, they thought, ‘It is wonderful, sirs, it is marvelous! This ascetic had died while sitting, but now he has come back to life!’ In this way, Evil One, the designation ‘Sañjīva like Sañjīva’ arose for the venerable Sañjīva."
)
commentary_pali:
507.Bhūtapubbāhaṃ pāpimāti kasmā idaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi? Thero kira cintesi – ‘‘ākāsaṭṭhakadevatānaṃ tāva manussagandho yojanasate ṭhitānaṃ ābādhaṃ karoti. Vuttañhetaṃ – ‘yojanasataṃ kho rājañña manussagandho deve ubbādhatī’ti (dī. ni. 2.415). Ayaṃ pana māro nāgariko paricokkho mahesakkho ānubhāvasampanno devarājā samāno mama kucchiyaṃ pavisitvā antānaṃ anto pakkāsayokāse nisinno ativiya paduṭṭho bhavissati. Evarūpaṃ nāma jegucchaṃ paṭikūlaṃ okāsaṃ pavisitvā nisīdituṃ sakkontassa kimaññaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ bhavissati, kiṃ aññaṃ lajjissati, tvaṃ mama ñātikoti pana vutte mudubhāvaṃ anāpajjamāno nāma natthi, handassa ñātikoṭiṃ paṭivijjhitvā mudukeneva naṃ upāyena vissajjessāmī’’ti cintetvā imaṃ desanamārabhi.

So me tvaṃ bhāgineyyo hosīti so tvaṃ tasmiṃ kāle mayhaṃ bhāgineyyo hosi. Idaṃ paveṇivasena vuttaṃ. Devalokasmiṃ pana mārassa pitu vaṃso pitāmahassa vaṃso rajjaṃ karonto nāma natthi, puññavasena devaloke devarājā hutvā nibbatto, yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā cavati. Añño eko attanā katena kammena tasmiṃ ṭhāne adhipati hutvā nibbattati. Iti ayaṃ māropi tadā tato cavitvā puna kusalaṃ katvā imasmiṃ kāle tasmiṃ adhipatiṭṭhāne nibbattoti veditabbo.

So me tvaṃ bhāgineyyo hosī

Vidhuroti vigatadhuro, aññehi saddhiṃ asadisoti attho. Appakasirenāti appadukkhena. Pasupālakāti ajeḷakapālakā. Pathāvinoti maggapaṭipannā. Kāye upacinitvāti samantato citakaṃ bandhitvā. Aggiṃ datvā pakkamiṃsūti ettakena sarīraṃ pariyādānaṃ gamissatīti citakassa pamāṇaṃ sallakkhetvā catūsu disāsu aggiṃ datvā pakkamiṃsu. Citako padīpasikhā viya pajjali, therassa udakaleṇaṃ pavisitvā nisinnakālo viya ahosi. Cīvarāni papphoṭetvāti samāpattito vuṭṭhāya vigatadhūme kiṃsukavaṇṇe aṅgāre maddamāno cīvarāni vidhunitvā. Sarīre panassa usumamattampi nāhosi, cīvaresu aṃsumattampi najjhāyi, samāpattiphalaṃ nāmetaṃ.

Vidhuro Appakasirenā Pasupālakā Pathāvino Kāye upacinitvā Aggiṃ datvā pakkamiṃsū Cīvarāni papphoṭetvā
commentary_english:
507. Why did the Elder begin this discourse with "<hi rend="bold">Having been in the past, I was an evil-doer</hi>"? The Elder, it seems, thought: "Even the smell of humans afflicts the deities dwelling in the sky who are stationed hundreds of *yojanas* away.

It was said, 'Indeed, Your Majesty, the smell of humans distresses the gods hundreds of *yojanas* away' (Dī. Ni. 2.415). But this Māra, a townsman, very pure, of great power, endowed with *anubhāva*, resembling a divine king, having entered my belly, being seated inside my intestines in a place for excrement, will be exceedingly corrupted. What other improper thing will there be for one able to enter and sit down in such a disgusting, repulsive place? What else will he be ashamed of? If it is said, 'You are my relative,' there is no tenderness to which he will not submit." Thinking, "Having pierced his lineage, I will dismiss him by a gentle means," he began this discourse.

"So, you are my nephew" - so you were my nephew at that time. This was said in the way of tradition. In the world of gods, however, there is no lineage of Māra's father, no lineage of his grandfather, doing kingship. By virtue of merit, he was reborn in the world of gods, having become a divine king, and after living as long as his life lasted, he passed away. Another, a certain one, by his own deed, becomes an overlord in that place, having become an overlord. Thus, this Māra, too, having passed away from there at that time, and again having done good, should be understood to have been reborn as an overlord in that place at this time.

"So, you are my nephew."

*Vidhuro* means without a yoke; that is, dissimilar to others. *Appakasirenā* means with little difficulty. *Pasupālakā* means goat-herds. *Pathāvino* means those who have entered upon the path. *Kāye upacinitvā* means having piled up a pyre all around. *Aggim datvā pakkamiṃsū* means having ascertained the measure of the pyre, thinking, "The body will reach complete consumption in so much," they gave fire in the four directions and departed. The pyre blazed like a lamp flame; it was as if it was the time when the Elder entered a water-cell and sat down. *Cīvarāni papphoṭetvā* means having risen from attainment, when the smoke had disappeared, he shook out the robes, trampling on the embers of *kiṃsuka* color. In his body, there was not even a bit of warmth; in his robes, not even a bit of soot was seen; this is the fruit of attainment.

*Vidhuro*, *appakasirenā*, *pasupālakā*, *pathāvino*, *kāye upacinitvā*, *aggiṃ datvā pakkamiṃsū*, *cīvarāni papphoṭetvā*.

mula_pali:
508. ‘‘Atha kho, pāpima, dūsissa mārassa etadahosi – ‘imesaṃ kho ahaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sīlavantānaṃ kalyāṇadhammānaṃ neva jānāmi āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatike anvāviseyyaṃ – etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosatha paribhāsatha rosetha vihesetha. Appeva nāma tumhehi akkosiyamānānaṃ paribhāsiyamānānaṃ rosiyamānānaṃ vihesiyamānānaṃ siyā cittassa aññathattaṃ, yathā taṃ dūsī māro labhetha otāra’nti. Atha kho te, pāpima, dūsī māro brāhmaṇagahapatike anvāvisi – ‘etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosatha paribhāsatha rosetha vihesetha. Appeva nāma tumhehi akkosiyamānānaṃ paribhāsiyamānānaṃ rosiyamānānaṃ vihesiyamānānaṃ siyā cittassa aññathattaṃ, yathā taṃ dūsī māro labhetha otāra’nti.

‘‘Atha kho te, pāpima, brāhmaṇagahapatikā anvāvisiṭṭhā dūsinā mārena bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosanti paribhāsanti rosenti vihesenti – ‘ime pana muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā kaṇhā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) bandhupādāpaccā ‘‘jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā’’ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti. Seyyathāpi nāma ulūko rukkhasākhāyaṃ mūsikaṃ maggayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati; evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā ‘‘jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā’’ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti. Seyyathāpi nāma kotthu nadītīre macche maggayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati; evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā ‘‘jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā’’ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti. Seyyathāpi nāma biḷāro sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīre mūsikaṃ maggayamāno jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati; evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā ‘‘jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā’’ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyanti. Seyyathāpi nāma gadrabho vahacchinno sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīre jhāyati pajjhāyati nijjhāyati apajjhāyati, evamevime muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kiṇhā bandhupādāpaccā ‘‘jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā’’ti pattakkhandhā adhomukhā madhurakajātā jhāyanti pajjhāyanti nijjhāyanti apajjhāyantī’’ti.

kaṇhā (syā. kaṃ. ka.)

‘‘Ye kho pana, pāpima, tena samayena manussā kālaṅkaronti yebhuyyena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti.
mula_english:
“Then, Evil One, the Mara Dusi considered thus: ‘I do not know the coming or the going of these virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character. Suppose I were to take possession of the *brāhmaṇa* householders, telling them: “Come now, abuse, revile, scold, and harass the virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character. Then perhaps, when they are abused, reviled, scolded, and harassed by you, some change will come about in their minds whereby the Mara Dusi may find an opportunity.”’

“Then, Evil One, the Mara Dusi took possession of those *brāhmaṇa* householders, telling them: ‘Come now, abuse, revile, scold, and harass the virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character. Then perhaps, when they are abused, reviled, scolded, and harassed by you, some change will come about in their minds whereby the Mara Dusi may find an opportunity.’

“Then, Evil One, when the Mara Dusi had taken possession of the *brāhmaṇa* householders, they abused, reviled, scolded, and harassed the virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character thus: ‘These bald-pated recluses, these swarthy menial offspring of the Kinsman’s feet, claim: “We are meditators, we are meditators!” and with shoulders drooping, heads down and all limp, they meditate, premeditate, out-meditate, and mismeditate. Just as an owl on a branch waiting for a mouse meditates, premeditates, out-meditates, and mismeditates, so too these bald-pated recluses, these swarthy menial offspring of the Kinsman’s feet, claim: “We are meditators, we are meditators!” and with shoulders drooping, heads down and all limp, they meditate, premeditate, out-meditate, and mismeditate. Or just as a jackal on a river-bank waiting for fish meditates, premeditates, out-meditates, and mismeditates, so too these bald-pated recluses, these swarthy menial offspring of the Kinsman’s feet, claim: “We are meditators, we are meditators!” and with shoulders drooping, heads down and all limp, they meditate, premeditate, out-meditate, and mismeditate. Or just as a cat by a door-post or a dust-bin or a drain, waiting for a mouse, meditates, premeditates, out-meditates, and mismeditates, so too these bald-pated recluses, these swarthy menial offspring of the Kinsman’s feet, claim: “We are meditators, we are meditators!” and with shoulders drooping, heads down and all limp, they meditate, premeditate, out-meditate, and mismeditate. Or just as a donkey unladen, standing by a door-post or a dust-bin or a drain, meditates, premeditates, out-meditates, and mismeditates, so too, these bald-pated recluses, these swarthy menial offspring of the Kinsman’s feet, claim: “We are meditators, we are meditators!” and with shoulders drooping, heads down and all limp, they meditate, premeditate, out-meditate, and mismeditate.’

“Now, Evil One, on that occasion most of those human beings, when they died, reappeared on the dissolution of the body, after death, in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell.
commentary_pali:
508.Akkosathāti dasahi akkosavatthūhi akkosatha. Paribhāsathāti vācāya paribhāsatha. Rosethāti ghaṭṭetha. Vihesethāti dukkhāpetha. Sabbametaṃ vācāya ghaṭṭanasseva adhivacanaṃ. Yathā taṃ dūsī māroti yathā etesaṃ dūsī māro. Labhetha otāranti labhetha chiddaṃ, kilesuppattiyā ārammaṇaṃ paccayaṃ labheyyāti attho. Muṇḍakātiādīsu muṇḍe muṇḍāti samaṇe ca samaṇāti vattuṃ vaṭṭeyya, ime pana hīḷentā muṇḍakā samaṇakāti āhaṃsu. Ibbhāti gahapatikā. Kiṇhāti kaṇhā, kāḷakāti attho. Bandhupādāpaccāti ettha bandhūti brahmā adhippeto . Tañhi brāhmaṇā pitāmahoti voharanti. Pādānaṃ apaccā pādāpaccā, brahmuno piṭṭhipādato jātāti adhippāyo. Tesaṃ kira ayaṃ laddhi – ‘‘brāhmaṇā brahmuno mukhato nikkhantā, khattiyā urato, vessā nābhito, suddā jāṇuto, samaṇā piṭṭhipādato’’ti.

Jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmāti jhāyino mayaṃ jhāyino mayanti. Madhurakajātāti ālasiyajātā. Jhāyantīti cintayanti. Pajjhāyantītiādīni upasaggavasena vaḍḍhitāni. Mūsikaṃ maggayamānoti sāyaṃ gocaratthāya susirarukkhato nikkhantaṃ rukkhasākhāya mūsikaṃ pariyesanto. So kira upasantūpasanto viya niccalova tiṭṭhati, sampattakāle mūsikaṃ sahasā gaṇhāti. Kotthūti siṅgālo, soṇotipi vadanti. Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭireti sandhimhi ca samale ca saṅkaṭire ca. Tattha sandhi nāma gharasandhi. Samalo nāma gūthaniddhamanapanāḷi. Saṅkaṭiraṃ nāma saṅkāraṭṭhānaṃ. Vahacchinnoti kantārato nikkhanto chinnavaho. Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭireti sandhimhi vā samale vā saṅkaṭire vā. Sopi hi baddhagatto viya niccalo jhāyati.

Jhāyinosmā jhāyinosmā Madhurakajātā Jhāyantī Pajjhāyantī Mūsikaṃ maggayamāno Kotthū Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire sandhi Samalo Saṅkaṭiraṃ Vahacchinno Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire

Nirayaṃ upapajjantīti sace māro manussānaṃ sarīre adhimuccitvā evaṃ kareyya, manussānaṃ akusalaṃ na bhaveyya, mārasseva bhaveyya. Sarīre pana anadhimuccitvā visabhāgavatthuṃ vippaṭisārārammaṇaṃ dasseti, tadā kira so bhikkhū khippaṃ gahetvā macche ajjhottharante viya, jālaṃ gahetvā macche gaṇhante viya, lepayaṭṭhiṃ oḍḍetvā sakuṇe bandhante viya, sunakhehi saddhiṃ araññe migavaṃ carante viya, mātugāme gahetvā āpānabhūmiyaṃ nisinne viya, naccante viya, gāyante viya, bhikkhunīnaṃ rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānesu visabhāgamanusse nisinne viya, ṭhite viya ca katvā dassesi. Manussā araññagatāpi vanagatāpi vihāragatāpi vippaṭisārārammaṇaṃ passitvā āgantvā aññesaṃ kathenti – ‘‘samaṇā evarūpaṃ assamaṇakaṃ ananucchavikaṃ karonti, etesaṃ dinne kuto kusalaṃ, mā etesaṃ kiñci adatthā’’ti. Evaṃ te manussā diṭṭhadiṭṭhaṭṭhāne sīlavante akkosantā apuññaṃ pasavitvā apāyapūrakā ahesuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘nirayaṃ upapajjantī’’ti.

Nirayaṃ upapajjantī
commentary_english:
508. "Abusing" is abusing by means of the ten instances of abuse.
"Reviling" is reviling verbally.
"Harassing" is striking.
"Injuring" is causing suffering.
All of this is simply a verbal expression of striking.
"Just as Māra the defiler" means just as Māra is a defiler of these.
"Would gain an opportunity" means would gain a gap, an object or a condition conducive to the arising of defilements—that is the meaning.
In "shavelings" and so forth, if it is fitting to say that the shaven are shaven or that ascetics are ascetics, then these scornfully say, "They are shavelings, pseudo-ascetics."
"Base" means householders.
"Blacks" means blacks, the meaning is dark.
In "Brahmā's foot-born offspring," here, "Brahmā" is Brahmā is intended (brahmā adhipreto).
For the Brahmins call him the Grandfather.
Offspring of the feet, foot-born of Brahmā, born from the back-foot of Brahmā—that is the intention.
Their conviction is this: "The *brāhmaṇa*s issued forth from Brahmā’s mouth, the *kṣatriya*s from his chest, the *vaiśya*s from his navel, the *śūdra*s from his knees, and the *śramaṇa*s from his back-foot."

"Meditating, we are; meditating, we are" means meditating, we are; meditating, we are.
"Of a sweet kind" means of a lazy kind.
"Meditating" means thinking.
"Meditating," etc., are augmented by means of prefixes.
"Seeking a mouse" means seeking a mouse in the evening for the sake of foraging, one who has come out of a hollow tree to a branch of a tree.
He stands motionless, as if approaching respectfully, and at the opportune time, he suddenly seizes the mouse.
"*Kotthū*" is a jackal, some also say a dog.
"*Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire*" means in a crack, in dirt, and in a rubbish heap.
There, "*sandhi*" means a crack in a house.
"*Samala*" means a drain for discharging excrement.
"*Saṅkaṭiraṃ*" means a rubbish heap.
"*Vahacchinno*" means one who has emerged from a wilderness, with the shoulder cut off.
"*Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire*" means in a crack or in dirt or in a rubbish heap.
He, too, like one whose body is bound, meditates motionlessly.

Meditating, we are; meditating, we are; of a sweet kind; meditating; meditating; seeking a mouse; *kotthū*; *sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire*; *sandhi*; *samala*; *saṅkaṭiraṃ*; *vahacchinno*; *sandhisamalasaṅkaṭire*.
"Falling into hell" means if Māra, having fixated on the bodies of humans, were to do this, there would be no unwholesomeness for humans, [but] there would be for Māra alone.
But without fixating on bodies, he shows an unsuitable object, an occasion for remorse; then, it is as if those monks quickly taking fish were sprinkling them, as if taking a net they were catching fish, as if raising a stick smeared with glue they were binding birds, as if together with dogs they were wandering in the forest hunting animals, as if taking a woman they were sitting in a tavern, as if dancing, as if singing, as if they were showing unsuitable men sitting or standing in the night-time and day-time dwellings of nuns.
Humans, even those gone to the forest, even those gone to the woods, even those gone to the monastery, having seen an object of remorse, come and tell others: "The *śramaṇa*s do such an unascetic and unsuitable thing; where is there wholesomeness from giving to these? Do not give anything to these!"
Thus, those humans, everywhere they saw them, abusing the virtuous, generating demerit, were hell-fillers.
Therefore, it was said, "Falling into hell."

Falling into hell.

mula_pali:
509. ‘‘Atha kho, pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘anvāviṭṭhā kho, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇagahapatikā dūsinā mārena – etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme akkosatha paribhāsatha rosetha vihesetha, appeva nāma tumhehi akkosiyamānānaṃ paribhāsiyamānānaṃ rosiyamānānaṃ vihesiyamānānaṃ siyā cittassa aññathattaṃ, yathā taṃ dūsī māro labhetha otāra’nti. Etha, tumhe, bhikkhave, mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharatha. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharathā’ti.

‘‘Atha kho te, pāpima, bhikkhū kakusandhena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena evaṃ ovadiyamānā evaṃ anusāsiyamānā araññagatāpi rukkhamūlagatāpi suññāgāragatāpi mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā vihariṃsu, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā vihariṃsu. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā vihariṃsu, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā vihariṃsu .
mula_english:
509. “Then, Evil One, the Blessed One Kakusandha, worthy and perfectly enlightened, addressed the monks: ‘The brahmin householders have been taken over by the Māra Dūsi. Come, monks, abuse, revile, scold, and harass the virtuous monks of good character. Perhaps, if you are abused, reviled, scolded, and harassed, some change will occur in their minds, whereby the Māra Dūsi might find an opportunity.’

Come, monks, abide pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (*maitrī-sahagatena cetasā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, and to all as to yourselves, abide pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will.

Abide pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion (*karuṇā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with a mind imbued with appreciative joy (*muditā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekṣā-sahagatena cetasā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, and to all as to yourselves, abide pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will.’

“Then, Evil One, when those monks had been thus advised and instructed by the Blessed One Kakusandha, worthy and perfectly enlightened, they abided pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (*maitrī-sahagatena cetasā*) when gone to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, and to all as to yourselves, they abided pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will.

Abide pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion (*karuṇā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with a mind imbued with appreciative joy (*muditā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekṣā-sahagatena cetasā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, and to all as to yourselves, they abided pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will.
commentary_pali: 509.Anvāviṭṭhāti āvaṭṭitā. Pharitvā vihariṃsūti na kevalaṃ pharitvā vihariṃsu. Kakusandhassa pana bhagavato ovāde ṭhatvā ime cattāro brahmavihāre nibbattetvā jhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahatte patiṭṭhahiṃsu.
commentary_english: 509. anvāviṭṭhāti āvaṭṭitā. pharitvā vihariṃsūti not only pervading they dwelt. But having stood in the instruction of the Blessed One Kakusandha, having developed these four Brahmavihāras, having increased insight, the basis of meditative absorption, they were established in Arhatship.

mula_pali:
510. ‘‘Atha kho, pāpima, dūsissa mārassa etadahosi – ‘evampi kho ahaṃ karonto imesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sīlavantānaṃ kalyāṇadhammānaṃ neva jānāmi āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā, yaṃnūnāhaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatike anvāviseyyaṃ – etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkarotha garuṃ karotha mānetha pūjetha , appeva nāma tumhehi sakkariyamānānaṃ garukariyamānānaṃ māniyamānānaṃ pūjiyamānānaṃ siyā cittassa aññathattaṃ, yathā taṃ dūsī māro labhetha otāra’nti . Atha kho te, pāpima, dūsī māro brāhmaṇagahapatike anvāvisi – ‘etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkarotha garuṃ karotha mānetha pūjetha, appeva nāma tumhehi sakkariyamānānaṃ garukariyamānānaṃ māniyamānānaṃ pūjiyamānānaṃ siyā cittassa aññathattaṃ, yathā taṃ dūsī māro labhetha otāra’nti. Atha kho te, pāpima, brāhmaṇagahapatikā anvāviṭṭhā dūsinā mārena bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti.

‘‘Ye kho pana, pāpima, tena samayena manussā kālaṅkaronti yebhuyyena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.
mula_english:
“Then, Evil One (pāpima), the Mara Dusi considered thus: ‘Even doing this, I do not know the coming or going of these virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character (*sīlavantānaṃ kalyāṇadhammānaṃ*). What if I were to take possession of the *brāhmin* householders (*brāhmaṇagahapatike*)? [I would say]: “Come now, honor (*sakkarotha*), respect (*garuṃ karotha*), revere (*mānetha*), and venerate (*pūjetha*) the virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character; then perhaps, when they are honored, respected, revered, and venerated by you, some change will come about in their minds whereby the Mara Dusi may find an opportunity.”’

“Then, Evil One, the Mara Dusi took possession of those *brāhmin* householders, telling them: ‘Come now, honor, respect, revere, and venerate the virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character; then perhaps, when they are honored, respected, revered, and venerated by you, some change will come about in their minds whereby the Mara Dusi may find an opportunity.’

Then, Evil One, when the Mara Dusi had taken possession of the *brāhmin* householders, they honored (*sakkaronti*), respected (*garuṃ karonti*), revered (*mānenti*), and venerated (*pūjenti*) the virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character.

“Now, Evil One, on that occasion most of those human beings (*manussā*), when they died (*kālaṅkaronti*), reappeared on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), in a happy destination (*sugatiṃ*), even the heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 510.Āgatiṃvā gatiṃ vāti paṭisandhivasena āgamanaṭṭhānaṃ vā, cutivasena gamanaṭṭhānaṃ vā na jānāmi. Siyā cittassa aññathattanti somanassavasena aññathattaṃ bhaveyya. Saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantīti idhāpi purimanayeneva attho veditabbo. Yathā hi pubbe vippaṭisārakaraṃ ārammaṇaṃ dasseti, evamidhāpi pasādakaraṃ. So kira tadā manussānaṃ dassanaṭṭhāne bhikkhū ākāse gacchante viya, ṭhite viya pallaṅkena nisinne viya, ākāse sūcikammaṃ karonte viya, potthakaṃ vācente viya, ākāse cīvaraṃ pasāretvā kāyaṃ utuṃ gaṇhāpente viya, navapabbajite ākāsena carante viya, taruṇasāmaṇere ākāse ṭhatvā pupphāni ocinante viya katvā dassesi. Manussā araññagatāpi vanagatāpi vihāragatāpi pabbajitānaṃ taṃ paṭipattiṃ disvā āgantvā aññesaṃ kathenti – ‘‘bhikkhūsu antamaso sāmaṇerāpi evaṃmahiddhiko mahānubhāvā, etesaṃ dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ nāma hoti, etesaṃ detha sakkarothā’’ti. Tato manussā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ catūhi paccayehi sakkarontā bahuṃ puññaṃ katvā saggapathapūrakā ahesuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī’’ti.
commentary_english:
510.
_āgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā_ means: I do not know either the place of arrival (āgamanaṭṭhānaṃ) in terms of rebirth (paṭisandhivasena), or the place of departure (gamanaṭṭhānaṃ) in terms of decease (cutivasena).

_siyā cittassa aññathatta_nti: there might be otherness (aññathattaṃ) of the mind (cittassa) due to joy (somanassavasena).

_saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī_ti: Here also, the meaning (attho) should be understood (veditabbo) in the same way as before (purimanayena).

Just as previously it shows (dasseti) an objective support (ārammaṇaṃ) that causes remorse (vippaṭisārakaraṃ), so also here it causes serenity (pasādakaraṃ).

It seems that then, in the place where people could see (dassanaṭṭhāne manussānaṃ), he made it appear (katvā dassesi) as if monks (bhikkhū) were going in the sky (ākāse gacchante viya), as if standing (ṭhite viya), as if sitting cross-legged (pallaṅkena nisinne viya), as if doing needlework in the sky (ākāse sūcikammaṃ karonte viya), as if reciting a book (potthakaṃ vācente viya), as if spreading out a robe in the sky (ākāse cīvaraṃ pasāretvā), as if causing the body to be warmed by the heat (kāyaṃ utuṃ gaṇhāpente viya), as if newly ordained monks (navapabbajite) were walking in the sky (ākāsena carante viya), as if young novices (taruṇasāmaṇere) were standing in the sky (ākāse ṭhatvā) and picking flowers (pupphāni ocinante viya).

People (manussā), whether they had gone to the forest (araññagatāpi), gone to the woods (vanagatāpi), or gone to a monastery (vihāragatāpi), having seen (disvā) that practice (taṃ paṭipattiṃ) of the renunciants (pabbajitānaṃ), having come (āgantvā), told (kathenti) others (aññesaṃ): "Even the novices (sāmaṇerāpi), at the very least (antamaso), among the monks (bhikkhūsu), are so mighty (evaṃmahiddhiko) and powerful (mahānubhāvā). What is given (dinnaṃ) to these (etesaṃ) is said to be of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ nāma hoti). Give (detha) and honor (sakkarothā) these (etesaṃ)!"

Then (tato), the people (manussā), honoring (sakkarontā) the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghaṃ) with the four requisites (catūhi paccayehi), having done (katvā) much merit (bahuṃ puññaṃ), were (ahesuṃ) filling (pūrakā) the path to heaven (saggapatha).

Therefore (tena), it was said (vuttaṃ): "They are reborn (upapajjantī) into the heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ)."

mula_pali:
511. ‘‘Atha kho, pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘anvāviṭṭhā kho, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇagahapatikā dūsinā mārena – etha, tumhe bhikkhū sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme sakkarotha garuṃ karotha mānetha pūjetha, appeva nāma tumhehi sakkariyamānānaṃ garukariyamānānaṃ māniyamānānaṃ pūjiyamānānaṃ siyā cittassa aññathattaṃ, yathā taṃ dūsī māro labhetha otāranti. Etha, tumhe, bhikkhave, asubhānupassino kāye viharatha, āhāre paṭikūlasaññino, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññino anabhiratasaññīno (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassino’ti.

‘‘Atha kho te, pāpima, bhikkhū kakusandhena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena evaṃ ovadiyamānā evaṃ anusāsiyamānā araññagatāpi rukkhamūlagatāpi suññāgāragatāpi asubhānupassino kāye vihariṃsu, āhāre paṭikūlasaññino, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññino, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassino.
mula_english:
511. Then, Evil One, the Blessed One Kakusandha, the *arhat*, the fully awakened Buddha, addressed the *bhikkhus*, saying: "Indeed, *bhikkhus*, the Brahmin householders are possessed by Dusi, the Mara. Come, *bhikkhus*, honor, respect, revere, and venerate the virtuous *bhikkhus* of good character (*kalyāṇadhamma*). Perhaps, if you are honored, respected, revered, and venerated, a change may come about in their minds whereby Dusi, the Mara, may find an opportunity. Come, *bhikkhus*, abide contemplating the foulness of the body, perceiving repulsiveness in food, perceiving disenchantment with all the world (*sabbaloka*), contemplating impermanence (*anicca*) in all formations (*sabbasaṅkhāra*)."

Then, Evil One, those *bhikkhus*, when thus advised and instructed by the Blessed One Kakusandha, the *arhat*, the fully awakened Buddha, having gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, abided contemplating the foulness of the body, perceiving repulsiveness in food, perceiving disenchantment with all the world, and contemplating impermanence in all formations.
commentary_pali:
511.Etha tumhe, bhikkhave, asubhānupassino kāye viharathāti bhagavā sakalajambudīpaṃ āhiṇḍanto antamaso dvinnampi tiṇṇampi bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā –

‘‘Asubhasaññāparicitena, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cetasā bahulaṃ viharato methunadhammasamāpattiyā cittaṃ patilīyati patikuṭati pativattati na sampasāriyati, upekkhā vā pāṭikulyatā vā saṇṭhāti.

Āhāre paṭikūlasaññāparicitena, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cetasā bahulaṃ viharato rasataṇhāya cittaṃ patilīyati patikuṭati pativattati na sampasāriyati, upekkhā vā pāṭikulyatā vā saṇṭhāti.

Sabbaloke anabhiratisaññāparicitena, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cetasā bahulaṃ viharato lokacitresu cittaṃ patilīyati patikuṭati pativattati na sampasāriyati, upekkhā vā pāṭikulyatā vā saṇṭhāti.

Aniccasaññāparicitena , bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cetasā bahulaṃ viharato lābhasakkārasiloke cittaṃ patilīyati patikuṭati pativattati na sampasāriyati, upekkhā vā pāṭikulyatā vā saṇṭhātī’’ti (a. ni. 7.49) evaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā –

Etha tumhe, bhikkhave, asubhānupassī kāye viharatha, āhāre paṭikūlasaññino sabbaloke anabhiratisaññino sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassinoti. Imāni cattāri kammaṭṭhānāni kathesi. Tepi bhikkhū imesu catūsu kammaṭṭhānesu kammaṃ karontā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā sabbāsave khepetvā arahatte patiṭṭhahiṃsu, imānipi cattāri kammaṭṭhānāni rāgasantāni dosamohasantāni rāgapaṭighātāni dosamohapaṭighātāni cāti.
commentary_english:
511. The Blessed One, wandering throughout the entirety of Jambudīpa, going to the dwelling places of even two or three bhikkhus, [said:]

“When a bhikkhu often dwells with a mind accustomed to the perception of unattractiveness, his mind shrinks away from sexual intercourse, turns back from it, rolls away from it, and is not drawn toward it, and either equanimity or revulsion becomes settled in him.

When a bhikkhu often dwells with a mind accustomed to the perception of revulsion toward food, his mind shrinks away from craving for flavors, turns back from it, rolls away from it, and is not drawn toward it, and either equanimity or revulsion becomes settled in him.

When a bhikkhu often dwells with a mind accustomed to the perception of non-delight in the entire world, his mind shrinks away from the world’s beautiful things, turns back from it, rolls away from it, and is not drawn toward it, and either equanimity or revulsion becomes settled in him.

But if, when he often dwells with a mind accustomed to the perception of impermanence, his mind shrinks away from gain, honor, and praise … and either equanimity or revulsion becomes settled in him, he should understand: ‘I have developed the perception of impermanence; there is a distinction between my earlier condition and my present one; I have attained the fruit of development.’"

"Come, bhikkhus, dwell contemplating unattractiveness in the body, perceiving revulsion toward food, perceiving non-delight in the entire world, contemplating impermanence in all conditioned things." He taught these four bases of mindfulness.

Those bhikkhus, engaging in these four bases of mindfulness, developing insight, destroying all the āsavas, were established in arahantship. These four bases of mindfulness are calming to lust, calming to aversion and delusion, and are the counter to lust and the counter to aversion and delusion.

mula_pali:
512. ‘‘Atha kho, pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā vidhurena pacchāsamaṇena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho, pāpima, dūsī māro aññataraṃ kumārakaṃ kumāraṃ (sī. pī.) anvāvisitvā sakkharaṃ gahetvā āyasmato vidhurassa sīse pahāramadāsi; sīsaṃ vobhindi sīsaṃ te bhindissāmīti (ka.). Atha kho, pāpima, āyasmā vidhuro bhinnena sīsena lohitena gaḷantena kakusandhaṃyeva bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Atha kho , pāpima, kakusandho bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho nāgāpalokitaṃ apalokesi – ‘na vāyaṃ dūsī māro mattamaññāsī’ti. Sahāpalokanāya ca pana, pāpima, dūsī māro tamhā ca ṭhānā cavi mahānirayañca upapajji.

‘‘Tassa kho pana, pāpima, mahānirayassa tayo nāmadheyyā honti – chaphassāyataniko itipi, saṅkusamāhato itipi, paccattavedaniyo itipi. Atha kho maṃ, pāpima, nirayapālā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – yadā kho te yato te (ka.), mārisa, saṅkunā saṅku hadaye samāgaccheyya. Atha naṃ tvaṃ jāneyyāsi – ‘vassasahassaṃ me niraye paccamānassā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, pāpima, bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni tasmiṃ mahāniraye apacciṃ. Dasavassasahassāni tasseva mahānirayassa ussade apacciṃ vuṭṭhānimaṃ nāma vedanaṃ vediyamāno. Tassa mayhaṃ, pāpima, evarūpo kāyo hoti, seyyathāpi manussassa. Evarūpaṃ sīsaṃ hoti, seyyathāpi macchassa.

yato te (ka.) 513

‘‘Kīdiso nirayo āsi, yattha dūsī apaccatha;

Vidhuraṃ sāvakamāsajja, kakusandhañca brāhmaṇaṃ.

‘‘Sataṃ āsi ayosaṅkū, sabbe paccattavedanā;

Īdiso nirayo āsi, yattha dūsī apaccatha;

Vidhuraṃ sāvakamāsajja, kakusandhañca brāhmaṇaṃ.

‘‘Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

‘‘Majjhe sarassa tiṭṭhanti, vimānā kappaṭṭhāyino;

Veḷuriyavaṇṇā rucirā, accimanto pabhassarā;

Accharā tattha naccanti, puthu nānattavaṇṇiyo.

‘‘Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

‘‘Yo ve buddhena codito, bhikkhu saṅghassa pekkhato;

Migāramātupāsādaṃ, pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayi.

‘‘Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

‘‘Yo vejayantaṃ pāsādaṃ, pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayi;

Iddhibalenupatthaddho, saṃvejesi ca devatā.

‘‘Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

‘‘Yo vejayantapāsāde, sakkaṃ so paripucchati;

Api vāsava jānāsi, taṇhākkhayavimuttiyo;

Tassa sakko viyākāsi, pañhaṃ puṭṭho yathātathaṃ.

‘‘Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

‘‘Yo brahmaṃ paripucchati, sudhammāyābhito sabhaṃ;

Ajjāpi tyāvuso diṭṭhi, yā te diṭṭhi pure ahu;

Passasi vītivattantaṃ, brahmaloke pabhassaraṃ.

‘‘Tassa brahmā viyākāsi, anupubbaṃ yathātathaṃ;

Na me mārisa sā diṭṭhi, yā me diṭṭhi pure ahu.

‘‘Passāmi vītivattantaṃ, brahmaloke pabhassaraṃ;

Sohaṃ ajja kathaṃ vajjaṃ, ahaṃ niccomhi sassato.

‘‘Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

‘‘Yo mahāmeruno kūṭaṃ, vimokkhena aphassayi;

Vanaṃ pubbavidehānaṃ, ye ca bhūmisayā narā.

‘‘Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

‘‘Na ve aggi cetayati veṭhayati (sī.), ‘ahaṃ bālaṃ ḍahāmī’ti;

veṭhayati (sī.)

Bālo ca jalitaṃ aggiṃ, āsajja naṃ sa ḍayhati.

‘‘Evameva tuvaṃ māra, āsajja naṃ tathāgataṃ;

Sayaṃ ḍahissasi attānaṃ, bālo aggiṃva saṃphusaṃ.

‘‘Apuññaṃ pasavī māro, āsajja naṃ tathāgataṃ;

Kinnu maññasi pāpima, na me pāpaṃ vipaccati.

‘‘Karoto cīyati pāpaṃ, cirarattāya antaka;

Māra nibbinda buddhamhā, āsaṃ mākāsi bhikkhusu.

‘‘Iti māraṃ atajjesi, bhikkhu bhesakaḷāvane;

Tato so dummano yakkho, natatthevantaradhāyathā’’ti.

Māratajjanīyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Cūḷayamakavaggo niṭṭhito pañcamo.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Sāleyya verañjaduve ca tuṭṭhi, cūḷamahādhammasamādānañca;

Vīmaṃsakā kosambi ca brāhmaṇo, dūsī ca māro dasamo ca vaggo.

Sāleyyavaggo niṭṭhito pañcamo.

Idaṃ vaggānamuddānaṃ –

Mūlapariyāyo ceva, sīhanādo ca uttamo;

Kakaco ceva gosiṅgo, sāleyyo ca ime pañca.

Mūlapaṇṇāsakaṃ samattaṃ.
mula_english:
512. Then, Evil One, the Blessed One Kakusandha, the worthy one, the perfectly enlightened one, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered a village for alms with the venerable Vidhura as his attendant.

Then, Evil One, the Mara Dusi, possessing a certain boy, taking a potsherd, gave a blow to the head of the venerable Vidhura; he split his head.

Then, Evil One, the venerable Vidhura, with his head split and blood dripping, followed the Blessed One Kakusandha, the worthy one, the perfectly enlightened one, from behind.

Then, Evil One, the Blessed One Kakusandha, the worthy one, the perfectly enlightened one, made an elephant's look, thinking, 'This Mara Dusi is not thinking highly (of me).'

With that look, Evil One, the Mara Dusi fell from that place and reappeared in the Great Hell.

There are three names for the Great Hell, Evil One: the hell of the six sense bases, the hell of being impaled with stakes, and the hell to be felt by oneself.

Then, Evil One, the wardens of hell approached me and said, 'Good sir, when stake meets stake in your heart, then you will know: "I have been roasting in hell for a thousand years."'

For many years, Evil One, for many hundreds of years, for many thousands of years, I roasted in that Great Hell. For ten thousand years I roasted in the auxiliary of that Great Hell, experiencing the feeling called that of emergence from ripening.

My body had such a form, Evil One, just like a human's. My head had such a form, just like a fish's.

513. "What kind of hell was it, where Dusi roasted? He assaulted Vidhura, the disciple, and Kakusandha, the Brahmin."

"There were a hundred iron stakes, all to be felt by oneself; Such was the hell where Dusi roasted, having assaulted Vidhura the disciple, and Kakusandha the Brahmin."

"The monk who directly knows this, is a disciple of the Buddha; By assaulting such a monk, Dark One, you will incur suffering."

"In the middle of the lake stand aerial mansions, enduring for an eon; Of lapis lazuli color, beautiful, radiant, and shining; There the Apsaras dance, in various and diverse colors."

"The monk who directly knows this, is a disciple of the Buddha; By assaulting such a monk, Dark One, you will incur suffering."

"The monk who was urged on by the Buddha, while the Sangha was watching, shook Migara's mother's palace with his big toe."

"The monk who directly knows this, is a disciple of the Buddha; By assaulting such a monk, Dark One, you will incur suffering."

"The monk who shook the Vejayanta palace with his big toe; Supported by the power of his psychic abilities, he stirred up the gods."

"The monk who directly knows this, is a disciple of the Buddha; By assaulting such a monk, Dark One, you will incur suffering."

"The monk who, in the Vejayanta palace, questioned Śakra: 'Do you, Vāsava, know the liberations through the destruction of craving?' To him Śakra explained the question truthfully, when asked."
"That monk who understands this is a disciple of the Buddha; Having approached such a monk, Kaṇha, you will meet with suffering."

"He asks Brahmā about the good doctrine, near the assembly; Even now, friend, is that your view, that view which you formerly held; Do you see the radiance in the Brahmā world as passing away?"

"To him Brahmā explained, in due order, the truth; 'That view is no longer mine, sir, that view which I formerly held.

'I see the radiance in the Brahmā world as passing away; So how could I say today, "I am permanent and eternal?"'"

"That monk who understands this is a disciple of the Buddha; Having approached such a monk, Kaṇha, you will meet with suffering."

"He who touched the peak of great Mount Meru with liberation; The forest of the Pubbavidehas, and those men who lie on the ground."

"That monk who understands this is a disciple of the Buddha; Having approached such a monk, Kaṇha, you will meet with suffering."

"Fire does not intend, 'I will burn the fool'; But the fool, having approached the blazing fire, is burned by it."

"Just so, Māra, having approached the Tathāgata; You will burn yourself, a fool touching the fire."

"Māra generated demerit, having approached the Tathāgata; What do you think, Evil One, that your evil will not ripen?"

"Evil accumulates for one who does it, for a long time, O End-maker; Māra, be disgusted with the Buddha, do not hope for the monks."

"Thus the monk rebuked Māra, in Bhesakaḷāvana; Then that Yakkha, with a sad mind, disappeared right there."

The Māratajjanīya Sutta, the tenth, is finished.

The Cūḷayamaka Vagga, the fifth, is finished.

Its summary:

Sāleyya, Verañja, two Tuṭṭhis, Cūḷa, Mahādhamma-samādāna; Vīmaṃsaka, Kosambi, and the Brahmin, Dūsī, and Māra, the tenth chapter.

The Sāleyya Vagga, the fifth, is finished.

This is the summary of the chapters:

Mūlapariyāya as well, Sīhanāda is supreme; Kakaca as well as Gosiṅga, and Sāleyya, these five.

The Mūlapaṇṇāsaka is complete.
commentary_pali:
512.Sakkharaṃ gahetvāti antomuṭṭhiyaṃ tiṭṭhanapamāṇaṃ pāsāṇaṃ gahetvā. Ayañhi brāhmaṇagahapatikehi bhikkhū akkosāpetvāpi, brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ vasena bhikkhusaṅghassa lābhasakkāraṃ uppādāpetvāpi, otāraṃ alabhanto idāni sahatthā upakkamitukāmo aññatarassa kumārassa sarīre adhimuccitvā evarūpaṃ pāsāṇaṃ aggahesi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘sakkharaṃ gahetvā’’ti.

Sīsaṃ vo bhindīti sīsaṃ bhindi, mahācammaṃ chijjitvā maṃsaṃ dvedhā ahosi. Sakkharā panassa sīsakaṭāhaṃ abhinditvā aṭṭhiṃ āhacceva nivattā. Nāgāpalokitaṃ apalokesīti pahārasaddaṃ sutvā yathā nāma hatthināgo ito vā etto vā apaloketukāmo gīvaṃ aparivattetvā sakalasarīreneva nivattitvā apaloketi. Evaṃ sakalasarīreneva nivattitvā apalokesi. Yathā hi mahājanassa aṭṭhīni koṭiyā koṭiṃ āhacca ṭhitāni, paccekabuddhānaṃ aṅkusalaggāni, na evaṃ buddhānaṃ. Buddhānaṃ pana saṅkhalikāni viya ekābaddhāni hutvā ṭhitāni, tasmā pacchato apalokanakāle na sakkā hoti gīvaṃ parivattetuṃ. Yathā pana hatthināgo pacchābhāgaṃ apaloketukāmo sakalasarīreneva parivattati, evaṃ parivattitabbaṃ hoti. Tasmā bhagavā yantena parivattitā suvaṇṇapaṭimā viya sakalasarīreneva nivattitvā apalokesi , apaloketvā ṭhito pana, ‘‘na vāyaṃ dūsī māro mattamaññāsī’’ti āha. Tassattho, ayaṃ dūsī māro pāpaṃ karonto neva pamāṇaṃ aññāsi, pamāṇātikkantamakāsīti.

Sīsaṃ vo bhindī Nāgāpalokitaṃ apalokesī

Sahāpalokanāyāti kakusandhassa bhagavato apalokaneneva saha taṅkhaṇaññeva. Tamhā ca ṭhānā cavīti tamhā ca devaṭṭhānā cuto, mahānirayaṃ upapannoti attho. Cavamāno hi na yattha katthaci ṭhito cavati, tasmā vasavattidevalokaṃ āgantvā cuto, ‘‘sahāpalokanāyā’’ti ca vacanato na bhagavato apalokitattā cutoti veditabbo, cutikāladassanamattameva hetaṃ. Uḷāre pana mahāsāvake viraddhattā kudāriyā pahaṭaṃ viyassa āyu tattheva chijjitvā gatanti veditabbaṃ. Tayo nāmadheyyā hontīti tīṇi nāmāni honti. Chaphassāyatanikoti chasu phassāyatanesu pāṭiyekkāya vedanāya paccayo.

Sahāpalokanāyā Tamhā ca ṭhānā cavī Tayo nāmadheyyā hontī Chaphassāyataniko

Saṅkusamāhatoti ayasūlehi samāhato. Paccattavedaniyoti sayameva vedanājanako. Saṅkunā saṅku hadaye samāgaccheyyāti ayasūlena saddhiṃ ayasūlaṃ hadayamajjhe samāgaccheyya. Tasmiṃ kira niraye upapannānaṃ tigāvuto attabhāvo hoti, therassāpi tādiso ahosi. Athassa hi nirayapālā tālakkhandhapamāṇāni ayasūlāni ādittāni sampajjalitāni sajotibhūtāni sayameva gahetvā punappunaṃ nivattamānā, – ‘‘iminā te ṭhānena cintetvā pāpaṃ kata’’nti pūvadoṇiyaṃ pūvaṃ koṭṭento viya hadayamajjhaṃ koṭṭetvā, paṇṇāsa janā pādābhimukhā paṇṇāsa janā sīsābhimukhā koṭṭetvā gacchanti, evaṃ gacchantā pañcahi vassasatehi ubho ante patvā puna nivattamānā pañcahi vassasatehi hadayamajjhaṃ āgacchanti. Taṃ sandhāya evaṃ vuttaṃ.

Saṅkusamāhato Paccattavedaniyo Saṅkunā saṅku hadaye samāgaccheyyā

Vuṭṭhānimanti vipākavuṭṭhānavedanaṃ. Sā kira mahāniraye vedanāto dukkhatarā hoti, yathā hi sinehapānasattāhato parihārasattāhaṃ dukkhataraṃ, evaṃ mahānirayadukkhato ussade vipākavuṭṭhānavedanā dukkhatarāti vadanti. Seyyathāpi macchassāti purisasīsañhi vaṭṭaṃ hoti, sūlena paharantassa pahāro ṭhānaṃ na labhati parigalati, macchasīsaṃ āyataṃ puthulaṃ, pahāro ṭhānaṃ labhati , avirajjhitvā kammakāraṇā sukarā hoti, tasmā evarūpaṃ sīsaṃ hoti.

Vuṭṭhānima Seyyathāpi macchassā
commentary_english:
512. "Having taken a stone (sakkharam gahetvā)" means having taken a stone that is the size of what can be held in a closed fist.

Indeed, this one, not obtaining an opportunity after having instigated Brahmins and householders to revile the monks, and after having caused gain and honor to arise for the Sangha of monks through the influence of Brahmins and householders, now, desiring to proceed by his own hand, having decided upon the body of a certain boy, seized such a stone.

With reference to that, it was said, "Having taken a stone."

"He would split your head (sīsaṃ vo bhindī)" means he would split the head; having torn apart the great hide, the flesh would be in two pieces.

The stone, however, having shattered his skull, turned back, striking the bone itself.

"He looked around with a nāga-look (nāgāpalokitaṃ apalokesī)" means, having heard the sound of the strike, just as a nāga-elephant, whether from here or there, desiring to look around, without turning his neck, turns around with his entire body and looks around.

Thus, he looked around, turning around with his entire body.

Just as, indeed, the bones of the great multitude are situated striking against a koṭi by a koṭi, the goads of private Buddhas, not so are those of Buddhas.

The heads of Buddhas, however, are situated having become joined as one, like linked mail; therefore, at the time of looking around backwards, it is not possible to turn the neck.

Just as, however, a nāga-elephant, desiring to look around at the back part, turns around with its entire body, thus it should be turned around.

Therefore, the Blessed One, like a golden image turned by a machine, turned around with his entire body and looked around, and having looked around, standing, said, "This ruining Māra does not think he knows measure."

Its meaning: This ruining Māra, doing evil, does not know measure; he did what exceeds measure.

He would split your head Nāga-look around look around

"With the looking around (sahāpalokanāyā)" means together with the looking around of Kakusandha, the Blessed One, at that very moment.

"He fell from that place (tamhā ca ṭhānā cavī)" means from that place, he fell from the abode of the gods, he was reborn in the great hell, is the meaning.

For a being departing does not fall, standing just anywhere; therefore, having come to the Vasavatti-deva world, he fell; and from the statement, "With the looking around," he should be understood as having fallen not from the Blessed One's looking around, but that this was merely a showing of the time of his fall.

In the case of the eminent great disciple, it should be understood that because of offending, like a tree struck by a mattock, his life right there was cut off and had gone.

"There are three names (tayo nāmadheyyā hontī)" means there are three names.

"Having six sense-fields of contact (chaphassāyataniko)" means a condition for feeling by means of individual sensation in the six sense-fields of contact.

With the looking around He fell from that place There are three names Having six sense-fields of contact

"Struck by a goad (saṅkusamāhato)" means struck together with iron spikes.

"To be felt individually (paccattavedaniyo)" means generating feeling by himself.

"May a goad come together with a goad in the heart (saṅkunā saṅku hadaye samāgaccheyyā)" means may an iron spike come together with an iron spike in the middle of the heart.

In that hell, it is said that the state of existence of those who are reborn there is three leagues; for the Elder also, such was it.

Then, indeed, the hell-wardens there, taking up by themselves burning, blazing, and radiant iron spikes the size of the trunk of a palm tree, repeatedly turning around, "Having thought with this place, you did evil," striking the heart in the opening of a cooking pot, as if pounding grain in a mortar, fifty people going with their faces toward the feet, fifty people going with their faces toward the head, thus, going for five hundred years, reaching both ends, and again turning back, they come to the middle of the heart in five hundred years.

With reference to that, it was said thus.

Struck by a goad To be felt individually May a goad come together with a goad in the heart

"Coming forth (vuṭṭhānima)" means feeling that is the coming forth of the result.

That, it is said, is more painful than the feeling in the great hell, just as seven days of abstinence from stimulating drinks are more painful for one addicted to stimulating drinks; thus, in the great hell, the feeling that is the coming forth of the result in an elevated place is more painful, they say.

"Just as in the case of a fish (seyyathāpi macchassā)" means for a man's head, indeed, is round; for one striking with a spike, the strike does not obtain a place, it slips off; the head of a fish is elongated and broad; the strike obtains a place, not deviating, because of the deed, it is easy; therefore, such is the head.

Coming forth Just as in the case of a fish
